title: UAE Halts Stock Markets For Two Days After Iran Strikes
body: The UAE has ordered its stock markets closed on Monday and Tuesday as the country reels from Iran’s retaliatory missile and drone strikes, in a sign of the growing economic disruption sweeping the Gulf. The UAE Capital Markets Authority said the Abu Dhabi Securities Exchange and Dubai Financial Market would remain shut on March 2 and March 3, citing its supervisory and regulatory role over the country’s capital markets. “The Authority will continue to monitor developments in the region and assess the situation on an ongoing basis, taking any further measures as necessary,” it said in a statement. The UAE’s two exchanges are home to some of the region’s most valuable listed companies. The closure keeps billions of dollars in listed assets in suspension as investors await clarity on the scale of damage from Saturday and Sunday’s strikes, which hit airports, ports and residential areas across the UAE and broader Gulf region. Gulf markets that did open on Sunday saw sharp declines. Saudi Arabia’s benchmark index fell more than 4% at the open, Oman dropped 3% and Egypt’s main index shed 5.44%, while Kuwait suspended trading entirely. All parties were advised to follow official UAE Capital Markets Authority, ADX and DFM channels for updates on the resumption of trading. title: SGX Opens Lower As Iran Tensions And Global Weakness Weigh On Asian Markets
body: Singapore’s stock market opened sharply lower on Monday as escalating tensions in the Middle East and weak global cues rattled investors. The Straits Times Index (STI) fell 96.96 points, or 1.94%, to 4,898.11 by 9.15 am, with 83 gainers against 333 decliners on a turnover of 501.97 million shares valued at S$847.42 million. The slide follows a modest rebound on Friday, when the STI added 30.69 points, or 0.62%, to finish at 4,995.07, ending a three-day losing streak that saw the index drop almost 80 points, or 1.7%. Gains from financials, property stocks and industrials were offset by weakness in trusts and REITs, leaving the index just below the 5,000-point plateau. Key movers included UOL Group, up 5.62%; Yangzijiang Shipbuilding, up 10.71%; and Venture Corporation, down 7.51%. Markets are bracing for renewed volatility after the outbreak of hostilities between the United States and Israel against Iran over the weekend. Crude oil prices surged as fears of Middle East supply disruptions intensified, with West Texas Intermediate for April climbing 2.6% to US$66.92 a barrel. The geopolitical uncertainty is expected to pressure Asian bourses, mirroring Friday’s declines in Europe and the U.S. Wall Street closed lower on Friday, with the Dow tumbling 521.28 points, or 1.05%, to 48,977.92, the NASDAQ falling 210.17 points, or 0.92%, to 22,668.21, and the S&P 500 down 29.98 points, or 0.43%, to 6,878.88. The weakness followed a Labor Department report showing U.S. producer prices rose 0.5% in January, higher than the anticipated 0.3%, adding to inflationary concerns and worries over AI-related layoffs. In Singapore, major banks including DBS and OCBC Bank opened lower, reflecting the cautious mood, while equity futures pointed to continued downside risk. Investors are also monitoring technical indicators in key derivatives, including Nikkei 225 and China A50 futures, as global risk-off sentiment drives flows into safe-haven assets. The market is expected to remain sensitive to both geopolitical developments in the Middle East and US economic data releases, with oil prices and currency movements likely to play a key role in the week ahead. title: Ringgit Opens Marginally Lower Against Greenback After Middle East Strike
body: The ringgit opened marginally lower against the US dollar on the first trading day of March as risk-off sentiment intensified following a joint United States-Israel strike on Iran over the weekend. At 8.01 am, the ringgit eased 0.19 per cent to 3.8985/9205 against the greenback from last Friday’s close of 3.8910/8960. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said key uncertainties centred on the duration and severity of the conflict. “Iran’s move to halt traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and the potential escalation into a regional conflict are immediate risks. As a result, crude oil prices could spike and business sentiment could weaken. “Coupled with concerns over the risk of stagflation in the US, which could also affect other countries, this risk-off environment could see the ringgit trade weaker today,” he told Bernama. At the time of writing, WTI crude rose 7.01 per cent to US$71.72 per barrel, while Brent crude gained 7.34 per cent to US$78.22 per barrel. At the opening, the ringgit strengthened against a basket of major currencies. It appreciated against the euro to 4.5835/6093 from 4.5898/5957 at last Friday’s close, rose against the Japanese yen to 2.4885/5027 from 2.4930/4963 and edged higher against the British pound to 5.2252/2546 from 5.2470/2538 yesterday. Against ASEAN currencies, the local note traded mixed. It edged up against the Singapore dollar to 3.0697/0873 from 3.0742/0784 at last Friday’s close and strengthened against the Thai baht to 12.4732/5512 from 12.5153/5370. However, it slipped against the Philippine peso to 6.76/6.80 from 6.75/6.76 and fell against the Indonesian rupiah to 232.1/233.6 from 231.7/232.2. title: Japanese Stocks Set To Slide As Iran Crisis Saps Risk Appetite
body: Japanese shares are poised to open lower in Tokyo as US-Israeli strikes on Iran hit risk appetite and boosted oil prices. Nikkei 225 CME futures expiring in March fell 1.7% as of 8:02 a.m. in Tokyo. Brent rallied as much as 13% to around US$82 a barrel. Equities are likely to see pressure across the board as investors flee risk assets. Exporters like carmakers and electronics may be weak due to worries around supply chains. Energy and oil-related shares like electricity firms and trading houses could provide some support, however. “Japan’s stock benchmarks could drop by as much as 2% today, based on overseas stock movements, Bitcoin’s decline, and Japan’s high dependence on Middle Eastern crude oil,” said Nobuhiko Kuramochi, vice president of Parasol Research Institute. Sectors like air, sea, and land transportation may face selling pressure due to the downside risk of higher oil prices, while defensive stocks could provide some support, Kuramochi said. Japanese auto parts suppliers like tire makers may also drop, as “sharp oil price increases” would reduce upside expectations for their earnings, wrote Citigroup analyst Arifumi Yoshida in a note. title: Gold Climbs As Middle East War Drives Investor Rush To Safety
body: Gold rose, as war in the Middle East rattled markets and sent investors flocking to safer assets, as reported by Bloomberg . Bullion climbed as much as 1.8% to nearly US$5,375 an ounce in early trading, having gained more than 3% in the previous week. Conflict spread in the Middle East over the weekend after the US and Israel attacked Iran and Tehran responded with waves of missiles at targets in multiple countries. Iran’s supreme leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, was killed on the first day of strikes. Geopolitical tensions have been a key factor in gold’s multiyear rally, which has also been supported by elevated central-bank buying and a wider investor shift away from sovereign bonds and currencies. The metal has gained about a quarter so far this year, despite an abrupt pullback from a record high at the end of January. Bullion posted its seventh consecutive monthly gain in February, the longest streak since 1973. Even ahead of the war with Iran, US President Donald Trump had adopted an increasingly aggressive foreign policy. American troops seized Venezuela’s then-president Nicolás Maduro in January and the administration made threats to annex Greenland. The US and Israel launched strikes across Iran on Saturday, while calling on the population to rise against the Islamic regime. Tehran’s retaliatory barrage hit targets in Israel, as well as US bases and sites in countries including Qatar, the United Arab Emirates, Kuwait and Bahrain. Spot gold rose 1.4% to US$5,353.61 an ounce as of 7.10 am in Singapore. Silver advanced 1.5% to US$95.23. Platinum rose, while palladium edged lower. The Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index, a gauge of the US currency, ended the previous week down 0.1%. title: Bursa Opens Lower As Iran Tensions Weigh On Market
body: Bursa Malaysia opened sharply lower on Monday, with major indices retreating as investors reacted to renewed geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and weak cues from global markets. As of 9.07 am, the FBMKLCI fell 24.52 points to 1,692.09, down 1.43%, while the broader FBM70 index declined 280.63 points or 1.60% to 17,261.84. The F4GBM dropped 14.61 points to 1,001.52, down 1.44%, and the FBMEMAS retreated 186.02 points to 12,425.41, a 1.48% fall. The FBMSHA shed 133.37 points to 12,084.19, a 1.09% decrease. The market continues to be pressured after four straight sessions of losses, with the FBMKLCI sliding nearly 45 points, or 2.6%, last week. Investor sentiment has been dampened by hostilities between the United States and Israel against Iran, which have sparked fears of wider regional instability and sent crude oil prices higher. Among the most active stocks in early trading were Widad Group, which slipped RM0.005 to RM0.010, Pharmaniaga down RM0.020 to RM0.275, and DNEX retreating RM0.025 to RM0.240. On the gainers’ side, Petronas Dagangan rose RM0.700 to RM22.68, Petronas Gas climbed RM0.380 to RM18.34, and Hibiscus Petroleum added RM0.280 to RM1.88. Meanwhile, major blue chips saw mixed movement as Nestle Malaysia fell RM2.30 to RM107.60, F&N declined RM1.84 to RM33.10, and Petronas Chemicals lost RM1.56 to RM30.72. Friday’s session had seen the FBMKLCI finish at 1,716.61, down 24.33 points or 1.40%, with losses concentrated in financials, plantation stocks, telecoms and industrials. The retreat mirrored weakness on Wall Street, where the Dow tumbled 521.28 points to 48,977.92, the NASDAQ slipped 210.17 points to 22,668.21, and the S&P 500 fell 29.98 points to 6,878.88. The decline follows a Labor Department report showing U.S. producer prices rose 0.5% in January, above the expected 0.3%, intensifying worries about inflation and a potential stagflation period. Coupled with concerns over AI-related layoffs and escalating tensions in the Middle East, analysts expect Bursa Malaysia to test support around the 1,700-point level in the coming days. Crude oil prices remain elevated, with West Texas Intermediate for April rising 2.6% to US$66.92 a barrel on Friday, further reinforcing the cautious sentiment among investors. body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has maintained its bearish stance on Hang Seng Index Futures (HSIF), advising traders to retain short positions initiated at 26,367 points on Feb 26, with a stop-loss set at 28,600 points. Based on the prevailing technical indicators, the firm anticipates the HSIF will resume its downward trajectory in the coming sessions and has kept its bearish bias unchanged. title: Weekly Recap: Kospi Soars Past 6,000 Before Profit-Taking Pullback
body: South Korean equities ended the week of Feb 23–27 on a mixed note, with the benchmark KOSPI hitting fresh record highs before retreating on late profit-taking. The KOSPI surged at the start of the week, climbing past the 6,000-point milestone on Feb 23, fueled by strong demand for semiconductor and technology stocks and positive global growth sentiment. Momentum extended to Feb 26, when the index briefly topped 6,300, reflecting enthusiasm over robust earnings prospects and artificial intelligence-led demand. Tech heavyweights and large-cap counters led the advance, with semiconductors particularly buoyed by sustained institutional and foreign buying. Investor optimism underpinned broad participation across growth-oriented sectors, propelling the index to historic levels. However, gains moderated late in the week as profit-taking intensified. On Feb 27, the KOSPI retreated about 1% to close at 6,244.13, snapping a six-day winning streak. Heavy foreign selling weighed on sentiment, while domestic retail and institutional investors helped cushion the decline. Despite the pullback, overall market sentiment remained constructive. The index continued to trade near record highs, supported by underlying strength in technology stocks and selective buying across major sectors, highlighting resilience in South Korea’s equity market following its historic rally. The week underscored the KOSPI’s bullish trajectory, even as short-term consolidation emerged after its landmark breakout. title: Oil Jumps 10%, Could Hit US$100 After Strike On Iran
body: Brent crude jumped 10 per cent to about $80 a barrel over the counter on Sunday, oil traders said, while analysts predicted that prices could climb as high as $100 after U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran plunged the Middle East into a new war. “While the military attacks are themselves supportive for oil prices, the key factor here is the closing of the Strait of Hormuz,” said Ajay Parmar, director of energy and refining at ICIS.Most tanker owners, oil majors and trading houses have suspended crude oil, fuel and liquefied natural gas shipments via the Strait of Hormuz, trade sources said, after Tehran warned ships against moving through the waterway. More than 20 per cent of global oil is moved through the Strait of Hormuz. “We expect prices to open (after the weekend) much closer to $100 a barrel and perhaps exceed that level if we see a prolonged outage of the Strait,” Parmar said. Middle East leaders have warned Washington that a war on Iran could lead to oil prices jumping to more than $100 a barrel, said RBC analyst Helima Croft. Barclays analysts also said prices could hit $100. The OPEC+ group of oil producers agreed on Sunday to raise output by 206,000 barrels per day (bpd) from April, a modest increase representing less than 0.2 per cent of global demand. While some alternate infrastructure could be used to bypass the Strait of Hormuz, the net impact from its closure would be a loss of 8 million to 10 million bpd of crude oil supply even after diverting some flows through Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline and Abu Dhabi pipeline, said Rystad energy economist Jorge Leon. Rystad expects prices to rise by $20 to about $92 a barrel when trade opens. The Iran crisis also prompted Asian governments and refiners to assess oil stockpiles and alternative shipping routes and supplies. title: Wall Street Ends Lower As AI Valuation Worries Mount
body: Wall Street closed in the red on Feb 27 as investors grappled with lofty technology valuations and lingering uncertainty over the broader impact of artificial intelligence (AI). Reuters reported that the benchmark S&P 500 fell 0.43%, the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 1.05% and the Nasdaq Composite slid 0.92%, as semiconductor stocks retreated from recent highs. Shares of Nvidia, the world’s most valuable company and a bellwether for the AI trade, fell 3.5%, extending losses from the prior session despite posting better-than-expected earnings. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index declined 1.2%. Globally, the MSCI All Country World Index slipped 0.25% on the day but still posted a weekly gain of 0.35%, while Europe’s STOXX 600 edged up 0.11%. US Treasury yields fell as investors sought safety, with the 10-year yield down 6.3 basis points (bps) to 3.96%, and the two-year yield also falling 6.3bps to 3.385%. Germany’s 10-year Bund yield slipped 1bps to 2.644%. In currency markets, sterling eased 0.07% to US$1.3447 after Britain’s Labour Party suffered an election setback in Greater Manchester. The dollar index was little changed, down 0.06% at 97.67, while the euro rose 0.14% to US$1.1813. The yen pared earlier gains to trade at 156.18 per dollar following softer Japanese inflation and factory output data. Safe-haven demand lifted precious metals, with spot gold climbing 1.5% to US$5,263.59 an ounce and silver surging 6.1% to US$93.74. Investors now turn their focus to further developments in AI-driven earnings momentum and geopolitical negotiations, both of which are likely to steer market sentiment in the weeks ahead. title: South Korean Stocks Snap Rally As Kospi Closes Down 1%
body: South Korea’s stock market slid at the close on Feb 27, with the Korea Composite Stock Price Index (Kospi) dropping 1% to 6,244.13, ending a six-day winning streak as foreign investors stepped up profit-taking after strong recent gains. Heavy net selling by overseas funds, around 6.8 trillion Korean won, drove much of the weakness, outweighing solid domestic buying from retail and institutional traders that helped cushion the market. Technology and large-cap stocks led declines, with heavyweight semiconductor names under pressure following broad market profit-taking and softer cues from global peers. Despite the pullback, the Kospi still posted strong weekly gains and remains elevated after clearing the 6,000 milestone earlier in the week as part of a broader February rally driven by export demand and artificial intelligence-linked tech optimism. Trading volume was brisk, reflecting active repositioning by investors ahead of month-end, while the Korean won softened against the US dollar amid the sell-off. title: Despite 4Q Decline Syarikat Takaful Remains Favourable
body: MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB Research) and Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) have maintained BUY calls on Syarikat Takaful Malaysia Keluarga Bhd (STMB), with revised target prices of RM3.95 and RM4.09 respectively, highlighting solid fundamentals, robust capital, and attractive dividend yields as key positives. The research house noted that both family and general takaful segments delivered strong growth, while management’s outlook remains neutral yet constructive. STMB reported FY25 core net profit of RM386 million, up 2% year-on-year, largely driven by higher takaful revenue which offset increased claims and tax charges. Fourth-quarter core profit fell 20% quarter-on-quarter to RM92 million, impacted by the absence of the previous quarter’s investment windfall. Despite the quarterly decline, results were broadly in line with market expectations, accounting for around 102% of consensus full-year forecasts. Gross written premiums (GWP) for the general takaful segment exceeded expectations, rising 14% year-on-year and outperforming the industry growth of 12.4%, supported by strong fire and motor results. The family takaful segment continues to benefit from a diversified bancassurance network, limiting exposure to any single loan product and allowing margins to remain stable. Management also flagged that retakaful repricing in FY25 was moderate, aided by a relatively benign claims environment. Looking ahead, STMB expects continued momentum, underpinned by sustained bank-led distribution, improving general takaful performance, and stable underwriting margins. Analysts highlighted that the group’s strong capital position and progressive dividend policy, targeting around 40% payout, provide flexibility for strategic initiatives, including retail expansion and digital investments. FY26 core net profit forecasts have been revised upwards to RM389 million by MBSB, with dividend yield projected at 5.4%, while HLIB projects RM390.2 million and a 5.5% yield. As of 3.31 pm, the stock price decreased 2.12% to RM3.23. title: Bitcoin Slide Below US$64,000 After Iran Strike
body: Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies fell sharply after the US and Israel began striking targets across Iran on Saturday, causing ripples across high-risk assets. Bitcoin dropped as much as 3.8% to $63,038, before stablising to trade around the $64,000 mark as of 6 a.m. in New York. Ether, the second-largest token, slid as much as 4.5% to $1,836. Roughly $128 billion in market value was erased across digital assets in the immediate aftermath of the news, according to data from CoinGecko. For Bitcoin, the weekend losses extend a months-long selloff in crypto markets, beginning with the liquidation of some $19 billion in leveraged positions in October. Bitcoin has fallen around 50% from its all-time peak of over $126,000 earlier that month, unable to latch on to rallies in gold and other safe-haven assets. title: Wall Street Slides As Nvidia Fails To Spark AI Rally
body: US stocks fell sharply on Thursday as a post-earnings sell-off in Nvidia weighed heavily on technology counters, dragging the Nasdaq lower and putting pressure on the broader market. The Nasdaq Composite dropped 273.69 points, or 1.18%, to 22,878.38, while the S&P 500 shed 37.27 points, or 0.54%, to 6,908.86. In contrast, the Dow Jones Industrial Average edged up 17.05 points, or 0.03%, to 49,499.20, supported by strength in cyclical sectors. Nvidia shares slid 5.5% despite posting fourth-quarter results that exceeded analysts’ expectations and issuing guidance above market estimates. Investors appeared unsettled by slowing revenue growth and increasingly challenging year-on-year comparisons. The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor index dropped 3.2%, leaving it close to ending what would have been a record 11-week winning streak. “It feels like an Nvidia hangover that’s specific to the AI space,” said Michael Green, chief strategist at Simplify Asset Management in Philadelphia. He added, “The S&P itself is being dragged down by Nvidia and the Magnificent 7, and the Nasdaq is really getting hammered.” “It’s as simple as investors being levered long in Nvidia and short the AI disruption,” Green added. He concluded, “And when that failed to materialize in a large enough scale, they sold out of their position, driving Nvidia down and pushing the stocks they were short back up.” Among the S&P 500’s 11 major sectors, technology and communication services posted the steepest losses, while financials rose 1.3%, lifted by gains in major banks. The software and services index climbed 1.4%, even as AI-linked volatility persisted. Trading volume on US exchanges totalled 19.55 billion shares, below the 20-day average of 20.31 billion. title: Tech Rally Lifts Wall Street To Two-Week High
body: Wall Street closed higher on Wednesday, with technology shares leading a rebound that pushed major indices to two-week highs as investors refocused on the long-term promise of artificial intelligence rather than its disruption risks. The Nasdaq Composite jumped 288.40 points, or 1.26%, to 23,152.08, marking the strongest percentage gain among the three major indices. The S&P 500 advanced 56.06 points, or 0.81%, to 6,946.13, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 307.65 points, or 0.63%, to 49,482.15. Chipmakers and software counters spearheaded gains. The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor index climbed 1.6% ahead of Nvidia’s earnings, while the S&P Software & Services index rebounded 2.9%, trimming part of its 23% year-to-date decline. Nvidia, at the forefront of the AI revolution, reported fourth-quarter revenue of $68.13 billion, beating analyst estimates. Its shares were up about 3% in extended trading. “We’re in the middle of a push-pull here between some negative sentiment and some extreme price action in parts of the market,” said Zach Hill, head of portfolio management at Horizon Investments in Charlotte, North Carolina. “I think the (AI) disruption concerns are more acute right now than worries over return on investment,” Hill added. “Investors are trying to grapple with what could potentially be existential risk, and that’s a bigger deal than not receiving as much payout as you would like.” Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin said it is not clear that the AI rollout will displace workers, adding that the technology could enable workers and improve labour market efficiency. Gains were broad, with advancing issues outnumbering decliners by 1.78-to-1 on the NYSE and 2.02-to-1 on the Nasdaq. However, pockets of weakness remained. Axon Enterprise surged 17.6% after beating quarterly profit estimates. In contrast, First Solar slid 13.6% and Lowe’s Companies fell 5.6% after issuing weaker-than-expected annual sales guidance, dragging housing and homebuilder stocks lower despite mortgage rates hitting a three-and-a-half-year low last week. Consumer staples also lagged. Brown-Forman dropped 7.6% and Molson Coors declined 4.8% after Diageo projected a 2% to 3% organic sales decline in 2026 and halved its interim dividend. GoDaddy tumbled 14.3% after forecasting annual revenue below expectations. Total trading volume reached 17.50 billion shares, below the 20-day average of 20.27 billion. title: Ringgit Opens Firmer On Positive Outlook, Gains On Softer US Dollar
body: The ringgit opened firmer against the US dollar on Thursday, underpinned by Malaysia’s positive economic outlook and a softer greenback. At 8 am, the local currency strengthened to 3.8850/8960 against the dollar from Wednesday’s close of 3.8900/8955. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the government is reviewing this year’s gross domestic product growth forecast, currently projected at 4.0 to 4.5 per cent. “Given last year’s performance, the revision is likely to be upward. That in itself signals a positive outlook,” he told Bernama . He added that monetary policy should remain supportive, with the central bank widely expected to keep interest rates unchanged. Meanwhile, the US dollar index slipped 0.17 per cent to 97.675, reflecting continued softness in the greenback. Mohd Afzanizam noted that the dollar-ringgit pair had hovered near its immediate support level of RM3.8722 on Wednesday before trading around RM3.8855 in the afternoon session. “The ringgit is likely to remain well supported in the near term, given the softer US dollar outlook and Malaysia’s positive economic prospects,” he said. At the open, however, the ringgit traded lower against a basket of major currencies. It eased against the Japanese yen to 2.4878/4950 from 2.4848/4885 at Wednesday’s close, slipped versus the British pound to 5.2669/2818 from 5.2585/2659 and fell against the euro to 4.5901/6031 from 4.5855/5920. The ringgit was mixed against its ASEAN peers. It rose against the Thai baht to 12.4988/5418 from 12.5121/5374, strengthened against the Indonesian rupiah to 231.2/232.0 from 231.5/231.9 and edged up versus the Philippine peso to 6.75/6.78 from 6.76/6.78. However, it slipped against the Singapore dollar to 3.0760/0850 from 3.0736/0782. title: Bullish On TSH After Positive Financial Move
body: Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) has upgraded TSH Resources Bhd to BUY from Hold, with a higher target price of RM1.40, citing a 14.8% capital upside and a 4.1% dividend yield. The research house noted that FY25 core earnings of RM195.2 million (+27.5% YoY) came in line with expectations, accounting for 100–103% of consensus estimates. The upgrade reflects the company’s strengthened financial position, consistent earnings and a 7.2% reduction in share base following the cancellation of 100 million treasury shares. TSH declared a final dividend of 5.0 sen per share (ex-date: 14 Apr 2026) and revised its dividend payout ratio to a minimum of 30% of net earnings, up from the previous 20–30% range. Core earnings for 4Q25 fell 30.4% quarter-on-quarter and 46.1% year-on-year to RM36.5 million, weighed by lower sales volume, softer crude palm oil (CPO) prices and higher production costs. Weaker refining margins from joint ventures also contributed to the quarterly decline. Despite the softer fourth-quarter performance, FY25 results were buoyed by higher realised palm product prices, increased CPO sales volume, lower production costs and controlled corporate expenses. Exceptional items for the year included fair value losses on derivatives (RM0.3 million), impairments (RM1.9 million), write-offs and write-downs (RM5.3 million), adjustments on biological assets (RM1.4 million), forest planting (RM1.7 million) and unrealised foreign exchange losses (RM2.7 million). TSH Resources’ financial moves, including the treasury share cancellation and revised dividend policy, underpin HLIB’s bullish stance. The target price of RM1.40 is based on 10.5 times the revised FY26 core EPS of 13.3 sen, offering investors both yield and capital growth potential amid a stable outlook for the plantation sector. As of 3.06 pm, the stock price was noted at RM1.22. title: Analyst Project 14% CAGR For Inta Bina
body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has maintained a BUY rating on Inta Bina Bhd with a target price of RM0.72, offering a 67% upside and a projected FY26F yield of 5%. RHB Research highlighted that FY25 core profit of RM38.6 million (+19% YoY) came broadly in line with expectations at 102% of RHB’s projection, though it fell slightly short of the Street consensus at 97%. The analyst remains optimistic on the company’s outlook, projecting a three-year earnings compound annual growth rate of 14%, underpinned by a sustainable annual orderbook replenishment of at least RM800 million and ongoing property development projects. INTA’s construction division posted a revenue decline of 11% YoY in 4Q25, yet its PAT rose 3% YoY, resulting in a 4Q25 margin of 5.8% versus 5% a year ago. Its property arm, driven by the Senuri Residence project with a gross development value of RM205 million, saw PAT triple to RM2.5 million from RM0.7 million in 4Q24, lifting its margin to 13.7% from 4.6%. The group held an outstanding orderbook of RM1.7 billion as of end-September 2025, representing 2.6 times FY25 construction revenue, alongside a tenderbook exceeding RM4.9 billion as of 25 February. New job wins for FY25 stood at approximately RM865 million, with a projected replenishment of RM1 billion for FY26. RHB Research’s target price reflects a sum-of-parts valuation pegged to FY26F earnings per share with an 11 times P/E multiple, including a 2% ESG premium based on a 3.1 ESG score. The stock currently trades at 5.9 times FY26F P/E, below the five-year mean of the Bursa Malaysia Construction Index at 14 times, a gap the analyst views as unjustified given INTA’s consistent project wins and upcoming property developments valued at around RM500 million. Potential upside catalysts include further job wins in Johor from long-term clients such as Ecoworld and UEM Sunrise, while sluggish job replenishment remains a key downside risk. As of 3.10 pm, the stock price was noted at RM0.425. title: Yen Slips Amid Policy Concerns, Australian Dollar Surges On Inflation Surprise
body: The Japanese yen hovered near a two-week low on Wednesday as the government nominated two academics perceived as willing to tolerate higher inflation to stimulate growth to join the Bank of Japan board. The yen was last at 155.77 per dollar, having dropped 0.8% overnight to 156.28. “According to the report yesterday, Takaichi-san looks to be negative on higher policy rates and then she chose at least one super-dovish member,” said Tohru Sasaki, chief strategist at Fukuoka Financial Group and former BOJ official, referring to Ayano Sato. “These choices reflect the reflationist tendencies of the Takaichi cabinet.” Elsewhere in Asia, the Australian dollar surged 0.7% to $0.7109 after a stronger-than-expected inflation reading raised the prospect of additional rate hikes. The New Zealand dollar edged higher to $0.5983, while sterling and the euro posted smaller gains, leaving the dollar at $1.3520 against the pound and $1.1796 against the euro. China’s yuan extended sharp gains to an almost three-year peak of 6.8703, supported by the U.S. Supreme Court striking down major tariffs and strong export performance. “The fundamental underpinnings for our CNY appreciation view – a starting point of deep currency undervaluation and the remarkable strength of the export sector – remain very much in place,” said analysts at Goldman Sachs. The yen has been under pressure for years due to Japan’s low interest rates, with concerns over fiscal strain intensifying after Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi took office in October. title: Wall Street Rebounds As AI Optimism Lifts Tech Stocks
body: Wall Street ended higher on Tuesday, led by a rally in technology counters as renewed enthusiasm over artificial intelligence helped markets recover from recent volatility. The Nasdaq Composite climbed 236.41 points, or 1.05%, to 22,863.68. The S&P 500 advanced 52.32 points, or 0.77%, to 6,890.07, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 370.44 points, or 0.76%, to 49,174.50. Semiconductor stocks outperformed, with the Philadelphia SE Semiconductor index leading gains. The S&P Software & Services index rose 1.3%, recovering from recent heavy losses driven by concerns that AI tools could disrupt traditional business models. Advanced Micro Devices jumped 8.8% after announcing plans to sell up to US$60 billion worth of AI chips to Meta Platforms over the next five years. Meta edged 0.3% higher. FactSet surged 5.9%, while US-listed shares of Thomson Reuters rallied 11.5%. Salesforce gained 4.1%, ranking among the Dow’s top percentage advancers. The gains came as artificial intelligence lab Anthropic unveiled new plug-ins aimed at sectors including investment banking and human resources. The tools were developed in collaboration with partners such as Thomson Reuters, Salesforce and FactSet. “Anthropic’s been busy with announcements that their product is going to do all these new and sort of wonderful things,” said Robert Pavlik, senior portfolio manager at Dakota Wealth in Fairfield, Connecticut. “It’s still early on in the process and certainly acceptance and the application of these tools is probably still a ways away.” Despite the rebound, uncertainty surrounding AI’s broader economic impact persisted. Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook warned the technology could lead to a possible rise in unemployment, while Governor Christopher Waller said he does not expect AI to disrupt the labour market. Trade policy concerns also lingered. The US Supreme Court last week struck down many of President Donald Trump’s tariffs, prompting threats of fresh levies on imported goods. “There are still questions about the deals that were in place already,” Pavlik said. “What happens to those? Are they still happening?” Market breadth was positive, with advancing stocks outnumbering decliners by roughly two-to-one on both the New York Stock Exchange and the Nasdaq. The S&P 500 recorded 46 new 52-week highs, while the Nasdaq posted 99 new highs. Airlines and travel-related stocks rebounded nearly 3% after sharp losses a day earlier caused by a winter storm that paralysed parts of the US Northeast. Home Depot rose 2.0% after beating fourth-quarter estimates and maintaining its annual guidance. Keysight Technologies soared 23.1% after forecasting second-quarter profit above expectations. “We’re in for a period of time where the market will be going through some uncertainty and today we’re seeing a little bit of a buy on the dip,” said Matthew Keator, managing partner in the Keator Group in Lenox, Massachusetts. “We’re going to see day-to-day movements but overall, there’s so much unknown in terms of how AI ends up being additive or disruptive to some of these companies.” Total trading volume reached 17.06 billion shares, below the 20-day average of 20.29 billion. title: Stock Today: Telekom Slides Near 5% As 5G Strategy Evolves
body: Telekom Malaysia Bhd (TM) saw its shares drop 4.79% to RM7.75, with a total of 16.7 million shares traded as of 4.02 pm, reflecting investor caution amid the company’s ongoing 5G transition. The stock opened at RM8.14, reached a high of RM8.19, and fell to a low of RM7.60 during the session. The decline comes after TM announced a new Multi-Operator Core Network (MOCN) arrangement with U Mobile, marking a strategic shift from the single-network model. TM also exercised its right to terminate its 5G wholesale access agreement with Digital Nasional Berhad (DNB), in line with the Malaysian government’s dual 5G network framework designed to encourage infrastructure competition. TM aims to leverage the MOCN model to enhance its “quad-play” offerings, integrating 5G more deeply across fixed, mobile, content, and smart services. The move is a key part of the Group’s “PWR 2030” strategy to transform into a digital powerhouse by 2030, optimising costs, service quality, and its role as Malaysia’s digital backbone. Financially, TM posted revenue of RM3.26 billion for 4Q2025, up 6.8% year-on-year, while profit after tax fell to RM222 million. For the full year, revenue reached RM11.8 billion, with PATAMI of RM1.71 billion. In line with strong shareholder returns, TM declared a second interim dividend of 14.5 sen per share and a special dividend of 4 sen, bringing total FY2025 dividends to 31 sen per share, or approximately RM1.19 billion. As TM enters 2026, CEO Amar Huzaimi Md Deris emphasised the Group’s focus on digitalisation and delivering integrated 5G solutions for consumers, SMEs, and large enterprises while streamlining operations for future growth. title: Nikkei Set To Breach 60,000 Milestone By Mid-2027 On Earnings Growth, Foreign Inflows
body: Japan’s Nikkei share average will probably gain only marginally through June before it pushes past the key psychological 60,000 mark by the middle of next year, a Reuters poll of equity strategists showed. The benchmark index, up over 13 per cent so far this year, has been supported by strong corporate earnings and optimism over fiscal stimulus under Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi. The Nikkei hit a record intraday high of 58,015.08 on Feb 12, days after Takaichi’s landslide victory in a snap election for the lower house. According to the median forecast of 15 analysts polled between Feb 13 and Feb 24, the index will stand at 57,500 at the end of June, about 0.3 per cent above Tuesday’s close of 57,321.09. That forecast was higher than 52,000 projected in a November poll. “Given the rapid run-up so far, we expect a period of time-based consolidation to continue for a while to dispel the sense of overvaluation,” said Hiroshi Namioka, chief strategist at T&D Asset Management. “However, we’re not expecting a price pullback.” Median forecasts showed the Nikkei reaching 58,500 by the end of 2026 and climbing to 60,750 by mid-2027. Foreign investor inflows are also expected to gather momentum amid a solid domestic earnings outlook, said Yugo Tsuboi, chief strategist at Daiwa Securities. The latest government data showed foreign investors bought a net 1.42 trillion yen ($9.16 billion) worth of Japanese stocks in the week to February 14, the largest weekly inflow since last October, helping lift the market to record highs. Strategists were also asked about artificial intelligence and the risk of a pullback in share prices. All 10 respondents said their views on AI as a driver of equities had changed little over the past three months. Demand across data centre supply chains, including semiconductors, chipmaking equipment and optical fibre should remain strong as long as US hyperscalers continue investing in AI, said Kiyohide Nagata, chief strategist at Tokai Tokyo Intelligence Laboratory. At the same time, selling pressure has intensified in sectors such as software over the past three months as companies in those areas could face disruption from AI, Nagata said. Nine of 10 respondents said a correction in the Nikkei, meaning a decline of 10 per cent from recent highs, was unlikely over the coming three months. “US equities are showing some wobble, such as the AI rally pausing … but a sharp correction looks unlikely. And any spillover to Japan should be mild,” said Hitoshi Asaoka, chief strategist at Asset Management One. title: Gold Dips For Second Day On Prospects Of Prolonged Rate Hold
body: Gold declined slightly, extending a loss in the previous session, on reduced expectations that the US Federal Reserve will cut interest rates in the near term, per Bloomberg . Bullion edged lower to around US$5,130 an ounce in early trading, following a 1.6% drop on Tuesday that snapped a four-day advance. Interest rates are likely to stay unchanged “for some time” as recent economic data shows an improvement in the American labour market, Fed Bank of Boston President Susan Collins said. Minutes from the Fed’s January policy meeting, published earlier this month, showed officials at the US central bank appeared to be wary of cutting rates. Higher borrowing costs are typically a headwind for precious metals, which don’t yield interest. Gold fell 0.3% to US$5,131.00 an ounce as of 7:27 a.m. Singapore time. Silver dropped 0.4% to US$86.80. Platinum and palladium also declined. The Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index ended the previous session marginally higher. body: Bursa Malaysia opened on a mixed note on Wednesday, with the benchmark FBM KLCI easing 1.94 points or 0.11% to 1,752.07, as investors navigated the debut of Teamstar Bhd and took cues from Wall Street’s late gains in technology shares. title: Wall Street Slides As AI Fears Rattle Markets
body: Wall Street ended sharply lower on Monday, with all three major benchmarks falling more than 1% as investors retreated from high-risk assets amid renewed tariff uncertainty and concerns over artificial intelligence disruption. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 821.91 points, or 1.66%, to 48,804.06. The S&P 500 fell 71.76 points, or 1.04%, to 6,837.75, while the Nasdaq Composite declined 258.80 points, or 1.13%, to 22,627.27. The retreat followed a 6-3 ruling by the US Supreme Court on Friday that President Donald Trump overstepped his authority by imposing reciprocal tariffs under an economic emergency law. The decision drew condemnation from Trump, who threatened a 15% temporary tariff on all imports despite existing trade agreements. At the same time, investors grappled with persistent unease over the cost and disruptive potential of emerging AI technologies. Financial stocks fell 3.3% and software-related firms slid 4.3%. “The question about AI is twofold: How much is it going to cost, and who all is going to be disrupted?” said Tom Hainlin, national investment strategist at US Bank Wealth Management in Minneapolis. “You’ve seen the market react to headlines, it’s ‘sell first, assess later.'” He added: “It’s a perspective of what may happen as opposed to what has happened.” Safe-haven demand pushed gold prices up 2.6%. Airlines and travel-related stocks dropped sharply as a severe winter storm paralysed parts of the Northeast, with flight cancellations in the New York area reaching as high as 98%, according to Flightaware.com. The Dow Transports index fell 2.9%. Among individual movers, Domino’s Pizza rose 4.1% after reporting stronger-than-expected quarterly same-store sales, while PayPal jumped 5.8% on reports of takeover interest. Healthcare outperformed, with Eli Lilly gaining 4.9% after rival Novo Nordisk saw its obesity drug underperform in a head-to-head trial. Decliners outpaced advancers by more than two-to-one on both the NYSE and Nasdaq. Total volume across US exchanges stood at 18.39 billion shares, below the 20-session average of 20.62 billion. body: Singapore shares opened in the red on Tuesday, with the benchmark Straits Times Index falling 43.73 points, or 0.87%, to 4,997.60 as at 9.05 am, weighed down by losses in the banking sector. UOB, Southeast Asia’s third-largest bank by assets, posted a 7% year-on-year decline in net profit to S$1.41 billion (US$1.11 billion) for October to December, as margin pressures offset loan growth. The result, however, beat the mean analyst estimate of S$1.35 billion. Earlier in 2025, UOB suffered a 72% plunge in third-quarter profit but rebounded in the fourth quarter on lower credit costs. Its net interest margin, a key measure of lending profitability, fell to 1.89% for the full year from 2.03% in 2024, while net interest income slid 3% to S$9.36 billion. On the positive side, net fee income hit a record S$2.6 billion, supported by wealth management and loan-related fees, with high-net-worth assets under management rising 6% to S$201 billion. The bank also declared a total dividend of S$1.56 per share for the year. Other banks were mixed in early trade. DBS Group traded at S$57.72, while OCBC Bank was at S$21.51. title: Stock Today: Sunway Construction Gains 2.7% Amid Record FY25 Results
body: Shares of Sunway Construction Group Bhd rose in afternoon trade, supported by strong full-year earnings and continued bullish analyst sentiment. As at 3.15 pm, Sunway Construction climbed 17 sen or 2.69% to RM6.48, with 49.47 million shares traded. The counter opened at RM6.36, hit an intraday high of RM6.57 and a low of RM6.36, compared with its last adjusted closing price of RM6.31. There were 181 lots on the buy side at RM6.48 against 2,737 lots on the sell side at RM6.49. The share price movement follows the group’s record-breaking FY2025 performance, with revenue surpassing RM5 billion for the first time to reach RM5.3 billion. Profit before tax surged 93% to RM525.5 million, while profit after tax jumped 94% to RM361.8 million, driven mainly by accelerated progress in advanced technology facilities (ATF)-related and data centre (DC) projects. For the fourth quarter ended 31 December 2025, revenue stood at RM1.0 billion, while profit before tax rose 47% to RM162.6 million. Profit margins expanded significantly, with PBT margin doubling to 16.0%. The construction segment posted quarterly revenue of RM940.8 million, with PBT rising 45% to RM155.3 million despite a lower topline, supported by improved cost discipline and margin expansion. The precast segment recorded a 62% increase in revenue to RM75.3 million, with PBT more than doubling to RM7.3 million. The group declared a fourth interim dividend of nine sen per share, bringing total FY25 dividends to a record 50.5 sen per share. Analysts have maintained strong buy recommendations on the stock. RHB Investment Bank raised its target price to RM7.96, implying a 26% upside, while MBSB Investment Bank set a RM7.18 target and Hong Leong Investment Bank maintained a RM7.00 target price. RHB noted that FY25 core net profit surged 148% year-on-year to RM425.6 million, exceeding expectations, supported by faster-than-anticipated progress on DC projects, which now account for 41% of the group’s RM5.7 billion order book. The group is also seen as well-positioned for further growth, with a tender book of RM17.5 billion and net cash of RM1.7 billion, providing visibility for future earnings. title: Stock Today: PetChem Slides Over 6% As Earnings Woes Weigh
body: Shares of Petronas Chemicals Group Bhd (PetChem) fell sharply in afternoon trade, declining 20 sen or 6.08% to RM3.09 as at 2.24 pm, with 120.8 million shares changing hands. The stock opened at RM3.27, touched an intraday high of RM3.27 and slipped to a low of RM3.07, reflecting renewed selling pressure. The decline comes amid continued cautious sentiment following weaker financial performance and a negative outlook from analysts. Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB) has maintained a SELL call on the counter, with a revised target price of RM2.04, implying further downside from current levels. The research house projects a total return of negative 34.8%, citing prolonged weakness in the olefins and derivatives segment as well as challenging sector conditions. PetChem reported a FY25 core net loss of RM534 million, reversing from a core net profit of RM1,175 million in FY24, missing both HLIB’s and consensus expectations. Fourth-quarter core losses narrowed to RM237 million, although revenue slipped 3% quarter-on-quarter to RM6,600 million. Plant utilisation fell to 88% in FY25 from 91% previously, affected by utilities disruptions, feedstock constraints and higher maintenance activities. HLIB expects the olefins and derivatives segment to remain subdued in FY26, forecasting a core net loss of RM327.5 million, while FY27 core profit projections have been cut sharply. The group declared a second interim dividend of 4 sen, bringing total FY25 dividends to 7 sen, lower than 13 sen in FY24. Ongoing supply-demand imbalances, volatile commodity prices and soft downstream demand continue to cloud the earnings recovery outlook, keeping investor sentiment fragile. Investors are also closely monitoring the Middle East, with the US and Iran preparing to resume nuclear talks. Trump pushed back on reports suggesting Pentagon concerns over a potential prolonged military campaign, while emphasising that his preferred outcome remains a deal. In early trade as of 7.40 am Singapore time, gold rose 0.2% to US$5,238.65 an ounce. Other precious metals advanced, with silver up 0.3% to US$88.49, platinum rising 0.6%, and palladium up 0.5%. title: Bonia Should Recover In 2H After Dismal Start
body: CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) has maintained a HOLD rating on Bonia Corp Bhd with a lower target price of RM0.86, down from RM0.87, following a subdued first half of FY26. The research house noted that Bonia’s core net profit (CNP) of RM5.8 million for 1HFY26 fell 32.4% year-on-year, coming in at only 30% of CIMB’s forecast and 33% of Bloomberg consensus estimates, due to weaker-than-expected revenue and elevated operating costs. Bonia’s 2QFY26 CNP rebounded strongly to RM5.8 million from a low base of RM29,000 in 1QFY26, driven by festive season sales and improved operating leverage. Revenue for 1HFY26 rose 3.8% year-on-year to RM195.4 million, supported by a 4.9% increase in Malaysian sales from aggressive promotions. This was partially offset by softer performance in Singapore, down 4.4% year-on-year and Indonesia, down 47.1%, reflecting subdued economic conditions and foreign exchange headwinds. Margins were under pressure, with 1HFY26 EBITDA margin contracting 2.0 percentage points to 18.4% due to the service tax on lease rentals effective July 2025, higher marketing and promotional expenses and rising operating costs, including utilities and staff expenses. Coupled with a higher effective tax rate of 40.6%, this led to the sharp decline in CNP. Bonia declared a 2 sen dividend for 2QFY26, bringing total 1HFY26 dividends to 2 sen, in line with expectations. Looking ahead, CIMB Securities expects a stronger half-on-half performance in 2HFY26, supported by Hari Raya festive spending, higher footfall from the Visit Malaysia 2026 campaign and more targeted digital marketing. Elevated costs are expected to be partially mitigated by ongoing efficiency initiatives and optimised marketing allocation. Following revisions to earnings forecasts for FY26–28, the target price reflects a P/BV of 0.4x, with Bonia’s dividend yield of 4.5–5.2%, net cash position of RM19.5 million and a deep discount to net tangible assets providing a buffer against downside risk. As of 11.55 am, Bonia’s stock price is up by 0.56% to RM0.90. title: Wall Street Futures Retreat As Policy Uncertainty Mounts, Dollar Slids
body: Wall Street futures and the dollar slid in Asian trade on Monday as renewed confusion over US tariffs unsettled investors and revived the “sell America” trade. Reuters reported that markets are heading into a pivotal week, with chip heavyweight Nvidia due to release earnings. The latest volatility follows a ruling by the US Supreme Court striking down President Donald Trump’s emergency tariffs. In response, the President announced a new 10% levy on imports from the rest of the world, before quickly raising it to 15%. The abrupt shift appeared to catch even some officials off guard. Investors are awaiting clarity on when the tariffs would take effect, which goods might be exempt and whether the 15% rate would apply to all countries. Rodrigo Catril, senior FX strategist at NAB, said the tariff backdrop had become even more uncertain, warning the US risked falling into a cycle of announcing tariffs, seeing them overturned and then reintroducing new measures. Markets across Asia were mixed. Japan’s Nikkei 225 was closed for a public holiday, although futures edged lower. South Korea’s KOSPI rose 1.2%, extending a rally that has already taken it to record highs, while Taiwan’s TAIEX also reached a fresh peak. In Europe, futures on the EURO STOXX 50 and DAX fell 0.5%, with FTSE 100 futures slightly lower. In the US, the main indices finished last week higher, but futures turned cautious ahead of Nvidia’s results. The company, which accounts for nearly 8% of the S&P 500, is expected to report a sharp rise in earnings. Options markets are pricing in a move of at least 6% in either direction, meaning the results could influence not only technology stocks but the wider AI sector. The bond market has also been affected by the tariff developments. Investors are assessing the risk that around $170bn in revenue may need to be repaid, potentially widening the US fiscal deficit to about 6.6% of GDP. At the same time, mixed economic data — weaker growth alongside firmer core inflation — have complicated the outlook for interest rates. Expectations of a June rate cut by the Federal Reserve have slipped back to just over 50%. The dollar, which had been steady last week, weakened against the yen and the Swiss franc, while the euro strengthened. Bitcoin also fell sharply. In the commodity side of things, gold rose as investors sought safer assets. Oil prices eased ahead of US-Iran talks in Geneva on Thursday. Brent crude and US crude both gave up some of last week’s gains as traders weighed diplomatic efforts against the ongoing risk of military action if no agreement is reached. RHB Research said Aumas Resources is poised to extend its upward movement after staging a bullish breakout. The stock printed a bullish candlestick on Friday and closed above the RM0.60 resistance level, signalling that positive momentum is in play. The research house expects the counter to potentially climb towards RM0.65, followed by RM0.70. However, it cautioned that a fall below the RM0.55 support level would negate the bullish setup and could trigger a correction phase. Meanwhile, RHB Research noted that Eversendai may continue its bullish trajectory after breaking above key resistance. The counter has remained above its 21-day simple moving average line, indicating a short-term uptrend, and closed above the RM0.53 resistance level. Following the breakout, the stock could advance towards the next resistance at RM0.56 and subsequently RM0.58, the research house said. A decline below the RM0.51 support level would invalidate the bullish view and signal a potential resumption of correction. RHB Research’s technical outlook suggests near-term trading opportunities for both counters, supported by strengthening price momentum and breakout patterns. title: HSIF Rebounds After 388-Point Slide, Bulls Defend 26,400 Level
body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has maintained its positive trading bias on Hang Seng Index Futures (HSIF), advising traders to hold on to long positions despite a sharp pullback in the latest session. The HSIF fell 388 points last Friday to close at 26,412 points, after opening at 26,740 points and hitting an intraday high of 26,888 points before sliding to a low of 26,347 points. The contract formed a long bearish candlestick during the day session. However, it rebounded 443 points in the evening session to last trade at 26,855 points. RHB Research noted that the Relative Strength Index is hovering around the 50% level, indicating that bullish momentum remains intact. The index may rebound from the immediate support at 26,400 points and attempt to climb above the 20-day simple moving average line. A bullish crossover above this short-term average would likely lift market sentiment and pave the way for a move towards the 27,500-point level. The research house said it would maintain its positive stance as long as the HSIF holds above the 26,400-point support, despite the ongoing retracement. Traders are advised to retain long positions initiated at 21,416 points on April 14, 2025, with a stop-loss set at 26,400 points. Immediate resistance is seen at 27,500 points, followed by 28,600 points, while the next support level stands at 25,500 points. title: Gold Rises As Trump Tariff Defeat Throws Trade Deals Into Doubt
body: Gold rose as uncertainty over what would happen to trade deals negotiated with the US, after the Supreme Court restrained President Donald Trump’s tariff powers, unsettled markets. Bullion climbed as much as 1.3% to above US$5,170 an ounce. Trump said Saturday he would impose a global tariff of 15% to preserve protective trade measures after the Supreme Court ruled against his use of emergency powers to set reciprocal duties. A weakening of the dollar following the decision is making the metal cheaper for many buyers. The court ruling has cast doubt over deals the US has negotiated with major trading partners. The European Parliament’s trade chief said he’ll propose delaying ratification of an agreement with Washington until there’s more clarity. Indian officials will postpone a trip to the US, while a member of Japan’s ruling party called the situation “a real mess.” The uncertainty is giving more impetus to gold’s recovery from a sudden rout at the turn of the month. The precious metal has rallied for the last three weeks as many of the long-term factors — including heightened geopolitical tensions and investor wariness of sovereign bonds and currencies – that have supported it have remained intact. Gold rose 0.7% to US$5,144.72 an ounce as of 8.25 am in Singapore. The Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index dropped 0.2% after declining 0.2% on Friday. Silver climbed 2.2% to US$86.47. Platinum and palladium also advanced. Bloomberg Related Bullion climbed as much as 1.3% to above US$5,170 an ounce. title: Bursa Malaysia Opens Higher, Tracking Wall Street Gains
body: Bursa Malaysia opened higher on Monday, taking its cue from Wall Street’s firmer close last week amid the latest developments surrounding United States tariffs. title: Bursa Malaysia Edges Higher Midday On US Tariff Reversal
body: Bursa Malaysia inched higher on early session as investors reacted to the US Supreme Court’s decision to revoke an emergency tariff increase. This comes after a volatile end to last week, when global markets reacted to the US Supreme Court’s ruling on Friday to revoke the emergency tariff increase. The decision eased immediate concerns over escalating trade tensions and provided a measure of relief to equity markets across the region. The benchmark FBM KLCI (FBMKLCI) climbed 5.03 points, or 0.29%, to 1,757.86 by 12:30 PM, while the broader FBM Bursa Malaysia All-Share Index advanced 41.14 points to 12,887.92. Trading volume for the half-day session reached 1.45 billion shares, with a transaction value of RM1.17 billion. Heavyweight counters leading the gains included Sime Darby (SIME) and Nestlé (NESTLE), providing support to the overall market. By midday, 515 stocks had risen, 421 declined and 521 remained unchanged, while 1,323 stocks were not traded. The ringgit was steady at 3.8915 against the US dollar. Other indices also recorded modest gains, with the FBM70 up 0.47% to 17,829.54, the F4GBM adding 0.34% to 1,039.03, the FBMEMAS rising 0.36% to 12,893.54 and the FBMSHA increasing 0.32% to 12,408.18. Top trading activity came from VS with 346 million shares changing hands at RM0.395, followed by Astro, Tanco, Zetrix and Velesto. Among the biggest gainers, Nestlé led with a RM2.50 increase to RM112.20, while UTDPLT, PPB, MPI and Chin Teck Technology also advanced. HLFG, Malayan Cement, Biport, Press Metal and Allianz were among the midday decliners. Asian markets broadly rose for half a day, although trading in China and Japan was closed for the Spring Festival and the Emperor’s birthday, respectively. title: Asia Shares Hesitant, Dollar Slips Amid Tariff Confusion
body: Share markets were hesitant, and the dollar slid in Asia on Monday as investors waited for some much-needed clarity on US tariffs, while confidence in the entire AI trade was set to be tested by results from tech-diva Nvidia this week. Oil prices eased ahead of another round of talks between the United States and Iran due in Geneva on Thursday, with the risk of US military strikes lingering if a deal is not done. Confusion loomed large after the US Supreme Court struck down President Donald Trump’s emergency tariffs, leading him to announce a new 10 per cent rate on the rest of the world, only to then lift it to 15 per cent in a move that seemed to surprise some of his own officials. “The tariff landscape is now more uncertain than before; uncertainty is not good news for any economy or market,” said Rodrigo Catril, a senior FX strategist at NAB. “Unless common sense prevails, we could be entering a circular process where new tariffs are announced, then potentially overturned, only for new tariffs to be announced, and we do the dance again.” It was not yet clear when these tariffs would be imposed, what might be excluded and whether every country would be slapped with 15 per cent. Some, including the UK and Australia, had 10 per cent tariff rates under the former rules, while many countries in Asia had higher rates. With so much up in the air, MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan edged up 0.5 per cent in light trade. Japan’s Nikkei was shut for a holiday but futures traded at 56,970 against a cash close of 56,825. South Korea extended its bull run with another 2.0 per cent rise, having already jumped 5.5 per cent last week to all-time highs. NVIDIA To Test AI Mood S&P 500 futures fell 0.3 per cent and Nasdaq futures 0.4 per cent ahead of earnings from Nvidia, which is sure to cause waves given the tech behemoth makes up almost 8 per cent of the S&P 500 index. The world’s most valuable company is expected to post a 71 per cent rise in earnings per share to US$7.76, though estimates range from as low as US$6.28 to as high as US$9.68. Options imply its shares could shift by at least 6 per cent in either direction on the announcement. The Treasury market had been sideswiped by the tariff news as it raised the risk the US government would have to repay around US$170 billion in revenue. Such an outcome would, on paper, widen the fiscal deficit by half a percentage point to around 6.6 per cent of GDP. The holiday in Japan meant cash Treasuries were not trading, but 10-year note futures were down 2 ticks. The market had also been tugged two ways by mixed data with economic growth badly missing forecasts in the December quarter, but core inflation surprising on the high side. That saw the probability of a June rate cut from the Federal Reserve come in to around 52 per cent, from over 60 per cent a week ago, and left the dollar firmer on the week. Early Monday, the dollar was under pressure amid speculation the chaos over US trade policy could reinforce the “sell America” theme evident in markets in recent months. The dollar eased 0.4 per cent on the Japanese yen to 154.36, while the euro added 0.4 per cent to US$1.1826. The dollar also dipped 0.5 per cent on the Swiss franc to 0.7718. In commodity markets, gold gained a safe-haven bid and firmed 0.8 per cent to US$5,143 an ounce. Silver gained 2 per cent to US$86.24 per ounce, after climbing almost 8 per cent on Friday. Oil prices were choppy, having gained last week as Trump said the US military could strike specific targets in Iran if a nuclear deal was not agreed on. Brent edged down 0.6 per cent to US$71.29 a barrel, while US crude lost 0.8 per cent to US$65.95 per barrel. title: Bitcoin, Ethereum Hold Steady As Trump Announces Global Tariff
body: The price of Bitcoin and Ethereum held steady on Saturday after US President Donald Trump said he would raise temporary tariffs on almost all imports from 10% to 15%. Bitcoin was up nearly 2% over a 24-hour period, trading at $68,273, at midday in New York, according to CoinGecko. Ethereum rose by 2% over the same time and was trading hands for close to $1,987.Trump wrote on his social media platform, Truth Social, that the move would be “effective immediately” on the “countries, many of which have been ‘ripping’ the US off for decades, without retribution (until I came along!).” The announcement came after the Supreme Court struck down his previous tariff program as invalid on Friday. Trump had hours after the court’s ruling imposed a 10% global tariff on foreign goods. T ariff shock no more? Crypto markets have previously reacted negatively to Trump’s trade announcements. In April, Trump’s Liberation Day speech shed billions of dollars off Bitcoin, Ethereum, and XRP. Markets then rebounded but were shocked again in May following further threats on the European Union. Though markets are less volatile now with Bitcoin and Ethereum well below the records they set in 2025 following two brutal selloffs. Crypto prices have struggled to recover following the biggest liquidation event in the history of the industry back in October. Bitcoin rose only slightly after the Supreme Court struck down Trump’s signature tariff policy on Friday, ruling that the president had acted unlawfully in applying the reciprocal tariffs. ETF flows Price action from Bitcoin and Ethereum comes after a week of more redemptions from top US exchange-traded funds. US investors cashed out nearly $316 million from the Bitcoin funds this week, with Friday the only day with positive flows. Their Ethereum counterparts, meanwhile, lost over $123 million. Heavy redemptions from the products — managed by the likes of BlackRock, Fidelity, and Grayscale — usually come as prices take a hit, and Bitcoin and Ethereum over the past seven days are down 2% and 5%, respectively. title: Wall Street Closes Up As Tariff Relief Offsets Weak Q4 GDP
body: US stocks advanced on Feb 20 after the Supreme Court struck down President Donald Trump’s sweeping tariffs under the 1977 International Emergency Economic Powers Act, easing trade uncertainty despite weak Q4 GDP data showing 1.4% growth. Reuters reported that the S&P 500 rose 0.7% after a choppy session, recovering from early losses triggered by disappointing fourth-quarter growth figures. Wall Street had opened lower but pushed into positive territory as investors digested the court’s 6-3 ruling that a 1977 emergency powers law does not authorise the president to impose tariffs. The Dow Jones Industrial Average and Nasdaq Composite also ended higher, reflecting cautious optimism that the removal of tariffs could ease price pressures and strengthen expectations for Federal Reserve rate cuts later this year. Many analysts stated markets had largely anticipated the ruling by the US Supreme Court, resulting in a relatively muted reaction. However, uncertainty remains elevated after the administration of Donald Trump signalled it could pursue alternative legal avenues to reinstate trade levies, keeping investors cautious about the longer-term policy outlook. That caution was reinforced by fresh economic data showing the US economy expanded at an annualised rate of 1.4% in the October-to-December quarter, falling short of the 2.5% pace forecast by analysts. Economists noted that a prolonged federal government shutdown during the period likely weighed on output, tempering concerns about underlying momentum but underscoring signs of cooling growth. Overseas, markets painted a mixed picture. In Asia, Hong Kong stocks declined as trading resumed after a three-day Lunar New Year break, while Tokyo also closed lower. In contrast, South Korea’s Kospi surged 2.3% to a record high, buoyed by gains in defence contractors including Hanwha Aerospace. European equities were firmer, supported by data showing eurozone business activity accelerated in February, signalling improving economic stability. London’s FTSE 100 and Paris’s CAC 40 both notched fresh record highs. In commodities, oil prices moved sideways after rallying earlier in the week on US suggestions of potential military action against Iran. President Trump said he was considering options after warning Tehran of consequences if a nuclear deal was not reached within an extended deadline. Against this backdrop of shifting trade policy, moderating growth and geopolitical tensions, market participants expect volatility to persist as investors reassess inflation trends and the prospects for monetary easing later this year. title: Gold Tops US$5,000 After Supreme Court Decision On US Tariffs
body: Gold topped $5,000 on Friday after the Supreme Court struck down President Trump’s most sweeping tariffs and Wall Street highlighted its bullish call on the precious metal. Gold rose nearly 2%, on pace for a weekly gain, even as President Trump announced a 10% global tariff following the high court’s ruling Geopolitical hedging, concerns about currency debasement, and expectations of Fed policy easing have all contributed to the steady demand for bullion. Even with a significant drawdown at the end of last month, gold is up 16% since the start of January, following a historic gain last year. Goldman Sachs analysts maintain that while structural purchases from central banks have slowed recently, they expect them to reaccelerate, with demand also stemming from the private sector if the Federal Reserve cuts rates this year. “Taken together, these two factors drive gold to slowly grind higher to $5,400/toz by end-2026,” they said. Additional private-sector diversification over perceived fiscal risks in Western countries could send prices even higher, the analysts said. title: Wall Street Ends Lower Amid Private Equity Slump And Tech Weakness
body: Wall Street closed lower on Thursday as losses in private equity firms and dips in major tech and retail stocks outweighed earnings-driven gains in industrials. The S&P 500 fell 0.28% to 6,861.89 points, the Nasdaq declined 0.31% to 22,682.73, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 0.54% to 49,395.16. Private equity stocks were hit after Blue Owl Capital announced it would sell US$1.4 billion in assets and freeze redemptions at one of its funds to manage debt and return capital. Shares of Blue Owl tumbled 6%, while peers including Apollo Global Management, Ares, KKR & Co and Carlyle Group fell between 1.9% and 5.2%, reflecting concerns over credit quality and lenders’ exposure to software stocks. Tech and retail stocks also weighed on sentiment. Apple dipped 1.4%, the largest drag on the S&P 500, while Walmart dropped 1.4% after new CEO John Furner unveiled a conservative fiscal 2027 forecast and a US$30 billion share buyback plan. AI-related technology stocks have faced pressure amid doubts that heavy investments are translating into meaningful revenue or profit growth. Industrial stocks were a bright spot. Deere & Co surged 11.6% after raising its annual profit forecast and beating first-quarter estimates. Omnicom jumped 15% following stronger-than-expected fourth-quarter revenue, while Carvana fell almost 8% after missing profit expectations. Software provider EPAM Systems plunged 17% after issuing a cautious first-quarter outlook. The S&P 500 energy index gained 0.6% on rising crude oil prices amid heightened US-Iran tensions, while the financial index slipped 0.9%. Declining stocks outnumbered advancing ones on the S&P 500 by a 1.5-to-one ratio, with 27 new highs and six new lows. Nasdaq recorded 62 new highs and 146 new lows. Trading volume was lighter than usual, with 16.4 billion shares changing hands versus the 20-session average of 20.5 billion. Investors also digested the Fed’s latest policy minutes, showing a split among policymakers on the future path of rates. Attention now turns to Friday’s Personal Consumption Expenditures report for clues on inflation and the central bank’s next moves, with interest-rate markets currently pricing a 50% chance of a rate cut by June. title: Stock Today: Nestlé Malaysia Edges Higher Amid Ice Cream Divestment Plans
body: Nestlé (Malaysia) Bhd shares edged up 0.46% to RM110.00 as of 12.02 pm, gaining RM0.50 from the previous close, on a traded volume of 19,800 shares. The stock opened at RM110.00, hit an intraday high of RM110.10 and a low of RM109.30, with the last average closing price at RM109.50. The modest uptick comes amid announcements that Nestlé Malaysia is exploring a potential sale of its local ice cream business to Froneri, the global joint venture with PAI Partners. Analysts at MBSB Investment Bank Bhd have maintained a SELL rating on the stock, with an unchanged target price of RM94.50, noting that the divestment aligns with the parent company’s strategy under CEO Philipp Navratil to focus on four high-growth pillars: Coffee, Petcare, Nutrition and Food & Snacking. The Malaysian operations include brands such as La Cremeria, Musang King sticks and Mat Kool, which were previously outside the scope of Froneri’s joint venture. The Board emphasised that the process remains at an early stage, involving due diligence, stakeholder engagement and regulatory compliance. MBSB Research highlighted that a successful divestment could allow Nestlé Malaysia to concentrate on higher-margin core categories, potentially improving operational focus and medium-term earnings quality. While financial details have not been disclosed, the company benefits from strong domestic brand equity, entrenched distribution networks and steady demand. title: Ringgit Opens Higher Against US Dollar Amid Geopolitical Tensions
body: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar on Friday as traders turned cautious amid escalating geopolitical tensions, an analyst said. At 8 am, the local currency rose to 3.8965/9160 against the greenback from 3.9045/9125 at Thursday’s close. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd Chief Economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said risk-off sentiment had become evident in global financial markets as traders focused on developments surrounding the US-Iran nuclear deal. “US President Donald Trump has set a 10-day deadline to conclude negotiations. At the same time, there are reports of US military forces building up in the Middle East,” he said to Bernama . He added that the US dollar-ringgit pair was expected to trade between RM3.91 and RM3.93 as markets remained wary of further escalation. Meanwhile, Mohd Afzanizam said recent US data showed imports had declined for five consecutive months, falling 2.6 per cent year-on-year in December 2025, while the trade deficit narrowed to US$70.3 billion from US$96.9 billion in December 2024. He said the data suggested softer domestic demand had dampened import growth in the US economy. “On the other hand, initial jobless claims fell slightly to 219,000 last week from 220,000 previously. “However, claims have been trending higher since early January, indicating the labour market may be softening, with continuing claims remaining at an elevated level,” he said. At the opening, the ringgit traded higher against a basket of major and ASEAN currencies. It strengthened against the Japanese yen to 2.5126/5250 from 2.5221/5275 at Thursday’s close, rose versus the euro to 4.5880/6103 from 4.6073/6168, and appreciated against the British pound to 5.2469/2725 from 5.2730/2838. Against its ASEAN peers, the ringgit advanced versus the Singapore dollar to 3.0732/0887 from 3.0817/0882, gained against the Thai baht to 12.4944/5657 from 12.5196/5521, edged up against the Indonesian rupiah to 230.8/232.0 from 231.1/231.6, and rose versus the Philippine peso to 6.72/6.76 from 6.73/6.75 previously. title: Late Bargain Hunting Lifts Bursa
body: Late bargain hunting in selected heavyweights, mainly financial counters, has lifted Bursa Malaysia to end marginally higher on Friday. At 5 pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) inched up 0.72 of a point, or 0.04 per cent, to 1,752.83 from Thursday’s close of 1,752.11. The benchmark had opened 0.68 of-a-point higher at 1,752.79, and moved between 1,746.08 and 1,754.20 throughout the trading session. However, the broader market was negative with losers thumping gainers 702 to 380, while 519 counters were unchanged, 1,157 counters untraded and 24 suspended. Turnover was slightly lower at 2.03 billion units worth RM2.20 billion compared to 2.04 billion units worth RM2.52 billion on Thursday. title: HSIF Rebound Signals Strong Base, RHB Keeps Long Call
body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) is maintaining its long position call on the Hang Seng Index Futures (HSIF) after the contract staged a firm rebound last Monday. However, a break below 26,400 points would invalidate the positive setup and open the door to further downside movement. For now, the research house is keeping a positive trading bias. title: Wall Street Gains As Oil Surges And Europe Hits Record High
body: US stocks finished higher on Wednesday, while European shares closed at a record high, as investors weighed Federal Reserve meeting minutes alongside fresh geopolitical tensions that pushed oil and gold prices sharply upward. The pan-European STOXX Europe 600 rose 1.19% to a record close, with defence and banking stocks leading gains. The broader FTSEurofirst 300 added 1.22%. Globally, MSCI’s world equity gauge climbed 0.60%. On Wall Street, the three major indices ended in positive territory despite trimming earlier gains. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.26% to 49,662.66, the S&P 500 gained 0.56% to 6,881.32, and the Nasdaq Composite advanced 0.78% to 22,753.64. Investor sentiment was shaped by minutes from the Federal Reserve’s latest policy meeting, which showed officials were broadly aligned in keeping interest rates unchanged, though divided over the timing of future adjustments. Strong US durable goods and housing data reinforced expectations that rates would remain on hold, pushing Treasury yields higher. The benchmark 10-year yield rose to 4.087%, while the 30-year yield climbed to 4.7108%. The dollar strengthened in response to the solid economic data and reports that European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde may leave her role earlier than expected. The dollar index rose 0.61% to 97.73, as the euro slipped 0.58% to $1.1784. “(Lagarde) has been a calming voice, and it’s been nice to have solid leadership in place,” said Ryan Detrick, chief market strategist at Carson Group in Omaha. He added, “Potential rumours that she might be leaving a tad earlier, it’s shaken up currency markets a little bit.” Geopolitical developments also fuelled market moves. Ukraine peace talks ended without a clear resolution, with President Volodymyr Zelenskiy accusing Russia of delaying progress. Meanwhile, Iran’s temporary closure of parts of the Strait of Hormuz heightened concerns over global oil supplies. This “double-whammy of continued geopolitical uncertainty … has led to higher oil and higher gold prices,” Detrick said. Crude prices surged on supply disruption fears. US crude settled up 4.59% at US$65.19 per barrel, while Brent climbed 4.35% to US$70.35. Spot gold rose 2.22% to US$4,985.46 an ounce, with US gold futures up 2.03%. In Asia, Japan’s Nikkei 225 rose 1.02%, while MSCI’s Asia-Pacific ex-Japan index edged up 0.09%. Emerging market equities gained 0.23%. Cryptocurrencies retreated, with bitcoin falling 2.15% to US$66,196.23 and ethereum down 3.08% to US$1,938.20.
