title: Stock Today: Press Metal Inches Higher As FY25 Core Profit Breakthrough Looms
body: Press Metal Aluminium Holdings Bhd (PMETAL) rose slightly to RM7.69, up 0.13% or RM0.01, on Thursday with a traded volume of 2.4 million shares, reflecting cautious optimism ahead of the group’s 4Q25 results. The stock opened at RM7.67, touched an intraday high of RM7.74 and a low of RM7.60, while the last done price aligned with the lower end of the buy-sell spread at RM7.69. RHB Research maintains its BUY call on Press Metal with a target price of RM8.50, highlighting strong fundamentals underpinned by elevated global aluminium prices and favourable input costs. Analysts project FY25 core profit after tax and minority interests to surpass RM2 billion for the first time, driven by a fourth-quarter PATAMI expected between RM650 million and RM730 million. The rally is underpinned by an 8% quarter-on-quarter rise in LME aluminium prices to an average of US$2,830 per tonne and a 10% drop in alumina costs to US$319 per tonne, improving the “alumina-to-aluminium” cost ratio to roughly 10%, well below the three-year average of 17%. Despite recent volatility triggered by U.S. Federal Reserve chair speculation, RHB analysts describe the group’s underlying fundamentals as “rock solid,” further supported by the scheduled wind-down of the 560,000-tonne Mozal plant in Mozambique. While a strengthening Ringgit poses a minor headwind for Press Metal’s US$-denominated exports, the company’s low-cost hydropower-powered smelting and its role as a proxy for global green metal supply-demand dynamics continue to underpin investor confidence. With a three-year CAGR of 27%, Press Metal remains a preferred pick for exposure to the global energy transition. title: Stock Today: CIMB Inches Up Amid Indonesia Stake Talks
body: Shares of CIMB Group Holdings Bhd were trading higher on Thursday afternoon, gaining 0.84% as investors considered the potential divestment of its Indonesian unit. As of 3.59 pm, the counter was last done at RM8.45, up seven sen from the previous close of RM8.38. The stock had touched a session high of RM8.48 and a low of RM8.41, with total traded volume at 130.48 million shares (’00 basis). The market’s focus remains on CIMB’s 92.4% holding in PT Bank CIMB Niaga TBK, as Indonesian regulators plan to raise the minimum free float requirement on the Indonesia Stock Exchange from 7.5% to 15%, ahead of an MSCI reassessment in May. Analysts suggest CIMB may reduce its stake by at least 7.4%, potentially generating one-off proceeds of around RM810 million based on Niaga’s current market capitalisation of approximately RM10.9 billion. Despite Niaga historically contributing about 25% to CIMB’s profit before tax, the impact of a potential stake reduction is expected to be minimal, with projected declines of 1.2% and 2.0% for FY26 and FY27 respectively. Analysts note that any divestment proceeds could be used to expand the loan book or enhance shareholder returns, complementing the bank’s RM2 billion capital return plan through 2027. Currency risk remains a factor, with every 1% depreciation of the Indonesian rupiah against its year-to-date average estimated to reduce CIMB’s profit before tax by about 0.3%. The assets comprise Segari Energy Ventures Sdn Bhd in Perak with a capacity of 1,303 megawatts, GB3 Sdn Bhd in Perak with 429 megawatts, and Prai Power Sdn Bhd in Penang with 350 megawatts. title: Ringgit Opens Lower Against US Dollar Following FOMC Minutes
body: The ringgit eased against the US dollar at the opening on Thursday, as the greenback strengthened amid Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) minutes which signalled a potential interest rate hike, an analyst said. At 8 am, the ringgit inched down to 3.8965/9160 versus the greenback compared to 3.8945/9055 at Monday’s close. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US Dollar Index (DXY) rose 0.57 per cent to 97.712 points as the latest FOMC minutes showed that several participants in the meeting would prefer a two-sided description of the committee’s decision. “This situation suggested that raising the interest rate could be a possible outcome should the inflation remain above target level,” he told Bernama today. However, Mohd Afzanizam said the ringgit is expected to linger around RM3.89 to RM3.91 today given the strong data points for the Malaysian economy. At the opening, the ringgit however traded higher against a basket of major currencies. It appreciated versus the Japanese yen to 2.5191/5318 from 2.5356/5430 at Monday’s close, strengthened against the euro to 4.5936/6166 from 4.6204/6335 previously, and rose vis-à-vis the British pound to 5.2583/2846 from 5.3137/3287. The local note traded mostly higher against its ASEAN peers. The ringgit improved versus the Singapore dollar to 3.0746/0905 from 3.0860/0949 last Monday, was higher vis-a-vis the Thai baht at 12.4640/5364 compared to 12.5205/5619 previously, and edged up against the Indonesian rupiah to 230.7/232.0 from 231.4/232.2. title: Gold Pauses After Rally Amid Strong Dollar And Lunar New Year Lull
body: Gold prices slipped on Thursday in a thinly traded market following a more than 2% gain in the previous session, pressured by a firm US dollar ahead of key inflation data that could influence the Federal Reserve’s interest rate decisions. Spot gold fell 0.2% to US$4,968.10 per ounce, while U.S. April gold futures declined 0.4% to US$4,987.60. “Gold is in a consolidation mood, reflective of thin liquidity conditions during the Asia holiday period rather than a shift in fundamentals,” said Christopher Wong, strategist at OCBC. Markets across Mainland China, Hong Kong, Singapore, Taiwan and South Korea remained closed for Lunar New Year holidays, contributing to the subdued trading. The dollar stayed near a one-week high, making bullion priced in greenbacks more expensive for holders of other currencies. January Federal Reserve minutes indicated near-unanimous agreement to hold interest rates steady, though policymakers remain divided on future moves, with some open to hikes if inflation persists and others leaning towards cuts should inflation ease. Market participants currently anticipate the first rate reduction this year in June, according to CME’s FedWatch Tool. Investors now await weekly US jobless claims and Friday’s Personal Consumption Expenditures report, the Fed’s preferred inflation gauge. Wong added that near-term consolidation is expected before gold and silver trend higher, with gold likely trading between US$4,800 and US$5,100 per ounce and silver in the US$70 to US$90 range. Spot silver held at US$77.18 per ounce after a more than 5% rise on Wednesday, while platinum eased 0.1% to US$2,069.58 and palladium remained steady at US$1,715.93. title: Dollar Firms As Fed Minutes Signal No Rush To Cut Rates
body: The US dollar held on to overnight gains in Asian trading on Thursday after minutes from the Federal Reserve’s latest meeting indicated policymakers were in no hurry to cut interest rates, with several even open to further hikes if inflation remains persistent. The euro remained below US$1.18 at US$1.1788, weighed down both by the stronger dollar and a report that European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde plans to step down before her term ends next October. Sterling traded at US$1.3497. US Treasury yields rose following the release of the minutes, which showed officials divided over the future path of rates. While some policymakers expect productivity gains to help ease inflationary pressures, “most participants” cautioned that progress may be slow and uneven, with several signalling that rate increases remain possible if inflation stays above target. “This suggests there isn’t a great deal of urgency to cut rates again, at least not until after current chair (Jerome) Powell’s term ends in May,” said Peter Dragicevich, Asia-Pacific currency strategist at Corpay. The Japanese yen weakened around 1% overnight and was steady at 154.78 per dollar, retreating from last week’s 152 level following Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s electoral victory. The currency also came under pressure after the Trump administration announced US$36 billion worth of projects as part of Japan’s pledged US$550 billion investment in the United States. “Direct Japanese investment into the U.S. will be a key watch factor this year, and one which adds to the very mixed picture on USD/JPY,” said Chris Turner, global head of research at ING. “The question for FX markets this year is whether this investment proves a supportive dollar flow or something like Japan’s FX reserves are used to guarantee new USD loans and avoid pressure on the yen. The latter seems to be the preferred outcome for Tokyo.” Elsewhere, the Australian dollar traded at US$0.7045 ahead of employment data that could shape expectations for further rate increases. The New Zealand dollar fell nearly 1.4% overnight — its steepest decline since April last year — after the central bank adopted a more cautious stance on future tightening, leaving the kiwi just below US$0.60. Trading volumes in Asia were lighter due to holidays in Hong Kong, mainland China and Taiwan. The offshore yuan held steady at 6.89 per dollar. Markets are now looking ahead to global purchasing managers’ index readings and US gross domestic product data due on Friday for further direction. title: Bursa Extends Upward Momentum
body: Bursa Malaysia continued its upward trend, closing higher on Thursday due to positive market sentiment driven by stronger-than-expected macroeconomic data. The bourse also benefitted from gains on Wall Street overnight and firmer regional markets. The market was closed on Feb 17 and Feb 18 for the Chinese New Year holidays. At 5 pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose by 10.85 points, or 0.62 per cent, to 1,752.11 compared with Monday’s close of 1,741.26. The benchmark index had opened 6.82 points higher at 1,748.08, and moved between 1,755.08 and 1,743.63 throughout the trading session. The broader market was also positive with gainers thumping losers 748 to 288, while 483 counters were unchanged, 1,218 counters untraded, and 11 suspended. Turnover was higher at 2.04 billion units, worth RM2.52 billion, compared to 1.81 billion units, worth RM1.81 billion, on Monday. IPPFA Sdn Bhd director of investment strategy and country economist Mohd Sedek Jantan said most regional equity markets closed higher, reinforcing the constructive risk tone that carried into the local benchmark index. “Major indices finished in positive territory, reflecting broad-based buying interest. Among benchmark constituents, banking stocks led the gainers on renewed risk appetite, while utilities counters lagged amid sector rotation. “On a sectoral basis, the energy index outperformed, advancing by more than two per cent, driven by a surge of over seven per cent in selected green energy stocks,” he told Bernama. title: Asian Stocks To Climb As Tech Lifts US Equities
body: Asian equities were set to open higher Thursday after a rebound in tech and robust economic data lifted US stocks. Higher Treasury yields supported the dollar, while oil jumped. Equity index futures for Japan and Australia rose, while markets in China remained closed for the Lunar New Year holiday. The S&P 500 gained 0.6% Wednesday and the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 advanced 0.8%. A gauge of chipmakers climbed 1% and an ETF tracking software firms jumped 1.3%. The action in New York trading offered a sign that concerns over the disruption of AI were easing, just as several stock pickers surveyed the wreckage for buying opportunities. The software stock selloff is likely “overdone” as that was a largely knee-jerk reaction, with investors trying to figure out the winners and losers from AI, according to Paul Stanley at Granite Bay Wealth Management. “While AI is very promising, investors should not assume that all companies will win on the AI front,” he said. Wednesday’s data showing the biggest increase in US industrial production in January sweetened the mood, while orders for business equipment rose in December by more than projected and housing starts hit a five-month high. Stock market bulls were even unfazed by minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee’s January meeting that revealed “several participants” said they would have preferred a post-meeting statement that raised the possibility of raising the federal funds rate “if inflation remains at above-target levels.” Fed funds futures pricing on Wednesday indicated traders slightly pared bets on rate cuts this year but still expect a further two 25 basis-point reductions in 2026. “From our perspective, the minutes support our view that rate cuts are off the table for the foreseeable future,” said Charlie Ripley at Allianz Investment Management. The US 10-year yield rose just over two basis points to around 4.08%, while the policy-sensitive two-year yield climbed three basis points to 3.46%. A $16 billion sale of 20-year bonds drew lackluster demand. The dollar gained 0.5% and gold advanced toward $5,000 an ounce. In Asia, data set for release Thursday includes core machine orders for Japan, labor market data for Australia and interest rate decisions in the Philippines and Indonesia. Markets in China, Hong Kong, Taiwan and Vietnam are closed. The yen had its worst day this month amid a broader selloff in major currencies as US economic data supported higher Treasury yields. Japan is set to sell 20-year bonds Thursday. Oil gained the most since October as traders weighed whether talks between the US and Iran will be enough to avert conflict, following a report that American military intervention could come sooner than expected. title: Late Tech Rally Pushes US Stocks To Modest Gains
body: US stocks finished slightly higher on Tuesday after a volatile session, with a late rebound in technology shares and strength in financial counters helping major indices recover from earlier losses. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 32.26 points, or 0.07%, to 49,533.19. The S&P 500 gained 7.05 points, or 0.10%, to 6,843.22, while the Nasdaq Composite added 31.71 points, or 0.14%, to 22,578.38. Technology shares staged a turnaround after earlier weakness, with gains in Nvidia and Apple offsetting declines in Microsoft and Oracle. The S&P 500 information technology sector, which had fallen as much as 1.5% during the session, ended 0.5% higher. Financial stocks also provided support, with banks including Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan Chase advancing and helping the Dow recover from an earlier decline of about 0.7%. Despite the rebound in some large-cap technology names, pressure persisted in parts of the software segment. The S&P 500 software index dropped 1.6%, with Intuit and Cadence Design Systems among the steepest decliners, each falling more than 5%. Consumer staples were the weakest sector overall, dragged lower by a 7% slide in General Mills after the company cut its annual core sales and profit forecasts. Market sentiment has been unsettled in recent weeks after worries that advances in artificial intelligence could disrupt business models across several industries. Concerns intensified after Alibaba Group unveiled its new AI model, Qwen 3.5, designed to independently carry out complex tasks. “There’s a lot of different trends going on in terms of where investors want to put money right now and you see that in this market where you just see spikes up and spikes down, on maybe not a daily basis, but on a regular basis,” said Tim Ghriskey, senior portfolio strategist at Ingalls & Snyder in New York. “The market is looking very short-term here and there will be a return to AI plays being very much in favor.” Investors are now turning their attention to upcoming economic data, particularly the personal consumption expenditure report, the Federal Reserve’s preferred inflation gauge. Cooler-than-expected consumer inflation figures released last week have already lifted expectations of interest-rate cuts later this year, with traders pricing in roughly a 63% chance of at least a 25-basis-point reduction by June. Several corporate developments also moved individual stocks. Shares of Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings surged 12.1% after activist investor Elliott disclosed a stake exceeding 10%. Fiserv jumped 6.9% following reports that Jana Partners had taken a position, while Masimo soared 34.2% after Danaher Corporation agreed to acquire the pulse-oximeter maker for US$9.9 billion including debt. Trading breadth was mixed. Advancers slightly outnumbered decliners on the New York Stock Exchange, while decliners held a narrow lead on the Nasdaq. title: Gold Holds Ground After Lunar New Year Lull
body: Gold steadied in early Asian trading after two sessions of losses, with activity subdued as several regional markets remained closed for the Lunar New Year holidays. Spot bullion was little changed at US$4,879.79 an ounce at 7:30 a.m. in Singapore, following a drop of more than 3% over the previous two sessions. The pullback came as the US dollar strengthened, with a key gauge of the currency rising as much as 0.4% on Tuesday before trimming gains. The Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index ended the prior session up 0.2% for the week. Trading conditions have been volatile since a sharp selloff in gold at the start of the month, leaving investors closely monitoring signals on US monetary policy for direction. Lower borrowing costs tend to support non-yielding assets such as bullion, and prices briefly rebounded last week after softer inflation data encouraged expectations of rate cuts. Comments from officials at the Federal Reserve remained in focus. Governor Michael Barr said on Tuesday that rates should remain steady “for some time,” until there is clearer evidence that inflation is moving toward the central bank’s 2% target. Meanwhile, Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said further rate cuts could be possible this year if inflation continues to ease toward that goal. Other precious metals were mixed. Silver was little changed at US$73.52 an ounce, while platinum rose 0.5% and palladium gained 0.4%, reflecting cautious positioning across the metals complex as investors weigh the outlook for US interest rates and the dollar. title: Veteran Analysts Warns Of Bitcoin Crash To Below US$10,000
body: Bitcoin the world’s first decentralised cryptocurrency, was launched in 2009 in the wake of the global financial crisis in 2008. The goal was to give financial autonomy to the people and liberate them from the clutches of Wall Street. But the way Bitcoin has increasingly become integrated into the mainstream financial system, macroeconomic forces now tend to affect King Crypto’s price trajectory.That is exactly what happened when U.S. President Donald Trump’s tariff threat against China led to a massive liquidation in the crypto market on Oct. 10 last year. Bitcoin had hit its all-time high (ATH) of $126,080 only a few days earlier on Oct. 6 and it is currently trading 45% lower.Earlier this month, Bitwise CIO Matt Hougan listed six major factors behind the crash in the crypto market. First, long-term crypto investors have been selling to front-run the four-year cycle. The general thesis is that crypto has historically followed four-year cycles, with down years being 2014, 2018, and 2022 previously. So, traders think 2026 is also going to be a down year and are therefore exiting markets after making gains. title: Gold Slips To Below US$5000 As CNY Holiday Pauses Trade
body: Gold slipped further below $5,000 an ounce in thin trading, with much of Asia closed for the Lunar New Year and after a US holiday on Monday. Bullion fell as much as 1.4% on Tuesday, having lost 1% in the previous session. The metal had rallied briefly on Friday when modest US inflation data boosted the case for the Federal Reserve to trim interest rates. Lower borrowing costs are a tailwind for non-yielding precious metals. A wave of speculative buying pushed a multiyear rally to breaking point in late January, with gold surging to a record above $5,595 an ounce. An abrupt, two-day rout at the turn of the month pulled the metal back to near $4,400, but it has since regained roughly half of its losses. Trading has been choppy since. Many banks — including BNP Paribas SA, Deutsche Bank AG and Goldman Sachs Group Inc. — have forecast that prices will resume their upward trend, with the factors that underpinned gold’s steady ascent set to persist. These include heightened geopolitical tensions, questions over the Fed’s independence and a wider shift away from currencies and sovereign bonds. body: The dollar held gains on Tuesday as markets awaited signals, expected later this week, about the potential timing of rate cuts by the Federal Reserve. However, we differ from the market in that we expect a follow-up cut in July.” “We judge that the most important driver of the dollar through 2026 will be the narrative of U.S. exceptionalism,” she added.The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies, was little changed at 97.12, after a 0.2 per cent gain in the previous session. title: Dollar Holds Firm As Rate-Cut Bets Build Ahead Of Fed Minutes
body: The US dollar held its gains on Feb 17 in subdued trading, as investors looked ahead to minutes from the Federal Reserve and advance US gross domestic product data for signals on the timing of potential interest rate cuts. Reuters reported that the dollar index was little changed at 97.12 after rising 0.2% in the previous session. The euro slipped 0.06% to US$1.1843, sterling eased 0.07% to US$1.3616, while the Japanese yen strengthened 0.15% to 153.28 per dollar. Trading conditions were thin, with several Asian markets closed for the Lunar New Year holiday and US markets shut on Monday for Presidents’ Day. Investor focus is firmly on the Federal Open Market Committee’s January meeting minutes due Wednesday. Recent data showing US consumer prices rose less than expected in January has given policymakers additional leeway to ease monetary policy later this year. The yen’s earlier rally stalled after official data showed Japan’s economy expanded at an annualised pace of just 0.2% last quarter, fuelling expectations that authorities may step up stimulus efforts. title: Copper Slips As Stockpiles Surge During Lunar New Year Lull
body: Industrial metals started the week on the back foot, with copper and aluminium slipping in thin Lunar New Year trading. With many Asian traders still away from their desks, the market lacked momentum. According to Bloomberg, rising stockpiles and uncertainty over US import tariffs are weighing on sentiment. Copper dropped as much as 0.8% to below $12,800 a tonne. Inventories tracked by the London Metal Exchange have climbed to their highest level in more than two decades, adding pressure to prices. Aluminium fell by up to 0.6% as investors waited for clearer signals on Washington’s tariff plans. US markets are due to reopen on Tuesday after the Presidents’ Day holiday. High prices have already cooled demand in China, the world’s biggest metals consumer. Stockpiles are rebuilding after heavy shipments to the US ahead of expected tariffs. Combined copper inventories across exchanges in Shanghai, London and New York are now well above one million tonnes, the highest level in decades based on exchange data. The LMEX Index, which tracks six key base metals in London, hit a record last month on strong Chinese buying and a weaker dollar. It has since pulled back as traders look for fresh direction, including updates on tariffs and signals from the US Federal Reserve. There was some brighter news from the mining sector. BHP Group said first-half earnings jumped by more than 20%, helped by years of investment in copper production. The metal now makes up more than half of the company’s profits, offsetting weaker performance in its iron ore and coal businesses. By late morning in Shanghai, copper futures were down 0.6% at $12,775.50 a tonne. Aluminium fell 0.5% to $3,037.50, zinc lost 0.7% to $3,268, and nickel edged 0.1% lower. title: Stock Today: Dayang Ent Gains 1.62% Despite Seasonal Weakness Outlook
body: Dayang Enterprise Holdings Bhd traded higher in active midday trading, supported by continued analyst optimism over its contract visibility and maintenance-focused operations. As of 2.51 pm, the stock was last done at RM1.88, up 3 sen or 1.62%, after trading between RM1.83 and RM1.88. The counter opened at RM1.85, with about 890,700 shares changing hands, compared with a last adjusted closing price of RM1.85. Analysts noted that Dayang delivered FY25 core earnings broadly in line with expectations at about RM180 million to RM183 million, although profit declined year on year as vessel utilisation and topside maintenance work orders normalised from earlier peaks. Quarterly earnings were also affected by monsoon conditions that limited offshore execution and reduced vessel utilisation. Looking ahead, research houses expect activity to remain seasonally softer in the first quarter of 2026 before recovering from the second quarter onwards, supported by healthy maintenance and modification demand under Petronas’ activity outlook for 2026 to 2028. body: 99 Speed Mart Retail Holdings Bhd fell 6.33% to RM3.70, with 37.85 million shares changing hands as of 12.24 pm. The stock opened at RM3.98, touched an intraday high of RM3.98 and a low of RM3.66, reflecting a pullback after a recent sharp run-up. The decline comes after the company reported a strong set of results for the financial year ended 2025 (FY25). Core net profit rose 20.2% year-on-year to RM614 million, supported by aggressive store expansion, resilient demand for essential goods, and improved profit margins. Revenue for FY25 increased 14.5% to RM5.3 billion, underpinned by higher same-store sales and a more optimised product mix. A key driver of the growth was the addition of 259 net new outlets, a 9.3% increase in store count, lifting same-store sales growth to 7.8% for the full year. Operational efficiency and product mix optimisation helped boost gross profit margins to 11.4%, while operating income rose 15.3%. The group’s effective tax rate fell slightly to 24.5%, supporting net profitability. In the fourth quarter, core net profit climbed 22.8% year-on-year to RM157.3 million, with revenue up 19%, though quarter-on-quarter profit slipped 2% due to higher staff costs and promotional spending. Analysts noted government cash assistance programmes, with around two-thirds of outlets participating, continue to drive footfall and spending among lower- and middle-income households. Following the results, CIMB Group raised its target price for 99 Holdings to RM3.92 from RM3.65 but downgraded the stock to “Hold,” citing the recent 29.5% share rally that has largely priced in near-term earnings growth. title: Ringgit Opens Firmer Against US Dollar, Tracking Positive Momentum On 4Q25 GDP Growth
body: The ringgit strengthened against the US dollar at the opening on Monday, tracking positive momentum on the better-than-expected fourth quarter (4Q) 2025 gross domestic product (GDP) growth of 6.3 per cent which was announced last Friday, an analyst said. At 8am, the ringgit opened firmer at 3.8970/9190 against the greenback, compared to 3.9060/9155 at last Friday’s closing. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the current official GDP forecast for 2026 of 4.0 per cent to 4.5 per cent is likely to be revised upward to account for the country’s resilient economy amidst external uncertainties. “This would mean the Overnight Policy Rate (OPR) would be kept steady in 2026 as there is no urgency to overstimulate the economy,” he told Bernama . Mohd Afzanizam said the interest rate gap between the US Federal Reserve (Fed) fund rate and the OPR would be narrowed as the Fed is expected to ease its monetary policy stance this year. Therefore, he said the ringgit-dollar (exchange rate) would make another attempt to break the psychological level of RM3.9000 today. At the opening, the ringgit traded mostly higher against a basket of major currencies. It appreciated against the euro to 4.6242/6503 from 4.6325/6390 at Friday’s close, and rose vis-à-vis the British pound to 5.3178/3479 from 5.3211/3286 last Friday, but depreciated versus the Japanese yen to 2.5501/5648 from 2.5435/5474. The local note traded higher against its ASEAN peers. The ringgit inched up versus the Singapore dollar to 3.0860/1042 from 3.0904/0950 and surged versus the Thai baht at 12.5273/6200 from 12.5607/5849. It also gained against the Indonesian rupiah to 231.4/232.8 from 231.9/232.4 at Friday’s close, and was higher against the Philippine peso at 6.71/6.76 from 6.73/6.74. title: Bursa Pares Earlier Losses To Close Slightly Higher Ahead Of CNY Holiday
body: Bursa Malaysia pared earlier losses to close slightly higher on Monday, as investors continued to adopt a measured, opportunistic approach rather than broad-based risk aversion ahead of the Chinese New Year (CNY) holidays. The market is closed on Feb 17 and Feb 18 for CNY holidays. At 5 pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) gained 1.72 points, or 0.10 per cent, to 1,741.26, compared with Friday’s close of 1,739.54. The benchmark index had opened 1.12 points higher at 1,740.66, and moved between 1,733.06 and 1,743.01 throughout the trading session. The broader market was positive, with gainers edging out losers 528 to 464, while 547 counters remained unchanged. A total of 1,198 counters remained untraded, and 11 were suspended. Turnover was lower at 1.81 billion units, worth RM1.81 billion, compared to 2.43 billion units, worth RM2.6 billion, on Friday. IPPFA Sdn Bhd director of investment strategy and country economist Mohd Sedek Jantan said selling pressure in the early session was gradually absorbed by selective accumulation in the afternoon, allowing the index to close in positive territory. He said the intraday recovery indicates that downside risks remain contained, with traders taking a cautious yet selective stance, favouring opportunistic moves over broad-based risk aversion. “Overall market activity was subdued, with trading volume falling below two billion shares, reflecting thinner liquidity ahead of the CNY holiday period across regional markets. “The modest upside in the index was therefore driven more by stabilisation and stock-specific positioning than by strong conviction buying,” he told Bernama. Among the heavyweights, Maybank was 12 sen lower at RM11.94, CIMB fell eight sen to RM8.38, IHH Healthcare slipped one sen to RM8.82, Public Bank inched up one sen to RM5.05, and Tenaga Nasional added 46 sen to RM14.42. Besides Tenaga Nasional, other top gainers were Petronas Gas, which rose 38 sen to RM18.60, Dutch Lady Milk advanced 32 sen to RM33.28, Nestle was 30 sen higher at RM109.30, and Knusford bagged 26 sen to 67.5 sen. On the most active list, Hong Seng gained half a sen to one sen, Zetrix AI inched up five sen to 85 sen, Tanco gained two sen to RM1.43, 99 Speed Mart fell 22 sen to RM3.73, and Pharmaniaga was half a sen higher at 31 sen. Joining 99 Speed Mart as top losers were United Plantations, which lost 36 sen to RM29.82, Allianz Malaysia slipped 24 sen to RM22.26, Alliance Bank was 22 sen lower to RM5.07, and Hong Leong Bank dipped 16 sen to RM23.96. title: Asia Shares Becalmed By Holidays, Dire Japan Data
body: Asian shares were quietly consolidating recent hefty gains on Monday as holidays made for thin trading, and dismal economic data out of Japan took some of the heat out of that booming market. The major data of the week are not out until Friday when surveys of global manufacturing hit and the U.S. reports gross domestic product for the fourth quarter. Median forecasts are for annualised growth of 3.0%, down from 4.4% the previous quarter but still solid. Japan on Monday reported its economy grew a miserly 0.1% annualised in the December quarter, far below the 1.6% gain forecast as government spending dragged on activity. The disappointing figures underline the tough task ahead for Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and should support her push for more aggressive fiscal stimulus. The disappointing update triggered broader selling in megacap tech names, including Apple, Nvidia, Broadcom and Amazon, as investors reassessed the sustainability of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven growth. Investor unease was compounded by concerns over massive AI-related capital spending, with Amazon, Alphabet, Meta and Microsoft expected to collectively invest about US$650 billion this year, raising questions about returns and profit margins. Landstar tumbled 15.6%, while CH Robinson and Expeditors International fell 14.5% and 13.2%, respectively, as investors recalibrated the sector’s outlook. Adding to the cautious tone, stronger-than-expected labour market data earlier this week dampened expectations for imminent interest rate cuts. Investors are now closely watching the Consumer Price Index report due Feb 13 for clues on the Federal Reserve’s policy path. With AI optimism giving way to questions over disruption and spending, and inflation data looming, investors are reassessing whether tech’s powerful rally can hold its ground. title: Wall Street Hesitates After Payrolls Surprise
body: Wall Street ended largely flat on Wednesday as a stronger-than-expected US jobs report lifted confidence in the economy but dampened expectations for aggressive interest rate cuts, leaving investors reassessing the Federal Reserve’s next move. The Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped 66.74 points, or 0.13%, to 50,121.40. The Nasdaq Composite fell 36.01 points, or 0.16%, to 23,066.47, while the S&P 500 edged down 0.34 points to close at 6,941.47. Earlier in the session, all three major indexes had traded firmly higher. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq touched their highest levels in more than a week after January payrolls data showed US job growth far exceeded expectations and the unemployment rate declined to 4.3%. However, optimism faded as traders trimmed bets on rate cuts. Although markets still expect at least one 25-basis-point reduction in June, the probability of rates remaining unchanged that month rose to 41% from 24.8%, according to CME Group’s FedWatch tool. Julia Hermann, global market strategist at New York Life Investments, said investors digested changes to rate cut bets “quite well” because they interpreted the strong jobs report as good news for the economy. “This is constructive news in that the economy is not in dire need of rate cuts because the jobs market has been showing some new signs of life,” she said. Julia added, “It comes down to the sweet spot of hiring being strong enough to show us the economy is resilient but not so strong as to derail expectations for future Fed easing.” Sector performance was mixed. Energy led gains with a 2.6% rise, followed by consumer staples up 1.4%, while financial services and communication services both dropped more than 1%. Chipmakers advanced, lifting the Philadelphia semiconductor index 2.3%, but software stocks slid 2.6%. Microsoft fell 2.2% and Alphabet declined 2.4%, weighing on the broader market. Robinhood tumbled 8.9% after missing fourth-quarter revenue expectations, while Generac surged 17.9% on strong results. Investors are now turning their focus to Friday’s Consumer Price Index report for further clues on inflation and the Fed’s policy path. title: Ringgit Opens Higher Against US Dollar On Steady Domestic Sentiment
body: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar, despite a firmer greenback, as continued confidence in Malaysia’s economic fundamentals supported the local currency. At 8 am, the local currency strengthened to 3.9100/9230 versus the greenback from Wednesday’s close of 3.9110/9170. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said encouraging domestic economic data and sustained investor confidence in Malaysia’s macroeconomic outlook continued to underpin local currency demand. “Strong data points for the Malaysian economy would also keep interest intact in the ringgit. As such, expect the US dollar-ringgit pair to oscillate within a range of RM3.91 to RM3.93 today,” he told Bernama. However, he added that stronger-than-expected US labour market data had lifted the US Dollar Index (DXY) by 0.13 per cent to 96.920 points, reflecting the resilience of the US economy. “Therefore, the US Federal Reserve would be inclined to keep the interest rate steady as the inflation rate is likely to stay above the two per cent target. “As such, traders might be tempted to take some profit due to the US Non-farm Payroll (NFP) releases,” he said. Mohd Afzanizam noted that the US NFP came in higher than expected at 130,000 in January versus consensus estimates of 66,000, while the US unemployment rate eased to 4.3 per cent from 4.4 per cent, and the US labour force participation rate rose to 62.5 per cent from 62.4 per cent. At the opening, the ringgit traded higher against a basket of major currencies. It rose versus the Japanese yen to 2.5514/5600 from 2.5527/5566 at Wednesday’s close, appreciated vis-à-vis the British pound to 5.3266/3443 from 5.3561/3643 yesterday and strengthened against the euro to 4.6431/6586 from 4.6611/6683 previously. title: Asian Stocks Soar As Strong US Jobs Data Shakes Rate Cut Bets
body: Asian stocks climbed to record levels on Thursday, propelled by gains in the technology sector, while the dollar strengthened against most major currencies except the yen. South Korea (.KS11) and Japan (.TOPX, .N225) both reached all-time peaks, helping MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares (.MIAP00000PUS) to another record, up 0.7% and lifting year-to-date gains to around 13%. Japanese shares have surged following Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s decisive election win over the weekend, with markets expecting increased economic stimulus. The yen rallied 2.7% this week, trading at 153.01 per dollar in afternoon trade, supported by hopes that Takaichi will pursue fiscal responsibility without the need to negotiate with opposition parties. “Yen shorts are collectively reassessing positions, although at this stage the bearish trend in JPY that started in early 2025 looks more like a reversion to the mean than the start of a structural bull market,” said Chris Weston, head of research at Pepperstone. “That said, traders need to stay open-minded as the macro picture evolves and where the market decides where it ultimately wants to take JPY.” Investor attention remains on the US, where a stronger-than-expected jobs report for January has dampened expectations of near-term rate cuts. Job growth accelerated unexpectedly while the unemployment rate fell slightly, signalling labour market stability that could prompt the Federal Reserve to keep rates unchanged. Thomas Mathews, head of markets for Asia-Pacific at Capital Economics, said, “If labour market conditions are tightening at this point, investors may be overestimating the case for further easing, and Treasuries could be in for a bit more pain.” Market expectations for a 25-basis-point Fed cut in March had been around 20% before the jobs data but dropped to about 5% after the report, according to CME’s FedWatch Tool. Traders still anticipate at least two rate cuts later in the year. The two-year US Treasury yield jumped 5.8 basis points to 3.505%—its largest single-day gain since late October. The dollar found support from elevated Treasury yields, rebounding against most currencies. Analysts cautioned, however, that uncertainties around Fed independence and policy risks suggest further positive data will be needed to maintain the recovery. “Improving global growth prospects and the continued outperformance of non‑US equities keep the case for USD weakness,” OCBC strategists noted. European futures pointed to a strong opening as investors continue to assess corporate earnings across the region. Market attention is now turning to US inflation data due on Friday, which will be the next key test for expectations of interest rate cuts. Commodities also reflected geopolitical and market sentiment. Oil prices rose amid concerns over escalating tensions between Iran and the US, with Brent crude up 0.4% at $69.70 per barrel and West Texas Intermediate crude rising 0.46% to $64.93 per barrel. In contrast, spot gold fell 0.44% to $5,058.49 after a more than 1% gain in the previous session. title: Yen Jumps As Election Result Boosts Confidence In Policy Outlook, Dollar Softens Ahead Of Payrolls
body: The Japanese yen surged on Wednesday as investors bet that Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s landslide election victory would strengthen control over fiscal policy, lifting confidence in Japan’s economic direction. The currency rose nearly 1% against the US dollar to 152.94 in Asian trading, extending gains from the previous session. The euro fell 0.7% to 182.27 yen, while sterling slipped 0.73% to 209.04 yen as the Japanese currency strengthened broadly. Analysts said the election outcome reduced uncertainty over fiscal direction. Vishnu Varathan, Head of Macro Research for Asia ex-Japan at Mizuho, noted that a decisive mandate could allow the government to pursue a more coherent fiscal strategy with fewer political compromises. Strategists at Deutsche Bank also pointed to signs that more market-friendly policies may be emerging, prompting them to close bearish positions on the yen and adopt a neutral stance. The dollar, meanwhile, remained under pressure ahead of key US non-farm payrolls data due later in the day. The greenback was weighed down by weaker-than-expected US retail sales and slower labour cost growth, reinforcing expectations that the Federal Reserve may ease policy later in the year. The dollar index slipped 0.33% to 96.60, while the euro rose to US$1.1914 and sterling edged up to US$1.3658. Elsewhere, the Australian dollar climbed above US$0.71 for the first time in three years, supported by hawkish signals from the Reserve Bank of Australia. Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser said inflation remains too high, while OCBC currency strategist Moh Siong Sim raised his year-end forecast for the currency to US$0.73 following the central bank’s recent rate hike to 3.85%. Investors are now focused on US labour market data, with economists expecting payrolls to have risen by about 70,000 in January, a figure that could shape expectations for the Federal Reserve’s policy path in the months ahead. title: Wall Street Mixed As Weak Retail Data Clouds Outlook
body: The Dow Jones Industrial Average notched its third consecutive record close on Tuesday, even as the S&P 500 and Nasdaq ended lower, with investors weighing weak retail sales data and bracing for a closely watched US jobs report. The Dow rose 52.27 points, or 0.10%, to finish at 50,188.14 after touching an intraday record earlier in the session. In contrast, the S&P 500 fell 23.01 points, or 0.33%, to 6,941.81, while the Nasdaq Composite dropped 136.20 points, or 0.59%, to 23,102.47. Market sentiment was tempered by data showing US retail sales unexpectedly stalled in December, missing economists’ expectations for a 0.4% increase. The weaker reading suggested consumer spending and economic growth may slow heading into the new year. Investors are also positioning cautiously ahead of the delayed nonfarm payrolls report due on Wednesday. White House economic adviser Kevin Hassett had earlier said US job gains could ease in the coming months due to slower labour force growth and productivity gains linked to artificial intelligence. “In anticipation of the jobs report, nobody wants to get too far above their risk budget in the event the number does cause some consternation,” said Mark Luschini, chief investment strategist at Janney Montgomery Scott. Expectations for monetary policy also shifted slightly, with the probability of an April rate cut rising to 36.9% from 32.2% a day earlier, according to CME Group’s FedWatch tool. Markets, however, still largely expect the Federal Reserve to keep rates steady until at least June. Technology shares were under pressure after Alphabet fell 1.8% following news that Google’s parent company sold US$20 billion in bonds. The move reinforced concerns about heavy spending by major technology firms to support the rapid expansion of artificial intelligence, with companies including Amazon, Alphabet, Meta and Microsoft expected to invest hundreds of billions in 2026. The communication services sector was the weakest performer in the S&P 500, reflecting the decline in Alphabet shares. Elsewhere, gains in Walt Disney and Home Depot, both rising more than 2%, helped lift the Dow, offsetting a 1.5% drop in Coca-Cola after the beverage maker missed fourth-quarter revenue estimates. Among other movers, Datadog surged 13.7% after beating quarterly forecasts, while Spotify jumped 14.7% after projecting stronger-than-expected first-quarter earnings on robust user growth and price increases. Marriott climbed 8.5% to a record high after forecasting a 35% rise in co-branded credit-card fees. On the downside, S&P Global slumped 9.7% after issuing a 2026 profit outlook below analysts’ expectations, dragging peers Moody’s and MSCI lower. Market breadth was positive on the New York Stock Exchange, where advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.47-to-1 ratio, while declines slightly outpaced gainers on the Nasdaq. Trading volume across US exchanges totalled 17.89 billion shares, below the 20-session average of 20.68 billion. title: Ringgit Opens Flat Against Greenback Amid Caution Ahead Of US Labour Data
body: The ringgit opened nearly unchanged against the US dollar on Wednesday, as investors adopt a cautious stance ahead of key United States labour market data release. At 8 am, the local currency opened at 3.9220/9345 against the greenback from Tuesday’s close of 3.9220/9260. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US dollar index (DXY) edged up slightly by 0.05 per cent to 96.865 points, despite weaker-than-expected US retail sales data. “US retail sales were unchanged month-on-month in December 2025 compared with consensus estimates of 0.4 per cent, suggesting weaker consumer sentiment and slower spending momentum. “As such, traders will be closely watching the Nonfarm Payrolls and unemployment rate, with consensus estimates at 70,000 jobs compared with 50,000 in December, while the unemployment rate is expected to remain unchanged at 4.4 per cent,” he told Bernama . Meanwhile, he said traders and investors remain positive on Malaysia, as the ringgit closed higher against the greenback yesterday. “High-frequency data continue to support the country’s economy, with the Industrial Production Index (IPI) and the Index of Services growing by 5.0 per cent and 6.5 per cent, respectively, in the fourth quarter of 2025, compared with 4.9 per cent and 5.5 per cent in the previous quarter,” he said. At the opening, the ringgit traded mostly higher against a basket of major currencies. It strengthened against the British pound to 5.3465/3635 from 5.3610/3664 at Tuesday’s close, and rose versus the euro to 4.6621/6769 from 4.6731/6778 previously. However, it weakened against the Japanese yen to 2.5382/5464 from 2.5264/5292 at Tuesday’s close. The local note also traded mostly higher against its ASEAN peers. It was slightly higher versus the Singapore dollar to 3.0989/1090 from 3.0994/1028 previously and strengthened against the Thai baht to 12.5420/5920 from 12.5866/6051. The ringgit was flat against the Philippine peso at 6.70/6.72 from 6.70/6.71 previously. It was also flat against the Indonesian rupiah at 233.3/234.1 from 233.3/233.6 at yesterday’s close. title: Asian Stock Markets Mixed As Traders Weigh US Data, Await Jobs
body: Asian stock markets fluctuated on Wednesday after a strong start to the week as investors weighed weak US consumer data that boosted the case for more interest rate cuts but stoked concerns about the world’s number one economy. The tepid performance followed a mixed day on Wall Street, where tech firms pared recent gains amid lingering worries about extended valuations and the vast sums pumped into artificial intelligence. Traders were also awaiting key jobs data due later in the day — and inflation figures at the end of the week — that could provide a clearer idea about the Federal Reserve’s plans ahead of its March policy meeting. The Commerce Department said Tuesday that US retail sales saw no growth in December, having grown 0.6 per cent in November. The figures provided the Fed with room to consider cutting borrowing costs next month, having held in January after three successive reductions. However, they also indicated there was unease among American consumers, who are a key driver of growth, and pointed to further weakness in the economy. And analysts said the previous “bad news is good news” adage, which has fuelled rate cut hopes in the past and propelled markets higher, might be a thing of the past. “The market is no longer responding uniformly to the idea that weaker data automatically lifts stocks,” said SPI Asset Management’s Stephen Innes. “Beneath the surface, anxiety around AI-related headline risk is clearly elevated.” Traders now see a greater chance of three rate cuts this year, with two already baked into prices, according to Bloomberg . Still, two decision-makers at the central bank made the case Tuesday to keep borrowing costs unchanged for now owing to elevated inflation. Cleveland Fed boss Beth Hammack said in a speech in Ohio that “based on my forecast, we could be on hold for quite some time”, adding that “I’d prefer to err on the side of patience as we assess the impact of recent rate reductions and monitor how the economy performs”. And Dallas Fed chief Lorie Logan told a forum in Texas another cut could be appropriate if there were “further material cooling in the labour market”, but she was currently “more worried about inflation remaining stubbornly high”. While the Dow edged up to another record on Wall Street, the S&P 500 and Nasdaq dropped, with tech firms among the main losers. Asia fared marginally better, with Hong Kong, Sydney, Seoul, Taipei and Manila up, while Shanghai, Singapore and Wellington were down. Tokyo was closed for a holiday. There was little major reaction to data showing Chinese consumer inflation eased last month. Traders remain on guard about developments in the tech space as they worry that the hundreds of billions of dollars firms have pumped into AI may not see any returns for some time. That was compounded on Tuesday after Google parent Alphabet raised more than $30 billion in debt in less than 24 hours as it looks to ramp up its capabilities. News that startup Altruist Corp had rolled out a tax-strategy tool added to the sense of unease on trading floors as it fanned concerns that the software would take business from mainstream firms. Sentiment was rattled last week after Anthropic unveiled a model that could replace numerous software tools, including those for legal work and data marketing. title: Yen Strengthens For Second Day As Dollar Softens Ahead Of US Data
body: The Japanese yen strengthened for a second consecutive session on Tuesday, supported by political developments in Japan and verbal warnings from authorities, while the US dollar eased ahead of key economic data expected to guide interest rate expectations. The yen firmed to about 155.24 per US$, extending gains after rising 0.8% in the previous session. Investor sentiment improved following the election victory of Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, with markets viewing the landslide win as potentially enabling greater fiscal discipline and reducing the need for negotiations with opposition parties. Attention has also turned to Japan’s US$1.4 trillion foreign currency reserves, which could be used in future currency interventions or to support fiscal measures. Analysts noted that speculation over how these reserves might be deployed has added to market focus on the yen. Despite the recent gains, some strategists expect the currency to weaken over the longer term, citing the possibility of looser fiscal policy. Forecasts from Commonwealth Bank of Australia suggest the dollar-yen pair could climb towards 164 by year-end. Meanwhile, the US dollar slipped as investors adopted a cautious stance ahead of a heavy week of economic data, including US employment and inflation reports. The dollar index hovered near a one-week low, reflecting softer demand for the greenback. Markets are currently pricing in two Federal Reserve rate cuts in 2026, with the first expected around mid-year, as investors weigh signs of moderating labour market momentum and the broader outlook for US growth. title: Ringgit Opens Firmer Against US Dollar On Weaker Greenback
body: The ringgit opened firmer against the US dollar on Tuesday, supported by broad-based weakness in the greenback amid concerns over reduced demand for US assets. At 8 am, the ringgit strengthened to 3.9250/9340 against the greenback from Monday’s close of 3.9325/9375. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US dollar weakened following reports that China’s authorities had advised domestic financial institutions to reduce their holdings of US Treasury bonds. “This has led to a softer US dollar, with the US Dollar Index (DXY) declining by 0.79 per cent to 96.865 points,” he told Bernama . Mohd Afzanizam said the main rationale behind the move was concerns over risk concentration and heightened market volatility. He said that based on the latest data, China’s holdings of US Treasury bonds stood at US$682.6 billion as of November 2025, significantly lower than the peak of US$1.3 trillion recorded in July 2011. “Yesterday, the ringgit closed higher against the US dollar. On that note, the ringgit is likely to remain firm at around RM3.92 to RM3.94 due to weakness in the US dollar,” he added. At the opening, the ringgit traded lower against a basket of major currencies. It depreciated against the British pound to 5.3698/3821 from 5.3482/3550, eased against the euro to 4.6723/6830 from 4.6647/6707 previously, and weakened against the Japanese yen to 2.5138/5197 from 2.5104/5137 at Monday’s close. The local note was, however, mostly higher against its ASEAN peers, except for a decline against the Singapore dollar to 3.1001/1077 from 3.0979/10.21 previously. It rose against the Philippine peso to 6.71/6.73 from 6.72/6.74 yesterday, appreciated vis-à-vis the Indonesian rupiah to 233.5/234.2 from 234.0/234.4, and strengthened against the Thai baht to 12.5813/6207 from 12.5876/6101. title: Gold Prices In Malaysia Slip, But Longer-Term Gains Remain Strong
body: Gold prices in Malaysia eased slightly, tracking weaker global prices as investors turned cautious ahead of key US economic data that could influence interest rate expectations. Data from GoldPrice.org showed gold in Malaysia fell about 0.58% on the day, with prices at RM635.86 per gram, RM19,777.40 per ounce and RM635,857.70 per kilogram as at early Tuesday. Despite the daily dip, the precious metal has posted strong gains over longer periods, rising 6.31% over the past 30 days, 40.50% in six months and 53.21% over the past year, reflecting sustained investor demand and global price momentum. Globally, gold prices also edged lower. Reuters reported that spot gold slipped about 0.7% to around US$5,030 per ounce, as markets awaited US retail sales, nonfarm payroll and inflation data later this week, which may provide clues on the US Federal Reserve’s rate path. A stronger US dollar also weighed on bullion, making it more expensive for overseas buyers. Analysts said short-term movements may remain volatile. According to RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research), gold has been showing increasing positive momentum but faces immediate resistance near US$5,090 per ounce, with the possibility of sideways consolidation unless a breakout occurs. The research house noted that downside pressure remains in the near term, with support seen around US$4,800. Silver prices in Malaysia also declined on the day, falling about 1.22%, although longer-term gains remain significant over six months and one year. Overall, while prices softened in the near term, gold continues to trade near historically high levels, supported by expectations of lower global interest rates and ongoing demand for safe-haven assets. title: AI Jitters Fade, Tech Stocks Lead Wall Street Higher
body: Technology stocks led a rebound on Wall Street on Monday, helping the Nasdaq and S&P 500 finish higher after last week’s sharp sell-off linked to concerns over artificial intelligence competition. The Dow Jones Industrial Average also edged up to record its second consecutive closing high, rising 20.20 points, or 0.04%, to 50,135.87. The S&P 500 gained 32.52 points, or 0.47%, to 6,964.82, while the Nasdaq Composite advanced 207.46 points, or 0.90%, to 23,238.67. Despite the gains, the S&P 500 ended just shy of its record closing level of 6,978.60, while the Nasdaq remained about 3% below its most recent peak reached in November. The recovery was driven largely by the technology sector, which rose 1.6% and extended Friday’s gains. The S&P 500 Software Services index climbed 2.9%, recouping part of its losses after a bruising seven-day stretch fuelled by fears that AI could intensify competition across the industry. Among individual stocks, Oracle surged 9.6% after D.A. Davidson upgraded the company to a “buy” rating from “neutral”, adding further momentum to the sector. Keith Lerner, chief investment officer at Truist Advisory Services, said improving sentiment also followed remarks attributed to OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman in a CNBC report, which Reuters could not independently verify, indicating the company’s ChatGPT chatbot had returned to exceeding 10% monthly growth. “You’ve a sharply oversold market where a little bit of good news can go a long way,” said Lerner, adding that “the rubber band was stretched too far for tech and software” in last week’s selloff. Even after the rebound, the software index remained nearly 13% below levels seen before the late-January decline, while the broader technology sector was less than 3% below its pre-sell-off levels. Outside technology, the materials sector rose 1.4%, supported by gains in gold and silver prices that lifted mining stocks. In contrast, consumer staples and healthcare were the weakest performers, each falling 0.86%. Waters led healthcare losses, plunging 13.9% after forecasting first-quarter profit below Wall Street expectations, while concerns also lingered over weakness in a unit acquired last year by Becton Dickinson. Semiconductor stocks also advanced, with the Philadelphia SE Semiconductor index gaining 1.4%. Nvidia rose 2.5%, providing the biggest boost to the S&P 500, as investors awaited the AI chipmaker’s results later this month. Several corporate developments weighed on individual counters. Hims & Hers Health dropped 16% for a seventh straight session after Novo Nordisk filed a patent infringement lawsuit related to a weight-loss drug. Workday fell 5% after announcing the return of co-founder Aneel Bhusri as chief executive, while Kyndryl plunged 54.9% after delaying its quarterly filing and flagging material weakness in financial reporting. On the upside, Kroger climbed 3.9% after naming former Walmart executive Greg Foran as chief executive. Investors are now focused on upcoming economic data, including the January nonfarm payrolls report due on Wednesday and the Consumer Price Index release on Friday, both seen as key indicators for the Federal Reserve’s interest-rate path. Markets are currently pricing in the first rate cut of the year in June, according to CME Group’s FedWatch tool, around the time US President Donald Trump’s nominee for Federal Reserve chair, Kevin Warsh, could assume the role. Market breadth was positive, with advancing stocks outnumbering decliners by roughly two to one on the New York Stock Exchange. Trading volume, however, was relatively light, with about 17.78 billion shares changing hands, below the 20-session average of 20.66 billion. title: Ringgit Opens Little Changed Against US Dollar On Mixed Global Sentiment
body: The ringgit opened nearly unchanged against the US dollar on Monday, as mixed global sentiment capped gains while investors assessed political developments and major currency moves. At 8 am, the ringgit traded almost flat at 3.9430/9560 against the greenback, compared with last Friday’s close of 3.9440/9525. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said multiple global factors are shaping foreign exchange markets, and expects the US dollar-ringgit pair to trade between RM3.93 and RM3.95 today. “We foresee emerging market currencies, including the ringgit, remaining on a positive note amid an improvement in market uncertainty,” he told Bernama. On external developments, he said the landslide victory by Japan’s Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) in Sunday’s election signalled that Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi is likely to proceed with further economic stimulus measures, a move that could weigh on the Japanese yen. At the same time, easing tensions between the United States and Iran over the nuclear programme following discussions on Friday has led to lower benchmark Brent crude prices, Mohd Afzanizam added. He said political developments in the region were also supportive of market sentiment, particularly Thailand’s general election, where the Bhumjaithai Party secured a comfortable margin, pointing to continued political and economic stability in the country. “In some sense, there is a bit of optimism in the market. However, the weaker yen has contributed to a firmer US Dollar Index (DXY),” he said. At the opening, the ringgit traded mostly lower against a basket of major currencies. It strengthened against the Japanese yen to 2.5075/5161 from 2.5111/5167 at last Friday’s close, but weakened versus the British pound to 5.3664/3841 from 5.3548/3663 and slipped against the euro to 4.6630/6784 from 4.6508/6608 previously. The local note was also mostly lower against its ASEAN peers. The ringgit traded nearly flat against the Indonesian rupiah at 233.6/234.5 from 233.6/234.3 at last Friday’s close, eased vis-à-vis the Singapore dollar to 3.1020/1125 from 3.0965/1034, fell against the Thai baht to 12.5386/5887 from 12.4609/4933 previously, and was flat versus the Philippine peso at 6.73/6.75. title: FBM KLCI Up 15 Points At Midday On Wall Street Optimism
body: Bursa Malaysia maintained a firm footing at midday of Feb 9, tracking the upbeat mood in regional markets following Wall Street’s strong overnight gains. title: Bitcoin Finds Its Footing Above US$70,000 After Whiplash Week
body: Bitcoin steadied above the US$70,000 mark in Asian trading on Feb 9, offering a brief reprieve to rattled investors after a week of stomach-churning volatility that underscored the cryptocurrency’s enduring boom-and-bust nature, Bloomberg reported. The world’s largest digital asset briefly slipped to as low as US$69,991 in early Singapore trading before recovering to around US$70,700 by mid-morning, little changed from its opening level. The calm contrasted sharply with last week’s violent swings, when Bitcoin plunged to US$60,033 on Feb 5, its lowest level since October 2024, before roaring back above US$70,000 a day later. Despite the stabilisation, traders remain firmly on edge. Bitcoin’s pullback from a record high of US$126,000 in October has unsettled bulls, particularly as it comes against an unusually supportive backdrop. A crypto-friendly White House, accelerating institutional adoption and the rapid growth of exchange-traded funds have so far failed to insulate prices from sharp drawdowns. The latest bout of turbulence has also reignited doubts about Bitcoin’s claim as “digital gold”. During a period of heightened geopolitical uncertainty, the token has struggled to behave like a safe haven, moving more like a high-beta risk asset than a store of value. Still, there are tentative signs that confidence is creeping back. US-listed Bitcoin exchange-traded funds saw net inflows of US$221 million on Feb 6, suggesting investors were willing to buy the dip after the market’s dizzying selloff. Technical levels are now firmly in focus. Bitcoin’s ability to remain comfortably above its 200-week moving average, around US$58,000, a level it rebounded from on Feb 6, is being watched as a key test of whether the world’s biggest cryptocurrency can regain momentum or whether another bout of volatility lies ahead. title: Asia Shares Soar As Japan Hits Record High After Takaichi Win
body: Asian equities surged on Monday, with Japan’s Nikkei leading the charge, after Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s decisive election victory fuelled optimism for reflationary policies. Investors also took comfort from Wall Street’s rebound at the end of last week. Japan’s Nikkei 225 jumped 4.2% to an all-time high as the LDP’s commanding majority cleared the way for additional spending and potential tax cuts. “Cutting the consumption tax on food is a positive for domestic consumption spending; increased military spending is a positive for defence stocks,” said Jamie Halse, managing director at Senjin Capital in Sydney. Broader regional markets followed suit. The MSCI Asia-Pacific ex-Japan index rose 1.0%, while South Korea’s tech-heavy KOSPI climbed 3.9%. US S&P 500 futures added 0.4%, and Nasdaq futures rose 0.6%, building on gains of more than 2% on Friday. Chip stocks drove much of the momentum, with Nvidia jumping almost 8%, Advanced Micro Devices up over 8%, and Broadcom rising 7%. Analysts at BofA noted, however, that concerns linger about whether massive AI-related investments will generate returns and which firms will ultimately benefit. Investors are also watching US economic data this week, which could influence Federal Reserve rate cut expectations. Payrolls are forecast to increase by 70,000 in January, keeping the unemployment rate at 4.4%, while retail sales are expected to rise 0.4%. Any surprises could affect Treasury yields and the dollar, as well as regional currencies such as the yen and pound. body: US stocks ended sharply lower on Feb 5, with heavy losses in Big Tech dragging the Nasdaq to its weakest close since November as investors recoiled from ballooning artificial intelligence (AI) capital spending plans. The selloff accelerated after Alphabet said it could double capital expenditure (capex) on AI, outlining plans for up to US$185 billion in spending in 2026. Alphabet slipped 0.6%, while Microsoft sank 5%, Palantir plunged 6.8% and Oracle slid 7%. Amazon fell 4.4% during regular trading before tumbling another 10% after hours, after projecting hefty capex next year, reinforcing fears that tech giants are far from easing their AI spending spree. Nvidia, a key AI beneficiary, still fell 1.4%. Investor unease has been growing over whether massive AI investments will translate into near-term revenue and profit gains, with added concerns that increasingly capable AI tools could cannibalise demand for traditional software. ServiceNow dropped 7.6%, Salesforce fell nearly 5%, and the S&P 500 software and services index slid 4.6% for a seventh straight session. Outside tech, Qualcomm sank 8.5% after issuing a weaker-than-expected outlook, while the CBOE volatility index briefly hit a two-month high as traders cut exposure to richly valued growth stocks. The rotation into cheaper names continued. The S&P 500 value index slipped 0.9% but stayed positive for the week, while the growth index was down more than 4%. The S&P 500 fell 1.23% to 6,798.40, the Nasdaq lost 1.59% to 22,540.59, and the Dow slid 1.20% to 48,908.72. Nine of 11 sectors ended lower, led by materials and consumer discretionary. Earnings reactions were mixed: Snap sank over 13% despite beating revenue estimates, Estee Lauder plunged 19% on a downbeat outlook, while Tapestry jumped 10% and Hershey climbed 9% after upbeat forecasts. On the macro front, jobless claims rose more than expected and job openings fell to a five-year low, adding to caution. Decliners outpaced advancers on the S&P 500 by nearly two to one, underscoring the market’s risk-off tone. title: RHB: Solarvest A Buy As 44% Upside Remains Despite China VAT Cut
body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has maintained its ‘Buy’ rating on Solarvest Holdings Bhd, with a target price of RM3.49, implying 44% upside from current levels. According to the research house, the stock is now trading at its three-year historical price-to-earnings mean of 23 times, which it views as a valuation floor given Solarvest’s robust earnings trajectory and strong project pipeline. It shared that the recent sell-off, partially fuelled by concerns over China’s upcoming value-added tax (VAT) export subsidy cuts, is seen as overdone. “Solarvest has secured a 2GW fixed-price blanket panel order for the next 18-24 months, providing major cost visibility and ensuring that key projects like LSS5, LSS5+ and Mukah remain unaffected. “Thus, the risk of supplier default is considered low, given top-tier, China-listed manufacturers with reputational and legal incentives to honour contracts,” RHB Research said. It emphasised that while China will remove the 9% solar panel export VAT rebate from April 2026 (with battery rebates falling to 6%), the impact on Solarvest’s earnings is negligible because stable polysilicon prices at US$7-US$8/kg and a 3.2%-ringgit appreciation against Chinese yuan further cushion cost pressures. RHB Research sees the current levels as an attractive re-entry point ahead of the next growth cycle, with the company well-positioned to pass through higher module costs in new contracts. Key risks include weaker contract wins, unexpected project cost increases, policy changes and heightened competition. title: Ringgit Gains As US Dollar Pauses Amid Mixed Data
body: The ringgit rose against the US dollar and major currencies on Thursday, supported by domestic strength and a rebound in oil prices, as the greenback consolidated after mixed US economic data. At 8 am, the ringgit climbed to 3.9270/9370 versus the US dollar, from Wednesday’s close of 3.9305/9345. IPPFA Sdn Bhd director of investment strategy and country economist Mohd Sedek Jantan said data from US automatic data processing (ADP) showed private payrolls rose by 22,000 in January, below consensus estimates of 46,000 and down from 37,000 in December, pointing to softer hiring momentum in the US labour market. Wage growth for job stayers, however, remained elevated at 4.5 per cent year-on-year, signalling persistent labour cost pressures. title: Qualcomm, Arm Weighed Down By Global Memory Chip Shortage
body: Shares of Qualcomm Inc and Arm Holdings Plc tumbled more than 8% in extended trading on Wednesday, following quarterly reports that highlighted concerns over a tightening memory chip supply, which is expected to constrain smartphone production and growth in the electronics industry. The historic expansion of artificial intelligence infrastructure is driving the shortage, as memory chips—essential for managing data—are increasingly prioritised for AI data centres. This has left fewer components available for smartphones, ultimately reducing the number of devices reaching consumers and contributing to higher prices. “Industrywide, memory shortages and price increases are likely to define the overall scale of the handset industry,” Qualcomm Chief Executive Officer Cristiano Amon told analysts. He noted that Chinese customers in particular have indicated they will build fewer phones than planned due to limited access to memory chips. Despite near-term challenges, both Qualcomm and Arm stand to gain from the ongoing AI boom, with opportunities to generate more revenue from data centre operators. The focus on premium smartphones is also helping bolster Qualcomm’s high-end chip sales and sustain Arm’s royalty income. Other industry players have echoed concerns. MediaTek Inc. described the memory shortage as an “evolving” issue, while Intel Corp. CEO Lip-Bu Tan said suppliers expect no relief until 2028. Major memory producers, including Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix, and Micron Technology, have focused heavily on supplying high-bandwidth memory (HBM) for AI workloads, limiting availability for consumer electronics. Efforts are underway to expand overall production capacity, but building and equipping new factories could take more than a year, meaning shortages are likely to continue affecting the smartphone market in the near term. title: HSIF Stay Constructive, RHB Keeps Bullish Stance
body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) maintains its long position on Hang Seng Index Futures (HSIF), citing strengthening upside momentum despite intraday volatility. title: Bitcoin Dips Below US$70,000
body: Bitcoin briefly dipped below $70,000 per token on Thursday after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent suggested the US government would not bail out the cryptocurrency. In a heated back-and-forth during a House Financial Services Committee on Wednesday, Bessent was asked if the US Treasury had the authority to buy bitcoin or other cryptos. “I do not have the authority to do that, and as chair of FSOC, I do not have that authority,” Bessent stated. Bitcoin fell to as low as $69,525 apiece early Thursday, continuing the slump on Wednesday that followed Bessent’s comments. The decline was also fueled by the broader selling pressure in markets and a warning from notable investor Michael Burry that a sustained decline in bitcoin’s price could “set in motion a death spiral leading to massive value destruction.” Bitcoin dropped sharply last weekend to notch its fourth straight month of losses. The move lower coincided with President Trump’s announcement last Friday selecting Kevin Warsh to lead the Federal Reserve when Jerome Powell’s term ends in May, a nomination markets view as hawkish. title: Asia Shares Falter As Global Tech Selloff Spooks Investors
body: Asian stocks faltered as concerns about the escalating costs of AI investment hounded the tech sector, though Wall Street futures were trying to make a comeback as chipmakers gained. Google parent Alphabet reported solid results after the bell, but it was targeting capital expenditure of US$175 billion to US$185 billion this year, sharply above analysts’ estimates. Shares swung wildly – down over 6 per cent at one point -before settling just 0.4 per cent lower after-hours. Investors have been rotating out of technology giants and into cyclical stocks amid fears of AI disruptions to jobs. The recent selloff, triggered by a new legal tool from Anthropic’s Claude large language model, has wiped out about US$830 billion in market value since January 28. Disappointing earnings results from Advanced Micro Devices didn’t help either, with the chipmaker tumbling 17 per cent overnight. “That increase in (Alphabet) capex was absolutely enormous,” said Tony Sycamore, analyst at IG. “At a time when everyone is hyper-sensitive and hyper-nervous about what’s going on with the software companies, with what’s going on with CAPEX and AI valuations… I would have thought the reaction would be quite negative, but it’s not flowing through to the Nasdaq futures.” The demand for more equipment spending helped chip giant Nvidia rally almost 2 per cent after the bell, partially reversing a 3.4 per cent tumble overnight. That likely lifted Nasdaq futures by 0.6 per cent and the S&P 500 by 0.4 per cent. Still, MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan skidded 1 per cent. South Korea’s KOSPI tumbled 1.7 per cent and Taiwanese shares lost 0.7 per cent Japan’s Nikkei was flat. Chinese blue chips lost 0.7 per cent, while Hong Kong’s Hang Seng index slid 0.8 per cent. Much attention is on Amazon’s results later in the day, as well as policy meetings from the Bank of England and the European Central Bank where rates are expected to be on hold. Yen Weak Ahead Of Japan Election The Japanese yen nursed a fourth straight day of losses ahead of a general election on Sunday where polls are tipping a decisive victory for Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, endorsing her spending ambitions that have raised concerns about the nation’s strained finances. The dollar was steady at 156.93 yen, having rallied 3 per cent from its low of 152.1 yen when chatter that the New York Federal Reserve conducted rate checks sent the Japanese currency flying high. In the Treasuries market, the benchmark 10-year yield was flat at 4.2715 per cent. The US nonfarm payrolls report for January has been pushed back from its scheduled release on Friday to February 11 due to a four-day partial government shutdown that has now ended. Oil prices fell on Thursday after two straight days of gains as the US and Iran agreed to hold talks in Oman on Friday, despite differences about the agenda. US West Texas Intermediate crude fell 1.4 per cent to $64.23 per barrel, while Brent crude futures also dropped 1.4 per cent to $68.47 per barrel. Gold and silver prices were up a little in early trade after an epic implosion last Friday that saw the two plunging from lofty record highs. Gold rose 0.3 per cent to $4,976 an ounce while silver inched up 0.2 per cent to $88.20 an ounce.
