title: AI Stocks Slide As Wall Street Questions Valuations
body: US stocks closed lower on Wednesday, with technology companies including Advanced Micro Devices, Palantir and Nvidia among the biggest decliners, as investors questioned high valuations and whether Wall Street’s AI rally has peaked. The S&P 500 fell 0.51% to 6,882.72 points, while the Nasdaq dropped 1.51% to 22,904.58 points. By contrast, the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.53% to 49,501.30 points. Despite the S&P 500’s overall loss, seven of its 11 sector indexes gained, led by energy up 2.25% and materials climbing 1.8%. Investors sold AI-related stocks amid concerns about the speed of industry disruption. “The size of the infrastructure buildout is unprecedented, and the pace of consumers and businesses adopting AI tools is also unprecedented. The stock market is having a really hard knowing where to price the stocks and what the future looks like. … The market is suddenly skeptical and concerned about it,” said Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital in St. Louis. Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) tumbled 17% after the chipmaker forecast quarterly revenue that disappointed investors and suggested it is struggling to compete with AI heavyweight Nvidia, which dropped 3.4%. The PHLX semiconductor index fell 4.4%. Palantir reversed sharp gains from the previous day, slumping almost 12% despite strong quarterly sales. Other software companies also lost ground, with Snowflake down 4.6% and Datadog 3.3% lower. “If you’ve got legacy software that’s old and clunky, you’re a ripe target for AI. We’re a bit bearish on software in general, with the whole impetus of AI,” said Josh Chastant, portfolio manager, public investments at GuideStone Funds. Investors shifted toward less pricey stocks that had largely sat out the tech rally. The S&P 500 value index gained for a fifth straight session, while the S&P 500 growth index declined. Amid the volatility, some companies posted gains. Super Micro Computer shares jumped 13.8% after raising its annual revenue forecast on strong demand for AI-optimised servers. Eli Lilly shares rallied about 10% after projecting 2026 profit above Wall Street expectations, helping to limit overall S&P 500 losses. Market activity was heavy, with 24.6 billion shares traded compared with a 20-session average of 19.9 billion. Advancing issues outnumbered falling ones on the S&P 500 by a 2.6-to-one ratio. The S&P 500 posted 93 new highs and 23 new lows, while the Nasdaq recorded 218 new highs and 318 new lows. Data from private payrolls showed that US January private employment rose less than expected, reflecting job losses in professional, business services and manufacturing. The government’s official January jobs report, originally scheduled for Friday, was delayed due to a four-day partial shutdown that ended on Tuesday. After the close, Alphabet regained 2% following an almost 2% fall earlier, as the company said it was aggressively increasing spending to deepen investments in AI. title: Wall Street Slides As AI Fears Rattle Tech Stocks
body: Wall Street closed sharply lower on Tuesday, weighed down by renewed anxiety over artificial intelligence intensifying competition for software companies, while investors stayed cautious ahead of earnings from Alphabet and Amazon later this week. Technology stocks bore the brunt of the sell-off, with AI leaders Nvidia and Microsoft each sliding nearly 3%. Alphabet fell 1.2% ahead of its results due on Wednesday, while Amazon lost 1.8% before its earnings release on Thursday. The pressure reflected growing concerns that AI advancements could erode margins across the software sector. Those worries were amplified by recent developments such as Anthropic’s launch of a legal tool for its Claude AI chatbot, which sharpened fears of disruption across the industry. “We’re looking at a lot of software names that are seen as companies that may well be disrupted when we start to see the advancement of artificial intelligence. We’re seeing a lot of software companies across the spectrum get hit,” said Art Hogan, chief market strategist at B. Riley Wealth. Several major software names saw steep declines. Salesforce, Datadog and Adobe dropped about 7%, while Synopsys and Atlassian slid roughly 8%. Intuit suffered the heaviest fall, plunging 11%. In contrast, AI data firm Palantir bucked the broader trend, rallying nearly 7% after posting strong quarterly results late on Monday. The S&P 500 software and services index fell 3.8%, marking its fifth straight day of losses. According to John Campbell, senior portfolio manager at Allspring Global Investments, stretched valuations are adding to market unease. “We’ve got an expensive market and expectations are really high. Many areas, especially around AI, are priced for perfection. That’s just got us in a skittish environment,” he said. Beyond technology, healthcare stocks also came under pressure after Novo Nordisk warned of a sharp drop in annual sales, sending its US-listed shares tumbling nearly 15%. Eli Lilly slipped 3.9%, while Structure Therapeutics fell 6.75%. There were a few bright spots. Walmart climbed about 3%, becoming the first physical retailer to reach a US$1 trillion market capitalisation. PepsiCo rose 4.9% after announcing price cuts on core brands such as Lay’s and Doritos. Merck gained 2.2% following its quarterly results, though Pfizer slipped 3.3% despite beating profit estimates. Elsewhere, Advanced Micro Devices declined 1.7% ahead of its earnings announcement after the closing bell. Walt Disney edged down 0.2% after naming theme parks chief Josh D’Amaro as chief executive, ending months of succession uncertainty. PayPal slumped 20% after forecasting 2026 profit below market expectations. By the close, the S&P 500 fell 0.84% to 6,917.81 points, while the Nasdaq dropped 1.43% to 23,255.19 points. The Dow Jones Industrial Average eased 0.34% to 49,240.99 points. Despite the overall decline, advancing stocks outnumbered decliners on the S&P 500 by a ratio of 1.2 to one. Trading activity was heavy, with 23.5 billion shares changing hands, well above the 20-session average of 19.6 billion. Six of the 11 S&P 500 sectors ended lower, led by information technology, which slid 2.17%, followed by a 1.28% drop in communication services. Attention is now turning to a packed earnings calendar, with around a quarter of S&P 500 companies due to report this week. Analysts expect earnings growth of nearly 11% for the December quarter, up from about 9% estimated at the start of January, according to LSEG data. On the political front, legislation aimed at ending a US government shutdown narrowly cleared a procedural vote in the House of Representatives, paving the way for a final vote later in the day. The partial shutdown has delayed the release of key labour market data, including jobs figures due on Friday and the JOLTS report that had been scheduled for Tuesday. The session saw the S&P 500 notch 81 new highs and 28 new lows, while the Nasdaq recorded 202 new highs against 311 new lows. title: Tasco Sees Brighter Road Ahead After Tough Period
body: MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB Research) has maintained a BUY rating on Tasco Bhd with a revised target price of RM0.56, down from RM0.64, citing an improving outlook in the freight forwarding and logistics segments. MBSB Research reported that the company’s Strategic Forward Pricing (SFP) scheme provides margin protection through risk-sharing, while the consolidation of cold chain operations and customers shifting from leased to owned warehousing could enhance utilisation and reduce inefficiencies. According to MBSB Research, freight forwarding volumes, which contribute 35% of Tasco’s total revenue, have begun to stabilise following earlier disruptions caused by tariff uncertainty. Ocean freight rates, which fell sharply from last year’s peaks, are showing early signs of recovery, while air freight remains softer amid weaker global demand. The SFP scheme has also helped secure new international tenders, supporting resilience in forwarding volumes and earnings despite ongoing rate volatility. Within Tasco’s contract logistics division, contributing 33% of total revenue, warehousing remained the largest segment, accounting for 48% of 3QFY26 revenue. Management highlighted that 50% of new warehouse space in the 400,000 sq ft Shah Alam and 300,000 sq ft Northport facilities has already been committed by existing customers transitioning from leased premises. The remaining space at Shah Alam may be converted into a cold chain, with both warehouses expected to commence operations in August 2026 (2QFY27). The cold chain division, representing 14% of total revenue, underperformed following the loss of a major F&B account. Tasco plans to consolidate operations by pausing one facility and relocating volumes to improve utilisation and reduce electricity and manpower inefficiencies, with the process targeted for mid-to-late March. MBSB Research noted that 3QFY26 results came in below expectations, prompting a trimming of earnings forecasts by 4.2% for FY26, 2.5% for FY27, and 2.8% for FY28 to reflect weaker warehousing activity and lower cold chain utilisation. The research house expects earnings momentum to improve as Tasco implements its expansion and consolidation plans. As of 12.20 pm, the stock price increased 2.17% to RM0.47. title: Southern Cable Set To Gain From Import Restrictions
body: Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB) has maintained its BUY call on Southern Cable Group Bhd, keeping its target price at RM2.59, implying a potential upside of 21%. HLIB reported that the company is expected to deliver strong fourth-quarter earnings for FY25, supported by a further ramp-up in East Coast Rail Link (ECRL)-related deliveries, while momentum is likely to continue into the first quarter of 2026. HLIB highlighted the company’s expanded cable capacity and improved margin outlook following the commissioning of its aluminium furnace as key growth drivers. The research house noted that Southern Cable’s full-year FY26 earnings forecast of RM151 million assumes the contribution from last year’s capacity expansion, which increased total cable production from around 47,000 kilometres at the start of the year to about 54,000 kilometres by year-end. The analyst added there is upside potential should the incremental four thousand kilometres of additional capacity, initially expected in the second half of 2026, come online earlier, alongside stronger-than-expected margins. The bank also pointed to Tenaga Nasional Bhd’s plans to progressively restrict 132kV cable imports as an incremental boost for domestic suppliers, including SCGBHD. The analyst said the group is in the final stages of certifying its 132kV cable range, with commercialisation targeted by the first half of 2026. Domestic orders are likely to displace imports, supporting near-term capacity utilisation and strengthening the company’s position in high-voltage and DC-related grid projects. HLIB maintained its forecasts and rating, citing Southern Cable’s leading position in Malaysia’s power cable market. The analyst added that growing electricity demand, ongoing national grid expansion, and a competitor exit provide opportunities for the company to capture additional market share. Southern Cable’s current market capitalisation stands at RM2.4 billion, with issued shares of 1,130 million and a dividend yield of 0.8%. As of 12.12 pm, Southern Cable’s stock price decreased 2.36% to RM2.07. title: Malaysia Gold Prices Jump As Safe-haven Demand Lifts Global Bullion
body: Gold prices in Malaysia surged on Wednesday, tracking a sharp rebound in global bullion prices amid heightened geopolitical tensions and renewed safe-haven demand. According to data from goldprice.org, the price of gold rose to RM641.27 per gram, up RM20.68 or 3.34% on the day, while prices per kilogram climbed to RM641,269.63, marking a 3.33% daily increase. Over the past year, gold prices in ringgit terms have risen more than 52%, reflecting both strong global demand and currency effects. The rally mirrors developments in the international market, where spot gold hovered near US$5,100 per ounce after posting its biggest daily gain in more than 17 years. Spot gold was last up 2.9% at US$5,082.94, after surging nearly 6% in the previous session, its strongest single-day rise since November 2008. Gold had reached a record high of US$5,594.82 last week. The rebound followed renewed geopolitical tensions after the US military shot down an Iranian drone in the Arabian Sea, reinforcing gold’s appeal as a safe-haven asset. Bullion had earlier slipped to a low of US$4,403.24 on Monday following its steepest two-day sell-off in decades. RHB Investment Bank Bhd noted that the recovery suggests underlying fundamentals remain intact despite recent volatility, with geopolitical risks and macroeconomic uncertainty continuing to support demand for gold. Silver prices in Malaysia also rose sharply, with silver gaining nearly 8% on the day in ringgit terms, in line with a strong rebound in global silver prices. Market participants are now awaiting further economic cues from the US, including labour market data, for indications on the Federal Reserve’s policy direction, which could influence the next move in precious metals. title: HSIF Consolidation May Set Stage For Breakout, RHB
body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has maintained its positive trading bias on Hang Seng Index Futures (HSIF), advising traders to keep their long positions intact as the broader technical structure continues to tilt upwards. HSIF ended the previous session marginally higher, gaining 33 points to close at 26,818 points. The index opened at 26,801 points and slid to an intraday low of 26,460 points before rebounding to a high of 27,158 points. However, late-session selling pared most of the gains, resulting in a candlestick with a long lower shadow. During the evening session, HSIF weakened further, falling 228 points to last trade at 26,590 points. RHB Research noted that the formation of a Doji pattern reflects market indecision, with bulls and bears remaining evenly matched. Despite this, the research house said the overall technical outlook remains constructive, as HSIF continues to hold above its 50-day simple moving average. It added that consolidation at current levels could form a base for a potential breakout. As long as HSIF stays above the 26,400-point support level, RHB Research views the bullish structure as intact and will maintain its positive stance unless the index closes decisively below this level. The research house reiterated its recommendation to hold the long position initiated at 21,416 points, the close on Apr 14, 2025. To manage downside risks, the stop-loss level has been raised to 26,400 points. In terms of technical levels, immediate support is seen at 26,400 points, followed by 25,500 points. On the upside, immediate resistance is pegged at 28,600 points, with the next resistance at 29,100 points. title: Crypto Rout Deepens As Nearly US$500 Billion Evaporates
body: The cryptocurrency market extended its selloff on Feb 4, with Bitcoin and Ethereum under pressure as investors retreated from risk assets amid heightened global uncertainty. Almost US$470 billion has been wiped off the total crypto market capitalisation in less than a week, Bloomberg reported. Meanwhile, according to CoinGecko data, total market value has fallen by US$467.6 billion since Jan 29, as a downturn led by Bitcoin gathered pace. Bitcoin tumbled to its lowest level since US President Donald Trump won re-election in early November 2024, marking a sharp reversal after optimism over a more crypto-friendly US administration. The world’s largest cryptocurrency hit an intraday low of US$72,877 before recovering some ground in Asian trading on Feb 4, last changing hands at around US$76,200 at 10am Singapore time. Bitcoin is now down 13% year to date and has shed about 39% from its Oct 6 peak above US$126,000. Ethereum mirrored the broader weakness, sliding to around US$2,270 after swinging between US$2,115 and US$2,351 during the session, reflecting fragile sentiment across digital assets. The crypto slump followed a volatile week across global markets, which also saw sharp moves in gold and silver. While precious metals attracted buyers after recent losses, cryptocurrencies failed to find similar support. Bitcoin and US equities declined in tandem as rising tensions between the US and Iran pushed investors towards traditional safe-haven assets. Bitcoin’s sharp drop has also reignited debate over its status as “digital gold”. Critics argue that the cryptocurrency has once again failed to behave as a hedge during periods of geopolitical stress. With volatility still elevated, market participants remain cautious as cryptocurrencies struggle to regain investor confidence. title: Coraza Set For Sharp Earnings Growth
body: CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) has maintained a BUY call on Coraza Integrated Technology Bhd with a target price of RM0.83, implying a 52% upside from its current market price of RM0.545 (US$68.2 million). The research house highlighted that Coraza’s fourth-quarter 2025 results are expected to show strong year-on-year and quarter-on-quarter growth, supported by high utilisation rates and new project ramp-ups in the semiconductor equipment cycle. According to CIMB Securities, Coraza’s valuation of 13 times FY26F price-to-earnings is below its peers, positioning the stock for a potential record-breaking fiscal year. About 80% of revenue is tied to the semiconductor supply chain, with 40–50% exposure to the front-end segment, while the company’s aerospace unit is also set for exponential growth. Capacity expansions at Plants 3 and 5 and new in-house secondary process capabilities are expected to enhance front-end penetration and automation project wins. The semiconductor equipment and materials sector continues to perform strongly, with Semiconductor Equipment and Materials International (SEMI) raising its 2026 forecast for global sales to US$145 billion, up 9% from US$138 billion in 2025. Major players such as ASML, Applied Materials, Lam Research and KLA Corp posted record orders and positive guidance, while automated test equipment provider Advantest exceeded expectations and raised profit guidance, signalling robust market demand. CIMB Securities noted that concerns over the US dollar’s weakness versus the ringgit are likely overblown. Approximately 70–80% of Coraza’s revenue is USD-denominated, with 55–65% of costs also linked to the currency, providing a natural hedge. The bank highlighted that every 1% change in the FX rate would only impact results by 1–2.5%. Coraza is scheduled to announce its FY25 results on Feb 24, and CIMB sees significant upside potential for FY26 forecasts, underpinned by strong guidance from key semiconductor customers. As of 11.06 am, Coraza’s stock price noted an increase of 2.75% to RM0.56. title: Chinese Stocks Open Lower As Market Awaits Policy Signals
body: Chinese equities opened lower on Wednesday, 4 February 2026, as investors remained cautious amid lingering concerns over economic momentum and policy signals. The benchmark Shanghai Composite Index slipped 0.08 per cent at the opening bell to 4,064.68 points, extending its subdued performance in recent sessions. Meanwhile, the Shenzhen Component Index saw steeper losses, opening 0.39 per cent lower at 14,072.41 points, weighed down by weakness in technology and growth-oriented stocks. Market participants were seen adopting a wait-and-see approach ahead of further clarity on domestic economic data and potential policy measures to support growth. Recent gains in mainland equities have also prompted some profit-taking, particularly in large-cap and high-beta names. Analysts said sentiment remains fragile, with investors closely monitoring developments in China’s property sector, consumption trends and external factors such as global interest rate expectations. Broader market direction is expected to hinge on upcoming macroeconomic indicators and any signals of additional stimulus from Beijing. title: WTI Stumbles After US$3 Slide, Yet Key Supports Keep Bulls In The Game
body: WTI crude oil staged a sharp reversal on Monday, sliding US$3.07 to close at US$62.14, but RHB Investment Bank Bhd said the broader bullish structure remains intact, prompting it to retain its long position on the commodity. RHB Research noted that prices opened higher at US$64.72 and briefly touched an intraday high of US$64.74 before sellers took control, dragging the contract down to a session low of US$61.39. The day ended near the lows, forming a long bearish candlestick that reflected growing selling pressure as the session progressed. The research house said the relative strength index has started to roll over, signalling that bullish momentum is easing. Even so, it pointed out that downside risks are still cushioned, with both the 50-day and 200-day simple moving averages continuing to provide technical support. RHB Research added that buyers may attempt to defend the US$62 level, which remains the first line of support. It maintained that the positive trading bias would stay in place unless selling pressure intensifies and forces a decisive break below US$58. Traders were advised to stay with the long position initiated at US$62.02, or from the close on Jan 14, with a stop-loss maintained at US$58 to manage risk. On the upside, RHB Research identified US$65 as the first resistance level, followed by a higher hurdle at US$68 should prices regain upward momentum. title: Wall Street Rallies As Investors Shrug Off Precious Metals Rout
body: Wall Street closed higher on Monday as investors brushed aside last week’s historic selloff in precious metals, taking comfort from strong US and global manufacturing data, solid corporate earnings and easing geopolitical tensions. US equities ended the session in the green, even as gold and silver extended their sharp declines. According to Reuters , the resilience in stocks came as investors focused on upbeat economic signals rather than volatility in hard assets. Manufacturing data was a key driver of sentiment. The US Institute for Supply Management’s manufacturing PMI jumped to 52.6 in January, marking the strongest growth in nearly four years and beating expectations from all economists surveyed by Reuters. The data reinforced the narrative of solid US economic momentum, with the Atlanta Fed’s GDPNow model estimating first-quarter growth at an annualised 4.2%. Sector-wise, US industrials, financials and consumer staples rose more than 1%, while energy stocks fell 2% amid a sharp drop in oil prices. Utilities declined 1.5% and consumer discretionary stocks eased 1%. In other markets, the US dollar strengthened by 0.7%, rising most against the Norwegian crown and Swiss franc as safe-haven demand eased. Treasury yields climbed by about four basis points across the curve, with the 2-year and 10-year spread briefly reaching its steepest level since April last year. Commodities remained under pressure, with gold sliding another 4% and silver falling 6%, extending Friday’s historic losses. Oil prices dropped 4.5%, while copper declined 1.5%. Despite the turbulence in metals and commodities, Wall Street’s ability to absorb the shock underscored investor confidence in the broader economic outlook, supported by firm data and improving global trade sentiment following a US-India trade agreement. title: Nintendo Holds Profit Outlook As Switch 2 Sales Momentum Faces Scrutiny
body: Japan’s Nintendo said on Tuesday it is maintaining its annual operating profit forecast of 370 billion yen, nearly a one-third increase from the previous financial year, as the gaming giant weighs strong early demand for its new console against mounting industry challenges. The Kyoto-based company also kept its full-year sales target for the Switch 2 unchanged at nineteen million units. The device, which was launched in mid-2025, has seen robust initial uptake, although investors remain divided over whether that momentum can be sustained beyond the launch window. Nintendo’s latest console follows the hugely successful original Switch, but the group has had to contend with global supply chain disruptions linked to US President Donald Trump’s trade war. Hardware makers more broadly are also grappling with sharply higher memory chip prices, driven by booming investment in artificial intelligence. Despite these pressures, analysts see Nintendo as relatively well insulated. Jefferies analyst Atul Goyal said the company’s “sizable inventories and long-term contracts will shield it for … several quarters,” pointing to its stronger position compared with peers. Pricing has also drawn attention. The Switch 2 retails at US$449.99 in the United States, significantly higher than the Japan-only version priced at 49,980 yen. The premium is widely seen as reflecting inflationary conditions overseas. Still, Serkan Toto, founder of Kantan Games, said, “It would be harder for Nintendo to raise prices than Sony as the Switch 2 is not a high-end product.” Goldman Sachs analyst Minami Munakata added that Nintendo’s long-standing policy of not selling hardware at a loss means “concerns about the Nintendo Switch 2 becoming unprofitable are overdone.” Some investors have also expressed concern over the current pipeline of blockbuster titles, particularly the absence of a new release from “The Legend of Zelda” franchise. Upcoming launches include “Mario Tennis Fever,” which is set to hit shelves next week. title: Nikkei Hits Biggest Intraday Gain Since Mid-January On Earnings Boost
body: Japan’s Nikkei 225 surged as much as 3.1% on Tuesday, driven by strong earnings from banks and tech firms and a revival in investor risk appetite after gold prices paused their decline. The broader Topix index climbed up to 2.5%, marking the largest intraday gains for both benchmarks since Jan 13. Mizuho Financial Group was among the top performers, rising as much as 5.6% after reporting quarterly profits above expectations and announcing an additional share buyback. Other lenders, including Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group, also recorded strong gains. Technology companies such as TDK Corp and Kyocera Corp boosted the blue-chip Nikkei further after posting robust earnings, while AI-related shares like Ibiden and Fujikura climbed, supported by overnight gains in US peers such as Intel and Texas Instruments. Investors are “turning more risk-on, with precious metals stabilising and the market liking the manufacturing data” from the US, wrote Andrew Jackson, Japan equity strategist at Ortus Advisors. US manufacturing activity unexpectedly expanded in January at its fastest pace since 2022, supported by solid growth in new orders and production. Jackson added that the “medley of upside” from strong US tech shares on Monday also provided a tailwind for Japanese equities on Tuesday. Hideyuki Ishiguro, chief strategist at Nomura Asset Management, noted that the dip in Japanese equities on Monday likely prompted some technical buying, saying, “The major indexes had reached attractive valuations by the previous day, making them ripe for a technical rebound.” Growing expectations of a landslide victory for Japan’s ruling party in the lower house election on Feb 8 also helped underpin the market. The rally reflects a combination of strong corporate earnings, stabilising global markets and supportive domestic political sentiment. title: KLCCP Stapled Potential Earnings Upside From Ombak Opening
body: MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB Research) maintained a NEUTRAL call on KLCCP Stapled Group Bhd with an unchanged target price of RM8.80, signalling a stable long-term outlook. The research house noted that while the retail segment remains solid, overall upside is limited, reflecting steady contributions from both retail and office divisions. KLCCP Stapled posted higher core net income of RM820.7 million in FY25, a 4.9% year-on-year increase, largely driven by the retail division. Profit before tax from the retail segment rose 2.77% amid low single-digit positive rental reversion, considered decent given the high base rental rate of Suria KLCC. Retail occupancy remained healthy at 98%, with footfall up 9%, benefiting from the mall’s strategic location in a prime tourist hotspot. Tenant sales, however, fell 8% as they normalised from the high base in FY24. MBSB Research highlighted that Visit Malaysia 2026 is expected to provide some support to tenant sales in FY26, although the impact is likely marginal, as 98% of leases are on fixed rent with only 2% tied to variable rent. The hotel division delivered improved results in FY25, with profit before tax up 12.3%, mainly supported by completed ballroom upgrades. Management expects FY26 performance to remain largely flat, despite potential catalysts from Visit Malaysia 2026, as apartment refurbishments are planned. Occupancy at Mandarin Oriental is expected to hold steady at around 60%, with enhanced product offerings projected to support growth in FY27. Incremental earnings from the management services division contributed positively, with a 7.6% increase in profit before tax driven by additional retail facilities management and new parking bays. The group also provides facilities management for Ombak KLCC, a new six-floor lifestyle mall near Suria KLCC, scheduled to open in 2026. The research house expects income from this operation to increase upon the mall’s launch. MBSB Research maintained its earnings forecasts for FY26 through FY28, citing stable contributions from the retail and office segments and retaining its Neutral rating on KLCCP Stapled Group due to limited near-term upside. As of 10.26 am, the stock price for KLCCP increased 0.32% to RM9.30. title: HSIF Sees Profit-Taking Yet Uptrend Remains Intact, RHB
body: Hang Seng Index Futures (HSIF) experienced a bout of profit-taking on Monday, snapping its recent rally but remaining within a broader bullish technical structure, according to RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research). RHB Research said the HSIF fell 715 points to close at 26,785 points after opening higher at 27,499 points and briefly touching an intraday high of 27,615 points. Selling pressure later emerged, dragging the index to a session low of 26,543 points before it ended the day with a bearish candlestick, signalling a mild corrective phase following recent gains. During the evening session, the HSIF recovered slightly, adding 168 points to last trade at 26,953 points. Despite the pullback, RHB Research said the overall bullish trend remains intact, noting that the HSIF continues to trade above its 50-day simple moving average, which is still sloping upwards and acting as dynamic support. As long as the index holds above the key 26,400-point level, bullish control of the prevailing uptrend is expected to persist. The research house added that if the consolidation phase continues, the HSIF may attempt to rebound near the 50-day SMA line. A move back above the 20-day SMA would likely signal a resumption of upside momentum, in line with the existing positive technical structure. RHB Research reiterated its recommendation for traders to maintain long positions initiated at 21,416 points or at the close on Apr 14, 2025. To manage downside risk, the stop-loss level has been revised higher to 26,400 points. On the technical levels, immediate support is seen at 26,400 points, followed by the next support at 25,500 points. On the upside, resistance is now pegged at 28,600 points, with a subsequent hurdle at 29,100 points. title: Gold, Silver Bounce Back After Sharp Sell-Off
body: Gold prices in Malaysia surged on Tuesday, marking one of the most significant daily gains in years. Spot gold rose sharply to RM622,864 per kilogram, up 12.6% from the previous session, while silver jumped 12.5% to RM37.86 per gram, according to GoldPrice.org. The rally comes after the global precious metals market staged a dramatic recovery following steep losses earlier this month. Analysts attributed the rebound to technical corrections and renewed investor appetite for safe-haven assets amid recent market volatility. On the international front, spot gold climbed 5.8% to US$4,935.56 an ounce by 0818 GMT, recovering from a low of US$4,403.24 on Monday, according to Reuters . US gold futures for April delivery also jumped 6.6% to US$4,958.50 per ounce. Silver gained 10% to US$87.40 an ounce, bouncing back from record losses of up to 27% in a single day last week. Kyle Rodda, senior market analyst at Capital.com, said, “It’s a reasonable call that this is somewhere around fair value potentially, if you consider that we saw a market behaving fairly irrationally for a few weeks there. The current prices take gold and silver back to where they were, early in the second half of January.” Despite the recent surge, RHB Investment Bank Bhd warned that the technical outlook for COMEX gold remains cautious. The report noted that gold had breached support levels at US$4,800, closing at US$4,652.60 on Monday, giving bears the upper hand. The report highlighted immediate support at US$4,550 and resistance at US$5,050, signalling potential further corrections if the market fails to sustain the rebound. In Malaysia, gold prices have shown robust year-on-year gains. Over the past year, the price of gold per kilogram has climbed 44.6%, while silver has risen 111.8%. Longer-term trends also reflect sustained growth, with gold up 151% over five years and 759% over two decades. The recent surge follows heightened market attention on global economic developments, US Federal Reserve policies and investor rotation into safe-haven assets amid geopolitical uncertainties. Analysts expect the bullish momentum for precious metals to continue, potentially reaching fresh record highs later this year. title: Gold Plunges After Biggest Drop In Decades As Rally Unwinds
body: Gold fell, following its biggest plunge in more than a decade, and silver whipsawed in choppy trading after a dramatic pullback from record highs. Spot gold fell as much as 6.3% on Monday. Silver swung sharply, dropping to around $75 an ounce having earlier climbed as much as 3.2%. The white metal recorded its biggest ever intraday loss in the previous session. “This isn’t over,” said Robert Gottlieb, a former precious metals trader at JPMorgan Chase & Co. and now an independent market commentator, adding that a reluctance to take further risk would constrain market liquidity. “We’ve got to see if it’s going to find support. The bottom line is that the trade was way too crowded.”Over the last year, precious metals have risen to all-time highs that have shocked even seasoned traders. The rally accelerated sharply in January, as investors piled into gold and silver on renewed concerns about geopolitical upheaval, currency debasement and the independence of the Federal Reserve. A wave of buying from Chinese speculators added froth to the rally. The trigger for Friday’s dramatic selloff was the news that US President Donald Trump would nominate Kevin Warsh to lead the Fed, which sent the dollar higher and undercut sentiment among investors who had bet on Trump’s willingness to let the currency weaken. Traders regard Warsh as the toughest inflation fighter among the final candidates, raising expectations of monetary policy that would underpin the dollar and weaken greenback-priced bullion. title: Chinese Yuan Fixed Lower At 6.96 Against Dollar
body: China on Monday set the central parity rates of the renminbi (yuan) against 25 major currencies, according to an announcement by the China Foreign Exchange Trade System (CFETS), as the country continues to manage the currency within its daily trading band. The central parity rate of the yuan against the U.S. dollar was fixed at 6.9695 per dollar, weaker than recent levels, reflecting market pricing ahead of the opening of the interbank foreign exchange market. Under China’s managed floating exchange rate system, the yuan is allowed to trade within a specified range around the daily midpoint. Against other major currencies, the yuan was set at 8.2651 per euro, 4.4926 per 100 Japanese yen and 8.9249 per 100 Hong Kong dollars. The parity rate against the British pound stood at 9.5385 per pound, while the Australian and New Zealand dollars were fixed at 4.8430 and 4.1916 respectively. In Asia-Pacific currencies, the yuan was set at 5.4759 per 100 Singapore dollars, 4.5257 per Thai baht and 5.6557 per Malaysian ringgit. The central parity rate against the South Korean won was fixed at 20,804 won per 100 yuan. For other global currencies, the yuan was pegged at 9.0099 per Swiss franc, 5.1098 per Canadian dollar, 10.9237 per Russian ruble, 2.3227 per South African rand and 6.2380 per Turkish lira. The currency was also set at 4,608.01 per 100 Hungarian forint, 50.968 per Polish zloty, 90.35 per Danish krone, 127.84 per Swedish krona and 138.36 per Norwegian krone. In the Middle East, the central parity rates were fixed at 5.2681 per UAE dirham and 5.3803 per Saudi riyal. CFETS said the central parity rate of the yuan against the U.S. dollar is calculated based on a weighted average of prices offered by market makers before the opening of the interbank market each business day. The rate against the Hong Kong dollar is derived from the yuan–U.S. dollar midpoint and the prevailing Hong Kong dollar–U.S. dollar exchange rate at 9 a.m. in international foreign exchange markets. Similarly, the yuan’s parity rate against the Macao pataca is determined using the yuan–Hong Kong dollar central parity rate and the pataca–Hong Kong dollar exchange rate at the same reference time. The parity rates against the remaining 22 currencies are set based on average prices quoted by market makers prior to the opening of the interbank foreign exchange market. China operates a managed floating exchange rate regime, allowing the yuan to fluctuate within a prescribed band around the daily midpoint, with the central bank aiming to maintain currency stability while reflecting market supply and demand conditions. title: Bitcoin Hovers Near US$77,000 As Sell-Off May Not Be Over
body: Bitcoin hovered near $76,000 per token on Sunday, with some strategists cautioning that its recent sell-off may not be over as investors seem reluctant to buy the dip, according to a news report by Yahoo Finance. The world’s largest cryptocurrency dropped sharply over the weekend to reach its lowest level since last April, and notch its fourth straight month of losses. The move lower coincided with President Trump’s announcement on Friday selecting Kevin Warsh to lead the Federal Reserve when Jerome Powell’s term ends in May, a nominee markets view as hawkish. Ether and other digital tokens also slid alongside gold, silver and other metals which crashed on Friday, with losses extending on Sunday evening. With bitcoin now nearing a $73,000 support level, “current flows suggest sentiment has shifted meaningfully,” said a 10X Research note on Sunday night. The firm’s strategists pointed to flow and positioning data, which indicates “investors are not yet positioned to buy the dip.” “While sentiment and technical indicators are approaching extreme levels, the broader downtrend remains intact,” wrote the researchers. “In the absence of a clear catalyst, there is little urgency to step in.”The firm noted traders remain focused on deleveraging and position unwinds rather than on preparing for a typical snapback rally. Pressure on digital assets reflects broader fragility across the crypto market. Aside from a brief bounce last month, bitcoin has struggled since October, when whale selling and forced liquidations swept through the industry. Bitcoin is down more than 12% year to date after a disappointing 2025, while ether has also plunged 23% since the start of the year. Altogether, cryptocurrencies have lost roughly $1.7 trillion in market value, or about 39% from last year’s peak, according to 10X Research. title: Gold, Silver Tumble As Investors Soothed By Trump’s Fed Pick
body: Gold and silver prices dived on Fridayv (Jan 30) and European stock markets ended the week up while Wall Street pulled back with investors reassured by US President Donald Trump’s pick to take over as head of the Federal Reserve. The precious metals, viewed as safe-haven investments, had already begun sliding on reports, later confirmed, that Trump had nominated former Fed official Kevin Warsh to replace Jerome Powell as chair of the US central bank. Trump announced his choice on Friday on social media, saying that Warsh, a former Morgan Stanley investment banker and Fed governor, “will go down as one of the GREAT Fed Chairmen, maybe the best”. Kathleen Brooks, research director at XTB trading group, said the “interesting pick … may give the market some hope that Fed independence will be preserved”.Trump’s personal attacks on Fed boss Jerome Powell – set to depart in May – have fuelled widespread fears among investors that the central bank’s policy independence is under threat, potentially posing an inflation risk to the US economy.Precious metals prices tumbled on Friday after surging in recent days when investors sought a safe haven over doubts about Trump’s policies. Gold fell as much as 12 per cent at one point, retreating below US$5,000 an ounce after hitting a record high near US$5,600 on Thursday. Silver, which on Thursday reached an all-time peak above $120 an ounce, shed around 30 per cent to about $82 an ounce. Financial markets have endured a roller-coaster ride this week as traders weathered a weaker dollar, Trump’s threats against Tehran, the president’s resumption of tariff threats and a possible US government shutdown.Asian stock markets closed out the week with some hefty losses following Thursday’s tech-led retreat on Wall Street on renewed concerns over vast investments in artificial intelligence. Healthy earnings from Meta, Samsung and SK Hynix provided much cheer early in the week, but Microsoft was punished over worries its costly AI program might not result in financial gains. There are fears that firms’ valuations may be a little too stretched and that markets could be in a bubble, having soared in recent years to record highs on the back of a tech-fuelled rally. The dollar pushed higher on Warsh’s nomination. “Most currency strategists would argue that his nomination may be good news for the dollar, which can price out some risks of a more dovish pick,” said Forex.com’s Fawad Razaqzada. “However, for as long as policy uncertainty hangs over the US economy with Trump’s tariff theatrics, the dollar debasement narrative is likely to hold back the greenback from making a meaningful comeback.”Among individual companies, Verizon surged 11.8 per cent as it reported its highest quarter of mobility and broadband subscription increases since 2019. title: Stocks Edge Higher As Trump Picks Kevin Marsh As Next Fed Chair
body: Global stocks edged higher on Friday, while the dollar rose and gold plunged after U.S. President Donald Trump nominatedKevin Warsh as his pick for the next Federal Reserve Chair. Warsh, a former Fed governor, is seen as an advocate of lower interest rates, but he is also considered to be one of the less radical choices among the various names that had been raised and is perhaps more cautious on heavy monetary stimulus than others.The MSCI world index was last 0.16 per cent higher as European shares rose, shrugging off a decline across Asia-Pacific stocks. The pan-European STOXX 600 was last 0.72 per cent higher, holding onto earlier gains after Trump’s announcement, and was on track to end January up more than 3 per cent.S&P 500 e-mini futures fell 0.3 per cent while Nasdaq e-mini futures were off 0.4 per cent, paring back some earlier declines. Precious metals had plunged after speculation about Warsh becoming the next Fed chair spread, with the selloff continuing following Trump’s announcement. Gold, which tends to benefit when the dollar falls, dropped as much as 5 per cent in one of its biggest one-day selloffs in years. MARKETS REACT TO TRUMP PICKING WARSH Now that Trump has made his choice, investors are weighing how Warsh could lead the Fed. “We will see from here because it’s one thing to appoint somebody and it’s entirely different to actually be Chairman of the Federal Reserve,” Chris Beauchamp, chief market analyst at IG Markets, said. While Trump wants low interest rates to be the priority, “the U.S. finds itself in a very difficult position right now in terms of inflation remaining stubborn, but economic data, as we should see in payrolls beginning to show signs of weakness with the unemployment rate moving higher,” he said. While Warsh will be seen as “Trump’s man” at the central bank, he may aim to distance himself subtly once he officially assumes office, Beauchamp said.Trump announcing his pick for Fed Chair also does not necessarily mean all uncertainty will be removed, said Sandra Horsfield, economist at Investec: “We still have the question whether this will actually get through to full confirmation by the Senate anytime soon, given that there is still the stand-off between some of the members of the Senate over Fed independence questions and Powell’s subpoena.” Horsfield noted that the broader backdrop still remains volatile, not least on Iran. Brent crude was last down around 0.6 per cent at $70.31, as oil markets weighed geopolitical risks, after Trump on Thursday signed an executive order declaring a national emergency and establishing a process to impose tariffs on goods from countries that sell or provide oil to Cuba. Also on Thursday, Trump said he was planning to talk to Iran amid rising tensions. DOLLAR RETREATS FROM HIGHS The U.S. dollar index, which measures its strength against a basket of six currencies, was last up 0.21 per cent at 96.38, slightly weaker than before Trump’s announcement.The yield on the U.S. 10-year Treasury bond was last up 1.8 basis points at 4.249 per cent, having traded at a session high of 4.279 per cent earlier on. Fed funds futures are pricing an implied 84.6 per cent probability that the U.S. central bank will hold steady on rates at its next meeting in March, slightly lower than the previous day’s 87.5 per cent chance, according to the CME Group’s FedWatch tool. A faltering rebound for precious metals fell short after a choppy session on Thursday. Gold fell around 5 per cent to $5,129.39 an ounce, while silver plunged 11 per cent to $103. title: Oil Heads For Rare Monthly Surge As Geopolitics Stoke Supply Fears
body: Oil prices are on track for their biggest monthly gains in years as escalating tensions in the Middle East, particularly over a possible US strike on Iran, fuel fears of supply disruptions from a key OPEC producer, Reuters reported. Brent crude futures hovered around US$70.50 a barrel after jumping 3.4% the previous session to their highest level since July 31. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) was near US$65.03 after also advancing sharply. Both benchmarks are poised to post their first monthly gains in six months, with Brent up more than 16% in January and WTI rising over 14%, driven by geopolitical risk premiums. Markets have been jittery amid reports of an expanded US military presence in the region and President Donald Trump’s warnings to Iran over its nuclear programme, raising the spectre of supply shocks if conflict disrupts exports or key transit routes like the Strait of Hormuz. Supply-side concerns are compounded by weather‑related export issues in Russia and production cuts in Venezuela, adding to an already tight market backdrop and underpinning crude’s rally. The strong monthly performance marks a striking rebound for oil after a period of sluggish trading, highlighting how quickly risk sentiment can shift on geopolitical developments and the potential impact on global energy markets. Broader gauges also moved higher, with the FBM 70 increasing 70.79 points to 17,538.22, FBM EMAS jumped 68.37 points to 12,759.87 and F4GBM gained 5.85 points to 1,027.91. Buying interest broadened across the market, lifting sentiment after recent jitters over potential index-related outflows. Market breadth tilted positive, with gainers edging losers 190 to 168, while 303 counters were unchanged. Trading activity was moderate, with 171.43 million shares changing hands for RM114.85 million. A total of 2,029 counters were untraded and 61 suspended. Among heavyweights, Maybank rose 10 sen to RM11.74, Public Bank gained five sen to RM4.90, TNB slipped four sen to RM13.96, while IHH Healthcare was flat at RM8.86. On the most active list, Dagang NeXchange Bhd fell 1.5 sen to 30.5 sen, Pharmaniaga Bhd rose half-a-sen to 29 sen, SP Setia Bhd climbed 3.5 sen to RM1.01 and Capital A Bhd was flat at 63.5 sen. Top gainers included Hong Leong Bank Bhd, up 38 sen to RM24.70; LPI Capital Bhd gained 22 sen to RM15.30; CIMB Group Holdings Bhd increased 12 sen to RM8.59; Hong Leong Financial Group Bhd improved by eight sen to RM21.78 and Hong Leong Industries Bhd up 10 sen to RM16.98. Leading decliners were Allianz Malaysia, down 32 sen to RM22.70; United Plantations Bhd dropped 18 sen to RM30.40; Bursa Malaysia Bhd eased six sen to RM8.96 and New Hoong Fatt Holdings, down five sen to RM1.56. The firmer open suggests near-term sentiment has stabilised, though investors remain cautious heading into the rest of the session. title: Bitcoin, Ethereum Slide As Risk-Off Mood Grips Crypto Markets
body: Bitcoin and Ethereum weakened on Jan 30 as selling pressure returned to the crypto market, driven by heightened volatility, liquidations and caution ahead of a major options expiry. Bitcoin fell to around US$82,500, down more than 6% from the previous session, after swinging between an intraday high near US$88,300 and a low of about US$81,200. Ethereum, meanwhile, slid more sharply, dropping over 7% to trade around US$2,730. Market participants pointed to a risk-off tone across global markets and the expiry of billions of dollars’ worth of Bitcoin and Ethereum options, which amplified short-term price swings. The sell-off triggered widespread liquidations of leveraged positions, adding to downside momentum. The weakness in the two largest cryptocurrencies dragged broader digital assets lower, underscoring fragile sentiment as traders await clearer macro and policy signals to stabilise the market. title: US Stocks Move Sideways, Shruggging Off Low-key Fed Meeting
body: Wall Street stocks finished little changed Wednesday after the Federal Reserve kept interest rates unchanged, while the dollar rebounded somewhat from the prior session’s slide. The Fed, as expected, voted to maintain rates at a range between 3.50 percent and 3.75 percent. Fed Chair Jerome Powell said the status-quo move made sense as the central bank monitors economic data after cutting three straight times due to signs of a weakening labor market. Major US indices, which were directionless before the 1900 GMT Fed announcement, moved in a choppy fashion after the decision. The S&P 500 finished nearly flat at 6,978.03 after earlier touching above 7,000 points for the first time. The market had “almost zero reaction” to the Fed, said Art Hogan of B. Riley Wealth Management “The statement and the press conference really delivered no news,” Hogan said Wednesday afternoon shortly before earnings announcements from Microsoft and other large companies. The dollar recovered some of its losses from the prior session, when comments from US President Donald Trump seeming to greet a weaker US currency, sending the dollar to a four and a half year low against the euro. But the strengthening euro was among the factors that dragged on European stocks. Also weighing on Europe was a downgrade to the German government’s 2026 growth forecast to one percent from 1.3 percent previously. “The expected stimulus from economic and fiscal policy measures did not materialize quite as quickly or to the extent that we had assumed,” Economy Minister Katherina Reiche told a Berlin press conference. The CAC 40 in Paris was dragged down by renewed concerns for the luxury sector after market heavyweight LVMH posted a 13 percent slide in annual profit. LVMH shares tumbled nearly seven percent in response, while British fashion label Burberry, traded in London, fell 4.7 percent. Elsewhere, the price of gold struck a new peak as skittishness over the dollar pushes some investors towards the metal as a safe-haven investment. US retail giant Amazon slid 0.6 percent after announcing that it is cutting 16,000 jobs worldwide as the company tries to streamline amid its major push into AI. But shares in Dutch tech giant ASML, the global leader in the machines that make semiconductors, jumped after the company announced a strong rise in annual profits and a buoyant outlook, while also saying it would cut hundreds of management jobs. title: SGX Opens Higher Amid Fed Pause Optimism
body: The Singapore Exchange (SGX) opened higher on Thursday, with the Straits Times Index (STI) rising 3.83 points, or 0.08%, to 4,913.17 as at 9.05 am. Market turnover stood at S$171.15 million on a volume of 120.3 million shares, with advancers outpacing decliners 117 to 61. Banking and technology stocks led early gains, with DBS up 0.24% to S$59.78, OCBC Bank at S$21.27, and ST Engineering trading at S$9.47. Real estate counters also saw moderate buying interest, with Hongkong Land USD at S$8.47 and Keppel at S$11.04. Shipbuilding stock YZJ Shipbuilding rose to S$3.35. The market opened cautiously higher following the Federal Reserve’s decision to hold interest rates steady at 3.50%-3.75% on Wednesday, signalling confidence in the US economy amid “diminished risks” to inflation and employment. The Fed’s pause could support regional equities by maintaining stable global liquidity and keeping borrowing costs predictable. Derivatives trading also showed moderate activity, with equity index futures volumes at 16,740 contracts. The FTSE China A50 Index futures were at 14,873, while Nikkei 225 futures traded at 53,325. FX futures indicated slight strength in the U.S. dollar, with USD/SGD futures at 1.2600 and USD/CNH at 6.9228. Other SGX benchmark indices reflected mixed early moves, with the iEdge Singapore Next 50 Index at 1,505.10 and the iEdge S-REIT Index at 1,125.12. Sustainability-focused and regional technology indices showed steady performance, highlighting investor appetite for both defensive and growth segments. Market participants are likely to track upcoming US economic data and corporate earnings in Asia for further cues, as investor sentiment remains sensitive to global rate policy and the trajectory of inflation in the coming months. title: Ringgit Opens Firmer Near Strongest Level Since 2018 After Fed Holds Rates
body: The Malaysian ringgit opened slightly stronger against the US dollar on Thursday, supported by confidence in Malaysia’s economic growth and resilient domestic fundamentals, as investors digested the Federal Reserve’s decision to keep interest rates unchanged. At 8 am, the local currency was quoted at 3.9130/9230 versus the greenback, up from Wednesday’s close of 3.9175/9235. This puts the ringgit near its strongest level against the US dollar since April 2018, when it touched 3.9030. Bank Negara Malaysia Governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour yesterday reaffirmed Malaysia’s solid economic fundamentals, highlighting the country’s diversified economy and resilient domestic demand. “No single country accounts for more than 15% of Malaysia’s exports. That shows how diversified we are,” he said. On fiscal matters, Abdul Rasheed pointed to subsidy rationalisation for fuel, electricity, water, and diesel as reflecting policy credibility. The Finance Ministry added that the shift from bulk RON95 petrol subsidies to targeted BUDI95 support is expected to generate annual savings of RM2.5 billion to RM4 billion. Sales tax on low-value goods contributed RM817 million in revenue last year, up from RM476 million in 2024. The ringgit also strengthened against a basket of major currencies and regional peers. It climbed versus the euro to 4.6870/6990 and the Japanese yen to 2.5558/5625, but eased against the British pound to 5.4097/4235. Gains were seen against regional currencies, rising to 3.1019/1103 versus the Singapore dollar, 12.5658/6097 versus the Thai baht, 233.9/234.7 versus the Indonesian rupiah, and 6.66/6.68 versus the Philippine peso. title: Hong Kong Exchange Fund Logs Recond Gains In 2025
body: Investment income of Hong Kong’s Exchange Fund in 2025 came in at a record 331 billion Hong Kong dollars (about 42 billion U.S. dollars) amid the global bull market, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) said on Wednesday. The gains included 142.2 billion Hong Kong dollars on bonds, 33.9 billion Hong Kong dollars on Hong Kong equities and 74.1 billion Hong Kong dollars on other equities. Annual investment return stood at 8 percent, according to the HKMA. Total assets of the Exchange Fund stood at around 4.15 trillion Hong Kong dollars by the end of December, up 70.4 billion Hong Kong dollars from the end of 2024. Eddie Yue, chief executive of the HKMA, said that the unprecedented gains came amid solid or even record upturns of major stock markets worldwide. Benefitting from capital inflows into the Hong Kong stock market, the Hang Seng Index rose by 28 percent in 2025. Yue acknowledged that the exceptional confluence of multiple favorable factors in the global financial markets in 2025 may not last for a long time. title: Gold Surges Past RM697,000 per Kilogram On Safe-Haven Demand
body: Gold prices in Malaysia surged sharply on Thursday, rising 4.37% to RM697.52 per gram, or RM697,522 per kilogram, reflecting a strong wave of safe-haven buying amid geopolitical tensions and economic uncertainty. Silver also advanced, gaining 3.15% to RM464.79 per kilogram. Analysts attributed the surge to global concerns over US political instability and monetary policy. “Gold prices are rising on safe-haven demand because of the strange geopolitical situation and even the political situation in the US, (which is) not looking great. There are concerns around Fed independence. And when that happens, investor trust in the financial system gets shaken up,” said ANZ analyst Soni Kumari, as cited by Reuters . Marex analyst Edward Meir added, “Growing US debt and uncertainty created by signs that the global trade system is splintering into regional blocs as opposed to a US-centric model are leading investors to pile into gold.” Gold has climbed past RM500,000 per kilogram for the first time this month and is on track for its ninth consecutive session of record-highs. RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) noted that COMEX gold gapped up to close at US$5,303.60 per ounce on Wednesday, with bullish momentum likely to test the US$5,500 resistance. “The commodity has been printing a series of higher highs with higher lows, showing that strong bullish momentum is in play,” RHB Research said, maintaining a long position while setting immediate support at US$4,800. Locally, the price of gold has jumped RM909 per gram over the past day, while monthly gains have reached RM3,225 per gram, reflecting a 18% rise over 30 days. Over the past year, Malaysian gold investors have seen gains of 69%, while silver has surged 221% in the same period, highlighting a strong shift toward precious metals amid global uncertainty. The rally has been supported by firm central bank buying, a weaker US dollar, and heightened investor demand for alternatives amid political volatility and ongoing geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. body: The decliners overwhelmingly outnumbered the gainers on Bursa Malaysia at the close on Jan 29, underscoring broad-based selling pressure across the market. title: Bursa Opens Lower As Fed Holds Rates Steady
body: Bursa Malaysia opened lower, with the FBMKLCI slipping 12.12 points, or 0.69%, to 1,744.37 as investors digested global monetary developments. The broader market followed suit, with the FBM70 and FBMEMAS declining 0.08% and 0.48% respectively in early trade. Market activity saw VELESTO leading the volume chart with 15.7 million shares traded at 30 sen, while TWL and ISF posted modest gains. Among top gainers, PANAMY rose 13 sen to RM7.39 and KSENG added 6 sen to RM5.62, while Nestlé and HEIM were notable decliners. Investors are responding to the Federal Reserve’s decision to keep interest rates unchanged in the 3.50%-3.75% range on Tuesday, following a 10-2 vote by policymakers. Fed Chair Jerome Powell said risks to inflation and employment had diminished, signalling a cautious approach to further rate cuts. The steady rate outlook has prompted a rotation in emerging markets, with local equities taking cues from global sentiment. The local market’s early session was also weighed down by losses in heavyweight counters. Maybank dropped 16 sen to RM11.64 and IHH slid 12 sen to RM8.90, reflecting profit-taking after recent gains. On the upside, investors bought selectively into mid-cap and small-cap names, with IG BREIT rising 5 sen to RM2.91 on strong trading volume. The FBMKLCI remains above the 1,740 support level despite the morning dip, supported by positive earnings reports and foreign inflows. The market is expected to remain sensitive to global interest rate signals and foreign portfolio flows, particularly as investors assess the impact of the Fed’s pause on emerging Asian assets. As of 9.14 am, total market volume stood at 120.3 million shares valued at RM171.15 million, with advancers outnumbering decliners 117 to 61. title: Asia Markets Pause As Tech Earnings Stir Caution
body: Asia’s stock markets eased on Thursday as mixed earnings from the technology sector prompted investors to take a more cautious stance ahead of Apple’s upcoming results. South Korea’s benchmark slipped 1.2%, despite a 21% gain so far this month, while the tech-heavy Taiwan market edged down 0.6%, having surged almost 14% year-to-date. Japan’s Nikkei was down 0.1%, pressured by sharp swings in the yen and rising domestic bond yields. MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan fell 0.6%. The cautious mood came even as Samsung Electronics posted a tripling of its operating profit, benefiting from surging chip prices amid the AI investment boom. On Wall Street, S&P 500 futures declined 0.2% and Nasdaq futures lost 0.1% after mixed results from major tech firms. Microsoft shares fell 6.5% in extended trading on concerns that its massive capital expenditure may not yield sufficient returns. Meanwhile, Meta raised its revenue and capex outlook for 2026, sending shares up 8% after hours and adding roughly US$140 billion to its market value. “A common theme so far from META and MSFT is the larger-than-expected capex spending, indicating the upward momentum for AI spending,” analysts at JPMorgan noted. “The difference, they added, was Meta also sharply raised its 2026 revenue outlook to well above market expectations.” Attention now turns to Apple, with JPMorgan expecting earnings to beat consensus thanks to stronger iPhone 17 demand and slower growth in expenses. The bank raised its end-2026 price target to US$315, up from US$305. Currency markets showed continued volatility, with the US dollar under pressure amid policy uncertainty and growing debt concerns. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent insisted the administration still favoured a “strong dollar” policy, even as President Trump appeared to condone a weaker currency. European officials expressed concern over the dollar’s decline, while European Central Bank officials suggested that further euro strength could justify interest rate cuts. The euro rose 0.2% to US$1.1973, while the dollar slipped 0.4% against the Swiss franc to 0.7657 and 0.3% versus the yen to 152.97. “Further dollar weakness would increase the likelihood of the ECB and other central banks cutting interest rates, as well as emerging markets repeating last year’s outperformance,” said Jack Allen-Reynolds, an economist at Capital Economics. Investor appetite for hard assets remained strong, with gold climbing 1.8% to US$5,485 an ounce for a 27% gain this month, silver and copper also advancing. Oil prices hit a four-month high, with Brent up 0.6% to US$68.80 a barrel and US crude rising 0.7% to US$63.65 per barrel, supported by concerns over potential US military action against Iran. The U.S. Federal Reserve kept interest rates on hold as expected, with Chair Jerome Powell noting a “clearly improving” economic outlook and broad support within the committee for a pause. Powell declined to comment on whether he would remain a governor after stepping down as Chair in May, amid Trump’s push for more aggressive rate cuts. title: Ringgit Opens Firmer On Dollar Weakness
body: The Malaysian ringgit opened stronger against the US dollar on Wednesday, boosted by weaker-than-expected US economic data that continued to pressure the greenback. At 8 am, the local currency was quoted at 3.9485/9500 versus the US dollar, a level not seen since May 2018, compared with Tuesday’s close of 3.9500/9555. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US Dollar Index (DXY) slid 1.32% to 95.759 points, following data that reinforced expectations of monetary easing later this year. “The US Conference Board’s Consumer Confidence Index fell more than expected to 84.5 points in January, below the consensus estimate of 90.6 points,” he said, adding that Americans have grown increasingly concerned about the rising cost of living and weaker job prospects. “This suggests consumer spending — a key pillar of the US economy — is likely to continue moderating.” Dr Mohd Afzanizam also noted that the Japanese yen had strengthened amid ongoing speculation over possible coordinated intervention by the Japanese government and the US Federal Reserve. He said the ringgit could breach the 3.95 level against the US dollar if dollar weakness persists. Against other major currencies and regional peers, the ringgit opened mixed. It eased against the British pound to 5.4592/4613 from 5.4103/4178 at Tuesday’s close, fell versus the euro to 4.7473/7491 from 4.6958/7023, and weakened against the Japanese yen to 2.5890/5902 from 2.5691/5730. The local currency was lower against the Singapore dollar at 3.1317/1332 from 3.1174/1219, slipped versus the Thai baht to 12.7639/7790 from 12.7247/7478, edged up against the Indonesian rupiah to 235.4/235.6 from 235.5/236.0, and remained flat against the Philippine peso at 6.68/6.69. title: Gold Prices Surge In Malaysia Amid Dollar Weakness And Geopolitical Concerns
body: Gold prices in Malaysia rose sharply on Wednesday, with spot gold hitting RM666.56 per gram, up RM20.55 or 3.2% from the previous day. The price per kilo climbed to RM666,558, marking a 6.7% increase, while gold per ounce reached RM20,732, per goldprice.org . The rally comes as the US dollar plunged to near four-year lows amid persistent geopolitical tensions and ahead of the Federal Reserve’s policy announcement. According to Kelvin Wong, senior market analyst at OANDA, gold’s surge is closely linked to dollar weakness, following remarks from former US President Donald Trump signalling a broad consensus for a weaker greenback. Ilya Spivak, head of global macro at Tastylive, said markets are adopting a defensive stance ahead of Fed Chair Jerome Powell’s comments. Deutsche Bank has projected gold could climb to US$6,000 per ounce in 2026, citing strong investment demand from central banks and investors seeking non-dollar and tangible assets. RHB Research noted that COMEX gold maintained bullish momentum, with resistance near US$5,200 and potential to move toward US$5,500 upon a breakout. Analysts recommended retaining long positions with support at US$4,800 and US$4,550, underscoring ongoing positive market sentiment. Silver and other precious metals also recorded gains, with silver up 6.9% to RM29.18 per kg, platinum rising 1.7% to US$2,686.50 per ounce and palladium increasing 1.3% to US$1,959.43. Analysts attribute the momentum to continued demand for hedging amid currency volatility and inflation concerns. The recent rally reinforces Malaysia’s growing interest in gold as both an investment and a hedge against currency fluctuations, with prices up more than 13.5% over the past month and over 66% year-on-year. title: Global Stocks Touch Fresh Records As Dollar Slides Ahead Of Fed
body: Global equity markets extended their rally on Tuesday, with stocks climbing for a fifth straight session and touching record levels, as investors turned increasingly optimistic over US corporate earnings. At the same time, the US dollar weakened sharply, sinking to its lowest point in nearly four years ahead of the Federal Reserve’s policy announcement. On Wall Street, trading was mixed but largely positive. The S&P 500 closed at a record high, while the Nasdaq Composite also advanced, supported by strong earnings sentiment. The Dow Jones Industrial Average, however, ended lower after being dragged down by sharp declines in select heavyweights. The Dow fell 408.99 points or 0.83% to 49,003.41. In contrast, the S&P 500 rose 28.37 points or 0.41% to 6,978.60, while the Nasdaq gained 215.74 points or 0.91% to 23,817.10. Losses in Boeing and UnitedHealth weighed heavily on the Dow. Boeing slid 1.6%, while UnitedHealth plunged about 20% after warning that its 2026 revenue would shrink. The decline in UnitedHealth alone accounted for roughly 420 points of downward pressure on the index. Health insurers broadly came under pressure following a lower-than-expected Medicare reimbursement proposal for 2027. Meanwhile, investors continued to assess a wave of major earnings releases, including results from Boeing and United Parcel Service, which said it would cut up to 30,000 operational roles this year. Attention is now turning to upcoming earnings from the so-called Magnificent Seven, including Microsoft, Apple, Tesla and Meta Platforms. Beyond the US, global markets also pushed higher. MSCI’s gauge of stocks worldwide rose 0.85% to 1,053.09, marking its longest winning streak this year. The index hit an intraday record of 1,053.88. In Europe, the STOXX 600 ended up 0.58%, supported by a 1.8% jump in banking stocks. Currency markets were dominated by a sharp slide in the greenback. The dollar index fell 0.9% to 96.23, after touching a four-year low of 95.566, putting it on track for its biggest daily percentage drop since April. The euro strengthened 0.81% to US$1.1975, while sterling climbed 1.14% to US$1.3833. “The dollar has had over the past ten days one of the biggest moves it’s had in the past five years… It puts a huge pressure on commodities, and we’re seeing oil up. We’re seeing commodities up, and you’re seeing all those stocks moving up in a very aggressive way,” said Adam Rich, deputy chief investment officer and portfolio manager at Vaughan Nelson Investment Management in Houston. The dollar also weakened against the Japanese yen, sliding 1.23% to 152.26, its lowest level since late October. The Korean won strengthened 0.97% to 1,431.85 per dollar after earlier losses, as South Korea sought to reassure the US over its commitment to a trade deal following fresh tariff threats from President Donald Trump. Markets are now bracing for the Federal Reserve’s policy statement, due on Wednesday. While the central bank is widely expected to keep interest rates unchanged, political developments surrounding the Fed leadership have added an extra layer of uncertainty. Commodities rallied strongly amid the weaker dollar and ongoing geopolitical concerns. Spot gold surged 3.19% to US$5,174.09 an ounce after hitting a record intraday high, while spot silver jumped 7.93% to US$121.13 an ounce. U.S. crude oil settled up 2.9% at US$62.39 a barrel, while Brent crude gained 3.02% to US$67.57 per barrel, as a winter storm disrupted production and halted US Gulf Coast crude exports over the weekend. In China’s spot foreign exchange market, the yuan is allowed to rise or fall by 2 percent from the central parity rate each trading day. The central parity rate of the yuan against the U.S. dollar is based on a weighted average of prices offered by market makers before the opening of the interbank market each business day. title: Wall Street Extends Gains Ahead Of Mega-Cap Earnings, Fed Meeting
body: Wall Street edged higher on Monday, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq logging their fourth consecutive session of gains as investors prepared for a wave of mega-cap earnings and a Federal Reserve policy update later this week. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 313.69 points, or 0.64%, to 49,412.40, while the S&P 500 gained 34.62 points, or 0.50%, to 6,950.23. The Nasdaq Composite added 100.11 points, or 0.43%, to 23,601.36. Both indexes hit their highest levels in over a week, marking their longest string of advances since December. Big tech led the rally, with Apple, Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta and Broadcom providing the largest boosts to the S&P 500. Investors are closely watching these names for signs of measurable returns on AI spending, with upcoming quarterly results seen as a key test for the tech-driven rally. “Communications and technology are trading well in advance of earnings from many large companies,” said Chris Zaccarelli, chief investment officer at Northlight Asset Management. “There’s cautious optimism ahead of earnings season.” Meanwhile, individual sectors showed mixed performance. Communications services surged 1.3% to lead S&P 500 sectors, while consumer discretionary declined 0.7%, dragged down by Tesla, which fell 3%. The materials sector rose 0.3% amid gold prices topping $5,000 an ounce, boosting miners including Newmont Corp. Shares of USA Rare Earth jumped 7.9% after reports that the U.S. government would acquire a 10% stake in the miner through a $1.6 billion debt-and-equity package. CoreWeave rose 5.7% following a $2 billion investment announcement from Nvidia. Conversely, Intel fell 5.7% after forecasting quarterly results below expectations, and prison operators GEO Group and CoreCivic tumbled on political backlash over ICE funding. Investors are also eyeing the Fed’s two-day meeting, where a hold on interest rates is widely expected, though market participants are looking for guidance on the central bank’s future rate path. Advancing issues outnumbered decliners on the NYSE and Nasdaq, with trading volumes slightly above the 20-day averages. title: Tech Sector Unlikely Impacted By Stronger Ringgit
body: The technology sector is expected to see moderate growth in 2026, with Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) maintaining a NEUTRAL call on the KLTEC index while highlighting ITMAX, UWC, and Frontken as top sector picks. The research house noted, from a recent field trip to 12 Penang-based companies, that management teams are broadly optimistic for 2026, with on-the-ground activity indicating that China+1 diversification is more advanced than previously anticipated. Positive feedback from global semiconductor players, including Intel, AMD, Lam Research, Infineon, SanDisk and Micron, points to rising engagement and capacity allocation in Malaysia, reinforcing its role as a strategic production and R&D hub. The field trip also indicated that US semiconductor tariffs are no longer a major concern following the deferment of China-related Section 301 tariffs to June 2027. Apple’s accelerated shift of iPhone production to India is creating tangible opportunities for Malaysian suppliers, with companies such as ViTrox already deriving around 5–7% of sales from India. Expansion by other multinational corporations is expected to support further growth for Malaysian EMS, OSAT, and equipment suppliers, while a robust pipeline of tech-related IPOs, including SkyeChip and NSW Automation, could add capital and expansion momentum in 2026 and beyond. Despite concerns over the strong ringgit, HLIB noted that historical data show only a weak negative correlation between the KLTEC index and RM/USD, with sector performance driven more by global semiconductor cycles and US Federal Reserve policies. The upcoming 4Q25 earnings season is expected to reflect a reasonable bar for large-cap companies, with investor attention likely focused on management guidance for 2026 and margin expectations. HLIB highlighted that stock selection remains critical, as stronger ringgit pressures could widen the gap between outperformers and laggards, making a selective approach essential in the current environment. title: Ringgit Opens Steady At 3.96 Against US Dollar As US-Japan Intervention Talks Intensify

title: Malaysia Gold Prices Slide Despite Global Rally
body: Gold prices in Malaysia eased slightly, with the price per kilogram falling 3.03% to RM14,279.84, or RM646.87 per gram, as of early New York trading hours. The decline marks a small retracement from recent gains amid heightened safe-haven demand globally. Silver prices in Malaysia also softened, down 3% to RM646.87 per kilogram, after surging in previous sessions to near record highs. Globally, gold hit an all-time high of US$5,110.50 per ounce on Monday, driven by geopolitical uncertainty and safe-haven demand. Silver surged 8% to US$117.69 per ounce, marking a rise of more than 50% so far this year. Analysts attributed the rally to escalating trade tensions, including US threats of higher tariffs on Canada and South Korea, and concerns over a possible US government shutdown. RHB Investment Bank said COMEX gold showed strong bullish momentum after breaching the US$5,000 resistance for the first time, with analysts maintaining a positive outlook. “After the breakout, the bulls will eye to test the US$5,200 mark, followed by the US$5,500 threshold,” RHB noted. In Malaysia, gold has seen strong gains over the past year, rising 66.3% over the last 12 months and up 171% over five years, reflecting the metal’s role as a hedge against global uncertainty and currency fluctuations.
