title: Dollar Faces Pressure As Trump Policies And Geopolitical Risks Shake Investor Confidence
body: The US dollar is under renewed pressure in early 2026 as investors reassess the impact of President Donald Trump’s policies and escalating geopolitical tensions. On Monday, the dollar was set for its largest three-day slide against a basket of major currencies since April 2025, reflecting growing market uncertainty. Trump’s aggressive trade stance, challenges to Federal Reserve independence and significant increases in public spending have all contributed to the greenback’s volatility. So far this year, the dollar has lagged behind major rivals such as the euro, sterling and Swiss franc. “There are a number of factors coming together and faster than expected,” said Seema Shah, chief global strategist at Principal Asset Management. Market attention has been drawn to Trump’s threats on Greenland, European tariffs and trade tensions with Canada, alongside domestic issues including immigration crackdowns and the risk of a government shutdown. Investors are also factoring in anticipated Federal Reserve rate cuts, which make US assets less attractive relative to other markets. Powell’s planned departure in May has further fueled speculation about his successor, with BlackRock’s Rick Rieder, a proponent of lower rates, now viewed as a frontrunner. Meanwhile, global equities have outperformed US markets over the past year, with the S&P 500 rising around 15% since Trump’s inauguration compared with gains of 95% in Seoul’s Kospi, 40% in Tokyo’s Nikkei and nearly 30% in Shanghai’s main index. “The trend is clear. Asset managers are keen to diversify away from the US,” said Chris Scicluna, economist at Daiwa Capital Markets. Chris added, “Many had been overweight US markets and are now rebalancing.” The dollar’s slide underscores mounting investor caution amid policy uncertainty and geopolitical risks, prompting a search for alternative safe havens such as gold and Japanese government bonds. title: Asian Stocks Track Wall St Gains, Seoul Brushes Off Tariff Threat
body: Asian markets rose Tuesday following gains on Wall Street, with tech firms leading Seoul to another record as investors brushed off Donald Trump’s threat to hike tariffs on South Korean goods. The yen held its gains after a two-day surge stoked by intervention talk, while geopolitical and economic uncertainty saw silver hit another fresh peak and gold hover just below its own high. Traders are also gearing up for a Federal Reserve policy meeting and earnings from tech titans, which will be pored over for an idea about sustainability of the AI investment surge. Equities enjoyed healthy buying despite the US president reverting to tariff threats, warning South Korea he would impose 25 percent tolls on goods including autos for falling short of expectations on an earlier pact struck with Washington. The announcement comes months after the two sides struck a trade and security deal following tense negotiations, setting levies at 15 percent. “South Korea’s Legislature is not living up to its Deal with the United States,” Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform. He added that he was increasing tariff rates “because the Korean Legislature hasn’t enacted our Historic Trade Agreement, which is their prerogative.” The presidential office in Seoul said it had not been informed in advance but added that Trade Minister Kim Jung-kwan, currently in Canada, would head to Washington for talks with US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick. Trump’s outburst follows a warning to Canada on Saturday that it faced 100 percent levies if it signed a trade deal with China, days after backing down from a threat to hit several European countries with measures over their opposition to his grab for Greenland. Still, Seoul’s Kospi continued its run to fresh record highs, with observers pointing to the US president’s history of rowing back the worst of his threats. While carmakers slipped, tech firms ploughed higher with chipmaking giant SK hynix up more than five percent and Samsung Electronics up two percent. There were also big gains in Hong Kong, Shanghai, Sydney, Singapore, Taipei, Manila and Jakarta. Tech firms are enjoying a fresh boost ahead of earnings releases as traders continue to pile into all things AI. Magnificent Seven members Apple, Microsoft, Meta and Tesla are due this week, with other bellwethers including Texas Instruments, Boeing and Mastercard providing an idea about the state of the economy. However, with questions being asked about the amount of cash being invested in artificial intelligence, there is a little nervousness on trading floors about when profits will be realised. “The AI capex cycle is increasingly colliding with the real world: debt markets, power grids, and regulation,” wrote Matt Weller, head of market research at City Index. He added that “2026 capex estimates for the largest ‘hyperscalers’ is widely forecast to hit the $600 bn+ range, driven primarily by AI infrastructure. At the same time, major tech firms have leaned more heavily into debt issuance to fund the infrastructure race”. “This matters for earnings because the market’s attention is moving from ‘who spends the most’ to ‘who can sustain the spend without eroding free cash flow’, especially if AI monetisation takes longer than expected.” Developments in Washington are also being followed after some senators warned they would vote against upcoming spending bills following the second killing of a US citizen in Minneapolis, threatening another possible government shutdown. The dollar remained under pressure after its latest selloff sparked by talk of a joint intervention between US and Japanese authorities to support the yen. And in corporate news, Hong Kong-listed shares in China’s Zijin Gold International rose more than one percent after it agreed to buy Allied Gold, which owns gold mines in Africa, for US$4 billion. Its parent, Zijin Mining Group, soared more than six percent. Zijin Gold’s shares have tripled since listing in September. title: Weakening Dollar Lifts Chinese Currency
body: The central parity rate of the Chinese currency renminbi, or the yuan, strengthened 86 pips to 6.9843 against the U.S. dollar Monday, according to the China Foreign Exchange Trade System. In China’s spot foreign exchange market, the yuan is allowed to rise or fall by 2 percent from the central parity rate each trading day. The central parity rate of the yuan against the U.S. dollar is based on a weighted average of prices offered by market makers before the opening of the interbank market each business day. The rise of regional currency, including the ringgit, has been attributed to the weakening dollar. title: SGX Opens Lower Amid MAS Policy Outlook, Semiconductor-Led Growth
body: Singapore’s stock market opened lower on Monday as investors weighed robust economic growth against the prospect of the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) maintaining current monetary policy settings later this week. At 9.06 am, the Straits Times Index (STI) stood at 4,879.25 points, down 12.20 points or 0.25% from Friday’s close, with 112 stocks advancing and 76 declining on a total volume of 153.81 million shares worth S$171.96 million. Bank counters led the early weakness, with UOB down 2.66% to S$38.45. DBS, OCBC, CapitaLand Investment, Singtel, ST Engineering and YZJ Shipbuilding also traded lower in early deals. Derivatives trading showed 29,340 contracts exchanged, with SGX FTSE Taiwan Index Futures at 2,586.75 and Nikkei 225 Futures at 53,065.00. Market watchers said investor sentiment was influenced by expectations that MAS will keep monetary policy unchanged at its review on Thursday. Singapore’s GDP expanded 4.8% in 2025, exceeding the government’s November forecast of around 4.0%, supported by strong semiconductor demand and a steady tech cycle, with the electronics PMI at 50.9 in December. Economist Tay Qi Hang from the Economist Intelligence Unit Asia noted that AI-related demand and rising memory chip prices are likely to continue supporting the sector. Standard Chartered chief economist Edward Lee said inflation remains under control, reducing pressure for immediate action, though MAS may tighten policy in April. Bank of America economists flagged the possibility of an earlier tightening following December inflation data, which showed price increases in travel-related and other sectors offsetting declines in raw food and beverage prices. MAS manages monetary conditions by letting the Singapore dollar trade within a band against currencies of its main trading partners, adjusting the slope, midpoint and width of the band as needed. Globally, major central banks are expected to hold rates steady in the near term, although market uncertainty remains over the US Federal Reserve’s independence. At 8 am, the local currency was quoted at RM3.9850/9950 against the US dollar, up from RM4.0045/0080 recorded last Friday. The ringgit last traded near this level on 24 May 2018, when it touched RM3.9797 against the greenback. Meanwhile, the ringgit eased against some major currencies. It weakened to 2.5680/5748 versus the Japanese yen, 5.4447/4584 against the British pound, and 4.7258/7377 versus the euro. It also dipped slightly versus the Singapore dollar and Thai baht but inched higher against the Indonesian rupiah and Philippine peso. The stronger ringgit reflects improved risk appetite among investors following BNM’s decision to maintain its monetary policy stance and signs of softness in the US dollar. title: Malaysian Gold Follows Global Record Surge
body: Gold prices in Malaysia surged to RM20,238.86 per ounce on Monday, marking a rise of RM257.18 from the previous session, as investors flocked to the safe-haven asset amid rising geopolitical tensions and a weaker US dollar. The precious metal is now trading at RM650.69 per gram and RM650,693.97 per kilogram. Globally, gold hit an all-time high of US$5,110.50 per ounce, extending a historic rally following a 64% surge in 2025, the largest annual gain since 1979. Analysts point to safe-haven demand, US monetary easing, record central bank purchases and inflows into exchange-traded funds as key drivers behind the rally. “We expect further upside. Our current forecast suggests that prices will peak at around US$5,500 later this year,” said Philip Newman, director at Metals Focus, per Reuters . RHB Research highlighted that COMEX gold has now recorded four consecutive sessions of gains, with a bullish breakout above US$5,000 likely to open the door towards US$5,200. Analysts advised traders to maintain long positions while monitoring support levels at US$4,550 and US$4,400. Market observers noted that heightened uncertainty over US trade and global policy decisions has fuelled demand for gold, while a weaker dollar has made the metal more affordable for international buyers. Spot silver also rose 4.8% to US$107.90 per ounce, alongside record levels in platinum and palladium. In Malaysia, the gold market continues to reflect global trends, with year-to-date performance already up 4.21% for silver and a similarly strong trajectory for gold, as investors seek stability amid ongoing geopolitical and economic uncertainties. title: Wall Street Ends Mixed As Intel Slump Caps Volatile Week
body: US stocks closed out a whipsaw week on a cautious note on Jan 23, as a sharp drop in Intel soured investor sentiment and nudged the Dow lower, Reuters reported. The Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped 285.30 points, or 0.58%, to 49,098.71, while the S&P 500 eked out a 0.03% gain to 6,915.61. Nvidia gained 1.5% following a report that Chinese regulators have allowed tech giants including Alibaba, Tencent and ByteDance to prepare orders for its H200 AI chips. Seven of the S&P’s 11 major sub-sectors finished higher, led by materials, up 0.9%. Energy rose 0.6% to notch a third straight record close, cementing its position as the week’s best performer. title: Silver Vaults Past US$100 Per 28g, Extends Historic Run
body: Silver blasted through the US$100-an-oz mark on Jan 23, cementing its stunning outperformance of gold as a cocktail of retail speculation, ETF inflows and multi-year supply tightness pushed the white metal to fresh highs. Reuters reported that spot silver jumped 5.1% to US$101, extending a 40% gain in early 2026 after a 147% surge in 2025, its strongest annual rise in LSEG data going back to 1983. The metal’s rally has outpaced even buoyant gold, which notched a record US$4,988 per oz on Jan 23. Silver’s outperformance has shrunk the gold-silver ratio to 50-to-one for the first time in 14 years, down from 105-to-one last April, a level many traders view as stretched and prone to correction. Technical analysts warn the market’s near-vertical ascent leaves it vulnerable to a sharp pullback. Behind the surge is a potent mix: Retail buying of bars and coins, inflows into physically backed ETFs and persistent structural deficits in a market where roughly 20% of annual supply comes from recycling. Yet secondary supply has struggled to rebuild amid shortages in high-grade refining capacity, according to Metals Focus. For now, silver’s blend of precious-safe-haven appeal and industrial demand (from solar to electronics) continues to entice momentum traders. Whether fundamentals or froth are in the driver’s seat may become clearer once liquidity normalises or when the first big correction hits. title: Wall Street Rises For Second Day As Tariff Relief And Strong Data Lift Sentiment
body: Wall Street ended higher on Thursday, marking a second straight session of gains as investors were buoyed by tariff relief from US President Donald Trump and upbeat US economic data. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 306.78 points or 0.63% to 49,384.01, while the S&P 500 advanced 37.73 points or 0.55% to 6,913.35. The Nasdaq Composite climbed 211.20 points or 0.91% to 23,436.02. The gains followed Trump’s decision to rescind tariff threats against European allies, a move that eased market jitters after earlier volatility linked to trade tensions over Greenland. The rally came a day after the S&P 500 recorded its biggest daily percentage gain in two months. “It’s very weird to wake up every day as a money manager and you do not know whether it is Christmas morning or Friday the 13th,” said Gregg Abella, CEO at Investment Partners Asset Management. Despite the recent rebound, the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite remain down about 0.4% for the week, while the Dow is broadly flat, after losses earlier in the week triggered by renewed tariff concerns. Risk appetite was also reflected in small-cap stocks, with the Russell 2000 rising 0.8% to a record closing high. All seven of the so-called Magnificent Seven technology stocks ended higher, led by Meta Platforms, which jumped 5.7%, and Tesla, which gained 4.2%. Corporate earnings continued to drive individual stock moves. Procter & Gamble rose 2.6% after reporting quarterly results, while Abbott slid 10%, its biggest one-day percentage drop since 2002, after forecasting current-quarter profit below expectations. GE Aerospace fell 7.4% despite projecting annual profit above estimates, and McCormick dropped 8.1% after flagging weaker profit prospects in 2026 due to higher costs. Economic data also supported sentiment. US consumer spending rose solidly in November and October, pointing to sustained economic momentum, while initial jobless claims increased less than expected. Separate data showed the US economy grew by a slightly stronger-than-expected 4.4% in the third quarter of 2025. Trading volume on US exchanges totalled 18.30 billion shares, compared with a 20-day average of 16.91 billion shares, indicating heightened market activity as investors repositioned amid shifting policy signals and earnings developments. title: Wall Street Snaps Back On Greenland Deal, Bank Earnings Boost
body: Wall Street closed higher on Wednesday, snapping a sharp selloff from the previous session, after news that the US had reached a framework agreement related to Greenland, easing concerns over fresh tariffs on European allies. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 588.64 points or 1.21% to end at 49,077.23, while the S&P 500 gained 78.76 points or 1.16% to 6,875.62, marking its biggest one-day percentage gain in two months. The Nasdaq Composite advanced 270.50 points or 1.18% to 23,224.83. Markets were buoyed after US President Donald Trump said a framework for a future deal on Greenland and the broader Arctic region had been reached, adding that previously planned tariffs on European countries scheduled for Feb 1 would not be imposed. The rebound followed Tuesday’s broad selloff, the worst daily performance for all three benchmarks since October, as investors reacted positively to the avoidance of a potential escalation in trade tensions. Analysts said the announcement allowed markets to refocus on economic fundamentals, particularly corporate earnings. Banking stocks were among the strongest performers, with the regional banking index jumping 4.7% to its highest close since November 2024, supported by upbeat earnings from several lenders. Citizens Financial Group surged 7.1% to a record high after posting a 31.7% jump in quarterly profit, while Truist Financial rose 1.8% on higher interest income and investment banking fees. All S&P 500 sectors ended the session in positive territory, led by energy stocks. Halliburton climbed 4.1% after beating earnings estimates, while EQT Corp and Expand Energy advanced 6.5% and 4.5% respectively as natural gas prices rose on cold weather. Airline stocks also gained after United Airlines rose 2.2% on a stronger-than-expected outlook for the first quarter and the full year. Delta Air Lines, American Airlines and Southwest Airlines added between 1.1% and 2.4%. Netflix, however, fell 2.2% after issuing a muted outlook and announcing a pause in share buybacks to fund the acquisition of Warner Bros Discovery’s studio and streaming businesses. Market participants said the rally reflected relief that tariff threats had been rolled back, reducing uncertainty at a time when investors remain sensitive to geopolitical risks and policy shifts. Despite the strong rebound, analysts cautioned that volatility could persist as markets continue to track developments in global trade relations, earnings momentum and policy signals from Washington. title: Global Chip Stocks Rally On AI Optimism As Huang’s Remarks Boost Sentiment
body: Global semiconductor stocks climbed on Thursday as comments by Nvidia’s Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang at the World Economic Forum in Davos reinforced investor enthusiasm for the artificial intelligence (AI) sector. The rally reflected growing confidence that the demand for AI hardware and chips remains robust, underpinning strength across global markets. Huang’s remarks at Davos helped support the broader AI trade, contributing to gains in memory and logic chip stocks as investors weighed the long-term potential of AI technologies to fuel demand for processing power and infrastructure. In related market activity, Nvidia invested US$150 million in AI startup Baseten, part of a US$300 million funding round, signalling a strategic shift to focus on inference workloads within AI, a segment analysts expect to grow substantially in coming years. NVIDIA’s shares rose around 2.9% on the news, rebounding from prior weakness in broader technology stocks. At Davos, top technology executives sounded bullish about the AI sector’s future despite geopolitical uncertainties. Huang dismissed concerns of an AI bubble, noting strong underlying demand for GPUs and related compute resources, with cloud and enterprise usage expanding rapidly. BlackRock CEO Larry Fink also weighed in at the forum, rejecting the notion that the AI boom constitutes a speculative bubble. He positioned the surge in AI investment within a broader competitive landscape between major economies, emphasising the need for collaboration and wider diffusion of AI technologies to sustain growth. Supporting the optimism in chip stocks, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (TSMC) reported better‑than‑expected fourth‑quarter results, boosting its shares by over 6% to record highs. Other major semiconductor names, including Nvidia, AMD, ASML and Micron, also saw notable gains, underscoring strong investor appetite for AI‑linked hardware demand. title: Tariff Jitters Send Wall Street To Worst Day In Three Months
body: US stocks suffered their steepest one-day losses in three months on Tuesday as investors reacted to renewed tariff threats from President Donald Trump, triggering a broad risk-off move across global markets. All three major Wall Street indexes recorded their worst daily performance since October 10, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite both slipping below their 50-day moving averages. The S&P 500 fell 143.15 points, or 2.06%, to close at 6,796.86, while the Nasdaq slid 561.07 points, or 2.39%, to 22,954.32. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 870.74 points, or 1.76%, to 48,488.59. The selloff coincided with Trump’s weekend remarks, which marked the first opportunity for investors to respond following the Martin Luther King Jr. Day market holiday. Trump said an additional 10% import tariff would take effect on February 1 on goods from Denmark, Norway, Sweden, France, Germany, the Netherlands, Finland and Great Britain, countries already subject to US tariffs. He later said the tariffs would rise to 25% from June 1 and remain in place until an agreement was reached for the US to purchase Greenland, a proposal rejected by leaders in Greenland and Denmark, who insisted the island was not for sale. The return of tariff rhetoric revived memories of April’s “Liberation Day”, when sweeping levies on global trading partners pushed the S&P 500 close to bear market territory. Market volatility surged, with the CBOE Volatility Index closing at 20.09, its highest level since November 24. Risk aversion rippled across asset classes. Gold surged to fresh record highs, US Treasury yields rose amid renewed selling pressure, and bitcoin fell more than 3%. Trading volumes also climbed, with about 20.6 billion shares changing hands, well above the 20-day average of 17.01 billion. Despite the sharp moves, some market participants questioned whether the reaction would have lasting consequences. Jamie Cox, managing partner at Harris Financial Group, said he did not see signs of a sustained investor exit. “I’m not at the point yet where I’m willing to say what is happening with Greenland, and the resurgence of the tariff threat back ⁠and forth, is going to precipitate a ⁠correction in the equities markets,” he said, adding that he would be surprised to see a 3% to 5% market drop this week. Bond markets also came under pressure globally. Japanese government bonds plunged, sending yields to record highs after Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s call for a snap election raised concerns over fiscal stability. The selloff spilled into Europe, pushing up long-term bond yields, while losses in US Treasuries were most pronounced at the long end of the curve. Looking ahead, investors are set to digest a slate of economic data this week, including third-quarter US GDP figures, January PMI readings and the Personal Consumption Expenditures report, the Federal Reserve’s preferred inflation gauge. Corporate earnings season is also gaining momentum, with several major companies due to report, including Netflix, which closed 0.8% lower ahead of its earnings announcement. title: RHB Underweight On Rubber Products Sector
body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) maintained an UNDERWEIGHT rating on the rubber products sector, citing persistent earnings risks despite seemingly attractive valuations. The research house highlighted that glove manufacturers are under pressure from a stronger RM and intensifying global competition, which may weigh on full-year 2026 earnings. The brokerage’s latest outlook assumes global rubber glove consumption will stabilise in 2026, growing by 8% to roughly 400 billion pieces from 370 billion pieces in 2025, based on disclosures from Hartalega Bhd. Growth is expected to moderate to around 6% in 2027, reaching 424 billion pieces, supported by structural improvements in global hygiene awareness and occupational safety standards. However, analysts warned that further capacity expansions, particularly from China-linked producers, could add up to 80 billion pieces annually, potentially disrupting the demand-supply balance. Average selling prices are expected to remain under pressure as manufacturers contend with incremental supply from China-based players and rising raw material costs. While a weaker US dollar could lower RM-denominated input costs, it may simultaneously reduce pricing power, leaving producers vulnerable to margin compression in a price-sensitive market. RHB Research noted that sector valuations appear inexpensive at 0.9 times forward price-to-book value, but this reflects ongoing structural headwinds. Among the listed players, Top Glove Bhd is favoured for its focus on latex products, which analysts say provides a buffer against aggressive pricing in the nitrile segment dominated by China. Weekly orders for the company have surged to 1.4 billion pieces, extending lead times beyond 60 days. Despite this, RHB Research maintains a NEUTRAL rating on Top Glove, warning that rising latex costs could erode its competitive advantage. The brokerage identified key risks that could alter the sector outlook, including fluctuations in the USD/RM rate, changes in glove selling prices, capacity expansion trends, raw material costs and tariff policies relative to competitors. title: Gold Prices Soar Above RM19,700 Amid Global Tensions
body: Gold prices in Malaysia surged on Wednesday, continuing a strong rally as investors flocked to the safe-haven metal amid heightened global geopolitical tensions. The precious metal rose 2.11% to RM633.73 per gram, translating to RM19,711.15 per ounce and RM633,728 per kilogram as of the time of writing, per goldprice.org . This marks a significant increase of 2.09% for the day, with year-to-date gains reaching 57.76% over the past year and more than 157% over the past five years. Silver also recorded modest gains, rising 0.27% to RM385.08 per ounce. The rally comes as spot gold climbed above US$4,880 per ounce globally, driven by investor concerns over escalating tensions between the US and NATO over Greenland, as reported by Reuters . Analysts say the move reflects fears of geopolitical uncertainty, a weakening US dollar, and rising global debt. US gold futures for February delivery rose 2.6% to $4,888.20 per ounce. According to Kyle Rodda, senior market analyst at Capital.com, “It’s the loss of trust in the US caused by recent actions that is pushing investors toward gold. This reflects broader fears about global geopolitical tensions.” RHB Investment Bank Bhd noted that COMEX gold closed at US$4,765.80 on Tuesday, up US$170.40, with the bullish momentum remaining strong. The research house highlighted that while pullbacks are possible, the broader bullish trend remains intact, with resistance levels seen at US$4,800 and US$5,000 per ounce. Support is marked at US$4,400, providing a buffer for investors. The weakening US dollar, which recently touched a near one-month low, has also helped make greenback-priced metals cheaper for overseas buyers, further supporting the rally. Market watchers say the sustained gains in gold reflect continued investor demand for safe-haven assets amid global uncertainty, with Malaysia’s local prices tracking closely with international benchmarks. title: Asian Stocks Slide As ‘Sell America’ Fears And Greenland Tensions Weigh
body: Asian equities extended losses for a third straight session on Wednesday as investor anxiety rose over US President Donald Trump’s threats to acquire Greenland and rekindled concerns of a global trade war. Markets reacted to fears of offshore selling of US assets (dubbed the “Sell America” trade) after Wall Street tumbled over 2% overnight and the US dollar fell sharply, marking its largest decline in more than a month. Precious metals surged as a result, with gold hitting a record high of US$4,806 an ounce, up 0.8%, and silver rising 0.4% to US$95.01 an ounce. “The ‘sell America’ trade was the driving force behind major market moves overnight, as investors looked to reduce exposure to the US, seen by many as an unreliable partner pursuing self-defeating policies,” said Mantas Vanagas, senior economist at Westpac. In early Asian trade, MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan slipped 0.3%, while Japan’s Nikkei 225 fell 1.2%, marking its fifth consecutive day of declines. European futures were also lower, with both EURO STOXX 50 and DAX contracts down 0.4%. The global bond market, already rattled by surging Japanese government bond yields, paused briefly. Yields on 40-year Japanese government bonds fell 6 basis points to 4.145%, retreating from a record 4.215% on Tuesday. US Treasury yields were largely steady, with the benchmark 10-year yield dipping 1 basis point to 4.285%. The currency market remained volatile. The U.S. dollar steadied at 98.56 against major peers after its overnight drop of 0.5%, the largest daily fall since early December. Meanwhile, the yen held at 158.19 per dollar, while the Swiss franc hit a record 200.19 yen. Oil prices retreated as temporary production halts in Kazakhstan were outweighed by geopolitical tensions and an expected rise in US crude inventories. West Texas Intermediate crude for March fell 1.31% to US$59.57 a barrel. All eyes are now on Trump’s upcoming speech at the World Economic Forum in Davos, where his remarks on Greenland and tariffs on Europe could further influence global markets. title: Trump’s Greenland Tariff Threats Rattle Markets, Spur ‘Sell America’ Trades
body: Asian stocks fell on Tuesday while the dollar remained under pressure and US Treasury yields climbed to their highest level in more than four months, as renewed trade-war concerns rattled risk sentiment. Citi has downgraded European equities, while analysts said gold remained near record highs as investors sought safe-haven assets amid uncertainty over US-Europe trade relations. The market turbulence follows US President Donald Trump’s threats to impose additional tariffs over Greenland, a move that risks intensifying trade tensions with Europe. Futures for the Nasdaq and S&P 500 fell around 1% in early trade, while the yield on the 10-year US Treasury note rose to 4.265%, marking its highest level since early September. title: Stocks Slide On Trump Tariff Threats As Gold Hits Fresh Records
body: Global equity markets retreated on Monday while gold and silver surged to new highs, after US President Donald Trump threatened additional tariffs on European goods linked to opposition over his Greenland plans. Market sentiment turned cautious as Trump said the US would impose an extra 10% levy from February 1 on imports from Denmark, Norway, Sweden, France, Germany, the Netherlands, Finland and Britain, with the rate set to rise to 25% from June 1 if no agreement on Greenland is reached. The move rattled investors already wary of escalating trade tensions between the US and Europe. European markets bore the brunt of the sell-off. The STOXX 600 fell 1.2%, while major indices in Frankfurt, Paris and London declined between 0.4% and 1.7%. In Asia, Japan’s Nikkei dropped 0.7%, although MSCI’s broad Asia-Pacific index outside Japan was largely flat. US cash equity markets were closed for the Martin Luther King Jr. Day holiday, but S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures slid more than 1.2%. “There is obviously a response (in financial markets) to the new tariff threats,” said George Lagarias, chief economist at Forvis Mazars. “It’s highly likely that the White House will use the threat of tariffs consistently, even when deals have previously been agreed.” Safe-haven assets benefited as uncertainty grew. Gold climbed to a record high of US$4,689 an ounce, while silver jumped to US$94.08. Oil prices were little changed, with Brent easing 0.1% to US$64.04 a barrel as traders weighed trade war risks against easing unrest in Iran. Currency markets saw an unusual reaction, with the US dollar weakening rather than strengthening. The euro rebounded 0.4% to US$1.1641, while the dollar slipped against the Swiss franc and yen. “Typically you see dollar strength in the wake of increased geopolitical risk but now we see dollar weakness as it is originating from the US,” said Handelsbanken FX strategist Tommy von Brömsen. In China, markets were steady after data showed economic growth slowed to 4.5% in the December quarter, slightly above expectations. Strong industrial output offset weak retail sales, highlighting fragile domestic demand. Attention is now turning to the World Economic Forum in Davos, where the tariff threats are expected to loom large as global leaders gather amid rising trade and geopolitical tensions. title: European Stocks Fall, Dollar Drops, Markets Focus On Trump’s Tariff Threat
body: European stocks fell in early trading on Tuesday, the dollar entered a second day of declines and U.S. Treasury yields hit a four-month high after U.S. President Donald Trump continued his push to take control of Greenland and threatened to reignite a trade war with Europe. Trump said he no longer thought “purely of Peace” after he did not win the Nobel Peace Prize, and reiterated a threat to increase tariffs on EU members Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Sweden, and the Netherlands, along with Britain and Norway, until the U.S. is allowed to buy Greenland. EU leaders will discuss options, including tariffs worth 93 billion euros ($109 billion) on U.S. imports, at an emergency summit on Brussels on Thursday. Stock markets fell, extending Monday’s declines, as the threats from the U.S. reignited a debate over the “Sell America” trade that emerged after Trump’s “Liberation Day” levies announced last April.E Europe’s STOXX 600 was down 1.4 per cent on the day at 0956 GMT, having fallen 1.2 per cent on Monday, while the MSCI World Equity Index was down 0.2 per cent. The FTSE 100 was down 1.4 per cent.Trump separately threatened to hit French wines and champagne with 200 per cent tariffs, in an apparent effort to cajole French President Emmanuel Macron to join his Board of Peace initiative. Amelie Derambure, senior multi-asset portfolio manager at Amundi in Paris, said that the downward move in markets was “precautionary profit-taking and some risk reduction” but that markets were helped by the macroeconomic backdrop. Recent economic data has pointed to growth and decelerating inflation, and her portfolios remain risk-orientated, she said. “The situation in Greenland (is) worrying the markets. For the moment it remains relatively contained, there is no panic,” she said. “I don’t see for the moment anything comparable to Liberation Day or to something very dramatic for markets,” she added. The dollar index was down 0.6 per cent on the day, in its second day of declines, at 98.485, and the euro was up 0.7 per cent against the dollar at $$1.1726, its highest since January 6.As investors weighed up the risk of Trump reigniting a trade war with Europe over Greenland, U.S. Treasury yields hit their highest since September in early trading. U.S. markets were closed on Monday for a public holiday, so the moves were a delayed reaction to the developments that began over the weekend. The spread between the U.S. 30-year yield and the 10-year yield, as well as the spread between the two-year and 10-year yield, were both set for their biggest one-day steepening since August 2025. Elsewhere, Japanese government bond yields hit record highs over concerns that tax cuts will make the government’s finances worse. Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi had called a snap general election on Monday. Oil prices edged higher, with Brent crude futures up 0.2 per cent at $64.01 a barrel and U.S. West Texas Intermediate up 0.5 per cent at $59.72 a barrel, as prices were supported by expectations for global economic growth. The yield on the U.S. 10-year Treasury bond rose 3 basis points to 4.2586%, while Fed funds futures implied a 94.5% probability that the Federal Reserve will keep rates on hold at its upcoming two-day meeting. Elsewhere, the Australian dollar slipped 0.1% to US$0.6710 and the New Zealand dollar edged down 0.1% to US$0.5794. title: Markets Jolt As Trump Threatens Tariffs On Europe Over Greenland
body: Global markets faced renewed volatility on Monday after US President Donald Trump threatened new tariffs on eight European nations, prompting a flight to safe-haven currencies and pushing the euro to a seven-week low in early trading. Trump said he would impose a 10% import tariff from February 1 on goods from Denmark, Norway, Sweden, France, Germany, the Netherlands, Finland and Britain, rising to 25% on June 1 if a deal on Greenland is not reached. Major European Union states condemned the move as economic blackmail, with France signalling potential countermeasures. In early Asia trade, the euro fell 0.2% to around US$1.1572, while sterling also dipped. The yen strengthened against the dollar as investors sought stability amid heightened geopolitical risk. “Hopes that the tariff situation has calmed down for this year have been dashed for now – and we find ourselves in the same situation as last spring,” said Holger Schmieding, chief economist at Berenberg. Trump’s earlier “Liberation Day” tariffs in April 2025 had similarly rattled markets, though investors largely viewed those threats as temporary, with global economic growth remaining resilient in the second half of the year. The greenback showed mixed performance, retaining its safe-haven appeal but under pressure from rising concerns about US policy credibility. Bitcoin, often seen as a risk proxy, was steady at US$95,330. Countries most exposed to the tariffs, including the UK and Germany, could see GDP reductions of 0.1% under a 10% tariff and 0.2–0.3% if tariffs rise to 25%, according to Capital Economics. European stocks remain strong, with Germany’s DAX and London’s FTSE both up over 3% so far this month, outpacing the S&P 500’s 1.3% gain. Defence stocks have surged nearly 15% as geopolitical tensions escalate, while Denmark’s crown remains under scrutiny amid the uncertainty. “The US-EU trade war is back on,” said Tina Fordham, geopolitical strategist and founder of Fordham Global Foresight. The move coincides with other global flashpoints, including unrest in Iran and renewed questions over Federal Reserve independence. Gold remained near record highs as investors sought security amid rising geopolitical risks. Economists warn that escalating US-Europe tensions could weigh on the dollar and US tech valuations if capital flows shift abroad. title: Gold, Silver Hit Records, And Stocks Fall As Trade Fear Returns
body: Gold and silver hit record highs on Monday (Jan 19) while most equity markets fell after United States President Donald Trump revived trade war fears by threatening several European nations with tariffs over their opposition to the US buying Greenland. Trump has fanned already-rising geopolitical tensions this month by insisting that Washington would take control of the North Atlantic island, citing national security needs.And on Saturday, after talks failed to resolve “fundamental disagreement” over the Danish autonomous territory, he announced he would hit eight countries with fresh levies over their refusal to submit to his demands. He said he would impose 10 per cent tariffs on Denmark, Norway, Sweden, France, Germany, the United Kingdom, the Netherlands and Finland from Feb 1 – rising to 25 per cent from Jun 1 – if they did not agree to the takeover. The announcement drew an immediate response, with a joint statement from the countries saying: “Tariff threats undermine transatlantic relations and risk a dangerous downward spiral.”The move also threatened a trade deal signed between the US and European Union last year, with German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul telling ARD television: “I don’t believe that this agreement is possible in the current situation.”Meanwhile, aides to French President Emmanuel Macron said he would ask the EU to activate a never-before-used “anti-coercion instrument” against Washington if Trump makes good on his threat. This measure allows for curbing imports of goods and services into the EU, a market of 27 countries with a combined population of 450 million. title: Dollar Slips As Trump Tariff Threats Spur Flight To Safe Havens
body: The dollar weakened on Monday as renewed tariff threats by US President Donald Trump unsettled markets, prompting investors to seek refuge in traditional safe-haven currencies such as the yen and the Swiss franc. The move followed Trump’s weekend comments that he would impose an additional 10% import tariff from Feb 1 on goods from Denmark, Norway, Sweden, France, Germany, the Netherlands, Finland and Britain, unless the United States is allowed to buy Greenland. The announcement revived concerns over escalating trade tensions and their potential impact on global growth. Safe-haven demand lifted the yen and Swiss franc, with the dollar falling 0.33% to 157.59 yen and sliding 0.45% against the franc to 0.7983. The dollar index, which tracks the greenback against a basket of major currencies, slipped 0.19% to 99.18. In early Asian trade, the immediate reaction saw the euro and sterling sold down to a seven-week low of US$1.1572 and a one-month trough of US$1.3321 respectively. Both currencies later recovered as attention shifted towards the broader implications of the tariff threats for the dollar itself. The euro rose 0.19% to US$1.1619, while the pound gained 0.17% to US$1.3398. Major European Union states criticised the tariff threat on Sunday, with France proposing a range of potential countermeasures in response to what officials described as economic blackmail linked to Greenland. Market participants drew parallels with last April’s “Liberation Day” announcement, when Trump unveiled sweeping global tariffs that triggered a sharp loss of confidence in US assets and led to heavy selling of the dollar. “My working assumption is that an ‘off ramp’ from these threats will soon be found, and that this turns into yet another ‘TACO moment’, or an example of the ‘art of the deal’, depending on how one views these things,” said Michael Brown, senior research strategist at Pepperstone. Elsewhere, the risk-sensitive Australian dollar edged down 0.02% to US$0.6690, with losses cushioned by the softer greenback, while the New Zealand dollar rose 0.16% to US$0.5761. title: Bitcoin Slips 3% Amid Trump’s Tariff Threats
body: Bitcoin slid about 3% to around US$92,000 in early Asian trading on Monday as investors cut risk following renewed tariff threats from US President Donald Trump, which rattled global markets and spilled into digital assets. The world’s largest cryptocurrency fell to about US$92,506, down 2.6%, as Trump said the US would impose an additional 10% import tariff from Feb 1 on goods from Denmark, Norway, Sweden, France, Germany, the Netherlands, Finland and Britain, with the rate set to rise to 25% on June 1 if no agreement is reached. The move was linked to his push for US ownership of Greenland and drew condemnation from European officials, who described the threat as coercive. The risk-off reaction first emerged in derivatives markets as US cash markets were shut for a holiday, thinning liquidity. US stock futures fell sharply in early Asian hours, with S&P 500 futures down 0.7% and Nasdaq futures losing 1.0%. Asian equities followed suit, led by a roughly 1% decline in Japan’s Nikkei, while Europe’s futures also pointed lower amid fresh trade uncertainty. Other major cryptocurrencies moved in tandem, with ether down 3% to around US$3,203 and XRP sliding 4.7% to US$1.96, pulling total crypto market capitalisation down 2.7% to about US$3.21 trillion. The decline accelerated as leveraged positions were unwound, with traders pointing to heavy long liquidations during the sell-off. In broader markets, investors sought safety, pushing gold up 1.5% to a record high, while silver also hit fresh peaks. Oil prices eased as concerns grew over the impact of a potential US-Europe trade conflict on global growth and demand. Strategists warned that beyond tariffs, capital flows could pose a larger risk. Deutsche Bank noted that European investors hold about US$8 trillion in US bonds and equities, cautioning that any shift in those holdings could prove more disruptive than trade measures themselves. title: Wall Street Rebounds As Banks And Chips Spark Buying
body: US stocks rebounded on Thursday after two consecutive sessions of losses, supported by strong earnings from major banks and upbeat signals from the semiconductor sector. Shares of Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley surged after both lenders posted higher quarterly profits, driven by a pickup in dealmaking activity. Goldman climbed 4.6%, providing the biggest lift to the Dow, while Morgan Stanley advanced 5.8%. The rally came despite lingering concerns over the banking sector earlier in the week, when mixed earnings and worries over US President Donald Trump’s proposed one-year cap on credit-card interest rates at 10% weighed on sentiment. Investors appeared to rotate into value and cyclical names. “It’s been growth, tech or bust in this market,” in recent years, said Jake Dollarhide, chief executive officer of Longbow Asset Management in Tulsa, Oklahoma. Today, “it’s the banks and old-school industrials” that are standouts. The S&P 500 industrials index closed at another record high. Technology stocks also moved higher, led by chipmakers, after TSMC, the world’s largest producer of advanced artificial intelligence chips, forecast robust annual growth and flagged plans to expand US manufacturing capacity. US-listed shares of the Taiwan-based company jumped 4.4%. The semiconductor index rose 1.8%, with gains across heavyweights including Nvidia, Broadcom and chipmaking equipment firm Applied Materials. With the rebound, the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 292.81 points, or 0.60%, to 49,442.44. The S&P 500 added 17.87 points, or 0.26%, to 6,944.47, while the Nasdaq Composite rose 58.27 points, or 0.25%, to 23,530.02. Some valuation concerns in technology stocks eased following the semiconductor news. “There was some worry as far as valuations – that they were getting a little too far ahead of themselves,” said Alan Lancz, president of Alan B. Lancz & Associates Inc. in Toledo, Ohio. He added, “That’s been kind of squashed this morning with the news from Taiwan Semiconductor.” Beyond large caps, market leadership continued to broaden. Both mid-cap stocks and the Russell 2000 small-cap index have outperformed the S&P 500 so far this year, with the Russell 2000 reaching a record closing high. The equal-weighted S&P 500 has risen about 4% since the end of December, compared with a 1.4% gain for the benchmark index. Among other financial stocks, BlackRock jumped 5.9% after a market rally boosted fee income and lifted its assets under management to a record US$14.04 trillion in the fourth quarter. Bank earnings have effectively kicked off the US fourth-quarter reporting season, which is set to gather pace next week as a wider range of companies release results. Trading activity was heavy, with volume on US exchanges reaching 19.12 billion shares, above the 20-day average of 16.81 billion. On the NYSE, advancing stocks outnumbered decliners by nearly two to one, while gains also outpaced losses on the Nasdaq. title: Malaysia Gold Prices Dip Amid Stronger US Data
body: Gold prices in Malaysia fell slightly on Friday as stronger-than-expected economic data from the United States boosted the dollar and reduced expectations for near-term Federal Reserve rate cuts. Spot gold in Malaysian Ringgit dropped 0.19% to RM601.02 per gram, or RM18,693.81 per ounce, according to goldprice.org . Despite the daily decline, gold remains on track for a weekly gain of around 2% after reaching a record high of RM18,925 per ounce earlier this week. Silver also slipped, down 1.22% to RM370.11 per ounce. Analysts attributed the retreat to a combination of factors, including easing geopolitical tensions and a stronger US dollar. “The downward move in gold began predominantly when there was some lowering of the odds of US intervention in Iran,” said Kyle Rodda, analyst at Capital.com. He added, “US economic data shows there is not an urgency to cut interest rates.” The US Labor Department reported that weekly initial jobless claims fell to 198,000, below economists’ expectations of 215,000, according to Reuters . A firmer dollar typically makes gold and other non-yielding assets more expensive for international buyers. Despite the pullback, demand for gold remains resilient in the region. The SPDR Gold Trust, the world’s largest gold-backed exchange-traded fund, saw its holdings rise slightly to 1,074.80 tonnes, the highest in over three years. Meanwhile, gold buying in India remained muted as prices hit record highs, while Chinese demand stayed steady ahead of the Lunar New Year. Over the past year, gold in Malaysia has surged by 53.76%, highlighting its continued appeal as a store of value amid global economic uncertainty. title: Kerjaya Prospek Kicks Off FY26 On Solid Footing, Prompting A TP Revision
body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) have maintained a BUY call on Kerjaya Prospek Bhd with a revised target price of RM3.35, indicating a 21% upside, citing a strong start to 2026. The research house reported that the company’s first contract win of the year, a RM201 million project from Greencove, a subsidiary of Kerjaya Prospek Property, reinforces its steady project pipeline and growth prospects. The project involves the main building works of two 39-storey blocks in Damansara Damai, Sungai Buloh, scheduled to commence on April 1 and expected to be completed within 40 months. The contract accounts for around 10% of RHB Research’s internal job replenishment estimate of RM2 billion for Kerjaya Prospek. The company’s outstanding orderbook now stands at RM4.4 billion, translating to an orderbook-to-revenue cover ratio of 2.5 times, with an estimated net profit margin of about 10% for this project. Kerjaya Prospek’s active tenderbook is currently valued at approximately RM2 billion, with over half stemming from related-party transactions, including KPPROP and Eastern & Oriental (Buy, TP: RM1.17), alongside other residential and industrial projects. RHB Research noted potential opportunities in ongoing land reclamation projects, including Andaman Island, which could yield contracts worth RM300–500 million. The group also owns about 89 acres of land, mainly in Penang, with an estimated gross development value of RM3 billion. Ongoing property projects such as The Vue@Monterez and Papyrus@North Kiara have take-up rates of 99% and 82% respectively as of November 2025 and new launches in Jalan Puchong, Selangor and Tanjung Bungah, Penang, are expected in FY26. RHB Research highlighted that industrial property development could further bolster revenue streams. Downside risks include potential property market slowdowns and prolonged cost pressures. As of 11.20 am, the stock price is up 1.81% to RM2.82. title: Dollar Poised For Third Weekly Gain As US Jobs Data Ease Rate-Cut Bets
body: The US dollar was set for a third consecutive weekly gain on Friday after better-than-expected employment data reduced expectations for an imminent rate cut by the Federal Reserve. The greenback rose overnight following a surprise drop in weekly jobless claims and remained steady in Asian morning trade, while the Japanese yen hovered near levels that could prompt intervention by Tokyo to defend its currency. Kyle Rodda, an analyst at Capital.com, said, “The US dollar is looking firmer to start the year. Weekly US jobless claims data, along with some manufacturing surveys, were better than expected, lowering the implied probabilities of imminent Fed rate cuts.” Initial claims for state unemployment benefits fell by 9,000 to a seasonally adjusted 198,000 for the week ended January 10, the Labor Department reported on Thursday, compared with economists’ expectations of 215,000. Fed funds futures have pushed back expectations for the next rate cut to June as central bank policymakers weigh strong employment figures and remain concerned about inflation. Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said Thursday that amid ample evidence of stability in the job market, the central bank should focus on getting inflation down. Kansas City Fed President Jeff Schmid described inflation as “too hot”, while San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said that incoming economic data looks promising. The dollar index, which tracks the greenback against a basket of currencies, was little changed at 99.36 and is on course for a 0.2 per cent gain this week. The euro held steady at US$1.1607. The yen strengthened slightly by 0.05 per cent to 158.58 per dollar but is poised to fall roughly 0.5 per cent for the week. Expectations that Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi may pursue more fiscally expansionist policies ahead of a snap election next month have weighed on the yen. Policymakers have warned they stand ready to act against one-way movements in the foreign exchange market, giving the currency occasional support. Economists also expect the Bank of Japan to delay any rate hikes until July. Elsewhere in the region, the Australian dollar was little changed at US$0.6699, while New Zealand’s kiwi gained 0.05 per cent to US$0.5745. Philip Lane, chief economist at the European Central Bank, said the ECB would not consider any rate changes in the near term if the economy remains on track, though new shocks, such as deviations from the Fed’s mandate, could alter the outlook. The ECB has held rates steady since ending a rapid cut cycle in June and signalled last month that it is in no hurry to adjust policy again. In cryptocurrencies, bitcoin rose 0.2 per cent to US$95,760.92 and ether gained 0.8 per cent to US$3,323.82. title: Crypto Markets Hold Firm As Bitcoin Eyes US$100K, Ethereum Steadies
body: Bitcoin and Ethereum extended a steady start to the year as institutional flows, easing macro concerns and balanced sentiment kept crypto markets on solid footing. title: Wall Street Dips On Tech And Bank Sell-Offs Amid Economic Uncertainty
body: Technology and banking stocks led Wall Street lower for a second consecutive session on Wednesday, as investors rotated out of high-flying sectors in search of bargains. Bank shares fell despite some positive earnings, with Bank of America down over 4%, Citigroup slipping 4.5%, and Wells Fargo sliding more than 5%. “After a nice run, and so-so or mediocre earnings, you’re seeing profit-taking and consolidation,” said Michael O’Rourke, chief market strategist at JonesTrading in Stamford, Connecticut. Michael added, “Generally speaking, people are still optimistic on the group.” Technology and growth stocks also retreated, with Broadcom and Fortinet declining after Chinese authorities reportedly imposed new limits on domestic companies using cybersecurity software from certain US and Israeli firms. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite closed 1% lower at 23,471.75, the Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped 0.09% to 49,149.63, and the S&P 500 fell 0.53% to 6,926.60. Data showing stronger-than-expected US retail sales and slightly higher producer prices in November have reinforced expectations that the Federal Reserve may implement two interest rate cuts later this year. Elsewhere in US markets, the Supreme Court delayed a ruling on the legality of Trump’s global tariffs, while luxury retailer Saks Global filed for bankruptcy protection, reflecting continued strains in the financial sector. title: Malaysia Gold Prices Dip Amid Profit-Taking, Global Sentiment Eases
body: Gold prices in Malaysia fell on Thursday, following a surge to record highs earlier this week and amid easing safe-haven demand globally, according to GoldPrice.org . Spot gold in Malaysia was quoted at RM600.43 per gram, down RM1.94 or 0.32% from the previous session, while gold per kilogram slipped to RM600,431.14, a decrease of RM1,938.37. On a per-ounce basis, gold stood at RM18,675.51, down RM60.30 from the prior session. The decline mirrors movements in the international markets, where spot gold dipped 0.3% to US$4,608.77 per ounce after hitting a record US$4,642.72 on Wednesday. According to Reuters , traders attributed the pullback to profit-taking and comments from US President Donald Trump signalling a softer stance on the Federal Reserve chair and the situation in Iran, reducing the urgency for safe-haven assets. “Today, we’re seeing that gold is down a bit after [Trump] said maybe we’re not going to intervene in Iran, staving off safe-haven demand, but the larger story [of the metal’s rise] is not going away,” said Ilya Spivak, head of global macro at Tastylive. Silver also fell sharply in Malaysia, with prices down 1.8% to RM363.33 per gram after hitting early-session highs, reflecting similar trends in international markets. Over the past year, gold in Malaysia has risen significantly, gaining 53% per gram and recording long-term growth of nearly 797% over 20 years, highlighting its continued role as a hedge against economic uncertainty and geopolitical tensions. Gold remains a popular investment in Malaysia, with the Royal Mint of Malaysia producing the Kijang Emas bullion coin in various denominations, prized for its purity and legal tender status. title: Asia Markets Mixed, Oil Slides On Trump’s Iran Comments
body: Asian markets showed a mixed picture on Thursday as oil and precious metals fell following comments from US President Donald Trump that dialled back threats of imminent military action on Iran. Jack Ablin of Cresset Capital Management noted that Trump’s proposed 10 percent cap on credit card interest rates added to broader market unpredictability, while analysts highlighted lingering unease over possible US interventions in Iran and Greenland and threats to Federal Reserve autonomy. Brent crude dropped three percent after Trump said he would “watch it and see” on potential intervention in Iran, a sharp reversal from earlier rhetoric that had spurred crude gains amid fears of disrupted global supplies. Gold and silver also slipped on the news, reflecting softer safe-haven demand. Markets in Hong Kong, Shanghai, Taipei, Wellington, Mumbai and Kuala Lumpur declined, while Sydney, Seoul, Bangkok and Manila posted modest gains. Wall Street had edged lower on Wednesday despite strong US bank earnings and a 0.6 percent rise in November retail sales. Traders also monitored the South Korean won, which slid to its weakest level in 16 years before gaining nearly one percent following comments from US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. Bessent said the won’s depreciation was “not in line with Korea’s strong economic fundamentals” and called market volatility “undesirable”. Brendan McKenna, strategist at Wells Fargo, noted the comments may provide near-term support, though broader fundamentals and political concerns could still dominate. Meanwhile, Tokyo eased 0.8 percent after gains driven by speculation over a snap election. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi plans to dissolve parliament next week, with her cabinet approving a record 122.3-trillion-yen (US$768 billion) budget for the fiscal year from April 2026 to tackle inflation and stabilise the economy. title: Wall Street Slips As Financial Stocks Drag On Trump Credit Card Cap Fears
body: US equities ended lower on Tuesday as selling pressure in financial stocks weighed on Wall Street, with investor concerns mounting over President Donald Trump’s proposal to cap credit card interest rates. Losses were led by banks and payment firms, extending a sell-off that began after Trump floated a 10% cap on credit card rates last Friday. Executives at JPMorgan Chase warned the proposal would hurt both lenders and consumers, adding to market unease. “Financials are getting hit by Trump’s credit-card proposal,” said Tim Ghriskey, senior portfolio strategist at Ingalls & Snyder in New York. “It seems to be sinking in. I think it’s going to be extremely difficult to have that become a reality, but it’s still out there.” Shares of Visa fell 4.5%, Mastercard dropped 3.8% and the broader financial sector declined 1.8%, making it the worst-performing group in the S&P 500. JPMorgan slid 4.2% despite reporting a better-than-expected fourth-quarter profit, as investors focused on weaker investment banking fees. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 398.21 points or 0.80% to 49,191.99. The S&P 500 slipped 13.53 points or 0.19% to 6,963.74, while the Nasdaq Composite edged down 24.03 points or 0.10% to 23,709.87. Earlier in the session, losses were partially cushioned by inflation data showing US consumer prices rose 2.7% year-on-year in December, in line with expectations. The reading helped preserve market hopes for interest rate cuts by the Federal Reserve later this year. The earnings season also began to take shape, with JPMorgan among the first major companies to report. Other large banks, due to release results later this week, also traded lower even as analysts expect broadly stronger performances for the final quarter of 2025. Elsewhere, Delta Air Lines shares fell 2.4% after the midpoint of its 2026 profit forecast came in below analysts’ expectations. Earnings momentum for the quarter is likely to remain positive, said Oliver Pursche, senior vice president and adviser at Wealthspire Advisors in Connecticut. “I suspect there are going to be some upward revisions” for 2026, he said, adding that the market pullback reflected “a little bit of letting the air out of the balloon” following recent record highs. Market breadth was mixed. Advancing stocks outnumbered decliners on the New York Stock Exchange, while declines led on the Nasdaq. Trading volume stood at 18.68 billion shares, above the 20-day average of about 16.4 billion. title: Rupiah Near Historic Low As Bank Indonesia Steps Up Market Interventions
body: Indonesia’s central bank will continue intervening in foreign exchange markets to ensure the rupiah reflects its fundamental value, Bank Indonesia (BI) said on Wednesday, as the currency hovers near a historic low. The rupiah has steadily depreciated this year, touching its weakest point since April 2025 on Tuesday before recovering slightly. As of 0230 GMT on Wednesday, the currency had slipped 0.03 per cent to 16,865 per U.S. dollar. Its all-time low against the dollar was recorded in April 2025. Erwin Gunawan Hutapea, head of monetary management at BI, said the currency’s decline mirrors movements in regional peers, driven by rising geopolitical tensions and market concerns over the independence of central banks in some developed countries. “Bank Indonesia will remain active in the market to ensure the rupiah exchange rate moves in line with fundamental values and sound market mechanisms,” Hutapea added, using a term the central bank employs to describe its interventions. BI has conducted interventions across offshore non-deliverable forward markets in Asia, Europe and America, as well as in the domestic spot, non-deliverable forward and bond markets, he said. Analysts noted additional pressure on the rupiah from domestic fiscal concerns, following the government’s report of a budget deficit of 2.92 per cent of GDP in 2025, close to the statutory limit of 3 per cent. title: Malaysia’s Gold Price Hits Fresh High As Global Rally Continues
body: Gold prices in Malaysia climbed to fresh highs at midday, tracking a global surge in bullion prices driven by expectations of interest rate cuts in the US and heightened geopolitical uncertainty. As of Jan 14, gold was priced at RM603.45 per gram, up RM4.46 or 0.74% on the day. On a larger unit basis, gold stood at RM18,769.56 per ounce, gaining RM138.76, while gold per kilogram rose to RM603,454.92, according to data from GoldPrice.org. The latest move extends gold’s strong upward momentum. Over the past 30 days, gold prices in ringgit terms have risen 6%, while gains over six months stood at nearly 32%. On a one-year basis, gold in Malaysia has surged more than 53%, reflecting strong safe-haven demand and currency effects. Silver prices in Malaysia also recorded sharp gains. Silver was up nearly 4% on the day, with longer-term performance showing a 35% rise over 30 days and more than 150% year-on-year, underscoring strong investor appetite for precious metals. The rally mirrors global markets, where gold climbed to a record high overnight after softer-than-expected US inflation data reinforced expectations of interest rate cuts. Spot gold rose to above US$4,630 per ounce, while silver breached US$90 per ounce for the first time, according to Reuters . Market analysts said the latest US consumer price index data showed inflation remaining contained, strengthening the case for monetary policy easing. Non-yielding assets such as gold tend to benefit in a lower interest rate environment and during periods of economic or geopolitical uncertainty. Gold’s strong performance has also been supported by concerns over US Federal Reserve independence and broader risk sentiment, with some banks forecasting prices to move higher in the first half of 2026. In Malaysia, the sharp rise in gold prices has reinforced the metal’s appeal as a store of value, with multi-year data showing gold prices in ringgit terms up more than 150% over five years and over 800% across two decades, highlighting its long-term defensive role amid market volatility. title: Installed Solar Capacity Far Below NETR Targets, Time To Catch Up
body: Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) maintains an OVERWEIGHT rating on the renewable energy sector, with BUY calls on Solarvest (TP: RM3.66) and Gamuda (TP: RM6.88). HLIB cites the country’s early-stage energy transition and accelerating demand driven by the data centre boom. The research house highlights that Malaysia’s installed solar capacity of 4.2GW as of July 2025 remains far below the 2050 NETR target of 57GW, supporting a multi-year pipeline of projects. In 2026, opportunities are expected from 2GW LSS5+ EPCC, 2GW LSS6, CRESS, the 300MW FiT 2.0 programme and additional standalone battery energy storage system (BESS) projects, representing over RM20 billion in potential EPCC contracts. The research house noted that long-term corporate renewable energy sourcing is expected to rise as multinational technology companies seek cost savings and green credentials. BESS integration is also expanding the total addressable market, with grid tolerance for renewable penetration rising from 40% to around 70% in many cases, enabling larger-scale solar adoption and higher contract values per megawatt. On the commercial and residential front, HLIB expects rooftop solar installations to rebound in 2026 under the Solar ATAP programme, which removes previous quota limitations and allows system sizes up to 100% of maximum demand. Cost pressures remain manageable despite a modest firming in module prices to around US$0.10–0.11 per watt, although silver price volatility warrants monitoring. HLIB said utility-scale projects, CRESS adoption and residential and commercial uptake will underpin the sector’s growth trajectory, with risks centred on execution delays, slower-than-expected data centre builds, materials prices and labour shortages. Solarvest and Gamuda are expected to benefit from extended orderbooks and structural demand drivers, supporting continued earnings growth across the sector. title: Consumer Sector To Remain Stable Amid Supportive Fiscal Measures
body: MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB Research) has maintained a POSITIVE call on the consumer sector, with top picks including MR D.I.Y (Buy, TP: RM2.20), AEON (Buy, TP: RM1.66) and Leong Hup International (Buy, TP: RM0.90). The research house also downgraded F&N to Sell, Life Water to Trading Sell and upgraded QL Resources to Buy, citing valuation and input cost considerations. Retail sales in Malaysia moderated in November 2025 but remained resilient, rising 6.4% year-on-year to RM69.02 billion despite a slight month-on-month pullback of 0.4%. Non-specialised stores led growth at 8.7% year-on-year, followed by food, beverages and tobacco at 6.3% and household equipment at 3.1%. Cumulatively, retail trade for the first eleven months of 2025 expanded 6.0% year-on-year to RM741.22 billion, underscoring sustained household consumption momentum ahead of the holiday season. Malaysia’s labour market strengthened, with the unemployment rate easing to 2.9%, marking an 11-year low. Headline inflation remained contained at 1.4% year-on-year, while core inflation held at 2.2%, supporting household purchasing power. Tourist arrivals also grew 6.8% year-on-year to 20.04 million in 11MCY25, providing incremental support to retail, FMCG and casual dining sectors, particularly in urban and tourist locations. Input costs for food and beverage producers continued to ease, with sugar, cocoa, crude palm oil and PET resin prices declining, partially offset by elevated coffee costs. Poultry markets saw egg prices correct sequentially, while chicken prices strengthened, and feed costs remained manageable with soybean meal easing despite corn edging higher. The Malaysian Ringgit’s appreciation to 4.09/USD further reinforced import cost tailwinds, improving margins for consumer-facing companies. MBSB Research noted that MR D.I.Y benefits from mass-market spending and favourable sourcing, AEON from stable mall traffic and rental income and Leong Hup from defensive exposure to staple protein demand. The sector outlook remains constructive under supportive fiscal measures, manageable input costs and incremental tourism-driven demand heading into Visit Malaysia Year 2026. title: Wall Street Hits Records Despite Powell Probe Concerns
body: US stocks hit record closing highs on Monday, with the S&P 500 up 10.99 points (0.16%) to 6,977.27 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average rising 86.13 points (0.17%) to 49,590.20, as investors shrugged off worries over a Justice Department criminal investigation into Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell. The Nasdaq Composite gained 62.56 points (0.26%) to 23,733.90. Shares of Walmart surged 3%, lifting the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq, where the retailer recently shifted its listing from the NYSE. Walmart is scheduled to join the Nasdaq-100 index on 20 January, a move expected to attract billions from passive index funds. Consumer staples rose 1.4%, leading sector gainers, while technology stocks also advanced. Stocks had opened lower earlier on Monday amid concerns over Powell, whose potential indictment centres on comments he made to Congress about a Fed building renovation project. Powell described the investigation as a “pretext” for exerting greater influence over interest rates, which President Donald Trump has urged to cut sharply since taking office in January 2025. “The news that Powell is being investigated by the Justice Department was basically telegraphed by Trump, and so I think the market is taking it in stride for now,” said Peter Cardillo, chief market economist at Spartan Capital Securities in New York. He added that support from former Fed governors has also reassured markets. Investors are now focusing on the upcoming fourth-quarter earnings season, which is expected to be led by the technology sector with a 26.5% year-on-year earnings gain, according to LSEG data. Overall, analysts see S&P 500 earnings for the quarter rising 8.8% from a year ago. The reporting period unofficially begins Tuesday with JPMorgan Chase and other major banks. Financials, however, lagged as President Trump called for a one-year cap on credit card interest rates at 10% starting 20 January. The S&P 500 financial sector fell 0.8%, with Citigroup down 3%, American Express 4.3%, and Capital One 6.4%. Buy-now, pay-later firm Affirm dropped 6.6%. Volume on US exchanges reached 17.29 billion shares, above the 20-day average of 16.40 billion. Advancing issues outnumbered decliners on the NYSE by a 1.68-to-1 ratio, with 725 new highs and 48 new lows. On the Nasdaq, 2,613 stocks rose and 2,144 fell, with advancing issues surpassing decliners 1.22-to-1. Investors also await Tuesday’s US consumer price index report, which could influence expectations for at least two more quarter-point rate cuts by year-end. title: South Korea Holds Key Rate At 2.50% Amid Currency Concerns
body: South Korea’s central bank is expected to keep its key interest rate steady at 2.50 per cent on Thursday, as the won’s recent decline limits room for further easing, according to a Reuters poll of economists. According to Reuters , Korean won has dropped nearly 2 per cent in the first two weeks of 2026, raising the risk of higher consumer prices and intensifying inflation concerns flagged by the Bank of Korea (BOK) at its November meeting. Asia’s fourth-largest economy recorded 2.1 per cent inflation in 2025, slightly below 2024’s 2.3 per cent but still above the BOK’s 2 per cent target. All 34 economists surveyed between Jan 6 and 12 forecast the BOK would maintain its base rate at 2.50 per cent at Thursday’s meeting. “Given the volatility in the FX market, it is too soon for the BOK to cut rates right now,” said Kelvin Lam, senior economist at Pantheon Macroeconomics. Lam noted that while the government has attempted to control housing supply, Seoul apartment prices remain elevated. “So the focus for the BOK is now turned to having a stable currency and also looking at instability stemming from the overheating apartment prices.” Data from the Korea Real Estate Board shows apartment prices in Seoul rose 0.18 per cent in the week ending 5 January and climbed 8.7 per cent over 2025, underscoring the challenges facing the central bank. The BOK has signalled it may be nearing the end of its current easing cycle, revising its guidance from “maintain its rate cut stance” to “the Board will decide whether and when to implement any further Base Rate cuts,” suggesting a longer pause may be likely. Expectations for further rate cuts have declined. In November 2025, more than 60 per cent of economists anticipated at least one cut in the first quarter, but the latest poll shows only 22 per cent foresee another reduction this quarter. Looking ahead, South Korea’s economy is projected to grow 2.0 per cent in 2026, slightly above the BOK’s forecast of 1.8 per cent, and 1.9 per cent in 2027 and 2028. Inflation is expected to average 1.9 per cent this year, slightly below the central bank’s 2.1 per cent estimate. title: Nikkei Hits Record On Wall Street Gains And Election Speculation
body: Tokyo’s Nikkei share average surged to a record high on Tuesday as investors reacted to Wall Street’s recent two-day rally and anticipated additional stimulus measures from the Japanese government. According to Reuters, the index jumped as much as 3.6% to 53,814.79, while the broader Topix gained 2.4% to 3,599.31, also reaching a record peak. Markets were boosted by expectations that Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi may call an early election to strengthen her coalition’s parliamentary majority, fuelling speculation of increased fiscal spending. “It’s widely believed in markets that if Takaichi dissolves parliament, the result will be a weaker yen, higher equities and lower bond prices,” said Maki Sawada, an equities strategist at Nomura Securities, citing the likelihood of proactive fiscal measures. Japanese investors appeared largely unfazed by the U.S. Justice Department’s criminal investigation of Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell, mirroring sentiment in global markets. The Nikkei’s rally followed all-time peaks on Wall Street, where the Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500 advanced, led by technology stocks. The yen’s decline since Friday further lifted sentiment, enhancing the overseas earnings of Japan’s export-heavy companies. Automakers performed strongly, with Toyota Motor climbing 5.1% and Subaru up 4.1%. Semiconductor shares led gains, with Advantest soaring 8.4% and Tokyo Electron jumping 7.7%. Of the Nikkei 225 constituents, 209 advanced while only 16 declined, underlining broad market strength. The potential early election would mark Takaichi’s first time facing voters, allowing her to capitalise on strong public approval ratings since taking office in October. title: Gold And Silver Soar As Investors Seek Safe Havens Amid Powell Probe
body: Gold hit a record above US$4,600 per ounce on Monday while silver also reached fresh highs, as investors flocked to safe-haven assets following heightened uncertainty over a Trump administration criminal investigation into Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell. Spot gold was up 2.2% at US$4,609.58 per ounce as of 1:38 p.m. ET (1838 GMT), after earlier reaching US$4,629.94. U.S. gold futures for February delivery settled 2.5% higher at US$4,614.70. Meanwhile, spot silver climbed to an all-time high of US$86.22, later trading at US$85.39 per ounce, up 6.8%. “Elevated uncertainty plays directly into the gold market, (and) every week we seem to have another area of uncertainty added,” said Michael Haigh, global head of commodities research at Societe Generale. He added that the backdrop for the rally looked unlikely to reverse soon. Last year, gold surged over 64%, its best performance since 1979, while silver posted a 146.8% gain, marking its strongest year on record. The Trump administration has intensified pressure on the Fed, threatening to indict Powell over his remarks about a building renovation project, which he called a “pretext” to gain control over the interest rates the President seeks. Powell’s term ends in May, and the administration is reportedly considering BlackRock’s Rick Rieder as a potential successor. Markets are still pricing in two additional rate cuts later this year, boosting the appeal of non-yielding assets like gold. Geopolitical tensions, including Trump’s responses to international developments in Iran, Venezuela, and Greenland, have further reinforced demand for precious metals. Gold and silver “go together,” said Ned Naylor-Leyland, gold and silver fund manager at Jupiter Asset Management, adding that silver often reacts more sharply due to its smaller market. Other precious metals followed the trend, with spot platinum up 3% to US$2,342.10 per ounce and palladium rising 2.5% to US$1,861.44.
