title: Asia Shares Rise As Nikkei Hits Records, Oil And Gold Gain
body: Asian stock markets climbed, led by a surge in Japan’s Nikkei, as investor optimism over AI and expectations of fiscal stimulus in Tokyo outweighed lingering concerns about the Federal Reserve’s independence. The Nikkei (.N225) returned from a public holiday with a 3.4% gain to record highs, helped by a weaker yen and speculation that Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi could call an early election to strengthen her coalition. South Korea (.KS11) and Taiwan (.TWII) also hit record levels, while Chinese blue chips (.CSI300) reached a four-year peak. Analysts at Citi forecast a 10% upside for the MSCI AC World index by year-end, citing AI-related tailwinds and a soft-landing macro environment. Investor sentiment was further supported by the yen’s decline, which boosts the value of overseas earnings for Japan’s exporters. In equities, automakers advanced, with Toyota Motor up 5.1% and Subaru rising 4.1%. Semiconductor shares saw the largest gains, including Advantest (+8.4%) and Tokyo Electron (+7.7%). Oil prices rose as unrest in Iran raised fears of supply disruptions. Brent crude added 0.5% to $64.19 a barrel, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate climbed 0.5% to $59.81, reaching seven-week highs. Meanwhile, President Donald Trump warned that any country trading with Iran would face a 25% tariff on U.S. business, adding to market uncertainty. title: Dollar Drops Sharply On Powell Indictment Threat
body: The dollar on Monday fell sharply against the euro and the Swiss franc while edging lower versus the Japanese yen after the Trump administration threatened Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell with a criminal indictment, a move that could endanger the greenback’s safe-haven status. The dollar index, which measures the greenback’s strength against a basket of six currencies, was recently 0.37 per cent lower at 98.759, snapping a five-day winning streak. Gold jumped to a record $4,600.33 per ounce after Powell released a video where he defended the central bank’s independence.”The point is that the central bank’s response function is likely to change fundamentally and in the long term if the White House succeeds (in gaining control of monetary policy),” said Thu Lan Nguyen, ‌head of forex and commodity research at Commerzbank, after flagging that the Fed is already in a rate-cutting ‌cycle and this scenario becomes relevant only if inflation risks rise. “However, as the foreign exchange market is forward looking, this already justifies a higher US dollar risk premium today,” she added. Some analysts said markets had not yet panicked because they expect U.S. President Donald Trump to appoint a credible successor to Powell and let that person steer policy.The dollar advanced in early Asian trade to a ‍one-month high after Friday’s jobs report bolstered expectations that the Federal Reserve will hold interest rates steady later this month, while reports of hundreds of deaths during protests in Iran heightened geopolitical tensions and stoked demand for safe-haven assets. Against the yen , the U.S. dollar was recently 0.1 per cent weaker at 157.80 yen, not far from its highest point in a year. On Sunday, the coalition partner of Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s party said she might hold a snap election on February 8 or 15, a move that ​made investors cautious. On Friday, media outlets reported she was ‌considering a vote in February, citing government sources. Geopolitical tensions in Iran “should be positive for the U.S. dollar but we haven’t seen any upside there yet,” said Kyle Rodda, senior market analyst at Capital.com in Melbourne. “The question from here is whether the momentum behind the protest movement continues ​and whether the regime cracks down even harder, opening the door to some U.S. involvement.” Reuters Related The dollar index, which measures the greenback’s strength against a basket of six currencies, was recently 0.37 per cent lower at 98.759, snapping a five-day winning streak. involvement.” Reuters Related “However, as the foreign exchange market is forward looking, this already justifies a higher US dollar risk premium today,” she added. involvement.” Reuters Related Against the yen , the U.S. involvement.” Reuters Related On Sunday, the coalition partner of Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s party said she might hold a snap election on February 8 or 15, a move that ​made investors cautious. involvement.” Reuters Related Geopolitical tensions in Iran “should be positive for the U.S. involvement.” Reuters Related Reuters Related Related

title: Wall Street Logs Fresh Records As Chip Rally Powers Strong Week
body: The S&P 500 notched a record close on Jan 9, capping 2026’s first full trading week with broad gains as chipmakers surged and a soft jobs report kept hopes alive for Federal Reserve rate cuts. Instead, investors leaned into cyclicals as long-lagging sectors joined Big Tech in the rally. Semiconductors stole the show. The PHLX Semiconductor Index jumped 2.7% to a record, fuelled by Lam Research’s 8.7% surge after a Mizuho price-target hike and an 11% pop in Intel after US President Donald Trump touted a “great meeting” with CEO Lip-Bu Tan. Energy-adjacent names followed a different script: Vistra soared 10.5% after Meta agreed to buy power from its nuclear plants. Meanwhile, GM slid more than 2% after flagging a US$6 billion charge tied to unwinding electric vehicle investments. Rate-sensitive housing and mortgage plays snapped higher after Trump said he would order representatives to buy US$200 billion in mortgage bonds to curb housing costs. LoanDepot jumped 19.3%, Rocket climbed 9.6% and Opendoor surged 13.1%, helping the Philadelphia Housing Index close up 5.7% at a two-month high. title: Tech Slips, Defence Rallies As Wall Street Ends Mixed
body: Wall Street finished Thursday on a mixed note, with weakness in major technology names offset by strong gains in defence stocks after President Donald Trump called for a sharply higher US military budget. Defence counters advanced after Trump said the 2027 military budget should reach US$1.5 trillion, well above the US$901 billion approved by Congress for 2026. Lockheed Martin rose 4.3%, Northrop Grumman gained 2.4% and Kratos Defense surged 13.8%. The move followed a volatile previous session, when some defence names fell after Trump warned he could block dividends and share buybacks if weapons production did not accelerate. Technology stocks, meanwhile, weighed on broader markets. NVIDIA slid 2.2%, Broadcom fell 3.2% and Microsoft eased 1.1%. The S&P 500 technology index dropped 1.5%, leaving it down about 1% so far in 2026, as investors grew more selective over richly valued AI-linked stocks. “While AI is still hot, there are going to be winners and losers,” said Art Hogan, chief market strategist at B. Riley Wealth. Art added, “It’s become a ‘show me’ sector. Show me how you monetise this. Show me if there’s going to be a return on the capex you’re putting into your development.” Alphabet gained 1.1%, a day after the Google parent overtook Apple in market capitalisation for the first time since 2019 to become the second most valuable US company. Apple shares slipped 0.5%. AI-related memory chipmakers also retreated after a strong rally. SanDisk dropped 5.4%, Western Digital slid 6.1% and Seagate fell 7.7%. Elsewhere, Ford jumped 4.7% after Piper Sandler upgraded the automaker to overweight from neutral. By the close, the S&P 500 edged up 0.01% to 6,921.45 points. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.55% to 49,266.11, while the Nasdaq declined 0.44% to 23,480.02. Markets are now turning their attention to macroeconomic signals. New applications for US unemployment benefits rose moderately last week, pointing to continued sluggish labour demand and reinforcing recent ADP employment and JOLTS data. Investor focus is firmly on Friday’s nonfarm payrolls report for December, one of the first major datasets released after the longest US government shutdown in history. Fitch has raised its US growth outlook, estimating GDP expanded 2.1% in 2025 and forecasting 2.0% growth in 2026 after factoring in delayed economic data from the shutdown period. Market breadth was positive, with advancing stocks outnumbering decliners on the S&P 500 by a 2.4-to-one ratio. The index recorded 43 new highs and 13 new lows, while the Nasdaq saw 133 new highs and 51 new lows. Trading activity was heavy, with 16.9 billion shares changing hands, above the recent 20-session average of 16.3 billion shares. title: Stock Today: Globaltec Eases Despite Indonesia CBM Development Progress
body: Shares of Globaltec Formation Bhd slipped 1.41% to RM0.70 as of 2.43 pm, with 686,000 shares traded. The stock opened at RM0.71, touched an intraday high of RM0.715 and fell to a low of RM0.695. Buy interest was seen at RM0.695 for 29,300 shares, while sell orders stood at RM0.70 for 101,100 shares, reflecting mild selling pressure during the session. The muted stock performance came despite recent developments at its energy arm in Indonesia. Globaltec previously announced that its 70%-owned subsidiary, NuEnergy Gas Limited, had entered into a collaboration agreement with PT Beijing Energy Link to advance its coalbed methane production sharing contracts in South Sumatra. The collaboration is aimed at developing Indonesia’s first coalbed methane Plan of Development, the Tanjung Enim POD 1, and supporting a transition from early gas sales of around 1 million standard cubic feet per day to a plateau production rate of up to 25 million standard cubic feet per day, as approved under the plan. Under the agreement, PT Beijing Energy Link will be appointed as the lead engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning contractor, financing 100% of the field development works at a capped contract price, with repayment to be made through future gas sales. The development scope includes drilling activities, construction of surface facilities and installation of in-field pipelines, as well as integration and testing to achieve first gas and sustained production. The Tanjung Enim project operates under a favourable 95:5 contractor-government split scheme approved by Indonesia’s Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources. title: Gold Continues Uptrend In Malaysia As Safe-Haven Appeal Strengthens
body: Gold prices in Malaysia rose on Friday, with gold trading at RM585.04 per gram, up 0.61% from the previous session, while silver increased 2.35% to RM314.22 per gram, according to goldprice.org . On a one-year basis, gold has surged nearly 50% in value, reflecting sustained demand for the precious metal as a safe-haven asset. The recent rally comes amid a broader global trend. title: Four Key Factors That May Impact CPO Outlook In 2026
body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has maintained a NEUTRAL call on the plantation sector for 2026, saying crude palm oil (CPO) prices are expected to average slightly lower year on year amid a more balanced global supply and demand outlook. The research house highlighted that geopolitical tensions and policy changes could still trigger volatility, but fundamental factors point to a steadier market. Top stock picks include Johor Plantations Group, Sarawak Oil Palms, IOI Corp and SD Guthrie. The bank cited four key factors shaping the outlook. A weak La Niña currently affecting global weather patterns is not expected to significantly disrupt South American soybean crops, keeping supply relatively stable. Indonesia’s planned B50 biodiesel mandate in the second half of 2026 could raise CPO demand by 2 million tonnes, but funding constraints and levy adjustments may influence the market. Meanwhile, uncertainties around China-US soybean agreements and potential delays in US biofuel policy could keep soybean oil prices subdued, affecting CPO competitiveness. CPO prices fell almost 20 per cent from a January 2025 peak of RM4,920 per tonne to around RM3,900-4,000 in late 2025, pressured by high stock levels in Malaysia and a narrower spread versus soybean oil. However, prices stabilised as the gap widened again, boosting imports by major buyers and bringing stock levels in China, India, Pakistan and Bangladesh to comfortable levels above historical averages. RHB Research projects CPO at RM4,250 per tonne for 2026 and RM4,100 per tonne in 2027. The bank expects the stock-to-usage ratio for palm oil to rise to 17.7 per cent in 2026, signalling a more stable market. The research house cautions that deviations from base assumptions, including geopolitical events, crude oil trends, weather extremes, or changes in biofuel policies, could disrupt the balance. Analysts attribute the pullback to profit-taking and anticipation of key U.S. economic data, which could influence risk appetite across asset classes. Options expirations also played a role, with roughly US$2.2 billion in Bitcoin and Ethereum options set to expire on Jan 9. title: Asian Markets Hold Breath As US Jobs And Tariff Ruling Loom
body: Asian stocks edged lower on Friday, with investors cautious ahead of a key US employment report and awaiting a Supreme Court decision on the legality of President Donald Trump’s global tariffs that roiled markets last year. The MSCI Asia-Pacific index outside Japan slipped 0.3% in early trade, remaining just below the record high set earlier in the week, while Japan’s Nikkei rose 0.8%, supported by strong earnings and guidance from Fast Retailing, operator of the Uniqlo brand. European stock futures added 0.4%. Much of the market focus rested on the potential Supreme Court ruling. Kyle Rodda, senior financial markets analyst at Capital.com, described the decision as the “real wildcard” for markets. “If the courts slap down US tariffs, it would be a big boost to market sentiment,” he said, while noting that the Trump administration is unlikely to abandon efforts to maintain the levies even if they are deemed unlawful. Investors also monitored oil markets, with Brent futures rising 0.6% to $62.36 per barrel and US West Texas Intermediate crude gaining 0.5% to $58.04. Geopolitical tensions in Venezuela, coupled with concerns over supplies from Russia, Iraq and Iran, lifted energy and defence stocks. US forces carried out a military raid in Caracas on Saturday, prompting further caution among traders. On the domestic front, the dollar held firm near a one-month high and yields on benchmark US 10-year Treasury notes eased slightly to 4.169% after climbing in the previous session. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent indicated that Trump is expected to make a decision soon on Jerome Powell’s replacement as Federal Reserve Chair, with Powell’s term ending in May. Markets anticipate a dovish appointment. Attention now turns to Friday’s US jobs report. Nonfarm payrolls are projected to rise by 60,000 in December after a 64,000 rebound in November, following a loss of 105,000 jobs in October, primarily from deferred federal buyouts. Traders are pricing in at least two rate cuts from the Fed this year, although the central bank previously indicated only one cut is likely in 2026. Rodda noted that a significant downside surprise would move markets, while a strong report would reinforce confidence in the US labour market. title: Wall Street Eases From Peaks As Jobs Data Looms
body: Wall Street retreated from record territory on Wednesday as investors turned cautious ahead of key US labour data. Both the Dow Jones Industrial Average and the S&P 500 slipped from all-time highs set a day earlier, after data showed US job openings fell in November and private-sector hiring rose less than expected in December. The softer figures tempered risk appetite, even as a services sector survey pointed to healthier growth at the end of the year. “The jobs data was not great, but did not trigger changes to perceptions about future Fed rate cuts,” said Steve Sosnick of Interactive Brokers. “We attempted to follow through from the rallies of the last couple of days, and so far we haven’t been able to.” The Dow ended the session down 0.9%, while the S&P 500 fell 0.3%. The Nasdaq Composite bucked the broader trend, edging 0.2% higher. Futures markets continue to expect the Federal Reserve to hold rates steady later this month, though analysts said Friday’s non-farm payrolls report would be critical in shaping expectations. In Europe, markets were mixed. Frankfurt’s DAX surged to a fresh record above 25,000 points, while Paris was flat. London slipped from a record high, weighed down by sharp losses in heavyweight energy stocks after oil prices declined. Crude extended losses after Trump said Venezuela would hand over millions of barrels to the US. West Texas Intermediate slid 2.0% to US$55.99 a barrel, while Brent fell 1.2% to US$59.96. US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said Washington would control Venezuelan oil sales “indefinitely”. Analysts noted the shipments reduced near-term supply risks but added that ample global supply, following OPEC+ output increases, pointed to softer prices. Elsewhere, US defence stocks dropped sharply after Trump threatened to cap executive pay and restrict dividends and share buybacks. Lockheed Martin, General Dynamics and RTX each fell more than 2.5%. Asian markets mostly weakened, with Tokyo and Hong Kong closing lower, while Shanghai edged up slightly. Currency markets saw the dollar firmer against the yen, while the euro and pound eased. The company also maintains selective participation in utility-scale solar projects, including LSS5+, LSS6 and CRESS and holds a dominant share of over 50% in Malaysia’s electrical low-voltage products market. Its recently acquired EPE Switchgear business is projected to contribute 26% to 35% of group revenue over 2025–2027, supported by a 40% market share among Tenaga Nasional medium-voltage switchgear suppliers. Maybank IBG projects Pekat’s earnings to grow at a compound annual growth rate of 45% over 2025–2027, underpinned by its RM745.6 million order book, operating leverage and rising contribution from higher-margin power distribution activities. body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has maintained its positive trading bias on Hang Seng Index Futures (HSIF) despite a pullback that it views as part of a consolidation phase within a broader bullish structure. RHB Research said the HSIF eased on Wednesday, retreating 246 points to close at 26,473 points after opening at 26,710 points. The research house noted that while bullish momentum has moderated, the overall uptrend remains intact. The relative strength index edged lower but continued to hold above the 50% level, indicating that underlying bullish traction is still present. The upward trend in both the 20-day and 50-day simple moving averages further reinforces the prevailing bullish setup. RHB Research said as long as the index remains above the key 25,000-point support level, the current retracement is likely to be temporary. Following the consolidation, the index could see renewed dip-buying interest, potentially driving it towards the 27,400-point resistance level. Immediate support is seen at 25,600 points, followed by 25,000 points, while resistance levels are pegged at 27,400 points and 28,000 points. title: Gold Slips In Malaysia Amid Firm Dollar Ahead Of Key US Jobs Data
body: Gold prices in Malaysia eased on Thursday, pressured by a firm US dollar and ahead of major US labour market data. As of early trading, gold was priced at RM578.50 per gram, down RM2.42 or 0.42% from the previous session, while the price per kilogram stood at RM578,501.78, falling RM2,421.91. Spot gold per ounce was RM17,993.43, down RM75.33 or 0.43%. Silver also retreated, with prices at RM307.60 per gram, down RM8.41 or 2.66% (goldprice.org). The recent dip follows trends in international markets. Spot gold in the US fell 0.4% to US$4,435.62 per ounce, while February gold futures dropped 0.4% to US$4,444.40 (Reuters). Traders are weighing heightened geopolitical tensions, including US involvement in Venezuela, against macroeconomic signals from the United States, according to Bernard Sin, regional director-Greater China at MKS PAMP. Softer US jobs data has boosted expectations of further Federal Reserve rate cuts, which support bullion, but sentiment remains cautious amid volatility and profit-taking. The gains for bullion remain substantial year-to-date, with gold up 50.21% over the past year and 141.05% over five years in Malaysian Ringgit terms. However, the market is approaching key resistance levels, with bullion about RM3,700 away from its record high of US$4,549.71 per ounce reached in late December. Analysts also note that the annual Bloomberg Commodity Index rebalancing, running January 9–15, may prompt short-term profit-taking, particularly in gold and silver (Reuters). Silver prices mirrored gold’s retreat, falling 2.52% to RM76.08 per ounce internationally, after hitting record highs in late December. Precious metals investors are closely monitoring the US non-farm payrolls report on Friday for cues on the Fed’s policy direction. title: Asian Equities Retreat As Investors Eye US Jobs Data
body: Equity markets in Asia mostly fell on Thursday as investors paused after the strong start to the year, focusing on upcoming US labour market data. Tokyo, Hong Kong, Singapore, Shanghai, Taipei, Mumbai, Bangkok and Jakarta all closed lower, while Sydney rose and Wellington remained flat. Traders were assessing the geopolitical backdrop following the U.S. removal of Venezuela’s president and ongoing tensions between China and Japan. Tokyo’s Nikkei 225 dropped 1.6% to 51,117.26, while the Hang Seng Index fell 1.2% to 26,149.31 and the Shanghai Composite dipped 0.1% to 4,082.98. London’s FTSE 100 opened down 0.2% at 10,023.82. In New York, the Dow Jones Industrial Average closed down 0.94% at $48,996.08. Market attention is squarely on Friday’s US non-farm payrolls report, seen as a key indicator for the Federal Reserve’s interest rate decisions later this month. “A very strong number forces markets to rethink timing. A very weak one reopens recession debates. Anything in between simply prolongs the range and keeps this market drifting sideways at altitude,” said Stephen Innes, managing partner at SPI Asset Management. Investors also monitored sector-specific developments, including Samsung Electronics’ announcement of a record fourth-quarter profit of US$13.8 billion. Tokyo stocks were pressured after China launched an anti-dumping probe into Japanese chemical imports used in semiconductor production. Oil prices edged higher, with West Texas Intermediate up 0.2% at US$56.10 per barrel and Brent North Sea crude rising 0.2% to US$60.09 per barrel, following news that Venezuela would supply the U.S. with millions of barrels of crude. Currency markets showed minor moves, with the euro down to $1.1675 and the pound at $1.3441. title: Stock Today: CIMB Shares Rebound Amid RM1.4 Billion Sukuk Lawsuit
body: CIMB Group Holdings Bhd shares rose 0.5% to RM8.03 as of 11.44 am, recovering slightly after a sharp drop to RM8.01 yesterday following reports of an RM1.38 billion lawsuit over its Sukuk issuance for the MEX II Highway project. The stock opened at RM7.94, hitting a high of RM8.05 and a low of RM7.90, with 3.8 million shares traded. The lawsuit, filed by 14 plaintiffs including Credit Guarantee Corporation Malaysia Bhd, Amanah Raya Bhd and Syarikat Takaful Malaysia Keluarga Bhd, names CIMB Investment Bank Bhd as a defendant alongside MEX II Sdn Bhd and other parties. Plaintiffs claim CIMB IB, acting as principal adviser and lead manager, failed to ring-fence sufficient funds for the highway project, resulting in losses after MEX II defaulted on principal repayments and periodic profit payments. CIMB has said the litigation is not expected to materially affect its operations or finances. Analysts remain positive on the group’s longer-term prospects. RHB Research maintained its BUY call, raising the target price to RM9 from RM8.55, signalling a potential 9% upside and an estimated FY26 dividend yield of around 6%. The research house highlighted CIMB’s strong balance sheet, prudent provisioning and the ongoing turnaround in Indonesia, where Bank CIMB Niaga reported a 3% year-on-year net profit increase for 9M25. RHB added that improvements in foreign exchange conditions, loan growth and potential capital management initiatives could support the group’s path to its 2027 return on equity target of 12% to 13%. With excess capital of around RM1.8 billion and a CET1 ratio of 14%, CIMB is well-positioned to optimise dividends and maintain flexibility in its core markets. title: Gold Slips To RM582 As Investors Book Profits Amid Stronger Dollar
body: Gold prices in Malaysia edged lower on Wednesday, with spot gold falling 1.11% to RM582.60 per gram, as investors booked profits after prices briefly touched a more than one-week high earlier in the week. In kilogram terms, gold traded at RM582,599.06, down RM1,069.02 from the previous session. Globally, spot gold slipped to US$4,449.38 per ounce, following a record high of US$4,549.71 hit last Monday. U.S. gold futures for February delivery also declined 0.8% to US$4,460.50. According to Reuters, analysts noted that a stronger dollar, which held near a two-week high, weighed on precious metals by making greenback-priced assets more expensive for other currency holders. “Prices are not being influenced that much from a fundamental perspective, there’s a lot of speculation… price action has for the most part been skewed to the upside, but it’s showing two-way volatility,” said Kyle Rodda, senior financial markets analyst at Capital.com. Market watchers remain attentive to upcoming U.S. data, including non-farm payrolls, ADP private payrolls and the JOLTS survey, which could set the tone for gold ahead of expectations for at least two Federal Reserve interest rate cuts this year. Fed Governor Stephen Miran also emphasised the need for aggressive rate cuts to support economic growth. Analysts from RHB Investment Bank noted that COMEX gold continues to show bullish momentum, eyeing the US$4,500 level and potentially extending towards US$4,800. They highlighted that short-term support remains near US$4,200, with a stop-loss threshold at US$4,000 for long positions initiated in September last year. Silver, platinum and palladium also retreated in line with gold, with silver down 1.08% to RM582.60 per gram, reflecting broader profit-taking in precious metals markets. title: Chip Rally Lifts Wall Street As Dow Hits Fresh Record
body: Wall Street closed higher on Tuesday, driven by a sharp rally in chip-related stocks on renewed optimism around artificial intelligence, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed to a record high and edged closer to the 50,000 mark. Semiconductor and memory stocks led the gains after Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang, speaking at the Consumer Electronics Show in Las Vegas, outlined developments including a new layer of storage technology. SanDisk surged more than 27%, while Western Digital jumped 17%, Seagate Technology rose 14% and Micron Technology advanced 10%, with all four stocks hitting record highs. The PHLX chip index also reached an all-time high, rising 2.75% and extending its gain in the first three trading sessions of 2026 to about 8%. Healthcare stocks added to the market’s strength, helped by Moderna, which jumped nearly 11% after BofA Global Research raised its price target on the drugmaker. The move lifted the S&P 500 healthcare index by 1.96%. “I think we’re going to have a very strong earnings season for Big Tech, and all those capex estimates that we hear about are going to be revised higher again,” said Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital in St. Louis. The S&P 500 gained 0.62% to close at 6,944.82 points, while the Nasdaq rose 0.65% to 23,547.17 points. The Dow climbed 0.99% to 49,462.08 points. Trading activity was relatively heavy, with 18.7 billion shares changing hands, above the 20-session average of 16.1 billion. Investors continued to assess economic signals as markets await key labour data later this week, including the Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey and Friday’s December jobs report. Any weaker-than-expected readings could strengthen expectations for central bank interest rate cuts. Data released on Tuesday showed S&P Global’s final composite PMI slipped to 52.7 in December from 53.0, while the services PMI eased to 52.5 from 52.9. Attention also turned to the fourth-quarter earnings season, with valuations remaining elevated. The S&P 500 is trading at about 22 times expected earnings, above its five-year average of 19, according to LSEG data. Elsewhere, oil stocks retreated after strong gains a day earlier, with Exxon Mobil and Chevron falling 3.4% and 4.5%, respectively. Shares of Johnson Controls slid 6.2% and Trane Technologies dropped 2.5% after comments from Nvidia’s Huang raised concerns about demand for data centre cooling systems. AIG tumbled 7.5% after announcing that Chief Executive Officer Peter Zaffino would step down. Market breadth was positive, with advancing issues outnumbering decliners on the S&P 500 by a 3.1-to-one ratio. The index recorded 62 new highs and eight new lows, while the Nasdaq posted 126 new highs and 42 new lows. body: Bursa Malaysia Securities Bhd will reclassify Central Global Berhad (CGB) from the Industrial Products & Services sector, under the Packaging Materials sub-sector, to the Construction sector with the Construction sub-sector. title: Wall Street Hits Record Highs As Energy And Banks Ride Venezuela Wave
body: Wall Street closed higher on Monday, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average hitting an all-time high, driven by a rally in financial shares and energy companies following a US military operation that captured Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro. Investors anticipated that the move could allow US firms access to Venezuela’s vast oil reserves. President Donald Trump’s administration is scheduled to meet with executives from US oil companies this week to discuss boosting Venezuelan production. The S&P 500 energy index rose 2.7% to its highest level since March 2025, with heavyweights Exxon Mobil and Chevron both posting strong gains. Weapons manufacturers also advanced, pushing the S&P 500 aerospace and defence index to a record high. “Energy stocks are really benefiting from the expectation that President Trump is intending to send them in to do more investment in Venezuela and ultimately make more money for themselves,” said Rob Haworth, senior investment strategist at US Bank Wealth Management. Financial shares rallied as well, with the S&P 500 financials index climbing 2.2% ahead of upcoming quarterly results. Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan Chase each rose more than 3% to record highs. “The mood has been favouring financial stocks in recent days and as people look beyond tech, this is a sector many are choosing to look toward,” said Steve Sosnick, chief market analyst at Interactive Brokers. Among individual stocks, Tesla climbed 3.1% after a seven-session losing streak, while Nvidia fell 0.4% and Apple declined 1.4%. Cryptocurrency-linked shares also advanced, with Strategy (formerly MicroStrategy) up almost 5% and Coinbase rising 7.8% following a Goldman Sachs upgrade. By the close, the S&P 500 gained 0.64% to 6,902.05 points, the Nasdaq rose 0.69% to 23,395.82 points, and the Dow increased 1.23% to 48,977.18 points. Trading volume on US exchanges was heavy at 19.1 billion shares, above the 20-day average of 15.9 billion. Wall Street’s main indexes recorded double-digit gains in 2025 for the third consecutive year, a streak last seen in 2021. Data on Monday also showed US manufacturing contracted more than expected in December, extending a 10-month slump. Investors are now eyeing Friday’s nonfarm payrolls report, which could influence Federal Reserve policy in 2026. Despite the near-term weakness, HSIF continues to trade above its 20-day and 50-day simple moving averages, indicating that the broader bullish structure remains intact. As long as the 25,000-point support holds, HSIF is expected to retain its ability to attract further positive price action. title: Venezuelan Crisis Sparks Bullion Buying, Gold Climbs In Malaysia
body: Gold prices in Malaysia climbed sharply on Monday, tracking global gains as heightened geopolitical tensions and safe-haven demand drove investor interest. Spot gold in Malaysia rose to RM579.61 per gram, up RM14.93 or 2.64% from the previous day, while the price per ounce reached RM18,027.85. Meanwhile, silver gained 4.63% to RM308.91 per gram, reflecting continued investor appetite for precious metals. According to an article by Reuters, the rally follows the United States’ capture of Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro over the weekend, an event described as Washington’s most controversial intervention in Latin America since the 1989 invasion of Panama. “The kidnapping of a foreign head of state naturally leads to high degrees of instability and in this environment, gold and silver are viewed as a solid hedge against uncertainty,” said Tim Waterer, chief market analyst at KCM Trade. Globally, COMEX gold is undergoing consolidation after dipping US$11.50 on Friday to close at US$44,329.60 per ounce. The metal initially traded at US$4,340, reaching a day’s high of US$4,414.80 before retreating to US$4,319.70. Analysts at RHB Investment Bank Bhd advised holding long positions, noting potential support at US$4,200 and US$4,000, with upside targets at US$4,600 and US$4,800. The Malaysian rally also mirrors last year’s record-setting global gains, with bullion posting a 64% increase in 2025, its largest annual gain since 1979. The metals market has been buoyed by central bank purchases, interest rate cuts and inflows into exchange-traded funds. Platinum and palladium also surged, with platinum hitting RM1,160 per gram and palladium climbing 1.6% to RM867 per gram. Analysts expect gold to maintain its positive bias, citing ongoing geopolitical uncertainty and a supportive low-interest-rate environment. title: Dollar Flexes At Start Of Year As Fed Bets Take Centre Stage
body: The dollar kicked off the first full trading week of the New Year with fresh momentum, climbing to a 3½-week high against the euro and a two-week peak versus the yen as traders zeroed in on a pivotal run of US economic data. According to Reuters , markets largely shrugged off the weekend’s dramatic US raid in Venezuela and the capture of President Nicolas Maduro, instead focusing on indicators that could shape the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) rate path in 2026. The greenback edged up 0.1% to US$1.1704 per euro, having earlier touched its strongest level since Dec 11. Against the yen, it rose 0.2% to 157.08, after hitting a December 22 high of 157.255. A string of resilient US data has prompted investors to reassess expectations for interest rate cuts, with some now betting the Fed may move more cautiously than previously thought. The week’s data calendar kicks off with ISM manufacturing figures on Jan 5 and culminates in the closely watched non-farm payrolls report on Jan 9. Traders are currently pricing in two US rate cuts this year, according to LSEG data based on futures. Adding another layer of uncertainty, investors are also awaiting US President Donald Trump’s pick for the next Fed chair, with Jerome Powell’s term ending in May. Trump has said he will name his choice this month and has signalled a preference for a chair who strongly favours lower interest rates. Elsewhere, the dollar gained 0.1% against sterling to US$1.3443 and rose 0.1% versus the Canadian dollar to C$1.3745. The Australian dollar slipped 0.2% to US$0.6682, underperforming as the greenback tightened its grip. title: Dollar Kicks Off 2026 Firmer As Markets Brace For Fed Signals

Attention is now squarely on next week’s US data, capped by the payrolls report on Jan 9, for clues on whether the Fed will cut rates further. Markets are fully pricing in two cuts this year, versus just one projected by a divided Fed. Politics is adding another layer of uncertainty. President Donald Trump has said he will name his pick for the next Fed chair this month, ahead of Jerome Powell’s term ending in May. Many investors expect a more dovish nominee, reinforcing bets on deeper easing. title: Shanghai Biren Shares Skyrocket On Hong Kong Debut
body: Shares of Chinese AI chip designer Shanghai Biren Technology (6082.HK) surged 82.1% in their Hong Kong debut, marking the first listing of 2026 in the financial hub. Biren opened at HK$35.7 each, well above the HK$19.60 offer price and climbed as high as HK$40 during trading. The strong debut follows a blockbuster year for Hong Kong’s equity market in 2025 and signals a likely wave of AI and semiconductor offerings this year as China accelerates efforts to develop domestic chip alternatives in response to U.S. technology export curbs. Biren raised HK$5.58 billion (US$717 million) by selling 284.8 million H shares at the top of its marketed range. Institutional demand was nearly 26 times the shares on offer, while the retail tranche was oversubscribed roughly 2,348 times, according to exchange filings. At the offer price, Biren’s market capitalisation stood at HK$46.9 billion, based on 2.396 billion shares outstanding. Founded in 2019, Biren develops general-purpose graphics processing units (GPUs) and intelligent computing systems for artificial intelligence and high-performance computing. While the IPO highlights opportunities from China’s push for tech self-sufficiency and policy support, the prospectus also flagged risks from U.S. export controls. Biren was added to Washington’s Entity List in October 2023, limiting its access to certain technology. title: Precious Metals Start 2026 Strong Amid Geopolitical Tensions And Rate-Cut Bets
body: Precious metals opened the New Year on a strong note on Friday, extending gains from a record-breaking 2025 as safe-haven demand remained supported by geopolitical tensions and expectations of lower interest rates. According to Reuters, spot gold rose 1.5% to US$4,378.75 per ounce as of 0553 GMT, rebounding after a two-week low earlier in the week and following a record high of US$4,549.71 on Dec 26. US gold futures for February delivery climbed 1.2% to US$4,392.20 per ounce. “(Precious metals) seem to be making amends for the year-end selling which afflicted them earlier in the week. Year-end position-squaring pressures have eased and gold is kicking off 2026 with gains, now that fundamentals are again in focus,” said Tim Waterer, chief market analyst at KCM Trade. Bullion staged a stellar rally in 2025, ending the year with annual gains of 64%, the largest since 1979. Interest rate cuts, expectations of further easing by the US Federal Reserve, geopolitical conflicts, strong central bank demand and rising holdings in exchange-traded funds had fuelled the rally last year. Silver performed even more strongly, ending 2025 with a 147% gain. Spot silver jumped 3.7% to US$73.90 per ounce on Friday, following an all-time high of US$83.62 on Monday. Platinum was up 2.5% at US$2,105.48 per ounce and palladium rose 2.1% to US$1,639.12 per ounce. Both metals also recorded their largest yearly gains on record. Investors expect at least two rate cuts by the Fed this year, supporting demand for non-yielding assets such as gold and silver. US jobless claims eased slightly last week, but labour market weakness under President Donald Trump’s second term is expected to keep rate-cut expectations intact. In Malaysia, gold prices mirrored the global rally. As of Friday, gold traded at RM571 per gram, RM17,764 per ounce and RM571,126 per kilogram, representing daily gains of about 1.2%. Over the past year, gold in Malaysia surged nearly 48%, continuing a multi-year bull run that has seen five-year gains surpass 125%. Silver also climbed, rising 3.3% to RM73 per gram, with a 12-month gain of 118%. The strong start to 2026 suggests continued momentum for precious metals, supported by global economic uncertainty, low-interest-rate expectations and sustained investor appetite for safe-haven assets. title: Dollar Struggles As Yen Holds Near 10-Month Lows
body: The US dollar began 2026 on a weak footing, continuing its struggles against most currencies seen last year, while the Japanese yen steadied near 10-month lows as investors awaited key economic data this month to gauge the trajectory of interest rates. The dollar’s losses in 2025 were driven by shrinking interest rate differentials with other economies, erratic trade policies and concerns over the Federal Reserve’s independence under President Donald Trump. The dollar index, which tracks the greenback against six major currencies, fell 9.4% last year, marking its steepest annual decline in eight years and stood at 98.243 on Friday. “The global economy enters 2026 with reasonable momentum, with the probability of recession remaining low,” said Anthony Doyle, chief investment strategist at Pinnacle Investment Management. Anthony added, “Outside of the United States, the central bank rate cut impulse is fading, which reduces one-way market moves and raises the importance of selection across regions, factors and asset classes.” Economic data in the coming weeks, including U.S. payrolls and jobless reports, will provide clues on the health of the labour market and the path of interest rates. Much attention is also on who President Trump will appoint as the next Fed Chair following Jerome Powell’s term ending in May. Markets are pricing in expectations of two rate cuts this year, reflecting hopes for a more dovish Fed. The euro and sterling remained steady in early Asian trading. The euro was at $1.1752 after surging 13.5% in 2025, its steepest annual rise since 2017, while sterling traded at $1.3474 following a 7.7% gain last year. The yen last traded at 156.74 per dollar, close to the 10-month low of 157.90 reached in November, which had sparked fears of intervention by Tokyo. Warnings from Japanese authorities in December helped keep the yen away from the intervention zone, though concerns persist. Elsewhere in the region, the Australian and New Zealand dollars began 2026 on the front foot. The Australian dollar rose 0.1% to $0.66805, following a near 8% gain in 2025, its strongest yearly performance since 2020. The New Zealand dollar, which ended a three-year losing streak last year with nearly a 3% gain, traded little changed at $0.5755. title: Bitcoin’s Super Calm Sets Stage For Major Price Swing In 2026
body: Bitcoin’s price chart looks super calm via Bollinger Bands, a volatility gauge, hinting at a massive swing ahead. BTC has traded in a tight range between $85,000 and $90,000 for the past two weeks. As a result, the gap between its Bollinger Bands, volatility bands placed two standard deviations above and below the 20-day simple moving average of the asset’s price, has narrowed to less than $3,500, the lowest since July, according to data source TradingView. This so-called Bollinger Bands squeeze indicates a low-volatility period in which the market is building energy for the next big move. History confirms massive price swings often follow these squeezes.For instance, the last Bollinger Band squeeze in late July capped a two-week sideways grind between $115,000 and $120,000. The squeeze paved the way for a three-month expansion, with prices swinging wildly from $100,000 to $126,000.A similar pattern unfolded in late February: a range between $94,000 and $98,000 tightened into Bollinger Band squeezes, followed by a slide to $80,000 by month-end. Bollinger Bands have accurately signaled volatility explosions since at least 2018. title: Asia Markets Edge Higher As Global Trading Resumes For 2026
body: Global stock markets offered a mixed but generally optimistic start to the first full trading session of 2026. While several major exchanges in the West and East remained shuttered for the New Year holiday period, active markets in Asia kicked off the year on a positive note, driven by resilient domestic demand and a rebounding tech sector. title: Stocks Pull Lower At End Of Record Year For Markets
body: Stock markets mostly retreated on Wednesday (Dec 31) in thin trading, following a year of record gains for key assets as central banks cut interest rates and the tech sector boomed thanks to the growth of artificial intelligence. Wall Street’s main indices dipped to close the final trading day of 2025, with little fresh economic data apart from a drop in both first-time and continuing claims for jobless benefits in recent weeks. Still, all three indices logged solid gains for the full year. The Dow added 13 per cent in 2025, the broad-based S&P 500 advanced 16.4 per cent and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite surged 20.4 per cent over the year. “Generally speaking, 2025 was a spectacular year for equities,” said Briefing.com analyst Patrick O’Hare. Across the globe, stock markets struck record highs and enjoyed double-digit gains in 2025, thanks in large part to interest rate cuts from the US Federal Reserve following drops in inflation. London’s benchmark FTSE 100 index jumped more than 21 per cent in 2025 – the biggest gain for 16 years. Frankfurt rallied 23 per cent in 2025, while Paris saw an annual gain of more than 10 per cent. In Asia, Seoul stocks rocketed 75 per cent higher, while Hong Kong’s Hang Seng index jumped 28 per cent, and Tokyo’s Nikkei 225 won more than 26 per cent.”To push meaningfully higher in 2026, equities will need confirmation that the Fed can deliver at least the two rate cuts still priced by the market, with growth unimpeded,” noted Stephen Innes of SPI Asset Management. Minutes of the Fed’s policy meeting in December, which were released on Tuesday, indicated that most of its officials see future rate cuts as appropriate, should inflation cool over time as expected. A surge in the tech sector on the back of the vast amounts of cash pumped into AI also helped push stocks to record highs, but concerns that valuations of AI stocks are too high gnawed at investors late in 2025. AI chip juggernaut Nvidia became the world’s first US$5 trillion company at the end of October, while its current worth stands at around US$4.5 trillion. The price of gold, seen as a safe-haven investment, scored multiple record highs this year. The precious metal has benefitted from weakness to the dollar caused by the Fed’s rate cuts and economic growth concerns triggered by President Donald Trump’s tariffs war. On Wednesday, the price of silver slid further, having struck record highs in December. Oil prices have retreated nearly 20 percent over the year, pressured by an oversupplied market. Bitcoin, emphasising the volatile nature of the cryptocurrency sector, soared to a record high above US$126,000 in October before ending the year around US$88,000. title: Bitcoin Posts First Annual Loss Since 2022
body: Bitcoin is on track to post its first annual loss since 2022, as macroeconomic pressures and fading momentum weighed on the world’s largest cryptocurrency. Despite reaching a fresh record high this year, bitcoin has struggled to regain its footing since October, and last month experienced its biggest monthly drop since mid-2021. Now, it is on track to end the year more than 6 per cent lower, after posting yearly gains the previous two years. It was last trading at $87,474.2.After soaring earlier this year with the election of crypto-friendly U.S. President Donald Trump, cryptocurrencies – along ‌with stocks – plummeted in April on his tariff announcements. They quickly rebounded, with bitcoin ‌hitting an all-time peak above $126,000 in early October. But just days later, on October 10, the market plunged again when Trump announced a new tariff on Chinese imports and threatened export controls on critical software. That sparked more than $19 billion worth of liquidations across leveraged crypto market positions, the largest liquidation in crypto history.The world’s main stock benchmarks have also had a turbulent year, repeatedly hitting record peaks and then pulling back as worries over tariffs, interest rates and a possible AI bubble whipsawed ‍markets. “In 2025, the market showed that bitcoin increasingly exhibits the characteristics of a risk asset within the global financial system, with a notable correlation to the U.S. equity market during multiple periods,” said Linh Tran, a senior market analyst at XS.com. Analysts say bitcoin’s gyrations in 2025 increasingly tracked stock market sentiment as traditional retail and institutional investors jumped into cryptocurrencies, which next year may be ​even more closely tethered to factors driving stocks ‌and other risk assets, such as monetary policy shifts and nervousness over the lofty valuations of AI-related stocks. Historically, bitcoin and stocks did not move in tandem because crypto was seen as an alternative investment. But ​with broader crypto adoption by traditional retail investors and some institutions, the correlation looks to be strengthening, analysts said.The crypto ⁠industry notched major regulatory wins in the U.S. under ‌the first year of the Trump administration, including the Securities and Exchange Commission’s swift move to dismiss Biden-era lawsuits against ​Coinbase, Binance and others, as well as the passage of a landmark law creating federal rules for dollar-pegged crypto tokens. But crypto market structure legislation and carve-outs from SEC rules that should fix core, longstanding problems ‍for the industry are yet to come, threatening to sap the industry’s celebratory mood, according to multiple industry executives. Trump courted industry ⁠cash pledging to be a “crypto president,” and his family’s own crypto ventures have helped to propel the sector into the mainstream, say executives. Crypto companies ​and executives donated more than $245 million ‌in the 2024 election cycle to promote pro-crypto candidates including Trump, according to Federal Election Commission ‍data. title: US Stocks Slip As Gold Rebounds On Year-End Session
body: US stocks ended lower on Tuesday, the penultimate trading day of 2025, while gold and silver staged a recovery after a sharp pullback from record highs. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 94.87 points, or 0.20%, to 48,367.06. The S&P 500 declined 9.51 points, or 0.14%, to 6,896.23, while the Nasdaq Composite dropped 55.27 points, or 0.23%, to 23,419.08 in a light-volume pre-holiday session. “At the end of the day, solid corporate profits can make up for a lot of sins,” said Ryan Detrick, chief market strategist at Carson Group in Omaha. “And in 2025, strong earnings have justified the bull market that we’ve seen this year.” “We see no major cracks to suggest a recession is coming,” he added. “We’re optimistic the labour market will get better and this bull market will probably have another few tricks up its sleeve in 2026.” Minutes from the US Federal Reserve’s final meeting of the year showed most policymakers agreed to cut rates, but revealed deep divisions over risks to the economy. “The Fed minutes only further confirm that there are really two sides to potential future policy and the divide likely will continue to grow,” Detrick said. Gold rebounded 0.3% to US$4,344.75 an ounce, while silver surged 5.4% to US$76.20 per ounce. The precious metals had faced profit-taking after a stellar year, with gold set for its best annual gain since 1979. Global markets showed mixed moves. MSCI’s gauge of stocks across the globe fell 0.06% to 1,020.07, while emerging market equities rose 0.17% to 1,404.09. MSCI’s Asia-Pacific ex-Japan index gained 0.13% to 722.72, whereas Japan’s Nikkei dropped 0.37% to 50,339.48. European shares, however, hit new record highs amid thin year-end trading. Oil prices remained steady amid fading hopes of a Russia-Ukraine peace deal and Middle East tensions, with US crude at US$57.95 per barrel and Brent at US$61.92 per barrel. In currencies, the dollar held gains following the Fed minutes, rising 0.23% to 98.23 on the dollar index, though it remains on track for its steepest annual decline in eight years. Bitcoin advanced 0.74% to US$87,888.55, while Ethereum rose 0.71% to US$2,955.35. US Treasury yields were mostly stable. The 10-year note yield ticked up 0.4 basis points to 4.12%, the 30-year yield edged 0.1 basis points higher to 4.805% and the 2-year note yield fell 1.9 basis points to 3.446%. body: Gold prices steadied in Asian trade on Tuesday, following a sharp retreat from record highs as investors trimmed year-end positions and awaited fresh signals from U.S. monetary policy. Spot gold rose 0.7% to US$4,362.30 an ounce by 00:12 ET, while U.S. gold futures advanced 0.8% to US$4,378.75. The volatility has been even more pronounced in silver, where thin holiday trading magnified moves. After hitting a record of around US$84 an ounce, silver plunged 8.7% in its biggest one-day drop since August 2020, before bouncing about 2.5% to US$74.1 on Tuesday. “We’ve had a cooling in the precious metals, but I don’t think this trend is over,” said Tony Sycamore, analyst at IG, noting that the Chicago Mercantile Exchange raised margin requirements, the cash traders must post to hold futures positions. Forced selling can intensify when exchanges raise margins and liquidity is thin, turning routine profit-taking into rapid, outsized price swings. In U.S. trading on Monday, spot gold fell 4.5% to US$4,330.79 after reaching a record US$4,549.71 on Friday, while February futures settled 4.6% lower at US$4,343.60. Platinum and palladium also tumbled, with platinum down 14.5% to US$2,096.53 and palladium down 15.9% to US$1,617.47. Gold has risen roughly 65% in 2025. Interest rate expectations remain a key driver for bullion. Gold, which does not yield interest, benefits when rates are expected to fall, as this reduces the opportunity cost of holding it. Conversely, expectations of higher rates can weigh on prices. Investors are also balancing profit-taking against persistent safe-haven demand amid rising geopolitical and military tensions. Global political risks added support for precious metals. In Europe, Russia’s Vladimir Putin told U.S. President Donald Trump that Moscow would review its stance in peace negotiations after what the Kremlin described as a Ukrainian drone attack on one of Putin’s residences; Ukraine denied the claims. Meanwhile, China staged its largest military drills around Taiwan, firing rockets to simulate a blockade, prompting criticism from Taipei. Looking ahead, investors are awaiting minutes from the Federal Reserve’s latest policy meeting, due later on Tuesday. These could influence the U.S. dollar and Treasury yields, affecting demand for gold, silver and platinum. For silver and platinum, industrial demand adds another layer of volatility, as growth expectations and manufacturing hedges adjust alongside macroeconomic shifts. title: Asian Stocks Mixed On Final Trading Day, With KLSE Shedding Gains
body: Asian stocks were mixed at the start of the final trading day of 2025 on Wednesday (Dec 31), with some tracking Wall Street losses as investors eased towards the New Year break. Trading remained thin in the holiday-shortened week, though precious metals appeared to steady after seeing a sharp pullback from recent record highs.Markets in Hong Kong and Australia edged lower while Shanghai and Taipei saw small morning gains in what has been a strong year for worldwide markets. The movements came after Wall Street’s main indices closed slightly lower on Tuesday as worries over valuations of artificial intelligence stocks lingered.Still, US indices remained on track for solid gains over 2025 as a whole, and markets in Asia similarly enjoyed a healthy year. Seoul’s Kospi climbed more than 75 per cent and Tokyo’s Nikkei 225 more than 26 per cent over 2025. Both markets were closed on Wednesday.Official data showed factory activity in China ticked up slightly in December, a silver lining to an otherwise lacklustre end to the year for the world’s second-largest economy. On the local front, the KLSE gave away the gains dropping 12 points to 1,672 diminishing hopes of a 1,680 closing for the year. The Federal Reserve’s monetary easing in the second half of this year has been a key driver of the global market improvements, compounding a surge in the tech sector on the back of the vast amounts of cash pumped into AI. Minutes of the Fed’s recent policy meeting in December indicated that most of its officials see future rate cuts as appropriate, if inflation cools over time as expected. Some of the biggest recent movement has come with precious metals like gold thanks to their status as a safe-haven investment amid geopolitical unrest. Both gold and silver climbed to records in the past week, though decreased in recent days. Gold sat at about US$4,370 per ounce on Wednesday, and silver at US$74.96. title: Wall Street Slips Into Final Week As Tech Stocks Retreat
body: Wall Street’s main indexes closed lower on Monday, starting the final week of the year on a softer footing as technology heavyweights pulled back after driving recent record highs. The S&P 500 fell 24.20 points, or 0.35%, to 6,905.74, while the Nasdaq Composite dropped 118.75 points, or 0.50%, to 23,474.35. The Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 249.04 points, or 0.51%, to 48,461.93. Technology stocks weighed on the broader market, with the information technology sector leading declines. Nvidia slipped 1.2% while Palantir Technologies fell 2.4%, reflecting profit-taking after last week’s rally that pushed the S&P 500 to record levels. “This is (not) the beginning of the end of the tech dominance, it’ll turn out to be a buying opportunity,” said Hank Smith, director and head of investment strategy at Haverford Trust. “A big reason for that is the top tech names, excluding Tesla, do not have challenging valuations given their growth rate, the moat around their business and their financial strength, which is unparalleled.” Tesla dropped 3.3% after reaching a record high last week, dragging the consumer discretionary sector lower. Materials stocks also slipped as precious metal miners fell, with silver retreating sharply after briefly topping US$80 an ounce, while gold eased following consecutive record highs last week. Energy stocks bucked the broader trend, rising nearly 1% in line with a 2% increase in oil prices. Bank stocks pulled back after a strong year-to-date rally, with Citigroup sliding 1.9% despite having gained nearly 68% so far this year. The pullback came as the S&P 500 hovered within 1% of the 7,000-point mark, while the Dow had posted a record closing high last week. Some investors had been hoping for a seasonal “Santa Claus rally”, which typically sees gains in the final trading days of the year and early January. Despite Monday’s decline, all three major indexes remained on track for solid monthly gains, with the Dow and S&P 500 poised for an eighth straight month of advances. The bull market that began in October 2022 remained intact, supported by optimism around artificial intelligence, expected interest rate cuts and a resilient economy. Looking ahead, investors will be watching minutes from the Federal Reserve’s previous meeting and weekly jobless claims data in an otherwise quiet week for economic releases. In individual stocks, DigitalBridge surged 9.6% after Japan’s SoftBank Group agreed to acquire the digital infrastructure investor in a US$4 billion deal. Market breadth was negative, with declining stocks outnumbering advancers on both the NYSE and Nasdaq, while trading volume stood at 13.08 billion shares, below the recent 20-day average. title: Pop Mart Shares Fall On Signs Of Cooling Labubu Demand
body: Pop Mart International Group Ltd shares fell sharply on Tuesday, marking the firm’s biggest drop in three weeks after reports suggested waning reseller demand for its Labubu toys. The Hong Kong-listed company’s shares dropped as much as 6.2%, making it one of the worst performers on the MSCI Asia-Pacific Index. Media reports indicated some scalpers had paused purchases following price swings in China’s secondary market, signalling softening appetite for the collectible dolls. The slump, which began in August, has sent Pop Mart shares down around 44%, wiping more than US$25 billion off its market value. Despite the recent decline, the stock has more than doubled this year, with the company valued at roughly four times larger than Japanese peer Sanrio Co. “With lingering investor worries that Pop Mart’s product buzz may be cooling, such reports of waning demand tend to hit the shares hard,” said Kenny Ng, strategist at China Everbright Securities International Co Ltd. Data from toy resale platform Qiandao showed average prices for full sets of mini Labubus or the Big Into Energy series have fallen below official retail levels. Amid the softening demand, Pop Mart is expanding its portfolio to other intellectual property characters, including Crybaby, Twinkle Twinkle and Hirono dolls. The Crybaby line recently held an exhibit in Shanghai as part of this push. Some analysts suggested the decline also reflects profit-taking among investors rotating out of China’s “new consumption” stocks. On Tuesday, Chinese jewellery maker Laopu Gold Co. fell more than 6%, while bubble tea chain Mixue Group dropped nearly 4%. title: Hang Seng Index Futures Correction Seen Attracting Dip Buyers
body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has maintained its positive trading bias on Hang Seng Index Futures (HSIF), viewing the latest pullback as a consolidation phase rather than a reversal of the broader uptrend. The HSIF eased 175 points on Monday to close at 25,635 points after opening at 25,904 points. The index initially climbed to an intraday high of 26,114 points before reversing to a session low of 25,615 points. The move resulted in a bearish candlestick formation. In the evening session, the contract slipped a further 32 points to last trade at 25,603 points. RHB Research said the retreat reflected selling pressure near the 50-day simple moving average line. However, the research house noted that the correction remains orderly. The relative strength index has softened but continues to hover around the 50% level, signalling that underlying bullish momentum is still intact. The 20-day and 50-day SMA lines continue to slope higher, reinforcing the prevailing uptrend. As long as the HSIF stays above the 25,000-point support level, RHB expects the correction to attract dip-buying interest and potentially set the stage for another test of the 26,500-point resistance. Traders were advised to maintain the long position initiated at 21,416 points, which was the close on April 14. To manage risk, RHB Research has set the stop-loss level at 25,000 points. Immediate support is identified at 25,000 points, followed by 24,300 points, while resistance levels are seen at 26,500 points and subsequently 27,400 points. title: Copper Prices Slip As Silver And Gold Retreat from Record Highs
body: Asian commodity markets steadied on Tuesday, with copper following a pullback in precious metals after silver and gold retreated from record levels. Silver, which hit a fresh high of around US$84 per ounce, fell 8.7% in its biggest one-day drop since August 2020, prompting gold and copper to decline alongside it. Silver rebounded 2.5% to US$74.10 per ounce on Tuesday, still poised for a remarkable annual gain of 156%. Gold edged up 0.7% to US$4,361 per ounce. The movements were attributed to thin liquidity in a holiday-shortened week, stop-loss triggers, and the Chicago Mercantile Exchange raising margin requirements, according to Tony Sycamore, analyst at IG in Sydney. “We’ve had a cooling in the precious metals, but I don’t think this trend is over. We still got deficits. We still got nation stockpiling. We’ve got export restrictions,” he said. Copper, which closely tracks movements in other metals, was affected by the same volatility, reflecting investor caution amid ongoing global uncertainties. Geopolitical tensions added to market jitters. Russia accused Ukraine of attacking President Vladimir Putin’s residence, while U.S. President Donald Trump indicated support for a possible strike on Iran. China conducted 10 hours of live-firing exercises around Taiwan, further fuelling risk sentiment. Despite the commodity swings, Asian shares were largely steady. MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan inched up 0.1%, while Japan’s Nikkei eased 0.1%. China’s CSI 300 rose 0.2%, and Hong Kong’s Hang Seng gained 0.4%. Oil prices held onto overnight gains, with Brent crude at US$61.92 per barrel and U.S. West Texas Intermediate at US$58.01, as markets weighed geopolitical risks against year-end positioning. title: Stock Today: Tanco Rises Nearly 1% Amid Focus On PD Development
body: Tanco Holdings Bhd shares edged higher in early trading, extending recent gains following the company’s latest strategic move in its port development plans. As at 12.21 pm, the property group’s shares rose one sen or 0.88% to RM1.14, after opening at RM1.13. The counter traded between an intraday high of RM1.15 and a low of RM1.13, with volume standing at 28.24 million shares. Buying interest outweighed selling pressure, with buy volume at 15.74 million shares compared with sell volume of 2.83 million shares. The stock has gained momentum over recent months, climbing from around 90.5 sen in early November, as investors digested developments surrounding its proposed Smart AI Container Port in Dickson Bay, Port Dickson. Last week, Tanco announced that its 79%-owned subsidiary, Midports Holdings Sdn Bhd, had appointed Hong Kong-based Ocean Bridge International Ports Management Co Ltd as the operator and manager of the proposed port. The agreement covers day-to-day terminal operations once the project is developed, while ownership and ultimate disposal rights remain with Midports. The proposed facility is expected to adopt AI-enabled automation technologies, including terminal operating systems to support container logistics, cargo handling and related services. Ocean Bridge will also provide technical advisory support, ranging from terminal design optimisation and feasibility studies to personnel training and port commissioning. Market participants have been watching the counter closely, with the port initiative seen as a longer-term catalyst that could diversify earnings beyond Tanco’s core property business, although execution and development timelines remain key factors for sentiment. title: Stock Today: KLK Hold Steady As JV With Mah Sing Supports Growth Outlook
body: Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd (KLK) opened flat, trading at RM20.00 as of 3.07 pm, with a volume of 434,700 shares. The stock’s intraday high reached RM20.18 while the low was RM19.98. Buy and sell orders stood at RM20.00 and RM20.02 respectively, according to Bursa Malaysia data. Market watchers note that KLK’s stability follows MBSB Investment Bank’s maintenance of a neutral call on the stock, with an unchanged target price of RM20.23. The research house highlighted KLK’s recent joint venture with Mah Sing to develop a 420-acre industrial park in Kulai, Johor, expected to generate a one-off profit of approximately RM131.5 million. KLK, through subsidiary Aura Muhibah Sdn Bhd, will hold a 40% stake in the newly formed MIDSB company, with Mah Sing taking the lead with 60%. The JV aims to transform 419.15 acres into an integrated industrial park within the Johor–Singapore Special Economic Zone, strategically located near Senai International Airport and accessible via the North–South Expressway. The deal, involving Mah Sing acquiring the land from KLK for RM273.9 million, is projected to provide recurring income and support future earnings growth. KLK management expects the net disposal gain to contribute 12.2 sen per share, which could be allocated for special dividends or reinvestment into brownfield estates. MBSB Research noted that the collaboration represents KLK’s second phase of pivoting into industrial land development, fitting its broader strategy of monetising land while maintaining a presence in high-growth projects. The research house maintained FY26F earnings forecasts and target price based on an EPS of 109.4 sen and a PER of 18.5 times, consistent with KLK’s near five-year historical average. title: Stock Today: ITMAX Edges Lower Amid New DBKL Smart City Contract
body: ITMAX System Bhd (ITMAX) slipped 0.83% to RM4.76 yesterday, with 211,000 shares traded as investors weighed the company’s latest contract wins and future growth potential. The technology group recently received a Letter of Acceptance (LOA) from Dewan Bandaraya Kuala Lumpur (DBKL) to provide operations and maintenance services for the city’s smart traffic light system, valued at RM42 million over three years. The contract covers roughly 600 traffic lights, with commencement pending DBKL’s Work Order Letter. Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB) Research noted that the contract is expected to contribute recurring annual revenue of about RM14 million and carry a net profit margin of 40% to 45%, aligning with ITMAX’s existing CCTV projects. The research house said the deal demonstrates ITMAX’s established relationship with DBKL, positioning the group to secure further smart city initiatives locally. HLIB highlighted the ongoing commercialisation of ITMAX’s 5,000-unit CCTV rollout for DBKL, expected to be fully operational by the first half of 2026, generating estimated revenue of RM60 million and profit of RM24 million. Additional expansions could see 5,000 to 10,000 more units deployed by 2028, supporting ITMAX’s long-term earnings growth. The research house also sees potential upside from CCTV projects in Johor, particularly across Greater Johor Bahru, with ITMAX already managing about 1,700 units in the state. HLIB maintained its “Buy” call on ITMAX with an unchanged target price of RM5.74, citing the company’s role in Malaysia’s smart city transformation and its capacity to monetise infrastructure through advanced applications such as digital twins and traffic analytics. As Malaysia continues its urban digitalisation drive, ITMAX’s stock performance is likely to remain closely linked to the pace of smart city project rollouts and broader adoption of city-wide technology initiatives. body: The Malaysian ringgit continued its upward momentum on Monday, marking a 12th consecutive session of gains as traders prepared for a holiday-shortened week leading into the New Year. Immediate support levels are at 25,000 points and 24,300 points, while resistance is seen at 26,500 points and 27,400 points. The bank’s analysis indicates that the HSIF continues to favour bullish strategies in the near term, with the market remaining resilient above key support levels. title: Gold Dips In Ringgit, But Bulls Still Shine Globally
body: Gold prices in Malaysia fell on Monday, trading at RM584.10 per gram, down RM6.08 or 1.03% from the previous session. Despite the local dip, gold remains up 57.75% over the past year and over 140% in the last five years, reflecting strong investor demand amid global economic uncertainty. The decline in Malaysian prices contrasts with continued gains on the COMEX in the United States, where gold added US$49.90 on Friday to close at US$4,552.70 per ounce. The commodity opened at US$4,523.50, set a day’s low at US$4,518 and reached a high of US$4,584. RHB Investment Bank Bhd noted that strong technical signals, including rising relative strength indicators and upward-trending 20- and 50-day moving averages, point to potential resistance levels at US$4,700 and US$4,800. Traders holding the long position initiated at US$3,562.90 are advised to manage risk with stop-losses at US$4,000, while the first support level is seen at US$4,200. The overall setup signals that bulls remain in control globally, even as local RM-based prices are affected by currency movements and domestic market factors. Silver also declined locally, down 3.81% to RM12.22 per gram, though it has risen 148% over the past year, in line with the broader precious metals rally. Investors in Malaysia are keeping a close eye on the US dollar, global supply and geopolitical developments, balancing safe-haven demand with domestic market trends. title: Crypto Markets End The Year Cautiously As Bitcoin, Ethereum Consolidate
body: The cryptocurrency market is closing out the year on a guarded note, with Bitcoin and Ethereum trading sideways amid thinning liquidity, year-end profit-taking and subdued investor sentiment. As the final trading sessions of the year unfold, the world’s two largest digital assets are showing resilience above key support levels, but lack the momentum needed for a decisive breakout. Bitcoin is trading just below US$89,000, consolidating within a narrow range after recent pullbacks. The price action reflects a market caught between long-term conviction and short-term caution, as institutional and retail participants rebalance portfolios ahead of the new year. Despite intraday volatility, Bitcoin has managed to defend critical psychological support near the US$88,000 level. Analysts note that a sustained break below this zone could invite sharper downside pressure, particularly during the low-volume holiday period. Conversely, a move back above resistance around US$92,000-US$94,000 could restore bullish momentum as liquidity returns in early January. Ethereum, on the other hand, is hovering near the US$3,000 mark, a level that has emerged as both technical support and resistance. While Ethereum has shown relative stability compared to broader market weakness, buyers have struggled to generate sufficient follow-through to confirm a breakout. Market participants are watching closely to see whether Ethereum can maintain support above the US$2,800-US$2,900 range. A decisive move higher could reignite optimism around Ethereum’s long-term fundamentals, while failure to hold these levels may extend the consolidation phase into the new year. Overall, while momentum has cooled, market observers caution against interpreting the current pause as a structural breakdown. Historically, year-end consolidation has often preceded renewed activity once institutional participation resumes in January. Bitcoin continues to anchor the market as the dominant store-of-value asset, while Ethereum’s broader ecosystem and utility keep it firmly on investors’ radar. The year ends with crypto markets subdued but structurally intact, setting the stage for a more decisive move when liquidity and confidence return in the new year. title: Bursa Slips At Midday On Profit-Taking, Lack of Catalysts
body: Bursa Malaysia retreated in the morning session as investors locked in profits on selected blue chips, with trading sentiment dampened by the absence of fresh market catalysts. At 12:30pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) slid 4.93 points, or 0.29%, to 1,672.17 from its close of 1,677.10 on Dec 26. Market breadth was firmly negative, with decliners overwhelming gainers by 574 to 267. Another 530 counters were unchanged, while 1,362 stocks were untraded and 58 suspended. Trading activity was moderate, with 1.07 billion shares changing hands for a value of RM700.56 million. Most key indices ended lower, with the FBM EMAS shedding 28.48 points to 12,311.40, the FBM SHA down 16.68 points to 12,088.93, the FBM 70 easing 10.27 points to 16,792.30 and F4GBM declined 2.6 points to 986.36. On the actives list, Pharmaniaga drew heavy interest despite ending flat at 30 sen, while Tanco Holdings edged up one sen to RM1.14. Insights Analytics stood out, jumping 11 sen to RM1.06, making it both one of the most active and a top gainer. Zetrix AI and Avangaad were slightly weaker. Gains were led by heavyweight Nestlé, which climbed RM1.50 to RM116.50, followed by Boustead Plantations and Dutch Lady. On the downside, Allianz Malaysia, MISC and MPI were among the notable laggards. Overall, cautious positioning and profit-taking defined the midday trade, with investors awaiting clearer cues to drive the market’s next move. Investors showed caution, taking modest profits while monitoring macro indicators and out-of-session developments. Financials were mixed, with banks and defensive names offering limited support as bargain hunting emerged in select industrial and real estate counters. Notable stock-specific action included renewed interest in large caps such as DBS Group Holdings, which saw sustained interest from long-term investors reflecting capital return strategies and dividend appeal, supporting broader sentiment around core Singapore financial stocks. title: Silver Smashes US$77 As Precious Metals Rally On Rate-Cut Bets
body: Precious metals surged to fresh records on Dec 26, led by a blistering rally in silver, as expectations of US rate cuts and persistent geopolitical tensions supercharged safe-haven demand. Spot silver leapt 7.5% to US$77.30 an oz after touching an all-time high of US$77.40, capping a staggering 167% year-to-date gain. Tight supply, its designation as a US critical mineral and strong investment inflows have fuelled the metal’s breakout. Gold followed suit, rising 1.2% to US$4,531.41 after scaling a record US$4,549.71 earlier in the session. US gold futures settled 1.1% higher at US$4,552.70. Markets are increasingly pricing in two Federal Reserve rate cuts in 2026, with hopes of a more dovish central bank stance adding momentum. Gold is now on track for its strongest annual performance since 1979. Platinum stole some of the spotlight, jumping 9.8% to US$2,437.72 after hitting a record high, while palladium surged 14% to a more than three-year peak. Physical demand showed strain at elevated prices, with gold discounts in India widening to six-month highs, though China’s discounts narrowed sharply. Still, the broader trend remains firmly bullish, with all precious metals posting weekly gains and platinum logging its strongest weekly rise on record. title: Oil Edges Higher Amid Venezuela Pressure, Nigeria Strikes
body: Oil prices ticked up on Dec 26 as geopolitical tensions flared, with the US ramping economic pressure on Venezuelan oil shipments and carrying out airstrikes against Islamic State militants in northwest Nigeria at the request of the Nigerian government. By 0114 GMT, Brent crude rose 24 cents, or 0.4%, to US$62.48 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) added 23 cents, also 0.4%, to US$58.58. Both Venezuela and Nigeria are key oil producers, and the Nigerian airstrikes heightened supply-side concerns, despite the country’s main oilfields being in the south. The White House emphasised economic measures over military action, ordering US forces to enforce a “quarantine” on Venezuelan oil for at least two months. Still, prices remain on track for their steepest annual slide since 2020, with Brent and WTI down roughly 16% and 18% respectively, amid expectations that supply will outpace demand next year. Further supply concerns emerged as Kazakhstan’s oil shipments via the Caspian Pipeline are set to fall by a third in December after a Ukrainian drone attack hit the main export terminal. Market watchers are now eyeing the US Energy Information Administration inventory data, delayed by the Christmas holiday, for fresh insight into demand trends in the world’s top oil consumer.
