title: Wall Street Clocks Fresh Records As Santa Rally Kicks Off
body: US stocks closed higher on Dec 24, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500 finishing at record highs in a broad-based rally during a thin, holiday-shortened session. Reuters reported that all three major indexes notched their fifth straight day of gains, lifted by a rebound in artificial intelligence-linked names and continued confidence in the economy’s resilience. The Dow rose 288.75 points, or 0.6%, to 48,731.16, while the S&P 500 gained 0.32% to 6,932.05. The Nasdaq Composite added 0.22% to 23,613.31. Trading volumes were muted ahead of the Christmas holiday, with US markets set to remain closed on Dec 25. Stocks found support from easing jobless claims data and expectations that the Federal Reserve could deliver around 50 basis points of rate cuts next year, even as a January move appears unlikely. Financials led sector gains, while energy was the lone decliner. Micron surged 3.8% to a record close, extending its post-forecast rally, while Nike jumped 4.6% after Apple CEO Tim Cook disclosed a sizable share purchase. The rally has fuelled hopes of a traditional “Santa Claus rally”, which officially began on Dec 24 and runs through early January. Despite bouts of volatility this year driven by tariffs, valuation worries and shifting rate expectations, the bull market that began in late 2022 remains intact, with Wall Street’s fear gauge hovering near year-lows and all three major indexes on track for a third straight annual gain. title: Wall Street Hits Fresh Records On Strong US Growth Data
body: Wall Street closed higher, with all three major benchmarks advancing after stronger-than-expected US economic data reinforced confidence in the resilience of the world’s largest economy. The S&P 500 rose 31.30 points, or 0.46%, to 6,909.79, surpassing its previous high to notch a fresh record close, supported by gains in growth stocks. The S&P 500 Growth Index climbed 0.8%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average added 79.73 points, or 0.16%, to end at 48,442.41, while the Nasdaq Composite gained 133.02 points, or 0.57%, to 23,561.84. Investor sentiment was lifted after data showed the US economy expanded at a faster pace than expected in the third quarter. Early estimates indicated gross domestic product grew at an annualised rate of 4.3%, well above economists’ expectations of 3.3%, driven largely by robust consumer spending. Some US economic releases have been delayed due to a prolonged federal government shutdown. “We’re still in this period of playing catch-up with economic data and GDP is dated … But it’s showing strength in the economy, and strength that’s above expectations,” said Tim Ghriskey, senior portfolio strategist at Ingalls & Snyder in New York. Beyond the US, MSCI’s global equity index gained 0.45% to 1,020.10, also on track for a record close, while Europe’s STOXX 600 ended 0.34% higher earlier in the session. In corporate news, US-listed shares of Novo Nordisk jumped 7.3% after the US Food and Drug Administration approved its weight-loss pill, strengthening the Danish drugmaker’s position in the competitive obesity treatment market. US Treasury yields were mixed. The benchmark 10-year yield edged down 0.4 basis points to 4.167%, while the 30-year yield fell 1.8 basis points to 4.8252%. In contrast, the 2-year yield rose 2.9 basis points to 3.532%, reflecting shifting expectations for Federal Reserve policy. title: Platinum Surges To Record High
body: Platinum prices jumped to an all-time high on Tuesday, extending a broad rally across precious metals as strong industrial demand, supportive policy developments and a weaker US dollar boosted sentiment. Spot platinum rose 6.8% to US$2,268.95 an ounce, after earlier scaling a record high of US$2,274.10. The metal’s sharp advance outpaced gains in gold and silver, while palladium also climbed strongly, rising 6.5% to a three-year high of US$1,874.22. Market participants noted a resurgence of optimism surrounding platinum group metals (PGMs), which are widely utilised in automotive catalytic converters to mitigate harmful emissions. Sentiment was further lifted after the European Commission earlier this month published plans to abandon an effective 2035 ban on combustion engine cars. “This news is a steroid jab for PGMs, prolonging their use in catalytic converters,” analysts at Mitsubishi said in a note this week. The broader precious metals complex remained well supported, with a weaker US dollar in a holiday-shortened trading week making dollar-denominated metals more attractive to overseas buyers. Safe-haven demand and expectations of lower US yields have also underpinned the sector. Geopolitical tensions added to the supportive backdrop. US President Donald Trump last week ordered a “blockade” of all sanctioned oil tankers entering and leaving Venezuela, keeping markets on edge and reinforcing interest in hard assets. title: Asian Shares Rise As Commodities Hit Record Highs In Year-End Rally
body: Asian equities edged higher on Wednesday, closing out a year dominated by artificial intelligence-driven gains, while commodities such as gold and silver extended their bullish run to new all-time highs. Spot gold climbed 0.8 per cent to $4,524 per ounce, marking a 72 per cent gain for 2025, while silver surged 1.2 per cent to $72.27 per ounce, set for its best annual performance ever with nearly a 150 per cent increase. Japan’s Nikkei advanced 0.4 per cent, bringing its yearly gain to 26 per cent, while South Korea outperformed with a remarkable 72 per cent surge. MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan rose 0.3 per cent, recording a 26 per cent increase for the year, its strongest showing since 2017. Overnight on Wall Street, the S&P 500 hit a closing record as the long-anticipated Santa Claus rally took hold. Data showing the U.S. economy expanded faster than expected in the third quarter lifted risk sentiment, though it weighed on bonds. “As equity markets enter the fourth year of a bull market, our underlying market call remains constructive,” said Scott Chronert, a U.S. equity strategist at Citi. “Yet, high performance dispersion within themes, sectors, and market cap is expected.” In currency markets, the yen strengthened for a third consecutive session amid intervention risk from Japanese authorities, with the dollar retreating 0.3 per cent to 155.78 yen. The euro remained steady at $1.18, after rallying 14 per cent this year, while the dollar fell around 10 per cent against major peers over 2025. U.S. Treasuries remained steady, with two-year yields at 3.532 per cent and 10-year yields at 4.1589 per cent, reflecting declines of 72 and 42 basis points respectively for the year. Oil prices held firm in early Asian trade, with Brent crude futures at $62.41 per barrel, though down 16 per cent over 2025. title: Wall Street Rises As Tech Rebound Lifts Holiday-Shortened Session
body: US equities ended higher on Monday, opening a holiday-shortened week on a positive note as renewed strength in technology stocks helped lift most sectors of the market. Gains were broad-based, with all but one of the 11 S&P 500 sectors closing in positive territory. Materials and energy led advances as commodity prices rose, while financials gained 1.3% to finish at a record. The technology sector added 0.4%. Chipmakers were a key driver. Nvidia shares rose and provided the largest boost to the S&P 500 after Reuters reported the company had told Chinese clients it aims to start shipping its second-most powerful AI chips to China before the Lunar New Year holiday in mid-February. Micron Technology climbed 4%, extending a rally sparked late last week by stronger-than-expected forecasts, while the Philadelphia SE Semiconductor Index rose 1.1%. “I don’t necessarily think it’s going to go much higher; it’s going to continue to churn,” said Ken Polcari, partner and chief market strategist at Slatestone Wealth in Jupiter, Florida. “Today we’re trading higher, but I wouldn’t be surprised if we back off again and then we just rally again right into about where we are.” The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 227.79 points, or 0.47%, to 48,362.68. The S&P 500 gained 43.99 points, or 0.64%, to 6,878.49, while the Nasdaq Composite added 121.21 points, or 0.52%, to 23,428.83. The S&P 500 and Dow now sit less than 1% below their record closing highs set on Dec 11. Market sentiment has been supported by optimism around artificial intelligence, signs of resilience in the US economy and expectations of monetary policy easing. These factors have outweighed concerns over US tariffs and placed all three major indexes on track for a third straight year of gains, with the S&P 500 up 17% so far this year. December has historically been a strong period for equities. Since 1950, the so-called Santa Claus rally has seen the S&P 500 rise an average of 1.3% over the last five trading days of the year and the first two trading days of January, according to the Stock Trader’s Almanac. This period begins on Wednesday and runs through Jan 5. Trading conditions remained thin ahead of the holidays. The CBOE volatility index closed at 14.08, its lowest level since Dec 13, 2024. Volume on US exchanges totalled 14.57 billion shares, below the 20-day average of 16.9 billion. US markets will close early at 1 pm ET on Wednesday and remain shut on Thursday for Christmas. “Tomorrow’s GDP number is going to be the last real piece of economic data that anyone really cares about,” Polcari said. Among individual movers, Tesla gained 1.6% after chief executive Elon Musk’s 2018 pay package was restored by the Delaware Supreme Court. Warner Bros Discovery rose 3.5% after Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison agreed to provide a personal guarantee of US$40.4 billion in equity financing for Paramount Skydance’s offer to acquire the company, lifting Paramount shares by 4.3%. Clearwater Analytics Holdings surged 8.1% after a group of private equity firms led by Permira and Warburg Pincus agreed to acquire the investment and accounting software maker for about US$8.4 billion, including debt. Advancing stocks outnumbered decliners by a ratio of 2.15 to 1 on the New York Stock Exchange and 1.61 to 1 on the Nasdaq. The S&P 500 recorded 42 new 52-week highs and five new lows, while the Nasdaq Composite logged 113 new highs and 128 new lows. title: Stock Today: Tenaga Nasional Ticks Higher As Grid Reliability Push Stays In Focus
body: Tenaga Nasional Bhd shares edged slightly higher in afternoon trade, reflecting steady investor sentiment as the utility group continues to advance network upgrades and leadership reforms. At 2.43 pm, Tenaga Nasional rose two sen or 0.15% to RM13.56, after opening at RM13.58. The stock traded between an intraday high of RM13.60 and a low of RM13.44, with volume at 24,436 lots. Buying interest was seen at RM13.56, while selling pressure stood at RM13.58. The last adjusted closing price was RM13.54. The modest uptick came as the group recently awarded a RM177.36 million contract to a consortium involving MN Holdings Berhad for the upgrading of a 132-kilovolt submarine power cable system linking PMU Kuala Perlis to PMU Teluk Apau No. 1. The project, which takes effect from Dec 22, 2025, includes the supply, installation, testing and commissioning of new primary equipment and a 150MVA submarine cable, alongside associated civil works and network connections. The works are expected to be completed within 450 days and form part of TNB’s ongoing efforts to strengthen grid reliability and system resilience. Separately, Tenaga Nasional has also announced refinements to its senior leadership structure , introducing the roles of Senior Chief Network Officer and Senior Chief Strategy & Sustainability Officer. The move is aimed at sharpening execution, reinforcing governance and supporting long-term strategic planning. The leadership enhancements are aligned with the group’s Reimagining TNB 2.0 roadmap, which underpins its transition towards a more sustainable and resilient energy system, in line with Malaysia’s net-zero ambition by 2050. title: Stock Today: Gamuda Gains On Strong Australian Project Wins And Robust Orderbook
body: Gamuda Bhd closed slightly higher at RM4.98, up RM0.01 or 0.20%, with 83.89 million shares traded. The stock opened at RM4.97, touching a high of RM4.99 and a low of RM4.94. Analysts at RHB Investment Bank Bhd, MBSB Investment Bank Bhd and Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd have maintained BUY ratings on the construction group, citing strong orderbook growth and recent project wins in Australia. RHB Research sees a 41% upside to a target of RM7.00, HLIB maintains a target of RM6.88, while MBSB Research values the stock at RM6.35, highlighting the significance of the latest contracts. Gamuda recently secured two major projects in Australia, adding a combined RM8.03 billion to its orderbook. Its wholly-owned subsidiary, Gamuda Engineering Pty Ltd, won the Sydney Metro West Stations Package West worth AU$D2.7 billion (RM7.32 billion), covering the design and construction of five metro stations. Planning and design will start in January 2026, with major works expected by late 2026 or early 2027 and completion scheduled for May 2031, marking Gamuda’s largest single contract in Australia to date. Meanwhile, DT Infrastructure Pty Ltd, another Gamuda subsidiary, was awarded the Carmody’s Hill Wind Farm Balance of Plant contract worth AUD265 million (RM718 million), covering turbine foundations, access roads, drainage, crane hardstands, underground cabling and site preparation. Construction is set to begin in early 2026 over a 28-month period. These wins bring Gamuda’s total outstanding orderbook to a record RM45.9 billion, surpassing its end-of-year target of RM40–45 billion. Analysts note that the group maintains a strong pipeline across water, data centres, rail, highways and renewable energy, with a rolling RM50 billion worth of tenders providing visibility for 2026 and beyond. Despite trading at a premium to the Bursa Malaysia Construction Index, analysts believe Gamuda’s Australian expansion and recurring income potential support its valuations and upside potential. title: Sarawak Plantation’s Strategy Delivers Better Yield
body: MBSB Investment Bank Bhd has maintained a NEUTRAL call on Sarawak Plantation Bhd, with an unchanged target price of RM2.88, citing stable earnings visibility and operational resilience. The research house highlighted that despite brief wet weather disruptions, the company’s FY26 performance is expected to be supported by nearly 1,000 hectares of expanding harvestable area, declining production costs and improving scale efficiencies. MBSB Research noted production and yield growth as key drivers. Sarawak Plantation is guided to deliver approximately 360,000 tonnes of output in FY25, with a further 20-25% increase expected in FY26 as newly matured hectarage contributes. Yield has structurally improved from 16 metric tonnes per hectare in 2023 to an estimated over 18 metric tonnes per hectare in FY26. Nine-month FY25 figures already show an oil extraction rate (OER) averaging 19.37%, above the Sarawak average and expected to edge up to 19.6% in FY26. MBSB Research highlighted management’s plan to strengthen internal production. While external fresh fruit bunch (FFB) purchases are projected to rise in absolute terms, their proportion of total intake is expected to fall from under 50% currently to less than 40% in FY26. The research house said this strategy improves quality control, harvesting timing and OER while reducing margin volatility, noting the stark margin gap between estate operations at around 35% and mill-based activities at roughly 4%. Cost structures and labour dynamics were also emphasised. Despite fertiliser prices averaging about RM1,400 per metric tonne in FY25, partially offset by a firmer ringgit, the estimated cost of crude palm oil production is below RM2,700 per metric tonne, set to decline to under RM2,400 in FY26 as volumes scale and fixed costs dilute. Labour availability has largely normalised, and management continues to embed operational expertise through tighter field supervision, improved road maintenance and pest control, enhancing decision-making and stabilising yields. MBSB Research concluded that the company remains focused on harvesting efficiency, cost discipline, and estate-level productivity, rather than pursuing aggressive expansion or mergers and acquisitions, which underpins a resilient operating performance in the future. As of 10.09 am (23 Dec), the stock price is down 1.08% to RM2.75. title: Logistics Sector Benefits From Phased Port Tariff Adjustments
body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) maintained a NEUTRAL call on the transport and logistics sector, citing a decent third-quarter performance and stable earnings from key players. The research house reported 9M25 results were largely in line with expectations, with marine port operator Westports and logistics firm FM Global Logistics meeting forecasts, while TASCO underperformed due to a one-off tax adjustment. RHB Research noted that Westports, which accounts for 96.5% of sector coverage, showed steady performance and continues to benefit from phased port tariff adjustments. The first phase of a 15% increase at Port Klang took effect in July 2025, with a second 10% hike scheduled for January 2026. The house reported the tariff adjustments are expected to boost revenue visibility for FY26, as gateway customers are billed on tariffs with volume-based rebates. The outlook for Malaysia’s external sector was described as more encouraging despite ongoing global uncertainties. RHB Research highlighted resilient global container demand, Asia’s economic dynamism and the operational model of major liner alliances as factors underpinning steady transhipment activity. RHB Economics projects Malaysia’s GDP to grow 4.7% in 2026, supported by a 9.3% rise in exports driven by global and regional growth, developments in US tariff policies and the resilience of electronics and electrical exports. On stock preferences, the house retained a NEUTRAL stance on Westports, believing the current valuation already reflects the tariff adjustments. They favour logistics players, with TASCO as their Top Pick due to its diversified client base, varied business segments and the cushion provided by integrated logistics services tax incentives. Overall, sector earnings are expected to continue in line with projections, underpinned by moderate container volume growth and supportive policy measures from Budget 2026. title: Gold Shines Brightest Yet On Economic Uncertainty And Global Risks
body: Spot gold rose to US$4,459.60 an ounce, extending gains amid heightened geopolitical tensions and expectations of further US interest-rate cuts. The metal advanced 2.4% on Monday, marking its biggest one-day jump in over a month, as traders anticipated that the Federal Reserve may reduce borrowing costs next year. Lower interest rates typically boost the appeal of precious metals, which do not yield interest. Investor demand for safe-haven assets has been further reinforced by rising tensions in Venezuela, where the US has blockaded oil tankers in an effort to pressure President Nicolás Maduro’s government. As of 7.35 am in Singapore, spot gold was trading slightly lower at US$4,456.12 an ounce. Silver rose 0.3% to US$69.21 an ounce, close to its previous session’s record of US$69.4549. Platinum and palladium also gained, while the Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index fell 0.4% in the previous session. title: Gold Climbs As It Breaks US$4,400 Resistance
body: Gold prices in Malaysia rose, with the price per gram reaching RM586.27, up RM4.91 or 0.85%, while the per kilogram rate increased to RM586,271.64. This marked a continuation of a strong annual performance, with prices up 54.07% over the past year and more than 136% over five years. The surge in local gold prices follows robust demand in global markets. On the COMEX, gold climbed above the US$4,400 resistance to close at US$4,469.40, after starting the day at US$4,369.90. The commodity touched a low of US$4,367.90 before reaching a high of US$4,484.50, forming a long bullish candlestick, signalling strong buying momentum. RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) noted that the Bullish Marubozu pattern, combined with an upward-trending RSI, indicates that bulls are in control. “After the breakout at US$4,400, the bulls are setting their sights on the next resistance at US$4,500. In the event of profit-taking, the commodity may pull back towards the 20-day SMA line, with stronger support anticipated at US$4,200,” the report stated. RHB Research advised traders to retain long positions initiated at US$3,562.90, with a stop-loss set at US$4,000. On the upside, the next key resistances are projected at US$4,500 and US$4,700. Locally, the performance of gold in Malaysian Ringgit has been equally notable. Prices have gained 6.61% over the past 30 days, 28.38% over six months, and 850.60% over 20 years, reflecting both global trends and the Ringgit’s performance. title: Yen Hits Record Low As BOJ Keeps Cautious Tone After Rate Hike
body: The yen languished near a record low to the euro on Monday, after Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda stuck to his usual cautious rhetoric following an interest rate hike on Friday. The Japanese currency traded near an 11-month trough versus the U.S. dollar and just shy of a 17-month low on the Aussie.A warning of possible currency intervention on Monday had little immediate effect on the market. Japan’s top currency diplomat, Atsushi Mimura, said he was “concerned” about “one-sided and ‌sharp” foreign exchange moves, and cautioned that officials “will take appropriate actions against ‌excessive moves.” The BOJ raised the policy rate by a quarter point to a three-decade peak of 0.75 per cent on Friday, in a clearly telegraphed move. The accompanying statement signalled a readiness to continue tightening policy, but Ueda, at his news conference, stressed the timing and pace of further hikes depended on incoming economic data.The lack of any hawkish hints sent the yen tumbling 1.3 per cent versus the euro, 1.4 per cent against the greenback and 1.5 per cent against ‍the Aussie, even as it triggered a broad selloff in Japanese government bonds that sent the 10-year yield – which moves inversely to the price – soaring past the symbolic 2 per cent mark to the highest since 1999. “While the BOJ statement noted that real yields remain ‘significantly low’ – potentially signalling further tightening ahead – Governor Ueda’s press conference offered little new insight, ​reiterating a data-dependent approach,” Tony Sycamore, ‌an analyst at IG, wrote in a client note. “The absence of clearer guidance on the pace of future hikes disappointed markets, triggering yen selling.” A decisive break above 158 yen per U.S. ​dollar would open the way to the high for the year from January at around 158.87, he said. The U.S. dollar ⁠edged down 0.1 per cent to 157.56 yen on Monday, ‌but remained close to last month’s high of 157.90. The euro eased 0.1 per cent to 184.51 yen, staying within ​touching distance of Friday’s record peak at 184.75. The single currency was flat at $1.1714.The Aussie weakened slightly to 104.20 yen, but was not far from the 104.39 yen mark reached ‍earlier this month for the first time since July of last year. It rose 0.1 per cent to $0.6616. The Aussie-yen pair “still has ⁠fundamental support from solid risk sentiment and more recently, by wider interest rate differentials between Australian and Japanese ten-year government bond ​yields,” Commonwealth Bank of Australia analysts ‌wrote in a client note, forecasting a rise to 109 yen per Australian dollar ‍by ​March. title: MBSB Maintains Neutral Call On KLK
body: MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB Research) has maintained a NEUTRAL call on Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd (KLK) with an unchanged target price of RM20.23, citing the group’s latest joint venture with Mah Sing to develop a 420-acre industrial park in Kulai, Johor. The partnership is expected to deliver a one-off profit of approximately RM131.5 million, leveraging KLK’s sizeable landbank while tapping Mah Sing’s development expertise and brand equity in Johor. KLK, through its subsidiary Aura Muhibah Sdn Bhd, will hold a 40% stake in the newly formed MIDSB company, while Mah Sing leads with 60%. The JV will transform 419.15 acres into an integrated industrial park within the Johor–Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ), with Mah Sing acquiring the land from KLK for RM273.9 million, or around RM15 per square foot. The research house noted that despite the discount compared with other recent land sales, KLK’s retained stake positions it to benefit from future earnings growth and recurring income. The MIDSB project, with an estimated gross development value of RM2.26 billion, is strategically located near Senai International Airport and connected via the North–South Expressway, enhancing its attractiveness to industrial and commercial tenants. KLK’s management expects the net disposal gain to contribute 12.2 sen per share, which could be directed towards special dividends or reinvestment into brownfield estates. MBSB Research affirmed that the KLK–Mah Sing collaboration marks the second phase of KLK’s pivot into industrial land development and fits within its broader strategy of monetising land while maintaining a presence in high-growth projects. The house maintained earnings forecasts and target price for FY26F, based on an EPS of 109.4 sen and a PER of 18.5 times, in line with KLK’s near five-year historical average. As of 10.34 am, KLK’s stock price is down 0.60%, bringing it to RM19.88. title: Close Watch On Narrowing Yield Spread In The REIT Sector
body: MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB Research) has maintained a NEUTRAL call on the REIT sector, noting that while earnings remain commendable, yield compression continues to be a concern. The research house highlighted Sunway REIT as a top pick, maintaining a BUY call with a target price of RM2.34, citing its strong earnings momentum. REITs under coverage posted largely in-line results for 3QCY25, with four of six reporting earnings meeting expectations and two exceeding forecasts. Sunway REIT and Pavilion REIT delivered earnings surprises, with Sunway’s performance boosted by its hotel division, which benefited from strong demand for meetings, incentives, conferences and exhibitions (MICE), lifting occupancy rates and food and beverage revenue. Pavilion REIT’s upside was driven by higher-than-expected contributions from Elite Pavilion Mall and lower operating expenses. Among peers, Axis REIT, Al-`Aqar Healthcare REIT, IGB REIT and KLCCP Stapled Group met earnings expectations. Sunway REIT recorded the highest earnings per unit growth, up 29.6% year-on-year in 9MCY25, underpinned by resilient retail contributions from Sunway Pyramid Mall and strong hotel performance. Pavilion REIT and Axis REIT saw growth of 9.8% year-on-year, with Pavilion supported by Pavilion Bukit Jalil, Elite Pavilion Mall and maiden contributions from Banyan Tree KL and Pavilion Hotel KL, while Axis benefited from positive rental reversions of industrial assets and contributions from new acquisitions. MBSB Research noted that the retail and industrial segments remain stable, while the office segment continues to be muted. Despite encouraging earnings, narrowing yield spreads below the long-term average suggest limited near-term income upside. Sunway REIT’s distribution yield is estimated at 4.7%, with its upgraded BUY rating reflecting positive earnings prospects and ongoing asset performance. title: Wall Street Rises As Tech Rebound Outshines Consumer Slump
body: US stocks closed higher on Dec 19, snapping back from a choppy week as strength in tech megacaps outweighed steep losses in consumer names such as Nike. Reuters reported that Micron Technology led the charge, jumping 7% to a record close after upbeat forecasts reignited investor optimism around artificial intelligence (AI)-linked shares. Nvidia rose 3.9% as the US kicked off a review of one of its high-powered AI chips, while Oracle surged 6.6% after ByteDance agreed to sell TikTok’s US operations to a consortium of investors that included the cloud giant. The gains helped the S&P 500 rise 0.88% to 6,834.50, while the Nasdaq advanced 1.31% to 23,307.62. The Dow added 0.38% to finish at 48,134.89. For the week, the S&P edged up 0.11% and the Nasdaq climbed 0.48%, while the Dow slipped 0.67%. But pressure was intense in consumer stocks. Nike tumbled 10.5% after reporting a second straight drop in gross margins on weaker China sales and a product overhaul. Lamb Weston cratered nearly 26% on muted demand signals, and Conagra shed 2.5% after weak earnings. Utilities and staples were the only S&P 500 sectors in the red. Market sentiment remains supported by cooling inflation, with November consumer prices rising less than expected. Traders are still pricing in at least two Fed rate cuts in 2026 and see a 20% chance of the first move as early as January. Forecasts of a Santa Claus Rally also buoyed spirits: Since 1950, the S&P has gained an average 1.3% over the final five days of December and first two sessions of the new year. The trading session on Dec 19 was heavy on volume and volatility, driven by “triple witching” expirations. Advancers outpaced decliners across both the NYSE and Nasdaq, with Micron and Nvidia shining brightest as Big Tech reclaimed the week’s momentum. title: United Malacca Surprises With Latest Results
body: CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) maintains a BUY call on United Malacca Bhd (UMB) with an unchanged target price of RM6.42, citing stronger-than-expected 1HFY26 production and a lower effective tax rate. The research house noted that the company’s first-half earnings exceeded expectations, driven by higher fresh fruit bunches (FFB) yield and palm kernel (PK) prices. UMB posted a core net profit of RM55 million in 2QFY26, up 95% year-on-year and 46% quarter-on-quarter, bringing 1HFY26 core net profit to RM91 million, an 89% increase YoY. Reported net profit rose to RM93 million after adding back an unrealised net forex loss of RM4.9 million. Quarterly sales increased 31% YoY, outpacing a 19% rise in cost of sales, supported by a 15% increase in FFB output and a 35% jump in Malaysia’s average PK price to RM3,580 per tonne. UMB declared a higher interim dividend of 7 sen, above the 12 sen full-year forecast. Malaysia operations contributed 81% of total EBITDA in 1HFY26, rising 40% YoY to RM123 million due to higher FFB production and stronger PK prices. The average crude palm oil price in Malaysia increased 3% YoY to RM4,180 per tonne. Meanwhile, Indonesia operations delivered faster growth, with EBITDA surging 2.49 times YoY to RM28.4 million, underpinned by a 26% increase in FFB production from prime-age palms and a 37% rise in PK prices to RM3,240 per tonne. The strong 2QFY26 results indicate that yield improvements in Indonesian estates are yielding results. CIMB Securities expects earnings to moderate amid softer crude palm oil prices, partially offset by better FFB yields and disciplined cost control, maintaining the rating and target price. Its wholly-owned subsidiary, Gamuda Engineering Pty Ltd, secured the Sydney Metro West Stations Package West worth AUD2.7 billion (RM7.32 billion), covering the design and construction of five metro stations, with planning and design starting in January 2026 and major works expected by late 2026 or early 2027. The latest wins bring Gamuda’s total outstanding orderbook to a record RM45.9 billion, surpassing its end-of-year target of RM40–45 billion. Analysts note that the group’s pipeline remains strong, with opportunities across water, data centres, rail, highways and renewable energy. HLIB highlighted that the company maintains a rolling RM50 billion worth of tenders, providing sustained visibility into new contracts for 2026 and beyond. Despite trading at a premium to the Bursa Malaysia Construction Index, analysts believe Gamuda’s expansion in Australia and recurring income potential from utilities and data centres support its valuations and upside potential. title: Wall Street Rises On Softer US Inflation, Tech Boosts Sentiment
body: US stocks rose on Thursday as softer-than-expected inflation data and strong tech results revived investor confidence. The Consumer Price Index for November increased 2.7% year-on-year, below economists’ forecast of 3.1%, raising hopes for more Federal Reserve rate cuts. The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 65.88 points, or 0.14%, to 47,951.85, while the S&P 500 rose 53.33 points, or 0.79%, to 6,774.76, led by the technology sector. The Nasdaq Composite advanced 313.04 points, or 1.38%, to 23,006.36, lifted by Micron Technology’s 10% jump following a strong forecast. “Micron’s news was helping to at least stabilise some of the sentiment around AI, which has been a rollercoaster,” said Garrett Melson, portfolio strategist at Natixis Investment Managers. Treasury yields edged lower, with the 10-year note falling 3.1 basis points to 4.12% and the 30-year bond down 2.8 basis points at 4.7999%. The 2-year note, sensitive to Fed rate expectations, declined 2.5 basis points to 3.46%. In currency markets, the dollar index rose slightly to 98.44, while the euro dipped 0.13% to $1.1724. Sterling strengthened 0.02% to $1.3378 after the Bank of England cut interest rates. title: Ringgit Opens Slightly Higher On Softer US Inflation, Eyes RM4.08
body: The ringgit opened slightly firmer against the US dollar, holding at the 4.08 level amid growing expectations of a softer US monetary policy outlook and recent developments from global central banks. At 8 am, the local currency strengthened to 4.0820/0940 from Thursday’s close of 4.0840/0880 against the greenback. The movement came after US inflation for November came in below expectations at 2.7 per cent, compared with forecasts of 3.1 per cent. Core inflation also moderated to 2.6 per cent from 3.0 per cent in September, reinforcing the case for a potential easing of US interest rates in 2026. In contrast, the European Central Bank kept its policy rate unchanged following an upbeat assessment of growth and inflation prospects for next year. Despite the softer US inflation, the US Dollar Index rose 0.07 per cent to 98.441 points overnight, while the ringgit closed 0.09 per cent higher on Thursday, outperforming most Asian peers. Analysts noted that the local unit may test a breach of the RM4.08 level if expectations of a lower US federal funds rate gain traction. Against other major currencies, the ringgit opened mostly lower. It fell against the British pound to 5.4629/4790 from 5.4513/4567, and weakened versus the Japanese yen to 2.6234/6313 from 2.6188/6217, while edging up slightly against the euro to 4.7861/8002 from 4.7869/7915. Regionally, the ringgit traded mixed against ASEAN peers. It declined versus the Singapore dollar to 3.1639/1736 from 3.1620/1653, slipped against the Thai baht to 12.9810/13.0287 from 12.9750/9935, remained almost flat against the Philippine peso at 6.97/6.99, and inched higher versus the Indonesian rupiah to 244.1/244.9 from 244.2/244.5. The broader market followed suit, with the FBM70 up 18.02 points (+0.11%) to 16,733.67, while the FBMEMAS rose 16.00 points (+0.13%) to 12,133.49. Among sectoral indexes, the FBMSHA added 14.19 points (+0.12%) to 11,991.43. Trading activity remained concentrated on mid- and small-cap stocks, with Velesto, Pharma, Omesti, IAB and Magma among the most actively traded counters by volume. F&N, UMCCA, PETDAG, Nestle and Aeon Credit led the gainers, while UTD Plantations, KLCC, NSOP, PetChem and PMETAL were the top decliners. The morning rally in Malaysia follows broader optimism in Asia. On the Singapore Exchange, the Straits Times Index (STI) inched up 2.51 points (+0.05%) to 4,573.12, supported by 138 advancers versus 53 decliners, according to SGX data. Global cues also buoyed sentiment. Wall Street ended higher on Thursday, with the S&P 500 climbing 53.33 points (+0.79%) to 6,774.76, the Nasdaq up 313.04 points (+1.38%) to 23,006.36 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average rising 65.88 points (+0.14%) to 47,951.85, boosted by softer-than-expected US inflation data and tech stock gains, according to Reuters. Investors are keeping an eye on upcoming economic reports and ongoing developments in US monetary policy, while regional markets continue to take cues from Wall Street’s late-week rebound. title: Bitcoin, Ethereum Trade Cautiously As Options Expiry Looms
body: The cryptocurrency market opened on a cautious note on Dec 19, with Bitcoin and Ethereum trading within tight ranges as investors positioned ahead of a major options expiry and continued to assess global macroeconomic signals. Bitcoin hovered around US$85,176, down about 0.9% from its previous close, after swinging between an intraday high of US$89,230 and a low of US$84,461. The world’s largest cryptocurrency remains under pressure following recent volatility, with traders adopting a wait-and-see stance. Market attention is firmly on the expiry of approximately US$2.7 billion worth of Bitcoin options, with heavy strike concentrations near the US$88,000 level. Analysts note that such expiries often amplify short-term price swings, particularly amid thinner year-end liquidity. Despite ongoing institutional accumulation, including continued purchases by corporate holders, Bitcoin has struggled to establish clear upside momentum, reflecting broader caution across global risk assets. Meanwhile, Ethereum showed relative resilience, trading at US$2,819, marginally lower by 0.2% on the day. Ethereum fluctuated between US$2,989 and US$2,781 during the session, outperforming Bitcoin on a percentage basis. Ethereum is also seeing elevated derivatives activity, with around US$459 million in Ethereum options expiring, contributing to near-term price consolidation. Options positioning suggests mild bearish sentiment, though buyers continue to defend key support levels, keeping the medium-term outlook constructive. Broader crypto market sentiment remains mixed as investors weigh improving inflation data against lingering uncertainty over global monetary policy, including expectations surrounding central bank decisions in major economies. The combination of macro headwinds and declining year-end liquidity has kept volatility elevated. Overall, traders are closely monitoring Bitcoin’s US$88,000 pivot level, where a decisive move could trigger sharp follow-through in either direction. For Ethereum, the ability to hold current support zones will be critical in sustaining interest in alternative digital assets. In the near term, the direction of crypto markets is likely to be dictated by options-related flows and broader risk sentiment, with a clearer trend expected to emerge once expiry-related distortions fade. title: Asian Shares Bounce As Tech Rebounds And BOJ Rate Decision Looms
body: Asian share markets recovered on Friday following a turnaround in Wall Street tech stocks, with investors keeping a close eye on the Bank of Japan’s likely interest rate hike. The central bank is widely expected to raise its policy rate by a quarter point to 0.75 per cent, with markets pricing in a 90 per cent chance. Analysts say any further tightening could support the struggling yen but add pressure on Japanese government bonds. Figures released Friday showed Japan’s core CPI rose 3.0 per cent year-on-year in November, unchanged from the previous month. Analysts at CBA noted that “core inflation has remained above the BOJ’s 2 per cent target in the past two years, and the sharp weakening of the yen in the past two months will also add to inflation.” Meanwhile, US inflation slowed unexpectedly in November, with the Consumer Price Index rising 2.7 per cent against forecasts of 3.1 per cent. While analysts warned the figures were distorted by the recent government shutdown, the data provided a mild boost to sentiment. Pricing for the Federal Reserve suggested only a 27 per cent chance of a rate cut in January, with March nudging up to 58 per cent from 54 per cent. Regional indices followed Wall Street’s lead. Japan’s Nikkei rose 0.6 per cent, South Korea climbed 1.2 per cent buoyed by strong results from chipmaker Micron Technology, and MSCI’s broadest Asia-Pacific index outside Japan added 0.2 per cent. S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures were flat after bouncing overnight. In bonds, 10-year US Treasury yields held at 4.126 per cent, while Japan’s 10-year yield matched a recent 18-year high at 1.980 per cent. European bond markets reacted to central bank moves with caution. The Bank of England cut rates in a tight 5-4 vote but signalled a cautious outlook for future easing. The European Central Bank held rates at 2.0 per cent, hinting that the easing cycle is likely over. Central banks in Sweden and Norway also stayed on hold. Currencies were mostly steady. Sterling hovered at $1.3378, the euro was at $1.1725, and the dollar was unchanged at 155.60 yen. Commodities saw mixed moves. Gold remained at $4,333 an ounce, below its October peak, while silver faced profit-taking. Palladium and platinum stayed in demand. Oil prices were supported by potential US sanctions on Russia and supply risks from Venezuelan tanker blockades. Brent rose 0.2 per cent to $62.04 per barrel, and US crude gained 0.2 per cent to $58.35. title: Wall Street Falls As Tech Stocks Drag On AI Concerns
body: Wall Street’s major indexes closed lower on Wednesday, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq hitting three-week lows amid persistent worries over the artificial intelligence trade. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 228.29 points, or 0.47%, to 47,885.97, while the S&P 500 lost 78.83 points, or 1.16%, to 6,721.43. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite dropped 418.14 points, or 1.81%, to 22,693.32. Technology stocks led the decline. Oracle dropped 5.4% after reports that its largest data centre partner, Blue Owl Capital, would not support a $10 billion deal for its next facility. Nvidia fell 3.8% and Broadcom slid 4.5%, pushing the broader chips index down 3.9%. Amazon fell 0.6% after announcing talks to invest about $10 billion in ChatGPT maker OpenAI. “There’s percolating anxiety about the AI trade… The primary driver is the level of capex and circular nature of some of the spending with OpenAI being at the centre of that,” said Ross Mayfield, investment strategist at Baird Private Wealth Management. “The broader question heading into the New Year is about the sustainability and return on investment of all this spending.” Alphabet shares declined 3.2% after reports that Google is launching a new initiative to compete with Nvidia’s software advantage, in collaboration with Meta. Media stocks also saw movement: Netflix rose 0.2%, while Paramount and Warner Bros fell 5.4% and 2.4%, respectively, following the rejection of a $108.4 billion hostile bid for Warner Bros by Paramount Skydance. Energy stocks bucked the broader trend, rising on crude gains after U.S. President Donald Trump ordered a “blockade” on sanctioned Venezuelan oil tankers. ConocoPhillips and Occidental Petroleum both gained over 4%. Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller provided some relief, stating the central bank still has room to cut interest rates amid a softening jobs market. Investors are now eyeing Thursday’s U.S. consumer inflation report from the Commerce Department for further direction. Declining issues outnumbered advancers by 1.5-to-1 on the NYSE and 2.11-to-1 on the Nasdaq. Trading volume reached 17.92 billion shares, above the 20-day average of 16.97 billion. The S&P 500 recorded 12 new 52-week highs, while the Nasdaq logged 85 new highs and 175 new lows. title: Top Glove’s Strong Rebound Fails To Appease Analysts
body: Top Glove Corp Bhd remains under a cautious spotlight as analysts from RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research), CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) and Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) maintained NEUTRAL to HOLD calls on the rubber glove maker despite showing a strong rebound in its 1QFY26 results. RHB Research kept a Neutral rating with a new target price of RM0.64, CIMB Securities reiterated a Hold with a TP of RM0.70, while HLIB maintained a Hold with a lowered TP of RM0.60, citing continued industry headwinds and limited pricing power. Top Glove posted a 1QFY26 core profit of RM39.0 million, up 38.6% quarter-on-quarter from a loss of RM18.3 million in 1QFY25, broadly in line with forecasts, with revenue however, largely flat at RM0.65 billion. The sequential sales volume improvement was driven by natural rubber gloves, with utilisation rising to about 75%, although softer average selling prices due to increased competition and a weaker US dollar against the Ringgit offset some of the gains. Management noted that weekly order inflows reached approximately 1.4 billion pieces, exceeding current production capacity and pushing lead times beyond 60 days. Plans are in place to reactivate six billion pieces of idle capacity across four factories, requiring an estimated RM20 million in capital expenditure and around 800 additional workers. Analysts highlighted that lower raw material costs supported the profit rebound, with natural latex prices down 16% year-on-year and nitrile butadiene rubber down 7% year-on-year, while cost per 1,000 pieces fell to US$15.30. However, an oversupply in global glove capacity, projected to rise by up to 15% in 2026, could limit further upside in selling prices despite supportive Ringgit movements. RHB Research raised FY26–28 earnings by up to 3% following updated capacity and cost assumptions, whereas CIMB Securities adjusted forecasts for lower input costs and HLIB revised FY27 earnings down 26% due to constrained pricing power. Top Glove’s outlook for 2QFY26 indicates steady sales growth, particularly in Europe, with a modest expected rise in selling prices, while operating leverage and lower natural gas costs are expected to offset forex headwinds. Despite these positives, analysts maintain cautious stances, reflecting the challenging competitive environment. As of 10.33 am, the stock price is up 3.85% to RM0.675. title: Stock Today: Top Glove Jumps 5.38% On Strong Q1 Profit Rebound
body: Top Glove Corporation Bhd shares rose by 5.38% to RM0.685 as of 12.25 pm, with a trading volume of 44.47 million units, reflecting investor optimism following the group’s robust start to financial year 2026. The stock opened at RM0.650, reached a high of RM0.685 and a low of RM0.645 during the session, with the last average closing price at RM0.650. The world’s largest glove manufacturer reported a sharp rebound in profitability for the first quarter ended Nov 30 2025, with profit after tax and minority interest (PATAMI) of RM39 million, representing a 680% year-on-year increase. Revenue came in at RM884 million, supported by higher sales volumes and improved plant utilisation, despite a highly competitive global environment. Sales volume rose 17% year on year, driven by recovering demand in key markets such as the United States, although revenue growth was moderated by lower average selling prices due to falling raw material costs and a stronger ringgit against the US dollar. Top Glove attributed the profit surge to better cost efficiency from higher plant utilisation, ongoing quality enhancements, cost optimisation measures, strategic marketing initiatives and organisational realignment. Part of the raw material cost savings was shared with customers, reinforcing long-term customer relationships. Managing Director Lim Cheong Guan said the strong start to FY2026 marked a significant milestone, with EBITDA margins restored to pre-pandemic levels. Foreign exchange headwinds were offset by lower raw material costs and active US dollar hedging, contributing to the group’s improved performance. The positive quarterly results and operational improvements appear to have supported investor confidence, driving Top Glove’s stock higher in the morning session. title: Stock Today: ITMAX Stays Flat As Investors Digest Immigration CCTV Contract
body: ITMAX System Bhd shares were flat at RM4.70 as at 2.33 pm, with trading activity reflecting a wait-and-see stance following recent contract announcements. The stock opened unchanged at RM4.70, touched an intraday high of RM4.75 and a low of RM4.68, with 1.15 million shares traded. The last average closing price stood at RM4.70. The subdued share price movement comes after ITMAX announced it had secured a RM36 million contract from the Immigration Department of Malaysia to install and rent closed-circuit television systems at key entry and exit points across Peninsular Malaysia. The 36-month contract will run from July 1 2026 to June 30 2029, with installation scheduled to begin on Feb 1 2026 and expected to be completed within five months. The project involves the deployment of more than 1,500 CCTV units nationwide, including at borders and airports, each equipped with multiple artificial intelligence features such as facial recognition, behavioural analysis and unattended-object detection. This marks ITMAX’s first project with the Immigration Department and its second non-municipal CCTV contract in FY25, following an earlier award from the Railway Asset Corporation. Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd has maintained a BUY call on the stock with a target price of RM5.74, noting that while the per-unit charge is lower than smart city projects, the contract is expected to deliver core profit margins of 40% to 45%. The bank also pointed to further potential contract opportunities in Kuala Lumpur and the greater Johor region, supporting ITMAX’s longer-term growth prospects in smart infrastructure. title: Ringgit Hits Five-Year Peak As Fed Watch Intensifies
body: The ringgit opened higher on Thursday at the 4.07 level against the US dollar, marking its strongest start in nearly five years, as investors continued to assess the US Federal Reserve’s policy outlook. At 8 am, the local currency was quoted at 4.0795/0915 against the greenback, up from Wednesday’s close of 4.0855/0940. The ringgit last traded near this level on March 3, 2021, when it ended the session at 4.0720 against the US dollar. Against other major currencies, the ringgit weakened against the British pound to 5.4555/4716 from 5.4439/4553, and edged lower versus the euro at 4.7897/8038 from 4.7866/7965. However, it strengthened against the Japanese yen, rising to 2.6236/6315 from 2.6267/6321. Regionally, the ringgit gained against its ASEAN peers, appreciating against the Singapore dollar to 3.1592/1688 from 3.1614/1682. Market participants are keeping a close watch on the Fed’s policy signals, which continue to influence the ringgit’s performance and regional currency movements. title: MN Holdings’ Big Anticipation On ‘Customer A’
body: Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) has maintained a BUY call on MN Holdings (MNHLDG) with a target price of RM2.23, citing expectations of sustained earnings momentum and a strong project pipeline. The research house highlighted that earnings may temporarily soften in the fourth quarter of FY26, but this air pocket is largely anticipated, with growth set to re-accelerate as Customer A rolls out additional contracts, including Plot 4 extensions, CLS packages for Plot 5 and Kempas Phase 2. MNHLDG, primarily engaged in underground utilities and substation engineering, carried an order book of RM864 million as of November 2025, largely driven by data centre and Tenaga Nasional Berhad works. The group’s tender book stood at RM1.1 billion, with management expecting it to approach RM2 billion in coming quarters, largely underpinned by Customer A’s expansion. Plot 4 extension in Nusajaya Tech Park and Kempas projects are nearing completion, while a new data centre in Klang Valley could deliver over RM200 million in additional works. Beyond Customer A, MNHLDG is in early discussions with other data centre clients, including Singapore and Middle East operators, though award timelines remain uncertain. In the solar segment, the group is in advanced stages to secure a RM20 million LSS5 contract, part of a RM121 million tender, with management projecting total substation works of RM120–150 million from LSS5. LSS5+ projects are expected to commence in the fourth quarter of CY26. HLIB expects MNHLDG’s earnings trajectory to resume in FY27 as new Customer A jobs begin rolling out, supported by the company’s strategic exposure to high-growth sectors such as solar and data centres and its position as a proxy for Malaysia’s rising power demand amid Tenaga’s capital expenditure cycle. As of 12.02 pm, the stock price is up 0.64% to RM1.58. title: Dollar Holds Firm Ahead Of Global Central Bank Decisions
body: The US dollar maintained gains against major currencies on Thursday as investors positioned ahead of key central bank meetings in Britain, Europe and Japan. Sterling remained under pressure after UK inflation unexpectedly fell, reinforcing expectations for a Bank of England (BoE) rate cut. “There’ll be a generally stronger dollar,” said Ray Attrill, head of FX strategy at National Australia Bank. He added the weak UK inflation print has sealed the deal for a BOE rate cut later today. Meanwhile, the yen pared losses from the previous session as the Bank of Japan (BoJ) began a two-day policy meeting, widely expected to result in a rate hike to a three-decade high. The euro was little changed at US$1.1743, while sterling stabilised at US$1.3373 following Wednesday’s 0.4% decline. The dollar index, which tracks the greenback against a basket of currencies including the euro and yen, remained steady at 98.35 after a 0.2% advance in the prior session. The yen gained 0.2% to 155.45 against the dollar, recovering from a 0.6% slide. Market expectations are pricing in nearly a 100% probability of a 25-basis-point cut by the BoE following November’s surprisingly soft inflation data, while the European Central Bank is expected to leave rates unchanged at its Thursday meeting. In Asia, the BoJ is set to lift short-term interest rates from 0.5% to 0.75%, as persistent high food costs keep inflation above its 2% target. Japan’s Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi emphasised proactive spending to boost growth and tax revenues, underlining the administration’s focus on strengthening a fragile economy. Investor attention in the US remains on the Federal Reserve, with uncertainty over the timing of future rate cuts and the succession of Fed Chair Jerome Powell. Fed Governor Christopher Waller noted on Wednesday that the central bank still has room to lower rates amid signs of job market weakness, contrasting with Atlanta Fed President Raphael Bostic, who sees no further reductions in 2026. In commodity and currency markets, the Australian dollar traded at US$0.6600, down 0.1%, while the New Zealand dollar fell 0.2% to US$0.5763 despite GDP growth in the third quarter. In cryptocurrencies, bitcoin rose 0.3% to US$86,240.24 and ether gained 0.6% to US$2,835.64. title: Stock Today: Gamuda Increases 2.52% On RM2.6 Billion Australian Renewable Energy Contract
body: Gamuda Bhd’s shares rose 2.52% to RM4.89 as of 4.36 pm, following the announcement of a major international contract in Australia. The construction and infrastructure group saw trading volume reach 12.1 million shares, with the stock opening at RM4.76 and hitting a high of RM4.90 during the session. The share price movement comes after Gamuda’s wholly-owned subsidiary, DT Infrastructure Pty Ltd (DTI), secured a contract valued at AU$994 million (approximately RM2.6 billion) for the Marinus Link project. The contract, part of the Marinus Link Stage 1 – Balance of Works Package, was awarded to the TasVic Greenlink joint venture, a 50:50 partnership between DTI and Samsung C&T Corporation of South Korea. Gamuda’s 50% stake in the joint venture is expected to contribute AU$497 million (around RM1.3 billion) in revenue over the five-year project, which is pivotal to Australia’s renewable energy transition. The project involves building converter stations in Heybridge, Tasmania, and Hazelwood, Victoria, as well as civil works for a 90km underground cable and other onshore installation tasks. Work is slated to begin in early 2026. The Marinus Link interconnector will strengthen electricity grid connections between Tasmania and Victoria, facilitating the flow of renewable power, particularly hydropower, to the mainland. The project is backed by Marinus Link Pty Ltd, a joint venture of the Commonwealth of Australia, Victorian Government and Tasmanian Government. Gamuda’s share performance today reflects investor optimism over the company’s expansion into international renewable energy infrastructure and its long-term revenue potential. title: Ringgit Firms To 4.07 Against US Dollar On Improved Sentiment
body: The ringgit strengthened against the US dollar in early trade on Wednesday, extending recent gains to hover around the 4.07 level, its strongest showing in nearly five years, supported by firmer domestic and external sentiment. At 8.01 am, the local currency rose to 4.0765/0935 versus the greenback, from 4.0835/0875 at Tuesday’s close. title: HSIF Wobbles, Yet RHB Sees Room For A Technical Rebound
body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) maintained its positive trading bias on Hang Seng Index Futures (HSIF) despite the contract extending its pullback in the latest session, citing intact key support levels that could still support a technical rebound. The research house said HSIF fell 402 points to settle at 25,251 points, after opening at 25,674 points and climbing to an intraday high of 25,732 points before reversing lower. The index later tested a session low of 25,110 points and closed with a bearish candlestick. During the evening session, HSIF slipped a further 32 points to last trade at 25,219 points. RHB Research noted that recent price action reflects sustained near-term downside pressure, with the relative strength index trending lower, signalling slowing momentum. The index is also trading below both its 20-day and 50-day simple moving averages, reinforcing the current corrective structure. “Should the softer tone persist, the HSIF may gravitate toward the 25,000-point support. A stabilisation around this level could attract a technical rebound attempt,” it said, adding that as long as the 25,000-point threshold holds, it continues to retain a positive trading bias. RHB Research reiterated its recommendation for traders to maintain long positions initiated at 21,416 points, which was the close on April 14. To manage downside risk, it set a stop-loss at 25,000 points. In terms of key levels, first support is seen at 25,000 points, followed by 24,300 points. Immediate resistance is pegged at 26,500 points, with the next resistance at 27,400 points. title: Asian Markets Cautious Amid Mixed US Jobs Data
body: Asian equities saw a mixed session as the release of US jobs data failed to reignite hopes for another Federal Reserve interest rate cut, while oil prices surged after former US President Donald Trump ordered a blockade of sanctioned Venezuelan oil tankers. US non-farm payrolls data showed the unemployment rate rising to a four-year high of 4.6 percent in November, signalling a slowing labour market. Analysts said the figures did little to shift expectations for a rate cut next month, with Bloomberg noting markets had priced in only a 20 percent chance of such a move. National Australia Bank senior economist Taylor Nugent commented that the increase in unemployment is unlikely to prompt near-term easing by the Fed. Technology and AI spending concerns weighed on investor sentiment, keeping Asian indices subdued. Markets in Tokyo, Seoul, Taipei, Manila and Jakarta advanced modestly, while Hong Kong and Shanghai were flat and Sydney, Singapore and Wellington declined. Oil prices jumped sharply, with West Texas Intermediate rising 1.2 percent to US$55.91 per barrel and Brent crude up 1.1 percent at US$59.53 per barrel, after Trump announced “a total and complete blockade of all sanctioned oil tankers going into and out of, Venezuela.” The move escalates US pressure on Caracas amid efforts to remove President Nicolas Maduro. In currencies, the yen strengthened against the dollar ahead of the Bank of Japan’s expected rate hike to a 30-year high on Friday, while the euro and pound edged higher versus the dollar. Corporate news saw Chinese chipmaker MetaX Integrated Circuits Shanghai soar more than 550 percent on its debut, following a $585.8 million IPO, echoing earlier gains by semiconductor firm Moore Threads. At 0230 GMT, Tokyo’s Nikkei 225 was up 0.4 percent at 49,553.71, while Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index and Shanghai Composite remained flat. title: Wall Street Edges Lower As Investors Await Jobs Data And Fed Clarity
body: Wall Street closed slightly lower as investors adopted a cautious stance ahead of a busy week of economic data, while also assessing developments surrounding the future leadership of the US Federal Reserve and fresh commentary from policymakers. Market focus has shifted to a series of key economic indicators due later this week, led by nonfarm payroll figures for October and November. The October jobs report had been delayed earlier in the quarter because of the government shutdown, heightening expectations around the upcoming releases. Investors are also awaiting data on retail sales, business activity and inflation for further direction on the interest rate outlook. “Markets today are struggling with where to find the leadership, in terms of not wanting all the eggs in the AI basket and not having a lot of data yet,” said BMO Family Office chief investment officer Carol Schleif. “People will hold their breath a little bit before the jobs numbers this week and whether or not those are supportive of more rate cuts.” The subdued performance followed sharp losses at the end of last week, when both the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq recorded their steepest daily declines in more than three weeks. The sell-off was driven by renewed concerns over inflation pressures and unease surrounding heavy, debt-funded investments tied to artificial intelligence. Traders were also weighing reports that White House economic adviser Kevin Hassett’s potential candidacy for the Fed chair position had faced pushback from individuals close to US President Donald Trump. With Jerome Powell’s term set to end in May, speculation over his successor has intensified, with markets increasingly pricing in the possibility of a more dovish chair who could support interest rate cuts next year. On the policy front, a New York Fed president said the central bank’s rate cut last week had placed it in a favourable position, while a Fed governor argued that current inflation readings do not accurately reflect underlying supply-and-demand dynamics. By the close, the Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped 41.49 points, or 0.09%, to 48,416.56. The S&P 500 declined 10.90 points, or 0.16%, to 6,816.51, while the Nasdaq Composite fell 137.76 points, or 0.59%, to 23,057.41. Sector performance was mixed. Eight of the 11 S&P 500 sectors ended higher, led by healthcare stocks, which gained 1.3%. Information technology shares fell 1%, weighed down by ServiceNow, which slid 11.5% after reports emerged that the company was in advanced talks to acquire cybersecurity start-up Armis. Among individual stocks, Tesla rose 3.5% after chief executive officer Elon Musk said the electric vehicle maker was testing its robotaxi service without safety monitors in the front passenger seat. In contrast, iRobot plunged 72.7% after the Roomba vacuum-maker filed for bankruptcy protection. Market breadth reflected the cautious tone. On the New York Stock Exchange, declining issues matched advancers at a one-to-one ratio, with 283 new highs and 93 new lows. On the Nasdaq, declining stocks outnumbered advancers by a 1.76-to-1 ratio, with 3,021 stocks falling and 1,715 rising. The S&P 500 recorded 30 new 52-week highs and six new lows, while the Nasdaq Composite posted 133 new highs and 198 new lows. Trading volume on US exchanges totalled 17.13 billion shares, broadly in line with the 20-day average of 17.10 billion shares, underscoring the market’s wait-and-see approach ahead of the key data releases. title: Stock Today: Astro Rises 4.76% On 3QFY26 Earnings Beat Despite Challenging Outlook
body: Astro Malaysia Holdings Bhd saw its share price rise 4.76% to RM0.110 at 12.13 pm, with 1.18 million shares traded, following the release of its third-quarter financial results for FY26. The stock opened at RM0.105, hitting an intraday high of RM0.110. Astro reported 3QFY26 core PATAMI of RM3.5 million, a 250% quarter-on-quarter increase but 75% lower year-on-year, lifting 9MFY26 earnings to RM5.2 million, down 77% from the same period last year. HLIB Research noted the results exceeded its forecast at 100% of FY26 estimates, driven by resilient margins and slightly stronger revenue, but fell below consensus expectations by 13%. Revenue rose 2% QoQ on stronger advertising (+13%) and higher sales of programming rights (+20%), offsetting a slight dip in subscription revenue (-0.2%). The company’s bottom line was weighed down by revenue weakness, contraction in EBITDA margin (-1.0% YTD) and a higher effective tax rate (31% vs 29% in 9MFY25). HLIB highlighted structural pressures facing Astro, including cord-cutting, slow adex recovery, and competition from global OTT platforms. While the launch of Astro One offers simplified, lower-priced Entertainment, Sports and Epic packs to defend market share, average revenue per user fell 4.7% YoY to RM95.10. Subscription revenue, historically 62–77% of turnover, is expected to remain under pressure. Despite these headwinds, HLIB raised FY26/27/28 earnings forecasts by 36%, 2% and 1% respectively and upgraded Astro to HOLD, citing the recent share price correction of 16.7% over the past month and a revised target price of RM0.11. title: Asian Stocks Slide As Investors Eye US Jobs, Inflation Data
body: Asian markets extended losses on Tuesday, following Wall Street lower, as investors positioned themselves ahead of key US jobs and inflation figures, amid lingering worries over a potential tech bubble. “After essentially missing the October jobs report due to a lack of survey data, the Fed will closely scrutinise the November figures when setting out the path of monetary policy through early 2026,” said Matt Weller, head of market research at City Index. “That said, traders are currently pricing in only a one-in-four chance of another rate cut in January, meaning that the market reaction to the release may be more limited unless it shows a large deterioration in the labour market.” Tokyo, Hong Kong, Shanghai, Seoul and Taipei all fell more than one percent, while Sydney, Singapore and Jakarta also posted declines. The sell-off was further compounded by concerns over the tech sector, with weak earnings from Oracle and Broadcom and questions over returns from heavy AI investments weighing on sentiment. “Jitters over the AI theme have resurfaced in recent sessions, not helped by Broadcom’s failure to provide concrete guidance for the quarter ahead, nor by reports that Oracle’s data centre construction may be delayed,” wrote Michael Brown from Pepperstone. Investors are also watching US Federal Reserve policy closely. In the commodities market, gold climbed above US$4,300 as a safe-haven asset, while bitcoin dipped to US$85,171. Oil prices edged lower, with West Texas Intermediate at US$56.64 per barrel and Brent at US$60.35. The yen held gains against the dollar ahead of an expected Bank of Japan rate hike on Friday. Key indices at 0230 GMT showed Tokyo’s Nikkei 225 down 1.3% at 49,523.56, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng off 1.7% at 25,205.57, and Shanghai Composite lower by 1.1% at 3,825.00. title: Ringgit Edges Higher As Economic Data Supports Local Currency

Data released last Friday by the Statistics Department Malaysia showed the Industrial Production Index (IPI) rose 6.0 % year-on-year in October 2025, led by a 6.5 % expansion in the manufacturing sector. Economists noted that export-oriented industries within manufacturing grew 7.2 %, up from 4.8 % previously, signalling robust external demand supporting the economy. In early trading, the ringgit also strengthened against several major currencies. It rose versus the British pound to 5.4670/4817 from 5.4789/4869, edged up against the Japanese yen to 2.6246/6318 from 2.6264/6304, and increased against the euro to 4.8007/8136 from 4.8037/8107. title: Bitcoin, Ethereum Ease As Traders Turn Cautious Ahead Of Key Macro Signals

Bitcoin slipped nearly 2% on the day, hovering around US$88,700, after failing to sustain momentum above the US$90,000 threshold. The pullback reflects growing caution among traders following last week’s rally, as profit-taking and defensive positioning emerged ahead of central bank signals and derivatives expiries. Market participants noted that while Bitcoin remains structurally strong, the absence of fresh upside catalysts has limited follow-through buying. Institutional desks appear selective, opting to manage exposure rather than chase short-term price strength. Ethereum, meanwhile, also mirrored the broader market tone, easing about 1.6% to trade near US$3,080. The second-largest cryptocurrency continues to consolidate above the psychologically important US$3,000 level, but upward momentum has slowed as traders balance accumulation against near-term profit-taking. Analysts point to rotation flows between Bitcoin and Ethereum and a lack of decisive directional conviction as key drivers of Ethereum’s muted performance. The Ethereum/Bitcoin ratio has shown intermittent movement, underscoring the market’s current tug-of-war. Overall sentiment remains cautious rather than bearish. With major US Federal Reserve decisions approaching and global risk assets subdued, crypto markets are reflecting a broader “wait-and-see” posture. Options positioning and institutional flows are also contributing to intraday volatility without establishing a clear trend. Bottom Line: Bitcoin and Ethereum are digesting recent gains, with stability replacing momentum as traders prioritise risk management over aggressive positioning. A decisive move may hinge on fresh macro or policy cues in the days ahead. Losses deepened after Federal Reserve officials who opposed this week’s rate cut cautioned inflation remains too high, pushing bond yields higher and pressuring growth stocks. title: Wall Street Splits, Dow Climbs To New Peak As Nasdaq Slips
body: Wall Street ended mostly higher on Thursday, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average and the Russell 2000 notching fresh record highs even as the Nasdaq closed lower, weighed by losses in major technology counters. The market’s performance unfolded against the backdrop of a sharp jump in US jobless claims, a reading that revived concerns over labour market weakness and sent both the US dollar and Treasury yields lower. Technology shares dragged the Nasdaq, with the information communications sector down 1% and tech falling 0.6%. Oracle plunged as much as 16% at one point, marking its worst session since 2001, though it later trimmed losses. Materials and financials, meanwhile, rose around 2%, supporting broader sentiment. The Dow and Russell 2000 outperformed as investors rotated into industrials and small-caps, while Mexico’s benchmark index also set a new record. The dollar index slid to a two-month low, with the greenback hitting a 14-month low against the Chinese yuan at 7.0550. The Brazilian real strengthened 1%. Bitcoin briefly dipped below US$90,000 before recovering. On the bond front, US Treasury yields fell by about 5 basis points at the shorter end, leading to a bull steepening of the yield curve. In commodities, oil fell 1.5%, while silver extended its rally to a new high above US$64 an ounce. The market moves came a day after Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell said the central bank sees stronger productivity as a potential path toward balancing firm economic growth with easing inflation pressures. Investors are now digesting what weaker labour indicators could mean for the Fed’s policy direction in early 2026. title: Lululemon CEO Exit Sends Shares Higher
body: Lululemon Athletica said CEO Calvin McDonald will step down in January after about seven years leading the company, with no immediate replacement named, while raising its annual profit forecast. The announcement sent shares up roughly 10% in extended trading on Thursday. The company appointed finance chief Meghan Frank and chief commercial officer André Maestrini as co-interim CEOs during the search for a permanent leader. Despite the upbeat forecast, US sales have struggled, with the stock down 61% over the past two years. Lululemon, known for premium leggings and athleisure, has lost ground to rivals such as Alo Yoga and private-label alternatives, with executives acknowledging product execution issues. The Wall Street Journal reported that founder Chip Wilson expressed frustration with marketing and had considered a proxy fight. Lululemon also approved a US$1 billion increase to its stock buyback programme. While the Thanksgiving period showed strong demand, McDonald said holiday shopping has slowed, with consumers trading down in apparel. The company expects higher discounts to clear aged inventory and plans for inventory units to fall below sales in 2026. Interim co-CEO Frank added that marketing investments will continue in the fourth quarter to boost traffic and brand awareness. The company now anticipates annual profit between US$12.92 and US$13.02 per share, up from previous guidance of US$12.77 to US$12.97, while raising its annual sales target. Lululemon expects a US$210 million impact from tariffs on 2025 operating income and an operating margin contraction of about 390 basis points. Analysts note challenges ahead, “Lululemon lost share in a competitive athleisure market and has struggled with its core women’s pants,” said Matt Jacob of M Science, adding that the issue will fall to the next permanent CEO. For the quarter ended Nov 2, Lululemon reported net revenue of US$2.57 billion, exceeding estimates of US$2.48 billion, according to LSEG data. Morningstar analyst David Swartz commented that investors are likely reassured by the board’s decisive action, despite recognising McDonald’s effectiveness as CEO. title: Bitcoin Slips, Ethereum Sees Rotation
body: After a volatile 24 hours driven by macro shocks and derivatives expiry pressures, Bitcoin and Ethereum are carving key levels as traders brace for year-end narrative shifts. Bitcoin’s price action has been uncomfortably tight yet tepid near the US$90,000-US$94,000 zone in recent sessions, failing to sustain rallies that briefly flirted with upside breakout territory. This comes amid a Federal Reserve (Fed) rate-cut response that markets interpreted as less dovish than hoped, cooling risk appetite across crypto and equities alike. Bitcoin’s pullback below major psychological support at ~US$90K was confirmed in overnight trade, with the largest crypto sliding about 2% on risk-off flows. Analysts noted that liquidity clusters and technical bids around US$87,000 as the next critical support band, a break there could trigger deeper deleveraging, while defended bids may fuel another short squeeze into year-end positioning. Ethereum’s trajectory, meanwhile, also mirrors Bitcoin’s macro sensitivity but with its own unique narrative: Large holders appear to be rotating capital from Bitcoin into Ethereum, with reported flows totalling over US$140 million into Ethereum in recent weeks. Technically, Ethereum has consolidated around US$3,200-US$3,300, struggling to sustain momentum above the 200-day average amid mixed sentiment. While both coins weather macro drag but Ethereum’s relative performance is noteworthy: Its steeper volatility range suggests short-term traders are pricing rotation and the potential for a breakout once market structure stabilises. Bottomline: The crypto markets are caught between macro risk-off pressures and positioning ahead of the year-end. Bitcoin is testing support floors while Ethereum edges with rotational interest, both setups could flip dramatically once macro catalysts align or break key technical zones. title: Wall Street Rallies As Fed Delivers Expected Rate Cut
body: US stocks closed higher on Dec 10 after the Federal Reserve (Fed) cut interest rates by a quarter point, a widely anticipated move that reassured investors even as policymakers signalled a pause in further easing for now. Reuters reported that markets took comfort from the Fed’s updated projections, which still pencilled in another quarter-point cut in 2026, while lifting its 2026 growth forecast to 2.3% from 1.8% and holding its unemployment outlook at 4.4%. Chair Jerome Powell avoided offering near-term guidance but underscored downside risks to the labour market, reinforcing hopes the Fed will act again if jobs weaken. The S&P 500 rose 0.67% to 6,886.68, closing just shy of its late-October record. The Dow Jones Industrial Average jumped 1.05% to 48,057.75, while the Nasdaq Composite added 0.33% to 23,654.16. Rate-sensitive stocks led the advance, with the Russell 2000 surging 1.3% to a record closing high, outperforming large caps as investors leaned into easing expectations. Sector gains were broad-based, with industrials leading the S&P 500, up 1.8%. GE Vernova soared 15.6% after forecasting stronger 2026 revenue, pointing to robust demand for artificial intelligence-linked energy infrastructure. Defensive corners lagged, with utilities down 0.1% and consumer staples barely changed. Market breadth was firmly positive. Advancers topped decliners nearly 3-to-1 on the NYSE, where new highs swamped new lows, while Nasdaq gainers also comfortably outnumbered losers. Trading volume was slightly below average, with 16.9 billion shares changing hands. For investors, the message was clear: The Fed may be pausing, but the door to further cuts and higher stocks remains open. title: Ringgit Hits 4.10 Best In Four Years As Fed Cut Drags USD
body: The ringgit surged to its strongest level in more than four years at its open on Dec 11 after the US Federal Reserve (Fed) cut interest rates by 25 basis points, weakening the greenback and lifting emerging-market currencies. At 8am, the ringgit strengthened to 4.1010/1075 against the US dollar, its best level since Oct 5, 2021, from the closing of 4.1155/1195 on Dec 10. Gains against the dollar, however, were not mirrored across major currencies as the local currency slipped versus the Japanese yen to 2.6342/6388, weakened against the British pound at 5.4896/4983 and edged lower against the euro to 4.7982/8058. By contrast, the ringgit firmed against most ASEAN peers, strengthening versus the Singapore dollar to 3.1737/1789, the Indonesian rupiah to 245.7/246.2, and the Thai baht to 12.9112/9382. It also opened higher against the Philippine peso at 6.92/6.94. The Fed’s move has reignited demand for regional currencies, with the ringgit emerging as an early beneficiary as markets reassess the US rate outlook.
