Spot gold gained 0.7% to US$4,236.57 per oz, while US gold futures for February delivery fell slightly to US$4,224.70. The Fed’s latest quarter-point rate cut came in a divided vote, with officials signalling a likely pause on further easing as they monitor the labour market and inflation. Lower rates boosted the appeal of non-yielding assets like gold, even as policymakers remain split over the scale of potential cuts next year. Spot silver surged to a record US$61.85 per oz, up 113% this year, driven by strong industrial demand, falling inventories, and its growing status as a critical mineral. Meanwhile, platinum fell 2.4% to US$1,654.55, and palladium dropped 2% to US$1,475.94, reflecting softer industrial metal sentiment. title: Bursa Malaysia Climbs On Fed Rate Cut

title: Wall Street Pauses Ahead Of Fed Decision As JPMorgan Warning Weighs On S&P 500
body: The S&P 500 closed slightly lower on Tuesday as investors braced for a potentially hawkish tone from the Federal Reserve even if policymakers deliver an expected rate cut this week. Sentiment was also hit by a slide in JPMorgan after the bank warned of higher expenses in 2026. The Fed began its two day meeting on Tuesday, with traders widely expecting a 25 basis point reduction despite inflation remaining above the central bank’s 2% target. Mixed signals from policymakers have added uncertainty, with some stressing risks of renewed price pressures while others have highlighted concerns about labour market softness. Fresh jobs data did little to settle the debate. Job openings rose marginally in October but hiring stayed subdued, while a survey by the National Federation of Independent Business indicated more companies intend to add workers soon. Jeff Schulze, head of economic and market strategy at ClearBridge, said the market now expects a “modestly less dovish Fed” following the job openings data. CME’s FedWatch Tool shows traders pricing in an 87% chance of a quarter point cut on Wednesday, although Schulze said investors are increasingly anticipating a potential pause after that move. US Treasury yields climbed ahead of the Fed’s update, adding further pressure on equities. Justin Bergner, portfolio manager at Gabelli Funds, said the rally in yields is making investors more cautious. The US 10 year yield rose to 4.18%, marking its fourth straight day of gains. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 179.03 points, or 0.38%, to 47,560.29. The S&P 500 slipped 6 points, or 0.09%, to 6,840.51, while the Nasdaq Composite gained 30.58 points, or 0.13%, to 23,576.49. The small cap Russell 2000 reached an intraday record before closing up 0.2%. Bank shares were volatile. The S&P 500 bank index reversed a near 1% rise to end down 2% after JPMorgan’s consumer and community banking chief Marianne Lake said expenses are expected to reach about US$105 billion in 2026 due to growth and volume related costs. JPMorgan closed 4.7% lower, its sharpest one day drop since April. Five of the 11 S&P 500 sectors finished in negative territory. Energy led gainers with a 0.7% rise while healthcare was the biggest laggard with a near 1% decline. Technology trading was choppy. US President Donald Trump said the administration would allow Nvidia to export its H200 AI chips to China subject to a 25% fee. However the Financial Times reported Beijing may limit access to the chips. Nvidia dipped 0.3% while the Philadelphia semiconductor index inched down 0.04%. Investors are also watching upcoming results from Oracle and Broadcom which may offer fresh clues on corporate spending for AI infrastructure. Media stocks were in focus as traders monitored the bidding battle between Paramount Skydance and Netflix for Warner Bros. Warner gained 3.8%, Paramount added 0.5% and Netflix slipped 0.08%. Among individual movers Campbell Soup dropped 5.2% after raising prices to offset rising costs. AutoZone fell 7.2% after missing quarterly expectations. Along with JPMorgan they were the S&P 500’s worst performers of the day. Market breadth was positive on both major exchanges. On the NYSE advancing stocks led decliners by a 1.14 to 1 ratio with 209 new highs recorded. The Nasdaq saw 2,642 gainers versus 2,137 losers and posted 100 new highs. Total trading volume across US exchanges reached 14.50 billion shares, below the 20 session average of 17.34 billion. title: Ringgit Opens Lower Vs US Dollar, Gains Against Other Major Currencies On Fed Cut Expectations
body: The ringgit opened lower against the US dollar on Wednesday as investors focused on incoming US economic data and the Federal Reserve’s anticipated 25-basis-point rate cut after its two-day meeting concludes later tonight. At 8 am, the local currency was quoted at 4.1140/1250 against the greenback, compared with 4.1105/1165 at Tuesday’s close. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US Dollar Index rose 0.13% to 99.220 amid mixed labour market signals. “The local note should remain well supported, although it may trade in a narrow range of RM4.11 to RM4.12,” he told Bernama. Mohd Afzanizam added that the market has largely priced in the 25-basis-point cut by the US Federal Open Market Committee on Wednesday. He noted that the key question now is whether the FOMC will maintain a cautious stance next year or pursue more aggressive rate cuts, especially with inflation potentially remaining elevated due to reciprocal US tariffs. The ringgit strengthened against other major currencies. It rose against the British pound to 5.4729/4875 from 5.4863/4943, improved versus the euro to 4.7838/7966 from 4.7900/7970, and edged higher against the Japanese yen to 2.6236/6307 from 2.6332/6373. However, the local currency slipped against regional peers. It declined versus the Singapore dollar to 3.1719/1807 from 3.1705/1753, fell against the Indonesian rupiah to 246.6/247.4 from 246.4/246.9, and weakened versus the Thai baht to 12.9225/9680 from 12.9172/9413. The ringgit also eased against the Philippine peso to 6.95/6.97 from 6.94/6.96. title: Crypto Market Firms As Ethereum Rallies, Bitcoin Consolidates
body: The cryptocurrency market strengthened on Dec 12, with Ethereum leading gains while Bitcoin held steady at elevated levels, signalling improving sentiment among investors toward year-end. Bitcoin consolidated above the US$91,000-mark, trading around US$92,258, up about 2.1% from the previous close. Prices swung between an intraday low of US$89,697 and a high of US$94,522, reflecting active but orderly trading. Market participants said Bitcoin’s ability to hold key support levels suggested that selling pressure had eased, even as investors remained sensitive to global macroeconomic signals. On the other hand, Ethereum outperformed as it surged 6.2% to roughly US$3,310.59. The world’s second-largest cryptocurrency moved within a range of US$3,093.37 to US$3,392.39, driven by renewed interest in its ecosystem. Optimism around staking demand, Layer-2 network growth and longer-term protocol upgrades helped lift sentiment, allowing Ethereum to extend gains ahead of the broader market. Despite the firmer tone, investors stayed cautious, closely watching US economic data and central bank policy expectations for direction. Institutional participation remained selective, with traders wary of sudden shifts in liquidity conditions that could trigger renewed volatility. Overall, Bitcoin’s consolidation and Ethereum’s stronger performance point to a market in recalibration rather than retreat, as investors position for potential opportunities in the final stretch of the year. title: Asian Shares Ease As Fed Cut Priced, Guidance Uncertain
body: Asian shares and Wall Street futures gave ground on Wednesday as crunch time neared for a divided Federal Reserve policy board, and earnings results threatened to test sky-high valuations in the AI space. With most assets frozen in the Fed headlights, attention was grabbed by a sudden slide in the Japanese yen and the continued dizzy ascent of silver prices, which both hit record peaks. The futures market, at least, is confident the Fed will cut rates by a quarter point to 3.50-3.75 per cent later in the day, pricing it at a 89 per cent probability. Yet it also assumes the guidance will be hawkish, implying just a 21 per cent chance of a January move. Much will depend on how many “dot plot” forecasts from Fed members see one, two or no more cuts next year. Analysts also suspect at least two of the 12 voters could dissent against an easing, putting Chair Jerome Powell in a difficult position.”Powell will likely get across that the bar for future cuts has risen and explain why some participants opposed a cut,” wrote David Mericle, chief U.S. economist at Goldman Sachs. “But the Fed cannot box itself in too much — especially at a time when we are two employment reports out of date — because a January cut could turn out to be appropriate.” The November payrolls report has been delayed to December 16 because of the government shutdown, while inflation figures are due two days later. Debt markets could be pleasantly surprised should analysts at BofA prove right and the Fed announces plans to start buying Treasury bills from January to head off a liquidity squeeze. For now, equity investors were putting discretion ahead of valour and kept trading to a minimum. Japan’s Nikkei started higher but soon fell 0.5 per cent, while South Korea lost 0.4 per cent. title: Wall Street Ends Lower Ahead Of Key Fed Decision As Treasury Yields Rise
body: Wall Street’s main indexes closed lower on Monday as investors awaited the Federal Reserve’s monetary policy update due on Wednesday, while US Treasury yields rose, adding pressure on equities. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 215.67 points, or 0.45%, to 47,739.32, the S&P 500 lost 23.89 points, or 0.35%, to 6,846.51, and the Nasdaq Composite dropped 32.22 points, or 0.14%, to 23,545.90. Most S&P 500 industry sectors finished in the red, with the exception of technology, which gained 0.9% boosted by Microsoft, Nvidia and Broadcom. Investor attention was partly on consumer spending data from last week, which showed moderate growth toward the end of the third quarter, bolstering expectations for a December rate cut. Traders are now pricing in an approximately 89% chance of a 25-basis-point reduction, according to CME’s FedWatch Tool. “It’ll be hard for the market to find a direction that it wants to follow until after the Fed meeting,” said Carol Schleif, chief market strategist at BMO Private Wealth. Market dynamics were further affected by US Treasury yields, with higher yields weighing on stocks. The 10-year Treasury yield rose soon after a powerful earthquake struck off Japan’s northeastern coast before US markets opened. In individual stock movements, Paramount Skydance’s $108.4 billion hostile bid for Warner Bros Discovery attracted significant attention. Shares of Warner Bros Discovery rose 4.4%, Paramount’s stock jumped 9%, while Netflix fell 3.4%, dragging down the S&P 500 Communication Services Index, which closed down 1.8%. Alphabet and Meta Platforms were also notable drags on the sector, with Alphabet falling more than 2%. Elsewhere, Marvell Technology fell 7% after missing out on a spot in the S&P 500 to Carvana, whose shares rose 12%. Confluent surged 29% after IBM announced an $11 billion acquisition, while Tesla declined 3% following a bearish note from Morgan Stanley. Looking ahead, the market will shift focus to upcoming tech earnings from Broadcom and Oracle, amid investor scrutiny over debt-driven AI spending. In a development expected to support AI companies, US President Donald Trump said he would sign an executive order establishing a single national rule for artificial intelligence. Trading volumes on the NYSE saw 16.12 billion shares change hands, with declining issues outnumbering advancers 2.04-to-1. On the Nasdaq, 2,092 stocks rose against 2,672 declines, while the S&P 500 posted 20 new 52-week highs and 10 new lows. Oppenheimer maintained a bullish outlook despite Monday’s declines, forecasting a year-end 2026 target of 8,100 points for the S&P 500, citing strong earnings and macroeconomic resilience. title: Stock Today: Tanco Dips 3.39% As Port Project HOA Announced
body: Tanco Holdings Bhd’s shares fell 3.39% to RM1.14 as of 12.18 pm, with a traded volume of 34.2 million shares. The stock opened at RM1.18, hit a high of RM1.20 and a low of RM1.10, while the last average closing price stood at RM1.18. The property developer signed a Heads of Agreement (HOA) with CCCC Dredging Southeast Asia Sdn Bhd yesterday, a subsidiary of China Communications Construction Company (CCCC), appointing the firm as contractor for the Sea Port Component of its Smart AI Container Port in Port Dickson. The engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) works carry a maximum contract value of RM3.53 billion, subject to final design, costing and commercial terms, with construction expected to be completed within three and a half years. Under the HOA, CDSA will prepare detailed engineering studies, reclamation and piling methodologies, marine structure designs, costing supported by external benchmarking and compliance plans aligned with Malaysian and international port standards. CDSA is a wholly-owned subsidiary of CCCC Dredging Group Co. Ltd, which has overseen major marine engineering projects globally, including Yangshan Deep-Water Port and Colombo Port City. The agreement marks a significant step for Tanco in expanding its infrastructure footprint, though the share price decline reflects market caution amid the large-scale project announcement. title: Ringgit Opens Slightly Lower Ahead Of FOMC Meeting, Trades In Narrow Range
body: The ringgit opened marginally weaker against the US dollar this morning, trading at 4.1120/1220, compared with 4.1100/1145 at yesterday’s close, as market participants awaited the start of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) two-day meeting. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid noted that the US Dollar Index (DXY) rose 0.10% to 99.087 points ahead of the meeting. “US Treasury bond yields were also higher as fixed income traders and investors become increasingly wary about what could be said and projected when the FOMC meeting concludes tomorrow,” he told Bernama. He added that a 25-basis-point US rate cut is widely expected, based on current labour market, business, and consumer data, though the interest rate path for 2026 remains uncertain. “The new Fed chairman could lean towards monetary easing,” he said. At the opening, the ringgit also weakened slightly against the British pound to 5.4797/4930 from 5.4729/4789, edged down versus the euro to 4.7868/7984 from 4.7873/7926, but rose modestly against the Japanese yen to 2.6384/6450 from 2.6429/6460. Against regional currencies, the ringgit strengthened versus the Singapore dollar to 3.1687/1769 from 3.1698/1735 and advanced against the Thai baht to 12.8822/9224 from 12.9006/9204, while slipping slightly against the Indonesian rupiah to 246.2/247.0 from 246.1/246.5. Analysts suggest that as long as gold remains above key support levels, the positive trading bias will continue. title: Aussie Dollar Rises As RBA Holds Rates Ahead Of Fed Meeting
body: The Australian dollar strengthened after the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) kept interest rates on hold, as investors await the US Federal Reserve’s policy meeting later this week. The Australian currency advanced 0.2% to $0.6639 after the central bank maintained rates for a third consecutive month at 3.6%, as widely expected, and cautioned that a pickup in inflation could be persistent. “The RBA didn’t try to tamp down hawkish market expectations,” said Sim Moh Siong, currency strategist at Bank of Singapore. “What was said in the meeting matches the market expectations that the RBA has tilted a bit more on the hawkish direction.” RBA Governor Michele Bullock added in a press conference that more rate cuts were not needed, helping the currency extend its gains. title: Asian Markets Slip As Investors Brace For Fed Signals
body: Asian equities retreated on Tuesday as traders grew increasingly cautious ahead of the US Federal Reserve’s final meeting of the year. With a rate cut on Wednesday seen as a foregone conclusion, attention has shifted to what policymakers project for 2025. Much of the focus now centres on the Fed’s “dot plot”, which will outline the expected path of interest rates. Investors will also scrutinise the statement released after the meeting and Jerome Powell’s press conference for any hints of the debate playing out among central bank officials. Market sentiment, once buoyed by hopes of a string of reductions next year, has softened. Bloomberg reported that traders are now pricing in two cuts in 2025 instead of the three anticipated just a week earlier. “This decision is unlikely to be unanimous, with dissent expected from hawks and doves,” wrote Fiona Cincotta, senior market analyst at City Index. “The focus will be on economic projections and the dot plot to provide further insight into the Fed’s plans for next year. The market sees two rate cuts by the summer. Should the Fed’s dot plot differ from this, there could be volatility.” Expectations for more aggressive easing had climbed in recent weeks thanks to data signalling a cooling labour market, which helped counter fears of persistent inflation. That optimism also received a boost last month after reports suggested President Donald Trump’s top economic aide Kevin Hassett was the frontrunner to take over the Fed once Powell’s term concludes. But some analysts warn that internal divisions at the Fed could complicate the road ahead. Pictet Wealth Management senior US economist Xiao Cui said, “We expect solid growth, above-target inflation, and a slowing labour market to increase internal divisions at the (policy board) and make 2026 a particularly challenging year for policymakers. Downside risks to the labour market should lead the Committee to cut once more in December, before shifting to a quarterly pace of cuts in March and June.” She added that her team “see risks that Fed cuts are delayed into the second half of 2026”. Asian markets struggled following declines across Wall Street’s major indexes. Hong Kong, Shanghai, Sydney, Seoul, Wellington, Taipei and Manila all drifted lower, while Tokyo, Singapore and Jakarta managed to edge into positive territory. Chip-makers traded in mixed fashion after Trump said he had reached an agreement with China’s President Xi Jinping to allow Nvidia to sell advanced artificial intelligence chips to China, in a shift away from the restrictions imposed under Joe Biden. Those rules had required semiconductor firms to design downgraded versions tailored specifically for the Chinese market. Tokyo-listed Renesas climbed more than 2 per cent, with Advantest also higher and SoftBank extending gains. In contrast, Samsung in Seoul shed more than 1 per cent and SK hynix lost nearly 2 per cent. TSMC slipped 1 per cent in Taipei. title: Stock Today: VS Industry Dips 1.06%, Eyes Remain On The Prize
body: VS Industry Bhd saw its share price slip 1.06% to RM0.465 as of 11.55 am, with 16.9 million shares traded. The stock opened at RM0.475, touched a high of RM0.480 and a low of RM0.460, with the last done slightly below the last closing price of RM0.470. The electronics manufacturing services provider recently reported its first quarter results for FY26, posting revenue of RM1.08 billion, down marginally from RM1.11 billion a year ago due to weaker sales in Indonesia. Profit after tax and non-controlling interest came in at RM30.6 million, in line with the same period last year, and marked a rebound from a net loss of RM33 million in 4QFY25. Quarter-on-quarter, revenue rose 25.6% from RM858.8 million, aided by higher sales orders and a reversal of impairment losses on trade receivables. Analysts remain positive on the stock despite the modest share price dip. RHB Investment Bank has maintained a BUY rating with a target price of RM0.65, citing improving operations in Malaysia and the Philippines, alongside new customer wins. CIMB Investment Bank upgraded VS Industry from Hold to BUY with a slightly higher target of RM0.66, highlighting operational improvements and trade diversion opportunities as key drivers. The company’s Malaysian division sustained pre-tax margins of 4.6%, while Philippine operations narrowed losses and are expected to break even by year-end with the commencement of a second production line. New floorcare and haircare lines in Malaysia are projected to contribute RM900 million–1 billion annually once fully operational, representing up to 25% of group revenue in FY26. A newly secured pool-cleaning customer contract worth RM300 million per annum will further support growth from March 2026. With the stock trading at 12 times CY26F P/E, near 1.5 standard deviations below its five-year mean, analysts see VS Industry at a potential inflection point, with re-rating catalysts from stronger contributions in the Philippines and a gradual recovery in global consumer spending. title: Stock Today: Sunway Climbs 2.39% As Healthcare Listing Gains Momentum
body: Sunway Bhd traded higher at midday as investors continued to react to fresh progress on the upcoming listing of its healthcare arm, Sunway Healthcare Holdings (SHH). As of 2.34 pm, the counter rose 2.39% to RM5.56, adding RM0.13 from the previous close. It opened at RM5.48 before moving within a range of RM5.46 to RM5.57, with more than 2.33 million shares changing hands. The latest gain follows the Securities Commission Malaysia’s approval on 4 December for SHH’s proposed Main Market listing, a move that positions the exercise as one of the largest healthcare IPOs planned in the country. The approval includes a significant share split that will expand SHH’s base from 1.21 billion to 10.93 billion shares, alongside a two-step distribution exercise involving 676.04 million SHH shares. These shares will be distributed to eligible Sunway shareholders via a dividend-in-specie at a ratio of one SHH share for every 10 Sunway shares held, excluding treasury shares. The final amount will depend on Sunway’s share base on the entitlement date. SHH is expected to list with 11.5 billion issued shares on Bursa Malaysia once the exercise is completed. title: Stock Today: IJM Dips 1.33% Amid Mixed Earnings Report
body: IJM Corporation Bhd (IJM) closed at RM2.22, down 1.33% from the previous session, with 23.03 million shares traded as of 4.04 pm. The stock opened at RM2.25, hitting a high of RM2.26 and a low of RM2.22 during the day. The decline comes after the group reported 1HFY3/26 core earnings of RM222 million, down 11% year-on-year, representing 40% of CIMB Securities’ previous full-year forecast and 41% of consensus estimates. The earnings shortfall was largely due to weaker property and port contributions, with property pre-tax profit dropping 51% to RM34 million and Kuantan Port pre-tax profit falling 40% to RM72 million. Despite this, IJM’s construction segment posted half-year pre-tax profits of RM72 million, up 37% year-on-year, while the industries division rose 16% to RM107 million, keeping the group on track to surpass its FY26 full-year target. IJM declared a first dividend of 2 sen per share for Q3 FY3/26, in line with last year. The group maintains a robust RM14.4 billion outstanding order book, including RM8.4 billion of domestic projects, with RM5.3 billion secured year-to-date and FY26 targets of RM6–8 billion still within reach. CIMB Securities maintained its Buy rating with a revised sum-of-the-parts target price of RM3.60, citing strong project execution and improved second-half earnings prospects. Last Thursday, the ringgit hit a four-year and five-month high of 4.1115/1165 versus the US dollar, surpassing the previous peak on June 16, 2021, when it closed at 4.1155. title: Bursa Ends Slightly Lower As Investors Brace For Key US Fed Meeting
body: Bursa Malaysia ended the trading session of Dec 8 on a muted note as investors turned defensive ahead of the scheduled US Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on Dec 9-10, with sentiment leaning cautious across the region. At the closing bell, the FBM KLCI slipped 3.74 points, or 0.23%, to 1,612.78, trimming deeper losses from earlier in the session. The benchmark opened marginally softer at 1,616.03 and briefly touched an intraday high of 1,616.49 before heavy selling pushed it to a low of 1,601.50 mid-morning. Bargain-hunting later helped the index claw back most of the declines. Market breadth, however, pointed to sustained weakness as decliners overwhelmed gainers 738 to 328, with 561 counters unchanged and more than 1,100 untraded. Turnover, however, improved to 3.32 billion shares valued at RM2.14 billion compared to 3.17 billion shares worth RM2.24 billion on Dec 5, suggesting active rotation but softer overall value participation. Across the broader indices, sentiment remained cautious, with the FBM 70 falling 70.57 points (0.42%) to 16,652.04, F4GBM slipping 2.33 points (0.24%) to 959.13, FBM Emas easing 36.76 points (0.31%) to 11,925.47 and FBM Shariah declining 12.18 points (0.1%) to 11,784.87. Market watchers said investors are largely in a wait-and-see mode as the FOMC outcome could set the tone for global risk appetite heading into year-end, particularly around the Fed’s interest rate trajectory for 2026. With the Fed looming and global markets turning cautious, traders expect Bursa to stay range-bound in the near term, with any decisive catalyst likely hinging on signals from Washington this week. title: Asia Shares Cautious Ahead Of Key Fed Meeting
body: Asian markets remained subdued on Monday as investors awaited the Federal Reserve’s policy decision later this week, amid expectations of a rate cut. Markets imply roughly an 85 per cent chance of a quarter-point reduction to the 3.75–4.0 per cent funds rate, with a steady decision seen as a potential shock. Michael Feroli, head of U.S. economics at JPMorgan, noted, “We expect at least two dissents in favour of no action and that only a slim majority of the 19 FOMC participants will indicate in their updated dots that a December cut was appropriate.” The upcoming Federal Open Market Committee meeting could mark a rare divergence, as the Fed has not seen three or more dissents at a meeting since 2019. Feroli added that a rate cut in January is likely as insurance against a sustained weakening in the labour market, followed by an extended policy pause. Markets currently price only a 24 per cent chance of a January move, with further easing not expected until July. Central banks in Canada, Switzerland, and Australia are also set to meet this week. The Swiss National Bank may wish to ease to offset franc strength but is hesitant to adopt negative rates, while the Reserve Bank of Australia appears unlikely to cut, with markets even anticipating a late-2026 hike. Equities have been supported recently by hopes for additional Fed stimulus, though cautious trading prevailed ahead of Wednesday’s meeting. S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures were largely unchanged in early trade. Earnings from Oracle, Broadcom, and Costco this week are expected to provide insight into AI demand and consumer trends. In Asia, Japan’s Nikkei slipped 0.3 per cent, while South Korea’s Kospi eased 0.3 per cent following last week’s strong gains. MSCI’s Asia-Pacific index outside Japan fell 0.1 per cent. Chinese blue chips await November trade data for fresh guidance on exports amid tariffs. Bond markets showed pressure as longer-dated Treasuries reacted to potential hawkish Fed guidance, with 10-year yields up slightly at 4.146 per cent. The dollar steadied at 99.013, trading flat against the yen at 155.37, while the euro held at $1.1638. Commodities saw support, with copper reaching record highs, gold at $4,202 an ounce, and oil prices edging higher amid geopolitical concerns. title: Wall Street Ends Week Slightly Higher As Rate-Cut Bets Stay Firm
body: US stocks inched higher on Dec 5, wrapping a choppy week with modest gains as a wave of long-delayed economic data reinforced expectations that the Federal Reserve (Fed) will cut interest rates next week. Reuters reported that with markets still digesting the backlog from the 43-day government shutdown, fresh Commerce Department figures showed consumer spending rose 0.3% in September, exactly in line with forecasts, while the Fed’s preferred inflation gauge, the PCE Price Index, also matched estimates with a 0.3% monthly gain. Annual PCE inflation ticked up to 2.8%. Consumer sentiment improved as well, with the University of Michigan’s index climbing to 53.3, topping expectations. The steady data kept traders confident: Markets are pricing in an 87% chance of a quarter-point cut at the upcoming Fed meeting, up sharply from below 30% two weeks ago after several officials endorsed easing even as a sizable bloc of dissenters is expected. The Dow rose 104.05 points, or 0.22%, to 47,954.99. The S&P 500 added 0.19% to 6,870.40 and the Nasdaq gained 0.31% to 23,578.13. All three major indexes secured a second straight weekly advance. In corporate action, Warner Bros Discovery jumped 6.3% after Netflix clinched a US$72 billion deal to buy its TV, film and streaming operations. Netflix shares slipped 2.9%, while rival bidder Paramount Skydance tumbled 9.8%. Communication services led sector gains, hitting a record close, while healthcare lagged after vaccine advisers dropped a long-standing recommendation for universal newborn hepatitis B shots. Small caps continued their resurgence: The Russell 2000 climbed 0.8% for the week after last week’s 5.5% surge. Ulta Beauty soared 12.7% on raised sales and profit forecasts. title: Wall Street Ends Flat As Investors Await Fed’s Next Move
body: US equities finished Thursday trading largely unchanged, with investors weighing fresh labour-market readings and other economic indicators as expectations for a Federal Reserve rate cut next week remained elevated. Market pricing now indicates an 87% probability of a 25-basis-point cut this month, according to CME’s FedWatch Tool. “Everybody’s waiting around to see what the Fed thinks with any of this data that they’ve seen come in because the last comments from Fed Chair Jerome Powell were a little bit on the hawkish side, but cuts are fully expected,” said Mike Dickson, head of research and quantitative strategies at Horizon Investments. He added, “The short of it is the gold standard is payrolls, and we just don’t have an updated figure there.” The absence of the November payrolls report, delayed due to the extended government shutdown, has pushed traders to rely on secondary indicators. Initial jobless claims fell to their lowest level in more than three years, though analysts noted the Thanksgiving holiday may have influenced the decline. A separate Chicago Fed estimate pointed to unemployment hovering near 4.4% in November. Major indices made only modest moves. The Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped 31.96 points, or 0.07%, to 47,850.94. The S&P 500 edged up 7.40 points, or 0.11%, to 6,857.12, while the Nasdaq Composite gained 51.04 points, or 0.22%, to 23,505.14. Trading activity on U.S. exchanges reached 15.13 billion shares, below the 20-day average of 17.98 billion. The S&P 500 recorded 31 new 52-week highs against five new lows, while the Nasdaq saw 114 highs and 52 lows. Among individual movers, Amazon weighed on the benchmark after its shares fell 1.4%. The company said it was in discussions with the U.S. Postal Service about their future working relationship as its contract approaches expiry next year. Tech names delivered mixed performances. Salesforce rose 3.7% after lifting its fiscal 2026 revenue and adjusted profit forecasts, driven by increasing demand for its artificial intelligence agent platform. Meta Platforms climbed 3.4% following a Bloomberg report that the company planned cuts of up to 30% to its Metaverse budget. Snowflake plunged 11.4% after its fourth-quarter product-revenue forecast fell short of investor expectations. Consumer-related stocks saw sharp divergences. The consumer staples sector was among the session’s weaker performers, dragged down by a 4.6% fall in Kroger after the grocer narrowed its annual sales outlook and missed quarterly estimates. Dollar General, meanwhile, surged 14% as the discount retailer raised its full-year profit forecast. Hormel Foods added 3.8% after projecting annual earnings above expectations. A delayed Commerce Department report also showed factory orders rising 0.2% in September, below the expected 0.5% gain, as earlier tariffs continued to pressure manufacturers following a downwardly revised 1.3% increase in August. Advancers outpaced decliners by a 1.06-to-1 ratio on the NYSE and 1.39-to-1 on the Nasdaq. title: Ringgit Opens Stronger As Fiscal Outlook Boosts Confidence
body: The Malaysian ringgit opened firmer, trading at around RM4.10 to the US dollar, buoyed by improving fiscal conditions and positive investor sentiment. Small caps continued to rally on rate-cut optimism, with the Russell 2000 up nearly 2% following last week’s 5.5% surge. title: Tech And REITs Drive Turnover Surge As SGX’s Next-30 Keep Pace With STI
body: Singapore Exchange (SGX) data show that the 30 most traded stocks outside the Straits Times Index in the second half of 2025 spanned all 12 sectors and carried a combined market capitalisation of S$74.4 billion. SGX said average daily turnover for this cohort jumped to S$214 million in 2H25 from S$115 million in 1H25 for the 27 stocks that were listed across both halves of the year, underscoring a marked lift in market liquidity beyond the headline STI names. Among the 30 counters, three were debutants, Yangzijiang Maritime, NTT DC REIT and Centurion Accommodation REIT (CAREIT) which together accounted for S$34 million of 2H25 ADT. The cohort delivered a median total return of about 25% for the year to December 3, roughly matching the STI’s performance, while median price to book multiples expanded from 1.22 times on 30 June to 1.56 times on December 3. Seven Singapore-listed REITs featured prominently, with a combined market value of S$19.5 billion and 2H25 ADT of S$53.1 million. The REIT group recorded net institutional outflows of S$135 million in 2H25, largely driven by post-listing redemptions at the two new trusts, NTT DC REIT and CAREIT, which together accounted for S$127 million of the net outflow. Suntec REIT, Lendlease Global Commercial REIT and Keppel REIT bucked the trend by attracting institutional inflows while delivering total returns of about 23–25% in 2H25. Technology names posted the second-largest aggregate ADT in the 30, rising to S$44.4 million in 2H25, more than double the S$18.8 million recorded in 1H25. CSE Global, iFAST Corporation and Frencken Group led the pack on net institutional inflow relative to market capitalisation. CSE Global in particular saw ADT surge to S$5.8 million from S$1.4 million in 1H25, following 9 per cent year-on-year revenue growth for 9MFY25, S$513 million in order wins and a strategic partnership with Amazon that could generate up to US$1.5 billion in contracts over five years and potentially give Amazon an 8% stake. Winners among the broader set included CNMC Goldmine, which posted the strongest 2H25 total return at 156 per cent, and PropNex, which gained 82 per cent as institutional interest increased. Other notable movers were Hong Leong Asia, Sheng Siong and ParkwayLife REIT, each recording double-digit 2H25 returns amid sector-specific drivers. SGX noted that research coverage on the 30 stocks increased through the period, with multiple analyst initiations and updates published on the exchange’s Analyst Research portal. The full table of the 30 most traded non-STI counters, with ADT, net institutional flows and total return metrics, is available on SGX’s website for investors seeking deeper detail. title: Ringgit Strengthens On US Rate Cut Speculation
body: The ringgit opened stronger on Thursday, trading at RM4.1100/1200 against the US dollar, up from Wednesday’s close of 4.1200/1235, as expectations of a potential interest rate cut by the US Federal Reserve bolstered sentiment. The US Dollar Index (DXY) fell 0.48% to 98.880 points amid growing market anticipation of monetary easing in the United States next week. “Recent ADP employment data, which showed a decline of 32,000 jobs in the private sector in November, indicates a soft US labour market that may require active Fed intervention through monetary stimulus,” said Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid, chief economist at Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd, speaking to Bernama. On Wednesday, the ringgit surged to a 14-month high against the greenback, reaching 4.1200 at the close, reflecting continued pressure on the US dollar from Fed rate cut expectations. Year-on-year, the local note has strengthened by 8.5%. Dr Mohd Afzanizam added that the ringgit is expected to remain positive today, trading within the 4.11 to 4.13 range. Against other major currencies, the ringgit’s performance was mixed during early trades. It fell slightly against the Japanese yen to 2.6499/6565 from 2.6476/6501, and weakened versus the British pound to 5.4852/4986 from 5.4697/4744, while gaining against the euro at 4.7947/8064 from 4.7982/8080. title: Malaysia Gold Prices Dip As Investors Eye Fed Meeting
body: Gold in Malaysia edged lower, with the price per ounce falling 1.63% (RM235.98) as investors booked profits and awaited next week’s U.S. Federal Reserve meeting for signals on interest rates. The local gold benchmark slipped 0.48% to RM17,240.33 (US$4,192.17) for holdings. Analysts pointed out that caution ahead of the FOMC meeting is weighing on the market. Data from the U.S. showed private payrolls dropped by 32,000 jobs in November, the largest decline in over two and a half years, though overall layoffs remain low. Markets currently price in an 89% probability of a rate cut at the Fed’s December 9–10 meeting, with lower rates typically boosting demand for non-yielding assets like gold. RHB Research highlighted that COMEX gold traded sideways after recouping US$11.70 to close at US$4,232.50 per ounce. “Although the commodity printed a bearish body candlestick, it remains above the US$4,200 breakout point, showing that the bulls still have the technical advantage,” the report said. Immediate support is at US$4,000, followed by US$3,800, while resistance lies at US$4,400 and US$4,500. title: Dollar Holds Near Five-Week Low
body: The US dollar remained steady near a five-week low on Thursday, supported by weak economic data that strengthened expectations for a Federal Reserve rate cut next week. The euro surged to a near seven-week high, while the Japanese yen recovered slightly from recent lows. Traders are pricing in an 85% chance of a quarter-point Fed rate cut at the December 10–11 meeting. Commerzbank FX analysts Thu Lan Nguyen and Antje Praefcke noted, “A Fed rate cut next week is already priced in. What will be decisive for the dollar, though, is whether there will be new hints regarding the direction of monetary policy in subsequent meetings.” Investor attention is also on potential changes at the Federal Reserve. Reports indicate that White House economic adviser Kevin Hassett may succeed Jerome Powell as Fed Chair in May, and he is expected to favour further rate cuts. Concerns over aggressive easing by Hassett have already put pressure on the dollar, with bond investors expressing worries to the US Treasury, the Financial Times reported. The dollar index, which tracks the currency against six major rivals, was little changed at 98.94, remaining down nearly 9% for the year after nine consecutive days of decline. Analysts caution that the strong US economy may limit how far the dollar could fall, despite expectations of medium-term rate cuts. The euro eased slightly to $1.1657 but stayed near its highest level since October 17, supported by euro zone business activity expanding at its fastest pace in 30 months. The currency has risen more than 12% this year, marking its strongest annual gain since 2017, boosted by a weaker dollar and rising likelihood of US rate cuts. Meanwhile, the yen held at 155.22 per dollar, slightly recovering from a 10-month low amid easing intervention fears. Sources familiar with Bank of Japan deliberations suggest the central bank is likely to raise rates in December, though the post-hike path remains uncertain. Wells Fargo’s Chidu Narayanan said, “A still cautious BOJ, attractive carry for long dollar/yen and persistent topside pressure to JGB yields on potential fiscal expansion is likely to keep the pressure on yen weakness.” Sterling remained near a three-week high at $1.3337, while the Swedish crown dipped after slowing annual inflation. The Chinese yuan edged lower but stayed close to a 14-month high following a series of weaker-than-expected official midpoints set by the People’s Bank of China. title: Asian Markets Hesitate As Fed Rate Cut Bets Firm
body: Asian markets struggled to maintain early gains, even after US economic data reinforced expectations that the Federal Reserve will cut interest rates for a third consecutive time next week. While Wall Street extended its recovery for a second day following Monday’s minor selloff, regional traders were more cautious amid lingering concerns over stretched valuations in the technology sector. Bets on a US rate reduction next Wednesday have surged to around 90 per cent in the past fortnight, following comments from several Fed officials emphasising that supporting employment takes precedence over controlling inflation. The latest figures from payrolls firm ADP showed 32,000 jobs were lost in November, versus an expected increase of 10,000, according to Bloomberg. “Hiring has been choppy of late as employers weather cautious consumers and an uncertain macroeconomic environment,” said ADP chief economist Nela Richardson. The report marks the largest jobs decline since early 2023 and underscores the fragility of the US labour market. Elias Haddad of Brown Brothers Harriman & Co added, “Right now, the data argues for additional Fed funds rate cuts. US labour demand is weak, consumer spending is showing early signs of cracking, and upside risks to inflation are fading.” Despite the upbeat sentiment on Wall Street, Asia’s performance was mixed. Tokyo rose alongside Sydney and Manila, but Hong Kong, Shanghai, Seoul, Singapore, Wellington, and Taipei all saw losses. Michael Brown of Pepperstone noted, “Path continues to point to the upside, with the bull case remaining a very solid one indeed, and with participants seeking to ride the coattails of the rally higher, especially amid the increased influence of FOMO/FOMU flows as we move into the end of the year.” Economists at Bank of America offered a note of caution, highlighting that “the most immediate source of volatility remains the US Federal Reserve. While inflation has moderated and the trajectory of policy easing is intact, uncertainty around timing persists. title: Bursa Opens Higher As Risk Appetite Returns, Tracking Wall Street Rally
body: Bursa Malaysia kicked off the trading session for Dec 3 on a firmer note, mirroring Wall Street’s overnight gains as renewed interest in risk assets, highlighted by Bitcoin’s surge, lifted overall sentiment. At 9.15am, the FBM KLCI edged up 0.53 point to 1,631.13, after opening slightly stronger at 1,631.46 from yesterday’s closing of 1,630.60. Market breadth was positive, with 202 gainers outpacing 176 losers, while 345 counters were unchanged and nearly 2,000 remained untraded. Turnover reached 147.45 million shares worth RM108.52 million, signalling a cautiously upbeat start to the trading day. title: Bitcoin Reclaims US$90,000 But Crypto Market Still Gripped By ‘Extreme Fear’
body: Bitcoin bounced sharply on Dec 2, vaulting back above US$90,000 after a punishing selloff that wiped out nearly US$1 billion in leveraged positions and rattled Wall Street. Bloomberg reported that the rebound, as much as 6.8% to US$92,323, offered temporary relief but did little to dispel broader jitters across the digital-asset space. Ether surged more than 8% to reclaim the US$3,000 mark, while altcoins including Cardano, Solana and Chainlink jumped over 10% amid a brief rush back into riskier tokens. Traders pointed to a handful of positive catalysts: SEC Chair Paul Atkins signalled upcoming details on an “innovation exemption” for crypto firms, and Vanguard Group’s decision of allowing crypto-heavy ETFs and mutual funds on its platform, a notable shift from its historically cautious stance. The bounce followed Dec 1’s plunge, sparked by concerns that Strategy Inc (formerly MicroStrategy) might sell Bitcoin to meet debt obligations. The firm later reassured markets by announcing a US$1.4 billion cash reserve. Still, signs of strain are everywhere. Bitcoin’s funding rate has flipped negative, indicating rising demand for bearish bets, while the token remains nearly 30% below its early-October record after US$19 billion in leveraged positions were flushed out. Trump-linked digital assets have been hit even harder. Shares of American Bitcoin Corp, co-founded by Eric Trump, collapsed by up to 51% in minutes, triggering multiple trading halts. TRUMP, the official memecoin, has plunged from US$73.40 in January to about US$6, while WLFI and MELANIA tokens have also suffered steep declines. Investor nerves remain frayed, with stablecoin balances on exchanges climbing as traders retreat to the sidelines. CoinMarketCap’s “Fear and Greed Index” held firmly in “extreme fear” territory, a stark reminder that despite Dec 2’s rally, the crypto market’s footing is still precarious. title: Wall Street Dips As Treasury Yields Rise
body: US equities ended lower on Monday, weighed down by rising Treasury yields and data showing a continued slump in the manufacturing sector, as investors looked ahead to the Federal Reserve’s policy announcement next week. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 427.09 points, or 0.90%, to 47,289.33, while the S&P 500 lost 36.46 points, or 0.53%, to 6,812.63. The Nasdaq Composite slipped 89.76 points, or 0.38%, to 23,275.92. The Institute for Supply Management’s survey revealed that U.S. manufacturing contracted for a ninth consecutive month in November, with factories struggling with weaker orders and lingering tariff effects. The data added pressure to sectors such as real estate and utilities, which are sensitive to higher bond yields. Investors are largely pricing in a 25-basis-point rate cut from the Fed at the conclusion of its two-day meeting on December 10, with an 85.4% probability, according to CME’s FedWatch Tool. Joe Saluzzi, partner and co-founder of Themis Trading, said, “The market actually is still obviously earnings-driven, we went through earnings season, but now it’s the Fed. I see no reason why the uptrend doesn’t continue, at least, not as quickly, but maybe more of a grind up to the end of the year.” Crypto-linked stocks faced significant pressure following a drop in bitcoin. Coinbase fell 4.8%, U.S.-listed Bitfarms shed 5.7%, and Strategy, the world’s largest holder of bitcoin, declined 3.3% after trimming its 2025 earnings forecast. Bitcoin briefly fell below $85,000, contributing to the crypto market losing over US$1 trillion in value from its peak of around US$4.3 trillion, according to CoinGecko. Meanwhile, big-box retailers saw modest gains amid Cyber Monday spending, with Walmart and Target rising 0.9% and 0.8%, respectively. The S&P 500 retail index edged up 0.2%. Semiconductor design software provider Synopsys jumped 4.9% after AI chip leader Nvidia announced a US$2 billion investment. Trading volumes were below the 20-day average, with 15.64 billion shares exchanged on U.S. exchanges, compared with the 18.64 billion average. On the NYSE, declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 1.86-to-1 ratio, while on the Nasdaq the ratio was 2.33-to-1. The S&P 500 posted 17 new 52-week highs and one new low, and the Nasdaq recorded 76 new highs and 78 new lows. Investors also awaited the delayed September report on the Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index, the Fed’s preferred gauge of inflation, due on Friday. title: Stock Today: TNB Slips 3.9% Despite Positive Outlook
body: Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) was trading at RM12.80, down RM0.52 or 3.9% on a volume of 18.98 million shares as of 4.40 pm. The stock opened at RM13.28, reached an intraday high of RM13.34 and a low of RM12.78, with the last average traded price at RM13.32. The decline comes amid profit-taking despite continued analyst support. MBSB Investment Bank Bhd and Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) maintain their BUY calls, citing a clearer outlook under the new tariff framework, the removal of a longstanding tax overhang and strong demand from data centres. MBSB keeps its target price at RM16.40, while HLIB raised its target to RM17.25, implying a potential total return of 33.6 percent. Analysts noted that the latest regulatory period (RP4) improves stability and transparency, particularly through the dynamic Automatic Fuel Adjustment mechanism, which accelerates fuel-cost recovery and boosts cash flow by at least 2 percent. Electricity demand in Malaysia is projected to rise 2.8 to 3.8 percent this year, with the commercial sector including malls, accommodation services and data centres driving growth. Tenaga currently operates 29 data centre projects with a peak demand of 3.8 GW and has secured 49 projects totalling 7.1 GW of potential demand. The company also received tax approval from the Ministry of Finance for Investment Tax Allowance claims from 2003 to 2024, enhancing future earnings and cash flow. Additionally, TNB has secured extensions for three gas-fired power plants with a combined capacity of 1,262 MW and is positioned for upcoming tenders for 1.4 to 2 GW of new gas and renewable energy projects by the end of 2025. Robust capital expenditure of RM12.0 billion is planned for 2025, supporting smart meters, grid reinforcement and energy transition infrastructure. Dividend yields are expected to remain attractive, with MBSB projecting 3.9 percent for FY26 and HLIB forecasting 4.1 percent, highlighting Tenaga’s appeal for long-term investors. title: Stock Today: Capital A Shares Skyrocket 71% On Robust Earnings And Airline Asset Swap
body: Capital A Bhd’s shares jumped 71.4% to RM0.42 as of 11.46 am, reflecting investor optimism after a robust earnings performance and strategic corporate developments. The counter saw a trading volume of 120.2 million shares, with the stock opening at RM0.325 and hitting a high of RM0.465. The rally follows Capital A’s report of a 3Q25 core net profit of RM236.2 million, bringing its 9M25 core net profit to RM545.3 million, or 107% of Maybank Investment Bank’s full-year estimate. Analysts attributed the outperformance largely to lower-than-expected jet fuel prices, averaging US$99 per barrel in 9M25, and a stronger US$/RM exchange rate of RM4.32, which reduced aviation operating costs denominated in US dollars by 60-70%. Non-aviation segments contributed RM111.1 million to 9M25 core net profit, slightly below expectations due to one-off consultancy, legal, and redundancy expenses. Meanwhile, Capital A’s 41%-owned Thai AirAsia reported a 3Q25 core net loss of THB1,238 million, a sharp decline from a 3Q24 net profit of THB57 million. Following the results, Maybank IB raised Capital A’s earnings forecasts for FY25-FY27 by 53%, 37%, and 39% respectively and increased its sum-of-the-parts target price to RM1.30 from RM1.09, rolling forward the valuation base year to FY26. December is set to be a crucial month for Capital A. The company will go ex-dividend on 2 December for a dividend in specie comprising 1.7 billion new AAX ordinary shares. These shares will be credited to shareholders later in the month alongside the disposal of Capital A’s five airlines to AAX. The move is expected to eliminate the company’s negative shareholders’ equity and could allow Bursa Malaysia to lift its PN17 classification, provided two profitable quarters are posted post-disposal. title: Ringgit Strengthens As Dollar Retreats Ahead Of Fed Meeting
body: The ringgit opened firmer against the US dollar and a basket of major currencies on Tuesday, lifted by expectations of US interest rate cuts following softer-than-expected US economic data. At 8 am, the local note rose to 4.1275/1380 against the greenback from Monday’s close of 4.1300/1365. The US Dollar Index (DXY) eased 0.06 per cent to 99.401 points as the market priced in a likely cut in the Federal Funds Rate next week. “Most respondents from the survey indicated wariness over higher operating cost due to higher import tariffs, which led them to rethink their hiring decision,” said Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid. He noted that the latest Institute for Supply Management (ISM) manufacturing index fell to 48.2 per cent in November, below the consensus estimate of 49.0 per cent, signalling weakening business sentiment. Dr Mohd Afzanizam expects the ringgit to trade around RM4.12–RM4.13 to the US dollar today, as investors remain cautious ahead of the Federal Open Market Committee meeting. The ringgit also strengthened against other major currencies, rising to 5.4528/4667 versus the British pound from Monday’s 5.4644/4730, and improving against the euro to 4.7916/8038 from 4.7995/8070. Against the Japanese yen, it edged higher to 2.6545/6616 from 2.6594/6637 previously. Regional currencies saw mixed moves, with the ringgit up against the Singapore dollar at 3.1836/1919 from 3.1880/1932 and the Indonesian rupiah at 247.6/248.4 from 247.8/248.3. It also appreciated versus the Thai baht to 12.8868/9296 from 12.9026/9290, while remaining flat against the Philippine peso at 7.05/7.07. title: Gold Prices Slip In Malaysia After Hitting Six-Week High
body: Gold prices in Malaysia eased on Tuesday following a six-week peak on Monday, as firmer US Treasury yields and profit-taking tempered market sentiment. At 3.07 am New York time, gold was trading at RM4,208.99 per ounce, down RM32.46 or 0.77% from the previous session. The price per gram stood at RM135.32, while a kilogram of gold was valued at RM135,322.07, reflecting a drop of RM1,043.61. Analysts attributed the decline to rising benchmark 10-year US Treasury yields, which reduced the appeal of non-yielding bullion. US gold futures for December delivery were down 0.6% at $4,250.70 per ounce. “Gold is having a soft performance today, but the fundamental picture has not changed – a picture which includes anticipated US rate cuts, which should be supportive of gold from a yield point of view,” said Tim Waterer, Chief Market Analyst at KCM Trade. Markets are also closely watching upcoming US economic indicators, including Wednesday’s November ADP employment report and Friday’s delayed September Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) index, the Federal Reserve’s preferred inflation gauge. Traders currently price in an 88% chance of a Fed rate cut in December. Precious metals broadly saw declines, with silver down 1.3% to $57.24 per ounce, platinum slipping 0.9% to $1,643.10 and palladium falling 0.4% to $1,419.50. Meanwhile, holdings in the SPDR Gold Trust, the world’s largest gold-backed ETF, rose 0.44% to 1,050.01 metric tons. Despite the near-term dip, analysts remain cautiously optimistic, citing potential US rate cuts as a supportive factor for gold in the medium term. title: FTSE ST Industrials Index Delivers 40% YTD Total Return In 2025
body: The FTSE ST Industrials Index has delivered a 36% total return over the first 11 months of 2025, rising to 40.7% when dividends are included, according to SGX Research. Consensus target prices among index constituents have also climbed 33% this year, from 777.9 to 1,031.9. Hong Leong Asia led the index with a 141% return on S$53 million of net institutional inflows, boosted by the launch of MTU Series 2000 engines by its China Yuchai joint venture in August. Average daily turnover for the stock surged from S$1.1 million in the first half of 2025 to S$4.1 million in the second half, reflecting heightened investor interest. Among small and mid-cap industrials, Hiap Seng Industries, Soilbuild Construction and ASL Marine posted the strongest turnover growth in the second half of 2025, with combined average daily turnover rising from S$0.09 million in 1H25 to S$2.52 million in 2H25. Hiap Seng Industries’ turnover increase followed Chandra Asri Group acquiring an 11.87% stake in July, prompting expectations of expanded business collaborations. Singapore’s industrial sector benefited from three main drivers this year: global economic diversification, rapid adoption of artificial intelligence and automation and robust construction activity domestically. Goods-producing industries recorded above-trend year-on-year growth in the past five quarters, while policy support continues to attract high-tech and data centre investments. Overall, the 16 constituents of the FTSE ST Industrials Index recorded S$269 million of combined net institutional inflows in 2025 to date. Median return on equity for the group was 9.2% as of 30 November, with a median price-to-earnings ratio expanding to 16.8x from 9.5x at the end of June. title: BofA Sees Fed Cutting Rates In December, Two More In 2026
body: Bank of America (BofA) Global Research expects the US Federal Reserve to reduce interest rates by 25 basis points at its December meeting, citing weak labour market conditions and dovish signals from policymakers. The brokerage had previously forecast borrowing costs to remain unchanged. Analysts at BofA noted that two additional quarter-point cuts could follow in 2026, in June and July, potentially bringing the terminal rate to 3.00%-3.25%. “Our forecast of additional cuts next year is due to the change in leadership, not our read on the economy,” BofA said, referring to White House economic adviser Kevin Hassett, who has emerged as the frontrunner to become the next Fed chair. The shift in expectations follows comments from key Fed officials, including New York Fed President and FOMC Vice Chair John Williams, which have fuelled speculation of an earlier rate cut. “By cutting rates next week, we think the Fed would increase the risk of pushing policy into accommodative territory, just as fiscal stimulus kicks in,” BofA added. Traders are largely pricing in an 87.6% chance of a 25-basis-point reduction in December, according to CME Group’s FedWatch Tool. Most major brokerages anticipate a cut next week, although some, including Morgan Stanley and Standard Chartered, expect the Fed to hold rates steady. The Federal Reserve’s policy meeting is scheduled for December 9 and 10, and market participants are closely watching for any indications of the central bank’s stance on interest rates for the year ahead. title: Optimism On Padini’s Resilience And Growth Potential
body: Padini Holdings Bhd has received multiple analyst upgrades following its first-quarter results for FY26, signalling optimism over the affordable fashion retailer’s resilience and growth potential. RHB Investment Bank Bhd upgraded Padini to BUY from Neutral with an unchanged target price of RM2.16, implying 20% upside and a projected FY26 dividend yield of 4%. RHB highlighted that strong quarter-on-quarter earnings growth underpinned the upgrade, noting that the company’s value-for-money pricing and strong brand equity have kept shopper demand intact despite cautious consumer sentiment. Meanwhile, MBSB Investment Bank Bhd maintained its BUY call with a revised target price of RM2.22, citing modest revenue and earnings growth that fell short of earlier expectations, and CIMB Investment Bank kept its BUY recommendation, adjusting its target price to RM2.40, expecting stronger quarters ahead backed by festive periods, margin gains from a stronger MYR against the RMB, and continued consumer downtrading. Padini’s 1QFY26 core net profit came in at RM21–22.5 million, representing around 12% of full-year forecasts, broadly in line with seasonal expectations for the typically softer first quarter. Revenue rose 2% year-on-year to RM401.1 million, supported by new store openings including Padini’s first standalone outlet in Limbongan, Melaka. Gross profit margin strengthened to 39.9%, up 4.3 percentage points from the previous year, lifted by a more profitable sales mix and favourable foreign exchange movements. EBITDA margin improved to 19.2% from 15.9% a year earlier, driven by higher gross margins and lower administrative expenses. Sequentially, revenue grew 2.3% quarter-on-quarter, while core net profit jumped over 200%, reflecting cost control and lower depreciation. The company declared a second interim dividend of 1.8 sen per share, with the first-half FY26 dividend totalling 3.6 sen, slightly higher than 1HFY25. Looking ahead, analysts expect Padini to benefit from seasonal demand increases linked to festive periods and school holidays, as well as tourism-related growth ahead of Visit Malaysia Year 2026. title: Looking Forward To BIMB’s Next Five-Year Strategy
body: Bank Islam Malaysia Bhd (BIM) continues to draw analyst attention, with MBSB Investment Bank maintaining its BUY call and unchanged target price of RM2.42, reflecting expectations of steady earnings growth and strong fee income expansion. The research house noted that the bank’s branch revamp initiatives have been highly successful, contributing to rapid gains in non-interest income (NOII), while recent growth in business loans and the expansion of digital touchpoints further support revenue momentum. BIMB’s valuation remains attractive, trading at a forward FY26 price-to-book value of 0.66 times, below -1 standard deviation of its 10-year mean, while offering a projected dividend yield of 6.6%. BIMB reported a 9MFY25 core net profit of RM382 million, down three percent year-on-year but broadly in line with expectations, representing 74% of MBSB’s and 71% of street full-year forecasts. The decline reflected weaker net interest income, higher operating expenses and increased provisioning charges, partly offset by stronger fee income. The third quarter alone saw core profit rise two percent quarter-on-quarter to RM129 million, as lower operating expenses and provisions mitigated pressure from net interest income and NOII. The bank declared a dividend per share of 10.0 sen for 9MFY25, representing a payout ratio of 59%. Looking ahead, management remains optimistic as BIMB closes its LEAP25 strategy, preparing a new five-year plan that emphasises higher-yielding non-retail assets and further NOII expansion. Growth in bancatakaful, wealth management, gold accounts, and al-Rahnu contributed to a 20% year-on-year increase in fee income, highlighting the success of branch revamp efforts. The bank is expected to maintain stable net interest margins in 4QFY25 under a revised calculation methodology. At the same time, cost control programmes have already delivered RM52 million in savings as part of the three-year CORE initiative. Nonetheless, operating expenses remain elevated due to workforce expansion, union salary negotiations and technology investments. BIMB’s asset quality remains strong, underpinned by ample loan loss coverage and robust provisioning buffers. The bank’s focus on primary housing loans and non-packaged personal financing is set to continue, supported by regulatory changes and competitive dynamics. Overlay top-ups and reduced net credit cost guidance indicate manageable credit risk, while seasonal upticks in delinquency are expected to normalise. Analysts caution that risks include poor cost control, steeper-than-expected NIM compression, and weaker NOII performance. With its attractive valuation, high dividend yield, and ongoing business transformation, BIMB remains positioned as a resilient player in Malaysia’s financial services sector. As of 11.56 am, the stock price increased slightly by 0.43% to RM2.31. title: December Starts Red For Crypto As Bitcoin, Ethereum Slide
body: Bitcoin and Ethereum kicked off December on a weak footing as markets faced renewed volatility, pressured by risk-off sentiment and lingering concerns over liquidity in the digital-asset ecosystem. Bitcoin slipped as much as 4.3%, falling below US$88,000, while Ethereum dropped nearly 6% to trade under US$2,900. The pullback underscores a shaky start to the month after November’s sharp retracement. The declines come amid heightened unease following a liquidity scare linked to a major decentralised finance platform, which sent ripples across the broader crypto market. The episode has amplified caution among traders already contending with shifting macroeconomic conditions. Market sentiment remains fragile as global investors reassess expectations of support from monetary-policy adjustments. Analysts note that fading hopes of near-term stimulus, coupled with a broader “risk-off” tone across financial markets, has weighed on digital assets. Still, some strategists argue that the scheduled end of the US Federal Reserve’s quantitative tightening programme on Dec 1 could offer a stabilising backdrop for Bitcoin, potentially marking an inflection point if liquidity conditions improve. Ethereum, despite its slide, continues to hover near a key multi-year support zone around US$2,850, a level that traders are watching closely for signs of resilience. Valuation models for Ethereum still signal upside potential, though meaningful recovery is likely to hinge on a broader pickup in market appetite. In the near term, traders are eyeing whether Bitcoin can hold the US$88,000-US$90,000 support band and whether Ethereum demand strengthens within the US$2,850-US$3,000 range. Both levels are increasingly seen as critical to preventing deeper pullbacks. With macro signals mixed and crypto-specific risks resurfacing, analysts expect a volatile start to December, though pockets of cautious optimism remain should liquidity conditions improve. title: Asian Markets Mixed Ahead Of US Data And Fed Decision
body: Asian equities were mixed on December 1, as investors awaited key US economic data that could influence the Federal Reserve’s policy ahead of a widely anticipated interest rate cut next week. After a late-November rebound across global markets, investor confidence remains elevated amid speculation that the US central bank could continue easing monetary policy into the new year. The rebound has helped offset lingering concerns about an AI-driven technology bubble that some analysts warn could trigger a painful market correction. Traders are particularly focused on this week’s release of private jobs data, services activity, and personal consumption expenditure figures, the Fed’s preferred gauge of inflation, to gauge the likelihood of a third consecutive rate cut on December 10, which is currently seen as roughly 90 per cent probable. Bets on lower borrowing costs surged in late November after several Fed policymakers indicated that a weakening labour market is a greater concern than persistently high inflation. Chris Weston, from Pepperstone, noted that as market anxiety from mid-November fades, it is being replaced by concerns about underperformance and missing out on gains. He added, “Risk managers remain highly astute to the landmines that could still derail the improving risk backdrop through December,” citing possibilities such as the Fed not cutting rates, a “hawkish cut”, potential Supreme Court rulings on trade tariffs, and upcoming US jobs and inflation reports. Reports that Kevin Hassett, a proponent of rate cuts, is the frontrunner to head the Fed next year also boosted sentiment among investors. Regional performance was mixed following strong gains last week and Wall Street’s Thanksgiving rally. Markets in Hong Kong, Shanghai, Singapore, and Bangkok rose, while Sydney, Seoul, Wellington, Manila, Mumbai, and Taipei fell. Tokyo lost 1.9 per cent as the yen strengthened amid expectations that the Bank of Japan may lift interest rates this month. BoJ Governor Kazuo Ueda stated the central bank would “consider the pros and cons of raising the policy interest rate and make decisions as appropriate,” with Bloomberg citing more than a 60 per cent chance of a December 19 hike. Meanwhile, oil prices jumped about 2 per cent after OPEC+ confirmed it would not increase output in the first quarter of 2026, citing lower seasonal demand. Traders remain cautious over crude’s outlook, watching for developments in Ukraine peace talks that could return Russian supply to global markets. title: Ann Joo Pins Recovery On Domestic Demand
body: CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) maintained its HOLD call on Ann Joo Resources Bhd with a lower target price of RM0.65 after the group’s third-quarter results showed narrower core losses. The research house said Ann Joo’s performance in the first nine months of 2025 was in line with expectations, although it noted that a meaningful recovery in domestic steel prices remains unlikely for now. CIMB Securities reported that Ann Joo’s core losses for the third quarter of 2025 narrowed by 33 percent quarter-on-quarter to RM46 million, supported by stronger domestic sales volumes and slightly better average selling prices following a brief recovery in Chinese steel prices in July and August. Revenue for the quarter rose 10 percent quarter-on-quarter. However, for the first nine months of 2025, revenue declined 13 percent year-on-year to RM1.6 billion due to weaker selling prices and softer volumes. This resulted in core net losses of RM193 million, compared with RM105 million a year earlier. CIMB Securities said the results are still considered to be within expectations as the fourth quarter may show further improvement alongside a gradual pickup in domestic demand. No dividends were declared for the period. The research house highlighted Ann Joo’s latest move to monetise part of its Prai industrial land bank. On 5 November 2025, the group accepted a letter of offer to dispose of 136 acres of freehold industrial land in Prai to Axis REIT for RM800 million. Ann Joo will lease back the land, which includes its main steel manufacturing plant, for eight years at an initial monthly rental of RM4.2 million. Rental adjustments will begin from the fifth to seventh year as Ann Joo progressively surrenders parts of the leased area. Part of the proceeds will be used to reduce the group’s borrowings. CIMB Securities noted that the entire process may take up to a year to complete. As of September 30 2025, Ann Joo’s net gearing stood at 1.6 times. The group is also assessing options to monetise the remaining 70 acres it owns in the Prai industrial area. CIMB Securities retained its Hold call but trimmed its target price to RM0.65 from RM0.75 after lowering the valuation multiple to account for uncertainties surrounding the proposed carbon tax. It added that Ann Joo’s expansion into downstream value-added steel products, electrification works and opportunities in Singapore may require more time to build momentum. The research house said domestic steel demand should gradually improve in line with the expected revival of infrastructure spending from the first half of 2026 and into 2027, although a strong price recovery remains unlikely in the near term. As of 3.08 pm, the stock price is down by 1.64% to RM0.60. title: Water Tariff Windfall For Ranhill
body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd maintained BUY calls on Ranhill Utilities Bhd, setting a target price of RM2.60 and noting a 41% upside from the current market price of RM1.84 (US$577 million market capitalisation). The company’s shares offer a 1% dividend yield for FY25 and the positive outlook is supported by a strong performance in the water segment and expected long-term demand from data centres, according to RHB. Ranhill Utilities recorded a 1QFY26 core profit of RM29.9 million, up 113% year-on-year, exceeding both RHB and Street estimates, comprising 58% and 41% of full-year projections respectively. Analysts attributed the positive deviation to stronger-than-expected gross profit margins and improved performance in the water segment following the latest tariff hikes. Revenue for the water segment surged 19% year-on-year to RM414.4 million, with segmental profit before tax at RM43.5 million, boosted by the August tariff adjustment. In contrast, the consultancy and services segment fell 39% year-on-year, affected by declining orderbooks at subsidiaries Ranhill Technologies and Ranhill Bersekutu, while the power segment reported a 32% revenue decline due to maintenance and finance costs. Following the results, RHB lifted FY26–28 earnings forecasts by 95%, 90% and 95%, reflecting better gross margin assumptions and anticipated higher water consumption in Johor’s residential, industrial and data centre segments. Analysts highlighted that data centres are expected to drive 15–20% of non-domestic water usage over the next three years, with all 48 planned data centres in Johor expected to be operational by 2030, representing a total committed capacity of 5,100MW. Currently, 15 data centres with 1,700MW capacity are operational and the incremental 3,400MW is estimated to require only 238 million litres per day of water. Additional water supply capacity is projected to come from upcoming water treatment plants such as Semanggar (60 million litres per day, completion 2026) and Layang 2 Phase 2 (150 million litres per day, completion 2027), with a further 890 million litres per day expected from three WTPs beyond 2027. Analysts noted that Johor’s plan to increase total water capacity to about 3,000 million litres per day by 2030 leaves ample room for industrial, residential and Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone consumption, alongside the Rapid Transit System Link project boosting demand in Johor Bahru. RHB cautioned that risks to the call include lower-than-expected water consumption, which could impact profitability, although current forecasts suggest robust growth from core water operations and long-term demand from the data centre sector. The stock is trading at 4.5 times FY26F EV/EBITDA, below the water sector’s 10-year mean of around 6.3 times, providing an attractive valuation entry point. title: US Stocks Rise In Thin Post-Holiday Trade As Rate-Cut Hopes Build
body: US stocks pushed higher on Nov 28 during a shortened, low-volume session after Thanksgiving, lifted by retail strength and a rebound in tech shares. Growing expectations that the Federal Reserve could cut rates as early as December helped support market sentiment throughout the week. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.61% to 47,716.42, the S&P 500 gained 0.54% to 6,849.09 and the Nasdaq Composite added 0.65% to 23,365.69. Every major S&P 500 sector advanced except healthcare, dragged by a 2.6% drop in Eli Lilly. Intel surged 10.2% after a TF International Securities analyst said the chipmaker could begin shipping Apple’s lowest-end M processor by 2027, making it one of the S&P’s strongest performers. All three major indexes ended the week in the green: The S&P 500 jumped 3.73%, the Nasdaq rallied 4.91% and the Dow climbed 3.18%. The gains on Nov 28 nudged the S&P and Dow back into positive territory for the month, though the Nasdaq still closed November down 1.51% as concerns over stretched tech and artificial intelligence valuations triggered profit-taking. Markets briefly wobbled early in the session after a CME Group outage halted trading in currencies, commodities and equity futures worldwide. CME attributed the disruption to a cooling issue at its CyrusOne data centres. CME shares ended slightly higher. The session capped the kickoff to the holiday shopping season — spanning Thanksgiving, Black Friday and Cyber Monday — a pivotal stretch for major retailers and a key gauge of US consumer strength heading into year-end. title: Railway And Highway Project Edge For Econpile
body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd and CIMB Investment Bank Bhd have both maintained BUY calls on Econpile Holdings (ECON MK), with target prices of RM0.50 and RM0.40 respectively, despite the company’s first-quarter fiscal year 2026 (1QFY26) results falling short of expectations. RHB noted that 1QFY26 core net profit of RM1.3 million represented a more than 100% year-on-year (YoY) increase but accounted for only 13% and 9% of their and Street’s full-year forecasts, citing overly optimistic margin assumptions. CIMB highlighted that the earnings miss was driven by minimal net margin uplift and top-line revenue falling short of the RM100 million quarterly target, with 1Q revenue at RM88 million. Econpile’s 1QFY26 revenue expanded 10% YoY, supported by a ramp-up in piling activities and favourable site conditions that optimised machinery and resource deployment. Gross profit margin improved to 8.9% from 6% in 1QFY25, aided by lower material costs. The group’s outstanding order book rose 30% quarter-on-quarter to RM646 million as of end-September 2025, with a tender book hovering around RM1 billion. Year-to-date new job wins reached RM214 million, representing 54% of its FY26 target of RM400 million, including significant piling packages under the Penang Mutiara Line LRT project. RHB and CIMB both cited Econpile’s strong track record in railway and highway-related projects as a key advantage. RHB highlighted potential rerating catalysts including faster-than-expected approvals or rollouts of the Sungai Klang Link project, estimated at RM300–500 million for piling works, as well as subsequent piling packages from the Penang LRT project. CIMB also noted that Econpile is conserving capacity to focus on these high-impact projects and is eyeing additional mixed-use jobs in the Klang Valley worth over RM50 million, expected to be awarded by end-2025 or 1Q26. In light of the earnings miss, both banks revised down their FY26–28F profit forecasts. RHB trimmed its bottom-line forecasts by 13%, 9% and 3% for FY26–28, rolling forward its valuation to FY27 and maintaining a P/BV-based target price of RM0.50. CIMB reduced FY26F/27F/28F core profits by 66%, 20% and 5% respectively, adjusting for lower pre-tax margins and higher input costs such as a 15–30% increase in concrete prices since early November 2025, while retaining a Buy call. Both analysts highlighted manageable net gearing of 15% and the company’s undemanding valuation as supportive factors, though further spikes in raw material prices remain key downside risks. As of 10.30 am, the stock price is noted at RM0.27.
