title: Kossan Rubber Downgraded After Poor 9M Results
body: CIMB Investment Bank Bhd and Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) have both downgraded Kossan Rubber Industries to HOLD , citing weaker-than-expected 9-month fiscal year 2025 (9M25) earnings and a challenging operating environment. CIMB revised its target price to RM1.15 from RM1.55, while HLIB lowered its target price to RM1.13 from RM2.30. Both analysts highlighted the company’s muted near-term catalysts, rising competition, and limited pricing power amid Ringgit strength as factors behind the downgrade. Kossan posted 9M25 core net profit of RM91.4 million, up 18.5% year-on-year, but below CIMB’s and HLIB’s full-year expectations, accounting for only 64–66% of forecasts. The shortfall was mainly attributed to weaker sales volumes and slower margin recovery in the Glove & Clean-room division, which suffered a 10-day production halt in April 2025 due to gas supply disruptions. Despite this, third-quarter fiscal year 2025 (3Q25) core net profit rose 10.9% quarter-on-quarter and 25.1% year-on-year to RM31.3 million, underpinned by higher average selling prices (ASPs) from an improved product mix and lower raw material costs, including nitrile butadiene rubber and natural latex, both down around 8% year-on-year. Revenue for the quarter increased 14.9% quarter-on-quarter, with the Glove & Clean-room segment up 13.9% and the Technical Rubber Product (TRP) segment rising 22.4%, reflecting spill-over orders from 2QFY25. Nevertheless, year-to-date group revenue fell 5.8%, dragged by lingering softness in both the Glove & Clean-room and TRP divisions. CIMB noted that sales volumes were approximately 4.4 billion pieces in 3Q25, implying a plant utilisation rate of 58%. Looking ahead, analysts expect Kossan to post flattish fourth-quarter results due to potential margin compression from Ringgit strength, ongoing demand-supply imbalances and rising competition from new overseas glove manufacturing plants in Indonesia. Cost-saving measures and continued product customisation may partially offset these pressures. Both CIMB and HLIB revised FY25–27 core profit forecasts downwards, reflecting lower ASPs, weaker sales volumes, and slower-than-expected margin recovery. Despite Kossan’s solid balance sheet, with net cash of RM1.6 billion providing liquidity to navigate industry headwinds, analysts remain cautious. The downgrade to Hold reflects the absence of near-term re-rating catalysts and heightened competitive pressures, signalling a more measured growth trajectory for Malaysia’s leading glove maker amid ongoing global market challenges. title: Bumi Armada Dragged By Lower FPSO Contributions
body: MBSB Investment Bank Bhd, CIMB Investment Bank Bhd and Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd have all reaffirmed BUY calls on Bumi Armada Bhd, with revised target prices of RM0.44, RM0.45 and RM0.49 respectively, citing the company’s strong balance sheet and long-term order book as key support despite underwhelming 9-month fiscal year 2025 (9M25) results. MBSB noted that core earnings of RM382 million came in below its expectations at 62% of the forecast but were broadly in line with the consensus at 72%. CIMB highlighted core net profit of RM375.1 million, representing 67.9% of its FY25 forecast, while HLIB observed core earnings of RM376.7 million, tracking 73.1% of consensus estimates. Bumi Armada reported third-quarter fiscal year 2025 (3Q25) core earnings of RM97.9 million, relatively flat quarter-on-quarter (+1.4%) but down 51.3% year-on-year. Revenue declined 11.4% quarter-on-quarter and 34.6% year-on-year to RM360.7 million, affected by the absence of distributions from the bankrupt former charterer of the Armada Perdana FPSO and lower operating and maintenance contributions from the Kraken FPSO. HLIB and CIMB both highlighted that Armada Kraken’s lower charter rate following the commencement of its annual option period in April 2025, along with reduced joint venture contributions, contributed to the earnings shortfall. Despite the weaker performance, analysts underscored the company’s robust financial position. Bumi Armada holds cash balances of approximately RM1.2 billion and maintains a low net gearing of 0.25x, providing flexibility for potential new FPSO bids and capital management initiatives. Its firm vessel contract order book stands at RM8.6 billion, with optional extensions totalling around RM9.2 billion, offering visibility for future revenue streams. title: Analysts Taking Cautious Stance On Inari Amid Weaker 1Q Results
body: Inari Amertron Bhd (INRI) faced a challenging start to FY26, with analysts taking a cautious stance amid weaker-than-expected first-quarter results. MBSB Investment Bank Bhd maintained a NEUTRAL rating with a revised target price of RM2.09, highlighting concerns over the radio frequency (RF) segment and the absence of immediate rerating catalysts, while noting the potential upside from the pending Lumileds acquisition. CIMB Investment Bank Bhd downgraded the stock to HOLD from Buy, raising its target price to RM2.50, citing moderation in RF demand and weaker utilisation, though anticipating some recovery from 2QFY26 onwards with new-generation smartphone launches. Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd also retained its HOLD rating with a lower target price of RM2.00, pointing to near-term headwinds from RF share allocation losses and a weaker US dollar but recognising medium-term catalysts such as optoelectronics growth and the Lumileds acquisition. Inari reported a core net profit of RM55.1 million for 1QFY26, down 28.8% year-on-year and 14.3% sequentially, deviating from its historical trend of stronger first-quarter earnings. Revenue fell 16% to RM325.8 million, affected by lower sales across all segments, particularly the RF business which contracted 21% year-on-year. Generic packages dropped 28% while optoelectronics remained relatively flat. Analysts noted that the decline was also exacerbated by foreign exchange pressures, as the Malaysian ringgit strengthened against the US dollar, along with lower interest income and higher tax expenses. Despite the disappointing earnings, Inari declared a first interim dividend of 1.33 sen, representing a payout ratio of around 97.8%, higher than the 1.0 sen in 1QFY25. Analysts highlighted that the dividend underscores the group’s commitment to shareholder returns even amid soft operational performance. The group continues to advance its strategic initiatives, including the proposed joint acquisition of Lumileds with Sanan Optoelectronics Co. Ltd, expected to close by the end of 3QFY26 or early 2026. Analysts view this move as a potential catalyst for re-rating, as it could diversify Inari’s revenue base and strengthen its advanced packaging capabilities. CIMB also highlighted that RF sales volumes could recover in the second quarter, supported by strong December shipments from a major North American smartphone maker, while HLIB expects opportunities from potential RF content recovery in the next model cycle and increased optoelectronics contributions. For the full year FY26–28, analysts trimmed earnings per share forecasts by 2–20% to reflect the softer RF volume and broader market headwinds, though they remain cautiously optimistic on medium-term prospects. Inari’s solid balance sheet, with RM2.2 billion in cash and zero borrowings, provides a buffer against near-term volatility, supporting dividend payouts and potential strategic expansions. As of 11.32 am, the stock price is down by 5.04% to RM2.26. title: US Dollar Heading For Worst Week Since July
body: The U.S. dollar was heading for its worst weekly performance since late July on Friday as investors increasingly count on further monetary easing in December by the Federal Reserve, while Thursday’s U.S. holiday thinned liquidity. An outage due to a cooling issue at CME Group’s CyrusOne data centres halted trade on its widely-used currency platform and in stock and commodity futures, though trading began to resume at 1200 GMT. “We are not expecting any significant impact on the market, maybe it is something to keep an eye on just in case, but we are going to have a fairly quiet end to the month and the week,” said Lee Hardman, senior currency analyst Global Markets Division for EMEA at MUFG. The dollar index, which measures the greenback’s strength against a basket of six major peers, was last trading up 0.2 per cent at 99.744, recovering some ground. But five days of declines still leave it set for its biggest one-week loss since July 21.U.S. Fed funds futures are pricing an implied 87 per cent probability of a 25-basis-point cut at the Federal Reserve’s next policy meeting on December 10, compared to a 39 per cent chance a week earlier, the CME Group’s FedWatch tool showed. The probability priced in by futures had been rising since New York Fed president John Williams said last week that the U.S. central bank could still cut interest rates “in the near term” without putting its inflation goal at risk. The remarks “give us more confidence that they will cut rates, as we have seen in the FX market since then, which has, at least temporarily, put a dampener on the dollar’s uptrend,” Hardman said. In Asia, the Japanese yen fluctuated after a period of decline. It was last flat at 156.2 yen to the dollar as labour market and inflation data firmed up the case for monetary tightening in Asia’s second-biggest economy, against a backdrop of persistent weakness in the currency that has raised the prospect of intervention from the Ministry of Finance. Consumer prices in Japan rose 2.8 per cent year-on-year in November, slightly faster than economists had expected and above the Bank of Japan’s 2 per cent target. “The yen has kind of stabilised at weaker levels this week, it has reduced pressure on Japan to step in and support the currency,” Hardman said. Hardman said the Japanese government’s comments last week came as a signal that if the yen continues to weaken, then the BOJ would bring forward plans to resume rate hikes. EURO AND STERLING SET FOR BEST WEEK IN OVER THREE MONTHS Elsewhere, the euro was last down 0.3 per cent at $1.1558 on the dollar, but still up around 0.5 per cent for the week and set for its biggest weekly gain since July, amid talks on a U.S.-backed plan to end the Russia-Ukraine war. “While there is considerable caution in markets about the prospects of a peace deal, any material progress from here should weigh on the dollar and support high-beta European currencies,” said Francesco Pesole, FX strategist at ING. Sterling fell 0.2 per cent at $1.3206 on the day, though it was heading for its best weekly performance since early August after British finance minister Rachel Reeves revealed her long-awaited budget earlier this week. Reeves fought back on Thursday against criticism of the government’s spending plans, which will fund extra welfare spending by raising the country’s tax burden to a post-World War Two high. title: Ringgit Advances As Markets Bet On US Rate Cut
body: The ringgit began Friday on a firmer footing against the US dollar, buoyed by growing conviction that the US Federal Reserve may trim rates in December and by improving sentiment toward emerging-market currencies. Opening at RM4.1230/1335, the local unit strengthened from Thursday’s RM4.1305/1345 close. The gains followed a slide in the US Dollar Index, which has slipped just below the 100-point mark as rate-cut expectations intensified. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said “market pricing for a December rate cut has surged to 85 per cent, compared with less than 40 per cent a week ago,” noting that the shift has already driven US Treasury yields lower. Since 14 November, the 2-year and 10-year Treasury yields have fallen by 17 and 14 basis points respectively, now standing at 3.45% and 4.00%. Dr Afzanizam said the downtrend “should provide further support for emerging-market currencies, including the ringgit,” adding that the local note is likely to stay within a narrow RM4.12 to RM4.13 band as traders await fresh US data ahead of the Federal Open Market Committee meeting. In early trading, the ringgit posted mixed movements against major currencies. It firmed against the yen at 2.6379/6448 but eased against the British pound to 5.4589/4728 and was largely unchanged against the euro at 4.7823/7944. Regionally, the ringgit strengthened across ASEAN currencies, rising to 3.1794/1877 against the Singapore dollar and 12.7904/8342 versus the Thai baht. It also appreciated against the Indonesian rupiah at 247.8/248.5 and improved to 7.01/7.03 against the Philippine peso. title: HSIF Stays In Sideways Gear As RHB Sticks To Long Call
body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd has advised traders to maintain their long positions on the Hang Seng Index Futures (HSIF), noting that the contract continued to consolidate while holding above key support levels. The research house said the HSIF edged up 12 points to close slightly higher at 25,943 points, extending its sideways movement below the 20-day simple moving average (SMA). The index opened at 25,884 points and swung between an intraday high of 26,113 points and a low of 25,731 points before settling near the middle of the range. In the evening session, the futures eased by 8 points to last trade at 25,935 points. RHB Research observed that both the 20-day and 50-day SMA lines are acting as near-term resistance, effectively capping further upside for now. Analysts highlighted that the Relative Strength Index (RSI) is also moving sideways, indicating neutral momentum and suggesting that the HSIF is likely to continue trading horizontally until a clearer bullish signal emerges. The consolidation, they noted, is expected to persist unless the index gathers enough strength to decisively break above the moving averages. RHB maintained its positive trading bias during this phase, emphasising that the immediate support stands at 25,000 points. Any profit-taking would likely cause the index to test this level, which remains critical for defending the ongoing upward structure. The next support level is placed at 24,300 points. On the upside, the immediate resistance is projected at 26,500 points, with a stronger barrier seen at 27,400 points. Traders are advised to retain positions initiated at 21,416 points on 14 April, while managing downside risk with a stop-loss at 25,000 points. RHB reiterated that despite the sideways movement, the broader trend remains constructive as long as the support level holds. title: Bursa Ends Week In The Red As KLCI Sinks Below 1,605
body: Bursa Malaysia closed sharply lower on Nov 28, extending its losses on the last trading session of the month as the market grappled with a lack of direction from Wall Street, absence of fresh catalysts and persistent broad-based selling pressure. title: Bitcoin, Ethereum Rebound on Rate-Cut Optimism
body: Bitcoin and Ethereum held steady on Nov 27 as the broader crypto market continued its cautious recovery from mid-November’s sharp downturn. Improved macro sentiment and renewed spot buying helped both assets consolidate recent gains, though analysts warn that momentum remains fragile. Bitcoin traded around US$91,001, slipping a modest 0.39% on the day but maintaining its grip above the crucial US$90,000 handle. The world’s largest cryptocurrency has rebounded sharply from lows near US$81,000 earlier this month, a decline triggered by heavy leveraged liquidations and thinning market liquidity. Market participants attribute the recent stabilisation to dip-buying and short-covering, with several indicators pointing to increased whale accumulation following the sell-off. With derivatives leverage reset and spot demand improving, traders are positioning for a potential retest of the US$95,000-US$100,000 zone in the coming weeks. Ethereum, meanwhile, traded near US$3,010, down 0.99% intraday. While the asset has also shown resilience after falling below US$2,900 during the November correction, technical analysts note that Ethereum’s recovery has been slower than Bitcoin’s, with price action still constrained by weak momentum and muted trading volumes. The Ethereum market experienced the same deleveraging shock that wiped out more than US$600 million in crypto positions on Nov 16 alone. As derivatives exposure unwinds, spot-driven price movements are beginning to reassert themselves, though analysts caution that Ethereum will need sustained liquidity inflows to break out decisively. A shift in macroeconomic expectations has provided a supportive backdrop. Growing confidence that the US Federal Reserve may move toward a rate cut has boosted risk sentiment across global markets. Crypto assets, which have historically benefited from looser monetary policy, have reacted positively to the shift. Bitcoin’s recent ability to rally independent of equity market strength has also caught investor attention, reinforcing its narrative as both a risk asset and potential macro hedge. Despite improving sentiment, analysts warn the market remains in a delicate consolidation phase. ETF outflows, uncertain macro data and the possibility of renewed deleveraging could limit upside potential. Both Bitcoin and Ethereum are expected to trade within tight ranges unless fresh catalysts emerge. The coming weeks will be pivotal. Investors are watching for clearer Federal Reserve policy signals, institutional inflow trends and on-chain data that may indicate whether the current rebound marks the start of a sustained uptrend or simply a technical bounce within a broader cooling phase. title: Wall St Extends Gains As Markets Bet On December Fed Rate Cut
body: Wall Street closed higher overnight as growing expectations of a December interest rate cut by the US Federal Reserve lifted sentiment, sending all three major indexes to a fourth straight session of gains. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.67% to 47,427.12, the S&P 500 gained 0.69% to 6,812.61 and the Nasdaq Composite advanced 0.82% to 23,214.69. Tech counters helped drive the rally, with sentiment improving after Nvidia’s upbeat results and Dell Technologies’ stronger-than-expected revenue and profit outlook. Dell jumped 5.8% after issuing a consensus-beating fourth-quarter forecast. However, Workday slid 7.9% after reporting subscription revenue below estimates, while Deere fell 5.7% following a weaker annual profit forecast attributed to tariff pressures. Analysts said optimism was supported by rising confidence that the Fed will cut rates in December. According to the CME FedWatch tool, markets are pricing in an 84.9% probability of a 25-basis-point reduction at the upcoming policy meeting. Airlines outperformed, with the S&P 1500 Airlines Index climbing 3.0% ahead of what is typically the busiest travel day of the year, reinforcing views of resilient consumer spending heading into the holiday shopping period. Economic data showed stronger-than-expected core capital goods orders for September, suggesting firmer corporate spending despite reporting delays caused by the government shutdown. Initial jobless claims came in below expectations, though continuing claims remain on an upward trend. Market breadth was strong, with advancing issues outnumbering decliners by more than three to one on the NYSE. Trading volume was lighter ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday. title: Stock Today: Sunway Slips 3% As Property And Healthcare Gains Offset By Construction Headwinds
body: Sunway Bhd (SWB) shares slipped 3.24% to RM5.37 as of 12.14 pm, reflecting a pullback amid relatively muted trading activity. The decline comes despite analysts maintaining positive stances on the stock, with MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB Research) holding a NEUTRAL rating and CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) a HOLD rating, citing steady operational performance underpinned by resilient property sales and recovering healthcare operations. MBSB Research recently revised its target price slightly higher to RM5.18 from RM5.13, while CIMB Securities raised its sum-of-parts target to RM5.60, factoring in new property launches and contributions from Sunway’s healthcare division. Sunway’s 3QFY25 core net profit of RM271.5 million rose 22.5% sequentially but fell 22.5% year-on-year, bringing 9MFY25 core earnings to RM703.9 million, down 6.8% from the previous year. Analysts noted that stronger contributions from the property investment and healthcare segments helped cushion weaker results from the construction division, which saw pre-tax profits decline 10% amid peak progress on one of the group’s data centre projects in the prior quarter. Healthcare operations showed notable recovery, with SMC Damansara reaching EBITDA breakeven in August 2025, supporting a 45% quarter-on-quarter rise in pre-tax profits to RM51 million. Property development remained a key driver, with new sales surging to RM1.8 billion in 3QFY25 from RM745.3 million in 2QFY25, largely attributed to the launch of Otto Place in Singapore with a gross development value of S$1 billion. This brought total 9MFY25 property sales to RM3.1 billion, representing 86% of the group’s RM3.6 billion annual sales target, while unbilled sales increased from RM3.7 billion to RM5.2 billion. Despite robust property sales and healthcare improvements, analysts highlighted ongoing headwinds from weaker earnings in Malaysia and healthcare start-up losses at SMC Ipoh. CIMB also pointed to three one-off items in 3QFY25, including unrealised gains from previous educational asset transactions with Sunway REIT, fair value gains on an integrated commercial building, and a reversal of impairment on spun pile assets, which contributed to results coming broadly in line with expectations. Year-to-date revenue rose 49% to RM7.5 billion, with core profit up 3% to RM754 million. Analysts remain cautiously optimistic on Sunway’s near-term outlook, noting that upcoming property completions and healthcare listings are likely to provide support, though upside at current levels is considered limited. The group’s net gearing improved to 35% as of September 2025, providing balance sheet stability and flexibility for future developments, which could underpin longer-term shareholder value. title: Stock Today: Farm Fresh Climbs 5% On Strong Earnings And Expansion Outlook
body: Farm Fresh Bhd (FFB) surged RM0.13 or 5.02% to RM2.72 in early trading, with a volume of 25.2 million shares. The stock opened at RM2.62, reaching a high of RM2.73 and a low of RM2.58, as investors reacted positively to the company’s robust financial performance and expansion plans. RHB Investment Bank Bhd and CIMB Securities have both reaffirmed bullish calls on Farm Fresh, citing solid earnings momentum, improved margins, and promising regional growth. RHB upgraded the stock from Neutral to BUY, assigning a target price of RM3.03, representing a 17% upside from its last close of RM2.59. CIMB maintained its BUY rating with a revised target price of RM3.00, highlighting the company’s 1HFY26 performance. Farm Fresh posted a 1HFY26 core net profit of RM68 million, up 30% year-on-year, exceeding RHB’s expectations thanks to better-than-anticipated margins and reduced exposure to whole milk powder. CIMB reported a slightly higher 1HFY26 core net profit of RM73 million, marking a 26.8% increase year-on-year, driven by higher sales volumes and improved operating leverage. Revenue for the half grew 13% year-on-year, boosted by new product launches including ice cream and milk powder, while ultra-high temperature (UHT) products continued to gain traction. Gross profit margin expanded 1.5 percentage points to 33.4%, supported by a favourable product mix and stable input costs. On a quarterly basis, 2QFY26 revenue rose 13% to RM295 million, lifted by school milk sales, new products, and initial exports to Cambodia. Core net profit for the quarter increased 16% quarter-on-quarter to RM37 million. Both analysts noted that results exceeded expectations due to conservative margin assumptions and stronger-than-expected sales volumes. Looking ahead, Farm Fresh’s growth is expected to be supported by domestic and regional expansion. The Bandar Enstek ice cream plant, slated for mid-2026, will triple output, while the Taiping plant upgrade has increased ice cream production to 300,000 units per day. Regional expansion remains a key priority, with strong traction in the Philippines and meaningful contributions from Cambodia since exports began in August 2025. Plans to explore Indonesia further enhance long-term growth prospects. Valuation remains attractive. RHB’s target price implies a 33x FY27F price-to-earnings ratio, 20% below large-cap consumer staple peers, while CIMB noted FFB trades at 29.8x one-year forward P/E, below its historical mean of 33.3x. Analysts highlighted the company’s diversified dairy portfolio, strong brand equity, and consistent earnings growth, with a projected three-year EPS CAGR of 18.2% (FY25–28F). Potential risks include expansion delays and input cost spikes, but these are manageable relative to Farm Fresh’s solid fundamentals and ASEAN growth opportunities. title: Stock Today: Alliance Bank Dips Slightly To RM4.66
body: Alliance Bank Malaysia Bhd (ABMB) slipped 1.06% to RM4.66 as of 2.49 pm, with a total traded volume of 1.12 million shares. The stock opened at RM4.70, reaching an intraday high of RM4.70 and a low of RM4.64, while the last adjusted closing price (LACP) stood at RM4.71. Market activity saw a modest buy interest of 28,800 shares against sell orders totalling 157,900 shares. Despite the slight pullback, both MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB Research) and Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB Research) maintained their BUY calls on ABMB, with target prices revised to RM5.11 and RM5.10 respectively. Analysts cited robust loan growth, stable asset quality, and untapped fee income potential as key drivers underpinning the positive outlook. MBSB Research reported that ABMB’s 2QFY26 core net profit rose 4% quarter-on-quarter to RM207 million, bringing the six-month total to RM405 million, representing an 11% year-on-year increase. The research house highlighted that while net interest margins are expected to remain stable, non-interest income offers multiple avenues for growth, including treasury gains and client fee income. Asset quality remains sound, with lower provisioning anticipated in the second half of FY26. ABMB’s Serendah plant partnerships and ACCELER8 initiatives are expected to drive efficiency improvements without significant capital expenditure. HLIB Research noted that 2QFY26 earnings of RM206.6 million represented an 8.8% year-on-year increase, supported by net interest income growth of 3.5% despite slightly lower margins, underpinned by expansion in the loan book. Improved asset quality metrics, including a lower gross impaired loan ratio of 1.91% and stronger loan loss coverage of 107.1%, reflected recoveries from corporate clients. Loan growth moderated to 8.1% year-on-year, while deposits rose 12.5%, lifting the CASA ratio to 39.1% and maintaining a healthy loan-to-deposit ratio of 96.3%. Analysts emphasised that ABMB is well positioned to capitalise on upcoming macroeconomic opportunities, including projects in data centres and the Johor Special Economic Zone, while consumer and SME lending remains the bank’s core focus. Fee income remains underutilised relative to peers, offering further upside potential, and high operating expenses are expected to taper post-FY26 as marketing and IT investments stabilise. Discussions regarding a potential stake recalibration involving DBS could also provide additional support for the share price. title: Malaysia Gold Prices Ease After Recent Rally Amid Fed Rate Speculation
body: Gold prices in Malaysia edged lower, following a near two-week high as investors booked profits while weighing the possibility of a U.S. interest rate cut in December. As of early trading, gold was priced at RM4,162.09 per ounce, down RM5.56 or 0.13%, while gold per gram fell to RM133.81 and per kilogram to RM133,814.2, according to GoldPrice.org. The dip comes after gold surged in recent weeks, rising over 57% year-on-year in USD terms, reflecting heightened demand for safe-haven assets amid uncertainty over U.S. monetary policy. Spot gold in New York fell 0.3% to US$4,153.49 per ounce, while U.S. December gold futures slipped 0.5% to US$4,150. Analysts attributed the pullback to profit-taking following Wednesday’s gains. “What they’re looking to do is take profits… The Fed isn’t clear of what they’re going to do next, so gold is just consolidating,” said Brian Lan, Managing Director of GoldSilver Central. Investor sentiment remains influenced by conflicting signals from the Federal Reserve. Some officials, including New York Fed President John Williams and Governor Christopher Waller, have indicated that a rate cut may be warranted due to labour market softness, which has also pressured Treasury yields. Meanwhile, several regional Fed presidents advocate a pause in easing until inflation shows a more sustained move toward the 2% target. title: Wall Street Climbs On Rate Cut Hopes Despite Tech Headwinds
body: Wall Street extended its rally on Tuesday as a wave of economic data supported expectations that the U.S. Federal Reserve may implement its third and final rate cut of the year in December, though softness in the technology sector capped gains for the Nasdaq. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 664.18 points, or 1.43%, to 47,112.45, while the S&P 500 gained 60.77 points, or 0.91%, to 6,765.89. The Nasdaq Composite added 153.59 points, or 0.67%, to 23,025.59, weighed down by a 2.6% decline in Nvidia shares. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index eked out a 0.2% gain. Economic reports released on Tuesday, including September retail sales and producer prices from the Commerce and Labor Departments, indicated softer consumer spending and cooling inflation. The Conference Board also reported a sharp 12% drop in consumer confidence, signalling weaker near-term expectations. “At the last Fed meeting, (Fed Chair Jerome) Powell pretty much said (the Fed) would be on hold at its next meeting due to a lack of economic data,” said Paul Nolte, market strategist at Murphy & Sylvest in Elmhurst, Illinois. “Then we had Fed governors speaking and we’ve gone from ‘we’re not going to do anything in December’ to ‘we need to cut in December because we’re seeing some serious weakening in the job market.’” Financial markets have reacted, currently pricing in an 84.7% chance of a rate cut in December, up from 50.1% a week ago. This follows dovish comments from New York Fed President John Williams and Fed Governor Christopher Waller. U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent noted there is a good chance President Donald Trump will announce his pick for Powell’s successor before Christmas, with White House economic adviser Kevin Hassett seen as a frontrunner. “We have an idea who the next Fed chair might be and he’s on the dovish side,” Nolte added. “So I think the markets are feeling pretty good that interest rates are on the way down throughout 2026.” Sector performance was mixed, with healthcare leading gains in the S&P 500 while energy shares suffered the steepest decline. Retail stocks saw a boost from generally positive earnings: Kohl’s surged 42.5% and Abercrombie & Fitch jumped 37.5% after raising annual earnings forecasts, though Burlington Stores fell 12.2% after missing revenue estimates. Tech stocks saw divergent moves as Alphabet rose 1.5% following reports Meta Platforms would utilise Google’s AI chips in its data centres from 2027 and lease chips from Google Cloud by next year. Meta added 3.8%. Meanwhile, U.S.-listed Alibaba slipped 2.3% despite beating quarterly revenue expectations. Advancing issues on the NYSE outnumbered decliners 4.05-to-1, with 181 new highs and 45 new lows. On the Nasdaq, 3,355 stocks rose against 1,296 declines, registering 140 new highs and 80 new lows. Trading volume on U.S. exchanges reached 16.68 billion shares, compared with the 20-day average of 19.78 billion. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid noted that the US Dollar Index (DXY) had dipped below 100 points to 99.809, following weaker-than-expected economic data. September US retail sales rose 0.2% month-on-month, falling short of the 0.6% forecast, while the Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index dropped to 88.7 points in November, below the street estimate of 93.5 points. “American households remain concerned about the cost of living amid higher import tariffs,” Dr Mohd Afzanizam added. US Treasury yields also eased, with the two- and ten-year yields each down three basis points to 3.43% and 4.01%, respectively. Analysts expect the ringgit to trade in the RM4.12 to RM4.13 range as investors price in the possibility of a Fed rate cut next month. Elsewhere, the ringgit showed mixed movements against other major currencies. It firmed against the Japanese yen to 2.6408/6485 from 2.6420/6451 but weakened versus the euro at 4.7706/7839 from 4.7635/7687, and fell against the British pound to 5.4285/4436 from 5.4235/4294. Among regional currencies, the ringgit traded higher. It strengthened against the Philippine peso to 7.00/7.02 from 7.01/7.02, rose versus the Singapore dollar to 3.1684/1775 from 3.1708/1745, firmed against the Thai baht to 12.7717/8184 from 12.7793/7999, and improved against the Indonesian rupiah to 247.6/248.4 from 247.9/248.3. The early gains reflect investor optimism that weaker US economic data could prompt the Federal Reserve to ease monetary policy later this year. title: Gold And Silver See Steady Rise In Malaysia
body: Gold prices in Malaysia rose slightly, with the price per kilogram reaching RM553,013, up RM2,371 or 0.43% from the previous session. Per gram, gold is now trading at RM553.01, reflecting steady demand in the domestic market. The increase continues a longer-term upward trend, with gold climbing 2.84% over the past 30 days and surging 45.99% over the past year. Over the last five years, gold prices have more than doubled, rising 135.43%, while over 20 years, the precious metal has gained over 800%. Silver also saw a notable uptick, rising 1.81% today to RM3.85 per gram. The white metal has gained 7.06% in the past month and 58.74% over the past year, signalling robust interest in precious metals amid global economic uncertainties. Globally, gold prices have been buoyed by strong demand across major currencies. Year-to-date, gold has appreciated by 57.8% in US dollars, 50.8% in Australian dollars, and 54.6% in Canadian dollars. Other markets have seen similar gains, with the metal up 64.3% in Japanese yen and 49.6% in British pounds. Analysts note that the price momentum is driven by ongoing investor interest in gold as a hedge against currency fluctuations and inflationary pressures. The continued strength of precious metals reflects their safe-haven appeal amid uncertainties in equities and other risk assets. Silver’s recent gains have been slightly more pronounced than gold on a percentage basis, with a six-month rise of 50.67% and a five-year increase of 130.25% in Malaysian Ringgit terms. This trend underscores growing investor appetite for both metals as part of diversified portfolios. With domestic prices closely following global trends, local investors and jewellery buyers are keeping a close watch on market movements as gold and silver remain key assets for wealth preservation and hedging strategies. title: Bitcoin, Ethereum Struggle For Direction As Market Volatility Persists
body: Bitcoin and Ethereum swung between gains and losses on Nov 26 as the broader crypto market continued to wrestle with thinning liquidity, cooling ETF inflows and a cautious macro backdrop. Bitcoin traded in the mid-US$87,000 range after a volatile session that saw intraday moves between US$86,170 and US$88,421. Despite brief recovery attempts, the world’s largest cryptocurrency remains down roughly 5%-6% over the past week, extending the slide from October’s highs. Market sentiment remains fragile, with analysts warning that Bitcoin may test lower support zones before any meaningful rebound takes shape. Still, pockets of bargain-hunting have begun to emerge as some investors view the current consolidation as a potential accumulation window. Meanwhile, Ethereum also mirrored Bitcoin’s choppy performance, hovering near US$2,960 after swinging between US$2,860 and US$2,978 during the day. The second-largest crypto has fallen around 3%-4% over the week, pressured by the same macro forces affecting Bitcoin. Despite the pullback, Ethereum appears to be drawing mild buying interest, signalling that traders remain cautiously optimistic about its medium-term trajectory. Overall, market observers attribute the current downturn more to macroeconomic headwinds than to weaknesses in crypto fundamentals. Shrinking liquidity, a slowdown in institutional inflows, particularly into spot ETFs, and risk-off sentiment across global markets have weighed heavily on digital assets. Technical indicators now place Bitcoin’s key support in the US$78,000- US$84,000 band, while Ethereum’s critical zone sits at US$2,600- US$2,800. Looking ahead, traders are watching for renewed institutional demand, macro easing signals and signs of technical stabilisation that could pave the way for a broader recovery. For now, both Bitcoin and Ethereum remain in a consolidation phase, one that could either form a base for the next leg up or open the door to a deeper correction depending on how global conditions evolve in the coming days. title: Yenher Could End Year Stronger Despite Recent Drop
body: Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) has maintained its BUY call on Yenher Holdings with a target price of RM1.51, up from RM1.41, citing the company’s earnings recovery and upcoming expansion. The research house noted that the stock offers a potential total return of 90.1%, driven by both a capital upside of 86.4% and a dividend yield of 3.7%. HLIB expects Yenher’s earnings to normalise in 4Q25 as the impact of front-loaded sales dissipates, while margin expansion should benefit from the stronger Ringgit. Yenher reported 3Q25 core PATAMI of RM4 million, bringing 9M25 core PATAMI to RM14.5 million, down 13.4% year-on-year. The quarterly results were below HLIB’s expectations, accounting for 61.4% of full-year forecasts, with the shortfall attributed to lower-than-expected sales caused by front-loading ahead of the SST implementation in July. Every quarter, core PATAMI fell 35.8% and year-on-year declined 39.8%, pressured by lower revenue and margin compression. Revenue in 3Q25 dropped 13.9% quarter-on-quarter, led by a 20.6% decline in the distribution segment, while manufacturing sales fell 5.6%, reflecting softer demand for premix, feed additives, and vitamins. Year-to-date, revenue rose 3.5%, driven by a 16.3% increase in manufacturing, offset by a 5.1% decline in distribution. Despite this, core PATAMI fell 13.4%, impacted by higher staff costs and additional rental and equipment expenses during facility downtime earlier in the year following a factory fire. Production has fully resumed since August, and HLIB expects the company to close the year on a stronger note, supported by normalised sales and improved margins. Looking ahead to FY26, Yenher’s expansion plans include commissioning the Black Soldier Fly facility in 1Q26, as well as new premix, complete feed, and biotech feed additives plants by June 2026, significantly increasing production capacity. HLIB also highlighted opportunities in the swine segment, where government initiatives aim to lift Malaysia’s pork self-sufficiency ratio above 90% by 2030, supporting a gradual recovery in sales. Tan added that Yenher’s proprietary premix formulations provide a competitive advantage, bolstering pricing power and customer expansion. Following adjustments for lower FY25 sales and higher pre-operating expenses in FY26, HLIB maintains its FY26 forecast, underlining Yenher’s multi-year growth potential as new facilities come online and structural trends in the Ringgit support margin expansion. As of 11.11 am, the stock price is stable at RM0.81. title: Wall Street Rallies On Fed Rate-Cut Hopes
body: Wall Street stocks closed higher on Monday, extending Friday’s rally as investors bet on a potential U.S. Federal Reserve rate cut in December, helping them look past concerns about stretched valuations in the tech sector. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 202.86 points, or 0.44%, to 46,448.27. The S&P 500 gained 102.13 points, or 1.55%, to 6,705.12, while the Nasdaq Composite jumped 598.92 points, or 2.69%, to 22,872.01. Strength in the so-called “Magnificent Seven” artificial-intelligence-related momentum stocks powered the Nasdaq ahead of other indexes. “The street is falling into the line of thinking that a rate cut is coming in December,” said Robert Pavlik, senior portfolio manager at Dakota Wealth in Fairfield, Connecticut. Dovish commentary from Fed Governor Christopher Waller, New York Fed President John Williams, and San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly also supported investor optimism, though other policymakers expressed dissenting views. Financial markets are currently pricing in an 85% chance of a December cut, up from 42.4% last week, according to CME’s FedWatch tool. Economic reports released belatedly after the recent six-week government shutdown hinted at labour market weakness and persistent inflation, further bolstering hopes for the Fed’s third and final rate reduction of 2025. Among the S&P 500’s 11 major sectors, communication services enjoyed the largest percentage gain, while consumer staples and energy were the only two sectors to close in negative territory. Advancing issues on the NYSE outnumbered decliners by a 2.3-to-1 ratio, with 116 new highs and 76 new lows. On the Nasdaq, 3,187 stocks rose versus 1,478 that fell. Third-quarter earnings reporting is winding down, with nearly 95% of S&P 500 companies having reported as of Friday. About 83% delivered better-than-expected results, prompting analysts to raise aggregate third-quarter earnings growth estimates for the index to 14.7%, up from 8.8% on 1 October, according to LSEG data. Investor attention will shift this week to additional economic indicators, including retail sales, producer prices, and new orders for durable goods, alongside independent reports such as Case-Shiller home prices, consumer confidence, and pending home sales data. The U.S. holiday shopping season begins with Thursday’s Thanksgiving holiday, providing another test for consumer spending, which accounts for roughly 70% of the economy. Despite recent layoff announcements and weak survey data, the National Retail Federation expects holiday sales to exceed $1 trillion for the first time. Earnings from consumer-facing companies such as Best Buy are also anticipated later in the week. Concerns over tech valuations remain, with AI bellwether Nvidia last week failing to fully assuage fears of a potential AI bubble. Deutsche Bank, however, boosted risk appetite by projecting the S&P 500 could reach 8,000 by the end of next year, marking the most bullish forecast among major global brokerages. Corporate news also supported markets, with Bristol-Myers advancing 3.3% after European rival Bayer revealed positive late-stage cardiovascular drug data, and Centene and Oscar Health jumping 4.6% and 22.3% respectively following reports that former President Trump is considering extending Affordable Care Act subsidies. Volume on U.S. exchanges totalled 18.32 billion shares, slightly below the 20-day session average of 19.94 billion shares. title: Stock Today: YTL Corp Rises On Subsidiary Acquisition News
body: YTL Corporation Bhd saw its share price rise 0.87% to RM2.33 as of 2:54pm on Monday, with a total volume of 6.18 million shares traded. The stock opened at RM2.32, reached a high of RM2.37, and a low of RM2.28. The last done price of RM2.33 came amid active buy orders totalling 2.11 million shares against 1.71 million shares on the sell side. The uptick follows market attention on YTL’s recent acquisition in Sarawak. Sarawak Consolidated Industries Bhd (SCIB) has entered into a conditional share sale and purchase agreement with YTL Cement (Sarawak) Sdn Bhd for the proposed disposal of 100% equity interest in SCIB Concrete Manufacturing Sdn Bhd. The total cash consideration for the transaction is RM113.0 million. The disposal includes 18,581,702 ordinary shares in SCIB Concrete Manufacturing, which will be transferred free from encumbrances together with all rights and advantages attached to them as at the completion date. The deal formalises SCIB’s strategy to divest its manufacturing business, which encompasses the trading of construction materials and the production of precast concrete pipes and related products. Under previous agreements between SCIB and its subsidiary, SCM had been granted tenancy and rights to build on seven parcels of land in Demak Laut Industrial Park, Kuching, with pre-agreed purchase prices amounting to RM38.19 million. Together with the disposal consideration, the total potential value of the transaction stands at RM151.19 million. SCIB said the divestment will allow the company to streamline operations and focus on its Construction and EPCC (Engineering, Procurement, Construction and Commissioning) segment. The disposal consideration represents a premium of 14.77% to SCM’s latest unaudited net assets of RM98.46 million as of 30 June 2025, and a premium of 26.91% to audited net assets of RM89.04 million as at 30 June 2024. The proposed disposal is estimated to generate a gain of RM11.29 million, strengthening the group’s net assets and earnings in the near term. Analysts say the transaction and the potential for enhanced financial flexibility could support YTL’s long-term growth, contributing to positive sentiment in the stock. title: Stock Today: Maybank Hold Firm On Strong 3Q25 Results And Analyst Support
body: Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) saw its shares rise slightly to RM9.98, up 0.2% with a trading volume of 8.99 million shares, as analysts continue to back the lender following its resilient third-quarter results. RHB Investment Bank Bhd, CIMB Investment Bank Bhd, MBSB Investment Bank Bhd and Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd maintained or upgraded their Buy calls, citing Maybank’s robust net interest margin (NIM) and strong non-interest income (NOII) performance. Maybank posted a 3Q25 net profit of RM2.62 billion, essentially flat quarter-on-quarter and up 3.3% year-on-year, bringing 9MFY25 core net profit to RM7.84 billion, within 76–83% of full-year forecasts. Pre-provision operating profit rose 2.7% YoY, supported by higher NOII, marginally stronger fund-based income and lower provisions despite a 25-basis-point overnight policy rate cut in July. Analysts noted that NIM expanded 2 basis points QoQ to 2.02%, outperforming peers including Public Bank and Affin Bank, while CASA growth remained strong, lifting the ratio to 39.9% from 37.8% in 2Q25. Loan growth in Malaysia and Singapore rose 1.4% and 1.3% QoQ, respectively, although Indonesia continued to weigh on overall growth. Asset quality remained resilient, with gross impaired loans edging slightly to 1.32% and loan loss coverage at 102.6%. Maybank achieved a net credit recovery of 15bps in 3Q25, supporting expectations for a net credit cost of ≤20bps for FY25 and a post-dividend ROE of 11.1% in FY26. CIMB Securities raised FY25–27 earnings forecasts by 5.3–10.1%, upgrading Maybank to Buy with a target price of RM10.50. HLIB Research reaffirmed its Buy with a target of RM10.70, citing attractive dividend yields of 6–6.4% and improving earnings visibility. Analysts highlighted capital optimisation opportunities, including potential upstreaming of dividends from subsidiaries and enhancements from Basel 3.1 credit risk-weighted asset realignments. Collectively, analysts view Maybank’s risk-reward profile as skewed to the upside, supported by resilient NIM, strong NOII momentum, steady loan growth and robust capital buffers. title: Stock Today: IOI Properties Rises On Strong Q1 FY26 Start
body: IOI Properties Group Bhd (IOIPG) shares climbed 2.26% to RM2.26 as of 12.01 pm today, supported by strong market interest following the Group’s robust start to its financial year ending 30 June 2026. The property developer saw 37.9 million shares change hands, with buying interest concentrated at RM2.24 and selling at RM2.26. The stock opened at RM2.24, touching an intraday high of RM2.29 and a low of RM2.23, with the last transacted price at RM2.26, indicating positive sentiment among investors. IOIPG reported a 41% increase in revenue to RM968.7 million for 1Q FY2026, up from RM687.9 million in the same period last year. Profit before tax surged more than fivefold to RM753.6 million, from RM133.7 million a year earlier, while profit after tax jumped to RM664 million from RM69 million. The exceptional performance was bolstered by a remeasurement gain of RM502.8 million following the completion of the South Beach acquisition, alongside improved contributions from its Property Development and Property Investment segments. Revenue growth was broad-based across the Group’s core businesses, with Property Development rising 47%, Property Investment up 31%, and Hospitality & Leisure increasing 44% year-on-year. Property Development sales reached RM473.6 million in the quarter, with domestic projects contributing RM384.2 million (81%) and China projects adding RM89.4 million (19%). Within Malaysia, the Klang Valley led at RM243.4 million, driven by the matured 16 Sierra township in Puchong South and the new Senna Puteri township in Salak Tinggi, Sepang. Johor contributed RM141.7 million, supported by Bandar Putra Kulai and Taman Kempas Utama townships. Group CEO Lee Yeow Seng said the results reflected the resilience of the Group’s core segments and its strategic focus on high-performing local and overseas developments. “While global economic challenges may persist, the favourable interest rate outlook in Singapore and the positive prospects for the hospitality sector ahead of Visit Malaysia 2026 augur well for the Group. Barring unforeseen events, financial performance for the year is expected to remain satisfactory,” he said. The strong quarterly performance and strategic acquisitions continue to position IOIPG for growth across its diversified property and hospitality portfolio, giving investors confidence in the stock’s near-term momentum. title: Ringgit Strengthens Amid Dovish US Fed Signals, Eyes RM4.10 By Year-End

title: Potential Upside For Kelington Despite At Premium
body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has maintained a BUY call on Kelington Group (KGRB MK) with an unchanged target price of RM6.10, implying a potential upside of 9.9% from its last traded price of RM5.55 and an estimated FY26 dividend yield of 2.4%. The research house highlighted that the company’s 3Q25 and 9M25 results were broadly in line, driven by net profit margin (NPM) expansion, while a sequentially stronger 4Q25 is expected on improved billings. Kelington’s earnings prospects are underpinned by a robust outstanding orderbook exceeding RM1.6 billion and a sizeable RM4.5 billion tenderbook, supporting a projected FY25–27 CAGR of 14%. For 3Q25, Kelington posted core earnings of RM44.5 million, up 38.2% quarter-on-quarter and 11.1% year-on-year, bringing 9M25 core earnings to RM98.7 million, which represents 66% of RHB’s forecast and 67% of consensus expectations. The key variance stemmed from stronger-than-expected gross and net margins. The company also declared a 4 sen dividend per share, including a 1.5 sen special dividend, with a dividend payout ratio of 68%. On segment performance, advanced engineering remained dominant, contributing 68% of 9M25 EBIT. Revenue in Malaysia and China fell by 22% and 23% respectively, offset by a 22% growth in Singapore. Industrial gas revenue declined 21% due to lower specialty gas sales, partially mitigated by steady demand for liquid carbon dioxide (LCO2). Overall, 9M25 EBIT grew 14% with gross profit margins expanding 3% YoY to 21.3%, driven by higher-margin projects. Kelington’s tenderbook highlights continued opportunities, including a second German semiconductor fab project in partnership with Taiwan’s largest foundry, which may come in lower than expected due to subcontracting by the principal. This is expected to be offset by potential ramp-ups in India with “offset manufacturing” processes. Looking ahead, Kelington is set to sign a joint venture for a 2MW green hydrogen (H2O) production hub with Worldwide Energy Development (WED) and SKS Coachbuilders (SKS) by December. The hub is expected to take six to nine months to construct, with initial production of 200 cum/hour allocated to SKS for its fleet of fuel cell buses. RHB Research views the recent share price pullback as a healthy correction following a strong year-to-date rally. At the current valuation of 26x FY26 fully diluted PER, Kelington trades above its historical PER mean (+1.5 standard deviations), supported by a record tenderbook, consistent earnings delivery and long-term upside from its carbon capture and utilisation (CCU) business, which the market has yet to fully price in. As of 12.29 pm, the stock price has plummeted 4.32% to RM5.31. title: Life Water Makes Splashing Start In FY26
body: MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB Research) maintained its NEUTRAL call on Life Water Bhd (LWSABAH) with an unchanged target price of RM1.11, citing a solid start to FY26 supported by capacity-driven growth. The house noted that the company’s 1QFY26 results came in line with expectations, underpinned by higher sales volumes of drinking water following the commissioning of the expanded Sandakan Sibuga Plant 1 in June 2025, as well as the consolidation of Twinine Sdn Bhd’s sauces and condiments business. Life Water reported 1QFY26 revenue of RM51.2 million, a 15.0% quarter-on-quarter increase and 20.3% year-on-year growth, while core PATAMI rose 3.0% QoQ and 24.8% YoY to RM9.4 million. The results accounted for 24% of MBSB’s full-year forecast and 31% of consensus estimates. No dividend was declared for the quarter. Revenue growth was primarily driven by drinking water, which contributed 84.8% of total sales, aided by enhanced production capacity and efficiency at the Sandakan Sibuga Plant. Carbonated drinks accounted for 11.0% of revenue, while fruit drinks contributed a marginal 0.1%. The first-time consolidation of Twinine added RM2.1 million, or 4.1% of total revenue, providing an incremental boost to the topline. Earnings improved on stronger operations, with PBT rising 34.5% QoQ to RM12.2 million. However, the absence of reinvestment allowances that had previously reduced taxable income led to a higher effective tax rate of 23.2%, compressing the PAT margin to 18.3% from 20.3% in 4QFY25. Gross profit margins improved to 48.5%, supported by better sales mix and enhanced plant utilisation. MBSB Research expects PAT margins to normalise around current levels, given that similar tax incentives are unlikely to recur. Life Water also extended the utilisation period for RM4.6 million of unutilised IPO proceeds allocated for an automated warehouse racking system at KK IZ8 Plant 1, lengthening the timeframe from 14 months to 32 months post-listing. The extension allows additional time for regulatory compliance checks, technical feasibility studies, vendor evaluation and procurement and installation of the customised storage system, ensuring funds are deployed with due diligence. Looking ahead, Life Water is expected to benefit from steady demand in East Malaysia, expanded production capacity, and the integration of Twinine’s portfolio. Completion of the Sandakan Sibuga Plant 1-line lifts annual capacity to 626 million litres, positioning the group for Visit Malaysia 2026 and rising regional consumption. Distribution capabilities have been strengthened through an enlarged fleet and additional warehouses, while disciplined pricing strategies and operational efficiencies support sustained growth for FY26. As of 11.30 am, the stock price noted an increase of 4.46% to RM1.17. title: Duopharma Set To Benefit From Several Margin Drivers
body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has maintained a BUY call on Duopharma Biotech (DBB MK) with an unchanged target price of RM1.60, implying a potential upside of 28.3% from its last traded price of RM1.25 and reflecting an 8% ESG premium. The house highlighted that the company’s upcoming Approved Products Purchase List (APPL) tender, which is expected to feature more stock keeping units (SKUs) than the current cycle, alongside expansion into higher-value verticals, provides medium-term rerating catalysts. The analyst noted that earnings visibility remains solid due to resilient pharmaceutical demand, although contributions from the K5 drug substance facility are not expected for at least three years. Looking ahead to 2026, Duopharma is expected to benefit from several margin drivers. Peak demand in the final year of the APPL tender (2024–2026), combined with de-bottlenecking initiatives at the Bangi and Klang facilities, should ease prior capacity constraints on private sector growth after the company prioritised public orders amid strong tender wins. Ongoing margin expansions are also anticipated as Active Pharmaceutical Ingredient (API) prices stabilise, the mix of lower-margin trading products such as insulin recedes, and the Malaysian ringgit strengthens. The company cautioned that the exceptional 1Q25 insulin sales surge of around RM30–35 million is unlikely to repeat in 2026, and labour costs are expected to rise with the implementation of new collective agreements from 1 January 2026. On insulin supply, Duopharma is currently fulfilling orders via local purchase orders (LPOs) after the previous contract expired on 28 October. Discussions with the Health Ministry (MOH) continue, with indications that future tenders may be split among multiple suppliers to ensure supply security. Should contracts be evenly shared, RHB Research estimates roughly a 5% earnings impact for 2026, assuming a 10% net profit margin. Longer-term growth remains anchored in higher-value verticals. Process validation batches are on track for the company’s third Highly Potent Active Pharmaceutical Ingredient (HAPI) oncology product, Gefitinib, with commercialisation expected in 2026. While the K5 facility is completed, it remains idle until at least one in-licensing agreement is finalised, with more expected in 2026. Duopharma also sees growth potential in paracetamol and ophthalmology within the consumer healthcare segment and is planning product launches such as low-dose erectile dysfunction treatments, contingent on regulatory approval for over-the-counter sales. RHB Research has adjusted earnings forecasts by -0%, +4%, and +1% for housekeeping and foreign exchange assumptions, leaving the target price unchanged. Key downside risks cited include lower-than-expected sales volume and intensifying competition in the pharmaceutical market. As of 12.30 pm, the stock price has risen 1.60% to a price of RM1.27. body: Bursa Malaysia opened slightly firmer, tracking positive sentiment from Wall Street and a growing market expectation of a US Federal Reserve rate cut in December. Market watchers noted that the early gains in Bursa mirrored broader optimism in global markets, particularly as investors priced in an increased likelihood of the Federal Reserve lowering its Fed funds target rate at its December meeting. Dovish commentary from US central bank officials in recent days has reinforced expectations of a third and final rate cut for 2025, boosting risk appetite. Top gainers in early trading included MPI (+0.44 sen to RM32.10), PETDAG (+0.30 sen to RM21.30), and HLIND (+0.18 sen to RM14.60), while top losers were HLBank (-1.02 sen to RM21.20), UTDPLT (-0.26 sen to RM28.10), and MCEMENT (-0.23 sen to RM6.42). title: Tech And Industrials Lead Singapore’s Institutional Inflow Surge
body: Singapore-listed stocks in the Technology and Industrials sectors dominated institutional inflows in 2H25, with several counters posting notable gains and trading activity, according to a report by SGX Research. Yangzijiang Maritime Development, spun off from Yangzijiang Financial Holding, closed 21 November at S$0.67, up 12% from its S$0.60 offer price. The company now represents 1.6% of the FTSE ST Mid & Small Cap Index, boosting the combined weight of the Yangzijiang group to 2.36% in the FTSE ST All-Share Index. CSE Global led the market-cap-weighted net institutional inflows among stocks with at least S$100 million market capitalisation, recording S$47.5 million in 2H25, equivalent to 6.4% of its market value. The stock hit S$1.00 in November for the first time since 2013, after announcing a proposed warrant deal with an Amazon subsidiary tied to US$1.5 billion in orders. Other top recipients of institutional interest included iFAST Corporation (S$108.7 million inflow), Venture Corporation (S$134.4 million), and City Developments (S$242.3 million), which reversed S$30.7 million of net outflows from 1H25. Technology and Industrials collectively accounted for eight of the top ten inflow stocks, with City Developments representing the only significant non-Technology/Industrials counter in the group. Addvalue Technologies stood out with a 207% price surge in 2H25, supported by S$5.2 million net institutional inflows, up from a minimal S$236,000 outflow in 1H25. Trading activity increased sharply, with average daily turnover jumping to 883,000 shares, 28 times the 1H25 level. The company’s growth was driven by its satellite and digital connectivity solutions, reporting US$8.75 million revenue in 1HFY26, up from US$5.7 million a year earlier. The report also highlighted that all top ten inflow stocks saw increased trading turnover in 2H25, underscoring strong market interest in well-performing mid and small-cap companies. This trend reflects a continued focus by institutional investors on Singapore-listed Technology and Industrials stocks that offer growth potential and robust earnings, particularly in sectors benefiting from digital, automation, and maritime services. title: Stock Today: Petronas Chemicals Slides To Top Loser As Shares Drop 8.62%
body: Petronas Chemicals Group Bhd (PCG) emerged as the top loser on Bursa Malaysia this afternoon after its share price fell sharply by 8.62% as at 2.30pm. The counter dropped 28 sen to RM2.97, slipping to its intraday low with heavy selling pressure. PCG opened at RM3.25 and never recovered its footing, trading lower throughout the session. Volume was notably high, with 148.8 million shares changing hands. Buy interest remained thin at 60,900 shares against sell orders of 246,400 shares. The decline comes at a time when the counter has already endured a difficult year, with the stock down 37% year-to-date amid prolonged weakness in its key business segments. MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB Research) recently revised its call on PCG to NEUTRAL from Sell, maintaining a target price of RM3.01 and noting that much of the downside risk has likely been priced in. The investment bank highlighted that the group remains weighed down by losses of RM289 million in 3QFY25 and RM1.39 billion in the first nine months of FY25. Revenue has also contracted, falling 10% year-on-year to RM20.88 billion for 9MFY25, pressured by weaker product prices, lower sales volumes, supply disruptions and a stronger ringgit. The Olefins & Derivatives and Specialties segments continue to drag performance, with both reporting significant revenue declines and losses after tax due to narrowed spreads, impairments and foreign exchange effects. However, the Fertiliser & Methanol segment has shown relative resilience, supported by seasonal demand and improved supply stability. MBSB Research said modest quarter-on-quarter improvements in some segments and a firm F&M business supported its decision to lift PCG’s rating, though demand conditions remain challenging. At RM2.97, PCG is trading just below MBSB’s RM3.01 target price, reflecting cautious sentiment as the market continues to digest the company’s earnings headwinds. title: Stock Today: MPI Rises On Strong 1QFY26 Performance
body: Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd (MPI) shares closed at RM31.16 today, up 1.23% or RM0.38, with a traded volume of 462,100 shares. The counter hit an intraday high of RM32.50 and a low of RM30.10. The gain comes on the back of MPI’s stronger-than-expected first-quarter results for FY26, which saw net profit surge 76% year-on-year to RM53 million. The performance was driven by robust server-related demand across all major regions, with revenue rising 23% YoY. Asia contributed 30% growth, the US 23%, and Europe 11%, reflecting a broad-based recovery from last year’s low base. Pre-tax profit climbed 94% to RM78 million, while gross profit increased 48% to RM87 million, pushing gross margin up by 330 basis points to 13.8%. MPI also declared a 10 sen dividend, in line with its historical payout trend. Analysts have highlighted additional growth catalysts, including recovering automotive demand and rising orders for AI-related power management solutions. Following the results, Kenanga Research raised its FY26 net profit forecast by 14.5% to RM201 million and FY27 estimates by 15% to RM230 million. Management noted that while server-related orders remain strong, the automotive segment—which contributed around 36% of revenue last quarter—could face near-term disruptions due to the recent Nexperia incident affecting global automotive supply chains. MPI continues to focus on cost optimisation through automation and strategic expansion into renewable energy, electric vehicles, and AI applications, positioning the group for sustainable growth despite sector volatility. title: Ringgit Edges Higher Against US Dollar On Mixed Fed Signals

title: RHB Sticks With Techbond On Ratings Cites Strong Order Momentum
body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has maintained its BUY rating on Techbond Bhd with an unchanged target price of RM0.42, implying a 35% upside, citing strong order momentum and higher gross profit margins. The house reported that the stock’s first-quarter FY26 results were broadly in line with expectations, with core earnings rising 10.1% quarter-on-quarter and 14.4% year-on-year, supported by margin improvements and operational efficiencies. Techbond declared a first interim dividend of 0.75 sen, up 25% year-on-year, translating into a 118% dividend payout ratio. Despite a weaker topline, earnings held steady due to lower operating expenses, production portfolio optimisation, and higher interest income from warrant conversion proceeds. The industrial adhesives, sealants and chemical segment accounted for 95% of total sales, though sequential weakness was seen following rationalisation of the chemical product range. Management noted that global macroeconomic conditions remain fluid, with policy shifts and evolving US reciprocal tariffs adding complexity to trade. However, ongoing regional diversification is expected to benefit ASEAN-based producers, with stronger export growth and steady demand from both existing and newly penetrated markets in Vietnam supporting an earnings recovery in FY26. RHB Research expects the company’s continued product optimisation and expanding client base to sustain earnings momentum, underpinned by Techbond’s vertically integrated operations and robust net cash position. The target price is based on a 14.5x CY26F price-to-earnings ratio. Key risks highlighted include weaker-than-expected demand and margins, as well as foreign exchange volatility, with a 5% change in USD/MYR estimated to affect earnings by about 7%. title: Has The Storm Subsided For PCG? MBSB Revises Ratings Call
body: Petronas Chemicals Group Bhd (PCG/PetChem) has been upgraded to NEUTRAL from Sell by MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB Research), with a maintained target price of RM3.01, reflecting cautious optimism for its fertiliser and methanol (F&M) segment amid continued headwinds in its Olefins & Derivatives (O&D) and Specialties businesses. The house highlighted that while PCG’s 3QFY25 and 9MFY25 losses remain significant at -RM289 million and -RM1.39 billion respectively, some segments have shown sequential improvements, and the current share price already factors in much of the downside risk. Revenue for PCG declined 10% year-on-year to RM20.88 billion for the first nine months of FY25, with 3QFY25 revenue falling 15% to RM6.79 billion. MBSB Research attributed the weakness to a stronger ringgit against the US dollar, reduced sales volumes, lower product prices and lower plant utilisation at 86% due to utility and feedstock supply disruptions and maintenance activities. The O&D segment saw a 24% drop in quarterly revenue to RM3.2 billion and a 20% decline for 9MFY25, while losses after tax reached -RM470 million and -RM1.5 billion respectively, pressured by narrower product spreads and unrealised foreign exchange losses. Conversely, the F&M segment demonstrated resilience, with 3QFY25 revenue rising 4.1% to RM2.22 billion and 9MFY25 revenue up 11.7% to RM6.98 billion. Profit after tax, however, fell 41% in 3Q to RM355 million and 15.6% for 9M to RM1.3 billion, largely due to lower product spreads. The house noted that this segment’s outlook remains relatively robust, supported by seasonal demand from the plantation sector and stable supply following maintenance activities. The Specialties segment continued to struggle, with 3QFY25 revenue down 13.6% to RM1.39 billion and 9MFY25 revenue falling 12.3% to RM4.54 billion. Losses after tax were reported at -RM87 million for 3Q and -RM531 million for 9M, impacted by lower margins, asset impairments at Perstorp, and negative foreign exchange effects. MBSB Research expects demand in both O&D and Specialties to remain subdued, with pricing complexity influenced by external pressures in heavy industries, though slight improvements may arise from favourable U.S. tariffs in O&D. Despite these challenges, MBSB highlighted a quarter-on-quarter recovery in O&D and Specialties compared with 2QFY25 and a firm F&M segment, supporting the decision to revise PCG’s call to NEUTRAL. The target price of RM3.01 is based on a price-to-earnings ratio of 18.5x applied to an FY26 earnings per share of 16.3 sen, slightly above the sector average to reflect optimism for the F&M business. PCG’s share price has fallen 37% year-to-date, suggesting much of the sector headwinds are already priced in. title: Hap Seng Poised For Strong End To 2025
body: Hap Seng Plantations Bhd is poised for a strong end to 2025, with analysts maintaining bullish calls on the stock. CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) has a BUY rating with a target price of RM2.45, citing expected bumper fourth-quarter crops and a robust net cash position, while Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB Research) also maintained a BUY with a slightly higher target of RM2.31, reflecting improved earnings assumptions and sustained production growth. HAPL is targeting 680,000 tonnes of fresh fruit bunches (FFB) in FY25, a 6.7% increase year-on-year, supported by a strong production trajectory in the final quarter. October production rose 16% month-on-month to 63,784 tonnes, with November output running ahead of October and peak harvest expected in December. CIMB Securities projects a 4Q25 core net profit of RM52 million, up from RM29 million in 3Q25, while HLIB expects FY25-27 core net profits to be slightly higher following adjustments for FFB yield and production cost assumptions. The group is addressing ageing estates, with an average age of 17.1 years, by ramping up replanting to nearly 1,000 hectares annually in 2025 and 2026. This is part of a broader capital management strategy, underpinned by a strong net cash balance of RM646 million, equivalent to 81 sen per share. Dividend guidance remains around 60% payout, translating to an estimated 11.25 sen for FY25, implying a final dividend of 9.75 sen or a yield of 4.43%. Operating costs for 3Q25 rose due to higher maintenance spending on estate infrastructure and labour costs, including the 2% mandatory EPF contribution for foreign workers effective October 2025. However, costs are expected to ease in 4Q25 with higher productivity, lower fertiliser application and reduced maintenance spending, bringing FY25 CPO production cost to approximately RM2,200 per tonne, down from a 9M25 average of RM2,614 per tonne after palm kernel credit. HLIB anticipates a slightly higher production cost of RM2,264 per tonne in FY26 as increased output is offset by higher fertiliser expenses. HAPL’s operational performance has been resilient despite early-year disruptions from excessive rainfall, which affected harvesting and cropping patterns. The group added 246 operational beds in 3Q25, contributing to improved efficiency. Both houses highlight the company’s low enterprise value per hectare of RM32,000, its healthy balance sheet and solid dividend yield as key investment positives. Share price closed at RM2.20, reflecting an upside potential of 11.4% per CIMB and capital gains of 8.9% per HLIB, with total expected returns including dividends ranging up to 14.6%. Analysts point to sustained production growth, strong cost management and a proactive replanting programme as drivers for HAPL to achieve its 4Q25 earnings and maintain momentum into FY26. title: Global Stocks Rally As Fed Rate Cut Bets Boost Sentiment
body: Global equities opened the week higher on Monday as investors welcomed growing expectations of a US Federal Reserve rate cut in December, despite lingering division among policymakers. In Asia, MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan rose 0.4%, while South Korea’s tech-heavy Kospi index gained 0.7%. Trading was light in Japan, where markets were closed for a holiday. In the US, Nasdaq futures climbed 0.64% and S&P 500 futures rose 0.45%, while EUROSTOXX 50 futures advanced 0.78%. The boost followed remarks from influential Fed policymaker John Williams, who suggested interest rates could fall “in the near term”, raising the likelihood of further easing. Goldman Sachs chief economist Jan Hatzius said, “We expect another Fed cut in December, followed by two more moves in March and June 2026 that take the funds rate to 3–3.25%. The risks for next year are tilted toward more cuts, as news on underlying inflation has been favourable.” Fed funds futures now indicate a 57% chance of a 25-basis-point cut next month, up from under 30% a week ago. Markets also tracked geopolitical developments, including the United States and Ukraine announcing an “updated and refined peace framework” with Russia, which could influence oil supply expectations. Brent crude eased 0.16% to US$62.46 a barrel, while US crude fell 0.17% to US$57.96. In the currency market, the Japanese yen remained near a 10-month low at 156.72 per US dollar, prompting speculation over possible intervention from authorities. Maybank’s Saktiandi Supaat said, “Dollar/yen will definitely be going upwards even if you try to intervene… the only way for them to do it is intervention to stop the pace maybe, but I don’t think they can stop the direction.” The dollar held firm against other major currencies, leaving the euro near a two-week low at US$1.1506 and sterling at US$1.3091 ahead of the UK budget announcement. Spot gold fell 0.3% to US$4,054.19 an ounce. Investors are also eyeing upcoming US data releases, including retail sales and producer prices, for further guidance on the economic outlook. title: Bitcoin, Ethereum Extend November Losses
body: The cryptocurrency market remained under pressure on Nov 24, with Bitcoin and Ethereum extending their November slide amid thinning liquidity, persistent ETF outflows and rising macroeconomic uncertainty. Bitcoin traded between the US$85,461 and US$88,005 range after dropping roughly 33% from its October peak. Ethereum mirrored the weakness, fluctuating between US$2,765 and US$2,862 as it struggled to hold support near the US$2,700 region. Market analysts say the downturn reflects a combination of risk-off macro sentiment, continued institutional rotation out of spot ETFs and technical exhaustion after months of overheated price action. Recent stable-coin supply contraction has further signalled declining risk appetite. Despite the correction, some stabilising signs emerged over the weekend. A sharp round of liquidations, totalling nearly US$200 million, helped reset leveraged positions, leading to a modest rebound on Nov 23 as traders speculated that selling pressure may be nearing exhaustion. Infrastructure developments also provided a counterweight to the negative sentiment. The Singapore Exchange launched regulated perpetual futures for Bitcoin and Ethereum on Nov 24, opening a new institutional gateway into an asset class increasingly shaped by derivatives demand. Industry observers say the move underscores Asia’s growing role in advanced digital-asset markets. Still, analysts warn that sustained recovery will require stronger inflows and a supportive macro backdrop. With rate-cut expectations softening and inflation volatility lingering, crypto continues to behave like a high-beta asset vulnerable to broader market jitters. For businesses with crypto exposure, the current climate highlights the need for tighter hedging strategies and reassessed risk frameworks. Trading desks expect a period of consolidation or further downside unless a clear catalyst such as renewed ETF inflows or improved liquidity conditions emerges. Key levels to monitor include Bitcoin’s US$78,000-US$84,000 support band and Ethereum’s US$2,600-US$2,800 zone.
