title: Analyst Neutral On Sarawak Plantation Post 3Q25 Results
body: MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB Research) has maintained its NEUTRAL call on Sarawak Plantation Bhd with an unchanged target price of RM2.88, citing stable fundamentals and steady earnings growth. The research house noted that while valuation has become relatively rich, trading at more than one standard deviation above peers in the double-digit PER range, the outlook remains underpinned by operational resilience and expanding harvestable areas. Sarawak Plantation’s 3QFY25 results came in within expectations, with core PATAMI of RM56.7m, marking a 22.1% year-on-year increase. This accounted for 76% of MBSB’s full-year forecast and 73% of Street estimates. The earnings performance was supported by higher operating profit of RM79.0m, with margins rising 2.5 percentage points, benefiting from an effective mills purchasing strategy. Operationally, fresh fruit bunch (FFB) production declined to 91,031 tonnes, down 8.1% year-on-year, reflecting delayed peak crop seasonality and biological factors affecting estate activity in 1QFY25. Crude palm oil (CPO) production fell 12% to 25,750 tonnes, driven by reduced FFB processing and prioritisation of higher-quality crops amid elevated CPO prices. Average realised CPO prices rose 5.8% to RM4,175 per tonne, while palm kernel (PK) prices jumped 29.5% to RM3,189 per tonne. Despite lower volumes, estate operations generated RM25.6m in profit, down 8.4% year-on-year, while mill operations posted RM5.4m, down 12%, reflecting narrower margins. The small increase in estimated all-in cost of production to above RM2,500 per tonne was noted, though overall estate and mill margins remained satisfactory. Analysts highlighted that Sarawak Plantation’s operations are purely domestic, insulating the group from regulatory risks affecting Indonesian peers. Looking ahead, MBSB Research retained its earnings estimates, with expectations of stable profitability supported by nearly 1,500 hectares of additional harvestable area and ongoing cost efficiencies in fertiliser and manuring strategies. Despite the lower production this quarter, the group’s fundamentals remain intact, underpinning its neutral rating. The research house also emphasised that the company’s valuation, while richer than peers, is justified by its operational stability, insulation from external regulatory risks and steady earnings outlook, making Sarawak Plantation a consistent performer in the local plantation sector. title: US Stocks Jump On Rate-Cut Hopes, But Weekly Losses Deepen
body: US stocks surged on Nov 21 as rising bets on a December Federal Reserve (Fed) rate cut outweighed persistent anxiety over stretched tech valuations, though all three major indexes still logged another week in the red. Reuters reported that the Dow climbed 493.15 points, or 1.08%, to 46,245.41. The S&P 500 advanced 0.98% to 6,602.99, while the Nasdaq gained 0.88% to 22,273.08. All 11 S&P sectors finished higher. A boost came after New York Fed President John Williams said the central bank could cut rates “in the near term” without jeopardising its inflation mandate. Traders quickly ramped up wagers, with markets now pricing in nearly a 72% chance of a December cut, up sharply from 39% a day earlier, according to CME’s FedWatch tool. Still, other Fed officials urged caution, reinforcing a split view on policy direction. Despite the rally, the week told a different story: The Dow shed 1.9%, the S&P 500 fell about 2% and the Nasdaq dropped 2.7%, its third straight weekly decline and longest losing streak since March. The tech-heavy index is now down 7% from its October peak. The small-cap Russell 2000 also posted a fourth consecutive weekly loss. Nvidia shares briefly spiked after reports the Trump administration may allow H200 AI chip sales to China, but the stock still closed 1% lower and finished the week down nearly 6% despite strong earnings and guidance. Elsewhere, Alphabet jumped 3.5%, Apple added 2% and Meta rose 0.9%. Eli Lilly gained 1.6% after becoming the first drugmaker to cross US$1 trillion in market value during the session. Trading was active, with US exchange volume hitting 21.06 billion shares, above the 20-day average. Advancers handily outpaced decliners on both the NYSE and Nasdaq. Volatility remained elevated as investors weighed lofty tech valuations, aggressive AI investment plans and uncertainty over the Fed’s next move — all against a backdrop of mixed labour data showing a delayed uptick in unemployment even as job growth surprised to the upside. title: Ringgit Firms At Opening As Markets Reassess US Rate Outlook
body: The ringgit began Friday’s session on a firmer note against the US dollar and other major currencies, opening at 4.1515/1645 compared with Thursday’s close of 4.1565/1645. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the latest US nonfarm payrolls report showed that 119,000 jobs were created in September, surpassing expectations. He added that a higher participation rate continued to reflect resilience in the labour market. He said the combination of stronger labour data may signal that the US Federal Reserve could maintain interest rates at its December meeting. “While the stronger labour reading should keep the US dollar supported in the near term, the ringgit’s early gains suggest markets are continuing to reassess the timing and scale of potential US rate cuts in 2026, especially with a new US Federal Reserve chair to be appointed in May. “The case for rate cuts is not totally off the table. It is a question of timing and quantum. For now, however, the US dollar is expected to remain on a positive trajectory,” he told Bernama. Dr Mohd Afzanizam noted that the ringgit had ended Thursday 0.24 per cent weaker against the greenback but may encounter near-term technical support, with trading expected within the RM4.15–RM4.17 range. title: KLCCP’s Upside Potential Reflected In Current Share Price
body: Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) has maintained its HOLD call on KLCCP Stapled Group Bhd, raising the target price to RM8.32 from RM7.90, reflecting a balanced risk-reward profile. Analysts noted that the group’s 3Q25 results were largely in line with expectations, underpinned by sustained performance across its retail and hotel segments, while near-term positives are broadly priced in. KLCC posted 3Q25 core net profit of RM209.1 million, up 4.3% quarter-on-quarter and 1.3% year-on-year, bringing 9M25 earnings to RM611.1 million, within 73% of HLIB’s full-year forecast and 72% of consensus. A quarterly dividend of 9.5 sen per share was declared, raising total dividends for 9M25 to 27.9 sen, slightly higher than 27.4 sen in the same period last year. Revenue in 3Q25 rose 4.7% quarter-on-quarter, largely driven by an 18.2% gain in the hotel segment. Retail revenue expanded moderately by 2.9%, while office income remained flat. Year-on-year, overall turnover was relatively steady, with minor declines in retail (-1.9%) and hotel (-5.6%), offset by 5.2% growth in management services. Lower finance costs, down 5.7%, helped lift core PATAMI by 1.3% year-on-year despite a slight increase in debt-related interest from the 40% acquisition of Suria KLCC in 2Q24. Occupancy rates remained robust, with retail at 98% and office at 100%, while the group’s gearing held steady at 32%. Analysts highlighted that these stable metrics support the group’s consistent earnings generation and underpin its ability to maintain dividends. Looking ahead, footfall at Suria KLCC is expected to remain strong through 4Q25, while Mandarin Oriental is projected to maintain firmer occupancy, aided by festive season and holiday-driven spending. For 2026, tourism initiatives including Visit Malaysia 2026 and the Malaysia–China mutual visa exemption are expected to bolster both the retail and hotel segments, particularly with a rebound in Chinese visitors. HLIB noted that although these factors provide upside potential, they are largely reflected in the current share price, resulting in a balanced risk-reward. The HOLD rating is supported by a rolled-forward FY26 dividend per unit, targeting a yield of 5.3%, benchmarked against the five-year mean spread versus the Malaysia Government 10-year bond. Analysts expect low single-digit growth in the near term, with the group’s core earnings underpinned by continued tourism and retail recovery. title: Bitcoin Falls To Six-Month Low Amid Strong US Jobs Data
body: Bitcoin dropped to its lowest level since April, as investors reduced exposure to riskier assets while reassessing the likelihood of another Federal Reserve rate cut. The flagship cryptocurrency fell to a low of US$86,325.81 and was last trading at US$86,690.11. Stronger-than-expected US jobs data intensified the sell-off. The economy added 119,000 jobs in September, well above the 50,000 projected by economists polled by Dow Jones. That report lowered the odds of a December rate cut, with the CME Group’s FedWatch tool showing around a 40% probability. Bitcoin’s pullback mirrored broader losses in the cryptocurrency market. Ether dropped more than 3% to trade below US$3,000, while XRP fell 2.3% to under US$2.00. Dogecoin remained largely unchanged. The digital currency’s decline also weighed on equities, despite a strong earnings report from Nvidia. Traders heavily invested in AI-focused stocks often hold bitcoin as well, creating a link between the two markets. The cryptocurrency has been on a downtrend since early October, when a series of liquidations of highly leveraged positions triggered a cascade of selling, pushing Bitcoin and other major tokens lower. title: Asia Tech Stocks Slide On AI Bubble Worries
body: Japanese and South Korean technology shares tumbled on Friday (Nov 21), with SoftBank dropping more than 10 per cent, as investors fretted over a potential artificial intelligence bubble. The sell-off followed a weaker session on Wall Street, where recent US jobs data cast doubt over further interest rate cuts and raised questions about the lofty valuations of AI-linked stocks. Seoul’s benchmark Kospi index fell nearly 4 per cent, while Tokyo’s Nikkei shed 2.3 per cent in morning trade. Samsung Electronics sank 4.8 per cent, and SK hynix plunged more than 9 per cent. The downturn came just a day after a region-wide rally triggered by strong earnings from AI bellwether Nvidia. The chipmaker exceeded expectations amid fierce demand for advanced processors used to power generative AI systems. Nvidia briefly became the first company with a market capitalisation above US$5 trillion last month, although it has since eased to around US$4.4 trillion. Multibillion-dollar investments into AI have been a key driver behind the global surge in technology equities, pushing valuations to record highs. Research firm Gartner estimates AI-related spending will reach approximately US$1.5 trillion by 2025 and over US$2 trillion in 2026, representing nearly 2 per cent of global GDP. Geopolitical tensions have further amplified the frenzy, with major projects aimed at constructing data centres that house tens of thousands of energy-hungry chips. SoftBank, a key backer of ChatGPT maker OpenAI, tumbled as much as 10.7 per cent in early trading. The firm, alongside OpenAI and cloud giant Oracle, is spearheading the US$500 billion Stargate project to build AI infrastructure in the United States. Analysts noted that the Asian markets remain highly sensitive to movements in US tech shares. “For now, movements in the domestic (South Korean) market are inevitably tied to day swings in US tech stocks, including Nasdaq futures and Nvidia’s after-hours trading,” said an analyst from Kiwoom Securities. He added that while Nvidia’s earnings were a positive surprise, strong catalysts can struggle to generate meaningful upside amid heightened short-term volatility. SPI Asset Management’s Stephen Innes said there was no single trigger for the sell-off. “What we saw was the market hitting a psychological air pocket – the kind of reversal every veteran trader has lived through, yet cannot reasonably quantify or make sense of in real time,” he commented. “Japan, Korea, Australia all opened on the defensive, with traders fully aware that the Nvidia-led optimism evaporated before the US lunch hour.” The Nasdaq’s after-hours trading and Nvidia’s strong forecast had previously calmed fears of an AI bubble, but the latest sell-off highlights lingering caution among investors over the sector’s sky-high valuations. title: Affin Shares Remain Attractively Valued, Says HLIB
body: Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) has maintained its BUY call on Affin Bank Bhd with an unchanged target price of RM3.00, citing an expected total return of 34.1% from its current price of RM2.30, supported by 3.7% dividend yield. The house highlighted the bank’s strong risk-reward profile, noting that the share price has fallen 17% year-to-date, while the bank continues to benefit from a robust lending pipeline, potential CASA expansion and avenues for net interest margin (NIM) improvement. Affin’s 3Q25 net profit rose slightly by 1.0% quarter-on-quarter to RM145.0 million, although it declined 0.6% year-on-year, bringing cumulative 9M25 net profit to RM412.6 million, up 10.1% from a year earlier. The performance was above expectations, accounting for 79.8% and 77.2% of HLIB and consensus full-year forecasts, respectively. The bank’s earnings were supported by positive Jaws, a lower effective tax rate and stable asset quality with gross impaired loans (GIL) ratio holding at 1.86%. Net interest income (NII) eased by 2.4% in 3Q25, compressing the NIM to 1.39% following July’s overnight policy rate (OPR) cut, while non-interest income fell 29.0% year-on-year. Islamic banking revenue, however, grew 28.8%, helping partially offset declines. Total loans grew 7.7% year-on-year, while deposits increased 4.5%, pushing the loan-to-deposit ratio (LDR) to 98.4%. Looking ahead, Affin has revised several key targets to reflect near-term headwinds. NIM is expected to remain under pressure into 1Q26, while return on equity (ROE) is projected at 4.8%, down from 6.0% and cost-to-income ratio (CIR) at 68.0%. Despite these adjustments, the bank remains confident in expanding its CASA portfolio through payroll-linked initiatives, including the launch of Selangor and Sabah cards, alongside its Fintura segment. Affin has also announced the acquisition of a 100% stake in Pheim Asset Management Sdn Bhd and its subsidiaries for RM50.0 million, marking its re-entry into the asset management space after the 2022 disposal of AHAM. The acquisition is expected to diversify revenue streams, enhance cross-selling opportunities across conventional and Islamic segments and leverage the bank’s high-net-worth client base. HLIB noted that meaningful contributions to profit are expected only from FY27 onwards, as the expansion of assets under management (AUM) will require a two-to-three-year gestation period. HLIB has adjusted FY25-27 earnings upward by 9.0%, 0.3% and 0.2%, respectively, reflecting lower loan loss provisions and recovering troubled accounts. title: US Tech Pauses Amid Nvidia Earnings, Wall Street Awaits Key Data
body: US stock futures steadied early on Wednesday after a tech-driven selloff this week, as investors prepared for earnings from artificial intelligence giant Nvidia Corp. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq had fallen for four consecutive sessions amid concerns over AI valuations, over-spending, and high leverage in the sector. While the small-cap Russell 2000 eked out a modest gain, broader selling pressures were compounded by disappointing forecasts from major companies such as Home Depot, which dropped 6% after missing quarterly earnings estimates. “Nvidia’s results could trigger the largest post-earnings market swing in its history, offering clues on whether AI investment is accelerating or cooling,” said market analysts. Shares of Nvidia rose over 4% in after-hours trading following an upbeat revenue forecast for the January quarter. US macro markets were relatively subdued. Shorter-dated Treasury yields fell after jobless claims data showed a surge in Americans on unemployment benefits, while longer-term yields largely reversed overnight. Investors are also closely watching minutes from the Federal Reserve’s last meeting, with futures markets pricing in no new rate cuts until March 2026. Overseas, Japan’s yen and government bonds fell to fresh lows amid concerns over fiscal policy and political pressure on the Bank of Japan to resist tightening monetary policy. Ten-, 30- and 40-year Japanese government bond yields surged, while the yen slipped to its weakest against the US dollar since January. Elsewhere, British inflation eased to 3.6% in October from September’s 3.8%, improving prospects for a Bank of England rate cut in December. In Canada, the dollar retreated slightly after Parliament approved Prime Minister Mark Carney’s first budget, avoiding the risk of a second election this year. This week’s focus for US investors includes corporate results from Nvidia, Walmart, Target, Lowe’s and others, alongside the release of the August trade balance and a US$16 billion 20-year Treasury bond auction. title: Ringgit Strengthens As Investors Eye US Economic Pause
body: The ringgit opened slightly stronger against the US dollar on Thursday, continuing its recent recovery as improved regional sentiment buoyed emerging Asian currencies. At 8 am, the local currency was quoted at 4.1475/1590 against the greenback, compared with Wednesday’s close of 4.1480/1530. The ringgit also advanced against other major currencies, appreciating to 2.6416/6490 versus the yen, 4.7858/7991 against the euro, and 5.4166/4317 versus the British pound. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid attributed the modest uptick to renewed uncertainty in the United States following delays in key economic data. “The US Bureau of Labour Statistics announced it would postpone the publication of October’s employment report to December 16,” he said. He added that the delay leaves the Federal Reserve operating without full information, suggesting it may not cut interest rates at its December 9–10 meeting. “In addition, the Federal Open Market Committee’s October minutes indicated members were generally inclined to keep rates steady for the rest of 2025,” he noted. Domestically, Dr Mohd Afzanizam highlighted that the ringgit had shown resilience in the previous session, closing 0.31 per cent firmer at 4.1505 against the US dollar on profit-taking. “Given the latest developments, the USD-MYR pair could trade between 4.15 and 4.17 today as participants may seek to lock in short-term gains ahead of upcoming US data releases,” he said. Against regional currencies, the ringgit strengthened versus the Thai baht to 12.7741/8182 and the Singapore dollar to 3.1755/1845. It remained little changed against the Indonesian rupiah at 248.2/249.0 and hovered around 7.04/7.06 against the Philippine peso. title: Nvidia Shares Surge After AI Chip Sales Beat Estimates
body: Nvidia (NVDA) reported third-quarter earnings on Wednesday, surpassing analysts’ expectations on both revenue and earnings per share, while projecting a stronger-than-anticipated outlook for the fourth quarter. For Q4, the AI chipmaker forecasts revenue of US$65 billion plus or minus 2%, ahead of Wall Street’s US$62 billion estimate. CEO Jensen Huang said, “Blackwell sales are off the charts, and cloud GPUs are sold out.” He added, “We’ve entered the virtuous cycle of AI. The AI ecosystem is scaling fast — with more new foundation model makers, more AI startups, across more industries, and in more countries. AI is going everywhere, doing everything, all at once.” Shares of Nvidia jumped more than 5% following the announcement. Other AI-linked stocks also gained in after-hours trading, including AMD (+4%) and Micron (+3%), while Amazon, Google, Meta, and Microsoft edged higher. For Q3, Nvidia reported earnings per share of US$1.30 on revenue of US$57.01 billion, beating analyst expectations of US$1.26 and US$55.2 billion, respectively. The company’s data centre division generated US$51.2 billion versus an expected US$49.3 billion, while gaming revenue came in at US$4.3 billion, slightly below the US$4.4 billion estimate. CFO Colette Kress highlighted that “Blackwell Ultra is now our leading architecture across all customer categories while our prior Blackwell architecture saw continued strong demand.” Revenue from its China-specific H20 chip was described as “insignificant.” The earnings report comes after Nvidia briefly reached a market capitalisation of US$5 trillion last month. Ahead of the results, major investors including Peter Thiel’s hedge fund and SoftBank Group sold off substantial stakes in the company, freeing capital for their own AI investments. Despite volatility, Nvidia shares are up over 37% year-to-date, with AMD rising 82% over the same period. Rival AMD CEO Lisa Su has projected that the data centre market could reach US$1 trillion by 2030. During the earnings call, Kress responded to investor Michael Burry’s criticism of AI companies’ accounting practices, emphasising that Nvidia’s accelerators have a long useful life thanks to ongoing CUDA software updates, allowing even six-year-old GPUs to remain in use. title: Nvidia Forecast Spurs Recovery In Japanese Markets
body: Japanese equities bounced back on Thursday as investors took heart from an upbeat earnings forecast by US chip giant Nvidia Corp, lifting AI-related stocks and ending a four-day losing streak. The Nikkei 225 climbed as much as 3.7% to 50,343.25, its strongest gain since early October, while the broader Topix index rose 2.3% to 3,319.54 in early Tokyo trading. Technology shares led the rebound, with SoftBank Group surging 9.1% and chip equipment makers Tokyo Electron and Ibiden advancing over 7%. Nvidia’s shares jumped more than 4% in after-hours trading following the company’s better-than-expected revenue forecast for the January quarter. “Nvidia’s results were virtually flawless, and have been well-received by investors,” said Takashi Ito, senior strategist at Nomura Securities. He added that the earnings should fuel a robust rebound in Japanese stocks. Technology had been among the largest drags on Japanese equities this week as global investors worried about high valuations. According to Ito, Nvidia’s results reassure the market that the pace of AI spending is “not an issue, for now.” Despite the positive sentiment, risks remain ahead of the expected announcement of Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s economic stimulus package on Friday. Government bond yields have climbed to multi-decade highs, while the yen extended its slide to around 157 against the US dollar overnight. “Growing concerns over Japan’s spending plans under Takaichi’s regime should keep investors on alert,” said Amir Anvarzadeh, Japan equity strategist at Asymmetric Advisors. He also highlighted the ongoing tensions between Tokyo and Beijing as a potential downside risk. title: Muhibbah Lacks Visibility For New Contract Orders: CIMB
body: CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) maintained a HOLD call on Muhibbah Engineering (Muhibbah) with a lower target price of RM0.54, citing muted visibility on new construction orders. The research house highlighted that while 9M25 results came in above expectations, the group’s core net profit was supported by a RM6.5 million reversal in net impairments linked to vessel disposals, masking weaker project billings and limited order wins for the year. CIMB Securities cuts FY26–27F core net profit forecasts by 9–18% and reduced new construction order book assumptions by 20–38% to RM200–500 million, noting that Muhibbah has yet to secure any major construction contracts year-to-date. Muhibbah reported 9M25 core earnings of RM65.5 million, up 57% YoY and representing 98% of both CIMB and consensus full-year expectations, despite a 32% fall in revenue to RM937 million following completion of several construction projects. Excluding the positive impact from vessel disposal reversals, 3Q25 core earnings would have contracted 32% QoQ to RM6.4 million. No dividends were declared for 3Q25 or 9M25. In mid-July 2025, Muhibbah’s 21%-owned Cambodia Airports secured a management contract to operate the new Techo International Airport (TIA) in Kandal Province, roughly 19 km south of Phnom Penh. The contract, effective from October 2025, is expected to see Phase 1 handle 15 million passengers between 2025 and 2030, rising to 30 million in Phase 2 (2030–50) and 50 million in Phase 3 (post-2050). CIMB Securities flagged the airport contract as a positive, partially offsetting the lack of new construction wins in Malaysia. The house noted that the decline in Muhibbah’s construction order book, which fell 48% to RM294 million as of November 13, is a key risk to near-term earnings growth. Analysts suggested that a revival of major job wins could act as a catalyst for stock rerating, while any loss of income from Phnom Penh airport concessions could weigh on valuations. Despite challenges, CIMB Securities raised FY25F net profit slightly to RM70 million to account for the vessel disposal reversal but emphasised that core net profit estimates for FY26–27F remain lower due to subdued order book visibility. The revised target price of RM0.54 reflects a 60% discount to Muhibbah’s sum-of-the-parts value, consistent with the Hold rating. The report underscores the mixed outlook for Muhibbah, balancing operational headwinds in the domestic construction market against strategic gains from its airport management contract in Cambodia. Analysts maintain caution on the stock until visibility on new major construction projects improves. body: Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) maintained its BUY call on Dialog Group Bhd with an unchanged target price of RM2.50, noting a potential 33.5% total return including dividend yield, after the company announced a major Engineering, Procurement and Construction (EPC) win. Dialog’s wholly owned subsidiary, Dialog E&C Sdn Bhd (DECSB), has secured an EPC contract valued at approximately RM1 billion from Pengerang Terminals (Two) Sdn Bhd (PT2SB), a 25%-owned joint venture. The contract covers the construction of 272,000 cubic metres of biofuel storage and handling facilities in Pengerang, scheduled for completion by December 2027. The scope includes dedicated tanks for bio-based feedstocks and finished products, along with all associated infrastructure, under an alliance framework between PT2SB and DECSB. HLIB described the development as positive for Dialog, as the expansion is expected to lift the group’s downstream EPC earnings from FY26 to FY28 while strengthening its strategic position within the renewable fuels value chain. The project includes sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) and other biofuels such as renewable diesel and Hydrogenated Vegetable Oil (HVO). Analysts highlighted that renewable fuel tank rates typically carry a 30-50% premium over conventional hydrocarbon tankage, supporting a stronger recurring income base for the company. The additional 272,000 cbm will expand PT2SB’s storage footprint by around 5% relative to Dialog’s current operating capacity of approximately 5.1 million cbm. Management has guided that the project carries a net margin of roughly 5-6%, in line with typical EPCC profitability, which is expected to reinforce normalised downstream margins. HLIB noted that the award falls within existing forecasts, which already factor in RM2.4-2.5 billion in downstream revenue over the same period. Dialog’s recurring income business model and position in Pengerang’s tank terminal expansion remain key positives, with analysts also noting that eventual long-term contracts for Phase 3 of PT2SB could help re-rate the stock. The group continues to leverage its expertise in EPCC, fabrication, plant maintenance, catalyst handling services and ownership of tank terminals and upstream assets to capture growth in the renewable fuels sector. title: Amway Struggling Amid New Consumer Landscape
body: CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) has maintained a REDUCE call on Amway (Malaysia) Holdings Bhd with a target price of RM4.29, citing ongoing challenges in the post-pandemic consumer landscape despite sequential improvements, the house noted. The house highlighted that the 3Q25 results reflected a modest recovery but that near-term earnings growth remains constrained. Amway posted a 3Q25 core net profit (CNP) of RM19.1 million, down 43.4% year-on-year but up 13.6% quarter-on-quarter, bringing 9M25 CNP to RM33.7 million, a 62.1% decline from the prior year. CIMB Securities said the results were broadly in line with expectations, representing 62% of its full-year forecast, with a stronger 4Q25 anticipated following a new product launch in 3Q25. A quarterly dividend of 5.0 sen was declared, keeping 9M25 dividends steady at 15.0 sen, in line with expectations. The year-on-year decline in profit was primarily due to weaker sales volumes and higher product costs, which also compressed the EBITDA margin by 7.1 percentage points. Revenue in 3Q25 fell 8.1% YoY to RM275.6 million, marking the 12th consecutive quarter of annual contraction. CIMB Securities attributed this to soft consumer demand for health, wellness, and home appliance products, alongside an unfavourable sales mix. Despite the yearly decline, revenue rose 3.3% quarter-on-quarter, supported by the new product launch and product price adjustments. Operating costs fell 4.3% QoQ, lifting the EBITDA margin by 7.2 percentage points. The house expects 4Q25 core net profit to post sequential improvement, driven by the recent product launch, enhancing the sales mix and supporting margin growth, alongside continued cost discipline. CIMB Securities’ Reduce call is premised on continued earnings softness amid subdued consumer sentiment and a competitive operating landscape, which may limit near-term recovery. Upside risks to the call include stronger-than-expected consumer demand and lower incentive payouts to Amway Business Owners (ABOs). The stock last traded at RM4.93, implying a downside of 13% to CIMB’s target price of RM4.29, with a dividend yield of 7.5% for FY25F. CIMB Securities said that while sequential gains may provide temporary relief, the longer-term outlook remains challenged by structural market pressures and a cautious consumer base. title: Tech Woes And Home Depot Drag US Stocks Lower
body: US stocks ended lower on Tuesday, with the S&P 500 recording its fourth straight day of losses, marking its longest losing streak in three months. Investor concerns over high valuations and disappointing guidance from major companies weighed on sentiment. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 498.50 points, or 1.07%, to 46,091.74, while the S&P 500 dropped 55.09 points, or 0.83%, to 6,617.32, and the Nasdaq Composite slid 275.23 points, or 1.21%, to 22,432.85. Home Depot shares tumbled 6% after the home improvement retailer cut its full-year profit forecast and missed quarterly earnings estimates. Marta Norton, chief investment strategist at Empower, said, “You’re having this massive sentiment correction during a period where earnings is delivering maybe above bull expectations, and, yet, there’s so much fear circulating in the market.” Adding to caution, Nvidia (NVDA) is set to release quarterly results on Wednesday. The AI-focused tech leader’s shares fell 2.8% in early trading, as investors gauge whether its results justify the market’s exuberance over AI-driven gains. The US September jobs report, delayed due to the long government shutdown, is scheduled for release on Thursday. Preliminary data showed a surge in Americans claiming jobless benefits between mid-September and mid-October, indicating a cooling labor market. Despite broad-market declines, earnings for this reporting season have largely exceeded expectations. S&P 500 year-on-year earnings growth now stands at 16.9%, up from 8.8% projected at the start of October, according to LSEG data. Some traders viewed the recent selloff as overdone, suggesting potential for a rebound, particularly among smaller-cap and non-megacap stocks. Sector performance was mixed, with six of the 11 major S&P 500 sectors ending higher. The Russell 2000 small-cap index gained 0.3%, even as mega-cap tech names like Amazon (AMZN) slid 4.4%. Technically, the S&P 500 and Nasdaq both fell below their 50-day moving averages on Monday, a key threshold last breached in late April, signalling a more cautious near-term outlook. Trading volume on US exchanges totalled 18.66 billion shares, slightly below the 20.2 billion average over the past 20 sessions. title: Stock Today: Nestle Malaysia Dips Slightly After Legal Settlement
body: Shares of Nestle (Malaysia) Bhd edged lower, with the stock last traded at RM112.40, down 0.27% from its previous close. Trading volume stood at 59,100 shares, while the stock opened at RM111.80, hitting a high of RM112.80 and a low of RM111.10 during the session. MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB Research) has downgraded Nestle Malaysia to SELL with an unchanged target price of RM94.50, citing that recent gains in the stock have largely priced in near-term upside. The research house noted that valuations remain stretched, with the stock trading at 58.26 times price-to-earnings ratio (PER), more than two standard deviations above its three-year average. The downgrade comes despite Nestle Malaysia reaching a full and final settlement with Mad Labs Sdn Bhd, formally ending a seven-year legal dispute over alleged unauthorised use of QR codes on certain Maggi products. The dispute, which dates back to 2019, involved claims that QR codes redirected users to inappropriate content, drawing police and regulatory attention. While Mad Labs initially sought RM139.34 million in damages, the High Court dismissed the damages claim in 2023, recognising only the entitlement to compensation for unauthorised QR code use. Both parties have agreed to bear their own legal costs and withdraw all pending claims, including those before the Court of Appeal. Nestle Malaysia confirmed that the settlement would not materially affect its financial performance or operations. Management anticipates growth momentum to remain firm into FY26, supported by strong export performance, easing input costs, and ongoing fiscal support for consumers, including Budget 2026 allocations to Sumbangan Tunai Rakyat (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA), with the next SARA disbursement scheduled for February 2026. Financial projections remain robust, with revenue expected to rise from RM6.66 billion in FY25 to RM7.48 billion by FY27, while core profit after tax and minority interests is forecast to increase from RM555.5 million to RM639.7 million over the same period. Dividend payments are projected at 225 sen per share this year, rising to 259.2 sen by FY27, translating to yields of 2.0–2.3%. Nestle Malaysia, a subsidiary of Nestle SA, continues to focus on its consumer products and services segment, benefiting from sustained demand for essential and packaged food products. Major shareholders include Nestle SA with 72.61% and the Employees Provident Fund Board with 13.03% of the shares. Analysts note that while the legal settlement is a non-disruptive resolution, the stock’s near-term upside is expected to remain limited due to elevated valuations. title: STI Hits New High With Strategic Shifts And Bank Gains
body: The Straits Times Index (STI) reached a new all-time high of 4,575.91 on 13 November, closing 14 November at 4,546.07, delivering a total return of 25.8% year-to-date, supported by analyst upgrades and strategic shifts across key stocks, according to SGX Research. The strong performance was underpinned by non-bank constituents reversing first-half 2025 net institutional outflows into net inflows, while upgrades to STI consensus target prices boosted investor confidence. ST Engineering led STI constituents with an 85% total return, reflecting a 74% upward revision in its target price this year. STI valuations remain competitive, with a price-to-book ratio of 1.5x, up from 1.3x in June. Other top-performing stocks include UOL (+74% YTD), DFIRG USD (+71%), and Singtel (+62%). STI ETFs saw a 36% year-on-year rise in assets under management to S$3.38 billion, driven by net inflows of S$349 million, including S$65 million in October. Monthly trading activity also peaked, with average daily turnover reaching S$6.5 million. Banking heavyweights DBS, OCBC, and UOB continued to influence the index, reporting combined non-interest income above S$5.0 billion for 3Q25 and net interest income remaining above S$8.0 billion for a twelfth consecutive quarter. DBS led total income growth among the trio, while OCBC posted strong non-interest income gains driven by wealth management fees. SGX Research highlighted that strategic transformations, value unlocking, and macroeconomic tailwinds were key drivers behind STI performance, with the combined weight of the three leading banks declining slightly from 53.7% at end-2024 to 50.4% this year. title: Ringgit Opens Higher Against US Dollar Ahead Of Fed Move
body: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar on Wednesday, reflecting cautious investor sentiment ahead of the US Federal Reserve’s interest rate decision next month. At 8am, the local note strengthened to 4.1570/1705 versus the greenback from Tuesday’s close of 4.1605/1660. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US Dollar Index (DXY) eased 0.04% to 99.550 points, with uncertainties surrounding the Fed’s monetary policy dominating market attention. “The initial jobless claims (IJC) rose to 232,000 compared with consensus estimates of 223,000 and the prior week’s 219,000,” he noted, adding that the latest labour market data following the 41-day US government shutdown indicates a weaker trajectory. Dr Mohd Afzanizam also highlighted mixed signals among Fed officials regarding the direction of monetary policy in December. “The ringgit has corrected against the US dollar after touching the RM4.12-RM4.13 level last week, closing weaker yesterday. We expect it to stabilise around RM4.14 to RM4.16 today as some technical indicators have entered neutral territory,” he said. The ringgit opened stronger against a basket of major currencies. It gained versus the Japanese yen to 2.6726/6815 from 2.6800/6838 at Tuesday’s close, climbed against the euro to 4.8138/8294 from 4.8216/8280, and advanced against the British pound to 5.4652/4830 from 5.4719/4791. title: Positive Sentiment Anchored On Dialog’s Pengerang Deal
body: Analysts are bullish on Dialog Group Bhd with BUY calls, with MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB Research) maintaining the call and target price of RM2.17, CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) with a target price of RM2.72, and Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) with a target of RM2.50. All three research houses highlighted the company’s recurring income from midstream and downstream operations, as well as the growth potential from recent tank terminal expansions in Pengerang. Dialog reported a 1QFY26 core net profit of RM138 million, a 6.1% year-on-year increase, supported primarily by improvements in the downstream segment, according to CIMB Securities. MBSB Research noted that sequentially, earnings were down 11.9% due to smaller contributions from joint ventures and associates, while HLIB attributed the marginal 0.1% quarter-on-quarter decline to higher depreciation, finance costs, and lower JV contributions. Despite these variations, revenue rose to RM657 million from RM634.8 million in 1QFY25, underpinned by strong midstream performance with tank utilisation rates above 90% and steady storage rates of SGD6.0–6.5 per cubic metre per month. The positive sentiment is anchored on the Phase 3 expansion of the Pengerang Deepwater Terminals (PDT) in Johor. Dialog secured a long-term service agreement with BP Singapore Pte Limited, adding 614,000 cubic metres to the existing storage capacity of 430,000 cubic metres for refined petroleum products. Coupled with a July 2025 agreement to increase Pengerang Biorefinery SB capacity by 272,000 cubic metres, Dialog’s midstream and downstream portfolio is poised for significant growth, analysts said. HLIB highlighted that the new storage capacity represents about 22% of total effective storage and is expected to be completed by mid-2028. CIMB Securities noted that the downstream segment delivered strong results, with net profit surging 5.3 times year-on-year and 1.8 times quarter-on-quarter due to cost optimisation, margin normalisation, and higher maintenance earnings from renewed service agreements. Meanwhile, upstream operations were weaker, affected by lower crude output and softer realised oil prices, but midstream stability helped offset the decline. Analysts across all three research houses maintained their earnings forecasts for FY26–28, with MBSB projecting a FY26 EPS of 7.6 sen at a PER of 28.7x, while CIMB Securities retained forecasts of 10 sen EPS for FY26 and FY27. HLIB introduced FY28f core PATAMI of RM2.1 billion. Key upside catalysts include the commencement of onshore plant turnaround activities and the ongoing recovery in downstream earnings, while cost overruns from the EPCC segment remain a potential downside risk. Dialog’s recurring income portfolio, particularly the robust midstream operations and expanding tank terminal capacity, underpins analysts’ positive outlook, providing a stable cash flow platform and a foundation for future growth in both domestic and regional energy infrastructure. title: Malaysia Tracks Global Gold Surge, YTD Gains Top 50%
body: Gold prices in Malaysia climbed to RM131.36 per gram, marking a 0.49% increase from the previous session. The price per kilogram rose to RM131,360.14, reflecting growing investor interest in safe-haven assets amid global market volatility. The rise in Malaysian gold mirrors international trends. Gold in the United States gained 0.47% to USD 4,085.76 per ounce, while other major markets such as India and the United Kingdom also saw increases of 60.2% and 38.4% year-to-date respectively. Over the past year, gold has surged more than 53% in USD terms, underlining strong demand worldwide. The gains might be attributed by a combination of macroeconomic factors including inflationary pressures, central bank policies and investor appetite for hedging against financial uncertainty. Historically, gold prices in Malaysia have generally tracked movements in international markets, though local demand and currency fluctuations influence the ringgit-denominated price. Comparatively, Malaysia’s gold price increase aligns closely with other Asian markets, including India where prices have surged 60.2% YTD and China up 50.9% YTD. title: Heavyweights Lead Decliners As Dutch Lady, F&N, Nestlé Slide
body: The stock market saw key consumer and industrial names under pressure in Nov 19 trade, with heavyweight food and beverage (F&B) counters leading the decliners even as plantation stocks powered to the top of the gainers’ list. Dutch Lady Milk Industries Bhd topped the losers, sinking 70 sen to RM28.60 on 23,600 shares traded, extending weakness in defensive consumer names. Fellow F&B giant Fraser & Neave Holdings Bhd (F&N) also retreated 40 sen to RM32.60 on brisk volumes of 711,300 shares, while global staple producer Nestlé (M) Bhd slipped 40 sen to RM112.30. Other laggards include energy retailer Petronas Dagangan Bhd who fell 38 sen to RM21.12 on 465,600 shares, while Malayan Cement Bhd eased 22 sen to RM6.28, with nearly 868,100 shares changing hands. On the flipside, plantation plays stole the spotlight among gainers. BLD Plantation Bhd surged RM2.02 to RM12.78 on moderate interest, making it the session’s strongest performer. Fellow planter United Plantations Bhd rose 96 sen to RM28 with heavier trading. Meanwhile, tech-related counter Mesiniaga Bhd climbed 25 sen to RM1.30, while port operator Bintulu Port Holdings Bhd added 20 sen to RM5.30, while brewer Heineken Malaysia Bhd also advanced 20 sen to RM22.80 on 104,300 shares. Market sentiment remained mixed, with defensive blue chips and consumer stocks facing selling pressure while commodity-linked names benefited from firm crude palm oil prices. title: Gamuda’s AU$50 Billion Potential Key Australia Projects
body: Analysts remain positive on Gamuda Bhd with BUY calls, with RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) maintaining the recommendation and a target price of RM7.00, citing a 34% potential upside, while MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB Research) and Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) also reaffirmed the calls with target prices of RM6.35 and RM6.88, respectively. All three research houses highlighted Gamuda’s growing presence in Australia, particularly in renewable energy and infrastructure projects, as a key driver for future earnings. RHB Research noted that Gamuda Engineering Australia (GEA) and DT Infrastructure (DTI) contributed about RM7 billion, or 60% of Gamuda Engineering’s revenue in FY25. GEA’s pipeline includes over AU$50 billion worth of opportunities between FY27 and FY29, with more than AU$10 billion in active tenders. Key projects include the Weasel Solar Farm (250MW plus battery energy storage system) in Tasmania, the 350MW Cellars Hill Wind Farm, the AU$1.5 billion Hunter Transmission Project and the AU$3.7 billion New England Renewable Energy Zone. Meanwhile, DTI currently holds AU$2.5 billion in work, with plans to double this to AU$5 billion in FY27-28 across rail, roads and bridges, defence and energy projects. MBSB Research highlighted that Gamuda is leveraging its construction expertise and financial strength to take equity stakes in renewable energy assets, allowing the group to participate across project lifecycles and enhance margins. The Australian market is expected to account for 40% to 50% of Gamuda Engineering’s revenue in FY27-28, following FY25 contributions of AU$2.5 billion from GEA and DTI combined. Several major tender awards are expected before year-end, including the Sydney Metro West Stations Package valued at AU$2.0 billion, a hybrid energy project in Victoria exceeding AU$1 billion and the Marinus Link project. Gamuda is also preparing to tender for the Northland Corridor expressway in New Zealand. HLIB noted that GEA is active across six core segments, including transmission, renewable energy, tunnelling and water, roads and bridges, special multi-discipline projects and equity/PPP. The unit has over AU$10 billion in outstanding tenders and more than AU$50 billion of pipeline opportunities between FY27 and FY29. DTI is targeting a pre-tax margin expansion to 10-15% for renewable energy projects, while other infrastructure segments carry margins of 8-9%. All three analysts flagged the potential risks, particularly slower-than-expected replenishment of new contracts, but emphasised Gamuda’s diversified order book of RM39.3 billion as of October 2025, underpinned by recurring opportunities in clean energy and public infrastructure. The houses also highlighted the broader Australian public infrastructure pipeline, now estimated at AU$242 billion between 2024 and 2029, as supportive of sustained growth for Gamuda. title: Bitcoin Rebounds From Seven-Month Low As Crypto Market Bleeds Trillions
body: Bitcoin clawed back some ground on Nov 18 after sinking below US$90,000 to a seven-month low, finding tentative buyers in a market still shunning risk. Reuters reported that the world’s largest cryptocurrency was last up 1.9% at US$93,532 after touching US$89,286.75, a level that erased all its gains for the year and left it trading 26% below its October peak above US$126,000. The broader crypto market has taken a heavy hit, with roughly US$1.2 trillion wiped out in the past six weeks, according to CoinGecko, as investors price in lingering doubts over future US rate cuts and a wobbling global equities rally. Sentiment has been further rattled by accelerating outflows from US spot bitcoin ETFs. Since equity markets plunged on Oct 10 amid renewed US-China tariff worries, about US$3.7 billion has exited spot bitcoin funds, including US$2.3 billion in November alone, Morningstar data shows. The unwind has dragged down crypto-exposed stocks including Strategy, Coinbase and miner Marathon Holdings, though many bounced intraday in line with bitcoin’s recovery. Standard Chartered warned that a sustained drop below US$90,000 could leave half of publicly listed crypto-treasury firms “underwater”. Listed companies collectively hold 4% of all Bitcoin and 3.1% of Ethereum, the bank noted. Strategy, the largest corporate holder, has continued adding to its trove. Founder Michael Saylor said the firm purchased 8,178 Bitcoin on Nov 17, bringing its stash to 649,870 tokens at an average cost of roughly US$74,433 per coin. Ethereum has also been battered, shedding nearly 40% from its August high above US$4,955, pressured by the same macro and liquidity headwinds rippling through bitcoin. Despite the modest rebound, traders say the market remains fragile — and confidence, as one analyst put it, “can erode with remarkable speed”. title: Wall Street Slumps Ahead Of Nvidia Earnings And US Jobs Data
body: US stocks extended their recent selloff on Monday as investors braced for a week packed with economic data releases, including the long-awaited September jobs report and quarterly earnings from AI bellwether Nvidia (NVDA.O). The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 557.24 points, or 1.18%, to 46,590.24, while the S&P 500 slipped 61.72 points, or 0.92%, to 6,672.39. The Nasdaq Composite shed 192.51 points, or 0.84%, to 22,708.08. Market participants were particularly cautious amid concerns over valuations in the artificial intelligence sector, which has powered much of Wall Street’s recent gains. “There’s follow-through on last week’s pullback, particularly in tech,” said Matthew Keator, managing partner at the Keator Group in Lenox, Massachusetts. “The question is do the valuations justify the stock price?” He added that employment data could influence investor sentiment on AI-driven jobs and broader market expectations. Treasury yields dipped as investors assessed whether the Federal Reserve will cut interest rates next month, following delays in official inflation and employment reports due to the government shutdown. The yield on the benchmark 10-year note fell 1.3 basis points to 4.135%, while the 30-year bond yield slipped 1.1 basis points to 4.735%. The 2-year note yield, closely tied to Fed rate expectations, declined 0.6 basis points to 3.608%. The US dollar firmed in reaction to the return of official economic data, with the dollar index rising 0.23% to 99.55. Against the yen, the greenback strengthened 0.44% to 155.21, while the euro fell 0.28% to $1.1588. Cryptocurrencies continued their downward slide, with Bitcoin falling 1.53% to $92,009, wiping out its gains for the year. Ethereum declined 1.66% to $3,021. Energy and precious metals also retreated. US crude dropped 0.3% to $59.91 per barrel, and Brent crude fell 0.3% to $64.20 per barrel as investors weighed global oversupply concerns against looming US sanctions on Russia’s Lukoil. Spot gold eased 0.9% to $4,042 an ounce, with US futures down 1.67% at $4,019.40. European shares mirrored US weakness, with the STOXX 600 sliding 0.54% and the FTSEurofirst 300 down 0.55%, while MSCI’s global stock gauge fell 0.8% to 987.45. In Asia, Japan’s Nikkei dipped 0.10% to 50,323.91, though broader emerging market equities in the region edged slightly higher. Analysts expect the week’s data flow, including Nvidia’s AI-focused earnings report on Wednesday and the US September jobs figures on Thursday, to guide market direction and test investor confidence after the longest government shutdown in US history. title: Technical Correction Pulls Ringgit Back Amid Steady Dollar Rally
body: The ringgit opened slightly weaker against the US dollar this morning, marking a technical correction following recent gains. At 8 am, the local currency was quoted at 4.1485/1595 versus the greenback, compared with yesterday’s close of 4.1480/1515. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the modest retreat was expected, given that the ringgit had been in an overbought position according to technical indicators. “Having said that, ringgit should remain constructive in the mid- to long-term, underpinned by resilient economic growth and narrowing fiscal deficits, which can be deemed credit-positive by credit rating agencies. Today, we expect the USD/MYR to range between RM4.14 and RM4.15 as traders and investors await United States data points,” he told Bernama. The US Dollar Index (DXY) firmed 0.24% to 99.53 points as market expectations for a potential Federal Reserve interest rate cut in December continued to diminish. Dr Mohd Afzanizam noted that the Fed has remained cautious on the timing of any policy easing, prompting investors to focus on the September US Nonfarm Payroll data, scheduled for release on Thursday, for clearer economic signals. “The Fed’s reluctance to cut rates has supported the US dollar, keeping the ringgit range-bound for now,” he added. Against other major currencies, the ringgit traded higher. It appreciated versus the yen to 2.6720/6792 from 2.6805/6829, rose against the euro to 4.8077/8204 from 4.8125/8166, and strengthened versus the British pound to 5.4561/4706 from 5.4608/4654. Performance versus ASEAN currencies was mixed. The ringgit firmed against the Thai baht to 12.7697/8111 from 12.7847/8018, and edged up versus the Singapore dollar to 3.1836/1922 from 3.1864/1893. Meanwhile, it remained largely unchanged against the Indonesian rupiah at 247.8/248.6 and flat against the Philippines’ peso at 7.04/7.06. title: Stock Today: Public Bank Dips Amid Mixed 3Q25 Results
body: Public Bank Bhd shares fell 1.16% to RM4.25 as of 4.37 pm, with a total volume of 16.27 million shares traded. The stock opened at RM4.30, reached a high of RM4.31, and a low of RM4.24 during the session, with the last done price below its 4.30 level average. The movement comes after the bank reported a net profit of RM1.84 billion for the third quarter ended 30 September 2025 (3Q25), down from RM1.91 billion a year earlier, affected by lower non-taxable income. Revenue for the quarter increased to RM7.41 billion from RM6.8 billion. For the first nine months of 2025, Public Bank posted a net profit of RM5.34 billion, while revenue climbed to RM22.08 billion compared to RM20.15 billion in the same period last year. Public Bank Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer Tan Sri Dr Tay Ah Lek described the results as reflecting “stable performance” despite operating headwinds. He noted that “proactive management of cost of funds and synergistic non-interest income supported consistent growth,” highlighting the bank’s 12.6% net return on equity as evidence of strong fundamentals. Looking ahead, Tay said the group expects Malaysia’s economic momentum to remain supported by domestic demand, investment activity, and tourism. He also cautioned that global risks, including tariffs and commodity volatility, may weigh on the outlook. He added that resilience will remain central to the bank’s strategy. “The group will stay vigilant, build on core competencies, and focus on synergistic growth, sound risk management and strong governance to stay competitive,” Tay said. Public Bank remains one of Malaysia’s top-performing financial institutions, with steady revenue growth offsetting a modest decline in quarterly profit, even as market sentiment reflected caution ahead of further economic developments. title: Stock Today: CelcomDigi Drops 3.3% After Q3 FY2025 Results
body: CelcomDigi Bhd saw its shares fall 3.32% to RM3.49 in mid-morning trade today, with 7.05 million shares changing hands, following the release of its third-quarter results for the 2025 financial year. The company reported service revenue of RM2.7 billion, up 1.5% year-on-year, supported by growth across Postpaid, Prepaid, Home & Fibre, and Enterprise Solutions. Postpaid revenue increased 4.2% to RM1,091 million, driven by a 5.3% rise in high-value subscribers and migration to convergence plans, while Home & Fibre revenue surged 40.8% to RM69 million, marking eight consecutive quarters of subscriber growth. Enterprise Solutions revenue rose 10.4% year-on-year. Despite revenue growth, CelcomDigi’s earnings moderated, with EBIT falling 16% to RM648 million and profit after tax down 20.5% to RM350 million. Acting CEO Albern Murty said profits were affected by strategic investments to strengthen future earnings capacity, while network integration and IT transformation initiatives are over 90% complete, supporting enhanced 4G/5G service quality and digital customer experiences. The company ended the quarter with 20.5 million subscribers and declared a third interim dividend of 3.6 sen per share, maintaining its dividend policy alongside strategic investment plans. body: 99 Speed Mart Retail Holdings Bhd’s shares edged higher, closing at RM3.27, up 0.62% from the previous session, on a volume of 12.48 million shares. title: STI Hits Record High On Analyst Upgrades And Strategic Shifts
body: The Straits Times Index (STI) closed last week at 4,546.07 after reaching a new all-time high of 4,575.91 on November 13 2025, delivering a total return of 25.8% year-to-date as of November 14. The rally was driven by upgrades to the STI consensus target price and a reversal of net institutional outflows into net inflows for non-bank constituents. A report by SGX Group noted that STI valuations remain competitive, with a price-to-book ratio of 1.5x, up from 1.3x at the end of June, while the median across the 30 constituents holds at 1.2x. ST Engineering led the index in 2025 with an 85% total return and a 74% upward revision to its consensus target price, maintaining the highest P/B ratio among the STI constituents at 9.8x. The three leading banks, DBS Group Holdings, Oversea-Chinese Banking Corporation (OCBC) and United Overseas Bank (UOB), reported combined non-interest income of S$5.06 billion in the third quarter, marking the first time the trio surpassed S$5 billion. Net interest income remained above S$8.0 billion for the twelfth consecutive quarter. DBS and OCBC reported total income growth of 3% and 7% quarter-on-quarter respectively, while UOB recorded a 2% decline in third-quarter total income. STI exchange-traded funds also saw strong inflows. Assets under management for the two STI ETFs reached S$3.38 billion, a 36% increase year-on-year. The SPDR STI ETF accounted for S$2.27 billion, while the Amova STI ETF held S$1.11 billion. Year-to-date net inflows totalled S$349 million, including S$65 million in October, which marked the highest monthly trading activity for the ETFs since April 2025. Other top-performing STI stocks in 2025 include UOL with a 74% total return, DF International Realty Group USD at 71%, JMH USD at 64% and Singtel at 62%. SGX Group attributed the index’s performance to strategic shifts, value unlocking and macroeconomic tailwinds, while the combined weight of the three banks in the STI has declined to 50.4% from 53.7% at the end of 2024. title: Asian Markets Poised For Decline Amid AI And Jobs Uncertainty
body: Asian stocks were set to open lower on Tuesday as investors avoided riskier assets ahead of Nvidia Corp.’s earnings report and the upcoming US jobs release. Equity index futures for Japan and Hong Kong signalled early losses after the S&P 500 dropped 0.9% and the Nasdaq 100 shed 0.8% in the previous session. An index of US-listed Chinese stocks fell 1.2%, while MSCI’s global stock gauge touched a one-month low. Australian shares also opened lower. Investors are cautious amid uncertainty surrounding interest rates and tech earnings. Nvidia’s quarterly results on Wednesday are under scrutiny as concerns grow over AI valuations, despite expectations of another earnings beat. The US jobs report, delayed by the government shutdown, is scheduled for Thursday. “The monthly jobs report would normally dominate this week’s economic calendar, but with the AI trade struggling the past couple of weeks, Nvidia’s earnings are once again looking like a key piece of the market’s momentum puzzle,” said Chris Larkin at E*Trade from Morgan Stanley. In the cryptocurrency market, Bitcoin traded around US$92,000 after Monday’s decline erased much of its annual gains. An index tracking the 50 smallest digital assets in a basket of 100 dropped to its lowest level since November 2020. Commodities also reflected investor caution. West Texas Intermediate crude fell 0.3% to US$59.71 a barrel as resumed activity at a Russian port was offset by wider geopolitical risks. Gold prices remained largely unchanged, while the Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index was steady. Fed officials signalled cautious monetary policy moves. Vice Chair Philip Jefferson noted downside risks to the labour market but urged policymakers to proceed carefully, while Governor Christopher Waller supports a December rate cut citing weak jobs. Strategists at Goldman Sachs, Barclays, and Bank of America expect upcoming US economic data to strengthen the case for a Fed cut. Corporate news this week includes Amazon raising US$15 billion in its first US dollar bond offering in three years, Xpeng Inc.’s fourth-quarter revenue forecast missing expectations, and Thoma Bravo’s bid for Clearwater Analytics. Rio Tinto announced nearly halving production at its Yarwun Alumina refinery in Australia. Gina Rinehart became the largest shareholder in US rare-earths producer MP Materials Corp. title: 99 Speed Mart Expected To Sustain Next Three Years Of Growth
body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research), CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) and Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) have all maintained their BUY calls on 99 Speed Mart Retail Holdings (99SMART), with target prices ranging from RM3.56 to RM3.80, citing strong earnings momentum and robust expansion plans. RHB Research expects a 10% upside with a FY26F yield of around 2%, while CIMB Securities projects a 12% potential gain, supported by resilient sales of daily essentials. HLIB anticipates an 18% total return, factoring in structural tailwinds and ongoing government support. The group’s 9M25 core net profit reached RM456–457 million, up 18% year-on-year, broadly meeting analyst expectations. Revenue rose 13% to RM8.4 billion, underpinned by the addition of 269 outlets, same-store sales growth of 6.5%, and a positive contribution from the government-backed Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) programme. Quarterly performance also showed resilience, with 3Q25 revenue surpassing RM3 billion, a 12% increase quarter-on-quarter, driven by longer operating hours and higher sales from SARA-enabled stores, although gross profit margins were slightly diluted by the higher proportion of subsidised items. Analysts highlighted 99SMART’s strong positioning as a key beneficiary of fiscal support schemes under Budget 2026, with over 2,000 outlets currently activated under SARA. The programme provides cashless e-credit for essential goods, boosting footfall and sales, particularly among lower-income consumers. Coupled with elevated disposable income and ongoing demand for mini-market shopping, the group is expected to sustain its three-year earnings growth target of 15%. 99SMART’s strategic initiatives include expanding its addressable markets through product diversification, developing a bulk sales platform, and measured international expansion. In China, the retailer operates three outlets in Fuzhou supported by a small distribution centre, with plans to grow the network to 12 stores over the medium term. Domestically, the group continues to target up to 250 new outlets annually, with East Malaysia and underserved regions remaining strategic priorities. The company also maintained its focus on operational efficiency and value propositions, including the nationwide “4-for-RM10” campaign and earlier opening hours, which have helped drive footfall and transaction volumes. Analysts noted that these initiatives, along with disciplined cost control, have underpinned margin expansion and earnings resilience despite inflationary pressures and higher operating expenses from wage adjustments. title: Stock Today: S P Setia Rises 4.8% Midday On New Sales Momentum And REIT Plans
body: S P Setia Bhd climbed 4.82% to RM0.87 as of 2.59 pm today, with 11.88 million shares traded, supported by growing industrial developments and upcoming property launches. The stock opened at RM0.835 and touched a high of RM0.87. Analysts from MBSB Investment Bank Bhd and CIMB Investment Bank Bhd have both maintained BUY ratings on S P Setia, citing strong new sales momentum, a growing industrial portfolio, and plans for a Setia REIT listing. MBSB has a target price of RM1.26, while CIMB’s target is RM1.18. S P Setia posted lower earnings of RM277.7 million for the first nine months of FY25, down 29.8% year-on-year, due to high 9MFY24 earnings from land sales and international projects in Australia and Vietnam. Despite this, third-quarter core profit excluding land sales returned to the black at RM86.9 million, up from a loss of RM3.5 million in the previous quarter. Analysts expect sequential earnings to strengthen in Q4 with higher seasonal progress billings, though land sales are expected to contribute minimally. The group achieved RM1.59 billion in new sales in Q3, up from RM1.18 billion in Q2, led by land sales of RM762 million, including monetisation of around 300 acres at Tanjung Kupang for RM522 million. Cumulatively, land sales contributed roughly RM1 billion or 29% of total nine-month sales, keeping the company on track for its RM4.8 billion full-year target. Twelve new launches are lined up for Q4, with combined GDV of RM1.7 billion, including S P Setia’s first Australian student accommodation projects in Sydney and Melbourne, totalling RM2 billion GDV. Industrial projects remain a key growth driver, including Setia Fontaines in Penang (GDV RM3 billion) and Setia Alaman Industrial Park in Klang Valley (GDV RM4 billion), both accelerated following rezoning approvals. In Vietnam, S P Setia is exploring two sites in Bin Duong to expand its industrial footprint alongside existing EcoXuan and EcoLakes developments with Becamex. The upcoming Setia REIT, targeted for H1 2026, is expected to inject assets valued at RM2.8 billion and generate proceeds of up to RM800 million, partially to reduce borrowings and strengthen capital management. Analysts view the REIT as a mechanism to unlock the value of key investment properties, including Setia City Mall, Sutera Mall, Mercu 2, and Aspire Tower, with projected yields of 6.5–7%. With a 79:21 domestic-international revenue split and an unbilled sales pipeline of RM4.2 billion, analysts note that S P Setia trades at a 72–75% discount to net asset value, supporting its position as a long-term growth investment. title: Stock Today: Pharmaniaga Dips 7.7% Amid Anticipated Slower December Sales
body: Pharmaniaga Bhd’s shares fell 7.7% to RM0.240 in early trade today, with 28.3 million shares changing hands as of 11.58 am. The stock opened at RM0.260, hit a high of RM0.265 and a low of RM0.240, reflecting profit-taking after recent gains. MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB Research) has maintained its BUY call on Pharmaniaga, revising its target price slightly downwards to RM0.29 from RM0.30, citing expectations of softer sales in December. The research house noted that while Pharmaniaga’s full-year 2025 earnings forecasts have been revised down by up to 23%, the company is expected to see improved operations in 2026, driven by government concessions for human insulin, expanded vaccine distribution and ongoing digitalisation and automation initiatives. Pharmaniaga’s third-quarter results for 2025 showed a 107% year-on-year rise in core PATAMI to RM65 million, while nine-month core earnings improved 226% to RM136 million, excluding one-off items such as a RM124.9 million penalty waiver and RM2.5 million from inventory adjustments. SKU volumes grew 19% year-on-year in the third quarter, surpassing growth rates in the first two quarters, while vaccine sales in October quadrupled compared to September. Strong demand was also noted for non-communicable disease drugs, with Tegoprazan and Parecoxib posting month-on-month increases of 50 times and 120 times respectively. The company is also expanding its Indonesian operations, opening a branch in Palu and relocating the Bekasi branch to a larger facility to support a 14,000-pallet capacity. Pharmaniaga’s medical device business, generating RM30–50 million annually, is expected to grow to larger equipment such as MRI, X-Ray and CT scanners, complementing its biopharmaceutical focus. Digitalisation and automation, including four new automated warehouses, are projected to save up to RM8 million annually in staffing and interest costs. MBSB Research expects Pharmaniaga’s exit from PN17 as early as 1Q2026, following completion of its regularisation plan and repayment of RM250 million in loans, with dividend payments anticipated to resume thereafter. The company is also set to benefit from a government concession of 400 million doses of human insulin in early 2026, alongside continued demand for generics under initiatives to curb medical inflation. Despite today’s share price decline, analysts remain positive on Pharmaniaga’s longer-term operational trajectory, underpinned by government support, expansion initiatives and cost optimisation measures. title: Ringgit Strengthens On Steady GDP, Eyes RM4.13-RM4.14 Range
body: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar on Monday, reversing some of last Friday’s losses, as renewed demand for the local currency was supported by steady domestic fundamentals following Malaysia’s latest gross domestic product (GDP) report. At 8.01 am, the local note was quoted at 4.1230/1390 against the US dollar, compared with Friday’s close of 4.1290/1345. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said Malaysia’s third-quarter 2025 GDP growth of 5.2%, in line with consensus expectations, reflected steady economic momentum and provided medium-term support for the ringgit. “We foresee the ringgit could experience some correction as the currency is already in the overbought condition. Meanwhile, the United States’ December rate cut is not a sure thing as there are US Federal Reserve members who prefer to keep it steady,” he said, adding that the ringgit is expected to trade in the RM4.13-RM4.14 range today. In early trading, the ringgit strengthened against a basket of major currencies. It rose versus the Japanese yen to 2.6667/6772 from 2.6690/6728 at Friday’s close, appreciated against the euro to 4.7880/8066 from 4.7983/8047, and firmed against the British pound to 5.4242/4453 from 5.4313/4385. title: Pace Picking Up At Malaysia Marine
body: MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB Research) has maintained its BUY call on Malaysia Marine & Heavy Engineering Holdings Bhd (MMHE), assigning a target price of RM0.46, citing a strong orderbook and more active construction phases expected to lift results in 4QFY25. The house reported the stock offers a potential upside of 24% from its current price of RM0.37, with weakness in FY25 largely priced in. MMHE reported 3QFY25 earnings of RM27.7 million, up 77.5% quarter-on-quarter from RM15.6 million, supported by better performance in the Heavy Engineering segment as newly secured projects moved into more active construction stages. Revenue for the quarter rose 18% sequentially, although the Marine division saw a slight decline. On a year-to-date basis, 9MFY25 revenue fell 50% to RM1.394 billion compared with the same period last year, while PATAMI dropped 41.2% to RM58.1 million, reflecting the absence of a significant project cost claim recorded in 2QFY24. MBSB Research noted that without this one-off claim, the results would be more comparable. MMHE’s orderbook stood at RM4.84 billion, down 6.5% from 2QFY25, with 99% of the outstanding orders tied to Heavy Engineering. The house highlighted concerns over orderbook replenishment, as only RM572 million of new projects had been secured year-to-date. The five-year historical trend shows a declining orderbook from a peak of RM6.32 billion in 2023, although the bulk of projects were secured in 2022, followed by RM2.8 billion in 2023 and RM1.73 billion in 2024. Despite the year-on-year decline in revenue, analysts from MBSB Research said the stock remains attractive due to stable earnings and its strong commitment to environmental, social and governance (ESG) practices. The target price is based on FY25 earnings per share of 4.4 sen, with a price-to-earnings ratio of 10.5 times, slightly below the company’s one-year average PER of 13 times and in line with the heavy engineering subsector’s PER range of 10.4 to 11 times. The house emphasised that the current valuation reflects the softness already seen in FY25 while positioning the company for potential gains as construction activity intensifies in the final quarter. Overall, MMHE’s earnings recovery every quarter, coupled with a robust albeit slowly replenishing orderbook, underpins the analysts’ confidence in the stock, signalling that market participants may have already priced in near-term weakness while the longer-term outlook remains supported by ongoing Heavy Engineering projects. title: Japanese Tourism And Retail Stocks Slide After China Travel Warning
body: Japanese travel and tourism-related shares fell sharply on Monday following a warning from Beijing advising its citizens against travelling to or studying in Japan amid rising diplomatic tensions. Department store operators J Front Retailing Co. and Takashimaya Co. saw their shares drop more than 6%, marking their steepest fall since April 7. Airline operator ANA Holdings Inc. declined up to 3.8%, while Tokyo Disney Resort operator Oriental Land Co. slipped over 4%. Fast Retailing, owner of Uniqlo, dipped 6.6%, its largest drop since mid-July. The directive from Beijing targeted students planning to study in Japan, citing heightened risks for Chinese nationals, and followed remarks by Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi that military action in a Taiwan conflict could be considered a “survival-threatening situation.” Catherine Lim, senior analyst at Bloomberg Intelligence, said the warning “threatens tourism-led sales-growth expectations” for Japanese retailers. She added that the move also raises “heightened risk of boycotts of Japanese goods within China,” potentially affecting mainland sales for Uniqlo, Asics Corp, and Ryohin Keikaku Co.’s Muji. Pan Pacific International Holdings, operator of Don Quijote stores, experienced the largest drop of the day, plunging as much as 8.9%, its sharpest fall since August 2024. title: Japan Tourism, Stock Market Plunge After China Travel Ban
body: Shares in Japanese tourism and retail firms fell sharply on Monday (Nov 17) after China warned its citizens not to travel to Japan in a spat over comments by Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi about Taiwan. In morning trade, shares in cosmetics firm Shiseido dived 9 per cent, department store group Takashimaya by more than 5 per cent and Fast Retailing – the owner of Uniqlo – by over 4 per cent.Shares in department store operator Isetan Mitsukoshi notched a drop of around 10 per cent. China is the biggest source of tourists to Japan.Before taking power last month, Takaichi, an acolyte of ex-premier Shinzo Abe, was a vocal critic of China and its military build-up in the Asia-Pacific. Her comments on Nov 7 were widely interpreted as implying that an attack on Taiwan, which is just some 100km from the nearest Japanese island, could warrant Tokyo’s military support. If a Taiwan emergency entails “battleships and the use of force, then that could constitute a situation threatening the survival (of Japan), any way you slice it”, Takaichi told parliament. Japan’s self-imposed rules say that it can only act militarily under certain conditions, including an existential threat. The comments came just days after Takaichi met Chinese President Xi Jinping for an apparently cordial first meeting on the sidelines of an APEC summit in South Korea. Takaichi, who has visited Taiwan in the past and called for closer cooperation, also met separately with Taipei’s representative at the summit. title: Wall Street Slumps On AI Stock Sell-Off, Interest Rate Concerns
body: Wall Street closed sharply lower on Thursday as steep losses in Nvidia, Tesla, Broadcom, and other artificial intelligence (AI) heavyweights weighed on major U.S. indexes. Investors scaled back expectations for interest rate cuts amid inflation worries and divisions among Federal Reserve policymakers over the health of the U.S. economy. The S&P 500 dropped 1.66% to 6,737.49 points, the Nasdaq fell 2.29% to 22,870.36 points, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 1.65% to 47,457.22 points, marking the steepest daily percentage declines in more than a month. Nine of the 11 S&P 500 sector indexes finished lower, led by consumer discretionary, down 2.73%, and information technology, down 2.37%. Shares of AI-focused companies were hit hard. Nvidia fell 3.6%, Tesla dropped 6.6%, and Broadcom declined 4.3%, reflecting a market rotation away from high-flying tech stocks. “There’s a lot of uncertainties about the state of the economy. What we’re going through is a little bit of a correction in the market in the AI sector,” said Peter Cardillo, chief market economist at Spartan Capital Securities. Other notable moves included Walt Disney tumbling 7.8% amid a potential prolonged dispute with YouTube TV over cable distribution, while Cisco Systems rallied 4.6% after raising full-year profit and revenue forecasts on strong demand for networking equipment. APA Corp gained 3.3% following news that Spain’s Repsol is considering a reverse merger of its upstream unit. Memory device makers suffered, with Western Digital falling 5.4%, Seagate losing over 7%, and SanDisk tumbling nearly 14% after Japanese firm Kioxia Holdings reported weaker sales and profits. Declining stocks outnumbered rising ones on the S&P 500 by a 2.8-to-one ratio. Investors also reacted to signals from Federal Reserve officials, who expressed hesitation over further interest rate cuts due to inflation and a relatively stable labour market after two rate reductions this year. Market expectations for a 25-basis-point cut in December dropped to roughly 47%, down from 70% last week, according to CME Group’s FedWatch tool. The sell-off followed recent data showing ongoing labour market weakness. Payroll processor ADP reported private employers shed over 11,000 jobs per week through late October, while Indeed Hiring Lab indicated a 16% decline in retail job postings from a year earlier. Trading volume on U.S. exchanges was relatively heavy at 20.8 billion shares, above the 20-session average of 20.3 billion. Market indicators suggested rotation toward value stocks, with the S&P 500 value index gaining about 1% this week while the growth index dipped 0.6%.
