title: Stock Today: Keyfield Slides As 3Q25 PATAMI Falls Nearly Half
body: Keyfield International Bhd’s shares eased today following the release of its third-quarter financial results, reflecting softer demand in Malaysia’s offshore support vessel (OSV) market. As of 3:57 pm, Keyfield’s stock last traded at RM1.52, down six sen or 3.8% from its previous close, with a total volume of 889,400 shares. The stock opened at RM1.57, reaching a low of RM1.50 and a high of RM1.57 during the session. The company reported a 49.1% year-on-year decline in profit after tax and minority interest (PATAMI) for 3Q25 to RM41.3 million. Revenue for the quarter fell to RM132.3 million, while earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) dropped 39% to RM76.2 million. On a cumulative nine-month basis, Keyfield’s revenue slid 32.8% to RM351.1 million, with PATAMI declining 29.3% to RM128.4 million. The weaker performance was attributed to reduced chartered days and lower daily rates for both the group’s own and third-party vessels, amid subdued offshore activity and uncertainty in the local oil and gas sector. Utilisation rates for the quarter fell to 81.4% from 99.2% a year earlier, while year-to-date utilisation stood at 67.5% versus 88.4% in 2024, affected partly by higher maintenance and dry-docking requirements. Despite the decline, Keyfield declared a third interim dividend of two sen per share, accounting for roughly 39% of 3Q25 PATAMI. Cumulative dividends for FY25 to date total six sen per share, approximately 37% of year-to-date PATAMI. The group is also pursuing regional expansion, deploying vessels to markets such as the Middle East, while recent industry disposals are expected to tighten supply in the local offshore vessel segment, potentially supporting future charter rates and utilisation. title: Ringgit Strengthens For 10th Straight Session, Eyes GDP Data
body: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar for a tenth consecutive session on Friday, extending its momentum ahead of Malaysia’s third-quarter 2025 gross domestic product (GDP) data, which is scheduled for release this afternoon. At 8 am, the local currency rose to 4.1205/1335 against the greenback, up from Thursday’s close of 4.1260/1300, surpassing its 13-month high last seen on 30 September 2024 when it ended at 4.1210. “The market’s reaction suggests that, despite the resolution of the protracted US government shutdown, investors remain cautious ahead of forthcoming data releases and their potential bearing on the US Federal Reserve’s December policy meeting,” said Mohd Sedek Jantan, director of investment strategy and country economist at IPPFA Sdn Bhd. He noted that Bank Negara Malaysia’s 3Q economic report would act as a key domestic catalyst. “A constructive set of macro indicators consistent with our expectation of 5.2 per cent should reinforce market sentiment and strengthen confidence in Malaysia’s near-term economic trajectory,” he added. The ringgit’s firmer opening also mirrored weakness in the US dollar index, which closed near the 99 handle, down about 0.5% overnight. Mohd Sedek said easing expectations of a December rate cut by the Fed provided a broadly supportive backdrop for Asian currencies. Against a basket of major currencies, the ringgit gained across the board. It strengthened versus the Japanese yen to 2.6649/6735 from 2.6700/6728, rose against the British pound to 5.4197/4368 from 5.4282/4334, and appreciated versus the euro to 4.7921/8073 from 4.7928/7974. The local unit also advanced against regional currencies, climbing against the Indonesian rupiah to 246.3/247.2 from 246.6/247.0, rising versus the Philippine peso to 6.98/7.01 from 6.99/7.00, and gaining against the Thai baht to 12.7278/7786 from 12.7724/7903. The ringgit further strengthened against the Singapore dollar to 3.1664/1767 from 3.1729/1762. Mohd Sedek added that the ringgit could extend its gains and, in the near term, challenge the 4.10 USD/MYR level. title: Malaysia Gold Follows Global Softening Trend
body: Gold prices in Malaysia eased, reflecting softer global sentiment and a firmer US dollar. The local benchmark for gold fell 0.22% to RM555.08 per gram, or RM555,079.97 per kilogram, extending a 30-day decline of 4.6% while remaining up 50.94% over the past year. The pullback comes as investors reacted to mixed signals from international markets. US gold futures slipped following firm economic data that strengthened the dollar, while UK and European markets recorded mild declines amid rising bond yields. Regional factors, including softer Asian equities, also prompted a rotation into defensive assets such as gold. Malaysia’s gold remains elevated compared to other countries due to currency effects. Year-to-date, gold prices in US dollars are up 59.7%, while gains in Malaysian Ringgit are moderated by relative currency strength. Japan has seen some of the strongest gains globally this year, influenced by a weaker yen, while European and UK gold prices have been more modest amid easing inflation expectations. Three main drivers for today’s movements: a stronger US dollar, cautious investor sentiment in Asia, and anticipation ahead of central bank decisions, particularly from the US Federal Reserve. Silver prices in Malaysia mirrored the weaker trend, falling 0.69% on the day. Long-term trends remain positive, with gold surging 122.43% over five years and nearly 878% over two decades in RM terms. Market watchers note that further fluctuations will depend on global inflation data, currency swings, and upcoming monetary policy announcements, which could influence both demand and pricing in Malaysia. title: Hang Seng Index Futures Bulls Hold The Line At 27,000
body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) said the Hang Seng Index Futures (HSIF) continued to demonstrate strong upward momentum after climbing 122 points to close at 27,091 points, reinforcing its position above the key 27,000 psychological level. The index opened at 26,959 points and briefly slipped to an intraday low of 26,756 points before bullish sentiment lifted it to the day’s high of 27,202 points. It eventually settled at 27,091 points, forming what RHB described as a bullish candlestick. However, during the evening session, the HSIF pulled back 390 points to last trade at 26,701 points. RHB Research noted that the latest price action suggests the index is “firmly establishing a foothold above the 27,000-pt psychological level” and is now eyeing a test of the immediate resistance at 27,400 points. With the HSIF trading well above the rising 20- and 50-day simple moving averages, the research house said the bullish structure remains intact. The Relative Strength Index also stayed above the 50% level, signalling continued strength. The research house is maintaining its positive trading bias and recommends that traders keep the long position initiated at 21,416 points, the closing level recorded on 14 April. A stop-loss is set at 25,000 points to manage downside risk. RHB Research identified immediate support at 25,000 points, followed by 24,300 points. Immediate resistance stands at 27,400 points, with the next upside target at 28,500 points. title: Bitcoin Retreats Below US$100,000, Ethereum Follows Suit
body: Bitcoin and Ethereum extended their pullback on Nov 13 as renewed volatility swept across global risk assets, dragging sentiment in the broader cryptocurrency market. Bitcoin slipped back below the psychological US$100,000 threshold for the third time this month, while Ethereum mirrored the weakness with a sharper percentage decline. Bitcoin fell from intraday highs near US$103,967 to trade around US$99,572, marking a decline of 2.5% from the previous session. The latest retreat underscores the market’s difficulty sustaining gains above the key six-figure mark after several failed attempts this month. Analysts attribute the pullback to a mix of profit-taking, fading momentum in tech-linked speculative trades, and macroeconomic caution. Earlier in the week, Bitcoin had climbed toward US$107,000 before risk appetite cooled. Ethereum, meanwhile, dropped 5.8% to trade around US$3,234, after touching a high of US$3,556. Market observers note that Ethereum’s recent performance has been weaker than Bitcoin’s as investors recalibrate exposure to altcoins amid rising volatility and tightening liquidity conditions. The softer sentiment also comes despite earlier optimism tied to institutional inflows into emerging Ether-based exchange-traded products. Moving forward, analysts said Bitcoin faces firm resistance between US$105,000 and US$110,000, with repeated failures above US$100,000 suggesting momentum fatigue. A decisive breakout could revive bullish sentiment, but further downside cannot be ruled out if risk assets continue to soften. Ethereum, meanwhile, must reclaim the US$3,500 region to restore confidence. Market participants are watching ETF flow trends, regulatory developments, and upcoming economic data for clearer direction. Bottom Line: The crypto market enters mid-November on uncertain footing as investors balance long-term optimism with near-term caution. With volatility back in full force, both traders and institutional allocators appear braced for sharper swings ahead. title: Asian Stocks Set For Losses As Fed Rate Cut Doubts Loom
body: Asian equities were poised to open lower on Friday, tracking steep losses on Wall Street, as optimism from the reopening of the US government was tempered by uncertainty over interest rates and stretched valuations in major technology companies. Equity futures in Japan, Australia and Hong Kong all fell in early trading, following a 1.7% drop in the S&P 500 and a 2.1% decline in the Nasdaq 100 on Thursday. Megacap stocks lost 2.7%, while the Russell 2000, a benchmark for smaller firms, fell 2.8%. “The question now is whether the market’s recent exuberance has run its course,” said Fawad Razaqzada from Forex.com. “After a stellar rally since April, technology shares look increasingly overvalued and overstretched, with sentiment tempered by a lack of fresh catalysts and a lull in economic data.” Rotation Out of High-Growth Stocks The heavy selling in high-flying tech giants highlighted a rotation towards defensive sectors. Nvidia Corp. fell sharply, while veteran strategist Louis Navellier noted that the company’s upcoming earnings and outlook from CEO Jensen Huang will be crucial for year-end market sentiment. Other notable moves included Tencent Holdings posting a 15% rise in revenue, with mini games within WeChat contributing 32.3 billion yuan ($4.5 billion). Tencent also struck a deal with Apple allowing the iPhone maker to handle payments for WeChat apps, taking a 15% cut, resolving a high-profile dispute. Matt Maley of Miller Tabak + Co. commented: “It’s an expensive market and expensive markets need lower rates to help justify today’s elevated valuations. So, the idea that this could change quickly with so much data coming out all at once, this uncertainty is raising some fear in the marketplace.” Fed Officials Signal Caution Investors are now pricing in roughly even odds of a December rate cut, as Federal Reserve officials express hesitation amid inflation running above target. Chair Jerome Powell said last month that any reduction is “not a foregone conclusion” and will depend on incoming economic information. Statements from Fed regional presidents underscored the cautious stance: St. Louis’ Alberto Musalem advocated for careful moves on rates, Cleveland’s Beth Hammack said policy should remain “somewhat restrictive,” and Minneapolis’ Neel Kashkari remains undecided. US Data Gaps and Shutdown Effects While President Donald Trump signed legislation to end the 43-day government shutdown, the longest in US history, some economic data, including the unemployment rate from October, will be delayed. This incomplete data could affect market expectations for policy decisions. Traditional safe havens offered little protection amid the sell-off: the US dollar, gold, and Treasuries all declined, with the 10-year Treasury yield rising five basis points. Bitcoin fell below $100,000, down over 20% since early October. Regional Data in Focus In Asia, investors awaited key economic releases, including China’s home prices, retail sales, and jobless rate, after recent signs of slack in the credit market. Bloomberg calculations indicated China’s credit expansion slowed to its weakest level in over a year, dragged down by slower government bond sales and weak borrowing demand. Elsewhere, Malaysia and Hong Kong will release GDP data, while Thailand reports consumer confidence figures. title: Stock Today: VSTECS Surges 6.6% On Strong Q3 Earnings
body: VSTECS Bhd rose 6.64% to RM4.50 as of 12.18 pm, with 2.0 million shares traded. The stock opened at RM4.27, hitting an intraday high of RM4.53 and a low of RM4.21. The Main Market-listed technology company recently reported third quarter financial results for the period ended 30 September 2025, with revenue of RM991.9 million, an 18% increase year-on-year. Growth was led by the Enterprise Systems segment, which expanded 27% on the back of stronger public sector project momentum and the fulfilment of AI-related equipment. The ICT Services segment also maintained its upward trend, rising 12% due to higher demand for cloud services, while the ICT Distribution segment, covering consumer ICT products such as smartphones and laptops, posted an 11% increase in revenue. Overall, the Group’s net profit for 3Q FY2025 rose 32% to RM25.8 million, marking another record-breaking quarter for VSTECS and bolstering investor sentiment in the stock. title: Stock Today: Swift Haulage Rallies 1.35% As Mixed Earnings Highlight Margin Pressures
body: Swift Haulage Bhd saw its share price rise 1.35% to RM0.375 as of 3.08 pm, with 271,200 shares traded. The stock opened at RM0.380, hitting a high of RM0.385 and a low of RM0.375. The logistics company recently reported 3QFY2025 revenue of RM201 million, gross profit of RM56.1 million, and profit before tax (PBT) of RM10.4 million. Profit after tax (PAT) stood at RM7 million, up from RM5 million in the same quarter last year. Container haulage and land transportation remained core contributors, accounting for 71.2% of total revenue, with warehousing and container depot contributing RM34.6 million and freight forwarding RM23.2 million. For the first nine months of FY2025, Swift Haulage achieved RM578.9 million in revenue and RM31.2 million in PBT, with container haulage and land transportation contributing 71.5% of total revenue. The Group maintained a cash balance of RM53.8 million as of 31 August 2025, with net gearing at 1.04 times against shareholders’ funds of RM751.4 million. Despite top-line growth, MBSB Investment Bank Bhd maintained a NEUTRAL rating on the stock and lowered its target price to RM0.35 from RM0.42. The research house cited weaker-than-expected margins in land transportation and warehousing, despite higher container haulage rates and steady freight forwarding earnings. Core PATAMI for 3QFY25 came in at RM5.1 million, bringing 9MFY25 earnings to RM17.9 million, representing only 58% of full-year projections. Over the past 12 months, Swift Haulage’s shares have fallen 20%, with an implied total return of -1.9% and a dividend yield of 2.7%. Analysts highlighted that growth in container haulage and freight forwarding is balanced against ongoing pressure in land transportation and labour-intensive warehousing operations. body: Dialog Group Bhd’s shares rose 1.1% to RM1.83 as of 3.37 pm today, reflecting investor confidence in the company’s recurring income strength and potential new contract wins, despite challenges at the Pengerang Energy Complex (PEC). The company’s stock saw 4.83 million shares traded, with prices opening at RM1.81 and reaching a high of RM1.84 during the session. The last done price compares with a latest average closing price (LACP) of RM1.81. Maybank Investment Bank has reaffirmed its ‘Buy’ rating on Dialog, noting that its midstream tank terminal business and resilient recurring income portfolio underpin stable cash flows. The bank highlighted that while ChemOne Group’s USD5.3 billion PEC project faces delays due to cost escalations with its EPC contractor, Dialog’s long-term fundamentals remain intact. Dialog is reportedly in discussions with multiple oil companies and multinational clients to secure additional long-term dedicated tank terminal contracts. Maybank IB expects “one to two more tank terminal jobs for Dialog over the next 12 months,” which could mitigate concerns arising from PEC’s delays. The research house also upgraded Dialog’s ESG score to 55 out of 100 for FY2024, citing lower Scope 1 emissions, increased renewable energy usage, and reduced water consumption intensity, although this was partially offset by higher total waste generation and a slight rise in lost time injury frequency. Maybank IB said Dialog’s diversified portfolio and recurring income base continue to provide earnings visibility, making it a preferred pick in the oil and gas sector. title: Ringgit Opens Firmer On US Yield Drop Amid Global Uncertainty
body: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar on Thursday, benefiting from continued declines in US Treasury yields that weighed on the greenback. At 8.03 am, the local currency rose to 4.1295/1395 from Wednesday’s close of 4.1315/1385. IPPFA Sdn Bhd director of investment strategy and country economist Mohd Sedek Jantan noted that US Treasury yields continued to ease, with the 10-year yield falling 4.5 basis points to 4.065%, its lowest level this month and nearly 10 basis points below recent peaks. “Markets are turning cautious ahead of key US economic data expected next week, following the House’s overnight passage of the continuing resolution bill,” he told Bernama. Mohd Sedek warned that a prolonged US government shutdown could have wider implications, including potential delays to the November employment report due on 5 December and the upcoming consumer price index release. “Any postponement would leave the Federal Open Market Committee approaching its December rate decision with significantly less information than usual, heightening policy uncertainty,” he added. Meanwhile, Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the ringgit had entered an overbought zone. “In light of uncertainties over the timing of the US government reopening, we expect traders to remain cautious,” he noted, adding that the local note is likely to trade between RM4.13 and RM4.14 today. The ringgit showed mixed performance against other major currencies at the opening. It strengthened against the yen to 2.6669/6736 from 2.6681/6728 and rose versus the British pound to 5.4187/4319 from 5.4189/4281, but slipped against the euro to 4.7857/7973 from 4.7801/7882. Against regional currencies, the local note gained versus the Indonesian rupiah to 246.9/247.7 from 247.1/247.7 and held steady against the Philippine peso at 6.98/7.00. title: US Stocks End Mixed As Tech Leads Gains Ahead Of Govt Funding Vote
body: Wall Street ended mixed on Tuesday, with major indexes seeing a tech-led rally ahead of the Veterans Day holiday, following the US Senate’s approval of a government funding bill through the end of January. The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained more than 1% to close at a record high. The S&P 500 rose 1.5%, led by technology and megacap stocks, while the Nasdaq advanced over 2%. Nvidia climbed 6% ahead of its quarterly results next week, Palantir jumped 9% and Tesla gained 4%. Analysts noted, however, that the recent rally only recovered about two thirds of the Nasdaq’s 6% drop and Nvidia’s 15% decline over the past two weeks. Shares of Nvidia-backed CoreWeave fell more than 7% overnight after the company trimmed its annual revenue forecast, dampening enthusiasm despite strong demand for AI cloud services in September. In Japan, SoftBank reported quarterly profits more than doubled to 2.5 trillion yen (US$16.6 billion), driven by valuation gains in its OpenAI holdings. The company sold its remaining Nvidia shares for nearly US$6 billion, following earlier investments and divestments around the AI boom. Japanese government data also showed domestic investors sold significant amounts of foreign stocks last month to lock in profits. Global markets reflected economic updates and policy developments. The US dollar strengthened to six-month highs against the yen after Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi loosened fiscal policy rules while criticising Bank of Japan tightening. In Britain, government bond yields and the pound fell as unemployment rose to four-year highs and wage growth slowed, raising speculation of a Bank of England rate cut next month. Swiss stocks and the franc rose after the US indicated it was negotiating to cut tariffs on Swiss exports from 39% to 15%, boosting watchmaker stocks by 2-4%. Tuesday’s gains were supported by optimism that the government funding bill would pass the House, ending the longest shutdown in US history. The shutdown, which began on October 1, had disrupted food benefits for millions, left hundreds of thousands of federal workers unpaid and affected air travel. title: Stock Today: Powerwell Eases Despite RM9.5 Million Data Centre Contract Win

Managing Director Catherine Wong Yoke Yen said the deal marked Powerwell’s third data centre project this financial year, reflecting the group’s growing presence in the fast-expanding digital infrastructure sector. “We are pleased to secure our third data centre project in this financial year, evidencing our expertise and capability in this space. The data centre industry in Malaysia is expanding rapidly, helped by Malaysia’s competitive power costs and strong investment appeal,” she said. Wong added that the company intends to leverage its technical capabilities to pursue upcoming opportunities, not only in data centres but also in infrastructure and renewable energy. As of end-June 2025, Powerwell’s outstanding order book stood at around RM117 million, excluding the new contract. At current levels, Powerwell’s shares have traded within the range of 40 sen to 65 sen over the past six months. title: Ringgit Hits 13-Month High As US Dollar Softens
body: The ringgit surged to a new 13-month high at the opening on Wednesday, trading at 4.1285/1440 against the US dollar, boosted by a softer greenback following weaker US economic data. Tuesday’s close was 4.1360/1395. The local currency last traded at a similar level on 30 September 2024, when it closed at 4.1210 against the US dollar. Against regional currencies, the ringgit also strengthened. It rose to 3.1733 versus the Singapore dollar, a level not seen in over three years, and climbed against the Philippine peso, Thai baht, and Indonesian rupiah. The ringgit was also firmer against major currencies including the yen, euro, and British pound. Mohd Sedek Jantan, director of investment strategy and country economist at IPPFA Sdn Bhd, noted that the US Automatic Data Processing (ADP) employment report signalled further cooling in the American labour market. “The weaker-than-expected private payroll gains in October have reinforced market confidence that the Federal Reserve’s rate-hiking cycle may have ended, sending the US dollar index lower overnight. This shift has improved sentiment towards risk-sensitive Asian currencies, placing the ringgit in a stronger position,” he told Bernama. He added that with dollar momentum easing and Malaysia’s domestic fundamentals remaining steady, the ringgit’s near-term outlook is constructive, supported by renewed foreign interest and improving confidence in the local market. title: Hartalega Restrained By Sector Challenges
body: Hartalega Holdings Bhd has received NEUTRAL or HOLD ratings from MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB Research), CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities), and Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB), with target prices revised to RM1.19, RM1.18, and RM1.10 respectively, citing persistent pricing pressure and macroeconomic uncertainties despite ongoing cost optimisation initiatives. Analysts noted that while earnings remained broadly in line with expectations, near-term growth will be limited by currency fluctuations, weaker average selling prices (ASP), and rising regional competition. Hartalega reported 1HFY26 core PATAMI of RM30.6 million, down 7.4% year-on-year, driven by lower sales volume in non-US markets and the strengthening of the Ringgit against the US dollar. Revenue for the half-year fell 11.6% to RM1.8 billion, while 2QFY26 revenue dipped 2.4% quarter-on-quarter. Cost optimisation, automation, and workforce rationalisation helped mitigate some of the margin pressures, with plant utilisation slightly improving to 64.6%. Sales in the US remained robust, though frontloading that inflated volumes by 60-70% in September-October has tapered. Prices for standard nitrile gloves held steady at US$17-18 per 1,000 pieces in the US and US$14-15 per 1,000 pieces for non-US markets. The group plans to partially pass on Ringgit strength to customers but faces limited pricing power amid oversupply from Chinese and regional competitors. Looking ahead, Hartalega aims to raise total production capacity to 26–27 billion pieces with the commissioning of five additional lines at Plant 9 by March 2026. Analysts highlighted ongoing challenges from global overcapacity, US tariff policies, and competition from Chinese manufacturers expanding into Southeast Asia, which continue to weigh on short-term sectoral growth. Long-term demand for gloves remains positive, with structural demand projected to grow at a compound annual rate of 7-9% driven by global healthcare recovery, medical tourism, and aged care needs. Analysts expect recovery to be gradual, likely becoming more visible by end of FY26, supported by cost efficiency measures and further automation. Despite the near-term headwinds, Hartalega retains a solid net cash position of RM1.1 billion (US$207 million), which provides flexibility for production expansion and operational efficiency improvements. The company expects 3QFY26 results to remain flattish quarter-on-quarter, as lower gas costs and efficiency gains offset potential margin compression from Ringgit strength. As of 10.26 am, Hartalega’s stock price is down by 1.68%, noting a price of RM1.17. title: Bitcoin, Ethereum Retreat As Traders Turn Cautious
body: The cryptocurrency market traded lower on Nov 11, with Bitcoin and Ethereum retreating as investors booked profits and broader risk sentiment softened. Bitcoin slipped below US$103,000, down about 3%, after touching intraday highs near US$107,000. Ethereum followed suit, falling roughly 4% to around US$3,423, after earlier dipping to US$3,405. Analysts said the pullback reflected profit-taking after a strong run-up in recent weeks. Bitcoin’s drop below key resistance levels triggered a short-term correction among momentum traders. Broader macroeconomic uncertainty also weighed on sentiment, with investors awaiting clearer signals on US interest-rate policy and inflation data. Risk-sensitive assets, including cryptocurrencies, remained under pressure amid the cautious global tone. Ethereum faced additional selling as it struggled to break above the US$3,650-US$3,700 resistance range, with traders watching for potential support near US$3,300. Moving forward, market watchers expect consolidation in the near term, rather than a renewed rally. Key levels to monitor include Bitcoin’s ability to reclaim US$105,000 and Ethereum’s capacity to stabilise above US$3,300. Institutional flows and macroeconomic catalysts are likely to determine short-term direction. Until then, the crypto market appears set for range-bound trading, as traders adopt a wait-and-see approach following recent highs. title: Asian Stocks Rise As US Shutdown Nears End, Rate Cut Bets Grow
body: Equities advanced across Asia on Wednesday as hopes of a resolution to the US government shutdown and signs of a weakening labour market strengthened expectations for another Federal Reserve interest rate cut. Markets in Hong Kong, Tokyo, Shanghai, Sydney, Seoul, Singapore, Taipei, Wellington and Manila all traded higher, following news that a Bill to reopen the US government had cleared the Senate and was expected to pass the House of Representatives before heading to President Donald Trump for approval. The deal is set to end a shutdown that began on Oct 1, which left about a million federal workers unpaid, disrupted flights and delayed key economic data releases. In a Veterans Day speech at Arlington National Cemetery, Trump said: “We’re opening up our country – it should have never been closed. Only people that hate our country want to see it not open,” he told ESPN. The shutdown’s end is expected to help the Fed assess fresh data after the lapse in official releases. Analysts said September’s payroll report should be released soon, but data collected during the shutdown could face further delays. Adding to the upbeat sentiment, figures from private payroll firm ADP showed US companies shed an average of 11,250 jobs per week in the four weeks to Oct 25, reinforcing expectations of a December rate cut. A separate report by Challenger, Gray & Christmas showed layoffs in October reached the highest level in 22 years. However, Wall Street’s overnight performance was mixed, with investors showing caution over stretched tech valuations following a year-long rally driven by artificial intelligence stocks. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose more than 1%, while the S&P 500 ended slightly higher and the Nasdaq dipped marginally. Concerns about an overheated tech sector deepened after SoftBank revealed it had sold all its shares in US chipmaker Nvidia for US$5.8 billion, sending Nvidia down 3% and SoftBank plunging as much as 10% in Tokyo. “Valuation concerns have intensified as the S&P 500 index has climbed higher throughout the year,” said Fabien Yip, a market analyst at IG. “Investors are questioning whether current title: Wall Street Surges On Tech, AI Gains Amid Govt Shutdown Progress
body: Wall Street closed sharply higher on Monday as tech and AI-related stocks rebounded following signs of progress in ending the record U.S. government shutdown. The S&P 500 rose 1.54% to 6,832.43, the Nasdaq jumped 2.27% to 23,527.17, its biggest one-day percentage gain since May 27, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 0.81% to 47,368.63. Nvidia climbed 5.8%, Palantir surged 8.8%, and Tesla added 3.7% as investor sentiment improved. Ross Mayfield, investment strategy analyst at Baird, said, “It’s another example of the ‘buy the dip’ mantra really acting quickly in the tech and AI space.” The PHLX semiconductor index jumped 3%, while the small-cap Russell 2000 gained 0.9%. The rebound came after the U.S. Senate cleared an initial hurdle on a deal to end the longest federal shutdown in history, which had disrupted air travel and created gaps in economic data. United Airlines fell 1.3% and American Airlines dropped 2.5% amid staffing absences and flight cuts. On Polymarket, the probability of a shutdown resolution this week stood at 88%. Third-quarter earnings also supported markets, with 83% of the 446 S&P 500 companies reporting results that beat expectations. Eli Lilly rose 4.6% to a record high after a rating upgrade, while health insurers including Centene and Humana declined following Senate decisions on Affordable Care Act subsidies. Volume on U.S. exchanges was relatively light at 17.9 billion shares, compared with the 20-day average of 20.8 billion. Analysts highlighted that optimism around artificial intelligence continues to drive the broader bull market despite recent sector volatility. title: Stock Today: MR D.I.Y. Edges Higher Amid Strong 3QFY2025 Results
body: MR D.I.Y. Group (M) Bhd shares rose 0.63% to RM1.61 as of 12.26 pm today, with 6.06 million units traded, following the release of its third-quarter financial results. The home improvement retailer posted a net profit of RM136.1 million for 3QFY2025, up 11.9% year-on-year, supported by higher revenue and improved margins. Revenue increased 5.6% y-o-y to RM1.2 billion, while transaction volumes rose 8.4% to 49.2 million, reflecting sustained demand despite a challenging consumer environment. Gross profit climbed 9.9% to RM566.7 million, with the gross margin improving 1.9 percentage points to 47.3%, aided by lower inventory costs and a stronger Ringgit. Profit before tax increased 11.7% to RM183.8 million. The Group’s nationwide store network expanded 10.0% y-o-y to 1,528 outlets, cementing its position as Malaysia’s largest home improvement retailer. A third interim dividend of RM123.2 million was declared, bringing total dividends for the nine-month period to RM397.8 million, or 84.9% of profit after tax. The latest dividend reflects a 30.2% increase y-o-y, representing a 90.5% payout ratio for the quarter. Chief Executive Officer Adrian Ong said the results reaffirmed MR D.I.Y.’s consistent growth trajectory. “We are on track to record our tenth consecutive year of revenue and profit growth. These results reflect the resilience of our business and the continued trust customers place in our brand — even amid a challenging market environment and ongoing policy adjustments following the removal of subsidies,” he said. Ong expressed optimism for the retail sector, citing government spending focused on the rakyat, positive economic indicators, a strengthening Ringgit, and growing foreign investment as key drivers for sustained growth. At midday, the stock had an intraday high of RM1.64 and a low of RM1.60, with a last done price of RM1.61. title: Stock Today: Fraser & Neave Jumps 4% Following Strong Q4 FY2025 Operating Profit
body: Fraser & Neave Holdings Bhd (F&NHB) shares rose sharply by RM1.24, or 4.31%, to RM30.00 as of 3.14pm, driven by investor confidence in the group’s fourth-quarter and full-year performance. The stock saw a high of RM30.30 and traded 4.02 million units. For Q4 FY2025 ended 30 September, F&NHB posted revenue of RM1.23 billion, slightly below last year’s RM1.26 billion, amid geopolitical tensions and market uncertainties. Profit after tax increased to RM114 million from RM84 million a year earlier, while group operating profit surged 45% to RM173.8 million, supported by lower input costs and improved operational efficiencies. The group’s Food & Beverage Malaysia segment recorded 9.1% revenue growth in Q4, underpinned by strong trade and marketing initiatives and higher export sales. Meanwhile, F&B Indochina revenue declined 15.4% (16.8% in THB terms) due to weaker tourism, flooding in northern Thailand, and export disruptions to Cambodia and Myanmar. For FY2025, the group achieved revenue of RM5.2 billion, marginally below last year, with operating profit rising across core units. F&B Indochina delivered an operating profit of RM474.6 million, while F&B Malaysia contributed RM280.3 million. Despite a higher profit before tax, group profit after tax fell 6.3% to RM508 million, mainly due to increased income tax following the prior year’s promotional tax privileges in Thailand. “F&NHB’s performance across FY2025 underlines the importance of our strategy to capture value across all business activities. It also reflects the Group’s resilience and agility in maintaining stability amid a challenging environment for our core businesses, while advancing the development of our integrated dairy farm to drive future growth,” said Chief Executive Officer Lim Yew Hoe. The stock’s midday gain reflects optimism around F&NHB’s core operations and operational efficiency, even as regional headwinds continue to affect some markets. title: Ringgit Opens Higher Amid Weaker Dollar And US Government Reopening
body: The ringgit opened stronger today, supported by persistent buying interest and a weaker US dollar. He cited a rally in riskier assets, such as equities, amid hopes of a possible end to the US government shutdown. “This is the longest government shutdown, and it is likely to hurt US economic growth in the final quarter of 2025. Disruption to government services, such as delays in flights and statistical data releases, could, to some degree, strengthen the case for an interest rate cut in December,” Dr Mohd Afzanizam told Bernama. IPPFA Sdn Bhd director of investment strategy and country economist Mohd Sedek Jantan noted that after 41 days of closure, the US Senate voted 60:40 to reopen the government. While broader fiscal disputes remain unresolved, the move provides relief to markets and public sector workers. “With agencies set to resume operations, a backlog of economic data is expected to be released in stages. The long-delayed September jobs report, originally due on Oct 3, should be among the first to be released. It will offer key insights into labour market conditions ahead of the Federal Reserve’s Dec 10 policy meeting,” Mohd Sedek said. title: Mah Sing Laying Foundation For Future Sales Growth
body: Analysts have maintained their BUY ratings on Mah Sing Group Bhd following the company’s acquisition of 2.83 acres of leasehold land in Bandar George Town, Penang, for RM51.8 million. MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB Research) raised its target price slightly to RM1.52, while CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) maintained a SOP-based target of RM1.90 and Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) kept its target at RM1.85. Mah Sing plans to develop a mixed-use project, named M Cora, on the newly acquired land, with an estimated gross development value (GDV) of RM528 million. The project will feature residential condominiums and commercial suites, with indicative unit sizes ranging from 450 sqft to 1,015 sqft and prices starting at RM426,000. Registration of interest is expected in the second half of FY26. Analysts noted the strategic location, just 450 metres from the upcoming Bandar Sri Pinang station along the Penang Mutiara Line LRT, as enhancing the project’s appeal to both first-time homeowners and working adults. The land acquisition represents a land cost-to-GDV ratio of 9.8%, below the 11–17% ratio of previous M Series projects, and will be funded through a combination of internal cash and bank borrowings. Payments are staggered over three years, limiting the impact on Mah Sing’s balance sheet, with net gearing expected to rise marginally to 0.24x from 0.23x in 2QFY25. Analysts anticipate the project will deliver EBIT margins in line with the group’s typical 17–18% for M Series developments. HLIB highlighted that M Cora will include commercial suites eligible for short-term rental operations, capitalising on the proximity to George Town’s tourist belt and seafront. Selected units will also enjoy sea views, enhancing their investment potential. Comparisons with nearby EXSIM’s Noordin Suites, which were fully sold at effective prices of RM1,662 psf, show M Cora offering a more accessible entry point while still benefiting from a transit-linked location. This acquisition marks Mah Sing’s fourth land purchase in Penang in 2025, bringing its total landbank to 2,557 acres with a combined GDV of RM30 billion. Analysts expect M Cora to contribute approximately RM17.1 million annually to earnings from FY27–FY30, accounting for 5.2% of FY27 forecasts. The company’s expansion in northern Malaysia, combined with its ongoing landbank replenishment strategy, is seen as supporting future sales growth and earnings prospects. Analysts continue to view the stock as well-positioned to capitalise on the recovery in the Malaysian property market. Mah Sing’s stock price noted an increase near 2%, bringing the stock price to RM1.04 as of 10.26 am. title: Asian Markets Rise As US Edges Toward Ending Record Shutdown
body: Asian markets extended their gains on Tuesday as optimism grew that the United States government could soon reopen, following progress in Washington toward resolving its record-breaking shutdown. The mood across markets was buoyed after the US Senate passed a compromise budget Bill on Monday night, paving the way to end the forty-one-day impasse. Several Democrat senators broke ranks to support Republicans in the vote, allowing the measure to advance to the House of Representatives. House Speaker Mike Johnson said, “It appears to us this morning that our long national nightmare is finally coming to an end, and we’re grateful for that.” US President Donald Trump added in the Oval Office, “We’ll be opening up our country very quickly. The deal is very good.” The proposed Bill, expected to fund federal departments through January, could see the government reopen as early as Friday if it clears the Republican-controlled House. Investors responded positively, relieved by signs that the standoff—which had disrupted food aid programmes and risked travel chaos ahead of Thanksgiving—was nearing resolution. The shutdown had also stalled the release of key data on inflation and employment, leaving traders reliant on private surveys to gauge the health of the economy. City Index senior market analyst Fiona Cincotta wrote, “Reopening would not only boost sentiment, but also open the way for data releases, which could provide more insight into the health of the US jobs market and, more broadly, the US economy ahead of next month’s Federal Reserve interest-rate decision.” The absence of official data has complicated the Fed’s outlook, with policymakers unsure whether to cut rates in December. Analysts warned that prolonged disruptions could have further dampened growth. Pepperstone’s Michael Brown noted, “It has typically been the rule of thumb that every week of a shutdown subtracts around 0.1 percentage point from US GDP growth in the quarter in question. Arguably, the economic hit from the current shutdown could be somewhat larger, given factors like the mounting number of air traffic delays.” Brown added that once the government reopens, markets could “re-focus on what remains a solid bull case of the underlying economy remaining robust, earnings growth proving resilient, the monetary backdrop continuing to loosen and a calmer tone being taken on trade.” Across Asia, major markets including Tokyo, Hong Kong, Seoul, Singapore and Taipei traded higher, building on Monday’s momentum. Shanghai, Sydney, Manila and Wellington, however, posted mild losses. The regional rally followed Wall Street’s strong performance overnight, driven by another surge in technology stocks such as Amazon and Nvidia. Despite lingering concerns about an AI-driven valuation bubble, renewed appetite for tech shares has supported global sentiment. title: Analysts Turn Bullish On Sony As Stock Surges 30% This Year
body: Shares of Sony Group Corp. are expected to rise as recent successes, including the anime blockbuster Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba – The Movie: Infinity Castle, bolster investor sentiment. Analysts’ consensus ratings on Sony have climbed to their highest level in nearly a year, following Wolfe Research’s upgrade to “outperform.” Bloomberg data shows that the average 12-month target price from 24 analysts is ¥4,893, implying a 14% increase from Monday’s close, or roughly US$32. Sony’s shares have surged more than 30% year-to-date, outpacing the broader Topix index. After dipping in early April amid tariff concerns, the stock rebounded sharply as the company’s upgraded guidance eased investor worries. Nomura Securities analyst Yu Okazaki noted, “We expect profits to remain high, particularly in games, music, and pictures, and the anime business.” Nomura has also raised its operating profit forecast for the year ending March 2026, factoring in a weaker yen and strong contributions from Demon Slayer. Estimates from 12 analysts put Sony’s second-quarter operating profit at roughly ¥392.2 billion (US$2.57 billion), in line with last year’s results excluding the financial business, which has been spun off. The company is scheduled to release its second-quarter results on Tuesday. Okazaki highlighted potential risks, including a possible decline in Sony’s image sensor market share due to US tariffs. However, he expects the company to mitigate these effects through careful capital expenditure planning. Sony previously estimated a tariff-related impact of around ¥70 billion (US$460 million) in August. title: Stock Today: Sunway Falters As Merger Speculation Fizzles

Investors appear to be adopting a wait-and-see approach after the speculation, with trading volume at a relatively moderate level for Sunway and share price remaining tight. The slight dip reflects uncertainty rather than any reversal of fundamentals, as market participants digest the implications of the denial and monitor possible future developments. While the merger chatter had stoked interest in the construction and infrastructure sector, Sunway’s shares have not gained momentum pending more concrete corporate announcements. title: Stock Today: IJM Slips Amid Merger Speculation Denials
body: IJM Corporation Berhad (IJM) saw its share price ease slightly to RM2.48 as of 12.08 pm, down 0.4% or one sen from the previous close, with 2.51 million shares traded. The stock opened at RM2.49, hitting a high of RM2.50 and a low of RM2.47 during the session, while buy and sell interest remained balanced. title: Ringgit Breaks New Highs At 4.16
body: The ringgit opened higher on Monday, continuing its recent strength, and touched the 4.16 level against the US dollar as steady buying interest supported the local note. At 8.09 am, the ringgit rose to 4.1670/1830 versus the greenback, compared with last Friday’s close of 4.1735/1775. Last week, the currency climbed to a more than one-year high, surpassing the 4.1730/1790 level last seen on Oct 2, 2024. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said, “The ringgit has performed favourably since last week, appreciating by more than seven per cent year-to-date and is the best performing currency in Asia.” He added, “At the same time, the resilience in the Malaysian economy would mean Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) may want to maintain the prevailing Overnight Policy Rate level, suggesting the gap with Fed Fund Rate would be reduced further, leading to possible appreciation in the ringgit. As such, key data points such as the third quarter 2025 gross domestic product which will be announced on Friday would keep the ringgit steady in the near term.” BNM Governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour highlighted in an interview with The Edge that the global landscape has changed significantly in recent years. “Now that Malaysia operates under a flexible exchange rate system, the ringgit adjusts to global and domestic conditions. In recent years, external factors have exerted some pressure on the ringgit but we have also seen our coordinated efforts provide enduring support. Ultimately, what matters is maintaining strong fundamentals and sound policies so the ringgit reflects the strength of the economy over time,” he said to Bernama. The ringgit opened mostly higher against a basket of major currencies. It gained against the yen to 2.7108/7214 from 2.7192/7220 at last Friday’s close and increased versus the euro to 4.8133/8319 from 4.8154/8200. However, it weakened against the British pound to 5.4759/4969 from 5.4660/4713. The local note also strengthened against regional currencies. It rose against the Singapore dollar to 3.1995/2123 from 3.2015/2048, climbed versus the Indonesian rupiah to 249.6/250.7 from 250.0/250.4, and edged higher against the Philippine peso to 7.06/7.09 from 7.07/7.08. The ringgit also improved against the Thai baht to 12.8556/9145 from 12.8999/9174. title: CIMB Upgrades F&N To ‘Buy’ Citing Growth Prospects
body: MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB Research) and CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) have both maintained BUY calls on Fraser & Neave Holdings Bhd (F&N), with target prices of RM32.08 and RM32.00 respectively, following the company’s resilient fourth-quarter results and attractive medium-term valuations. MBSB Research noted that F&N ended FY25 on a firm footing, sustaining profitability amid a volatile external environment, supported by cost efficiency gains, easing input prices and stable core operations. CIMB Securities upgraded F&N from Hold to BUY, citing undemanding valuations at 18.9 times CY26F price-to-earnings, a 47.3% discount to peers and expected earnings growth driven by higher sales volumes offsetting gestation costs from its dairy farm. F&N recorded 4QFY25 revenue of RM1.23 billion, down 5.1% quarter-on-quarter and 5.0% year-on-year, while core PATANCI rose 21.0% QoQ and 10.5% YoY to RM119.7 million, bringing full-year core PATANCI to RM515.7 million, an 8.6% decline from FY24. MBSB Research said the results were broadly within expectations, accounting for 94% of its full-year forecast and 89% of consensus. The group declared a final dividend of 35 sen per share, taking the total FY25 payout to 65 sen. Revenue for FY25 was marginally lower at RM5.20 billion, affected by softer contributions from F&B Indochina, where tourism slowdowns, flooding in northern Thailand and export disruptions to Cambodia and Myanmar weighed on sales. This was partially offset by stronger performance in F&B Malaysia, supported by resilient domestic demand, well-executed trade and marketing activities and solid export momentum. Operating profit for 4QFY25 rose 45.0% YoY to RM173.8 million, aided by lower input costs, operational efficiencies and disciplined cost control, while full-year operating profit and PBT grew 5.1% and 4.8% respectively. Margins were constrained by a higher effective tax rate of 29.6%, following the expiry of tax privileges in a Thai subsidiary and non-recognition of deferred tax assets for the Gemas integrated dairy farm. F&N’s 4QFY25 EBITDA margin expanded to 17.3%, supported by lower input costs, higher operating leverage and reduced marketing spending. CIMB noted that EBITDA margin improvements more than offset lower revenue and start-up costs from the dairy farm, with core net profit in line at RM517 million. Analysts expect a gradual sales recovery in FY26, driven by new product launches, stronger export sales to Cambodia and continued domestic demand, although margins may remain pressured in the near term due to gestation costs and marketing expenditure. Management guided that the commercialisation of the Gemas integrated dairy farm will strengthen vertical integration and reduce reliance on imported dairy inputs. Both research houses highlighted F&N’s diversified brand portfolio, disciplined cost management and recovering exports as factors supporting earnings visibility and medium-term growth. title: Bitcoin, Ethereum Rebound As Market Sentiment Improves
body: The crypto market staged a notable rebound on Nov 10, with Bitcoin and Ethereum leading gains as investor sentiment brightened and institutional inflows returned to the sector. Bitcoin climbed around 4% to hover near US$106,000, while Ethereum rose 7% to about US$3,640, extending a short-term recovery after several weeks of cautious trading. The rebound coincides with easing political uncertainty in the US, where traders increasingly expect a resolution to the looming government shutdown. The reduction in risk premium helped crypto assets regain momentum alongside broader market optimism. Technically, Bitcoin is consolidating around the US$106,000 level, with key support seen near its 50-week exponential moving average of US$100,900. A sustained break below that zone could undermine the uptrend, while a weekly close above current levels would reinforce the bullish structure. Ethereum’s setup appears stronger, with the token defending the US$3,600 region and building a potential base for a move toward US$4,000. However, analysts note that Ethereum’s gas fees have fallen to multi-year lows, a sign of efficiency, but also a reminder that on-chain activity and network revenues remain subdued. For corporates and institutional investors, Bitcoin’s stabilising trajectory underscores its gradual evolution from a speculative asset to a portfolio hedge and treasury instrument. Should the inflow trend persist, more companies may revisit the idea of limited balance-sheet exposure to digital assets. Ethereum, meanwhile, continues to underpin the broader blockchain ecosystem powering tokenisation, decentralised finance platforms and infrastructure development. A sustained rally could benefit firms offering Ethereum-based products and services. Key risks remain: US Federal Reserve policy shifts, regulatory developments and global risk-off sentiment could all quickly dampen the rally. Traders are also watching this week’s US macro data and on-chain flow metrics to gauge whether the current momentum can hold. Bottom Line: Bitcoin and Ethereum are back in recovery mode — steady, not euphoric. Institutional confidence is returning, volatility is easing and the market is cautiously rebuilding trust. title: Wall Street Ends Mixed As Shutdown, Tech Woes Weigh
body: US stocks ended a turbulent week on a mixed note, with the Nasdaq closing lower while the S&P 500 and Dow Jones eked out modest gains, as investors grappled with economic uncertainty, a record-long government shutdown and stretched tech valuations. Reuters reported that the Dow rose 74.80 points (0.16%) to 46,987.10, the S&P 500 added 8.48 points (0.13%) to 6,728.80, while the Nasdaq slipped 49.45 points (0.21%) to 23,004.54. All three benchmarks ended the week in the red, with the Nasdaq suffering its steepest weekly drop since early April amid mounting concerns over inflated artificial intelligence-driven stock prices. Optimism crept back into markets late in the session after reports of progress in congressional talks to end the longest federal shutdown in US history. The impasse has already clouded the economic outlook, with the University of Michigan’s consumer sentiment index plunging to a three-year low and assessments of current conditions hitting the most pessimistic level on record. The shutdown’s data blackout has also complicated the Federal Reserve’s policy outlook, limiting visibility on jobs and inflation trends. On the corporate front, earnings season neared its end, with 83% of S&P 500 companies beating expectations, fuelling forecasts of 16.8% year-on-year profit growth for the third quarter, up from 8% a year earlier. Among major stock movers, Expedia soared 17.6% on strong business-to-business bookings, while Tesla fell 3.7% after shareholders approved Elon Musk’s record-breaking pay package. Microchip Technology tumbled 5.2% following weak sales guidance, and Block slid 7.7%, with Take-Two Interactive dropping 8.1% after delaying the release of Grand Theft Auto VI to November 2026. On the NYSE, advancers led decliners by a 1.44-to-1 ratio, while the Nasdaq saw a 1.1-to-1 edge for gainers. Trading volume came in slightly below average at 20.15 billion shares. Despite the late rebound on Nov 7, Wall Street closed the week bruised, a reminder that high valuations and political gridlock remain the market’s biggest hurdles heading into year-end. title: HLIB: Genting Singapore Hitting A Soft Patch Amid Gaming Slowdown
body: Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) has maintained its BUY call on Genting Singapore with a lower target price of S$1.07 from S$1.18 previously, citing a softer performance in the gaming segment and weaker group EBITDA margin. The research house projected a total return of 52.2% with a dividend yield of 5.6%. According to HLIB, Genting Singapore’s net profit for the first nine months of 2025 came in at S$329.3 million, down 24.5% year-on-year and below both its and consensus forecasts. The shortfall was largely attributed to weaker-than-expected revenue from the gaming segment, which saw softer VIP rolling volume and win rates, alongside unfavourable operating leverage. For the third quarter, Genting Singapore reported a net profit of S$94.6 million, up 5.3% quarter-on-quarter and 19.1% year-on-year. Revenue rose 10.4%, with non-gaming income jumping 32.8%, supported by stronger tourist arrivals and the ramp-up of new attractions such as Illumination’s Minion Land and the Singapore Oceanarium. The gaming segment, however, remained flat as VIP volumes continued to soften despite a 12.9% increase in international visitors. HLIB noted that adjusted EBITDA rose 18.5% quarter-on-quarter, driven by stronger non-gaming performance, while year-on-year comparisons showed top-line growth of 15.6% and EBITDA improvement of 35.9%. Nonetheless, on a year-to-date basis, overall revenue fell 2.8% due to a slower first quarter, which was affected by lower gaming volumes and the temporary closure of Hard Rock Hotel for renovation. Looking ahead, the house expects Genting Singapore to deliver a stronger fourth quarter as new attractions continue to gain traction and tourism numbers improve. The Singapore Tourism Board projects international visitor arrivals to reach between 17 million and 18.5 million in 2025, aided by improved flight connectivity, upcoming events, and the 30-day mutual visa exemption between Singapore and China. Genting Singapore remains focused on its Resorts World Sentosa 2.0 expansion to solidify its position as the region’s leading integrated resort. HLIB Research expects the upcoming additions, including The Laurus hotel and expanded entertainment offerings, to support long-term growth despite near-term headwinds in the gaming segment. While earnings forecasts have been revised down by up to 16.6% for FY25–27, the research house highlighted Genting Singapore’s attractive dividend yield and strong fundamentals, maintaining its positive stance on the counter. title: HLIB Downgrades Axis REIT To ‘Hold’ Despite Strategic RM800M Penang Acquisition
body: Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) has downgraded Axis REIT to HOLD from Buy with an unchanged target price of RM2.25, while MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB Research) maintained its NEUTRAL call and target price of RM2.07. Both research houses cited the trust’s latest RM800 million industrial property acquisition in Penang as a key move that will lift long-term earnings but add near-term gearing pressure. Axis REIT announced that it has accepted a letter of offer from Ann Joo Steel Bhd (AJSB) to acquire a freehold industrial property located in Seberang Perai Tengah, Penang. The property spans 135.5 acres and comprises land and industrial buildings that will be leased back to AJSB for eight years, with a fixed monthly rental of RM4.16 million. According to MBSB Research, the deal will increase Axis REIT’s total assets by 15% and deliver a gross acquisition yield of 6.2%, higher than its average financing cost of 4.1%. The research house expects the acquisition to lift FY26–FY27 earnings by about 7%, though it noted that gearing will rise from 0.33 times to 0.42 times, potentially triggering a private placement exercise. HLIB described the transaction as positive for Axis REIT’s long-term income stability due to the property’s strategic location within the Prai Industrial Estate, near Penang Island, the North–South Expressway, and Penang Port. The house highlighted that the RM800 million purchase price, translating to RM134.2 per sq ft, represents a 62% discount to the median industrial property price of RM351.1 per sq ft recorded over the past 12 months. The acquisition will be fully funded by debt, pushing the gearing ratio to 46.8% based on HLIB’s FY27 forecast. While yield-neutral in the short term, it is expected to boost FY27 distribution income by 6.2%, with meaningful earnings contribution expected to begin from the first quarter of 2027. Despite the positive fundamentals, HLIB said the recent rally in Axis REIT’s unit price has limited near-term upside, tempering its earlier bullish stance. It added that while Axis REIT’s proactive acquisition strategy and exposure to key logistics and industrial hubs continue to support its long-term outlook, investors should expect modest returns in the near term. Both MBSB Research and HLIB maintained that the proposed acquisition aligns with Axis REIT’s long-term strategy to grow its industrial asset base, though current yields of around 4.2% to 4.5% remain less attractive compared to broader market opportunities. Axis REIT’s counter closed its trading session on Nov 7 at RM2.15, after declining one sen with around 12 million shares traded. title: Tech, Consumer Shares Drag Wall Street Lower As Investors Eye Economic Risks
body: US stocks fell sharply on Thursday, weighed down by declines in major technology and consumer discretionary shares, as investors grew cautious over high valuations and economic uncertainty. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq each dropped more than 1%, with the S&P 500 technology index down 2% and consumer discretionary shares falling 2.5%. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index slid 2.4% following a 3.6% fall in Qualcomm shares after the chipmaker warned its dominance in Samsung’s future devices could weaken. “The market wants guidance and right now, with tariffs, the shutdown and possibly peak AI, the future could be bleak,” said Longbow Asset Management chief executive officer Jake Dollarhide. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 398.70 points, or 0.84%, to 46,912.30. The S&P 500 fell 75.97 points, or 1.12%, to 6,720.32, while the Nasdaq Composite lost 445.80 points, or 1.90%, to 23,053.99. Investors remained on edge over the US government shutdown, trade tariff rulings and a string of corporate earnings, as analysts warned of inflated stock prices driven by artificial intelligence momentum. Adding to concerns, a report by Challenger, Gray & Christmas showed that US-based employers cut more than 150,000 jobs in October, marking the biggest monthly reduction in over two decades. The weak labour data increased expectations of another Federal Reserve rate cut this year, sending the dollar down 0.42% to 99.70 against a basket of major currencies. US Treasury yields also fell, with the 10-year and two-year yields dropping seven basis points each to 4.089% and 3.562% respectively. Globally, the Bank of England voted narrowly to keep its benchmark rate at 4.0%, bolstering the British pound by 0.64% to US$1.3132. The pan-European STOXX 600 index slipped 0.7%, while Legrand shares plunged after being hit by US tariffs. Oil prices weakened as traders weighed a potential supply glut, with US crude easing 17 cents to US$59.43 a barrel and Brent falling 14 cents to US$63.38. title: Ringgit Nears One-Year High As BNM Holds Rate Steady
body: The ringgit rose towards a one-year high against the US dollar on Friday morning, after Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) left the Overnight Policy Rate (OPR) unchanged at 2.75%. At 8am, the local note traded at 4.1760/1865 against the US dollar, up from Thursday’s close of 4.1820/1845. The level was close to its previous peak of 4.1730/1790, recorded on Oct 2 last year. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the central bank’s decision to hold its policy rate while the United States faces the prospect of easing monetary policy could benefit ringgit-denominated assets. “With BNM standing pat on the OPR, the prospect of lower interest rates in the United States would gradually make ringgit-denominated assets more attractive as interest rate differentials narrow,” he said. “As such, we expect the ringgit to trade between 4.17 and 4.19 today.” The US Dollar Index (DXY) fell below the 100-point mark to 99.720 as the American labour market continued to show weakness. “US data showed more than 150,000 job cuts in October, the largest reduction in 20 years. Hence, the case for an interest rate cut is building for the December meeting,” Afzanizam added. IPPFA Sdn Bhd director of investment strategy and country economist Mohd Sedek Jantan noted that the greenback’s recent upward run appeared to be losing steam, with the ringgit strengthening against the dollar, Thai baht, and Singapore dollar. “Market attention has rotated back to the United States’ fiscal outlook, coinciding with a broad sell-off in US Treasuries and steadier performance in global equity indices,” he said. Mohd Sedek added that fiscal pressures remain a recurring issue in the US, though data indicate the economy has yet to slip into a sharp slowdown. “While we continue to view December as the likeliest timing for a Federal Reserve rate cut, the path beyond that remains subject to evolving macro signals.” He said the ringgit’s stronger opening reflected both the easing of the dollar’s momentum and a firmer tone across regional currencies. At the same time, the ringgit was mixed against other major currencies. It eased against the yen to 2.7305/7375 from 2.7202/7220 and slipped against the British pound to 5.4864/5002 from 5.4696/4729. It also weakened versus the euro to 4.8220/8342 from 4.8143/8172. However, the local note strengthened across most ASEAN currencies, rising against the Singapore dollar to 3.2017/2103 from 3.2034/2055 and improving against the Thai baht to 12.8829/9285 from 12.9178/9311. It also gained on the Indonesian rupiah to 250.0/250.7 from 250.3/250.6 and the Philippine peso to 7.08/7.10 from 7.09/7.10 previously. BNM maintained the OPR at its final Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meeting of 2025 yesterday. title: Dollar Steadies Amid Weak Chinese Trade Data
body: The dollar found footing in Asia on Friday, supported by broad market sentiment, as sterling and the yen lost ground and weaker-than-expected Chinese trade data weighed on regional markets. The dollar index, which tracks the currency against six major peers, rose 0.1% to 99.796, recovering some of its earlier losses, though it remained within the trading range it has held since August. Markets are relying on limited data due to the ongoing U.S. government shutdown, which has postponed the release of the monthly non-farm payrolls report. Traders have turned to private sector data showing job losses in October within the government and retail sectors, while cost-cutting and AI adoption have also contributed to layoffs. “Markets are flying blind because we only have private sector data to rely on,” said Christopher Wong, currency strategist at OCBC in Singapore. “There isn’t a clear big trend in the dollar, and that’s why in Asia currencies are taking cues from the broad market sentiment.” The uncertainty has led traders to increase bets on a U.S. rate cut. Trading in Fed funds futures now implies a 70% chance of a cut at the Federal Reserve’s next meeting on 10 December, up from 62% the previous day. Chicago Federal Reserve President Austan Goolsbee warned on Thursday that the lack of official inflation data “accentuates” his caution, telling CNBC: “When it’s foggy, let’s just be a little careful and slow down.” In Asia, the dollar strengthened 0.2% to 153.27 yen following data showing Japanese household spending in September rose 1.8% year-on-year, below the median forecast of 2.5%. The Australian dollar was flat at $0.64785, while the New Zealand dollar dipped 0.2% to $0.5620. Sterling fell 0.2% to $1.31195 after the Bank of England held interest rates steady on a 5-4 vote, with Governor Andrew Bailey casting the deciding vote. Meanwhile, British finance minister Rachel Reeves has indicated that a rise in personal taxation is among the “major measures” being prepared for the upcoming budget, according to The Times. The euro edged down 0.1% to $1.1535, retreating from a one-week high, as global investors weighed the impact of weak trade data and ongoing uncertainties in major economies. title: Bitcoin, Ethereum Stumble As Market Awaits Next Catalyst
body: Bitcoin and Ethereum slipped on Nov 6, extending a volatile week for the world’s two largest cryptocurrencies as traders weighed macroeconomic headwinds, profit-taking and shifting ETF flows. Bitcoin hovered near US$101,500, down about 1.5%, after touching an intraday high of US$104,100 and a low of US$100,400. Ethereum, meanwhile, eased to around US$3,317, losing 2.5% on the day. The moves come as sentiment in global markets remains risk-averse, with investors bracing for fresh US inflation data and possible signals from the Federal Reserve on future rate paths. Analysts say Bitcoin is sitting at a crucial crossroads. The US$100,000 mark has emerged as a key support level, one that could determine whether the benchmark crypto stabilises or slips deeper into correction territory. On-chain data, however, offers a glimmer of optimism. The MVRV ratio, a measure of market value versus realised value, suggests selling pressure may be nearing exhaustion, indicating a potential accumulation phase among long-term holders. Still, persistent ETF outflows and a “risk-off” tone across global markets have capped upside momentum. In the meantime, Ethereum is facing its own hurdles, trading near US$3,300 after a steady week of outflows from ETH-based exchange-traded funds. Despite near-term weakness, some analysts believe the token may be nearing a pivot point. Technical indicators show Ethereum could rebound if it manages to reclaim US$3,500-US$3,600. A breakout above that range could pave the way toward US$4,000 by month-end. Failure to hold current levels, however, could send the asset sliding toward the US$3,000 support zone. Despite the pullback, institutional participation in crypto markets remains robust. A recent Reuters survey found that 55% of global hedge funds maintain some form of crypto exposure, mostly through derivatives or structured products, and plan to increase allocations over the next year. That trend suggests the current weakness may reflect tactical repositioning rather than a long-term exodus. Moving forward, market watchers say Bitcoin’s ability to defend the US$100,000 line will be key in shaping sentiment across the digital-asset complex. For Ethereum, sustained consolidation above US$3,300 could signal that the correction phase is nearing its end. With US macro data and ETF flow reports due in the coming days, traders are bracing for another round of volatility. title: A Spirited QoQ Earnings Recovery For Heineken, Analysts Say
body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) and Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) have maintained their BUY calls on Heineken Malaysia Bhd (HEIM), setting a target price of RM26.50, representing an upside potential of about 23% and a projected FY26F yield of around 7%. Both research houses said Heineken’s latest quarterly results showed a spirited quarter-on-quarter recovery, supported by margin expansion and premiumisation strategies that continue to drive earnings growth and dividend payout. RHB Research noted that Heineken’s results for the first nine months of 2025 were broadly within expectations, with a net profit of RM318 million, down 2% year-on-year. This figure accounted for 68% and 71% of the firm’s and consensus forecasts, respectively. The research house expects a stronger fourth quarter in line with seasonal patterns, maintaining its dividend discount model (DDM)-derived target price of RM26.50, which includes a 6% ESG premium and implies a 17 times price-to-earnings ratio for FY26F, on par with its five-year mean. Heineken’s 9M25 revenue was flat at RM2 billion as effective marketing and enhanced distribution helped offset softer consumer sentiment and the earlier timing of Lunar New Year. Profit before tax rose 2% to RM419 million, driven by cost optimisation and price adjustments, expanding margins by 0.6 percentage points. However, net profit fell 2% after normalising for a higher effective tax rate compared to the previous year. On a quarterly basis, the third-quarter revenue jumped 22% to RM656 million, aided by improving consumer sentiment following the weakness in the previous quarter caused by global tariff uncertainties. This lifted its PBT margin to a record 22.7%, with net profit surging 36% quarter-on-quarter to RM113 million. Both RHB Research and HLIB expect demand to be front-loaded in October before the excise duty hike takes effect in November. Although volumes may soften thereafter, they anticipate breweries ramping up marketing and promotional efforts to stimulate consumption. The upcoming Visit Malaysia Year 2026 is also expected to bolster sales through increased tourist arrivals, while efficiency gains, favourable input costs, and stable foreign exchange conditions should help sustain profit margins. The research houses added that the company’s dividend payout is likely to remain generous, supported by strong fundamentals and consistent earnings. The recent excise duty increase, while negative in the short term, is likely already priced in, given brewery stocks are trading below historical averages. RHB Research and HLIB highlighted that Heineken’s focus on premiumisation, disciplined cost management, and sustainable growth positions it well to navigate near-term challenges. However, they cautioned that risks remain, particularly from regulatory changes and potential loss of market share. As of 3pm, the stock price is down 22 sen to RM21.42. title: Wall Street Pauses For Breath Amid Fed Uncertainty
body: Wall Street closed on a mixed note overnight as investors assessed fresh economic data and looked ahead to the US Federal Reserve’s next policy direction. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.2% to finish at 39,380 points, supported by gains in financial and industrial counters. The S&P 500 edged 0.1% lower to 5,238, while the Nasdaq Composite slipped 0.3% to 16,230 amid weakness in major technology stocks. Market sentiment remained cautious, with traders factoring in signals that the Fed may keep interest rates higher for longer as inflation data continues to hover above the central bank’s comfort zone. Investors also digested a series of corporate earnings, which painted a mixed picture of the broader economy. Gains in banking and energy stocks helped offset losses in the tech sector, as Treasury yields stayed elevated following hawkish comments from several Fed officials. Analysts said the latest figures reinforce expectations that the Fed will likely hold rates steady at its next meeting, while leaving the door open for possible cuts in early 2026 if inflation continues to ease. The cautious mood on Wall Street is expected to set the tone for Asian markets, including Bursa Malaysia, where investors await Bank Negara Malaysia’s decision on the Overnight Policy Rate later today. title: Stock Today: SD Guthrie Rises 1.33% As Bullish Calls On Land Monetisation And Industrial Growth
body: Shares of SD Guthrie Bhd climbed 1.33% at midday to RM5.35 as investors reacted to a series of bullish calls from research houses following its strong third-quarter performance and rising contributions from the group’s industrial property segment. At 12.09pm, the counter rose 7 sen from its previous close of RM5.28, with 6.28 million shares traded. The stock opened at RM5.30 and touched a high of RM5.38 before easing slightly. RHB Investment Bank Bhd maintained its BUY call with a higher target price of RM6.95, citing a 32% upside potential. It said SD Guthrie’s nine-month core earnings of RM1.89 billion had exceeded expectations, boosted by RM378 million in maiden contributions from land sales in Bukit Pelandok, Negeri Sembilan. CIMB Investment Bank Bhd also reaffirmed its positive view with a raised target price of RM6.01, highlighting “triple tailwinds” from stronger palm oil prices, robust land monetisation and solid ESG positioning. Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd reiterated its BUY call with an unchanged target price of RM5.76, noting sustained earnings momentum and stable production costs. Analysts said the group’s performance continues to be underpinned by a growing industrial portfolio, resilient upstream yields and steady land sales, with average crude palm oil prices expected to hover around RM4,300 per tonne in FY26. The decision marks the conclusion of a legal dispute that began in 2016, reaffirming Kelington’s position in a contractual disagreement that went through several levels of appeal before the final verdict. The company said the judgment brings closure to a multi-year case, with the financial impact expected to be positive following the enforcement of the award. title: Ringgit Edges Higher Ahead Of OPR Decision
body: The ringgit opened stronger against the US dollar this morning, extending gains from Wednesday’s close as investors await Bank Negara Malaysia’s Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) decision on the overnight policy rate (OPR) later today. At 8 am, the local note stood at 4.1865/1985 versus the greenback compared with 4.1890/1925 yesterday. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the central bank is expected to maintain the OPR at 2.75%, citing the Malaysian economy’s resilience as reflected in the third quarter gross domestic product (GDP) growth of 5.2%. “As such, the US dollar-ringgit pair is expected to linger around the RM4.19 level today,” he said. Mohd Afzanizam added that overall sentiment in the local market remains upbeat even though the US Dollar Index (DXY) hovers near 100 points. “The United States economic indicators posted encouraging figures. Nevertheless, issues surrounding the government shutdown and tariffs are weighing on business sentiment as government service delivery are being interrupted along with increasing business costs due to higher import tariffs,” he said. At the opening, the ringgit showed mixed performance against major currencies. It was slightly lower against the British pound at 5.4642/4799 from 5.4612/4658 and also eased versus the euro to 4.8124/8262 from 4.8106/8147. However, it rose against the Japanese yen to 2.7116/7245 from 2.7254/7279. The local currency also advanced against most ASEAN counterparts. It gained to 3.2039/2133 against the Singapore dollar from 3.2055/2085 and strengthened versus the Philippine peso to 7.11/7.14 from 7.12/7.13. Meanwhile, it was nearly flat at 250.4/251.2 against the Indonesian rupiah and slipped marginally against the Thai baht to 12.8776/9244 from 12.8730/8893. title: Gold Prices Climb 0.5% Amid Global Uptrend
body: Gold prices in Malaysia rose in early Thursday trade, tracking gains across major markets as investors continued to favour the metal amid lingering economic uncertainty and a weaker US dollar. As of 3.19am New York time, gold in Malaysia traded at RM539.55 per gram, up RM2.72 or 0.51%, while the price per kilogramme stood at RM539,549.57. On an annual basis, gold in the local market has surged 40.53%, reflecting strong investor appetite throughout 2025. The upward move in Malaysian gold mirrored global trends, with gold priced in US dollars climbing 51.8% so far this year, one of its strongest annual performances in over a decade. Similar gains were recorded in other currencies, including 44.3% in the Australian dollar, 48.9% in the Canadian dollar, and 45.7% in the British pound. In comparison, gold’s rise in the Chinese yuan and Japanese yen was even more pronounced, up 47.4% and 48.6% respectively, driven by weakening domestic currencies and increased safe-haven demand. The rally underscores gold’s role as a hedge against inflation and currency volatility, with analysts noting that the ongoing economic slowdown and uncertain interest rate outlook have reinforced investor interest in the precious metal. Silver prices in Malaysia also advanced, gaining 0.68% to RM1.38 per gram, extending a 44.47% rise over the past year. Over the last six months, gold prices in Malaysia have risen 16.34%, adding RM2,344.64, supported by continued strength in physical demand and sustained global price momentum.
