title: Stock Today: Westports Leads Bursa On Earnings And Expansion Drive
body: Shares of Westports Holdings Bhd climbed 5.9% to RM5.40 at midday, emerging as the top gainer on Bursa Malaysia, buoyed by sustained investor optimism following upbeat earnings and positive analyst calls. CIMB Investment Bank and Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB) have both maintained their BUY ratings on the port operator, citing solid earnings momentum supported by recent tariff hikes, higher container throughput and improved operational efficiency. CIMB Securities reaffirmed its target price at RM6.20 after Westports’ third-quarter FY2025 core net profit rose 15% quarter-on-quarter and 17% year-on-year to RM267 million. It said the stronger results were driven by tariff adjustments, a favourable cargo mix and higher rental income. Westports management has maintained its mid-single-digit container volume growth guidance for 2025, supported by steady transhipment demand. HLIB forecasts a 9% earnings growth for FY2026, projecting total returns of about 32.7%, backed by strong cash flow and its dividend reinvestment plan. title: Stock Today: PJBumi Shares Plunge 24% Amid Unexplained Market Activity
body: PJBumi Bhd’s shares tumbled 24.29% to close at RM1.34 on 5 November 2025, following unusually heavy trading of 2.47 million units, prompting scrutiny from Bursa Malaysia. The stock opened at RM1.48, hit a low of RM1.24, and recorded a last done price of RM1.34. Earlier, Bursa Malaysia had issued a query to PJBumi under its Unusual Market Activity (UMA) procedures, seeking clarification on the sharp decline in the company’s share price. In response, PJBumi stated that after consulting its board members, it was unaware of any undisclosed corporate developments, ongoing negotiations, or other factors that could explain the unusual trading. “The Board is not aware of any corporate development relating to the Group that has not been previously announced, including those in the stage of negotiation and evaluation,” the company said. The group added that it did not know of any rumours or reports that could have triggered the price movement and pledged to make the necessary announcements in compliance with Bursa’s Main Market Listing Requirements should any material agreements be executed. This comes amid heightened market sensitivity, as investors reacted to the sharp fall in PJBumi shares despite the company confirming no new developments. title: Ringgit Holds Firm Ahead Of Key Rate Decisions
body: The ringgit traded almost unchanged against the US dollar this morning as investors awaited key lending rate announcements both in Malaysia and the United States. At 8 am, the local currency stood at RM4.1945/2050 against the greenback, compared with Tuesday’s close of RM4.1950/1985. Bank Negara Malaysia’s Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) is set to announce its Overnight Policy Rate (OPR) decision tomorrow, while market participants are eyeing the US Federal Reserve’s next move on the Federal Funds Rate (FFR) in December. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the MPC is widely expected to maintain the OPR, while the Fed is likely to continue with rate cuts, a move that would narrow the rate gap further. “That, coupled with ongoing fiscal reforms in Malaysia, is credit-positive for the country. More foreign funds would likely be attracted to Malaysian Government Securities and Government Investment Issues,” he told Bernama. He added that the bid-to-cover ratio for government bonds remained healthy, averaging 2.6 times in the first 10 months of 2025, compared with the 2022–2024 average of 2.2 times. As for the greenback, the US Dollar Index (DXY) continued edging towards the 100-point mark as the prolonged Washington shutdown entered its 35th day. “It appears that the Fed should continue cutting interest rates, but mixed views among its members have challenged that outlook. This has lent support to the US dollar in the immediate term,” Mohd Afzanizam noted. He forecast that the US dollar–ringgit pair would likely trade within a narrow range of RM4.19 to RM4.20 today. At the opening, the ringgit mostly traded higher against major currencies. It rose against the British pound to 5.4612/4749 from 5.4795/4841 and strengthened versus the euro to 4.8174/8294 from 4.8238/8279. The local note, however, slipped slightly against the Japanese yen to 2.7322/7392 from 2.7331/7355 previously. Against regional currencies, the ringgit advanced to 3.2075/2158 versus the Singapore dollar from 3.2131/2160 and firmed to 12.8701/9118 against the Thai baht from 12.8859/9026. It was little changed against the Indonesian rupiah at 251.0/251.8 and steady against the Philippine peso at 7.16/7.19. title: Malaysia’s Gold Prices Climb 0.34% Amid Strong Global Rally
body: Gold prices in Malaysia edged higher today, tracking gains across global markets as investors continued to hedge against inflationary pressures and geopolitical uncertainty. According to data from goldprice.org, the price of gold in Malaysia rose 0.34% to RM534.99 per gram, an increase of RM1.84 from the previous session. On a per-kilogram basis, gold was valued at RM534,990.27, up RM1,836.12. The local market’s performance reflects a broader global rally in gold, with the precious metal seeing a 50.5% surge in US dollar terms since the start of 2025. Gains were also notable in other major currencies, with increases of 43.5% in Australian dollars, 47.4% in Canadian dollars, and 46.9% in Chinese yuan. The uptrend to persistent demand for safe-haven assets amid slowing global economic momentum and expectations that key central banks, including the US Federal Reserve, may cut interest rates in early 2026. Over the past six months, gold in Malaysia has risen 14.71%, while its one-year gain stands at 41.17%, reflecting robust investor appetite amid a volatile financial landscape. Over the past five years, the metal’s value has more than doubled, up 105.72%. Meanwhile, silver prices in Malaysia also advanced slightly, gaining 0.21% to RM0.42 higher for the day, with a remarkable 45.11% increase year-on-year. Market observers said gold’s sustained momentum could continue into the final quarter of 2025, particularly if inflation remains sticky and global tensions persist. “Gold remains a key hedge against economic and political risks. With the dollar’s recent softness and potential policy shifts ahead, bullion demand is likely to stay elevated,” said one commodities strategist. At the regional level, similar gains were observed, with gold prices climbing in Singapore and Hong Kong by around 0.3% to 0.4%, mirroring Malaysia’s trend. As of early Wednesday, global spot gold traded near US$2,500 per ounce, maintaining its bullish trajectory that began in mid-2024, making it one of the year’s best-performing assets. title: Malaysia Debuts First SRI-Qualified ETF
body: Bursa Malaysia Bhd and AmInvest today launched the FTSE4Good Bursa Malaysia ETF, marking the country’s first and only sustainable and responsible investment (SRI)-qualified exchange-traded fund. The fund aims to track the FTSE4Good Bursa Malaysia Index, which selects constituents from the FTSE Bursa Malaysia EMAS Index based on Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) criteria and liquidity standards developed by FTSE Russell in collaboration with the Exchange. The Index, introduced in December 2014, was designed to advance ESG practices in Malaysia’s capital market and guide investors in making ESG-focused investment decisions while highlighting companies demonstrating strong ESG performance. Dato’ Fad’l Mohamed, Chief Executive Officer of Bursa Malaysia, said, “This collaboration reflects our shared commitment to product innovation, investor empowerment and advancement of sustainability in Malaysia’s capital market. FTSE4Good Bursa Malaysia ETF adds to the growing and diverse range of ETFs listed on the Exchange – from domestic and regional equities to fixed income, commodities, Shariah-compliant assets, and now, ESG-focused indices.” AmInvest, the country’s largest ETF provider with RM1.8 billion in assets under management and 75.4% market share, manages a total of nine SRI-qualified funds. Jamie Ling, Group Chief Executive Officer of AmBank Group, said, “The launch of Malaysia’s first and only SRI-qualified ETF is a meaningful milestone for us at AmInvest. This ETF not only broadens our suite of responsible investment solutions but also reinforces our ambition to lead the market in shaping a more sustainable financial ecosystem.” Goh Wee Peng, Managing Director of AmBank Group Wealth Management, added that the Fund allows investors to access Malaysian companies with strong ESG practices across sectors such as banking, healthcare, utilities, telecommunications and construction, with a low initial investment of just 100 units. The launch reflects a broader national push towards a lower-carbon and more sustainable economy, providing investors with opportunities to align their portfolios with ethical and sustainable investment practices. title: China Sunsine Share Sale Highlights Strong Momentum In SGX Next 50 Index
body: The iEdge Singapore Next 50 Index has continued its strong performance, generating an 18% total return in the second half of 2025 to 4 November, supported by higher trading activity among mid-cap stocks such as PropNex, Hong Leong Asia, China Sunsine, UOB-Kay Hian and Banyan Tree. Among the standout developments, China Sunsine’s majority shareholder Success More Group completed its first strategic share sale since the company’s 2007 IPO. The group sold 42 million shares for S$27.7 million to institutional and high-net-worth investors while retaining a controlling stake and committing to a six-month moratorium on further sales. Following the transaction, Success More’s ownership in China Sunsine fell from 61.6% to 57.2%. Executive Chairman Xu Cheng Qiu said the move was designed to enhance liquidity and optimise shareholding structure while maintaining control. He added that the group remained committed to delivering sustainable growth and creating long-term shareholder value. The placement, executed through Maybank Securities, lifted China Sunsine’s average daily trading turnover (ADT) in 2025 to S$606,000, up from S$80,000 in 2024. The company’s return on equity stands at 10.4% with a price-to-earnings ratio of 7.6 times as of 4 November. In its 1HFY25 results, the chemical producer posted a 29% year-on-year rise in net profit to RMB242.7 million, marking a record half-yearly sales volume. SGX Research noted that the iEdge Next 50 Index has maintained a strong correlation with the FTSE ST Mid & Small Cap Index, sharing 42 constituents. Collectively, the 50 companies represent a combined market capitalisation of S$88 billion, with an average daily turnover of S$165 million year-to-date, up from S$107 million in 2024. Stocks that recorded the largest increase in trading activity this year included Hong Leong Asia, Banyan Tree, China Sunsine, UOB-Kay Hian and PropNex. These companies demonstrated diverse growth strategies such as digital innovation, regional expansion and corporate restructuring. Hong Leong Asia, for instance, expanded its high-power engine portfolio through its MTU Yuchai Power joint venture, while PropNex’s investments in PropTech solutions continued to drive operational efficiency. Banyan Tree is on track to celebrate its 100th property milestone with the opening of Mandai Rainforest Resort, and SIA Engineering expanded its presence in Cambodia, the Philippines and Malaysia. In the technology space, six Next 50 constituents collectively booked S$179 million in net institutional inflows in 2H25, led by iFAST with S$120 million and CSE Global with S$39 million. These firms generated an average total return of 29% for the period, underscoring strong investor appetite for Singapore’s technology-driven mid-cap sector. The iEdge Next 50 Index, introduced under SGX Group’s Equity Market Development Programme, aims to enhance market depth and investor engagement by spotlighting companies poised to graduate into Singapore’s main benchmark indices. SGX Research said the momentum within the Next 50 cohort illustrates how mid-cap and technology-linked counters continue to attract institutional participation, contributing meaningfully to Singapore’s broader market vibrancy. title: Bursa Opens Lower As Investors Turn Cautious Ahead Of OPR Decision
body: Bursa Malaysia opened lower this morning as investors remained cautious ahead of Bank Negara Malaysia’s Overnight Policy Rate (OPR) decision, with sentiment mirroring weakness across regional markets. At 9.40am, the FBM KLCI fell 6.43 points, or 0.40%, to 1,617.07 after opening at 1,622.24. Broader market performance was also weak, with the FBM70 slipping 0.66% to 16,777.93 and the FBM Emas Index declining 0.47% to 11,998.08. The Shariah Index also dropped 0.53% to 11,991.68. Decliners outpaced gainers across the exchange, with market sentiment dampened by global uncertainty and muted risk appetite. Turnover stood at 148.29 million shares valued at RM556.97 million. Among heavyweights, Hong Leong Bank slipped 14 sen to RM21.10, Heineken Malaysia shed 20 sen to RM21.32 and Malaysian Pacific Industries dropped 36 sen to RM30.20. PJBumi remained the top loser, plunging 53 sen to RM1.24 after recent volatility prompted a query from Bursa Malaysia. Gainers were led by Hong Leong Industries, which rose 22 sen to RM14.34, followed by Petronas Dagangan up 16 sen to RM22.76 and United Plantations gaining 10 sen to RM25.10. On the active list, NEXGBina traded unchanged at 4.5 sen with 189.5 million shares exchanged, while MMAG eased 3 sen to 11 sen. Regional markets were mostly weaker in early trade, with Singapore’s Straits Times Index falling 0.88% and Japan’s Nikkei down 2.5% as investors turned risk-averse following overnight declines on Wall Street. Trading on Bursa is likely to stay cautious ahead of the OPR announcement tomorrow and lingering global rate uncertainties, with the FBM KLCI expected to hover around the 1,610 to 1,625 range today. title: Asian Markets Tumble As Tech Bubble Fears Grow
body: Tech companies led a sharp sell-off across Asia on Wednesday (Nov 5) as investors grow increasingly worried about an artificial intelligence bubble following a rally this year that has seen valuations hit record highs. Global markets have soared this year as an eye-watering flood of cash piled into companies linked to AI, including United States titans Nvidia, Amazon and Apple, as well as Asian firms Samsung and Alibaba.But despite strong earnings releases in recent quarters, traders have started questioning the wisdom of chasing ever-higher prices, with cash mostly funnelled into a handful of big-name companies. The gains have also been helped by an easing of US trade tensions and expectations that the Federal Reserve will continue to cut interest rates into the new year.After an uncertain start to the week on Monday, Wall Street tumbled on Tuesday, with the tech-rich Nasdaq down more than 2 per cent and the S&P 500 off more than 1 per cent. US software firm Palantir slumped 8 per cent despite reporting a 63 per cent surge in revenues and profits. Asia took up the baton in the morning, with Seoul and Tokyo the hardest hit, having just hit record highs.Seoul tanked 6 per cent at one point, as chip giants Samsung and SK hynix each lost around 7 per cent. “I view today’s decline as a correction to cool off an overheated market – a phase of adjustment,” Chung Hae-chang, analyst at Daishin Securities, told AFP. “The recent rally was extremely steep, so this is the counterbalance.” He also warned Seoul’s Kospi index could decline 5 per cent further and that “SK hynix and Samsung may also see corrections proportional to their earlier gains”. Tokyo dived more than 4 per cent as tech investment giant SoftBank shed 14 per cent and Sony more than 2 per cent. Nintendo, however, briefly jumped more than 10 per cent a day after the gaming firm hiked forecasts for its Switch 2 console and annual profits. “SEA OF RED” Taipei was off more than 2 per cent as market heavyweight and chipmaker TSMC gave up 3 per cent. There were also big losses in Hong Kong, Shanghai, Singapore, Sydney, Wellington, Manila and Jakarta. “It’s a sea of red across broad markets, and one that offers a gloomy and damp portrayal of risk,” said Chris Weston at Pepperstone. “In the lead-up to the session, traders had been rotating out of the lower-quality end of the market and into the higher-quality plays, and this dynamic resulted in poor breadth within the US equity indices.” He said that dynamic had changed and traders were “cutting back on their winners and locking in performance, with the Magnificent Seven (leading tech stocks) basket and AI plays driving equity risk lower”. And Mike Gitlin, president and chief executive officer of Capital Group, said that while earnings are strong, “what’s challenging are valuations”, according to Bloomberg. His comments came at a financial summit organised by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority on Tuesday, where other business leaders, including Morgan Stanley boss Ted Pick and Goldman Sachs’ David Solomon, warned of a big correction. Meanwhile, Saxo Markets’ Charu Chanana said two questions were echoing across portfolios. “Those who’ve ridden the rally from early 2023 are sitting on substantial gains and wondering if it’s time to lock in profits (and) those still on the sidelines are feeling the pull of (fear of missing out, questioning if they’ve missed the best entry point. “Both are fair concerns. The AI boom has pushed the ‘Magnificent’ names to new highs, but under the surface, their stories have begun to diverge between companies monetising AI today and those still investing for tomorrow.” The uncertainty across markets was also felt in the crypto universe, where bitcoin briefly fell below US$100,000 for the first time since June, a month after topping out at a record high above US$126,000. On the local front, the KLCI drops 7 points to 1,651 as of midday. title: Wall Street Rises On Amazon–OpenAI Deal As Dollar Strengthens
body: Wall Street saw mixed performance on Monday as most major indexes advanced following Amazon.com’s US$38 billion cloud-computing deal with OpenAI, even as the US dollar strengthened on easing expectations of aggressive Federal Reserve rate cuts. The S&P 500 added 11.77 points or 0.17% to 6,851.97, while the Nasdaq Composite gained 109.77 points or 0.46% to 23,834.72. The Dow Jones Industrial Average, however, slipped 226.19 points or 0.48% to 47,336.68. MSCI’s global stock index rose 0.15% to 1,007.70, and the pan-European STOXX 600 inched up 0.07%. Amazon’s shares climbed 4% after news of the multiyear deal, which investors viewed as a major boost to the artificial intelligence (AI) sector. “We’re still looking at this as a market driven by the technology revolution that is certainly in full swing given AI,” said Tim Ghriskey, senior portfolio strategist at Ingalls & Snyder in New York. Investors will turn their attention to a slew of upcoming corporate results this week, with Advanced Micro Devices, Qualcomm, Uber and McDonald’s among the names set to report. After the closing bell, Palantir Technologies rose about 1% after forecasting stronger-than-expected fourth-quarter revenue. Uncertainty over US monetary policy capped gains as traders scaled back bets on another Fed rate cut in December. Fed Chair Jerome Powell said last week that another cut was “not a foregone conclusion,” prompting markets to price in a roughly 70% chance of a 25-basis-point reduction, down from 94% a week earlier. Meanwhile, the US dollar extended its rally against major currencies, rising 0.08% to 99.89 on the dollar index. The euro slipped 0.1% to US$1.1522, while sterling eased 0.12% to US$1.3135 ahead of the Bank of England’s policy decision this week. The dollar also strengthened against the yen to 154.2. In commodities, US crude rose 7 cents to US$61.05 a barrel, and Brent crude added 12 cents to US$64.89 as traders digested reports that OPEC+ plans to end its supply increases. Spot gold slipped marginally to US$4,000.26 an ounce. US Treasury yields edged higher as the government announced a fourth-quarter borrowing estimate of US$569 billion, slightly below July’s forecast. The benchmark 10-year yield was last at 4.107%, while the two-year yield held near 3.6%. title: Stock Today: S P Setia Dips After RM273 Million Land Sale To Mah Sing
body: Shares in S P Setia Bhd edged lower at midday as investors digested news of its RM273.51 million land disposal to Mah Sing Group Bhd, a move aimed at strengthening liquidity and rebalancing its land bank portfolio. As of 12.06pm, S P Setia’s share price slipped 1.78% or 1.5 sen to 83 sen, with 6.15 million shares changing hands. The counter opened at 84.5 sen and traded between 82 sen and 84.5 sen during the morning session. The decline came a day after the property developer announced it was disposing of 275.4 acres of freehold land in Mukim Beranang, Ulu Langat, Selangor, to Mah Sing for a total cash consideration of RM273.51 million. According to its Bursa Malaysia filing, the transaction involves two inter-conditional sale and purchase agreements between S P Setia’s wholly-owned subsidiary Petaling Garden Sdn Bhd and Mah Sing’s subsidiaries Peninsular Connection Sdn Bhd and Mont Meridian Development Sdn Bhd. The land forms part of the Glengowrie Estate, a former 805-acre oil palm estate located about 16 kilometres southeast of Kajang and 43 kilometres from Kuala Lumpur. The area is surrounded by a mix of residential and commercial developments and is accessible via the LEKAS Highway. S P Setia said the disposal aligns with its strategy to move toward an asset-light model, optimise its capital structure and enhance cash flow. “The disposal will optimise the Group’s capital structure, enhance cash flow and contribute positively to profitability,” the company said in its statement. It added that proceeds from the sale will allow it to focus on ongoing developments in the Semenyih–Bangi Corridor, where it still holds about 1,231 acres of undeveloped land. Mah Sing, on the other hand, is expected to expand its footprint in Selangor through the acquisition, reinforcing its position as a major player in the Klang Valley’s residential and township market. title: Stock Today: Frontken Steady As Investors Weigh Semiconductor Outlook And M&A Prospects
body: Shares of Frontken Corporation Bhd were unchanged at RM4.45 at mid-day trading on Bursa Malaysia as investors digested its latest quarterly performance and the continued optimism surrounding the semiconductor recovery. At 2.51 pm, the counter saw 5.1 million shares traded, with prices ranging between RM4.36 and RM4.47. The stock opened at RM4.46 and last traded at RM4.45, giving the group a market capitalisation of about RM7 billion. Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) has maintained its BUY call on Frontken with an unchanged target price of RM4.95, valuing the stock at 37 times its FY26 earnings per share. The research house said the valuation remains supported by Frontken’s strong balance sheet, steady semiconductor demand, and potential upside from merger and acquisition (M&A) activities in the United States. Frontken’s third-quarter results for FY25 came broadly within expectations, with core net profit rising 16% year-on-year to RM41.6 million and cumulative nine-month earnings reaching RM124 million, about 70–72% of full-year forecasts. Revenue climbed 3.5% quarter-on-quarter to RM162 million, supported by stronger performance in Malaysia and steady semiconductor demand in Taiwan. HLIB noted that Frontken’s expansion remains on track, with Taiwan’s AGTC unit preparing new semiconductor lines for 2-nanometre process technology by 2026, while its Singapore operations are being upgraded for a new client. The company is also in talks with potential US-based targets, including a dry-cleaning technology firm and a private equity-owned semiconductor company valued at over RM1 billion. With a net cash balance of RM563 million, HLIB said Frontken has sufficient financial headroom to fund these expansions and M&A opportunities. The research house expects sustained earnings delivery and progress on these deals to support a potential valuation re-rating. title: Stock Today: CIMB Rises 1.21% On Strong Panda Bond Reception
body: CIMB Group Holdings Bhd saw its share price climb to RM7.51, up 9 sen or 1.21% in early trading today, with a total volume of 8.45 million shares. The stock opened at RM7.42, reached an intraday high of RM7.57 and a low of RM7.40. The rise comes after CIMB Bank Bhd successfully priced its maiden RMB3 billion (RM2 billion), three-year Panda Bond in China’s Interbank Bond Market, marking the largest single-tranche issuance by a Malaysian institution to date. The bond, carrying a fixed 2.18% coupon rate, attracted strong demand with an order book of RMB4.64 billion from both onshore and offshore investors. Rated AAA by China Chengxin Credit Rating Group, the issuance is the second-largest Panda Bond ever by an ASEAN institution and achieved a record-low coupon rate for the region. The issuance was arranged in collaboration with 11 Chinese, regional and international financial institutions, highlighting CIMB’s growing presence in the Chinese capital market. CIMB’s share performance reflects investor confidence in the bank’s regional franchise and strategic growth initiatives following the successful bond placement. title: Ringgit Strengthens As US Dollar Faces Policy Uncertainty
body: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar today, supported by weakness in the greenback as investors remained cautious over the US Federal Reserve’s policy direction. At 8 a.m., the local note stood at 4.1900/2065 against the US dollar, compared with Monday’s close of 4.1980/2025. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the ringgit is likely to trade within a narrow range around the RM4.20 level today, as markets digest mixed signals from the Fed. According to Bernama, he noted that Fed Governor Lisa Cook acknowledged signs of a softening labour market but did not provide rate guidance for the December meeting. Meanwhile, Governor Stephen Miran, who voted for a 50-basis-point cut, described the current monetary policy stance as restrictive. “The US Dollar Index (DXY) remained at an elevated level, rising 0.07% to 99.871 points in response to the remarks,” he said. Afzanizam added that the US Institute for Supply Management (ISM) Manufacturing Index fell to 48.7 points in October, marking the eighth straight month below the 50-point threshold, reflecting continued contraction in the sector. “Judging from the ISM survey responses, most businesses have been pessimistic, as tariffs have led to higher prices and supply chain disruptions, given the limited options to source production inputs domestically,” he said. At the opening, the ringgit strengthened against major and regional currencies. It rose to 2.7157/7265 against the yen from 2.7230/7261, to 5.5006/5223 against the British pound from 5.5099/5158, and to 4.8244/8434 versus the euro from 4.8344/8396 previously. title: Gold Takes A Breather After Shining Year
body: Gold prices in Malaysia slipped slightly today, tracking a mild correction in global markets after a months-long rally driven by economic uncertainty and safe-haven demand. According to data from GoldPrice.org, the price of gold per gram in Malaysia fell 0.17% to RM539.38, while gold per kilogram declined RM900.22 to RM539,377.88. On a daily basis, gold per ounce stood at RM16,776.54, down RM28. Despite the dip, gold remains sharply higher over the past year, gaining more than 41% in Ringgit terms and over 20% in the past six months. The long-term trend continues to be bullish, with a five-year increase of more than 108%. Globally, gold prices showed a similar pattern. In the United States, gold is up 52.5% year-to-date, supported by weaker bond yields and expectations of interest rate cuts by the Federal Reserve. Gains were also recorded in major markets, including Australia (+44.2%), Canada (+48.9%), China (+48.8%), and India (+58.1%). The short-term decline reflects profit-taking after recent highs, but the underlying demand remains strong amid geopolitical tensions and slowing global growth. In comparison, silver prices in Malaysia dropped more steeply, down 1.19% to RM2.41 per gram, though it remains up 43% year-on-year. Gold’s strong performance across major currencies this year highlights its resilience as investors seek stability against inflation and currency volatility. With Malaysia’s gold prices mirroring global trends, market watchers expect fluctuations to persist as investors balance risk and opportunity ahead of key central bank decisions. title: Stock Today: Mah Sing Eases Slightly As Investors Digest Semenyih Land Acquisition
body: Shares of Mah Sing Group Bhd slipped 0.96% to RM1.03 as of 4.20 pm, with 28.5 million shares traded, as investors weighed the property developer’s latest land acquisition in Semenyih. The counter opened at RM1.04 and traded between RM1.02 and RM1.05 during the session, with buying interest seen at RM1.02 and selling pressure at RM1.03. The movement followed Mah Sing’s announcement that it had acquired a 275-acre freehold parcel adjoining its existing 500-acre M Legasi township in Semenyih for about RM273.5 million. The land, which forms part of a 305-acre tract, is slated for development as M Legasi 2, an integrated township featuring mixed residential and commercial components. According to Mah Sing, roughly 175 acres will be dedicated to residential and commercial developments, with a gross development value (GDV) of approximately RM1.7 billion, subject to approvals. The remaining 100 acres have been earmarked for potential strategic partnerships or institutional collaborations. The developer said the new township will feature two-storey superlink, linked semi-detached and semi-detached homes, serviced apartments and shop lots, continuing the success of its earlier M Legasi project. At current levels, Mah Sing’s share price has been trading within the RM1.00–RM1.10 range over the past month, with investors awaiting further details on the group’s project rollout and financial performance in the coming quarters. title: SGX Buyback Surge Hits 10-year High As S$1.91 Billion Reclaimed On Open Market
body: Singapore Exchange (SGX) reported that total share buybacks by primary-listed companies reached a 10-year high, with S$1.91 billion in shares repurchased on the open market in the first 10 months of 2025. According to SGX Research, nearly 80 companies conducted buybacks during the period, marking a 90% increase from S$1.01 billion recorded over the same stretch last year. The surge surpasses the previous decade’s high of S$1.89 billion logged in 2015, underscoring renewed corporate confidence amid recent market volatility. The benchmark Straits Times Index (STI) fell about 8% in the first half of April, coinciding with a quarter of the total repurchase value this year, while 2015’s S$1.89 billion total was similarly driven by a 13% market dip between August and September. Among the top buyback counters, United Overseas Bank (UOB) led with S$658.5 million in repurchases, followed by Oversea-Chinese Banking Corporation (OCBC) at S$445 million and DBS Group Holdings with S$371 million. These three banks collectively accounted for nearly 80% of the total value of open-market buybacks by primary-listed firms. Other notable participants included Keppel (S$94.1 million), Sembcorp Industries (S$64.4 million), and Singapore Technologies Engineering (S$52.8 million). Singapore Exchange itself bought back S$22.4 million worth of shares, while SATS and Olam Group followed with S$18.9 million and S$20.7 million respectively. SGX said that 92% of this year’s buyback consideration came from 11 large-cap stocks with market capitalisations above S$10 billion, while small- and mid-cap (SMID) firms contributed S$144 million. Companies with a market capitalisation of S$100 million or less accounted for only S$6 million in repurchases. 17Live Group emerged as a key SMID contributor, buying back S$6.2 million worth of shares, equivalent to 3.4% of its market capitalisation under a programme launched in December 2024. Global Investments Limited followed with S$4.5 million, citing active capital management across its diversified asset portfolio. Catalist-listed firms have also re-entered the buyback scene, with Jason Marine Group conducting its first repurchase since 2015 after posting a 40% jump in annual revenue. Other Catalist counters, including Ever Glory United Holdings, Jumbo Group, Kimly, and Ocean Sky International, have also executed buybacks this year. SGX noted that buybacks are often deployed to improve financial metrics such as earnings per share (EPS) and return on equity (ROE), or to manage capital more efficiently during periods of undervaluation. The exchange added that the recent surge in buybacks reflects a mix of strategic capital deployment and opportunistic market positioning, particularly as companies respond to global rate uncertainty and regional growth slowdowns. title: Ringgit Nears One-Year High Ahead Of OPR Decision
body: The ringgit opened stronger against the US dollar on the first trading day of November, nearing its one-year high as traders anticipate Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) to keep the overnight policy rate (OPR) unchanged at 2.75%. At 8 am, the local note stood at 4.1795/2005 against the greenback, compared to last Friday’s close of 4.1860/1930, a level last seen on October 2 2024 when it traded at RM4.1760. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the ringgit is likely to maintain its positive momentum ahead of BNM’s monetary policy committee (MPC) meeting on November 6. “We expect the OPR to remain unchanged as the narrowing of interest rate differentials between the OPR and developed countries’ policy rate is seen to be the key driver for the ringgit, especially when BNM is anticipated to maintain their monetary stance in light of steady economic growth as well as benign inflation rate going forward,” he said to Bernama. He added that the government’s commitment to reduce the fiscal deficit to 3.5% of gross domestic product next year would be credit-positive, potentially attracting foreign investors to Malaysian government securities. “Given that there is a lack of United States data due to the US government shutdown, traders would probably be looking at domestic factors in order to form their opinion on the currency movement. Expect USDMYR to range between 4.18 and 4.20 today,” he added. The ringgit also traded higher against other major currencies, strengthening to 2.7104/7242 against the yen, 5.4889/5165 versus the British pound and 4.8177/8419 against the euro. It also advanced against most ASEAN currencies, trading at 3.2103/2267 against the Singapore dollar and 12.8683/12.9425 against the Thai baht. title: Malaysia’s Banking Sector Displays Impressive Resilience
body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research), Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) and MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB Research) have all maintained positive stances on Malaysia’s banking sector, citing firm loan growth, improving liquidity, and attractive dividend yields. RHB Research and HLIB reiterated their OVERWEIGHT calls, while MBSB Research kept its POSITIVE rating for the industry. RHB Research said Malaysia’s banking system continued to show resilience in September 2025, with system loans expanding 5.5% year-on-year, driven by both household and business segments. The investment bank said the trend was supported by accelerating loan disbursements and better interest rate spreads, suggesting that net interest margin (NIM) pressure could remain contained in the near term. It added that improved confidence among banks could position the sector for a stronger start to 2026. According to RHB Research, household loans grew steadily at 5.5% year-on-year, mainly from residential mortgages and hire purchase loans, while business lending accelerated, supported by strong performances in finance, manufacturing and utilities. System deposits also increased 4% year-on-year, with current and savings account (CASA) deposits climbing 8%. Liquidity and capital indicators remained robust, with a liquidity coverage ratio of 152% and a CET-1 ratio of 14.2%. RHB’s top picks were CIMB, Hong Leong Bank and Public Bank. Similarly, HLIB Research maintained its view on the sector, noting that September charted resilient system loan growth of 5.5% year-on-year alongside 4% deposit growth. It said stabilising NIMs in the fourth quarter is likely, underpinned by easing competition for fixed deposits and disciplined repricing strategies. HLIB added that gross impaired loans improved slightly to 1.41%, reflecting stable asset quality across both household and business loans. The research house also highlighted attractive sector valuations, with banking stocks trading below historical averages while still delivering solid returns on equity. It said the sector’s compelling dividend yield of over 5% and potential for foreign inflows make it appealing for investors seeking catch-up opportunities, especially as KLFIN continues to lag the broader market. HLIB reiterated BUY calls on Affin, AMMB, CIMB, Maybank, Public Bank and RHB. Meanwhile, MBSB Research said the overall outlook remains POSITIVE, with the sector showing “a whole lot of positives” in September. It pointed to strong business and SME loan growth offsetting weaker retail lending, while liquidity conditions benefited from a surge in CASA deposits due to the low-interest-rate environment. The research house also observed declining fixed deposit rates and improving average lending rates, signalling easing margin pressures. MBSB added that the sector’s fundamentals remain sound, supported by stable asset quality, strong dividend prospects, and its role as a key beneficiary of emerging market inflows. It said improved economic sentiment and geopolitical clarity are likely to sustain momentum into 2026. Overall, analysts agreed that Malaysia’s banking sector is poised for stronger earnings recovery, underpinned by improving loan demand, stable liquidity, and resilient asset quality. title: Gold Shines In Malaysia, Up 40% Over The Year
body: Gold prices in Malaysia continued their upward climb, tracking global gains as investors sought safety amid persistent economic uncertainty and interest rate volatility. As of 3.08 am New York time, gold in Malaysia was priced at RM543.19 per gram, up RM4.21 or 0.78% from the previous session. On a per-kilogram basis, prices stood at RM543,185.82, gaining RM4,202.43. Over the past six months, local gold prices have jumped 20.45%, while the year-on-year increase reached 40.05%, reflecting steady demand for safe-haven assets and the weakening ringgit against the US dollar. Globally, the rally in gold prices has been widespread, with the precious metal showing its strongest year-to-date performance in over a decade. Based on data from Goldprice.org, gold has risen 52.5% in US dollar terms so far in 2025, 44.3% in Australian dollars, and 48.5% in Canadian dollars. The Chinese yuan saw gains of 48.7%, while in euros, gold climbed 37%. Compared with these figures, Malaysia’s 40% annual gain sits in the mid-range globally, boosted by both local currency depreciation and rising international demand. In the United Kingdom, gold in pounds sterling surged 45.4% this year, while in Japan, the yen-denominated price recorded a sharp 49.4% increase, underscoring how currency movements have amplified the metal’s performance in key economies. The surge to persistent geopolitical tensions, strong central bank purchases, and expectations that major economies, including the US and the eurozone, may delay rate cuts into 2026. This has driven investors to rebalance their portfolios toward gold and other tangible assets. Gold’s performance over the longer term remains equally robust, with prices in Malaysia up 112.35% over the past five years and a massive 868% over the last two decades, signalling its enduring role as a store of value in uncertain times. title: Frontken Fueled By AI Euphoria, Closes In Global Expansion Plans
body: Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) has maintained its BUY call on Frontken Corporation Bhd with an unchanged target price (TP) of RM4.95, valuing the stock at 37 times its FY26 earnings per share. The research house said the valuation remains supported by continued semiconductor recovery, strong balance sheet fundamentals and potential upside from merger and acquisition (M&A) opportunities in the United States. Frontken’s third-quarter results for FY25 came broadly within expectations, with core net profit rising 16% year-on-year to RM41.6 million, bringing cumulative nine-month earnings to RM124 million or about 70–72% of both house and consensus full-year forecasts. The sequential decline of 20% quarter-on-quarter was attributed to softer oil and gas contributions and higher upfront expansion costs in Taiwan and Singapore. Revenue for the quarter climbed 3.5% to RM162 million, lifted by stronger performance in Malaysia and steady semiconductor demand in Taiwan. On a year-on-year basis, revenue rose 12%, driven by improved semiconductor activity and the full resumption of operations at its Kulim facility, which had previously been affected by a fire. This, alongside efficiency gains and a better product mix in Taiwan, helped lift profitability. For the nine months, revenue grew 7% to RM451 million while core net profit increased 31% to RM124 million, reflecting stronger contributions from its Taiwan unit AGTC and disciplined cost management. HLIB said Frontken continues to execute its expansion strategy, with Taiwan’s AGTC currently relocating TFT/LCD cleaning lines to make way for new advanced semiconductor lines capable of supporting 2-nanometre process technology. The new facilities are targeted for completion between end-2025 and the first half of 2026. In Singapore, minor renovations are also in progress to meet the specifications of a new customer expected to begin operations next year. The research house also highlighted Frontken’s active pursuit of M&A opportunities to strengthen its global footprint. Management confirmed discussions with two potential US-based targets and one joint-venture partner. Among them is a possible acquisition of a US dry-cleaning technology company valued in the hundreds of millions of Ringgit, which complements Frontken’s wet-cleaning expertise and could be fully funded from its net cash position. The company is also considering a larger deal exceeding RM1 billion with a private equity-owned US firm, potentially financed by proceeds from warrant conversions. HLIB said Frontken remains well-positioned to benefit from structural semiconductor tailwinds, particularly those driven by artificial intelligence and the industry’s migration toward advanced process nodes. With a solid net cash balance of RM563 million, or 35 sen per share, the group has financial headroom to fund expansions in Taiwan, Singapore and the US. The research house added that sustained earnings delivery and visible M&A execution could help absorb share overhang and trigger a valuation re-rating. The stock price is down by 0.44% as of 11.14 am, noting a price of RM4.50. title: Bursa Opens Higher As Ringgit Nears One-Year High Ahead Of BNM Decision
body: Bursa Malaysia opened slightly higher on Monday, supported by gains in blue-chip counters as the ringgit strengthened near its one-year high ahead of Bank Negara Malaysia’s (BNM) monetary policy decision this week. At 9.09 am, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose 1.56 points or 0.10% to 1,610.71 from last Friday’s close of 1,609.15. The benchmark index opened at 1,611.62 and moved between 1,609.09 and 1,611.62 in early trade. Broader market sentiment was positive, with the FBM70 advancing 48.26 points to 17,104.33, while the FBM Emas Index added 16.29 points to 12,039.65. The FBM Shariah Index also gained 7.86 points to 12,105.97. Turnover stood at 247.6 million units valued at RM131.8 million, with gainers outpacing losers. Top gainers included Nestle Malaysia, which climbed RM1.10 to RM114.10, followed by Malaysian Pacific Industries (MPI) up 80 sen to RM30.80, and Fraser & Neave Holdings (F&N) rising 34 sen to RM28.50. Among the top losers were MMAG Holdings, down 21 sen to 25 sen, and Petronas Dagangan, which slipped 20 sen to RM22.48. On the active list, DNeX gained 2 sen to 32.5 sen with over 11.7 million shares traded, while GenM was unchanged at RM2.33 and Careplus slipped 1 sen to 8.5 sen. The cautious optimism in the local bourse came as the ringgit opened stronger at 4.1795/2005 against the US dollar, nearing its one-year high. Traders are largely expecting BNM to maintain the overnight policy rate (OPR) at 2.75% when the monetary policy committee meets on November 6. Economists have attributed the ringgit’s strength to narrowing interest rate differentials and the government’s commitment to fiscal consolidation. The stable domestic outlook, coupled with subdued inflation, has also lifted investor sentiment in Malaysian assets. Regionally, markets in Asia opened mixed as traders assessed the Federal Reserve’s rate outlook and awaited key economic data from the US and China. title: Bitcoin, Ethereum Slide On Profit-Taking, Macro Jitters
body: Bitcoin and Ethereum fell on Nov 3 as traders locked in profits following a recent rally, while broader risk sentiment weakened amid renewed macroeconomic uncertainty. Bitcoin dropped 2.9% to US$107,550, retreating from an intraday high of US$111,184, while Ethereum slipped 4.6% to US$3,714 after touching US$3,913 earlier in the session. The declines came as total crypto market capitalisation fell about 3% to US$3.69 trillion, according to data from AInvest. Analysts attributed the pullback to profit-taking by large holders and a wave of leveraged liquidations. Around US$334 million in long positions were wiped out over the past 24 hours, with Ethereum accounting for a significant share. The sell-off followed reports that major wallets offloaded an estimated US$600 million worth of Bitcoin, triggering a chain of stop-loss orders and forced liquidations across major exchanges. A stronger US dollar and cautious signals from the Federal Reserve, which suggested that interest rate cuts may not come as soon as expected, further dampened investor appetite for risk assets. Bitcoin is now hovering near a key support range between US$106,000 and US$108,000, while Ethereum faces technical support around US$3,650-US$3,700. Traders said a break below those levels could lead to further selling, although most view the move as short-term consolidation rather than the start of a deeper correction. Despite the pullback, sentiment among long-term investors remains positive. Analysts said the current correction is part of a normal market cycle following months of gains. title: Asian Markets Edge Higher As Investors Eye AI Earnings And Fed Signals
body: Asian equities climbed on Monday as investors digested last week’s technology earnings that underscored hefty spending on artificial intelligence, while the US dollar held firm near a three-month high amid hawkish tones from Federal Reserve policymakers. The MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan rose 0.2% to 726.98, staying close to a four-and-a-half-year high achieved last week. The index has surged more than 27% so far this year, setting it on track for its strongest annual gain since 2017. Japanese markets were shut for a public holiday, leading to subdued activity in Asian trading hours. Meanwhile, commodities painted a mixed picture. Gold slipped 0.4% to US$3,985.35 per ounce, moving further away from record levels seen for much of the past month. Oil prices firmed after OPEC+ opted to delay planned production hikes into the first quarter of next year, easing concerns of oversupply. Brent crude futures rose 0.49% to US$65.10 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate crude gained 0.61% to US$61.33. Investors are still digesting key developments from last week, including global central bank meetings and a year-long trade truce between the US and China. While the agreement met expectations, doubts persist about whether the fragile truce can endure the full term. Fed Officials Signal Diverging Views A series of Federal Reserve presidents voiced unease on Friday over the decision to reduce interest rates, signalling divisions within the central bank. Fed Governor Christopher Waller, however, defended the case for more policy easing to support a softening labour market. Fed Chair Jerome Powell, speaking after the October policy meeting, said that a December rate cut was “not a foregone conclusion”, tempering expectations that had previously priced it as a certainty. Goldman Sachs strategists said in a note, “We continue to think that the motivation for the rate cuts is consistent with our premise for further dollar downside. The US economy will not outperform to the same degree as before, which will lead to a weaker dollar over time.” Markets are now pricing a 68% probability of a rate cut in December, down from near certainty a week ago. The dollar remained firm, with the euro trading at US$1.1524 near a three-month low, while sterling eased 0.27% to US$1.3134. The yen hovered around 154.18 per dollar, its weakest since mid-February. The ongoing US government shutdown, now entering its fifth week since it began on Oct 1, is expected to delay major labour data, including job openings and nonfarm payrolls. Analysts say focus will shift to the ADP employment report and the ISM employment index for insights into labour market conditions. AI Spending Still in Focus as Earnings Continue With earnings season still underway, investor sentiment remains pinned on technology results. Last week’s mixed performance from megacap firms reflected ongoing scrutiny over the hefty capital poured into AI infrastructure. Upcoming reports from chipmakers Advanced Micro Devices and Qualcomm, alongside data analytics firm Palantir Technologies, will be closely watched. McDonald’s and Uber are also due to report next week. While enthusiasm over AI continues to fuel global stock rallies, analysts caution that markets could be vulnerable to overexuberance unless companies begin showing tangible returns from their investments. title: Weekly Review: STI Wraps October Range-Bound And Reflective

On Oct 27, the index climbed about 0.4% to 4,440.3, lifted by regional relief following signs of US-China trade talks and broad‐based gains in Singapore equities. However, the lift proved short-lived and by week’s end the market was trading in a tighter range. While positive corporate results in heavyweights (such as Keppel Corporation which posted a 25% profit rise) helped underpin sentiment, overall investor appetite remained cautious amid macro and trade uncertainties. The STI slipped to around 4,428.6 by close, down roughly 0.2 % for the week. The week’s pattern highlights the tug-of-war between optimism over global trade prospects and caution over earnings and liquidity. Financials and large cap banks held up initially, but the follow-through lacked conviction and breadth narrowed. With the index hovering around the 4,420-4,450 band, the near-term tone is expected to remain sideways unless fresh catalysts emerge. Investors are likely to favour selective names over broad market exposure. Key factors to monitor in the upcoming weeks: Global central bank policy signals, the next wave of major Singapore corporate earnings and any further movement in the US-China trade narrative. Until then, expect the Singapore market to remain in consolidation mode, leaning on defensive plays and high-dividend stocks. title: Market Review: Seoul Stocks Hit Record Highs Before Cooling As Investors Turn Cautious
body: South Korea’s stock market capped off a volatile final week of October with record-setting highs followed by mild profit-taking, as investors weighed trade optimism against global uncertainty. The benchmark Kospi surged past the 4,000-point mark for the first time on Oct 27, driven by robust gains in chipmakers and export-oriented firms, before easing toward the month-end as traders turned defensive ahead of major global events. The rally was led by technology giants like SK Hynix, shipbuilders and other export-heavy sectors, buoyed by sustained foreign inflows. Analysts cited optimism over a potential thaw in US-China trade tensions and resilient tech demand as key drivers behind the surge. However, the momentum cooled midweek. On Oct 28, the index dipped 0.8% to 4,010.41 as investors locked in profits and adopted a wait-and-see approach ahead of the upcoming APEC 2025 Korea Summit and an expected meeting between US and Chinese leaders. Concerns also resurfaced after data hinted that October exports could fall year-on-year, underscoring lingering vulnerabilities in the domestic economy. Market analysts said the tone has shifted from “full throttle” to “measured optimism”. Heading into November, investors will be watching for signals from global trade talks and the APEC summit while keeping an eye on South Korea’s macro data for cues on whether the rally can sustain. For now, the market narrative remains one of selective strength, favouring tech and export champions, but with caution as the bull run shows early signs of fatigue. title: Crypto Recap: Bitcoin, Ethereum End October Mixed After Volatile Week

Bitcoin briefly surged past US$115,000 on Oct 27, buoyed by optimism over potential US Federal Reserve rate cuts and easing trade tensions between Washington and Beijing. However, the rally proved short-lived as the world’s largest cryptocurrency slipped back toward US$109,700 by Oct 31, marking its first October decline since 2018. Analysts said the pullback reflected investors locking in profits ahead of key central bank announcements and geopolitical uncertainties. Ethereum initially outperformed its larger peer, climbing above US$4,200 early in the week on strong institutional inflows and renewed enthusiasm for decentralised finance projects. By month-end, however, Ethereum eased to the US$3,850-US$3,900 range, mirroring the broader market’s subdued tone. Despite the dip, Ethereum maintained relative strength thanks to its ongoing network upgrades and deflationary token model. Market strategists say the crypto space remains highly sensitive to global economic signals. title: Wall Street Climbs As Amazon Ignites Rally, But Fed Caution Tempers Mood
body: Wall Street ended higher on Oct 31, lifted by Amazon’s blockbuster earnings forecast, even as cautious signals from the Federal Reserve (Fed) capped enthusiasm, Reuters reported. The S&P 500 rose 0.26%, the Nasdaq Composite added 0.61% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average edged up 0.09%, wrapping up a strong week and extending their longest monthly winning streaks in years. Amazon stole the spotlight, soaring 9.6% to a record high after projecting sales above estimates, powering the consumer discretionary sector to a 4% surge, its best day since May. However, Apple slipped 0.4%, as upbeat iPhone sales guidance was overshadowed by CEO Tim Cook’s warning of supply constraints. Investor optimism over interest rate cuts dimmed after Fed officials Raphael Bostic and Beth Hammack downplayed the likelihood of imminent easing. Traders now see a 65% chance of a December rate cut, sharply lower than a week ago, according to CME’s FedWatch tool. Despite the Fed jitters, the S&P 500 gained 0.7% for the week and 2.27% for October, its sixth straight monthly rise, the longest since 2021. The Nasdaq surged 4.7% for its seventh monthly advance, the longest streak since 2018, while the Dow added 2.5%. Earnings season remains a bright spot: Of 315 S&P 500 firms that have reported, 83.2% have beaten estimates, well above the long-term average. Elsewhere, Warner Bros Discovery jumped 8.7% on reports Netflix may bid for its studio and streaming arm, while Netflix rose 2.7% after unveiling a 10-for-1 stock split. title: Oil Ends Higher After Volatile Session
body: Oil prices finished slightly higher on Oct 31 after a rollercoaster trading session driven by geopolitical headlines and mixed economic signals. Reuters reported that Brent crude settled at US$65.07 a barrel, up seven cents (0.11%), while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) rose 41 cents (0.68%) to US$60.98. Prices spiked early after media reports suggested US air strikes on Venezuela could begin within hours, but gains faded when President Donald Trump denied the reports on social media. Adding to market uncertainty, sources told Reuters that Saudi Arabia may cut its December crude prices for Asian buyers to multi-month lows, signalling potential weakness in regional demand. Oil sentiment also softened after official data showed China’s factory activity contracted for a seventh straight month in October, underscoring persistent pressure on global demand. Despite the uptick on Oct 31, both benchmarks are on track for monthly losses with Brent down 2.6% and WTI off 2% as OPEC+ producers ramp up output and US production hits a record 13.6 million barrels per day, according to the Energy Information Administration. A Reuters poll, meanwhile, forecast Brent averaging US$67.99 a barrel in 2025, up marginally from last month’s outlook, while WTI is expected to average US$64.83. Meanwhile, OPEC+ is reportedly leaning toward a modest output increase in December, as supply from major producers, including Saudi Arabia and Russia, continues to climb. On the trade front, Trump said China had agreed to begin purchasing US energy, including oil and gas from Alaska though analysts remain sceptical about how quickly Chinese demand will rebound. title: Wall Street Slips As Tech Giants Disappoint, Trade Talks End With Limited Progress
body: Wall Street closed lower on Thursday as investors reacted to mixed Big Tech earnings and the conclusion of a high-profile meeting between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping. The S&P 500 fell 0.99% to 6,822.34, while the Nasdaq Composite slid 1.57% to 23,581.14. The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 109.88 points, or 0.23%, to 47,522.12. The sell-off in tech counters weighed heavily on sentiment, with Meta, Microsoft, and Nvidia among the major laggards. Despite Alphabet gaining 2.5% after posting strong results, Meta plunged more than 11% and Microsoft dropped nearly 3%, as investors grew wary of their higher spending forecasts. Portfolio manager Jed Ellerbroek of Argent Capital Management described the pullback as a “value day.” He told CNBC, “Because tech has been leading the market recently, the move from investors is probably a natural, healthy thing,” though he noted that “all signs remain that AI infrastructure spending is extremely strong.” While tech stocks retreated, bank shares such as JPMorgan and Bank of America advanced, and Eli Lilly rallied almost 4% after raising its full-year guidance. Meanwhile, trade developments between Washington and Beijing also dominated headlines. Trump announced that tariffs on Chinese fentanyl would be reduced to 10%, bringing the average levy on Chinese imports down to 47% from 57%. As part of the agreement, China pledged to curb fentanyl exports to the US and to resume purchases of American soybeans and other agricultural goods. Beijing also postponed its latest restriction on rare earth exports by one year. “Rare earth issue has been settled,” Trump said. However, several key disputes remain unresolved, including export controls on Nvidia chips and the forced divestiture of TikTok. China’s Ministry of Commerce said it was willing to work with the US to “resolve issues related to TikTok” but offered no further details. Ellerbroek cautioned that volatility tied to Trump’s trade policies will persist. “This is not at all over. The Trump-related trade volatility is going to remain a feature of our capital markets as long as he’s president,” he said. Semiconductor stocks such as Broadcom and AMD were also under pressure, with Ellerbroek adding, “Semiconductors are the ball that’s being batted around between the US and China. If you want that growth and data centre exposure, you have to subject yourself to political volatility.” Thursday’s declines followed a mixed session the day before, when the Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq all touched fresh intraday highs. However, both the Dow and S&P ended Wednesday in negative territory after Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell signalled that another rate cut in December was unlikely. title: Stock Today: BAT Malaysia Sinks 15% After Steep Profit Drop And Regulatory Pressures
body: Shares of British American Tobacco (Malaysia) Bhd (BAT Malaysia) tumbled sharply, falling 15.25% to RM4.78 as of 11.47 am, following the release of its weak third-quarter results that showed a steep decline in profit and revenue. The counter saw active trading with 3.06 million shares changing hands, opening at RM4.70 and ranging between RM4.50 and RM4.83 during the morning session. Its last traded price marked a significant drop from the previous close of RM5.64, wiping out nearly RM250 million in market value. The sell-off came after BAT Malaysia announced that its net profit for the third quarter ended 30 September 2025 plunged to RM7 million from RM67 million a year earlier, as revenue halved to RM300 million from RM609 million. The company attributed the poor performance to new regulatory requirements, including the implementation of Pictorial Health Warnings and the Retail Display Ban, which demanded heavy investment and operational adjustments. BAT Malaysia said the measures led to a 2.5% decline in the legal combustible industry volume, while its own shipment volume dropped 21%, partly due to its transition out of the Vuse vape segment. Despite the downturn, cumulative revenue for the year-to-date stood at RM1.25 billion, supported by ongoing cost optimisation efforts that reduced operating expenses by 12.3% from the previous quarter. The group noted that its premium brand, Dunhill, continued to strengthen market presence, gaining 0.2 percentage points in market share and maintaining leadership in the legal tobacco segment. In line with its earnings announcement, BAT Malaysia’s Board declared a third interim dividend of 5 sen per share, amounting to RM14.3 million, payable on 5 December 2025. At current levels, BAT Malaysia’s share price is hovering near its lowest point in two years, reflecting investor concerns over tightening regulations, declining volumes, and the group’s limited exposure to the growing vape market. title: Ringgit Holds Steady As Markets Weigh Fed’s Hawkish Cut
body: The ringgit began trading on a steady note against the US dollar on Friday morning, as investors remained cautious following the US Federal Reserve’s surprisingly hawkish rate cut. At 8 am, the local currency stood at 4.1935/2050 per US dollar, little changed from Thursday’s close of 4.1935/1985. According to Bank Muamalat Malaysia chief economist Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid, market sentiment stayed subdued while traders evaluated the Fed’s next move ahead of its December policy meeting, especially as the US government shutdown limits fresh economic data. He noted that the ringgit weakened 0.20% against the greenback to close at 4.1960 on Thursday, briefly breaching the 4.20 level during intraday trading. “The ringgit is expected to maintain a cautious tone, with the dollar-ringgit likely to trade within the 4.19 to 4.20 range,” he said. Mohd Afzanizam added that there were signs of easing tensions between the United States and China after a meeting between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in South Korea. “The discussion resulted in trade concessions, including a reduction in average tariff rates for Chinese goods from 57% to 47%, and China’s agreement to resume purchases of US soybeans,” he said. At the same time, the ringgit traded mixed against a basket of major currencies. It strengthened against the yen to 2.7246/7323 from 2.7266/7300, and also rose versus the pound to 5.5182/5334 from 5.5304/5370, though it eased slightly against the euro to 4.8527/8660 from 4.8716/8774. title: Gold Prices In Malaysia Surge 0.4%, Outpacing Global Gains As Ringgit Weakens
body: Gold prices in Malaysia continued to climb on Friday, with the metal trading at RM542.10 per gram, up RM1.94 or 0.36% from the previous session, as the weaker ringgit lent further support to local bullion prices. According to data from GoldPrice.org, gold in Malaysia reached RM542,100 per kilogram, while the price per ounce stood at RM16,861.21. Over the past month, gold prices in the local market have risen 3.9%, while on a yearly basis, the metal has surged 40%, reflecting persistent investor demand for safe-haven assets amid global economic uncertainties. In comparison, gold priced in US dollars has gained 52.5% year-to-date, outperforming most major currencies, including the Australian dollar (+43.9%), Canadian dollar (+48.2%), and British pound (+45.1%). The yen saw the steepest annual rise at +57.9%, reflecting Japan’s currency weakness and investors’ flight to safety. Silver also posted notable gains, rising 1.03% to RM2.12 per gram, with a 43.7% increase over the past year, tracking gold’s upward momentum. title: Bitcoin Slides Below US$109,000 As Fed Caution Weighs On Crypto Rally
body: Bitcoin and Ethereum fell sharply on Oct 30 as renewed caution from the US Federal Reserve (Fed) cooled risk appetite and triggered heavy selloffs across digital assets. At the time of writing, Bitcoin slipped 1.4% to around US$109,000, while Ethereum dropped 2.7% to US$3,830, retreating from the key US$4,000 mark. The pullback followed Fed Chair Jerome Powell’s warning that further rate cuts were “not guaranteed”, erasing optimism after the recent 25-basis-point cut. The global crypto market cap fell below US$4 trillion, while US$1.1 billion in leveraged positions were liquidated in 24 hours as traders unwound bets on a continued rally. Analysts say Bitcoin is now consolidating between US$110,000 and US$118,000, with downside risk if it breaks below US$105,000. Ethereum faces similar pressure near the US$3,800-US$4,000 range. For investors, the latest dip underscores crypto’s growing sensitivity to global monetary policy. A dovish Fed could reignite the rally; further caution could deepen the pullback. Moving forward, Bitcoin’s medium-term trend remains constructive if it can hold above US$105,000, with potential to retest US$120,000 should liquidity conditions improve. Ethereum’s path, meanwhile, will depend on regaining its strength above US$4,000, as investors watch developments in staking demand and network upgrades. Both assets are expected to stay range-bound in the near term as traders await clearer signals from the Fed and global macro data. title: Yen Slides As BOJ Holds Rates, Two Members Dissent
body: The yen weakened after the Bank of Japan (BOJ) kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged, with two policy board members opposing the decision. Japan’s currency slipped as much as 0.2% against the dollar to 152.96, marking a further decline in what has been a tough month for the yen. The move was widely anticipated, with about 90% of economists surveyed by Bloomberg expecting no change in policy. Still, the yen has lost more than 3% against the greenback this month, performing the worst among G-10 currencies. Markets have been reacting to Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s inclination toward easier monetary policy and fiscal expansion, a stance that could complicate the BOJ’s path forward. Despite the current weakness, some analysts believe a rate hike could still be on the horizon. Domestic inflation remains elevated, while a key price indicator has accelerated on the back of higher energy costs. Growth Strategy Minister Minoru Kiuchi said the government is closely watching the weak yen’s effect on the economy. Earlier this month, BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda reiterated that the central bank would continue normalising policy once confidence in its economic outlook strengthens. Japanese bonds, meanwhile, found mild support amid speculation that Takaichi’s fiscal policies may not be as aggressive as initially expected. Known for her past advocacy of strong monetary and fiscal stimulus, Takaichi has recently softened her approach, promising to pursue “expansionary but responsible” fiscal management. However, any major spending initiative could still raise concerns about increased bond issuance and a steeper yield curve. Investors are now awaiting Ueda’s press conference later today for guidance on the BOJ’s next move, as sustained inflation and continued yen weakness heighten the pressure for policy action. body: Tasco Bhd was last done at RM0.505 as of 3.28 pm, with 522,300 shares traded. title: Stock Today: IJM Slides 1.14% Despite Bullish Outlook On DC Wins
body: IJM Corporation Bhd’s shares edged lower midday trade, falling 1.14% or 3 sen to RM2.61 as at 12.01 pm, with 28.88 million shares changing hands. The counter opened at RM2.65 and traded between RM2.61 and RM2.67 during the session. The construction group’s share price retreat came despite strong buy calls from several research houses, which continue to highlight IJM’s growing exposure to high-value data centre projects and robust orderbook momentum. RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research), MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB Research) and Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) all maintained their BUY recommendations, with target prices ranging between RM3.50 and RM3.62—signalling an upside potential of more than 30% from current levels. RHB Research said IJM’s latest RM873.9 million mechanical and electrical (M&E) contract for a hyperscale data centre at Elmina Business Park adds to the RM1.26 billion core-and-shell package secured earlier from Sime Darby Property Bhd, bringing total data centre (DC) project value to RM2.1 billion. The research house noted that IJM has clinched RM5.1 billion worth of DC jobs this year, boosting its domestic orderbook to RM8.2 billion—nearly half derived from the digital infrastructure segment. MBSB Research said IJM’s orderbook currently stands at RM9.33 billion and could grow to RM15.2 billion when including overseas ventures in the United Kingdom and Singapore. It added that the company’s prudent balance sheet with a 0.26× net gearing and strong contract replenishment momentum underscore its resilience. Meanwhile, HLIB said IJM’s latest win lifted its year-to-date contract value to RM5 billion, giving it a 3.7× cover on FY25 revenue. It expects earnings acceleration into FY27, driven by data centre and infrastructure projects, with margins anticipated at the upper end of its 6–9% range. title: Powell’s Words Keep Bursa Watchful Despite Rate Cut Lift
body: Bursa Malaysia traded slightly higher at midday, supported by cautious optimism following the US Federal Reserve’s decision to cut interest rates by 25 basis points for the second consecutive meeting. At 12.30 pm, the FBM KLCI rose 2.34 points or 0.15% to 1,613.88, moving between 1,611.83 and 1,615.18 throughout the morning session. Gains in selected blue-chip stocks lent support to the benchmark index, while broader market sentiment remained mixed. The FBM 70 slipped 0.52% to 17,072.85, the FBM Emas eased 0.05% to 12,047.39, and the FBM Shariah Index edged down 0.17% to 12,118.43. Borneo Oil remained the most actively traded counter with 653.8 million shares changing hands at 0.005 sen, followed by PTRANS, which lost 2 sen to 36.5 sen, and TWL, flat at 2.5 sen. Among gainers, Nestle rose RM1.90 to RM111.10, LPC Group surged 40 sen to 50 sen, and United Plantations gained 36 sen to RM24.64. Meanwhile, Malaysian Pacific Industries (MPI) fell 84 sen to RM30.28, leading the losers list. The positive tone came after the Federal Reserve reduced its benchmark rate to a range of 3.75%-4.00%, marking the second straight cut after September. The decision was backed by a 10-2 vote, with dissenting voices split between calls for a deeper reduction and no change at all. Fed Chair Jerome Powell said policymakers were divided on whether to cut again in December. “A further reduction in the policy rate at the December meeting is not a foregone conclusion. Far from it, policy is not on a preset course,” he said, citing incomplete economic data due to the ongoing US government shutdown. Powell noted that the economy continued to expand moderately, though “consumers are bifurcated, stressed at the low end of the income distribution but spending robustly at the top.” He also said inflation was expected to rise temporarily due to import tariffs before easing toward the 2% target. title: Alphabet Soars 6% As Q3 Revenue Hits US$102.4 Billion, Driven By AI Cloud Surge
body: Alphabet Inc’s shares jumped more than 6% in after-hours trading after the Google parent reported stronger-than-expected third-quarter results, with both earnings and revenue beating Wall Street’s forecasts amid booming demand for artificial intelligence (AI) cloud services. For the quarter ended September 30, Alphabet recorded revenue of US$102.4 billion, surpassing the US$99.85 billion projected by analysts and marking a sharp rise from US$88.3 billion a year earlier. The company’s adjusted earnings per share came in at US$2.87, ahead of expectations of US$2.27 and higher than last year’s US$2.12. A major contributor was Google Cloud, which posted a 34% revenue surge to US$15.2 billion, exceeding Bloomberg’s US$14.8 billion forecast. The segment’s backlog, representing future revenue from customer contracts, climbed to US$155 billion. Chief executive officer Sundar Pichai said the surge was fuelled by enterprise adoption of AI tools. “We have signed more deals over US$1 billion through Q3 this year than we did in the previous two years combined,” he told investors during the earnings call. The results reinforce Alphabet’s growing position as one of the biggest beneficiaries of the AI boom. Its Gemini AI models have gained traction, and several industry players have inked multi-billion-dollar partnerships with Google Cloud. Among them, Meta reportedly signed a US$10 billion deal with Google Cloud, while Anthropic announced an agreement to use up to one million of Google’s custom AI chips (TPUs), a partnership that Bank of America estimates could generate as much as US$10 billion annually for Alphabet. Chief financial officer Anat Ashkenazi said the company had raised its capital expenditure forecast to US$92 billion from the previous US$85 billion, citing heavy investment in AI infrastructure. She noted that demand for AI computing resources currently exceeds supply. Despite growing competition from OpenAI’s ChatGPT, which recently launched its Atlas Web browser, Alphabet’s core search business continues to expand. The company reported US$56.6 billion in search revenue, beating Bloomberg’s forecast of US$55 billion. Pichai described the current AI momentum as “an expansionary moment,” highlighting that AI was increasing the number of search queries and supporting overall business growth. title: Stock Today: Sunway REIT Eases As Investors Weigh Hotel Sale And Future Growth
body: Sunway Real Estate Investment Trust (Sunway REIT) traded lower at midday, slipping 1.82% to RM2.16 as of 12.22 pm, even as analysts maintained neutral outlooks following its RM60 million disposal of Sunway Hotel Seberang Jaya (SHSJ). MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB Research) maintained a NEUTRAL call on Sunway REIT with an unchanged target price of RM2.10, while CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) reiterated a HOLD recommendation with a target price of RM2.14. Both research houses viewed the disposal as part of the trust’s strategic capital recycling initiative aimed at strengthening long-term income growth. At the time of writing, Sunway REIT’s counter moved between RM2.15 and RM2.20, with 21.31 million shares traded. The stock opened at RM2.20 and recorded a low of RM2.15. CIMB Securities noted that the disposal price represents a 9.1% premium to the asset’s appraised value of RM55 million, implying a capitalisation rate of 5.3%. The transaction will yield a gross disposal gain of RM4 million, but the bank added that the earnings impact is expected to be minimal as SHSJ contributed just 0.6% to the trust’s FY2024 net property income. The sale will free up capital for Sunway REIT’s new 192-room hotel project atop Sunway Carnival Mall in Penang, a RM140 million development slated for completion by the fourth quarter of FY2027. The upcoming property is expected to offer higher average room rates and improved yield due to its prime location and direct mall connectivity. MBSB Research described the move as “slightly positive” for long-term income, noting that earnings from the new hotel are anticipated to offset the loss from SHSJ once operational. Both research houses, however, flagged limited short-term upside potential, citing dividend yields of 4.6% to 5.5% amid recent share price gains. Despite the mid-day decline, analysts expect Sunway REIT’s stable retail and healthcare-linked portfolio to provide earnings resilience, supported by its consistent focus on asset recycling and integration with its retail operations.
