title: Stock Today: LPI Rises On Solid Premium Growth
body: Shares of LPI Capital Bhd inched up 0.28% to RM14.38 at 2.59pm, following renewed investor confidence after MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB Research) reiterated its BUY call on the insurer with an unchanged target price of RM15.70. The counter saw 863,000 shares traded, with prices hovering between RM14.36 and RM14.44. The stock has traded steadily over the past six months, supported by consistent earnings momentum and robust premium growth from its fire insurance segment. For the nine months ended September 2025, LPI recorded a core net profit of RM296 million, representing 77% of MBSB’s full-year forecast. Despite being 2% lower year-on-year due to higher insurance and reinsurance costs, revenue rose 10% alongside stronger investment results. In the third quarter, net profit surged 38% quarter-on-quarter to RM115 million, lifted by higher investment income and improved insurance service results. Gross written premium (GWP) for the quarter climbed 12% to RM516 million, pushing the cumulative nine-month total to RM1.54 billion, up 8% from a year earlier. MBSB Research identified LPI’s fire insurance segment as the key driver, growing 11.4% year-on-year, outperforming expectations despite slower residential mortgage expansion. Its motor and miscellaneous segments also posted steady growth of 8.4% and 7%, respectively, both ahead of the industry average. LPI’s combined ratio rose to 75.2% for the nine months compared with 71.2% a year earlier, reflecting higher claims and operating costs amid tougher competition and unfavourable weather. However, the figure improved quarter-on-quarter to 73.1% as operating expenses eased. MBSB also pointed to the anticipated disposal of LPI’s Public Bank shares, expected to yield a special dividend once completed by June 2026, as a potential catalyst for future upside. It added that collaboration between LPI and Public Bank would likely enhance cost efficiency and operational synergies. Trading at a forward FY26F price-to-book value of 2.25 times and offering a 6.2% dividend yield, LPI’s valuation remains attractive relative to its 10-year mean of 2.79 times. MBSB expects earnings growth of 3% in FY25, followed by 7% in both FY26 and FY27, underpinned by steady GWP expansion and resilient investment income. At current levels, the research firm said the stock continues to offer compelling value, supported by strong fundamentals and long-term growth prospects. body: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar on Wednesday, buoyed by improved investor sentiment following the successful conclusion of the 47th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits in Kuala Lumpur, Bernama reported. At 8am, the ringgit rose to 4.1870/2065 per US dollar from Tuesday’s close of 4.1935/1985. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the summit had reinforced confidence in regional stability and economic integration, which helped lift the local note. “That, to some degree, helped reduce the market risk premium and contributed to the ringgit’s appreciation,” he said to Bernama. The US dollar index slipped 0.12% to 98.667 points ahead of the US Federal Reserve’s expected 25-basis-point rate cut at the Federal Open Market Committee meeting later tonight. Optimism over a potential trade deal between the US and China also bolstered risk appetite. “The US Treasury bond yields for the three-month and five-year notes fell to 3.73% and 3.63%, respectively, from 3.81% and 3.71% at the previous auction,” Dr Afzanizam noted, adding that the ringgit is likely to remain firm with the dollar-ringgit pair trading between RM4.19 and RM4.20 today. At the opening, the ringgit traded higher against most major and regional currencies. It strengthened against the British pound to 5.5591/5850 from 5.5845/5911, improved versus the euro to 4.8804/9031 from 4.8884/8942, and edged up against the Japanese yen to 2.7591/7722 from 2.7605/7640. Among ASEAN currencies, the ringgit appreciated against the Singapore dollar to 3.2372/2525 from 3.2460/2502, firmed against the Indonesian rupiah to 252.0/253.3 from 252.4/252.9, and inched higher against the Philippine peso at 7.08/7.12 from 7.09/7.10. However, it slightly eased against the Thai baht to 12.9420/13.0111 from 12.9214/9424 previously. Related At 8am, the ringgit rose to 4.1870/2065 per US dollar from Tuesday’s close of 4.1935/1985. title: Nvidia Surge Pushes Wall Street To Record Highs As Earnings Optimism Builds
body: Wall Street’s main indexes closed at fresh record highs on Tuesday, lifted by gains in Nvidia and Microsoft as investors grew more upbeat ahead of a packed week of corporate earnings from major technology firms, Reuters reported. The S&P 500 gained 0.23% to 6,890.89, the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.34% to 47,706.37, and the Nasdaq Composite advanced 0.8% to 23,827.49. Nvidia led the rally after its shares jumped 5%, adding more than US$230 billion in market value. The company’s CEO Jensen Huang said it will build seven artificial intelligence (AI) supercomputers for the US Department of Energy, adding that Nvidia now holds US$500 billion worth of AI chip bookings. The surge placed Nvidia on the verge of becoming the world’s first US$5 trillion company. Microsoft’s stock also gained 2% after announcing a deal allowing OpenAI to restructure into a public benefit corporation, with Microsoft holding a 27% stake. The move reinforced investor confidence in the tech giant’s AI strategy. “Momentum and earnings are pushing the market higher,” said Peter Cardillo, chief market economist at Spartan Capital Securities in New York. “Earnings have been good. Of course, we’re waiting for the big tech stocks.” Investors are closely watching earnings from Apple, Alphabet, Amazon and Meta Platforms this week for clues on AI-related spending. Apple shares rose 0.1% after briefly crossing the US$4 trillion market valuation mark. Meanwhile, United Parcel Service (UPS) shares jumped 8% after posting better-than-expected results, signalling progress in its major cost-cutting overhaul that includes closing hundreds of facilities and offering buyouts to drivers to achieve US$3.5 billion in savings next year. On the macro front, optimism was tempered by trade and policy developments. The Wall Street Journal reported that US President Donald Trump and China’s leader Xi Jinping are discussing a framework to lower US tariffs in exchange for Beijing curbing exports of fentanyl precursor chemicals. Market participants are also awaiting Wednesday’s Federal Reserve meeting, where policymakers are widely expected to deliver a 25-basis-point rate cut. Investors will be looking for clues on the Fed’s outlook amid a month-long US government shutdown that has delayed key economic data releases. According to LSEG data cited by Reuters, earnings from 180 S&P 500 companies so far show third-quarter profits up 10.5% year-on-year, exceeding earlier estimates. Market breadth was negative despite the record closes, with declining issues outnumbering advancers by 1.35-to-1 on the NYSE and 1.53-to-1 on the Nasdaq. Trading volume totalled 20.5 billion shares, roughly in line with the 20-day average. title: Investors Await Windfall From LPI Capital
body: MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB Research) has maintained its BUY call on LPI Capital Bhd, with an unchanged target price of RM15.70, citing stronger-than-expected gross written premium (GWP) growth led by its high-performing fire insurance segment. The research house noted that despite a higher combined ratio and increased competition in the general insurance space, LPI’s earnings momentum remained impressive and within expectations. For the nine months ended September 2025, LPI posted a core net profit of RM296 million, which was 77% of MBSB’s full-year forecast, indicating that the insurer remains on track to meet its annual projections. However, earnings were marginally lower by 2% year-on-year due to higher insurance and reinsurance expenses that offset a 10% rise in insurance revenue and stronger investment results. No dividend was declared for the quarter. In the third quarter alone, LPI’s core net profit jumped 38% quarter-on-quarter to RM115 million, supported by higher investment income and stronger insurance service results. The quarter also saw remarkable GWP growth of 12% to RM516 million, pushing cumulative nine-month GWP to RM1.54 billion, up 8% year-on-year. MBSB highlighted the fire segment as the standout performer with 11.4% year-on-year growth, despite expectations of slower residential mortgage loan expansion. The motor and miscellaneous segments also posted solid growth of 8.4% and 7%, respectively, surpassing the industry average. The research house, however, noted that LPI’s combined ratio for the nine-month period rose to 75.2% from 71.2% a year earlier, reflecting a higher claims ratio and expense ratio amid adverse weather conditions and competitive pricing pressures. On a quarterly basis, the combined ratio improved slightly to 73.1% from 75.2% in the previous quarter due to lower operating expenses. MBSB also said that all eyes are now on the anticipated disposal of Public Bank shares by LPI, which is expected to result in a sizeable special dividend, although the transaction window has been extended to June 2026. The research firm added that ongoing collaboration between LPI and Public Bank could further enhance cost efficiency and operational synergies over time. With the company trading at a forward FY26F price-to-book value of 2.25 times and offering a healthy 6.2% dividend yield, MBSB said the current valuation remains attractive relative to its 10-year mean of 2.79 times. The research house maintained its forecasts, projecting steady earnings growth of 3% in FY25, 7% in FY26, and 7% in FY27. While MBSB remains cautious about potential downside risks, such as weaker premium growth, adverse weather patterns, and intensified competition, it reaffirmed its bullish stance on LPI’s fundamentals, backed by resilient GWP expansion and robust investment income. As of 10.26 am, LPI Capital’s stock price increased by 0.14% to RM14.36. title: Gold Shines Brighter In Malaysia As Prices Surge 36% Year-on-Year
body: Gold prices in Malaysia continued their upward momentum with the precious metal trading at RM538.39 per gram, rising RM2.98 or 0.56% from the previous session, according to data from GoldPrice.org as at 3.50am New York time. On a per kilogram basis, gold stood at RM538,390, reflecting a 36.39% gain over the past year and a 16.66% increase over six months. The strong performance underscores renewed investor demand for safe-haven assets amid lingering global inflationary pressures, geopolitical risks, and expectations of slower US economic growth. In comparison, silver also saw a rally, climbing 1.53% to RM3.03 per gram, translating to a 33.52% year-on-year gain. Over the past six months, silver prices in ringgit terms surged 42.54%, outperforming gold in short-term momentum though still trailing gold’s broader 2025 performance of 51.2% globally in US dollar terms. The sustained gold rally was attributed to persistent uncertainty in global markets and the anticipation that major central banks, particularly the US Federal Reserve, could maintain higher interest rates for longer than expected, thereby driving investors towards metals as a hedge against currency volatility. The ringgit’s softness against the US dollar also amplified gold’s gains in local terms. As the Central Bank of Malaysia (BNM) continues to focus on managing exchange rate volatility while maintaining independent monetary policy, investors have turned to gold as a store of value against inflation and currency depreciation. Globally, gold was trading at US$2,475 per ounce, supported by steady buying from Asian markets and central banks increasing their bullion reserves. Meanwhile, silver hovered near US$28.90 per ounce, lifted by industrial demand linked to renewable energy and semiconductor manufacturing. Over a five-year horizon, gold prices in Malaysia have more than doubled, soaring 113.36%, while silver surged 102.20%, reflecting consistent long-term investor interest in precious metals as a hedge amid global financial volatility. Market watchers expect local gold prices to remain buoyant through the year-end, with analysts forecasting continued upward pressure if geopolitical tensions persist and the US dollar remains elevated. title: Cautious Trading Drags Bursa Midday As Investors Eye Fed Decision
body: Bursa Malaysia drifted lower at midday as investors adopted a cautious stance ahead of the US Federal Reserve’s policy announcement, while regional markets traded mixed following overnight rallies on Wall Street. At 12.35 pm, the FBM KLCI slipped 4.82 points or 0.30% to 1,608.74, retreating from an early high of 1,617.02 as mild profit-taking emerged in heavyweights such as Petronas Dagangan and Kuala Lumpur Kepong. Broader market sentiment was also subdued, with the FBM70 down 0.32% to 17,129.31 and the FBMEMAS easing 0.28% to 12,032.08. Losers outpaced gainers as investors stayed on the sidelines amid expectations of a quarter-point rate cut in the United States later tonight, which could set the tone for global equity flows. Among the top decliners, Petronas Dagangan fell 32 sen to RM22.14, Bintulu Port eased 26 sen to RM5.00, and Kuala Lumpur Kepong dropped 22 sen to RM20.64. Petronas Gas was also weaker, slipping 10 sen to RM18.50. In contrast, Nestle rose RM2.60 to RM109.70 and Malayan Cement gained 28 sen to RM6.70, offering some cushion to the benchmark. Tech-related counters also showed selective buying, with DUFU up 15 sen to RM1.88 and Pentamaster advancing 12 sen to RM4.43. Turnover stood at 2.97 billion shares valued at RM1.76 billion. Borneo Oil remained the most actively traded stock, unchanged at 0.5 sen with over 1.5 billion shares changing hands. Other actives included Perak Transit, which fell 2 sen to 37.5 sen, and Zetrix, down 2 sen to 81.5 sen. Regionally, most Asian bourses tracked Wall Street’s momentum, though gains were uneven. Japan’s Nikkei jumped over 2%, buoyed by tech optimism, while South Korea’s KOSPI added 1.3% to fresh highs. Taipei and Shanghai posted modest gains, but Sydney’s ASX edged lower, and Hong Kong remained closed for a public holiday. Barring surprises from the Fed, market watchers expect the KLCI to remain rangebound between 1,600 and 1,620 ahead of month-end positioning. title: Bitcoin, Ethereum Slip Ahead Of Fed Decision
body: The cryptocurrency market faced a mild pullback on Oct 28 as Bitcoin and Ethereum retreated ahead of the US Federal Reserve’s (Fed) interest rate decision, with traders bracing for potential volatility. Bitcoin hovered around US$112,500, down 1.7%, after trading between US$112,130 and US$116,048 during the session. Ethereum slipped 3.7% to US$3,983, with intraday lows near US$3,947. The decline came as investors grew cautious before the Fed’s closely watched meeting, where policymakers are expected to cut interest rates by 25 basis points, a move that could set the tone for risk assets, including cryptocurrencies. Despite optimism for easier financial conditions, the market saw over US$217 million worth of leveraged crypto positions liquidated within 24 hours, reflecting heightened uncertainty and thinning liquidity. Analysts said while lower rates typically favour digital assets, the recent rally in Bitcoin, which has surged more than 40% this year, has left it vulnerable to profit-taking and sharper swings if the Fed delivers a less dovish message. However, open interest in Bitcoin futures continues to rise, signalling growing institutional participation but also amplifying the risk of sharp reversals. Meanwhile, Ethereum remains range-bound, with traders watching whether the token can break out above the US$4,200 level to regain momentum. Market watchers say the next 24 hours could prove pivotal for crypto sentiment as the Fed’s guidance on future rate cuts will likely determine whether the rally in digital assets continues or stalls. Moving forward, with liquidity tight and leverage high, both Bitcoin and Ethereum are entering a make-or-break phase. Traders are advised to stay alert as volatility is likely to remain elevated in the days ahead. title: Asian Markets Rally On AI Frenzy And Hopes Of US Rate Cuts
body: Asian stock markets surged on Wednesday morning, mirroring record gains on Wall Street as optimism over artificial intelligence (AI) and expectations of imminent interest rate cuts in the United States fuelled a fresh wave of investor enthusiasm. The region’s rally came ahead of the US Federal Reserve’s policy announcement later in the day, with analysts widely anticipating a quarter-point reduction in lending rates to sustain economic momentum. Adding to the buoyant mood were signs of progress in US-China relations, with US President Donald Trump expected to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping in South Korea amid hopes of averting a renewed trade war. Trump, who arrived in South Korea after visits to Malaysia and Japan, said he was “confident in reaching an agreement” with Xi, calling the meeting a “great outcome for the world.” The upbeat sentiment spilt over from Wall Street, where AI giant Nvidia soared 5% overnight, helping push key US indices to fresh record highs. “It’s the tech show, and this is where capital remains firmly centred,” said Chris Weston of Pepperstone, noting that investors appeared unfazed by the approaching Fed meeting. Japan’s benchmark index climbed more than 2%, while Seoul jumped over 1%, both hitting new records. Taipei and Shanghai posted moderate gains, though Sydney’s main index edged lower. Hong Kong markets were closed for a public holiday. Investors are now eyeing earnings reports from major US tech players including Microsoft and Meta, which are expected to provide further insight into the AI-fuelled rally that has defined markets this year. Trump and Xi are scheduled to meet on Thursday on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Gyeongju, a meeting seen as critical to cooling trade tensions and shaping global market sentiment. title: AI Rally And Fed Hopes Fuel Asian Market Gains
body: Asian shares rose on Wednesday, buoyed by renewed optimism in artificial intelligence (AI) and expectations that the US Federal Reserve will soon announce a rate cut. Japan and South Korea led the region’s early advances, while Hong Kong remained closed for a public holiday. The upbeat tone followed Wall Street’s overnight gains, where the S&P 500 closed slightly higher and the so-called “Magnificent Seven” tech giants jumped 1.3%. Nvidia Corp. surged nearly 5% after Chief Executive Jensen Huang announced several new AI partnerships during his keynote at the Nvidia AI Summit in Washington, dismissing fears of an AI bubble. Tech optimism continued to lift sentiment, with Nvidia supplier SK Hynix climbing up to 4% on record profits. “We expect another strong round of megacap tech earnings reports, given the relentless demand for AI technology and infrastructure,” said Clark Bellin of Bellwether Wealth. “While profitability in AI remains an unknown, investors for now are willing to overlook this as the AI arms race heats up.” Market watchers are now eyeing the Federal Reserve’s meeting outcome, with expectations running high for a 25-basis-point rate cut. Traders are also betting that the Fed may end its quantitative tightening programme soon. “The markets have a massive wall of event risk to scale this week,” said Kyle Rodda, senior analyst at Capital.com. The US dollar index slipped for a third straight day, while the yen strengthened after US Treasury Secretary acknowledged Japan’s flexibility in allowing the Bank of Japan policy space. Meanwhile, gold prices edged higher by 0.2% to US$3,961.46 per ounce, while oil steadied after a three-day decline amid signs of oversupply. Adding to the global backdrop, President Donald Trump is set to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday, with reports suggesting the US may roll back some tariffs if Beijing curbs fentanyl-related exports. The move has pushed copper prices near record highs. Corporate news also added colour to the session. OpenAI restructured its ownership, granting Microsoft Corp. a 27% stake. Apple Inc. is reportedly preparing significant updates to its MacBook Air and iPad lineup, while Visa Inc. beat earnings forecasts on strong global spending. Ping An Insurance posted an 11.5% rise in profit, and Bank of China reported a 5% increase for the third quarter. Across asset classes, the Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index and major currencies traded mostly flat. Bitcoin hovered near US$112,825, while ether inched up 0.2%. The yield on 10-year Treasuries was unchanged at 3.98%, while Japan’s 10-year yield ticked up one basis point to 1.65%. The upbeat tone from the AI sector and policy optimism ahead of the Fed decision are keeping Asian equities on firmer ground, setting a hopeful tone for the week’s trading sessions. title: Wall Street Hits Fresh Record Highs On US-China Trade Hopes And AI Momentum
body: Wall Street’s main indices closed at record highs for the second consecutive session on Monday, lifted by optimism over a potential US-China trade breakthrough and strong gains in technology shares ahead of major earnings reports. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 337.47 points, or 0.71%, to 47,544.59. The S&P 500 climbed 83.47 points, or 1.23%, to 6,875.16, its first-ever close above 6,800, while the Nasdaq Composite advanced 432.59 points, or 1.86%, to 23,637.46. Investors are closely watching a meeting between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping scheduled for Thursday, where both leaders are expected to discuss a framework to ease tariffs and address China’s rare-earth export restrictions. Hopes for progress grew after US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said over the weekend that discussions in Malaysia had included agreements on China purchasing US soybeans and rare-earth exports. “The market expects to hear confirmation that all this AI capital expenditure is coming through and that the revenues and profits from AI are being realised,” said Scott Wren, senior global market strategist at Wells Fargo Investment Institute. Technology shares led the rally, with the sector rising 2% to a new record. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index jumped 2.7% as Qualcomm surged 11% after unveiling two new AI chips for data centres, while Nvidia gained 2.8% to provide the biggest lift to the S&P 500. Communication services rose 2.3%, driven by a 3.6% rise in Alphabet shares, while consumer discretionary stocks added 1.5%, led by Tesla’s 4.3% increase on optimism over US-China ties. However, Synovus vice president of investments Christopher Brown warned that Tesla’s rally could be short-lived, noting the stock “remains expensive even with the best negotiated US-China trade deal.” Among the S&P 500’s 11 sectors, consumer staples fell 0.27% and materials slipped 0.25%. US-listed rare-earth miners tumbled as easing trade fears reduced supply concerns. Critical Metals plunged 13.7%, NioCorp Developments fell 11.5%, and Ramaco Resources lost 2.6%. Chinese tech companies traded in the US also advanced, with Alibaba, JD.com, and PDD Holdings up between 2.7% and 3%, while Baidu jumped 4.8%. Cooler inflation data last week cemented expectations for a 25-basis-point rate cut by the Federal Reserve on Wednesday. Investors are also awaiting remarks from Fed Chair Jerome Powell for signals of another possible cut in December, as the ongoing government shutdown delays key economic data releases. In corporate news, Keurig Dr Pepper rose 7.6% after raising its annual sales forecast and securing about US$7 billion to fund its purchase of Dutch coffee maker JDE Peet’s. Lululemon gained 1.8% after announcing a partnership with the National Football League, while Janus Henderson jumped 11.3% following confirmation of an acquisition proposal from Trian and General Catalyst. Argentine stocks listed in the US soared following President Javier Milei’s election win. YPF climbed 23.8%, Banco Macro added 37.6%, and Grupo Financiero Galicia jumped 38.7%. Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.74-to-1 ratio on the NYSE, with 659 new highs and 69 new lows. On the Nasdaq, advancers topped decliners 1.21-to-1, with 132 new highs and 57 new lows. Total volume on US exchanges was 19.76 billion shares, compared with the 20-session average of 20.85 billion. title: Stock Today: IJM Rises 2.34% Propelled By RM1.26 Billion Contract
body: IJM Corporation Bhd shares were trading higher in mid-session, with the counter last done at RM2.62, up 6 sen or 2.34% from yesterday’s close. The stock saw a total volume of 3.19 million units by 2.56 pm, with intraday movement ranging between RM2.56 and RM2.63. The boost comes after the company secured a RM1.26 billion hyperscale data centre contract at Elmina Business Park, Selangor, its first such project in the Klang Valley. The contract, awarded by a subsidiary of Sime Darby Property Bhd, covers core-and-shell construction on a 77-acre site, scheduled to begin in the fourth quarter of 2025 and expected to complete by mid-2027. RHB Research highlighted that the new award raises IJM’s total data centre projects to five, with cumulative wins worth about RM3.5 billion. The firm’s domestic order book now stands at roughly RM7.4 billion, with data centre contracts accounting for nearly 38% of that value. MBSB Research noted that the Elmina project aligns with IJM’s FY26 replenishment goals, supported by a strong order pipeline, including the Pulai DC project and the NPE highway extension. The research house expects earnings momentum to strengthen over FY26–FY27, driven by high-margin industrial and data centre developments, while the company’s total order book, including international projects, exceeds RM14.2 billion. HLIB described the Elmina win as a “significant step into the big leagues” of hyperscale data centre construction, projecting the order book could rise to RM8.5 billion with potential mechanical and electrical fit-out packages. Analysts agreed that IJM’s expanding data centre portfolio and disciplined balance sheet underpin continued earnings growth, despite broader construction sector competition. title: Stock Today: IGB Commercial REIT Dips Slightly Amid Steady Fundamentals
body: IGB Commercial Real Estate Investment Trust (IGBCR) was last traded at RM0.620, down 0.8% from its previous close, with 210,100 units changing hands as of 4 pm. The REIT opened at RM0.625, hitting an intraday low of RM0.620 and a high of RM0.625, while its last average closing price (LACP) stood at RM0.625. RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) and Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) have both maintained their BUY calls on IGBCR, citing resilient performance and robust occupancy across its key assets, particularly within the Mid Valley City development. RHB Research set a target price of RM0.72, implying an 18.6% upside, while HLIB maintained its target at RM0.64, representing a 12% expected total return. According to RHB Research, IGBCR’s third-quarter 2025 results were in line with expectations, supported by steady topline growth and stable net property income margins. Core profit for the first nine months rose 26.1% year-on-year to RM71.5 million, meeting 78% of full-year estimates. The research house noted that portfolio occupancy improved to 92% from 87% a year earlier, largely driven by tenant intake at Kuala Lumpur City assets. The REIT declared a 3Q25 distribution per unit of 1 sen, bringing total DPU for 9M25 to 3.1 sen, up from 2.9 sen in the previous year. RHB highlighted that gearing remained healthy at 26.3%, while key assets such as Southpoint Tower maintained full tenancy and GTower’s occupancy climbed to 88%. HLIB Research noted that revenue and net property income remained stable quarter-on-quarter, with financing costs down 11.3% year-to-date. The research house pointed out that IGBCR’s well-located properties, especially within the integrated Mid Valley ecosystem, are well-positioned to capture demand from high-value and technology-driven sectors. Both analysts expect continued growth ahead as Malaysia shifts toward high-tech and service-oriented industries, with RHB reporting that 76% of expiring leases have been renewed in 3Q25 and management targeting further tenant diversification through multinational corporations. Flexible workspace operators such as INFINITY8 and WORQ have also expanded within IGBCR properties, reflecting rising demand for premium adaptable office spaces. RHB Research maintained its DDM-derived target price of RM0.72, implying a FY26 yield of 6.6%, while HLIB reiterated its target of RM0.64 based on a 7% yield. Both firms expect stable performance in the coming quarters, supported by prime locations, high occupancy, and disciplined cost management. title: Stock Today: CIMB Eases 0.8% As Investors Await November Earnings
body: CIMB Group Holdings Bhd’s share price slipped 0.81% to RM7.39 as at 12.17 pm today, down from its last close of RM7.45, with 48.4 million shares traded. The counter opened at RM7.45 and touched an intraday low of RM7.39. Despite the mild decline, RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research), MBSB Investment Bank (MBSB Research) and Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB) have reaffirmed their BUY calls on CIMB, with target prices of RM8.40, RM8.22 and RM8.80 respectively. RHB Research expects CIMB’s third-quarter results to rebound on the back of stronger trading and foreign exchange income, lower tax rates and potential non-loan expected credit loss writebacks. The research house noted that while year-on-year growth may be capped by a high base effect and narrower net interest margins (NIM), operational momentum remains positive. RHB added that CIMB’s loan pipeline has strengthened, particularly in consumer segments in Malaysia and Singapore, though drawdowns have been slower than anticipated. The pace is expected to pick up in late 2025 or early 2026. MBSB Research also sees a strong quarter ahead, projecting higher non-interest income (NOII) driven by trading and forex gains. The firm expects continued NIM compression in Singapore but said Malaysia’s margin outlook has stabilised after deposit campaign rate adjustments earlier this year. Meanwhile, HLIB maintained that CIMB remains one of its top value picks among large-cap banks, supported by stable asset quality and robust capital ratios. The bank’s next quarterly results, due on November 28, are expected to show firmer NOII and improving loan growth despite subdued margins. All three research houses noted that CIMB’s steady regional operations, healthy liquidity in Indonesia and consistent dividend record position the group well heading into year-end. HLIB’s RM8.80 target price implies nearly 25% total return, while RHB and MBSB project potential gains of 14% and 17% respectively. title: Ringgit Strengthens On US-Malaysia Trade Deals And Softer US Dollar
body: The ringgit continued its upward momentum against the US dollar on Tuesday, lifted by renewed investor appetite following several US-Malaysia trade agreements that bolstered confidence in the local currency. At 8am, the ringgit advanced to 4.2040/2140 per US dollar from 4.2085/2135 at Monday’s close. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the recent trade deals are expected to lend further support to the ringgit as Malaysia maintains strong diplomatic and economic ties with its trading partners. “The nation’s foreign and trade policies are consistently geared towards promoting greater global integration, especially in areas related to the supply chain,” he said. Meanwhile, the US dollar index weakened by 0.17% to 98.783 points as optimism grew over a potential breakthrough in trade discussions between the United States and China, ahead of the scheduled meeting between the two leaders on Thursday. Market sentiment was also buoyed by expectations of a 25-basis-point interest rate cut by the US Federal Reserve on Wednesday, further weighing on the greenback. “In light of the market optimism, the ringgit could make another attempt to break the RM4.20 level today,” Mohd Afzanizam added. At the opening, the ringgit also traded higher against most major currencies. It rose against the Japanese yen to 2.7538/7606 from 2.7550/7582 on Monday, and gained against the British pound to 5.6077/6211 from 5.6158/6225. However, it slipped slightly against the euro to 4.8981/9097 from 4.8974/9032. Among ASEAN currencies, the local note strengthened against most regional peers. It edged up against the Singapore dollar to 3.2433/2513 from 3.2460/2502, appreciated vis-à-vis the Indonesian rupiah to 252.9/253.6 from 253.1/253.6, and firmed against the Philippine peso to 7.13/7.16 from 7.14/7.16. The ringgit, however, eased slightly against the Thai baht to 12.8767/9145 from 12.8633/8837 at Monday’s close. title: Malaysian Gold Prices Slip Amid US-China Trade Hopes
body: Gold prices in Malaysia eased, retreating from the record levels hit earlier this month. The pullback follows a brief cooling in demand for safe-haven bullion as global investors reacted to signs of progress in US-China trade negotiations. According to Reuters, spot gold on global markets fell 1% to US$3,941.65 per ounce, marking the lowest level since October 10, while US gold futures for December delivery dropped 1.5% to US$3,957.50 per ounce. KCM Trade Chief Market Analyst Tim Waterer noted that optimism over a potential trade deal between President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping has reduced safe-haven buying, tempering recent price gains. title: Chinese Earnings Jump But Markets Keep Eyes On Trump-Xi Talks
body: China’s corporate sector is expected to post its strongest earnings growth in years, though market sentiment remains firmly tied to geopolitics rather than fundamentals. Profits of onshore-listed firms are projected to expand by 5.8% year-on-year in the third quarter, according to China International Capital Corp., marking the fastest pace since mid-2021 and a sharp improvement from 1.6% growth in the previous quarter. The CSI 300 Index had gained for five consecutive months through September, buoyed by optimism in key sectors. However, the rally was interrupted in early October as renewed US-China trade tensions rattled investors. Signs of progress in trade discussions have since helped restore confidence, with the index climbing 1.2% on Monday after top negotiators reached consensus on several contentious issues. Despite the earnings rebound, many analysts say the market’s direction hinges more on diplomatic developments than on corporate results. Investors are now focused on a high-profile meeting between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, expected to take place in South Korea later this week. “While the modest upturn in earnings sentiment helps at the margin, we believe that macro chatter around the US-China trade tensions and retail flows related to the AI boom are more impactful drivers for China’s equity markets,” said Homin Lee, macro strategist at Lombard Odier Singapore Ltd. The profit recovery remains uneven. Much of the growth has been concentrated in sectors such as artificial intelligence and materials, which have benefited from global demand and Beijing’s measures to reduce overcapacity. AI chipmaker Cambricon Technologies Corp., often dubbed “China’s Nvidia,” saw a 14-fold surge in quarterly revenue, fuelled by robust demand for semiconductors and domestic innovation drives. Meanwhile, Zijin Mining Group Co. reported a 57% jump in net income, supported by record-high gold prices. By contrast, consumption and property-linked industries continue to struggle. Guangzhou Zhujiang Brewery Co. recorded its first decline in quarterly revenue since 2022, while developer Poly Developments and Holdings Group Co. posted a net loss. “Divergence among different industries is becoming more prominent, with sectors such as finance and technology expected to see stable or even improving earnings, while other industries such as consumption may face greater pressure,” said Shen Meng, director at Chanson & Co. Still, long-term investors appear encouraged by the improving trajectory. Data from Bloomberg show that analysts’ 12-month forward earnings estimates for CSI 300 members have risen by more than 6% since July. On Wall Street, opinion remains divided over how the Trump-Xi meeting could shape the market’s next move. Goldman Sachs and Bank of America maintain an optimistic stance, while Morgan Stanley and Nomura urge caution. “We advise a balanced approach with focus on earnings quality in the near term while awaiting trade tension clarity,” Morgan Stanley analysts including Laura Wang wrote. “Stick to quality stocks with high earnings visibility and dividend plays for now.” Bloomberg Related The CSI 300 Index had gained for five consecutive months through September, buoyed by optimism in key sectors. “Stick to quality stocks with high earnings visibility and dividend plays for now.” Bloomberg Related Despite the earnings rebound, many analysts say the market’s direction hinges more on diplomatic developments than on corporate results. “Stick to quality stocks with high earnings visibility and dividend plays for now.” Bloomberg Related “While the modest upturn in earnings sentiment helps at the margin, we believe that macro chatter around the US-China trade tensions and retail flows related to the AI boom are more impactful drivers for China’s equity markets,” said Homin Lee, macro strategist at Lombard Odier Singapore Ltd. “Stick to quality stocks with high earnings visibility and dividend plays for now.” Bloomberg Related The profit recovery remains uneven. “Stick to quality stocks with high earnings visibility and dividend plays for now.” Bloomberg Related By contrast, consumption and property-linked industries continue to struggle. “Stick to quality stocks with high earnings visibility and dividend plays for now.” Bloomberg Related Still, long-term investors appear encouraged by the improving trajectory. “Stick to quality stocks with high earnings visibility and dividend plays for now.” Bloomberg Related On Wall Street, opinion remains divided over how the Trump-Xi meeting could shape the market’s next move. “Stick to quality stocks with high earnings visibility and dividend plays for now.” Bloomberg Related Bloomberg Related

title: Ringgit Strengthens Ahead Of Fed Meeting On Interest Rate Cut Expectations
body: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar on Monday as investors turned cautious ahead of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting scheduled for Oct 28–29, with expectations building for another interest rate cut by the US Federal Reserve. At 8 am, the local note appreciated to 4.2145/2350 against the greenback from 4.2210/2255 at Friday’s close. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said September’s consumer price index (CPI) of 3% came in slightly below the 3.1% consensus estimate, suggesting that the Fed remains on course for a second rate cut. “The US central bank has shifted its focus to reviving the job market, meaning the interest rate differential between the Fed fund rate and the overnight policy rate (OPR) will narrow in the near future,” he said. He added that Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) is in no rush to adjust its OPR and is expected to maintain its current rate through the remainder of 2025. “From a policy rate perspective, this should be ringgit-positive. Therefore, we shall see the dollar-ringgit pair linger around RM4.21 to RM4.22 today,” he said. Mohd Afzanizam also noted that US President Donald Trump’s presence at the ASEAN Summit in Kuala Lumpur reflects Washington’s commitment to global trade and dialogue, which could benefit Malaysia and support the ringgit in the medium to long term. At the opening, the ringgit traded mostly higher against major currencies. It strengthened against the Japanese yen to 2.7553/7689 from 2.7592/7623 at Friday’s close and advanced against the British pound to 5.6150/6423 from 5.6232/6292. title: Ringgit Gold Slips As US Dollar Steals The Spotlight
body: Gold prices in Malaysia slipped in early trading today, tracking global declines as a stronger US dollar and renewed optimism over a potential US-China trade deal dampened demand for the safe-haven asset. According to data from GoldPrice.org at 3.10am NY time, gold prices in Malaysia dropped 1.21% to RM551,859.76 per kilogramme, or RM551.86 per gramme. On a per-ounce basis, gold stood at RM17,164.77, down RM210.59 from the previous day. The decline follows a volatile week for bullion, with the ringgit-denominated price still recording a 7.53% gain over the past 30 days and a strong 45.66% rise year-on-year. Globally, spot gold fell 0.7% to US$4,082.77 per ounce while US gold futures for December delivery slipped 1% to US$4,095.80, Reuters reported. The pullback came as the US dollar climbed to a two-week high against the yen, making gold more expensive for non-dollar holders. A Reuters report by Brijesh Patel noted that sentiment shifted after Washington and Beijing agreed on the framework of a new trade deal, reducing immediate geopolitical tensions. Capital.com analyst Kyle Rodda said the development was “a positive surprise for the markets broadly,” though it also meant “negative momentum for gold” as investors moved towards riskier assets. The world’s largest gold-backed exchange-traded fund, SPDR Gold Trust, also reported a 0.52% decline in holdings to 1,046.93 metric tonnes on Friday, reflecting easing investor demand for bullion-backed assets. Meanwhile, other precious metals were mixed. Spot silver dipped 0.3% to US$48.42 per ounce, palladium eased 0.2% to US$1,426.06, while platinum edged up 0.1% to US$1,607.24. Despite today’s dip, analysts believe gold’s uptrend may hold if central banks maintain loose monetary policies. The US Federal Reserve is widely expected to cut interest rates by 25 basis points this Wednesday, a move that could support gold prices in the medium term. In Asia, gold prices in India and China also slipped slightly in morning trade, mirroring the global trend, though both markets continue to see firm jewellery demand ahead of the festive season. While Malaysia’s gold price fell today, the long-term trend remains strong, a 122.54% increase over the last five years and a staggering 873.98% gain in two decades, underscoring gold’s enduring appeal as a hedge against inflation and market uncertainty. title: Potential Rerating For ViTrox From Tax Incentives, Sector Recovery
body: CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) has maintained its HOLD call on ViTrox Corp Bhd with an unchanged target price of RM4.60, citing a solid order pipeline driven by artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, 5G expansion and automotive applications. The research house said the company’s outlook remains positive with its R&D momentum shifting into high gear to support multiple new product rollouts. ViTrox guided for its fourth quarter FY2025 revenue between RM199 million and RM231 million, reflecting year-on-year growth of 55.2% and a quarter-on-quarter increase of 1.1% at the upper end of the range. CIMB Securities noted that total purchase orders reached a record RM269 million as of end-September 2025, while the book-to-bill ratio improved to 1.2 times, signalling solid demand visibility across its key machine vision system tray-based (MVST) and automated board inspection (ABI) segments. The research house highlighted that ViTrox’s growth is being fuelled by sustained demand from AI-related hardware buildout, coupled with a rebound in the smartphone and automotive sectors. For the first nine months of 2025, ViTrox’s revenue climbed 37% year-on-year to RM553 million, already surpassing its full-year 2024 revenue. The expansion was broad-based across markets, led by China (+35%), Malaysia (+16%), Taiwan (+13%) and the United States (+13%), which collectively contributed 77% of total revenue. CIMB Securities also expects ViTrox’s effective tax rate to normalise from 25% in FY2025 to around 15% in FY2026, supported by new tax incentives and an evolving product mix towards higher-value solutions. The company plans to introduce a next-generation AXI system under its QX Series, targeting AI servers, telecommunications and automotive applications, alongside a new vision system for heat dissipation inspection, key to the microchannel lid (MCL) cooling technology used in AI chips. ViTrox continues to invest heavily in research and development, spending RM59.4 million or 10.7% of revenue in the first nine months of 2025, above its five-year average of 9.2%. While higher R&D spending may temporarily compress margins, CIMB said it positions ViTrox to strengthen its edge in advanced vision inspection technologies and maintain competitiveness against regional peers. The investment bank believes potential re-rating catalysts for the stock include new pioneer tax incentives, favourable government policies under the National Semiconductor Strategy and a sustained recovery in the global semiconductor industry. However, it warned of downside risks such as prolonged inventory corrections, intensified competition from North Asian manufacturers and possible delays in policy implementation. CIMB’s valuation for ViTrox remains pegged at 42 times CY2027F price-to-earnings ratio, consistent with the Malaysian automated test equipment (ATE) sector’s five-year mean, reflecting steady confidence in the group’s earnings visibility and regional diversification. title: Japan’s Nikkei Tops 50,000 Mark For First Time On Stimulus Euphoria
body: Japan’s Nikkei share average climbed past the 50,000 level for the first time on Monday, continuing a run of successive records on expectations of sizeable spending from the nation’s new prime minister. Crossing the key psychological threshold is the latest milestone for the blue-chip share gauge that has been red hot since fiscal dove Sanae Takaichi began her ascent to power. As of 0040 GMT, the Nikkei 225 Index was up 2.17 per cent at 50,367.38, taking its gains for the year to 25.8 per cent. The broader Topix rose 1.72 per cent to 3,325.82. “The Nikkei’s gains were supported by expectations for the Takaichi administration, whose policy is focused on growth,” said Hiroyuki Ueno, chief strategist at Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Asset Management.”The market kept buying stocks. Even as the Nikkei fell after Takaichi was elected, the decline did not last long because investors who were not able to catch up with the latest rally scooped up stocks on dip,” said Ueno. Chip-testing equipment maker Advantest jumped 4.83 per cent to give the biggest boost to the Nikkei on Monday, while Uniqlo-brand owner Fast Retailing rose 2.55 per cent. The gauge broke through 45,000 on September 16 and has marched through successive round numbers at a rapid clip. It marks a dramatic turnaround for a long-moribund market that saw the Nikkei take 34 years to finally recover to its Bubble Economy peak in February 2024. The index rose to the brink of 50,000 last Tuesday, when Takaichi cleared a parliamentary vote to become premier. The Nikkei finished the week 3.6 per cent higher as Takaichi pledged a proactive spending policy, with an economic stimulus package expected to exceed 13.9 trillion yen ($92.2 billion). “Fiscal packages tend to be welcomed by the market, irrespective of their actual impact on the overall economy,” said Norihiro Yamaguchi, lead Japan economist at Oxford Economics. “The fact that Takaichi’s policy focus is on strategic investment and other market-friendly areas is another reason why the stock market reacted strongly.” Japanese equities have been on the upswing since mid-July, when an electoral drubbing for the ruling Liberal Democratic Party sparked bets that fiscally hawkish Shigeru Ishiba would resign as prime minister. Ishiba finally announced in September he would step aside, setting up a party leadership vote won by Takaichi, a devotee of the “Abenomics” stimulus policies of late premier Shinzo Abe. Takaichi will meet Donald Trump later on Monday and hold a summit with him on Tuesday, having had her first call with the U.S. president over the weekend. title: Is An Upswing Momentum Due For Public Bank Shares?
body: Public Bank Bhd (PBBANK) shares edged slightly higher on Monday, closing at RM4.22, up 0.24%, as the stock began to show signs of stabilising near its recent low of RM4.20. The move follows a mild pullback last week, with analysts suggesting that the downside momentum may be easing as the counter consolidates below its short-term averages. According to Kenanga Research, the stock is currently trading just below its 5-day simple moving average (SMA), indicating that selling pressure is waning and a potential rebound could be forming at current levels. The stochastic oscillator, now at 7.02, is stabilising in oversold territory, signalling that selling momentum is likely reaching exhaustion. Meanwhile, the Relative Strength Index (RSI) stands at 42.97 and is beginning to turn upward — an early sign of improving sentiment. Kenanga noted that these technical developments point to the possibility of a short-term recovery as the counter finds support. The research house identified immediate resistance at RM4.27 (13-day SMA). A sustained breakout above this level could pave the way for a move toward RM4.32 (50-day SMA), RM4.37 (200-day SMA), and potentially RM4.51, the recent swing high. On the downside, support is seen at RM4.20, the lower bound of the recent consolidation range. Additional support levels are located at RM4.14 (78.6% Fibonacci retracement) and RM4.03, which analysts view as a crucial defensive level. Kenanga recommends entering near RM4.22, with a take-profit target of RM4.50, representing an upside potential of about 6.6%. To manage downside risks, a stop-loss at RM4.02 is advised, which would limit potential losses to approximately 4.7%. The research note concludes that while sentiment on the broader banking sector remains cautious amid subdued loan growth expectations, Public Bank’s solid fundamentals and consistent dividend record continue to provide support for long-term investors. title: Foreign Investors Remain Net Sellers, Outflow Eases Sharply
body: Foreign investors remained net sellers on Bursa Malaysia for the third consecutive week, but outflows eased sharply to RM14.6 million, a steep decline from the RM962.8 million recorded in the previous week, according to data compiled by Kenanga Research. The moderation in selling pressure reflects improved market sentiment and selective buying activity across key sectors, though overall participation levels softened. Foreign investors were net sellers on two out of four trading days last week, with the heaviest selling recorded on Wednesday (-RM73.3 million) and Tuesday (-RM68.9 million). However, this was offset by net buying on Thursday (RM97.5 million) and Friday (RM30.1 million). The top sectors attracting foreign inflows included consumer Products & Services (RM195.7 million), Industrial Products & Services (RM83.0 million) and Technology (RM66.9 million) Meanwhile, the sectors that saw the largest net outflows were healthcare (-RM200.7 million), Financial Services (-RM142.7 million) and Telecommunication & Media (-RM52.4 million) Analysts noted that sustained interest in consumer and tech counters suggests a continued preference for defensive and growth-oriented plays, while selling in financial and healthcare sectors may indicate short-term profit-taking. Local institutional investors extended their three-week buying streak, with net inflows of RM111.1 million, underscoring continued confidence in domestic fundamentals and value-driven accumulation. Conversely, local retailers continued their seven-week selling streak, albeit with a much smaller outflow of RM96.5 million, compared with RM357.4 million the week before — a decline of nearly forthcoming. Overall market participation was weaker, with the average daily trading volume (ADTV) declining across all investor groups. Local retailers saw activity fall 26.3%, local institutions 18.8%, and foreign investors 25.1%, reflecting a cautious tone amid global macroeconomic uncertainty and earnings season consolidation. Kenanga Research expects near-term market activity to remain range-bound, with investors likely to stay selective ahead of upcoming corporate results releases and global monetary policy signals. title: Bitcoin Tops US$115,000, Ethereum Jumps Over 6% Amid Risk-On Rally
body: The cryptocurrency market surged on Oct 26 as improved global risk sentiment and optimism over US-China trade progress lifted major digital assets, with Bitcoin and Ethereum leading the gains. Bitcoin climbed past US$115,000, rising about 3.4% from the previous close, while Ethereum jumped 6.8% to trade above US$4,200. Bitcoin touched an intraday high of US$116,174, while Ethereum reached US$4,249.69, according to crypto market data. Analysts attributed the rally to a combination of factors, including expectations of potential US interest rate cuts, renewed optimism surrounding a US-China trade framework and a short squeeze that forced traders to unwind bearish positions. The surge also follows weeks of muted trading, and market observers say the move could signal a near-term shift in sentiment. However, they cautioned that volatility remains high and the rally may be driven more by short-term positioning than by sustained buying momentum. Key technical levels to watch include US$116,000-US$116,500 as resistance for Bitcoin, and US$4,200-US$4,400 for Ethereum. The broader crypto market also saw gains across altcoins, with total market capitalisation edging higher as liquidity expectations improved. While the tone has turned bullish, analysts warned that any reversal in macroeconomic trends or regulatory developments could quickly temper the momentum. title: Asian Stocks Surge On US-China Trade Deal Breakthrough
body: Asian equities surged Monday (Oct 27) as investors cheered a breakthrough in US-China trade talks that set the stage for leaders Donald Trump and Xi Jinping to finalise a deal, averting an escalation in the world’s biggest trade dispute. Markets rallied after US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the threat of the US president imposing an additional 100 per cent tariff on Chinese goods was “effectively off the table” following weekend negotiations in Malaysia.”The tariffs will be averted,” Bessent told ABC News on Sunday, adding that China agreed to delay rare earth export controls and make “substantial” soybean purchases. Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng said the two sides reached a “preliminary consensus” on tariffs, export controls and fentanyl cooperation, describing the talks as “candid, in-depth and constructive”.The progress paves the way for Trump and Xi to meet Thursday in South Korea on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, their first face-to-face meeting since Trump returned to office. Tokyo led gains in Asia, with the Nikkei 225 adding more than 2 per cent and closing above the 50,000 mark for the first time, buoyed by Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s pro-stimulus stance and a weaker yen that benefits the export sector. The breakthrough also comes ahead of Trump’s visit to Tokyo, with Takaichi having pledged to raise defence spending to 2 per cent of GDP this fiscal year – two years ahead of schedule. “The Nikkei’s breakout isn’t a technical fluke – it’s the pricing of a national renaissance,” said Stephen Innes of SPI Asset Management.”Seoul, too, ended more than 2 per cent higher, surpassing the 4,000 mark for the first time, with tech titan Samsung gaining more than 3 per cent and chipmaker SK hynix jumping nearly 5 per cent. Hong Kong, Shanghai, Taipei, Singapore and Sydney also made gains, though Jakarta and Manila fell. In Europe, London and Frankfurt opened with gains, while Paris dipped into the red. The positive sentiment follows a strong finish on Wall Street Friday, after benign US inflation data set the stage for another Federal Reserve interest rate cut. Trump expressed confidence about reaching a comprehensive agreement with Beijing. “They want to make a deal and we want to make a deal,” he told reporters Sunday in Kuala Lumpur. “The assumption, of course, remains that that is just a negotiating gambit, with this week’s talks leading to a restoration of the ‘status quo’ and a truce between the two nations,” said Michael Brown of Pepperstone. The Republican president is on a five-day Asia tour that includes stops in Malaysia, Japan and South Korea, with trade deals topping the agenda at every destination. Futures for US copper surged on the trade deal optimism, bolstering the outlook for global demand. The breakthrough came after months of escalating tensions, with Trump threatening the massive tariff hike in response to China’s October expansion of rare earth export controls – a move Washington called “economic coercion”. Under the framework deal, China would defer its rare earth restrictions “for a year while they reexamine it”, Bessent said. title: Weekly Review: Singapore Stocks Inch Higher On Strong Export Data
body: Singapore stocks ended the trading week of Oct 20 slightly higher as upbeat export data lifted sentiment, though gains were capped by lingering global uncertainty and muted trading activity. The Straits Times Index (STI) advanced modestly over the week, closing around 4,422 points on Oct 24 after opening near 4,340 points on Oct 20. The index added 0.13% on the final trading day, reflecting cautious optimism among investors. Market sentiment improved early in the week after Singapore’s non-oil domestic exports surged 6.9% year-on-year in September, exceeding expectations and bolstering confidence in the city-state’s trade-dependent economy. However, gains were tempered by concerns over global growth, shifting monetary policies and persistent geopolitical risks. Traders also remained on the sidelines ahead of key earnings and economic data releases in the US and China. Analysts said the STI continues to consolidate within the 4,350-4,450 range, with near-term resistance seen at 4,450. A decisive move above that level could pave the way for further upside, while a dip below 4,300 may trigger renewed caution. Looking ahead, investors will be watching for fresh catalysts from corporate earnings, regional trade updates and macroeconomic data that could define the STI’s next direction in the final quarter of the year. title: Market Wrap: Gold Ends The Week On A Softer Note After Hitting Record Highs
body: Gold prices took investors on a volatile ride from Oct 20 to 24, surging to record levels early in the week before easing as profit-taking and a stronger US dollar capped gain. In Malaysia, the precious metal touched a new peak of RM18,475 per oz for 24-karat gold on Oct 20, marking the year’s highest level. The rally was fuelled by robust global demand as investors flocked to safe-haven assets amid ongoing geopolitical and inflation concerns. According to Bank of America Global Research, gold funds attracted US$8.7 billion in inflows in the week leading up to Oct 22, pushing spot prices to above US$4,381 per oz, a fresh milestone for the metal. However, by Oct 24, prices had cooled off, settling around RM17,365 per oz locally, with 24-karat gold averaging RM558.38 per gram, according to market data. The week’s gold movements were driven by several key factors such as safe-haven demand, interest rate expectations, stronger US dollar and profit-taking. Moving forward, market watchers remain divided on gold’s next move. A dovish shift by major central banks or renewed inflation concerns could reignite buying interest. Conversely, a sustained dollar rebound may limit upside momentum in the near term. For now, the metal remains firmly supported by risk aversion but traders are treading cautiously, with attention turning to upcoming economic data and policy signals from the US Federal Reserve. title: Market Recap: Bursa Malaysia Ends Week Slightly Higher As Investors Await Global Cues
body: Bursa Malaysia wrapped up the trading week on a firmer note, with the benchmark FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) closing marginally higher amid cautious sentiment ahead of key global developments. The FBM KLCI added 5.27 points, or 0.33%, to end its trading week on Oct 24 at 1,613.27, extending its modest gains from earlier in the week. Trading volume eased to 2.98 billion shares worth RM2.43 billion compared to 3.44 billion shares valued at RM2.66 billion the previous day, reflecting a more subdued tone as investors took a wait-and-see approach. Market sentiment was supported by reports of progress in US-China relations, with confirmation of an upcoming meeting between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping. The news buoyed regional markets and helped Bursa Malaysia play catch-up following its Deepavali break earlier in the week. On Oct 21, when trading resumed, the local bourse surged 9.65 points, or 0.6%, to 1,616.83, mirroring gains across major Asian markets. However, mid-week momentum softened as investors turned cautious ahead of the weekend. Heavyweights provided steady support to the index, with Maybank rising six sen to RM9.90, CIMB Group added four sen to RM7.37, while TNB gained 10 sen to RM13.22. Market breadth remained positive, with 610 gainers outpacing 445 losers. Analysts noted that the FBM KLCI remains range-bound between the 1,600 and 1,630 levels, with resistance expected near the upper band. A decisive breakout above 1,630, they said, could pave the way for stronger upside momentum. Looking ahead, traders are expected to focus on upcoming corporate earnings and policy developments, both domestically and abroad. Unless new catalysts emerge, Bursa Malaysia is likely to continue trading within its current range, with the 1,630-level serving as a key indicator for the market’s next direction. title: Wall Street Hits Record Highs On Cooling Inflation, Earnings Optimism
body: Wall Street closed at record highs on Oct 24, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average surging 472.51 points, or 1.01%, to 47,207.12, while the S&P 500 gained 0.79% to 6,791.69 and the Nasdaq Composite jumped 1.15% to 23,204.87, lifted by cooler inflation data and robust corporate earnings. Reuters reported that the rally marked all-time closing highs for all three major US indexes, capping their strongest week since mid-year. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq logged their biggest weekly percentage gains since August, while the Dow recorded its largest week-to-week rise since June. September’s Consumer Price Index came in slightly below expectations, easing inflation fears and reinforcing expectations for a 25-basis-point Federal Reserve (Fed) rate cut next week. The data, one of few releases amid a government shutdown, reassured investors about tariff impacts and policy direction. Earnings optimism also fuelled the rally, with 143 S&P 500 companies having reported so far, showing an average 10.4% year-on-year earnings growth, up from 8.8% earlier this month, according to LSEG. Tech and financial stocks led gains, with Alphabet rose 2.7% after Anthropic expanded its artificial intelligence chip deal, while Coinbase jumped 9.8% following a JPMorgan upgrade. Ford rallied 12.2% on a profit beat, though Deckers Outdoor tumbled 15.2% after cutting its sales outlook. With heavyweight earnings from Meta, Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon and Apple on deck next week, investors are gearing up for another pivotal stretch as Wall Street rides record-breaking momentum into the Fed’s policy decision. title: Wall Street Rises As Trump-Xi Meeting Lifts Trade Hopes, Tech Leads Gains
body: Wall Street advanced on Thursday as investors digested a mix of corporate earnings and geopolitical developments that lifted sentiment across markets. All three major US indices ended higher, led by the Nasdaq, while the small-cap Russell 2000 emerged as the day’s best performer. The market found renewed momentum after the White House confirmed that US President Donald Trump will meet Chinese President Xi Jinping next week during his Asia tour. The announcement helped ease recent trade tensions that had intensified following a series of retaliatory measures between Washington and Beijing. “The Trump-Xi confirmation is clearly positive,” said Horizon Investments Head of Portfolio Management Zachary Hill. “That’s a good checkpoint for sentiment, which has been really up and down on trade, and that’s obviously playing a role today.” The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 144.20 points, or 0.31%, to close at 46,734.61. The S&P 500 added 39.03 points, or 0.58%, to 6,738.43, while the Nasdaq Composite climbed 201.40 points, or 0.89%, to 22,941.80. Trump also announced new sanctions against Russian oil companies, marking a significant escalation in pressure on Moscow over its war in Ukraine. The move sent global oil prices higher and lifted energy stocks on Wall Street. Energy companies were the top-performing sector on the S&P 500, rising 1.3%. Exxon Mobil and Chevron advanced 1.1% and 0.6% respectively, while independent refiner Valero Energy jumped 7.0% after posting stronger-than-expected quarterly profits. Corporate earnings continued to set the tone for trading. Tesla rebounded 2.3% after a profit miss, while Honeywell rallied 6.8% as strong aerospace demand led it to raise its annual profit forecast. American Airlines rose 5.6% after upgrading its full-year outlook, while Southwest Airlines slipped 6.3% despite reporting a surprise profit and record quarterly sales. IBM’s shares fell 0.9% after reporting slower growth in its cloud software segment despite an earnings beat. Dow Inc. surged 13% after reporting a smaller-than-expected quarterly loss, supported by higher volumes and cost-cutting measures. Earnings results from S&P 500 companies have been largely positive so far, with 86% beating consensus expectations, according to LSEG data. Analysts now project overall third-quarter earnings growth of 9.9% year-on-year, up from 8.8% estimated earlier this month. Quantum computing stocks also gained after reports that the Trump administration is considering taking equity stakes in select firms in exchange for federal funding. IonQ, D-Wave Quantum, Quantum Computing and Rigetti Computing all rose between 7.1% and 13.8%. Broader market breadth was positive, with advancing issues outnumbering decliners by a ratio of 2.05 to 1 on the NYSE. Volume on US exchanges totalled 19.07 billion shares, below the 20-day average of 20.62 billion. Rising geopolitical tensions have also benefited aerospace and defence stocks, with the S&P 500 Aerospace and Defence Index gaining 2.2%. Overall, optimism around earnings and easing trade concerns helped lift investor sentiment, with markets looking ahead to further corporate reports and potential developments from the Trump-Xi meeting next week. title: Stock Today: Kossan Rubber Edges Lower Amid Persistent Sector Pressures
body: Kossan Rubber Industries Bhd (Main Market, 7153) saw its share price fall 0.81% to RM1.23 as of 4.15 pm, with 1.87 million shares traded. The stock opened at RM1.24, reached an intraday high of RM1.26 and a low of RM1.23. RHB Research has identified Kossan Rubber Industries as its top sector pick, citing the company’s focus on higher-margin products such as cleanroom gloves, which provide better resilience amid sector challenges. Despite a rebound in Malaysia’s glove exports in the third quarter, led by restocking after inventory depletion, the rubber products sector continues to face structural pressures. RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) maintains its UNDERWEIGHT call, highlighting prolonged oversupply, intensifying competition in US and non-US markets, and weak pricing power as ongoing headwinds. Exports to non-US markets now account for a larger share, with the US representing 45% of Malaysia’s glove exports, down from 75% in June. Intense price competition persists in the US market, where Malaysian producers, including Top Glove, have reduced selling prices to maintain market share. Rising latex concentrate costs in Southeast Asia could further narrow cost advantages. Operating costs are expected to rise modestly in the second half of the year, with limited impact from foreign worker EPF contributions and exemption from SST on imported raw materials. A multi-tier levy on foreign labour in 2026 could increase production costs marginally. RHB Research noted that valuations in the sector have re-rated to near three-year averages but fundamental risks remain, with earnings disappointments more likely than short-term gains, except for efficient producers with non-generic, higher-margin products. title: Stock Today: Gamuda Dips As Market Awaits Progress On UK Expansion Plans
body: Shares of Gamuda Bhd slipped slightly by 0.2% to RM5.04 as at 11.51 am today, even as the construction and property group continues to make strategic headway in its overseas expansion, particularly in the United Kingdom. The counter traded between RM5.02 and RM5.09 in the morning session, with over 1 million shares changing hands. It opened at RM5.05, down marginally from its last closing price of RM5.05. Investor sentiment remained steady despite recent announcements from its property arm, Gamuda Land, which unveiled the acquisition of a prime site at 14 Marshgate Lane in Stratford, London. The development, a purpose-built student accommodation (PBSA) project with an estimated gross development value (GDV) of RM600 million, marks Gamuda Land UK’s first fully owned, self-developed and managed PBSA venture. The Marshgate Lane acquisition is part of Gamuda’s plan to deliver up to 3,000 student beds across key UK cities within five years, strengthening its pipeline of recurring income-generating assets. The 321-bed development, located near UCL East and the London College of Fashion, is slated for completion in the 2028/29 academic year. According to Gamuda Land chief executive officer Chu Wai Lune, the PBSA segment remains a counter-cyclical asset class supported by robust student demand and limited supply. “This structural undersupply, coupled with universities’ ongoing global appeal, gives us confidence in long-term earnings visibility,” he said. Gamuda Land’s UK portfolio now totals 1,232 beds across three projects, with an overall development pipeline worth approximately £1.5 billion. This includes the flagship £1.2 billion redevelopment of 75 London Wall in partnership with Castleforge, which is on track to sign its main contract with Multiplex this quarter. At the current level, Gamuda’s market capitalisation stands steady as investors await further updates on its international property ventures and the group’s ongoing diversification strategy to strengthen earnings resilience across economic cycles. title: Ringgit Finds Its Footing Before US Inflation Test
body: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar on Friday, supported by cautious sentiment ahead of the release of the US inflation report later tonight. At 8.02 am, the local currency strengthened to 4.2190/2285 against the greenback from 4.2250/2285 at Thursday’s close. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the market’s focus is on the upcoming US consumer price index (CPI) data, which will be released despite the ongoing US government shutdown. He said consensus estimates point to a 3.1% rise in headline CPI for September, following a 2.9% increase in August. “It seems that the US tariff on imports has started to have an impact on general prices, with US Customs duties collection surging 200% in the first nine months of this year to US$174 billion. The US Dollar Index (DXY) has been hovering between 98 and 99 points, so we expect the ringgit to trade within a narrow range today, around RM4.22 to RM4.23,” he told Bernama. At the opening, the ringgit traded mostly higher against major currencies. It advanced against the British pound to 5.6227/6353 from 5.6395/6442, and inched up against the Japanese yen to 2.7655/7719 from 2.7687/7712. However, it eased slightly versus the euro to 4.9021/9131 from 4.8976/9017. The ringgit also strengthened across most ASEAN currencies, rising to 3.2491/2570 against the Singapore dollar from 3.2513/2542, and to 7.20/7.22 versus the Philippine peso from 7.21/7.22. It also edged up against the Thai baht to 12.8608/8977 from 12.8772/8937, and improved against the Indonesian rupiah to 253.6/254.4 from 254.0/254.4. Beyond Meat Inc. swung sharply in volatile trading, echoing previous meme-stock frenzies, while International Business Machines Corp. reported weaker revenue from its Red Hat unit. Investor caution deepened after the Trump administration said it was considering restrictions on software exports to China, raising concerns over renewed trade frictions. Oil prices climbed after Washington imposed sanctions on Russia’s biggest producers in its latest effort to pressure President Vladimir Putin to end the war in Ukraine. The selloff extended to assets popular among retail momentum traders, including precious metals, cryptocurrencies and artificial intelligence-related stocks. The Bloomberg US Pure Momentum Portfolio, which tracks high-momentum equities, has fallen sharply in recent days. Bespoke Investment Group said the recent pullback marked a cooling in enthusiasm for speculative names that had surged since August. “It appears that, at least temporarily, the music has stopped and the party has ended for the most speculative names,” Bespoke strategists said. “No one knows when the music will pick back up again, but usually, the higher they go, the harder they fall.” In the bond market, the yield on 10-year US Treasuries fell one basis point to 3.95% after a strong US$13 billion sale of 20-year bonds. Bitcoin declined 2.6%, gold dropped as much as 2.9% before paring losses, and the dollar wavered. Despite the broader decline, earnings season has provided some optimism. The proportion of S&P 500 firms beating profit expectations this quarter is the highest since 2021, according to Bloomberg Intelligence. JPMorgan Chase & Co.’s Dubravko Lakos-Bujas said corporate results remain supported by strong AI investment, government spending and resilient consumer demand. Separately, the Federal Reserve has presented US regulators with a plan to significantly relax a Biden-era bank capital proposal for the country’s largest lenders. The central bank is also facing data challenges after payroll services firm ADP Research stopped providing private-sector employment figures, which cover about 20% of the US labour force, amid the ongoing government shutdown. title: Stock Today: RHB Bank Rises 1.35% As Sector Outlook Improves
body: RHB Bank Bhd (1066) saw its shares climb 1.35% to RM6.76 at 4:36 PM today, with a total volume of 3.53 million shares traded. The stock opened at RM6.69, hitting an intraday high of RM6.78 and a low of RM6.67. The gain comes amid a positive sector outlook from RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research), which recently upgraded its view on the Malaysian banking sector to OVERWEIGHT from Neutral. The research house cited improving fundamentals heading into 2026, supported by resilient domestic economic conditions, stabilising credit costs, and attractive dividend yields averaging 5.8%. RHB Research highlighted that banks such as CIMB Group Holdings Bhd, Hong Leong Bank Bhd and Public Bank Bhd remain top picks, with corporate lenders expected to benefit from strong loan pipelines while overall asset quality holds steady. Sector profit after tax and minority interests (PATMI) is projected to rebound to 5% in 2026, compared to an estimated 2% this year. The research firm also noted that a lower interest rate environment and potential capital management initiatives could further bolster sector performance, particularly for banks with regional exposure. Foreign institutional inflows are expected to provide an additional catalyst, with CIMB and PBK likely to benefit most. Despite the positive outlook, RHB Research cautioned that third-quarter results for 2025 may be modest due to the July policy rate cut, although non-interest income from wealth management, markets-related fees, and treasury activities is expected to anchor operating income. The local banking system remains resilient, according to Bank Negara Malaysia’s Financial Stability Review for H1 2025, with asset quality supported by stable household and business gross impaired loans and the ongoing transition from KLIBOR to MYOR. body: Shares of MBM Resources Bhd edged higher by 0.38% to RM5.22 at midday, with 38,100 shares traded as investors maintained a cautious stance on the automotive sector despite signs of recovery toward year-end. Both houses expect stronger sales in the fourth quarter but warned of challenges from competition, price pressures linked to the delayed Open Market Value (OMV) revision, and a lack of near-term catalysts. RHB Research raised its 2025 total industry volume (TIV) forecast by 9% to 795,000 units, while CIMB Securities lifted its projection by 3.9% to 790,000 units. Both pointed to steady EV demand and improving macroeconomic indicators as potential year-end drivers. Still, concerns remain over the sector’s structural challenges, particularly limited EV charging infrastructure and the expected expiry of tax exemptions for completely built-up (CBU) electric vehicles in January 2026. MBM Resources, which has exposure through Perodua, continues to benefit from national carmakers’ resilience. Proton’s sales rose 13.6% in the third quarter of 2025, while national brands now hold a combined 63% market share.
