title: Stock Today: IGB Commercial REIT Rises 2.46% On Strong Fundamentals, Analyst Optimism
body: Shares of IGB Commercial Real Estate Investment Trust (IGBCR) rose 2.46% to RM0.625 as of midday trading, supported by continued analyst optimism and resilient third-quarter performance. The counter opened at RM0.610 and climbed to an intraday high of RM0.625, with 286,400 shares traded. RHB Investment Bank Bhd and Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd have both reiterated their BUY calls on IGBCR, citing sustained growth momentum and robust occupancy across key office assets, particularly within the Mid Valley City development. RHB Research maintained its target price (TP) at RM0.72, implying an 18.6% upside, while HLIB Research kept its TP at RM0.64, representing a total expected return of 12%. The positive sentiment follows IGBCR’s third-quarter 2025 (3Q25) results, which were in line with expectations. Core profit for the first nine months of 2025 rose 26.1% year-on-year to RM71.5 million, meeting 78% of RHB’s full-year estimate. This growth was driven by higher occupancy—improving to 92% from 87% a year earlier—and positive rental reversions, particularly in its Kuala Lumpur City assets. The REIT declared a 3Q25 distribution per unit (DPU) of 1 sen, bringing total DPU for the first nine months to 3.1 sen, up from 2.9 sen last year. Gearing remained healthy at 26.3%, while Southpoint Tower maintained full tenancy and GTower’s occupancy rose to 88%. HLIB Research noted that 3Q25 core net profit grew 27.7% year-on-year to RM23.8 million, supported by stronger rental income and an 11.3% year-to-date decline in financing costs. Both research houses highlighted that IGBCR’s well-located office properties, integrated within the Mid Valley ecosystem, remain well-positioned to capture demand from high-value and technology-driven sectors. At the time of writing, IGBCR traded between RM0.610 and RM0.625, with buying interest supported by its steady dividend yield and exposure to Malaysia’s growing service-oriented economy. Both RHB and HLIB expect IGBCR to sustain stable performance in the coming quarters, anchored by strong occupancy, prudent cost management and ongoing tenant diversification. title: MBSB Maintains Neutral On Eco World, Noting Valuations At Premium
body: MBSB Investment Bank Bhd has maintained its NEUTRAL call on Eco World Development Group Bhd (Eco World) with an unchanged target price of RM2.19, noting that while the developer’s southern Klang Valley projects continue to show robust momentum, valuations appear rich as shares trade at a 24% premium to its latest net tangible asset value of RM1.70 per share. The research house said Eco World’s townships in Semenyih, including Eco Majestic, Eco Forest and the upcoming Eco Radiance, are expected to underpin its steady performance in the coming years. Following a visit to these developments, MBSB Research noted that the group’s township model remains appealing, particularly for families and young buyers seeking modern, secure and well-connected living environments. Eco Majestic, launched in 2014, remains the group’s highest sales contributor with total sales of RM4.6 billion. The 1,089-acre township, linked to the LEKAS Highway via its dedicated interchange, continues to attract multi-generational and affluent buyers, with terrace homes priced at around RM1 million and bungalows starting from RM2 million. The research house highlighted that its commercial component, Majestic Labs, has achieved a 70% occupancy rate, anchored by tenants such as Nando’s, Caring Pharmacy and Believe Fitness, adding to Eco World’s recurring income targets of 20–30% in the medium term. Meanwhile, Eco Forest, launched in 2017 on 493 acres near Broga Hill, has seen strong traction among middle-income buyers. The township, which has generated RM1.1 billion in total sales with more than 1,600 units sold, caters primarily to the mass market segment, offering terrace houses starting from RM600,000. Its remaining undeveloped landbank of 114 acres carries a gross development value (GDV) of RM1.37 billion. Looking ahead, MBSB Research said Eco World is set to expand further with Eco Radiance, its third Semenyih township, following the acquisition of 847 acres of land in November 2024 and an additional 22.73 acres of commercial land recently. The combined 870-acre site, with an estimated GDV of RM5.16 billion, will feature higher-end residential and commercial properties designed to cater to the growing demand in the area. The project is slated for launch in the first half of FY2026. The research house maintained that Eco World’s near-term earnings outlook remains positive, supported by earnings recognition from land sales and consistent demand across its developments. However, it also cautioned that the current valuation limits upside potential despite strong fundamentals and steady execution. Eco World’s stock price noted a slight increase (0.48%) to RM2.11 as of 10.22 am. title: Gold Surges Amid Global Rally, Hitting RM559 per Gram
body: Gold prices in Malaysia rose sharply on Thursday, with the commodity trading at RM559.51 per gram, up RM8.70 or 1.58% from the previous day, according to GoldPrice.org. On a per-kilogram basis, the yellow metal reached RM559,514, marking a daily gain of RM8,708. The increase mirrors global trends, as investors continue to view gold as a hedge against economic uncertainty. In other markets, gold prices have also climbed this week: the United States saw prices rise by 54.3% year-to-date in US dollars, while Australia recorded a 47.1% increase, Canada 50%, and the Eurozone 50.6%. Asia markets, including Japan and India, also reported significant gains of 58.2% and 44.5% respectively for the year. Over the past month, gold in Malaysia has gained RM1,408.75 per gram, a rise of 8.96%, and over the past year, the precious metal has jumped 44.10%, reflecting strong demand and safe-haven buying. Analysts attribute the surge to a combination of local currency strength, rising global inflation expectations, and geopolitical uncertainties that continue to boost investor interest in precious metals. Silver prices also climbed, up 1.94% to RM3.96 per gram, showing a similar upward momentum alongside gold. With global and regional markets experiencing sustained gains, Malaysia’s gold remains competitive for investors seeking to diversify portfolios amid ongoing economic volatility. title: Stock Today: Petronas Gas Slips Amid Ongoing RM68 Million Lawsuit
body: Shares of Petronas Gas Bhd (PetGas) traded lower this afternoon, extending losses as investors continued to assess the potential fallout from a RM68 million lawsuit filed by residents of Taman Putra Harmoni, Putra Heights. As of 2.40 pm, PetGas’ stock was down 0.85% or 16 sen to RM18.68, with 178,600 shares traded. The counter opened at RM18.76 and moved between RM18.60 and RM18.82 during the morning session. The decline comes days after PetGas confirmed in a filing that it was among five defendants named in a lawsuit by 36 residents seeking damages over an alleged gas explosion and fire incident. The plaintiffs, represented by Messrs Tommy Thomas, have accused PetGas of negligence and breach of statutory duty under the Gas Supply Act 1993 and the Petroleum (Safety Measures) Regulations 1985. The residents are seeking around RM68 million in special damages, along with general, aggravated and exemplary damages. PetGas said it has appointed legal counsel to represent the company and does not expect the claim to have any material financial or operational impact at this stage. Despite the legal development, trading volume remained moderate, and the stock is still up about 3% year-to-date. title: Stock Today: CIMB Eases To RM7.30 Amid Mixed Performance From Thai Unit
body: CIMB Group Holdings Bhd’s share price edged down 0.68% to RM7.30 as at 12:18 p.m. on Tuesday, with 1.66 million shares traded, reflecting cautious investor sentiment following its Thai subsidiary’s latest earnings report. The stock opened at RM7.35 and traded between RM7.29 and RM7.36 during the session. CIMB Thai Bank, a subsidiary of CIMB Group, reported a net profit of THB 1,830.4 million for the nine months ended 30 September 2025, representing a 3.2% year-on-year (YoY) decline. The dip was mainly due to higher credit provisions, which surged 59.5% YoY, despite lower operating expenses and stronger investment income. President and CEO of CIMB Thai Bank, Wut Thanittiraporn, said the results reflected the bank’s prudent approach to credit risk management amid challenging economic conditions. “While operating income was slightly lower, the Bank maintained strong pre-provision profitability, reflecting disciplined cost control and effective risk management,” he said. For the period, operating income slipped 2.2% YoY to THB 10,549.4 million, primarily due to a 15.1% drop in net interest income and a 0.5% decline in fee and service income. However, other income rose 34.0%, supported by higher net investment gains. Operating expenses decreased by 19.4%, resulting in a cost-to-income ratio of 50.2% compared to 61.0% last year. Despite narrower loan margins, CIMB Thai’s pre-provision operating profit climbed 24.6% YoY to THB 5,248.4 million. Its net interest margin declined to 1.9% from 2.3% a year earlier, reflecting lower yields on loans. Total gross loans contracted 3.7% to THB 242.1 billion, while total deposits eased 1.7% to THB 318.5 billion, resulting in a loan-to-deposit ratio of 76.0%. Asset quality remained stable, with gross non-performing loans holding at THB 6.3 billion and a gross NPL ratio of 2.6%. The loan loss coverage ratio strengthened to 158.1%, while total allowances for expected credit losses rose to THB 9.8 billion, exceeding regulatory requirements by THB 1.5 billion. CIMB Thai also maintained a strong capital position, with total capital funds of THB 61.4 billion and a BIS ratio of 21.1%, including 16.6% Tier-1 capital. At current levels, CIMB shares remain near the lower end of their six-month trading range between RM7.29 and RM7.50. Analysts expect the Group’s upcoming quarterly results to provide clearer visibility on earnings momentum and regional contributions, particularly from its Thai and Indonesian units. title: Solarvest’s Fundraising Exercise Gets Analysts’ Nod
body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has maintained its BUY call on Solarvest Holdings Bhd, with a revised target price of RM3.49, implying a 10% upside. The research house said the solar energy group’s proposed private placement of up to 10% of its issued shares would help strengthen its balance sheet and enhance flexibility for expansion. According to RHB Research, Solarvest aims to raise as much as RM254.1 million through the placement at an indicative issue price of RM3.00 per share, representing a 4.15% discount to its five-day volume-weighted average price of RM3.13. The exercise is expected to be completed by the first half of 2026, pending regulatory approvals. The proceeds from the placement will primarily fund business expansion, particularly new solar photovoltaic projects such as Large-Scale Solar (LSS) 5, LSS5+, and the Mukah project over the next two years. RHB Research noted that around RM124.6 million, or 49% of the proceeds, will go towards capital expenditure for these projects. Another RM50 million will be used to reduce borrowings, while RM79.2 million will be channelled to working capital to support the group’s growing engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning (EPCC) orderbook worth RM1.18 billion. The remaining RM0.3 million will be allocated for expenses related to the placement. Post-placement, Solarvest’s share capital will increase to RM570 million from RM315.9 million, with total issued shares rising to 932.4 million from 847.7 million. The group’s net assets per share are expected to improve to RM0.77 from RM0.55, while gearing should fall to 0.38 times from 0.69 times. RHB Research said the stronger equity base will enable Solarvest to take on larger-scale renewable energy projects and accelerate portfolio diversification. RHB Research also highlighted that Solarvest has 59.2 million outstanding employee share options, with 23.2 million already vested under its employee stock option scheme (ESOS). The firm expects the improved capital structure and lower leverage to translate into stronger earnings over the medium term. The research house has factored in the private placement’s impact into its forecasts, projecting higher earnings for FY2026 to FY2028 by 4.6%, 9.4%, and 9% respectively, mainly due to lower interest costs. It also adjusted borrowing cost assumptions and raised the target price-to-earnings multiple for Solarvest’s associate-level and solar asset investments. The new target price includes an 8% ESG premium, supported by Solarvest’s above-median ESG score of 3.4 compared with Malaysia’s country median of 3.0. Contrary to the call, Solarvest’s stock price as of 10.35 am noted a decrease of 2.84% to RM3.08. title: Malaysia Gold Prices Edge Higher Despite Global Correction
body: Gold prices in Malaysia edged higher to RM564.71 per gram (RM564,705.26 per kilogram) as of early Wednesday, reflecting a 1.35% gain for local investors. Gold per ounce was at RM17,564.31, up RM234.69, marking a continued strong year-to-date performance with a 46.6% gain over the past 12 months. Globally, gold was under pressure following sharp declines earlier this week. Spot gold fell 0.4% to US$4,109.19 per ounce as of 0236 GMT, after tumbling more than 5% on Tuesday in its steepest drop since August 2020. US gold futures for December delivery, however, rose 0.4% to US$4,124.10 per ounce. StoneX senior analyst Matt Simpson said the decline was a technical pullback. “Simmering of trade tensions between the US and China was the snowflake which caused the avalanche and reversal of gold’s momentum trade,” he noted, adding that dips were likely to attract buyers. The easing came amid signs that US-China trade tensions were cooling, with US President Donald Trump anticipating a fair trade deal with Chinese President Xi Jinping next week in South Korea. Meanwhile, Washington and New Delhi are reportedly close to a long-stalled trade agreement that would reduce US tariffs on Indian imports from 50% to 15–16%. Gold has surged roughly 56% this year, reaching a record peak of US$4,381.21 on Monday, fuelled by geopolitical and economic uncertainties, rate-cut expectations, and sustained central bank purchases. Investors are now awaiting the September US consumer price index report due Friday for cues on the Federal Reserve’s interest rate policy, which is expected to include a 25-basis-point cut next week and another in December. Other precious metals showed mixed movements: spot silver edged 0.1% higher to US$48.82 per ounce, platinum slipped 1.5% to US$1,528.15, and palladium gained 0.7% to US$1,418.09. title: Dow Leads As Wall Street Ends Mixed Amid Busy Earnings Day
body: Wall Street closed mixed on Tuesday, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average rising as solid earnings from major industrial and consumer companies lifted sentiment, while weakness in tech and chip stocks weighed on the Nasdaq. The Dow added 218.16 points or 0.47% to finish at 46,924.74. The S&P 500 edged up just 0.22 points to 6,735.35, while the Nasdaq Composite slipped 36.88 points or 0.16% to 22,953.67. Among the 11 major S&P 500 sectors, consumer discretionary and industrial stocks were the top performers, while utilities suffered the largest decline. Third-quarter earnings season gathered pace with upbeat results from General Motors, Coca-Cola, 3M and GE Aerospace. General Motors lifted its forecast and downplayed its anticipated tariff hit, sending its shares up 14.9%. Coca-Cola gained 4.1% after beating expectations on strong consumer demand, while 3M surged 7.7% after raising its full-year forecast, supported by cost controls and higher-margin products. Aerospace and defence names also climbed, as Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman and RTX all raised their forecasts on the back of strong demand for war machinery. The S&P 1500 Aerospace and Defence Index advanced 1.9%. Shares of Warner Bros Discovery jumped 11% after the company announced a strategic review and said it was weighing an outright sale, having rejected an offer from Paramount Skydance. Meanwhile, Netflix fell 5.8% in after-hours trading after missing earnings targets, signalling challenges ahead for the streaming giant. So far, 78 S&P 500 companies have reported results, with 87% beating Wall Street estimates. Analysts now expect aggregate third-quarter earnings growth of 9.2% year-on-year, up from the 8.8% forecast at the start of October, according to LSEG data. Michael Green, chief strategist at Simplify Asset Management in Philadelphia, said investors appeared uncertain about the broader market direction. “We’re at a little bit of a point of indecision, where nobody feels particularly strongly about anything,” he said. “That reflects itself in reduced reaction to earnings surprise.” He added, “The earnings are better than expected as companies continue to gain slightly in terms of margins, which suggests that companies have to be passing through the tariffs or pushing the tariffs back onto the importers.” On the policy front, the US government shutdown has stretched into its third week, leaving markets without key economic data and complicating the Federal Reserve’s data-dependent decisions. A Reuters poll showed economists expect two more 25-basis-point rate cuts before the end of the year, though opinions remain split on the Fed’s 2026 outlook. President Donald Trump struck an optimistic tone ahead of his expected meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping at next week’s economic summit in South Korea, saying he expects to reach a “fair deal” while playing down tensions over Taiwan. Advancers outnumbered decliners by a 1.27-to-1 ratio on the NYSE, with 302 stocks hitting new highs. On the Nasdaq, 2,203 stocks rose while 2,454 fell. title: Wall Street Rebounds On Optimism Over Earnings, Shutdown Hopes
body: Wall Street surged on Monday as upbeat earnings and improved sentiment in the banking and technology sectors lifted investor confidence. All three major US indices closed sharply higher, led by gains in finance and tech counters. The Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed 515.97 points, or 1.12%, to 46,706.58, while the S&P 500 added 71.12 points, or 1.07%, to 6,735.13. The Nasdaq Composite advanced 310.57 points, or 1.37%, to 22,990.54. The small-cap Russell 2000 outperformed, rising 2%. Apple shares hit a record high, while Meta, Netflix and Alphabet gained between 1.3% and 3.3%. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index also touched an all-time high, closing 1.6% higher. Paul Nolte, senior wealth advisor and market strategist at Murphy & Sylvest in Elmhurst, Illinois, said, “It’s a good, solid, across-the-board move, there’s not a lot of negative in the market. There’s some relief from the financials … investors are looking at it as maybe a bit of an overreaction on the downside last week. As far as the market’s concerned, everything is wonderful again.” Among individual movers, Boeing advanced 1.8% after receiving approval from the US Federal Aviation Administration to increase 737 MAX production to 42 planes per month. WeightWatchers soared 9.3% following news of its partnership with Amazon for weight-loss drug delivery. Earnings season is now in full swing, with results from Tesla, Netflix, IBM, Intel, General Motors and Ford expected later this week, alongside several major industrials. Analysts estimate S&P 500 earnings growth of 9.3% year-on-year for the third quarter, slightly above the 8.8% projection earlier this month. “A lot of the uncertainty that the businesses were concerned about – tax legislation, the tariffs – earlier this year has subsided for the time being, and that’s allowed companies to focus on earnings and profitability,” said Matthew Keator, managing partner at the Keator Group in Massachusetts. Investor confidence was further boosted after White House economic advisor Kevin Hassett said the federal government shutdown was likely to end this week. The shutdown, now in its 20th day, has resulted in limited economic data, though the Labour Department is expected to release the September consumer price index (CPI) on Friday. The data could guide the Federal Reserve’s next move on inflation and interest rates. Trade tensions between the United States and China remained in focus as President Donald Trump hinted at easing tariffs if Beijing resumes purchases of key agricultural goods such as soybeans. Trump attributed the latest standoff to China’s rare earth export controls. Of the 11 major S&P 500 sectors, communication services recorded the strongest gains, while consumer staples and utilities edged lower. Advancers outnumbered decliners by a 4.81-to-1 ratio on the NYSE and 3.34-to-1 on the Nasdaq. The S&P 500 recorded 23 new 52-week highs and four new lows, while the Nasdaq Composite posted 77 new highs and 69 new lows. Trading volume on US exchanges reached 17.5 billion shares, below the 20-day average of 20.21 billion. title: Stock Today: EcoWorld Dips Slightly Amid Semenyih Land Acquisition
body: Eco World Development Group Bhd (EcoWorld) was trading at RM2.12 as of 11.51 am today, down 0.47% or RM0.01 from its last close of RM2.13, with a total volume of 1.47 million shares. The stock opened at RM2.13 and has fluctuated between RM2.11 and RM2.16 during the morning session, while buy orders remained thin compared with sell volume at RM2.13. The property developer is expanding its presence in Selangor’s Semenyih corridor through the acquisition of a 22.7-acre freehold commercial land parcel adjacent to its upcoming Eco Radiance township. The purchase, made via EcoWorld’s 81%-owned subsidiary Mutiara Balau Sdn Bhd, involves RM82.19 million in cash from Boustead Balau Sdn Bhd, a wholly owned unit of Boustead Properties Berhad. The newly acquired land measures approximately 92,000 square metres and will complement the 847-acre Eco Radiance mixed-development project, which has a projected gross development value of RM4.6 billion. The preliminary GDV for the new parcel is estimated at RM560 million, bringing the total combined GDV for Eco Radiance to around RM5.16 billion. EcoWorld said the addition will enhance the township’s visibility and frontage along Jalan Broga, offering potential development for retail outlets, serviced apartments, and the group’s Duduk by EcoWorld series. Funding will be sourced through internal funds, shareholders’ advances, and project-level bank borrowings, with the final mix subject to financing arrangements and gearing considerations. Investors are closely watching how the acquisition will impact EcoWorld’s overall financials, particularly as the company continues to expand its footprint in high-growth corridors within the Klang Valley. title: RHB Overweight On Property Despite Recent Sell-Down
body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has maintained its OVERWEIGHT rating on the real estate sector, viewing recent market disruptions as temporary and reiterating that the sector’s core story remains intact. The research house continues to favour Sime Darby Property Bhd and Sunway Bhd as its top picks. RHB Research noted that the mild sell-down and profit-taking activities seen in the past two weeks were largely triggered by factors such as the overhang ahead of Budget 2026, the dissolution of the Sabah state assembly, and rising trade tensions between the US and China. It believes sentiment will gradually recover, with developers likely to report stronger earnings in the third quarter of 2025. The research house said Budget 2026 appeared neutral to the sector as it offered no significant new measures. However, it highlighted the extension of full stamp duty exemptions for first-time home buyers for houses priced up to RM500,000 until 31 December 2027, as well as a flat 8% stamp duty for foreigners, up from 4% previously. While the higher rate may affect sentiment among foreign buyers, RHB Research said demand for high-end properties, particularly in Iskandar Malaysia, is unlikely to be severely impacted given the region’s ongoing infrastructure and economic catalysts. The dissolution of the Sabah state assembly earlier this month is expected to result in some near-term uncertainty. According to RHB Research, the upcoming state election, which must be held within 60 days, could weigh on sentiment temporarily. However, it expects confidence to return once the political situation stabilises, supported by the sector’s resilient fundamentals. Developers remain optimistic about the second half of 2025, RHB Research said, noting that property sales tend to strengthen during this period as companies ramp up project launches. It observed that the Iskandar Malaysia property market continues to show robust demand, particularly for township developments, mid-range high-rise residential units, commercial spaces, and industrial properties. Tier-1 developers such as Eco World Development, Sime Darby Property, and Mah Sing Group Bhd are also actively seeking new landbanks in Johor, Negeri Sembilan, and Selangor for future developments. RHB Research added that the industrial property segment continues to thrive, supported by the trade tensions between the US and China. It said foreign direct investments are increasingly flowing into Southeast Asia, with developers reporting higher enquiries from East Asia-based multinational companies looking to establish production hubs or warehouses in Malaysia. At current levels, the sector is trading at a 53% discount to its revalued net asset value (RNAV), hovering between +1 standard deviation and its long-term historical mean. RHB Research described valuations as more appealing now and believes the prevailing negative sentiment will ease as demand remains steady, aided by a stable interest rate environment and sustained investment inflows. title: MBSB Downgrades Capital A After Last Hurdle Cleared
body: MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB Research) has downgraded Capital A Bhd to NEUTRAL from Buy, maintaining its target price at RM0.95, citing that the stock is now fairly valued following the waiver of the final regulatory condition tied to its aviation unit disposal. According to MBSB Research, Capital A and AirAsia X Bhd (AAX) have agreed to waive the requirement imposed by the Thai Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) for an exemption from conducting a mandatory tender offer for Asia Aviation PCL (AAV), the Thai-listed parent of Thai AirAsia (TAA). The waiver was achieved through a new tender approach and effectively removes the last regulatory overhang, significantly de-risking the completion of Capital A’s long-awaited corporate restructuring. The research house explained that both Capital A and AAX have entered into a third supplemental agreement to the AirAsia Aviation Group Ltd (AAAGL) sale and purchase agreement, which will see the transfer of AAAGL into AirAsia Group Sdn Bhd (AAG). AAG will take over AAX’s listing status and consolidate all AirAsia-branded airlines under a single listed aviation entity. Under the revised agreement, the mandatory tender offer for AAV shares will now be undertaken jointly with a Thai partner who will fully fund and assume all acceptances. As a result, AAX’s effective 40.71% stake in AAV, held through AAAGL, will remain unchanged. AAV will continue to be listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand (SET), with no impact expected on Thai AirAsia’s operating licence or daily operations. MBSB Research noted that with the Thai regulatory issue resolved, all conditions precedent for the disposal of Capital A’s aviation unit are expected to be fulfilled by the end of October. The transaction is anticipated to be completed by December 2025, marking a key milestone in the group’s effort to exit its financially distressed PN17 status. The next steps include a RM1 billion private placement, capital reduction and distribution, and the allotment and listing of new AAG shares. Capital A is also expected to submit its PN17 uplift application by year-end and has requested to be exempted from the requirement to record two consecutive profitable quarters, having already satisfied other conditions. MBSB Research made no changes to its earnings estimates, projecting Capital A’s revenue to rise from RM22.4 billion in FY2025 to RM25.5 billion in FY2027, with net operating profit expected to increase to RM801 million over the same period. The research house concluded that while the regulatory clarity provides much-needed visibility, the current valuation reflects most of the near-term catalysts, prompting the downgrade to a Neutral stance. title: Japanese Stocks Seen Extending Rally As Takaichi Takes Helm
body: Japanese equities are expected to continue their record-breaking rally on Tuesday as investors bet that Japan’s incoming Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi will maintain expansionary fiscal policies. Nikkei futures pointed to further gains at the 9 am Tokyo open, following Monday’s record close, as Takaichi’s Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) finalised a coalition agreement with the Japan Innovation Party (Ishin). The broader Topix index remains near an all-time high. Takaichi has pledged to channel more government spending into key sectors including defence, technology, cybersecurity and nuclear energy. The LDP–Ishin coalition agreement outlines plans to boost private-public investments through responsible fiscal expansion and improve government efficiency via spending reforms. However, investors remain cautious. Japan’s sovereign bond yields have climbed to multi-year highs amid concerns that fiscal expansion could lead to excessive government borrowing. The yen traded at 150.74 against the US dollar at 7:55 a.m. in Tokyo, holding near its weakest level since February, as markets scaled back expectations of an imminent rate hike from the Bank of Japan (BOJ). “The coalition is not a green light for Takaichi to pursue the more extreme policies which investors feared during the LDP leadership election,” said James Athey, portfolio manager at Marlborough Investment Management Ltd. “Her ability to push a hugely expansionary agenda is severely limited by politics and economics, so there shouldn’t be a significant second leg of the ‘Takaichi trade’.” Despite political uncertainty, BOJ board member Hajime Takata said on Monday that “the time is ripe” for a rate hike. Yet, overnight index swaps still price in only a 25% chance of an increase this month. “I think Takaichi’s economic policy will be more balanced after the Ishin joins the government,” said Masayuki Murata, general manager of balanced portfolio investment at Sumitomo Life Insurance Co. “It will be difficult for her to block a rate hike by the BOJ by ignoring all of the BOJ’s logic.” Bloomberg Economics’ Taro Kimura noted that “Ishin’s participation could restrain fiscal largesse while keeping the door open for investment in strategic fields such as AI.” Still, questions linger over whether the LDP–Ishin coalition can maintain unity in Japan’s divided parliament and deliver on its promises without undermining fiscal credibility. title: Gold Pulls Back In Malaysia After Record Surge, Investors Take Profits
body: Gold prices in Malaysia slipped on Tuesday as investors booked profits following a record surge in the previous session, supported by expectations of further interest rate cuts by the US Federal Reserve and safe-haven demand. As of early NY trading, spot gold was down RM 5.58 per gram (-0.95%), at RM 584.41 per gram, while gold per kilo fell to RM 584,406.26. The decline follows an all-time high in US gold markets on Monday, where spot gold reached US$4,381.21 per ounce, before easing 0.3% to US$4,340.29. US December gold futures were at US$4,356.40 per ounce, down 0.1%. Tim Waterer, Chief Market Analyst at KCM Trade, said, “Profit-taking moves and an abating of safe-haven flows combined to just take the edge off the gold price today… any pullbacks on gold will be viewed as buying opportunities whilst the Fed remains on their current rate-cutting trajectory.” Investors are closely watching the US Consumer Price Index (CPI) data, expected later this week after a delay caused by the government shutdown, as it could influence Fed policy. The government shutdown has also delayed other key economic data, leaving markets in a temporary data vacuum ahead of next week’s Fed meeting. In related precious metals, silver slipped 2.66% to RM 5.88 per gram, platinum eased 0.7% to US$1,627.62 per ounce, while palladium gained 0.5% to US$1,503.17 per ounce. Global market observers also noted that ongoing trade discussions, including expected talks between US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng in Malaysia, could influence risk sentiment and commodity flows. title: Bursa Rides Wall St Wave, KLCI Opens Higher On Tech Boost
body: Bursa Malaysia opened higher tracking gains across global markets as investor sentiment improved following Wall Street’s sharp rebound overnight. title: Singapore Stocks Open Higher As Strong Exports Lift Market Mood
body: Singapore shares opened slightly higher on Oct 20, supported by stronger-than-expected export data that boosted confidence in the city-state’s trade outlook. The Straits Times Index (STI) edged up to around 4,340 points in early trade, as gains in industrial and electronics stocks offset mild weakness in banks and REITs. Analysts expect the benchmark to stay range-bound between 4,300 and 4,350 amid cautious global sentiment. Official data released on Oct 17 showed non-oil domestic exports rising 6.9% year-on-year in September, far exceeding forecasts. The rebound, driven by electronics and petrochemicals, came just days after the Monetary Authority of Singapore kept monetary policy unchanged on Oct 14, citing a steady growth outlook and manageable inflation. Earlier this year, Singapore announced a S$5 billion market development plan and tax incentives to boost stock listings and liquidity, a move seen as part of efforts to revitalise the Singapore Exchange. Analysts said sustained momentum above 4,350 could signal improving investor confidence, while a dip below 4,300 would point to lingering caution. title: Oil Prices Slip As Trade Tensions, Supply Glut Fears Weigh
body: Oil prices edged lower on Oct 20, pressured by fears of a global supply glut and renewed US-China trade tensions that heightened concerns over weaker energy demand. Reuters reported that Brent crude fell 24 cents, or 0.4%, to US$61.05 a barrel at 0032 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate slid 21 cents, or 0.4%, to US$57.33, erasing the modest gains on Oct 17. Both benchmarks lost more than 2% last week, marking a third straight weekly decline, after the International Energy Agency warned of a potential supply surplus in 2026. Trade friction between the world’s two largest oil consumers intensified as Washington and Beijing imposed additional port fees on each other’s cargo, raising risks of disrupted freight flows. The World Trade Organisation cautioned last week that prolonged decoupling could slash global output by up to 7% in the long term. On the supply front, US drillers added oil and gas rigs for the first time in three weeks, according to Baker Hughes, signalling potential output gains. Meanwhile, geopolitical uncertainty lingered after US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin agreed to hold another summit on the war in Ukraine, even as Washington pressed India and China to curb Russian oil purchases. title: Asia Stocks Climb As Earnings Optimism, Fed Cut Bets Lift Sentiment
body: Asian stocks rose on Oct 20 as investors bet on a robust corporate earnings season and further US interest rate cuts, while Chinese data due this week is expected to highlight the need for fresh stimulus, Reuters reported. Japan’s Nikkei led regional gains, jumping 1.5% after reports that the Liberal Democratic Party and Japan Innovation Party agreed to form a coalition government, paving the way for Sanae Takaichi to become the country’s first female prime minister. Markets are pricing her as pro-stimulus, a stance seen as supportive for equities but negative for the yen and bonds. Shares in South Korea added 0.6%, while MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan edged up 0.1%. Futures for Europe and Wall Street were also firmer ahead of a packed week of earnings releases. Major US companies including Tesla, Ford, GM, Netflix, Procter & Gamble, Coca-Cola, RTX, IBM and Intel are all set to report results, with analysts expecting S&P 500 earnings to have risen 8.8% year-on-year in the third quarter, according to LSEG IBES. Investors remain confident that cooling US inflation, expected to hold at 3.1% in September, will not derail the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) rate-cut trajectory. Markets are fully pricing in two quarter-point cuts by year-end, taking rates to around 3% by mid-2026. In currency markets, the dollar held steady as the yen weakened near 151 per dollar amid fading bets on a Bank of Japan rate hike. The euro hovered around US$1.165, supported by lower US bond yields. Gold prices stayed elevated at US$4,245 an oz, after surging nearly 6% last week, while Brent crude was flat at US$61.28 a barrel as ample OPEC+ supply kept oil subdued. title: Glittering Week For Gold, Rising 8% As Investors Pile Into Safe-Haven Assets
body: Gold prices skyrocketed this past week, soaring 8% to an all-time high above US$4,300 per oz, as investors piled into safe-haven assets amid renewed geopolitical tensions, a weakening US dollar and rising bets on US interest rate cuts. The precious metal opened the week on Oct 13 around US$4,079 per oz and peaked at US$4,378 per oz before settling near US$4,330 per oz on Oct 17, its strongest weekly performance in years. Analysts said the rally was driven by a combination of US-China trade friction, expectations that the Federal Reserve (Fed) may begin cutting rates soon and a broad retreat in Treasury yields that boosted the appeal of non-yielding bullion. Additionally, a weaker dollar further supported gold, making it cheaper for foreign buyers, while central bank purchases and steady physical demand added momentum. Despite the strong rally, traders cautioned that gold could face a short-term technical pullback, with prices entering overbought territory after the sharp climb. Outlook: Investors will be watching closely for signals from the Fed and moves in the dollar and bond markets, which could determine whether gold’s record-breaking run continues or cools in the coming week. title: Crypto Review: Bitcoin, Ethereum End Volatile Week On Weak Note

Bitcoin briefly rebounded to around US$115,000 on Oct 13 after plunging earlier in the week following the US’ announcement of new tariffs on China, a move that wiped billions off the global crypto market. Ethereum followed suit, jumping about 10% to over US$4,150, buoyed by technical support and derivatives unwindings. However, the rebound proved short-lived because by Oct 17, Bitcoin had fallen back to around US$104,700, marking its lowest level since June, while Ethereum slipped nearly 8%, as traders pared exposure ahead of key US economic data and lingering uncertainty around global growth. Market analysts attributed the volatility to a combination of factors including heavy leveraged liquidations, shifting expectations on US monetary policy and thin liquidity conditions following the sharp weekend sell-off. Bitcoin now faces immediate support at US$107,000, with a break below that level potentially triggering a deeper slide toward the US$90,000-US$100,000 range. Ethereum, meanwhile, needs to hold above the US$3,800-US$4,000 zone to sustain any rebound momentum. Looking ahead, traders will be watching US trade developments, macroeconomic data releases and ETF flow trends for direction in the coming week. title: Wall Street Rebounds As Trump Softens Tone On China
body: Wall Street stocks staged a solid comeback on Oct 17 after US President Donald Trump signalled a conciliatory tone toward China and investors brushed off renewed worries over regional banks. The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 0.9%, the S&P 500 rose 1.1% and the Nasdaq Composite climbed 1.3%, snapping a two-day losing streak that had been fuelled by trade tensions and banking sector concerns. In an interview with Fox Business , Trump said he planned to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping during next month’s APEC summit in South Korea, just a week after he threatened to cancel the meeting and impose hefty tariffs in retaliation for China’s rare-earth export controls. He added that higher tariffs were “not sustainable”, a remark investors read as an attempt to de-escalate tensions that have rattled global markets. Nevertheless, the more optimistic trade outlook also helped calm nerves in the banking sector. Shares of regional lenders, which were battered on Oct 16, bounced back strongly. Zions Bancorp jumped 4.8% after tumbling the day before on news of a US$50 million charge linked to troubled California commercial loans, while Western Alliance Bancorporation gained 5.1% following reassurances about its exposure to a failed borrower. The rebound came as investors reassessed fears of wider contagion in the banking system after last month’s bankruptcies of First Brands and subprime lender Tricolor. Still, sentiment overseas remained fragile as European markets closed sharply lower, with Deutsche Bank falling 6%, Societe Generale losing nearly 5% and Barclays down 5.7% amid renewed stress across the region’s lenders. In Asia, Hong Kong and Shanghai each lost more than 2%, while Tokyo also closed in negative territory. Meanwhile, a prolonged US government shutdown continues to cloud the outlook, delaying key economic reports that the Federal Reserve (Fed) uses to guide monetary policy decisions. Even so, traders are taking comfort in expectations that the Fed will likely cut interest rates at least once more this year to cushion growth. title: SGX Closes Lower On Oct 17 As Regional Headwinds, Export Data Weigh
body: Singapore’s stock market closed in the red on Oct 17, with the Straits Times Index slipping 0.6% to 4,328.93 as regional declines and investor caution dampened sentiment. Broad market breadth skewed negative, with 446 decliners against 186 gainers, and total turnover reaching S$1.6 billion. CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust bucked the trend as the top gainer on the index, rising 0.8%, while UOL Group led losses, down 2.5%. Banking stocks weighed heavily on market performance. DBS fell about 1%, OCBC dipped 0.5% and UOB lost 0.8%, reflecting persistent investor wariness about regional financial resilience. title: Hong Kong Stocks Tumble On US-China Tensions, Policy Fears
body: Hong Kong stocks suffered their steepest fall in more than six months on Oct 17, as renewed US-China tensions and caution ahead of key Chinese economic data and a major Communist Party policy meeting spurred heavy selling. The Hang Seng Index (HSI) tumbled 2.5% to 25,247.1, marking its biggest one-day decline since April 7 and extending weekly losses to 4%. The Hang Seng Tech Index slumped 4.1%, dragged by sharp losses across major technology and electronics counters. On the mainland, the CSI 300 Index dropped 2.3%, while the Shanghai Composite Index shed 2% as traders braced for next week’s raft of economic releases and policy signals from Beijing. Among Hong Kong heavyweights, BYD Electronics plunged 8.1% to HK$37.74, SMIC fell 6.5% to HK$69.10 and Alibaba lost 4.2% to HK$154.40. Tencent slipped 1.9% to HK$608 and Meituan dropped 4.3% to HK$94.50. Defying the downtrend, Hansoh Pharmaceutical gained 2.1% to HK$36.50 after licensing a new drug to Roche, while Chow Tai Fook Jewellery Group surged 5% to HK$16.52 on reports of planned price hikes. The sell-off underscores growing profit-taking pressure after the HSI rallied more than 30% this year, making it one of the world’s best-performing markets. Official data this week showing persistent deflation in China and slowing household inflows into equities further dampened sentiment. Investors are now focused on China’s third-quarter GDP, retail sales and industrial production data due Oct 20. Economists expect GDP to expand 4.7% year-on-year, the slowest pace in a year. Markets are also eyeing the Communist Party’s fourth plenary session, beginning Oct 20, where President Xi Jinping and party leaders will set economic and social development goals through 2030. Analysts expect renewed emphasis on technological self-sufficiency, debt cleanup in the property sector and fiscal reforms, with growth targets potentially easing to around 4% toward the end of the decade. Despite the pullback, Morgan Stanley said the correction may present a buying opportunity, noting that a 10%-15% decline in the MSCI China Index could be attractive given expectations for earnings upgrades and a possible Xi-Trump meeting later this month. “The market is in a consolidation phase, not a reversal. Investors should consider accumulating on dips as policy clarity emerges,” the bank said. title: Xiaomi Shares Post Worst Week In 3 Years As Accidents Stoke EV Safety Concern
body: Shares of Chinese EV maker Xiaomi suffered their biggest weekly loss in more than 3-1/2 years on Friday, after media reported two separate accidents involving its best-selling model this week. Xiaomi shares ended the day 3.7 per cent lower at HK$45.96 ($5.92), the lowest close since April 22. For the week, they tumbled 11.7 per cent, the worst such decline since late January 2022, though year-to-date, the shares are still up by a third.On Friday morning a SU7 sedan lost control in the central city of Wuhan, where it knocked down guard rails in the middle of the road, drove into the opposite lane and collided with a van, according to the Sanxiang Metropolitan Daily, a government-backed newspaper. Video from the scene circulated by the newspaper showed the car’s left front wheel axle had broken. It was not clear if there were any casualties.That followed an incident on Monday involving a 31-year-old man, suspected of drunk driving, who was killed in a collision in Chengdu. When passersby tried to pull him out of his burning SU7 Ultra they were unable to open the car doors, Chinese media reported. Xiaomi hasn’t publicly acknowledged that the accidents involved its electric vehicles. Chinese police issued a statement that detailed the Chengdu incident but did not name Xiaomi. The company didn’t respond to a request for comment. In a speech to an industry event in Beijing on Thursday, his first public appearance after the Chengdu accident, Xiaomi CEO Lei Jun made no mention of the crash, but called on the industry to focus resources and energy on technology R&D under the government’s guidance and with safety as the basis. He also urged a joint boycott of online trolls and malicious negative campaigns. The Chinese smartphone maker turned EV maker launched the SU7 in March 2024. The electric sedan had begun outselling Tesla’s Model 3 on a monthly basis since December, before handing the lead back in September. Under a product recall issued last month by the market regulator, Xiaomi announced a software update for over 115,000 SU7 sedans to fix potential safety issues when its assisted driving features are used. It saw bumper orders for its electric SUV YU7 in late June, despite a deadly crash involving an SU7 in assisted driving mode at the end of March. title: Wall Street Falls As Bank Fears And Trade Tensions Drag Markets Lower
body: Wall Street ended lower on Thursday as renewed concerns over regional banks and US-China trade tensions weighed on sentiment. Zions Bancorporation dropped 13% after reporting unexpected losses on two loans in its California division. The disclosure raised fears of hidden credit risks among lenders dealing with high interest rates. Western Alliance fell 10.8% after filing a fraud lawsuit against one of its borrowers. Investors remained cautious following the recent collapses of auto parts supplier First Brands and car dealership Tricolor. “There’s some level of minimal nervousness associated with the credit markets,” said Ron Albahary, chief investment officer at LNW in Philadelphia. “If you’ve been doing this long enough, you don’t ignore anything that might be a yellow flag in the credit markets.” The S&P 500 slipped 0.63% to 6,629.07 points, the Nasdaq fell 0.47% to 22,562.54 points, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 0.65% to 45,952.24 points. Financials led losses with a 2.75% drop, followed by energy, which lost 1.12%. Investors were also unsettled after President Donald Trump threatened to impose 100% tariffs on Chinese goods from November 1. The move came after Beijing announced export restrictions on rare earth minerals. “With the added uncertainty of US and China trade and increased rhetoric, I think that’s adding to market instability,” said Tom Hainlin, investment strategist at US Bank Wealth Management. In corporate updates, TSMC gave an optimistic forecast for AI-related spending, though shares in Palantir, Meta Platforms, and Tesla fell between 0.8% and 1.5%. Salesforce rose 4% after forecasting revenue above US$60 billion for 2030, exceeding Wall Street estimates. Among insurers, Travelers Companies lost nearly 3% after missing revenue expectations. Marsh & McLennan declined 8.5% after reporting flat margins and slower growth in its risk and insurance business. Economic data showed the Philadelphia Fed Business Index dropped 12.8 points, missing expectations for an 8.5-point rise. Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said he supported an additional rate cut in October, citing mixed signals from the labour market. Trading was active, with 22.4 billion shares exchanged compared with an average of 20.5 billion over the past 20 sessions. Declining stocks outnumbered advancers by 2.7 to one on the S&P 500, which posted 29 new highs and 16 new lows. title: Stock Today: Pharmaniaga Rises 3.77% As Investors Eye PN17 Exit
body: Shares of Pharmaniaga Bhd gained 3.77% to RM0.275 as of 11.46am, continuing their upward trend as investors remained optimistic over the company’s improving fundamentals and potential exit from Practice Note 17 (PN17) status. The counter, which opened at RM0.265 and traded between RM0.265 and RM0.280, saw an active volume of 33.39 million shares. Buy and sell quotes stood at RM0.27 and RM0.275 respectively, reflecting firm buying interest ahead of its third-quarter results. MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB Research) maintained its BUY call on Pharmaniaga with an unchanged target price of RM0.32, highlighting the group’s strengthening turnaround momentum and anticipated PN17 uplift. The research house said management remained confident of declaring dividends by FY26, targeting a payout ratio of 50% to 70% of profit after tax and minority interests (PATAMI). According to MBSB Research, the logistics and distribution segment continued to underpin growth, with SKU volumes in the first half of FY25 already surpassing full-year FY24 levels due to the activation of new government concession products under the Approved Product Purchase List (APPL). Pharmaniaga’s 3QFY25 results are expected to show improvement, supported by higher government concession orders. A moderation, however, is anticipated in the fourth quarter as public sector demand typically tapers off towards year-end. The group has also reduced borrowings by about 4% year-on-year in the first half of FY25, easing financing costs and improving its balance sheet. Progress on its insulin manufacturing facility under Pharmaniaga Lifesciences Sdn Bhd also remains on track. Equipment validation for production lines and sterile systems has been completed, with regulatory approval for commercialisation expected by the second half of 2026. Vaccine production is scheduled to follow in 2027, beginning with the PV13 vaccine before expanding to the hexavalent 6-in-1 range in 2028–29. MBSB Research noted that Pharmaniaga’s new 9,000-square-metre facility, capable of producing 2.5 million doses per month, positions it well to serve Malaysia’s demand for 25 million insulin doses annually among four million diabetic adults. On the commercial front, the group’s Human Insulin products have already secured RM3 million in tenders from teaching hospitals, while the Influenza vaccine launched in March 2025 generated RM1.5 million in sales by mid-year. Five newly launched generic drugs added RM750,000 in sales, with full-year contributions expected to reach RM3 million. MBSB Research maintained its FY25–27 forecasts and reaffirmed its positive stance on Pharmaniaga, citing its resilient concession-based revenue stream and strategic expansion into biopharmaceuticals. However, it cautioned that currency fluctuations in its Indonesian operations and uncertainties over future government contracts for insulin supply remain key risks. At the current level, Pharmaniaga offers an estimated total return potential of 18.5%, according to the research house. title: Ringgit Rallies As Markets Bet On US Rate Cut
body: The ringgit opened stronger against the US dollar on Friday, lifted by growing expectations of an imminent US interest rate cut and a broader risk-off sentiment across global markets. At 8 am, the local note advanced to 4.2160/2335 against the greenback from Thursday’s close of 4.2275/2300. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said markets were leaning towards risk aversion, as gold prices reached new highs while US Treasury yields declined. “These developments are being compounded by the ongoing US government shutdown, which has delayed key economic data releases needed for informed monetary policy decisions,” he told Bernama. He added that the US Dollar Index slipped 0.46% to 98.336, further weighing on the greenback. “With the US Federal Reserve expected to cut interest rates at the upcoming Federal Open Market Committee meeting at the end of this month, the ringgit may see further appreciation. “Additionally, the latest issues surrounding US lenders warrant closer scrutiny to assess how they might evolve and affect credit markets. Again, such news can be dollar-negative,” he said. At the opening, the ringgit traded mostly lower against major currencies except for the British pound, which firmed to 5.6663/6898 from 5.6792/6826 at Thursday’s close. title: People’s Budget Boost For 99 Speedmart
body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has maintained its BUY call on 99 Speed Mart Retail Holdings Bhd (99SMART) with a higher target price of RM3.56 from RM2.81, implying a 14% upside and a forecast dividend yield of around 2% for FY26. The research house described 99SMART as the prime beneficiary of Malaysia’s strengthening fiscal support programmes, particularly the Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) initiative, which it said could drive earnings growth and further valuation rerating. RHB Research noted that 99SMART’s outlet expansion into underserved regions continues to support a steady three-year earnings growth projection of 15%. The firm said the company’s role as one of Malaysia’s major grocery distributors should also translate to higher sales volumes as consumer sentiment normalises, especially towards popular Nestle products. According to the research house, the SARA initiative has become an increasingly preferred tool for government fiscal support. While Budget 2026 maintained the overall RM15 billion allocation for the Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and SARA programmes, RHB Research observed a shift in emphasis towards SARA. The move is seen as positive for the consumer retail sector, as more funds are channelled into groceries and daily essentials. The house estimated that over RM3 billion in 2026 will flow into the segment, boosting sales for large-cap consumer companies such as 99SMART. The research report added that 99SMART has been gaining significant market share under the SARA programme, supported by its wide network and brand strength. The faster-than-expected rollout of SARA-enabled stores and the higher budget allocation have prompted RHB Research to raise its earnings forecasts for 99SMART by 5%, 13% and 14% for FY25, FY26 and FY27 respectively. The house estimated that over 1,400 99SMART outlets have been enrolled for SARA, out of roughly 5,700 stores listed on the MyKasih website, which it noted does not yet reflect the current total of about 7,300 outlets. RHB Research said it has revised its discounted cash flow (DCF)-based valuation to RM3.56 per share, which implies a price-to-earnings ratio of 41 times for FY26. The firm made no ESG premium or discount adjustments but reflected more upbeat assumptions due to stronger fiscal tailwinds. Looking ahead, the house believes 99SMART is well-positioned to capture gains from rising disposable income among lower-income groups and the ongoing downtrading trend amid inflationary pressures. The company’s extensive store network and consumer preference for mini-markets, the house added, provide a strong foundation for continued earnings growth. It said long-term growth will likely be supported by 99SMART’s efforts to expand its market reach through diversified sourcing, improved product offerings and the development of a bulk sales platform. title: Karex OEM Business Gets Uplift From ‘Customer D’s’ Expansion Plans
body: CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) has maintained its BUY call on Karex Bhd with a target price of RM1.60, citing sustained demand for its synthetic nitrile condoms and an optimistic long-term growth outlook despite currency and tariff headwinds. The research house said the positive view followed a recent meeting with Karex Chief Financial Officer and Strategy Officer Wong Your Can, who provided updates on capacity expansion, product development and global demand trends. They also noted that Karex’s synthetic nitrile condoms, produced under an exclusive original equipment manufacturer (OEM) supply deal with a leading global brand known as Customer D, continued to see strong reorders and favourable consumer response across 18 countries. Customer D also plans to expand the rollout into key Asian markets between FY2026 and FY2028. The firm highlighted that Karex is undertaking research and development to refine its synthetic nitrile formulations based on European consumer feedback, with the goal of introducing new variants tailored for Asian markets. CIMB Securities said this would strengthen Karex’s innovation pipeline and reinforce its position in the premium condom segment. Currently, Karex operates six production lines with an annual capacity of about 150 million pieces, but the company is targeting a major scale-up. Ten additional lines are expected by the end of FY2026, followed by another ten each in FY2027 and FY2028, lifting total installed capacity to roughly 900 million pieces a year. The expansion aligns with the growing demand from Customer D and potential new OEM clients once the exclusivity period ends. According to CIMB Securities, Karex has been in talks with several global sexual wellness brands interested in OEM collaborations, underscoring its growing reputation as the world’s only manufacturer with a patented nitrile condom technology. This could pave the way for further OEM wins, especially as the broader sexual wellness market recovers and premiumisation trends accelerate. The report acknowledged some near-term challenges from the stronger ringgit against the US dollar and a 19% tariff hike on imported products from Malaysia and Thailand. CIMB said Karex remains cautious in managing these pressures, focusing on preserving long-term customer relationships and maintaining pricing stability in ongoing contracts. Nonetheless, the research firm believes these headwinds will be offset by higher-margin contributions from nitrile condoms, which deliver gross margins above 50%. This, they added, would improve the company’s overall product mix and reduce reliance on lower-margin latex-based and tender products. CIMB Securities made no changes to its earnings forecasts for FY2026–FY2028, valuing Karex at 18.8 times CY2027 price-to-earnings ratio, in line with global peers in the intimate wellness sector. The stock is currently trading at 11.6 times CY2027 P/E, which CIMB considers undemanding given its projected three-year compound annual profit growth rate of 91.3% and dividend yields of up to 5.1%. The firm cautioned that key downside risks include potential delays in expanding nitrile condom capacity, weaker US dollar performance against the ringgit, and slower-than-expected sales growth for synthetic condoms. Karex’s stock price is stable at RM0.985 as of 10.30 am. title: HSBC Forecast Gold’s Bull Rally To Hit US$5,000 In 2026
body: HSBC on Friday forecast that gold’s bull rally would drive prices as high as $5,000 an ounce in 2026, supported by elevated risks and the impact of new entrants into the market. Spot gold breached the $4,300 level on Thursday and was headed for its strongest week since December 2008.The advance has been fueled by geopolitical tensions, robust central bank buying, rising exchange-traded-fund inflows, expectations of U.S. rate cuts and tariff-related economic uncertainties. “The bull market is likely to continue to press prices higher for 1H’26 and we could very well reach a high of $5,000/oz some time in 1H 2026,” HSBC said in a research note.HSBC also raised its 2025 average gold price forecast to $3,455 per ounce from $3,355 previously. It increased its 2026 average gold price forecast to $4,600, up from its previous estimate of $3,950.The bank cited geopolitical risks, economic policy uncertainty and rising public debt as factors supporting the price. HSBC said that, given the sharp rise in prices during the second half of 2025 and heightened risks from new market entrants, it expects gold prices to remain elevated and potentially spike further through early 2026. But the bank also expects significant volatility and some price moderation in the second half of 2026. “Unlike previous rallies we believe many of these new buyers are likely stay in the gold space – even after the rally ends – not so much for appreciation necessarily as for gold’s diversification and ‘safe haven’ qualities,” the bank said. HSBC joins analysts at the Bank of America and Societe Generale, who earlier in the week forecast that gold could reach $5,000 an ounce in 2026. title: Dollar Slides Amid Fed Dovish Signals And Banking Worries
body: The US dollar fell for a fourth consecutive day, heading for its largest weekly decline in more than three months as Federal Reserve officials signalled potential rate cuts and concerns over regional banks intensified. The Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index extended its weekly loss to 0.7%, the worst since June, while two-year Treasury yields fell to a six-week low. Traders increased bets on Fed easing, pricing in 53 basis points of cuts by year-end compared with 46 on Wednesday. Fed Governor Christopher Waller said Thursday that officials could continue lowering interest rates in quarter-percentage-point increments to support a weakening labour market. Governor Stephen Miran also suggested that a move twice that size might be appropriate this month. “The lack of economic data does not seem to be a problem for the Fed and we expect another 25-basis-point rate reduction at the October meeting,” Morgan Stanley economists led by Michael Gapen wrote in a note. The dollar was further pressured as shares of US regional banks slumped amid lending-standards concerns, while easing political risks in Japan and France also weighed on safe-haven demand. Options markets reflected a shift toward near-term bearish sentiment, although positioning still favoured a stronger dollar later in the year. Investors remain cautious as the US government shutdown enters its third week, contributing to uncertainty in economic data flow. title: Bitcoin Falls Below US$109,000 As Global Risk-Off Sentiment Hits Crypto Markets

The benchmark cryptocurrency fell 2.4% to US$108,503 by midday trading, extending its weekly losses to over 10%, its sharpest pullback since March. The retreat follows a turbulent week after a US$19 billion liquidation event rattled markets and reignited anxiety over US-China trade tensions. Broader market weakness also continued to weigh on altcoins, with Ethereum sliding 2.2% to US$3,931 and XRP shedding 2.7% to US$2.36. Analysts said momentum across the crypto complex remains subdued as traders reduce exposure ahead of potential regulatory developments and macroeconomic risks. However, Solana stood out as a relative outperformer. Bitcoin’s recent decline marks a stark reversal from its record high of US$126,000 on Oct 6. The token, often viewed as digital gold, has not mirrored the rally seen in physical precious metals, with gold and silver both hitting new highs this week. title: Asian Shares Drop, Gold Hits Record On Banking Concerns
body: Asian equities slid as investors reacted to fresh signs of stress in the US banking sector, while gold reached a record before easing slightly and oil prices hit five-month lows. The developments weighed heavily on US banking stocks and pressured the U.S. dollar, boosting the yen and Swiss franc. title: Analysts Confident On Alliance’s 2Q Citing Loan Growth And Decline In NCC
body: Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) has maintained its HOLD call on Alliance Bank Malaysia Bhd (ABMB) with an unchanged target price of RM4.80, implying a potential capital upside of 7.4% and an expected total return of 11.6%. The research house said the bank’s earnings trajectory remains resilient for FY26 to FY28, supported by steady loan growth and easing credit costs. HLIB said it remains confident in ABMB’s performance ahead of its upcoming 2QFY26 results, which are expected to show resilience on a sequential basis. This outlook is driven by robust loan growth and a decline in net credit cost (NCC) from the high base in the previous quarter, which stood at 59 basis points compared with its FY26 guidance of 30 to 35 basis points. The research house noted that the bank’s loan book expansion target of 8% to 10% for FY26 remains intact, with momentum likely to pick up in the second half of the financial year as uncertainty from US tariff-related developments subsides. Both consumer and domestic SME segments continue to show healthy activity, while the bank maintains prudent oversight on its corporate exposures. HLIB added that Alliance Bank’s ability to sustain strong asset yields despite stiff competition stems from its focus on tailored services and close client relationships. This strategic positioning allows the bank to maintain a steady balance between growth and risk management. The report highlighted that net interest margin (NIM) may compress quarter-on-quarter in 2QFY26 following the Overnight Policy Rate (OPR) reduction in July, from 2.42% in 1QFY26. However, HLIB expects a positive turnaround from 3QFY26 onwards as fixed deposit repricing gradually adjusts downward. The bank’s FY26 NIM guidance of between 2.37% and 2.43% is expected to remain intact. While treasury income may ease due to higher 10-year Malaysian Government Securities yields, which climbed to 3.7% from the previous quarter’s average of 3.6%, HLIB said this will likely be offset by improving NCC and lower provisioning requirements amid a more stable operating environment. The research house made no changes to its FY26 to FY28 earnings forecasts and values ABMB at 0.95 times FY26 price-to-book, based on assumptions of 9.8% return on equity, 10.2% cost of equity, and 3% long-term growth. HLIB said the premium valuation compared with the sector’s average of 0.9 times is justified by ABMB’s superior ROE generation, which is one percentage point higher than peers over the past five years, and its consistent gain in market share. However, HLIB added that the bank’s risk-reward profile remains balanced, citing stretched valuations and a modest dividend yield of 4%. Despite these factors, it said Alliance Bank’s earnings outlook remains solid and reflective of prudent management and focused execution across key segments. As of 10.34 am, the stock price for Alliance Bank noted an increase of 0.67% to RM4.50. title: US Stocks Edge Higher As Bank And Chip Earnings Lift Sentiment
body: US stocks closed mixed on Wednesday, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq advancing as upbeat earnings from major banks and chipmakers boosted market confidence despite persistent US-China trade tensions. The S&P 500 gained 0.40% to 6,671.06 points, while the Nasdaq Composite rose 0.66% to 22,670.08. The Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped marginally by 0.04% to 46,253.31. Morgan Stanley jumped 4.7% to a record high and Bank of America climbed 4.4%, after both lenders surpassed Wall Street’s profit estimates on strong dealmaking activity. The S&P 500 banking index rose 1.2%, marking its first three-day winning streak in over three weeks. “People are spending, and the consumer seems to be fine,” said Thomas Martin, senior portfolio manager at GLOBALT in Atlanta. “Employment is not falling like a stone. Both inflation and employment are within ranges that are basically reasonable.” Chip stocks also surged as renewed optimism around artificial intelligence lifted the sector. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index gained 3% after ASML reported stronger-than-expected third-quarter orders and operating income, with its US shares rising 2.7%. Seven of the S&P 500’s 11 sectors advanced, led by real estate and utilities, which gained 1.5% and 1.29%, respectively. Meanwhile, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Washington was not seeking to escalate trade tensions with Beijing and confirmed President Donald Trump’s readiness to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping in South Korea later this month. In corporate moves, Abbott fell 2.4% after weaker-than-expected quarterly revenue, while Progressive Corp slid 5.8% on its third-quarter results. Grain trader Bunge jumped nearly 13% despite lowering its 2025 earnings outlook following its merger with Viterra. Trading volume was relatively heavy, with 21.5 billion shares changing hands on US exchanges, above the recent 20-day average of 20.4 billion. title: TSMC Posts Record Q3 Profit On AI Chip Demand Surge
body: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (TSMC), the world’s largest contract chipmaker, reported a record-breaking third-quarter net profit of T$452.3 billion (US$14.76 billion), marking a 39.1% increase from a year earlier. The figure surpassed the LSEG SmartEstimate of T$417.7 billion, which factors in projections from analysts known for higher accuracy. The company, which counts Nvidia and Apple among its biggest clients, attributed the surge to growing demand for semiconductors powering artificial intelligence technologies. TSMC continues to play a pivotal role in the global chip supply chain as tech giants ramp up investment in AI-driven applications. title: Stock Today: Genting Rises Over 4% As Prospects Brighten For New York Casino Licence
body: Genting Bhd’s share price climbed in active morning trade on Wednesday, supported by improving prospects for its United States gaming ambitions following the withdrawal of a key competitor from the Downstate New York (DNY) casino race. As of 11.53 am, the counter rose 4.12% or 14 sen to RM3.54, with 44.46 million shares changing hands. The stock opened at RM3.43 and traded between RM3.40 and RM3.59. CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) has maintained its Hold call on Genting Malaysia Bhd (GENM), the operator of Resorts World New York City (RWNYC), with a target price of RM2.35. The research house said MGM Empire City’s exit from the DNY licence bidding process significantly boosts RWNYC’s chances of securing one of up to three full casino licences to be issued by the New York Gaming Commission by year-end. CIMB Securities noted that RWNYC’s US$600 million offer for a 30-year licence, which is US$100 million higher than the minimum requirement, positions Genting favourably, particularly as it could be the sole DNY full casino operator for at least four years following MGM’s withdrawal. The firm added that this exclusivity could allow Genting to maximise gross gaming revenue during the early operational period. The brokerage, however, maintained a cautious stance, highlighting uncertainties over the final licence tenure. If the commission opts for a 15-year term instead of 30 years, applicants may revise or withdraw their bids. Still, CIMB Securities believes the odds remain strongly in Genting Malaysia’s favour given the reduced competition and its readiness to invest significantly in New York’s gaming expansion. Genting’s latest rally reflects investor optimism over the company’s overseas growth prospects, particularly in the United States, even as global economic uncertainties weigh on sentiment in other sectors. title: Ringgit Opens Firmer On Improved Market Sentiment
body: The ringgit began Thursday’s trading session on a stronger footing against the US dollar, lifted by improving domestic sentiment amid heightened global market developments. At 8 am, the local currency was quoted at 4.2220/2430 against the greenback, up from Wednesday’s closing level of 4.2305/2355. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said renewed trade tensions between the United States and China had weighed on the dollar’s strength. “The US Dollar Index (DXY) declined by 0.26% to 98.793 points, as the escalating trade conflict is expected to reinforce the case for a potential interest rate cut by the US Federal Reserve,” he said. He added that the ringgit is expected to remain firm, with the USD/MYR exchange rate likely to hover around RM4.22 to RM4.23. Despite the stronger performance against the US dollar, the local note traded mostly lower against several major currencies. It appreciated against the euro to 4.9165/9410 from 4.9213/9272 previously but slipped against the British pound to 5.6579/6860 from 5.6469/6535 and eased versus the Japanese yen to 2.7957/8097 from 2.7948/7983. Meanwhile, the ringgit gained ground across most ASEAN currencies. It strengthened against the Thai baht to 12.9708/13.0425 from 12.9933/13.0151, rose versus the Singapore dollar to 3.2585/2749 from 3.2648/2689, improved against the Indonesian rupiah to 254.7/256.0 from 255.2/255.6, and appreciated against the Philippine peso to 7.27/7.31 from 7.29/7.30. title: KLCI Edges Higher At Midday On Genting And Nestle Gains, Tracks Regional Rebound
body: Bursa Malaysia edged higher at midday, supported by buying interest in heavyweights Genting and Nestle, as regional markets staged a mild rebound following overnight gains on Wall Street. Market breadth remained positive as investors took cue from improving sentiment in Asia, where Tokyo’s Nikkei 225 and Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index both traded higher amid easing US Treasury yields and better risk appetite ahead of key earnings reports. Among the most active counters, TWL climbed 0.005 sen to 3 sen with over 504 million shares traded, followed by Genting, which gained 14 sen to RM3.54 on volume of 457 million shares. Tanco edged up 1.5 sen to 88 sen while Dnex slipped 0.5 sen to 28.5 sen. Top gainers included Nestle, which jumped RM1.50 to RM104.20, and Carlsberg, up 76 sen to RM16.18. Meanwhile, PetDag was the biggest loser, falling 52 sen to RM22.48, followed by Petron Malaysia, which eased 15 sen to RM3.69, and Kelington Group, which slipped 14 sen to RM5.70. title: Hang Seng Index Futures Find Firm Footing At 25,000, Eyes 27,400 Next
body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has maintained its long position on the Hang Seng Index Futures (HSIF), citing renewed bullish momentum as the index continues to show strong upside recovery. The research house said the HSIF gained 382 points on Wednesday to close at 25,898 points after rebounding from an intraday low of 25,328 points to reach as high as 25,996 points. In the evening session, the index slipped 50 points to last trade at 25,848 points. RHB Research noted that the white-bodied candlestick formed during the session reflected a strong intraday recovery, fuelled by buying interest near the 25,000-point support level. This, it added, confirmed the area as a firm consolidation base for the ongoing bullish setup. “The index has crossed above the 50-day simple moving average (SMA) line, indicating that bullish sentiment has returned to dominate price action,” it said. “The RSI has started trending higher, suggesting that positive momentum could persist in the near term.” With bulls regaining control, RHB Research said the next resistance is eyed at 27,400 points, followed by 28,500 points, while support levels are placed at 25,000 and 24,300 points. “We maintain a positive trading bias in view of the resumption of upward momentum,” it said, advising traders to hold the long position initiated at 21,416 points (14 April’s close) and keep the stop-loss threshold at 25,000 points to manage trading risks. title: Asian Markets Brace For Volatile Session As US-China Tensions Escalate
body: Asian stocks were set for a turbulent Thursday as investors tracked Wall Street’s swings and digested fresh signs of strain in US-China trade relations. Futures pointed to gains in Shanghai and Tokyo, while Hong Kong looked weaker and Sydney was seen flat, reflecting regional caution after President Donald Trump confirmed that the US was “now locked in a trade war with China.” Overnight, Wall Street saw sharp reversals, with the S&P 500 rising as much as 1.2% before swinging between gains and losses. The US dollar eased for a second straight day, while Treasury yields edged higher, with the two-year note closing around 3.5%. In commodities, oil rebounded from a five-month low after Trump claimed Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi had agreed to halt purchases of Russian crude, a move that could tighten global supply. Gold surged past US$4,200 an ounce for the first time as investors sought safety amid market uncertainty. Traders are now betting on at least one aggressive Federal Reserve rate cut by year-end to cushion potential economic fallout. Meanwhile, Chinese Premier Li Qiang is expected to visit Singapore later this month, signalling efforts to strengthen regional ties.
