title: Repayment By Major Borrower Could Lift RHB’s FY25 ROE
body: CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) has reaffirmed its BUY call on RHB Bank Bhd with a target price of RM7.35, citing the bank’s improving earnings profile and sustainable long-term returns under its PROGRESS27 strategy. The research house noted that RHB is on track to achieve its return on equity (ROE) target of at least 12% by 2027, supported by tactical initiatives in credit recovery, cost control and balance sheet optimisation. Following a recent meeting with the bank, CIMB Securities raised its FY25 net profit forecast by 3% to reflect lower credit provisions, after factoring in a planned repayment by a major oil and gas borrower. The revision lifted its FY25 ROE forecast from 9.2% to 9.5%, with dividend per share increased to 44 sen from 43 sen. The house maintained forecasts for FY26 and FY27, projecting steady NIMs of around 1.8%, loan growth of 5% and dividend yields between 6.6% and 6.9%. The brokerage said that RHB’s tactical realisation of fair value through other comprehensive income (FVOCI) gains could strengthen liquidity and non-interest income in the second half of 2025. Reserves of around RM600 million provide flexibility for the bank to capitalise on rate easing while redeploying proceeds into higher-yielding loans for SMEs and mid-market clients. CIMB Securities also highlighted RHB’s strong performance in wealth management through bancassurance and structured investment sales. Partnerships with Tokio Marine and Syarikat Takaful Malaysia have enabled the bank to expand insurance and advisory offerings, while assets under management have grown to RM47.3 billion as of June 2025, with expectations to surpass RM50 billion by year-end. On margins, RHB’s FY25 net interest margin guidance remains unchanged at 1.80% to 1.83%, following July’s overnight policy rate cut. The bank aims to cushion NIM pressures through portfolio rebalancing, focusing on higher-yielding loans and managing costly deposits. Its strong funding position, reflected by a loan-to-fund ratio of 82%, is further supported by RM1.3 billion in upfront access fees from long-term bancassurance deals. CIMB said the group’s disciplined RM500 million cost takeout plan by 2027 is a key part of maintaining operational efficiency, targeting a cost-to-income ratio of below 45%. Leveraging AI and automation to enhance productivity and reduce manual processes, RHB expects to optimise headcount while sustaining service quality. The research house believes that capital optimisation, higher dividends and RHB’s sustainability agenda will continue to attract investors. RHB aims to mobilise RM90 billion in sustainable finance by 2027, with RM48 billion already achieved as of June 2025. The bank’s solid CET1 ratio of 15.9% also supports a payout ratio of about 60%. CIMB concluded that RHB’s valuation, trading at 0.86 times FY25 forecasted price-to-book value, remains appealing relative to peers. With rising returns, prudent credit management and alignment with Malaysia’s “Just Transition” sustainability goals, the bank is well-positioned for steady earnings expansion through FY27. title: Banking Boost Lifts Dow As Trade Tensions Cap Wall Street Gains
body: Wall Street ended mixed on Tuesday as investors balanced upbeat earnings from major US banks, remarks by Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell, and renewed tensions between Washington and Beijing. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.44% to 46,270.46, supported by strength in industrial stocks. The S&P 500 slipped 0.16% to 6,644.31, while the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.76% to 22,521.70. Ten of the eleven S&P 500 sectors advanced, led by consumer staples which climbed 1.72%, followed by a 1.17% gain in industrials. Banking stocks led gains, with Wells Fargo jumping 7.15%, its biggest one-day rise since November 2024, and Citigroup climbing almost 4% after both beat expectations for third-quarter profit. JPMorgan Chase raised its full-year net interest income forecast, while Goldman Sachs reported stronger-than-expected earnings though both shares slipped around 2%. BlackRock hit a record US$13.46 trillion in assets under management, boosting its shares by more than 3%. The S&P 500 banking index rose sharply on the back of these results, reflecting optimism in the sector’s investment banking performance. Advancing issues outnumbered decliners on the S&P 500 by a 3.4-to-one ratio, while the Nasdaq recorded 123 new highs and 93 new lows. Renewed trade tensions kept investors cautious. title: Wall Street Bounces Back As Trump Softens China Tone
body: Wall Street staged a sharp rebound on Monday as investors reacted positively to US President Donald Trump’s conciliatory remarks about trade tensions with China. The S&P 500 jumped 1.56% to 6,654.72, while the Nasdaq advanced 2.21% to 22,694.61, marking its strongest single-day gain since May. The Dow Jones Industrial Average also climbed 1.29% to close at 46,067.58. Chipmakers and AI-related tech counters spearheaded the rally. Broadcom surged nearly 10% following its partnership with OpenAI to produce the startup’s first in-house artificial intelligence processors. Nvidia and Micron Technology added 2.8% and over 6% respectively, sending the PHLX chip index up almost 5%. Oracle gained 5.1% after brokerages raised price targets, while Estee Lauder rose 5.8% on an upgrade by Goldman Sachs. The upbeat mood came after Trump sought to calm markets, saying over the weekend that “it will all be fine” and that the US did not wish to “hurt” China. His statement came days after escalating tensions, when he announced plans to impose 100% tariffs on Chinese imports and new export controls on critical US-made software from 1 November. China had earlier moved to tighten rare earths export restrictions but refrained from further countermeasures following Trump’s remarks. Adding to optimism, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Fox Business Network that Trump was expected to meet his Chinese counterpart in South Korea soon to discuss ways to de-escalate the dispute. “AI continues to be the momentum driver, and it’s not surprising investors have purchased the dip,” said CFRA Research Chief Investment Strategist Sam Stovall. He added, however, that caution remains warranted until the trade conflict sees concrete resolution. After last week’s selloff, when the S&P 500 and Nasdaq suffered their steepest declines in months, ten of eleven S&P 500 sectors turned positive, led by information technology and consumer discretionary stocks. The index now sits about 1.5% below its record high reached on 8 October. Investors are also turning their attention to upcoming corporate earnings, with JPMorgan Chase, Goldman Sachs, Citigroup, and Wells Fargo set to report on Tuesday, kicking off the quarterly season. title: Ringgit Extends Gains On BNM Optimism And Fed Shift Hopes
body: The ringgit strengthened against the US dollar early Tuesday, buoyed by improved domestic sentiment following upbeat comments from Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) and renewed expectations of a possible shift in US Federal Reserve policy. At 8am, the local currency stood at 4.2220/2315 against the greenback, appreciating from Monday’s close of 4.2265/2295. Analysts said the ringgit’s firm tone reflected growing investor confidence amid signs that monetary tightening in the US may be nearing its end. Market optimism picked up after BNM governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour remarked that the ringgit has potential to strengthen to RM4 against the dollar by year-end. His statement helped shore up confidence in the local unit, which has been under pressure from external headwinds in recent weeks. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid noted that while the US Dollar Index (DXY) remains firm amid the ongoing US government shutdown, the rally may not be sustainable. He said Philadelphia Federal Reserve President Anna Paulson had hinted that interest rates should move towards a more neutral level, as the inflationary impact from tariffs appeared manageable. “As such, the rise in DXY seems unsustainable. Should the US government shutdown be resolved, DXY could experience a correction,” he said. “For now, it remains dollar-positive. Hence, the US dollar-ringgit pair is expected to hover around RM4.22 today,” Mohd Afzanizam told Bernama. The ringgit also advanced against a basket of major and regional currencies. It rose to 4.8832/8942 versus the euro from 4.9006/9041 and strengthened against the Japanese yen to 2.7694/7758 from 2.7775/7796. The local note improved to 5.6292/6419 against the British pound from 5.6369/6409. title: Gold Could Hit US$5,000 As Bank Of America Turns Bullish
body: Bank of America (BofA) has raised its 2026 price outlook for gold to a record US$5,000 an ounce, with an average forecast of US$4,400, while also upgrading its projection for silver to US$65 an ounce, averaging US$56.25. The US lender said that despite the risk of a near-term correction, it still expects further upside for both metals next year. In a note released on Monday, the bank said the White House’s “unorthodox policy framework” would likely remain supportive for gold, given ongoing fiscal deficits, rising debt levels, efforts to narrow the current account deficit, and a push to cut interest rates even as inflation stays around 3%. BofA is the first major financial institution to project a US$5,000-per-ounce target for gold by 2026. Spot gold recently surpassed the US$4,000 level and traded at US$4,073.69 per ounce as of 10:10 GMT, marking a 55% gain so far this year. The bank added that a further rally to US$6,000 would require investors to increase their gold holdings by at least 28%. Silver, meanwhile, is expected to remain resilient despite an anticipated 11% drop in demand next year, supported by ongoing supply shortages. The Silver Institute has projected a structural market deficit for the fifth consecutive year. BofA noted that the recent transfer of silver inventories from London to New York, in anticipation of tariffs that ultimately did not materialise, has tightened the London market significantly—reflected in higher lease rates. “There is scope for recent dislocations to slowly start to normalise, which could then also increase volatility and put pressure on silver quotations near-term,” the bank said. Spot silver recently climbed to a record US$51.70 per ounce, while December 2025 Comex silver futures traded at US$49.72. title: Genting Takeover, Analysts Advising To Accept Offer
body: Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) has upgraded Genting Malaysia Bhd to ACCEPT from Maintain with a revised target price of RM2.35, while maintaining a BUY call on Genting Bhd (GenT) with a lower target price of RM3.75. The research house’s call comes after Genting announced plans to undertake a RM6.7 billion unconditional voluntary takeover offer for all remaining shares in GenM that it does not already own. GenT, which currently holds a 49.4% stake in GenM, offered RM2.35 per share, representing a 9.8% premium to GenM’s last closing price of RM2.14. HLIB advised existing GenM shareholders to accept the offer, noting that the price is higher than its previous sum-of-parts (SOP)-derived target price of RM2.06, representing a 14.1% premium. Completion of the offer is expected by the fourth quarter of 2025. According to HLIB, the takeover will only become unconditional once GenT’s total shareholding exceeds 50% of GenM’s issued shares, excluding treasury shares. The offer document is set to be dispatched to shareholders within 21 days of the announcement, after which the acceptance period will remain open for at least 21 days. GenT has also indicated that it is not desirous of maintaining GenM’s listing status on Bursa Malaysia, suggesting a potential delisting post-acquisition. HLIB said the rationale for the takeover centres on GenM’s subsidiary, Genting New York LLC, being one of four remaining contenders for up to three downstate New York gaming licences. Should the group secure the licence, the project would require substantial capital investment. The research house noted that full control of GenM would strengthen GenT’s financial position and network to support this development. The total cash consideration will be financed through up to RM6.3 billion in debt and internally generated funds. HLIB noted that this would lift GenT’s FY26 net gearing ratio from 0.21 times to 0.32 times, while slightly reducing its FY26 profit after tax and minority interests (PATMI) by RM3.5 million, or around 0.4% of its forecast. This is mainly due to higher interest expenses and associated one-off costs of RM90 million. Despite the near-term financial strain, HLIB maintained a neutral stance on the offer price, highlighting potential value accretion if GenM successfully secures the New York casino licence. “The acquisition price of RM2.35 per share, while above our previous SOP-derived valuation, could appear reasonable given that a full casino licence could unlock an additional RM0.31 per share in value,” it said. The research house continues to favour GenT for its diversified global operations that help mitigate regulatory and country-specific risks. It also sees potential upside from TauRx Pharmaceuticals should its Alzheimer’s drug HMTM receive US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval. Forecasts for both GenT and GenM remain unchanged pending the completion of the takeover offer. title: Asian Stocks Slide Amid Renewed China-US Trade Tensions
body: Asian equities fell sharply on Tuesday (Oct 14) after China imposed sanctions on US subsidiaries of South Korea’s Hanwha Ocean, reigniting trade war concerns that had appeared to ease over the weekend. The sell-off hit Tokyo hardest, compounded by domestic political uncertainty. Questions have arisen over Sanae Takaishi’s prospects of becoming Japan’s first female prime minister following the collapse of the ruling coalition after junior partner Komeito withdrew support. Earlier, markets had rallied on hopes of a thaw in US-China trade tensions. Traders were buoyed on Sunday when former US President Donald Trump posted on social media, insisting that “it will all be fine” and that he wanted to “help” China, prompting US stocks to climb. However, Asia’s recovery proved short-lived. Beijing accused five US subsidiaries of Hanwha Ocean of assisting Washington’s Section 301 investigation into the shipping industry, calling the probe a threat to China’s sovereignty and the rights of Chinese enterprises. The investigation earlier this year concluded that US-imposed port fees on Chinese ships were justified, prompting retaliatory measures by China. Markets across the region retreated, with Hong Kong down nearly 2%, while Shanghai, Singapore, Seoul, Wellington, Taipei, Mumbai, Bangkok, and Jakarta also fell. Shares of Hanwha dropped more than 5% in Seoul. Neil Wilson of Saxo Markets noted, “Given the recent rally, positioning was stretched… any bad news is a cue to sell risk … which indicates the market is looking for an excuse for a selloff.” Analysts also highlighted concerns over an AI-driven equity rally this year, with fears that some markets may have reached bubble territory. Tokyo’s benchmark index tumbled 3% at one point as investors returned from a long weekend, weighing the political upheaval that could thwart Takaichi’s premiership. Hopes of stimulus measures and looser monetary policies that had boosted stocks after her election now face uncertainty as opposition groups seek to block her. In commodities, gold and silver declined from record levels, with silver earlier hitting US$52.90 and gold reaching a peak of US$4,179.70. Oil prices also fell amid renewed concerns over a potential trade war escalation between China and the US. Related The sell-off hit Tokyo hardest, compounded by domestic political uncertainty. title: US Futures Rebound As Trump Hints At Possible China Deal
body: US stock futures climbed on Monday after President Donald Trump signalled openness to a potential trade deal with China, easing fears following the worst market drop since April. Contracts on the S&P 500 rose 0.9% while Nasdaq 100 futures gained 1.2% as investors saw signs of a possible thaw in trade tensions. The rebound comes after Trump’s administration announced new tariffs and export restrictions on Chinese goods last Friday, triggering a sharp selloff that wiped 2.7% off the S&P 500 and 3.5% from the Nasdaq 100. Trump’s latest remarks hinted at a diplomatic off-ramp for Chinese President Xi Jinping, though he warned that a full-blown trade war would severely impact China. His comments followed US Vice President JD Vance’s statement urging Beijing to “choose the path of reason.” “The market’s instinct remains to buy the dip,” said Roundhill chief executive officer Dave Mazza. “After an extended rally, markets needed a reason to cool off, and President Trump’s tariff headlines provided it.” Last week’s escalation began after Beijing introduced new port fees on US ships and launched an antitrust probe into Qualcomm Inc., following Washington’s latest trade restrictions. In response, Trump announced a 100% tariff on Chinese imports and export controls on critical software starting November 1, a move seen as retaliation for China’s curbs on rare-earth exports essential to US tech firms. Friday’s selloff was broad-based, hitting semiconductors, consumer and financial stocks. Amazon fell 5%, Best Buy dropped 6.4%, and the VIX volatility index spiked near a four-month high of 22. Analysts at Goldman Sachs said the slump reflected a rush to hedge positions rather than a full exit from equities. Despite the turbulence, investors are turning their attention to the third-quarter earnings season starting Tuesday with reports from JPMorgan Chase and other major banks. “Markets were overdue for a pullback both in positioning and seasonality,” said Frank Monkam, head of macro strategy at Buffalo Bayou Commodities. “Earnings season will ultimately dictate the depth of the dip.” While many see the selloff as a temporary correction, others warn that rising geopolitical risks could strain an overvalued market. “The market has been priced for perfection,” said Matt Maley, chief market title: Stock Today: MCE Eases 0.6% Amid Strong EV Policy Tailwinds
body: Shares of MCE Holdings Bhd (MCE) slipped 0.6% to RM1.70 at mid-afternoon trade despite strong earnings prospects tied to Malaysia’s growing electric vehicle (EV) ecosystem. At 3.37pm, the counter eased 1 sen with 141,400 shares changing hands. It traded between RM1.66 and RM1.70 during the session, with the last close at RM1.71. Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) has maintained its BUY rating on MCE with an unchanged target price of RM2.40, citing multiple policy tailwinds expected to support the group’s growth. According to the research house, the end of excise duty exemptions for fully imported EVs next year while maintaining those for locally assembled EVs until end-2027 will boost demand for national carmakers such as Perodua. This is set to benefit MCE, a key supplier of infotainment and advanced driver-assistance system components for Perodua’s upcoming locally assembled EV. HLIB also noted that localisation incentives and the vehicle scrapping scheme under Budget 2026, which offers up to RM4,000 for replacing vehicles over 20 years old, could spur production for national carmakers Proton and Perodua. Collectively, they account for about 80% of MCE’s revenue. The research house said the company’s strong cash position of RM73.3 million or 50.5 sen per share provides room for expansion and steady dividend payouts. HLIB projects a dividend yield of 5.3% for FY2026, supported by expectations of an earnings rebound as Malaysia’s EV localisation accelerates. MCE currently trades at about 15 times mid-FY27 earnings, with analysts viewing it as an under-the-radar proxy to Perodua’s EV development amid Malaysia’s early-stage transition to electric mobility. title: Stock Today: Heineken Malaysia Slips 1.63% Amid Market Reaction To Upcoming Excise Duty Hike
body: Shares of Heineken Malaysia Bhd (HEIM) slipped 1.63% to RM20.46 as at 2.33pm today, reflecting mild investor caution ahead of the upcoming 10% excise duty hike on alcoholic beverages set to take effect on November 1 under Budget 2026. The counter, which opened at RM20.50, traded between RM20.34 and RM20.68, with 239,400 shares changing hands. Its last closing price was RM20.80. RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has maintained its BUY call on Heineken with a revised target price of RM26.50, implying a 27% upside potential and an estimated 8% yield for FY2026. The research house said the excise duty increase has largely been priced in, given the stock’s current valuation levels below historical averages. “While the excise duty increase poses a short-term challenge, demand is expected to normalise over time,” RHB Research said, adding that margin expansion and premiumisation strategies remain key drivers for earnings and dividend growth. The firm noted that brewers are likely to pass the additional costs to consumers through 4–5% adjustments in average selling prices (ASP). It also expects frontloaded sales in October as retailers and distributors stock up ahead of the duty hike. Despite trimming its FY2026–FY2027 earnings forecasts by 4% and 3% respectively to reflect softer volume assumptions, RHB Research remains optimistic, citing firm profit margins supported by cost efficiency, favourable input prices and stable foreign exchange trends. The research house also expects Visit Malaysia Year 2026 to spur beer demand through increased tourist arrivals. However, it cautioned that a rise in the contraband trade, currently estimated at 25% of the market, and weak consumer sentiment could weigh on performance. title: Budget 2026 Hopes Keep Ringgit Anchored At RM4.22
body: The ringgit opened unchanged against the US dollar on Monday as optimism from Budget 2026 helped cushion the local currency against sustained demand for the greenback. At 8 am, the ringgit stood at 4.2200/2260 against the US dollar, the same level recorded at Friday’s close. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the government’s fiscal discipline reflected in Budget 2026 could lend some support to the ringgit after recent corrections. “Perhaps there could be some support for the ringgit after experiencing a correction. He noted that the fiscal deficit is projected to narrow further to 3.5% of gross domestic product in 2026 from 3.8% this year. title: Bitcoin, Ethereum Lead US$19 Billion Crypto Wipeout Amid Liquidity Shock
body: Bitcoin and Ethereum bore the brunt of a sharp crypto market selloff on Oct 10 that triggered over US$19 billion in liquidations, marking one of the most severe intraday meltdowns this year. Bitcoin plunged as much as 12% while Ethereum tumbled 20% in a rapid cascade of forced selling before both partially recovered. The crash, which also sent Solana down 24.6%, was sparked by renewed US-China trade war fears following former US president Donald Trump’s threat to impose a 100% tariff on Chinese imports and Beijing’s countermeasures restricting rare earth exports. “The selloff was a textbook example of how fragile crypto market liquidity can be,” Derive.xyz founder Nick Forster said. He added that when volatility spikes and market makers pull back, order books thin out dramatically. In that environment, forced liquidations snowball and even modest sell orders can cause violent price dislocations. According to Derive.xyz data, implied volatility across Bitcoin and Ethereum options surged across all maturities, a sign traders expect prolonged turbulence rather than a quick rebound. “Typically, volatility spikes in short-dated options (one to seven days to expiry) during market stress. But on Oct 10, volatility increased across both short- and long-dated expiries, indicating broader uncertainty. “We saw traders aggressively buying puts not just for immediate protection but also for medium-term coverage. The cross-expiry volatility shift shows the market now expects choppier conditions extending into year-end,” Forster noted. In the Bitcoin options market, traders bought US$115,000 and US$95,000 puts for the Oct 31 expiry, while call selling concentrated around the US$125,000 strike for Oct 17, pointing to a bearish short-term bias. For Ethereum, flows centred on US$4,000 and US$3,600 puts for October, while notable demand emerged for US$2,600 puts expiring Dec 26, suggesting rising caution toward Ethereum’s medium-term outlook. Forster said the trigger, renewed geopolitical tension, exposed deeper structural weaknesses in crypto’s liquidity profile. “The underlying issue isn’t just macro fear; it’s the fragility of crypto liquidity,” he said. “When macro shocks hit and derivatives leverage is high, price cascades like Oct 10’s are inevitable. Until market depth improves, Bitcoin and Ethereum will remain vulnerable to these liquidity vacuums.” Despite partial recovery over the weekend, both Bitcoin and Ethereum remain volatile, with traders bracing for further swings amid heightened global uncertainty. title: Weekly Review: Singapore Shares Ease As Investors Turn Cautious
body: Singapore shares ended the trading week slightly lower as investors locked in profits and adopted a cautious stance ahead of key global economic data and inflation readings. The Straits Times Index (STI) fluctuated in a narrow band throughout the week of Oct 6-10, closing marginally weaker after retreating from early gains. The benchmark began the week on a firmer footing, rising 0.2% to around 4,421 points on Oct 6, supported by buying interest in banking and real estate counters. However, midweek selling pressure emerged as traders turned defensive amid mixed regional cues and profit-taking. Market sentiment softened further on Oct 10, with investors trimming exposure to cyclical and growth stocks in favour of yield-oriented and defensive plays such as real estate investment trusts (REITs) and utilities. Analysts described the week as a “healthy consolidation phase” following recent strength in local equities. Financial stocks continued to anchor the STI, with DBS Group Holdings, OCBC Bank and UOB attracting steady institutional interest amid stable earnings prospects and dividend yields. In contrast, the technology sector came under pressure after AEM Holdings faced patent-infringement allegations, which weighed on sentiment toward chip-related counters. The company denied the claims, but the uncertainty added a layer of caution for investors. REITs and infrastructure players saw renewed buying interest, buoyed by expectations that stable yields could outperform in a higher-for-longer interest rate environment. Overall, Singapore equities tracked a softer tone across Asia as concerns over US interest rates, China’s economic outlook and global inflation data dampened risk appetite. Regional markets were broadly mixed, with foreign fund flows remaining uneven across ASEAN exchanges. Looking ahead, traders are expected to monitor upcoming US inflation figures, regional earnings reports and foreign fund flows for cues on near-term direction. Despite the subdued finish, analysts remain cautiously optimistic about Singapore’s medium-term outlook, citing resilient banking earnings, robust fiscal fundamentals and steady investor appetite for dividend and REIT plays. body: South Korean shares rallied this week, with the Kospi breaking above the 3,600 level as investors returned from the Chuseok holidays with renewed risk appetite and optimism over semiconductor demand. Sentiment was further supported by the government’s decision to delay a planned capital gains tax hike, easing investor concerns over equity market policy. Technology and semiconductor heavyweights powered the rally, with Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix leading advances on expectations of stronger global demand for memory chips in the final quarter of 2025. The KOSDAQ, which tracks smaller and tech-heavy firms, also gained momentum, reflecting broad confidence in the sector’s earnings prospects. Financials and consumer-related stocks added support, benefitting from improved domestic consumption trends following the extended holiday period. Analysts noted that overall trading sentiment remained upbeat, underpinned by Korea’s reputation as one of Asia’s best-performing equity markets this year. Despite these cautionary signals, the Seoul market ended the week on a strong footing, buoyed by foreign inflows, earnings optimism and domestic policy stability. title: Wall Street Sinks As Trump Escalates Trade War With China
body: Wall Street tumbled on Oct 10 after US President Donald Trump abruptly intensified his trade confrontation with China, rattling investors and sending technology stocks sharply lower. Reuters reported that the Dow Jones Industrial Average plunged 878.82 points, or 1.9%, to 45,479.6, while the S&P 500 slid 2.71% to 6,552.51 and the Nasdaq Composite sank 3.56% to 22,204.43, their steepest one-day drops since April 10. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index nosedived 6.3%, extending losses after the closing bell. Trump announced late on Oct 10 that the US will impose an additional 100% tariff on Chinese imports and introduce export controls on key US-made software, hours after Beijing tightened restrictions on rare earth exports, a critical component in high-tech and defence industries. The move deepened fears of renewed trade hostilities between the world’s two largest economies. The announcement sent Nvidia, Tesla, Amazon and AMD down more than 2% in after-hours trading, compounding losses from the regular session. Shares of Chinese tech majors Alibaba, JD.com and PDD Holdings plunged between 5% and 8.5%, while Qualcomm fell 7.3% after China’s regulator opened an antitrust probe into its proposed acquisition of Israel’s Autotalks. The sell-off on Oct 10 capped the S&P 500’s worst week since May and the Nasdaq’s sharpest weekly drop since April, as Trump’s renewed trade offensive reignited fears of global economic disruption. Analysts warned that escalating tariffs and supply chain risks could hit sectors reliant on rare earth materials, including electric vehicles, semiconductors and aerospace. Meanwhile, the US government entered its 10th day of a partial shutdown, delaying official economic data releases and leaving investors to rely on private surveys. Federal Reserve officials maintained a cautious tone on interest rates. Investors will next turn their focus to the start of third-quarter earnings season next week, with major banks including JPMorgan Chase, Goldman Sachs, Citigroup and Wells Fargo set to report on Oct 14. Analysts expect S&P 500 earnings to rise 8.8% year-on-year, down from 13.8% growth in the prior quarter, according to LSEG data. title: Hang Seng Falls 1.7% As Tech Stocks Slide, Trade Fears Resurface
body: Hong Kong equities posted a sharp reversal of recent gains, with the Hang Seng Index down 1.73% to close the trading session on Oct 10 at 26,290.32, extending losses into a fifth straight session. The Hang Seng Tech Index tumbled even harder, slipping about 3.27% as major technology and semiconductor names came under pressure. Heavyweights such as Alibaba dropped more than 4%, while SMIC declined over 7%, reflecting a broad pullback in artificial intelligence (AI), chip and export-sensitive themes. The Hang Seng China Enterprises Index also slipped, down ~1.8%, illustrating the spillover to mainland-exposed names. Weakness in tech and semiconductor names led declines, while a few property and consumer stocks bucked the trend. For instance, Hang Lung Properties gained ~2%, aided by solid tenant sales during the recent holiday stretch. Meanwhile, Poly Property jumped ~19.5% on news of equity restructuring. The selloff was partly driven by heightened fears of renewed US tariff escalation on China, strengthening the negative correlation between Hong Kong’s tech names and global macro risk. Markets earlier took cues from a downbeat Wall Street session, where tech names led the retreat. Investor caution was amplified as valuations in AI and chip sectors are now under scrutiny given recent warnings of overextension in those themes. The near-term trajectory for Hong Kong equities will hinge heavily on developments in US-China policy, trade headlines and any fresh regulatory steps in Beijing. On the domestic front, property default risk and liquidity conditions will remain focal. Should markets digest the current negative tone without fresh catalysts, further downside cannot be ruled out, especially in tech and high-beta names. title: Bitcoin Tumbles As Trump’s China Tariff Escalation Sparks Global Market Sell-Off

Reuters reported that the world’s largest cryptocurrency by market value fell 8.4% to US$104,782 as of 5:20pm ET (2120 GMT), while Ethereum, the second-largest token, dropped 5.8% to US$3,637. The move deepened fears of an all-out trade war and sent shockwaves through global financial markets. Risk appetite evaporated across asset classes, with the S&P 500 Index sliding more than 2% and tech stocks bearing the brunt of the sell-off. Bitcoin, often seen as a proxy for broader risk sentiment, mirrored the downturn as traders sought safety in cash and US Treasuries. The latest drop extends Bitcoin’s volatile run over the past month as investors grapple with shifting macroeconomic conditions, central bank policy uncertainty and renewed geopolitical stress. title: Ringgit Holds Steady Ahead Of Budget 2026 Tabling

title: Yen’s Haven Appeal Weakens As Confidence Fades
body: The Japanese yen’s long-held status as a global safe-haven asset is losing ground. Investors are turning cautious as political uncertainty and doubts over the Bank of Japan’s (BOJ) next move weigh on confidence. The currency slipped to an eight-month low after Sanae Takaichi’s surprise victory in the ruling party leadership race raised concerns over a continued pro-stimulus stance. For years, the yen was seen as a safe retreat during financial crises. Japan’s strong current-account surplus and political stability made it a dependable hedge when global markets fell. That perception is now fading as the yen behaves less predictably against risk assets. “Historically, there were times we went long the yen from a hedging perspective,” said Keiko Kondo, head of multi-asset investments for Asia at Schroder Investment Management. “Currently, we don’t have enough reasons to be wanting that hedge,” she said, citing higher costs and lower reliability. Recent data shows that the dollar-yen pair no longer moves consistently with global sentiment. At times, it strengthens when risk appetite rises and weakens during selloffs. The BOJ’s cautious approach to tightening has added to uncertainty. “I’m not using the yen as a risk barometer much anymore,” said Ken Peng, head of investment strategy for Asia at Citigroup Inc. “The yen has become more of a reflection of expectations about how much the BOJ will hike rates.” Speculative pressure continues to grow. Asset managers have reduced net long positions by about 40% since April, while hedge funds are now shorting the currency. The yen remains one of the weakest G-10 performers this year despite brief gains against the dollar. Some analysts believe the weakness may not last. “While the so-called ‘Takaichi trade’ is tilted toward yen weakness, it is regarded as temporary,” said Hirofumi Suzuki, chief FX strategist at Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corp. He added that a move toward 160 per dollar could prompt intervention. For now, the yen’s appeal as a safe-haven asset is fading. Investors are choosing other options such as gold and the Swiss franc as Japan’s currency becomes less dependable in times of global uncertainty. title: HLIB Downgrades Pavilion REIT Post Rally
body: Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) has downgraded Pavilion Real Estate Investment Trust (Pavilion REIT) to HOLD from Buy, despite raising its target price to RM1.85 from RM1.77. The research house said the recent rally in Pavilion REIT’s share price, which closed at RM1.95, has made its risk-reward balance less compelling, even as operational and cost factors continue to improve. HLIB said Pavilion REIT’s outlook remains resilient, supported by the rebranding of Da Men Mall into Easyhome Mall and the easing of financing and electricity costs. The rebranding effort, through a master lease agreement with China-based Easyhome International, marks a turnaround for the Subang Jaya asset, which has been loss-making since 2020. Easyhome took over operations in April and has begun refurbishment works, with the mall expected to reach breakeven from October. The research house noted that Easyhome Mall’s current occupancy stands at about 33%, with anchor tenants such as Jaya Grocer and Big Pharmacy continuing operations during the transition. HLIB viewed the new arrangement positively, citing its potential to stem net property income erosion and allow for future profit sharing should performance exceed expectations. On the cost side, HLIB said Pavilion REIT is expected to benefit from margin support following a 25-basis-point cut in the Overnight Policy Rate (OPR) in July 2025. With roughly 80% of borrowings on floating rates, the REIT could see financing costs decline by around 20 basis points, translating to annual savings of approximately RM6 million, or 1.6% of forecast FY26–27 earnings. Electricity costs have also eased, with the management reporting savings of around RM100,000 monthly between June and August. While the new 8% sales and service tax (SST) may pose a mild headwind, management remains confident that resilient traffic and a stronger tenant mix will sustain the REIT’s performance. Footfall and tenant sales have shown no signs of weakening since the SST implementation. Pavilion Bukit Jalil, one of its key assets, continues to perform strongly, with occupancy at 90% and on track to reach 95% by year-end, supported by rising interest from Chinese retailers. Reflecting the lower financing and operating costs, HLIB has raised its earnings forecasts for Pavilion REIT by 1.0%, 2.6%, and 2.5% for FY25, FY26, and FY27 respectively. The research house maintained that Pavilion REIT’s prospects remain underpinned by a favourable tourism outlook, which should continue to boost footfall and tenant spending across its portfolio, including Pavilion KL and Pavilion Elite. However, after a sharp rally in share prices, HLIB said the valuation has caught up, leading to its downgrade to Hold. As of 11 am, the stock price noted a decrease of 1.03% (RM1.930). title: Driving Investment Into MVV Techvalley
body: MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB Research) has maintained a BUY call on Matrix Concepts Holdings Bhd with an unchanged target price of RM1.65, saying the company’s latest collaboration supports long-term growth in its flagship Malaysia Vision Valley (MVV) development. Matrix Concepts recently signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with Golog Holdings Sdn Bhd to jointly develop the China-Malaysia Air Silk Road Dual Hub Industrial Park (CMAS Industrial Park) at MVV TechValley in Negeri Sembilan. The 618-acre project, with a gross development value (GDV) of RM8 billion, will be developed in three phases. The MOU, which will expire in six months, is expected to be formalised within that timeframe. According to MBSB Research, the agreement is a positive development that will accelerate the growth of MVV TechValley, a key component of the group’s MVV 2.0 master plan. Matrix Concepts currently owns 2,382 acres in MVV 2.0, with 1,000 acres earmarked for industrial development. Golog’s expertise in artificial intelligence, automation and intelligent cold chain logistics is expected to strengthen the project’s positioning and enhance the value of the MVV TechValley ecosystem. MBSB Research noted that the broader MVV City development remains a near-term catalyst for Matrix Concepts, with a total GDV of RM15 billion and a 12-year development timeline. Revenue contribution from MVV City is projected to start in FY26, mainly from land sales. Together with ongoing progress in the Sendayan township in Seremban, the research house expects these projects to drive earnings growth in the coming years. The research house made no changes to its earnings forecasts for FY26 to FY28, adding that the group’s fundamentals remain strong, supported by steady sales from its landed residential projects in Negeri Sembilan. Dividend yields are also expected to remain attractive at around 5.3%, further enhancing shareholder returns. MBSB Research said the MOU with Golog reinforces Matrix Concepts’ strategy to expand its industrial property portfolio and diversify beyond residential development. It added that the collaboration could attract more domestic and international investors to MVV TechValley, given the park’s strategic location and integration with logistics and technology-driven operations. Overall, MBSB Research reiterated its Buy rating on Matrix Concepts, viewing the company as well-positioned to capitalise on the industrial and urban expansion in Negeri Sembilan through its MVV City and MVV TechValley projects. title: CIMB Initiates Coverage On Karex
body: CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) has initiated coverage on Karex Berhad with a BUY rating and a target price of RM1.60, implying an upside potential of 88.2%. The research house said Karex is entering a structural earnings upcycle, supported by the commercialisation of its patented nitrile synthetic condoms, which are moving from pilot phase to mass market rollout. According to CIMB Securities, Karex’s exclusive global partner, believed to be Durex, has already expanded distribution to 18 countries following a successful launch in France. This marks a transition from years of research and development to a phase of strong earnings delivery, with production capacity expected to grow fivefold to 900 million pieces per year by the end of FY2028. The nitrile synthetic condoms, which are softer, thinner and offer better heat transfer compared to latex alternatives, are projected to generate gross profit margins exceeding 50%. CIMB Securities said Karex is now positioned to capture premium pricing and strengthen its leadership as the world’s largest condom manufacturer. After a period of weak earnings from FY2022 to FY2025 due to heavy R&D spending, certification delays, and losses in its glove division. The firm expects Karex to deliver a three-year compound annual net profit growth rate of 91.3% from FY2025 to FY2028. Once the exclusivity with its global partner lapses, Karex will be able to sell its nitrile condoms under its own brands such as ONE and to other original equipment manufacturers, creating a new growth leg. CIMB Securities values Karex at 18.8 times its CY2027 forecast earnings, in line with global intimate wellness peers, supported by its global leadership position, unique patented innovation and robust earnings outlook. The research house expects dividend yields between 1.9% and 5.9% over FY2026–FY2028, backed by a 50% payout ratio. As of 10.55 am, Karex’s stock price rose 10% to RM0.935. title: Wall Street Slips From Record Highs As Shutdown Fuels Economic Uncertainty
body: Wall Street retreated overnight as concerns over the prolonged US government shutdown and weakening economic signals dampened investor sentiment, pulling the major indices back from record closing highs. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.20% to 46,602.98, the S&P 500 slipped 0.38% to 6,714.59, and the Nasdaq Composite dropped 0.67% to 22,788.36, snapping a seven-day winning streak. A New York Fed survey showing declining consumer expectations and higher inflation projections further weighed on sentiment amid the absence of official data due to the shutdown. “Traders probably used the report as an excuse to take profits,” said CFRA Research’s chief investment strategist Sam Stovall, adding that uncertainty will linger as long as the data blackout continues. Economically sensitive sectors such as homebuilding, airlines, and transport underperformed, while utilities and consumer staples led modest gains. Among movers, Tesla tumbled 4.5% after unveiling a low-cost Model Y, while AMD surged 3.8% following a bullish upgrade by Jefferies. Constellation Brands rose 1% after a smaller-than-expected drop in sales, and IBM climbed 1.5% after announcing a partnership with AI startup Anthropic. Meanwhile, crypto-related stocks such as Coinbase and Riot Platforms slid as bitcoin retreated from recent highs. The sell-off comes as Fed Governor Stephen Miran reiterated support for further rate cuts, cautioning against overly restrictive monetary policy. body: he ringgit opened stronger against the US dollar and other major currencies today, buoyed by upbeat sentiment ahead of Budget 2026 and a sharp rise in Bank Negara Malaysia’s reserves. The investment bank added that despite bond outflows, net foreign exchange reserves reached a three-year high of US$73.3 billion, supported by ongoing corporate forex repatriation that continues to underpin the ringgit’s resilience. Kenanga said the ringgit remained one of ASEAN’s best-performing currencies, extending its rally for the eighth straight month in September. While softer global demand may weigh on growth in the second half of 2025, Kenanga expects domestic momentum to hold up, supported by services, household spending and structural reforms. title: Philippine Peso Set For Recovery On Central Bank Backing And Remittances
body: The Philippine peso appears poised for a rebound in the coming months, as analysts anticipate central bank intervention and seasonal remittance inflows to support one of Asia’s weakest-performing currencies. The peso weakened 3.2% in the September quarter, pressured by foreign stock outflows and deteriorating sentiment amid US tariff measures and domestic corruption allegations. Analysts, however, say the outlook is showing signs of improvement. MUFG Bank Ltd. expects the peso to strengthen to 56.50 per US dollar by end-March 2026, implying a gain of roughly 3% from Tuesday’s close. Rizal Commercial Banking Corp. forecasts it to trade between 56.50 and 57.50 by end-2025, citing indications from the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) that it may support the currency. Analysts also pointed to a likely softer US dollar as a supporting factor. BSP Governor Eli Remolona said the central bank would intervene more forcefully during periods of extended peso weakness to curb inflation. With higher fuel costs weighing on the import-dependent economy, most economists surveyed by Bloomberg expect the BSP to hold interest rates at its meeting on Thursday. “The central bank’s support for the peso would also help manage inflation better,” said Michael Ricafort, chief economist at Rizal Commercial Banking in Manila. “A stable peso would help stabilise import costs.” Beyond monetary policy, the potential inclusion of Philippine government bonds in JPMorgan Chase & Co.’s emerging-market bond index could boost demand for local assets. Analysts also highlighted seasonal remittances as a key factor, noting that overseas Filipinos typically send more money home in the fourth quarter for the Christmas and New Year holidays. The Philippines received about US$9 billion in remittances in the last quarter of 2024, the highest for any quarter that year. Despite lingering risks from graft allegations and a global trade slowdown linked to US tariffs, analysts remain optimistic. “We reckon this underperformance may be overstretched for now and should reverse course,” said Christopher Wong, currency strategist at Oversea-Chinese Banking Corp Ltd. title: Gold Hits Record High Above US$4,000 As Investors Flee To Safety
body: Gold surged past US$4,000 an ounce for the first time on Wednesday as investors sought refuge amid mounting global uncertainty and growing expectations of further interest rate cuts by the US Federal Reserve. Spot gold rose 0.5% to US$4,002.53 per ounce by 0213 GMT, while US gold futures for December delivery gained 0.5% to US$4,025. The metal has jumped 52% so far this year after a 27% rise in 2024, underscoring its strength as a traditional store of value during instability. “There’s so much faith in this trade right now that the market will look for the next big round number which is 5,000, with the Fed likely to continue to lower rates,” said independent metals trader Tai Wong. Gold’s rally has been fuelled by expectations of interest rate cuts, persistent political and economic risks, strong central bank buying, inflows into gold-backed exchange-traded funds, and a weaker dollar. The ongoing US government shutdown, now in its seventh day, has further unsettled markets as key economic data releases remain delayed. Investors are currently pricing in a 25-basis-point rate cut this month, with another expected in December. Political turmoil in France and Japan has also intensified demand for the safe-haven metal. Analysts say a “fear of missing out” is amplifying the move. “What we see now is that investors are buying gold, despite the price being high, and this is amplifying the move further,” said UBS analyst Giovanni Staunovo. Meanwhile, spot silver rose 0.5% to US$48.03 per ounce, platinum gained 2.2% to US$1,653.21, and palladium climbed 1.3% to US$1,355.32. title: Wall Street Futures Climb As AI Momentum And Rate-Cut Bets Lift Sentiment
body: Wall Street futures edged higher on Monday, supported by optimism surrounding artificial intelligence (AI) dealmaking and growing expectations of an interest-rate cut amid signs of a cooling US labour market. At 6.38 am ET, Dow E-minis gained 82 points or 0.17%, S&P 500 E-minis advanced 25.5 points or 0.38%, while Nasdaq 100 E-minis rose 146.5 points or 0.59%. The advance extended last week’s gains despite a federal government shutdown entering its sixth day. “The current AI infrastructure buildout is structurally more durable than prior large cycles. It’s funded by strong cash flows and AI adoption can happen without costly consumer device upgrades,” said BofA Securities senior analyst Vivek Arya. Market optimism persisted even as the shutdown delayed the release of key economic data, including the nonfarm payrolls report. However, alternative indicators last week suggested sluggish hiring, reinforcing the likelihood that the Federal Reserve will trim rates by 25 basis points at its next meeting. Goldman Sachs noted that the approaching military pay date on 15 October could pressure lawmakers to end the political deadlock, warning that 1.3 million uniformed personnel could go unpaid if no resolution is reached. Still, the brokerage added that data delays could leave the Fed with limited visibility on the economy in the coming weeks. Attention is also turning to the third-quarter earnings season beginning next week, which analysts believe will offer crucial insight into the economy’s resilience. “The next two weeks of earnings are going to matter more than usual,” said Easterly EAB global macro strategist Arnim Holzer. “The most ‘boots on the ground’ data that the Fed is going to have is going to be the earnings data and the forecasts.” Among stocks, Micron Technology jumped 3.5% after Morgan Stanley upgraded it to “overweight”. Crypto-related counters also gained as bitcoin hovered near record highs, with Coinbase Global up 2.4%, Riot Platforms rising 4.1% and MARA Holdings climbing 3.4%. Tesla advanced 2.4% after teasing an event scheduled for Tuesday on social media platform X, while Critical Metals surged 69.6% following a Reuters report that President Donald Trump’s administration was considering taking a stake in the company. Comerica rallied 13.8% after Fifth Third Bancorp announced a US$10.9 billion acquisition deal. Shares of Fifth Third slipped 1.5%. title: Takaichi’s Win Lifts Market Hopes, Yen Slides
body: Japan’s yen weakened sharply as markets reacted to the ruling Liberal Democratic Party’s decision to elect pro-stimulus lawmaker Sanae Takaichi as its new leader, paving the way for her to become Japan’s first female prime minister. Nikkei stock futures on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange surged over 4%, reflecting optimism that Takaichi’s expansionary policies will boost demand-driven sectors. The yen slipped as much as 1.4% against the dollar, nearing the key 150 level, and touched record lows versus the euro. Oil prices also advanced after OPEC+ agreed to restore just 137,000 barrels per day of previously halted output — a slower pace than in earlier months — while S&P 500 futures edged higher in tandem. Investors had largely expected the premiership to go to Shinjiro Koizumi, a political scion seen as more fiscally restrained and likely to let the Bank of Japan pursue policy normalisation. In contrast, Takaichi has pushed for fiscal expansion, saying in a Kyodo survey that interest rates should remain unchanged for now. While her stance has bolstered growth expectations, it has raised concerns over potential increases in government bond supply and reduced prospects of a Bank of Japan rate hike this month. “It might be more of a positive surprise for equities,” said cross-asset investment strategist Anna Wu of VanEck Australia. “I won’t be too surprised if the long-end yields go up a bit on Monday, given her overarching fiscal policy,” she added, while noting that Takaichi is unlikely to overstimulate and market volatility should remain limited. Elsewhere in Asia, futures point to modest gains in Australia but slight declines in Hong Kong. Mainland Chinese markets remain closed for the holidays, while Sydney’s public holiday may amplify movements in local trading. In global markets, US equity futures advanced after the S&P 500 ended little changed on Friday amid a tech-led selloff. Bitcoin reached another record high over the weekend, buoyed by optimism around the so-called “Uptober” trend and easing concerns about a US government shutdown. Attention will also turn to Europe, where traders are eyeing French bond futures following President Emmanuel Macron’s decision to retain much of his previous cabinet. Roland Lescure was named finance minister and now faces the challenge of steering the national budget through a divided parliament. The euro slipped early Monday amid a stronger US dollar. title: Stock Today: Solarvest Edges Lower As Analysts Maintain Strong Buy Ratings
body: Solarvest Holdings Bhd slipped 0.34% to RM2.93 as of 3.50 pm today, with a total traded volume of 1.532 million shares. The counter opened at RM2.95, reaching an intraday high of RM2.96 and a low of RM2.89. Despite the minor dip, both RHB Investment Bank Bhd and Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd have maintained their BUY calls on the company, citing strong earnings visibility following Solarvest’s latest milestone in Sarawak. RHB Research lifted its target price to RM3.58, while HLIB kept its valuation at RM3.50, indicating potential upside of more than 20% from the current level. The positive sentiment is underpinned by Solarvest’s 60% stake in the 100MWac Mukah Solar Powerplant, a first for the company in Borneo. The facility has entered a 30-year power purchase agreement with Syarikat Sesco Sdn Bhd and is expected to commence commercial operations in November 2027. RHB Research projects the plant could contribute an average annual net profit of RM6.5 million, representing up to 9% of the company’s FY2026 earnings. HLIB highlighted that the Mukah project adds around RM300 million worth of EPCC works to Solarvest’s existing RM1.2 billion unbilled orderbook, bringing the company closer to its RM3 billion target by FY2026. The project also increases Solarvest’s effective ownership of utility-scale solar assets to 490MWp, potentially lifting recurring revenue to RM110 million annually. Analysts noted that the expansion positions Solarvest strategically within Sarawak’s renewable energy roadmap, aligning with Malaysia’s National Energy Transition Roadmap and the state’s ambition to boost solar capacity to 1.5GW by 2035. title: Stock Today: IHH Healthcare Rises 2.09% On Positive Outlook After India Regulatory Approval
body: Shares of IHH Healthcare Bhd rose 2.09% to RM8.30 at 11.46 am, extending recent gains as investor sentiment remained buoyant following renewed optimism over its expansion prospects in India. The counter climbed 17 sen from its previous close of RM8.13, with 8.2 million shares traded. It opened at RM8.13 and touched an intraday high of RM8.32 before easing slightly. The buying momentum came after RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) and CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) both reaffirmed their BUY calls on IHH, with an upgraded target price of RM9, citing stronger growth potential following regulatory developments in India. The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) recently approved for IHH to proceed with its long-delayed mandatory takeover offers (MTO) for Fortis Healthcare Ltd and Fortis Malar Hospitals Ltd, ending a seven-year regulatory overhang. RHB Research said the decision “reopens IHH’s growth story in India”, noting that if the open offers are fully accepted, IHH’s stake in Fortis would rise from 31% to about 57%, cementing its control over the hospital chain. CIMB Securities said the approval “effectively ends a seven-year stalemate”, adding that it raised its target price for IHH to RM9 from RM8.50 after adjusting subsidiary valuations and profit forecasts. Both research houses remain positive on IHH’s long-term outlook, backed by its diversified regional portfolio, strong execution record, and premium positioning across key markets. At current levels, IHH’s share price is up nearly 5% over the past month, reflecting investor confidence in its strategic direction and earnings resilience ahead of Visit Malaysia 2026, which is expected to boost medical tourism. title: Potential Upside For Solarvest After Sarawak Venture
body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) and Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) have both maintained their BUY calls on Solarvest Holdings Bhd, citing strong earnings visibility following the company’s latest milestone in Sarawak. RHB Research raised its target price to RM3.58 from RM3.26, while HLIB maintained its RM3.50 valuation, reflecting a potential upside of more than 20% from the counter’s last traded price of RM2.94. RHB Research said the latest win, the development and operation of a 100MWac large-scale solar photovoltaic (PV) plant in Mukah, Sarawak marks Solarvest’s first asset in Borneo and underscores its growing portfolio of income-generating renewable energy assets. The research house said the project reinforces Solarvest’s position as one of Malaysia’s leading solar players, with its record-high engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning (EPCC) orderbook and robust project pipeline supporting future earnings. Solarvest will hold a 60% stake in Mukah Solar Powerplant (MSP), which has entered into a 30-year power purchase agreement (PPA) with Syarikat Sesco Sdn Bhd, the utility arm of Sarawak Energy, to develop and operate the 100MWac facility. The remaining 40% will be held by Press Metal Aluminium Holdings Bhd. Commercial operation is expected by November 2027, with total capital expenditure estimated at RM380 million, funded mainly through internally generated funds. RHB Research projected that Solarvest could generate an average annual net profit of around RM6.5 million from the project, representing up to 9% of its FY2026 earnings, assuming an internal rate of return (IRR) of 7% to 8% and a debt-to-equity ratio of four times. The expansion, it said, is aligned with the company’s goal of achieving 30% recurring income contribution, with full earnings from the project expected by FY2029. HLIB similarly highlighted that the Mukah project adds about RM300 million worth of EPCC works to Solarvest’s existing unbilled orderbook of RM1.2 billion, bringing the company closer to its RM3 billion target by the end of FY2026. It added that the latest development will increase Solarvest’s effective ownership of utility-scale solar assets to 490MWp from 336MWp previously, potentially lifting recurring revenue to RM110 million annually. The research house also noted that the project strategically positions Solarvest within Sarawak’s renewable energy expansion plan, as the state targets to raise installed generation capacity from 5.7GW to 10GW by 2030 and 15GW by 2035, including 1.5GW of solar capacity. HLIB said Solarvest’s deepening presence in Sarawak is timely, given the state’s growing demand from industries and data centres and its ambition to become a regional renewable energy hub. Both RHB Research and HLIB agreed that Solarvest is well placed to benefit from Malaysia’s National Energy Transition Roadmap (NETR), which supports private sector participation in renewable energy projects. body: Gold prices in Malaysia climbed sharply in tandem with the global rally, rising 1.37% to RM533.07 per gram as of 3.43 am New York time, according to data from GoldPrice.org. In ringgit terms, the price per kilogram stood at RM533,074.73, up RM7,228.76 from the previous session. Globally, spot gold smashed through the US$3,900 mark for the first time in history, trading at US$3,910.09 per ounce, while US gold futures for December delivery gained 0.7% to US$3,935, Reuters reported. Over the past year, gold prices in Malaysia have surged 44.38%, while the six-month gain stood at 23.04%. The rally has been further fuelled by a weaker US dollar and growing geopolitical uncertainties, prompting investors to flock to bullion as a hedge against volatility. Silver also saw strong gains, climbing 1.49% to RM3.01 per gram, extending a 48.29% rise over the past year. Analysts said gold’s upward trajectory may continue if the Federal Reserve confirms further monetary easing, with the record high reinforcing its status as a global store of value. title: US Shutdown Sparks Bitcoin Surge to $125,689 Record
body: Bitcoin has reached a new all-time high, climbing to as much as $125,689 on Sunday in Asia. This surge is part of a wider risk rally sparked by concerns over the US government shutdown, which began on Wednesday. The rise was supported by gains in US equities and renewed inflows into Bitcoin-linked exchange-traded funds (ETFs). Investors are viewing the shutdown as a factor driving demand for safe-haven assets, a trend some market participants refer to as the “debasement trade.” Bitcoin’s performance this year has been strong, gaining more than 30% and exceeding its previous high of $124,514 set on August 14. The largest digital asset by market value has steadily appreciated over the past year, helped by the supportive legislative environment in Washington under President Donald Trump. Public companies, notably Michael Saylor’s Strategy, have boosted demand by stockpiling Bitcoin as a corporate asset, a strategy that has spread to other cryptocurrencies like Ether, lifting digital assets broadly. Joshua Lim, co-head of markets at crypto prime brokerage FalconX, noted that Bitcoin’s rise fits within a broader trend where various assets including equities, gold, and even collectibles like Pokémon cards are hitting record levels, driven by concerns over the weakening value of the US dollar. October is also historically a strong month for Bitcoin, nicknamed “Uptober,” with the token having posted gains in nine of the last ten Octobers. This seasonal pattern adds to the bullish sentiment surrounding the cryptocurrency. US stocks also touched record highs on Friday, driven by major artificial intelligence deals and partnerships, offsetting concerns over a prolonged government shutdown and weak business activity. Treasuries and the dollar fell, while gold was on track for a seventh consecutive weekly gain, bolstered by central bank purchases amid declining US interest rates and ongoing inflation concerns. Geoff Kendrick, global head of digital assets research at Standard Chartered Plc, said the current shutdown could have a greater impact on Bitcoin than previous ones. He noted that during the 2018–2019 shutdown, Bitcoin traded less in line with traditional risk assets, but now it appears to respond more closely to broader market trends. title: Japanese Markets Eye Gains After Takaichi LDP Win
body: Japan’s stock market is likely to gain support following the surprise victory of pro-stimulus Sanae Takaichi in the ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) leadership election, while the yen and long-term government bonds could come under pressure. Investors and strategists, including those at Pepperstone Group Ltd. and Nomura Securities Co., expect the yield curve to steepen as a result. Takaichi, a strong advocate of easy fiscal and monetary policy, is expected to raise concerns over rising bond issuance, while lowering expectations of a Bank of Japan (BOJ) rate hike later this month. “This was very much a surprise result and not the one that markets had been discounting,” said Michael Brown, senior research strategist at Pepperstone. He added that Takaichi’s win is “likely to be yen negative, on the dovish BOJ repricing, coupled with a steeper JGB curve given her looser fiscal views, though both of those combined should be a boost for the Nikkei.” Takaichi is set to become Japan’s first female prime minister later this month in a parliamentary vote. Investors had expected the leadership to go to political scion Shinjiro Koizumi, who was seen as more fiscally cautious and supportive of BOJ rate normalisation. Bank stocks are likely to struggle amid expectations that rate hikes will be delayed, while domestic demand and small-cap shares could see a “significant tailwind” in the short term, said Richard Kaye, co-head of Japan equity strategy at Comgest Asset Management. Market participants, including foreign investors, are likely to welcome any signs of a return to Abenomics, the economic policies of the late former prime minister Shinzo Abe. As a protege of Abe, Takaichi has advocated for cash handouts and tax rebates to help households grappling with inflation, and has openly supported additional bond issuance to finance fiscal stimulus. Before Takaichi’s win, bond investors had been cautious about fiscal spending, particularly with opposition calls for tax cuts and speculation over BOJ rate hikes. This caution pushed 10-year yields near their highest levels since 2008 and strengthened the yen against the dollar in the past week. Meanwhile, the Nikkei 225 hit a fresh all-time high, benefiting from a global rally in technology stocks. According to Mari Iwashita, executive rates strategist at Nomura Securities, Takaichi’s unexpected victory is likely to revive a market trend characterised by a weaker yen, higher stock prices, and a steeper yield curve. With the prospect of an October BOJ rate hike fading, she expects the central bank to hold off on increasing rates in the near term. However, Rong Ren Goh, fixed income portfolio manager at Eastspring Investments, cautions that any yen weakness resulting from her win may be limited due to narrowing Japan-US interest rate differentials and continued uncertainty over the Federal Reserve’s policy direction. Takaichi faces challenges in implementing her domestic agenda, as her party no longer holds a majority in either house of parliament. She is also expected to face an early diplomatic test with a reported visit from former US President Donald Trump later this month. Looking ahead, Richard Kaye expresses optimism about Japan’s stock market, highlighting that a shift in perception towards Japan could drive new approaches in deregulation, monetary policy, and Japan-US trade relations. title: Wall Street Posts Record Weekly Gains as Dow and S&P 500 Close at New Highs
body: Dow and S&P 500 hit record closing highs on Friday, while the Nasdaq fell in a volatile session, Reuters reported. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 238.56 points, or 0.51%, closing at 46,758.28. The S&P 500 eked out a gain of 0.44 points, or 0.01%, to 6,715.79, marking a record closing high despite choppy trading. However, the Nasdaq Composite slipped 63.54 points, or 0.28%, to 22,780.51. Market sentiment was bolstered by expectations of potential interest rate cuts from the Federal Reserve amid ongoing concerns that the U.S. government shutdown was entering its third day. The shutdown delayed the release of key economic data, such as September’s U.S. nonfarm payrolls report. Still, a separate survey from the Institute for Supply Management showed continued contraction in services employment, reinforcing hopes for easing rates. Sector-wise, the S&P 500 technology sector softened, with Applied Materials shares dropping 2.7% after the company forecasted a $600 million revenue hit for fiscal 2026. Tesla shares declined 1.4%, while utilities led the day’s sector gains, rising 1.2%. For the week, the Dow and S&P 500 both rose 1.1%, while the Nasdaq gained 1.3%. Despite a typical market resilience to government shutdowns, strategists caution that a prolonged closure could delay or obscure crucial economic data, impacting investment decisions and Federal Reserve policy. Elsewhere, USA Rare Earth jumped 14.3% after its CEO said the company was in close contact with the White House. Market breadth was positive, with advancing issues outnumbering decliners by a 1.72-to-1 ratio on the NYSE. Trading volume reached 20.47 billion shares, above the 20-day average of 19.01 billion. While shutdowns have historically had limited market impact, some strategists cautioned that a prolonged closure could delay key economic data and complicate Fed policy decisions. “The market generally looks past government shutdowns,” said Anthony Saglimbene, chief market strategist at Ameriprise Financial. “But the longer it goes… it could cloud some of the data we will eventually get because the collection wasn’t happening.” Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee, meanwhile, signalled caution on committing to a series of rate cuts, citing persistent inflation pressures. title: Wall Street Left Waiting as Payroll Data Frozen by US Shutdown
body: The typically unmissable U.S. jobs data release will not happen this Friday due to the government shutdown, leaving traders with unexpected free time but also a challenge in reading the economic landscape. With deep partisan divisions preventing a funding deal, the U.S. Labour Department has suspended its economic data releases, including the closely watched monthly employment report. This disruption has quietened trading floors and investment firms that normally focus intently on the jobs report at 8:30 am. Michael Brown, a senior research strategist in London, joked that Friday now “has all the makings of a rather long lunch,” highlighting how the usual suspense has vanished. Matthew Miskin, co-chief investment strategist at Manulife John Hancock Investments, noted the unusual calm, saying it would be a relief for market watchers not to have their eyes glued to the screen waiting for the report. The absence of payroll data—the so-called “king of the numbers”—is particularly striking given its importance. Investors rely heavily on labour market statistics to gauge the Federal Reserve’s potential moves on interest rates. Recent volatility, including a surprise weak jobs report that led to the firing of a top Labour Department official by President Donald Trump, has made this data even more crucial. Beyond trading desks, the jobs report fuels widespread discussion on social media. Typically, tens of thousands of posts tagged #NFP flood platforms around the release, reflecting intense public and professional interest. Without the data, regular contributors like Steve Sosnick, chief strategist at Interactive Brokers, say they will have an unusually quiet morning, while others warn that missing data could increase market uncertainty. James Cordier, a veteran commodities trader, cautions that if the data drought extends beyond mid-October, some traders may have to close positions early due to excessive risk. Karl Schamotta, chief market strategist at Corpay, warns that the void may be filled with misleading rumours and incomplete private data, potentially causing overreactions in the markets. This shutdown-driven data gap is reminiscent of the last government shutdown in 2013 that delayed the employment report by weeks. Until the government reopens fully, investors and traders alike must navigate heightened uncertainty without one of their most critical economic indicators. title: Oil Prices Slide 8% Weekly Amid Expected OPEC+ Supply Boost
body: Oil prices posted an 8.1% weekly loss despite settling higher on Friday amid news of potential increases in OPEC+ supply. Brent crude futures closed up 42 cents, or 0.7%, at $64.53 a barrel, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude rose 40 cents, or 0.7%, to $60.88. However, both benchmarks faced their highest weekly declines in over three months, with Brent down 8.1% and WTI tumbling 7.4%. The expected increase in OPEC+ production, combined with the resumption of flows from the Iraq/Kurdish pipeline after a two-year shutdown, is maintaining selling pressure on crude. Eight OPEC+ countries are to raise output in November, with Saudi Arabia advocating a significant boost to regain market share, while Russia favors a more moderate rise. Analysts warn that higher OPEC+ supply, alongside seasonal drops in demand and ongoing refinery maintenance, will weigh on oil market sentiment. Rystad Energy highlighted weakening demand indicators in the Atlantic Basin as summer ends, pointing to an over-supplied market from October onwards. JPMorgan also forecasted a turning point in September, anticipating a sizeable oil surplus through the fourth quarter and into next year. Additional downward pressure came from U.S. data showing higher crude, gasoline and distillate inventories last week, as refinery activity and demand softened, the Energy Information Administration reported. Oilfield services firm Baker Hughes stated producers cut two rigs this week, bringing the total oil rig count down to 422. Separately, a fire broke out overnight at Chevron’s El Segundo refinery in California, one of the largest on the U.S. West Coast. Local officials said the blaze was contained to one area, and analysts noted the incident was unlikely to have a significant impact on the wider oil market. title: Kospi Climbs 2.7% Ahead of Chuseok Holiday on Tech Optimism
body: Seoul shares closed sharply higher on Oct 2, with the benchmark KOSPI jumping 2.7% (93.38 points) to 3,549.21, lifted by gains across heavyweight technology and financial stocks. The index opened at 3,525.48 and traded firmly higher through the session, touching an intraday peak of 3,565.96 — also its 52-week high — before paring back slightly into the close. The rally was driven primarily by significant gains in semiconductor stocks, notably Samsung Electronics, which surged over 4%, and SK Hynix, which soared nearly 11%, following reports of a new partnership with OpenAI to supply advanced memory chips for AI data centers. This collaboration highlights South Korea’s pivotal role in the global artificial intelligence supply chain. Despite stronger inflation data showing consumer prices rose 2.1% in September—above market expectations—investors remained optimistic about the technology sector’s prospects and the overall market outlook. The KOSPI’s gains reflect a broader trend of robust growth, with the index up over 11% in the past month and more than 38% year-on-year. With the upcoming Chuseok holiday closure from October 3 through October 9, market participants positioned themselves ahead of the break, balancing enthusiasm from corporate developments with caution over inflation and policy implications from the Bank of Korea. Looking ahead, investors will closely watch economic data releases and the central bank’s policy stance as they navigate the balance between supporting economic growth and maintaining price stability. title: Wall Street Climbs To Fresh Highs On Tech Momentum
body: US stocks extended their record-breaking run on Thursday, driven by gains in technology shares despite political headwinds from the government shutdown. The S&P 500 inched up 0.1% while the Nasdaq 100 rose 0.4%, both reaching new highs. The rally was bolstered by an OpenAI share sale valuing the company at US$500 billion, which spurred demand for chip stocks. “Tech momentum shows no sign of fading — as if gravity doesn’t exist — with headwinds brushed aside and every AI headline sparking bursts of euphoria,” said Hebe Chen, analyst at Vantage Markets in Melbourne. Treasuries edged higher, with the 10-year yield easing to around 4.08%, while the dollar strengthened 0.1% after three days of losses. Oil prices slipped further, with West Texas Intermediate dipping below US$61 a barrel, its lowest in four months. Meanwhile, gold cooled after hitting a record high. Investors continued to weigh political uncertainty, as Republicans pushed for deep cuts to federal jobs to reopen the government. With key labour data expected to be delayed by the shutdown, money markets still largely priced in a quarter-point rate cut by the Federal Reserve this month and another in December. title: Tech Surge Lifts Nikkei As US Rate-Cut Hopes Offset Shutdown Fears
body: Tokyo’s Nikkei led Asian equities higher on Friday (Oct 3), rising 1.9% as investors headed into the weekend, buoyed by hopes of further US rate cuts despite a partial government shutdown in Washington. Other regional markets, including Sydney, Singapore, Bangkok, Wellington, Taipei, Jakarta and Manila, also closed higher, while Hong Kong fell 1% after gaining over 4% in the previous three sessions. Shanghai remained closed for a holiday. The rally has been largely driven by massive investment in artificial intelligence, pushing valuations of major tech firms to record levels, with Nvidia surpassing US$4 trillion. Recent news of South Korean chipmakers Samsung and SK hynix striking a preliminary deal with OpenAI for its Stargate project added momentum to the sector. On Friday, Japan’s Hitachi announced a strategic partnership with OpenAI to collaborate on AI and energy projects, sending its shares up more than 9%. Renesas followed with a similar gain, while Sony rose 2.8%, Advantest over 3%, and SoftBank more than 3%. Data suggesting a slowdown in the US labour market has further fuelled the rally, signalling the Federal Reserve may continue cutting borrowing costs. Analysts noted that the government shutdown, which has halted some services and delayed key jobs data, is unlikely to prevent the Fed from a second rate cut this month. Pepperstone’s Chris Weston said, “The shutdown could shave US$15-$20 billion off US GDP, but it will largely be backfilled and should have only a negligible lasting impact.” In company news, Japanese brewer Asahi fell more than 1% after a cyberattack disrupted its ordering and delivery system, forcing production stoppages at several factories. Shares have dropped around 7% this week. The positive sentiment has also lifted bitcoin, which regained levels above US$120,000 for the first time since mid-August, when it reached a record US$124,515. The tax assessments, dated 26 May 2023, covered the years of assessment 2017 to 2021. Collectively, they amounted to RM78.49 million.
