title: Stock Today: SunCon Dips Slightly Amid Strong Sector Outlook
body: Sunway Construction Group Bhd (SUNCON) closed at RM5.94 on Friday, down 9 sen or 1.49% from its previous close, with a total trading volume of 1.24 million shares. The counter opened at RM6.01, reaching a high of RM6.04 and a low of RM5.90 during the session. Despite the minor setback, Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) maintains an OVERWEIGHT stance on the construction sector, reaffirming its BUY rating on Sunway Construction with a target price of RM6.70. The research house highlighted that domestic contract awards remained robust in the first nine months of 2025, rising 24% year-on-year to RM39.7 billion, marking the highest level since 2016. HLIB noted that data centres and public sector projects including roads, railways, and water infrastructure, were key drivers of the sector. While third-quarter awards fell 16% quarter-on-quarter to RM10.7 billion, full-year projections remain strong, with expected contract awards around RM50 billion for 2025, up from RM44.2 billion in 2024. The quarter also saw significant wins, such as Gamuda’s RM2.14 billion data centre project in Puncak Alam and a RM1.13 billion Northern Coastal Highway contract in Sarawak through a joint venture with Naim Holdings. IJM Corp secured a RM1.4 billion hyperscale data centre project in Johor. HLIB expects the construction momentum to carry into the final quarter, with pending data centre contracts, East Malaysian road projects, renewable energy EPCC jobs, and Penang LRT subcontract packages potentially boosting activity. Large-scale water project awards are anticipated in 2026. While commercial and residential projects softened due to the removal of the SST exemption for construction services in July, HLIB projects the sector’s growth cycle to extend into 2026, supported by delayed mechanical, electrical, and plumbing works for data centres, though risks remain from slower property activity, potential AI chip demand restrictions, and subsidy rationalisation. title: Ringgit Rises On Fed Policy Bets Amid US Shutdown Concerns
body: The ringgit opened stronger against the US dollar on Friday, lifted by expectations that a prolonged US government shutdown could pressure the Federal Reserve (Fed) into easing monetary policy. At 8 am, the local note rose 30-pip to 4.2010/2150 from Thursday’s close of 4.2040/2090. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US dollar-ringgit exchange rate was likely to remain steady, trading between 4.20 and 4.22 during the day. “Market participants expect economic uncertainty from the shutdown to pressure the Fed to cut interest rates in the coming months, easing demand for the greenback and supporting emerging market currencies such as the ringgit,” he told Bernama. He added that traders and investors are increasingly turning to private company surveys of the labour market to gauge economic conditions following the suspension of official data. Mohd Afzanizam recalled that the longest US shutdown, which lasted from Dec 22, 2018 to Jan 25, 2019, reduced US gross domestic product growth by 0.1 and 0.2 percentage points in the fourth quarter of 2018 and the first quarter of 2019, respectively. In early trade, the ringgit was also firmer against major currencies. It strengthened to 4.9248/9412 versus the euro from 4.9410/9468, advanced against the British pound to 5.6482/6671 from 5.6741/6809, and climbed to 2.8543/8640 against the Japanese yen from 2.8669/8705. title: Winning Full NYC Gambling License Could Boost Genting’s Fair Value
body: CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) has maintained its HOLD call on Genting Malaysia Bhd (GENM) with an unchanged sum-of-parts (SOP) based target price of RM2.15, as its wholly owned Resorts World New York City (RWNYC) moves closer to securing one of three Downstate New York (DNY) full casino licences. The brokerage noted that RWNYC received unanimous approval from the Community Advisory Committee (CAC) on 25 September to redevelop its existing slots facility into a US$5.5 billion (RM23.1 billion) integrated resort. The approval followed overwhelming support at two public hearings, leaving RWNYC among just four remaining applicants vying for the licences. Other shortlisted contenders include MGM’s Empire City Casino, Bally’s Bronx and Steve Cohen-Hard Rock’s Metropolitan Park, while four other proposals were rejected. The Gaming Facility Location Board (GFLB) will now evaluate submissions based on criteria such as economic activity and business development, which carry a 70% weighting. CIMB Securities believes RWNYC has an edge over rivals due to its ability to begin offering table games within six months of receiving a licence, a full year ahead of MGM and several years ahead of new entrants. RWNYC’s proposed development also stands out in scale, with plans to feature 6,000 slots, 800 tables, 2,000 hotel rooms, a 7,000-seat entertainment venue, more than 30 food and beverage outlets and extensive convention space by 2030, making it the largest integrated resort in the United States. The decision by the GFLB is expected by 1 December, with licences issued by the Gaming Commission by year-end. CIMB Securities estimates that winning a full casino licence could boost GENM’s fair value by 52 sen per share, equivalent to a 24% upside to its target price. In terms of financing, RWNYC’s remaining US$3.9 billion (RM16.4 billion) investment, after accounting for US$1.1 billion already spent, is projected to be deployed over 2026–2030, averaging US$780 million (RM3.3 billion) per year. CIMB Securities expects 70% of this to be debt-funded, with the remainder to be covered by RWNYC’s internally generated funds. Additional support could also come from potential asset disposals, such as the sale of GENM’s Miami land, although the timing remains uncertain. However, the research house cautioned that GENM may skip paying dividends in FY2025 and FY2026 to conserve cash, potentially saving RM567 million annually. Its earnings outlook also remains subdued in the near term, with core net profit projected to fall to RM367 million in FY2025 before recovering gradually in FY2026–2027. CIMB Securities concluded that while RWNYC’s casino licence bid offers significant upside potential, the risks of dividend suspension and execution challenges warrant a neutral stance. GENM’s shares closed at RM2.12, just shy of the target price of RM2.15. Genting Malaysia’s stock price is currently down by 0.47% as of 9.58 am to RM2.110. title: Tech Surge Lifts Asia As Weak US Jobs Data Fuels Fed Cut Bets
body: Asian stock markets advanced on Thursday, led by technology shares, while gold hovered close to record highs and the dollar remained subdued, as weak US labour data bolstered expectations of interest rate cuts by the Federal Reserve. The Philadelphia SE semiconductor index jumped more than 2 per cent overnight, lifting Wall Street to fresh records and setting the tone for Asia. Japan’s Nikkei gained about 0.5 per cent, Taiwan’s tech-heavy bourse rose 1.5 per cent, and South Korea’s KOSPI climbed 2.8 per cent after Samsung and Hynix announced partnerships to supply OpenAI data centres. Hong Kong’s Hang Seng added 0.5 per cent. The rally came after the private ADP employment report showed the US economy unexpectedly shed jobs in September, with August figures also revised lower. The data convinced traders that quarter-point rate cuts at the Fed’s final two meetings this year were all but certain, despite the US government shutdown halting the release of the official payrolls report on Friday. “The ADP report suggests the US economy is in almost dire need for further policy support,” said Kyle Rodda, analyst at Capital.com. “As a result, the markets are discounting a much higher probability of rate cuts in October and December.” Rodda added that the shutdown itself had little immediate impact. “After some initial jitters, the markets shrugged off the US government shutdown, at least for now. Historically, the impact of shutdowns has been trivial, although the delay of critical economic data could increase uncertainty about the path forward for US monetary policy – and therefore lift volatility,” he said. The shutdown began on Wednesday after political gridlock in Washington prevented Congress and the White House from reaching a funding deal, threatening a prolonged standoff. Meanwhile, gold surged to a new record of US$3,895.09 an ounce overnight before easing to around US$3,865. US Treasury yields fell sharply, with the two-year yield dropping to 3.531 per cent in Tokyo trading, its lowest in two weeks. The dollar index languished near a one-week low of 97.459, last seen at 97.672. The greenback steadied at 147.01 yen after a three-day slide, while the euro edged up to US$1.1738 and sterling rose to US$1.34835. Oil prices also found support, with Brent crude futures gaining 0.2 per cent to US$65.50 a barrel and US West Texas Intermediate crude climbing 0.2 per cent to US$61.92, as markets weighed the potential of tighter sanctions on Russian crude. title: PetGas Reorganisation Plan Should Lead To Greater Shareholder Value
body: MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB Research) has maintained its Neutral call on PETRONAS Gas Bhd (PETGAS) with an unchanged target price of RM19.25, noting that while the company’s internal reorganisation is expected to bring long-term operational and shareholder benefits, the near-term impact on earnings remains minimal. PETGAS announced it had received approval from the Ministry of Finance for a tax exemption to facilitate the restructuring of its business segments into regulated and non-regulated activities through a members’ scheme of arrangement. Under the plan, the company will transfer its gas transportation, gas processing and utilities operations into wholly owned subsidiaries via business transfer agreements. The gas transportation arm will be moved to PG Transco Sdn Bhd, gas processing to PG Gas Processing Sdn Bhd, and the utilities business to PG Utilities East Sdn Bhd, which falls under holding company PG Energia Sdn Bhd. The group expects to make the necessary application within three months, with completion targeted for the third quarter of 2026, barring any unforeseen delays. According to MBSB Research, the exercise is aimed at streamlining operations, reducing redundancies and optimising processes, which will ultimately allow PETGAS to better focus on regulatory and compliance standards. The analysts added that the restructuring will enhance transparency and accountability across divisions, as each unit will be required to manage its own operational and financial records. This, they said, will provide clearer visibility into the performance of individual segments. The clearer structure is also seen as potentially easing future corporate exercises, such as mergers, acquisitions, joint ventures or divestitures, by making the group’s underlying value more evident to the market. MBSB Research noted that while the reorganisation will not affect PETGAS’s issued share capital or the holdings of substantial shareholders, nor will it materially impact earnings or net assets for financial years ending 2025 and 2026, the longer-term outlook points towards improved efficiency, cost savings and better capital management. These factors, it said, should lead to greater shareholder value in the future. As of 10.23 am, PetGas noted a slight decrease of 0.11% to RM18.580. title: Near-Term Cost For KPJ’s Latest Digitalisation Efforts
body: MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB Research) has maintained a NEUTRAL call on KPJ Healthcare Bhd with an unchanged target price of RM2.65, noting that the group’s latest move to adopt a secure digital communication platform aligns with its broader digitalisation strategy but carries operational and cost-related risks. The research house said KPJ will implement NetSfere’s secure communication system across all 30 of its hospitals, following an initial rollout at its Pasir Gudang and Ampang Puteri specialist facilities. The platform provides healthcare professionals with encrypted messaging, voice and video calls, secure file sharing and administrative controls designed to comply with the Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA) and international healthcare standards. MBSB Research highlighted that NetSfere, hosted on Amazon Web Services (AWS), is a global provider of enterprise messaging and collaboration solutions often adopted in highly regulated industries such as healthcare. The system is also designed to meet international regulatory frameworks, including HIPAA, GDPR and SOX, while ensuring that complete data is stored within Malaysia in line with local requirements. The research firm said the initiative supports KPJ’s ongoing efforts to enhance hospital management and patient experience through digitalisation. By replacing consumer-grade messaging apps with a compliant and secure alternative, the platform is expected to streamline clinical workflows while allowing the use of personal devices, which could help the group optimise hardware costs. However, MBSB Research cautioned that such platforms come with potential challenges. These include stringent protocols that may slow urgent communication, the need for staff training during the transition, risks of information overload, high implementation and maintenance costs, as well as IT management complexities for personal devices. Cybersecurity threats remain a persistent risk, though the analysts noted NetSfere’s enterprise-grade security should provide sufficient safeguards. As digitalisation forms part of KPJ’s long-term strategic plan, the analysts said the adoption of NetSfere had already been factored into their valuation. With no material changes to earnings forecasts, the Neutral call and RM2.65 target price remain unchanged. KPJ Healthcare’s stock price is down 0.72% to RM2.770. title: Markets Scale New Highs As Investors Downplay US Shutdown Risks
body: Global equities surged to record levels on Wednesday, as traders shrugged off the first United States government shutdown in almost seven years and placed stronger bets on further interest rate cuts from the Federal Reserve. The S&P 500 rose 0.3% while the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 added 0.5%, lifting both indices alongside an MSCI global benchmark to fresh highs. The rally extended into Asia, with early Thursday trading showing gains in futures for Australia, Japan and Hong Kong. Treasuries advanced after a weaker-than-expected private payrolls report suggested the labour market is cooling, reinforcing speculation that the Fed will ease policy further. The 10-year yield slipped five basis points to about 4.1%. Gold inched up to a new peak, while the dollar held steady. “The market is going to have to focus on independent private sources to get a sense of what’s going on,” said Brij Khurana, portfolio manager at Wellington Management, noting that the shutdown could delay crucial government data. The ADP report revealed an unexpected fall in September payrolls at US companies, adding to signs of labour market softness. Factory activity contracted for a seventh consecutive month, according to ISM figures. Traders increased wagers on two more Fed rate cuts this year, with Berenberg economist Atakan Bakiskan saying officials would have “enough information about the labour market” to deliver another 25-basis-point reduction in October even if nonfarm payroll data is delayed. While investors remained calm over Washington’s political standoff, concerns are mounting about the possibility of prolonged disruption. Vice President JD Vance told reporters he did not expect the shutdown to last long, though he cautioned layoffs would follow if it extends beyond days. White House Budget Director Russell Vought indicated non-essential federal staff could be swiftly dismissed. Analysts noted this shutdown carries unique risks. “What sets this shutdown apart is the threat of permanent layoffs for non-essential federal staff, which, while possibly political bluster and subject to legal challenges, could prolong the drag on public sector payrolls,” said Thomas Ryan, North America economist at Capital Economics. Still, some strategists remain unfazed. Citigroup’s head of US equity trading strategy Stuart Kaiser said equity markets are unlikely to be hit unless the shutdown drags on significantly, creates large-scale job losses or triggers instability in bond markets. In the corporate sector, BYD Co. reported its first monthly sales decline in more than a year and a half. Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix secured initial deals to supply chips and equipment for OpenAI’s Stargate artificial intelligence project. Oil prices slipped after a volatile session as investors weighed prospects of OPEC+ accelerating output increases, even as US crude inventories expanded. West Texas Intermediate hovered at US$61.70 a barrel, while Brent settled near US$65. Gold traded around US$3,860 an ounce. Bitcoin rose slightly to US$117,893, while Ether fell to US$4,320. Former Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers cautioned that the shutdown fight was “all about the future of American healthcare,” warning that millions could face losing access to affordable coverage if political brinkmanship deepens. title: Dollar Falls As Traders Assess Govt Shutdown, Poor Jobs Data
body: The dollar fell to near a one-week low on Thursday as traders weighed the impact of a U.S. government shutdown, while poor jobs data boosted expectations the Federal Reserve will cut interest rates two more times this year. The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of six currencies, fell 0.2 per cent to 97.52.After four straight days of losses for the dollar, traders were weighing how long the U.S. government shutdown might last, its effect on economic data releases, and how that will play into the Fed’s decision making. The ADP National Employment Report showed on Wednesday that U.S. private employment shrank by 32,000 jobs last month after a downwardly revised 3,000 decline in August. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast private employment to increase by 50,000.”U.S. ADP employment data triggered dollar weakness,” said Kit Juckes, Societe Generale’s chief currency strategist. “The sense is that the market was happy to react to yesterday’s figures but will not be comfortable taking the dollar too far on less reliable data,” he said. The jobs report came amid a U.S. government shutdown, which has put the brakes on the flow of federal economic data at a moment of uncertainty and division among policymakers. The Trump administration on Wednesday froze $26 billion for Democratic-leaning states, following through on a threat to use the shutdown to target Democratic priorities. “With many major U.S. data releases withheld due to the government shutdown, alternative measures (yesterday’s ADP, today’s Challenger data) are set to have a longer-lasting impact on markets than usual,” said Francesco Pesole, FX strategist at ING. Data also showed on Wednesday that U.S. manufacturing activity edged up in September, though new orders and employment were subdued as factories grappled with the fallout from President Donald Trump’s sweeping tariffs. In the meantime, the U.S. Supreme Court said it would hear arguments in January over Trump’s attempt to remove Fed Governor Lisa Cook. Money markets are expecting two further Fed interest rate cuts this year. title: Wall Street Futures Slip As Shutdown Fears Cloud Economic Outlook
body: US stock index futures edged lower on Tuesday as investors grew cautious over the looming risk of a government shutdown, while awaiting key labour market and consumer sentiment reports that could shape the Federal Reserve’s policy stance. At 5:07 a.m. ET, Dow E-minis fell 104 points, or 0.22%, S&P 500 E-minis slipped 11.25 points, or 0.17%, and Nasdaq 100 E-minis lost 39 points, or 0.16%. Analysts noted that while shutdowns typically result in short-lived disruptions, the timing of the current threat is more delicate given uncertainties around growth and inflation. “Shutdowns are more apt to be a temporary disruption rather than a permanent drag where the short-term economic impacts are often recouped over time,” said Jack Janasiewicz, lead portfolio strategist at Natixis Investment Managers. “However, the length of any shutdown can impact the collection and release of important economic data, especially at a time when the economy is at a crucial juncture.” The Federal Reserve’s data-dependent approach has heightened the importance of upcoming releases, with investors looking closely at the Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey for August and the Conference Board’s consumer confidence index later in the day. A busy slate of Fed speakers, including Vice Chair Philip Jefferson and regional presidents Susan Collins, Austan Goolsbee and Lorie Logan, is also on watch for policy cues. Despite the jitters, equities have held firm through the third quarter. The S&P 500, Nasdaq and Dow are all set to post gains for a second straight quarter, heading into what is historically a strong fourth quarter driven by year-end positioning and holiday spending. Corporate updates are expected to play a bigger role in the coming weeks. Nike is due to report earnings after Tuesday’s close, offering insights into consumer demand and margins at a time of price hikes. In other moves, Wolfspeed surged 49% a day after exiting bankruptcy, while Firefly Aerospace tumbled 10.7% following a testing mishap that destroyed the core booster of its Alpha rocket. title: Stock Today: V.S Industry Edges Higher Despite Weak FY25 Earnings
body: V.S Industry Bhd’s (VSI) share price inched up in early trade today, rising 0.85% to RM0.595 at 11.58 am, despite analysts maintaining cautious views following the group’s disappointing fourth quarter and full-year FY25 performance. The counter added half a sen from the previous close of RM0.590, with 39.3 million shares traded. It opened at RM0.590 and touched an intraday high of RM0.620 before paring gains. Buy and sell queues stood evenly balanced, with 2.48 million shares on the bid and 1.84 million on the offer side. CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) and Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) have both reiterated Hold calls on VSI, lowering their target prices to RM0.64 and RM0.54 respectively. VSI had slipped into a core net loss of RM6 million in 4QFY25, reversing from a RM23.7 million profit in the preceding quarter. The group also posted a net loss of RM33 million for the quarter compared with a RM23.1 million net profit in 3QFY25. No dividend was declared. For the full year, VSI’s core net profit plunged 69.6% year-on-year to RM62.5 million, while revenue dropped 10.8% to RM3.79 billion, missing both CIMB’s and consensus forecasts. Analysts attributed the slump to weaker orders from a US customer, the loss of Customer Y, rising Malaysian labour costs, and expansion-related losses in the Philippines, where operations recorded a pre-tax loss of RM24.9 million. HLIB noted that FY25 core profit after tax and minority interest stood at RM38.1 million, down 79.5% year-on-year and well below expectations at only a third of its forecast. Losses at the Philippines plant, cost-down initiatives, and impairments linked to HT Press were the key drags. Looking forward, both CIMB and HLIB revised down their FY26–27 earnings projections by up to 43%, citing ongoing demand uncertainty, inflationary pressures, and risks tied to reciprocal US tariff measures. Nonetheless, CIMB highlighted early signs of recovery with improved order flows in 1QFY26 and new models entering mass production, while management aims for breakeven in the Philippines by FY26. HLIB also expects losses at the plant to narrow by March 2026, though recovery may be slower than initially hoped. title: Stock Today: PPB Slips Slightly Despite Upgrade To Buy
body: PPB Group Bhd closed at RM10.14 as of 4.08 pm, down 6 sen or 0.59% from its previous close, with 826,400 shares traded. The stock opened at RM10.20, reaching a high of RM10.44 and a low of RM10.14 during the session. MBSB Investment Bank Bhd recently upgraded its call on PPB to BUY from NEUTRAL, raising the target price to RM11.02 from RM9.01. The research house cited the conclusion of a major litigation involving PPB’s associate, Wilmar International, as a key factor in removing overhangs on the stock. The litigation verdict required compensation of approximately US$708.9 million plus a fine of US$298,000, already deposited with Indonesia’s Attorney General’s Office and set to be transferred to the State Treasury. While this will cause Wilmar to report a net loss in Q3 FY25, the fine is not considered material relative to its typical quarterly earnings of US$300–400 million. MBSB Research revised Wilmar’s FY25 earnings forecast down 49.3% year-on-year to US$730.2 million (RM579.3 million), which led to a 38.1% cut in PPB’s earnings projection to RM778.4 million. Dividend forecasts were also trimmed to 25 sen per share, yielding 2.5%. Despite these near-term impacts, the research house expects Wilmar’s rebound from FY26 to support PPB’s long-term growth. Improvements in most of Wilmar’s divisions, alongside stabilising wheat prices and prudent feedstock procurement, are projected to sustain recovery. PPB’s core businesses are expected to maintain operating profits above RM360 million annually over the next three years. title: Stock Today: Maybank Edges Higher At Midday, Backed By Resilient Sector Outlook
body: Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) saw its shares trade marginally higher at midday, rising 0.20% to RM9.93 with 29.4 million shares changing hands as of 2.55 pm. The counter touched an intraday high of RM9.97 before easing slightly. The movement comes as analysts maintain a steady outlook on the banking sector. Both RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) and CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) have reiterated a NEUTRAL stance, though Maybank remains among their preferred picks alongside Hong Leong Bank, CIMB and Public Bank. RHB Research highlighted that banking system loans grew 5.4% year-on-year in August, in line with its full-year target of 4.5–5%. Growth was supported by a 5.7% expansion in household loans, particularly in mortgages and auto financing, as well as a 5% rise in non-household loans from finance, transport, communications and wholesale trade sectors. Deposits also posted steady growth, up 4% year-on-year, largely driven by current and savings accounts (CASA), which rose 6% and lifted the CASA ratio to 31.4%. Fixed deposit rates have trended lower since June, easing funding pressure on banks and helping to manage net interest margins. Meanwhile, asset quality across the sector remains stable, with gross impaired loan ratios holding at about 1.4%. Liquidity coverage ratios stayed elevated at 146–147%, while capital buffers were maintained with a CET1 ratio of 14.5%. Looking ahead, RHB Research expects stronger loan drawdowns from non-household segments towards year-end, supported by trade activity with the US. CIMB Securities, however, cautioned that the impact of July’s 25-basis-point policy rate cut on credit demand will take more time to materialise. Maybank, the country’s largest bank by assets, continues to be viewed by analysts as a resilient play given its scale, diversified earnings base and strong capital ratios. title: Gold Rises To RM523 per Gram, Tracks Global Gains

Over the past month, gold in Malaysia has gained 8.58%, while six-month performance shows a 16.24% increase. Year-on-year, prices have surged 46.45%, reflecting one of the strongest rallies in recent years. Silver also climbed higher, advancing 1.34% to RM2.62 per gram. The metal has outperformed gold in annual terms, rising 48.12% over the past year, with a five-year gain of nearly 97%. Globally, gold has posted strong annual returns in multiple currencies. In US dollar terms, the metal has risen 46.5% so far in 2025, its steepest climb since 2020. Gains were also notable in other major markets, with prices up 41.7% in Canadian dollars, 42.9% in Chinese yuan, and 52.1% in Indian rupees. Robust central bank purchases, steady demand from Asia, and ongoing geopolitical risks are key drivers of the rally. With inflationary concerns persisting and rate cuts from major central banks on the horizon, traders expect gold to remain well-supported heading into the final quarter of the year. title: Stock Today: Genting Malaysia Hovers Amid NYC Casino Licence Race
body: Genting Malaysia Bhd (GENM) was last done at RM2.10 as of 4.10 pm, down 0.47% or RM0.01, with 2.9 million shares traded so far. The stock opened at RM2.11, reaching an intraday high of RM2.13 and a low of RM2.09. Investors are closely monitoring Genting Malaysia’s unit, Resorts World New York City (RWNYC), which has emerged as a frontrunner in New York City’s bid for up to three new casino licences. RWNYC recently received unanimous backing from the Community Advisory Committee (CAC), a key step before proposals advance to the state’s Gaming Facility Location Board. Of eight submissions lodged in June, only RWNYC and MGM Resorts’ bids have received unanimous local support. RWNYC’s USD5.5 billion proposal offers faster delivery and larger scale compared with MGM’s USD2.3 billion bid, with an expected opening by mid-2026. Analysts at Kenanga Research said the project ticks three major boxes — speed, scale, and safety — but noted Genting may still require USD2–3 billion in additional funding to complete the project, which could involve debt, asset disposals, or equity issuance, adding execution and dilution risks. GENM currently has net debt of RM11.3 billion and limited additional borrowing headroom. Past attempts to sell non-core assets, including a Miami land parcel valued at USD1.2 billion, have yet to materialise. Kenanga maintained its Market Perform rating and RM2.00 target price, noting that a successful licence bid could potentially lift GENM’s valuation by RM0.50 per share, though risks remain from funding, execution, and macroeconomic headwinds. So far today, the stock has seen a buy volume of 845,800 shares against a sell volume of 385,600 shares, reflecting investor interest as RWNYC’s licence bid progresses. title: Stock Today: Gamuda Edges Up Near 1% Amid Singapore Land Win
body: Gamuda Bhd’s stock rose 0.91% to RM5.57 as of 2.53 pm, with 8.73 million shares traded, following the group’s recent acquisition of a prime land parcel in Singapore’s Chencharu Close. The stock opened at RM5.52, reaching a high of RM5.63 and a low of RM5.52, reflecting steady investor interest. MBSB Investment Bank Bhd and Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) have both maintained their BUY calls on Gamuda, with target prices of RM6.35 and RM6.88 respectively. Analysts cited the company’s all-time high order book of RM35.8 billion, diversified portfolio across construction, property and utilities, and strong recurring income prospects as key positives. The Chencharu Close project, won by a consortium led by Gamuda’s wholly owned subsidiary Gamuda (Singapore) Pte Ltd with Evia MCS Pte Ltd and H108 Pte Ltd, was secured for S$1.01 billion (RM3.33 billion), 19.8% above the next bid. The 29,450 sq m site carries a 99-year leasehold tenure and is earmarked for an integrated residential and commercial development, including 875 homes, 12,600 sq m of commercial space, a bus interchange, and a hawker centre. Gamuda holds a 50% stake in the joint venture. HLIB highlighted that the mixed-use parcel represents a quick-turnaround development with meaningful earnings potential, projecting Gamuda’s profit share from the project to reach RM380 million to RM520 million at low to mid-teens margins. Earnings contributions are expected to begin in FY27, with the project slated for launch in November 2026. MBSB Research said the acquisition complements Gamuda’s portfolio of quick-turnaround projects, supporting a sales target of RM5.5 billion for FY26, driven by Vietnam projects and new mid-upper range launches in Malaysia. Both research houses kept earnings forecasts unchanged, with HLIB slightly revising FY27 core profit after tax and minority interest (PATAMI) upwards by 3.2% following the inclusion of the project. Investors appear confident that Gamuda’s regional expansion, coupled with strong momentum in its construction and property segments, will sustain growth, reinforcing the stock’s appeal amid attractive valuations. title: Stock Today: AEON Credit Climbs 2.6% As Investors Look Past Profit Slip
body: AEON Credit Service (M) Bhd’s (AEON Credit) shares gained 2.62% at midday, closing at RM5.49, up 14 sen from the previous close of RM5.35, with 6.88 million shares changing hands. The stock traded between RM5.31 and RM5.49 during the session. The buying interest came despite weaker quarterly earnings, as AEON Credit’s 2QFY26 net profit slipped 6.9% quarter-on-quarter to RM72.2 million, though it edged up 1.5% year-on-year. Higher impairment provisions on financing receivables and losses from AEON Bank weighed on the bottom line, bringing first-half profit to RM149.8 million, down 15.7% from a year earlier and below expectations. CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) has maintained a HOLD rating with a target price of RM5.70, citing mixed credit quality and persistently high net credit costs, which climbed to 5.02% from 4.98% in the preceding quarter. While AEON Credit declared a dividend of 13 sen, lower than 14.25 sen a year earlier, its non-performing loan ratio improved marginally to 2.49% from 2.57%. CIMB Securities noted that the stock’s current valuation of 0.9 times FY26 price-to-book value is below its five-year average of 1.2 times but considers the discount fair given limited catalysts for a re-rating. Key risks flagged include further AEON Bank losses, funding cost pressures, and potential asset quality deterioration, though upside could come from stronger receivables growth. title: Ringgit Edges Higher Against US Dollar
body: The ringgit opened stronger against the US dollar on Tuesday, standing at 4.2125/2210 compared with Monday’s close at 4.2150/2200. The local note was supported by concerns that a potential United States government shutdown could weigh on the greenback. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said a US government shutdown would be significant, as it could hamper the functioning of key agencies such as the Bureau of Labor Statistics. “If materialised, it would result in difficulties in discerning the latest trend in the US labour market at a time when the Federal Reserve (Fed) has highlighted increased downside risks to employment,” he told a local news outlet. He noted that the release of important data points, such as the nonfarm payroll report due this Friday, might be delayed. Mohd Afzanizam said the US Dollar Index (DXY) was down about 0.25% to 97.906 points. He added that the ringgit, which gained 0.12% to RM4.2175 against the US dollar yesterday, is expected to trade between RM4.20 and RM4.21 today. “Again, the ringgit could attempt to breach the psychological level of RM4.20, especially if the Fed proceeds with interest rate cuts should a government shutdown occur,” he said. At the opening, the ringgit was mostly higher against a basket of major currencies. It firmed to 2.8340/8399 against the Japanese yen from 2.8365/8400 at Monday’s close, and increased to 5.6582/6696 against the British pound from 5.6612/6679. However, it slipped to 4.9404/9504 versus the euro from 4.9387/9446. The local note was also mostly higher against ASEAN currencies, except for the Thai baht. It advanced to 3.2653/2723 vis-à-vis the Singapore dollar from 3.2664/2706, edged up against the Indonesian rupiah at 252.5/253.1 from 252.6/253.1, and appreciated versus the Philippine peso at 7.24/7.26 from 7.25/7.26. It eased, however, to 13.0669/1002 against the Thai baht from 13.0649/0857 previously. title: Hiap Teck Shines From China’s Steel Curb
body: Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) has maintained its BUY call on Hiap Teck Venture Bhd (HTVB) with a higher target price of RM0.36 from RM0.34 previously, citing stronger earnings prospects from its associate Eastern Steel Sdn Bhd (ESSB) and improving industry conditions. At the current price of RM0.295, the research house said the stock offers a potential capital upside of 22% and an expected total return of 25.4%, including dividends. For the financial year ended July 2025, HTVB’s core net profit rose 11% to RM101.8 million, mainly driven by higher contributions from ESSB, in which it holds a 27.3% stake. ESSB’s core earnings surged 81% to RM126.7 million from RM70.1 million a year earlier, supported by increased output from its new blast furnace, the commencement of hot-rolled coil (HRC) production in the third quarter of FY25 and lower production costs from improved economies of scale and cheaper inputs. These contributions helped offset weaker performances in HTVB’s trading and downstream businesses, which were affected by softer selling prices and subdued domestic construction activities. HLIB Research noted that steel prices have begun to stabilise following the Chinese Government’s announcement of a new steel industry action plan. The measures, which include a ban on additional capacity and the accelerated phase-out of outdated equipment, are intended to address persistent oversupply in the market. While previous attempts have had limited success, management at HTVB believes the likelihood of success is higher this time, pointing to early signs of capacity reduction in China. Looking ahead, HLIB Research said HTVB’s trading and downstream segments, currently impacted by the transitional effects of the extended Sales and Service Tax, are expected to recover from early 2026. This will be supported by upcoming infrastructure projects such as the Northern Perak Water Supply Scheme and potential nationwide water pipe replacement initiatives, where HTVB is well-positioned with a sizeable pipe-making capacity of about 550,000 metric tonnes per annum. Meanwhile, utilisation at ESSB’s HRC plant, which began operations in December 2024, has increased to about 70% from 55% in the fourth quarter of FY25. Management aims to lift this rate to around 90% by the end of 2025, which would further lower unit conversion costs. In addition, the scaffolding business delivered a pre-tax profit of RM18 million in FY25 and is expected to strengthen further into FY26, supported by a pick-up in construction activity. HLIB Research raised its FY26–27 core net profit forecasts for HTVB by 15.4% and 15.2% respectively, to reflect higher earnings assumptions at ESSB. The research house said it continues to favour HTVB for its healthy balance sheet, with a net gearing of 0.26 times as at July 31 2025 and attractive valuations. At the current trading level, HTVB is priced at 4.9 times FY26 price-to-earnings and 0.33 times price-to-book, which are below its five-year historical averages. HLIB Research added that ESSB’s competitive cost structure has allowed it to sustain earnings despite a challenging environment and positions the company to benefit from demand recovery once market conditions improve. At 10.26 am, the stock price is stable at RM0.295. Over the past year, silver prices have increased by 50.73%, indicating a strong long-term performance despite the recent dip. The rise in gold prices reflects a global trend where investors are turning to precious metals as a hedge against economic instability and currency fluctuations. Analysts suggest that the ongoing economic challenges and geopolitical uncertainties may continue to support the upward momentum in gold prices in the near term. title: Buy On PPB Group After Removal Of Key Overhang
body: MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB Research) has upgraded its call on PPB Group Bhd to BUY from NEUTRAL with a revised target price of RM11.02 from RM9.01, noting that the conclusion of a major litigation involving its associate Wilmar International has removed a key overhang. At RM10.00, the stock offers an expected total return of 14.38%, inclusive of dividends. The research house said the final verdict on Wilmar International’s subsidiaries, collectively known as the Wilmar Respondents, required compensation of about US$708.9 million alongside a fine of US$298,000. The compensation, already deposited with Indonesia’s Attorney General’s Office and to be transferred to the State Treasury, covers profits gained, state financial losses and business and household sector damages. While the penalty will result in Wilmar recording a net loss in its third-quarter FY25 results, the fine itself is not considered material compared with Wilmar’s usual quarterly earnings range of US$300–400 million. Following the ruling, MBSB Research revised Wilmar’s FY25 earnings forecast lower by 49.3% year-on-year to US$730.2 million (RM579.3 million), which led to a 38.1% cut in PPB’s earnings projection to RM778.4 million. The dividend per share forecast was also trimmed to 25 sen from 35 sen, translating into a yield of 2.5%. Despite this near-term setback, MBSB Research said it sees most short-term risks as largely priced in, with PPB’s long-term outlook underpinned by Wilmar’s expected rebound from FY26 onwards. Improvements across most of Wilmar’s divisions, excluding plantation and sugar milling, are expected to sustain recovery, while moderating wheat prices and prudent feedstock procurement are set to support better crushing margins in the grains and agribusiness segment. The research house added that PPB’s core businesses are projected to maintain operating profit above RM360 million annually over the next three years. With risks from the litigation now cleared, valuations are seen as attractive relative to the group’s earnings potential, underpinning the decision to lift its recommendation to BUY. As of 10.30 am, the stock price is up by 1.20% to RM10.120. title: Sony Financial Share Jumps 40% In Market Debut
body: Shares in Sony Financial jumped as much as 40 per cent in their Tokyo trading debut on Monday, after the business was spun-off from entertainment and technology conglomerate Sony. Sony distributed shares in its finance arm, which includes banking and insurance, to shareholders through dividends in kind as it focuses on entertainment.It is the first partial spin-off in Japan taking advantage of a 2023 tax change and the first direct listing in more than two decades. The shares rose as high as 210 yen after changing hands for the first time at 10:13 a.m. in Tokyo, an hour and 13 minutes into the session, before trading at 201.6 yen as of 10:30 a.m. The reference price was 150 yen ($1.00).Sony Financial has said it will buy back up to 100 billion yen ($671.1 million) of its shares. Sony aims to expand its presence in entertainment from games to movies and music, and maintain its position as the leading manufacturer of image sensors. title: Dollar Slides As US Shutdown Fears Loom, Yen Strengthens Ahead Of Key Data
body: The US dollar fell on Monday amid growing concerns over a potential government shutdown, with the yen outperforming the euro ahead of a series of US economic releases that could shed light on the Federal Reserve’s policy trajectory. The dollar index, which tracks the greenback against a basket of major currencies, declined 0.22% to 97.90, after rising 0.5% last week following data that tempered expectations for Fed rate cuts. Traders currently price in 40 basis points of easing by December and 110 basis points by the end of 2026, roughly 25 bps lower than mid-September levels. Investors are closely watching whether Congress will pass a funding bill before the fiscal year ends on Tuesday. Without approval, parts of the government would shut down on Wednesday, potentially disrupting the release of Friday’s non-farm payrolls report and other key economic data. Bob Savage, head of macro strategy at BNY, noted a prolonged shutdown could hinder markets’ ability to correctly price the Fed’s easing cycle. The dollar was down 0.6% against the yen at 148.67 but gained ground against the euro and sterling, which rose 0.25% to $1.1729 and 0.34% to $1.3445 respectively. Analysts highlighted that eurozone inflation data is unlikely to shift the policy outlook, while geopolitical tensions, particularly the war in Ukraine, remain key drivers. Investors are also monitoring the legal challenge over Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook’s potential removal, with the Trump administration seeking Supreme Court approval to fire her. Analysts say any threat to the Fed’s independence could pose a greater risk to the dollar than a government shutdown. Elsewhere, the Australian dollar was last up 0.35% at $0.6571 ahead of the Reserve Bank of Australia’s rate announcement on Tuesday, where rates are expected to remain unchanged. title: Asia Stocks Cautious As US Shutdown Looms
body: Asian markets opened the week on edge with investors preparing for a potential US government shutdown that could stall the release of September’s payrolls and other key economic data. President Donald Trump is scheduled to meet congressional leaders from both parties later on Monday to negotiate government funding. Without an agreement, a shutdown will begin Wednesday, coinciding with new tariffs on heavy trucks, pharmaceuticals and other goods. Bank of America analysts wrote, “If the shutdown lasts beyond the Fed meeting, the Fed will rely on private data for its policy decisions. On the margin, we think this may lower the likelihood of an October cut, but only marginally.” Markets currently price in a 90% chance of a Federal Reserve cut in October, with about a 65% probability of another in December. Analysts also noted that each week of closure would shave only 0.1 percentage point off growth, though permanent worker layoffs could weigh on payrolls and consumer sentiment. A prolonged shutdown may also leave the Fed “flying blind” at its October 29 meeting. Elsewhere, geopolitical focus turned to Quantico, Virginia, where Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth will convene U.S. generals and admirals on Tuesday, with Trump expected to attend. Despite the risks, analysts pointed to seasonal support, as the fourth quarter has historically been strong for equities. The S&P 500 has advanced in 74% of fourth quarters. S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures rose 0.2%, while Eurostoxx 50, FTSE and DAX futures each added 0.3%. In Asia, Japan’s Nikkei fell 0.7% but still showed a 6% gain for September. South Korea’s market climbed 1.2% to bring monthly gains to 6.3%. MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan rose 0.4%, up nearly 4% for the month. Bond markets saw Treasuries steady at 4.17% after upbeat US data last week curtailed expectations of deeper Fed cuts. The dollar index held at 98.134, with the euro at $1.1708 and the yen at 149.49. Gold traded just below record highs at $3,764 an ounce. Oil slipped after crude resumed flowing from Iraq’s Kurdistan to Turkey for the first time in 2½ years. Brent crude was down 0.8% at $69.57 per barrel, while U.S. crude eased 0.9% to $65.14. title: Wall Street Rises But Weekly Losses End Winning Streaks
body: US stocks closed higher on Sept 26 as investors welcomed in-line inflation data, though all three major indexes ended the week in the red after a choppy stretch of trading, Reuters reported. The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 299.97 points (0.65%) to 46,247.29, the S&P 500 rose 38.98 points (0.59%) to 6,643.70 and the Nasdaq Composite added 99.37 points (0.44%) to 22,484.07. For the week, the Dow slipped 0.2%, the S&P 500 fell 0.3% and the Nasdaq lost 0.7%, snapping three-week winning streaks for the latter two. The gains on Sept 26 followed the Commerce Department’s personal consumption expenditures (PCE) report for August, which showed inflation rising 0.3% on the month and 2.7% year-over-year, exactly matching forecasts. The PCE index, the Federal Reserve’s preferred inflation gauge, reinforced expectations that price pressures are cooling gradually even as consumer spending and incomes rose more than expected. The data comes as markets weigh a resilient US economy against prospects for further Fed rate cuts. The central bank lowered rates last week for the first time since December and signalled more easing ahead. In stock moves, Paccar rallied 5.2% after President Donald Trump unveiled new import tariffs, including on heavy-duty trucks, a segment where Paccar manufactures largely within the US Eli Lilly gained 1.4% after tariffs were also placed on pharmaceutical products. Electronic Arts surged 14.9% amid reports the video game maker is in advanced talks to go private. Meanwhile, Costco Wholesale fell 2.9% after posting quarterly results that disappointed investors. Investors now turn to the September jobs report due Oct 3, with a potential government shutdown looming as a wildcard for data releases and market sentiment. President Lee Jae Myung unveiled plans to shift the foreign exchange market to 24-hour trading to boost access and support Korea’s MSCI developed market ambitions. Analysts expect continued volatility as investors monitor US data, Fed signals and trade developments. title: Wall Street Ends Lower As Data Clouds Rate-Cut Outlook
body: US stocks finished weaker on Thursday as fresh economic data cast doubt on the pace of future interest rate cuts by the Federal Reserve. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 173.96 points or 0.38% to 45,947.32, the S&P 500 shed 33.25 points or 0.50% to 6,604.72, while the Nasdaq Composite declined 113.16 points or 0.50% to 22,384.70. Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee warned against cutting rates too quickly, adding to market caution. The developments tempered expectations of another 25 basis-point cut in October, with the CME FedWatch Tool showing odds easing to 83.4% from 92% a day earlier. Investors now await Friday’s Personal Consumption Expenditures price index, the Fed’s preferred inflation gauge. Most S&P 500 sectors closed in the red, though energy gained 0.9% and technology eked out a 0.03% increase as Intel surged 8.9% on reports of talks with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company. CarMax plunged 20.1% after disappointing results, while Accenture slipped 2.7% despite beating revenue forecasts. The weakness on Wall Street is expected to weigh on Asian markets, with Singapore’s Straits Times Index opening marginally higher on Friday but broader sentiment cautious, while Hong Kong futures pointed lower and Japan’s Nikkei traded firmer. The increase continues a broader upward trend, with gold up 9.48% over the past 30 days, 16.65% in six months, and 44.47% over the past year. Over five years, the price of gold has more than doubled, rising 101.13%, and in two decades it has surged 803.92%, highlighting its role as a long-term store of value. Silver mirrored this trend, rising 12.48% over the past month and 44.92% over the past year. Globally, gold has also been gaining. In US dollars, the annual increase for 2025 stands at 42.5%, while in euros it is 26.6% and in British pounds 33.8%. Gold has also recorded notable gains in other markets, with a 47.8% rise in India and 35.8% in Japan. Market observers note that ongoing economic uncertainty and global inflation pressures have driven demand for precious metals as a hedge, while fluctuations in currency rates continue to influence local prices. The Malaysian Ringgit’s performance against major currencies contributes to the upward momentum of gold domestically. title: Bargain Hunting Drives FBM KLCI Past 1,609
body: Bursa Malaysia rebounded strongly on Sept 26, closing the week on a positive note as investors chased bargains in heavyweight stocks, defying a broader regional downtrend triggered by fresh US tariff concerns. At 5pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) climbed 10.58 points to 1,609.05 compared to yesterday’s close of 1,598.47. The benchmark opened weaker at 1,597.01 but recovered to trade between 1,595.32 and 1,611.32 throughout the day. Regional markets slipped after US President Donald Trump announced additional tariffs on furniture, heavy trucks and pharmaceuticals, including a 100% levy on branded or patented drugs unless manufactured domestically in the US. Index-linked stocks led the rebound, with Maybank adding 10 sen to RM9.89, Public Bank rising six sen to RM4.34 and TNB advancing 14 sen to RM13.34. Healthcare giant IHH Healthcare rebounded 13 sen to RM7.50, while CIMB Group edged up one sen to RM7.25. Among actively traded counters, Zetrix AI, Tanco Holdings and VS Industry each inched up one sen, while Bumi Armada gained half a sen to 36.5 sen. Pharmaniaga, however, slipped 1.5 sen to 26.5 sen. On the broader market, the FBM Emas Index rose 53.02 points to 11,993.44, the FBM 100 Index gained 56.71 points to 11,725.04, and the FBM Emas Shariah Index climbed 30.91 points to 12,048.47. The FBM ACE Index added 49.20 points to 5,200.46, while the FBM 70 Index eased 7.13 points to 16,850.35. Sector indices also saw broad gains. The Financial Services Index jumped 125.64 points to 18,156.84, the Industrial Products and Services Index added 1.68 points to 173.76, the Energy Index advanced 2.61 points to 782.52, and the Plantation Index gained 4.84 points to 7,762.65. Analysts said the rebound reflected opportunistic bargain hunting in key blue chips, though external trade tensions may continue to weigh on regional sentiment in the near term. title: Wall Street Slips As Investors Trim Gains Ahead Of Inflation Data
body: Wall Street ended lower on Wednesday, with investors locking in profits near record highs after US Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell cautioned that stock valuations may be stretched. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 171.50 points, or 0.37%, to 46,121.28. The S&P 500 lost 18.94 points, or 0.28%, to 6,637.98, while the Nasdaq Composite shed 75.62 points, or 0.33%, to finish at 22,497.86. Powell on Tuesday remarked that “asset prices appeared fairly highly valued”, underscoring the delicate balance the Fed faces in supporting a soft labour market without fuelling inflation. Some analysts compared his warning to Alan Greenspan’s “irrational exuberance” remark in 1996. Ron Albahary, chief investment officer at LNW in Philadelphia, said: “With the S&P pricing in 23-24 times expected earnings and expectations priced into that multiple of about 15% annualised earnings growth over the next five years, that sounds pretty rich to me. So not that we’re market timers at all, but the idea that people might be using this, using the Fed’s comments, Powell’s comments as just a reason to trim back a little bit makes sense to me.” Valuation measures for US equities are at their highest since 2021. A continued climb would push them to levels not seen since the internet boom. Among sectors, materials fell 1.6%, with Freeport-McMoRan plunging 17% after declaring force majeure at its Grasberg mine in Indonesia. Energy stocks bucked the trend, rising 1.2% as crude oil hit a seven-week high following an unexpected drop in US inventories. Elsewhere, data showed US new home sales surged 20.5% in August. In corporate moves, Lithium Americas nearly doubled after reports that the Trump administration is considering a 10% equity stake in the firm alongside a potential US$2.26 billion government loan for its Thacker Pass project with General Motors, which rose 2.3%. UBS upgraded GM to “buy” from “neutral.” Micron Technology lost 2.8% after earnings, while Oracle slid 1.7% following reports it is seeking US$15 billion in corporate bond sales. Investors now await the Fed’s preferred inflation gauge, the personal consumption expenditures (PCE) index, due later this week. Declining stocks outnumbered advancers by 1.88 to 1 on the NYSE and 1.35 to 1 on the Nasdaq. The S&P 500 logged 21 new highs and 10 new lows, while the Nasdaq posted 85 new highs and 55 new lows. title: Stock Today: MISC Slips Amid Ammonia-Fuelled Tanker Milestone
body: MISC Bhd slipped 0.55% to RM7.24 as of 12.04 pm today. The movement comes as the group, in collaboration with Samsung Heavy Industries (SHI), announced it has obtained Approval in Principle (AiP) from Bureau Veritas Marine & Offshore (BV) for the design of the world’s first ammonia-fuelled LR2 tanker powered by Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cell (PEMFC) technology. The design integrates PEMFC technology from Vinssen with an Ammonia Cracking System engineered by Panasia Co. Ltd., enabling full-scale power for vessel propulsion, cargo handling and onboard energy needs. MISC will serve as the ship owner and operator, SHI is responsible for vessel design and system integration, while BV ensures compliance, risk assessments and technical validation. The vessel aims to meet International Maritime Organization regulations while achieving zero direct emissions, reducing maintenance costs and preparing for future carbon taxation. MISC President and Group CEO Zahid Osman said, “Collaboration is the catalyst for maritime transformation and through this partnership, we are uniting industry leaders in realising a future where new technologies solve maritime’s greatest challenge, energy transition and decarbonisation.” Samsung Heavy Industries Chief Technical Officer Haeki Jang added, “Our ammonia-fuelled LR2 tanker powered by fuel cell represents a true step forward — delivering zero emissions, meeting future regulations, improving operational efficiency and offering scalability for wider adoption.” Related The movement comes as the group, in collaboration with Samsung Heavy Industries (SHI), announced it has obtained Approval in Principle (AiP) from Bureau Veritas Marine & Offshore (BV) for the design of the world’s first ammonia-fuelled LR2 tanker powered by Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cell (PEMFC) technology. title: Ringgit Holds Steady Against US Dollar Amid PBoC Fixing
body: The ringgit opened unchanged against the US dollar on Thursday at 4.2120/2170, as market sentiment was weighed by the People’s Bank of China’s (PBoC) weaker-than-expected yuan reference rate. SPI Asset Management managing director Stephen Innes said the move caught regional players off guard and added downside momentum on the local note. “With positioning heavily skewed toward short US dollar trades, the near-term outlook remains fragile, though any sharp moves are likely to be limited over the next 24 hours,” he said. He added that investors are now awaiting US data, with Friday’s personal consumption expenditure (PCE) inflation and next week’s non-farm payrolls (NFP) to determine the US Federal Reserve’s next policy stance. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid noted the US Dollar Index (DXY) remained elevated at 97.687 points. “As such, the ringgit is likely to remain soft in the near term, hovering around RM4.21 and RM4.23,” he said. At the opening, the ringgit traded higher against the Japanese yen at 2.8310/8346 from 2.8400/8436 on Wednesday. It eased to 5.6647/6714 against the British pound from 5.6761/6828 and slipped to 4.9453/9512 against the euro from 4.9567/9626. The local note was mixed against ASEAN currencies. It advanced to 3.2687/2731 versus the Singapore dollar from 3.2724/2738, and strengthened to 13.1109/1334 against the Thai baht from 13.1572/1781. It was unchanged against the Indonesian rupiah at 252.4/252.8 and the Philippine peso at 7.33/7.34. title: Carlsberg, Farm Fresh Lead Gainers As Market Ends On Positive Breadth
body: The stock market saw a firmer close on Sept 25, with market breadth remaining positive as gainers outpaced decliners, supported by selective buying in consumer, plantation and construction-related counters. Carlsberg Brewery Malaysia Bhd topped the gainers’ list, rising 26 sen to RM16.86 with 278,300 shares traded. It was followed by Farm Fresh Bhd, which surged 24 sen to RM2.41 on heavy volume of 20.2 million shares, making it the most actively traded among the top gainers. Other top gainers include Malayan Cement Bhd, which added 23 sen to RM6.73 with 3.8 million shares transacted, while Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd advanced 22 sen to RM20.26 and Ajinomoto (Malaysia) Bhd gained 18 sen to close at RM13.82. On the flip side, Dutch Lady Milk Industries Bhd led the losers, slipping 24 sen to RM27.06, followed by Allianz Malaysia Bhd, which fell 22 sen to RM18.50. Petronas Dagangan Bhd eased 18 sen to RM22.12, Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd shed 16 sen to RM29.60, and Fraser & Neave Holdings Bhd slipped 14 sen to RM27.26. Market sentiment was underpinned by rotational play in selected blue chips, although profit-taking in consumer heavyweights capped further upside. title: Bullish Engulfing Lifts Hang Seng Index Futures, Pullback As Opportunity
body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has retained its long position on the Hang Seng Index Futures (HSIF) after the contract rebounded strongly on Wednesday, signalling easing bearish momentum. The HSIF gained 282 points to close at 26,484, after opening at 26,204 and dipping to the day’s low of 26,065 before recovering to a high of 26,582. It ended the session with a Bullish Engulfing candlestick pattern. However, in the evening session the index slipped 90 points to 26,394. title: Asian Stocks Set To Slip As Wall Street Rally Loses Steam
body: Asian equities were poised to retreat on Thursday, mirroring Wall Street losses as the momentum behind this year’s artificial intelligence-driven rally showed signs of fatigue. Futures for Australia and Hong Kong declined after the S&P 500, Nasdaq 100 and a global equities gauge each shed 0.3% overnight, extending the previous session’s drop. The selloff contrasted with a 2.8% gain in an index of US-listed Chinese companies. US Treasury yields advanced across the curve, with the 10-year yield climbing four basis points to 4.15%, while the dollar index rose 0.6%. The pullback suggests investors are pausing after a sharp run-up that has lifted the S&P 500 about 12% this year, led by AI heavyweights such as Nvidia Corp. Analysts said traders are now awaiting fresh catalysts amid headwinds from slowing labour markets and sticky inflation. “Timeout called,” said Craig Johnson of Piper Sandler. “The trend of strong gains isn’t over yet, but the short-term risk-reward profile is becoming more compressed as momentum fades.” In corporate news, Micron Technology Inc. slipped despite issuing an upbeat forecast, while Intel Corp. was reported to be seeking an investment from Apple Inc. Oracle Corp. raised US$18 billion through a debt sale. Policy risks added further pressure. South Korea’s prime minister warned that major investment projects in the US could stall over visa issues, while the Trump administration launched investigations into robotics, industrial machinery and medical device imports, raising fears of broader tariffs. Meanwhile, Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco President Mary Daly said more rate cuts may be needed but stressed caution in their implementation. At Bank of America, Savita Subramanian flagged that the S&P 500 is trading at statistically expensive levels on 19 of 20 metrics, although optimism remains tied to resilient corporate profits and AI-fuelled growth. Elsewhere, commodities were mixed. Copper prices surged after Freeport-McMoRan Inc. declared force majeure at its Grasberg mine in Indonesia. Gold dropped 0.7% while oil extended its gains for a second day. title: Press Metal Poised For Growth As Aluminium Prices Strengthen
body: Aluminium’s upward price trend is expected to underpin Press Metal Aluminium Holdings Bhd’s earnings momentum, Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB Research) said. In its latest note, HLIB said average LME aluminium prices climbed 7% quarter-on-quarter to US$2,560 per tonne in 3Q25, supported by tightening supply. “China’s production is operating near its 45 million tonnes per annum (Mtpa) cap, limiting further output growth, while LME inventories have dropped to multi-year lows at 468,000 tonnes compared to 751,000 tonnes in 2024,” the research house added. However, the research house noted that the MJP premium fell 41% to US$108 per tonne on subdued demand and elevated supply in Asia, which contributes about 60% of Press Metal’s revenue. Even so, realised selling prices are expected to hold steady, backed by hedging, with 50%-60% of FY25 sales already locked in at US$2,600 per tonne. HLIB Research further highlighted that Press Metal’s earnings are also set to benefit from softer input costs. “Carbon anode prices slipped 5% QoQ to RMB4,750 per tonne, while alumina costs remain manageable despite a modest 2% increase to US$362 per tonne in 3Q25,” it said. HLIB expects alumina prices to stay range-bound at US$330-US$370 per tonne, given a market surplus from new refining capacity in China and Indonesia. Looking ahead, the research house said Press Metal is expanding its upstream capabilities. Its 21.7%-owned Nan Shan Aluminium aims to double capacity to 4.0 Mtpa by 1H26, while the 80%-owned PT KAN refinery in Indonesia (Phase 1: 1-1.2 Mtpa) is targeted for completion by FY27. These projects are expected to eventually cover 45%-55% of Press Metal’s alumina requirement, strengthening feedstock security amid Indonesia’s bauxite export ban. “Aluminium prices should stay supported by supply restraint in China and growing demand from clean energy applications,” HLIB said, adding that Press Metal’s locked-in energy costs, track record as Malaysia’s aluminium proxy and hydro-powered operations give it a competitive edge. HLIB’s forecast remains unchanged, with a ‘Buy’ recommendation and target price of RM6.60, pegged to a 25 times FY26 earnings multiple. As of 11.30am, the counter is trading at RM5.75, up one sen from its Sept 23’s closing of RM5.74, with more than 2.34 million shares traded. title: Wall Street Extends Record Run As Tech Lifts Indexes
body: All three major US stock indexes closed at record highs for a third straight session on Monday, driven by gains in technology shares. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 66.27 points, or 0.14%, to 46,381.54. The S&P 500 gained 29.39 points, or 0.44%, to 6,693.75, while the Nasdaq Composite advanced 157.50 points, or 0.70%, to 22,788.98. Shares of Nvidia climbed 3.9% after the company announced plans to invest up to $100 billion in OpenAI and supply data centre chips, fuelling further optimism about artificial intelligence. Apple shares surged 4.3% after Wedbush raised its target price on stronger signs of demand for the iPhone 17, while Tesla rose 1.9%. Technology stocks led S&P 500 sector gains, ending 1.7% higher. “We’re certainly pointing out to clients and having portfolios reflect that we’re at all-time highs and valuations are getting stretched,” said Oliver Pursche, senior vice president and advisor for Wealthspire Advisors in Westport, Connecticut. “There needs to be a catalyst for stocks to move materially higher, and markets appear to be kind of ignoring potential headwinds.” The S&P 500 is now up 13.8% in 2025 and has gained 3.6% in September, a month traditionally weak for equities. Market breadth was positive, with advancing issues outnumbering decliners by a 1.22-to-1 ratio on the NYSE, and 1.38-to-1 on the Nasdaq. Some Federal Reserve officials voiced scepticism over the need for additional rate cuts. St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem and Atlanta Fed President Raphael Bostic both said last week’s quarter-point reduction was appropriate to manage unemployment risks, but stressed that lowering inflation remains the priority. Fed Governor Stephen Miran, who dissented at the last meeting, reiterated that “monetary policy is well into restrictive territory.” Investors are also watching political developments after US President Donald Trump introduced new visa fees for foreign workers, which drew criticism from technology executives. Tylenol maker Kenvue dropped 7.5% during trading on concerns Trump would link the painkiller to autism. After the market closed, he announced the FDA would advise pregnant women against acetaminophen use, sending Kenvue shares back up 4.7%. Volume on US exchanges reached 18.65 billion shares, compared with the 20-day average of 17.5 billion. A key focus this week will be the US personal consumption expenditures price index, a closely watched inflation gauge. title: Stock Today: KESM Jumps 10% Following Q4 Turnaround
body: KESM Industries Bhd surged 10.36% to RM3.73 as of 3.30 pm, with 550,500 shares traded, following the release of its fourth-quarter results ended July 31, 2025. The stock opened at RM3.40, hitting a high of RM3.80 and a low of RM3.40 during the session. The world’s largest independent provider of burn-in and test services returned to profitability in 4Q25, posting a net profit of RM0.22 million, reversing a net loss of RM0.98 million in the same quarter a year ago. Revenue for the quarter slipped slightly to RM53.5 million from RM56.5 million in 4Q24. The profit turnaround was attributed to tighter cost controls and operational efficiencies, helping the group end the financial year on a firmer footing despite challenging conditions. For FY25, KESM recorded a revenue of RM210.5 million, down 13% from RM243 million in FY24, with a net loss of RM8.2 million compared to a modest net profit of RM0.2 million previously. CEO Samuel Lim Syn Soo said, “FY25 tested the strength and adaptability of our team. Our decisive actions have enabled us to close the year on a stronger footing. This positive fourth quarter demonstrates our readiness to capture new opportunities as the market improves.” With global semiconductor sales projected to hit US$1 trillion by 2030, KESM sees artificial intelligence-driven technologies, data centres, and automotive applications as key growth drivers for its testing services. The company also announced an interim dividend of six sen per share, payable on October 28, 2025. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the move showed the authorities were taking a pragmatic approach to fiscal discipline. “At the same time, efforts are being made to ensure the risk of higher living costs does not erode consumers’ purchasing power. In some sense, it can be deemed credit-positive as the measure allows the technology embedded in MyKad to be fully utilised as part of policy tools. “Perhaps there will be more fine-tuning on how subsidies can be further rationalised, focusing on income levels. On that note, such a move can be constructive for the ringgit in the mid to long term,” he told a local news outlet. SPI Asset Management managing director Stephen Innes said the government’s subsidy, providing 300 litres per month to all Malaysians regardless of income, had effectively raised household disposable income. “With less money spent on fuel, consumers have more to spend elsewhere, offering additional support to the local economy. This, combined with global US dollar weakness, positions the ringgit to continue trading on a favourable trajectory today,” he said. Mohd Afzanizam also pointed out that the US Dollar Index (DXY) eased 0.31% to 97.34 points amid mixed signals from US Federal Reserve officials. “Atlanta Fed President Raphael Bostic, St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack were in the hawkish camp. “Meanwhile, Fed board member Stephen Miran, who voted for a 50 basis point cut at the last Federal Open Market Committee meeting, said the neutral rate is at 2.0%, suggesting the current monetary policy stance is highly restrictive,” he added. title: Pharmaniaga’s Reliance On Govt Both Risky And Beneficial
body: MBSB Research has maintained a BUY call on Pharmaniaga Bhd with a target price of RM0.32, projecting a potential return of 23.1% as the group moves beyond its regularisation plan and into new growth areas, particularly in biopharmaceuticals. The research house said Pharmaniaga completed its capital reduction exercise in August, with 19 new investors participating in a private placement. This resulted in the dilution of substantial shareholders’ holdings to 44% from 55%, and MBSB Research expects the company to exit PN17 status by the first quarter of 2026. A key driver for growth will be Pharmaniaga’s expansion into biopharmaceuticals. The company is expected to introduce over 91 new products in the next five years, including human insulin, which has already secured procurement from teaching hospitals and awaits the Ministry of Health (MoH) tender. MBSB Research noted that the product, expected to receive halal certification from JAKIM by the end of 2025, could potentially contribute up to 400 million doses to the public market over three years if the tender is secured. Other upcoming products include GLP-1, targeted for distribution from 2027, as well as vaccines such as influenza, hepatitis, PCV13 and hexavalent, with the latter in clinical trials. The group also aims to accelerate the production of generic drugs, planning to launch at least 10 new products annually compared to 2–3 previously, while expanding penetration into the private sector. To strengthen logistics, Pharmaniaga recently acquired a freehold factory and office building in Seberang Perai Selatan, Penang, for RM30 million. This acquisition is part of a government concession that requires the development of four new warehouses in Penang, Terengganu, Sabah and Sarawak. MBSB Research expects disposal gains from older facilities once these new warehouses are operational in 2027. The Indonesian operations, despite being profitable, face growth limitations due to logistics challenges and high interest rates, prompting Pharmaniaga to review its long-term strategy for the segment. Meanwhile, its environmental, social and governance (ESG) efforts may improve through plans to consolidate seven Klang Valley warehouses into one larger facility by 2029, which would cut costs and carbon footprint. On financials, the company recorded RM1.98 billion in revenue and RM33.5 million in core PATAMI for the first half of 2025, marking year-on-year growth of 10% and 18% respectively. Pharmaniaga has guided for logistics and distribution volumes to grow by 10–12% in the second half, with segment revenue expected to rise 15–20%. MBSB Research highlighted two challenges for Pharmaniaga: potential policy changes in drug pricing and dependency on government tenders, particularly for insulin. However, it said these risks are manageable given the company’s competitive pricing, halal certification, and vaccine concessions. In addition to pharmaceuticals, Pharmaniaga is also diversifying into consumables and small medical devices, which already contribute RM35–45 million annually. Looking ahead, the research house said the group is well-positioned to benefit from global pharmaceutical growth trends, including a market projected to exceed US$3 trillion by 2034. “Despite the challenges, the main positive driver for the group lies in its continued collaboration with the government to distribute its products to hospitals,” MBSB Research reported. “Manufacturing biopharmaceuticals, consumables trading and improvements in its Indonesia segment will be the growth areas moving forward.” As of 10.17 am, the stock price rose 1.92% to RM0.265. title: Deep Funding Pool Access For Solarvest
body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has maintained its BUY call on Solarvest Holdings Bhd with a higher target price of RM3.26 from RM2.95, representing a 20% upside potential. The research house said the proposed joint investment with Brookfield CTF Asia Holdings enhances Solarvest’s long-term earnings sustainability and solidifies its role in Malaysia’s energy transition. The agreement with Brookfield, a unit of Brookfield Asset Management which manages US$1 trillion in assets, will see both parties developing at least 1,500MWp of renewable energy projects in Malaysia over the next three to five years, mainly under the Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme (CRESS). Financing will be structured on a project basis, combining loans, bonds or sukuk, with Solarvest holding a 51% stake in each special purpose vehicle and Brookfield the remaining 49%. RHB Research noted that access to Brookfield’s deep funding pool and corporate offtaker network significantly improves project feasibility while accelerating renewable energy development in line with the National Energy Transition Roadmap. It added that this marks Brookfield’s first investment in Malaysia through its Catalytic Transition Fund, which has a US$5 billion mandate to channel capital into clean energy and transition assets in emerging markets across South and Southeast Asia. Through this partnership, Solarvest could potentially secure between RM3 billion and RM5 billion in engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning contracts, including those involving battery energy storage systems. The group will take the lead in project development, handling regulatory approvals, site identification, land leases and delivery, which could also provide additional earnings via developer margins and electricity sales. As of the first quarter of FY26, Solarvest’s outstanding orderbook stood at RM1.2 billion, with 77.8% comprising utility-scale projects. Management has guided for the orderbook to expand to RM2 billion by the end of 2025, supported by the upcoming MyBeST programme rollout in the fourth quarter of 2025, Large Scale Solar 5+ awards expected in the first half of 2026 and continued growth in utility-scale solar and CRESS-linked projects. The stock price is stable at RM2.720 as of 10.36 am. title: Bitcoin Dips 3% Before Clawing Back Losses
body: Cryptocurrency markets tumbled on Sept 22 as more than US$1.5 billion in bullish bets were liquidated, triggering the steepest wave of losses since March and wiping hundreds of billions off digital-asset valuations, Bloomberg reported. Ether, the world’s second-largest token, plunged as much as 9% to US$4,075 after nearly half a billion dollars of leveraged long positions were liquidated, according to Coinglass. Bitcoin sank 3% to US$111,998 before clawing back some losses, while other coins such as Solana, Algorand and Avalanche also dropped. Data showed over 407,000 traders saw their positions liquidated in 24 hours, dragging the overall crypto market below US$4 trillion, CoinGecko reported. By mid-morning in London, Bitcoin was trading around US$112,700 and Ether at US$4,170, both still lower on the day. Analysts noted the selloff was broad and deep, though without a clear catalyst. “Unless Bitcoin can get back above US$115,000 and hold, the risk of deeper downside remains,” market commentators warned. The rout comes just weeks after Bitcoin and Ether hit record highs in August, fuelled by demand from listed vehicles hoarding tokens. That momentum has since cooled as shares of digital-asset treasury firms, including Michael Saylor’s Strategy and Japan’s Metaplanet Inc, retreated. Bitcoin has largely traded in a narrow US$110,100-US$120,000 band since July, even as gold — often compared to the original crypto — surged to fresh records near US$3,720 an oz. While easing US monetary policy has lifted equities and precious metals, crypto markets have struggled to sustain gains, with several top tokens nursing double-digit losses over the past week.
