title: Asia Stocks Outshine US As Dollar Weakens
body: The MSCI Asia Pacific Index has risen 22% this year, outpacing the S&P 500 Index by approximately eight percentage points, marking its largest annual outperformance since 2017. The regional rally is supported by cheaper valuations and a shift away from American assets. “Given this backdrop we are increasing our exposure to non-US equities including Asian equities relative to US equities,” said Chang Hwan Sung, a multi-asset portfolio manager in Invesco’s investment solutions team in Hong Kong. The preference, he added, is mainly driven by a bearish view on the greenback and “US capital outflows seeking international diversification and foreign currency appreciation.” The MSCI Asia gauge trades at 16 times forward earnings estimates, well below the S&P 500’s 23 times. The Hang Seng Tech Index, which surged to a four-year high last week, is valued at around 21 times forward earnings, compared to 27 times for the Nasdaq 100 Index, according to Bloomberg data. “We are tactically constructive on APAC equities’ relative performance in the remainder of the year versus US equities,” said Homin Lee, senior macro strategist at Lombard Odier Singapore Ltd. Stable commodity prices, lower US rates and easing trade disruption provide a favourable backdrop for Asian markets, he noted. While the Federal Reserve’s latest interest rate cut was widely expected, it reinforced a bearish outlook for the US currency and created space for Asian central banks to loosen policy further. Traders in the options market are paying a premium to hedge against continued strength in Asian currencies, with risk reversals staying positive for months. “The US remains the centre of gravity for AI and corporate earnings power, but Asia offers distinct angles,” said Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo Markets, pointing to “India’s domestic demand story, Japan’s banks amid Bank of Japan tightening, and selective China tech plays where policy support and monetisation are starting to align.” Still, risks remain. Any inflation-driven pause in the Fed’s rate-cut cycle, a hawkish shift in policy, or renewed deterioration in US-China ties could quickly reverse sentiment. Political uncertainties in Indonesia, Thailand and Japan are also being closely watched. title: Stock Today: Sunway Rises 1.49% Amid Singapore Expansion
body: Sunway Bhd shares climbed 1.49% to close at RM5.46 today, with a total volume of 13.7 million shares traded. The stock opened at RM5.40, reaching a high of RM5.47 and a low of RM5.38 during the session, reflecting investor interest amid its recent regional expansion moves. The gains come as Sunway finalises its S$738.7 million (RM2.4 billion) acquisition of Hongkong Land (MCL) Holdings Ltd in Singapore, a deal that does not require shareholder approval and is expected to be completed in the fourth quarter of FY25. The purchase significantly boosts Sunway’s footprint in Singapore, encompassing five mid-market residential projects with a combined gross development value of S$2.96 billion and an average take-up rate of 90%. Analysts view the move as a strategic expansion. MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB Research) maintained a NEUTRAL call on Sunway with a revised target price of RM5.13, citing MCL’s long-established track record with 48 residential projects completed since 1992, which will allow Sunway to leverage expertise and accelerate growth in the Singapore market. CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) kept its HOLD recommendation with an unchanged target price of RM5.15, noting that the acquisition will nearly triple Sunway’s unbilled sales in Singapore to RM5.9 billion. CIMB highlighted that the purchase consideration was pegged to MCL’s adjusted net asset value, providing immediate earnings visibility through strong take-up rates. Proforma estimates for FY24 suggest Sunway’s net profit could rise 6.1% to about RM1.2 billion, although net gearing is expected to increase to 55% from 41% as of December 2024. Sunway’s expansion also touches Malaysian operations, with MCL managing condominium projects in Wangsa Maju and Seremban, as well as owning Wangsa Walk Mall, which Sunway plans to redevelop into an integrated project. MBSB Research highlighted potential synergies in property development and investment, particularly in Klang Valley and Seremban. Earnings contribution from MCL is projected to be positive, with Sunway estimating net earnings of approximately RM67 million, potentially lifting FY26 forecasts by 7%. Analysts, however, caution that much of the upside is already priced into the stock, suggesting limited near-term re-rating potential despite the strategic benefits. body: Gamuda Bhd’s shares closed at RM5.65 on Monday, rising 13 sen or 2.36% from the previous day, with 13.4 million shares traded. The stock opened at RM5.60, reached a high of RM5.66 and a low of RM5.53, reflecting investor confidence following the release of the company’s record-breaking FY25 results. CIMB Securities noted Gamuda crossed the RM1 billion profit mark for the first time in FY25, clinching RM22.1 billion in new contracts and lifting its order book to RM38.4 billion, half of which is domestic. HLIB highlighted record-high unbilled sales of RM8 billion supporting property contributions in FY26, while expecting the year-end order book target of RM40–45 billion to be achievable. title: South Korea Exports Falter Under US Tariffs
body: South Korea’s exports showed signs of weakness in September as higher United States tariffs disrupted shipments, raising concerns for the trade-dependent economy. Exports adjusted for working days fell 10.6% in the first 20 days of the month compared with a year earlier, customs office data released on Monday showed. This contrasted with a revised 6% gain for the full month of August. Unadjusted exports, however, rose 13.5%, while imports climbed 9.9%, leaving a trade surplus of US$1.89 billion. South Korean exporters had front-loaded shipments in August before the US imposed a 15% universal tariff on Korean goods. That provided a temporary lift, but with early orders cleared, exports are now feeling the full drag from higher duties and softer global demand. Smartphones and laptops remain exempt, though President Donald Trump has warned he may extend tariffs to semiconductors. Semiconductors, the key driver of shipments this year, gained 27% in the first 20 days of September, extending momentum after a 30% jump in August. Auto exports rose by about 15%, while petrochemicals continued to face pressure from both tariffs and weaker global demand. Auto exporters also remain under strain as the 25% US tariff on Korean cars is still in effect until President Trump signs an executive order to bring it into line with the 15% universal rate. Lingering diplomatic frictions have further weighed on sentiment. An immigration raid in Georgia that led to the detention of more than 300 Korean workers at a battery plant under construction has complicated trade talks between Seoul and Washington. Although the workers were later released and sent home, the incident has heightened uncertainty in negotiations. title: Ringgit Opens Higher Against US Dollar On Credit Outlook, Economic Data
body: The ringgit opened slightly higher against the US dollar on Monday, supported by Malaysia’s stable sovereign credit outlook and stronger domestic economic data. At 8.02 am, the local note was quoted at 4.2000/2200 versus the greenback compared with Friday’s close of 4.2040/2115. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said S&P Global Ratings’ recent affirmation indicated that the government’s sovereign rating remains stable. He noted that Malaysia’s fiscal consolidation has contributed positively to its creditworthiness, with the fiscal deficit narrowing to 4.2% of gross domestic product (GDP) in the first half of 2025 from 5.5% in the same period last year, while government debt at 62% of GDP remains below the statutory limit of 65%. On Sept 20, the Ministry of Finance said S&P had reaffirmed Malaysia’s sovereign credit ratings at ‘A-’ with a stable outlook, underscoring confidence in the country’s macroeconomic management despite global trade uncertainty. The ministry added that the rating was supported by Malaysia’s well-diversified economy, political stability, steady growth momentum, balanced external position and narrowing fiscal deficits. Meanwhile, Mohd Afzanizam said the US Dollar Index (DXY) had rebounded after the US Federal Reserve delivered an interest rate cut last week. He said the DXY is hovering around 97 points and may continue to do so as traders and investors await further signals, with a series of Fed officials scheduled to speak at public forums and key data such as personal consumption expenditures (PCE) inflation being closely watched. SPI Asset Management managing director Stephen Innes said expectations of two more US rate cuts this year should limit the ringgit’s downside in the near term. He added that this followed a positive phone conversation between China’s President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump on Friday, which could pave the way for an in-person meeting at the 2025 APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting in South Korea next month. At the opening, the ringgit was also higher against a basket of major currencies. It rose versus the Japanese yen to 2.8348/8485 from 2.8419/8471 at Friday’s close, firmed to 5.6540/6810 against the British pound from 5.6775/6876, and strengthened to 4.9279/9513 versus the euro from 4.9447/9536. The local note also advanced against ASEAN currencies. It appreciated to 3.2670/2830 versus the Singapore dollar from 3.2744/2805, strengthened to 13.1707/2405 against the Thai baht from 13.1973/2271, edged up to 252.9/254.3 versus the Indonesian rupiah from 253.2/253.8, and firmed to 7.35/7.39 against the Philippine peso from 7.36/7.38. body: Gold prices in Malaysia continued their upward trajectory, with 24-carat gold trading at RM502.47 per gram as of early Monday, marking a daily gain of 0.81% or RM3.94. Per kilogram, gold rose to RM502,472.71, up RM3,941.45 or 0.79% from the previous session. Silver also saw gains, rising 1.20% or RM2.17 per gram, with similar long-term upward trends recorded across 30 days, six months, and one year. The consistent rises in the region mirror global investor interest in precious metals amid economic uncertainties. title: BOJ Plans Century-Long ETF Sell-Down, Markets Absorb News
body: The Bank of Japan will begin a century-long plan to unwind its ¥75 trillion (US$507 billion) stockpile of exchange-traded funds, aiming to reduce holdings by about ¥620 billion in market value each year. Markets initially reacted with declines on Friday but quickly pared losses, focusing on the gradual pace of the programme. The announcement came at the end of a week when the Nikkei-225 and Topix hit fresh record highs, underscoring confidence in Japanese equities after earlier shocks from the end of negative interest rates in 2024 and more recent US tariffs. Futures point to further gains in Tokyo on Monday. “Investors had been nervous about when the BOJ would start selling ETFs — a lot of them have been asking me about it,” said Seiichi Suzuki, chief equity analyst at Tokai Tokyo Intelligence Laboratory Co. “The timeframe for the sell-down of ETFs is positive and suggests limited market impact.” According to a person familiar with the matter, the sales could begin early next year. Investors are expected to watch closely the impact on heavily weighted Nikkei names, including Fast Retailing Co., which fell 4.5% on Friday and SoftBank Group Corp., which rose 0.7%. Kohei Onishi, senior investment strategist at Mitsubishi UFJ Morgan Stanley Securities Co., said the sales should be absorbed smoothly. “Japanese companies, under pressure from regulators and shareholders to stop cash hoarding, are buying back a large amount of their own shares annually,” he noted. Global investors have also driven the advance in Japanese equities, citing cheaper valuations compared to the US. Corporate governance reforms have supported this momentum, encouraging buybacks, M&A and stronger focus on shareholder returns. title: Stock Today: UWC Jumps Nearly 10% On Optimism From NVIDIA Deal
body: UWC Bhd surged 9.61% to RM3.65 as of 2.51 pm Friday, marking strong intraday gains for the semiconductor and electronics firm. The rally follows Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd’s (HLIB) reiteration of a BUY call on UWC, with a higher target price raised to RM4.20 from RM3.30. HLIB cited an expected turnaround in back-end (BE) orders tied to NVIDIA’s new partnership with one of UWC’s major customers, Customer I. NVIDIA announced plans to co-develop next-generation chips for data centres and PCs with Customer I, alongside a proposed US$5 billion investment in the company pending regulatory approval. HLIB projected that this development could accelerate Customer I’s recovery, particularly in CPUs, and significantly boost UWC’s volumes. UWC previously saw revenue contributions from Customer I decline from RM180 million in FY22 and RM107 million in FY23 to below RM30 million by FY25, with production line utilisation for this client currently below 30%. HLIB raised its assumptions for Customer I-linked revenue to RM64 million in FY26 and RM148 million in FY27, leading to an 11% and 37% uplift in earnings forecasts for FY26 and FY27, respectively. The research house also highlighted UWC’s expansion into front-end (FE) semiconductor segments as a structural positive, complementing the expected BE recovery and potential margin gains. Analysts noted that while risks remain, including potential cuts in semiconductor capital expenditure, UWC’s earnings outlook is supported by both structural and cyclical growth factors. title: Stock Today: MPI Rises 1.6% On Infineon Thailand Acquisition Plans
body: Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd (MPI) shares gained 1.61% to RM29.00 as at 2.30 pm today, with a high of RM29.60 and a low of RM28.54, on a volume of 451,200 shares. The stock opened at RM28.54, reflecting renewed investor interest amid the company’s ongoing expansion in the semiconductor sector. Both RHB Investment Bank Bhd and CIMB Investment Bank Bhd have reiterated BUY calls on MPI, raising their target prices to RM35 following the company’s proposed acquisition of Infineon Technologies Thailand Ltd (IFTH) for US$78 million (RM328 million). RHB Research said the acquisition will expand MPI’s semiconductor backend manufacturing footprint, strengthen regional diversification, and deepen ties with Infineon. While neutral in the near term, the research house expects stronger performance in FY26, supported by MPI’s technology roadmap and high-growth segments such as power semiconductors. RHB also noted that the purchase price, about 0.7 times IFTH’s FY24 net assets of RM470.7 million, is reasonable compared with the cost and time to build new facilities. CIMB Securities highlighted the strategic benefits of the deal, describing it as earnings-accretive over the medium term. IFTH’s existing customer base, including Infineon, ensures immediate offtake support, while MPI can drive operational efficiencies and lift margins closer to group levels. CIMB projected IFTH to contribute 8–12% of MPI’s revenue in FY27–28, boosting the group’s core net profit CAGR to 24% over FY25–28. The acquisition will be funded fully in cash, supported by MPI’s net cash of RM988 million and proceeds from the Dynacraft disposal. Completion is expected by 2QCY26 and does not require shareholder approval, as the transaction falls below the 25% threshold. RHB Research rolled forward its valuation to CY26, increasing its target price to RM35 from RM30.50, while CIMB lifted its target to RM35 from RM28.50, factoring in IFTH’s expected earnings contribution, AI data centre infrastructure rollouts, new power module programmes, and automotive segment recovery. Both research houses cautioned on potential risks including slower-than-expected industry recovery, customer loss, technology obsolescence, and currency fluctuations, but highlighted MPI’s exposure to silicon carbide and gallium nitride as a strong proxy for rising demand in power semiconductors. title: Ringgit Holds Below Key RM4.20 Level Despite Early Strength
body: The ringgit opened firmer against the US dollar on Friday, tracking the stronger performance of regional currencies, but later eased past the RM4.20 level as profit-taking set in. At 8 am, the local note stood at 4.1865/2100 against the greenback compared with Thursday’s close of 4.1945/1995. However, by 8.09 am it had weakened to 4.2005/2105. On Thursday, the ringgit depreciated 0.21% to RM4.197 against the greenback, staying below the RM4.20 psychological level although it briefly touched RM4.2013 at mid-day. At the same time, the ringgit was higher against a basket of major currencies. title: Palm Oil Prices Edge Up On Weak Ringgit, Lower Output Forecast
body: Palm oil rebounded from a one-week low, supported by a weaker Malaysian ringgit and expectations of lower production in the second-largest producer in September. “Output trend in Malaysia has been lower this month,” said Abdul Hameed, director of sales at Manzoor Trading Co. in Lahore. He added that the further fall in the ringgit attracted bargain buying, with traders covering October demand. However, gains in palm oil may be limited as festival buying in India, the world’s largest edible oil importer, is largely over, according to Gnanasekar Thiagarajan, head of trading and hedging strategies at Kaleesuwari Intercontinental. Malaysian palm oil exports rose 2.6% between September 1-15 compared with the previous month, according to Intertek Testing Services, while AmSpec Agri data showed exports were largely unchanged. On the markets, palm oil for December delivery on Bursa Malaysia Derivatives rose as much as 0.6% to 4,463 ringgit per tonne before trading at 4,447 ringgit at the midday break. Soybean oil for December in Chicago gained 0.1% to 51.17 US cents per pound, while refined palm oil for January on the Dalian Commodity Exchange rose 0.5% to 9,352 yuan per tonne. Soybean oil for January increased 0.8% to 8,352 yuan per tonne. Bloomberg data showed soybean oil’s premium over palm at around US$70 per tonne, above the one-year average of US$43, while palm’s premium over gasoil stood at US$359 per tonne, compared with a year-average of US$323. title: Japanese Stocks Gain As Investors Await BOJ Decision
body: Japanese equities advanced on Friday, buoyed by a Wall Street rally after the US Federal Reserve delivered its first interest-rate cut of the year, with investors turning their attention to the Bank of Japan’s policy decision later in the day. The Nikkei 225 Stock Average rose 0.7% to 45,635.80 while the broader Topix index added 0.5% to 3,174.04 as of 9.02 am Tokyo time. In the US, four key benchmarks closed at record highs as risk-on sentiment spread through the market. “The BOJ meeting is expected to pass uneventfully, with Governor Kazuo Ueda unlikely to offer clues on the timing of the next rate hike at his press conference,” said Masahiro Ichikawa, chief market strategist at Sumitomo Mitsui DS Asset Management Co. “The resignation of Prime Minister Ishiba, known for his fiscal discipline, has fueled expectations of greater fiscal spending ahead of the LDP leadership race, providing support for Japanese equities.” Most BOJ watchers expect policymakers to lift the benchmark interest rate by January, with the largest share predicting a move next month. The central bank is widely expected to keep rates unchanged today, following the resignation of Prime Minister Shigeru Ishiba earlier this month. The Liberal Democratic Party will vote for his successor on Oct 4. Markets will also be closely watching developments in the leadership race. Right-wing pro-stimulus contender Sanae Takaichi announced her candidacy on Thursday and is scheduled to outline her policy objectives at a press conference in Tokyo at 2:30 p.m. Friday. Investors are expected to parse her proposals for potential implications on equities, government bonds and the yen. title: Intel Soars On Nvidia Stake As Wall Street Hits Fresh Records
body: Wall Street’s major indexes closed at record highs on Thursday, lifted by a rally in semiconductor stocks after Nvidia revealed a US$5 billion stake in Intel, its struggling rival. Intel surged 22.8%, its sharpest daily jump since October 1987, following the announcement. Nvidia climbed 3.5%, reversing losses from the previous session when reports emerged that Chinese firms might cut back on buying its chips. The broader semiconductor index rose 3.6%, boosting the Nasdaq and the S&P 500 technology sector, which gained 1.36%. Advanced Micro Devices slipped 0.8%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average advanced 124.10 points, or 0.27%, to 46,142.42. The S&P 500 added 31.61 points, or 0.48%, to 6,631.96, while the Nasdaq Composite gained 209.40 points, or 0.94%, to 22,470.73. Seven of the 11 S&P 500 sectors ended higher. Meanwhile, the small-cap Russell 2000 index notched its first record close since November, rising to 2,466 points. Small-cap firms are seen as beneficiaries of a lower interest-rate environment. On Wednesday, the Federal Reserve delivered a quarter-point rate cut, with Chair Jerome Powell stressing the need to address a weakening jobs market and signalling that further reductions could be considered. “We are looking for support for economic growth and justification of stretched valuations and the prospect of lower interest rates helps that,” said Sam Stovall, chief investment strategist at CFRA Research. Fresh labour market data showed initial jobless claims fell last week, though signs of cooling remain as demand for and supply of workers diminish. Investors now expect around 44.2 basis points in cuts by the end of 2025, according to LSEG data. Among other movers, CrowdStrike rallied 12.8% after at least nine brokerages raised their price targets, while Darden Restaurants slumped 7.7% on weaker quarterly results. Consumer staples and consumer discretionary stocks were the biggest decliners on the S&P 500. The S&P 500 registered 31 new 52-week highs and eight new lows. The Nasdaq Composite recorded 156 new highs and 42 new lows. Trading volume reached 19.30 billion shares on US exchanges, above the 20-day average of 16.67 billion. title: Dollar Steadies As Markets Eye BOJ Decision, Fed Outlook
body: The US dollar held largely steady in Asian trading on Sept 19, edging up against the yen as investors awaited a policy decision from the Bank of Japan (BOJ) and weighed the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) cautious stance on rate cuts. Reuters reported that the dollar index rose 0.1%, recovering slightly from a three-and-a-half-year low hit on Sept 17 after the Fed trimmed rates by 25 basis points but signalled no rush to ease further. The greenback remains on track for a third straight weekly loss. Against the yen, the dollar firmed 0.1% to 148.09, after Japanese data showed core consumer prices grew at their slowest pace in nine months. Markets widely expect the BOJ to keep its policy rate unchanged at 0.5% later today. Investors are also watching US political risks, with the Supreme Court set to hear arguments in November on the legality of President Donald Trump’s sweeping tariffs, a cornerstone of his trade agenda. Trump has also escalated his criticism of the Fed and sought to fire Governor Lisa Cook, a move unprecedented in the central bank’s history. Treasury data showed sustained foreign appetite for US government debt, with overseas holdings hitting a record high in July, led by Japan and the UK. title: Wall Street Mixed As Fed Cuts Rates, Labour Market Fears Grow
body: The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 262.26 points, or 0.56%, to 46,012.75 on Wednesday, while the Nasdaq Composite slipped 73.10 points, or 0.33%, to 22,260.85. The S&P 500 fell 6.63 points, or 0.10%, to close at 6,600.13. The US Federal Reserve cut interest rates by 25 basis points, in line with expectations, and projected two more quarter-point reductions before year-end. Policymakers pointed to a weakening labour market as a key risk. “In a press conference, Powell tempered some of the initial enthusiasm in the markets for a more aggressive path of monetary easing. He noted the softness in the labour market, but reserves a larger cut for more serious conditions that are not present today,” said Michael Rosen, chief investment officer at Angeles Investments. “The Fed also raised its inflation forecast, highlighting the delicate balance between setting monetary policy to offset a weaker labour market versus bringing inflation lower,” he added. The central bank’s move had already been priced in, according to LSEG data. Powell noted that downside risks to employment were rising relative to inflation, but stressed that inflation risks still required management. The Fed’s decision and guidance will test Wall Street’s recent rally, which has been fuelled by optimism over rate cuts and strong trading in AI-linked stocks. Nvidia shares dragged on the Nasdaq after a report said China’s internet regulator had instructed top tech firms to halt purchases of the US chipmaker’s products. Elsewhere, Workday surged following reports that activist investor Elliott Management had taken a stake exceeding US$2 billion. Lyft also climbed after Alphabet’s Waymo confirmed plans to introduce autonomous cab rides in Nashville with the ride-hailing firm, while Uber shares retreated. Powell fielded several questions on the Fed’s independence from the executive branch. His remarks came a day after White House economic adviser Stephen Miran was sworn in as a Fed Governor, and an appeals court rejected President Donald Trump’s bid to dismiss Governor Lisa Cook. The Dow swung during Powell’s speech but closed in positive territory, contrasting with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq, which ended the session lower. body: Shares of Scientex Bhd rose 4.02% to RM3.36 today, supported by the group’s fourth-quarter results and plans to fully acquire its packaging subsidiary. The packaging manufacturer and property developer reported a net profit of RM154.3 million for the fourth quarter ended 31 July 2025, up 13.6% from RM135.9 million a year earlier, driven mainly by contributions from its property division. Quarterly revenue rose 2.1% to RM1.19 billion, while full-year revenue hit a record RM4.52 billion, slightly up from RM4.48 billion in FY24. Full-year net profit stood at RM530.8 million compared with RM545.2 million previously. The board recommended a final dividend of six sen per share, with an ex-date of 7 January 2026 and payable on 23 January 2026. Analysts highlighted Scientex’s proposed selective capital reduction (SCR) to acquire the remaining 28.11% stake in Scientex Packaging (Ayer Keroh) Bhd (SciPack) at RM1.50 per share, valuing the transaction at RM147.8 million. If approved, SciPack will become a wholly owned subsidiary of Scientex and be delisted. BIMB Research said the deal could add about RM5.5 million annually to Scientex’s profit after financing costs, representing roughly 1% earnings per share accretion, and views the offer as fairly valued. TA Research added that the move aligns with Scientex’s long-term strategy to consolidate packaging operations, optimise resources, and strengthen management oversight, with only a marginal increase in gearing expected. Both research houses maintained “buy” calls on the stock, with target prices of RM3.81 (BIMB Research) and RM4.85 (TA Research). title: Ringgit Slips As Fed Cut Boosts Greenback
body: The ringgit opened weaker against the US dollar on Thursday after the Federal Reserve’s 25 basis-point rate cut strengthened the greenback. At 8am, the local note stood at 4.1943/1988 against the greenback from Wednesday’s close of 4.1860/1900. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said profit-taking in emerging market currencies was expected after the US Dollar Index rose 0.25% to 96.873 points. He noted that the ringgit had appreciated 0.35% to 4.1880 against the dollar on Wednesday. “The US dollar-ringgit is likely to hover between RM4.19 and RM4.20 as the Fed has signalled that its rate cuts will be gradual,” he said. The Fed lowered its benchmark interest rate at its September meeting on Wednesday, its first cut since December 2024, and signalled further reductions are likely before year-end. The ringgit traded mixed against major currencies. It strengthened against the Japanese yen at 2.8522/8585 from 2.8607/8636 but weakened to 5.7156/7217 against the British pound from 5.7131/7185 and slipped to 4.9589/9642 versus the euro from 4.9583/9631. title: Asian Markets Mixed As Fed Rate Cut Ripples Through Region
body: The United States Federal Reserve cut interest rates by a quarter of a percentage point on Wednesday, lowering the policy rate to the 4 per cent to 4.25 per cent range. Policymakers indicated two more reductions of the same size are expected at the remaining meetings this year as signs of weakness in the job market shift their focus from inflation to employment. Hong Kong’s central bank followed suit, cutting its base rate via the overnight discount window by 25 basis points to 4.50 per cent on Thursday. “The reduction will have a positive impact on the city’s property market and economy,” Hong Kong Monetary Authority Chief Executive Eddie Yue said, adding that financial and monetary markets continue to operate in a smooth and orderly manner. Yue also noted that the Fed might cut rates further by 50 basis points before year-end, though he cautioned “the extent and pace of future US interest rate cuts are subject to uncertainty.” Asian markets opened mixed in response. Japan’s Nikkei 225 Index climbed 0.3 per cent to 44,938.40 in early trade, briefly touching a record high of 45,055.99, while the broader Topix slipped 0.1 per cent. Resonac Holdings surged 8.7 per cent and Screen Holdings rose 4.8 per cent, while Tokyo Electric Power dropped 4.4 per cent and Tokyo Gas slid 4.1 per cent. South Korea’s KOSPI rose 0.38 per cent to 3,426.37 at 9.47am, led by heavyweight chipmakers. Samsung Electronics gained 1.21 per cent and SK Hynix climbed 3.6 per cent, extending an artificial intelligence-driven rally. LG Energy Solution edged down 0.43 per cent, while Hyundai Motor and Kia rose 0.12 per cent and 0.30 per cent, respectively. Gains in Japan, South Korea and Taiwan steadied MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan, which edged 0.1 per cent lower as declines in Australian and New Zealand stocks weighed on the benchmark. Singapore’s Straits Times Index fell 0.14 per cent and Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index dropped 0.19 per cent at around 10 am. title: Analysts Single Out Pavilion, Axis Among REIT Performers
body: MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB Research) has maintained a NEUTRAL stance on the REIT sector, with Pavilion REIT singled out as the only Buy under its coverage at a target price of RM1.88, while CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) also reiterated a NEUTRAL call with Axis REIT as its top pick. According to MBSB Research, the 1HCY25 earnings season saw most REITs meeting expectations, with Axis REIT being the sole outlier that beat forecasts on the back of stronger rental income growth from newly acquired properties and positive rental reversions. Sunway REIT delivered the highest earnings per unit (EPU) growth of 24.6%, driven by contributions from Sunway Pyramid Mall and the reconfiguration of its Oasis wing, while IGB REIT and Axis REIT also posted encouraging growth of 9% and 9.4% respectively. Pavilion REIT’s 1HFY25 earnings rose 12.5% year-on-year, supported by Pavilion Bukit Jalil and Elite Pavilion Mall, while KLCCP Stapled Group gained 5.9% during the same period. The house noted that retail-focused REITs have continued to benefit from resilient consumer spending and robust footfall, with retail sales rising 5.9% year-on-year to RM466.6 billion in the first seven months of 2025. This was further underpinned by higher tourist arrivals, which reached 12.85 million in 1HCY25, up 8.8% year-on-year. The upcoming Visit Malaysia 2026 campaign is expected to provide an additional boost, particularly for Pavilion REIT, KLCCP Stapled Group, Sunway REIT and IGB REIT, whose malls are located at key tourist destinations. Still, MBSB Research flagged concerns over narrowing yield spreads, with the KL REIT Index retreating 2.6% in August 2025 after a strong run earlier in the year. The yield spread between the KL REIT aggregate and the 10-year Malaysian Government Securities (MGS) narrowed to below 150 basis points, under its long-term average of 164 basis points, which MBSB said could limit upside for the sector given the less attractive risk-reward profile. CIMB Securities echoed similar sentiments, stating that REITs under its coverage posted aggregate 2Q25 core net profit growth of 16.4% year-on-year, largely in line with expectations and supported by acquisitions made in FY24. However, sequential earnings contracted 6.6% quarter-on-quarter due to festive season spending being concentrated in the first quarter. CIMB added that Axis REIT and Sunway REIT benefitted most from asset acquisitions, while Sentral REIT and Al-Aqar Healthcare REIT were impacted by asset disposals and tenant exits. The brokerage expects earnings momentum to strengthen in 3Q25F, helped by lower borrowing costs following July’s 25 basis point overnight policy rate cut, electricity cost savings, and rising tourist arrivals. It also highlighted ongoing concerns from the Malaysian REIT Managers Association and the Malaysia Shopping Malls Association regarding the expanded 8% Sales and Service Tax (SST) on leasing services, which could add pressure to rental affordability and mall operators’ margins. CIMB Securities said its preferred pick remains Axis REIT, supported by resilient rental income streams and an anticipated 7.9% earnings growth in FY25F, with distribution yields projected at 4.9–5.5% across FY25–27F. MBSB Research, meanwhile, continues to favour Pavilion REIT for its strategic mall assets and positive rental reversion outlook, while maintaining a cautious view on the broader sector due to yield compression. title: Wall Street Slips Ahead Of Fed Rate Decision
body: Wall Street’s main indices ended lower in volatile trading on Tuesday as investors turned cautious before the Federal Reserve’s interest rate decision. Markets are pricing in a 25 basis-point cut at the end of the Fed’s two-day meeting on Wednesday, responding to signs of a weakening US labour market. Data released on Tuesday showed retail sales rose more than forecast in August, though this did little to shift expectations. “The resilient economic data will only reaffirm the hawks on the FOMC … and could give a little bit of fuel for (Fed chair Jerome) Powell to come out as slightly more hawkish than the market is hoping for,” said Baird Private Wealth Management investment strategist Ross Mayfield. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 125.55 points, or 0.27%, to 45,757.90. The S&P 500 slipped 8.52 points, or 0.13%, to 6,606.76, while the Nasdaq Composite shed 14.79 points, or 0.07%, to 22,333.96. Six of the 11 S&P 500 subsectors ended weaker, with utilities down 1.81% and real estate 0.66% lower. The CBOE Volatility Index rose to 16.04, its highest in more than a week. UnitedHealth Group dropped 2.3%, while Nvidia lost 1.6% after Reuters reported weak demand in China for its new AI chip, weighing on the Dow. Despite the declines, both the S&P 500 and Nasdaq had closed at record highs on Monday, extending gains in September, a month often regarded as weak for equities. Market breadth was mixed, with decliners outnumbering advancers on the NYSE, while the Nasdaq recorded a slight lead for advancers. title: Dollar Rebounds Ahead Of Powell’s Fed Remarks
body: The US dollar rebounded on Wednesday as investors awaited Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell’s press conference, which could provide clues on the central bank’s policy direction. After hitting a four-year low against the euro on Tuesday, the dollar rose amid expectations that Powell may endorse a dovish path without signalling a prolonged series of cuts. Markets are pricing in 68 basis points of Fed easing by year-end and a total of 147 basis points by the end of 2026. “The real story is not the size of the move this week, but how Powell frames the path,” said Laura Cooper, senior macro strategist at Nuveen. “A hawkish cut risks deflating the risk rally in the near term.” The dollar index, which tracks the U.S. unit against six major currencies, gained 0.20% to 96.84, recovering from Tuesday’s low of 96.554. The index has fallen nearly 11% this year, with traders bracing for further losses. The euro eased 0.25% to $1.1838, down from a four-year high of $1.18785 hit on Tuesday. Sterling declined 0.13% to $1.3630, close to 2½-month highs after British inflation data met expectations. Other currencies also showed notable moves. The Swiss franc eased 0.22% to 0.7875 per dollar, near the decade high it reached earlier, while the Australian dollar rose to an 11-month peak at $0.6674. The Japanese yen strengthened to 146.22 per dollar, its strongest in a month ahead of the Bank of Japan policy meeting, expected to keep rates unchanged. “The strong yen may reflect market expectations that Shinjiro Koizumi, considered more moderate, is entering the Liberal Democratic Party leadership race, contrasting with the yen-bearish stance of Sanae Takaichi,” said Chris Turner, head of forex strategy at ING. The Fed began its two-day policy meeting on Tuesday, with Governor Lisa Cook participating fully after a federal appeals court blocked efforts to remove her. Data released the same day showed U.S. retail sales exceeding expectations, though weakening employment and rising prices remain downside risks. Analysts noted that Powell is unlikely to provide strong forward guidance at this stage. Thierry Wizman, global forex and rates strategist at Macquarie Group, said, “Powell will highlight downside risks to employment growth but refrain from signalling a long string of cuts. title: Asia Stocks Scale New Highs As Investors Eye Fed Cut
body: Asia stocks climbed on Tuesday (Sep 16) while the dollar was on the back foot as investors bet the United States Federal Reserve (Fed) would resume its easing cycle this week and potentially leave the door open to further rate cuts. Markets hardly reacted to news that the US Senate narrowly confirmed Stephen Miran to the Fed’s Board of Governors, while a US appeals court separately declined to allow President Donald Trump to fire Fed Governor Lisa Cook. Both moves were seen as unlikely to shift the needle for the Fed’s decision on Wednesday, where a 25-basis-point cut is fully priced in. “There are certainly concerns around the politicisation of the Fed and President Trump’s pressure … to try to sort of, I guess, stack the board,” said Tony Sycamore, a market analyst at IG.”But I think … a 25-basis-point cut still remains in place.” Expectations of imminent Fed rate cuts have kept the market mood buoyant over the past few sessions and sent stocks scaling new highs. While the KLCI is closed for Malaysia Day, MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan rose to a more than four-year top early on Tuesday and last traded 0.3 per cent higher, while Japan’s Nikkei and Topix indexes notched fresh records. Just as important for markets will be Fed members’ “dot plot” projections for rates and guidance from Fed Chair Jerome Powell on the extent and pace of any further easing. Futures already have 127 bps worth of cuts priced in by July 2026, so anything less than dovish will disappoint investors. “There do seem to be quite a few rate cuts priced in now. On balance, maybe that suggests that the bar for a hawkish surprise is a little lower than that for a dovish one,” said Thomas Mathews, head of markets for Asia Pacific at Capital Economics. “It’s likely though that the Fed will stick with its cautious communication approach and not give much away.” EUROSTOXX 50 futures eased 0.09 per cent while FTSE futures gained 0.08 per cent. Nasdaq futures were flat while S&P 500 futures dipped 0.02 per cent, after both indexes scaled all-time highs in the cash session overnight. Shares of Nvidia ended slightly lower after China on Monday accused the artificial intelligence chipmaker of violating the country’s anti-monopoly law in the latest escalation in the Sino-US trade war. In other news, US and Chinese officials said on Monday they have reached a framework agreement to switch short-video app TikTok to US-controlled ownership that will be confirmed in a Friday call between Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping.The Fed cut bets have in turn kept pressure on the dollar, which on Tuesday was struggling near a roughly two-month low against the British pound. Sterling steadied at US$1.3599, while the euro last bought US$1.1758, not too far from a one-and-a-half-month high of US$1.1780 hit last week. The risk-sensitive Australian dollar rose to a 10-month high of US$0.6677. “The Aussie has been outperforming in recent weeks because markets have been expecting the Federal Open Market Committee to restart interest rate cuts, and that’s positive for the global economic outlook, and at the same time … trade uncertainty has eased,” said Carol Kong, currency strategist at Commonwealth Bank of Australia. US Treasury yields rose slightly after falling in the previous session, with the two-year yield last at 3.5409 per cent. The benchmark 10-year yield was up about 1 bp to 4.0451 per cent. In commodities, oil prices extended their rise from the previous session, as investors assessed the impact of Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian refineries. Brent crude futures rose 0.25 per cent to US$67.59 per barrel, while US crude edged 0.22 per cent higher to US$63.44 a barrel. Spot gold scaled a record high of US$3,689.27 an ounce, supported by a weaker dollar and Fed cut expectations. title: Oil Prices Steady As Investors Weigh Ukraine Strikes, US Demand Outlook

Brent crude edged up three cents to US$67.02 a barrel by 0009 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate gained eight cents to US$62.77. Both benchmarks rose more than 1% last week as Ukraine intensified strikes on Russian oil infrastructure, including the Primorsk export terminal and the Kirishinefteorgsintez refinery, which together handle a sizable share of Russia’s crude flows. Primorsk, Russia’s largest western port, has a capacity of one million barrels per day (bpd), while the Kirishi refinery processes about 355,000 bpd, or 6.4% of national output. Despite disruptions, regional officials said production would be maintained following a separate drone attack in Bashkortostan. Geopolitical tensions remain high as US President Donald Trump pressed Europe to toughen sanctions on Russian oil purchases, while trade negotiations between Washington and Beijing in Madrid added another layer of uncertainty. Meanwhile, investors are eyeing US economic signals after weak job growth and higher inflation last week raised concerns about demand, with attention now on the Federal Reserve’s Sept 16-17 meeting where a rate cut is widely expected. title: Weekly Recap: Korea Stocks Soar As Tax Relief, AI Buzz Lift Kospi
body: South Korea’s equity market ended the week at record highs, with the benchmark Kospi surging as government tax relief measures and renewed optimism in semiconductors and artificial intelligence (AI) stocks fuelled investor appetite. The Kospi climbed about 1.5% on Sept 12, extending year-to-date gains to more than 38%, making it one of Asia’s top-performing markets in 2025. Markets rallied after President Lee Jae Myung scrapped a controversial plan to lower the capital gains tax threshold for large shareholders, a policy that had unsettled investors earlier this year. The reversal cleared a major overhang and drew strong buying interest. Tech and chipmakers also led the charge, supported by expectations that South Korea will remain central to global AI infrastructure demand. Despite the momentum, analysts cautioned that stretched valuations could pose risks, particularly if corporate earnings fail to meet lofty expectations. Investors are also monitoring foreign fund inflows, trade policies and the government’s next steps on taxation. Bottom line: With tax clarity and AI-driven optimism, the Kospi closed the week on a powerful note but sustaining the rally will hinge on earnings strength and global demand for chips. title: Market Review: Japan Stocks Hit Record Highs On Trade Hopes, Political Shift
body: Japanese stocks surged to new heights this week as investors bet on supportive policies amid political change, easing trade tensions and a weaker yen that boosted exporters. The benchmark Nikkei 225 climbed past 44,000 for the first time on Sept 9, gaining nearly 0.9%, while the broader Topix advanced 0.4%. Export-driven sectors including autos, technology and industrials, led the rally, buoyed by expectations of stronger demand abroad. Investor sentiment improved after Prime Minister Shigeru Ishiba’s resignation, which opened the door for pro-stimulus candidate Sanae Takaichi to seek the leadership of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party. Markets view her as likely to favour expansive fiscal and monetary policy. At the same time, confirmation that the US will cut tariffs on Japanese autos by mid-September and continued yen weakness added fuel to the rally. However, risks remain. Bond markets reflected fiscal concerns, with the 30-year Japanese government bond yield rising to 3.285%, a record high. Analysts warned that stretched equity valuations, potential yen volatility and uncertainty over Japan’s political transition could trigger volatility in the weeks ahead. Bottom line: Japan’s market ended the week on a strong note, lifted by trade optimism and political transition hopes. But with the Nikkei at record levels, investors are now watching whether policy and earnings will justify the rally’s momentum. body: The Nasdaq climbed to a record high of 22,141.10 on Sept 12, powered by gains in Microsoft and Tesla, as investors braced for next week’s Federal Reserve (Fed) meeting, where a 25-basis-point rate cut is widely expected amid softening jobs data, Reuters reported. Microsoft gained 1.8% after sidestepping a potential European Union antitrust fine by offering discounted Office products excluding Teams. Tesla, meanwhile, surged 7.4% after its board chair reassured investors that CEO Elon Musk remains fully engaged despite political controversies. In contrast, the Dow Jones fell 0.59% to 45,834.22, weighed by declines in Goldman Sachs and Sherwin-Williams, while the S&P 500 slipped 0.05% to 6,584.29. Seven of 11 S&P sectors retreated, led by health care and materials. For the week, all three major indexes posted gains: The Nasdaq added 2%, the S&P 500 rose 1.6%, and the Dow climbed nearly 1%, buoyed by renewed interest in artificial intelligence stocks after Oracle’s strong forecast and a media-sector rally led by Warner Bros Discovery. Investor attention now turns to the Fed meeting, with markets pricing in potential interest rate cuts totalling 75 basis points by year-end. body: Oil prices inched higher on Sept 12 after a Ukrainian drone strike halted loadings at Russia’s largest western port, Primorsk, underscoring lingering geopolitical risks, Reuters reported. Brent crude rose 62 cents, settling at US$66.99 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate added 32 cents to US$62.69. Early gains were tempered by signs of weaker US demand. The Labour Department revised job growth downward by 911,000 for the past year, while the consumer price index jumped 0.4% in August, the largest increase since January. Meanwhile, OPEC+ plans output increases and India’s Adani Group barred sanctioned tankers, potentially limiting Russian oil shipments to the country. Analysts say the oil market remains finely balanced between geopolitical tensions and global supply-demand dynamics, keeping traders cautious. title: Wall Street Hits Record Highs As Tesla And Micron Surge
body: Wall Street’s main indexes closed at record highs on Thursday, led by gains in Tesla and Micron Technology, as investors bet on potential Federal Reserve interest rate cuts amid sticky inflation and weaker job data. The S&P 500 rose 0.85% to 6,587.47 points, the Nasdaq gained 0.72% to 22,043.08 points, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed 1.36% to 46,108.00 points. Ten of the 11 S&P 500 sectors advanced, with materials up 2.14% and health care rising 1.73%. Tesla jumped 6%, helping both the S&P 500 and Nasdaq reach record levels. Micron Technology surged 7.5% to $150.55 after Citigroup raised its price target to $175 from $150, pushing the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index to an all-time high. Warner Bros Discovery soared 29% following reports that Paramount Skydance is preparing a majority cash bid for the struggling media company. Centene advanced 9% after reaffirming its annual profit forecast and confirming Medicare plan quality ratings. In contrast, Oracle slipped 6.2%, giving back part of its prior 36% surge, while Delta Airlines fell 1.55% after reaffirming its annual profit guidance. U.S. consumer prices in August rose more than expected, with the annual increase marking the largest in seven months. Initial jobless claims for the week ended September 6 reached 263,000, near a four-year high. “Inflation has been sticky … we are in a period that is unusual relative to the last several years, as the job market is slowing while inflation does not follow suit,” said Atsi Sheth, Chief Credit Officer at Moody’s Ratings. Sheth predicts a 25-basis-point Fed rate cut next week, followed by another 25-basis-point reduction by year-end. Futures trading suggests traders are confident of at least a 25-basis-point rate cut at the upcoming Fed meeting, with only a 7% chance of a 50-basis-point cut. Advancing issues outnumbered decliners on the S&P 500 by a 6.8-to-one ratio. The S&P 500 recorded 42 new highs and 4 new lows, while the Nasdaq posted 143 new highs and 42 new lows. Trading volume reached 18.2 billion shares, above the 20-day average of 16.1 billion. title: Stock Today: Mynews Dips 4.48% Despite Buy Call
body: Shares of Mynews Holdings Bhd slipped 4.48% in afternoon trade, falling 3 sen to 64 sen as at 3.34pm. The counter, trading under stock code 5275, saw an intraday low of 63 sen and a high of 69 sen, with 26.55 million shares changing hands. It opened at 69 sen compared with the last close of 67 sen. At current levels, Mynews remains below RHB Investment Bank Bhd’s target price of 80 sen, which implies a 19% upside. RHB Research has maintained its BUY recommendation, citing intact turnaround momentum supported by stronger earnings visibility and improving margins. For the nine months ended July 2025, Mynews posted a core profit of RM13.6 million, up 70.2% year-on-year, achieving 70% of RHB’s forecast and 81% of consensus estimates. Revenue rose 9% to RM649.4 million, driven by stronger same-store sales and the opening of 53 new outlets, lifting its total network to 679. Quarter-on-quarter, revenue climbed 14% to a record RM230.9 million, while core profit more than doubled to RM6.6 million. Margin improvements were supported by tighter wastage control, better product mix and higher contributions from CU, which commands stronger margins. RHB expects CU to turn profitable by FY2026 with improved product assortment and wastage control. Supervalue outlets are also anticipated to benefit from the Basic Rahmah Assistance (SARA) redemption programme, while Visit Malaysia Year 2026 could provide further upside for outlets in tourist areas. The research house maintained its earnings forecasts and discounted cash flow (DCF)-derived target price of 80 sen, which includes a 2% ESG premium. Risks flagged include weaker consumer sentiment, higher operating costs and the possibility of CU slipping back into losses. title: Stock Today: Gamuda Rises 1.62% On Singapore Land Bid Prospects
body: Gamuda Bhd’s shares gained 1.62% in late afternoon trade, rising 9 sen to RM5.64 at 4.39pm. The counter saw 7.67 million shares traded, with an intraday high of RM5.68 and a low of RM5.56. Analysts also pointed to Gamuda’s record RM35.8 billion order book, with targets of RM40-45 billion by year-end, supported by data centres, renewable energy ventures and potential wins in Australia and New Zealand. title: Stock Today: Bermaz Auto Hits Record Low As Earnings Slump, Competition Intensifies
body: Bermaz Auto Bhd’s shares tumbled to a record low on Friday after the car distributor reported a sharp decline in quarterly earnings, weighed by fierce competition from Chinese automakers. The counter fell 8.15% to close at 61.5 sen, with 162.9 million shares traded, making it one of the most active on Bursa Malaysia. The stock, which opened at 65 sen, touched a low of 61.5 sen during the session. The Mazda, Kia and Xpeng distributor said first-quarter net income ended July plunged 88% year-on-year to RM8.28 million, while revenue slumped 42% on lower sales volumes in its domestic operations. The company warned that the challenging operating environment, marked by an influx of low-priced Chinese-made vehicles, is expected to persist. “Vehicle sales in the country are impacted by the influx of Chinese-made vehicles, which are making inroads with their low pricing strategy,” Bermaz said. The steady drop in earnings has erased about 75% of the company’s market value since July last year. Apex Securities downgraded Bermaz to “sell” from “hold,” cutting its target price to 50 sen from 93 sen, citing heightened competitive pressures and weaker projected sales across key models. Bermaz said sales of upcoming Mazda models, including the CX-60 and CX-80, may offer some support in the coming quarters. title: Ringgit Gains On Dollar Retreat After Weak US Jobs Data
body: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar on Friday as the greenback eased following weaker-than-expected US jobs data, which raised expectations of interest rate cuts. At 8 am, the local unit stood at 4.2065/2225 per dollar, stronger than Thursday’s close of 4.2185/2240. Core CPI held steady at 3.1% for a second month. “The CPI print was within expectations, clearing the path for the Federal Reserve to cut interest rates next week,” he told local news media outlet. Against a basket of major currencies, the ringgit slipped. It eased to 2.8569/8680 versus the yen, fell to 5.7095/7312 against the pound, and weakened to 4.9351/9538 against the euro. title: HLIB Keeps Hold Call On UMedic Despite Strong 4Q Results
body: Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) has maintained its HOLD call on UMediC Group Bhd with a higher target price of RM0.36 from RM0.315, despite the company delivering stronger-than-expected results for the fourth quarter of financial year 2025 (4QFY25). UMediC posted a core profit after tax and minority interest (PATMI) of RM2.9 million in the quarter, up 60% quarter-on-quarter but down 6.2% year-on-year, bringing its full-year FY25 core PATMI to RM8.2 million. Although this was 15.4% lower compared to the previous year, the results exceeded both HLIB and consensus expectations by 113-126%, mainly due to stronger-than-expected profit margins in the Distribution division. Revenue in the quarter rose 5.6% compared to the preceding quarter, with both Distribution (+2.4%) and Manufacturing (+10.8%) divisions contributing to growth. The stronger product mix boosted the Distribution division’s profit before tax (PBT) margin sharply to 40% from 13% previously, fuelling the quarter’s earnings improvement. On a yearly basis, revenue fell 17.4% as the Distribution division saw weaker demand for medical devices and consumables, though this was partially offset by a 13.9% growth in the Manufacturing division, supported by higher demand for respiratory-related products. For the full year, revenue contracted 11%, affected by softer demand across both segments and a weaker US dollar against the ringgit, which impacted the Manufacturing business. HLIB noted that it has revised upwards UMediC’s FY26 and FY27 profit forecasts by 16% and 12% respectively to reflect higher margin assumptions for the Distribution division. Even so, the investment bank cautioned that the company’s share price has run ahead of fundamentals, leading to the decision to keep its rating unchanged. Looking ahead, HLIB said sales in the Manufacturing division are expected to be supported by global healthcare megatrends such as the ageing population and growing demand for respiratory products. However, it added that ongoing uncertainty in the Distribution division could weigh on the group’s overall performance. As of 10.28 am, the stock price is stable at RM0.380. title: Bermaz Auto Downgraded To Sell After Weak 1Q Results
body: Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) has downgraded Bermaz Auto Bhd (BAuto) to SELL from Hold, cutting its target price to RM0.54 from RM0.78, citing weak earnings and a challenging operating landscape. The downgrade implies a -20% capital downside from its current RM0.675 share price, with analysts projecting an expected total return of -14.1% despite a dividend yield of 5.9%. The company reported a disappointing first-quarter FY26 core net profit (PATMI) of RM8.8 million, down 58.9% quarter-on-quarter and 87.3% year-on-year. The results came in well below expectations, meeting only 6.6% to 8.9% of consensus and HLIB’s full-year estimates. The first interim dividend declared stood at 0.75 sen per share. Earnings weakness was attributed mainly to lower automotive sales volume, which fell 11.1% quarter-on-quarter and 48.4% year-on-year, coupled with thinner margins and negative contributions from associates due to reduced production volumes. HLIB noted that while Bermaz Auto maintains a strong balance sheet with net cash of RM182.6 million, its profit outlook remains pressured. The research house expects earnings to stay soft in the coming quarters before a potential rebound in the fourth quarter of FY26, driven by new contributions from the Mazda CX-60 and CX-80 plug-in hybrid models. The group’s recently acquired distributorship for Xpeng electric vehicles is also contributing positively, while its Philippines operations are stabilising with stronger demand for premium models such as the CX-60 and CX-90. However, HLIB flagged intensifying competition in Malaysia’s automotive market, particularly from new Chinese original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) entering at attractive price points. Compounding the pressure, many of Mazda’s core models in Bermaz Auto’s line-up are approaching the end of their product cycles, with new generations only expected in two years. Following the weak performance, HLIB slashed its FY26 and FY27 earnings forecasts by 42.4% and 31.5% respectively, while introducing FY28 estimates at RM112 million. The research house concluded that despite a healthy balance sheet, Bermaz Auto’s earnings prospects remain muted, justifying the downgrade to Sell. The stock price decreased by 7.41% as of 10.22 am, to RM0.625. title: Tech Surge Sends Japan, Taiwan To Record Highs
body: Japanese and Taiwanese equities climbed to record highs on Thursday as technology stocks rallied and optimism built that US inflation would allow the Federal Reserve to ease policy as early as next week. Markets are also wagering on the possibility of two more cuts before year end. Japan’s Nikkei advanced 0.8 per cent to a fresh peak, led by gains in energy firms, utilities and tech counters. In Taiwan, the benchmark index rose 1 per cent as heavyweight chipmaker TSMC added 2.5 per cent. SoftBank surged nearly 9 per cent after US partner Oracle posted its strongest one-day rally since 1992, soaring 36 per cent overnight on expectations of robust AI-driven demand for its cloud services. Broader sentiment in Asia was mixed. MSCI’s Asia-Pacific ex-Japan index slipped 0.1 per cent, weighed by Hong Kong where the Hang Seng lost 0.9 per cent. On Wall Street futures, Nasdaq was up 0.2 per cent and S&P 500 gained 0.1 per cent. The moves followed a softer-than-expected US producer prices reading, which bolstered bets that the Fed will cut rates by 25 basis points next week. Futures markets are now pricing an 8 per cent chance of a larger 50 basis-point reduction. Attention has turned to the August consumer price index due later on Thursday. Economists polled by Reuters forecast a 2.9 per cent annual rise, the strongest since January, with core CPI seen holding at 3.1 per cent. “Unless CPI delivers a significant upside shock, investors are likely to maintain their dovish outlook,” said Julien Lafargue, chief market strategist at Barclays Private Bank. “This shift in inflation dynamics could prove pivotal for the US Fed, which now faces fewer constraints in pursuing a more aggressive rate-cutting cycle.” In commodities, Brent crude was steady at US$67.49 a barrel, while US crude traded at US$63.65. Spot gold edged up 0.1 per cent to US$3,644 an ounce, near record highs. Oil markets remained firm after Poland shot down suspected Russian drones and the US pressed the EU for tighter sanctions on buyers of Russian oil. Currency markets showed little movement, with the US dollar index flat at 97.81, off a seven-week trough of 97.25. The Australian dollar touched a 10-month high of US$0.6636 before easing to US$0.6616. In bonds, US 10-year Treasury yields rose 2 basis points to 4.0531 per cent after a strong 10-year note auction, while the 30-year yield climbed to 4.7028 per cent ahead of a US$22 billion sale later in the day. The European Central Bank is due to announce its decision later Thursday and is expected to keep rates unchanged, though analysts believe it will leave the door open for further easing given political and trade uncertainties. UWC’s orderbook also strengthened to RM180 million, with semiconductor-related orders making up 84% and FE equipment now accounting for 35%, reflecting its growing exposure to advanced chipmaking tools. HLIB expects UWC’s earnings to grow 72% in FY26 on the back of higher FE orders, margin gains and customer localisation efforts in Malaysia, with AI-linked capital expenditure seen as a key demand driver. The research house cautioned, however, that any sharp pullback in semiconductor capital spending could pose downside risks to the outlook. title: Stock Today: Pansar Hold Steady After Securing RM217 Million Highway Contract
body: Pansar Bhd’s shares closed unchanged at 53 sen, following news that the group secured a RM216.998 million contract from the Sarawak Public Works Department (JKR Sarawak). The counter saw 1.86 million shares traded, with an intraday high of 54.5 sen and a low of 52.5 sen. At the last done price of 53 sen, Pansar carried a market capitalisation of about RM261 million. The Sarawak-based engineering and construction group said in a Bursa Malaysia filing that the latest contract was awarded to its wholly-owned unit Perbena Emas Sdn Bhd for Section 2 of Package 1 of the Serian–Gedong–Samarahan dual carriageway highway project. The job involves upgrading a 4km stretch of the existing two-lane road between Simpang Gedong Isthmus and Simpang Lubok Teranggas into a four-lane dual carriageway. Work is scheduled to begin this month and is expected to take 36 months. This marks Pansar’s second major win under the same highway project. In January, the group secured a RM477.69 million contract, also through Perbena Emas for Section 1B of Package 1, which covers an 8.5km dual carriageway from Simpang Tanah Puteh to Gedong Isthmus with two bridges and an autonomous rail transit reserve. With both Section 1B and Section 2 in hand, Pansar’s total contract value under the Serian–Gedong–Samarahan highway project has risen to about RM694.69 million. The full highway spans roughly 93km, including 19km from Serian to Gedong and 74km from Gedong to Samarahan. title: Stock Today: Eurospan Trades Higher Amid Takeover Offer
body: Shares in Eurospan Holdings Bhd were last traded at RM2.73 at 3.15 pm on Thursday, edging up 0.37% or 1 sen, with 6,500 shares exchanging hands. The counter opened at RM2.72 and moved between RM2.72 and RM2.73 during the session. The performance comes as EC Synergy (M) Sdn Bhd’s unconditional mandatory takeover offer for Eurospan remains open. The offer, priced at RM2.30 per share, was triggered after EC Synergy acquired a 74.14% stake in the Penang-based furniture maker on 20 August through direct business transactions valued at RM75.75 million. With the acquisition crossing the statutory 50% control threshold, EC Synergy is required to extend the offer for the remaining 25.86% equity interest, or 11.49 million shares. The offer, which will close on 1 October unless extended, is advised by AmInvestment Bank. Samuel Ng Heng Hong, sole shareholder and director of EC Synergy, is the ultimate offeror. He also heads EC Excel Wire Holdings Sdn Bhd and intends to strengthen Eurospan’s financial standing while diversifying its business lines. Eurospan, traditionally focused on furniture manufacturing, has struggled with losses due to global trade disruptions and rising costs. For the financial year ended 31 May 2025, it reported a pre-tax loss of RM5.28 million. The company has since diversified into trading sealed lead-acid and automotive batteries. The offer price represents a discount to Eurospan’s last traded price of RM2.86 on 4 September as well as to its six-month volume-weighted average price of RM2.62. EC Synergy has said it plans to maintain Eurospan’s listing status and ensure compliance with the minimum public shareholding spread. title: Wall Street Ends At Record Highs On Fed Rate Cut Bets
body: Wall Street’s three major indexes closed at record highs on Tuesday as weaker US jobs data bolstered expectations that the Federal Reserve will cut interest rates next week. The S&P 500 climbed 0.27% to 6,512.61 points, surpassing last Thursday’s record. The Nasdaq gained 0.37% to 21,879.49, marking its second consecutive record close, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.43% to 45,711.34, exceeding its previous peak on August 28. The US Labour Department reported that payroll growth between April 2024 and March 2025 was overestimated by 911,000 jobs, suggesting labour market weakness. Markets have now priced in a 25 basis point cut at the Fed’s policy meeting, with futures pointing to a near 10% chance of a 50 basis point move. Eight of the 11 S&P 500 sectors advanced, led by communication services, which rose 1.64%, followed by a 0.71% gain in utilities. Year to date, the S&P 500 is up about 11% and the Nasdaq 13%. Among notable movers, UnitedHealth rallied after saying enrolment in its top-rated Medicare insurance plans was in line with expectations, while JPMorgan Chase rose 1.7% on stronger investment banking and markets revenue guidance. Technology shares were mixed: Apple fell 1.5% following the launch of new iPhones, while Broadcom slipped 2.6% after a run of gains. AI infrastructure firm Nebius soared nearly 50% on a US$17.4 billion deal with Microsoft, and rival CoreWeave gained 7%. Albemarle slumped 11.5% on easing supply concerns as China’s CATL prepared to restart output at a lithium mine. Meanwhile, Fox Corp Class B shares dropped 6.7% and News Corp fell 4.5% after Rupert Murdoch confirmed an agreement handing control of the media empire to his son Lachlan. Traders will turn their attention to US producer price inflation due Wednesday and consumer price data on Thursday to assess the impact of tariffs and the case for further rate cuts. title: Kospi Nears Record High On Policy Optimism
body: South Korea’s Kospi briefly traded above its all-time closing peak from 2021 on Wednesday, with expectations of policy reforms and favourable global sentiment keeping the benchmark among the world’s strongest equity performers this year. The index jumped as much as 1.4%, powered by heavyweights Samsung Electronics Co and SK Hynix Inc. The rally has now lifted the Kospi more than 37% in 2025, driven by enthusiasm for corporate governance changes and the ongoing artificial intelligence boom. Foreign investors have poured into South Korea’s US$2.2 trillion stock market, encouraged by prospects of more shareholder-friendly policies. This marks a stark contrast to 2021, when a surge of retail trading during the pandemic pushed the Kospi to its previous high. Recent months have seen policymakers back key revisions to the commercial code, aimed at holding board members legally accountable to all shareholders. Proposals include strengthening the voting system for board selection and limiting treasury stock practices — reforms targeting the dominance of family-run conglomerates, or chaebols. “Expectations that the revision of the commercial code will fuel corporate governance reforms have lifted the index thus far,” said Han Sangkyoon, chief investment officer at Quad Investment Management Co. “Further gains depend on real corporate action and additional legal reforms to encourage companies to increase shareholder returns,” he added. Market sentiment has also been boosted by speculation that President Lee Jae Myung may abandon a plan to lower the threshold for capital-gains tax on stock investments. The proposal, unveiled in July, drew strong criticism from retail investors and dragged the index down in August, interrupting a four-month winning streak. South Korean equities are also gaining from wider expectations of US Federal Reserve rate cuts, with Japan’s stock market hitting fresh records this week on similar optimism. title: Asia Stocks Rise As Fed Cut Bets Strengthen, Bonds Retreat
body: Asian stocks advanced on Wednesday while bonds retreated as traders sharpened bets that weakness in the US labour market will push the Federal Reserve to deliver at least a quarter-point rate cut next week. Gold steadied after hitting a record high on Tuesday, while the dollar edged higher ahead of key US inflation data due later this week. Crude oil remained elevated after Israel’s strike on Hamas leadership in Qatar. Japan’s Nikkei added 0.3%, South Korea’s KOSPI gained 1.3% and Taiwan’s benchmark rose 1%. Hong Kong’s Hang Seng climbed 0.5% while mainland Chinese blue chips added 0.2%. Overnight, the S&P 500, Nasdaq Composite and Dow Jones Industrial Average each closed at record highs, with S&P futures pointing 0.2% higher on Wednesday. Market pricing shows traders see a Fed cut next Wednesday as virtually certain, with CME Group’s FedWatch tool assigning a 7% probability to a larger half-point reduction. Only a week ago, markets had given a 7% chance of no move, but another weak payrolls report last Friday convinced investors the Fed could no longer delay easing to support the economy. The final inputs before the decision will be producer price data on Wednesday followed by consumer inflation figures on Thursday. “An upside inflation surprise could rock the boat slightly and lead to an unwinding of rate cut probabilities, not so much for September, but for subsequent months,” said Capital.com senior financial markets analyst Kyle Rodda. He added that the sharp deterioration in US economic data, particularly on jobs, explains why investors expect aggressive easing, while still betting the measures will shield the economy from recession. US Treasury yields extended their rise for a second day, with the 10-year adding nearly 2 basis points to 4.093% after climbing 3 basis points on Tuesday. Japanese government bond yields gained 1.5 basis points to 1.575%. The US dollar held on to Tuesday’s gains, with the dollar index steady at 97.78. The greenback traded little changed at $1.1705 per euro and eased 0.06% to 147.33 yen. Attention also turned to central bank decisions in Europe and Asia. The European Central Bank meets Thursday and is widely expected to leave rates unchanged. While economists a month ago were divided on the chances of more cuts, inflation near the 2% target and record-low unemployment have shifted sentiment. The Bank of Japan announces its decision next Friday and is expected to keep policy steady, though reports this week differed on whether a rate hike could come later this year. Investors are also monitoring political developments, including Japan’s leadership transition following Shigeru Ishiba’s departure and France’s fifth prime minister in two years. Gold rose 0.2% to US$3,633 an ounce after surging to a record US$3,673.95 on Tuesday. Brent crude futures advanced 0.5% to US$66.74 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate rose 0.6% to US$62.99, adding to the previous session’s gains after Israel’s attack in Doha threatened to derail peace talks. title: Stock Today: Solarvest Climbs 5% Midday On Strong Orderbook Momentum

Management targets RM1 billion in revenue for FY26, representing an 86% increase year-on-year, with guidance of a RM3 billion unbilled orderbook by end-2026. Key drivers include ongoing Corporate Green Power Programme projects, progress on the fifth large-scale solar (LSS5) programme, and a growing tender pipeline in solar and battery energy storage systems. Solarvest’s recurring income base is expected to expand through ownership of 336MWp in solar assets via joint ventures and associates, potentially generating over RM90 million in annual revenue once operational. Its recent shortlisting in LSS5+ adds another 94MWac through a consortium with Malakoff. HLIB also highlighted improved economics for the Corporate Renewable Energy Supply (CRESS) programme following tariff revisions and lower system access charges, which could boost adoption among data centres. The research house maintained that Solarvest is well-positioned in the domestic renewable energy sector, with regional presence and strategic partnerships, though risks such as cost escalations, execution challenges and policy shifts remain. title: Nasdaq Hits Record As Traders Bet On Rate Cuts
body: The Nasdaq closed at a record high on Monday, lifted by gains in Broadcom and optimism that the Federal Reserve will move to cut interest rates. The index rose 0.45% to 21,798.70 points, while the S&P 500 gained 0.21% to 6,495.15 points and the Dow Jones Industrial Average advanced 0.25% to 45,514.95 points. After last Friday’s weak nonfarm payrolls report, traders have fully priced in a 25 basis point rate cut at the Fed’s policy meeting ending on 17 September. Futures also show a 10% chance of a 50 bps move, according to CME Group’s FedWatch tool. “The focus is on next Wednesday’s Fed rate cut. The market is greedy. It’s already discounted 25 basis points. Now, if people are buying because they expect 50, well, that’s not going to happen,” said Jake Dollarhide, chief executive officer of Longbow Asset Management in Tulsa, Oklahoma. Barclays has lifted its forecast to three cuts of 25 bps each this year, while Standard Chartered expects a 50 bps trim in September, double its earlier projection. Broadcom surged 3.2% to extend its rally after projecting sharp artificial intelligence-related revenue growth last week, pushing its market value to US$1.6 trillion, making it the seventh most valuable US company. The S&P 500 technology index rose 0.67%, though utilities slid 1.07%. The S&P 500 has gained around 10% so far in 2025, with the Nasdaq up 13%. Trading volume was active, with 16.2 billion shares changing hands, above the 20-session average of 16.1 billion. Declining stocks outnumbered gainers within the S&P 500 by a ratio of 1-to-1. Robinhood Markets jumped 16% and AppLovin soared 12% after both were confirmed to join the S&P 500 on 22 September. EchoStar rallied 20% following a deal to sell wireless spectrum licences worth about US$17 billion to SpaceX for its Starlink network. In contrast, telecommunications stocks slumped, with AT&T and Verizon both losing over 2% and T-Mobile sliding almost 4%. This week, traders will watch inflation data and the Bureau of Labour Statistics’ payroll revision for more insight into the US economy. “The growth scare from the labour market is going to overwhelm even hot inflation because the Fed right now is viewing any tariff-induced inflation as a one-time price increase,” said Jeff Schulze, head of economic and market strategy at Clearbridge Investments. title: Stock Today: BAT Malaysia Trades Flat At RM4.75
body: British American Tobacco (Malaysia) Bhd (BAT Malaysia) was unchanged at RM4.75 as of 12.25 pm on 8 September 2025, trading within a narrow range of RM4.74 to RM4.78. The stock opened at RM4.77 and saw 954,000 shares exchanged, reflecting muted trading momentum. The share price has been consolidating near the lower end of its 52-week range of RM4.16 to RM8.26, as investors weigh stronger second-quarter earnings against persistent headwinds in the tobacco industry. For the second quarter of financial year 2025, BAT Malaysia posted a 40% year-on-year increase in net profit to RM51 million, even as revenue slipped 2.5% to RM624.7 million. The improvement came from cost controls and stronger margins, lifting earnings per share to 18 sen from 13 sen a year earlier. This rebound followed a difficult first quarter, when profits plunged by more than 22% to RM23.3 million, the lowest in two decades, partly due to lower sales volumes and the early Ramadan period. The poor start to the year saw the stock lose close to 10% in a single day. Despite the recovery, the company remains pressured by the illicit cigarette trade, which accounts for an estimated 55% of the market in Malaysia. BAT Malaysia continues to focus on its flagship Dunhill brand in the premium segment while working with enforcement agencies to curb smuggling.
