title: Pop Mart Shares Plunge Nearly 7% Amid Demand Fears And Post-Index Rally Sell-Off
body: Pop Mart International Group Ltd’s stock dropped sharply on Monday, plunging 6.65% to HK$289 during intraday trading, with earlier lows touching HK$282.20 before recovering slightly. The sharp decline reflects growing investor concerns over product demand and profit-taking following its inclusion in major stock indices. Market watchers attribute the sharp move partly to the toymaker’s recent elevation into the Hang Seng Index and Hang Seng China Enterprises Index, prompting some investors to cash in on rapid gains ahead of index-linked buying pressures. Analysts have raised red flags over weakening secondary-market demand for its iconic Labubu series, particularly the newly released mini Labubu dolls. “Secondary market prices have been declining due to restocking and cooling demand for some series,” observed Jeff Zhang of Morningstar Inc., adding that growing negative feedback on new product quality is an issue the company needs to address promptly. Pop Mart’s meteoric rise had already made waves—its share price has surged nearly 600% over the past year, fuelled by Gen-Z enthusiasm for “designer toys” and collectable blind-box models. Labubu and other series helped spark this frenzy, driving exponential revenue and profit growth across collectables markets. However, intensified restocking efforts have triggered a sharp drop in resale values. Recent reports indicate that some Labubu series now resell at roughly half of what they once commanded, underscoring cooling investor sentiment. Despite these headwinds, not all analysts are bearish. Morgan Stanley sees the current correction as a buying opportunity, citing Pop Mart’s strong IP engine, direct-to-consumer model, and the fading of artificially inflated resale prices should bring a more sustainable balance. Overall, today’s sharp pullback signals an investor recalibration: balancing the company’s remarkable growth track record against rising concerns over product saturation and quality perception. title: Indonesia Earnings Optimism Outshines Unrest, Analysts Say
body: Indonesia’s stock market is poised to look past the country’s worst social unrest in years as analysts remain bullish on corporate earnings, underpinned by resilient consumption and firm commodity prices. Forward 12-month profit estimates for companies in the Jakarta Composite Index have climbed more than 4% since protests began two weeks ago, Bloomberg data showed. By comparison, regional benchmarks saw little change, reinforcing Indonesia’s position as one of Asia’s strongest equity markets. “The protests reflect micro-level discontent, but they don’t derail the medium-term earnings trajectory due to positive long-term fundamental factors,” said Mohit Mirpuri, senior partner at SGMC Capital Pte, citing interest-rate cuts and supportive market conditions. The unrest, triggered by rising living costs and inequality, has eased, allowing markets to stabilise. The Jakarta Composite Index gained 0.5% last week after Finance Minister Sri Mulyani Indrawati pledged to improve government policies. Still, global investors withdrew a net US$254 million from Indonesian equities during the week, while Fitch Ratings cautioned that prolonged instability could weigh on the country’s credit profile. Analysts, however, believe Bank Indonesia’s expected rate cuts and its renewed “burden-sharing” deal with the finance ministry will lend further support. Earnings momentum remains robust, with profit estimates for Indonesia’s equity benchmark up 19% this year, implying more than 45% growth over the next 12 months. That makes it the strongest among major Asian markets, according to Bloomberg data. Bond investors are also favouring Indonesia over India. The yield gap between Indonesia’s 10-year bonds and India’s is around 10 basis points, with economists surveyed by Bloomberg expecting it to widen to 20 basis points by the third quarter of next year. “Protests haven’t shifted the bullish macro case,” said Nirgunan Tiruchelvam, analyst at Aletheia Capital in Singapore. title: Axis’s Latest RM50 Million Acquisition Flags Caution
body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd has maintained its BUY call on Axis REIT with a target price of RM2.23, offering a potential 9% upside and a forecast yield of 5% for FY25, while MBSB Investment Bank Bhd kept its NEUTRAL stance with an unchanged target price of RM2.07. The differing views come after Axis REIT announced its second acquisition of the year, a RM50 million industrial facility in Bandar Sultan Suleiman, Port Klang. RHB Research said the deal reinforces Axis REIT’s position as a proxy to Malaysia’s resilient industrial property sector, citing steady inorganic growth, strong execution capabilities, and a healthy balance sheet. They noted that the acquisition, fully funded by bank borrowings, would only nudge the trust’s gearing to 33.6% from 32.7% in 2Q25, still well below the 50% threshold, with an estimated post-acquisition debt headroom of RM853 million. The transaction is expected to be completed by the first quarter of 2026. The asset, acquired from Barry Callebaut Malaysia, consists of a single-storey detached factory with annexed offices, a standalone office and canteen block, and a detached warehouse with offices, with a total gross floor area of 240,600 square feet. Built between 1993 and 1998, it sits on a 9-acre leasehold plot with tenure until 2104. While the property is currently vacant, RHB Research expects reasonable leasing prospects given its strategic location near North Port and access to major highways. RHB valued the acquisition price of RM50 million as fair, being in line with the independent valuation of RM50.3 million. It is estimated that, once leased, the property could generate a gross yield of about 7% based on prevailing rental benchmarks in Port Klang. However, it cautioned that the lack of an existing tenant could delay income contributions, unlike Axis REIT’s recent sale-and-leaseback deals. Even so, the brokerage maintained its earnings forecasts and target price, citing a stable outlook for industrial assets and a spread of 120 basis points over the 10-year Malaysian Government Bond yield. MBSB Research, meanwhile, was more cautious, noting that while the purchase aligns with Axis REIT’s expansion strategy, the lack of tenants made the acquisition yield uncertain. Analysts said Axis REIT has historically secured assets with long-term tenants and yields above 6%. Although confident the trust could find tenants upon completion, they highlighted the minimal earnings impact, estimating contributions of only about RM1 million annually, or less than 1% of FY26 earnings. MBSB Research also pointed out that the transaction involved a related party, as the sale agent was linked to Axis REIT’s Non-Independent Non-Executive Deputy Chairman, Tew Peng Hwee. Despite this, the research house said the pricing was reasonable, aligned with the market value of the property. It maintained its Neutral rating, citing limited upside and an unattractive dividend yield of 4.4%. As of 11.30 am, the stock price is up by 0.49% at RM2.050. Oil extended losses, with Brent settling 2.2% lower at US$65.50, as traders braced for more OPEC+ supply. title: Oil Slips Ahead Of OPEC+ Output Talks
body: Oil prices edged lower in early Asian trading on Sept 5, extending losses for a third straight session as investors awaited a weekend OPEC+ meeting that could bring fresh supply to the market. Reuters reported that Brent crude futures fell 0.3% to US$66.77 a barrel at 0012 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate slipped 0.3% to US$63.29. Eight OPEC+ members, including Russia, will discuss raising production in October at Sept 7’s meeting, sources told Reuters . A move to unwind an extra 1.65 million barrels per day of cuts, roughly 1.6% of global demand, would bring forward supply increases by more than a year. Adding pressure, US crude inventories rose by 2.4 million barrels last week, defying expectations of a draw, as refiners entered maintenance season. Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump urged European leaders to halt purchases of Russian oil, a step that could tighten supplies if enacted and put upward pressure on prices. title: Markets Rally On Softer US Labour Data, Fed Signals
body: Wall Street and global stocks advanced on Sept 4 while US Treasury yields slipped, as softer labour market data and dovish signals from Federal Reserve (Fed) officials bolstered expectations of an interest rate cut this month. Reuters reported that US private payrolls in August grew below forecasts and jobless claims rose, reinforcing views that the Fed will ease policy at its meeting in under two weeks. Money markets are now pricing in a near-100% chance of a rate cut. Benchmark 10-year Treasury yields fell five basis points to 4.16%, while the two-year yield dropped to 3.59%, its lowest since May. The Dow Jones Industrial Average, S&P 500 and Nasdaq all gained between 0.75% and 1%. In Europe, the FTSEurofirst 300 rose 0.6%, though Chinese markets tumbled after reports that Beijing plans measures to cool its surging tech sector. The STAR 50 index slid more than 6% in its sharpest drop since April, while the CSI300 lost 2.6%. Oil prices weakened after reports that OPEC+ may lift output targets, with Brent crude settling just under US$67 a barrel. The dollar firmed ahead of Sept 5’s closely watched US jobs report, while gold eased from Sept 3’s record high. One notable drag was Salesforce, whose shares fell nearly 5% after quarterly revenue missed expectations amid slow adoption of artificial intelligence (AI)-powered products. Analysts said the result underscored waning investor enthusiasm after months of AI-driven market gains. Elsewhere, Asian equities mostly rebounded, with Tokyo’s Nikkei climbing 1.5% and Australia’s ASX 200 up 1%. India’s Sensex rose 1% as the government cut levies to spur consumption. European bond yields also eased, with Germany’s 30-year yield at 3.3% and France’s at 4.39%, retreating from multi-year highs. Investors remain focused on the US payrolls report due on Sept 5 for confirmation that the labour market is slowing enough to pave the way for the Fed’s first rate cut since 2020. title: Stock Today: TNB Steady Amid Robust Electricity Demand And IRB Update
body: Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) edged slightly lower at midday, with its share price at RM13.08, down 2 sen or 0.15% from its previous close, as trading volume reached 4.93 million shares. The stock traded within a range of RM13.04 to RM13.18 as of 4.22 pm, with the last done price marginally below the last closing average of RM13.10. Analysts from MBSB Investment Bank and CIMB Securities have maintained their BUY recommendations for TNB, citing strong earnings momentum supported by robust electricity demand, particularly from data centres, and greater tariff stability under Regulatory Period 4 (RP4). CIMB Securities set a target price of RM15.75, while MBSB Research pegged it at RM16.40. The utility’s generation operations have strengthened, with the equivalent plant availability factor rising to 86.1% in 1H25, surpassing the full-year target of 83.2%. CIMB highlighted that demand from data centres surged 217% year-on-year in the same period, driven by 24 completed projects totalling 3.5GW. Commercial electricity consumption also rose 6.5% YoY to 24,277GWh in the first half of 2025. On capital expenditure, TNB utilised RM5.2 billion of regulated capex in 1H25, including the 500kV Bentong South–Lenggeng transmission line, while smart meter installations reached 38% progress and distribution automation 41% of targeted substations. Total FY25 capex guidance has been revised to RM18 billion, with non-regulated spending reduced to RM6 billion. TNB’s ongoing tax dispute with the Inland Revenue Board over a potential RM10.02 billion exposure remains unresolved, but management has received positive feedback from the Ministry of Finance on its Investment Allowance resubmission. CIMB Securities noted that no provisions are necessary at this stage, and neither dividends nor credit ratings are expected to be affected. Despite minor intraday fluctuations, investor sentiment remains supported by the company’s stable operations, growth in electricity demand, and proactive regulatory engagement. title: Ringgit Opens Higher Ahead Of BNM Policy Decision
body: The ringgit opened stronger against the US dollar on Thursday ahead of Bank Negara Malaysia’s (BNM) decision on the Overnight Policy Rate (OPR) later today. At 9 am, the local currency rose to 4.2125/2330 from Wednesday’s close of 4.2230/2285. Market consensus expects BNM to maintain the OPR at 2.75%. IPP Wealth Managers Ltd’s Head of Strategy and Country Economist Mohd Sedek Jantan said with headline inflation at 1.2% and the unemployment rate at 3.0%, maintaining the OPR would ensure policy stability, support domestic demand, and preserve accommodative monetary conditions without adding inflationary pressure. He added that July’s positive export growth further reinforced confidence in Malaysia’s external sector. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd Chief Economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid noted that the US Job Openings and Labour Turnover Survey (JOLTS) data for July showed vacancies slipping to 7.181 million, below consensus estimates of 7.38 million. This has raised expectations of a possible US Federal Reserve rate cut in September, he said, adding that the ringgit could strengthen further after closing 0.13% higher at 4.2257 yesterday, with trading likely between 4.21 and 4.23 today. At the opening, the ringgit traded mixed against major currencies. It appreciated versus the euro to 4.9126/9365 from 4.9223/9287 but weakened against the Japanese yen to 2.8469/8609 from 2.8430/8469, and slipped against the British pound to 5.6620/6896 from 5.6614/6687. Against ASEAN currencies, the ringgit was mostly higher. It firmed against the Indonesian rupiah to 256.5/257.9 from 257.2/257.7, rose against the Singapore dollar to 3.2706/2867 from 3.2777/2822, was steady versus the Philippine peso at 7.35/7.39 from 7.37/7.38, and slightly stronger against the Thai baht to 13.0454/1158 from 13.0529/0759. title: Nasdaq, S&P 500 Rise As Alphabet And Apple Rally; Dow Slips
body: The Nasdaq climbed 1% and the S&P 500 gained 0.5% on Wednesday, lifted by strong moves in Alphabet and Apple alongside expectations of a Federal Reserve interest rate cut this month. The Dow Jones Industrial Average, however, edged down 0.05% as Boeing shares dropped 2.1%. Alphabet surged 9.1% after a US judge ruled late Tuesday that the Google parent could retain control of its Chrome browser and Android operating system, while blocking certain exclusive contracts with device makers and browser developers. Apple rose 3.8% as the ruling also safeguarded billions in payments from Google. “Google and Apple got a lifeline … They won the sweepstakes,” said Jake Dollarhide, chief executive officer of Longbow Asset Management in Tulsa, Oklahoma. “The courts just cemented their reputation.” Several Federal Reserve officials reinforced market expectations for rate reductions. Governor Christopher Waller said the central bank should cut at its next meeting, while Atlanta Fed President Raphael Bostic reiterated that a reduction was coming, though without specifying timing. Data earlier showed US job openings fell in July, pointing to a cooling labour market. Rate futures are now pricing a 96% probability of a 25 basis point cut at the conclusion of the Fed’s two-day policy meeting on 17 September, according to CME Group’s FedWatch tool. Investors are also awaiting Friday’s monthly jobs report for further direction. Peter Cardillo, chief market economist at Spartan Capital Securities in New York, said September may not be “as trying as it usually is because of the fact that the Fed is expected to lower rates.” Macy’s shares soared 20.7% after the retailer raised its annual forecasts, while Dollar Tree tumbled 8.4% as it projected current-quarter profit below estimates, citing tariffs as a factor driving up costs. With the second-quarter US earnings season concluded, investors are shifting focus to third-quarter estimates and the potential impact of President Donald Trump’s tariff war. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 24.58 points to 45,271.23, the S&P 500 gained 32.72 points to 6,448.26, and the Nasdaq Composite advanced 218.10 points to 21,497.73. On the NYSE, advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.33-to-1 ratio, with 224 new highs and 45 new lows. On the Nasdaq, decliners outpaced advancers by 1.03-to-1. Volume on US exchanges totalled 14.95 billion shares, below the 20-day average of 16.18 billion. title: Wall Street Stumbles As Trump Tariff Ruling Sparks Market Jitters
body: US stocks closed lower on Tuesday, the first trading day of September, after a federal appeals court ruled that most of President Donald Trump’s sweeping tariffs were illegal, unsettling investors already wary of a traditionally volatile month for equities. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 249.07 points, or 0.55%, to 45,295.81. The S&P 500 dropped 44.72 points, or 0.69%, to 6,415.54, while the Nasdaq Composite slid 175.92 points, or 0.82%, to 21,279.63. The Cboe Volatility Index, Wall Street’s fear gauge, ticked higher as traders pared losses late in the session. “Has the Trump administration alienated our trading partners as well as given up the revenue from tariffs? That’s what’s plaguing markets,” said Oliver Pursche, senior vice-president and adviser for Wealthspire Advisors in Connecticut. He added, “It’s too early to call this the beginning of a great correction… August and September tend to be more volatile and a little more challenging for investors before we get into the fourth quarter, which tends to be a pretty solid one.” Real estate shares led sector declines, falling 1.7%, as US 30-year Treasury yields climbed to their highest since mid-July. Traders also shifted focus to Friday’s US payrolls report, which will show whether weak job growth extended into August for a fourth straight month. Among corporate movers, Kraft Heinz slumped 7% after announcing a split into two companies, one centred on groceries and the other on sauces and spreads. PepsiCo, meanwhile, gained 1.1% after activist investor Elliott Management disclosed a US$4 billion stake. US rate futures continued to price in a 92% probability of a 25-basis-point Federal Reserve rate cut at its September 17 meeting, according to CME FedWatch. title: Japan Stocks Face Muted Open Amid Political Uncertainty
body: Nikkei 225 futures in Osaka slipped as low as 41,690 overnight before trimming losses to 42,180, 0.4% below Tuesday’s close, as of 8 am. The weakness pointed to a lacklustre start for Tokyo trading on Wednesday. The yen fell as much as 1.2% against the dollar on Tuesday evening after Liberal Democratic Party Secretary-General Hiroshi Moriyama revealed his intention to resign. The currency was trading around 148.5 to the dollar as of 8 am. “Traders are seeing uncertainty building around the political outlook for Japan, which is jacking up volatility, especially for the yen,” said Anna Wu, cross-asset investment strategist at VanEck in Sydney. Local media reported that other senior LDP members, including policy chief Itsunori Onodera, are also preparing to step down. According to a Mainichi report, Taro Aso is expected to call for an early party election. In the medium to long term, equities could benefit if Prime Minister Shigeru Ishiba weakens alongside the LDP, Wu added. “If Ishiba is determined to stay on, he’s going to lean increasingly fiscally aggressive, raising strategic industry investment and potentially putting more doubts on the BOJ’s rate hike path. That’s actually good for growth, and a tailwind for risk assets,” she said. However, Wu noted that in the near term, Japanese shares are likely to remain under pressure. “US tech stocks are losing steam, and there are multiple tariff headwinds, including an escalation in US-China chip tensions. The entire market is feeling a chill,” she said. title: ITMax Cornering Smart Parking Contracts
body: Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) has maintained its BUY call on ITMAX System Bhd with an increased target price of RM5.71 from RM5.17, citing earnings uplift from the group’s latest Selangor smart parking contract. The research house reported the revised valuation reflects a 34.6% capital upside from its current price of RM4.24, with total expected return at 35%. ITMAX, through its 70%-owned subsidiary Selmax, has secured a Letter of Appointment from Majlis Perbandaran Selayang (MPS) to operate the Selangor Intelligent Parking (SIP) system and manage parking compounds for a 10-year term, with an option for a five-year extension. The appointment, its third in Selangor, covers around 15,000 gazetted parking bays and adds to contracts previously secured in Subang Jaya (MBSJ) and Shah Alam (MBSA). HLIB said the Selayang win expands ITMAX’s footprint to approximately 116,000 parking lots under management in Selangor, surpassing the 60,000 lots it operates across seven councils in Johor. Selmax will bear the costs of maintaining the spaces and related infrastructure, including cameras, enforcement vehicles and equipment, while managing parking attendants. Based on HLIB’s estimates, the contract could contribute RM3.5 million in annual revenue to ITMAX, translating into around RM1.4 million net profit per year after factoring in a 40% margin and minority interest. With the additional contribution, HLIB raised its FY26F and FY27F earnings forecasts by 12% and 15%, respectively. The research house noted that ITMAX has now secured seven out of 16 councils in Johor, with further opportunities expected as the state moves towards a single system policy covering CCTV, traffic lights and parking. In Selangor, Phase 2 of the SIP rollout will cover the remaining eight councils once current operator contracts expire in the first half of 2026. HLIB also highlighted ITMAX’s long-term growth prospects in smart city infrastructure. It said ITMAX’s ongoing rollout of 10,000 CCTV units for Kuala Lumpur City Hall is modest compared to Singapore’s 90,000 units, with the republic targeting 200,000 by 2030. The analysts expect further monetisation of its infrastructure through applications such as digital twins, traffic impact assessments and analytics. The target price of RM5.71 is based on a discounted cash flow valuation, using a 7% weighted average cost of capital and a 3% terminal growth rate. HLIB said the stock’s premium is justified given ITMAX’s position as a key beneficiary of national digitalisation and smart city initiatives. ITMAX’s stock price is up by 1.42%, standing at RM4.30 as of 10.35 am. title: Google Escapes Forced Split, Shares Jump 6%
body: Shares of Alphabet, Google’s parent company, jumped 6% in premarket trading on Wednesday following a US federal judge’s decision to prevent a forced breakup of the tech giant. The ruling allows Google to retain control of its Chrome browser and Android operating system, while limiting certain exclusive contracts with device makers and browser developers. The judge’s decision permits Google to continue payments to partners such as Apple to feature its search engine, a key component of its online dominance. Apple shares also rose 2.6% in premarket trading. Analysts at MoffettNathanson described the outcome as “a home run for the status quo,” noting that being found guilty of monopolistic behaviour but facing a benign remedy is highly favourable for the company. The ruling also preserves Alphabet’s potential to integrate its Gemini AI into future Apple devices. The decision removes a significant regulatory overhang that had weighed on Alphabet’s valuation, which had traded at a discount to peers amid fears of a forced divestiture. Year-to-date, Alphabet shares are up nearly 11.7%, outperforming Amazon but trailing Meta and Microsoft. The US government sued Google in 2020 for allegedly maintaining a search monopoly through exclusionary agreements, and Judge Mehta had ruled last year that Google violated antitrust laws. However, the rise of AI tools such as ChatGPT was cited as emerging competition, leading to a more lenient remedy. title: Global Bond Yields Surge As Gold Hits Record High
body: A global slide in long-dated bonds extended into Asia on Wednesday, while gold climbed to a new peak as investors worried over government debt and slowing economic growth. Japan’s 30-year government bond (JGB) yield jumped 8 basis points to a record 3.28 per cent ahead of a scheduled debt sale on Thursday, following a run-up in similarly dated gilts and US Treasuries overnight. The Nikkei opened 0.5 per cent lower, mirroring declines on Wall Street after data showed US manufacturing contracted for a sixth consecutive month in August. “The rise in bond yields is sort of weighing on your tech sector in the US,” Skye Masters, head of markets research at National Australia Bank, said in a podcast. “It is all about concerns about government budget deficit positions and the implications for bond issuance.” The yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note rose 0.4 basis points to 4.281 per cent, while the 30-year Treasury yield climbed 0.7 basis points to 4.978 per cent, approaching levels last seen in mid-July. Bond yields, which move inversely to prices, have been soaring around the world, reflecting investor caution over the scale of government debt in Japan, the United States, and Europe. In Europe, attention is turning to services sector data due on Wednesday to assess the impact of US tariffs, while key US labour data on Friday is expected to signal whether the Federal Reserve will cut interest rates later this month. Markets currently price in an 89 per cent chance of a 25-basis-point rate reduction. US President Donald Trump announced on Tuesday that his administration will seek an expedited Supreme Court ruling on tariffs previously deemed illegal by an appeals court, which allowed the duties to remain until 14 October. MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan rose 0.1 per cent, while Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 fell 0.9 per cent following second-quarter GDP data. US stock futures were largely steady, with S&P 500 e-minis up 0.1 per cent at 6,430.5, while pan-European futures indicated higher openings. The pan-region Euro Stoxx 50 futures rose 0.6 per cent, DAX futures gained 0.5 per cent, and FTSE futures were up 0.3 per cent. The US dollar strengthened 0.3 per cent to 148.79 yen, while the dollar index remained flat at 98.431 after a 0.7 per cent surge on Tuesday. Sterling traded at US$1.33716, down 0.2 per cent, having slumped 1.1 per cent in the previous session, while 30-year gilt yields hit their highest since 1998 following the British government’s sale of 10-year debt at a 17-year peak. In Europe, French Prime Minister Francois Bayrou is expected to lose a confidence vote over opposition to government spending cuts, while British finance minister Rachel Reeves is preparing to raise taxes in the autumn budget to meet fiscal targets. Commodity markets were mixed, with US crude up 0.2 per cent at US$65.69 a barrel, and spot gold climbing to a record US$3,546.99, reflecting safe-haven demand. title: US Stock Futures Edge Higher As Markets Brace For Crucial September Data
body: US stock futures rose slightly on Tuesday, offering a steadier start to September after a technology-led selloff as traders prepared for a busy month of economic data and Federal Reserve decisions. Contracts on the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 gained 0.2% in quiet trade with cash equities and Treasuries closed for the US Labor Day holiday. The moves came as Wall Street hovered near record highs following a four-month rally. Attention is turning to a series of catalysts in the coming weeks including jobs data, inflation figures and the Fed’s policy meeting on Sept 17 which will determine whether stocks can extend gains or lose momentum. September has historically been the weakest month for US equities. “The bar to derail a Fed rate cut on Sept 17 appears high,” said Deutsche Bank economist Peter Sidorov. He noted that markets are pricing in more than 140 basis points of easing by the end of 2026, a pace typically seen only during recessions. In Europe, the Stoxx 600 rose 0.2% led by defence shares such as BAE Systems Plc and Rheinmetall AG after reports that Europe is preparing detailed plans for possible post-conflict deployments in Ukraine. Asian markets were mixed with Alibaba Group surging 19% while semiconductor stocks retreated. In commodities, silver climbed above US$40 an ounce for the first time since 2011. Gold edged closer to record highs as expectations grew for a Fed rate cut this month. European bonds weakened as investors assessed political risks in France ahead of a confidence vote next week although the French-German 10-year spread was little changed at 79 basis points. Despite recent volatility, strategists at Evercore ISI said market pullbacks should be viewed as opportunities and projected a 20% gain in the S&P 500 by the end of 2026. title: Stock Today: CIMB Dips Amid Sluggish Loan Growth Despite Solid 1H25 Profit
body: CIMB Group Holdings Bhd was trading at RM7.23 as of 12.02 pm, down 20 sen or 2.69% from its previous session, with a traded volume of 33.95 million shares. The stock opened at RM7.35, reaching an intraday high of RM7.35 and a low of RM7.07, while its last average closing price (LACP) stood at RM7.43. Maybank Investment Bank Bhd has maintained its HOLD rating on CIMB, with an unchanged target price of RM7.60, citing the bank’s relatively higher exposure to regional volatility as overseas operations contributed about 40% of group pretax profit in 1H25. CIMB reported a net profit of RM3.86 billion for the first half of 2025 (1H25), broadly in line with expectations, representing 50% of Maybank Investment Bank’s full-year forecast and 49% of consensus estimates. The second quarter ended June 2025 saw a net profit of RM1.89 billion, down 4% both year-on-year and quarter-on-quarter, despite stable net interest margins and lower provisions. Reflecting the decent profit, CEO Novan Amirudin said the board declared an interim dividend of 19.8 sen per share, translating into a payout ratio of 55.5%, compared with 20 sen (excluding a 7 sen special dividend) in the first half of 2024. Loan growth remained sluggish, rising just 1% year-on-year in 2Q25 (+3.6% on a constant currency basis), trailing management’s FY25 target of 5–7%. CIMB revised its net interest margin guidance to a compression of 5–8 basis points, from an earlier projection of up to 5 basis points. Other FY25 targets, including a cost-to-income ratio below 46.7%, credit cost guidance of 25–35bps, and return on equity of 11–11.5%, remain intact. Maybank Investment Bank has left its FY25 net profit forecast unchanged, adjusting assumptions for slower loan growth, slightly wider NIM compression, marginally lower cost-to-income ratio, and minor credit cost tweaks. Net profit projections for FY26 and FY27 were revised marginally by +1% and -1% respectively, with the bank’s dividend payout policy of 40–60% remaining unchanged. title: HLIB Maintains Hold On IOI Corp
body: Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) has maintained its HOLD rating on IOI Corporation Bhd with an unchanged target price of RM4.02, valuing the stock at 20 times its CY26 core earnings per share of 20.1 sen. During IOI’s post-results briefing, management reiterated that the plantation division will continue to be the group’s primary earnings growth driver in FY26. The company expects fresh fruit bunch (FFB) output growth of between 5% and 10% next year, supported by more plantation areas entering maturity and more favourable weather conditions. This follows a subdued 1.3% increase in FY25, which had been dampened by accelerated replanting programmes and adverse weather. The company also anticipates a marginal decline in crude palm oil (CPO) production costs in FY26. Although fertiliser prices and application rates are expected to rise alongside labour costs following the reinstatement of EPF contributions for foreign workers and higher minimum wages, productivity gains are projected to cushion the impact. On the manufacturing side, IOI continues to face challenges from stiff competition in refining due to Indonesian levy differentials and overcapacity, as well as high input costs in oleochemicals. However, management noted signs of improving demand in selected product segments, particularly low-contaminant oils, which could provide some relief. Management also addressed the weak performance of IOI Palm Wood, attributing it to production inefficiencies. While a timeline for recovery has yet to be set, the group remains optimistic about the subsidiary’s long-term outlook, citing favourable demand trends and ongoing efforts to improve efficiency. Capital expenditure for FY26 has been guided at around RM900 million, higher than the RM700 million spent in FY25. The bulk of this will go into accelerated replanting covering 12,000 hectares, coconut planting of 1,000 hectares and downstream expansion, including capacity growth at the fatty ester plant in Penang. IOI also unveiled its new five-year strategic roadmap, covering 2025 to 2029, which aims to position the group as a global leader in sustainable palm products and ingredients. The plan will focus on strengthening its product portfolio to unlock new markets, driving innovation to provide differentiated offerings, enhancing productivity and cost efficiency and reinforcing resilience through sustainability and climate-focused initiatives. Despite the subdued demand outlook for non-AI applications weighing on the sector, HLIB said IOI’s plantation business remains the key earnings driver while its strategic initiatives and sustainability commitments support long-term prospects. The stock price is stable at RM3.860 as of 11.12 am. title: Gold Surges Past US$3,500 On Fed Rate-Cut Hopes

Bullion for immediate delivery climbed as much as 0.9% in early Asian trading to an unprecedented US$3,508.73 an ounce, eclipsing April’s peak. The metal has advanced more than 30% so far this year, cementing its position as one of the strongest-performing commodities. The latest rally has been fuelled by growing bets that the US central bank will cut interest rates this month, after Fed Chair Jerome Powell signalled a possible reduction. Attention now shifts to a key US jobs report due Friday, which is expected to underline labour market weakness and bolster the case for easing. Gold’s allure has also been magnified by mounting political and economic uncertainty. The precious metal, long regarded as a hedge in turbulent times, has gained support from fears of financial instability linked to President Donald Trump’s trade war. His increasingly sharp attacks on the Fed have sparked investor concern that the central bank’s independence could be undermined, further denting confidence in the US economy. body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research), MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB Research) and Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) have all maintained BUY calls on Gamuda, with target prices of RM6.52, RM6.35 and RM6.88, respectively, after the group secured a RM2.14 billion contract to build two hyperscale data centres in Eco Business Park V, Selangor. The contract, awarded by Quantum Alpha, a wholly owned subsidiary of Eco World Development, covers the construction, completion, testing and commissioning of two data centre blocks, a consumer substation and a water reservoir, together with associated infrastructure. Work is set to begin in the third quarter of 2025 and will take two years to complete. The project scope covers only the shell and core, with mechanical and electrical works expected to be awarded later, potentially lifting the total contract value to between RM3.5 billion and RM4 billion. RHB Research noted that the latest win, estimated to yield an 8% pretax margin, could translate into a combined data centre capacity of 140 to 175 megawatts, with more packages likely to emerge from additional land sales in Eco Business Park V. It said Gamuda’s outstanding order book now stands at RM39.8 billion against its RM40–45 billion target by end-2025, with near-term prospects including more data centre projects in the Klang Valley and renewable energy contracts in Australia. MBSB Research highlighted that this marks Gamuda’s second contract win for FY27, lifting its estimated outstanding order book to RM35.8 billion after accounting for the burn rate. It expects Gamuda to comfortably achieve its RM40–45 billion order book target by year end, supported by tenders for seven data centres, the RM4 billion Sabah water project, additional works on the Xizhi Donghu MRT, and renewable energy contracts in Australia. It also flagged potential variation orders from the Sydney Metro West tunnelling project, with the project pipeline in 2026 remaining robust across Australia and New Zealand. HLIB Research said the group’s position is strengthened further by the prospect of securing a mechanical, electrical and plumbing package worth around RM2.4 billion, with higher margin potential. It added that Gamuda remains in the running for several multi-billion-ringgit data centre contracts expected to be awarded in 2025, while 2026 could see major conversion of large projects, including the Perak and Sabah water supply, large-scale solar, pumped hydro, and the Taiwan MRT. All three research houses maintained their earnings forecasts, noting that the new win is within expectations and consistent with Gamuda’s strategy of expanding its recurring income base through renewable energy and utilities. The stock price for Gamuda is RM5.480, down by 1.44% as of 11.01 am. title: BNM Decision And US Jobs Report Keep Ringgit In Check
body: The ringgit opened higher on Tuesday but is expected to trade cautiously as investors await Bank Negara Malaysia’s Monetary Policy Committee meeting on Thursday and the release of the United States non-farm payrolls report on Friday. At 8 am, the local note rose to 4.2205/2300 against the US dollar from Friday’s close of 4.2230/2275. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said BNM is likely to keep the overnight policy rate unchanged at 2.75%. “BNM has delivered a pre-emptive cut in OPR. I suppose the degree of monetary policy accommodation is sufficient to support growth. More importantly, markets would want to see the latest assessment by the central bank concerning the current state of the economy and its prospects,” he told local media. He added that global sentiment remains cautious after the University of Michigan consumer sentiment index fell more than expected to 58.2 points in August, below market forecasts of 58.6 points. The index averaged 59.8 points in the first eight months of this year compared with 73.0 points in the same period last year, indicating American consumers have become more wary of the economy. The upcoming US non-farm payrolls data is seen as a key indicator for the Federal Reserve’s rate decision on Sept 17. “Consensus estimates have put NFP at 74,000 in August, slightly higher than July’s 73,000,” Mohd Afzanizam said. He expects the ringgit to trade between RM4.21 and RM4.22 today, supported by a softer US dollar against other major currencies. The ringgit, however, was mixed against a basket of currencies. It strengthened against the Japanese yen to 2.8690/8758 from 2.8708/8741 but eased against the British pound to 5.7171/7300 from 5.6833/6894 and weakened against the euro to 4.9443/9554 from 4.9291/9343. title: Oil Holds Steady As Supply Disruptions Offset Tariff, Output Concerns
body: Oil prices traded narrowly lower on Sept 1, as worries about rising global output and softer demand from US tariffs outweighed supply risks from escalating Russia-Ukraine attacks, Reuters reported. Brent crude slipped 12 cents to US$67.36 a barrel by 0046 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate eased 13 cents to US$63.88. Trading was muted due to a US bank holiday. Markets remain wary of Russian supply after weekly shipments fell to a four-week low of 2.72 million barrels per day (bpd), according to tanker data. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy vowed to intensify strikes on Russian territory after drone attacks on Ukraine’s power facilities, raising fears of further energy infrastructure damage. Still, expectations of oversupply are capping gains. US crude output hit a record 13.58 million bpd in June, while OPEC+ is set to meet on Sept 7 to discuss production levels. A Reuters poll last week suggested prices are unlikely to rally meaningfully this year amid abundant supply and trade tensions. title: Gold Surges To Four-Month High On Fed Cut Bets
body: Gold prices climbed to their highest level in more than four months on Sept 1, buoyed by rising expectations of a US Federal Reserve (Fed) rate cut later this month. Reuters reported that spot gold gained 0.7% to US$3,470.69 per oz by 0238 GMT, its strongest since April 23, while US gold futures advanced 0.8% to US$3,543.70. Silver jumped 1.6% to US$40.31, crossing the US$40 mark for the first time since September 2011. The rally comes after US PCE inflation data matched forecasts, reinforcing bets on looser monetary policy. Traders see an 87% probability the Fed will lower rates by 25 basis points this month, according to CME FedWatch. Non-yielding bullion typically benefits from lower interest rates. Investors now await Sept 5’s US nonfarm payrolls report for further signals on the Fed’s policy path. Among other precious metals, platinum rose 0.9% to US$1,376.95, while palladium added 0.8% to US$1,118.12. title: Asian Stocks Slip On Tech Pullback, Ahead Of Payroll Readings
body: Asian shares started the new month in the red on Monday after a court ruling threw another wrench into U.S. tariff policy and investors braced for a reading on U.S. jobs that could determine the course of rate cuts there. A holiday in the United States made for thin conditions, though Wall Street and European futures were still trading with small gains after retreating on Friday.The dollar and bonds were little moved ahead of a busy week for data which includes surveys of manufacturing and services, and a range of labour numbers culminating in the August payrolls report on Friday. Median forecasts are for an increase of 75,000, though estimates range widely from zero to +110,000 due to the uncertainty caused by July’s surprisingly weak report, while the jobless rate is seen ticking up to 4.3 per cent.Analysts also cautioned the August report has shown a bias to undershoot forecasts over the past decade. A result in-line or softer would cement market expectations for the Federal Reserve to cut rates at its meeting on September 17, which futures imply is a near 90 per cent probability. “Although inflation and growth data don’t scream out for a rate cut, at this stage it would likely require a significant positive employment surprise to stop the Fed from moving forward, given their concern about the sharp recent deceleration in job growth,” said Michael Feroli, chief U.S. economist at JPMorgan. The prospect of lower borrowing costs has underpinned Wall Street near record highs, and would be timely given September has been the worst performing month of the year for the S&P 500 over the past 35 years. Early Monday, S&P 500 futures were up 0.2 per cent, while Nasdaq futures added 0.3 per cent. EUROSTOXX 50 futures firmed 0.3 per cent, while FTSE futures rose 0.1 per cent and DAX futures gained 0.3 per cent. Japan’s Nikkei fell 0.9 per cent, tracking a drop in U.S. tech stocks on Friday, while South Korea’s market slipped 0.5 per cent.MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan inched down 0.1 per cent, having hit a four-year high last week on the back of a bull run in Chinese stocks. Trade uncertainty remained a drag after a U.S. Court of Appeals ruled many of President Donald Trump’s sweeping tariffs were illegal, but left them in place until mid-October awaiting an appeal to the Supreme Court. The White House has other means to apply sectoral levies but it puts a question mark over trade agreements already reached or being negotiated. Talks with Japan have hit a stumbling block over rice, while negotiations with South Korea have bogged down. “If the Supreme Court upholds the ruling, the Treasury would still need to return most of the now-close to $100 billion in additional customs duties collected over the past five months, and there is a danger that other countries would back-track on any preliminary agreements,” noted Paul Ashworth, chief North America economist at Capital Economics. title: Samaiden’s Growth Outlook Underpinned By LSS5
body: Samaiden Group Bhd is set for a stronger financial year ahead, backed by a swelling order book and new large-scale solar (LSS) contracts, according to MBSB Research, which reiterated its ‘Buy’ call with a revised target price of RM1.48. For 4Q25, Samaiden’s core net profit jumped 37.5% year-on-year to RM5.7 million, driven mainly by progress on Corporate Green Power Programme (CGPP) projects. Full-year core net profit rose 18.2% to RM19 million, meeting 87.6% of house estimates and 94.3% of consensus forecasts. Quarterly revenue more than doubled to RM135 million, though margins were slightly compressed by tighter pricing on CGPP projects. The group’s growth outlook is underpinned by its participation in LSS5, where it was shortlisted in late 2024 to develop a 99.99MW solar farm in Pasir Mas, Kelantan, supported by a 21-year power purchase agreement with Tenaga Nasional Bhd effective from October 2027. More recently, Samaiden secured its third LSS5 EPCC contract to build a 95MWac solar farm in Hilir Perak, a project slated for completion by 2027. Including the latest win, Samaiden’s outstanding order book has swelled to RM699.2 million, providing at least two years of earnings visibility. The company aims to lift this to RM1 billion by FY26, with active bids in the pipeline spanning upcoming LSS5+ projects, battery energy storage systems and rooftop solar solutions for both residential and industrial clients. MBSB Research highlighted Samaiden as a key beneficiary of Malaysia’s long-term renewable energy ambitions under the National Energy Transition Roadmap and expects FY26 to be driven by CGPP completions and the rollout of new LSS5 EPCC projects. Samaiden closed its trading session for the week at RM1.16, down one sen with more than three million shares traded. title: Is Genting Getting The House In Order?
body: Genting Bhd’s 2Q25 results came in weaker than consensus expectations, but analysts remain positive on the group’s longer-term growth prospects, citing recovery in tourism, new attractions in Singapore, narrowing losses in Las Vegas and potential upside from its pharmaceutical arm TauRx. According to CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd, Genting Malaysia Bhd (GenM) was the key earnings driver, with core net profit jumping 130% YoY to RM244 million, supported by higher casino volumes at Resorts World Genting and stronger UK operations. However, margins are expected to narrow in 2H25 due to higher electricity tariffs, a broader sales tax scope and increased marketing costs. Genting Singapore, however, saw 11% YoY earnings decline to S$98 million on phased closures under the RWS 2.0 transformation. Analysts expect a rebound in 2H25 as new assets, including the Singapore Oceanarium, Weave Mall and Laurus Hotel, open progressively. Plantations arm Genting Plantations Bhd weighed on results with an 81% YoY plunge in profit to RM15.7 million, dragged by weaker CPO prices, downstream losses and a land write-down. Meanwhile, Resorts World Las Vegas showed signs of recovery, with Ebitda surging 92% QoQ though still down sharply YoY. Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB Research), meanwhile, highlighted Genting’s 2Q25 core PATMI of RM124.3 million, down 71.5% YoY and below its and consensus forecasts. The absence of interim dividends was also seen as a negative surprise. HLIB Research cut FY25-FY27 earnings forecasts by up to 38% and lowered its target price to RM3.77 (from RM4.44), but maintained a ‘Buy’, noting Genting’s diversified global presence and potential value-add from TauRx’s Alzheimer’s drug candidate. CIMB Securities, meanwhile, lifted its SOP-based target price to RM4.20 (from RM4.12) after factoring in stronger GenM valuations. It expects Genting’s earnings to rebound in FY26-FY27, driven by Visit Malaysia Year 2026, Singapore’s new attractions and narrower RWLV losses. Both houses agree that while margin headwinds may persist in 2H25, Genting’s long-term growth story remains intact, offering investors exposure to tourism recovery and strategic catalysts across multiple markets. As of 12noon, the counter is trading at RM2.87, with an increase of RM1.06, with around 10.3 million shares traded. title: AI Stock Losses Pull Wall Street Off Record Highs
body: US stocks closed lower on Aug 29, retreating from record highs as losses in Dell and Nvidia dragged the market, while fresh inflation data showed tariffs beginning to feed into prices, Reuters reported. The S&P 500 fell 0.64% to 6,460.26, the Nasdaq dropped 1.15% to 21,455.55 and the Dow slipped 0.2% to 45,544.88. Despite the pullback, all three indexes logged solid monthly gains, supported by expectations that the Federal Reserve (Fed) will cut rates by 25 basis points in September. Dell shares tumbled nearly 9% after surging costs for artificial intelligence (AI)-optimised servers and fierce competition overshadowed its upbeat demand outlook. Nvidia fell 3.4%, extending a three-day slide after its earnings report tempered sky-high investor expectations. Marvell sank almost 19% on weak revenue guidance, while Caterpillar shed 3.7% as tariff-related costs clouded its 2025 outlook. In contrast, Alibaba jumped 13% after reporting robust cloud growth and unveiling a new AI chip, making it one of Wall Street’s most-traded stocks. Healthcare and consumer staples led sector gains, while technology slumped 1.6%. Economic data showed consumer spending rising at the fastest pace in four months, with services inflation firming. Economists said this is unlikely to derail Fed rate-cut plans, even as tariffs on imports add mild price pressures. For August, the S&P 500 rose 1.9%, the Dow gained 3.2%, and the Nasdaq added 1.6%. The Russell 2000 dipped 0.5% on the day but climbed 7% in the month. US markets will be closed on Sept 1 for the Labour Day holiday. title: RHB Upgraded To ‘Buy’ On Strong Loan Recovery, Improving Asset Quality
body: RHB Bank Bhd has been upgraded to ‘Buy’ with a revised target price of RM7.21, as MBSB Research analysts see strong loan recoveries and improving asset quality driving earnings momentum and higher shareholder returns. The bank posted a 6MFY25 core net profit of RM1.55 billion, up 7% year-on-year and meeting 51% of full-year forecasts. 2QFY25 net profit climbed 7% quarter-on-quarter to RM804 million, buoyed by stronger non-interest income that offset higher operating costs and tax charges. Dividend prospects remain attractive, with a 15 sen interim dividend declared and a 6.7% forward yield, while management signalled the potential for a higher payout if second-half performance holds. Although RHB trimmed its FY25 net interest margin guidance to 1.81%-1.83% amid interest rate cuts and forex volatility, MBSB Research expect broad-based recoveries, rising CASA inflows via its Higher Education Ministry partnership and cost discipline under the Progress27 plan to offset margin compression. The bank’s gross impaired loan ratio stood at 1.51%, with management confident of further improvements, particularly within the SME segment and Cambodian operations. Loan growth remains stable, supported by targeted strategies in overseas markets. Trading at a forward FY26F price-to-book ratio of 0.8 times, near its 10-year mean, and offering one of the highest dividend yields in the Malaysian banking sector, RHB is increasingly seen as a value play. MBSB Research noted that key risks flagged include steeper-than-expected margin compression, weaker non-interest income, and higher credit costs. Nevertheless, analysts believe its recovery-driven earnings trajectory and dividend appeal position the bank favourably versus peers. As of 12:13pm, the counter is trading at RM6.53 with more than 3.9 million shares traded hand. title: Dow, S&P 500 Hit Records As Fed Cut Hopes Lift Wall Street
body: Wall Street closed higher on Thursday with the Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500 notching fresh record highs, buoyed by optimism over US economic growth and expectations of interest rate cuts, even as Nvidia shares slipped on China concerns. Investors also drew confidence from revised US economic data showing second-quarter growth was stronger than initially estimated, driven in part by business spending on intellectual property, including AI. Currency markets reflected rate-cut expectations, with the dollar weakening against the euro and yen ahead of the Federal Reserve’s 16–17 September policy meeting. Traders are pricing in an 84% chance of a September cut, with 138 basis points of easing anticipated by end-2026, according to CME’s FedWatch tool. US Treasury yields were mixed as some investors booked profits. The two-year note rose 1.6 basis points to 3.639%, while the 10-year yield slipped 2.7 basis points to 4.211%. Commodities also gained ground, with Brent crude rising 0.8% to US$68.62 a barrel and gold climbing 0.6% to US$3,416.14 an ounce, its highest since late July. The benchmark index moved between 1,572.24 and 1,587.30 throughout the day. The market tracked cautious sentiment ahead of the release of the US Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index, the Federal Reserve’s preferred inflation gauge, which could shape expectations for future interest rate decisions. Actives included Genetec Technology, down 12.5 sen to 51 sen; Tanco Holdings, down two sen to 70.5 sen; Reneuco, down one sen to 1.5 sen; and Zetrix AI, down one sen to 86 sen, while Sime Darby gained 12 sen to RM2.07. Sectoral indices ended broadly lower, with the Financial Services Index losing 64.42 points to 18,111.02, the Energy Index down 5.83 points to 740.22, and the Plantation Index retreating 17.45 points to 7,594.45. title: Wall Street Slips As Nvidia Forecast Fails To Spark Rally
body: Wall Street ended lower on Tuesday after Nvidia Corp.’s outlook disappointed investors, dragging down technology shares and stalling the momentum of the AI-fuelled rally. The S&P 500 slipped from record highs after a US$660 billion ETF tracking the index fell in late trade. Nvidia shed 2.5% as its forecast for fiscal third-quarter revenue of about US$54 billion matched consensus but fell short of more bullish expectations. The company also unveiled US$60 billion in new buybacks, but sentiment remained subdued. The tech-heavy Nasdaq joined the retreat, with traders questioning whether the artificial intelligence boom can sustain its blistering pace. Despite adding nearly US$2 trillion in value since April, Nvidia’s results failed to clear the sky-high bar set by investors. Bond markets were steadier, with short-dated Treasuries extending gains on bets of Federal Reserve rate cuts. The 30-year yield was little changed as political headlines out of Washington added noise, including President Donald Trump’s firing of Fed Governor Lisa Cook amid allegations of mortgage fraud. title: Stock Today: Sime Darby Climbs As Analysts Reaffirm Positive Calls
body: Sime Darby Bhd’s shares rose in morning trade, climbing 6 sen or 3.16% to RM1.96 as of 12 pm, supported by upbeat analyst sentiment following its FY25 results. The counter saw active trading with 561.3 million shares changing hands, touching a high of RM2.05 before easing to RM1.96. RHB Investment Bank Bhd, CIMB Investment Bank Bhd and Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd all reiterated BUY ratings, setting target prices of RM2.10, RM2.24 and RM2.50 respectively, compared with the stock’s last close of RM1.90. Analysts pointed to the group’s resilient industrial operations and steady UMW contributions as key growth drivers, though performance was tempered by motor division losses in China. RHB Research said Sime Darby’s FY25 core earnings of RM1.17 billion came in largely in line with estimates, down 11% year-on-year, accounting for 96% of its full-year forecast. It highlighted that the industrial segment contributed around half of group profit before interest and tax, offsetting weakness in the motor business. CIMB Securities noted a sharp turnaround in 4QFY25, with headline net profit surging fourfold quarter-on-quarter to RM763 million, lifted by a one-off land disposal. Core net profit climbed 98% quarter-on-quarter to RM334 million, aided by stronger industrial margins and UMW’s improved showing, though full-year core earnings still slipped 9% year-on-year to RM1.16 billion. Meanwhile, Hong Leong Investment Bank said Sime Darby finished FY25 on a stronger note, with core net profit after minority interest of RM1.37 billion, above both its forecast and market expectations. It lifted its target price to RM2.50 from RM2.12, citing a robust RM4.5 billion orderbook, largely from the Australian mining sector, alongside sustainable dividend payouts of 13 sen per share. Analysts broadly agreed that Sime Darby’s industrial business remains its key earnings engine, benefiting from resilient demand in mining, improved after-sales contributions and UMW’s full-year consolidation. However, they remained cautious on the motor segment, particularly in China where stiff competition continued to weigh on margins. At current levels, Sime Darby trades near the upper end of its 52-week range of RM1.90 to RM2.05, with analysts expecting dividend yields of between 6.8% and 7% over the next two years. title: Stock Today: Berjaya Food Share Price Flat Amid Narrowing Losses
body: Berjaya Food Bhd (BJFood) closed at RM0.295 today, unchanged from its previous trade, with a total volume of 2.61 million shares. The stock traded in a range of RM0.280 to RM0.300, reflecting modest activity amid broader market movements. Analysts from CIMB Securities have retained a REDUCE call on BJFood, citing ongoing challenges in the operating environment despite a narrowing of the group’s losses. The company reported a 4QFY25 core net loss of RM24.0 million, down from previous periods, supported by post-Ramadan demand recovery, easing boycott-related pressures, and closure of underperforming outlets. Full-year FY6/25 core net loss stood at RM125.0 million, slightly below CIMB’s and consensus forecasts. Revenue for the quarter fell 11.2% year-on-year to RM115.9 million, impacted by store closures and weak consumer sentiment, though quarterly revenue rose 2.0% on recovering demand. Operating expenses dropped 19.2% following the net closure of 19 outlets, improving efficiency and EBITDA margins. Looking ahead, analysts warn that BJFood faces continued headwinds from regulatory changes, including the expansion of the 8% Sales and Service Tax on leasing services from July 2025, which could reduce earnings by RM4–5 million annually. CIMB Securities expects gradual revenue recovery through easing boycott pressures and ongoing store rationalisation, while retaining a Reduce call and a target price of RM0.20. Over the past year, BJFood’s share price has fallen 34.1%, underperforming the broader market, as consumer sentiment and external pressures weighed on operations. Strategic measures such as store rationalisation remain key for navigating the coming financial periods. title: Stock Today: Alliance Bank Holds Steady Amid NIM Pressure
body: Alliance Bank Malaysia Bhd (ABMB) remained stable in early trading, with its share price last done at RM4.51 as of 2.33 pm, unchanged from the previous close. Trading volume stood at 1.15 million shares, with the stock opening and high at RM4.51 and RM4.52 respectively, while the low touched RM4.50. Analysts have maintained a neutral stance on the stock. MBSB Investment Bank Bhd kept its NEUTRAL rating on ABMB, revising its target price up to RM4.69 from RM4.20, while Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) reiterated a HOLD with an unchanged target of RM4.80. ABMB posted a solid first-quarter performance for FY26, with core net profit of RM199 million, rising 12% year-on-year and 1% quarter-on-quarter, representing 26% of its full-year forecast and 27% of street estimates. Earnings growth was supported by high loan expansion and strong non-interest income from forex trading, wealth management, and investment returns. Despite the positive earnings, both research houses highlighted challenges ahead. MBSB noted net interest margin compression and asset quality concerns, while HLIB pointed to a nine-fold increase in loan loss provisions and a slight rise in gross impaired loans ratio to 1.96%, mainly in the consumer segment. Valuations remain stretched, with ABMB trading at 0.92 times its current price-to-book value, above the 10-year average of 0.81 times. Analysts expect further pressure on NIM following the July 2025 Overnight Policy Rate cut but believe selective lending and optimised funding costs will help cushion earnings. No dividend was declared for the quarter, in line with the bank’s usual practice. Both MBSB and HLIB concluded that ABMB’s growth prospects are supported by strong topline expansion, although near-term upside is limited due to high valuations and asset quality risks. Analysts highlighted that the index’s Relative Strength Index (RSI) is pointing lower, suggesting a softening of bullish momentum. The HSIF is likely to test the 20-day simple moving average (SMA), with a breach below this level potentially extending the correction toward the 50-day SMA. Despite the retracement, both moving averages continue to slope upwards, signalling that the broader bullish trend remains intact. RHB Research advised traders to maintain long positions initiated at 21,416 points on 14 April, with a stop-loss set at 23,800 points. title: Chinese Yuan Rises As Beijing Seeks Currency Stability
body: The Chinese yuan strengthened on Thursday, with the central parity rate rising 45 pips to 7.1063 against the U.S. dollar, according to data released by the China Foreign Exchange Trade System (CFETS). Under China’s managed floating exchange rate regime, the yuan is allowed to fluctuate by up to 2% above or below the daily central parity rate in the onshore spot foreign exchange market. The yuan’s latest adjustment reflects ongoing efforts by Chinese authorities to maintain currency stability amid global economic uncertainties, including fluctuating U.S. interest rate expectations and volatile capital flows in emerging markets. Analysts noted that the move comes as Beijing seeks to balance support for export competitiveness with the need to anchor investor confidence in the currency. A stronger yuan can help ease import costs and curb inflationary pressures, but an overly firm currency may pose challenges for China’s exporters, who are already navigating weaker global demand. The yuan has faced significant volatility in recent months, influenced by shifting U.S. Federal Reserve policy, China’s domestic economic conditions, and global commodity price swings. Market watchers will continue to monitor how the PBoC manages the exchange rate as China works to sustain economic growth while preserving financial stability. body: US stocks ended mixed on Tuesday as investors weighed earnings expectations against looming inflation data. The S&P 500 rose 0.4% after fluctuating between small gains and losses throughout the day. The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 0.3%, while the Nasdaq Composite also added 0.4%. Wednesday’s results are expected to serve as a barometer for both the chipmaker and the broader market. Dell and Marvell Technology are scheduled to report on Thursday. Looking further ahead, investors are also awaiting Friday’s July PCE inflation report, the Federal Reserve’s preferred measure. Economists expect core PCE to rise 2.9% year-on-year, slightly higher than June’s 2.8%. title: Stock Today: Public Bank Slides 2% Amid Cautious ROE Outlook
body: Public Bank Bhd slipped 2.04% to RM4.33 as of 2.45 pm Wednesday, with 23.5 million shares traded on Bursa Malaysia. The stock opened at RM4.43, hitting a high of RM4.43 and a low of RM4.32 during the session, while its last average closing price stood at RM4.42. Analysts continue to view Public Bank as a defensive play, though both MBSB Research and CIMB Securities flagged potential challenges in meeting its full-year return on equity (ROE) target for FY25. MBSB maintained a BUY call with a slightly revised target of RM4.82, while CIMB retained its BUY recommendation with a reduced target of RM4.90. Both cited net interest margin (NIM) pressure as a key headwind. For the first half of FY25, Public Bank posted a core net profit of RM3.5 billion, up 2% year-on-year, supported by stronger net interest income and non-interest income. This accounted for 48% of MBSB’s and 47% of street estimates, broadly in line with expectations. The bank declared a first interim dividend of 10.5 sen per share, representing a 58% payout ratio. MBSB noted management’s cautious tone on NIM guidance and suggested that achieving a 13% ROE for FY25 may require an ambitious 14% return in the second half. CIMB highlighted that while operating income rose 7.1% year-on-year to RM3.6 billion in 2QFY25, higher overheads kept the cost-to-income ratio at 35.6%. Despite these pressures, analysts said Public Bank’s fundamentals remain resilient. CIMB noted the bank recorded the highest sector ROE at 12.2% in 1HFY25 and maintained the lowest cost-to-income ratio among peers. MBSB highlighted attractive valuations, with the stock trading at 1.54 times its price-to-book value versus a 10-year mean of 1.90 times. Looking ahead, management guided for loan growth of 5–6% and deposit growth of 4–5% for FY25. Both research houses expect fee-based income from bancassurance and unit trust distribution to be key contributors in the second half. Analysts agreed that Public Bank’s strong capital position, stable asset quality, and dividend yield of around 5% make it a defensive choice amid sector pressures. title: Stock Today: Maybank Edges Higher At Midday
body: Shares of Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) traded slightly higher at midday, with analysts maintaining a cautious stance on the stock amid concerns over softer loan growth and margin pressure. At 12.30 pm, Maybank’s share price rose 5 sen or 0.51% to RM9.80, after touching an intraday high of RM9.83. The counter saw 34.7 million shares traded, making it among the most active in the financial services sector. MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB Research) has maintained a NEUTRAL call on Maybank, with a revised target price of RM9.92 from RM10.20, while CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) reiterated its HOLD call with an unchanged target price of RM9.85. Both research houses flagged weaker loan growth and net interest margin (NIM) compression as key risks, despite Maybank’s solid second-quarter results. The bank reported a 3.9% year-on-year rise in net profit to RM2.63 billion for the second quarter of FY25, underpinned by stronger non-interest income. Earnings were up 1.5% quarter-on-quarter, supported by lower tax expenses and improved associate performance, which helped offset higher provisions and operating costs. For the first half, net profit stood at RM5.22 billion, up 4.1% from the same period last year, meeting around half of both analysts’ full-year forecasts. MBSB Research noted that Maybank’s dividend yield remains attractive at about 7.1%, though valuations appear fair, with the bank trading near its 10-year price-to-book value mean of 1.26 times. Asset quality is stable, though certain wholesale banking accounts require monitoring. CIMB Securities warned that earnings momentum could soften in the second half of the year, citing July’s overnight policy rate cut in Malaysia, slower loan growth from weaker trade flows, and persistent cost pressures tied to wage inflation and technology spending. On the positive side, both analysts said Maybank’s fundamentals remain sound, with robust capital buffers and a healthy liquidity coverage ratio of 138.1%. Strong CASA growth and leadership in residential mortgages are expected to provide some stability. Management has also expressed confidence in sustaining revenue from investment securities and debt capital market flows, while working to optimise NIM through funding cost adjustments, particularly in Singapore. A first interim dividend of 30 sen has been declared, translating to a payout ratio of 67%, underscoring Maybank’s continued focus on rewarding shareholders. Still, with peers such as RHB Bank and CIMB Group potentially offering more competitive yields in the near term, analysts said Maybank’s dividend appeal may not be enough to offset growth headwinds, justifying their neutral stance. body: IOI Properties Group Bhd (IOI Properties) saw its shares climb 6.19% to RM2.23, as of 3.45 pm on Wednesday, following the release of its FY25 results, with a total traded volume of 11.4 million shares. Unbilled sales increased to RM851 million at the end of the year, offering earnings visibility ahead. At 8 am, the local unit stood at 4.2060/2265 versus Tuesday’s close of 4.2160/2210. title: Bursa Opens Softer As Global Sentiment Stays Mixed
body: Bursa Malaysia opened lower on Wednesday, tracking the cautious mood across Asian markets as investors weighed trade tensions and the prospects of further policy easing in the United States. At 9.13 am, the benchmark FBM KLCI slipped 4.45 points, or 0.28%, to 1,577.14 after opening at 1,582.42. Broader market performance was mixed, with the FBM70 gaining 0.23% to 16,490.61, while the FBM Emas eased 0.13% to 11,718.61. The FBM Shariah Index was little changed at 11,676.78. On the active counters list, Magma rose 3 sen to 33.5 sen with over 220 million shares traded, followed by Pharmaniaga, which edged up half a sen to 17.5 sen. TWL was flat at 2.5 sen, while Avangard and VTC gained marginally to 30.5 sen and 31.5 sen respectively. Regionally, equity markets opened on a guarded note after Wall Street ended mixed overnight. The Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped as trade worries resurfaced, while the technology-heavy Nasdaq inched higher on renewed optimism in chip stocks. Japan’s Nikkei was down in early trade, while South Korea’s Kospi also dipped amid weak export data. The cautious trading tone comes as investors brace for the next move from the US Federal Reserve, with growing expectations of a rate cut in September following weaker consumer confidence readings. At the same time, escalating tariff disputes between Washington and key trading partners continued to cloud the global outlook. Back home, sentiment remained fragile ahead of the upcoming corporate earnings releases and as investors assessed the ringgit’s movement against the US dollar. The local currency had strengthened in early trade on rate cut bets, helping offset some pressure from external headwinds. Turnover stood at 166.14 million securities with a value of S$230.19 million. Market breadth showed 109 gainers against 79 decliners, reflecting a relatively balanced but cautious market tone. title: Wall Street Pulls Back As Powell’s Caution Tempers Rally
body: Wall Street ended lower on Monday as investors weighed the US interest rate outlook and turned their focus to Nvidia’s upcoming quarterly results, following Friday’s rally that lifted the Dow Jones Industrial Average to a record high close. The S&P 500 fell 0.43% to 6,439.32, the Nasdaq shed 0.22% to 21,449.29 and the Dow retreated 0.77% to 45,282.47. Nine of the 11 S&P 500 sector indexes slipped, led by a 1.62% drop in consumer staples and a 1.44% decline in health care. Markets had surged on Friday after US Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell suggested at the Jackson Hole Symposium that a rate cut could be considered as early as September, citing labour market weakness. However, he also cautioned that any move was not guaranteed, leaving traders to reassess expectations. “The market has a Jackson Hole hangover,” said Longbow Asset Management chief executive Jake Dollarhide. “Investors are taking a little bit of a breather.” Attention now shifts to key economic data, with the Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index – the Fed’s preferred inflation gauge – due on Friday, followed by nonfarm payrolls next week. “The focus right now is the labour market,” said Cetera Investment Management investment director Brian Klimke. “We have the job market that’s rolling over a little bit and the economy is weakening, so the Fed needs to act sooner than later and they’re seeing it too.” Traders currently price an 84% chance of a September cut, according to CME FedWatch, with Powell’s remarks prompting Barclays, BNP Paribas and Deutsche Bank to forecast a 25-basis-point reduction in borrowing costs. Policymakers John Williams and Lorie Logan are set to speak later on Monday, with markets seeking further clues on the Fed’s stance. Meanwhile, Nvidia rose 1% ahead of its highly anticipated earnings on Wednesday. The AI chipmaker, now the world’s most valuable company, makes up around 8% of the S&P 500, meaning its results will carry significant weight for index funds relied upon by American savers. “This is an incredibly important event from a market participant standpoint,” said Michael Green, portfolio manager at Simplify Asset Management. Corporate moves also shaped trading. Keurig Dr Pepper plunged 11.5% after announcing an US$18.4 billion cash acquisition of JDE Peet’s. Furniture retailers RH and Wayfair dropped more than 5% each after President Donald Trump said his administration would investigate furniture import tariffs. Intel slipped 1% following Trump’s comments that the government was taking a stake in the chipmaker, with similar deals expected. Volume on US exchanges was relatively light at 14.2 billion shares, compared with the 20-session average of 17.1 billion. Declining issues outnumbered advancers on the S&P 500 by a ratio of four-to-one. title: Stock Today: Yenher Rises 3.3% On Solid 2Q25 Results
body: Yenher Holdings Bhd’s share price climbed 3.31% to RM0.780 as of 3.25 pm on Tuesday, reflecting investor confidence following a strong second-quarter earnings report. The stock opened at RM0.780, hitting a high of RM0.785, while trading volume stood at 11,000 lots. Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) has maintained its BUY call on Yenher, with an unchanged target price of RM1.41, citing robust earnings momentum expected in the second half of 2025. The livestock health products manufacturer reported a core net profit of RM6.2 million for 2Q25, up 42.8% quarter-on-quarter and 18.2% year-on-year, bringing first-half profit to RM10.6 million. Revenue for the quarter rose 11% quarter-on-quarter and 21.2% year-on-year, driven by stronger poultry demand and frontloaded purchases ahead of the expanded sales and service tax implemented in July. HLIB noted that gross profit margin eased to 17.5% from 18.6% a year earlier, due to a higher contribution from lower-margin distribution products such as grain and oil seeds. The research house highlighted that Yenher overcame operational disruptions following a January fire, completing repairs by end-July and resuming production in August. With operations stabilising, HLIB expects stronger performance in 2H25, supported by robust poultry sales and margin improvements from a firmer Ringgit, given that nearly 90% of the company’s input costs are denominated in US dollars. Looking ahead, HLIB anticipates a step-change in earnings from upcoming capacity expansions, including a black soldier fly plant in 1Q26 and enlarged biotech feed additives and premix production by mid-2026. These initiatives, along with Yenher’s proprietary formulations and growing customer base, are expected to reinforce the company’s structural growth outlook. Yenher’s steady 40% payout ratio translates into a forecast dividend yield of 4.2% for FY25, offering investors a combination of growth and income potential, HLIB added. title: Stock Today: PetDag Dips As 2H Earnings Cloud Looms
body: Petronas Dagangan Bhd (Petdag) saw its share price slip to RM22.02 as of 12.35 pm Wednesday, down RM0.78 or 3.42%, amid analyst concerns over second-half earnings. CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) has maintained a HOLD rating on the stock with an increased target price of RM22.30 from RM20.90, while Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) downgraded Petdag to HOLD from Buy, raising its target price slightly to RM22.45 from RM22.38. Both research houses cited potential earnings pressure in 2H25. Petdag reported 2Q25 core net profit of RM272.8 million, down 5.2% year-on-year and 7.5% quarter-on-quarter, reflecting weaker retail performance following diesel subsidy rationalisation in June 2024. Retail volumes fell 9%, though the commercial segment performed better than expected with higher jet fuel and diesel volumes and lower feedstock costs amid softer Brent crude prices. This lifted 1H25 core net profit to RM567.7 million, up 10% year-on-year and above CIMB’s estimates. CIMB Securities warned that commercial margins could soften to 3–4% in the second half if oil prices remain high, potentially driving a 7.7% decline in core net profit compared with 1H25. Retail growth is expected to remain constrained by economic conditions and subsidy changes. HLIB noted that 2Q25 earnings of RM270 million fell 6% year-on-year and 8% quarter-on-quarter, dragged by weaker retail and convenience contributions despite resilience in commercial operations. The bank also highlighted that Petdag’s share price has gained about 12% year-to-date, pushing valuations close to historical averages with forward price-to-earnings at around 20 times and dividend yields below 5%. Looking ahead, HLIB expects retail volumes to stabilise due to regulated RON95 pump prices, though long-term pressures from slower internal combustion engine vehicle sales and rising electric vehicle adoption remain. On the commercial side, jet fuel demand may benefit from a rebound in air travel, with MAVCOM projecting passenger traffic growth of up to 15.6% in 2025. Both CIMB Securities and HLIB pointed to Petdag’s strong balance sheet and steady dividend payouts as positives, but warned that volatility in commercial earnings and weaker retail demand limit upside potential at current levels.
