title: Stock Today: MISC Dips Amid Mixed Half-Year Results
body: MISC Bhd closed lower at RM7.48 today, down 22 sen or 2.86% from Monday’s close, with a trading volume of 1.94 million shares on the Main Market. The stock opened at RM7.70, reaching an intraday high of RM7.79 and a low of RM7.41, while the last average closing price (LACP) stood at RM7.70. Despite the decline, analysts retained Buy calls on the stock. MBSB Investment Bank Bhd maintained a target price of RM8.13, CIMB Securities at RM9.19, and Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) trimmed its target slightly to RM8.11 from RM8.14. MBSB Research noted that MISC’s first-half FY25 results came in broadly within expectations, at 54% of its full-year estimates. Revenue fell 26% year-on-year to RM5.5 billion, affected by weaker contributions from Gas Assets and Solutions (GAS) and Marine and Heavy Engineering (MHE), as ongoing projects neared completion and new projects were still in early stages. Higher freight rates and stronger petroleum earnings partly cushioned the decline. GAS earnings dropped 12% to RM543.2 million due to lower charter rates and vessel disposals, while the Petroleum and Product segment fell 18% to RM671.2 million, pressured by foreign exchange effects and lower charter margins. In contrast, Offshore earnings surged 55% to RM488.6 million following the commencement of an FPSO operation, though MHE suffered a steep decline as activity slowed. MBSB highlighted potential FPSO contracts under Petronas’ 2025–2027 activity outlook as a medium-term catalyst. CIMB Securities described MISC’s half-year results as largely in line, with core net profit of RM1.2 billion representing 56% of its full-year forecast. Second-quarter core profit slipped 19% quarter-on-quarter to RM557.3 million, mainly due to the absence of a one-off FPSO gain recorded in the first quarter. CIMB retained its Buy rating, pointing to steady dividends and potential upside from new FPSO projects. HLIB Research similarly reported first-half core profit of RM1.3 billion, up 5.7% year-on-year, despite weaker LNG contributions from contract expiries and lower charter rates. Stable petroleum earnings and Offshore growth from the Mero-3 FPSO charter partially offset the declines. HLIB expects petroleum demand and offshore projects to support FY25 performance and noted the stock’s dividend yield of around 5% as additional support. title: Stock Today: Flat Trading Mirrors Subdued Profits For Bank Islam
body: Bank Islam Malaysia Bhd (BIMB) saw its share price hold steady at RM2.32 as of 12.17 pm, with a daily trading range between RM2.31 and RM2.33 and a total volume of 886,300 shares. The stock opened at RM2.31, with buy and sell quotes at RM2.32 and RM2.33, respectively, reflecting limited intraday movement. MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB Research) has maintained a NEUTRAL call on BIMB, revising its target price down slightly to RM2.31 from RM2.36, citing weaker-than-expected earnings momentum and subdued return on equity prospects. Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) kept its HOLD rating with an unchanged target price of RM2.40, pointing to similar concerns. BIMB’s 2Q25 results fell short of expectations, with net profit of RM127 million flat quarter-on-quarter, weighed by net interest margin compression and rising operating expenses. For the first half, core net profit stood at RM253 million, down 5% year-on-year and meeting only around 43–46% of full-year forecasts, prompting MBSB Research to trim FY25–27 net profit projections by up to 10%. Both research houses highlighted that while loan growth has picked up, elevated credit costs and uncertainties in the retail financing portfolio remain a concern. Management also flagged potential capital constraints amid strong asset growth and dividend payouts. Despite an attractive dividend yield of roughly 6.6%, ongoing margin compression and higher costs are expected to limit near-term upside. HLIB noted that operating expenses rose 17% year-on-year, pressuring profitability, while gradual deposit repricing may help stabilise net financing margins over six to nine months following the July overnight policy rate cut. Both analysts concluded that valuations remain undemanding with price-to-book ratios below historical averages, but limited earnings visibility and weak return generation keep BIMB’s risk-reward profile balanced. title: Ringgit Opens Softer On Profit-Taking Pressure
body: The ringgit slipped against the US dollar at Tuesday’s open as profit-taking weighed on sentiment, following a 0.73% climb in the US Dollar Index (DXY) to 98.430 overnight. At 8 am, the local note was quoted at 4.2080/2175 compared with Monday’s close of 4.2045/2105. The index is expected to hold steady at 2.6% in July based on consensus estimates. “On that note, the USD/MYR could see similar moves as traders may look to lock in profits. The ringgit is likely to trade between 4.20 and 4.23 against the dollar today, as markets stay wary ahead of the PCE report on Friday,” he told Bernama. Despite its weaker showing against the dollar, the ringgit gained ground against several major currencies at the opening. title: Bitcoin Dips To Seven-Week Low As Ether Gains Momentum
body: Bitcoin fell to its lowest level in nearly seven weeks, retreating from the record highs set in mid-August. The largest cryptocurrency dropped as much as 0.8% to US$108,719 in early Asia trading on Tuesday, briefly slipping below its 100-day moving average before recovering slightly, according to Bloomberg data. Meanwhile, Ether has emerged as the preferred digital asset for traders after hitting an all-time high of US$4,955 on Sunday. Although it has pulled back somewhat since the weekend, investors are increasingly betting on further gains for the second-largest token. The shift in investor sentiment is evident in exchange-traded fund flows. In August, US Bitcoin ETFs recorded over US$1 billion in net withdrawals, while Ether-linked funds drew inflows of US$3.3 billion, signalling a rotation in favour of Ether. Sean Dawson, head of research at Derive.xyz, said, “It’s been a bloody start to the week for the majors, with over US$900 million in liquidations across crypto markets. The majority came from ETH (US$324 million) and BTC (US$209 million), and nearly all were long positions forced underwater after a broad-based correction.” Derivatives data also indicate growing caution among traders. Dawson noted that the 25-delta skew, a measure of whether traders are paying more for downside protection than upside exposure, has turned negative for both Bitcoin and Ether. This points to stronger demand for put options, suggesting that investors are bracing for potential retests of US$100,000 for Bitcoin and US$4,000 for Ether. As of 7.24 am London time on Tuesday, Bitcoin was trading at US$110,095 and Ether at US$4,420. title: Dow Hits Record Close As Powell Signals Possible September Rate Cut
body: Wall Street ended sharply higher on Aug 22, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average notching a record close after Federal Reserve (Fed) Chair Jerome Powell hinted at a possible interest-rate cut as soon as September, Reuters reported. Powell, speaking at the Jackson Hole Symposium, underscored the need to watch upcoming jobs and inflation data but acknowledged conditions for easing policy were strengthening. Traders boosted bets on a September cut to nearly 90%, up from about 75% before his remarks. The Dow surged 846.24 points, or 1.89%, to 45,631.74, surpassing its previous record from December 2024. Consumer discretionary led with a 3.18% rally, while chipmakers powered the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index 2.7% higher. Tesla soared 6.2%, Intel gained 5.5% amid reports of a US government stake purchase, and Coinbase rallied 6.5% as crypto-linked shares caught a bid. The rally snapped a five-day losing streak for the S&P 500, which had been weighed down by profit-taking in megacap techs earlier in the week. For the week, both the Dow and S&P logged gains, while the Nasdaq slipped 0.6%. Investor sentiment was further buoyed by an upbeat outlook from UBS, which raised its year-end target for the S&P 500 for the second time in two months, citing resilient earnings, easing trade frictions and expectations of Fed support. title: Wall Street Slips Ahead Of Powell’s Jackson Hole Speech
body: US stocks ended lower on Thursday as investors positioned cautiously before Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell’s appearance at the Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 152.81 points, or 0.34%, to 44,785.50, while the S&P 500 lost 25.61 points, or 0.40%, to 6,370.17. The Nasdaq Composite shed 72.54 points, or 0.34%, to close at 21,100.31. Traders have trimmed expectations for a September rate cut, with bets on a 25-basis-point reduction dropping to 79% from nearly 100% a week earlier, LSEG data showed. “We still have roughly 80% likelihood that the Fed will cut interest rates, but that is now being brought into question. So that is, in a sense, being worked into investors’ forecasts,” said Sam Stovall, chief investment strategist at CFRA Research. “Investors are saying, ‘You know what? Let’s take some profits right now.’” Thin August trading volumes are adding to the nervousness, with turnover at 12.28 billion shares compared with the 20-day average of 17.08 billion. “Jitters over what’s going to transpire tomorrow at Jackson Hole is certainly weighing on risk appetite a little bit with Chair Powell’s speech,” said Adam Turnquist, chief technical strategist at LPL Financial. “There could be a decent selloff if we get a more hawkish than expected event.” Multiple policymakers, including Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, Atlanta’s Raphael Bostic, and Kansas City’s Jeffrey Schmid, have recently emphasised the importance of remaining data-driven. A private report showed business activity accelerated in August, while July sales of existing homes unexpectedly rose, complicating the outlook for policymakers. Treasury yields advanced on the data, adding to pressure on equities. Nine of the 11 S&P 500 sectors closed in negative territory, led by consumer staples. Walmart slumped 4.5% after it raised its annual sales and profit guidance but missed quarterly profit expectations, citing higher costs from tariffs. Investors were also watching Target and Home Depot for signals on consumer resilience in the face of tariffs. “There’s a bit of a mixed picture within the consumer space and there’s uncertainty in the economy – whether that’s the job market or whether that’s prices (increasing) from a tariff pass-through,” said Chris Zaccarelli, chief investment officer at Northlight Asset Management. Technology names remained under pressure, including Nvidia, Meta, Amazon and AMD, following a selloff earlier in the week that raised questions about valuations and regulatory risks. Coty tumbled 21.4% after the beauty company warned of weaker US spending and forecast lower current-quarter sales. Declining issues outnumbered advancers on the NYSE by a ratio of 1.6 to 1. The S&P 500 recorded six new 52-week highs, while the Nasdaq logged 63 new highs against 101 new lows. title: Stock Today: SunCon Jumps 4.1% Following Strong Q2 Earnings
body: Sunway Construction Group Bhd (SunCon) saw its stock climb 4.1% to RM6.09 as of 3.25 pm on Friday, with 12.1 million shares traded. The stock opened at RM5.96, hitting a high of RM6.20 and a low of RM5.96, reflecting robust investor interest after the company posted impressive second-quarter results. The construction firm reported a 127% surge in revenue to RM1,476.9 million for Q2 FY2025, up from RM651.2 million a year earlier. Profit before tax rose 144% to RM122.6 million, while net profit jumped 118% to RM83 million, driven primarily by accelerated progress on data centre projects. SunCon’s construction segment led the earnings growth, recording a 140% increase in revenue to RM1,433.5 million, with profit before tax climbing 159% to RM121.4 million. The strong performance was underpinned by peak construction activity across multiple data centre developments, boosting overall margins. For the first half of FY2025, the group more than doubled its revenue to RM2,877.4 million, compared with RM1,256.0 million in the same period last year. Profit before tax jumped 157% to RM235.8 million, from RM91.9 million previously, highlighting the company’s strengthened earnings visibility. SunCon also declared a second interim single-tier dividend of 7.25 sen per share for FY2025, bringing the total interim dividends for the year to 12.25 sen per share. As of June 2025, the group’s outstanding order book stood at RM6.72 billion, with new contracts worth RM3.81 billion secured, covering projects such as data centres, transit-oriented development, and prefabricated components. title: Stock Today: Sime Darby Property Holds Steady Amid Analyst Buy Calls
body: Sime Darby Property Bhd held steady at RM1.51 on Bursa Malaysia on Friday, with a total volume of 1.635 million shares traded as of 12.01 pm. The stock opened at RM1.51, touched a high of RM1.52 and a low of RM1.50, while the last done price was RM1.51, in line with its last closing price. Buy orders stood at 671,400 units at RM1.50, while sell orders totalled 119,500 units at RM1.51. Analysts remain optimistic on the property developer despite a softer second quarter. RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) and Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB Research) have both maintained Buy calls on Sime Darby Property, with target prices of RM2.33 and RM2.05, respectively. RHB Research noted that earnings were below expectations as some projects remain in early construction stages, but strong property sales of RM2 billion in 1H25 keep the group on track for its RM3.6 billion full-year target. The research house highlighted plans to start three more warehousing facilities at Bandar Bukit Raja following full occupancy at Metrohub 1 and near full take-up at Metrohub 2, supporting recurring income and the planned REIT listing, while maintaining a quarterly dividend of 1.5 sen. HLIB described the 2QFY25 results as within expectations, with core profit after tax and minority interest of RM142.5 million, bringing first-half earnings to RM258.1 million. The research house noted that earnings should remain resilient, underpinned by a diversified portfolio across residential, commercial and industrial segments. HLIB also cited the upcoming East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) completion by end-2026 as a potential boost for Sime Darby Property’s industrial landbank near Klang. The recurring income base is expanding with assets such as the KLGCC Mall, scheduled to open in October 2025 with 85% occupancy already committed, while data centre leasing to Google from FY27 adds a medium-term earnings catalyst. Both research houses maintained their forecasts, with HLIB valuing the stock at a 20% discount to its estimated revalued net asset value of RM2.56, affirming Sime Darby Property as a multi-year growth story driven by industrial demand and resilient landed residential sales in the Greater Klang Valley. body: Citaglobal Bhd edged higher on Bursa Malaysia as of 4.09 pm, closing at RM0.820, up 0.61% or RM0.005, with 327,800 shares traded. The stock opened at RM0.820, touched an intraday high of RM0.820 and a low of RM0.815, while the last average closing price stood at RM0.815. The modest gain comes on the back of Citaglobal’s recent RM168.88 million contract award from Malaysia’s Public Works Department (JKR) for the FT3 Road Upgrade project. The contract adds to the group’s orderbook, now valued at RM1.3 billion, and covers the upgrading of existing roads, six bridges, five junctions, earthworks, geotechnical works, drainage, road pavement, road furniture, traffic management, road and traffic lights, and other miscellaneous works. The FT3 Federal road project will expand the Jalan Kota Bharu–Kuala Terengganu stretch from a two-lane single carriageway into a four-lane dual carriageway built to JKR standards. The new contract underscores Citaglobal’s growing presence in major infrastructure projects, providing investors with confidence in the group’s revenue visibility amid ongoing government development initiatives. title: Standard Chartered Shares Jump On US DOJ Ruling
body: Shares of Standard Chartered rose 3% on Friday following a favourable ruling by the US Department of Justice in a long-running civil case, the bank said. The London-headquartered, Asian-focused lender had faced recent pressure after US Republican lawmaker Elise Stefanik wrote to Attorney General Pam Bondi, urging a probe into the bank over alleged sanctions evasion. Stefanik noted that an unspecified case against Standard Chartered was set to expire next week and requested action before that date. In a statement late Thursday, Standard Chartered said it was “pleased and unsurprised by the Department of Justice’s filing in the legacy Brutus qui tam case, which continues to demonstrate what we’ve always known: the claims underlying this case are false.” Reuters Related The London-headquartered, Asian-focused lender had faced recent pressure after US Republican lawmaker Elise Stefanik wrote to Attorney General Pam Bondi, urging a probe into the bank over alleged sanctions evasion. title: Stocks Ebb, Bonds Gain As Powell Speech Looms
body: Asian markets looked set for a subdued open on Thursday as traders positioned cautiously ahead of Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell’s speech at the Jackson Hole symposium. Share futures in Japan dipped slightly while contracts for Chinese and Australian equities edged higher. A gauge of US-listed Chinese stocks advanced in New York, bucking the tech-driven weakness that dragged US benchmarks lower. The S&P 500 slipped 0.2% while the Nasdaq 100 dropped 0.6% overnight. Treasuries strengthened across the curve, pulling the 10-year yield down by two basis points. Traders appeared to discount inflation risks flagged in the Fed’s July meeting minutes, with swaps continuing to price in a strong chance of a September rate cut. “The minutes are consistent with Powell’s hawkish comments last meeting,” said David Russell of TradeStation. “The bulls might get some cold water splashed in their faces at Jackson Hole.” The dollar was little changed while the yen held steady after gains earlier in the week. Oil edged higher as US inventories fell, adding some support to commodity-linked currencies. Evercore’s Marco Casiraghi said the Fed remains “well positioned to respond in a timely way to potential economic developments,” but warned that unless the labour market tightens and inflation worsens, a September rate cut looks likely. Meanwhile, pressure on Wall Street’s biggest technology stocks has raised concerns about the durability of this year’s rally. The S&P 500 fell for a fourth straight session on Wednesday despite most sectors closing higher. Analysts cautioned that the outsized role of mega-cap techs could turn sector rotation into a broader market pullback. “Rotation can only take place if the tech stocks hold up,” said Matt Maley at Miller Tabak. “If they decline, the only rotation we’ll see will be into cash.” Others pointed to valuation risks. “The stock market is currently discounting a bright future ahead, and that assessment is largely justified thanks to stronger-than-expected earnings and greater clarity on trade and tax policy,” said Carol Schleif of BMO Private Wealth. Key Asian releases Thursday include Japan’s S&P Global PMIs, Australia’s consumer inflation expectations and Hong Kong’s inflation print. Markets in the Philippines are closed. title: Stock Today: PetChem Soars On Supply Cuts And Potential Price Upswing
body: Petronas Chemicals Group Bhd (PCHEM) surged 14.6% to RM4.79 as of 3.21 pm, buoyed by investor optimism over regional petrochemical supply adjustments. The stock recorded a high of RM4.82 and a low of RM4.18, with 43.2 million shares traded. Market watchers attributed the rally to a recent agreement among 10 South Korean petrochemical producers to cut 25% of their naphtha cracking capacity in response to a weak market. The capacity reductions, equivalent to 2.7–3.7 million tonnes or 1.4–1.9% of global ethylene output, could tighten supply and support higher petrochemical prices in FY26. Kenanga Investment Bank Bhd (Kenanga IB) noted that while it is premature to confirm a structural long-term uptrend, the proposed cuts, coupled with potential short-term supply disruptions, could trigger price recovery akin to upcycles seen in 2018 and 2022. Separately, China is reportedly preparing a major overhaul of its petrochemical and refining sectors. Plants over 20 years old, representing roughly 40% of the capacity under review, may require retrofitting, which could create temporary supply tightness next year. Kenanga IB said if the restructuring plans in South Korea and China proceed, effective global supply could temporarily fall by 3–4%, potentially signalling the start of a cyclical recovery in petrochemical prices in 2026. The stock’s bullish performance reflects investor expectations that regional supply constraints, combined with limited immediate new capacity, could lead to meaningful price gains in the near term. title: Ringgit Strengthens As Dollar Slips After Fed Minutes
body: The ringgit opened stronger on Thursday, lifted by a weaker US dollar following the release of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) minutes. At 8 am, the local unit stood at RM4.2190/2335 against the greenback, compared with Wednesday’s close of RM4.2250/2290. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the minutes indicated the US Federal Reserve was in a holding pattern as it assessed tariff-driven shocks on the economy, particularly inflation. “The debate hinges on whether the impact will be transitory or persistent,” he said. Mohd Afzanizam noted that Michelle Bowman and Christopher Waller, the two FOMC members who dissented and favoured a 25 basis-point cut, strongly believed the tariff-driven inflationary impact would be temporary. The US Dollar Index (DXY) slipped 0.05% to 98.218 after the minutes sent mixed signals to investors. Attention is now turning to Fed Chair Jerome Powell’s speech at the Jackson Hole Symposium on Friday. “Perhaps there will be more clues as to how the Fed might decide at the September FOMC meeting. In the meantime, we expect the ringgit to trade within a narrow range as traders remain cautious, although the odds of a 25 bps cut in September are high,” Mohd Afzanizam added. He said the local currency was likely to hover around RM4.22 to RM4.23 against the US dollar during the day. The ringgit also advanced against a basket of currencies. It gained against the euro to 4.9156/9325 from 4.9196/9242 on Wednesday, inched up against the Japanese yen to 2.8646/8747 from 2.8648/8677, and strengthened against the British pound to 5.6809/7004 from 5.7033/7087. title: HKEX Posts Record High Revenue In H1
body: The Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing Limited (HKEX) on Wednesday posted its revenue and other income for the first half of the year reaching 14.076 billion HK dollars, marking a 33 percent year-on-year increase and setting a new record for the group’s half-year performance. Driven by positive market sentiment, growing investor appetite for non-U.S. dollars assets and increasing participation of international and the Chinese mainland investors, the average daily turnover in securities trading for the first half of 2025 was 240.2 billion HK dollars, up 118 percent year-on-year. The Hong Kong ETF market continued to deliver impressive growth during the period, reaching a record average daily turnover of 33.8 billion HK dollars, up 184 percent compared with the same period last year. Stock Connect also continued to gain traction during the period, achieving record half-yearly turnover in both Northbound and Southbound Trading. Northbound Bond Connect also set a new trading record with the average daily turnover up 3 percent year-on-year. In the first half of 2025, Hong Kong regained its position as the world’s No. 1 IPO venue. IPO equity funds raised were more than eight times that of the first half of 2024, and the number of active IPO applications increased to 207 as of June 30, 2025, more than double the 84 applications as at Dec. 31, 2024. Bonnie Chan, chief executive officer of the HKEX, said that the group enters the second half of 2025 with new initiatives that are underway to further enhance the competitiveness and attractiveness of our markets, including preparations for a shorter cash market settlement cycle, the expansion of paperless listing regime, as well as implementing enhanced IPO price discovery requirements and the first phase of reduced minimum spreads. title: CIMB Downgrades Amway After Dismal 1H
body: CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) has downgraded Amway Malaysia Holdings Bhd to REDUCE from Hold with a lower dividend discount model-based target price of RM4.25, down from RM5.71, after the group’s 1HFY25 results came in below expectations due to weaker-than-anticipated sales and higher product costs. Amway posted a core net profit of RM1.4 million for 2QFY25, a sharp decline of 93.9% year-on-year and 89.3% quarter-on-quarter. This brought first-half earnings to RM14.6 million, down 73.6% compared to the same period last year. CIMB said the figures accounted for only 22% of its and 26% of consensus full-year forecasts, underscoring the extent of the shortfall. Revenue for 2Q25 fell 10% year-on-year to RM266.7 million, marking the 10th consecutive quarter of contraction. The research house attributed the weakness to softer consumer demand, particularly for health and wellness products and home appliances, while profitability was further pressured by higher Amway Business Owner (ABO) incentives and an unfavourable sales mix. On a quarter-on-quarter basis, revenue slipped 9.4%, with margins narrowing as cost savings failed to offset the weaker top line. CIMB Securities noted that Amway’s EBITDA margin dropped 7.7 percentage points year-on-year to 4.4% in 1H25, driven by elevated operating costs and higher product costs. Consumer sentiment has remained muted as households prioritise essential purchases amid rising cost pressures, while heightened competition in the wellness segment is expected to continue weighing on sales. Despite the earnings disappointment, Amway maintained its dividend payout, declaring 5 sen for 2Q25, in line with expectations. This raised its first-half dividend to 10 sen, translating to a 112% payout ratio compared to 29.6% a year ago. However, the house warned that sustaining such payouts could be challenging, and it has revised down its dividend forecasts for FY25–27F by 14%. Looking ahead, the research house expects Amway to focus on cost management to cushion margin pressures, but said the weak demand environment and rising competition would likely constrain earnings recovery. Following the downgrade, CIMB Securities cut its FY25–27F earnings forecasts by 15–22%, reflecting the weaker sales outlook and higher costs. title: Yuan’s Central Parity Weakens Against USD
body: The Chinese yuan’s central parity rate weakened modestly on Wednesday, with the reference rate set 25 pips lower at 7.1384 against the U.S. dollar, according to the China Foreign Exchange Trade System (CFETS). Under China’s managed floating exchange rate system, the yuan is permitted to fluctuate by up to 2 percent in either direction from the daily central parity rate in the spot foreign exchange market. The mechanism is designed to balance market forces with regulatory oversight, allowing flexibility while maintaining stability in the currency market. Analysts note that the yuan’s movement comes against a backdrop of cautious global financial markets, with investors closely monitoring China’s economic indicators and potential stimulus measures from Beijing. The modest weakening of the reference rate reflects both external pressures from a stronger U.S. dollar and internal considerations as policymakers seek to maintain a stable trade environment. Market participants say the PBoC is likely to continue striking a balance between supporting the yuan to prevent excessive capital outflows and keeping the currency flexible to accommodate economic realities. Despite near-term fluctuations, the yuan has generally traded within a controlled band this year, underscoring Beijing’s commitment to currency stability amid ongoing global uncertainties. title: Wall Street Drops As Tech Selloff Persists, European Shares Steady
body: Shares on Wall Street dropped for a second successive day on Wednesday as weakness in the tech sector persisted while a key meeting of central bankers later this week remained in focus for currency and rates traders. The S&P 500 declined 0.8 per cent and the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite dropped nearly 1.5 per cent in early trade, as the pressure persisted after a steep fall on Tuesday. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 0.2 per cent.Analysts pointed to a confluence of factors behind weakness in tech stocks, including concerns over steep valuations, investors exiting profitable positions and a general mood of risk aversion. “I think we were priced for perfection in the U.S. and there was quite a lot of complacency in markets, so some summer volatility should have been expected,” said Ben Laidler, head of equity strategy at Bradesco BBI.Wariness over U.S. President Donald Trump’s growing influence over the sector has also been in focus for investors. U.S. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is looking into the government taking equity stakes in Intel as well as other chip companies, two sources told Reuters. The potential moves follow other unusual revenue-sharing deals Washington has recently struck with U.S. companies, including AI chip giant Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices. While the individual developments may be brushed aside by markets, they fall into the broader bucket of concerns over the institutional framework in the United States, Laidler said. European shares managed to hold on to their gains from earlier in the day, and the pan-European STOXX 600 index was up 0.2 per cent. Britain’s FTSE 100 climbed to a record high, boosted by gains in consumer and healthcare companies. The U.S. dollar weakened slightly against a basket of peers after Trump called on Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook to resign. title: Tech Slide Drags Wall Street Lower Ahead Of Powell Speech
body: Wall Street ended mixed on Tuesday as investors braced for Federal Reserve chair Jerome Powell’s remarks at Jackson Hole, with technology stocks leading the retreat. The Nasdaq Composite shed 314.82 points, or 1.46%, to close at 21,314.95, while the S&P 500 slipped 37.78 points, or 0.59%, to 6,411.37. The Dow Jones Industrial Average edged up 10.45 points to 44,922.27 after briefly touching a record high. Losses in megacaps weighed on sentiment, with Nvidia tumbling 3.5%, its steepest drop in nearly four months. Technology and communication services fell more than 1.9% and 1.2% respectively. Steve Sosnick, chief strategist at Interactive Brokers, said, “Some investors are taking some profits from tech stocks and rotating into other sectors. (This move) spills into the broader market because of those stocks’ weight in major indices.” Powell’s speech at the Fed’s annual symposium in Wyoming from Aug 21-23 is seen as the week’s key event. “It seems like folks are hedging a little going into Jackson Hole, thinking Powell might be more hawkish than markets currently appreciate,” said James Cox, managing partner at Harris Financial Group. Interest rate futures suggest two quarter-point cuts this year, beginning in September, according to LSEG data. Sentiment on AI stocks also wavered after OpenAI’s CEO Sam Altman told The Verge last week that the sector is “in a bubble.” Despite the tech rout, six S&P 500 sectors advanced, led by real estate with a 1.8% gain on upbeat housing data. Home Depot rose 3.17% even as it missed quarterly estimates, while Lowe’s added 2.18%. Both retailers maintained their forecasts. Intel surged 7% after securing a US$2 billion investment from Japan’s SoftBank Group, and Palo Alto Networks jumped 3.06% on a strong revenue outlook. Medtronic slipped 3.13% after revealing plans to add two new directors following Elliott Investment Management’s stake purchase. Advancing issues outnumbered decliners on the NYSE by 1.06-to-1. The S&P 500 posted 13 new 52-week highs, while the Nasdaq recorded 56 new highs and 88 new lows. A Reuters poll on Tuesday showed the S&P 500 is forecast to end 2025 just below its current levels at 6,300 points, with analysts citing uncertainty over Donald Trump’s tariffs and the pace of Fed rate cuts. title: Stock Today: SunCon Rises After MACC Clarification
body: Sunway Construction Group Bhd (SunCon) saw its share price gain as of 9.52 am today, rising 1.91% to RM5.87, following clarification from the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) that its investigation pertains solely to an individual employee and not the company or its subsidiaries. RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has maintained its BUY call on SunCon, raising its target price to RM6.80 from RM6.55, reflecting an 18% potential upside. The research house noted that the MACC confirmation reassures investors that the matter remains isolated and does not implicate the company under the MACC Act 2009. SunCon’s board has emphasised its commitment to integrity, transparency and governance, including obtaining ISO 37001 Anti-Bribery Management System certification in May 2025, which involved extensive employee training, audits and monitoring. The ESG score for the group was also revised upward to 3.3 from 3.1 on the back of governance improvements. Despite unchanged earnings estimates, RHB Research highlighted that SunCon is trading at 21 times FY26F price-to-earnings, below its target P/E of 23.5 times plus a 6% ESG premium, with potential for re-rating if new data centre contracts are secured. The company currently holds RM15.9 billion in active tenders, largely comprising data centre projects, including the Seremban Sentral project valued around RM2 billion and upcoming expansion works for the JHB1X0 data centre in Sedenak. The house cautioned that lower-than-expected job wins could pose a downside risk to valuations, but the latest MACC update is expected to bolster investor confidence in SunCon’s compliance and governance framework. title: Ringgit Holds Steady As Markets Await Powell’s Signal
body: The ringgit began Wednesday’s trade flat against the US dollar as investors stayed cautious ahead of US Federal Reserve chair Jerome Powell’s address at Jackson Hole this Friday. At 8am, the local currency stood at 4.2215/2420 against the greenback, unchanged from Tuesday’s close of 4.2215/2255. Yesterday, it had slipped marginally to RM4.2235, down 0.04 per cent. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid noted the US Dollar Index (DXY) fluctuated between 97.95 and 98.29 points as traders awaited policy cues. “Market participants are searching for clues on the Fed’s stance on monetary policy and how it will shape their decision in the upcoming Federal Open Market Committee meeting on Sept 16-17. “Markets are pricing higher odds for a 25 basis points (bps) cut. title: Dollar Rises Ahead Of Powell’s Jackson Hole Speech
body: The US dollar extended its advance on Wednesday as traders positioned cautiously before the Federal Reserve’s annual Jackson Hole symposium, where Chair Jerome Powell is expected to deliver a closely watched address on Friday. Markets are bracing for any push back against expectations of a September rate cut. Traders currently price in an 84% chance of a reduction next month and about 54 basis points of easing by year-end. The dollar index climbed to 98.393, its highest since August 12, after gaining 0.4% over the previous two sessions. “Given the relatively high bar for Powell to meet, there’s a bit of risk being baked into the markets that he leans to the hawkish side and the proverbial rug gets pulled from beneath investors,” said Kyle Rodda, analyst at Capital.com. The Fed will also release minutes from its July 29-30 meeting later on Wednesday, though they may hold limited relevance as they predate the weak payrolls report and soft inflation figures that strengthened the case for cuts. In Asian trading hours, the Reserve Bank of New Zealand is set to decide on rates, with most economists expecting a 25 basis-point cut. The New Zealand dollar edged down to $0.5895, near a two-week low. “There’s little reason for RBNZ to keep rates on hold,” Rodda said, pointing to inflation within target and unemployment at post-COVID highs. The greenback gained 0.1% against the yen to 147.78, while the euro slipped to $1.1633, its weakest since August 14. Sterling fell 0.1% to $1.3476, the lowest since August 12, and the Australian dollar dipped to $0.64485, a level last seen on August 1. title: Asian Markets Slip As Tech Selloff And Ukraine Talks Stir Uncertainty
body: Asian markets mostly fell on Wednesday morning, tracking an overnight rout of United States technology giants as investors waited for signals of a possible interest rate cut in the world’s largest economy. The declines followed sharp losses on Wall Street on Tuesday, where major technology stocks including Nvidia, Palantir and Oracle shed significant market value. The selloff deepened concerns over whether the year’s extended rally in tech shares can withstand growing global economic uncertainties, including tariffs imposed by President Donald Trump on key US trading partners. In Asia, Tokyo’s Nikkei dropped sharply in morning trade, while Hong Kong, South Korea, Taipei and Bangkok also saw losses. Shanghai, Sydney and Manila bucked the trend, recording modest gains. The unease was compounded by geopolitical developments, as top US and European military leaders met in Washington on Tuesday to discuss the mechanics of a potential Ukraine peace deal. Recent days have seen intense diplomatic activity after Trump’s high-profile meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Alaska. Attention now turns to a possible direct meeting between Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who has signalled readiness for face-to-face talks. Oil markets have also been volatile, reversing Monday’s gains with losses on Tuesday as investors weighed the potential impact of negotiations on energy demand. Adding to the pressure, Japan reported its steepest export drop in more than four years last month, underlining the fragility of global trade flows as tariffs and geopolitical risks continue to weigh on sentiment. Investors are now looking ahead to Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell’s keynote speech at the Jackson Hole symposium in Wyoming on Friday. Markets are hoping for clearer guidance on the timing of a widely expected interest rate cut at the Fed’s September policy meeting, following mixed US inflation data last week. “Powell’s Wyoming speech is being framed as a high-wire act,” said Stephen Innes of SPI Asset Management. “Too dovish, and he risks stoking long-end inflation fears; title: Stock Today: AMMB Rises On Modest Q1 PATAMI Gain
body: AMMB Holdings Bhd (AMMB) saw its stock rise to RM5.50 as of 2.39 pm, gaining 5 sen or 0.92% on active trading of 3.12 million shares. The intra-day range for the financial services group was between RM5.45 and RM5.56, with the last done price matching the buy quote at RM5.50. The midday gains follow the release of AMMB’s Q1FY26 results, which showed profit after tax and minority interest (PATAMI) inching up 3.2% year-on-year (YoY) to RM516.2 million. The improvement was supported by a 9.5% YoY increase in net income to RM1.29 billion, driven by stronger net interest income (NII) of RM924.7 million and higher non-interest income (NoII) of RM366.0 million. Operating expenses rose 8.3% to RM563.9 million, reflecting higher personnel costs, but the cost-to-income ratio improved to 43.7%. Pre-provision operating profit climbed 10.5% YoY to RM726.8 million, while net impairment charges surged to RM72.4 million due to higher Stage 3 provisions in Business Banking. Performance varied across business segments, with Wholesale Banking leading growth on a 66.2% YoY PAT jump to RM270.6 million. Business Banking and Retail Banking were weighed down by higher costs and provisions, while Group Treasury & Markets nearly tripled PAT to RM190.3 million. title: Ringgit Edges Higher Despite US Dollar Strength
body: The ringgit opened slightly stronger against the US dollar on Tuesday, rebounding even as the greenback extended gains ahead of key policy signals from the Federal Reserve. At 8am, the local note stood at 4.2190/2320 compared to Monday’s close of 4.2200/2240. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said market attention was centred on US President Donald Trump’s talks with his Ukrainian counterpart Volodymyr Zelenskyy, alongside the Federal Reserve’s upcoming interest rate decision. “The US Dollar Index (DXY) is climbing ahead of the US Fed’s meeting minutes and Jackson Hole Economic Symposium this week. It appears that traders and investors are waiting for more indications whether the US central bank will cut the policy rates in the upcoming meeting in September,” he said. Trump met Zelenskyy in Washington on Monday before holding further discussions with leaders from Britain, Germany, France, Italy, Finland, the European Union and NATO. The meeting, billed as a European summit at the White House, comes as global markets weigh the broader geopolitical and economic implications. Against major currencies, the ringgit opened firmer across the board. title: Ringgit Rally Poised For Renewed Momentum As Analysts Eye Rate Cuts
body: Malaysia’s ringgit is set for another round of gains as expectations build over further easing by Bank Negara Malaysia and the government’s commitment to fiscal reforms. Analysts see the currency advancing to its strongest level in almost a year, with forecasts pointing towards RM4.10 to RM4.15 against the dollar by December. Oversea-Chinese Banking Corp projects the ringgit at 4.15 in the fourth quarter, while Malayan Banking Bhd anticipates 4.10 by year-end. MUFG Bank expects a 1.5% appreciation from current levels, boosted by Malaysia’s improved export competitiveness following a US tariff deal. The ringgit closed last week at 4.2120 against the greenback. The currency’s rebound from April lows has stalled in recent weeks, but upcoming inflation data could reignite expectations of further monetary easing. Bank Negara already moved with a 25-basis-point cut in July, ending its position as the last rate-cut holdout among Southeast Asian central banks. Global investors poured a record US$4.3 billion into Malaysian bonds in the second quarter, betting that looser policy would enhance returns. While lower rates can weigh on currencies, the Federal Reserve’s expected cut in September reduces the risk of capital flight. Analysts believe Malaysia’s policy stance, combined with steady structural reforms, will instead provide enduring support for the ringgit. “The government’s commitment to follow through on fiscal consolidation is key,” said Christopher Wong, executive director and foreign-exchange strategist at OCBC, who expects another rate cut later this year. Risks, however, remain. The US recently agreed to reduce its reciprocal tariff rate on Malaysian goods to 19% from a threatened 25%, but analysts caution that trade volatility continues to pose challenges. “The prolonging of trade uncertainty, and the lingering possibility that tariffs land higher than current levels, presents a sizable risk for Malaysian businesses,” warned Matthew Ryan, head of market strategy at Ebury Partners. “In this scenario, we would expect a moderate hit to Malaysia’s economy, and a more pronounced sell-off in the ringgit.” Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim has unveiled a five-year plan aimed at lifting growth through 2030, supported by a one-time RM2.8 billion stimulus package that includes cash handouts and lower fuel prices. At the same time, the government is making efforts to tighten fiscal discipline by reducing diesel subsidies and expanding the sales and service tax. Analysts believe this balancing act between fiscal prudence and growth incentives is central to sustaining investor confidence. Lloyd Chan, currency strategist at MUFG, said contained inflation could reinforce expectations for more policy easing and in turn strengthen the currency further. “What stands out for the ringgit is the ongoing government-led structural reforms aimed at boosting productivity and enhancing fiscal discipline, which should provide enduring support for the currency,” he said. title: Markets Rise As Fed Symposium Looms
body: Asian shares inched higher on Monday as investors positioned for a pivotal week in US interest rate policy, while oil prices slipped after the threat of tighter restrictions on Russian supplies appeared to recede. US President Donald Trump met Russian President Vladimir Putin in Alaska on Friday and signalled a shift in tone, appearing more open to a peace deal with Ukraine rather than pushing first for a ceasefire. Trump is expected to meet Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy and European leaders later in the day, though concrete proposals remain unclear. Attention now turns to the Kansas City Federal Reserve’s annual Jackson Hole symposium from August 21 to 23, where Chair Jerome Powell is set to outline the central bank’s policy outlook. “Chair Powell will likely signal that risks to the employment and inflation mandates are coming into balance, setting up the Fed to resume returning policy rate to neutral,” said Andrew Hollenhorst, chief economist at Citi Research. However, he added Powell was unlikely to commit to a September cut until jobs and inflation data are released. Markets currently imply an 85% chance of a quarter-point cut at the Fed’s 17 September meeting, with expectations of further easing before year-end. The prospect of cheaper borrowing costs has lifted equities worldwide, with Japan’s Nikkei advancing 0.5% to another record high, while MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan hovered just below last week’s four-year peak. US futures also edged higher, buoyed by a strong earnings season. The S&P 500 rose on the back of 11% annual EPS growth, with 58% of companies raising their guidance. “Earnings results have continued to be exceptional for the mega-cap tech companies,” analysts at Goldman Sachs noted, highlighting a 26% year-on-year EPS jump for the so-called Magnificent Seven. Bond markets remain caught between rate cut hopes and structural fiscal pressures, leaving the US yield curve at its steepest since 2021. European debt has faced similar strain, with German long-term yields climbing to 14-year highs on the back of rising defence spending. Currency markets reflected the dovish Fed outlook, with the dollar slipping 0.4% last week against a basket of peers, holding at 97.851 on Monday. The euro was steady at $1.1704, while the dollar edged firmer to 147.33 yen. Traders are also watching New Zealand, where the central bank is expected to trim rates to 3.0% on Wednesday. In commodities, gold steadied at $3,328 an ounce after sharp losses last week. Oil retreated as geopolitical risks eased, with Brent down 0.4% at $65.61 a barrel and US crude dipping 0.2% to $62.67. title: Analysts View Empire Asset Disposal As Positive For Genting
body: CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) has maintained a HOLD call on Genting Malaysia Bhd (GenM) with a higher target price of RM2.15, while Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) also reiterated its HOLD recommendation with an unchanged target price of RM1.82, after Empire Resorts proposed to sell its non-gaming assets in New York for US$525 million (RM2.2 billion). Empire, a wholly owned subsidiary of GenM, announced it would dispose of the 332-room Resorts World Catskills hotel, the 99-room Alder Hotel, the Monster Golf Course, a 2,500-seat event venue, and several restaurants to the Sullivan County Resort Facilities Local Development Corporation (SCRFLDC). The proceeds will be channelled into the purchase of 1,554.6 acres of land from EPR Properties for US$201.3 million (RM848 million) and the redemption of US$300 million (RM1.26 billion) in senior unsecured notes, which will leave the unit debt-free. As part of the agreement, Empire will lease back the land under the non-gaming assets from SCRFLDC until 2066 and manage the facilities for 20 years, with options for renewal. Both sides are in the process of finalising the terms, which analysts expect to be completed within the next three to six months. CIMB Securities said the move would materially reduce Empire’s net losses, which stood at RM252 million in 2024, through lower interest costs, the removal of depreciation from non-gaming assets and the cessation of land lease payments to EPR. Additional revenue streams from management fees and lease income with SCRFLDC would also provide support. The investment bank, however, continues to ascribe zero equity value to Empire, citing the uncertain outlook for its gaming operations, though it acknowledged that a turnaround could boost GenM’s earnings by as much as 55% in 2026–2027. HLIB also viewed the proposals positively, estimating that Empire could save US$22.5 million (RM94.8 million) annually in interest costs, equivalent to 38% of its 2024 losses. The research house expects the initiatives to strengthen both the balance sheet and earnings profile, although it maintained its forecasts for now, noting that the deal is still at a preliminary stage. Should the restructuring be implemented by end-2025, HLIB said its target price could be revised upwards to RM2.00. Both brokerages highlighted potential risks, including weaker-than-expected VIP gaming revenue at Resorts World Genting and rising costs across GenM’s key markets. On the upside, analysts noted that securing a Downstate New York casino licence by late 2025 could add as much as 50 sen to the company’s valuation. The current stock price is RM2.060. title: Oil Traders Brace For Cautious Start As Trump-Putin Talks Ease Sanctions Risk
body: Oil prices are expected to open on a steady footing on Aug 17 after US President Donald Trump’s talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin signalled a softer stance on sanctions and tariffs tied to the Ukraine war. At their Alaska meeting, Reuters reported that Trump said he and Putin agreed to push directly for a peace settlement in Ukraine rather than a ceasefire, a shift that could alter the trajectory of negotiations involving Kyiv and European allies. He also announced a pause on plans to impose tariffs on countries such as China that continue purchasing Russian crude, a move that traders say reduces near-term supply risks. The reprieve comes after months of uncertainty over whether Washington would expand secondary sanctions to Moscow’s largest oil buyers, including China and India. Such measures could have disrupted trade flows and tightened global supply at a time when demand growth is slowing. Brent crude ended at US$65.85 a barrel on Aug 15, while US West Texas Intermediate closed at US$62.80, both slipping nearly US$1 ahead of the summit. Analysts expect limited price movement when markets reopen, with investors waiting for clarity from Trump’s upcoming meeting in Washington with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy. European leaders are also expected to attend. Since Western sanctions, including an EU oil embargo and a G7 price cap, Russia has pivoted exports toward Asia, reshaping global crude trade. Any US policy shift on those flows will be closely watched by traders seeking signals on whether the Alaska talks mark the start of a longer-term détente. title: Stock Today: Keyfield Steady As 2Q Profit Declines Amid Lower Vessel Utilisation
body: Keyfield International Bhd’s shares remained unchanged at RM1.50 as of Friday afternoon, with 2,597,600 shares traded, following the release of its second-quarter financial results. The offshore support vessel operator reported weaker performance for the quarter ended 30 June 2025 (2Q25), with revenue falling to RM131.97 million from RM198.98 million a year earlier, while net profit eased to RM66.36 million from RM70.04 million. The decline was largely attributed to lower vessel utilisation, reduced charters for both owned and third-party vessels, and softer domestic OSV demand. Utilisation rates slipped to 74.6% in 2Q25 from 96.9% a year ago. For the cumulative six-month period, Keyfield posted revenue of RM218.72 million, down 28.4% from RM305.37 million, and net profit of RM87.04 million, a 13.3% decrease. To strengthen resilience, the group is expanding internationally and recalibrating its fleet, including a two-year charter of its AHTS vessel in the UAE, deployment of its cable-laying barge Keyfield Blessing to Saudi Arabia, and the disposal of Keyfield Lestari, generating a RM25.7 million gain in 2Q25. Despite the lower profit, Keyfield declared a second interim dividend of three sen per share, bringing total payouts for the year to four sen, representing around 37% of PATAMI. Market watchers noted that the stock has largely absorbed the earnings decline, reflecting investor confidence in Keyfield’s international diversification and ongoing fleet optimisation initiatives. body: Shares in Johor Plantations Group Bhd (JPG) slipped in mid-day trade on Friday despite the plantation group reporting a sharp 51% jump in first-half profit and declaring a dividend. As at 12.17 pm, the counter eased 1 sen or 0.75% to RM1.33, with 4.41 million shares changing hands. The stock traded between RM1.33 and RM1.37, after opening at RM1.35. The last closing price was RM1.34. Revenue for the six months rose 12.6% to RM738.72 million. For the second quarter ended 30 June 2025 (2Q25), revenue increased 10.4% year-on-year to RM398.29 million, while net profit climbed 50% to RM75.37 million. CPO sales contributed RM323.39 million, up 4.8% on a 1.9% rise in delivery volumes to 74,667 metric tonnes, while PK sales jumped 46.1% to RM73.07 million. Managing director Mohd Faris Adli Shukery said disciplined upstream operations, cost optimisation and sustainable practices underpinned the strong performance. “While mindful of potential demand-supply imbalances in the CPO market, the focus remains on optimising price realisation, sustaining production growth and advancing downstream expansion,” he said. The board declared a second interim dividend of 1.25 sen per share, bringing the total payout for the period to RM31.25 million. The group expects seasonal production growth in the second half of 2025 and remains “prudently optimistic” about sustaining its growth trajectory. In a leadership update, chief financial officer Aziah Ahmad will retire on 1 September 2025 after more than a decade with Johor Corporation. She will be succeeded by deputy CFO Zain Azrai Zainal Abidin, a Certified Public Accountant with over 27 years of experience, who joined the group in June. title: S&P 500 Closes At Record High Despite Rate-Cut Doubts
body: Wall Street ended Thursday mixed, with the S&P 500 inching up 0.03% to a fresh closing high of 6,468.54, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average dipped 0.02% to 44,911.26 and the Nasdaq slipped 0.01% to 21,710.67. Seven of the S&P 500’s 11 sectors finished in the red. The rally cooled after US producer prices for July rose at their fastest pace in three years, driven by higher costs for goods and services, which fueled expectations of broader inflation. Traders scaled back Federal Reserve rate-cut bets for 2025 to 56.7 basis points, from 63 bps before the data, though markets still fully expect a quarter-point cut in September. “The implication is that the Fed is going to offer a 25-basis-point) cut in September. But it will be a hawkish cut. It’s way too early still for the Fed to wish to guide the market towards an extended easing cycle,” said Thierry Wizman, global FX and rates strategist at Macquarie Group. He added the upcoming Expenditures Price Index would be key in determining whether inflation in services could unsettle markets. St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said a half-point cut in September is not warranted, while Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent earlier suggested it was possible. Intel shares surged 7.4% following reports the Trump administration is considering taking a stake in the chipmaker. Cisco Systems fell 1.6% after issuing a forecast that failed to excite investors. Deere & Co tumbled 6.8% after reporting lower quarterly profit and tightening its annual forecast, while Tapestry plunged 15.7% after projecting annual profit below estimates. Both Deere and Tapestry warned of tariff impacts. Sam Stovall, chief investment strategist at CFRA Research, noted: “US stocks are pricy,” with the S&P 500 trading at a forward P/E ratio of 23 — nearly 40% above its 20-year average. “The hotter-than-expected PPI report now has investors pulling petals from a daisy saying ‘They will cut rates, they won’t cut rates’,” he added. Meanwhile, a separate report showed jobless claims fell last week, signalling continued labour market resilience. In geopolitical developments, attention is turning to President Donald Trump’s upcoming meeting with Russia’s Vladimir Putin, aimed at halting the Ukraine conflict. On the NYSE, declining issues outnumbered advancers by 2.29 to 1, while on the Nasdaq the ratio was 2.14 to 1. title: Ringgit Slips Past RM4.20 As US Dollar Strengthens On Hot PPI Data
body: The ringgit edged lower against the US dollar at the opening on Friday, with cautious sentiment prevailing ahead of Malaysia’s second quarter 2025 gross domestic product (GDP) announcement later today and a stronger greenback in play. At 8 am, the local note stood at 4.2100/2210 versus Thursday’s close of 4.2090/2145. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US dollar received a lift overnight after producer-level inflation accelerated sharply. He noted that the July US Producer Price Index (PPI) surged 3.3% year-on-year, outpacing the 2.5% forecast, while core PPI jumped to 3.7% compared with 2.9% previously. Meanwhile, US initial jobless claims fell slightly to 224,000, better than the 225,000 estimate, signalling a resilient labour market. “Apart from that, those who applied for unemployment benefits fell last week, which gave the impression that the labour market was still healthy,” he told Bernama. Following the data, the US Dollar Index (DXY) climbed 0.42% to 98.254 points, with traders dialling back expectations of an interest rate cut by the US Federal Reserve at its upcoming Federal Open Market Committee meeting. On the domestic front, Mohd Afzanizam said the ringgit is expected to move between 4.21 and 4.23 against the US dollar today, with profit-taking tempting investors amid uncertainty over the Fed’s stance. “The USD-MYR was quite volatile yesterday. It reached RM4.1858 during the morning session but weakened later to RM4.2118. It appears that RM4.20 is the psychological level and the USD-MYR did pierce such a level momentarily,” he added. Against other major currencies, the ringgit opened firmer. title: Wall Street Rises On Rate Cut Hopes As Global Markets Join Rally
body: US stocks advanced on Wednesday, buoyed by growing optimism that the Federal Reserve will lower interest rates at its September meeting. The S&P 500 gained 0.3% to 6,466.58, marking another all-time high, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average surged 463.66 points, or 1%, to 44,922.27. The Nasdaq composite edged up 31.24 points, or 0.1%, to a record 21,713.14. Treasury yields fell, with the 10-year yield easing to 4.23% from 4.29% the previous day and down from 4.50% in mid-July, reflecting heightened expectations for policy easing. The consensus view is that the Fed will deliver its first rate cut of the year, making borrowing cheaper for households and businesses — though at the risk of stoking inflation. The rally rippled across Asia in the wake of Tuesday’s stronger-than-expected US inflation data. Hong Kong’s Hang Seng leapt 2.6%, Japan’s Nikkei 225 rose 1.3%, and South Korea’s Kospi added 1.1%. European markets, which had already digested the data a day earlier, saw more modest gains, with Germany’s DAX and France’s CAC 40 each climbing 0.7%. On Wall Street, companies most sensitive to borrowing costs led gains. Homebuilders rallied as lower mortgage rates could spur demand, with PulteGroup up 5.4% and Lennar gaining 5.2%. Brinker International rose 1.6% after reporting stronger-than-expected quarterly results, with CEO Kevin Hochman declaring, “Chili’s is officially back, baby back!” M&A activity also stirred trading. HanesBrands climbed 3.7% after agreeing to sell itself to Gildan Activewear in a $2.2 billion cash-and-stock deal. Gildan shares listed in the US jumped 11.8%. Elsewhere, cryptocurrency exchange Bullish made a powerful debut on the New York Stock Exchange, soaring 83.8%. However, some sectors struggled. Grocery and delivery firms fell after Amazon announced same-day fresh grocery delivery to over 1,000 locations. Kroger slid 4.4% and DoorDash dropped 3.8%, while Amazon gained 1.4%. Cava Group tumbled 16.6% after disappointing revenue figures and a 2025 sales forecast cut. CoreWeave sank 20.8% after reporting a larger loss than analysts anticipated. President Donald Trump has kept up pressure on the Fed to cut rates, often criticising its chair, but officials remain cautious. They have warned that Trump’s tariffs could fuel inflation, and that premature easing might “add oxygen to a growing fire.” Markets now await Thursday’s US wholesale inflation report, expected to show a slight acceleration to 2.4% in July from 2.3% in June. title: Stock Today: Petronas Chemicals Dips Amid RM1 Billion Loss
body: PETRONAS Chemicals Group Bhd (PCG) shares were down 0.28% to RM3.59 as of 11.08am today, as sentiment remained weak following the group’s announcement of a RM1.0 billion loss after tax for the second quarter ended June 2025. Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB) has reiterated its SELL call on the stock, cutting its target price to RM2.18 from RM2.50, while flagging expectations for the group to remain loss-making for the rest of the financial year. HLIB said PCG’s 2Q25 core net loss of RM83 million, which compared with a RM79 million profit in 1Q25 and RM444 million profit in 2Q24, came in below both its own and consensus forecasts. The earnings miss was attributed to weaker market conditions, feedstock supply disruptions at PC Fertiliser Kedah, and substantial one-off charges, including RM431 million in impairment losses on Perstorp’s assets, RM99 million in inventory write-downs, RM22 million in inventory write-offs, and RM446 million in net foreign exchange losses. Group revenue for the quarter dropped 16% quarter-on-quarter to RM6.4 billion, weighed by lower sales volumes and average product prices. Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) plunged 56% to RM395 million, driven by narrower spreads for urea and methanol and reduced contribution from Pengerang Petrochemical Company Sdn Bhd (PPCSB), which also recorded unrealised foreign exchange losses. Plant utilisation fell sharply to 77% from 94% in the preceding quarter as feedstock supply issues, repairs, and maintenance work curtailed output. This included downtime at PC Ethylene for vessel wall rectification and scaled-back operations at PC Aromatics due to weak paraxylene–naphtha economics. PPC’s Creditor Reliability Test, which began in late June, has seen utilisation improve to around 80–90%, though HLIB noted EBITDA losses at the unit narrowed only slightly to RM135 million from RM140 million in 1Q25. Despite the weak results, PCG declared an interim dividend of 3 sen per share, equivalent to RM240 million, payable in September. The group is pressing ahead with strategic projects, including the Melamine plant in Kedah, ready for start-up, and the Isononanol (INA) plant in Johor, which commenced commercial operations on 12 August. The INA facility will supply oxo-alcohols for plasticiser production and complement Perstorp’s product offerings in Asia Pacific. Looking ahead, HLIB warned that persistent oversupply, muted downstream demand and margin compression in the olefins and derivatives segment will continue to weigh on earnings, while the Specialties segment faces price competition from Chinese producers and demand weakness in residential construction. The research house has trimmed its earnings forecasts for FY25 to FY27 by up to 43% to reflect lower plant utilisation and sales volumes. PCG’s share price has fallen from RM3.60 at yesterday’s close, with trading volume at 4.23 million shares so far today. At RM3.59, the counter is trading at about 26 times HLIB’s projected FY26 earnings. title: Stock Today: MR DIY Dips 2.5% Despite Solid Q2 Profit Growth
body: MR DIY Group Bhd’s shares fell 2.5% to RM1.56 at 2.28 pm today, as the stock responded to broader market movements despite the company reporting a marginal rise in second-quarter profits. The volume stood at 9.7 million shares, with the stock opening at RM1.62 and reaching a high of RM1.63 and a low of RM1.55 during the morning session. The home improvement retailer posted net earnings of RM158.6 million for 2QFY2025, a 2.2% year-on-year increase, while revenue rose to RM1.2 billion, supported by contributions from newly opened stores. Transaction volumes increased 5.0% to 48.5 million, with the Group’s store network expanding 12.1% year-on-year to 1,502 outlets. Gross profit for the quarter climbed 6.4% to RM579.5 million, boosted by lower inventory costs through centralised procurement and the stronger Malaysian Ringgit. Profit before tax grew 2.0% to RM212.0 million, offset slightly by higher administrative expenses, including staff costs, following the revised minimum wage implemented in February 2025. MR DIY also declared a second-quarter dividend of RM142.1 million, up 25.2% year-on-year, representing an 89.6% payout ratio. The total dividend for the first half of FY2025 now stands at RM274.7 million, equating to an 82.5% payout of the six-month profit. Based on the trailing four quarters, the total dividend of 5.7 sen translates to a dividend yield of around 3% using the current share price. Despite the healthy results and robust dividend policy, the stock’s midday dip reflects cautious investor sentiment, with market watchers monitoring the impact of recent domestic policy changes, including the revised Sales and Service Tax and the new 2% EPF contribution for foreign workers. title: Ringgit Pauses After Gains As Fed Rate Cut Speculation Builds
body: The ringgit was nearly unchanged against the US dollar on Thursday morning, as market sentiment turned cautious despite stronger expectations for a US interest rate cut in September. At 8.05 am, the local note stood at 4.2045/2160 against the greenback, slightly softer than Wednesday’s close of 4.2040/2085. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid attributed the slower momentum to uncertainty over the US Federal Reserve’s next policy move. He said market odds for a US rate cut have risen sharply following remarks from US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who suggested the Fed should slash its funds rate by 50 basis points at the upcoming Federal Open Market Committee meeting. “The Fed is independent, and the Treasury Secretary has no authority to interfere, but such a suggestion points to a weakening US economy that needs help,” he noted. Mohd Afzanizam added the ringgit could gain further ground, potentially pushing the USD/MYR rate below RM4.20. “Yesterday, the ringgit appreciated against the greenback by 0.57% to RM4.2063,” he said. Against major currencies, the ringgit traded mostly lower in early deals. It fell to 2.8608/8688 versus the Japanese yen from 2.8554/8586 previously, and slipped to 5.7106/7262 against the British pound from 5.7078/7139, though it rose to 4.9243/9378 from 4.9305/9357 against the euro. title: Bitcoin Hits Fresh High In Anticipation Of Fed Cut
body: Bitcoin hit a record high on Thursday as increasing expectations for easier monetary policy from the Federal Reserve added to tailwinds from recently announced financial reforms. The world’s largest crypto-asset by market capitalisation climbed as much as 0.9 per cent to $124,002.49 in early Asia trading, surpassing its previous peak hit in July. On the day, the second largest crypto-token ether hit $4,780.04, the highest level since late 2021. Bitcoin’s rally is being powered by increasing certainty of Fed rate cuts, sustained institutional buying and moves by the Trump administration to ease investment in crypto assets, said IG market analyst Tony Sycamore. “Technically a sustained break above $125k could propel BTC to $150,000,” he wrote in a note. Bitcoin has risen nearly 32 per cent so far in 2025 on the back of long-sought regulatory wins for the sector following President Donald Trump’s return to the White House. Trump has called himself the “crypto president” and his family has made a series of forays into the sector over the past year. An executive order last week paved the way to allow crypto assets in 401(k) retirement accounts, highlighting an increasingly favorable regulatory environment in the United States. Crypto has scored multiple regulatory wins in the U.S. over 2025, including the passage of stablecoin regulations and the U.S. securities regulator’s move to overhaul regulations in order to accommodate the asset class. Bitcoin’s surge has also sparked a broader rally in the asset class over the past few months, shrugging off the tremors of Trump’s wide-ranging tariff policies. According to data from CoinMarketCap, the crypto sector’s overall market capitalisation has ballooned to over $4.18 trillion, up from about $2.5 trillion in November 2024, when Trump won the U.S. presidential election. The latest push for crypto adoption in the United States came via an executive order on Thursday last week, which would ease access to the asset class in 401(k) retirement accounts. The executive order could also be a boost for asset managers such as BlackRock and Fidelity, which operate crypto exchange-traded funds (ETFs). Crypto’s push into retirement savings can also be peppered with risks, as the asset class tends to experience much more volatility than stocks and bonds, which asset managers had typically relied on for such accounts. title: Wall Street Climbs To Fresh Highs On Softer Inflation, September Rate Cut Hopes
body: The S&P 500 and Nasdaq ended at record highs on Tuesday, fuelled by fresh bets on a Federal Reserve rate cut next month after US inflation data matched expectations. The Consumer Price Index rose 0.2% in July, while annual inflation increased 3.1%, slightly below forecasts. Yields on short-dated Treasury bonds slipped, and futures markets priced in an 88.8% chance of a 25-basis-point cut in September. “The CPI data is supportive for equities overall, getting some good news with the Fed looking more on track to cut in September,” said Katherine Bordlemay, co-head of client portfolio management at Goldman Sachs Asset Management, adding that mega-tech remained a key conviction. Alphabet gained 1.2% after Perplexity offered US$34.5 billion in cash for its Chrome browser. Intel jumped 5.6% after President Donald Trump met chief executive Lip-Bu Tan, days after demanding his resignation over alleged China ties. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 483.52 points, or 1.10%, to 44,458.61. The S&P 500 added 72.31 points, or 1.13%, to 6,445.76, while the Nasdaq climbed 296.50 points, or 1.39%, to 21,681.90. Relief also came as the US and China extended their tariff truce until November 10, averting triple-digit duties on each other’s goods. “Just as the Fed will be beginning to cut rates in the autumn, that’s when inflation data will probably start to register more direct tariff price increases,” cautioned John Velis, macro strategist at BNY. The Russell 2000 index rose nearly 3%, while airline stocks surged 8.87%, their biggest one-day gain in over a month, after airfares rose 4% in July. Bank stocks advanced 2.1% as analysts said a steeper yield curve could boost lending margins. Cardinal Health fell 7% after announcing a US$1.9 billion purchase of healthcare management firm Solaris. US stock inflows last week were the largest in two years, according to BofA Global Research. Advancers outpaced decliners on the NYSE by more than four to one, with 484 new highs recorded. Nasdaq advancers led by 2.69 to one, posting 104 new highs and 96 new lows. Trading volume reached 16.4 billion shares, below the 20-day average of 18.3 billion. title: Stock Today: Sunway REIT Rises Amid Mixed Q2 Results And Positive Analyst Outlook
body: Sunway Real Estate Investment Trust (Sunway REIT) shares edged up 0.47% to RM2.16 as of midday, buoyed by recent financial results and analyst optimism despite some segmental challenges. For the second quarter ended June 2025, Sunway REIT reported an 11% decline in net profit to RM129 million, down from RM145 million a year earlier, even as revenue rose 20.4% to RM211.4 million. Net property income (NPI) increased 19.8% year-on-year to RM154.9 million, supported primarily by growth in the Retail and Industrial segments. The Retail segment continued to perform strongly, with revenue jumping 29% to RM160 million and NPI surging 32% to RM114.1 million, driven by contributions from recently acquired assets and the expanded Sunway Pyramid Mall following the opening of its Oasis Wing in November 2024. However, the Hotel segment faced a 13% revenue decline to RM16.7 million and a 16% fall in NPI to RM15.6 million, impacted by lower occupancy due to fewer one-off events and regional airspace restrictions in June. Office segment revenue eased slightly by 2% to RM20.4 million, with NPI dipping 6% amid marginal occupancy declines. The Industrial & Others segment nearly doubled its revenue to RM4.5 million and saw a 57% rise in NPI to RM3.2 million, boosted by rental income from new tenants and recent acquisitions. Year-to-date Q2 revenue reached RM430.3 million, with NPI at RM312.1 million, underpinned by steady contributions from retail and industrial properties. Analysts from RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) and Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) have maintained their BUY ratings on Sunway REIT, citing resilient growth prospects supported by ongoing acquisitions and asset enhancement initiatives. RHB Research raised its target price to RM2.42 from RM2.13, implying a 13% upside and about 6% yield, while HLIB kept its target price at RM2.31, reflecting a total expected return of approximately 12.7%. RHB Research estimates Sunway REIT’s half-year core profit at RM200.9 million, with HLIB’s projection slightly higher at RM206.7 million. Both figures represent roughly half of the analysts’ full-year earnings forecasts. The REIT declared a semi-annual distribution per unit of 5.7 sen for Q2 2025, up from 4.7 sen in the previous year. Despite a 3.4% quarter-on-quarter revenue dip attributed to the absence of festive periods affecting retail footfall, core profit rose due to stronger interest income from advance rental collections ahead of the sales and service tax expansion. Retail occupancy remained high at 97%, while hotel and industrial occupancies improved to 60% and 83% respectively. Analysts expect Q3 to remain seasonally soft for retail turnover rent but foresee potential benefits from an extra public holiday in September and government stimulus measures. RHB Research forecasts high single-digit rental reversions for FY25, underpinned by full occupancy and strong landlord bargaining power. HLIB anticipates mid-single-digit reversions in line with management guidance. Both research houses flagged the hotel segment’s ongoing challenges amid heightened competition and soft leisure demand, but anticipate a recovery ahead of Visit Malaysia 2026 and improved tourist arrivals following Malaysia–China visa exemptions. Industrial and office assets continue to provide stable income streams, with occupancy rates steady or improving. The REIT’s acquisition pipeline remains a critical earnings growth driver, bolstered by its sponsor Sunway Bhd’s active property development pipeline. RHB Research expects robust profit growth of 13.1% for FY25, while HLIB highlighted recent electricity cost savings as a positive development, albeit too early to include in forecasts. title: Stock Today: Carlsberg Edges Higher Amid Stable Earnings And Dividend Payouts
body: Carlsberg Brewery Malaysia Bhd shares inched up 0.23% to RM17.32 at 2.10 pm on Wednesday, with a trading volume of 773,600 units. The stock opened at RM17.48, reaching a high of RM17.62 and a low of RM17.30 during the morning session. The price movement comes after the group reported a 3.2% year-on-year increase in net profit to RM81.9 million for the second quarter ended 30 June 2025, despite a 3.4% decline in revenue to RM490.2 million. Earnings per share (EPS) for the quarter rose to 26.80 sen from 25.97 sen a year earlier. For the first half of FY25, Carlsberg posted a 5.4% increase in net profit to RM176.5 million, although revenue fell 6.5% to RM1.15 billion. The growth in earnings was partly attributed to the absence of additional deferred tax liabilities from its Sri Lankan associate, Lion Brewery (Ceylon) PLC, which contributed RM9.1 million in Q2, up from RM8.3 million in the same quarter last year. The Board of Directors declared a second interim dividend of 20 sen per share for the quarter, bringing the cumulative interim payout for the first half of FY25 to 43 sen per share. RHB has a target price of RM22.50, implying a 30% upside, while HLIB’s revised target price of RM24.14 reflects potential total returns of 46.1%. Both brokerages highlighted the upcoming single-digit price increase in Malaysia from September 2025 as a potential margin booster. RHB Research expects further margin expansion from easing input costs and favourable foreign exchange trends, while HLIB noted historical resilience to price hikes, which have previously had minimal impact on earnings. Despite softer sales in Singapore due to cautious consumer sentiment and competitive pressures, Carlsberg’s diversified operations and strategic cost discipline position the group to maintain earnings stability and continue delivering shareholder value.
