title: Soft US Inflation Lifts Ringgit To Three-Day High
body: The ringgit climbed for a third straight day against the US dollar on Wednesday, buoyed by a weaker greenback after headline US inflation came in below expectations. The US Dollar Index (DXY) slipped 0.43% to 98.097. At 8am, the local note opened at RM4.2115/2285 against the dollar, improving from Tuesday’s close of RM4.2290/2320. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the currency is likely to stay supported, with the US dollar-ringgit pair expected to hover between RM4.20 and RM4.23 amid a high probability of a US interest rate cut. He said the softer July inflation reading of 2.7% was largely driven by a moderation in the Owner’s Equivalent Rent (OER) to 4.1% after holding at 4.2% for two consecutive months. OER accounts for roughly 25% of the Consumer Price Index’s weightage. “The US benchmark equity indices rose more than 1%, while the yield on the two-year US Treasury note eased by four basis points to 3.73%,” he said, adding that the lower-than-expected headline inflation has strengthened rate cut bets and fuelled Wall Street’s rally. Against major currencies, the ringgit was mixed at the opening. It weakened to 2.8502/8619 versus the Japanese yen from 2.8490/8512 and slipped to 4.9182/9380 against the euro from 4.9090/9125. However, it edged higher against the British pound to 5.6876/7106 from 5.6905/6946. The local note fared better versus regional peers, rising to 3.2825/2960 against the Singapore dollar from 3.2867/2893 and strengthening to 12.9965/13.0570 against the Thai baht from 13.0135/0300. It also advanced to 258.5/259.6 versus the Indonesian rupiah from 259.6/259.9 and improved to 7.38/7.41 against the Philippine peso from 7.41/7.42. title: Japan’s Nikkei Hits 43,000 For First Time, Extends Rally To Sixth Straight Session
body: Japan’s Nikkei share average rose above 43,000 for the first time on Wednesday, with the broader Topix index also marking a fresh all-time high, tracking Wall Street’s overnight gains and extending the rally into a sixth straight session. The Nikkei gained as much as 1.4 per cent by 0140 GMT to touch a record 43,309.62 and extend its winning run to 7.5 per cent since August 4. Monday of this week was a national holiday in Japan.The broader Topix advanced 1 per cent to an unprecedented 3,097.94, also rising for the sixth straight session. Overnight, the S&P 500 and Nasdaq closed at record highs as a moderate reading of July inflation bolstered bets for a Federal Reserve interest rate cut next month.”A sense of relief is permeating through markets” following the U.S. Consumer Price Index (CPI) data, leading Japanese stocks “to take a step higher,” said Maki Sawada, an equities strategist at Nomura Securities.At the same time, “there are signs that the Nikkei is overheated after its extremely steep rally, and a steep drop at any time wouldn’t come as any surprise,” she added. The Nikkei’s relative strength index (RSI) rose above 75, well beyond the 70 line that many analysts consider indicative of an overheated market. The RSI was at a similar level on July 24, and the Nikkei fell in the following four sessions. A stronger yen exchange rate, after Fed easing expectations hurt the dollar, also limited Japanese stock gains in the latest session, Sawada said. A strong yen reduces the value of overseas revenues at Japan’s heavyweight exporters. Of the Nikkei’s 225 components, 183 rose, 41 fell and one traded flat. Tech shares stood out, with chipmaker Renesas Electronics jumping more than 7 per cent, chip-testing equipment maker Advantest rising more than 2 per cent and Sony Group gaining 4.6 per cent. title: Wall Street Slips Ahead Of Key US Inflation Data
body: US stocks closed lower on Monday as investors awaited crucial inflation figures this week to gauge the outlook for interest rates while keeping a close watch on US–China trade relations. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 200.52 points, or 0.45%, to 43,975.09. The S&P 500 shed 16.00 points, or 0.25%, to 6,373.45, and the Nasdaq Composite slipped 64.62 points, or 0.3%, to 21,385.40. Tuesday’s July consumer inflation report is expected to shape Federal Reserve policy expectations. Market data from LSEG suggests traders anticipate a 60-basis-point rate cut by December, with recent signs of labour market weakness adding to the case for a more dovish stance. “The inflation data is starting to embody the more direct tariff impacts on the consumer, raising concern that inflation will remain sticky,” said Eric Teal, chief investment officer at Comerica Wealth Management. “Lower inflationary readings and slower growth numbers are needed to support the case for lower rates.” Semiconductor stocks were volatile after a US official told Reuters that major chipmakers, including Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices, agreed to share 15% of their revenue from advanced chip sales to China with the US government. Analysts warned the levy could erode margins and set a precedent for taxing other critical US exports. Nvidia fell 0.35% and AMD dropped 0.28%. US President Donald Trump signed an executive order extending a 90-day pause on sharply higher tariffs on Chinese imports. The extension comes as a key US–China agreement, allowing semiconductor sales to China, is set to expire on Tuesday. Trump praised China’s cooperation during talks. Intel climbed 3.5% following reports CEO Lip-Bu Tan had arrived at the White House, days after Trump called for his removal. Micron Technology jumped 4% after raising its fourth-quarter revenue and adjusted profit outlook. TKO Group surged 10% after Paramount secured exclusive rights to distribute UFC events for seven years in a US$7.7 billion deal. Despite the declines, Citigroup and UBS Global Research raised their year-end targets for the S&P 500 following last week’s strong performance by the index and the Nasdaq. On the NYSE, declining issues outpaced advancers by 1.18-to-1, while the Nasdaq saw a 1.24-to-1 ratio of decliners to advancers. Trading volume was light, with 15.5 billion shares changing hands compared to the 20-day average of 18.3 billion. title: Stock Today: Bintulu Port Rises 5.28% Amid Sarawak’s Clean Energy Deals
body: Bintulu Port Holdings Bhd shares rose 5.28% to RM5.38 in mid-afternoon trading on Tuesday, marking a 27 sen gain from its previous close of RM5.11, with low trading volume of just 100 shares. The stock traded consistently at RM5.38 throughout the session. The surge in share price comes on the back of the company’s recent announcement of three strategic memoranda of understanding (MoUs) aimed at boosting Sarawak’s clean energy ambitions. These partnerships, formalised during the launch of the Sarawak Energy Transition Policy, focus on decarbonisation and sustainable fuels, including bioethanol, bio-LNG, and hydrogen energy. One MoU with Sakura Ferroalloys Sdn Bhd targets the production of bioethanol and sustainable aviation fuel to align with Sarawak’s Net Zero 2050 goals and international carbon regulations. Another agreement with Borneo Biogas Pte Ltd involves bio-LNG development using palm oil and agricultural waste, coupled with new bunkering infrastructure. The third MoU with China’s Jiangsu Guofu Hydrogen Energy Equipment Co Ltd will see the establishment of a liquid hydrogen facility to support both local demand and export ambitions. These collaborations are set to progress with feasibility studies and technical discussions, reinforcing Bintulu Port’s strategic role in positioning Sarawak as a global leader in renewable and low-carbon energy solutions. title: Ringgit Strengthens Ahead Of Q2 GDP Data Release
body: The ringgit continued its upward momentum against the US dollar and other major currencies at the opening on Tuesday, ahead of Malaysia’s second quarter 2025 gross domestic product (GDP) figures due on Friday. At 8am, the local note appreciated to 4.2270/2460 versus the greenback from Monday’s close of 4.2320/2360. It also ended firmer against major currencies, edging up to 2.8528/8658 against the yen from 2.8657/8686, improving to 4.9097/9317 against the euro from 4.9269/9316, and rising to 5.6777/7032 versus the British pound from 5.6933/6987. The ringgit also traded higher against regional peers, strengthening to 3.2841/2999 against the Singapore dollar from 3.2936/2973, advancing to 13.0198/0884 against the Thai baht from 13.0569/0769, inching up to 259.6/260.9 against the Indonesian rupiah from 259.9/260.3, and gaining to 7.41/7.44 against the Philippine peso from 7.42/7.43. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the ringgit is expected to trade within a range of RM4.23 to RM4.25 against the US dollar today. He noted that the US Dollar Index (DXY) climbed 0.35 per cent to 98.52 points ahead of the US consumer price index (CPI) release later tonight. “Consensus estimates have pegged the headline and core CPI at a much higher rate of 2.8 per cent and 3.0 per cent, respectively, in July, up from 2.7 per cent and 2.9 per cent in June. Against such a backdrop, the US Federal Reserve (Fed) is seen to be keeping steady in the upcoming meeting in September,” he said. Mohd Afzanizam added that traders are watching Malaysia’s GDP numbers for monetary policy cues, although with markets largely focused on trade talks, the data would need to significantly exceed expectations to provide strong support for the ringgit. He also pointed out that the Reserve Bank of Australia is set to announce its interest rate decision today, with consensus expecting a 25-basis point cut to 3.60 per cent. title: Nikkei Surges To Record As Tariff Truce Fuels Export Rally
body: Japan’s Nikkei 225 Stock Average soared to an all-time high on Tuesday, fuelled by renewed optimism over global trade after the United States was reported to have extended its tariff truce with China for another 90 days. The blue-chip index climbed as much as 1.1% to 42,298.21, breaking past its July 2024 peak. Export-focused giants including Sharp Corp. and Advantest Corp. were among the session’s strongest gainers. Last week, the Nikkei also received a boost after Japan’s top trade negotiator revealed that Washington had assured Tokyo it would end the stacking of universal tariffs and proceed with promised cuts to car levies. A senior Trump administration official confirmed on Friday that the US was working to finalise an announcement on the tariff stacking. The milestone follows the broader Topix’s record-breaking rally late last month. While the Topix has been outperforming this year on strong domestic demand, the Nikkei – with its heavy concentration of exporters such as automakers and tech firms – had lagged amid tariff concerns until this latest breakthrough. “Japan is a bit more of a known entity now on the tariff front,” noted Tim Waterer, chief market analyst at KCM Trade. title: Bulls Back In Charge As Hang Seng Index Futures Climbs Towards Key Resistance
body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has maintained its long position on the Hang Seng Index futures (HSIF) as the benchmark staged a recovery on Monday, gaining 60 points to close at 24,894 points and hovering near its 20-day simple moving average (SMA) line. The index opened at 24,815 points before dipping to an intraday low of 24,740 points. It then rebounded to test the session high of 24,943 points, ending near the upper end of the day’s range and forming a bullish candlestick that erased the previous session’s losses. However, in the evening session, it pared some gains, retreating by 129 points to last trade at 24,765 points. RHB Research noted that the latest price action suggests selling pressure has eased, with bullish momentum strengthening, as indicated by the upward slope in the relative strength index (RSI). Closing near the 20-day SMA line also signals that the near-term trend remains constructive. “As long as the HSIF holds above the 23,000-point support, the recent pullback is viewed as healthy consolidation within a broader uptrend,” RHB Research said, adding that the positive trading bias remains intact in line with the prevailing bullish setup. The research house recommended traders maintain the long position initiated at 21,416 points (closing level on 14 April), with the stop-loss threshold fixed at 23,000 points to minimise downside risks. It pegged immediate support at 23,800 points, followed by 23,000 points, while resistance levels are set at 26,000 points and 27,000 points. title: Asia Stocks Climb On US–China Tariff Truce
body: Asian equities advanced on Tuesday, with Japan’s Nikkei hitting an all-time high and Australia’s ASX scaling record peaks, as investors welcomed the 90-day extension of a tariff truce between the United States and China. The move prevented triple-digit duties on Chinese exports to the US and boosted sentiment across the region, even as market reaction remained relatively muted. Marc Velan, head of investments at Lucerne Asset Management, noted, “The tariff truce extension was largely priced in, which explains the muted reaction.” Japan’s benchmark Nikkei was lifted by sharp gains in technology counters and renewed optimism over trade with the US. China’s blue-chip CSI300 index gained 0.5%, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng was little changed, and the MSCI broad Asia-Pacific index outside Japan rose slightly. European futures pointed higher, while Nasdaq futures were up 0.15%. In Australia, shares extended gains after the Reserve Bank of Australia cut its cash rate by 25 basis points to 3.60%, the lowest in two years. The Australian dollar was choppy in response, as the central bank remained cautious on future easing. The truce extension follows months of tit-for-tat tariff exchanges and negotiations in Geneva, London, and Stockholm aimed at scaling back retaliatory duties. The easing of trade tensions allows investors to focus on an event-heavy week, including US inflation data and Friday’s planned summit between US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin. US consumer price inflation figures for July are due later on Tuesday. Economists polled by Reuters expect month-on-month core CPI to have risen 0.3%, compared with 0.2% in June. Mike Houlahan, director at Electus Financial in Auckland, said, “I think the Fed will go ahead and cut in September, partly due to political pressure and partly due to the softening labour data. But it’ll be a conundrum for them if inflation starts to tick higher.” An upside surprise in inflation could temper market expectations for rate cuts this year. Futures pricing points to at least two cuts in 2025, while JPMorgan anticipates four consecutive cuts starting in September. In commodities, gold traded at $3,353 after falling 1.6% on Monday when Trump said there would be no tariffs on imported gold bars. Oil prices edged higher ahead of the August 15 Trump–Putin meeting, which is aimed at negotiating an end to the war in Ukraine. The White House has hinted at further pressure on Moscow if no peace deal is reached. Currencies were steady, with the US dollar little changed against the euro and yen. Bitcoin slipped to $118,680, while ether gained 1% to $4,290. title: Ringgit Rebounds After Two-Day Decline Ahead Of US CPI Data
body: The ringgit started the week stronger against the US dollar, rising to 4.2365/2515 at 8 am on Monday from last Friday’s close of 4.2420/2480, rebounding after two consecutive sessions of losses. Analysts attributed the move to market caution amid concerns over the impact of fresh US tariff proposals on semiconductors and pharmaceuticals, a measure seen as potentially disrupting both domestic and global trade. US President Donald Trump’s latest policy manoeuvres, they said, were adding to already fragile investor sentiment. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the ringgit is likely to stay within a narrow band of 4.24 to 4.25 in the near term, as investors await key data releases. “The ringgit will continue to trade cautiously ahead of the US Consumer Price Index data on Tuesday,” he said, noting consensus forecasts for July inflation to edge up to 2.8 per cent from 2.7 per cent, with core inflation ticking up to 3.0 per cent from 2.9 per cent. He added that Malaysia’s second-quarter GDP figures, due on Friday, will also be closely watched. Preliminary estimates released in July pointed to 4.5 per cent growth in Q2 2025, but slower Industrial Production Index (2.0 per cent) and Services Index (5.0 per cent) readings suggest a potential downside risk to the final figure. The US dollar remained supported by mixed signals from recent US Federal Reserve comments, with the dollar index at 98.243 points, up 0.06 per cent. At the open, the ringgit also strengthened against major currencies, improving to 2.8693/8796 versus the yen, 4.9343/9517 against the euro, and 5.6951/7153 against the British pound. Gains were also recorded against regional peers, including the Singapore dollar at 3.2966/3086, Thai baht at 13.0801/1381, Indonesian rupiah at 260.0/261.0, and Philippine peso at 7.42/7.45. title: Malaysian Rubber Market Extends Gains On Regional Futures Rally
body: The Malaysian rubber market closed higher on Aug 11, continuing the uptrend on Aug 8 in tandem with gains in regional rubber futures, particularly in Japan, amid expectations of US interest rate cuts, Bernama reported. The report stated that sentiment was further buoyed by concerns over tightening raw material supply in major natural rubber-producing countries such as Thailand, where wet weather has disrupted output. However, gains were capped by weaker crude oil prices as investors awaited developments on the US-China tariff truce, which is set to expire this week. As of writing, benchmark Brent crude was down 0.84% at US$66.03 per barrel. At 3pm, the Malaysian Rubber Board quoted Standard Malaysian Rubber (SMR) 20 at 736.00 sen per kg, up 10.0 sen, while latex in bulk rose 5.0 sen to 574.00 sen per kg. On the global market, RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research)’s research unit said COMEX gold surged above the US$3,450 resistance, closing higher at US$3,464 on Friday amid strong demand. The precious metal touched an intraday low of US$3,418 before rallying to a high of US$3,503.70. RHB Research noted that the uptrending Relative Strength Index (RSI) signals bullish momentum, with the commodity now eyeing the next resistance level at US$3,600 and potentially US$3,700 thereafter. “At this juncture, the Shooting Star pattern formed on April 22 has weakened. Riding on the strong bullish momentum, the commodity is setting its sights on the next resistance level at US$3,600,” it said. title: Bursa Opens Higher, Tracks Wall Street’s Gains On Apple Boost
body: Bursa Malaysia opened higher on Monday, mirroring Wall Street’s rally last Friday that was driven by gains in Apple shares after the tech giant unveiled fresh investment plans in the United States. At 9.05 am, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) was up 1.05 points or 0.07% at 1,558.03, compared with last Friday’s close of 1,556.98. The index opened 0.76 of a point firmer at 1,557.74. Market breadth, however, was negative, with 128 losers edging out 121 gainers, while 287 counters were unchanged, 1,987 untraded and nine suspended. Turnover stood at 103.16 million shares worth RM42.8 million. Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng said trading patterns would likely hinge on market sentiment towards ongoing tariff developments in the US. “Meanwhile, the US 10-year yield edged higher at 4.285 per cent. Thong noted that the FBM KLCI had maintained its uptrend last week, closing near the 1,560 mark on Friday, with gains largely concentrated on laggards despite muted volumes. title: Analysts Maintain ‘Hold’ On Maybank With Higher Target
body: CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) has maintained its HOLD rating on Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) with a higher target price of RM9.85, up from RM9.40, after rolling forward valuations to FY26. The revision is based on a FY26F price-to-book value (P/BV) multiple of 1.21 times, underpinned by a return on equity (ROE) of 10.4% and a cost of equity of 9.1%. The research house said that while Maybank remains fundamentally sound with strong capital buffers, liquidity and a diversified ASEAN franchise, the balance of risks and rewards appears neutral in the short term due to subdued near-term earnings momentum. CIMB Securities noted that macro headwinds such as global supply chain disruptions and softer trade activity could weigh on domestic economic momentum from the second half of 2025 into early 2026. It expects Maybank’s 2H25 earnings to be pressured by net interest margin (NIM) compression following Bank Negara Malaysia’s 25-basis point Overnight Policy Rate (OPR) cut in July, a moderation in loan growth, persistently high operating costs and softer non-interest income from wealth management and investment banking. The broker highlighted that the timing mismatch in asset and liability repricing could see funding costs remain elevated in the near term, as most deposit costs will only adjust lower over the next nine to 12 months. While Maybank guides for a stable 2025 NIM of around 2.04%, CIMB Securities warned that this forecast may be at risk, with an estimated RM300 million hit to annualised net interest income from the OPR cut, front-loaded into the second half of the year. Although Maybank offers a respectable forecast dividend yield of 6.0–6.7% for FY25–27, CIMB Securities observed that peers such as RHB Bank and CIMB Group provide higher yields and more compelling valuations, with stronger earnings growth prospects. The research house lowered its FY25–27 earnings forecasts for Maybank by up to 7.9%, factoring in reduced NIM assumptions, slower loan growth, higher operating expenses and a more cautious non-interest income outlook. CIMB Securities acknowledged Maybank’s unique regional positioning, with an extensive ASEAN presence and growth initiatives under its seven ‘Super Growth’ engines, including wealth management, middle-market banking and foreign exchange sales. These are expected to support structural ROE expansion beyond 2026 but are unlikely to offset macro-driven headwinds in the near term. The research house concluded that Maybank remains a solid defensive core holding, offering resilience, strategic clarity and well-diversified earnings. However, it maintained its Hold rating pending clearer upside catalysts such as NIM stabilisation, improved regional economic momentum or stronger-than-expected traction from its growth engines. title: Weekly Review: STI Eases On Global Jitters As SGX Posts Record Profit, Strong IPO Pipeline
body: Singapore stocks ended the trading week on a softer note, with the Straits Times Index (STI) slipping 0.43% to close at around 4,240 points on Aug 8, tracking mixed Asia-Pacific markets as geopolitical tensions and global economic uncertainty kept investors cautious. The STI’s decline was in line with regional peers, where markets reacted to volatile commodity prices, the prospect of delayed US interest rate cuts and ongoing trade frictions. Early-week losses for the STI were tempered by selective buying in blue chips, but gains were not sustained amid persistent caution over external risks. The subdued index performance came despite upbeat corporate news from Singapore Exchange (SGX). The bourse operator posted record annual adjusted net profit of S$609.5 million for the financial year ended June, up 15.9% from the previous year, driven by an 11.7% jump in revenue to S$1.3 billion. Growth was fuelled by higher trading volumes in equities, currencies and commodities, reflecting both heightened market activity and product diversification. SGX also highlighted its strongest IPO pipeline in years, with more than 30 companies actively pursuing listings. Chief executive Loh Boon Chye described the pipeline as a “multi-sector and multi-geography” mix, indicating broad investor and issuer interest. The exchange raised its final quarterly dividend to 10.5 Singapore cents per share, up from nine cents a year earlier, and outlined plans to lift payouts progressively between financial year 2026 (FY26) and FY28. Despite the strong results and promising growth outlook, SGX shares fell 2.5% on Aug 8 as investors locked in profits after a rally that has left the stock up around 25% year-to-date. Analysts said the pullback reflected short-term market positioning rather than any change in the company’s fundamentals. Sector-wise, financials and property counters were mixed, while industrials saw marginal losses. Defensive plays in the utilities and consumer staples segments attracted interest amid broader risk aversion. Turnover for the week was steady, underpinned by institutional flows into selective large-cap stocks. Looking ahead , market strategists said the STI’s near-term trajectory will hinge on upcoming US inflation data, China’s economic stimulus signals and regional corporate earnings. title: Weekly Recap: Hang Seng Ends Week Higher Despite Late Pullback On Trade Uncertainty
body: Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index (HSI) booked a weekly gain of 1.4% from Aug 4 to Aug 8, closing at 24,859 on Aug 8, despite a late sell-off that erased part of its earlier advance. The retreat came as renewed concerns over US-China trade tensions tempered optimism built up earlier in the week. The index opened the week on a strong note, climbing 0.9% on Aug 4 to 24,733, driven by resilient mainland inflows and investor hopes for progress in trade negotiations. Gains continued through midweek, with the HSI briefly surpassing the 25,000-mark, its highest level in over a month, after Chinese trade figures showed exports and imports holding up better than expected, easing fears of a deeper slowdown in global demand. However, sentiment shifted on Aug 8 as the August 12 deadline approached for extending the US-China trade truce. Technology counters bore the brunt of the sell-off, with Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corp (SMIC) sliding almost 8% on profit-taking and valuation concerns. Consumer and tourism-related stocks also came under pressure, with Mixue Group, Trip.com, and Sands China posting notable losses. For the week, financial and property shares provided some cushion, supported by a softer Hong Kong dollar and expectations that the US Federal Reserve would maintain its current rate stance in the near term. Still, analysts cautioned that the HSI’s trajectory remains vulnerable to external headlines, especially trade developments and China’s upcoming inflation and industrial production data. Market watchers see 25,000 as a key resistance level; a sustained break above it could reinforce bullish momentum, while a fall below 24,200 may reignite selling pressure. title: US Inflation Data To Test Stock Market Rally Amid Pullback Risks
body: US equities face a key test this week as fresh inflation data threatens to interrupt a powerful rally that has pushed benchmarks to record highs. The S&P 500 is up more than 8% this year and nearing all-time highs, while the Nasdaq Composite closed at a record on Aug 8. Reuters reported that strategists at Deutsche Bank and Morgan Stanley warn that stocks may be due for a pullback after a four-month surge that has lifted the S&P 500 by 28% since April, driving valuations to over 22 times forward earnings, well above the long-term average of 15.8. The rally has persisted despite mounting risks from new tariffs and a historically weak seasonal period, with August and September averaging negative returns over the past 35 years. The July Consumer Price Index report on Aug 12, expected to show a 2.8% annual rise, could spark volatility. A stronger-than-expected reading may temper expectations for imminent Federal Reserve (Fed) rate cuts, which markets currently see as highly likely following weak jobs data. The tariff backdrop adds another layer of uncertainty. The US has just enacted its steepest average import duties in a century, with new levies targeting semiconductor chips and pharmaceuticals. China could face further tariff hikes on Aug 12 unless President Donald Trump extends an existing truce. Investors say any surprise uptick in inflation could force the Fed to hold off on easing, a move that could test the resilience of the market’s record-breaking run. title: Market Review: KOSPI Gains 2.9% For The Week Despite Tax Hike Jitters
body: South Korea’s benchmark KOSPI index ended higher for the week, rising 2.9% despite midweek volatility sparked by an unexpected tax hike. Gains in technology and financial shares offset profit-taking in defence and heavy industries. The KOSPI closed its trading week on Aug 8 at 3,210.01, down 17.67 points, or 0.55%, as investors locked in gains from earlier in the week. Still, the index recorded its strongest weekly advance in over a month, buoyed by resilient demand for technology and financial stocks. Trading opened on a firm note on Aug 4, with the index climbing 0.91% to 3,147.75 on bargain hunting and optimism over potential US interest rate cuts. Sentiment, however, turned midweek after the government announced increases to corporate income and securities transaction taxes, triggering the steepest one-day drop since April. Foreign investor appetite remained intact, with net inflows of US$4.52 billion in July, the highest in nearly 18 months. Sector-wise, technology stocks led the rally on expectations of sustained demand in artificial intelligence and semiconductors, while financial and industrial counters also contributed to gains. Trading volumes, meanwhile, remained moderate, with institutional and foreign investors adjusting positions in response to policy developments. Analysts cautioned that while the KOSPI’s recovery momentum is intact, market direction in the coming weeks will depend on clearer corporate reform measures and the government’s stance on the new tax plan. Market sentiment was dampened by soft regional cues, with traders hesitant to take on risk ahead of key global data releases. In corporate news, the Singapore Exchange (SGX) posted its strongest annual results since listing, with adjusted net profit surging 15.9% to S$609.5 million for the year ended June 30. Revenue rose 11.7% to S$1.30 billion, driven by higher trading activity and listings. SGX declared a quarterly dividend of 10.5 Singapore cents per share, up from 8.5 cents previously, and signalled modest annual increases through the 2028 financial year. The bourse operator also highlighted its most promising IPO pipeline in years, underscoring optimism for future growth. Despite the exchange’s robust earnings, broader market gains remained capped. Analysts noted that while SGX’s results point to long-term resilience, near-term volatility is likely to persist given external headwinds. title: Nasdaq Hits Another Record As Tech Surge Lifts Wall Street
body: US stocks ended higher on Aug 8, with the Nasdaq Composite closing at a record high for the second straight day as technology shares rallied and optimism grew over potential interest rate cuts, Reuters reported. The Nasdaq climbed 207.32 points, or 0.98%, to 21,450.02 — its 18th record close of the year — while the S&P 500 rose 49.45 points, or 0.78%, to 6,389.45, just shy of its own record. The Dow Jones Industrial Average added 206.97 points, or 0.47%, to 44,175.61. All three major indexes posted solid weekly gains: S&P 500 up 2.4%, Dow up 1.3%, and Nasdaq up 3.9%. Apple Inc shares jumped 4.2% on Aug 8 and 13.3% for the week, marking their best weekly performance since 2020. The rally followed President Donald Trump’s announcement that Apple will invest an additional US$100 billion in the US, bringing its total planned commitment to US$600 billion over four years. The S&P 500’s technology and communication services sectors led the advancement on Aug 8, both ending at record highs. Gilead Sciences surged 8.3% after raising its full-year outlook, while Expedia gained 4.1% on upgraded revenue and bookings guidance. Weaker US economic data has bolstered bets on Federal Reserve (Fed) rate cuts. According to CME’s FedWatch Tool, traders see an 89.4% chance of at least a 25-basis-point cut in September, up from 80.3% a week ago, with two cuts expected by year-end. Investor focus also turned to Trump’s nomination of Council of Economic Advisors Chair Stephen Miran to a short-term Fed board seat after Adriana Kugler’s abrupt departure. Looking ahead, markets face a key test with Aug 12’s Consumer Price Index report, while geopolitical tensions persist after India shelved planned US arms and aircraft purchases in response to higher tariffs. title: Weaker US Jobs Data Boosts Ringgit To RM4.22
body: The ringgit opened stronger against the US dollar on Friday, buoyed by rising expectations of a rate cut at the US Federal Reserve’s upcoming policy meeting, following weaker-than-expected economic data. At 8 am, the local note appreciated to 4.2205/2405 against the greenback compared to Thursday’s close of 4.2340/2385. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US Dollar Index dipped 0.09% to 98,084 points as expectations of a rate cut in September gain traction. “Expect the ringgit against the US dollar to hover around RM4.22 to RM4.23 today,” he added. He noted that initial US jobless claims rose to 226,000 last week, exceeding market forecasts of 221,000. This marked a second straight weekly increase, suggesting signs of weakness in the labour market, although the Federal Open Market Committee still requires more data before its September meeting. On the domestic front, he said the ringgit could find support after facing some selling pressure during the previous afternoon session. The local unit also strengthened against most regional peers in early trade. It appreciated against the Singapore dollar to 3.2906/3064 from 3.2973/3013, firmed versus the Thai baht to 13.0653/1346 from 13.0954/1146, and rose against the Philippine peso to 7.39/7.44 from 7.42/7.44. The ringgit also gained on the Indonesian rupiah to 259.1/260.4 from 259.9/260.3. However, it was mostly lower against major currencies. It eased against the Japanese yen to 2.8750/8888 from 2.8732/8765 and fell against the British pound to 5.6770/7039 from 5.6596/6656. It did, however, strengthen against the euro to 4.9283/9516 from 4.9411/9463. title: Stock Today: SD Guthrie Rises As Net Profit Hits RM1 Billion
body: SD Guthrie Bhd’s shares continued their upward climb today, trading at RM4.83 as at 2.30 pm, up 1.26% from the previous close. The stock opened at RM4.77 and touched a high of RM4.86, buoyed by strong earnings momentum and investor confidence. This comes just a day after the plantation giant reported a record-breaking net profit of RM1.07 billion for the first half ended 30 June 2025, marking a 71% year-on-year surge from RM626 million a year earlier. For the second quarter alone, net profit rose 22% to RM505 million. The bullish performance was largely driven by the Group’s Upstream segment, which saw a twofold increase in profits. SD Guthrie benefitted from higher crude palm oil (CPO) and palm kernel (PK) prices, which rose by 3% and 50% year-on-year, respectively, to RM4,146 and RM3,247 per metric tonne. Fresh fruit bunch (FFB) production also grew 4%, with all segments contributing to the increase. Despite a weaker showing from its Downstream arm, SD Guthrie International (SDGI) — which recorded a 44% decline in profit before interest and tax (PBIT) to RM126 million in 2Q FY2025 — the Group’s strong upstream fundamentals helped sustain overall performance. SDGI continued to face lower demand and tighter margins in Asia Pacific and Europe, though it reported higher margins and volumes in Oceania. With trading volume at 1.44 million shares and strong investor sentiment following its earnings report, SD Guthrie appears poised for continued momentum heading into the second half of the year. title: Stock Today: Pentamaster Slides Despite Analyst Optimism Amid Tech Sector Rebound
body: Shares in Pentamaster Corp Bhd fell 3.66% to RM3.69 in late afternoon trade on Thursday, even as analysts maintained a bullish outlook on the stock due to signs of recovery in the automated test equipment (ATE) segment. As at 3.45 pm, the stock was down 14 sen, with 1.42 million shares traded. It opened at RM3.79 and traded between a low of RM3.67 and a high of RM3.82 during the session. The stock was quoted at RM3.69 on the buy side and RM3.70 on the sell side, with heavier selling interest noted. The weakness in share price came a day after RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) reaffirmed its BUY call on Pentamaster, raising its target price to RM4.25 from RM3.72. The investment bank cited stronger earnings visibility for the second half of 2025, driven by a recovery in the ATE segment and improving demand from semiconductor clients. Pentamaster’s first-half core net profit stood at RM30.4 million, down 30.4% year-on-year, on revenue of RM276.5 million. While revenue was impacted by delays in medical-related factory automation projects, the ATE segment saw a 25.2% year-on-year growth, fuelled by demand from the electro-optical and semiconductor sectors. RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) also highlighted the company’s long-term growth potential in high-value testing equipment for AI and silicon photonics applications, with contributions expected to ramp up from FY2026 onward. The group is also exploring diversification into renewable energy, healthcare automation and data centres. Despite Thursday’s pullback, Pentamaster shares remain up from their early-year levels, as investors monitor orderbook developments and regional tech sector momentum. title: Nasdaq Hits Record High As Trump Tariffs Rattle Markets, Apple And Nvidia Gain
body: US stocks ended Thursday on a mixed note as fresh tariffs introduced by President Donald Trump took effect, casting a shadow over market sentiment even as technology shares rallied. The Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC) climbed nearly 0.4% to a new all-time high, buoyed by optimism in the tech sector, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI) slipped 0.5% and the S&P 500 (^GSPC) ended virtually unchanged. The losses came despite Trump’s nomination of Stephen Miran, current chairman of the Council of Economic Advisors, to the Federal Reserve Board of Governors. Miran, if confirmed, will serve until 31 January 2026, following Adriana Kugler’s resignation. Sentiment in the tech sector was lifted further by remarks from Trump suggesting some exemptions in his proposed 100% semiconductor tariffs. Nvidia (NVDA) gained 0.7% on the day, contributing to the Nasdaq’s strong performance. Apple (AAPL) shares also rose after Trump and Apple CEO Tim Cook announced a landmark US$100 billion investment in the United States. Under the plan, Apple will produce iPhone and Apple Watch cover glasses in Kentucky, a move seen as strengthening domestic manufacturing. The tariffs, which took effect at 12:01 a.m. ET on Thursday, affecting imports from nearly 200 countries. The average effective tariff rate is projected to jump to 18.6%, the highest since 1933, according to the Yale Budget Lab. Duties now range from 10% to 50%. Toyota (TM) has flagged a US$9.5 billion impact from the tariffs in its latest earnings report, reinforcing concerns among global automakers. Meanwhile, Eli Lilly’s (LLY) stock plunged 14% despite reporting better-than-expected earnings. The drop came after lacklustre trial results for its much-anticipated oral GLP-1 pill. Elsewhere, unemployment claims continue to rise, with 1.974 million continuing claims filed, the highest since November 2021. This comes on the heels of a disappointing July jobs report and downward revisions for May and June, placing the labour market under renewed scrutiny. title: Gold Prices Climb Amid Strong Momentum, Analysts See Further Upside
body: Gold prices in Malaysia continued to edge higher, with the local benchmark rising 0.41% to RM462,990.32 per kg as at 03.16 NY time, up RM1,871.46 from the previous session. On a daily basis, gold gained RM61.52 or 0.43%, while its 1-year performance showed a surge of 32.28%, and a five-year gain of 68.34%, underscoring the metal’s haven appeal amid global uncertainties. RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) maintained its bullish stance on COMEX gold, recommending traders to hold on to their long positions after prices rallied by US$20 overnight to close at US$3,425.20. The precious metal had earlier opened at US$3,403.90 and climbed to an intraday high of US$3,455 before easing slightly by the close. With the Relative Strength Index (RSI) trending upwards, RHB noted that bullish momentum remains intact, and a breakout above the US$3,450 resistance is likely, potentially setting gold on course for the US$3,500 level. It added that in a strong bullish setup, resistance levels may prove fragile, supported by an uptrend in the 20- and 50-day simple moving averages. The firm advised traders to maintain long positions initiated at US$3,402.40, with the stop-loss pegged at US$3,150. Immediate support is revised to US$3,350, followed by a lower support level at US$3,250. If bullish momentum continues, resistance could extend to US$3,600 in the near term. title: Bursa Malaysia Edges Higher At Midday On Bargain Hunting, Strong Trade Data

title: Stock Today: Pentamaster Powers Up Despite Profit Slump, Jumps 4.6% On Recovery Hopes
body: Pentamaster Corp Bhd surged 4.57% to close at RM3.89 today, rebounding sharply despite a steep 40% drop in second-quarter net profit, as investors rallied behind signs of a potential recovery in the second half of the year. The Penang-based automation solutions provider recorded a gain of 17 sen during the session, trading between a low of RM3.57 and a high of RM3.94. Volume was strong, with 3.92 million shares exchanging hands, reflecting renewed optimism from the market. Pentamaster’s latest financial report, released on Aug 6, revealed a 2Q2025 profit after tax of RM11 million, down from RM19 million a year earlier amid macroeconomic headwinds, margin pressure and delayed customer projects caused by global trade tensions and supply chain disruptions. First-half profit before tax stood at RM38.2 million, a sharp decline from RM62.9 million in 1H2024. Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) also slipped 28.9% to RM52 million, while basic earnings per share fell to 3.47 sen from 5.52 sen. Still, the company expressed cautious optimism for the coming months, citing improved order visibility in its automated test equipment (ATE) segment. The group sees stronger demand from the logic and power semiconductor sub-segments, alongside continued expansion efforts by its factory automation solutions (FAS) unit. Today’s rally on Bursa Malaysia suggests investors are willing to look past short-term pains, betting on Pentamaster’s ability to capitalise on recovering capital expenditure cycles in the semiconductor space. title: Stock Today: Inari Amertron Rises Amid Acquisition Optimism
body: Inari Amertron Bhd saw its share price climb 2.15% to RM1.90 as of noon, with a total volume of 17 million shares traded. The stock opened at RM1.87, reaching a high of RM1.94 and a low of RM1.85 during the session. The best bid stood at RM1.89, matched by a selling offer at RM1.90. Investor interest has been partly fuelled by Inari’s recent strategic move to expand its optoelectronic business through a joint acquisition of Lumileds International, announced earlier this month. The deal involves a total enterprise value of US$239 million (RM1.03 billion), with a further US$41 million (RM176.3 million) to be injected for working capital, bringing the total investment to US$280 million (RM1.2 billion). Inari’s share of the funding is approximately RM307 million, largely sourced from previous private placement proceeds. Completion is expected by the first quarter of 2026. Analysts at MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB Research) maintained their neutral stance on Inari with an unchanged target price of RM2.13. They acknowledged the acquisition could strengthen Inari’s manufacturing capabilities and broaden its customer base internationally but expressed caution over the uncertain timeline for Lumileds’ turnaround, which remains loss-making. Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB Research) also reaffirmed its hold recommendation with a target price of RM2.10. HLIB highlighted the potential product and customer diversification the acquisition offers, reinforcing Inari’s OSAT (outsourced semiconductor assembly and test) business strategy. However, concerns linger due to Lumileds’ losses of US$67 million in FY24 and US$17 million in the first quarter of FY25. The partnership with Sanan Optoelectronics, China’s largest LED chipmaker and co-acquirer, is expected to mitigate some competitive pressures from industry leaders such as Nichia and Osram. Both research houses noted that near-term catalysts are limited, with flat radio frequency (RF) segment growth and the impending expiry of a key supply agreement in mid-2026. Nonetheless, they remain constructive on Inari’s longer-term outlook, citing recovery potential in optoelectronics and prospective gains in the upcoming product cycle. As of the latest trading session, Inari’s share price performance reflects cautious optimism amid its strategic acquisition, balancing growth prospects against ongoing market uncertainties. title: Ringgit Firms Against US Dollar, Mixed Against Others
body: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar on Thursday, supported by a softer greenback as expectations of interest rate cuts by the United States Federal Reserve (Fed) strengthened. At 8 am, the local currency traded at 4.2185/2260 versus the greenback, compared with Wednesday’s close of 4.2235/2305. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said recent remarks from Fed officials indicated possible policy adjustments to address labour market weaknesses, boosting market confidence in a potential rate reduction at the next Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting. The meeting, scheduled for September 16–17, is expected to deliver a 25-basis-point cut in the Fed Funds Rate, he noted. “This would likely be ringgit-positive, as a Fed rate cut would narrow the interest rate differential with the Overnight Policy Rate (OPR). In light of current market conditions, the ringgit is expected to trade between 4.21 and 4.22 against the US dollar today,” he told Bernama. Against a basket of major and regional currencies, the ringgit was mostly weaker in early trade. It slipped to 2.8654/8707 against the Japanese yen from 2.8570/8619, fell to 5.6342/6442 versus the British pound from 5.6160/6253, and declined to 4.9192/9279 against the euro from 4.8929/9010. The local note also eased against the Singapore dollar to 3.2824/2885 from 3.2806/2863, and depreciated against the Thai baht to 13.0402/0715 from 13.0291/0567. Conversely, it strengthened versus the Philippine peso to 7.33/7.35 from 7.34/7.36 and firmed against the Indonesian rupiah at 257.8/258.4 from 258.1/258.6. title: Asian Shares Rally On Fed Easing Hopes, Dollar Slips
body: Asian equities climbed on Thursday, with Japanese stocks reaching record highs, driven by tech gains on Wall Street, stronger corporate earnings, and rising expectations for U.S. interest rate cuts. Japan’s broad Topix index rose 0.9 per cent to an all-time peak, while the tech-focused Nikkei advanced by a similar margin. Taiwan’s benchmark surged 2.3 per cent to a more-than-one-year high, and South Korea’s KOSPI gained 0.6 per cent. Hong Kong’s Hang Seng increased 0.4 per cent, and mainland Chinese blue chips edged up 0.3 per cent. Australian shares slipped slightly after hitting a record high the previous day. The improved mood on Wall Street also buoyed U.S. stock futures, with contracts for the S&P 500 and Nasdaq both rising 0.3 per cent. On Wednesday, the S&P 500 climbed 0.7 per cent, while the Nasdaq Composite jumped 1.2 per cent. Capital.com analyst Kyle Rodda noted, “Wall Street seems to have gotten its mojo back,” but warned that downside risks persist, including increasing surprises in official data, stretched valuations with forward price-to-earnings ratios near four-year highs, and ongoing trade uncertainties. The dollar weakened against major currencies amid growing bets on Federal Reserve easing, fuelled by softer macroeconomic data and President Donald Trump’s recent appointments to the Fed board, expected to align with his dovish monetary stance. The dollar index, which measures the currency against a basket including the euro and sterling, rose slightly to 98.245 after a 0.6 per cent drop on Wednesday. The euro held steady at $1.1657 following a 0.7 per cent jump the previous session, while sterling remained firm at $1.3356 ahead of the Bank of England’s policy announcement later Thursday. The BoE is widely expected to cut interest rates by a quarter point for the fifth time in 12 months, although policymakers are divided, with some members pushing for a half-point cut and others favouring no change due to inflation concerns. The dollar rose 0.1 per cent against the yen to 147.53. Gold prices gained 0.4 per cent to about $1,382 per ounce, supported by the softer dollar. Oil prices recovered some losses after a dip on Wednesday, when Brent and West Texas Intermediate crude each fell about 1 per cent. Brent crude futures increased 20 cents, or 0.3 per cent, to $67.09 a barrel, while WTI crude added 22 cents, or 0.3 per cent, to $64.57 a barrel. Meanwhile, the prospect of a U.S. President Trump meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin to discuss the Ukraine conflict also supported market sentiment and strengthened the euro, while weighing on oil prices as traders assessed the implications for sanctions on Moscow. title: Stock Today: Tenaga Nasional Eases As Policy Changes Loom, Analysts See Limited Impact
body: Shares of Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) traded lower this afternoon, falling 14 sen or 1.05% to RM13.14 at 3.35 pm, amid investor caution surrounding upcoming energy policy shifts. Trading volume stood at 29.52 million shares, with the stock opening at RM13.28 and moving between RM13.08 and RM13.30. The dip coincides with the government’s review of the Net Energy Metering (NEM) programme and the impending launch of a replacement scheme. While some traders expect minimal disruption to TNB’s core business, analysts maintain a relatively neutral view on the impact. The tariff framework introduced in July introduces sharper billing components, including capacity and network charges, which critics say may reduce returns for NEM solar users, particularly commercial and residential adopters. However, brokerage notes indicate that TNB is unlikely to face meaningful operational or financial strain. A recent sector analysis by TA Securities highlighted the expansion of NEM quotas—residential (NEM Rakyat) increased by 150 MW to 600 MW, and commercial/industrial (NEM NOVA) expanded by 300 MW to 1,700 MW, strengthening overall momentum for rooftop solar adoption, with industrial players poised to benefit. Separately, RP4 tariff revisions effective July 1 are expected to improve TNB’s regulated asset base and strengthen its cash flow outlook. HLIB Research and CIMB Securities view the new pricing framework as largely neutral under the incentive-based regulation model, which ensures TNB recovers its regulatory-allowed return. Nevertheless, ongoing uncertainties remain. In early July, TNB shares fell sharply after a Federal Court ruling in favour of the Inland Revenue Board in a long-running tax dispute, resulting in increased provision risk. Brokers, including Maybank maintain a “Buy” call on TNB, citing strong dividend prospects and robust operational footing despite the overhang. title: Stock Today: Hartalega Falls 5.3% Amid Weak Q1 Earnings And Uncertain Outlook
body: Hartalega Holdings Bhd saw its shares decline 5.3% to RM1.25 at midday, down seven sen from yesterday’s close, as sentiment weakened following the company’s disappointing first-quarter results and cautious industry outlook. As of 11.52 am, the counter recorded a trading volume of 173.7 million shares, making it one of the most actively traded on Bursa Malaysia. The stock opened at RM1.28 and touched an intraday high of RM1.28 before slipping to a low of RM1.23. The last done price of RM1.25 marks a sharp drop from its last close at RM1.32. The selling pressure follows Hartalega’s announcement that its profit after tax for the quarter ended June 30 fell 60% year-on-year to RM12 million, while revenue declined 5% to RM553 million. The group attributed the weaker performance to lower average selling prices (ASP), reduced sales volume across key markets and intensified competition, particularly from Chinese manufacturers. Analysts also flagged a challenging near-term outlook. Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB) Research noted that industry rebalancing could be delayed until 2029, citing oversupply and pricing pressures. The research house maintained its “Hold” call on Hartalega, cutting its target price to RM1.32 from RM1.48. Hartalega aims to mitigate these challenges through an RM200–300 million investment plan over the next 9–15 months, focusing on automation and energy efficiency. The company is also banking on an anticipated recovery in orders from US customers starting this month. Despite receiving an additional RM101 million tax bill from the Inland Revenue Board, Hartalega said it maintains a strong financial position, supported by a net cash balance of RM986 million as of 1QFY26. title: Ringgit Opens Higher At 4.2180 Against US Dollar On Weak US Data
body: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar today, supported by weaker United States economic data that dragged the greenback lower and shifted investor sentiment. At 8 am, the local note rose to 4.2180/2315 versus the greenback compared to Tuesday’s close of 4.2260/2310. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the softer-than-expected US ISM Services Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) reinforced expectations of a possible Federal Reserve rate cut in September. “Weaker US economic data, including last Friday’s non-farm payrolls, has shifted the narrative. The likelihood of rate cuts is rising as policymakers seek to support growth,” he told Bernama. title: Stock Today: Inari Inchs Up Amid Neutral Analyst Outlook, Lumileds Acquisition In Focus
body: Inari Amertron Bhd traded marginally higher at mid-afternoon today, rising 0.50% or one sen to RM2.00 as of 2.35 pm, with 11.3 million shares changing hands. The counter opened at RM2.02 and moved between RM1.99 and RM2.02. The uptick comes a day after MBSB Investment Bank Bhd and Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) reaffirmed their cautious stance on the semiconductor packaging and testing company, maintaining NEUTRAL and HOLD calls respectively. Both research houses kept target prices unchanged at RM2.13 (MBSB) and RM2.10 (HLIB). The outlook follows Inari’s joint acquisition of Lumileds International with Sanan Optoelectronics for an enterprise value of US$239 million (RM1.03 billion), to be completed by the first quarter of 2026. The deal, which includes an additional US$41 million (RM176.3 million) for working capital, brings the total outlay to US$280 million (RM1.2 billion). Inari’s commitment amounts to RM307 million, funded mainly from its previous private placement proceeds. Analysts view the acquisition as a strategic move to diversify products and customers in the optoelectronic segment, although concerns linger over Lumileds’ loss-making status, with US$67 million in FY24 and US$17 million in 1QFY25. HLIB noted that collaboration with Sanan, China’s largest LED chipmaker, could strengthen Inari’s competitiveness against global players such as Nichia and Osram. Both houses flagged limited near-term catalysts, citing flat RF growth and the expiry of a key supply agreement in mid-2026, although longer-term prospects remain positive on potential recovery in optoelectronics and upcoming product cycles. title: SGX Opens Higher As Fed Rate-Cut Expectations Lift Investor Sentiment
body: The Straits Times Index (STI) kicked off the day strongly, advancing 13.17 points or 0.31% to 4,210.40 as risk appetite improved amid speculation of an imminent US interest rate cut. Market breadth favoured gainers, with 121 stocks rising against 50 decliners. Turnover remained moderate, with 117.92 million shares traded, valued at S$109.56 million. Global drivers buoyed trading in Singapore. Weaker-than-expected US non-farm payroll data in July and downward revisions for May and June added to expectations of a Federal Reserve rate cut in September. Futures now indicate a roughly 85% probability of easing, leading to a sharp drop in US Treasury yields and a decline in the dollar. These developments supported regional equities, especially energy-sensitive and export-focused markets. STI gains followed a broader Asia-Pacific rebound, where sentiment improved after major indices pulled back earlier in the week due to regional trade uncertainty. Domestically, analysts say sectors sensitive to interest rates—such as REITs, telecommunications and industrial stocks—stand to benefit if US rates decline. Singapore’s banks may face margin pressure but remain structurally resilient given strong balance sheets. Regional liquidity flows into Singapore equities have been strong in anticipation of rate cuts and relative tariff insulation while valuation levels remain attractive. The outlook remains cautiously optimistic: domestic-themed counters are expected to outperform, while export-reliant and highly rate-sensitive stocks may remain volatile amid ongoing global uncertainty. title: Ringgit Strengthens On Rate Cut Speculation

Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US dollar weakened as markets priced in the likelihood of a Federal Reserve policy easing following last week’s soft labour market data. “It appears that emerging market currencies against the US dollar are in a sweet spot, as the Federal Reserve seems poised to cut its policy rate, perhaps at an accelerated pace, to demonstrate to markets that it is on top of the situation. “The September Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting is likely to see a 25-basis-point rate cut,” he noted, adding the ringgit is expected to trade between RM4.22 and RM4.23 today. title: Asian Markets Track Wall Street On Fed Rate Cut Bet
body: Stock markets rose on Tuesday (Aug 5) as investors grow increasingly confident the Federal Reserve will cut interest rates next month, despite concerns about the United States economy and Donald Trump’s tariffs. The gains tracked a rally on Wall Street, where traders rediscovered their mojo following Friday’s sell-off that was fuelled by news that fewer-than-expected American jobs were created in July, while the previous two months’ figures were revised down sharply. The reading raised concerns that the world’s biggest economy was in worse shape than expected, though it also fanned bets the Fed will slash in September, with markets pricing the chance of a 25-basis-point reduction at about 95 per cent, according to Bloomberg. There is also talk that bank officials could go for twice as much as that.”The narrative flipped fast: soft jobs equals soft Fed, and soft Fed equals risk-on,” said Stephen Innes at SPI Asset Management. But he warned that “if cuts are coming because the labour market is slipping from ‘cooling’ to ‘cracking’, then we’re skating closer to the edge than we care to admit”. He added: “That dichotomy – between rate cuts as stimulus and rate cuts as warning flare – is now front and centre. “If the Fed moves proactively to shield markets from the tariff storm and weak labour, the equity rally has legs. But if policymakers are reacting to a sharper downturn that is in full swing, the runway shortens quickly.”In early trade, Tokyo, Hong Kong, Shanghai, Sydney, Seoul, Singapore, Taipei, Manila and Jakarta were all in the green. However, while there is a broad expectation that the Fed will cut rates, Lazard chief market strategist Ronald Temple remained sceptical. “I continue to believe the Fed will not reduce rates at all this year, given rising inflation caused by tariffs and a relatively stable unemployment rate,” he wrote. “I would align with the majority of the FOMC members who believe it is more appropriate to hold policy constant until there is greater clarity in terms of the effects of tariffs and stricter immigration enforcement on inflation and employment.” Traders were keeping an eye on trade talks between Washington and dozens of its trade partners after Trump imposed tariffs of between 10 and 41 per cent on them. Among those to strike a deal is India, which Trump on Monday threatened to hit with “substantially” higher rates over its purchases of Russian oil. body: Tokyo stocks extended losses on Monday as the market followed the declines on Wall Street, where concerns over a weakening U.S. economy had triggered a sell-off following softer-than-expected employment data. The benchmark Nikkei stock index, the 225-issue Nikkei Stock Average, closed at 40,290.70, down 508.90 points or 1.25 percent, from the previous trading day. Selling pressure was broad-based, with semiconductor stocks, such as Advantest, leading the declines. Financial stocks, including banks and insurers, also dropped significantly as domestic long-term interest rates fell. Additionally, a stronger yen against the U.S. dollar weighed on export-oriented stocks. At one point, the Nikkei fell more than 900 points, briefly dipping below the psychologically important 40,000 mark. title: Bursa Slips Amid US Tariff Jitters And Weak Global Cues
body: Bursa Malaysia’s benchmark index, the FBM KLCI, slid modestly by 5.3 points (‑0.35%) to 1,528.05 at midday as broader concerns over trade policy uncertainties weighed on investor sentiment. The broader indices also showed weakness with the FBM70 down 0.47%, FBM EMAS easing 0.37% and FBM Small Cap retreating 0.25%. Market breadth was adverse at midday with decliners outperforming gainers and the most active stocks included INARI, which fell 7.1 sen to RM1.99 on elevated volume and MAGMA, down 3.5 sen to RM0.38 among the heavy turnover names. Nestlé, Allianz, UTD Plantations, SHL and Petronas Gas led the index gainers while HEIM, MPI, Hong Leong Bank and Petronas Dagang were among the largest decliners. The dip reflects spillover fears following aggressive new US tariffs and a tepid US jobs report that triggered sharp declines in global equities. US markets fell sharply as President Trump’s sweeping tariffs ranging from 10% to 41% took effect on various trading partners, while a weak non-farm payroll report dampened confidence in economic resilience. Malaysia welcomed this 90-day tariff pause between the US and China, viewing it as a window to diversify supply chains and attract foreign companies seeking alternatives to the US-China corridor. Economists see an opportunity for Malaysia to strengthen its position as a regional manufacturing hub, especially in semiconductors, electronics and digital infrastructure. Adding momentum, China Galaxy Securities and CICC recently announced plans to launch over US$1 billion in investment funds targeting Southeast Asia, including Malaysia’s tech, healthcare and advanced manufacturing sectors, underscoring increasing regional capital flows. Analysts have maintained a cautiously optimistic long-term view on Bursa, citing Malaysia’s robust foreign direct investment inflows, favourable macro policy frameworks and domestic corporate earnings growth. Some brokerage forecasts peg the FBM KLCI year-end 2025 target around 1,750 points despite near-term volatility. Looking ahead, market leaders across technology, energy and consumer sectors may offer selective buying opportunities as investors recalibrate risk. Meanwhile, local regulators and MITI are expected to continue outreach efforts to support SMEs and export-dependent industries faced with evolving global tariff regimes. body: Bursa Malaysia opened in negative territory this morning, with the benchmark FBM KLCI slipping 0.57% to 1,524.57 at 9:17 am, amid caution over global trade tensions and weaker regional cues. Wider indexes also declined, with FBM70 down 0.99%, FBM EMAS off 0.67%, and the FBM Shariah Index falling 0.72%. Market breadth tilted bearish, with 74 advancing stocks versus 121 decliners, while trading volumes remained moderate at 114.47 million shares valued at S$190.41 million. Local benchmarks appear pressured following overnight declines on Wall Street driven by weak US economic data and renewed expectations of a Federal Reserve rate cut. Meanwhile, regional markets remained subdued, with heightened volatility amid uncertainty around trade policies. Domestic sentiment has also been influenced by Malaysia’s latest trade developments. On August 1, the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry (MITI) confirmed that US tariffs on Malaysian exports were reduced from 25% to 19%, emphasising efforts to engage the US diplomatically and mitigate risks using the New Industrial Master Plan and export diversification strategies. While tariff relief offers some relief, caution persists amid ongoing trade friction. Sectorally, financial stocks weighed on the market. DBS Group eased to S$47.38, while OCBC, UOB, Singapore Airlines, and ComfortDelGro all posted lower or flat starts. Beyond immediate macro concerns, investor attention is shifting to MMC Port Holdings, which is preparing for an October IPO expected to raise over US$1.5 billion, potentially lifting confidence in Malaysia’s capital markets and infrastructure sector. title: Asian Stocks Set To Slide As US Jobs Slump Spurs Fed Cut Bets
body: Asian equities are expected to open lower on Monday after weak US employment data triggered a sell-off on Wall Street and strengthened speculation of a Federal Reserve interest rate cut in September, pushing US Treasury yields sharply lower. Futures for equity indices in Japan, Australia and Hong Kong all pointed to early losses, with Tokyo contracts down more than 2%, indicating that Friday’s risk-off sentiment is spilling into Asian markets. On Wall Street, the S&P 500 ended Friday 1.6% lower, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 dropped 2%, marking the steepest single-day decline in months for both benchmarks. US index futures were little changed in early Asian trading. Oil prices retreated 0.6% after OPEC+ confirmed another significant production increase in September, completing the unwinding of earlier supply cuts. Meanwhile, the US dollar traded mixed against its Group-of-10 peers following a 0.9% slide on Friday, as Treasury yields plunged. The US labour market slowed markedly over the past three months, with May and June payroll figures revised down by almost 260,000 jobs. July data showed an average monthly gain of just 35,000 jobs, the weakest pace since the pandemic. The 10-year US Treasury yield dropped 16 basis points on Friday, while two-year yields fell 28 basis points, reflecting heightened expectations that the Fed will ease policy at its September meeting. Some analysts even anticipate a 50-basis point cut, double the usual move. “September is a lock for a rate cut and it might even be a 50-basis point move to make up the lost time,” said Jamie Cox, managing partner at Harris Financial Group. Elsewhere in Asia, Thai Prime Minister Paetongtarn Shinawatra faces a Constitutional Court deadline today to submit a defence in an ethics case. In the UK, the Bank of England is expected to deliver a rate cut later on Monday. In Brazil, President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva signalled willingness to engage in trade talks with Donald Trump, provided Brazil is treated as an equal. Meanwhile, Trump’s recent comments on India and a proposed 25% tariff rate have rattled markets, with the US president also warning of additional 40% tariffs on goods deemed to be “transshipped” through other countries. Gold held steady after rising on Friday, as Trump announced the deployment of two US nuclear submarines in response to remarks by former Russian President Dmitry Medvedev. The US president further inflamed tensions by calling for the dismissal of Bureau of Labor Statistics Commissioner Erika McEntarfer following the jobs report, and demanded the Federal Reserve Board assume control of monetary policy if Chair Jerome Powell fails to cut rates. title: Weekly Review: Hang Seng Suffers Steepest Weekly Drop On Tariff Fears, Weak US Data
body: Hong Kong stocks tumbled for the week ended August 1, with the benchmark Hang Seng Index (HSI) posting a sharp 3.47% decline to close at 24,507.81, as renewed US trade tariffs and soft US labour data rattled investor sentiment. The sell-off marked the HSI’s steepest weekly drop in over three months and capped a volatile July marked by geopolitical uncertainty and macroeconomic headwinds. The index shed 1.07% on Aug 1 alone, touching a two-week low, as global investors digested the sweeping tariffs announced by Washington. On July 31, the US administration unveiled a broad-based tariff package on imports from China, Taiwan, India and other Asian economies. The move triggered widespread risk aversion across Asian markets, with export-heavy and tech-linked stocks bearing the brunt of the selloff. Adding to the gloom, US non-farm payrolls data released on Aug 1 came in below expectations, dampening hopes of a September interest rate cut by the Federal Reserve. The double hit of trade friction and weak labour data sent shockwaves through global equities. In Hong Kong, sentiment was particularly fragile. The Hang Seng China Enterprises Index and the Hang Seng Tech Index each slipped around 1% on the day. Major laggards included vaping giant Smoore International, which plunged 7.8%, and luxury fashion house Prada, which fell 4.8%. Market analysts said the sharp weekly drop underscored rising investor unease about both external trade pressures and domestic economic fragility. China’s latest PMI data pointed to a contraction in manufacturing activity, with the July reading slipping to 49.5 — below the expansionary threshold. Looking ahead, market participants will be closely monitoring the next round of US-China trade developments and any potential policy support from Beijing to counteract the slowdown. title: Weekly Recap: KOSPI Slides Nearly 4% As US Tariffs, Rate Jitters Rattle Investors
body: South Korea’s KOSPI index plunged 3.88% for the week ended Aug 1, closing at 3,119.41, its steepest weekly loss since April. Rising trade tensions and weak US job data triggered a broad sell-off in Korean equities, with tech and export-heavy counters leading the decline. Market sentiment soured after the US slapped fresh tariffs on a group of Asian economies, including a 15% duty on South Korean goods, raising fears of renewed pressure on the country’s key export sectors. At the same time, disappointing US employment figures tempered hopes for near-term interest rate cuts by the Federal Reserve, putting further pressure on risk assets globally. South Korea’s high-beta market reacted sharply, with major names like Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix sliding over the week. Domestic sentiment was also dented by debate over proposed tax changes that could affect capital gains, prompting retail outflows. Despite a strong rebound in recent months, the KOSPI had risen over 35% since April — the latest external shocks have halted the rally. Analysts now expect the index to enter a period of consolidation as investors weigh trade negotiations and potential policy support from the Korean government. title: SGX Recap: STI Gains 1.7% Amid Policy Boost, Global Tailwinds
body: The Singapore stock market ended the week on a firmer note, with the Straits Times Index (STI) climbing 1.7% to close at around 4,154, underpinned by positive policy developments and improved global sentiment. The weekly advance marked a strong rebound from April lows, although a mild pullback on Aug 1 capped gains after a 14-day winning streak. Investor confidence was buoyed early in the week by the Monetary Authority of Singapore’s (MAS) announcement of a S$1.1 billion allocation to the Equity Market Development Programme, aimed at supporting small-cap investments. The move helped lift sentiment across mid- and small-cap stocks and signalled deeper structural support for the local equity market. The rally, which had pushed the STI more than 250 points or 6.2% higher over the past two weeks, paused slightly toward the end of the week as traders took profits ahead of month-end. The STI slipped about 0.5% on Aug 1 but remained firmly in positive territory for the week. Global tailwinds also helped drive gains, with encouraging US economic data and easing trade tensions attracting capital inflows into defensive markets like Singapore. Analysts noted that the city-state’s high dividend-yielding blue chips continue to appeal to investors seeking stability amid global uncertainties. Among the week’s top performers, DFI Retail Group surged 13% on upbeat earnings and dividend expectations. Property developer City Developments Ltd rose around 8%, while ST Engineering gained 7% on improving order book prospects. Meanwhile, real estate investment trusts (REITs) lagged, with Keppel DC REIT and Mapletree Logistics Trust posting declines as rental pressures and occupancy challenges weighed on distribution payouts. Despite the slight pullback on Aug 1, analysts remain optimistic about the STI’s near-term outlook, projecting a consolidation phase in the 4,200-4,260 range. Focus is expected to shift to upcoming US inflation data and earnings releases from local blue-chip firms. With MAS-led reforms underway and investor appetite for defensive plays intact, the Singapore market continues to be viewed as a relative safe haven in the region. title: Wall Street Sinks As Tariffs, Weak Jobs Data Rattle Investors
body: US stocks tumbled on Aug 1, with the S&P 500 plunging 1.6% in its worst single-day performance since May, as a combination of fresh tariffs, disappointing jobs data and underwhelming corporate earnings sparked a broad sell-off across Wall Street. Reuters reported that the Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 542.40 points (1.23%) to close at 43,588.58, the Nasdaq Composite sank 472.32 points (2.24%) to 20,650.13 and the S&P 500 dropped 101.38 points to 6,238.01. Markets were rattled after President Donald Trump signed an executive order imposing new tariffs on imports from key trading partners, including Canada, Brazil, India and Taiwan, escalating trade tensions just hours before the duties took effect. Sentiment was further dented by a weaker-than-expected July jobs report, which showed slowing job growth and downward revisions to June’s data, signs the labour market may be losing steam. The bleak report pushed the odds of a Federal Reserve (Fed) rate cut in September to 86.5%, up sharply from 37.7% a day earlier, according to CME’s FedWatch Tool. Amazon.com was the session’s biggest drag, plunging 8.3% after cloud unit AWS missed growth expectations. The selloff in Amazon dragged the consumer discretionary sector down 3.6%, making it the worst-performing group in the S&P 500. Apple fell 2.5%, despite offering upbeat revenue guidance, as CEO Tim Cook warned tariffs could cost the company $1.1 billion in the current quarter. For the week, the S&P 500 dropped 2.36%, the Dow fell 2.92% and the Nasdaq lost 2.17%. Declining stocks outnumbered advancers by more than two-to-one on both the NYSE and Nasdaq, with volume surging to 19.51 billion shares, above the 20-day average.
