title: Tariff Relief Could Retest KLCI Towards 1,550 Zone
body: Asian markets largely closed lower on Friday as investors adopted a cautious stance ahead of the highly anticipated US nonfarm payrolls data and a significant August 1st tariff deadline. Sentiment was further dampened by weaker-than-expected China Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) readings for July, which came in at 49.3 for manufacturing, highlighting persistent economic softness and the ongoing US-China trade tensions. Globally, trade developments remained a key focus. The United States finalised a tariff agreement with South Korea, imposing a 15% tariff on imports from Seoul as part of a “full and complete trade deal.” However, the US also implemented steeper duties on imports from Brazil (50%) and India (25%), signaling a continued assertive stance on trade. On Wall Street, major indices ended lower, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average experiencing its fourth consecutive decline, shedding 330 points to close at 44,131. Robust second-quarter earnings from tech giants Meta and Microsoft failed to entirely offset growing concerns over a diminishing likelihood of a Federal Reserve rate cut in September. Investor sentiment remained wary following elevated June core Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) inflation data, which rose 2.8% year-on-year, and upcoming deadlines for broader US trade actions. After market close, Apple saw a 2% gain on better-than-expected results, while Amazon fell 6% following disappointing earnings. In Malaysia, the FBM KLCI extended its consolidation phase, slipping 11.3 points to close at 1,513.3. Investors in the local market were weighing the implications of the recently tabled 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP), a comprehensive development blueprint for the nation, and awaiting further clarity on US-Malaysia trade developments. Despite the headline loss, market breadth improved significantly, with advancing stocks outnumbering declining ones at a ratio of 1.15, up from 0.66 previously. Trading activity also saw a notable jump, increasing by 42% to 3.77 billion shares valued at RM3.10 billion (+50% day-on-day). Foreign funds continued their selling streak for the fifth consecutive day, recording outflows of RM85 million, contributing to a year-to-date net outflow of RM13.06 billion. In contrast, local institutions (+RM50 million) and retailers (+RM35 million) emerged as significant net buyers, providing some counter-balance to the foreign selling pressure. Technical Outlook for KLCI: The KLCI’s close at 1,513.3 saw it breach a critical uptrend line support that extended from the 1,386 “Liberation Day” low. This technical breakdown raises the risk of a deeper correction, potentially towards the 1,500 psychological mark and the near-term support at 1,488, which represents its one-month low. To regain bullish momentum, the index needs to reclaim its position above the broken trendline. A firm breakout above 1,525 (the 50-day moving average) and 1,530 (the 20-day moving average) would act as key triggers for a potential rally. Sustained strength beyond these levels could pave the way for a retest of the one-month high at 1,551 and the 200-day moving average resistance at 1,561. Market Outlook: Following the announcement of a 19% tariff under the US-Malaysia trade deal – an improvement from the initially threatened 25% – and the unveiling of a pragmatic 13MP, HLIB sees the KLCI experiencing a much-needed relief rebound. This could potentially see the index retest the 1,530–1,550 resistance zones. However, overall market sentiment may remain cautious throughout August, weighed down by persistent foreign net outflows, expectations of a subdued August earnings season, and the index’s historical seasonal weakness in August (with 10-year, 20-year, and 30-year averages showing declines of -0.7%, -1.2%, and -2.2% respectively). Additionally, domestic challenges such as ongoing subsidy rationalization efforts and the expansion of the Sales and Service Tax (SST) may further dampen consumer sentiment and hinder corporate earnings visibility. title: Singapore Shares Slip For Fifth Session As Growth Concerns Mount
body: The Singapore stock market extended its losing streak on Aug 1, with the Straits Times Index slipping 0.48% to close at 4,153.83, its fifth straight day of losses and the longest such streak since early April. The decline of 19.94 points came amid broad-based weakness, particularly in blue-chip stocks sensitive to global trade and regional economic conditions. Investors remained cautious following recent signals from the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) highlighting risks to the economic outlook. MAS kept its exchange rate policy unchanged earlier this week but warned of slowing growth in the second half of 2025, citing a pullback in exports and industrial output momentum. The policy stance suggests limited room for monetary easing, placing greater emphasis on fiscal support and long-term structural reforms. Investor sentiment remains fragile as traders await corporate earnings and key regional economic data. With global uncertainties still clouding the near-term outlook, analysts expect markets to stay range-bound until clearer signals emerge from third-quarter economic activity and policy responses. title: KOSPI Suffers Steepest Drop In Four Months On Tax Reform Fears, Trade Tensions
body: South Korean stocks plunged on Aug 1, with the benchmark KOSPI index tumbling 3.88% to close at 3,119.41, its sharpest daily loss since April. The sell-off was triggered by investor anxiety over proposed tax reforms and growing global trade tensions. The market shed 126.03 points as foreign investors dumped local equities, pulling out an estimated 656 billion won. The sell-off followed the South Korean government’s proposal to raise corporate taxes and lower capital gains thresholds for large shareholders, a move widely seen as unfriendly to capital markets. Heavyweight stocks led the rout. Samsung Electronics fell 3.5%, while chipmaker SK Hynix dropped 5.7%. Automakers Hyundai and Kia, along with defence contractors and other export-oriented firms, also posted steep losses. The tech-heavy KOSDAQ index fared even worse, plunging 4.03%, reflecting heightened concerns over the sector’s vulnerability to policy and external shocks. Currency markets also reacted sharply. The South Korean won weakened past the 1,400 won per US dollar mark, its lowest level in over two months, as capital outflows gathered pace. Adding to the pressure were escalating global trade tensions. The US recently announced fresh tariffs of up to 15% on key South Korean exports, compounding worries about the country’s trade outlook. Outlook: Analysts warn that investor sentiment is likely to remain fragile in the near term. Market watchers are now closely monitoring the government’s next steps and potential adjustments to the proposed tax measures. Until then, volatility is expected to persist, with traders looking to the third quarter data and policy signals for clarity. title: Hang Seng Dips As US Tariffs Stir Investor Unease
body: Hong Kong’s benchmark Hang Seng Index fell 0.8% on Aug 1, closing lower in line with broader regional softness as markets responded to escalating US trade tensions. The downturn came after US President Donald Trump signed sweeping tariff orders targeting imports from key trading partners, including India, Taiwan, Thailand, South Korea and Canada, sparking fresh volatility across Asian equities. Unlike some regional peers, Hong Kong was relatively resilient as equities slipped. While the Hang Seng retreated modestly, regional sentiment was notably weaker as South Korea’s KOSPI dropped over 3% and Taiwan’s index declined nearly 1%. Investors grew cautious amid geopolitical uncertainty and an uncertain global demand outlook. The recent tariff hike heightened concerns over export-dependent sectors in the region. Analysts say modest dips in Hong Kong may reflect defensive positioning in traditionally stable sectors like finance and property. Still, offshore sentiment suggests the Hang Seng may remain vulnerable if trade escalations persist. title: Stock Today: Westports Dips To RM5.59 As US Tariffs Loom Over Trade Flows
body: Westports Bhd’s share price slipped 0.18% to RM5.59 at midday on Friday, with 10.44 million shares traded on Bursa Malaysia. The counter opened at RM5.61 and moved between RM5.53 and RM5.65 during the session, compared to its previous close of RM5.60. The marginal decline follows renewed attention on global trade flows after the United States announced revised reciprocal tariffs on multiple trading partners. Under the new structure, Malaysian exports will face a 19% duty. While Westports primarily handles transhipment cargo, prolonged trade friction could indirectly affect shipping volumes and port activity, given Malaysia’s role in regional trade routes. Domestically, the company is expected to benefit from the phased increase in terminal handling charges (THC) approved earlier this year. The first hike of 15% took effect on July 15, with additional increases of 10% and 5% scheduled for January 2026 and January 2027. These adjustments aim to enhance revenue and sustain infrastructure investments, including the ongoing Westports 2 expansion, which is projected to raise handling capacity beyond the current 14 million TEUs by 2028. For the first quarter of FY2025, Westports reported a net profit of RM222 million on revenue of RM621 million, supported by stable margins despite softer container volumes attributed to seasonal factors and maintenance works. The company maintains guidance for container throughput growth of 0–5% for the year, while analysts forecast long-term earnings growth driven by tariff adjustments and operational efficiencies. Westports’ shares have gained approximately 28% over the past 12 months and 68% over the past three years, outperforming the broader market. Research houses project modest upside from current levels, with target prices ranging between RM5.40 and RM6.08, reflecting a mix of positive outlook from local tariff revisions and cautious sentiment over global trade headwinds. title: Stock Today: Gamuda Rallies Over 5% On Strong Construction Order Book
body: Shares of Gamuda Bhd (KLSE: GAMUDA) surged 5.02%, rising to RM 5.44 at midday amid heightened momentum in Malaysia’s infrastructure sector. Trading volume totalled around 13.18 million shares. The stock opened at RM 5.22 and traded between RM 5.22 and RM 5.44. Built on a solid foundation of construction and infrastructure projects, Gamuda’s strong share price gain reflects a robust pipeline and favourable policy tailwinds. As of the latest quarter, core net profit reached RM 246.8 million, up 5.6% year-on-year, with revenue rising 24.1% to RM 3.09 billion, in line with a high order book of RM 37 billion covering both domestic and overseas contracts. Buoying investor sentiment, the company’s order book expanded significantly, benefiting from strong domestic infrastructure demand—including progress on upcoming rail investments like the MRT Circle Line, Penang LRT project and Pan‑Borneo Highway—as well as international work on data centres and renewable energy projects in Australia. Industry analysts regard Gamuda’s diversified portfolio and project execution track record as key advantages in navigating a competitive construction environment. Analyst forecasts remain largely bullish. Simply Wall St updated its target price to RM 8.83, predicated on earnings growth of 26.3% per annum and revenue growth of 17%. Meanwhile, RHB Investment Bank reaffirmed Gamuda as an overweight pick, citing substantial net development expenditure under Malaysia’s 2025 budget, including major transport sub‑sector allocation. However, not all views are uniformly optimistic. AmInvestment Bank downgraded the stock from ‘Buy’ to ‘Hold’, reducing its target price to RM 4.70, citing uncertainties in the data centre segment and a stretched valuation amid slower-than-expected new wins. Gamuda’s dividend policy continues to support its appeal among investors. The Group recently declared a second interim dividend of five sen per share, payable in August, with a dividend reinvestment scheme in place. Despite volatile sentiment around data centre demand, earnings visibility remains underpinned by infrastructure commitments and property quick-turnaround projects in Malaysia and Vietnam. As Malaysia’s construction sector rebounds—fuelled by sustained capital expenditure and unmatched demand for local infrastructure—Gamuda is viewed as a bellwether. Nevertheless, investors are closely monitoring the pace of project deliveries, additional contract wins, and sector-wide shifts including labour costs and regulatory levies. title: Stock Today: CAB Cakaran Dips 2.19% Amid RM231 Million Cargill Feed Acquisition Announcement
body: CAB Cakaran Corporation Bhd saw its share price ease 2.19% to RM0.67 at mid-afternoon on Friday, with 2.91 million shares traded. The counter opened at RM0.685, hit a high of RM0.685 and touched an intraday low of RM0.67, compared to its previous close of RM0.685. The decline comes as the poultry and feed group announced a RM231 million acquisition of Cargill Feed Sdn Bhd, a move aimed at strengthening its integrated poultry business. Through a conditional share purchase agreement signed via its wholly-owned subsidiary, CAB Cakaran will acquire 100% equity interest in Cargill Feed, which currently operates four feed mills in Malaysia. The acquisition will see CAB Cakaran transition from a key customer of Cargill to the owner of its feed operations in the country. Post-completion, CAB will control feed mills in Melaka, Butterworth, Westport and Kota Kinabalu, with a combined annual capacity of about 400,000 metric tonnes. Group Managing Director Christopher Chuah Hoon Phong said the deal delivers the final component in CAB’s “farm-to-fork” model, making the group fully vertically integrated. The company now spans the entire poultry value chain, including feed production, breeder farms, hatcheries, growout farms, processing facilities, logistics and distribution. Cargill Feed, established in Malaysia in 1986, is known for producing commercial compound feed tailored for livestock and aquaculture, serving a wide range of commercial farms and retailers. It sources raw materials locally and internationally. While the acquisition is expected to enhance long-term operational efficiency and reduce dependency on external suppliers, near-term sentiment has been cautious, as investors assess the financial impact of the RM231 million purchase and integration costs. title: SGX Opens Firm As Traders Watch US Tariffs, Singapore Economy Sentiment
body: Singapore’s Straits Times Index (STI) opened positive at 4,182.49, rising 0.21%, with 127 stocks advancing and 103 declining in early trading. Volume stood at 174.14 million shares, valued at S$240.77 million. Financials such as DBS, OCBC, Singtel, UOB, SIA, Keppel, and Seatrium feature among the top movers by volume and value, reflecting solid activity in domestic banks and telecoms. Traders remain cautious as attention shifts to the broader economic backdrop. The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) has warned that US-imposed tariffs could inflict a “negative income and demand shock” on the trade-reliant city-state. Though Singapore faces a modest 10% baseline tariff on US imports—lower than its regional peers—export volumes could still suffer from spillover effects. MAS has downgraded its growth forecast for 2025 to 0–2%, citing trade-related uncertainties and weaker global demand. With trade accounting for more than three times GDP, Singapore’s economy is highly sensitive to such disruptions. Amid these concerns, market analysts see opportunities for Singapore to benefit as buyers look for tariff‑friendly alternatives. Its exports remain relatively less taxed compared to regional counterparts, potentially making it a more attractive supplier in sectors like electronics and pharmaceuticals. Despite the headwinds, Maybank Research recently raised its 2025 STI year-end target to 4,185, citing domestic resilience, capital rotation, and momentum from key initiatives like the Johor‑Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS‑SEZ) and AI-led efficiencies in listed firms. Market watchers will continue monitoring developments in US trade policy, emerging fiscal stimulus, and upcoming economic indicators to assess the outlook for Singapore’s equities. title: Ringgit Firms Against Singapore Dollar Amid Tariff Relief, FOMC Cues
body: The ringgit traded stronger against the Singapore dollar in early trade as investors assessed the impact of Washington’s revised tariff on Malaysian imports and the outcome of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting. At 8 am, the local note rose to 3.2856/3012 from Thursday’s close of 3.2889/2953 against the Singapore dollar. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the tariff revision, cutting the US rate on Malaysian goods to 19%, could boost sentiment and lend support to the ringgit. “Nevertheless, the US dollar remains firm after the FOMC signalled a restrictive stance to contain inflation. The US Dollar Index (DXY) climbed 0.15% to 99.968 points as the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index advanced to 2.6% in June,” he said. The stronger-than-expected inflation data suggests the Federal Reserve may keep its policy rate unchanged in September, underpinning demand for the greenback and capping gains in the ringgit. Yesterday, the local note slipped 0.61% to end at RM4.2690 against the US dollar. As at this morning, the ringgit was almost flat versus the greenback at 4.2650/2850, compared with 4.2650/2730 at Thursday’s close. It also advanced against the Japanese yen to 2.8277/8411 from 2.8443/8498, strengthened against the British pound to 5.6328/6592 from 5.6426/6532, and improved against the euro at 4.8711/8939 from 4.8766/8857. Regionally, the ringgit was little changed against the Philippine peso at 7.31/7.35 and flat against the Indonesian rupiah at 259.1/260.5. It edged higher versus the Thai baht at 13.0169/0876 from 13.0448/0753. Market players are expected to monitor developments in US trade policy and upcoming economic indicators for further direction. title: Market Closes Higher As 13MP Optimism, US Tariff Cut Boost Investor Sentiment
body: The stock market closed higher on Aug 1, buoyed by renewed investor confidence following positive developments on both domestic and international fronts, namely, the unveiling of the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP) and the US tariff reduction on Malaysian exports from 25% to 19%. The broader market reflected improved sentiment with 570 gainers outpacing 452 losers, while 521 counters remained unchanged. Despite the upbeat tone, trading volume eased to 3.16 billion shares valued at RM2.23 billion compared to 3.77 billion shares worth RM3.1 billion previously. The optimism was visible in key movers. UMS Integration Limited led the top gainers, jumping 50 sen to RM5.50 on strong buying interest. Heavyweights Tenaga Nasional Bhd and CIMB Group Holdings Bhd also advanced, rising 28 sen to RM13.30 and 24 sen to RM6.79, respectively. Other notable gainers included Ajinomoto (Malaysia) Bhd and Gamuda Bhd where both counters grew 22 sen to close the trading week at RM13.08 and RM5.40, respectively. The rally followed the government’s announcement of the RM611 billion 13MP blueprint, which aims to drive sustainable and inclusive growth through economic diversification, innovation and small and medium enterprises empowerment. Analysts believe the plan will offer medium- to long-term support to sectors impacted by global uncertainties. In addition, the revised 19% US tariff on Malaysian exports was viewed as a diplomatic win and a lifeline for exporters, especially in high-margin sectors like electrical and electronics, machinery and rubber products. However, some blue-chip counters saw profit-taking. Heineken Malaysia Bhd dropped 34 sen to RM23.58, Nestle (M) Bhd eased 28 sen to RM87.80 and Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd fell 16 sen to RM19.42. Rounding off the top decliners of the day include Mesiniaga Bhd, which dropped 16 sen to RM1.30, and PPB Group Bhd, which lost 15 sen to RM9.28. Overall, market watchers said the twin positives of the 13MP and the US tariff cut may signal brighter prospects ahead. title: Hang Seng Index Futures Slips Below 20-Day SMA, Is The Bull Run Over?
body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has reiterated its long position on the Hang Seng Index Futures (HSIF) despite the index falling sharply below the 20-day simple moving average (SMA) line, signalling waning bullish momentum. On Thursday, HSIF opened on a firm note at 25,180 points and oscillated between a high of 25,217 and a low of 24,733 points before closing at 24,746 points with a long bearish candlestick. During the evening session, the index slipped another 38 points to last trade at 24,708 points. “The price action suggests weakening bullish control, with the index now trading below the short-term moving average. Meanwhile, the RSI is pointing south, indicating increasing bearish momentum,” the research house said in a note. RHB Research cautioned that if the correction deepens, HSIF may revisit the immediate support level of 23,800 points. However, it expects bulls to stage a rebound near this level, maintaining a positive trading bias unless the index closes below 23,000 points. Traders are advised to keep the long positions initiated at 21,416 points on April 14, with the stop-loss threshold placed at 23,000 points. The research house pegged immediate resistance at 26,000 points, followed by 27,000 points, while the next key support levels remain at 23,800 points and 23,000 points. title: Gold Price Inches Up In RM Terms As Global Market Holds Bullish Bias
body: Gold prices in Malaysia edged higher on Friday, with the price per kilogram rising 0.15% to RM452,917.29, or RM452.92 per gram, based on goldprice.org data. This marks an increase of RM696.48 per kilogram from the previous session. Year-to-date, gold remains a strong performer in local terms, gaining 28.88% over the past year and 11.51% in the last six months, despite a marginal 0.07% decline in the past 30 days. On the global stage, COMEX Gold slipped US$20.60 to settle at US$3,293.20 per ounce in the previous session. The metal opened at US$3,272.90, reached an intraday high of US$3,312, and closed slightly below that level, forming a bullish candlestick despite the earlier dip. According to RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research), the price action suggests the commodity is still navigating a consolidation phase after falling below its 20-day and 50-day simple moving averages. The Relative Strength Index (RSI) indicates weak momentum, but the broader bullish structure remains intact as long as gold trades above US$3,150. Immediate support is at US$3,250, followed by US$3,150, while resistance levels are set at US$3,450 and US$3,600. RHB Research recommends maintaining long positions from June 12’s close of US$3,402.40, with a stop-loss placed at US$3,150. Gold’s resilience continues to be supported by global macroeconomic uncertainties, inflationary pressures, and expectations of prolonged accommodative policies by major central banks, keeping the metal attractive as a hedge against currency weakness and volatility. title: Bursa Opens Higher As 19% Tariff Imposed By US
body: Bursa Malaysia opened stronger on Friday, buoyed by improved sentiment after the United States (US) imposed a reduced 19% tariff on Malaysian imports instead of the earlier proposed 25%. The benchmark FBM KLCI rose 0.66% to 1,523.21 points, while the FBM70 climbed 0.39% and the F4GBM index gained 0.61% as of 9.17 am. The softer tariff rate, announced yesterday, follows weeks of negotiations and is viewed as a positive step to alleviate concerns about severe trade disruptions. Analysts said the move provides breathing space for Malaysian exporters and mitigates risks to the country’s external sector, which had faced mounting uncertainty since April. “The tariff reprieve signals a temporary relief for Malaysian trade, supporting market sentiment in the near term,” said an economist, noting that a 25% levy could have weighed heavily on manufacturing and electronics exports. Market breadth was positive with 127 advancers against 103 decliners, and 174.14 million shares worth RM240.77 million traded in early deals. Among the most active counters were TWL, TRIVE and PHARMA, while blue chips like banking and plantation stocks underpinned index gains. Investors remain watchful of global trade developments as Washington proceeds with wider tariff hikes on other nations. At the same time, attention is on the Federal Reserve’s next policy stance after signalling continued vigilance on inflation risks. Oil prices holding above US$69 per barrel also offered some support to energy-linked shares. Bank Negara Malaysia recently trimmed its 2025 growth forecast to 4.0%–4.8% amid external headwinds, and its surprise 25-basis-point rate cut to 2.75% in July reflected efforts to cushion the economy. Market watchers believe Malaysia’s inclusion in global supply chains and initiatives under the 13th Malaysia Plan will help sustain resilience despite tariff pressures. title: Stock Today: CIMB Inches Higher As Analysts Reaffirm Positive Outlook For 2H
body: Shares of CIMB Group Holdings Bhd traded marginally higher at RM6.56 as of 3.18 pm, up 1 sen or 0.15%, with 10.9 million shares changing hands on Bursa Malaysia. The counter opened at RM6.55 and touched an intraday high of RM6.58 before slipping to a low of RM6.53. The uptick comes as analysts maintain confidence in the banking group’s fundamentals, projecting stronger performance in the second half of FY2025. MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB Research) and Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) both reiterated their BUY calls on CIMB, setting target prices at RM8.22 and RM8.80, respectively. The research houses highlighted CIMB’s attractive dividend yield of around 6% and inexpensive valuation, trading at 0.91–0.93 times FY2026 price-to-book value. They cited the bank’s disciplined strategy, solid execution track record and improving liquidity outlook as key factors expected to support topline growth. CIMB Niaga, contributing about a quarter of the group’s pre-tax profit, posted a 1% year-on-year rise in core net profit to IDR3.46 trillion for 1H25, driven by lower provisions. However, 2Q25 net profit fell 9% due to higher provisioning linked to adjustments in expected credit loss models. Net interest margin contracted by 6 basis points to 3.93% quarter-on-quarter, reflecting a less favourable loan mix, though management expects an improving liquidity outlook as bond maturities ease funding costs. Management reaffirmed its FY25 return on equity target of 14–15% and lowered credit cost guidance to 60–80 basis points. Analysts said loan growth remained resilient, particularly in hire purchase and corporate lending, with deposits growing strongly on double-digit CASA gains. Asset quality stayed manageable with the gross non-performing loan ratio at 1.88%, still below industry averages. Both research houses kept earnings forecasts unchanged, signalling confidence in CIMB’s ability to mitigate margin pressure and leverage its regional presence while maintaining robust dividend payouts. title: Bursa Malaysia Ends At Intraday Low Despite 13MP Optimism
body: Bursa Malaysia closed at its intraday low today, tracking weaker regional sentiment despite optimism over Malaysia’s strategic policy vision unveiled under the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP). The benchmark FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) slipped 11.25 points or 0.74% to 1,513.25 from Wednesday’s close of 1,524.50. The index opened slightly firmer at 1,523.99 and touched an early high of 1,524.05 before declining throughout the day. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim tabled the 13MP at the Dewan Rakyat, outlining measures to accelerate medium-term economic transformation. However, late selling pressure capped earlier gains, with investors remaining cautious amid external uncertainties. Market breadth was slightly positive, with gainers edging losers 545 to 475, while 483 counters were unchanged. Turnover rose to 3.77 billion shares worth RM3.10 billion from 2.65 billion shares worth RM2.07 billion on Wednesday. Regionally, sentiment mirrored the local market. Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index dropped 1.60% to 24,773.33, Singapore’s Straits Times Index fell 1.06% to 4,173.77, and South Korea’s Kospi eased 0.28% to 3,245.44, while Japan’s Nikkei 225 bucked the trend with a 1.02% gain to 41,069.82. Still, Mohd Sedek noted that investor sentiment remained fragile ahead of the United States trade tariff negotiations deadline, with concerns over potential new tariffs on Malaysia and other trading partners weighing on confidence. Among heavyweights, Maybank declined six sen to RM9.39, Public Bank eased eight sen to RM4.21, and Tenaga Nasional fell 26 sen to RM13.02, while CIMB was unchanged at RM6.55 and IHH Healthcare added two sen to RM6.65. title: Wall Street Retreats As Fed Decision Looms, Earnings Disappoint
body: US stocks closed lower on Tuesday as investors weighed a slew of corporate earnings and fresh economic data ahead of the Federal Reserve’s policy decision. The S&P 500 ended its six-day record run, slipping 0.3%, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite fell 0.4%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped about 200 points, or 0.4%. Markets are bracing for a critical week, with the Fed kicking off its two-day meeting on Tuesday. While policymakers are expected to keep rates unchanged, traders are on edge for any hint of future cuts as economic signals remain mixed. The latest Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey (JOLTS) showed declines in both job openings and hirings for June, intensifying focus on Friday’s nonfarm payrolls report. Consumer confidence ticked up in July, but concerns about job availability persisted. Adding to the uncertainty, President Donald Trump’s Friday deadline for trade deals looms large. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent suggested extending the tariff truce with China by 90 days, noting that outstanding issues were “minor.” Corporate earnings drove much of the market action. Boeing delivered better-than-expected results, but weaker performances from Spotify, Merck and UnitedHealth dragged sentiment. Starbucks also reported its sixth consecutive quarterly drop in US same-store sales, though the 2% decline was less severe than forecasts. Global sales fell 2%, while adjusted earnings per share of US$0.50 missed estimates. Investors now turn their attention to Wednesday’s Fed decision and Chair Jerome Powell’s press conference for clues on whether a September rate cut is on the table. title: Stock Today: IGB REIT Rises Amid Strong 2QFY25 Earnings And Expansion Plans
body: Shares of IGB Real Estate Investment Trust (IGB REIT) traded higher today, buoyed by robust second-quarter results and optimism surrounding its upcoming portfolio expansion. At 12.01 pm, the counter was last done at RM2.78, up 1.46% or 4 sen, with 3.69 million units changing hands. It opened at RM2.75 and traded between RM2.75 and RM2.81. The uptick follows IGB REIT’s announcement yesterday of a 13% increase in net profit to RM92 million for the quarter ended 30 June 2025, compared to RM81 million in the previous corresponding period. Revenue rose 6.8% year-on-year to RM160.1 million, while net property income (NPI) climbed 9.5% to RM119.9 million. Year-to-date, revenue stood at RM331.5 million, with NPI reaching RM253 million. The manager approved a distribution of 97.5% of quarterly distributable income, amounting to RM102.2 million or 2.82 sen per unit. Based on the unit price of RM2.54 as of 30 June, this translates into an annualised distribution yield of 4.77%. Despite headwinds from rising costs and the expanded coverage of the sales and service tax (SST), the trust remains positive on long-term prospects. The proposed RM2.65 billion acquisition of The Mall, Mid Valley Southkey in Johor Bahru is expected to complete in 4Q25, positioning the trust to benefit from strategic developments such as the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) and the Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link. The retail sector outlook remains cautious, with Retail Group Malaysia revising its 2025 retail sales growth forecast to 3.1% from 4.3% due to inflationary pressures and normalised seasonal demand. However, cross-border spending, aided by a strong Singapore dollar, is expected to support tenant sales and visitor footfall at IGB REIT’s malls. title: Stock Today: Bursa Malaysia Eases To RM7.58 At Midday Amid Lower Half-Year Earnings
body: Bursa Malaysia Bhd’s share price slipped 1.04% to RM7.58 as of 12.35 pm today, down eight sen from its previous close of RM7.66. The stock opened at RM7.67 and traded between RM7.57 and RM7.67, with 704,300 shares changing hands. The softer performance follows the exchange operator’s recent announcement of a 19.3% decline in profit after tax, zakat and minority interest to RM125.5 million for the first half ended 30 June 2025, compared with RM155.5 million in the same period last year. Revenue for 1H2025 fell 8.1% to RM344.3 million, while second-quarter profit after tax dropped to RM57 million from RM80 million a year ago. Bursa attributed the earnings contraction to lower trading activity, coupled with a 6.6% increase in operating expenses to RM189.3 million, driven by higher staff and technology-related costs, as well as administrative and building expenses. Despite these headwinds, the derivatives market provided a bright spot, with trading revenue rising 8.1% to RM56.1 million, supported by higher average daily contracts for crude palm oil futures. The Islamic Market also saw growth, with revenue increasing 23% to RM11 million, boosted by Bursa Suq Al-Sila’ and a doubling of gold dinar trading revenue. Data business revenue climbed 6.4% to RM40.5 million on the back of strong demand for actionable financial and sustainability data. Looking ahead, Chief Executive Officer Dato’ Fad’l Mohamed said Malaysia’s capital market remains resilient, underpinned by sound economic fundamentals and government policies that create growth opportunities in strategic sectors. The board has declared an interim dividend of 14 sen per share for the financial year ending 31 December 2025, amounting to RM113.3 million and representing a payout ratio of 90.3%. title: Ringgit Steady As Traders Await Fed Policy Signal

The counter, which opened at RM0.430, slid to an intraday low of RM0.380 on heavy trading volume of about 66 million shares. While its toll operations posted a 13% year-on-year revenue increase, bolstered by strong traffic and RM66.7 million in compensation for toll freezes, its construction segment slowed following the completion of the Setiawangsa–Pantai Expressway project. The group also reported a year-to-date loss before tax of RM30.4 million, weighed down by financing costs and delayed compensation for DUKE highways. Analysts have flagged Ekovest as undervalued relative to its toll and property assets, with some projecting fair values between RM0.60 and RM0.77. However, they caution that high debt levels and a lack of clarity on asset monetisation plans, including a potential sale of its Duke highways arm, remain key risks. Today’s decline underscores investor jitters as the group navigates strategic uncertainty despite stable recurring income from toll operations. title: S&P 500 Closes At Record High For Sixth Straight Session As Trade Deal Lifts Sentiment
body: The S&P 500 inched higher on Monday to secure a record close for the sixth consecutive session, while the Nasdaq also ended at an all-time high in a volatile trading day as investors assessed the US-European Union trade pact and braced for a busy week of economic events and earnings reports. The Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped 64.36 points, or 0.14%, to finish at 44,837.56, while the S&P 500 edged up 1.13 points, or 0.02%, to 6,389.77. The Nasdaq Composite gained 70.27 points, or 0.33%, to settle at 21,178.58. The latest record closes come as US President Donald Trump and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen announced a trade framework slashing EU import tariffs to 15%, half the rate initially scheduled to take effect on August 1. However, the deal drew criticism from France, which labelled it a “submission.” “This is feel-good in the sense that it doesn’t represent Armageddon, if the draconian tariffs went into place,” said Scott Welch, chief investment officer at Certuity in Maryland. “But it’s much too soon to pass judgment on the long-term effects on how that will play out. It’s better than the alternative for sure, and so I hope they continue.” The benchmark index has now logged its 15th record close of the year, driven by optimism surrounding artificial intelligence, improving trade sentiment, and expectations of stronger-than-anticipated corporate earnings. Investor attention now turns to the Federal Reserve’s policy announcement on Wednesday, where the central bank is widely expected to keep interest rates unchanged, despite Trump’s continued pressure on Fed Chair Jerome Powell to lower borrowing costs. A slew of tech giants, including Meta, Microsoft, Amazon, and Apple, are set to report earnings this week, which could set the tone for the broader market. Meanwhile, key economic data such as the Personal Consumption Expenditure (PCE) report—the Fed’s preferred inflation gauge—and the government payrolls report are also due. Energy led the S&P sectors with a 1.15% gain, buoyed by a more than 2% rise in oil prices, while real estate and materials were the weakest performers, dropping 1.75% and 1.44%, respectively. Nike surged 3.89% after J.P. Morgan upgraded the stock to “overweight” from “neutral,” advising investors to “just buy it.” Market breadth was negative, with declining issues outnumbering advancers by a ratio of 1.81-to-1 on the NYSE and 1.48-to-1 on the Nasdaq. Trading volume on US exchanges hit 17.58 billion shares, slightly below the 20-day average of 17.84 billion. title: Ringgit Opens Higher On Optimism Over Easing Trade Tensions
body: The ringgit opened higher on Tuesday against the US dollar and most major and regional currencies, supported by improved investor sentiment following signs of easing global trade tensions. At 8.01 am, the local note stood at 4.2140/2460 against the greenback, strengthening from Monday’s close of 4.2275/2345. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said sentiment was lifted by progress in US-China trade talks, which were taking place in Sweden. However, he noted that the US Dollar Index (DXY) had gained 1.03% to 98.653 points amid optimism ahead of the negotiations. “At the same time, the two-day Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, which begins today, will be in the spotlight, with consensus expecting no change to the Fed Funds Rate,” he told Bernama. The economist said attention will also turn to the July Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) report on Friday, with markets anticipating a softer print of 108,000 versus 147,000 in June. Mohd Afzanizam highlighted that the ringgit weakened 0.21% against the greenback on Monday to RM4.2310, amid ongoing talks between Malaysia and the US aimed at averting the 25% tariffs scheduled for Aug 1. Putrajaya is pushing for a rate below 20%. “Extended US-China negotiations could point to a prolonged truce, showing that President Donald Trump’s administration is sensitive to tariffs’ potential domestic impact. However, tariff shocks remain a downside risk to global growth in the second half of 2025,” he said. He added that with Fed Chair Jerome Powell’s term ending in May next year, a successor more aligned with Trump’s preference for lower interest rates appears likely. The ringgit is expected to trade between RM4.23 and RM4.24 today. title: Stock Today: TNB Dips Amid Additional Tax Assessment Concerns
body: Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) shares traded lower at midday, slipping 12 sen or 0.88% to RM13.48 as of noon today, compared with the previous close of RM13.60. The stock saw an intraday high of RM13.60 and a low of RM13.36, with 4.77 million shares changing hands. The dip came after CIMB Investment Bank Bhd reiterated its Buy call on TNB with an unchanged target price of RM15.75, while cautioning about potential financial implications following a Notice of Additional Assessment issued by the Inland Revenue Board (IRB). According to CIMB, the IRB has imposed an additional tax assessment of RM840.1 million for 2022, bringing TNB’s cumulative amount for the years 2013–2022 to RM5.89 billion. The research house warned there is a risk of further assessments for 2023 and 2024, potentially increasing the total to around RM8 billion. Despite the looming tax liabilities, CIMB believes the impact on valuation could be limited if TNB succeeds in its application for Investment Allowance under Schedule 7B. In the worst-case scenario where the utility giant pays the full amount, the research house estimates an 8–9% downside to its current discounted cash flow-based valuation. TNB continues to trade at a forward EV/EBITDA of 7.0 times and offers dividend yields of 3.3–4.0% for FY25–27F. CIMB maintained its optimistic stance, citing reasonable valuations and stable cash flow, pending the Finance Ministry’s decision on the tax incentive application. title: Stock Today: Malakoff Edges Higher Amid Power Demand Growth Prospects
body: Malakoff Corporation Bhd’s shares rose 1.10% to RM0.920 at 3.10 pm, up from the previous close of RM0.910, as trading volume reached 21.92 million shares. The stock opened at RM0.915, touched a high of RM0.925 and a low of RM0.915. The positive price action follows optimism over Malaysia’s surging power demand, which is expected to grow 5–6% annually over the next six years, driven by foreign investments in energy-intensive industries and data centres, according to CGS International. Malakoff, the country’s largest independent power producer, is seen as well-positioned to capitalise on this demand. The group has submitted bids to extend power purchase agreements (PPAs) for three gas plants with a combined capacity of 2.3GW until 2029 and holds initial letters of notification for two new gas-fired plants totalling 2.8GW. Analysts expect these PPA extensions to generate RM40 million in annual net profit from 2026 onwards. Additional contributions could come from its RM950 million mini-hydro project due in 2027 and a RM660 million waste-to-energy facility slated for 2029. Despite recent gains, CGS International maintains an “Add” call with a target price of RM1.20, citing attractive valuations at 5.2 times 2026F EV/EBITDA and a 5.5% dividend yield. Key re-rating catalysts include new project wins and improved plant reliability, while risks involve fuel margin volatility and plant outages. title: Ringgit Opens Slightly Higher Amid Cautious Market Mood
body: The ringgit started Monday marginally stronger against the US dollar, supported by cautious trading as investors await clarity on whether the trade truce between the United States and China will be extended. At 8 am, the local unit stood at 4.2110/2310 versus the greenback, compared to last Friday’s close of 4.2195/2245. He noted that attention is now on the US Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on July 29-30, with consensus expecting the Federal Funds Rate to remain unchanged at 4.25%-4.50%. “Based on recent developments, most countries appear accommodating in offering favourable terms to the US. It remains to be seen whether this will effectively narrow the trade balance in the near term. “However, the cost of doing business in the US is likely to rise, and it also appears the US may be relying on a weaker dollar to boost export competitiveness. Against this backdrop, we expect the ringgit to remain within a narrow range of RM4.22 to RM4.23 versus the US dollar,” he told local news media. title: Oil Ticks Up As US-EU Tariff Deal Cools Trade War Fears
body: Oil prices edged higher on Monday after the United States secured a trade pact with the European Union and signalled an extension of tariff talks with China, easing fears of a slowdown that could hit fuel demand. Brent crude futures rose 20 cents, or 0.29%, to US$68.64 a barrel by 0336 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) gained 15 cents, or 0.23%, to US$65.31. Analyst Tony Sycamore of IG Markets said, “With the risk of a prolonged trade war and the importance of the August tariff deadlines being steadily defused, markets have responded positively.” The US-EU agreement, announced on Sunday, imposes a 15% tariff on most EU goods, half the previously threatened rate, averting a major trade war between the two blocs that account for nearly one-third of global trade. In a related development, senior negotiators from Washington and Beijing are meeting in Stockholm to discuss extending a tariff truce before the Aug 12 deadline. Despite Monday’s uptick, gains were limited by expectations of additional oil supply. A panel of OPEC+ members is scheduled to meet later in the day, and sources indicate it is unlikely to alter plans to raise output by 548,000 barrels per day (bpd) in August. ING projects the group will fully restore 2.2 million bpd of voluntary cuts by September, with a possible hike of at least 280,000 bpd next month. JP Morgan reported global oil demand climbed by 600,000 bpd in July year-on-year, while inventories increased by 1.6 million bpd. Meanwhile, Yemen’s Houthi rebels warned they would target vessels linked to Israeli ports in a renewed escalation of their campaign tied to the Gaza conflict. title: Bursa Opens Higher, Tracks Wall Street Gains
body: Bursa Malaysia rebounded on Monday, opening higher in line with overnight gains on Wall Street. The benchmark FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose 4.03 points, or 0.26%, to 1,537.79 at 9.10 am, after starting the day 4.29 points firmer at 1,538.05. Market breadth was positive with 224 gainers against 133 losers, while 293 counters remained unchanged. A total of 182.48 million shares worth RM110.09 million changed hands. Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd equity research vice-president Thong Pak Leng said the upbeat performance was supported by strong United States corporate earnings and trade optimism, following President Donald Trump’s signal that more deals could be concluded before the August 1 deadline. “Back home, we believe the market is taking a breather and is poised to resume its climb. As such, we expect the index to hover within the 1,530–1,540 range today,” he told the news media. Tenaga Nasional, however, eased four sen to RM13.56. On the actively traded list, YTL Corporation advanced eight sen to RM2.56, Sapura Energy edged up half-a-sen to four sen, and Ekovest improved one sen to 41 sen. title: Weekly Review: Singapore Stocks Ease As MAS Policy Review Looms
body: Singapore stocks ended the week slightly lower as investors adopted a cautious stance ahead of the Monetary Authority of Singapore’s (MAS) upcoming policy review, despite the benchmark Straits Times Index (STI) hitting record highs earlier in the week. The STI surged to an all-time closing high of 4,231.28 on July 23, buoyed by strong corporate earnings, sector rotation into real estate and mid-cap counters, and robust institutional inflows. Top-performing stocks included City Developments, Seatrium and DFI Retail Group, while overall market sentiment remained upbeat midweek. On July 22, the market saw the index at 4,207.1, marking a 0.4% daily gain and extending its month-to-date rise to over 5%. The rally was further fuelled by the MAS’ launch of its S$1.1 billion Equity Market Development Programme, aimed at improving liquidity and research coverage for mid-sized listed companies. Major asset managers such as Avanda, Fullerton, and JP Morgan have reportedly begun participating in the initiative. However, momentum tapered off toward the week’s end. The STI slipped 0.28% on July 25 to close at 4,261.00, as profit-taking set in and investors stayed on the sidelines in anticipation of potential policy shifts from the MAS on July 30. Average daily turnover ranged between S$1.3 billion and S$1.6 billion, with trading activity dominated by institutional flows. While REITs and mid-cap stocks drew support, retail participation remained cautious following the sharp gains earlier in the week. Analysts expect the STI to consolidate in the 4,200-4,260 range in the near term, barring significant surprises from the central bank. title: Weekly Recap: Hong Kong Stocks Rally On Trade, Stimulus Hopes
body: The Hong Kong stock market posted a strong performance for the week ended July 25, with the Hang Seng Index rising 2.27% to close at 25,388, marking its third consecutive weekly gain. Investor sentiment was lifted by optimism over potential US-China trade progress and expectations of fresh economic stimulus from Beijing. The rally was driven by gains in property, technology and electric vehicle (EV) sectors, as traders bet on additional measures by Chinese authorities to support growth amid ongoing structural economic challenges. Property stocks led the charge, with the Hang Seng Mainland Properties Index climbing 3.7% during the week. Notable performers included Longfor Group and Shimao Group, each advancing over 4.5%, buoyed by speculation that Beijing may roll out targeted support to stabilise the real estate sector. Technology and EV shares also saw renewed investor interest. Market heavyweight Tencent jumped 6.1%, while Baidu gained 3%. Among EV makers, BYD and Geely Auto posted weekly gains of between 2% and 2.8%, as growth-focused investors returned to risk assets. Traders were encouraged by signs of upcoming US-China trade engagement and Beijing’s willingness to deploy further stimulus to safeguard its GDP targets. Recent resilience in China’s trade and economic data further supported the bullish tone. However, analysts cautioned that policy momentum will be key to sustaining the rally. Despite lingering macro uncertainties, sentiment has clearly turned more constructive, as institutional and retail investors position ahead of policy moves and upcoming earnings from major Chinese firms. title: Market Recap: KOSPI Extends Weekly Gains On Trade Optimism
body: South Korea’s benchmark KOSPI Composite Index posted its third consecutive weekly gain, lifted by improving sentiment around US-South Korea trade talks and strong buying interest in financial and shipbuilding stocks. The KOSPI closed 0.18% higher on July 25 at 3,196.05, recovering from midweek volatility and capping a steady weekly advance. The index traded within a range of 3,169.9 to 3,237.97 during the week, reflecting cautious optimism amid external headwinds. Investors were encouraged by signs of progress in trade negotiations with the US ahead of a key Aug 1 tariff decision. The improved tone spurred inflows into key sectors, particularly banks and exporters. Leading the rally were financial stocks: Shinhan Financial, KB Financial and Hana Financial that gained between 1.7% and 2.7%. Meanwhile, HD Hyundai Heavy Industries surged nearly 6% and Hanwha Ocean rose more than 1%, helping lift the broader industrial sector. However, gains were tempered by weakness in major tech counters. Samsung Electronics slipped 0.2%, SK hynix fell over 1% and LG Energy Solution declined amid concerns over demand and supply chain risks tied to potential trade restrictions. The trading session on July 25 saw turnover of approximately 9.8 trillion won, with 386 million shares traded. Foreign and institutional investors were net buyers, contributing 269 billion won and 110 won billion respectively, while retail investors locked in profits with net sales of 461 billion won. Market breadth remained negative, with 504 decliners outnumbering 370 gainers. While the tech sector’s underperformance weighed on broader sentiment, analysts remain optimistic about continued support from domestic institutions and improving export conditions. Looking ahead, traders expect the index to remain range-bound between 3,170 and 3,200, pending further developments in trade negotiations and second-quarter corporate earnings from major electronics firms. title: Market Recap: Gold Ends Week Flat As Rally Stalls Near Key Resistance
body: Gold prices ended the week of July 21-25 broadly flat, as momentum from an early-week rally faded and investors turned cautious ahead of fresh macroeconomic signals. The precious metal hovered near the US$2,300 per oz mark, a key psychological and technical resistance level. Prices moved within a narrow band between US$2,280 and US$2,310, reflecting a consolidation phase driven by mixed market cues. Early gains were fuelled by safe-haven buying amid lingering geopolitical risks and disappointing global economic data. However, stronger US Treasury yields and a rebound in risk appetite later in the week curbed further upside. Investor appetite for gold was also tempered by slowing inflows into gold-backed ETFs and reduced speculative positioning in futures markets. Analysts noted that market participants were in wait-and-see mode, anticipating US Federal Reserve (Fed) commentary and upcoming economic indicators that could offer clarity on the interest rate path. For now, gold remains supported by ongoing concerns over inflation, central bank policy uncertainty and geopolitical tensions, all of which keep the long-term bullish case intact. Market watchers are eyeing this week’s US GDP and Personal Consumption Expenditures inflation data, as well as speeches from key Fed officials, for direction. Any signs of easing inflation or dovish rhetoric could provide renewed fuel for gold bulls. title: Crypto Review: Crypto Markets Consolidate After Rally As Institutional Inflows Surge
body: The cryptocurrency market entered a phase of consolidation during the week of July 21-July 25, as Bitcoin and Ethereum held steady following early-month gains, while altcoins posted mixed performances. Record institutional inflows and growing regulatory clarity helped sustain investor confidence despite profit-taking pressures. Bitcoin ended the week down about 2.2%, closing around US$118,300, after struggling to maintain momentum above the key US$120,000 resistance level. Ethereum, however, outperformed it by climbing roughly 1.4% to end the week near US$3,780, buoyed by strong ETF inflows. Altcoin performance was mixed as Solana surged nearly 9%, while Avalanche and Cardano rose more than 15% each. In contrast, XRP and several other large-cap tokens reversed earlier gains, falling 4%-6% by July 25. A highlight of the week was the surge in institutional interest. Crypto investment products attracted US$4.39 billion in inflows, setting a new weekly record, as investors responded to Ethereum ETF momentum and increased regulatory visibility. Ethereum-focused products notably outpaced Bitcoin for the first time in 2025, led by funds such as BlackRock’s ETHA, which surpassed US$10 billion in assets under management. The shift follows the US House’s passage of the CLARITY Act, a key bill providing legal definitions and frameworks for digital assets. The development was widely praised by market participants, who have long called for clearer regulatory guardrails to enable broader institutional participation. Despite the inflows, Bitcoin’s failure to break through US$120,000 signalled caution among traders. Analysts noted that macroeconomic uncertainty, Federal Reserve (Fed) policy expectations and ongoing shifts in sector leadership were contributing to a more defensive trading posture. Looking ahead, market participants are closely watching Bitcoin’s ability to hold support above US$115,000 and regain momentum, continued ETF-driven demand for Ethereum, altcoin volatility as capital rotates across tokens and US regulatory updates and macroeconomic signals from upcoming Fed guidance. A recent investor survey also revealed growing retail appetite for crypto exposure, though many respondents cited a lack of reliable information and market access as key barriers. While the market paused to consolidate recent gains, sentiment remains supported by regulatory progress and historic capital inflows, setting the stage for a potential breakout or deeper correction in the weeks ahead. title: S&P 500, Nasdaq Close At Record Highs On Trade Deal Hopes
body: The S&P 500 and Nasdaq closed at record highs on July 25, buoyed by optimism that the US is nearing a trade agreement with the European Union (EU), as investors cheered strong corporate earnings and easing geopolitical tensions. Reuters reported that the S&P 500 rose 0.4% to end at 6,388.64, while the Nasdaq gained 0.24% to 21,108.32. The Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed 0.47% to 44,901.92. This marks the fifth straight record close for the S&P 500, its first “perfect week” of all-time highs since November 2021, according to S&P Dow Jones Indices. Investors are increasingly confident that a framework trade deal could be reached this weekend, ahead of a planned meeting between European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and US President Donald Trump in Scotland. Trump said on July 25 that the chances of a deal were “50-50”. Shares of Deckers Outdoor surged 11% after the footwear company behind UGG boots and Hoka sneakers posted better-than-expected quarterly results, driven by strong international demand. Meanwhile, Intel tumbled 8.5% after forecasting steeper quarterly losses and announcing job cuts, dragging on the broader chip sector. Charter Communications plunged 18% following a sharper-than-expected loss in broadband subscribers, hit by intensifying competition from 5G bundles. Centene jumped 6.1% after forecasting improved profitability across its government-backed health insurance operations by 2026, while Paramount Global slipped 1.6% after regulators cleared its US$8.4 billion merger with Skydance Media. Separately, nine of the 11 major S&P sectors advanced, led by materials (1.17%) and industrials (0.98%), reflecting broader confidence in economic resilience and global trade momentum. For the week, the S&P 500 climbed 1.5%, the Nasdaq added 1%, and the Dow gained 1.3%. Volume remained light ahead of the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) meeting next week, with 17.7 billion shares traded versus the 20-day average of 18.1 billion. All eyes now turn to the Fed, which is expected to hold rates steady at its policy meeting on July 31. However, traders are pricing in a 60% chance of a rate cut by September, according to CME’s FedWatch tool. Trump reiterated his call for lower rates, expressing confidence Fed Chair Jerome Powell may soon act. Looking ahead, earnings season continues next week, with market heavyweights Microsoft, Apple, Amazon and Meta Platforms set to report. Analysts expect S&P 500 earnings to rise 7.7% year-over-year in the second quarter, led by gains from the tech sector. body: Singapore shares closed slightly lower on July 25 as investors adopted a cautious stance ahead of the Monetary Authority of Singapore’s (MAS) upcoming policy announcement, while selective gains in transport and property counters offered some support. title: KOSPI Edges Higher For Third Straight Day Amid Trade Talk Optimism
body: South Korean stocks ended slightly higher on July 25, marking their third consecutive day of gains, as investors remained cautiously optimistic about ongoing trade negotiations between Seoul and Washington. The benchmark KOSPI rose 0.18%, or 5.6 points, to close at 3,196.05, supported by strong performances in financial and shipbuilding stocks, even as heavyweight tech shares lost ground. Officials from both countries are in active negotiations, aiming to reach a deal before the Aug 1 deadline. Markets remain on edge as the possibility of 25% duties on autos and electronics remains unresolved. title: Hang Seng Drops As Rate Jitters Rattle Tech, China Stocks
body: Hong Kong stocks closed lower on July 25, reversing the previous day’s gains, as unexpectedly strong US jobs data dampened investor expectations for near-term interest rate cuts. A broad sell-off in technology and mainland-linked shares led the decline. The prospect of higher-for-longer rates prompted risk-off moves across Asian equity markets, with Hong Kong particularly exposed due to its concentration of growth and tech stocks. Analysts noted that the sharp reversal followed a modest rebound on July 24 and reflected increasing caution ahead of upcoming macroeconomic releases and central bank commentary. Technology shares bore the brunt of the sell-off, as investors rotated out of high-growth sectors amid rising bond yields and reduced liquidity expectations. Mainland Chinese firms also declined, weighed down by lingering concerns over regulatory tightening and economic recovery uncertainties in China. Market Outlook: The Hang Seng’s retreat underscores renewed global volatility as markets reassess the timeline for monetary easing. Investors remain focused on incoming economic data from both the US and China, with particular attention on inflation indicators, central bank signals and earnings guidance. title: Wall Street Splits As Tech Triumphs, Dow Takes A Hit
body: US equities closed mixed on Thursday, with the S&P 500 (^GSPC) logging its fourth consecutive record high as robust earnings from Alphabet reinforced optimism around artificial intelligence (AI) growth prospects. The S&P 500 edged up 0.1% to end at 6,363.35, while the Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC) advanced 0.2%, also securing a fresh record. In contrast, the Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI) slid 0.6%, pressured by a sharp drop in IBM shares following weaker-than-expected quarterly results. Alphabet, the parent company of Google, exceeded Wall Street’s second-quarter expectations and reiterated its commitment to heavy AI investments, driving its shares higher. The upbeat results lifted other AI-linked stocks such as Nvidia, which gained 1.7%, further supporting the tech-heavy indices. However, Tesla weighed on sentiment within the “Magnificent Seven” cohort after its earnings miss and a warning from CEO Elon Musk about upcoming “rough quarters” amid the removal of EV tax credits under President Trump’s budget bill. The electric vehicle maker also reported continued weakness in European sales. Beyond corporate earnings, optimism over global trade negotiations added to market support. Reports indicated the EU and US are nearing an agreement to set a 15% tariff on most European imports, down from an earlier threat of 30%. The proposed tariff adjustment, expected to take effect on 1 August, follows Trump’s comments on reciprocal trade measures and builds on the momentum from a recent US-Japan pact. title: Stock Watch: Nestlé’s Counter Rises On Strong 2Q25 Results
body: Shares of Nestlé (M) Bhd rose RM1.28 to trade at RM83.60 as of midday on July 25, surging from its previous close of RM82.32 following the release of stronger-than-expected second quarter ended June 30, 2025 (2Q25) results. On July 24, the consumer giant reported RM1.7 billion in revenue for 2Q25 (+10% year-on-year [YoY], -6% quarter-on-quarter [QoQ]) and a core net profit of RM110.9 million (+42% YoY, -36% QoQ), driven by resilient domestic demand, solid export momentum and operational efficiency gains. The quarter also saw a 1.2 percentage point drop in its effective tax rate and improved EBIT margins, helping offset the impact of commodity cost volatility. Cumulatively, its first half of 2025 revenue grew 4% YoY to RM3.4 billion, while core profit dipped 3% YoY to RM283 million, mainly due to margin compression and a slightly higher tax burden. Outlook: While near-term margin pressures remain, Nestlé’s ability to sustain earnings growth amid cost headwinds and its consistent dividend track record continue to appeal to defensive investors. body: The FBM KLCI surged 10.5 points to close at 1,540.3 yesterday, buoyed by late-session buying driven by optimism surrounding ongoing US-Malaysia trade negotiations and investor-friendly measures under the Anwar administration’s “Appreciation Package.” However, market breadth narrowed, suggesting profit-taking as turnover slipped 9.2%. Foreign funds emerged as net buyers for a second consecutive day, injecting RM22 million into the market. This contrasts with local institutions and retailers, who were net sellers, pulling out RM4 million and RM18 million, respectively. Year-to-date, foreign funds remain net sellers at RM12.56 billion. According to HLIB Research, the KLCI’s strong close above key moving averages at 1,540.3 suggests an imminent bullish triangle breakout, with potential upside targets at 1,551–1,564. This rally is underpinned by the government’s market-friendly signals, the return of foreign inflows, and hopes that recent trade pacts with Japan, Indonesia, and the Philippines could pave the way for broader US-Asia deals. title: Wall Street Climbs As US-Japan Trade Deal Sparks Optimism; Tesla And Alphabet Earnings In Focus
body: US stocks advanced on Wednesday after a trade agreement between the US and Japan lifted hopes for more tariff pacts ahead of the August deadline. The Dow Jones Industrial Average surged 1.14%, or about 508 points, to close at 45,010.29, just four points shy of its first record close this year. The S&P 500 gained nearly 0.8%, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite added around 0.6%, both ending at record levels. The deal sees a 15% tariff imposed on Japanese imports, down from the previously threatened 25%, while Tokyo pledged US$550 billion in US investment. “It’s a great deal for everybody,” President Donald Trump said on Tuesday. The breakthrough boosted optimism that similar deals with the European Union, India, and China could follow before sweeping tariffs take effect on Aug 1. Economists noted that an average tariff rate of 15% could be manageable for global growth, tempering recession fears. After hours, Tesla reported a slight miss on earnings and revenue for Q2 but confirmed plans for its “more affordable” model to enter production in 2025. Alphabet, Google’s parent company, beat expectations on both revenue and profit, driven by strength in advertising and cloud services. However, the tech giant raised its capital expenditure forecast to US$85 billion, up from US$75 billion. title: Asian Stocks Rally As Trade Optimism And Strong Earnings Lift Sentiment
body: Asian markets surged on Thursday, with the Australian dollar hitting an eight-month peak, buoyed by optimism surrounding trade agreements and robust earnings from major US firms. Japan’s Topix index climbed 1.4% to a record high, marking its second day of strong gains after a US-Japan trade pact fuelled hopes of further deals to avert sweeping tariffs. Wall Street’s earlier rally added momentum, with Nasdaq and S&P futures inching higher as Alphabet’s earnings beat expectations, kicking off the “Magnificent Seven” reporting season. The US has secured agreements with the Philippines and Indonesia, while a trade deal with the European Union is reportedly close. EU officials signalled a 15% tariff on European imports with some exemptions, while Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent confirmed upcoming talks with China in Stockholm. “Worst-case concerns about tariffs in the US are probably dissipating to some degree, but tariffs are going up and that is a hurdle for consumers,” said Brian Martin, ANZ’s head of G3 economics. Second-quarter earnings season in the US has seen 85% of S&P 500 companies beating forecasts so far, according to LSEG data. Alphabet outperformed expectations and announced higher capital expenditure to meet surging demand for cloud services. In contrast, Tesla reported its worst quarterly sales drop in over a decade and profits that missed estimates. MSCI’s Asia-Pacific index outside Japan rose 0.3%. The Australian dollar touched $0.6604, its strongest level since November 2024, before settling at $0.66. The US dollar slipped 0.1% to 146.38 yen. In commodities, US crude added 0.4% to $65.5 a barrel, while spot gold edged up to $3,390.84 per ounce. Euro Stoxx 50 futures jumped 1.3%, mirroring gains in German DAX futures. Meanwhile, S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures were up 0.13% and 0.4%, respectively. title: US Stocks End Mixed As Tariff Pressures Weigh On Corporate Earnings
body: US stock markets closed Tuesday on a mixed note as fresh trade developments and lacklustre corporate earnings tempered investor enthusiasm. The S&P 500 edged up 0.1% to another record high, while the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.4%, dragged lower by chipmakers including Nvidia. The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 0.4%, or 179 points, buoyed by optimism surrounding international trade pacts. President Donald Trump announced new trade agreements with the Philippines and Indonesia, adding to a flurry of recent economic diplomacy. Investors are now closely watching for further announcements ahead of the 1 August White House deadline, which could see broader tariffs imposed on other countries. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent noted that US-China trade ties were in a “very good place,” suggesting a truce could be extended, but reiterated that the August deadline remains firm for new levies. Meanwhile, earnings season continued with mixed results from blue-chip companies. General Motors saw its profit shrink despite stronger sales, with automotive tariffs weighing heavily on margins. Its shares dropped 8.1% on the news. RTX also saw a hit to earnings, prompting the aerospace and defence giant to slash its annual profit forecast, sending its stock lower. Lockheed Martin and Coca-Cola also reported results, though market reaction remained relatively muted. With geopolitical tensions and trade policies driving corporate uncertainty, investors remain cautious on outlooks. Beyond equities, gold prices surged 1.1% to a record high of US$3,439.20 per troy ounce, supported by a weaker dollar and falling Treasury yields. The 10-year Treasury yield declined to 4.337%, offering some relief to rate-sensitive sectors. Bitcoin rose 2.2% to US$119,342, continuing its recent rally amid broader risk appetite. Global markets were mixed. Major European indices slipped, while Hong Kong and mainland China stocks posted gains as regional investors digested the latest global trade signals. title: Tokyo Stocks Ended Higher After Japan-US Reach Trade Deal
body: Tokyo stocks ended higher on Wednesday after Japan and the United States reached a trade deal with 15 percent U.S. tariffs on autos and other products. Japan’s benchmark Nikkei stock index, the 225-issue Nikkei Stock Average, ended up 1,396.40 points, or 3.51 percent, from Tuesday to 41,171.32, its highest level since July 16, 2024. The broader Topix index, meanwhile, finished 90.19 points, or 3.18 percent, higher at 2,926.38. title: Tariff Talk Tailwind Boosts Ringgit
body: The ringgit opened stronger against the US dollar on Wednesday, buoyed by a weaker greenback and hopes of trade relief ahead of the looming August 1 tariff deadline. At 8.03 am, the ringgit stood at 4.2195/2375 against the dollar, up from Tuesday’s close of 4.2300/2370. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid expects the ringgit to trade between RM4.22 and RM4.24 today, noting that investors are still cautious as the tariff deadline nears. Despite its early rise against the dollar, the ringgit was mostly weaker against other major currencies. It eased to 2.8767/8891 against the Japanese yen from 2.8690/8739 and slipped versus the euro to 4.9528/9740 from 4.9512/9594. Against the British pound, it rose slightly to 5.7052/7295 from 5.7088/7183. Regionally, the local note showed firmer performance. It strengthened against the Singapore dollar to 3.3001/3144 from 3.3011/3071 and advanced versus the Indonesian rupiah to 258.5/259.7 from 259.1/259.7. The ringgit also edged higher against the Philippine peso at 7.39/7.43 from 7.41/7.43 but slipped against the Thai baht to 13.1138/1767 from 13.0899/1172. title: Stock Today: Tenaga Nasional Gains After PM’s Assurance On New Tariff Structure
body: Tenaga Nasional Bhd’s share price advanced on Wednesday following Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s assurance that the new electricity tariff structure, effective July 1, would have minimal impact on domestic users. As at 3.45 pm, the counter traded at RM13.96, up 18 sen or 1.31% from the last close of RM13.78. It opened at RM13.78 and moved between RM13.76 and RM14.00, with 3.74 million shares changing hands. Anwar, during a live address earlier today, reaffirmed that 85% of domestic users would not see any increase in electricity bills under the revised structure. The government will also maintain the RM40 monthly rebate for hardcore poor households registered under the e-Kasih system, with RM55 million allocated this year. The Energy Transition and Water Transformation Ministry explained that the tariff now consists of four components: energy charge, capacity charge, network charge and retail charge. It aimed at transparency and fair cost distribution. Domestic users consuming 600kWh or less monthly will be exempted from retail charges, while small businesses and households using up to 1,000kWh will receive energy efficiency incentives. At the same time, the ministry announced that the new Automatic Fuel Adjustment (AFA) mechanism would replace the Imbalance Cost Pass-Through (ICPT) system, adjusting fuel costs monthly but exempting households using less than 600kWh. Analysts said the government’s move to maintain cost stability and transparency could ease investor concerns over earnings volatility for Tenaga. title: Stock Today: Sunway Edges Higher Despite Construction Probe Concerns
body: Sunway Bhd shares inched up by 0.21% to RM4.81 at 2.39 pm on Wednesday, with over 7.1 million shares traded, as investors digested mixed signals surrounding the group’s performance and prospects. The counter opened flat at RM4.80 and traded within a narrow range between RM4.79 and RM4.83. Trading interest remained steady, with more than 151,000 shares exchanged in the morning session. The gain comes a day after CIMB Investment Bank Bhd maintained its Hold rating on the stock, with an unchanged target price of RM4.90. The research house acknowledged positive momentum from Sunway’s property arm, particularly the robust launch of the Otto Place condominium project in Singapore. A 65%-owned venture, Sunway recorded a 59% take-up rate at launch, driven by demand from HDB upgraders opting for larger units under the Deferred Payment Scheme. Meanwhile, sentiment surrounding Sunway’s construction subsidiary, Sunway Construction Group (SunCon), has been tempered by news of an ongoing probe by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission involving one of its staff. Although the issue appears isolated and unrelated to contract awards, CIMB flagged that near-term job replenishment may be affected. The construction segment contributed RM115 million in pre-tax profit in 1Q25, accounting for 38% of group profits. Despite the ongoing investigation, foreign shareholding in SunCon rose from 7.2% in April to 13% in June, signalling continued confidence from institutional investors. CIMB expects property contributions to remain supportive in the coming quarters, noting the group’s recent joint acquisition of a 3.9-acre plot at Chuan Grove, Singapore, for RM2.3 billion, with potential for high-end private condominium development. With share price movement remaining largely stable, Sunway continues to trade just below CIMB’s valuation, reflecting the balance of optimism in property sales and caution in its construction division. title: Stock Today: Pavilion REIT Holds Firm Despite Minor Dip
body: Pavilion Real Estate Investment Trust (Pavilion REIT) closed 1 sen lower at RM1.70 on Tuesday, registering a slight dip of 0.58% despite continued optimism from analysts following its recent first-half earnings. The counter traded between RM1.70 and RM1.74 throughout the day, with an opening price of RM1.72 and a volume of 1.98 million shares. The drop came after Pavilion REIT’s 1H25 results reaffirmed analysts’ bullish views, with RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research), MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB Research) and Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd all maintaining their BUY calls. RHB Research raised its target price to RM2.00, projecting a 17% upside, while MBSB Research and HLIB maintained their targets at RM1.88 and RM1.77, respectively. The REIT’s strong performance was underpinned by a 28.1% year-on-year jump in net property income, led by Pavilion Bukit Jalil. 1H25 core net profit came in at RM169.1 million, representing 52% of RHB Research’s full-year estimate. Similarly, MBSB Research noted 1H earnings accounted for 51.7% of its forecast, backed by resilient mall footfall and new revenue streams from its hospitality asset acquisition. HLIB observed that Pavilion KL and Pavilion Elite made up 67% of the trust’s revenue, with tourism recovery providing further tailwinds. Occupancy rates held at 87%, and gearing improved to 36% from 38% in the previous quarter. Despite the slight quarter-on-quarter earnings dip, analysts remain confident in Pavilion REIT’s prospects going into 2H25, expecting a boost from festive sales, rising tourist traffic and contributions from newly acquired hotels. title: Singapore Market Opens Calm, Eyes Global Cues
body: The Straits Times Index (STI) opened marginally higher on morning, gaining 5.10 points or 0.12% to 4,213.36, buoyed by broader optimism in regional markets and sustained gains among heavyweight counters such as DBS and ST Engineering. Early trading saw 276.79 million securities changing hands with a total market turnover of S$219.48 million. Market breadth was positive, with 169 gainers against 79 decliners, signalling cautious optimism amid ongoing global and regional developments. Financial stocks led the morning upside, with DBS rising 0.53% to S$47.50 and OCBC inching up to S$17.14. The gains came as investors weighed the impact of OCBC lowering its 2025 inflation forecast for Malaysia to 1.5%, a move that could signal easing regional cost pressures and improved consumer sentiment. Meanwhile, ST Engineering continued to attract investor interest, trading at S$8.34, as defence-related sentiment remained elevated following Malaysia’s heightened engagement with Türkiye’s military sector. The developments may have stirred investor appetite for regional defence and engineering plays. Singtel and ComfortDelGro traded flat, while Genting Singapore hovered at S$0.745, with tourism-linked stocks showing mixed signals amid ongoing discussions over Southeast Asia’s recovery momentum. The iEdge suite of indices also reflected broader strength in ESG and regional financial segments, with the iEdge-UOB APAC Yield Focus Green REIT Index gaining, in tandem with a firm showing across Singapore REITs. Investor attention is expected to remain focused on upcoming US tech earnings and regional economic prints, particularly China’s stimulus signals and ASEAN trade data, which could provide further catalysts for SGX stocks in the days ahead.
