title: KLCI Gains As PM Slashes RON95 Price
body: The FBM KLCI edged higher by midday, rising 4.89 points or 0.32 % to reach 1,524.29, with broader indices FBM70, FBMEMAS, FBMSHA, and F4GBM also posting mild gains. Market participants appear to be responding positively following Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim’s announcement of a RM100 cash handout for all adults and a reduction in RON95 fuel prices to RM1.99 per litre, expected to ease public cost-of-living burdens. Advantageous moves in global markets are also supporting sentiment. The US dollar weakened amid renewed scrutiny over the Federal Reserve’s independence, while US Treasury yields softened after last night’s rally. Concurrently, ASEAN stock markets have steadied on hopes that next week’s US tariff deadline could be postponed. Crude oil and gold rebounded, further improving risk appetite. Locally, comfort in daily necessities has buoyed consumer-facing counters. Notably, NEXG led midday volumes, trading at RM0.515 with a 1.97 % gain, as the easing in fuel costs is expected to benefit the household and retail sectors. Residential sentiment also improved after the PM reaffirmed structural reforms to support affordable housing targets, reinforcing confidence in both macroeconomic and social policy continuity. Despite the cautious global environment, reflected in a muted recovery in European markets, Malaysian equities reflect growing optimism. Bullish investor tone was also supported by recent government assistance announcements, which may help shore up domestic consumption if implemented effectively. The energy space has responded to the reduced fuel price guidance, while the broader market registers mild gains as liquidity conditions stabilise and short-term political concerns dissipate. The central bank’s continued accommodative stance, alongside fiscal measures, is expected to reinforce the positive trajectory into the afternoon session. Looking ahead, attention will shift to how the PM’s targeted subsidies interact with inflation data and whether US trade decisions near August 1 continue to influence sentiment. For now, Bursa remains calm yet positive as midday marks a tentative recovery from recent volatility. Related Advantageous moves in global markets are also supporting sentiment. title: Hang Seng Index Futures Eyes 26,000 As Bulls Take The Reins
body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has reiterated its long position on the Hang Seng Index Futures (HSIF) as the index continues to chart an upward path, closing 150 points higher at 25,134 during Tuesday’s trading. The index began the session at 24,986 and briefly touched a low of 24,916 before surging to a high of 25,168, ending near the peak with a strong bullish candlestick. This pattern further reinforces the ongoing uptrend. In the evening session, HSIF added another 187 points, last seen at 25,321. RHB Research noted that the bullish momentum remains intact, supported by the Relative Strength Index (RSI) staying above the 50% level and the upward slope of both the 20-day and 50-day simple moving averages (SMA). With these technical indicators aligned positively, the index is expected to head towards the 26,000 resistance level in the near term. The firm has advised traders to maintain their long positions, first initiated at 21,416 on 14 April, with a stop-loss set at 23,000 to manage downside risk. Immediate support is identified at 23,800, while resistance levels are seen at 26,000 and subsequently at 27,000 if the bullish trend continues. title: Gold Price In Malaysia Slips 0.33% As Global Momentum Points To Further Upside
body: Gold prices in Malaysia dipped slightly despite continued bullish sentiment in global markets, with the local rate for the precious metal easing by 0.33% or RM1.54 per gram to RM465.08 per kilogram as at 2.41 am New York time, according to data from GoldPrice.org. In daily terms, the metal saw a decrease of RM48.52. However, gold’s long-term trajectory remains positive, with a 3.04% gain over the past 30 days and a sharp 28.64% rise over the past year. Over five years, prices have soared by 79.17%, while 20-year gains stand at a staggering 803.42%. Globally, COMEX Gold extended its rally for the third consecutive session, surging US$37.30 to settle at US$3,443.70, having traded as high as US$3,447.50 during intraday movement. RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) noted the strong bullish momentum, backed by a rising RSI and long bullish candlestick patterns, indicating that an upside breakout could be imminent. The investment bank maintained its long position initiated at US$3,402.40, with expectations that the metal could break above US$3,450 and potentially reach US$3,600. Immediate support remains at US$3,250, with a stop-loss set at US$3,150. Despite today’s local dip, the broader bullish narrative continues to support gold’s haven appeal amid ongoing economic uncertainties and anticipated monetary policy shifts. title: Bursa Opens On Cautious Note As Global Trade Talks Influence Markets
body: Bursa Malaysia’s benchmark FBMKLCI opened with modest gains on Wednesday morning, climbing 1.38 points or 0.09% to 1,520.78, as cautious sentiment returned ahead of the new US tariff deadline looming on August 1 and fresh trade developments from Washington. The early session saw 276.79 million shares traded, valued at RM219.48 million, with 169 stocks advancing compared to 79 decliners, a modest preference for buying amid lingering regional uncertainties. Asian markets took their cue from mixed overnight US and European performance, as investors remain hesitant while awaiting progress in US trade talks with partners including Japan, the Philippines, and Indonesia. The unresolved tariff saga continues to cast a shadow, in contrast to earlier optimism when a US court blocked certain Trump-era tariffs, a decision that had briefly buoyed markets in May. On Bursa, small-cap and ACE Market stocks are drawing attention, notably NexG, which rose to RM0.52 on strong volume, echoing a resurgence in IPO and technology-focused counters as Malaysia anticipates more listings later this year. Financial shares remained relatively steady; however, sentiment is being tempered by global cost and trade pressures amid renewed US tariff concerns. Market analysts suggest the FBMKLCI may remain within the 1,510–1,530 range as investors await clarity from the US trade deadline, with eyes also on upcoming Wall Street earnings and the Fed’s policy signals. In the near term, Bursa will likely be influenced by any developments on the US trade front, domestic IPO momentum and movements in global equity markets, particularly in China and ASEAN, all factors that will shape investor sentiment for the remainder of the week. title: Wall Street Climbs Ahead Of Earnings Deluge As Tariff Deadline Looms
body: US stocks edged higher on Monday as investors braced for a wave of corporate earnings and mounting trade pressure, while Treasury yields dipped and gold reached its highest level in five weeks. The S&P 500 rose 0.14% to 6,305.68, the Nasdaq added 0.38% to 20,974.18, while the Dow Jones dipped slightly by 0.04% to 44,323.53. The upward push was led by momentum in tech-adjacent names and communication services, with Alphabet and Tesla among the high-profile megacaps set to report earnings later this week. Other big names such as IBM and Intel, along with industrial giants like General Motors and Union Pacific, are also on the schedule. Market sentiment was underpinned by hopes surrounding trade discussions, although actual breakthroughs remain elusive with the August 1 deadline fast approaching. US President Donald Trump has threatened to implement sweeping tariffs unless a deal is struck. European equities, in contrast, ended in the red as traders weighed uneven earnings and limited progress on trade talks. “There’s been optimism around trade, and it’s early days, but we’ve had pretty good earnings so far,” said Zachary Hill, Head of Portfolio Management at Horizon Investments. “So it feels a little bit like a summertime, don’t-fight-the-trend environment at the moment.” US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent reignited debate on central bank independence, stating, “I think that what we need to do is examine the entire Federal Reserve institution and whether they have been successful,” amid ongoing speculation that Trump may fire Fed Chair Jerome Powell. Oliver Pursche of Wealthspire Advisors dismissed the idea, saying, “This is highly politically motivated… I don’t believe that is their objective or desire.” The dollar weakened against the yen after Japan’s ruling coalition lost its upper house majority over the weekend. The dollar index dropped 0.53% to 97.88, while the yen gained nearly 1% to 147.37. The euro rose to $1.1689. Gold prices rallied to a five-week high, gaining 1.47% to US$3,398.43 an ounce, supported by a softer greenback and lower yields. US gold futures mirrored the rise, settling at US$3,402.30. In the bond market, the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield fell 4.7 basis points to 4.384%, while the 30-year yield dipped 5 basis points to 4.9491%. The 2-year note slipped to 3.863%. Bitcoin reversed earlier gains, falling 1.11% to US$116,822.34 despite the recent passage of the GENIUS Act, which was seen as favourable for the crypto sector. Ethereum declined slightly to US$3,734.50. Oil prices closed marginally lower. Brent settled at US$69.21 a barrel, while West Texas Intermediate dipped to US$67.20. Investors shrugged off new European sanctions on Russian crude, seeing minimal supply disruption amid demand concerns tied to prolonged trade uncertainty. body: Shares of Sunway Construction Group Bhd (SunCon) fell 1.82% to RM5.39 as at 11.46 am on 22 July, despite analysts maintaining a positive outlook on the stock. The share movement comes in the wake of a recent graft probe involving a suspended SunCon employee, but both RHB Investment Bank Bhd and MBSB Investment Bank Bhd have reiterated their BUY calls on the counter. RHB Research has trimmed its target price to RM6.55 from RM6.80, while MBSB Research maintains its target price at RM6.44, citing confidence in SunCon’s strong fundamentals, solid governance and robust project pipeline. The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission had arrested a contracts manager under Op Ways, but management has clarified that the investigation does not implicate the company itself. Analysts view the incident as isolated, with no systemic risks to operations or financials. The group’s RM7.90 billion order book and exposure to major upcoming infrastructure projects continue to support earnings visibility. Despite the price weakness, both research houses see further upside potential, especially if sentiment recovers and new contract wins materialise. title: Stock Today: CIMB Climbs Modestly At Midday On Trade Sentiment And GDP Upgrade News
body: CIMB Group Holdings Bhd (CIMB) ticked up 0.61% to RM6.56 as at 12:30 pm today, trading within a tight range of RM6.53 on moderate volume of 2.07 million shares. The assessment suggests households and businesses may draw support from better export conditions, while Bank Negara Malaysia could consider an OPR cut in Q3. This backdrop is directly supportive for regional banks like CIMB. Investor sentiment has also been assisted by neutral to positive commentary from regional research houses. CIMB Securities, for example, sees the Malaysian equity outlook remaining constructive, with the banking sector, together with construction and utilities, expected to anchor earnings growth in 2025. There have been no recent firm-specific corporate announcements affecting CIMB today. However, longer-term bullish themes remain intact: the bank’s emphasis on cost efficiency, sustainable financing and regional growth aligns with its updated forecasts on partnerships and expansions. title: Ringgit Tracks US Dollar Weakness Ahead Of Tariff Deadline
body: The ringgit opened stronger against the US dollar on Tuesday morning, lifted by weakness in the greenback as markets brace for the United States’ tariff decision set for August 1. At 8.01 am, the local unit stood at 4.2230/2450 against the US dollar, strengthening from Monday’s close of 4.2320/2365. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid believes the ringgit’s upward momentum could persist throughout the day, although market sentiment remains cautious due to uncertainties surrounding the looming tariff plans. “The back-and-forth statements on the tariff plans would mean the scope for negotiation is widely open,” he told Bernama. Mohd Afzanizam noted that while signals from Washington remain mixed, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has indicated the Trump administration prioritises the quality of trade deals over timing. He added that Malaysia’s economy has held up fairly well in the first half of 2025, with support from Bank Negara Malaysia’s proactive rate cut and an expansionary fiscal stance, which are expected to sustain GDP growth going into the second half. Though the outlook is not without challenges, growth prospects remain resilient, he said. Elsewhere, the ringgit traded mostly softer against major currencies. It slipped to 2.8638/8789 against the Japanese yen and eased to 4.9371/9628 versus the euro. Against the British pound, however, it inched higher to 5.6951/7248. Among ASEAN peers, the ringgit showed a mixed performance. It rose to 3.2969/3146 against the Singapore dollar and to 258.7/260.1 versus the Indonesian rupiah, while declining against the Thai baht to 13.0986/1750. It also edged slightly higher against the Philippine peso to 7.38/7.42. title: Bursa Treads Lightly As Tariff Tensions Cast A Long Shadow
body: Bursa Malaysia’s main benchmark, the FBM KLCI, slipped to 1,519.03 by 12.30 pm today, down 5.56 points or 0.36 %, pressured by broad weakness in the market. Key sub‑indices also declined: the FBM70 by 0.45 %, FBM Emas by 0.38 % and FBM Shariah by 0.44 %. Market participants are increasingly wary of fresh concerns surrounding US tariffs. Investors continue to digest the impact of America’s recently enhanced reciprocal duties on trading partners, including Malaysia, tightening trade outlook and softening sentiment in the process. These tariffs have nudged down foreign interest in large-cap stocks, with the Financial Services Index registering losses. Nonetheless, some analysts remain upbeat that Malaysia may benefit from a broader regional slowdown in exports as competitors face similar policy headwinds. Rakuten Trade expects the KLCI to hold within the 1,520–1,550 range for the rest of the week, despite mid‑session weakness. Among the most active counters, Zertrix led trade volumes at RM0.93, NexG and Tanco showed modest gains, while Pharma and iCents saw heavier turnover. Focus remained squarely on export‑centric and financial stocks. There were no major local corporate announcements at midday to shift market dynamics. However, investors remain cautious ahead of potential developments in ongoing US-Malaysia tariff negotiations. In summary, Bursa’s midday retracement reflects global trade uncertainty and tariff pressures, but analysts suggest the market may remain range‑bound as negotiations continue and the regional context unfolds. title: Yen Jumps As Japan’s Ruling Bloc Loses Upper House Majority
body: Japan’s yen surged as much as 0.7% to 147.79 per dollar after early results showed the ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) and coalition partner Komeito failed to retain their majority in the upper house, according to public broadcaster NHK. With Monday being a holiday in Japan, both the stock and government bond markets remained closed, leaving the yen as the key asset reflecting investor sentiment. “Uncertainty usually tends to favour the yen, at least initially,” said Rodrigo Catril, currency strategist at National Australia Bank in Sydney. “Overall, the election outcome is not good news for Japanese assets and we would look to fade yen strength.” This marks the first time since 1955 that an LDP leader will govern without holding a majority in at least one legislative chamber. Prime Minister Shigeru Ishiba is now expected to seek support from the opposition, pushing Japan into a stretch of political instability. Investors had long braced for this scenario. Polls hinting at defeat for the ruling bloc had fuelled fears of a triple dip in Japanese bonds and stocks. Traders remained on edge in the weeks leading up to the vote amid speculation that a weak showing by Ishiba’s government could trigger further fiscal stimulus, including spending and tax cuts. The heightened expectations for looser policy had weighed on the yen and pushed Japanese government bond yields to multi-year highs. The yen has also been volatile in recent months due to trade concerns. US President Donald Trump’s first tariff move in April introduced further uncertainty, and the outcome of the Japanese election has not clarified matters. Japan still faces an August 1 deadline on tariffs and talks with the US have made little headway. title: Stock Today: SunCon Dives Over 13% As EPF Ceases To Be Substantial Shareholder
body: Sunway Construction Group Bhd (SunCon) saw its share price tumble by 13.38% to RM5.18 as of 12.30 pm today, following a major sell-off that saw the Employees Provident Fund (EPF) cease to be a substantial shareholder in the company. The counter, which opened at RM5.84, plunged as low as RM4.93 before recovering slightly by midday. Over 65 million shares changed hands, making it one of the most actively traded stocks on Bursa Malaysia. SunCon’s sharp decline came on the back of the EPF disposing of 20 million shares via Citigroup Nominees (Tempatan) Sdn Bhd, bringing its stake below the 5% threshold to 4.27%, effectively removing its status as a substantial shareholder. Despite the fall, the stock has been buoyed in recent months by major contract wins, including an RM260 million data centre project and an RM1.16 billion job to deliver general contractor services for two additional data centres. Under Bursa Malaysia’s Intraday Short Selling (IDSS) rules, the stock remains under close watch, although it has yet to trigger the 15% threshold that would suspend further short-selling activity. The steep correction may present an opportunity for investors still bullish on SunCon’s construction pipeline, but the exit of a key institutional investor has rattled market sentiment in the near term. body: MN Holdings Bhd saw its share price fall 4.12% to RM1.63 by midday trading, amid heavy volumes following its clarification distancing itself from a high-profile corruption probe in Johor. In a statement earlier today, MN Holdings categorically denied any involvement in the RM180 million data centre project under MACC scrutiny, stressing it had not participated in the project “directly or indirectly” and was not among the companies being investigated. The company also reaffirmed its commitment to ethical practices and regulatory compliance. The clarification came after several arrests were made by the MACC, including a contract manager, his wife, and two company directors, with RM7.5 million in cash believed to be bribes reportedly seized. title: S’pore Dollar Pressured By Tariff Threats And MAS Easing Signals
body: The Singapore dollar is facing mounting pressure amid fresh US trade tensions and rising speculation that the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) could ease its policy stance this month. In what may be a turbulent few weeks ahead, analysts say the city-state’s currency is likely to weaken further against the US dollar. On Monday morning, it stood at S$1.2846 per greenback. But that figure may slide closer to S$1.30 soon, especially if US inflation stays elevated and pushes back expectations for a rate cut by the Federal Reserve. “The tariff uncertainty, with higher tariffs on pharmaceuticals likely Aug. 1, could add to growth headwinds for Singapore in the second half,” said Moh Siong Sim, currency strategist at Bank of Singapore. US President Donald Trump’s threats of fresh levies on pharmaceuticals and semiconductors — two of Singapore’s key exports — have added a layer of uncertainty to the outlook. The potential for further economic headwinds is prompting expectations that the MAS may act sooner rather than later. Barclays economists, in a note last week, projected the MAS will flatten the slope of its Singapore dollar nominal effective exchange rate (S$NEER) policy band by 50 basis points to zero when it meets this month — a more dovish move than waiting until October. Unlike central banks that tweak interest rates, the MAS manages inflation through adjustments to the S$NEER band. Currently, the exchange rate is trading near the top end of that band. A flatter slope would effectively limit the currency’s strength against its trading partners. “With the MAS likely to stay on an easing path and flatten the slope of the S$NEER this month, our bias is for further Singapore dollar weakness,” said Priyanka Kishore, principal economist at Asia Decoded. She also warned that Singapore may be hit with a rise in the US base tariff rate from 10%, on top of specific sectoral duties. “Singapore is not only at a disadvantage from the prospect of sectoral tariffs on pharmaceuticals and semiconductors, but may also see an increase in the base rate of 10% on Aug. 1,” she said. Economists widely expect core inflation data due July 23 to come in at just 0.7% year-on-year for June — a key factor reinforcing the case for MAS policy easing. Meanwhile, Bloomberg Intelligence analysts have flagged that the Singapore dollar is increasingly used in funding carry trades. According to their models, investors are already going long on the Indonesian rupiah while shorting the Singapore dollar — a strategy that reflects weakening sentiment on the city-state’s currency. As trade pressures mount and monetary policy turns more dovish, the road ahead looks rough for the Singapore dollar. title: Gold Holds Ground As Fed Voices Split On Rate Cuts
body: Gold prices steadied at the start of the week, trading near $3,350 an ounce, as investors absorbed mixed signals from US Federal Reserve officials regarding interest rate policy and the broader economic impact of President Donald Trump’s tariff strategy. As of 8.54 am in Singapore, spot gold was slightly higher at $3,353.80 an ounce. The Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index edged 0.1% lower, while silver and platinum saw little movement. Palladium recorded a slight rise. Last week, bullion saw a modest decline but remains elevated, having climbed over 25% this year amid escalating geopolitical risks and doubts surrounding dollar-denominated assets. Despite that, the precious metal has largely traded within a narrow band in recent months as markets await clearer cues on global trade talks, interest rate directions, and tariff implications. The divide among Fed officials continues to widen. Governor Christopher Waller has come out in favour of a rate cut, while Governor Michelle Bowman signalled she is also open to the idea. However, other policymakers are treading carefully, citing persistent inflationary risks tied to tariffs. Lower borrowing costs are typically seen as supportive for gold, which does not yield interest. Meanwhile, Trump’s influence on the central bank has not gone unnoticed. The White House is reportedly assessing potential candidates to replace Fed Chair Jerome Powell, whose term ends in May, with a preference for someone who would favour rate reductions. Trump also rejected a Wall Street Journal report alleging Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned him that sacking Powell could provoke a negative market reaction. On the global stage, attention is turning to trade. The European Union is expected to convene this week to prepare a response in case of a breakdown in negotiations with Trump. The US president has set an August 1 deadline for introducing what he calls reciprocal tariffs, and markets are closely tracking developments with multiple trading partners. title: Seoul Stocks Dip As Tariff Tensions Offset Early Gains
body: South Korean shares ended slightly lower on July 18, as the KOSPI index dipped 4.22 points, or 0.13%, to close at 3,188.07. The market was weighed down by investor caution surrounding potential new US tariffs and anticipation of second-quarter earnings reports. Despite a positive lead from Wall Street, the KOSPI reversed early gains amid renewed trade uncertainty. President Donald Trump recently indicated that steep tariffs on select trading partners could take effect as early as Aug 1, which dampened risk appetite across regional markets. Trading volume was moderate, with around 390 million shares changing hands, valued at 11.8 trillion won. Declining stocks outnumbered advancers 589 to 303, signalling a broadly cautious sentiment. Among the key movers for the trading session were Samsung Electronics, which rose 0.6% to 67,100 won, Hyundai Motor, which inched up 0.24% to 210,500 won, and large industrials like HD Hyundai, KEPCO, Korean Air and HMM all closed lower, reflecting sectoral divergence in investor sentiment. In the bond market, yields slipped slightly as investors sought safety amid global uncertainty. The three-year government bond yield fell 0.5 basis points to 2.474%, while the five-year yield declined 1.8 basis points to 2.645%. Despite the dip, the KOSPI ended the week with a modest 0.39% gain, supported by resilience in global markets and improved expectations for tech-sector performance. title: Stock Today: SunCon Climbs Nearly 3% As Momentum Builds On Infrastructure Play
body: Sunway Construction Group Bhd (SunCon) surged in active trade today, gaining 2.94% to RM5.95 as at 2.44 pm, driven by renewed investor confidence in the infrastructure sector amid a stronger government push for public works and green infrastructure. The counter rose 17 sen from its previous close of RM5.78, marking one of its strongest single-day performances in recent weeks. It touched an intraday high of RM6.00 before easing slightly, with volume spiking to nearly 4.6 million shares — well above its recent average. The rally comes on the back of investor optimism following the group’s positive track record in securing high-value infrastructure jobs, including its involvement in Mass Rapid Transit 3 (MRT3) and various hospital and data centre developments across the country. Trading activity was also likely fuelled by broader interest in construction counters, buoyed by recent state-level announcements such as Gamuda’s RM5 billion water project in Perak and heightened expectations for Budget 2026 to include higher public infrastructure allocations. SunCon opened at RM5.78 and quickly gained ground, with buying momentum building as market sentiment improved across Bursa Malaysia. At the time of writing, there were more sell queues (340,700 shares) than buy queues (161,100 shares), indicating some profit-taking pressure near the RM6.00 psychological level. Analysts have generally maintained a bullish outlook on SunCon, citing a strong order book, earnings visibility and its ESG credentials as key differentiators in the current construction cycle. If the current momentum holds, the stock may test the RM6.10–RM6.20 resistance range in the near term, provided sentiment across the broader construction and infrastructure theme remains intact. title: Stock Today: Gamuda Rises Almost 3% On Positive Momentum From Perak Water Project Win
body: Gamuda Bhd’s share price rose by 2.91% to close at RM5.30 today, gaining 15 sen with strong buying interest following recent developments in its RM5 billion water project in Perak. The stock hit an intraday high of RM5.31 on volume of 21.9 million shares. This upward movement reflects growing investor confidence after Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) maintained a BUY rating on the construction group, raising its target price to RM5.70 from RM5.50. The revision follows the announcement that Gamuda’s 50%-owned joint venture with Perbadanan Kemajuan Negeri Perak (PKNPk) has been appointed by the Perak state government to develop and operate the Northern Perak Water Supply Scheme (NPWSS). HLIB estimates Gamuda’s share of the construction value at RM4 billion, with the contract expected to be formalised in 2026. The scheme is projected to generate more than 40 years of recurring income and deliver 1,500 million litres of water per day to support both agricultural and industrial activities in northern Perak and Penang. The research house noted that the NPWSS will likely become Gamuda’s second major domestic recurring income source after the Ulu Padas hydro project in Sabah. HLIB has revised its earnings forecasts upwards for FY26 and FY27, citing improving margins and consistent contract wins that have pushed Gamuda’s orderbook to RM37.2 billion. At the last traded price of RM5.30, the counter remains below HLIB’s target price, implying further potential upside for investors. title: S&P 500 And Nasdaq Close At Fresh Highs As US Retail Sales Surge, Markets Brush Off Tariff Fears
body: Wall Street closed at fresh record highs Thursday, buoyed by a stronger-than-expected US retail sales report, which helped ease investor concerns over tariffs, interest rates and Federal Reserve leadership stability. The S&P 500 rose 0.5% to finish at 6,297.36, while the Nasdaq Composite added 0.7% to end at 20,885.65. The Dow Jones Industrial Average also climbed 0.5% to close at 44,484.49. US retail sales in June jumped 0.6% to US$720.1 billion, reversing May’s 0.9% drop and topping analyst expectations. The data reassured investors wary of the ongoing earnings season and economic uncertainty. “The news on the economy this week has been good enough,” said Steve Sosnick of Interactive Brokers. Jack Ablin of Cresset Capital Management noted that both economic data and earnings “are coming in better than expected.” Markets also found support in the latest US jobless claims, which remained modest, indicating continued economic resilience. Art Hogan of B. Riley Wealth Management said the strength of the latest macro indicators has tempered recent concerns about trade wars and earnings. Investors shrugged off volatility from the day before when reports surfaced suggesting US President Donald Trump was planning to fire Federal Reserve Chairman Jerome Powell over interest rate policies. Trump later denied the claims, helping markets rebound. Despite Trump’s repeated criticism of Powell, the dollar rose again Thursday, with analysts suggesting markets still view US monetary policy as credible. On the corporate front, United Airlines gained 3.1% after offering a positive travel outlook for the second half of 2025, even as second-quarter profits slipped. In global markets, Frankfurt’s DAX climbed 1.5%, Paris’ CAC 40 rose 1.3%, and London’s FTSE 100 added 0.5%. In Asia, the Nikkei 225 advanced 0.6%, while Shanghai’s Composite rose 0.4%. Hong Kong’s Hang Seng slipped 0.1%. Oil prices also gained, with Brent crude up 1.5% to US$69.52 per barrel and West Texas Intermediate climbing 1.8% to US$67.54. title: Ringgit Strengthens As US Rate Cut Bets Rise
body: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar on Friday, climbing to 4.2340/2580 at 8 am from Thursday’s close of 4.2465/2510, buoyed by weaker demand for the greenback amid mounting expectations of a US Federal Reserve interest rate cut. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid noted that US Fed Governor Christopher Waller had hinted at a potential rate cut this month, suggesting the central bank should not wait for signs of labour market weakness before acting. He also flagged continued uncertainty over the impending US tariff measures, with investors cautious as the August 1 implementation date looms. “Issues surrounding the US tariff remain high on the agenda,” he told local media. On the domestic side, investors are focused on Malaysia’s second-quarter 2025 gross domestic product (GDP) advance estimate due later today. Mohd Afzanizam said the bank projects a 4.5% growth, supported by front-loading of export activities, strong labour market conditions and sustained investment spending. Given these developments, he expects the ringgit to move within the RM4.24 to RM4.25 range against the US dollar throughout the day. The ringgit also made gains against a basket of major and regional currencies. It appreciated against the euro to 4.9178/9457 from 4.9217/9269, advanced versus the British pound to 5.6867/7189 from 5.6886/6946 and strengthened against the Japanese yen to 2.8523/8687 from 2.8548/8580. Among ASEAN currencies, the ringgit rose against the Singapore dollar to 3.2939/3131 from 3.3013/3051, gained on the Thai baht to 13.0385/1201 from 13.0521/0720, appreciated versus the Indonesian rupiah to 259.1/260.6 from 259.8/260.2, and edged higher against the Philippine peso to 7.39/7.44 from 7.41/7.43. title: Asia Stocks Rise On Wall Street Momentum, Yen Slips Before Japan Election
body: Asian shares edged higher on Friday, tracking strong gains on Wall Street, where both the S&P 500 and Nasdaq once again closed at record highs. Robust US retail sales and jobless claims data helped fuel optimism, indicating a modest recovery in the economy and giving the Federal Reserve some breathing room to assess the inflationary impact of rising tariffs. The MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan climbed 0.8%, touching its highest level since late 2021 and posting a 1.7% weekly gain. Chinese blue-chips advanced 0.3%, while Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index added 1.2%. TSMC shares in Taipei rose 2.2% after the world’s top AI chip manufacturer posted a record quarterly profit on Thursday. The company, however, warned that upcoming earnings may take a hit due to US tariffs. Japan’s Nikkei slipped 0.2%, weighed down by election jitters, as polls showed Prime Minister Shigeru Ishiba’s coalition might lose its majority in Sunday’s upper house vote. The yen was weaker at 148.54 to the dollar, marking a weekly drop of around 0.7%. “If PM Ishiba decides to resign on an election loss, USDJPY could easily break above 149.7 as it would usher in an initial period of political turbulence,” said Jayati Bharadwaj, head of FX strategy at TD Securities. “JPY could reverse the recent dramatic weakness if the ruling coalition wins and can make swift progress on a trade deal with Trump,” he added. Japan’s core inflation slowed in June, largely due to temporary utility bill cuts, though it remained above the Bank of Japan’s 2% target. Rising costs of essentials like rice continue to be a key factor behind the prime minister’s waning popularity. Netflix beat analysts’ earnings expectations for the second quarter, supported in part by a weaker dollar. However, its shares slid 1.8% in after-hours trading as analysts noted much of the upside had already been priced in. The US dollar eased again on Friday, after rebounding 0.3% overnight on the back of strong economic data. For the week, it is set for a 0.6% gain, recovering further from the 3½-year low recorded more than two weeks ago. Fed Governor Christopher Waller stated on Thursday that he still believes interest rates should be cut at the end of the month. However, most Fed officials have signalled no urgency to adjust rates. Fed funds futures now imply little to no chance of a move on July 30, while a September cut is roughly 62% priced in. US Treasury yields dipped slightly in Asia, with 10-year yields slipping 2 basis points to 4.445%, and two-year yields also down by 2 bps at 3.8981%. Oil prices steadied on Friday, after a $1 gain overnight following the fourth consecutive day of drone strikes on oil facilities in Iraqi Kurdistan. US crude rose 0.2% to $67.66 per barrel, while Brent added 0.2% to $69.68. Both benchmarks are headed for a weekly loss of around 1%. Spot gold prices remained steady at $3,337 an ounce, but were poised for a 0.5% weekly drop. title: Wall Street Recovers After Powell Firing Rumour Spooks Markets
body: Wall Street closed higher on Wednesday despite a midday panic triggered by reports that US President Donald Trump was planning to fire Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell. The Nasdaq Composite rose 0.26% to end at 20,730.49, marking its fifth record high in six sessions, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed 0.53% to 44,254.78. The S&P 500 gained 0.32% to settle at 6,263.70. Markets tumbled briefly after a Bloomberg report cited an unnamed White House official suggesting Trump was ready to oust Powell. The dollar plunged, Treasury yields spiked, and the S&P 500 and Nasdaq dropped over 1% before rebounding. Trump later denied the rumour, although he renewed criticism of Powell for not cutting interest rates. “The Fed’s independence is hugely important to our overall economy, so you saw the market react when that initial headline came out,” said Dylan Bell, Chief Investment Officer at CalBay Investments. Bank stocks were mixed following Q2 earnings. Goldman Sachs rose 0.9% after a 22% earnings jump, while Bank of America and Morgan Stanley fell 0.3% and 1.3% respectively, despite reporting higher profits. Johnson & Johnson surged 6.2% after slashing its projected tariff costs and raising its full-year outlook, becoming the second-best performer on the S&P 500. Meanwhile, semiconductor stocks cooled down, with the SOX index slipping 0.4%, despite earlier optimism over Nvidia’s approval to sell its H2O chips in China. Investor nerves also reflected in the CBOE Volatility Index, which hit a three-week high before easing. Analysts noted that while headline-driven volatility remains a risk, economic fundamentals continue to support equities. Data released Wednesday showed US producer prices remained flat in June, adding to earlier signs that tariff-related inflation may be moderating, though consumer inflation remains sticky. title: Stock Today: Gamuda Up 2.4% As Analyst Flags 15% Total Return Potential
body: Shares of Gamuda Bhd rose 2.39% to RM5.15 in midday trade, adding 12 sen from the previous close, buoyed by investor confidence following news of its involvement in the Northern Perak Water Supply Scheme (NPWSS) and a fresh target price upgrade by Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB). As of 2.00 pm, the stock traded actively with a volume of 1.2 million shares, ranging between RM5.05 and RM5.17. The counter opened at RM5.06 and recorded a last done price of RM5.15. Buy-side demand remains relatively modest at 18,000 units against a sell queue of over 160,000 units, suggesting retail profit-taking after a strong institutional-driven climb. The rally comes after HLIB maintained a BUY call and revised its target price to RM5.70 from RM5.50, reflecting a more bullish long-term outlook on Gamuda’s earnings, supported by its recent RM5 billion water project win in Perak. Gamuda, through a 50%-owned joint venture with Perbadanan Kemajuan Negeri Perak (PKNPk), has been appointed to develop and operate the NPWSS. While the construction contract is expected to only materialise in 2026, HLIB estimates Gamuda’s portion of the construction value at RM4 billion, with recurring income potential extending over 40 years. The project will serve the Kerian Integrated Green Industrial Park and Penang, supplying up to 1,000 million litres per day for domestic and industrial use. It is being undertaken on a privatisation model with a minimum concession period of 40 years. HLIB expects minimal gearing impact from Gamuda’s estimated RM500 million investment. The research house also adjusted its earnings forecasts upwards by 2.1% and 4.4% for FY26 and FY27, incorporating the conversion of the upcoming contract, which is expected to yield 10% to 12% pre-tax margins. Gamuda’s current outstanding orderbook stands at RM37.2 billion, driven by steady contract wins both locally and overseas, including its foray into renewable energy infrastructure in Australia. At the last traded price of RM5.15, the stock now sits closer to HLIB’s revised fair value, offering a potential capital upside of 10.7% with a total expected return of 15.4% including dividends. The improved outlook positions Gamuda as one of the top infrastructure counters riding on domestic water security and regional green energy expansion themes. title: Malaysia’s Crypto Market Poised For Bullish Outlook In 2H25
body: Malaysia’s cryptocurrency market is gearing up for a promising second half of 2025 (2H25), following a strong rebound in 1H25, according to Luno Asia Pacific General Manager Aaron Tang. Tang shared that amid a resurgence of Bitcoin and altcoin activity globally, the Malaysian market has shown signs of maturing, buoyed by increasing institutional interest and a supportive regulatory landscape. “Bitcoin reached a new all-time high of over US$120,000 in July, signalling renewed investor confidence after a volatile start to the year. “It’s been an intriguing first half of the year in financial markets,” said Tang, pointing to geopolitical and macroeconomic shifts such as US President Trump’s pro-crypto policies, tariff tensions and expectations of lower interest rates as key drivers of crypto market performance. Despite early headwinds in 2025, altcoin markets are now “seeing signs of life after a tepid first half”, Tang said to BusinessToday . Malaysia’s Growing Institutional Interest Locally, Tang emphasised the growing participation of Malaysian institutional investors, particularly family offices, in digital assets. “We are seeing interest spark within the local institutional space, especially among family offices, which want to include crypto in their investment mix,” he said. He added that this shift comes as Malaysians increasingly view cryptocurrencies as a means to diversify portfolios beyond traditional assets such as equities, bonds, real estate and precious metals. The classification of crypto as a security under Malaysian law has offered a level of regulatory certainty that supports this evolution. Positioning Malaysia as a Digital Asset Hub Tang pointed out that Malaysia is well-positioned to leverage its strengths in fintech and blockchain innovation as the country is already home to several influential players in the global crypto space, including CoinGecko and Etherscan. “Further recognition of crypto beyond securities could strengthen Malaysia as a hub for financial innovation, attracting fintech startups, blockchain developers, and global investors,” Tang added. He also highlighted Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s commitment to positioning Malaysia as a regional leader in digital assets. Bullish Indicators For 2H25 Tang revealed that the crypto outlook for 2H25 appears increasingly bullish. Tang says if Malaysia’s regulatory frameworks continue to evolve in tandem with market needs, the country could cement its place as a Southeast Asian hub for digital asset innovation and investment in the months ahead “Global developments, such as the expected easing of US interest rates and the rapid rise of institutional investment vehicles like Bitcoin ETFs, are likely to serve as tailwinds for continued market growth. “The approval and explosive growth of Bitcoin ETFs in the US, particularly BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust, which now ranks among the top revenue-generating ETFs, are bringing in billions in net inflows. Even traditional financial giants like JPMorgan are entering the space, with trademark filings for crypto platforms that could offer trading, payments and digital asset issuance. “These developments globally reflect a maturing and increasingly accessible crypto market,” Tang said. He emphasised that Malaysia has a real opportunity to benefit from this global momentum, provided that an innovative and supportive regulatory environment is established. Tang highlighted that Luno commands 90% of the regulated market share in Malaysia. “As for the number of crypto investors, Luno have over one million customers investing in the crypto market through our platform,” he shared. Conclusion With a solid performance in 1H25 and a convergence of global and local tailwinds, Tang emphasised that Malaysia’s cryptocurrency market stands on firm footing. “If regulatory frameworks continue to evolve in tandem with market needs, the country could cement its place as a Southeast Asian hub for digital asset innovation and investment in the months ahead,” he said. title: KLCI Risks Deeper Pullback
body: Most Asian markets wavered alongside Wall St overnight plunge, as persistent US tariff jitters ahead of 1 Aug deadline eclipsed the latest China 2Q25 GDP print and a fresh US nod for NVDA chip sales to China. In the US, the Dow rose 232 pts after a 437-pt drop previously, as traders weighed mixed earnings from mega stocks (GS, BAC, MS, JNJ) and softer-than-expected PPI data following sticky CPI print a day ago. Sentiment improved further after Trump dismissed reports of plans to fire Powell, despite ongoing criticism over high Fed rates and the costly Fed HQ renovation. Focus now shifts to Q2 earnings with TSMC, ASML, Netflix, and PepsiCo on deck, while key macro data—retail sales and consumer sentiment—will be pivotal for Fed rate trajectory amid mounting inflation and trade risks. Domestically, the KLCI tumbled 13.9 pts to 1,511.5, weighed down by lingering uncertainty over US-Malaysia tariff negotiations, the risks of potential US export controls on AI chip shipments to Malaysia and persistent foreign outflows. Sentiment took a further hit after Indonesia secured a 19% tariff deal with the US, threatening Malaysia’s export competitive edge in ASEAN. Foreign investors remained net sellers (-RM174m; July MTD: -RM542m; YTD: -RM12.66bn), extending their exit streak. In contrast, local retailers (+RM173m; July MTD: -RM34m; YTD: +RM1.62bn) and institutions (+RM1m; July MTD: +RM576m; YTD: +RM11.04bn) stepped in as major support pillars. With the breakdown below key support at 1,528 (20-day MA) and 1,518 (trendline), the KLCI risks a deeper pullback toward 1,500 and 1,489 (23 June low). On the upside, a swift reclaim above 1,518 is crucial to reignite bullish momentum, with resistance seen at 1,528, 1,539 (23.6% FR) and1,551 (4 July high). MARKET OUTLOOK Amid persistent foreign outflows and external headwinds, the KLCI is likely to be stuck in consolidation ahead of the US-Malaysia tariff decision and clarity on potential US export curbs on AI chip shipments. Domestically, the upcoming August results season may add pressure, with looming policy shifts—fuel and electricity subsidy rationalisations, port tariff hikes, and SST expansion in 2H25—set to dampen consumer sentiment and cloud earnings visibility. title: Gold Cools Off In Ringgit, Traders Eye US$3,250 Support
body: Gold prices in Malaysia slipped in early trading, tracking a mild global consolidation phase despite recent bullish attempts in the international market. As of 2.25 am New York time, gold was priced at RM454,931.55 per kg, down RM2,783.89 or 0.61%. On a per-gram basis, the price fell RM83.67 or 0.59%, reflecting a slight retreat after steady gains seen over the past six months. Despite the day’s pullback, gold remains firmly higher on longer-term horizons up +16.98% over six months and +24.29% year-on-year, with five- and twenty-year returns of +83.85% and +789.01% respectively. RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research), in a note released, said the COMEX Gold futures recorded a “fresh positive price action” overnight, opening at US$3,330.50 and closing higher at US$3,359.10. Prices traded between US$3,326.10 and US$3,385.80, forming a bullish candlestick and maintaining levels above the 50-day simple moving average (SMA). However, the bank noted that the 20-day SMA is now “rounding downwards,” pointing to possible near-term weakness. “The commodity may undergo further consolidation before staging a fresh attempt to resume the upside movement,” RHB said. Support is expected at US$3,250, followed by a stop-loss threshold at US$3,150, while resistance is seen at US$3,450 and US$3,600. RHB Research recommends traders retain their long positions initiated at US$3,402.40 and keep a bullish trading bias for now. The movement comes amid mixed signals in the broader market, with traders closely watching inflation data and US Federal Reserve rate expectations, both of which heavily influence gold as a safe-haven asset. title: Ringgit Slips Against US Dollar As Greenback Strengthens
body: The Malaysian ringgit opened lower against the US dollar on Wednesday, pressured by a stronger greenback as expectations for an imminent interest rate cut by the United States faded. At 8 am, the local currency traded at 4.2480/2575 per US dollar, down from Tuesday’s close of 4.2395/2440. US Inflation Data Dents Rate Cut Hopes Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the latest US Consumer Price Index (CPI) report, released on Tuesday, showed inflation accelerating, reducing the likelihood of a Federal Reserve rate cut this month. “The US CPI came in at 2.7 per cent higher year-on-year in June from 2.4 per cent in the preceding month and similarly, the core CPI rose 2.9 per cent during June after sustaining 2.8 per cent increases for three consecutive months,” he told local media. Dr Mohd Afzanizam also pointed to China’s economic performance, noting that second-quarter gross domestic product (GDP) growth moderated to 5.2 per cent from 5.4 per cent in the previous quarter. This slowdown contributed to a 0.15 per cent weakening of the Chinese yuan against the US dollar, which traded at 7.1825 yuan. “In light of the latest US CPI and China’s GDP, the ringgit could experience some knee-jerk reaction with the US dollar-ringgit pair at around RM4.24–RM4.26 today,” he added. Despite its decline versus the greenback, the ringgit showed resilience against other major currencies. It strengthened to 2.8552/8618 against the Japanese yen from 2.8702/8734, firmed to 5.6893/7021 versus the British pound from 5.7047/7107, and rose to 4.9311/9421 against the euro from 4.9539/9591. Against ASEAN currencies, the ringgit’s performance was mixed. It edged up against the Singapore dollar to 3.3066/3145 from 3.3095/3133 and gained slightly against the Thai baht to 13.0355/0783 from 13.0784/0988. However, it slipped against the Indonesian rupiah to 261.1/261.8 from 260.6/261.0 and dipped against the Philippine peso to 7.49/7.51 from 7.47/7.49. title: Stock Today: Zetrix AI Dips After Bursa Fines Directors
body: Zetrix AI Bhd shares fell 5.6% to RM0.93 as of 11.56 am, following a public reprimand and RM150,000 fines imposed on seven directors by Bursa Malaysia. The penalties relate to breaching Main Market listing requirements by issuing a misleading announcement in July 2023 concerning a government collection agent appointment . The drop comes amid broader weakness in local tech stocks, with foreign investors withdrawing a net US$2.7 billion from Malaysian equities year‑to‑date, a trend blamed on global trade uncertainties . Zetrix’s decline adds to pressure on the technology sector as confidence wanes. Earlier, in late June, the company rebranded from MyEG Services to Zetrix AI, reflecting its pivot towards artificial intelligence and blockchain services . This shift was underlined by news of a strong quarterly performance: revenue of RM300 million and net profit rising 16%, largely driven by its blockchain-based platform rollout across Southeast Asia . However, those fundamentals have taken a back seat to governance concerns following the Bursa action. In response, Zetrix AI has applied for a judicial review against the reprimand, signalling it will dispute the regulator’s findings . Market watchers will be watching closely to see if enforcement action and investor sentiment continue to weigh on the stock, or whether strong earnings momentum can offer support. title: Stock Today: Hong Leong Slides Slightly As Investors React To Global Financial Headwinds And Local Rate Cut
body: Hong Leong Financial Group (HLFG) was trading at RM16.24 as of 2.10 pm, down 0.12%, amid cautious sentiment in the financial sector both globally and locally. The stock saw thin trading volume, reflecting investor wariness. Global hedge fund positioning is weighing on financial counters, with recent data showing a continued reduction in exposure to banking stocks in favour of defensive consumer staples. This shift comes ahead of key US inflation data and major bank earnings, heightening uncertainty in financial markets. Domestically, Bank Negara Malaysia cut the overnight policy rate by 25 basis points to 2.75% on July 9, citing external risks including escalating US tariffs and global trade friction. While the rate cut is expected to stimulate loan growth, it also pressures net interest margins across the banking industry. Despite sector headwinds, HLFG’s fundamentals remain relatively steady. The group recently posted a 0.4% rise in profit after tax and minority interest (PATAMI) to RM2.4 billion for the first nine months of FY2025, driven by resilient commercial banking contributions. Its key subsidiary, Hong Leong Bank, also reported a 9.2% increase in normalised profit before associates, underpinned by healthy topline growth and cost control. Market sentiment on HLFG remains largely optimistic. Analysts maintain a ‘Buy’ rating with an average target price around RM21.87, representing significant upside potential. The stock trades at a forward price-to-earnings ratio of approximately 5.7 times and a price-to-book ratio of 0.58, suggesting it remains undervalued relative to fundamentals. As macroeconomic pressures and global financial developments continue to unfold, HLFG’s stock performance will depend on its ability to sustain lending growth while maintaining asset quality. Investor focus will remain on earnings guidance from regional banking peers and further monetary policy actions at home and abroad. title: Stock Today: AEON Ease As Consumer Sentiment Wavers
body: Shares of AEON Co (M) Bhd fell 2.13% to RM1.38 by mid-afternoon, reflecting investor caution amid mixed signals from both global and domestic markets. Trading volume stood at 880,200 shares, as some profit-taking followed the stock’s recent rally to its 2025 peak of RM1.41. The sell-off coincides with signs of consumer belt-tightening both locally and overseas. Malaysian retail indicators have shown early signs of softness as inflationary pressures persist. The recent strengthening of the ringgit has curtailed tourism and imported raw material costs, but also weighed on exporters and retailers who rely on tourists and foreign sales. Globally, elevated US inflation readings this year have triggered expectations of continued interest rate support from the Federal Reserve, diminishing risk appetite and pressuring consumer-focused shares. As Malaysia is not immune, AEON shares have taken some of the fallout, in line with declines across the broader consumer services sector. Analysts note that AEON’s earnings are closely linked to domestic consumer health. The stock’s current valuation at approximately 18 times forward price-to-earnings ratios reflects a mix of optimism over stable retail footfall and caution about possible policy tightening and slower economic momentum in the second half. Despite near-term volatility, AEON remains monitored for domestic economic triggers: upcoming retail sales data, developments from the central bank, and changes in consumer spending habits during the festive season. Investors will also be watching broader market developments, including global inflation trends and monetary policy cues, to gauge whether consumer-facing equities can regain momentum. title: Ringgit Opens Higher On Strong China Data, Tracks Yuan Gains
body: The ringgit opened stronger against the US dollar on Tuesday, buoyed by gains in the Chinese yuan following upbeat economic data from China, said Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid. As of 8am, the ringgit stood at 4.2445/2670 against the greenback, improving from Monday’s close of 4.2505/2560. According to Mohd Afzanizam, China’s positive June readings, including export growth, new loan issuances and money supply expansion, point to encouraging outcomes from recent stimulus measures. title: Markets Hold Steady Ahead Of Data Deluge, Nasdaq Hits Fresh Record
body: Wall Street closed with modest gains on Monday as traders braced for a busy week of corporate earnings and economic data, showing little reaction to US President Donald Trump’s latest tariff threats targeting the European Union and Mexico. The Nasdaq Composite rose 0.27% to 20,640.33, clinching its seventh record close since 27 June. The S&P 500 climbed 0.14% to 6,268.56, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average edged up 0.20% to 44,459.65. Trading activity was muted, with 15.43 billion shares changing hands below the 20-day average of 17.62 billion. Trump had pledged over the weekend to impose a 30% tariff on most EU and Mexican imports from 1 August if no agreement is reached, but markets barely flinched. The EU has delayed retaliatory measures until early August, signalling hope for ongoing negotiations. “Investors are largely desensitised to Trump’s frequent tariff announcements and policy reversals,” said one market strategist. The energy sector was the biggest laggard, down 1.2%, after Trump’s separate threat of tariffs on Russian oil buyers sent US crude down 2.2%, potentially shaking global energy flows. Still, communication services led the gains, rising 0.7%. Netflix and Warner Bros. Discovery provided a boost, with the latter’s new Superman film enjoying a strong box office debut. Bitcoin surpassed US$120,000, lifting crypto-related stocks. Coinbase gained 1.8% and MicroStrategy surged 3.8%. Meanwhile, Waters Corp plunged 13.8% after announcing a US$17.5 billion merger with Becton Dickinson’s diagnostics arm. Looking ahead, investors will be watching consumer price data on Tuesday, followed by producer and import price indexes on Wednesday, key indicators of how recent tariffs are affecting inflation and supply chains. The second-quarter earnings season also kicks off, with major Wall Street banks set to report. title: KLCI Expected To Consolidate Amid Global Tariff Threats
body: The Kuala Lumpur Composite Index (KLCI) is likely to remain in a consolidation phase in the near term as investors grapple with a confluence of external and domestic factors, according to a recent market outlook by HLIB. The report highlights that renewed tariff rhetoric from President Donald Trump, targeting key US trading partners, is a significant concern. This adds to a backdrop of rising global uncertainties, including escalating trade tensions, new tariff threats, and ongoing logistics disruptions, all of which are increasingly weighing on business confidence and global growth prospects. Domestically, key overhangs include uncertainty surrounding US-Malaysia tariff negotiations, with a potentially prolonged process to ease the 25% import duties ahead of an August 1 deadline. Additionally, risks associated with potential US export controls on AI chip shipments to Malaysia could dampen sentiment within the vital technology and semiconductor sectors. The local market continues to see persistent foreign outflows, with net selling amounting to RM280 million in July month-to-date. Year-to-date, net foreign selling stands at RM12.4 billion, slightly improved from a peak of RM12.9 billion as of April 22. Furthermore, domestic policy changes are expected to contribute to market pressures. The looming subsidy rationalization for fuel and electricity, alongside anticipated port tariff hikes and the expansion of the Sales and Service Tax (SST) in the second half of 2025, may dampen consumer sentiment and impact corporate earnings visibility. HLIB provided key support levels for the KLCI at 1,500, 1,510, and 1,528, while resistance levels are identified at 1,551, 1,563, and 1,570. title: Bursa Opens Higher Amid Regional Optimism And Strong China Data
body: Bursa Malaysia opened slightly higher on Tuesday, tracking positive regional sentiment following upbeat economic data from China and easing trade tensions, providing a boost to investor confidence. At 9.01am, the FBM KLCI advanced 1.76 points to 1,539.27 from Monday’s close of 1,537.51. The index opened at 1,538.91. Market breadth was positive with gainers outpacing losers, 179 to 112, while 277 counters remained unchanged. Turnover stood at 168.93 million shares valued at RM73.82 million. Investors were encouraged by China’s latest June data, which showed improvements in exports and credit growth, signalling the effectiveness of recent stimulus efforts. This lifted risk sentiment across Asian markets, with the ringgit also strengthening to 4.2445 against the US dollar. Meanwhile, Wall Street’s muted gains overnight, despite fresh tariff threats from US President Donald Trump, showed resilience, as markets now expect constructive negotiations ahead of a packed week of US economic data and earnings reports. Locally, energy and financial counters showed early momentum, while tech-related stocks gained traction on spillover demand from US tech optimism. Analysts expect cautious optimism to persist ahead of key earnings season releases and macroeconomic updates globally. title: Bursa Dips Midday Amid US Tariff Concerns And Global Market Jitters
body: Bursa Malaysia ended the morning session in negative territory on Tuesday, with the benchmark FBM KLCI easing 4.25 points or 0.28% to 1,533.26 as investors adopted a cautious stance following renewed trade tensions between the United States and the European Union. Broader market weakness was seen across key indices, with the FBM 70 down 36.13 points to 16,751.07, the FBM Emas lower by 27.60 points at 11,530.86, and the Shariah Index falling 27.79 points to 11,532.81. The F4GBM index, which tracks ESG-compliant stocks, slipped 2.56 points to 932.42. The subdued sentiment came as the European Union warned it had prepared tariffs on US goods totalling €21 billion (US$24.5 billion) in response to Washington’s move to impose a 30% tariff on European imports beginning 1 August. Market participants are now watching for any retaliation that could further rattle global supply chains and impact trade-exposed counters on Bursa. Zetrix AI Berhad was the most active counter at midday, falling 5.5 sen or 5.58% to 93 sen with over 1.14 billion shares traded, as the tech-heavy stock came under pressure from broader profit-taking. NextGen (NEXG) rose half a sen to 47.5 sen while NatGate Holdings jumped 8 sen to RM1.69 on robust volume, possibly reflecting sector rotation towards semiconductor and AI-related counters amid regional interest in the space. Meanwhile, sentiment remained cautious ahead of US Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell’s testimony later this week, which may provide further clarity on interest rate direction. The ongoing uncertainty over China’s economic recovery and Malaysia’s upcoming Budget 2026 policy signals are also weighing on local investor sentiment. title: Stock Today: Top Glove Grips Gains As Sector Sentiment Improves
body: Top Glove Corporation Bhd’s shares rose 1.46% to RM0.695 as of 3.33pm on Monday, buoyed by investor sentiment around a potential recovery in the glove and healthcare sector. The stock opened at RM0.685 and hit an intraday high of RM0.705 before retreating slightly. Trading volume was robust, with over 86 million shares changing hands. The counter’s buy volume stood at 1.84 million shares, while sell volume was heavier at 28.48 million. The uptick in share price comes amid renewed optimism over improved average selling prices (ASPs) and lower raw material costs in the glove industry. Analysts have recently noted that the sector may be nearing a bottom after more than two years of declining margins. Top Glove’s performance also coincides with expectations of increased demand from key markets like the US and Europe, following signs of restocking activities and inventory normalisation. Investors are additionally keeping an eye on the upcoming quarterly earnings season, hoping for signs that glove makers are beginning to stabilise after aggressive cost-cutting and capacity rationalisation. Despite the slight rise, Top Glove remains far off its pre-pandemic highs, and analysts remain mixed on the near-term outlook given ongoing global competition and price pressures from China-based manufacturers. title: Stock Today: Genting Slips At Midday Amid Weak Market Mood, Global Growth Concerns
body: Genting Bhd saw its shares dip 1.29% to RM3.07 at midday on Monday, as broader market sentiment remained cautious amid regional growth concerns and a lack of strong domestic catalysts. The stock opened at RM3.11 before slipping to an intraday low of RM3.06, with over 23 million shares traded as of 12.30pm. The dip also followed a weak showing on the FBMKLCI, which hovered marginally lower at 1,535.63 points. Investor sentiment remained tepid, in part due to lingering concerns over China’s slowing economic momentum. Soft trade data and cautious consumer recovery in the world’s second-largest economy have weighed on regional equities, particularly those in consumer-linked sectors such as Genting. The group’s diversified exposure, particularly in gaming, leisure, and hospitality through Genting Malaysia and international operations, leaves it sensitive to macroeconomic shifts, tourism trends, and consumer spending. With China remaining a key tourism market for regional gaming hubs, slow recovery in outbound travel may continue to impact investor confidence in the near term. Adding to the pressure, investors are also keeping a close eye on developments around global central bank policies and geopolitical tensions, which have stirred volatility in recent weeks. Despite the decline, Genting remains above its early-year lows, having traded within the RM2.75–RM3.30 range over the past six months. Any further cues on China’s economic stimulus measures or recovery in global travel flows could influence the group’s near-term share trajectory. As of now, no new company-specific developments have been announced to drive momentum either way, leaving Genting to move broadly in line with prevailing market forces. title: Stock Today: Alliance Bank Edges Up Amid Cautious Optimism In Financial Sector
body: Shares of Alliance Bank Malaysia Bhd (ABMB) rose 0.44% to RM4.55 as of 12.02pm today, with over 520,000 shares changing hands, reflecting a mild uptick in investor sentiment despite broader market uncertainty. The stock, which opened at RM4.55 and reached a high of RM4.57 earlier in the session, remains within a steady range seen over the past three months. Since mid-April, ABMB has generally hovered between RM4.36 and RM4.57, showing resilience amid a flurry of regulatory updates and macroeconomic pressures. The slight gain comes as the financial sector braces for potential shifts in the interest rate environment, following Bank Negara Malaysia’s recent signal that it may hold the Overnight Policy Rate steady in the near term to support domestic growth amid global economic volatility. Investors may also be digesting broader concerns linked to the government’s ongoing subsidy rationalisation efforts, which could indirectly affect consumer sentiment and lending activity. However, banks like Alliance, with strong retail and SME portfolios, may benefit from improved margins should interest rates remain elevated longer than expected. Market watchers are also keeping an eye on corporate earnings season, which could provide clues on asset quality trends, especially for mid-tier banks navigating a softer property and SME lending environment. With its stock currently trending near the higher end of its six-month trading range, Alliance Bank remains a counter to watch as sector-related catalysts and fiscal policy developments unfold in the coming weeks. title: STI Opens Higher Amid Regional Optimism, Banks Lead Gains
body: The Straits Times Index (STI) opened firmer on Monday, gaining 15.56 points or 0.38% to 4,103.37 at 9.04am, supported by gains in heavyweight banking counters and broader optimism across Asia despite lingering concerns over global trade tensions. Among the top movers, DBS rose 0.5% to S$46.22 while OCBC Bank added to the upbeat mood at S$16.98. UOB remained unchanged at S$36.95. Singtel hovered at S$4.06 while SIA was flat at S$7.29. The iEdge suite of indices also saw positive momentum, with the iEdge-OCBC Singapore Low Carbon Select 40 Capped Index up at 3,174.86 and the iEdge S-REIT Leaders Index opening at 1,026.57. The iEdge Southeast Asia+ TECH Index, which reflects regional tech sentiment, stood strong at 4,241.16. Investors continued to keep a close watch on global developments after renewed US tariff threats over the weekend. However, Singapore’s recent stronger-than-expected GDP growth and construction-led recovery have helped buffer market sentiment, with investors turning their focus to domestic resilience and regional earnings. Market participants are expected to closely track upcoming corporate earnings and inflation readings from key global economies, which could set the tone for the STI’s momentum throughout the week. title: Singapore’s Largest IPO Sees Muted Debut
body: Despite its initial public offering (IPO) being oversubscribed, market reaction to a data centre-focused real estate investment trust (REIT) that was billed as the largest to debut on the Singapore bourse since 2017 was muted on the first day of trade. The NTT DC REIT, which started trading on the Singapore Exchange (SGX) at 2pm on Monday (Jul 14), opened at US$1.02, above its offer price of US$1. During the afternoon, the REIT’s share price rose as high as US$1.03, before closing at US$1.The trust raised a total of US$773 million and is backed by Singapore’s sovereign wealth fund GIC and Japan’s telecommunications giant NTT Group. It is the biggest listing on the exchange since 2017, when fibre network-centred NetLink NBN Trust raised S$2.3 billion (US$1.8 billion). NTT Group is the world’s third-largest data centre provider through its global data centre business NTT GDC, according to the IPO’s prospectus. Mr Yutaka Torigoe, chief executive officer of the manager of NTT DC REIT, said he was encouraged by the “excellent debut” and said it underscores confidence in the quality of the REIT’s portfolio, its growth prospects and the outlook for data centres globally. title: Ringgit Rises On US Tariff Shock, Gains Against Major Currencies
body: The ringgit opened stronger against the US dollar on Monday, buoyed by investor reaction to new US tariff announcements targeting major trading partners. At 8am, the local note rose to 4.2405/2635 versus the greenback, up from Friday’s close of 4.2475/2525. The gains followed President Donald Trump’s weekend announcement of fresh tariffs: 30% on goods from the European Union and Mexico, and 35% on Canadian products starting 1 August. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said, “Clearly, the tariff policy instrument has been weaponised by the US to address economic imbalances.” He warned that global growth risks remain high, and inflation pressures in the US could complicate the Federal Reserve’s rate cut outlook. “The ringgit is expected to remain within a narrow range of RM4.24 to RM4.25 amid ongoing global uncertainties,” he added. The ringgit also recorded gains against several major and regional currencies. It advanced against the Japanese yen to 2.8792/8950 from 2.8893/8929, and strengthened against the British pound to 5.7234/7544 from 5.7524/7592. Against the euro, it climbed to 4.9546/9815 from 4.9679/9737. Within the region, the ringgit appreciated against the Singapore dollar to 3.3119/3303 from 3.3186/3228, edged up versus the Indonesian rupiah to 261.4/263.0 from 261.8/262.3, and strengthened against the Philippine peso to 7.51/7.55 from 7.52/7.53. title: Nestlé Tops Losers As Market Ends Lower On Weaker Turnover
body: The stock market closed in negative territory on July 14 as weaker turnover and cautious investor sentiment weighed on the broader market, with heavyweights like Nestlé (M) Bhd leading the decline. The benchmark index softened as 514 counters declined, outpacing 432 gainers, while 510 stocks were unchanged, 962 remained untraded and nine were suspended. Total turnover slipped to 2.93 billion shares worth RM1.67 billion, down from 3.37 billion shares valued at RM2.30 billion on July 11, reflecting a slowdown in market participation. Nestlé was the day’s top loser, dropping 64 sen to RM76.74, followed by Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd down 28 sen to RM20.38 and Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd, which fell 22 sen to RM20.78. Other laggards for the trading session include Dutch Lady Milk Industries Bhd and Hong Leong Industries Bhd which lost 20 sen each to close at RM28.28 and at RM13.60, respectively. On the gainers’ side, Fraser & Neave Holdings Bhd and Hong Leong Bank Bhd both rose 38 sen, closing at RM28.98 and RM19.56, respectively. Other notable risers included Apollo Foods Holdings Bhd, which added 17 sen to RM6.40, Kotra Industries Bhd, which grew 12 sen to RM4.23, and Far East Holdings Bhd, which increased 11 sen to RM3.70. Investors remained cautious amid global trade tensions and ahead of key earnings announcements, keeping the market range-bound with light trading activity. title: Hang Seng Index Futures Heat Up, Resistance In Sight
body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) is maintaining its long position on the Hang Seng Index Futures (HSIF), as strong bullish momentum continued last Friday with a 137-point gain, closing at 24,160 points. According to RHB Research, the index began the session at 24,014 points, fluctuated between 23,884 and 24,532 points, before closing with a bullish candlestick. In after-hours trading, it dipped slightly by 72 points to 24,088. The research house noted that the HSIF is now trading above the 20-day simple moving average (SMA), with the relative strength index (RSI) trending above the 50% mark, both indicating growing bullish momentum. The rising 50-day SMA also continues to provide technical support for the positive setup. RHB Research sees potential for the index to stage a fresh breakout above 24,500 points, which would further solidify the bullish outlook. A breakout could pave the way for a push toward the next resistance level at 26,000 points. The research house advises traders to maintain long positions, first initiated at 21,416 points on 14 April, and recommends a stop-loss at 23,000 points. Key support levels are at 23,000 and 22,000 points, while resistance lies at 24,500 and 26,000 points. title: Gold Glitters Again With Gains In US$ And RM
body: Gold prices continued their upward climb on Monday, buoyed by strong technical momentum and safe-haven demand. As of writing, gold was trading at RM459.31 per gram in Malaysia, up 0.07% or RM0.34, while the price per gram rose 0.08% or RM11.07 today alone. On the international front, COMEX gold closed last Friday’s session US$38.30 higher at US$3,364, signalling a firm continuation of bullish momentum. RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) said the precious metal has now moved above both the 20- and 50-day simple moving averages (SMA), with the Relative Strength Index (RSI) also climbing past the 50% mark, both indicators pointing to growing buying strength. The firm expects gold to maintain its upward trend, eyeing a near-term target of US$3,450, with further gains possible if resistance is breached. “The bulls are technically in control,” RHB Research noted, advising traders to hold their long positions initiated at US$3,402.40 and placing stop-loss at US$3,150. Immediate support levels are at US$3,250 and US$3,150, while resistance is seen at US$3,450 and US$3,600. Over a longer horizon, gold has risen 26.07% year-on-year and 17.76% in the last six months, amid persistent geopolitical tensions, rate-cut expectations and demand from central banks. The strengthening of gold prices in RM also reflects the local currency’s softness and investors’ continued appetite for inflation hedges. With mounting uncertainty in global markets, gold appears to be regaining its shine as a defensive asset. title: Global Markets Dip As Trump’s Tariff Threats Rattle Investors
body: Global markets edged lower on July 14 as renewed US tariff threats from President Donald Trump unsettled investor sentiment, just as earnings season kicks off and key economic data looms. Reuters reported that Wall Street and European futures slipped in Asian trading after Trump announced plans to impose 30% tariffs on most imports from the European Union (EU) and Mexico starting Aug 1, escalating trade tensions. While the EU vowed to seek a negotiated settlement, Germany’s finance minister called for retaliation if tariffs proceed. Despite the tough talk, market reaction remained measured. The MSCI Asia-Pacific Index (ex-Japan) dipped 0.1%, while Japan’s Nikkei was flat. Chinese blue chips rose 0.2%, buoyed by stronger-than-expected export growth of 5.8% in June, even as exports to the US declined nearly 10%. In Europe, EUROSTOXX 50 futures fell 0.6%, DAX futures dropped 0.7% and FTSE futures held steady. In the US, S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures each eased 0.4%, ahead of a busy earnings week led by major banks. Corporate profits for S&P 500 firms are now expected to grow 5.8% year-over-year, down from April’s 10.2% forecast. Investors are bracing for a volatile week, balancing geopolitical risks with a flood of corporate earnings and crucial US economic data, including June inflation and retail sales figures.
