title: CIMB Forecasts New Decade Low Earnings Base For O&G Sector
body: CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) has maintained a NEUTRAL stance on the oil and gas sector, citing structural headwinds that continue to cloud the earnings outlook for 2025. The brokerage’s view follows expectations of a subdued second quarter, with sector-wide core net profit projected to decline 8.8% quarter-on-quarter before staging a 24.1% rebound in the following quarter. Despite this, the firm forecasts a 6.3% year-on-year contraction in core net profit for calendar year 2025, setting what it described as a new decade-low earnings base. The house reported that the weakness will likely be led by a sharp earnings drop from Bumi Armada, down an estimated 42% quarter-on-quarter due to a 70% reduction in charter rates for FPSO Kraken following a contract revision. Petronas-linked companies are also set to post softer results. MISC is expected to record a 24.9% earnings drop without the benefit of a one-off gain from FPSO Bunga Kertas in the prior quarter, while Petronas Chemicals’ ongoing operational disruptions and Petronas Dagangan’s margin pressure are set to weigh on their respective performances. CIMB Securities highlighted Yinson’s expected turnaround and Dayang’s post-monsoon activity ramp-up as positive offsets, with both names likely to deliver quarter-on-quarter improvements. However, the broader sector remains pressured by a muted order book, margin compression and recurring operational issues. The firm also flagged a potential capital expenditure pullback by Petronas, which could further dampen sector sentiment. With Brent crude averaging US$70.72 per barrel year-to-date, below Petronas’s US$75–80 guidance range, the house noted that a possible RM6 billion cut to the national oil company’s 2025 spending is on the table. This could affect project rollouts and profitability, particularly for firms with heavy Petronas contract exposure, such as Dayang and Dialog. Despite this caution, CIMB Securities believes the anticipated ramp-up in plant turnaround works from the fourth quarter of 2025 and increased decommissioning contracts could provide some upside. Petronas’s roadmap includes 153 wells and 37 offshore structures earmarked for removal over the next three years, potentially unlocking RM2–3 billion worth of contract value. Dayang is viewed as a strong contender for this work, alongside names like T7 Global, Uzma and Velesto. The brokerage continues to favour MISC and Dialog as its top sector picks, citing their recurring income streams and defensive balance sheets. MISC’s long-term charters in LNG, petroleum and FPSO segments offer earnings visibility, while Dialog’s high terminal utilisation and strong EPCC prospects enhance its earnings quality. The research house also retains BUY calls on Bumi Armada, Yinson and Dayang, with HOLD ratings on Petronas Chemicals and Petronas Dagangan. Lotte Chemical Titan is the only name in the sector with a REDUCE recommendation. title: Asian Markets Falter As Tariff Tensions Return, Wall Street Futures Weigh
body: Asian stocks slipped on Monday as Wall Street futures retreated, pressured by renewed tariff threats from US President Donald Trump, who announced plans to impose a 30% duty on most imports from the European Union and Mexico beginning 1 August. The European Union responded by extending its suspension of countermeasures until early August, expressing hope for a negotiated solution, though Germany’s finance minister called for firm retaliation if the tariffs proceed. Investors, however, appeared more cautious than alarmed. MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan was largely flat, while Japan’s Nikkei fell 0.5%. US futures showed weakness, with S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures down 0.4% each. Wall Street’s earnings season, which kicks off this week with major US banks reporting, is adding to the market’s watchlist. “It’s difficult to price the array of headlines purportedly defining where tariffs will sit from August when negotiations are ongoing,” said Taylor Nugent, senior markets economist at NAB. “The muted market response could be resilience—or just complacency.” Analysts at BofA said the S&P 500 may still post a modest 2% earnings beat, noting a significant downgrade from earlier forecasts of 10.2% growth. Consensus now sees just 4% growth, down from 13% the previous quarter. Meanwhile, political pressure on the Federal Reserve is escalating. While Chair Jerome Powell remains patient on rate cuts, White House economic adviser Kevin Hassett suggested Trump might consider removing Powell over cost overruns at the Fed’s headquarters. Trump echoed the sentiment, stating Sunday it would be “a great thing” if Powell stepped down. Bond markets saw a slight safety bid, with 10-year US Treasury yields holding at 4.41%. Markets slightly increased their pricing for rate cuts in 2026. Traders are closely eyeing the US Consumer Price Index for June due Tuesday, which could reveal early inflationary effects from tariffs. Additional data expected this week includes producer and import prices, along with retail sales figures. From China, June trade data is due Monday, followed by industrial output, GDP and retail sales on Tuesday. In the currency space, the euro weakened 0.2% to US$1.1665 on the tariff escalation, while the US dollar added 0.1% against the yen to 147.53. The greenback rose 0.3% to 18.6900 against the Mexican peso as President Claudia Sheinbaum expressed optimism for a trade deal before the August deadline. Commodities saw mild moves, with gold gaining 0.3% to US$3,366.00 an ounce on safe-haven demand. Oil prices ticked up as markets speculated that Trump may announce new sanctions on Russia, targeting buyers of Russian crude. Brent edged up to US$70.45 per barrel, while US crude hovered at US$68.50. body: Wall Street closed slightly lower for the week ended July 11, as renewed trade tensions weighed on sentiment despite fresh record highs in major indices midweek. title: Wall Street Hits New Highs Despite Trump’s 50% Tariff On Brazil
body: US stocks closed higher Thursday, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq reaching new record highs, as investors shrugged off President Donald Trump’s announcement of a 50% tariff on Brazilian goods, the highest yet in a week of escalating trade measures. The sharp tariff move, aimed at Latin America’s largest economy, marked a departure from the 10% baseline levied on other nations during the so-called “Liberation Day” wave of trade letters. The Brazilian real, which plunged 2.3% on Wednesday, rebounded 0.8% against the dollar following the announcement. “Markets have largely dismissed the week’s tariff announcements, but Brazil’s treatment caused a shock,” said William Jackson of Capital Economics. “Countries with tense US ties now look increasingly exposed.” The White House also confirmed a 50% tariff on copper imports, effective Aug. 1, sending copper prices and mining stocks surging. London’s FTSE 100 rallied to a fresh record, buoyed by the sector. Other major market movers included WK Kellogg, whose shares jumped after Ferrero confirmed a US$3 billion takeover of the cereal giant. Despite global trade tensions, bond yields edged up slightly — the 10-year Treasury yield rose to 4.35% from 4.34% — while crude prices dropped. WTI futures fell 2.6%. Bitcoin continued its bull run, hitting a new all-time high above US$113,000. title: Ringgit Caught Between Dovish Daly And Patient Musalem
body: The ringgit opened marginally softer against the US dollar on Friday, as mixed signals from the US Federal Reserve and a slightly firmer US Dollar Index (DXY) continued to influence sentiment. title: Bursa Opens Flat Amid Global Tariff Tensions And US Fed Uncertainty
body: Bursa Malaysia opened flat on Friday, mirroring cautious sentiment across regional markets as investors weighed the impact of fresh US tariff moves and mixed signals from the US Federal Reserve. Investor sentiment was clouded by US President Donald Trump’s latest 50% tariff imposition on Brazilian goods, a move that spooked emerging markets and raised concerns of broader trade disruptions. Meanwhile, hawkish and dovish remarks from US Fed officials have left markets uncertain about the timing of interest rate cuts, further curbing risk appetite. In early trade, TWL Holdings Bhd led the actives but slipped half a sen to 2.5 sen on 81.4 million shares, followed by A1AKK which was unchanged at 25 sen. Jiankun International Bhd, EA Holdings, and HKB also traded flat, signalling subdued retail participation. Markets are expected to remain rangebound as investors digest recent global developments and await firmer policy cues both domestically and abroad. body: Bitcoin surged to a record high on July 10, driven by renewed institutional interest and supportive signals from US President Donald Trump’s administration, Reuters reported. The world’s largest cryptocurrency climbed to an unprecedented US$116,046.44 as of 2127 GMT, surpassing the previous peak of US$113,734.64 reached earlier in the day. Bitcoin is now up roughly 24% year-to-date, reflecting bullish sentiment across the digital asset market. The rally is being fuelled in part by growing demand from institutional investors, as well as a wave of regulatory optimism under the Trump administration, which has expressed openness to pro-crypto policies and innovation-friendly oversight. Ethereum, the second-largest cryptocurrency by market value, also gained momentum, rising 3.01% to US$2,905.24 as of 2130 GMT. title: Stock Today: Hong Leong Bank Slips Amid OPR Cut
body: As of 12.08pm, Hong Leong Bank’s share price fell 1.14%, trading at RM19.14, down RM0.22 on significantly lower volume compared with recent levels. The dip follows rising investor caution in light of domestic monetary policy developments and external economic pressures. The stock’s decline coincides with this week’s surprise 25‑basis‑point cut in Malaysia’s Overnight Policy Rate (OPR) to 2.75%. Banks generally face a margin squeeze due to lower lending rates, and Hong Leong Bank is no exception. Analysts from RHB Research and MIDF Research had previously noted that modest rate reductions could compress net interest margins by 1–2%, with smaller regional lenders bearing the brunt. Hong Leong, however, was identified by HLIB with the potential to better absorb the squeeze thanks to earlier reductions in fixed deposit rates and strengthened liquidity from a statutory reserve ratio cut. At the same time, the rally in ASEAN currencies, including the ringgit, has lifted sentiments in regional equities, yet with rate differentials narrowing, Malaysia’s financial stocks have seen mixed reactions. The firm’s support for mid‑caps has been buoyed by improved liquidity. However, caution persists as investors await quarterly earnings for more clarity. Hong Leong’s share drop today may also reflect tentative investor posture ahead of the updated OPR outlook, set to hinge on the Federal Reserve minutes and global trade tensions. Any further US tariff developments or slower regional growth could weigh on sentiment. Despite the dip, HLIB reaffirmed their OVERWEIGHT stance on the banking sector. They highlighted Hong Leong Bank as a resilient pick among peers, thanks to disciplined funding strategies and robust provisions that are likely to support its financial health through a potential interest-rate trough. The stock is expected to benefit from dividend stability and operational prudence in the coming quarters. Overall, while Hong Leong Bank shares face immediate pressure following policy rate changes, analysts remain optimistic about underlying fundamentals and the broader recovery potential within Malaysia’s banking sector. title: Ringgit Opens Firmer As Market Eyes Post-OPR Cut Momentum
body: The ringgit opened stronger against the US dollar on Thursday, defying expectations after Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) slashed the Overnight Policy Rate (OPR) by 25 basis points to 2.75% on Wednesday. At 8am, the local currency appreciated to 4.2350/2570 versus the greenback compared to Wednesday’s close of 4.2500/2540. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the move likely reflected an initial reaction from traders locking in gains. “The OPR decision is seen as timely, given heightened economic uncertainties following the United States’ tariff shocks,” he told Bernama. He said the rate cut should be positive for the ringgit from a broader perspective, adding that the USD/MYR pair could retrace towards the RM4.23–RM4.24 range today. “On that note, the ringgit could see some retracement after depreciating 0.27% at yesterday’s close of RM4.2520,” he added. He also noted that the US Dollar Index (DXY) held relatively stable at around 97.555 points, as attention shifted to the upcoming Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) minutes. The minutes suggested that members were open to interest rate cuts as early as the next meeting on July 29–30, 2025. Afzanizam further noted that the current US policy stance was “moderately restrictive” and inflation appeared to be easing. At the same time, the ringgit also opened higher against a basket of major currencies, except the Japanese yen. It rose against the British pound to 5.7579/7878 from 5.7787/7842 and improved against the euro to 4.9702/9960 from 4.9780/9827. However, it eased slightly versus the yen to 2.8987/9140 from 2.8983/9012. The local note was also stronger across the board against its ASEAN counterparts. It advanced against the Singapore dollar to 3.3096/3271 from 3.3182/3219, strengthened versus the Thai baht to 12.9796/13.0535 from 12.9946/13.0128, edged up against the Indonesian rupiah to 260.4/262.0 from 261.3/261.8, and firmed against the Philippine peso to 7.48/7.53 from 7.51/7.52. title: Nasdaq Hits New High Despite Tariff Storm As Tech Leads Wall Street Rally
body: Wall Street climbed higher overnight, brushing off escalating tariff threats from President Donald Trump, as investor confidence remained intact on the back of strong tech momentum and resilient economic indicators. The Nasdaq surged 0.94% to close at a fresh record of 20,611.34, fuelled by a rally in Nvidia, which briefly hit a market capitalisation of US$4 trillion. The S&P 500 gained 0.61% to finish at 6,263.26, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average added 0.49% to settle at 44,458.30. The Russell 2000, representing small caps, jumped 1.07% to 2,252.49, suggesting broader market optimism. Trump’s announcement of a 50% tariff on Brazilian imports, starting Aug 1, came after trading hours. While the move targeted Brazil over its legal actions against former president Jair Bolsonaro, investors appeared unfazed. Market watchers believe the most severe tariff threats may not materialise, with the Federal Reserve and global partners watching closely. Meanwhile, US Treasury yields continued to fall, with the 10-year yield settling at 4.339% amid strong demand for a US$39 billion bond auction. The VIX, Wall Street’s fear gauge, plunged over 5% to 15.94, signalling a drop in market anxiety. Other key market moves: Bitcoin dipped 0.48% to US$111,200.73 after reaching a record close the day before. Gold inched up 0.17% to US$3,326.80 , maintaining investor interest as a hedge. Crude oil slid 0.42% to US$68.09 on signs of rising US inventories. Copper futures fell 3.6% , reversing Tuesday’s record after Trump announced possible levies on the metal. Despite policy uncertainty, Wall Street appears to be betting on a sustained economic expansion, with traders still digesting Fed minutes that show Chair Jerome Powell in no rush to cut rates, despite political pressure. The coming sessions will likely hinge on further tariff details, corporate earnings, and inflation data expected later this week. title: Bursa Flatlines At Midday As Trade Tensions Loom And Rate Cuts Sink In
body: The FTSE Malaysia KLCI inched higher, trading at 1,529.47 (+0.02%), while the broader FBM70, FBMEMAS, and F4GBM indexes recorded modest gains in the range of 0.05–0.16%. The FBMSHA lagged slightly, down 0.07%. Trading activity remains selective, with small-cap and penny stocks dominating volumes , notably SAPNRG, ECOSHOP, ZETRIX, NEXG and MAGMA. Aside from these micro-movements, investors are eyeing several macro developments shaping market sentiment. First, this week’s 25bp cut in Malaysia’s Overnight Policy Rate to 2.75% has sparked speculation over the direction of banking sector earnings. While margin pressures are anticipated, analysts have emphasised that improved liquidity via the SRR cut and potential bond trading gains may cushion impacts. Internationally, investor focus has turned to the upcoming US executive actions, including an anticipated 25% across-the-board tariff set to take effect on August 1. The spectre of rising trade tension and its potential drag on commodity, shipping and manufacturing-linked listings on Bursa keeps a lid on broader appetite. At the same time, regional dynamics remain in play: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio is currently attending the ASEAN Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in Kuala Lumpur, adding a diplomatic element to investor consciousness. Sector-wise, the muted midday performance reflects this careful investor posture: banks and industrials are trading flat to subdued, while select small-caps in green energy and technology are outpacing on speculative flows. Notably, ECOSHOP is up by one sen on active volume nearing 41 million units, signalling retail interest in sustainability-themed plays. With the global trade backdrop clouding sentiment and domestic policy tightening in process, Bursa’s performance appears pinned between cautious optimism on interest rate relief and anxiety over external trade shocks. The midday lull may continue unless fresh triggers emerge, such as clarity on US tariff implementation, further OPR guidance, or tangible outcomes from the ASEAN meetings held in Kuala Lumpur. Investors are likely to remain focused on these evolving factors into the afternoon session. If Malaysian banks report resilience in response to the monetary easing or if US policymakers provide reassurance around trade policy, Bursa could see a late-day upside tilt. title: Wall Street Pauses Near Highs As Tariff Jitters, Fed Hopes Jostle Sentiment
body: US stocks struggled for direction overnight as investor optimism over possible Federal Reserve rate cuts was offset by renewed fears of a global trade war, following fresh tariff threats from former President Donald Trump. The S&P 500 was flat at 6,225.52, hovering near record highs but showing signs of exhaustion after a strong rally since April. The Nasdaq 100 also closed little changed, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.4%. Small-caps, represented by the Russell 2000, outperformed with a 0.7% gain. Markets were rattled after Trump declared that he would not extend the August deadline for introducing reciprocal tariffs and floated a 50% tariff on imports, particularly targeting China and the EU. Meanwhile, copper prices surged, with Freeport-McMoRan Inc. rallying on the news. Trump’s additional comment that pharmaceutical firms could be granted a one-year reprieve from a proposed 200% tariff caused wild swings in the healthcare sector. Amazon.com Inc. slipped at the start of its Prime Day event, with early sales reported to be down 14% year-over-year . In contrast, Tesla Inc. edged higher amid steady sentiment on tech megacaps. Bond Market and Tariffs in Focus US Treasuries sold off, pushing 30-year yields close to 5%, as weak demand was seen in a US$58 billion three-year note auction. The yield on 10-year Treasuries rose three basis points to 4.41%, while similar moves were seen across German and UK government bonds. Investors were also responding to Trump’s warning that a new tariff rate on the EU could be unilaterally declared “within two days,” citing frustration with the bloc’s fines against US tech giants. “There’s growing headline risk, but unlike the March-April plunge, the market seems to believe talks will resume,” said Bret Kenwell of eToro. Still, he cautioned that the situation could flip “from bark to bite,” prompting a potential 5–10% correction. Analysts Weigh In Despite the trade anxiety, several Wall Street houses upgraded their forecasts: Goldman Sachs raised its 12-month S&P 500 target to 6,900, citing expected Fed rate cuts and resilient earnings. Bank of America hiked its year-end forecast to 6,300, pointing to solid corporate guidance. Piper Sandler’s Craig Johnson maintained a bullish stance, saying markets are growing desensitised to tariff noise. Ulrike Hoffmann-Burchardi of UBS expects US effective tariff rates to end the year at 15%, which she said would pose a drag on growth but not enough to trigger a recession. title: Trump’s Tariff Bombshell Jolts Markets, Copper At Risk Of 50% Levy
body: Asian and US stock markets were mixed on Wednesday as investors reacted to fresh tariff threats from President Donald Trump, who warned there would be no further extensions to his new trade deadline of Aug 1. At a cabinet meeting on Tuesday, Trump declared, “Today we’re doing copper. I believe the tariff on copper, we’re going to make it 50%,” adding that investigations into pharmaceuticals, semiconductors, lumber and critical minerals could lead to more levies. The president also said pharmaceutical products may soon face a 200% tariff, though implementation would come after a one-year to 18-month grace period. “They’re going to be tariffed at a very, very high rate,” Trump stated, underscoring the escalation of his protectionist agenda. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick later told CNBC that the copper tariff could take effect by the end of July or on 1 August, coinciding with the deadline for countries to strike bilateral tariff deals with the US. Trump reiterated, “No extensions will be granted,” after pushing back the previous 9 July cut-off. The latest wave of trade threats expands on existing sector-specific duties already imposed on autos and steel, both of which were hit with 25% tariffs earlier this year. Despite the aggressive rhetoric, global markets responded with caution rather than panic. Wall Street closed on a mixed note, while in Asia, gains in Shanghai, Singapore, Seoul, Taipei, Manila and Jakarta helped offset losses in Hong Kong, Sydney and Wellington. Tokyo ended the session flat. SPI Asset Management’s Stephen Innes remarked, “This is the market equivalent of driving with one foot on the gas and one on the brake – negative headline risk can impact sentiment one minute, while hopes of negotiation breakthroughs ease it the next.” He added that Trump’s social media posts now function as “a de facto risk barometer” for global markets. IG market analyst Fabien Yip noted that the compounding effects of country-specific tariffs could lead to broader inflationary pressure, saying, “The impact on prices of goods and services can be far more severe than current levels suggest.” Meanwhile, China’s latest consumer data provided a faint silver lining, with June marking the first rise in consumer prices since January. However, a sharper-than-expected drop in factory gate prices signalled persistent deflationary concerns. With the clock ticking toward Trump’s Aug 1 deadline, negotiations between the US and key trade partners are expected to intensify in the coming weeks. title: Stock Today: YTL Power Inches Lower Amid Broader Utilities Caution And Mixed Economic Signals
body: YTL Power International Bhd (YTL Power) saw its share price slip by 0.24% to RM4.15 as of 12.30pm today, trading in a narrow RM4.09–4.19 range. Trading volume remained modest at approximately 5.06 million shares, reflecting cautious sentiment in the utilities sector. The decline comes as investors digest recent updates from Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB), which has maintained an OVERWEIGHT rating on the utilities sector, backing YTL Power and Tenaga Nasional while noting that a stronger ringgit may temper short-term gains. HLIB highlighted key in-market developments, especially Malaysia’s rising data centre (DC) demand and tariff reforms under RP4, which support long-term growth but may contribute to short-term volatility as regulatory adjustments take effect. YTL Power’s stock fell slightly as markets considered mixed factors: supportive utility fundamentals underpinned by rising DC infrastructure and a potential new gas-fired power plant award, alongside uncertainties stemming from global trade tensions. The recent tariff clatter from the United States, where Malaysia faces new duties of up to 25% has raised concerns over possible macroeconomic slowdowns, which could dampen industrial power demand. Other current events also play into investor caution. Strength in the ringgit has reduced the appeal of YTL Power’s earnings denominated in foreign currencies, especially Singapore dollar and British pound revenues. Although these currency gains enhance purchasing power, they may neutralise some benefits from overseas operations. Further weighing on sentiment is the tightening of monetary conditions globally. HLIB noted the Automatic Fuel Cost Adjustment mechanism under RP4 now boosts cost transparency, but the upside remains capped, meaning major growth catalysts may remain confined to data centre segment expansion, which is still ramping up. Despite the midday dip, YTL Power continues to benefit from supportive long-term trends. Data centre capacity already stands at 2.8 GW, with another 3.6 GW under construction, according to industry watchers. While share price consolidation persists, any fresh updates on new plant awards, progress in DC uptake, or FX movements may serve as catalysts later in the day. Investors are now watching closely for HLIB’s upcoming commentary on DC commissioning updates and broader macroeconomic indicators, particularly any signals regarding US–Malaysia trade diplomacy, which could shift sentiment for both industrial demand and utility pricing. title: Stock Today: HeiTech Padu Surges 8.5% On Bonus Shares And Government Digital Contracts
body: HeiTech Padu Bhd’s share price jumped 8.48% to RM1.79 as of 11.53am today, buoyed by positive developments surrounding its bonus issue and contract wins in Malaysia’s ongoing digital transformation initiative. The technology firm implemented a bonus issue on 9 July, granting one additional share for every four held, with the entitlement date set for July 10. This corporate action, announced on June 25, aims to enhance shareholder value and liquidity, ahead of a scheduled listing of bonus shares on July 11. Amid this backdrop, HeiTech Padu has secured several government contracts integral to national digitalisation efforts. It extended a RM28.26 million maintenance contract for the Malaysian Immigration System (MyIMMs), effective Feb 18 2025, to Feb 17 2027. The company has also been awarded a significant RM190.01 million contract by the Road Transport Department, covering ICT infrastructure and support for the MySIKAP system through open tender. These contracts come in addition to HeiTech’s major RM892.2 million National Integrated Immigration System (NIISe) project and an RM903 million stake in an RM2.5 billion hydroelectric EPCC deal via a partnership with Voith Hydro. The firm has also announced plans for an RM43.7 million private placement to fund the NIISe project and working capital, following the bonus issue. Market sentiment has been further supported by the Malaysian government’s push for digitalisation, channelled through the new Ministry of Digital and MyKasih Foundation initiatives. Local technology providers, including HeiTech Padu, benefit from an estimated RM1.3 billion in contracts awarded over the past year. The stock’s rally reflects investor confidence in HeiTech Padu’s strong standing in the e-government space and pipeline of recurring public-sector work. The bonus issue increases shareholder participation, while assured contract income enhances near- to mid-term earnings visibility. As Malaysia accelerates its digital infrastructure rollout, HeiTech Padu appears well-positioned to capitalise on the wave, with its integrated systems and service solutions offering sustained growth potential. title: Ringgit Dips As BNM Policy Decision Looms, Economists Split On OPR Cut
body: The ringgit opened slightly lower against the US dollar on Wednesday as investors remained cautious ahead of Bank Negara Malaysia’s (BNM) Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meeting, with economists split over the likelihood of an Overnight Policy Rate (OPR) cut. At 8am, the local note eased to 4.2380/2660 against the greenback from Tuesday’s close of 4.2365/2445. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the case for a 25-basis-point cut is becoming increasingly clear, as downside risks mount in the second half of 2025 amid tariff shocks. “The current monetary policy stance is also deemed restrictive, with the real interest rate rising to 1.80 per cent in May, well above the long-term average of 0.88 per cent. “Even so, the ringgit is expected to trade within a narrow range, likely between RM4.23 and RM4.24, as investors await the MPC’s latest policy assessment,” he told Bernama. On external developments, Mohd Afzanizam noted that the US Dollar Index (DXY) remained relatively stable at around 97.516 points, despite concern over the potential impact of new US tariffs. He also observed that US benchmark equities retreated, with the S&P 500 index down 0.07 per cent to close at 6,255.52 points, while the 10-year US Treasury yield inched up two basis points to 4.40 per cent. “Markets appear less rattled by the Trump tariff rhetoric compared to April. There may be lingering doubts about the sustainability and implementation of such a policy, given the Trump administration’s track record of flip-flopping,” he added. At the open, the ringgit was firmer against a basket of major currencies. It rose against the Japanese yen to 2.8850/9042 from 2.8970/9026, strengthened versus the British pound to 5.7569/7949 from 5.7591/7700, and appreciated against the euro to 4.9682/5.0010 from 4.9745/9839. The local note was mixed against ASEAN currencies. It improved vis-à-vis the Singapore dollar to 3.3102/3323 from 3.3152/3217 and rose against the Thai baht to 12.9900/13.0839 from 13.0182/0488. However, it slipped against the Indonesian rupiah to 261.5/263.3 from 261.4/262.0 and eased versus the Philippine peso to 7.52/7.57 from 7.51/7.53. title: US Stocks Slide As Tariff Worries Resurface
body: US stock markets closed lower on Monday as investor sentiment soured following President Donald Trump’s announcement of new tariffs on imports from Japan and South Korea, reigniting fears of escalating trade tensions. The Dow Jones Industrial Average shed 422.17 points, or 0.94%, to close at 44,406.36, while the S&P 500 dropped 0.79% to 6,229.98. The Nasdaq Composite lost 188.59 points, or 0.92%, ending the day at 20,412.52. Meanwhile, the 10-year US Treasury yield edged up to 4.387%. Trump said in social media posts that he had sent formal letters to Japan and Korea, informing them of 25% tariffs effective 1 August, with the levies adding to any retaliatory tariffs from either country. While Trump postponed his self-imposed tariff deadline from July 9 to August 1, he indicated that formal notifications would still be sent by the earlier date, with Korea and Japan being the first to receive them. Investors are now bracing for further tariff announcements that could affect additional trading partners. Trump also reiterated plans to impose an extra 10% tariff on countries he claims align with the “anti-American” policies of the BRICS group. Economists warned that escalating trade tensions could push up inflation and weaken economic growth, raising concerns of potential stagflation. WNS soared 14.13% after Capgemini said it would acquire the company for US$3.3 billion in cash. title: Stock Today: Pentamaster Dips 2.6% Amid Global Tariff Uncertainty
body: As of 12.05pm on 8 July, shares in Pentamaster Corporation Berhad closed down RM0.09 or 2.62% at RM3.34, with trading volume totalling approximately 1.176 million units. This decline follows a broader sell-off in technology and export-driven stocks on concerns over fresh US tariff measures targeting Malaysian goods. Earlier this July, US President Trump announced a 25% tariff on imports from Malaysia, later clarified to exempt semiconductor hardware but still raising investor caution. While Malaysia’s tech sector has seen renewed interest, particularly from companies benefiting from China‑plus‑one supply chain diversification, Pentamaster has not been spared from the risk-off sentiment sweeping global markets. Fundamentally, Pentamaster posted a one-third drop in net profit to RM13.07 million for the first quarter ended March 31 2025, on a 23% fall in revenue attributable to weaker orders in its factory automation segment. This reflects broader caution among clients, with some delaying capital investments in light of geopolitical and tariff uncertainties. Yet there is a silver lining. The company revealed plans to enter the advanced packaging and testing segment for AI chips, investing 5–10% of annual revenue in R&D, with products expected to launch in early 2026. This strategic pivot positions Pentamaster to capitalise on the region’s growth in semiconductor equipment. Analysts have also highlighted that Malaysia’s position as a beneficiary of shifts away from China could support tech stocks longer term if trade tensions ease. Should the tariff landscape stabilise, particularly with ongoing trade negotiations, Pentamaster may regain investor confidence by delivering its new AI‑chip packaging proposition. For now, the market remains cautious, weighing near‑term revenue pressures against the company’s medium‑term pivot into high‑growth tech segments. title: Ringgit Slips As US Tariff Hike Sparks Market Caution
body: The ringgit opened lower against the US dollar on Tuesday, sliding to 4.2345/2430 from Monday’s close of 4.2310/2400, as investor sentiment turned cautious following the United States’ latest reciprocal tariff adjustments set to take effect on Aug 1, 2025. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid noted that the US Dollar Index climbed 0.31% to 97.480 points, driven by the announcement that the pause period on tariffs would end soon. Malaysia’s revised tariff rate was raised to 25% from the previous 24%, prompting concerns of a broader “risk-off” mood in the market. Afzanizam added that while some countries such as Laos, Cambodia and Bosnia saw tariff reductions, others including Malaysia faced slight increases. He said the ringgit could trade within the RM4.23 to RM4.25 range for the day. Against other major currencies, the ringgit weakened against the British pound (5.7691/7807) and euro (4.9700/9800), but appreciated against the Japanese yen (2.9029/9092). title: Stock Today: YTL Power Slides 3.6% As US Chip Ban On Nvidia Sends AI Proxy Stocks Reeling
body: Shares of YTL Power International Bhd fell as much as 3.6% to RM3.97 by midday, dragged lower by broader sentiment over tightening US export controls on Nvidia’s AI chips, which rattled global markets and hit AI-related proxies in Malaysia. The counter opened at RM4.00 and touched a low of RM3.81 before recovering slightly to RM3.97 at 12.30pm. Trading volume surged to over 22.4 million shares, reflecting heightened investor anxiety. The stock had last closed at RM4.12. YTL Power has been one of Bursa Malaysia’s standout performers over the past year, buoyed by its growing exposure to AI-driven data centre power demand and its partnership with Nvidia-linked ecosystem players. However, news that the US government is set to broaden its AI chip restrictions, limiting shipments of Nvidia semiconductors to the Middle East and other non-aligned markets, has triggered a sharp reassessment of growth proxies in the AI supply chain. Market watchers said the selldown in YTL Power reflects worries that escalating restrictions on Nvidia could indirectly slow the AI data centre buildout in regions where the group is aggressively expanding. “YTL Power has been priced as a high-beta AI proxy. Any sign of Nvidia’s business being throttled—even in adjacent markets—tends to spill over into local sentiment,” said a fund manager with exposure to large-cap Malaysian infrastructure stocks. Despite today’s drop, YTL Power is still up more than 80% year-to-date, backed by strong earnings momentum and continued investor interest in digital infrastructure exposure. Analysts are expected to reassess valuations should the US further widen the scope of its export bans or if China retaliates with new tech restrictions of its own. The US ban has already impacted chipmakers globally and triggered pullbacks in tech-heavy indices, including Bursa Malaysia’s F4GBM Index, which slid 0.94% by midday. NationGate Holdings Bhd, another AI-linked stock, also tumbled 7.9% earlier in the session. Analysts warn that volatility in stocks like YTL Power may persist in the near term as geopolitical risks inject uncertainty into AI supply chains and infrastructure planning. title: Stock Today: NationGate Drops 8% On US AI Chip Export Jitters
body: Shares in NationGate Holdings Bhd fell sharply in morning trade, down 7.87% to RM1.64 as of 11.52am, amid market jitters linked to the United States’ proposed restrictions on AI chip exports to Southeast Asia, including Malaysia. The counter opened at RM1.57 and hit a low of RM1.53 before recovering slightly. Trading volume spiked to 56 million shares, significantly above average, indicating heightened investor caution following news reports that US President Donald Trump’s administration may implement new licensing requirements for AI chip exports to Malaysia and Thailand. Although the draft rule has yet to be finalised, market watchers have raised concerns over its potential impact on electronics and semiconductor supply chains in the region. NationGate, which is involved in electronics manufacturing services and provides assembly and testing for semiconductors, could face indirect exposure through supply chain delays or dampened sentiment. NationGate had recently gained investor interest on expectations of robust demand from US tech companies expanding data centres and AI operations in Malaysia. However, the latest policy uncertainty appears to have triggered profit-taking on the stock, which has been on a steady climb since early this year. Traders said the selloff reflects broader worries over geopolitical risks and technology decoupling between the US and China, especially as Malaysian firms remain deeply integrated into global semiconductor supply networks. title: Ringgit Opens Higher Ahead Of Key BNM Policy Meeting, Eyes On Potential OPR Cut
body: The ringgit opened stronger against the US dollar on Monday as investors turned cautious ahead of Bank Negara Malaysia’s (BNM) monetary policy committee meeting scheduled for 9 July, amid growing expectations of a possible overnight policy rate (OPR) cut. At 8am, the local note rose to RM4.2060/2320 against the greenback from Friday’s close of RM4.2180/2260. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said BNM may cut the OPR by 25 basis points in light of heightened economic uncertainties potentially affecting second-half growth momentum. “There is a clear justification for BNM to support growth,” he said, adding that traders were also cautious ahead of the United States tariff pause deadline on 9 July. “All eyes will be on the July 9 deadline with regards to the US tariff which has been paused for 90 days since April 9 this year,” he added. He also noted that OPEC+ members have agreed to raise oil production by 548,000 barrels per day starting August, indicating commitment to restoring global oil supplies. In the meantime, the ringgit is expected to trade cautiously between RM4.22 and RM4.23 today, said Mohd Afzanizam, pointing out that the ringgit had strengthened by 0.3% week-on-week against the US dollar last week, reaching as high as RM4.1980 on 1 July. title: Is WCT Making A Strong Comeback In Construction?
body: MIDF Amanah Investment Bank Bhd (MIDF Research) has maintained its BUY recommendation on WCT Holdings Bhd with an unchanged target price of RM0.95, implying a potential total return of 41.8% from its current price of RM0.67. The research house is basing its valuation on forecast FY26 earnings per share of 5.6 sen, pegged to a price-to-earnings ratio of 17 times, in line with WCT’s two-year historical mean. The reaffirmed call comes after WCT secured an RM365.2 million contract from Projek Lebuhraya Usahasama Bhd (PLUS) for the North-South Expressway additional lane project. The award will cover works on the Sedenak to Simpang Renggam stretch, with construction scheduled to begin on 28 July 2025 and completion targeted by mid-2028. MIDF Research noted that the contract win aligns with its earlier assumption of RM1 billion in job replenishment for the year and should contribute progressively to earnings starting FY26. Despite 1QFY25 results falling short of expectations due to seasonally slower construction activity, the house has kept its earnings forecasts unchanged, anticipating stronger billings in the latter part of the year. The PLUS contract lifts WCT’s outstanding order book to an estimated RM2.9 billion, offering greater visibility into near-to-medium-term earnings and reaffirming its positioning within Malaysia’s civil infrastructure upcycle. MIDF Research believes WCT is well-placed to benefit from upcoming public-sector contracts, particularly in expressways, airport expansion and utility infrastructure, citing its experience and existing tender book of over RM13 billion. The group is expected to secure further jobs in the second half of 2025, driven by increased government emphasis on transport and public infrastructure upgrades, including data centres and road projects. The research house also noted the recent listing of Paradigm REIT in June 2025 as a significant milestone in WCT’s strategy to monetise its property assets and enhance financial flexibility. In the meantime, its property investment and development divisions continue to anchor earnings while construction activity gradually picks up. On the tax front, MIDF Research believes the 6% Sales and Services Tax (SST), which came into effect on July 1, 2025, will have minimal impact on project margins. The contract sum already includes SST and exemptions on key materials like steel and cement, further mitigating cost pressures. The house also highlighted that large infrastructure projects typically have tax pass-through clauses, which WCT is adept at managing. With its operations primarily focused on Malaysia, the investment bank considers WCT to have limited exposure to geopolitical and trade-related risks. This domestic concentration offers a strategic advantage amid ongoing global uncertainties, particularly in contrast to more export-reliant construction players. The central parity rate of the yuan against the U.S. dollar is based on a weighted average of prices offered by market makers before the opening of the interbank market each business day. body: Bursa Malaysia extended its losses at midday, weighed down by selling across key indices and heavyweight counters amid ongoing concerns over regional tech supply chains and cautious sentiment in global markets. title: Asian Markets Slip As Tariff Confusion Deepens
body: Asian stock markets edged lower on Monday amid rising confusion over US tariff policy, after officials flagged a delay in trade levies but failed to issue details or formal documentation. US President Donald Trump said over the weekend that new tariff rates will be notified to trading partners by 9 July and take effect on 1 August. However, his remarks suggesting levies could range from 10% to as high as 70% further clouded the outlook. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said countries not making progress on trade would “boomerang” back to April tariff levels. Markets reacted cautiously. S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures each dipped 0.3%. Japan’s Nikkei lost 0.3%, South Korea’s Kospi dropped 0.7%, while MSCI’s Asia-Pacific ex-Japan index eased 0.1%. Analysts at ANZ warned that if reciprocal tariffs were implemented in full, downside risks to US growth and upside inflation pressures would intensify, especially as key trade partners like the EU, India and Japan are in sensitive negotiation stages. Investors sought safety in bonds. US 10-year Treasury yields fell nearly two basis points to 4.326%. The dollar index hovered near four-year lows at 96.913. The euro traded at $1.1787, while the greenback dipped to ¥144.38. Gold slipped 0.3% to US$3,324 per ounce, though it gained nearly 2% last week as the dollar weakened. Oil prices fell after OPEC+ surprised markets by agreeing to increase output by 548,000 barrels per day in August. The group also hinted at a similar hike in September, leading analysts to suspect an effort to squeeze out higher-cost producers such as US shale. Brent crude slid 52 cents to US$67.78 a barrel, while US crude dropped US$1.01 to US$65.99. title: Analysts Raise Maybank’s Target Price Post Growth Plan Strategy
body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has reiterated its BUY call on Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) with a target price of RM10.90, offering an estimated 12% upside and a forecast dividend yield of around 6% for FY2025. Following Maybank’s “Super Growth” investor day held on July 4, the house highlighted three key areas set to drive growth: wealth management, mid-market lending and global market FX sales, most of which are capital-light and non-interest income segments. In wealth management, Maybank’s group assets under management reached RM341 billion as of end-1Q25, split largely between Malaysia (55%) and Singapore (44%). Its strength lies in the affluent and emerging affluent segments, with further ambitions to tap into ultra-high-net-worth clientele through its established corporate banking network. Wealth management fees generated RM1.17 billion in 2024, contributing 15% of core non-interest income. With around 78% of AUM still in deposits versus the 40–60% seen at Singaporean peers, Maybank sees strong conversion potential to wealth products. It aims to double total financial assets, revenue and wealth contributions to fee income through digital initiatives and geographical expansion into Indonesia and the Philippines. In the mid-market segment, Maybank’s current exposure represents 15% of global banking loans in Malaysia and 20% in Singapore. While this remains a smaller portion of the overall loan book, targeted efforts in high-growth regions such as Penang, Johor, Sarawak and Singapore as well as sectors like semiconductors and data centres, are beginning to show results. The bank estimates this segment yields a return on assets of 1.5%, compared to the group’s 2024 ROA of 1%. Notably, RHB Research highlighted that this expansion has not come at the expense of asset quality. Maybank’s FX sales strategy is centred around expanding its FX ecosystem and revenue base via cross-selling, client customisation and increased wallet share. Its wholesale banking strength in Singapore and Malaysia underpins this push with a clear emphasis on integrating FX offerings with broader banking services to deepen client relationships. While the group’s operating expenses remain elevated particularly in the wealth segment due to personnel costs, Maybank is stepping up investments in technology and digital infrastructure. Cost-to-income ratios vary across the growth pillars with wealth management CIR exceeding 40%, while mid-market and FX sales remain more efficient. RHB Research also applied a 4% valuation premium in its target price to reflect Maybank’s ESG score of 3.2, which is above Malaysia’s country median of 3.0. With relatively low foreign shareholding at approximately 19%, a commitment to dividend payouts and robust RM1.8 billion overlay buffers, the house sees Maybank as a defensive pick with clear visibility on future growth drivers. title: Weekly Wrap-up: STI Hits 52-Week High, Extends Winning Streak
body: The Singapore stock market ended the week on a strong note, with the benchmark Straits Times Index (STI) reaching a 52-week high of 4,019.57 on July 3 before closing this week’s session slightly lower at 4,014 points. However, it marks the first time the STI has crossed the 4,000-point level, while gaining approximately 0.2% for the week, bringing its year-to-date increase to 6.1%. The rally was driven by broad-based buying across financials, real estate and REITs, fuelled by easing global bond yields and increased risk appetite among investors. Sentiment was further boosted by favourable domestic policy signals and cooling inflationary pressures abroad. Average daily turnover remained robust, with S$1.17 billion traded across 1.64 billion shares, underscoring strong investor interest. Financial and property counters led the market, supported by optimism over interest rate stability and renewed confidence in Singapore’s real estate sector. Notably, Bukit Sembawang Estates saw a boost following the release of strong full-year financial results, reinforcing investor faith in mid-cap property stocks. Meanwhile, falling yields on 10-year Singapore government bonds provided additional support, making equities more attractive amid a stable monetary backdrop. Geopolitical optimism and a cautious but constructive global outlook also contributed to the STI’s momentum, with investors positioning for potential upside as second-half economic data and corporate earnings roll in. Looking ahead, analysts expect the STI to trade within the 4,000-4,040 range, while keeping a close eye on upcoming US inflation data, global interest rate cues and regional policy developments. Bottomline: Singapore’s market is riding a wave of solid fundamentals and investor confidence, capped by a milestone week for the STI. As the second half of 2025 unfolds, investors remain cautiously optimistic, watching for macro signals that could influence the next leg of the rally. title: Weekly Wrap-Up: KOSPI Ends Week Lower Amid Tech Selloff, Global Uncertainty
body: South Korea’s benchmark KOSPI index closed the first week of July in negative territory, slipping 1.2% as investors grappled with a global tech pullback, lingering trade tensions and cautious sentiment ahead of upcoming US tariff decisions. After a strong start to the year, the index struggled to maintain momentum, with heavyweight tech and semiconductor stocks, led by Samsung Electronics and Sk Hynix, leading declines amid weaker chip outlooks and softening demand in key export markets. Investor caution also grew ahead of the July 9 US tariff deadline, sparking concerns over potential disruptions to South Korean trade, especially with the US and China. Meanwhile, a stronger Korean won and profit-taking added to market pressure. On the macro front, Korea’s latest purchasing managers index data showed moderate expansion in manufacturing, but export growth slowed, adding to signs of a bumpy recovery. Analysts say short-term volatility may persist, but longer-term fundamentals for tech and green energy sectors remain intact. Investors are now eyeing the upcoming US inflation data and earnings season, which could set the tone for global equity sentiment in the weeks ahead. title: Weekly Review: Wall Street Rallies To New Highs On Jobs Data, Trade Relief
body: US stocks closed the week on a high note despite a shortened trading schedule, with all major indexes rallying to new highs on the back of stronger-than-expected employment data and easing trade tensions. The S&P 500 rose approximately 1.8%, while the Nasdaq-100 climbed 1.7%, buoyed by continued strength in tech stocks and renewed investor confidence. The Dow Jones Industrial Average led gains with a 2.3% increase, nearing fresh record territory. The Russell 2000 surged 3.4%, marking a strong rebound for small-cap stocks. Markets were boosted by upbeat June jobs data released midweek. The US economy added 147,000 jobs, beating forecasts of 118,000, while the unemployment rate dipped to 4.1%. The positive surprise sparked a strong rally on July 2 and carried momentum into the July 4th holiday. Tech stocks, particularly those in the artificial intelligence and semiconductor sectors like Nvidia and Broadcom, remained in focus, helping anchor the market despite some rotation into value and small caps. Investors also found relief in global trade developments. A temporary easing of US tariffs on certain Asian imports, including a pause in new duties on Vietnamese goods, helped ease geopolitical concerns and support broader sentiment. Meanwhile, Treasury yields edged higher following the jobs report, briefly strengthening the US dollar and signalling improved economic confidence. Despite this week’s bullish tone, investors remain wary of looming policy risks, especially the July 9 deadline for US tariff decisions. Market watchers expect potential volatility if trade talks falter or tariffs are reimposed. With earnings season set to begin in mid-July and Federal Reserve guidance on inflation and interest rates on the horizon, analysts are advising a cautious but optimistic outlook for the second half of 2025. Bottomline: Wall Street’s strong showing this week reflects economic resilience and easing trade concerns, but all eyes are now on upcoming policy decisions that could shape the market’s next move. title: Weekly Review: Hang Seng Pulls Back After Strong 1H25 Rally
body: The Hang Seng Index (HSI) ended the week lower, falling 1.52% to close at 23,916.06, as investors locked in profits following a robust first-half rally and grew increasingly cautious over global trade tensions and sector-specific pressures. The pullback comes after the index surged over 21% in the first half of 2025 (1H25), its best performance in years, fuelled by strong capital inflows from mainland China. However, concerns over renewed US tariffs and a cautious global economic outlook triggered a wave of selling, particularly in export-sensitive and tech-driven sectors. On July 4, the index dropped 0.64%, closing at a weekly low, led by declines in technology and electric vehicle stocks. Tightening margins and heightened market competition contributed to broad sector weakness, while stronger-than-expected US jobs data midweek raised concerns about delayed rate cuts, adding to risk-off sentiment. Mainland-linked Chinese stocks also lost ground, despite having powered earlier gains. The retreat suggests a pause in investor optimism as markets digest external headwinds. Despite the week’s losses, analysts remain cautiously optimistic. The HSI could regain momentum if Beijing introduces new stimulus measures or if trade tensions ease. Key technical support lies at the 23,000 level, with resistance seen around 24,500. Bottomline: After an explosive 1H25, Hong Kong’s equity market is experiencing a natural correction amid rising external pressures. Investors are watching closely for policy signals and global macro developments that could shape the next leg of the market’s trajectory. title: Crypto Review: Bitcoin Holds Firm As Ethereum Leads Weekly Crypto Gains
body: Cryptocurrency markets posted a mixed but resilient performance for the week ending July 4, with Bitcoin holding near US$108,000 and Ethereum climbing steadily above US$2,500, buoyed by strong institutional interest and options market activity. Bitcoin briefly touched highs above US$110,000 midweek, driven by robust inflows into spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs), which neared US$50 billion in assets under management. However, momentum eased on July 4 following a stronger-than-expected US jobs report and renewed trade policy concerns, bringing Bitcoin back to close the week around US$108,165, down slightly from its peak. Analysts say a decisive break above the US$114,000 resistance level could open the door to a rally as high as US$143,000, while support remains solid around US$106,000. Ethereum, meanwhile, outperformed the broader market, rising roughly 6%-7% over the week and settling near US$2,515. The second-largest cryptocurrency broke through key resistance at US$2,520, aided by renewed staking demand and interest from institutional investors. Analysts also pointed to bullish options positioning and a maturing outlook for Ethereum as a foundational asset in decentralised finance. Meanwhile, the altcoin space showed early signs of momentum, with Solana, Arbitrum, Uniswap, and Pepe posting noticeable gains, suggesting the early stirrings of a potential “altseason”. Market outlook: The week reinforced the role of institutional demand in stabilising crypto markets, particularly through ETFs such as BlackRock’s IBIT. However, macroeconomic uncertainty including US fiscal policy and potential new tariffs could inject further volatility in the near term. For now, the technical setup and investor sentiment suggest a cautiously optimistic outlook, with eyes firmly on Bitcoin’s US$114,000 breakout threshold and Ethereum’s ability to sustain levels above US$2,520. title: KOSPI Sinks 2% As Tariff Fears, Profit-Taking Weigh On Market
body: South Korea’s benchmark KOSPI Index closed sharply lower on July 4, falling 1.99% or 61.99 points to end at 3,054.28, as investor sentiment turned cautious amid renewed global trade tensions and broad-based profit-taking. The decline followed a strong rally in previous weeks, with traders locking in gains while closely monitoring US tariff threats that could destabilise global trade flows. Reports that the US may issue tariffs ranging from 10% to 70% on several trading partners heightened anxiety across Asian markets. Technology and automotive stocks were among the biggest losers as Samsung Electronics slipped 0.78% to 63,300 won, SK hynix plunged 2.87% to 270,500 won, LG Energy Solution declined 2.51% to 310,500 won, and Hyundai Motor and Kia fell 1.86% and 1.00%, respectively. Institutional investors offloaded about 444 billion won worth of shares, while retail and foreign investors attempted to stabilise the market with selective buying. The pullback comes as South Korea prepares for high-level trade talks in Washington, with Trade Minister Yeo Han-koo scheduled to meet US officials ahead of the July 8 tariff decision deadline. Analysts say the market is likely to remain volatile in the coming days, with global policy signals and geopolitical developments dictating investor direction. Bottomline: The KOSPI snapped its recent winning streak, dragged lower by global trade concerns and profit-taking. With tariff decisions looming and diplomatic efforts underway, investors are bracing for more volatility in the days ahead. title: Hang Seng Ends Lower Amid Global Trade Jitters
body: The Hong Kong stock market closed in the red on July 4, with the Hang Seng Index falling 0.64% to end the day at 23,916.06, weighed down by global trade concerns and uncertainty over US economic policy. Investor sentiment remained cautious as markets awaited potential new US tariffs, with analysts warning that heightened geopolitical tension could further pressure regional equities. The technology and export-heavy sectors were among the hardest hit, dragging the index lower. While Chinese A-shares edged higher by 0.3% to 0.4% amid hopes of domestic stimulus, Hong Kong stocks underperformed, reflecting local economic fragility and external risks. Tech giants such as Alibaba Group Holding Ltd and JD.com Inc posted notable losses, contributing to the market’s decline. title: Global Stocks Slip As Trump’s Trade Deadline Looms, Dollar Slides
body: Stocks edged lower on July 3 as investors digested the economic impact of US President Donald Trump’s sweeping tax and spending bill and braced for the July 9 deadline for countries to strike trade deals with the US or face sharply higher tariffs, Reuters reported. With US markets closed for the Independence Day holiday, global sentiment weakened. Europe’s benchmark STOXX 600 index fell 0.5%, with banks, mining firms, and retailers leading the decline. Meanwhile, S&P 500 futures slipped 0.6%, after the benchmark index had closed at a record high on Thursday, buoyed by a stronger-than-expected US jobs report. Trump’s 869-page legislation, passed narrowly in the House late on July 3, averts a potential government default but adds an estimated US$3.4 trillion to the national debt, funding increased military and border security spending. Adding to market jitters, Trump confirmed that Washington would begin sending letters on July 11 outlining new tariff rates for countries that fail to secure deals with the US by July 8. While deals with Vietnam, China and the UK are already in place, talks with Japan and South Korea appear to have stalled, and an agreement with India remains pending. Although the US bond market was closed, Treasury yields climbed on July 3, with the 10-year yield rising 4.7 basis points (bps) to 4.34% and the two-year yield jumping 9.3bps to 3.88%, reflecting investor unease over swelling US debt levels. Bottomline: Markets are grappling with the dual impact of Trump’s aggressive trade policy and expansive fiscal strategy. With a major tariff deadline just days away, global investors are adopting a risk-off stance as the world’s largest economy charts a bold, unpredictable path forward. title: Wall Street Scales Fresh Highs As US Job Market Surprises To The Upside
body: Wall Street extended its record-setting rally on Thursday, buoyed by a stronger-than-expected US jobs report that reinforced investor confidence in the economy’s resilience despite tariff headwinds. The S&P 500 jumped 0.8% to close at 6,279.35, notching its fourth all-time high in five days. The Dow Jones Industrial Average surged 344.11 points, or 0.8%, to 44,828.53, while the Nasdaq Composite gained 1% to 20,601.10. Widespread gains were led by sectors linked to consumer confidence, with Expedia rising 3.2% and Norwegian Cruise Line up 2.9%. Banks also rallied, with Citigroup climbing 2.3% and JPMorgan Chase advancing 1.9%. The rally followed a US government report showing employers added 147,000 net new jobs in June, defying concerns that escalating tariffs might dampen economic momentum. A separate report indicated a decline in weekly jobless claims, suggesting continued labour market strength. “There is nothing to complain about here,” said Carl Weinberg, Chief Economist at High Frequency Economics, noting the lack of any recession signals in the data. In the bond market, yields surged as traders scaled back expectations of near-term interest rate cuts by the US Federal Reserve. The 10-year Treasury yield rose to 4.34% from 4.30%, while the two-year yield jumped to 3.88% from 3.78%, reflecting reduced odds of easing. Futures markets now see less than a 5% chance of a Fed rate cut at its upcoming meeting, down from nearly 24% a day earlier, according to CME Group data. Despite President Donald Trump’s repeated calls for lower rates, Fed Chair Jerome Powell has signalled a cautious approach, awaiting clearer signs of inflationary pressure from pending tariffs. title: Stock Today: Gas Malaysia Dipped Despite Full Supply Resumption Post-Disruption
body: Gas Malaysia Bhd’s share price slipped 1.13% to RM4.38 as of 2.58pm on Friday, down from its last closing of RM4.43, with 683,000 shares traded. The stock opened at RM4.43 and touched an intraday low of RM4.37. This dip comes despite the full resumption of gas supply operations at the company’s Shah Alam and Batu Tiga City Gate stations, following the three-month disruption caused by the Putra Heights PGU pipeline explosion. According to MIDF Amanah Investment Bank Bhd (MIDF Research), which has maintained a Neutral call on the stock with an unchanged target price of RM4.48, the impact on Gas Malaysia’s full-year earnings is expected to be minimal. The investment bank estimates that the disruption affected less than 2% of the company’s annual volume, with a projected earnings reduction of under 1% for FY25. This limited impact was attributed to Gas Malaysia’s swift response in securing alternative supply sources and mitigating losses for its industrial customers. The house also noted that liability for the incident is unlikely to fall on Gas Malaysia, as the Department of Occupational Safety and Health (DOSH) concluded the pipeline damage was due to soil instability and falls under the jurisdiction of the supplier, Petronas. Looking ahead, MIDF Research remains confident in Gas Malaysia’s earnings outlook, supported by potentially higher average selling prices in the second half of FY25, driven by rising Brent crude oil prices and market reference price adjustments. The company’s recent strategic collaboration with Levidian on LOOP carbon-reduction technology is also seen as strengthening its long-term value proposition. title: Stock Today: Capital A Slips At Midday As MAG Eyes Bigger Jet Deal With Airbus
body: Capital A Bhd’s shares edged 1.18% lower to RM0.84 by midday Thursday, shedding one sen from the previous close, as trading momentum softened ahead of wider sector developments. The counter hovered between RM0.835 and RM0.855, with over 4.8 million shares traded by 2.06pm. The market’s subdued sentiment came as industry attention turned to Malaysia Aviation Group’s (MAG) potential aircraft order expansion. According to industry sources, MAG, the parent of Malaysia Airlines, is close to firming up an order for additional Airbus A330neo long-haul jets, with a possible announcement expected during Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim’s official visit to Paris this week. While the deal has no direct bearing on Capital A, which operates the low-cost AirAsia fleet, the anticipated order underscores MAG’s growth ambitions in full-service long-haul operations, a segment Capital A has also explored in the past through its widebody arm, AirAsia X. The Airbus development, paired with broader industry moves in aerospace and fleet modernisation, is seen by some investors as a potential reconfiguration moment for Malaysia’s aviation landscape. The earlier 2022 agreement between MAG and Airbus included 20 confirmed A330neo orders with options for another 20, which the group is now considering exercising. MAG has also signalled interest in evaluating larger aircraft such as the Airbus A350, Boeing 787 and Boeing 777X. Capital A continues to focus on digital expansion and its MRO business through Asia Digital Engineering, but investor sentiment has remained cautious amid increased competition and slow financial clarity on the group’s transformation. The counter has been consolidating just below the RM0.90 threshold in recent weeks, with aviation stocks broadly reacting to both global macro headwinds and shifting strategic alignments among key players. title: Tech Rally Sends S&P 500, Nasdaq To Record Highs; Dow Slips Ahead Of US Jobs Report
body: Wall Street ended Wednesday’s session on a high note, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite closing at fresh record levels, buoyed by gains in heavyweight technology stocks and a trade breakthrough between the US and Vietnam. The Dow Jones Industrial Average, however, edged 10.52 points lower to 44,484.42, just 1.18% shy of its all-time high. The S&P 500 rose 29.41 points, or 0.47%, to settle at 6,227.42, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq surged 190.24 points, or 0.94%, to end at 20,393.13. The rally was largely driven by strong performances from Nvidia, Apple, and Tesla, with the latter rebounding 5% despite a sharp drop in second-quarter deliveries. Traders noted that Tesla’s figures were less severe than feared. The markets reversed early losses triggered by weaker-than-expected US private payroll data, with job gains for May also revised downwards. However, sentiment turned positive after Washington and Hanoi inked a trade deal imposing 20% tariffs on several Vietnamese exports, calming nerves over prolonged trade tensions. Talks of a potential agreement with India also boosted optimism. “There is some relief in regards to progress on trade. The deal with Vietnam was welcomed news,” said Michael Arone, Chief Investment Strategist at State Street Global Advisors. Centene Corp plunged 40%—its lowest in eight years—after withdrawing its 2025 earnings forecast due to a significant drop in expected revenue from its marketplace health plans. Market participants are now turning their attention to Thursday’s non-farm payrolls report, expected to provide further clues on the Federal Reserve’s rate path. Economists forecast a slowdown in job growth and a slight uptick in the unemployment rate to 4.3%. “Employment softening and inducing the Fed to lower rates would be a positive,” said Jim Awad, Senior Managing Director at Clearstead Advisors. “But if it softens too much, that would be a negative for growth and profits.” Trading volume on US exchanges stood at 16.95 billion shares, just below the 20-day average of 17.82 billion. Markets will be closed on Thursday for Independence Day. title: Stock Today: Tenaga Nasional Falls 4.1% Amid Tax Ruling Concerns
body: Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) saw its share price slide 4.1% to RM14.00 by midday Wednesday, shedding 60 sen from its previous close of RM14.60, as investors reacted to a recent Federal Court ruling involving a disputed tax allowance claim. The stock opened at RM14.26 and traded between RM13.86 and RM14.26, with trading volume reaching nearly 1.57 million shares. The sharp drop comes after the court ruled that TNB qualifies for the Investment Tax Allowance (ITA) under Schedule 7B of the Income Tax Act but not the Reinvestment Allowance (RA) under Schedule 7A, resulting in an additional tax assessment of RM6.8 billion for the years 2013 to 2018. Although the utility giant plans to pursue its ITA entitlement, the uncertainty surrounding the process has raised concerns over a potential one-off tax provision that could impact near-term financials. Despite the selloff, Hong Leong Investment Bank maintained its ‘Buy’ call on the stock with a target price of RM16.20, suggesting confidence in a negotiated outcome that could ease pressure on TNB’s balance sheet and cash flow over time. title: Stock Today: Samaiden Rises As Solar Ambitions Expand
body: Shares of Samaiden Group Bhd rose 0.85% to RM1.18 as of 2.46pm today, following renewed investor confidence fuelled by its land acquisition for future solar development and ongoing progress under the government’s large-scale solar (LSS) programme. The counter added 1 sen from the previous close of RM1.17, with 1.19 million shares changing hands. The stock opened at RM1.18, touching a high of RM1.18 and a low of RM1.16 during intraday trading. Analysts from MIDF Amanah Investment Bank Bhd (MIDF Research) have reaffirmed their BUY call on Samaiden, maintaining a target price of RM1.59, underpinned by its positioning in Malaysia’s renewable energy landscape. The group’s strategic move to acquire 185.57 hectares of land in Teluk Intan for RM45.5 million is seen as a major step towards its evolution from an EPCC (engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning) player to a renewable energy asset owner. The land is earmarked for future solar farm development, with analysts highlighting its proximity, just 5km from the nearest grid connection, as a critical advantage. This acquisition builds on Samaiden’s existing momentum after being shortlisted for a 99.99MW solar farm project in Kelantan under LSS5 and sealing a 21-year power purchase agreement with Tenaga Nasional in March. With an outstanding order book of RM441.8 million, 53% of which is tied to utility-scale solar, Samaiden is aggressively targeting an RM1 billion book by FY2026 and bidding for RM1.8 billion worth of contracts. Among its latest wins are three key solar EPCC contracts worth over RM250 million combined, covering projects in Pasir Mas, Kulim, and Bestari Jaya. Further upside could emerge from the anticipated LSS5+ announcement, expected to open doors for LSS6 and expanded solar development quotas. Samaiden’s proactive landbanking, expanding project pipeline, and alignment with the National Energy Transition Roadmap (NETR) continue to position it as a frontrunner in Malaysia’s clean energy shift. title: Ringgit Rebounds As Traders Turn Cautious Ahead Of US Tariff Deadline
body: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar on Thursday, recovering from a weaker close the previous day as traders trimmed their greenback exposure ahead of the July 9 expiry of the United States’ 90-day tariff pause. At 8 am, the local note stood at 4.2205/2295 against the US dollar, strengthening from Wednesday’s close of 4.2245/2305. The US Dollar Index also eased 0.04% to 96.776 following signs of labour market weakness. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid noted that the US private sector unexpectedly shed 33,000 jobs in June, according to data from Automatic Data Processing (ADP), contrary to market expectations of a 99,000 increase. “Job losses were most apparent in the services sectors such as financial activities and professional and business services. Tonight’s nonfarm payroll (NFP) report will be closely watched, given the positive correlation between ADP and NFP readings,” he told local media. He said the softening labour market could influence the US Federal Reserve’s monetary policy stance and strengthen the case for rate cuts. On Wednesday, the ringgit depreciated 0.7% to RM4.2275 from RM4.1980, likely due to profit-taking ahead of the tariff decision. Afzanizam also highlighted potential US tariff concessions, pointing to Vietnam’s recently reduced reciprocal tariffs. “Given these developments, the ringgit may remain range-bound as market participants stay cautious ahead of tonight’s NFP data and the upcoming US tariff decision,” he said. At the opening, the ringgit was mixed against a basket of major and ASEAN currencies. It strengthened against the British pound to 5.7606/7728 from 5.7859/7941, rose against the Singapore dollar to 3.3154/3230 from 3.3167/3217, and edged up against the Indonesian rupiah and Philippine peso. title: Dollar Advances After Stronger Than Expected Job Data
body: The U.S. dollar advanced against major currency pairs including the yen, euro and Swiss franc on Thursday after data showed that the U.S. economy created more jobs than analysts estimated, signaling that the Federal Reserve might take longer to cut interest rates. The dollar strengthened 0.77 per cent to 144.78 and was up 0.58 per cent to 0.797 against the Swiss franc. The euro weakened 0.47 per cent at $1.1743 against the dollar. The rise in the greenback following the data was accompanied by a rise in U.S. Treasury yields. The 2-year note yield, which typically moves in step with interest rate expectations for the Federal Reserve, rose 8.9 basis points to 3.88 per cent. The yield on benchmark U.S. 10-year notes rose 4.9 basis points to 4.342 per cent. title: Ambiguity Between DNB And U Mobile’s Role In 5G Remains A Concern
body: Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) Research has reiterated its NEUTRAL call on the telecommunications sector, highlighting continued earnings challenges from 5G policy ambiguity and stiff fibre broadband competition, while favouring fixed-line operators for their infrastructure exposure. Its top pick remains Telekom Malaysia Bhd ( BUY , target price RM7.90), with BUY calls also maintained on Axiata Bhd (TP: RM2.50) and Maxis Bhd (TP: RM4.20), while CelcomDigi Bhd and TIME dotCom Bhd are rated HOLD at TP of RM4.00 and RM4.98 respectively. The sector saw mixed performance in 1H25, gaining 2.3% and outperforming the FBM KLCI, which declined 6.7% over the same period. CelcomDigi and TIME dotCom led with double-digit gains, while TM and Maxis remained flat and Axiata fell 7.2%. HLIB noted the rebound in telco valuations during 2Q25 was driven by dividend appeal and investor preference for defensive stocks amid macroeconomic uncertainty. In the mobile segment, service revenue growth is expected to remain subdued in 2H25 due to a saturated market and limited upside in data monetisation. HLIB believes mobile players will continue focusing on cost efficiencies while awaiting clarity on key 5G policies, especially the restructuring of Digital Nasional Berhad (DNB) and the Ministry of Finance’s put option deadline in November 2025. The wholesale access fee for 5G is also under scrutiny, with any downward revision seen as a potential re-rating catalyst for CelcomDigi and Maxis. HLIB flagged that policy ambiguity, particularly after U Mobile was appointed the second 5G network operator last year, remains unresolved. While U Mobile’s anticipated IPO could shed light on rollout strategies, HLIB stressed that greater regulatory direction from the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) is essential to harmonise the structural mismatch between DNB as a wholesale player and U Mobile as a retail-focused operator. On the fixed-line front, heightened competition in fibre broadband continues to pressure average revenue per user (ARPU) and subscriber additions. TM, while exposed to retail downside, still benefits from wholesale revenue under the High-Speed Broadband Access (HSBA) model, offering margin protection. HLIB expects CelcomDigi to eventually moderate its aggressive fibre customer acquisition once it attains scale, similar to Maxis’ prior strategic pivot. Foreign shareholding remains low across local telcos, ranging between 6.9% and 15.5%, though TM bucked the trend in 2024 with a rise in foreign interest on expectations of data centre-linked growth. HLIB expects renewed interest in TM as data centres are progressively commissioned, with its joint venture with Singtel’s Nxera scheduled to be operational by mid-2026. HLIB concluded that while sector valuation appears reasonable, the investment case hinges on clarity in 5G policy and stabilisation in competitive dynamics. It favours fixed-line players due to their broadband infrastructure roles and sees TM as best positioned to benefit from Malaysia’s accelerating data centre landscape.
