title: Trump Deadline, Dollar Slide Weigh On Asian Markets
body: Asian equities retreated on Wednesday as markets responded to growing uncertainty over US interest rates and a looming trade deadline set by President Donald Trump. MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan dipped 0.23%, pulling back from a November 2021 high reached last week. Japan’s Nikkei slumped 0.78%, driven by weakness in tech shares. Tech-heavy indices in Taiwan and South Korea also tracked lower, mirroring a broader sell-off in US technology stocks following a sharp rally in June. Adding to the cautious sentiment was Trump’s renewed insistence that the Jul 9 deadline for trade negotiations will not be extended. He expressed doubts over a deal with Japan but remains optimistic about reaching an agreement with India. Meanwhile, investor attention is increasingly shifting to the outcome of the ‘One Big Beautiful Bill’ Act (OBBBA), which passed the US Senate by a razor-thin margin and now awaits a vote in the House of Representatives. The legislation, expected to expand the national debt by US$3.3 trillion, has sparked fiscal concerns, though market reaction was initially muted. Benchmark US 10-year Treasury yields held steady at 4.245%. Aninda Mitra, Head of Asia Macro Strategy at BNY Investment Institute, said the Bill “hard wires” fiscal deterioration in the US and added that elevated term premia may persist due to the uncertainty. “We don’t think long-term yields will fall back materially in the 6 to 12-month horizon,” he added. US economic data released Tuesday showed a rise in job openings for May, suggesting a still-resilient labour market. Investors are now closely watching Thursday’s payrolls report to assess the likelihood of Federal Reserve rate cuts. Despite pressure from Trump to ease rates immediately, Fed Chair Jerome Powell reiterated the central bank’s cautious stance, saying it will “wait and learn more” about tariff impacts before making any moves. Markets are pricing in 64 basis points of Fed rate cuts this year, though only a 21% chance of a cut in July. This has weakened the US dollar, which is facing its worst first-half performance since the 1970s, down more than 10% year-to-date. The euro traded at US$1.1793, just below its recent three-and-a-half-year high, while the yen was steady at 143.52 per dollar. “Any disappointing economic data can prompt further dovish repricing of FOMC rate cuts and another round of USD selling,” said Carol Kong, a currency strategist at Commonwealth Bank of Australia. She also warned that developments in OBBBA and trade policy “have the potential to further weaken the USD if they undermine investor confidence about the US economy”. Reflecting a flight to safety, spot gold edged lower to US$3,332.19 per ounce, after a 1% jump in the previous session. title: Tech Selloff Drags Nasdaq, S&P Lower As Dow Climbs On Stimulus Hopes
body: Wall Street ended mixed on Tuesday, with the Nasdaq Composite and S&P 500 retreating from recent highs as large-cap tech stocks lost steam, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average surged, buoyed by gains in economically sensitive sectors. The Nasdaq fell 166.84 points or 0.82% to 20,202.89, and the S&P 500 slipped 6.94 points or 0.11% to 6,198.01. In contrast, the Dow jumped 400.17 points or 0.91% to close at 44,494.94, led by materials and small-cap stocks. The NYFANG Index, which tracks 10 top tech names, tumbled 1.8%, as investors unwound recent positions amid overbought signals. “We got to very overbought levels on tech and Nasdaq over the past weeks,” said Farz Azarm of Mizuho Americas. “Today you are seeing a massive unwind.” Tesla shares plunged 5.4% after former President Donald Trump threatened to end federal subsidies to Elon Musk’s companies, reigniting tensions over Trump’s tax and spending package. Despite the tech rout, transportation stocks staged a strong rally, with the Dow Transportation Index gaining 2.9%, its biggest one-day jump since May 12. Meanwhile, investor sentiment found some support after Trump ruled out extending the 9 July trade deal deadline, reducing fears of prolonged negotiations. Optimism was also bolstered by Senate approval of Trump’s tax package, although concerns remain over its multi-trillion dollar cost. On the economic front, US job openings rose unexpectedly in May, signalling resilience in the labour market. The ISM manufacturing PMI climbed to 49.0 in June, slightly above expectations, suggesting a tentative rebound in factory activity. Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell maintained a cautious stance, reiterating that the central bank would wait for more data before cutting rates, despite Trump’s calls for immediate action. Investors are now awaiting Thursday’s nonfarm payrolls report, which could reshape expectations for a potential July rate cut. Markets are currently pricing in a 21.2% chance of a cut this month, with 64 basis points in total reductions forecast for 2025. Elsewhere, casino stocks surged after Macau posted a rise in June gambling revenue. Wynn Resorts, Las Vegas Sands, and MGM Resorts all rallied more than 7%. title: Stock Today: Bermaz Auto Slips As FY26 Outlook Clouds Sales Recovery
body: Shares of Bermaz Auto Bhd (BAuto) slipped 0.63% to RM0.785 as at 2.48 PM, extending losses amid a wave of analyst downgrades and lowered earnings guidance. The counter opened at RM0.790, hit a low of RM0.770, and registered a trading volume of 41.92 million shares. It last changed hands at RM0.785, down RM0.005 from the previous close of RM0.790. The subdued performance comes after several research houses either downgraded or maintained a Neutral call on the company, citing a bleak FY26 outlook. RHB Research and MIDF Research slashed their target prices to RM0.86, while CIMB Securities trimmed it to RM0.80, flagging intense competition from Chinese carmakers, falling sales volumes, and margin pressures. BAuto’s FY25 core earnings of RM157 million fell short of consensus, with Mazda and Kia sales dropping sharply in the fourth quarter. Total group sales for the year fell 35% to 15,466 units, and regional operations underperformed, particularly in the Philippines. Despite a healthy net cash position of RM207 million and a 10% dividend yield, analysts warned of further downside risks if order replenishment remains weak and new model launches fail to lift volumes. title: RHB Maintains Call On Kerjaya Prospek Pending Further Details On GDV
body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has maintained its BUY call on Kerjaya Prospek with an unchanged target price of RM2.80, implying a 35% upside and a yield of around 6%, following the group’s aggressive landbank expansion moves totalling RM224.8 million. The group has entered into three separate sale and purchase agreements to acquire three parcels of freehold land in Jalan Puchong, Kuala Lumpur, for a combined RM112.8 million. At the same time, Kerjaya Prospek has also inked a joint venture and shareholder agreement with Aspen Vision Tanjung (AVT) to develop 4.5 acres of land in Tanjung Bungah, Penang. This mixed-use project will feature serviced apartments, residential units, retail lots and office blocks. The Jalan Puchong acquisition involves a 3.9-acre plot from Sunrise Bright City for RM59.1 million, while the remaining 1.7 and 1.8-acre plots will be bought from Top Up Properties for RM53.7 million. The average price of RM350 per sq ft is considered fair, with recent transactions in surrounding areas ranging between RM300 and RM417 per sq ft. These land parcels are strategically located with access to major highways such as the Federal Highway, LDP and Lebuhraya Shah Alam, and the acquisitions are expected to be completed by September. For the Penang joint venture, a new special purpose vehicle, Tanjung Bungah Development (TBD), will be formed, with Kerjaya’s subsidiary holding a 60% stake. The total land consideration is RM117 million, with RM105 million in cash and RM12 million in-kind via property units. TBD will reimburse AVT RM60 million for prior payments and pre-development costs, while the remaining RM52 million will be settled through borrowings or internal funds. The transaction is expected to close by December. RHB Research noted that Kerjaya Prospek could fund these acquisitions using its sizeable net cash balance of RM316.7 million as of end-1Q25. When combined with other ongoing developments such as Rivanis Ventures in Seberang Perai Tengah and a 49% stake in Aspen Vision Land in Batu Kawan, Kerjaya’s total landbank stands at approximately 83 acres with an estimated gross development value (GDV) of at least RM7 billion. While the house has kept its earnings estimates unchanged pending further details such as GDV figures and deal completion, it views the company’s forward FY26F P/E of 13 times as attractive, compared to the 16–17 times P/E seen during the 2017 construction sector peak. A potential rerating catalyst would be the securing of new industrial jobs in FY25, with the last such job awarded in October 2022. title: Return Of Foreign Investors Could Edge KLCI Up To 1,560 Range
body: The Kuala Lumpur Composite Index (KLCI) is poised to target the 1,548-1,560 range, buoyed by a resurgence in foreign investment and robust technical indicators, as global markets navigate a mix of trade optimism and geopolitical shifts. The Malaysian bourse closed up 8.5 points at 1,541.5 on Tuesday, extending its rally to a five-week high. HLIB noted that this upward momentum was primarily driven by renewed foreign fund inflows, marking the fourth net buying session in five, with an impressive RM106 million injected into the market. This contrasts sharply with June’s net foreign outflow of RM1.30 billion and a year-to-date outflow of RM12.01 billion, signalling a potential reversal in foreign investor sentiment. Bargain hunting in heavyweights like TENAGA, GAMUDA, YTLPOWR, YTL, and SUNWAY further underpinned the index’s gains. Local institutions and retail investors, however, ended as net sellers, shedding RM23 million and RM83 million respectively. Across Asia, markets generally opened the third quarter on a positive note. Easing tensions in the Middle East and optimism surrounding US trade talks ahead of the July 9 deadline provided a tailwind. Expectations of fresh stimulus from China’s upcoming Politburo meeting, following the finalisation of US-China trade deals last week, also contributed to the buoyant mood. However, Japan’s Nikkei 225 bucked the trend, slipping 1.2% after US President Donald Trump threatened new tariffs on Tokyo. In the United States, major indices displayed a mixed performance. While the S&P 500 (-7 points to 6,198) and Nasdaq (-167 points to 20,202) pulled back from their record highs, the Dow Jones Industrial Average surged 400 points to 44,495, marking its seventh gain in eight sessions. This divergence was attributed to investors rotating out of technology stocks and into healthcare-related names such as AMGN, JNJ, MRK, and UNH. Markets continued to digest ongoing US trade negotiations, cautious remarks from Federal Reserve Chairman Jerome Powell at the central bank forum in Portugal, and political developments including Trump’s narrow 51-50 Senate win on his “Big Beautiful Bill,” eyed for July 4 passage. Economic data showed a stronger-than-forecast May JOLTS report, boosting hopes for robust jobs figures, while ISM Manufacturing remained weak but indicated sticky input prices, posing a risk to disinflation hopes. title: Is Kimlun Poised For A Re-Rating?
body: Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) has maintained its BUY rating on Kimlun Corporation with an unchanged target price of RM1.42, citing improving earnings momentum, robust orderbook growth and strong positioning in key construction markets across Johor, Sarawak and Singapore. HLIB said Kimlun’s 1QFY25 core PATAMI of RM25.7 million had already surpassed full-year FY24 earnings, supported by revenue of RM459.7 million, marking its strongest quarterly performance since listing. The outperformance was largely driven by stronger-than-expected results from its property division, while construction and precast segments also exceeded the firm’s internal assumptions. Management is targeting RM1.5 billion to RM2.0 billion in new construction wins for FY25, backed by a healthy tenderbook of RM3 billion to RM4 billion. Projects include residential developments in Johor and infrastructure jobs in East Malaysia, where Kimlun is expected to bid for the second phase of the Sarawak-Sabah Link Road (SSLR), estimated at RM1 billion. The property segment is expected to play a larger role in FY25, with RM1.4 billion worth of launches planned, including Pinegate Residences Phase 2 and Arden@One Bukit Senyum via its 49%-owned joint venture. The company has seen encouraging demand, with booking rates for Arden surpassing 60% shortly after launch, reflecting strong buyer interest in the Johor Bahru RTS corridor. Meanwhile, precast revenue has seen a notable uplift following the completion of a 30% capacity expansion at its Johor plant in late 2024. The facility is now running at full utilisation, while its Senawang plant is operating at around 50% to 60%, with potential upside once the Penang LRT project gains momentum. Kimlun’s supplies to Singapore’s MRT CRL project and broader infrastructure cycle, particularly Changi T5, are expected to support steady precast revenue growth. HLIB made no changes to its earnings forecasts and values Kimlun at 9.0x FY25 P/E, in line with sector valuation benchmarks. The research house noted that the stock could see further re-rating if earnings momentum continues to strengthen, given its solid fundamentals, strong execution track record, and positioning in high-growth construction markets. title: Wall Street Rallies To Record Highs As Hopes Rise For Trade Deals, Rate Cuts
body: Wall Street closed out its strongest quarter in over a year on a high note on June 30, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq notching record closing highs amid renewed optimism over global trade talks and expectations of US interest rate cuts. Reuters reported that the S&P 500 jumped 10.57% for the quarter, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq surged 17.75%, its best showing since late 2022. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 4.98% and the Russell 2000 small-cap index added 8.28%. Despite the rally, all three major indexes posted their weakest first-half gains since 2022, as persistent uncertainty around trade and fiscal policy cast a shadow over markets earlier in the year. Tensions flared in April after President Donald Trump announced sweeping tariffs, rattling investors. However, progress in US trade negotiations with China and the UK has helped ease fears of a global trade war. Optimism is also building ahead of Trump’s self-imposed July 9 trade deadline, with market watchers hoping more deals will be reached in time. The gains on June 30 were partly driven by end-of-quarter “window dressing”, as fund managers adjusted their holdings to reflect stronger performance. The economic calendar this week is packed, with key data including non-farm payrolls and purchasing manager indexes for June. Federal Reserve (Fed) Chair Jerome Powell and several central bank officials are also scheduled to speak, with markets betting on possible rate cuts later this year amid soft data and speculation Trump may replace Powell with a more dovish figure. On June 30, nine of the S&P 500’s 11 sectors ended in the green. The Dow rose 275.5 points to close at 44,094.77, the S&P 500 gained 31.88 points to 6,204.95 and the Nasdaq added 96.28 points, finishing at 20,369.73. Financials led the gains as major US banks rallied after passing the Fed’s annual stress test, opening the door to significant shareholder returns. Top performers included Hewlett-Packard Enterprise (11.1%), First Solar (8.8%) and Juniper Networks (8.45%). Trading volume on US exchanges hit 17.12 billion shares, slightly below the 20-day average of 18.23 billion. title: Stock Today: Sapura Energy To Exit PN17 Despite Massive 1Q Loss
body: Sapura Energy Bhd is trading at four sen as of 10am on July 1, with more than 83.24 million shares changing hands, as investors digested a hefty first-quarter loss and news of a major breakthrough in the company’s financial recovery plan. On June 30, the group reported a loss after tax and minority interest of RM478 million on revenue of RM801 million for the quarter ended April 30, 2025. The poor performance was attributed to expected losses from a troubled engineering & construction (E&C) project in Angola, along with weaker activity across other business segments. Despite the steep quarterly setback, Sapura Energy is pressing ahead with its turnaround as the group expects earnings to improve in the coming quarters, supported by progressive revenue recognition from ongoing E&C contracts and the redeployment of drilling rigs secured under new deals. Meanwhile, in a significant development, Bursa Malaysia Securities Bhd has approved Sapura Energy’s proposed regularisation plan (PRP), paving the way for the group to restructure its debts and exit its Practice Note 17 (PN17) status, a classification for financially distressed companies. A general meeting of shareholders will be held to approve the PRP, with implementation expected to follow soon after. The group is targeting a restructuring effective date in August 2025, with a final deadline set for March 11, 2026. If successful, Sapura’s restructuring would mark one of the most complex corporate recovery efforts in Malaysia’s history and a potential turning point for the energy services group. title: Stock Today: PetGas Shares Ease Despite Blaze Report Rules Out Sabotage
body: Shares of Petronas Gas Bhd (PetGas) slipped six sen to RM17.56 as of 10:49am on July 1, with more than 85,200 shares traded, following renewed investor focus on the financial impact of the April 1 pipeline explosion near Putra Heights. The Selangor state committee on June 30 released the findings of its investigation into the massive fire and explosion, concluding there was no evidence of sabotage or negligence behind the incident. The blaze caused widespread damage in the Kampung Tengah, Puchong area, affecting more than 200 homes with 81 houses severely damaged and 57 others partially impacted. In response to the incident, the state has formalised a special task force focused on enhancing preventive measures and improving response protocols to avoid future disasters involving critical infrastructure. The explosion raised nationwide concern over pipeline safety, zoning near industrial sites and emergency readiness. In May, PetGas disclosed a profit impact of RM60 million for its financial year 2025 due to the incident. The company estimated repair and restoration costs at RM170 million, with revenue losses limited to around RM20 million thanks to swift mitigation and recovery efforts. PetGas stated that it activated its business contingency plans immediately after the incident, working closely with authorities and stakeholders to restore services with minimal disruption. While the investigation’s conclusion may offer some reassurance to stakeholders, market sentiment remains cautious as the company navigates financial and reputational recovery in the wake of one of its most significant infrastructure incidents in recent years. title: Oil Prices Dip On OPEC+ Output Hike Expectations, Tariff Concerns
body: Oil prices slipped in early trading on July 1 as markets weighed the likelihood of another OPEC+ supply hike in August and growing concerns over a potential global economic slowdown triggered by looming US tariffs. Brent crude futures for September delivery edged down 16 cents, or 0.24%, to US$66.58 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate crude fell 20 cents, or 0.31%, to US$64.91 a barrel. Market sentiment turned cautious after sources told Reuters that OPEC+ are planning to increase production by 411,000 barrels per day (bpd) next month. If confirmed at the group’s July 6 meeting, it would mark the fourth consecutive monthly hike and bring the total supply increase for the year to 1.78 million bpd, over 1.5% of global demand. Adding to the pressure, investors remain wary of the July 9 US tariff deadline, when rates on a broad range of imports could jump sharply. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has warned that countries could face tariff hikes of up to 50%, even if negotiations are ongoing, intensifying concerns over slowing global trade and energy demand. Morgan Stanley has revised its oil outlook, projecting Brent crude to ease to around US$60 a barrel by early 2026, citing strong supply growth and fading geopolitical risks. The bank expects an oversupply of 1.3 million bpd that year. Geopolitical tensions earlier in June had pushed oil prices sharply higher, with Brent briefly surging above US$80 following a 12-day conflict that began with Israeli strikes on Iranian nuclear facilities. However, prices quickly retreated after President Donald Trump brokered a ceasefire, with Brent now hovering near US$67. Analysts note that while geopolitical risks have eased, near-term volatility remains as the market digests the dual impact of policy shifts and supply dynamics. title: HLIB Remains Confident On Hiap Teck Despite Net Profit Falling Below Expectations
body: Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) has maintained its BUY rating on Hiap Teck Venture Bhd (HTVB) despite the group’s 9MFY25 core net profit falling below expectations. The research house revised its target price to RM0.37 from RM0.42, citing weaker-than-expected steel prices and margin compression across HTVB’s trading and downstream segments as key downside risks. HTVB reported a core net profit of RM48.5 million for the nine-month period, down 41% year-on-year, accounting for only 46.6% of HLIB’s full-year estimate. The decline was attributed to soft selling prices and lower sales volumes, compounded by narrower margins in both the trading and downstream operations. Its 3QFY25 profit came in at RM19.9 million, marking a quarter-on-quarter drop of 24.7% and a year-on-year decline of 59.9%. On a sequential basis, the performance was dragged by lower contributions from HTVB’s 27.3%-owned Eastern Steel Sdn Bhd (ESSB), along with a higher effective tax rate. Year-on-year, the profit was affected by a double blow of weaker demand and pricing in steel markets and reduced trading volume. Nevertheless, the 9MFY25 performance was partially supported by ESSB’s improved production volume and profitability. HLIB noted that HTVB’s management has adopted a more cautious outlook, reflecting persisting industry challenges, especially from China, the global steel bellwether. The sentiment is further dampened by former US President Donald Trump’s decision to double steel import tariffs to 50%, heightening uncertainty in global steel trade. Despite the weaker near-term backdrop, HLIB believes HTVB’s scaffolding segment and economies of scale at ESSB may provide a buffer. The research firm revised its FY25–FY27 core net profit forecasts by -33.5%, -17.0%, and +12.6% respectively, reflecting expectations of lower volumes and tighter margins ahead. The new target price of RM0.37 is based on a 7x revised FY26 core earnings per share of 5.3 sen, translating to an implied FY25 price-to-book ratio of 0.45 times. At the current share price of RM0.27, HLIB sees a capital upside of 37%, with an expected total return of 40.7% including dividend yield. HTVB, a key player in Malaysia’s building materials sector, continues to face structural headwinds, but HLIB’s revised valuation suggests room for upside as the group focuses on operational efficiencies and diversification through its property and scaffolding ventures. title: Gold Climbs As Fed Cut Bets Grow, Tariff Deadline Looms

Bloomberg reported that spot gold climbed 0.3% to US$3,311.64 an oz as of 8:44am in Singapore, after gaining 0.9% on June 30. Bullion remains near a record high and is up nearly 25% year-to-date, buoyed by geopolitical risks, a weakening dollar and safe-haven demand. Investor sentiment has shifted sharply in favour of looser monetary policy, with traders now pricing in the likelihood of at least two Fed rate cuts in 2025. A closely watched US jobs report due July 3 could further bolster gold if it triggers a drop in Treasury yields, a scenario that historically benefits the precious metal. Adding to the bullish momentum, the Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index dipped another 0.1% on July 1, bringing its year-to-date decline to nearly 11%, its worst first-half performance since 1973. Elsewhere in the precious metals market, platinum rose 0.6% to US$1,367.10 an oz after surging nearly 29% in June, its strongest monthly performance on record, amid tightening supply and robust demand from Chinese jewellers. Silver and palladium also posted gains, supported by speculative buying from both US and Chinese markets. title: FBM KLCI Extends Rally To Five-Week High
body: Bursa Malaysia’s benchmark index continued its upward momentum for the fourth straight session, with the FBM KLCI climbing to a five-week high amid sustained foreign buying and improving investor sentiment. The index advanced 8.57 points, or 0.56%, to close at 1,541.53, marking its highest level since late May. The gain was also the largest single-day increase since June 23, reflecting renewed confidence in Malaysia’s economic outlook. The rally was supported by broad-based buying interest, particularly in blue-chip counters, as investors responded positively to easing global trade tensions and increased foreign appetite for Malaysian assets. Meanwhile, the ringgit strengthened to a nine-month high, appreciating 0.38% against the US dollar to 4.1933, its strongest level since October 2024. The local currency also edged up slightly against the Singapore dollar but recorded mild losses versus the pound sterling and euro. Currency analysts attributed the ringgit’s performance to robust foreign bond inflows and a weaker greenback, as expectations for slower US rate hikes and global risk-on sentiment drove capital toward emerging markets. Market watchers expect the current momentum in Malaysian equities and the ringgit to hold, provided macroeconomic indicators remain supportive and foreign interest persists. title: Analysts Anticipate A Strong Rebound From Yinson
body: Analysts from CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd and RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) are projecting a strong second-half rebound for Yinson Holdings Bhd, underpinned by steady progress across its FPSO portfolio and a growing foothold in renewable energy. The bullish outlook is anchored on Yinson’s solid US$19.6 billion order book and earnings visibility from its three flagship floating production storage and offloading (FPSO) assets — Maria Quitéria, Atlanta and Agogo. Notably, FPSO Agogo is tracking ahead of schedule, with first oil expected in 3QFY26, a key catalyst for revenue acceleration. RHB Research sees substantial upside, assigning a target price of RM3.69, while CIMB has raised its FY26 earnings forecast by 22.5% and reaffirmed a target of RM2.93. Both firms cite Yinson’s strong execution, margin recovery and timely project delivery as key drivers of renewed investor confidence. Yinson’s renewable energy and green technology units are also gaining momentum, with solar ventures in Peru and India, and electric vehicle charging infrastructure in Malaysia expanding its sustainability profile. While the GreenTech division posted a RM17 million loss in 1QFY26, analysts see this as a temporary, early-stage dip in an otherwise promising segment. Short-term softness in 2QFY26 is expected due to tapering EPCIC contributions, but both brokerages anticipate a sharp earnings recovery in the second half of the year (2H25), fuelled by recurring income from operational FPSOs and project ramp-ups. With a diversified energy portfolio, strong ESG credentials and accelerating contributions from clean energy, Yinson remains a top pick in Malaysia’s oil & gas space, well-positioned for long-term growth. title: Tech Rally Lifts Asia Stocks; Dollar Slips Ahead Of US Jobs Data
body: Asian shares climbed on Monday, powered by unrelenting demand for technology stocks as S&P 500 futures soared to another record high, while the US dollar remained under pressure ahead of key labour market data. The bullish momentum in Wall Street’s tech sector driven by megacaps like Nvidia, Alphabet and Amazon, sent Nasdaq futures up 0.3%, and S&P 500 e-minis 0.2% higher. Japan’s Nikkei gained 1.0%, South Korea’s market added 0.5%, while the MSCI Asia-Pacific index excluding Japan edged up 0.1%. The dollar weakened as investors braced for a softer US nonfarm payrolls report, expected a day earlier due to Friday’s holiday. Economists forecast a 110,000 job increase in June with unemployment ticking up to 4.3%, potentially reinforcing expectations of a July rate cut by the Federal Reserve. Michael Feroli, JPMorgan’s head of US economics, noted continued job market softening. “The unemployment rate in June should tick up to 4.3%, with a significant risk of reaching 4.4%,” he said. Markets are currently pricing in 63 basis points of rate cuts this year, with the odds of a July easing standing at 18%—numbers likely to shift on any labour data disappointment. Meanwhile, attention also turned to the slow progress of a US tax and spending bill, with the Congressional Budget Office warning it could add US$3.3 trillion to national debt, raising concerns about foreign appetite for US Treasuries. Despite debt jitters, 10-year Treasury yields held steady at 3.27%, cushioned by the growing prospect of Fed rate cuts. The dollar index dipped to 97.163, as the euro rose to $1.1731, its highest since September 2021 and sterling hovered near $1.3719. Against the yen, the dollar slipped to 144.48 after a 1% weekly loss. James Reilly of Capital Economics highlighted a historic trend. “The dollar has fallen more so far this year than in any other since 1973,” he said, suggesting further weakness could become self-reinforcing. Fed Chair Jerome Powell is expected to speak at the ECB’s Sintra forum on Tuesday, where markets will look for more signals on US monetary policy. In commodities, gold retreated to US$3,266 an ounce, sliding further from April’s record US$3,500, while oil prices extended losses. Brent crude fell 55 cents to US$67.22, and US crude dropped 68 cents to US$64.84, amid concern over OPEC+ output plans. title: Stock Today: Top Glove Dips Amid Persisting Market Caution
body: Top Glove Corporation Bhd’s share price slipped to RM0.710 as of 11.47 am, down 1.39% or one sen from the previous close of RM0.720. The stock opened at RM0.725 and traded between a high of RM0.735 and a low of RM0.710, with a trading volume of 1.4 million shares. The decline followed bearish sentiment from analysts, with both RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) and Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) maintaining Sell calls on the stock. RHB Research revised its target price downward to RM0.65 from RM0.75, while HLIB slashed its valuation to RM0.60 from RM0.76, citing ongoing margin compression, weaker average selling prices (ASP) and intensifying competition. Despite a 4% quarter-on-quarter increase in sales volume in 3QFY25 and improved US market sales, Top Glove’s earnings remained underwhelming. RHB Research reported a 3QFY25 core loss of RM2.3 million, while HLIB, adjusting for non-operating items, flagged that operational performance remains fragile despite reporting a headline core PATMI of RM16 million. With concerns over upcoming capacity expansions by Chinese rivals and the looming 9 July US tariff decision, analysts remain cautious. The stock continues to trade below its three-year historical mean, with limited upside unless ASPs recover and plant utilisation improves. title: Stock Today: Gamuda Rallies As Investors Cement Optimism
body: Gamuda Bhd rose sharply at midday, climbing 11 sen or 2.37% to RM4.76 on strong buying interest following reaffirmed BUY calls by multiple research houses. The construction heavyweight saw 114.9 million shares changing hands as of 12.35pm, making it one of the most actively traded large-cap counters on Bursa Malaysia. The stock opened at RM4.70 and touched a high of RM4.78 before easing slightly. It last closed at RM4.65. Its intraday range spanned RM4.68 to RM4.78, indicating continued investor interest amid upbeat sentiment on its long-term project pipeline. Gamuda has been buoyed by its RM34.6 billion orderbook and growing momentum in domestic construction and digital infrastructure projects. Analysts from RHB Research, MIDF Research, CIMB Securities and HLIB all maintained their positive outlooks on the stock, with target prices ranging from RM5.42 to RM5.6 suggesting upside potential of 14% to 18% from its last traded price. RHB highlighted the company’s accelerating tender momentum, including high-conviction bids for Sabah’s RM3–4 billion water supply project and data centre ventures in Elmina and Negeri Sembilan. CIMB also pointed to Gamuda’s record RM15.8 billion job wins this year, positioning it well to meet its ambitious RM40–45 billion year-end orderbook goal. Gamuda’s earnings for 9MFY25 came in broadly within expectations for most analysts, despite property delays in Vietnam. Domestic revenue growth and a surge in local construction activity were cited as key earnings drivers. HLIB, which recently lifted its target price to RM5.50, noted further upside from the group’s Springhill data centre hub and anticipated spillover from delayed Vietnam property sales into FY26. With a diversified pipeline across domestic and regional markets, including Australia, Taiwan and New Zealand, Gamuda remains one of the top construction picks among institutional investors as the second half of the year begins. title: Ringgit Rallies As Uncle Sam Talks Cuts
body: The ringgit extended last week’s momentum, opening higher against the US dollar and other major currencies, buoyed by a weakening US Dollar Index (DXY) and ongoing fiscal policy discussions in the US Senate. At 8.01 am, the local note strengthened to 4.2190/2365 against the greenback compared to Thursday’s close of 4.2300/2355. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the ringgit stood to benefit from the anticipated fiscal impact of US policy changes, with the Senate debating tax cuts, slashes to Medicaid spending and clean energy subsidies. “All this is expected to raise fiscal deficits and US government debt level, with the Congressional Budget Office (CBO) projecting the bill would increase the deficits by nearly US$3.3 trillion from the year 2025 to 2034, while 11.8 million Americans would become uninsured by 2034,” he told Bernama. “The US government credit matrix would be weakened, which could add further pressure on the value of the US dollar,” he said. He also noted that the ringgit had gained 0.1% to RM4.2327 on Thursday and projected it would continue trading within the RM4.22 to RM4.23 range. The fiscal bill currently under deliberation carries a deadline of 4 July 2025. In broader currency performance, the ringgit was firmer across a basket of major and regional currencies. title: Oil Down 1% On Eased Tensions, Expected OPEC+ Increase
body: Oil prices slipped around 1% on June 30 as easing geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and expectations of a fresh OPEC+ production boost in August improved the global supply outlook, Reuters reported. Brent crude futures for August delivery fell 66 cents, or 0.97%, to US$67.11 a barrel by 0031 GMT, just ahead of the contract’s expiry. The more actively traded September contract dropped 83 cents to US$65.97. Meanwhile, US West Texas Intermediate crude slid 94 cents, or 1.43%, to US$64.58 a barrel. The decline comes after a volatile month driven by a sharp escalation and subsequent de-escalation in Middle East tensions. Brent crude had surged past US$80 earlier in June after the US bombed Iranian nuclear facilities in response to Israeli strikes. However, prices plunged following President Donald Trump’s announcement of a ceasefire between Iran and Israel. Despite last week marking the biggest weekly drop in oil prices since March 2023, both benchmarks are still set to post their second consecutive monthly gain in June, each rising more than 5%. Adding further pressure to prices, four OPEC+ delegates confirmed the group plans to raise output by 411,000 barrels per day in August, following similar increases over the previous three months. The move would mark the fifth consecutive monthly hike since the alliance began unwinding pandemic-era production cuts in April. The next OPEC+ policy meeting is scheduled for July 6. Market watchers now turn their focus to OPEC+ strategy, demand outlooks and the durability of the Iran-Israel ceasefire, all of which remain key drivers for oil prices heading into the second half of the year. title: Weekly Review: KOSPI Ends Trading Week Near Multi-Year High
body: South Korea’s benchmark KOSPI index closed the last trading week of June on a strong note, rising to 3,055.94 on June 27, its highest level since 2021, driven by a tech rally, easing geopolitical tensions and robust foreign inflows. The index had dipped to 2,992.2 on June 23 amid profit-taking and global uncertainty, but rebounded sharply over the following days. A ceasefire between Israel and Iran helped restore investor confidence across Asia, triggering a risk-on rally led by chipmakers. SK hynix soared nearly 9%, while Samsung Electronics climbed more than 4%, as optimism returned to tech-heavy markets. Continued buying by foreign institutional investors also provided a significant boost, pushing the index back above the key 3,000-point level. “This is the strongest first-half performance for KOSPI since 1999, with gains of over 27% year-to-date,” noted a Seoul-based equity strategist. Despite the impressive rally, analysts warn of a potential short-term correction due to overbought technical conditions. Still, the broader sentiment remains bullish, with markets buoyed by expectations of stable US interest rates and strong global tech earnings. Looking ahead, traders will closely watch upcoming macroeconomic data and corporate results, particularly from the US and China, for further cues. Analysts expect the KOSPI to consolidate within the 3,000-3,100 range in the near term. title: Crypto Review: Bitcoin Holds Steady Ahead of US$40 Billion Options Expiry

title: KOSPI Retreats On Profit-Taking After Strong Rally
body: South Korea’s benchmark KOSPI Index ended lower on June 27, slipping 0.77% to close at 3,055.94, as investors opted to take profits following a robust June rally that had pushed the index above 3,100 earlier in the week. This marks the second consecutive session of losses, driven largely by broad-based selling in battery, auto and tech sectors. Foreign investors were net sellers, offloading around 855.4 billion won worth of shares, while institutional and retail investors absorbed some of the pressure with net combined purchases of approximately 805 billion won. Despite the pullback, the KOSPI remains up around 15% for the month, bolstered by easing geopolitical tensions and increased institutional inflows that had earlier sent the index to its highest levels in over three years. Battery and automotive stocks led the decline, with LG Energy Solution falling nearly 3% and Hyundai Motor dropping 2.15%, as investors locked in gains. In tech, Samsung Electronics edged up 1%, but SK hynix lost 3.07%, reflecting mixed sentiment in the semiconductor space. Internet giant Naver dipped 1.3%, while SK Innovation slid 2.5% amid broader weakness in energy shares. The recent decline is widely viewed as a natural correction after June’s sharp gains. At home, recent economic data, including a 0.6% rise in the Leading Economic Index for April, suggest a gradual improvement in macro conditions. All three major indexes posted strong gains in a broad-based rally. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 404.41 points, or 0.94%, to close at 43,386.84. While the first quarter GDP was revised lower due to soft consumer spending and jobless claims hit multi-year highs, durable goods orders and pending home sales beat forecasts, helping buoy investor sentiment. June 26 saw a further uptick following US government reports showing a decline in crude oil and fuel inventories, coupled with rising refining activity and consumer demand. Moreover, a weakening US dollar bolstered oil prices, reaching a three-year low amid speculation over imminent Federal Reserve interest rate cuts. A depreciating dollar typically makes oil more attractive to holders of other currencies, thereby supporting prices globally. The market sentiment also shifted positively as Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu expressed optimism about the potential for peace following the ceasefire with Iran, alleviating persistent concerns over regional supply disruptions. Looking ahead, market participants remain cautious amidst ongoing geopolitical tensions and evolving demand dynamics, which continue to influence oil price movements globally. title: Stock Today: Axiata Edges Higher On Midday Trade
body: Axiata Group Bhd saw its share price inch up 0.45% to RM2.21 in midday trade on Wednesday, supported by market optimism over its ongoing financial turnaround strategy. The counter opened at RM2.20, reached a high of RM2.23 and a low of RM2.18 before settling at RM2.21 as at 12.30pm, with 32.77 million shares changing hands. The stock’s modest gain followed heightened investor interest after Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB) Research reaffirmed its BUY call on Axiata, maintaining a Sum-of-Parts-based target price of RM2.50. The research house cited the potential monetisation of Axiata’s tower arm Edotco as a key catalyst, especially after the group divested its Myanmar assets paving the way for new deals. Recent reports suggest Khazanah Nasional Bhd and the Employees Provident Fund are in talks to acquire Axiata’s 63% stake in Edotco, which is valued at around US$3.5 billion (RM14.9 billion). If realised, HLIB estimates Axiata could net RM6.3 billion, which would significantly lower its holding company debt and save up to RM210 million in interest costs. HLIB also noted that the recent completion of the XLSmart merger in Indonesia is expected to strengthen Axiata’s balance sheet through equalisation payments totalling US$475 million. These developments, coupled with Edotco’s potential disposal could cut Axiata’s net debt-to-EBITDA ratio from 3.0x to 1.0x, providing greater financial flexibility and enhancing dividend prospects. Despite possible volatility in Axiata’s upcoming 2Q results due to deconsolidation effects and forex swings, HLIB said the market is likely to focus on the broader restructuring story and improving fundamentals. title: SST Clarity Offers Bright Prospects For The Real Estate Sector
body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has maintained its OVERWEIGHT call on the real estate sector, with Buy ratings on all nine stocks under its coverage, citing resilient industrial demand and favourable SST clarification as key drivers. Sime Darby Property and Sunway were highlighted as top picks by RHB Research. Despite headwinds from global tariff uncertainty and geopolitical tension in the Middle East, RHB analysts believe the outlook remains constructive, particularly for industrial properties, supported by sustained foreign interest in data centre investments in Malaysia. The sector is also expected to benefit from a stable interest rate environment, aiding housing demand recovery. The Government’s decision to exempt serviced apartments built on commercial titles from the Sales and Service Tax (SST), provided they are for residential use under the Housing Development Act, was seen as a relief for developers. Analysts noted that key construction materials such as cement, aggregates and sand remain taxed at 0%, mitigating cost concerns. As a result, only certain components of industrial and commercial projects will bear the 6% SST impact. In Iskandar Malaysia, sentiment continues to strengthen, with robust take-up rates for new launches and property prices trending higher. According to RHB Research, demand has been particularly strong during weekends, with hotel occupancy remaining high. Retail and rental prices in some commercial clusters are now on par with those in the Klang Valley, signalling heightened investor confidence. The house expected this momentum to be further reinforced by the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone and the 2026 completion of the Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link. While the Johor market appears vibrant, developers are expected to adopt a more cautious approach in other regions. RHB forecasts steady demand for landed residential, industrial and commercial properties, which continue to attract end-users and investors. However, the higher-end high-rise segment may face some resistance, although affordable units are likely to remain resilient. Despite the sector trading at a 55% discount to its RNAV—compared to a recent peak of 45%, RHB Research said the underlying property demand remains intact, even as broader equity markets may be disrupted by regulatory shifts in the US. The research house reiterated that valuations are now more compelling, offering investors an opportunity to capitalise on potential upside. title: Port Charges Up, So Is Westports’ Outlook
body: Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) has maintained its BUY call on Westports Holdings Bhd with an upward revision to its discounted cash flow-derived target price to RM6.08 from RM5.00, citing improved earnings prospects following the Ministry of Transport’s (MoT) approval of a port tariff hike effective July 15, 2025. According to the house, the tariff revision will see a 30% increase in container handling charges, while charges for conventional and marine services will rise by 15%. These adjustments will be implemented in three phases through to January 2027 and are expected to boost Westports’ earnings and cashflow. HLIB has raised its earnings forecast for Westports by 4.1% for FY25, 18.4% for FY26 and 23.6% for FY27. The tariff restructuring comes at a pivotal time for Westports, which is executing an ambitious expansion to double its container handling capacity from 14 million to 28 million twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs). This expansion includes the development of terminals CT10 through CT17, with CT10 expected to commence operations by mid-2028 and CT11 by end-2029. Construction is slated to begin in the first quarter of 2027, while dredging and land reclamation works are already in progress. Despite concerns over the global economic outlook, Westports is operating at 80% utilisation of its current capacity and expects mid-single-digit growth in container throughput until 2027. HLIB noted that the company’s operational growth remains resilient and is unlikely to be significantly impacted by global trade headwinds. To support the capital-intensive expansion, Westports has also introduced a Dividend Reinvestment Plan (DRP), offering shares at a discount of less than 10% to the five-day volume-weighted average market price before price fixing. Major shareholders Pembinaan Redzai and South Port Invest, holding a combined 69.1% stake, have committed to participate in the DRP, ensuring continued financial stability for the group. HLIB believes the combination of tariff hikes, DRP proceeds and steady throughput growth will sustain earnings and enhance shareholder value. Westports’ share price closed at RM5.30, reflecting a potential capital upside of 14.7%, with an expected total return of 18.5% including dividends. title: Banking Sector Subdued By Macroeconomic Conditions
body: CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) has maintained a NEUTRAL rating on the banking sector following a broadly subdued earnings season for the first quarter of 2025, with Buy calls reaffirmed for Alliance Bank Malaysia (ABMB), Hong Leong Bank (HLBB), Public Bank (PBB) and RHB Bank, citing dividend yields and, in ABMB’s case, potential merger and acquisition (M&A) catalysts. According to the house, four major banks, Affin Bank, HLBB, PBB and RHB reported earnings that fell below expectations, largely due to softer loan growth, weaker net interest income and a drop in net interest margin (NIM). HLBB’s results were further impacted by a one-off dilution loss tied to its China associate, although this was partially offset by substantial write-backs in pre-emptive provisioning. CIMB Securities’ own results were slightly underwhelming, coming in 1.1% below consensus expectations, while ABMB delivered in line with forecasts. AMMB and Maybank were the only outperformers for the quarter. AMMB surprised on the upside with stronger-than-expected non-interest income and modest loan loss provisions, while Maybank’s better showing was mainly attributed to lower-than-expected loan loss provisions. Sector-wide, net earnings slipped 0.9% quarter-on-quarter (QoQ) in 1Q25, marking the first sequential decline since 1Q23. Year-on-year (YoY) earnings growth slowed to 2.6%, down from 9.5% in 4Q24, with benign loan loss provisioning continuing to support sector earnings. Despite the broadly weaker performance, CIMB Securities is keeping its sector call unchanged, stating that banking stocks are likely to trade rangebound in the coming months until there is greater clarity on macroeconomic conditions, particularly tariffs and operating costs. Key upside risks highlighted include lower credit costs, a recovery in NIM and gains from non-interest income. However, the firm cautioned against downside risks such as elevated funding costs, liquidity outflows and deteriorating asset quality. Among key valuations, Affin is rated Hold with a target price of RM2.80, AMMB Hold at RM5.70, Maybank Hold at RM9.40, while Buy ratings are maintained for ABMB (RM4.80), HLBB (RM21.50), PBB (RM5.10) and RHB (RM7.50). CIMB is not rated in this round-up. title: Wall Street Rockets As Ceasefire Fuels Rally
body: Wall Street surged on Tuesday, buoyed by easing geopolitical tensions and a dramatic drop in oil prices. The S&P 500 climbed 1.1% to 6,092.18, now just 0.8% shy of its all-time high set in February. The Dow Jones Industrial Average jumped 507 points to 43,089.02, while the Nasdaq composite gained 1.4% to finish at 19,912.53. The rally followed a global upturn, with markets in France, Germany, Japan and Hong Kong rising more than 1%. Investor confidence returned after former US President Donald Trump announced a “complete and total ceasefire” between Israel and Iran. The truce appeared to hold even after Monday’s limited retaliatory strikes by Iran, which notably avoided oil facilities. title: Fed Pause Fuels Ringgit Rally
body: The ringgit extended its gains on Wednesday, opening stronger against the US dollar and a basket of major and regional currencies, as sentiment improved following the US Federal Reserve’s signal that it would not rush into interest rate cuts. At 8am, the ringgit appreciated to RM4.2350/2450 against the greenback from Tuesday’s close of RM4.2410/2465, marking a continued upward trajectory with a year-to-date gain of 5.47%. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid noted that Fed chair Jerome Powell’s testimony to the US House Financial Services Committee showed a cautious stance, as policymakers chose to observe the economic outlook before making any rate decisions. “If the tone was less hawkish, it would cause bond yields to ease, and lower yields tend to make the US dollar less attractive to investors,” he told Bernama. In tandem, the US Dollar Index (DXY) slipped further to 97.858 points, while Brent crude declined to US$67.14 per barrel. Afzanizam added that the ringgit could potentially breach its immediate support and hover around RM4.23 to RM4.24 throughout the day. He also highlighted that the ringgit closed 1.19% higher against the greenback on Tuesday, settling at RM4.2438. The ringgit also gained ground against major currencies: rising to 2.9211/9282 against the Japanese yen (from 2.9256/9296), to 5.7651/7787 versus the British pound (from 5.7707/7782), and to 4.9173/9289 against the euro (from 4.9225/9289). Among ASEAN peers, the local note improved to 3.3083/3164 against the Singapore dollar, to 12.9701/13.0147 against the Thai baht, to 258.9/259.6 against the Indonesian rupiah, and to 7.40/7.43 versus the Philippine peso. body: Shares of Sunway Bhd rose slightly to RM4.69 in active afternoon trading, up 0.64% or 3 sen from the previous close, as investors digested recent updates on the group’s healthcare expansion and earnings outlook. At 3.20pm, the counter saw a trading volume of 3.7 million shares, with prices fluctuating between RM4.67 and RM4.74 during the day. Buy and sell queues were relatively balanced, with more than 200,000 shares on the buy side and over 790,000 on the sell side. While Sunway’s healthcare segment is expected to benefit from upcoming EPF Account 2 withdrawal policies for health insurance, analysts said the stock’s near-term upside is limited. The research house also highlighted that the group’s strong FY24 performance driven by Singapore contributions is likely to normalise in FY25, with healthcare profit before tax share declining due to startup and pre-operational costs at new hospitals. Still, with ongoing hospital developments in Putrajaya and planned expansion to 3,000 beds by 2030, investors appear cautiously optimistic, keeping the stock in focus as a long-term growth play. title: Stock Today: Mynews Inches Up Despite Trimmed Targets
body: Shares of Mynews Holdings Bhd edged 0.94% higher to RM0.535 at mid-afternoon today, despite earnings for the first half of FY25 coming in below expectations, with analysts maintaining a bullish stance on the group’s recovery prospects. As at 2.05pm, the counter saw 2.5 million shares changing hands, with intraday prices ranging between RM0.530 and RM0.555. The stock opened at RM0.540, slightly higher than its last closing price of RM0.530. RHB Research and CIMB Securities both reaffirmed their ‘BUY’ calls on the counter, although target prices were revised lower; RHB to RM0.80 and CIMB to RM0.73, after trimming earnings forecasts by up to 25%. Mynews reported a core net profit of RM6.9 million for 1HFY25, up 57.2% year-on-year, but still only meeting 28–31% of analysts’ full-year estimates. Revenue rose 7.8% to RM418.4 million, supported by 38 new store openings and stronger in-store sales, although the second quarter saw a sequential dip due to Ramadan-linked seasonality and reduced trading days. Despite short-term setbacks, both houses expect stronger performance in the third quarter as consumer demand stabilises. Analysts are also banking on improved margins, ongoing outlet expansion, and a potential breakeven for CU stores by year-end to lift earnings further. The group’s fundamentals remain attractive, according to CIMB, which highlighted a three-year net profit CAGR of 35.9% and consistent profitability since FY24. RHB noted scale efficiencies and better cost controls as supporting factors for its positive outlook. title: Stock Today: AirAsia X Jumps Nearly 8% Amid Rising Regional Travel And Airfare Demand
body: Shares of AirAsia X Bhd surged 7.84% to RM1.65 in midday trading on Monday, extending its upward momentum amid increasing regional travel activity and strong summer demand in the aviation sector. The long-haul budget airline opened at RM1.62 and climbed to an intraday high of RM1.66 before settling slightly lower. Trading volume stood at 29.5 million shares as of 12.17pm, indicating heightened investor interest in the counter, which has gained over 60% year-to-date. The stock’s rise coincides with the ongoing school holiday travel season across Southeast Asia and the return of long-haul routes to Australia, Japan and China. Analysts have noted that pent-up travel demand, especially for budget-friendly options, has lifted forward bookings and load factors across the region. Adding to investor optimism is AirAsia X’s announcement earlier this month of potential new route expansions and wet lease agreements, which are seen as strategic moves to boost capacity without the burden of immediate capital expenditure. The group is also reportedly exploring collaboration opportunities with other regional carriers to improve route connectivity and aircraft utilisation. Market sentiment for aviation counters in Malaysia has been broadly positive, fuelled by easing jet fuel prices and a stronger-than-expected rebound in passenger volumes, particularly on medium- to long-haul segments. According to the Malaysian Aviation Commission (MAVCOM), total passenger traffic for international routes rose 15% in May compared to April, signalling a continued upward trend. Additionally, AirAsia X could be benefiting from improved investor sentiment toward its parent company Capital A Bhd, which is currently undertaking a strategic review of its aviation assets to unlock shareholder value. While no formal decisions have been made public, the restructuring of aviation operations has long been anticipated by the market. AirAsia X last closed at RM1.53 and has since added 12 sen as investors respond to a combination of favourable travel demand and renewed focus on operational expansion. title: Ringgit Strengthens Against US Dollar Amid Middle East Ceasefire Hopes
body: The ringgit opened stronger against the US dollar on Tuesday, buoyed by growing optimism of military de-escalation in the Middle East following US President Donald Trump’s announcement of a tentative ceasefire between Israel and Iran. At 8 am, the local note was quoted at 4.2770/2980 against the greenback, improving from Monday’s close of 4.2915/2980. The US Dollar Index also slipped 0.29% to 98.416 points. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said traders and investors were moving away from safe-haven currencies, as the risk premium stemming from the Israel-Iran conflict appears to be easing. “Brent crude prices plunged to US$71.48 per barrel after hovering close to US$80 per barrel yesterday as prospects for de-escalation of military conflict are rising,” he said. He added that the ringgit and other emerging market currencies are expected to trade favourably in light of these positive developments. However, at the same time, the ringgit weakened against a basket of major currencies. It slipped against the Japanese yen to 2.9315/9461 from 2.9028/9074, declined versus the British pound to 5.7932/8216 from 5.7437/7524, and eased against the euro to 4.9605/9848 from 4.9236/9311 previously. The local unit also showed a mixed performance against its ASEAN peers. It strengthened against the Indonesian rupiah at 259.3/260.7 from 260.2/260.7, and edged up versus the Philippine peso to 7.42/7.46 from 7.44/7.46. Meanwhile, it fell against the Singapore dollar to 3.3339/3507 from 3.3188/3243 and dipped against the Thai baht to 13.0361/1081 from 12.9998/13.0250. title: Asian Markets Gain On Iran-Israel Ceasefire Talk
body: Asian markets posted strong gains while oil prices retreated, following an announcement by US President Donald Trump of a ceasefire agreement between Iran and Israel, temporarily quelling fears of an energy supply shock. Tehran’s muted response to a US strike on its nuclear facilities helped calm investors. Iran confirmed it had fired missiles at a major US base in Qatar, but the base remained stable and oil infrastructure was not impacted. “Tehran played it cool. Their ‘retaliation’ hit a US base in Qatar—loud enough for headlines, quiet enough not to shake the oil market’s foundations,” said Stephen Innes of SPI Asset Management. Brent and WTI crude futures plunged over 7% overnight and fell another 2% on Tuesday, as the “war premium” was swiftly priced out of the market. Asian bourses responded positively. Seoul led gains with a 2.7% jump, followed by Tokyo and Hong Kong at 1.4%, Taipei at 1.8%, Sydney at 1.1%, Shanghai at 0.8%, and Singapore at 0.7%. Jakarta, however, declined 1.7%. Trump said the ceasefire, though staggered, was aimed at bringing an “official end” to hostilities, even as Israeli strikes continued on Tehran. Iran’s foreign minister signalled no further attacks if Israel ceased its aggression. “Details of the ceasefire agreement are still sparse at the time of writing and as such the detente and de-escalation is not a done deal,” said Michael Wan at MUFG. However, he noted the risk of severe oil supply disruptions had “meaningfully diminished.” Meanwhile, in currency markets, the US dollar weakened after Federal Reserve Governor Michelle Bowman said she would support a rate cut in July if inflation remains steady. The market is still pricing in a September move, but Bowman’s remarks added momentum to dovish expectations. Bowman added that “ongoing progress in tariff negotiations” was helping to create a less risky environment for monetary adjustments. title: Utilities Sector Buoyed By New Tariff Structure: MIDF
body: MIDF Amanah Investment Bank Bhd (MIDF Research) has MAINTAINED a POSITIVE stance on the utilities sector and reiterated Buy calls on Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TP: RM16.40), YTL Power International Bhd (TP: RM4.51), Samaiden (TP: RM1.59) and Pekat (TP: RM1.86), following the Energy Commission’s announcement of a revised base tariff and a new monthly fuel adjustment mechanism under Regulatory Period Four (RP4). The base tariff has been revised upwards to 45.40 sen/kWh from 39.95 sen/kWh in RP3, representing a 13.6% increase. The updated rate, although slightly below the earlier approved 45.62 sen/kWh, is set to take effect from 1 July 2025 to 31 December 2027. Accompanying the tariff hike is the replacement of the half-yearly Imbalance Cost Pass-Through (ICPT) mechanism with a more responsive monthly Automatic Fuel Adjustment (AFA), which allows for real-time adjustments based on fluctuations in fuel prices and exchange rates. This new framework is expected to provide better financial clarity for utility firms, especially Tenaga, by removing cost pass-through lags. The AFA mechanism, capped at a 3 sen/kWh monthly change without Cabinet approval, is designed to keep tariffs more in sync with current cost conditions. According to MIDF Research, the move ensures that Tenaga’s regulated generation and retail margins remain shielded from volatility in coal, oil and gas prices, supporting more predictable cash flows. Reflecting this, the research house raised its target price for Tenaga to RM16.40 from RM15.13, citing the utility’s strong electricity demand growth and its strategic positioning in Malaysia’s energy transition. The new tariff structure also includes the reclassification of customer categories into just domestic and non-domestic users based on voltage level, replacing the previous five-tier system. Most domestic users consuming less than 1,000 kWh and small businesses using under 200 kWh monthly are not expected to see tariff increases. An Energy Efficiency Incentive will also be introduced, which may offer rebates of up to 5 to 6 sen/kWh, although exact figures were not disclosed. In addition to reforms aimed at price stability, MIDF Research noted several tailwinds for the sector. Peak electricity demand has continued to rise, hitting 20.75GW in May, while a new request-for-proposal for gas-fired power generation is expected to add 8GW of capacity. Independent power producers such as Malakoff and YTL Power are seen as likely contenders for these new generation contracts. The renewable energy space also remains a preferred segment, supported by policy incentives under the National Energy Transition Roadmap and continued rollout of large-scale solar initiatives. The house said Samaiden and Pekat are well-positioned to capitalise on these developments. title: Stock Today: Dialog Lifts 3.25% Despite Analysts’ Cautious Take On Sabah PSC
body: Dialog Group Bhd saw its share price rise 3.25% to RM1.59 as of late morning trade on Monday, with over 4.7 million shares changing hands, amid investor optimism following its upstream expansion via a new production sharing contract (PSC) with Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas). The energy services group opened at RM1.58 and touched a high of RM1.61 before settling at RM1.59 by 11:51am. This marked a 5 sen increase from its last close of RM1.54, continuing a steady upward trajectory since mid-April, when it was trading at RM1.25. Maybank Investment Bank Research has maintained a ‘BUY’ call on Dialog with an unchanged sum-of-parts-based target price of RM2.34. The firm noted that the new 14-year PSC with Petronas, covering the Mutiara Cluster off the coast of Sabah, marks a strategic move in Dialog’s upstream ambitions, although its near-term financial impact is expected to be minimal. The contract allows Dialog full operational control and 100% participation in the asset during the initial two-year pre-development phase, with a projected capex of just US$2 million. The final investment decision will determine whether it progresses to a development stage. While analysts view the move as neutral for short-term earnings, they highlighted the company’s upstream portfolio now contributes around 30% of its core net profit. Risks related to production, capex burden and oil price volatility were flagged, but Dialog’s recurring income base—mainly from tank terminal operations in Pengerang—continues to offer earnings stability, accounting for 55% of profits. Maybank Research also pointed to new contract opportunities from mega-projects in Pengerang, such as ChemOne Group’s Pengerang Energy Complex and Petronas’ RM6 billion biorefinery joint venture with Eni and Euglena, which could benefit Dialog’s long-term outlook. At its current price of RM1.59, Dialog is trading at a discount to its target valuation, as investors weigh the balance between growth opportunities and upstream-related risks. title: Middle East Tensions Stir Markets, Ringgit Holds Firm
body: Despite a firm US Dollar Index (DXY), the ringgit opened stronger on Monday against the greenback and a slew of major and regional currencies, with geopolitical anxieties dominating sentiment. At 8am, the local unit stood at 4.2420/2655 against the US dollar, up from Friday’s close of 4.2505/2565. This came as the US launched airstrikes on Iranian nuclear sites, raising fears of a broader conflict involving Israel and Iran. “The focus is clearly on how it might impact crude oil prices and risk sentiment,” said Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid. He noted Brent crude had jumped 2.49% to US$78.93 a barrel — its highest level since January 2025 — amid concerns that Iran could respond by leveraging control of the Straits of Hormuz. Afzanizam added that while the ringgit firmed initially, the currency market remains cautious, with potential downside risks as traders shift into risk-off mode. The US Dollar Index has reached 98.937 points, while spot gold rose 0.27% to US$3,377.42 per ounce. Against other major currencies, the ringgit rose to 2.9023/9186 against the Japanese yen from 2.9245/9289, strengthened to 5.7000/7316 versus the British pound from 5.7356/7437, and edged up to 4.8800/9070 against the euro from 4.9000/9069. The ringgit also posted gains against regional peers — improving to 3.2948/3133 against the Singapore dollar, 12.9243/13.0042 versus the Thai baht, 258.6/260.2 vis-a-vis the Indonesian rupiah, and 7.42/7.46 against the Philippine peso. body: As a recognised disruptor and market innovator, CUCKOO International (MAL) Bhd (CUCKOO Malaysia) — known for its cutting-edge Korean-inspired home and wellness solutions — is poised to mark a major milestone with its upcoming debut on the Main Market of Bursa Malaysia Securities. This listing signals the company’s ambitious expansion strategy and its intent to deepen its foothold in the Malaysian consumer tech space. Yet, the broader IPO landscape has not been as buoyant as in previous years. With subdued investor sentiment and mixed performances in the consumer appliance sector — as seen in the experiences of Senheng and Panasonic Malaysia — the spotlight is firmly on CUCKOO Malaysia. The key question: What unique value proposition does CUCKOO Malaysia bring to the table to reinvigorate investor confidence and stand out in a competitive market? Ahead of its listing, BusinessToday spoke with Chief Executive Officer Hoe Kian Choon to understand the rationale behind the timing, the earlier postponement from April and how CUCKOO Malaysia plans to distinguish itself as a future-ready consumer-tech leader. IPO Timing: “The Right Moment” Hoe shares that the rental-based home appliance and household goods segment is projected to grow at a CAGR of 9.9% from 2024 to 2029 Originally slated for listing on April 30, CUCKOO Malaysia chose to delay the move due to global market volatility. However, Hoe is confident that the time is now ripe for a successful debut. “We view this year as the right time for our IPO, supported by our strong financial fundamentals and dominant position in a rapidly growing industry,” said Hoe. He pointed to the rental-based home appliance and household goods segment — a market projected to grow at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 9.9% from 2024 to 2029. With current market penetration estimated at just 10%-15%, Hoe sees significant untapped potential. “The delay wasn’t a setback, but a strategic decision to further strengthen our fundamentals and ensure we enter the market from a position of strength,” he noted. CUCKOO Malaysia has raised approximately RM154.74 million in gross proceeds from the IPO. The funds will catalyse strategic initiatives across multiple fronts, including product diversification and expansion, omnichannel distribution, including new cash-and-carry stores, operational improvements, regional expansion in Malaysia and Singapore, and debt reduction to enhance financial flexibility. “The IPO proceeds are not just about scaling,” said Hoe. “They’re about building a future-proof company rooted in innovation and operational excellence.” A Differentiated Model: Recurring Revenue and Dividends While many tech listings on Bursa Malaysia have struggled to gain traction, CUCKOO Malaysia believes its subscription-based rental model sets it apart. “Our model generates stable, recurring income — an attractive proposition for both retail and institutional investors,” Hoe explained. More compellingly, CUCKOO Malaysia plans to offer a dividend payout ratio of at least 20% of net profit annually, balancing short-term investor returns with long-term strategic growth. Post-listing, CUCKOO Malaysia is planning to expand beyond water and air purifiers CUCKOO Malaysia’s post-listing blueprint is built on vertical diversification and market depth. Hoe shared that the company’s plans to expand beyond water and air purifiers into a broader portfolio. “There’s a huge opportunity in cross-selling. Currently, over 70% of our customers own just one CUCKOO product — that’s a goldmine we’re ready to tap into,” said Hoe. The company has collaborative partnerships with brands like Fujiaire, Ogawa, Wonderlab, WonderKlean, and WonderDewi. Future-Proofing: Scaling with Agility Hoe acknowledged the operational risks of scaling, from reliance on limited sales channels to logistics challenges. To address these, CUCKOO Malaysia is building a robust omnichannel ecosystem, expanding its service hubs and investing in digital transformation. “Our goal is to increase delivery capability from 31.3% in 2024 to 83% by the end of 2025. It’s a bold target, but it reflects our ambition,” he said. CUCKOO Malaysia is building a robust omnichannel ecosystem, expanding its service hubs and investing in digital transformation to address the issue of limited sales channels and logistics challenges Key to this transformation is CUCKOO Malaysia’s focus on data-driven insights and digital infrastructure to ensure the company remains agile in a fast-evolving landscape. Reflecting on CUCKOO Malaysia’s IPO journey, Hoe emphasised that the listing is not just about raising funds. “This IPO is about catalysing a broader transformation — redefining consumer wellness, deepening customer trust and setting new standards for resilience in a volatile market,” he said. “For investors, CUCKOO Malaysia offers a rare combination of recurring income, dividend potential and visionary leadership. For the industry, we represent a new category of consumer-tech companies — one rooted in sustainability, wellness and innovation.” CUCKOO Malaysia will be listed on the Bursa Securities Main Market on June 24 after an earlier scheduled date of April 30. The listing exercise will be among the most anticipated for the year, with a valuation estimate of RM1.55 billion. title: Wall Street Mixed As Triple-Witching and Global Tensions Roil Markets
body: US stocks ended mixed on June 20 as escalating tensions between Iran and Israel rattled investor confidence ahead of the weekend, while uncertainty over potential US involvement in the conflict kept markets on edge. The S&P 500 dipped 0.22% to close at 5,967.84, while the Nasdaq Composite lost 0.51% to finish at 19,447.41. The Dow Jones Industrial Average bucked the trend, inching up 35.16 points or 0.08% to 42,206.82. For the week, the S&P 500 shed 0.2%, while the Nasdaq edged 0.2% higher and the Dow was little changed. Geopolitical fears intensified as Iran ruled out nuclear talks under Israeli attack, and the White House said President Donald Trump would decide within two weeks whether the US will intervene in the ongoing air conflict. Israel has reportedly struck dozens of Iranian military targets, heightening regional instability. Tech megacaps, including Nvidia, dragged on the broader indexes, with chip stocks leading losses in the Nasdaq and S&P 500. Adding to volatility was a “triple-witching” event — the simultaneous expiration of stock options, index futures, and index options — which drove trading volume to 20.91 billion shares, well above the recent average of 18.06 billion. Investors also digested mixed signals from the Federal Reserve (Fed). While Chair Jerome Powell warned inflation may accelerate due to new tariffs, Fed Governor Christopher Waller said rate cuts could come as early as the next meeting. In contrast, Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin urged caution. Market breadth was negative, with declining stocks outnumbering advancers by a 1.1-to-one ratio on the NYSE and 1.4-to-one on the Nasdaq. As geopolitical and economic uncertainties converge, investors are bracing for more turbulence in the weeks ahead. title: KOSPI Closes Above 3,000 Amid Rally On Market Reform Optimism
body: South Korea’s benchmark KOSPI surged 1.48% to close at 3,021.84 on June 20, marking its highest finish in over three and a half years as investors cheered pro-market reforms and steady foreign inflows. This milestone, its first close above 3,000 since Dec 28, 2021, is attributed to excitement around the new administration’s planned regulatory revisions, including enhancements to fiduciary duties, expanded dividend payouts and more aggressive share buybacks. The benchmark ended the week with a 4.4% gain, its largest weekly jump in recent memory. Some of the key drivers for the growth include the rally led by foreign and institutional investors that was drawn by policies aimed at closing the “Korea Discount” and signalling continued interest in South Korean equities, the strengthening of Korean won to around ₩1,365-1,372/US dollar which further boosted foreign investor confidence and the broad-based gains led by defence and shipbuilding stocks, while tech giants like Samsung and SK hynix posted mixed results. However, some analysts caution that the rally may pause as retail investors lock in profits after the steep climb. Sustaining upward momentum will likely depend on corporate earnings improvement, continued foreign inflows and progress in capital market reforms, alongside expected US rate cuts. With the KOSPI comfortably over the 3,000 mark, attention now turns to whether it can break through the 3,100-3,200 range by year-end.
