title: Can Loob Live Up To The Expectation Or Is The Valuation Beyond Just A Cup Of Tea?
body: The following analysis commentary was contributed by Tey Eng Xin, a financial columnist and co-author of an international academic journal about investor sentiment Malaysia’s 2025 IPO landscape has thus far been defined by tepid investor sentiment, underwhelming debuts and frothy valuations that have tested the patience of institutional money. Yet within this subdued climate, local consumer brands have emerged as bright exceptions. The breakout success of Oriental Kopi Holdings Bhd and Eco-Shop Marketing Bhd signalled an inflection point, investors are shifting their focus toward businesses they understand, interact with and inherently trust. Now enters Loob Bhd, the parent of the ubiquitous Tealive franchise, poised to test the resilience of this trend. With its IPO priced at upper echelon, sceptics may argue the valuation has overshot the fundamentals. But as regional analogues such as China’s Mixue and Chagee have demonstrated, the market has proven willing to reward household brands embedded in consumers’ daily rituals. Local Champions in an Era of Global Uncertainty Viewed through a macroeconomic lens, Loob’s IPO reflects a deeper realignment in investor preferences. Domestic champions such as Mr DIY, 99 Speedmart, Farm Fresh, and now Tealive are gaining market traction for their relatability and resilience. As global trade frictions intensify and supply chains strain under geopolitical stress, local consumer brands are increasingly seen as antifragile assets. Loob’s strength lies in its insulation from such exogenous shocks. Unlike export-dependent plays, it rides on a bedrock of domestic consumption, robust distribution channels and an expanding youth demographic. It echoes the success of Farm Fresh, which challenged incumbents like Dutch Lady by building a brand narrative that was local-first, authentic and culturally relevant. More Than Tea: The Lifestyle Narrative With over 800 physical outlets and a loyalty app boasting more than two million users, Tealive has achieved what few retail brands manage: Omnichannel ubiquity. It’s visible on high-street corners, petrol stations, MRT platforms and equally omnipresent across food delivery apps, social media and mobile rewards ecosystems. What sets Tealive apart is its brand architecture. It doesn’t merely compete on pricing or flavour innovation; it curates an experience. Co-branded product lines, influencer-led campaigns and seasonal launches fuse the digital and physical in a way that cultivates loyalty, not just traffic. In this sense, Tealive mirrors the brand ethos of Starbucks: The product is not the point; the community is. Operational Precision Powered by Data Beyond its consumer-facing charm, Loob is executing a highly data-centric strategy. Its proprietary Centralised Business Intelligence System provides real-time analytics on footfall, inventory turnover, promotional effectiveness and franchisee adherence. This operational backbone enables fast feedback loops and agile response to shifting consumer behaviour. Moreover, Loob’s loyalty ecosystem serves as a rich data mine. Purchase histories, customisation trends and dwell-time analytics empower Tealive to fine-tune promotions, tailor seasonal menus and explore new business verticals, from FMCG crossovers to lifestyle merchandise. In a digital landscape where customer acquisition costs continue to climb, Loob’s first-party data advantage is a substantial competitive moat. Through its loyalty app, Tealive tracks customisation habits, timing of purchases and visit frequency, granular insights that enable hyper-targeted promotions, location-specific product development and possibly third-party monetisation. Valuation: A Steep Tag or Strategic Premium? Loob’s IPO is expected to fetch 30 times price earnings ratio. In other words, it will command a valuation at the upper echelon of Bursa Malaysia’s listings, joining other mega IPO like Mr DIY, 99 Speedmart, Oriental Kopi and Eco-Shop. But so did Oriental Kopi early this year and it has rewarded investors handsomely. Investors will need to weigh this valuation premium against several tailwinds: Brand Equity: A culturally resonant and digitally fluent brand, aligned with Gen Z and Millennials. Data & Distribution Moat: Ownership of both consumer insight and sales channels, enabling precision marketing and cost efficiencies. Domestic Defensibility: Structural insulation from foreign exchange risk, geopolitical disruptions and trade volatility. However, this is not without caveats. Tealive’s delivery-related expenses in 2024 amounted to RM31 million, roughly 10% of its administrative costs, indicating potential pressure points as margins tighten. Consumer tastes are also notoriously fickle; what feels “Instagrammable” today may be obsolete tomorrow. To sustain its premium, Loob must remain relentlessly innovative. Joint ventures (JV), regional forays and product diversification akin to JV formed by Magma and Chagee or the QL Resources-FamilyMart playbook, may be necessary next acts. Brewed for Growth, Served with Caution Loob offers what many recent IPOs have lacked: A clear, relatable story with tangible roots and scalable ambition. It occupies a rare middle ground of between the volatility of global tech and the stagnation of traditional sectors anchored by a brand Malaysians know, love and trust. For retail investors navigating a cautious capital market, Loob is not just another listing; it’s a proxy for consumer sentiment, a bet on homegrown resilience and potentially, a franchise of the future. The pricing may be lofty, but in a market searching for conviction, Loob’s offering could very well be worth the premium. If the second half of 2025 belongs to domestic champions, then Loob may very well be its boldest brew. title: Wall Street Futures Dip Amid War Fears And Fed Uncertainty
body: US stock futures fell on Thursday as geopolitical tensions and mixed signals from the Federal Reserve weighed on investor sentiment. The S&P 500 futures dropped 0.6%, with trading volumes light due to a US public holiday. The market downturn came as concerns mounted over the possibility of the United States joining Israel’s airstrikes on Iranian nuclear sites. President Donald Trump kept observers guessing, telling reporters, “I may do it. I may not do it.” The Wall Street Journal reported that Trump had already approved military strike plans but was delaying execution, pending Iran’s position on its nuclear programme. Analysts warned of further volatility. “Speculation is rife that the US will intervene,” said Kyle Rodda of Capital.com. “Such a scenario would risk a greater regional conflict, impacting energy supply and global growth.” In Europe, the STOXX 600 extended its losing streak for a third day, down nearly 2.5% for the week, marking its steepest decline since April. Meanwhile, the Federal Reserve kept interest rates unchanged and reaffirmed expectations of two rate cuts this year. However, Fed Chair Jerome Powell struck a cautious tone, warning of “meaningful” inflation due to trade tariffs. Market strategists at MUFG suggested the Fed is underestimating underlying economic fragility, particularly in the labour market. Investors now turn their attention to upcoming policy decisions from the Bank of England and the European Central Bank. title: Stock Today: Malakoff Edges Up On 22MW WTE Boost
body: Shares of Malakoff Corp Bhd rose slightly on Friday following news of a key concession secured by its subsidiary for a waste-to-energy (WTE) project in Melaka. As at 11.51am, the counter was trading at RM0.790, up 0.64% or 0.005 sen from the previous close, with 7.1 million shares changing hands. It opened at RM0.785 and hit a high of RM0.795. Buy and sell volumes stood at 1.74 million and 879,000 shares respectively. The movement comes a day after the company announced that Sungai Udang WTE Sdn Bhd, a joint venture 60%-owned by Malakoff, had entered into a 34-year Public Private Partnership Concession Agreement with the federal government. The agreement allows the company to design, build, operate and eventually demolish a WTE facility that will process 1,056 tonnes of municipal solid waste daily, generating 22MW of renewable energy to be sold to Tenaga Nasional Berhad. The facility is expected to begin construction in 2026, subject to financing and regulatory approvals. title: Stock Today: Dialog Trades Flat Despite Upstream Ambitions In Sabah
body: Shares of Dialog Group Bhd remained unchanged at RM1.58 as at 2:09pm today, amid steady trading volume and cautious investor sentiment surrounding its latest upstream move in Sabah. The counter saw 23.66 million shares traded, with the stock opening and peaking at RM1.58, while dipping slightly to an intraday low of RM1.56. Buy and sell volumes were relatively muted, with 8,500 and 2,600 lots respectively. The stagnant price action follows the group’s recent Production Sharing Contract (PSC) with Petronas for the Mutiara Cluster Small Field Asset, which marks a strategic expansion into upstream operations. The 14-year PSC grants Dialog full operational control over the marginal oil and gas fields off the coast of Sabah. Despite the long-term growth potential, analysts have rated the news as neutral in the short term, citing the early-stage nature of the project and limited near-term financial impact. title: Stellar Performance By China Unit Raises Hong Leong Bank’s Prospects
body: CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) has upgraded its rating on Hong Leong Bank Bhd (HLBB) to BUY from Hold , with an increased target price of RM21.50, citing improved prospects driven by its China associate’s stellar performance and anticipated dividend yield uplift following Basel III implementation. The bank’s strong exposure to Bank of Chengdu Co Ltd (BOCD), in which it holds a 17.8% stake, remains a key valuation anchor. BOCD’s share price surged 21.7% from a February low, reaching RMB19.57, partly due to positive sentiment following the finalisation of US tariffs on China. CIMB noted that market sentiment towards BOCD has turned decisively bullish, with 19 of 21 brokerages currently issuing Buy ratings. HLBB’s share of BOCD’s market capitalisation jumped by nearly RM1 billion since February, reflecting the rally. However, HLBB’s overall market cap softened by 9.3% over the same period, largely due to the one-off RM408 million dilution loss in 3QFY25. Despite the recent drag, CIMB Securities said the dilution loss is unlikely to recur and believes the market has over-penalised HLBB’s domestic operations, whose implied value dropped by a sharper 13.5%. BOCD’s robust fundamentals, coupled with resilient credit quality and strong property-backed loans, are expected to continue supporting HLBB’s asset strength. The house also revised its dividend payout assumptions upward, forecasting yields of 4.5% for FY26F and 5.1% for FY27F, underpinned by a rise in group CET1 capital under Basel III. HLBB’s projected net dividends per share have been raised to 88 sen for FY26F and 99 sen for FY27F. On fundamentals, HLBB posted a core net profit of RM4.2 billion in FY24, and is expected to record RM4.3 billion in FY25F despite a marginal dip in FY26F earnings. CIMB attributed this to prudent provisioning and noted the bank’s loan loss coverage, though reduced to 95% in 3QFY25, remains adequately backed by collateral and cumulative provisions. With asset quality trends consistently outperforming the industry, and dividend visibility improving, CIMB Securities sees the risk-reward balance now skewing favourably for HLBB. The brokerage maintained its fair value P/BV at 1.1 times and raised its FY26F return on equity forecast slightly to 9.8%. title: HLIB Cuts UMediC’s Earnings Forecast On Softer Revenue
body: Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) has reiterated its HOLD call on UMediC Group, lowering its target price to RM0.40 from RM0.43, citing a weaker outlook for the fourth quarter of FY25 due to foreign exchange volatility and subdued government demand. The research house cut its FY25 to FY27 earnings forecasts by 8.5%, 6.3% and 7.5% respectively, anticipating softer revenue across both its manufacturing and distribution segments. In a recent update following discussions with management, HLIB noted that the stronger ringgit against the US dollar since early April appreciating by 4.1% has led to order delays in the company’s Manufacturing division. This comes just after a strong rebound in 3QFY25, where the segment recorded RM4.4 million in revenue, a 78.6% quarter-on-quarter increase, thanks to recovering orders from Spain, South Korea and Thailand following earlier regulatory and distributor-related disruptions. Despite reaffirming that its HydroX product line will achieve a capacity of one million bottles per month by July 2025, UMediC clarified that this will not be operational until July 2026 due to a required one-year qualification period. Until then, the group will maintain operations at 300,000 bottles monthly. On the distribution front, UMediC’s Marketing and Distribution division reported a 20.6% quarter-on-quarter decline in 3QFY25 revenue to RM7.2 million, dragged by weaker orders from the Ministry of Health (MoH). This downtrend is expected to persist into 4QFY25, with flat quarter-on-quarter performance anticipated due to continued softness in public sector demand. Nonetheless, management remains hopeful for a recovery in FY26, citing positive feedback from customer surveys. Demand from the private sector continues to look promising, bolstered by brownfield and greenfield expansion plans across players like IHH Healthcare, KPJ Healthcare and Sunway Healthcare Group. Despite three consecutive quarters of underwhelming profits and a muted near-term outlook, HLIB is maintaining its Hold stance due to the stock’s inexpensive valuation. The revised target price of RM0.40 is derived from a 19x price-to-earnings multiple, which is two standard deviations below UMediC’s three-year historical mean, applied to its CY26 EPS forecast of 2.1 sen. HLIB noted that while the company faces challenges in the immediate quarters, its long-term positioning in the healthcare supply chain and capacity expansion plans provide a foundation for potential upside, especially if public sector demand rebounds more strongly than currently anticipated. title: Nikkei Slips From Four-Month High On Middle East Tensions
body: Japan’s Nikkei 225 Index fell 0.8% on Thursday, pulling back from a four-month peak as geopolitical fears surrounding the Israel-Iran conflict and the potential involvement of the United States dampened investor appetite for risk assets. The broader Topix Index also declined, losing 0.6%. The market retreat halted a three-day winning streak that had lifted the Nikkei to its highest level since Feb 20. Tensions in the Middle East continued to cloud sentiment as the conflict between Israel and Iran entered its seventh day. Nomura strategist Fumika Shimizu commented, “Heightened tensions in the Middle East continue to cool investor sentiment, with the downside appearing to widen.” In terms of market breadth, decliners far outpaced advancers, with 175 stocks down on the Nikkei compared to just 48 gainers. Taiyo Yuden led the laggards, dropping 3.1%, while Sumitomo Pharma fell 3%. However, not all was negative on the board. Nippon Steel Corp stood out as the top performer, surging 4.3% after finalising its long-awaited US$14.9 billion acquisition of US Steel, a move seen as bolstering its global footprint. Investor caution intensified after US President Donald Trump offered ambiguous signals regarding possible American involvement in airstrikes against Iran’s nuclear facilities. The uncertainty prompted a flight from equities into safer assets, cutting short the Nikkei’s upward momentum. title: Fed Holds Rates, Ringgit Holds Ground
body: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar this morning, supported by gains across major and regional currencies, even as market sentiment remained cautious following the US Federal Reserve’s interest rate decision and persistent geopolitical tensions. At 8am, the local unit strengthened to 4.2435/2650 against the greenback compared to the previous close of 4.2500/2550. He added the ringgit weakened by 0.22% against the greenback on Thursday following a dollar rally, with investors also cautious ahead of the end of the 90-day tariff pause period in early July. “On that note, we shall expect the ringgit to stay soft in the near term as sentiments in the market remain guarded,” he said. The ringgit showed broad gains in early trade. It advanced against the euro to 4.8698/8945 from 4.8888/8945, rose to 5.6922/7211 from 5.7218/7285 against the British pound, and improved to 2.9276/9426 from 2.9322/9359 versus the Japanese yen. Among regional peers, the ringgit appreciated to 3.3018/3188 against the Singapore dollar, strengthened to 12.9794/13.0536 versus the Thai baht, and edged higher to 260.1/261.5 against the Indonesian rupiah. title: Wall Street Slumps As Mideast Tensions Rattle Investors, Economic Data Weakens Outlook
body: Wall Street ended sharply lower as rising geopolitical tensions and a batch of weak economic indicators triggered a broad-based selloff across US equities. The S&P 500 slid 0.8%, while the Nasdaq 100 lost 1%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 0.7%, and the Russell 2000 shed 1.1%. Risk-off sentiment dominated trading amid escalating conflict in the Middle East, with renewed concerns that the US could become directly involved following former President Donald Trump’s call for Iran’s “unconditional surrender”. Investor nerves were further frayed by soft US economic data. Retail sales declined for a second straight month, industrial production dipped, and confidence among homebuilders fell to its lowest level since late 2022 — all signalling potential weakness in consumer sentiment and housing momentum. Meanwhile, 10-year Treasury yields fell six basis points to 4.39%, as investors piled into safe havens on bets the Federal Reserve may need to cut rates again later this year. The Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index rose 0.5%, marking its biggest daily gain in a month. In corporate moves, JetBlue Airways announced a shakeup in leadership and route cuts, Lennar Corp. missed forecasts for quarterly home orders, and Eli Lilly acquired Verve Therapeutics in a US$1.3 billion biotech deal. According to a Bank of America survey, only 23% of global asset managers now expect US stocks to be the top-performing asset class over the next five years, compared to 54% who favour international equities. title: Ringgit Holds Its Nerve As Fed Decision Looms
body: The ringgit opened marginally stronger against the US dollar today as investors stayed on edge ahead of a key interest rate decision from the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), expected later tonight. He also warned that escalating tensions in the Middle East could complicate the Fed’s policy direction, particularly in an already uncertain global economic climate. At the same time, the ringgit traded firmer against most major currencies. title: Retail Spending Remains Buoyant Amid Low Inflation, Peak Employment
body: MIDF Amanah Investment Bank Bhd (MIDF Research) has maintained its POSITIVE call on the consumer sector, citing robust performance in the first quarter of 2025 driven by festive spending and ongoing resilience in retail demand. The research house continues to favour Fraser & Neave Holdings Bhd (F&N) with a target price of RM32.68, Aeon Co (M) Bhd at RM1.77 and Life Water Industries Bhd at RM1.00, while it downgraded Oriental Kopi to Neutral and upgraded Spritzer Bhd to Buy on valuation grounds. In its latest sector update, MIDF Research noted that Malaysia’s retail trade grew 4.7% year-on-year in April to RM66.76 billion. This followed stronger growth in March at 6.6%, reflecting a typical post-Hari Raya normalisation. Despite a mild month-on-month pullback of 0.3%, the research house said cumulative retail trade in the first four months of 2025 still expanded by 6.3% to RM265.02 billion, anchored by firm household spending and stable macro fundamentals. Labour market strength continues to support the sector. Malaysia’s unemployment rate eased to 3.0% in April, the lowest since the pandemic began. Combined with firm wage growth and relatively low inflation headline CPI remained at 1.4% year-on-year and core CPI rose marginally to 2.0%, household purchasing power remained intact. The house highlighted that this environment helped sustain both essential and discretionary spending. The research firm also pointed to continued momentum in tourism as a catalyst for the broader consumer sector, with increasing tourist inflows contributing positively to retail and F&B segments. Meanwhile, the appreciation of the ringgit in May was viewed as a supporting factor for cost stability, particularly for import-heavy sectors like food and beverage. MIDF Research noted that policy normalisation is underway for poultry, with cost trends generally supportive. In the F&B space, mixed commodity trends were observed, though sugar and wheat showed cost relief, which could benefit manufacturers’ margins in upcoming quarters. Looking ahead, the consumer outlook remains constructive. MIDF Research expects retail demand to stay resilient, supported by structural drivers such as civil service wage increases, adjustments in minimum wages, targeted government cash assistance and the ongoing tourism recovery. These factors are likely to offset uncertainties from external macroeconomic risks and sustain private consumption. Aeon continues to stand out as a preferred pick due to its defensive nature, strong positioning in the mass-market retail space and recurring income from property management services, which MIDF believes offer a stable earnings base across market cycles. title: Gamuda Favoured In Achieving RM40 Billion Targets
body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has reiterated its BUY call on Bhd Gamuda with a revised target price of RM5.64, citing an 18% potential upside and underpinned by solid earnings momentum and a robust project pipeline. The research house expects third-quarter FY25 core earnings to come in between RM230 million and RM250 million, marking a year-on-year increase of 4% to 13%, supported by steady progress on projects such as the Sydney Metro West. Gamuda remains one of the strongest contenders in Malaysia’s construction sector, not only for its conventional infrastructure capabilities but also for its growing footprint in data centre and renewable energy construction particularly in Australia, the research house reported. These strengths justify a premium valuation of 19.7 times FY26 forward earnings, compared to the 10-year Bursa Malaysia Construction Index average of 14 times. Gamuda’s unbilled orderbook was estimated at RM32 billion as at end-2024. With a burn rate of around RM1 billion per month, the company would require RM20 billion to RM25 billion in new project wins in calendar year 2025 to meet its end-year orderbook target of RM40 billion to RM45 billion. So far, contracts secured this year include the RM5 billion Penang Light Rail Transit Segment 1 and RM1 billion in data centre enabling works in Negeri Sembilan, leaving RM14 billion to RM19 billion to go. RHB Research expressed confidence in Gamuda’s ability to achieve this, even after losing out on the Suburban Rail Loop Line Wide Package in Australia, estimated at RM10 billion. The company is still in contention for about RM24 billion worth of contracts with a high probability of success, along with another RM12 billion in lower-certainty projects. This pipeline, the analyst said, should offer sufficient cushion to close the current gap in its orderbook target. Potential near-term wins could include a RM3 billion water supply scheme in Sabah and the second phase of Pearl Computing Malaysia’s data centre at Elmina, valued at approximately RM2 billion. The house is also encouraged by Gamuda’s early contractor involvement in several Australian renewable energy projects, which typically have higher conversion rates and could be worth at least AUD3 billion collectively. Despite trimming its job replenishment forecast for FY25 to RM20 billion from RM25 billion, the investment bank has raised expectations for FY26 and FY27 to RM21 billion and RM17 billion, respectively. This, along with more conservative billing projections for large-scale infrastructure like the Penang LRT, led to downward revisions of FY25 to FY27 earnings by up to 9.6%. Factoring in an 8% ESG premium, RHB Research’s new sum-of-parts valuation of RM5.64 reflects Gamuda’s 3.4 ESG score, which surpasses Malaysia’s 3.0 median. Upside catalysts could come from faster-than-expected execution of major infrastructure contracts, although key risks remain in the form of slower job wins. title: Wall Street Bounces Back As Oil, Gold Retreat Amid Easing Middle East Fears
body: Calm returned to Wall Street on Monday as US stocks rebounded sharply, oil prices slipped from recent highs, and investors began shifting their focus from Middle East tensions to this week’s key US Federal Reserve decision. The S&P 500 surged 0.9%, regaining much of its losses from last Friday, closing at 6,033.11. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 317.30 points, or 0.8%, to 42,515.09, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq composite jumped 1.5% to 19,701.21. The rally was part of a broader global market rebound, with gains seen across Asia and Europe. Investors were initially rattled last week after Israel struck Iranian nuclear and military sites, sparking fears of a wider conflict that could disrupt global oil supplies. But by Monday, oil prices retreated sharply as markets grew hopeful that the conflict may remain contained. US crude slid 1.7% to US$71.77 per barrel, while Brent fell 1.3% to US$73.23, after both had jumped nearly 7% on Friday. Similarly, gold pulled back from its safe-haven spike, down 1% to US$3,417.30 per ounce. Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi hinted at diplomacy, suggesting a US intervention with Israel “may pave the way for a return to diplomacy” – remarks that helped ease geopolitical concerns. Meanwhile, traders are keeping a close eye on this week’s Federal Reserve meeting. The US central bank is widely expected to keep interest rates steady, though markets are looking for clues in its economic projections. Economists at Bank of America anticipate the Fed may signal just one rate cut in 2025, followed by more in 2026. In the bond market, the 10-year Treasury yield ticked up to 4.45% from 4.41% on Friday, reflecting easing anxiety in financial markets. Among notable gainers, Sage Therapeutics rocketed 35.4% after Supernus Pharmaceuticals announced a deal to acquire the company for up to US$795 million. US Steel rose 5.1% following an executive order signed by President Donald Trump backing its investment deal with Japan’s Nippon Steel, giving him direct influence under the terms. On the flip side, defense stocks gave back some of their war-premium gains: Lockheed Martin dropped 4%, while Northrop Grumman slid 3.7%. title: Today’s Shares: Westports Up 5%, Continuing Momentum
body: Westports Holdings Berhad surged 5.17% to RM5.29 at 11.50am today, buoyed by the Malaysian government’s new port tariff structure, though regional tensions cast a shadow over future volumes. Analysts at RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) noted the staggered 30% tariff increase at Port Klang, effective from June 15, 2025 to 2027, should lift earnings as the house has upgraded its forecasts by 11% for FY25 and FY26 and by 13% for FY27, raising its target price to RM4.90 with a 2% ESG premium. CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) also views the tariff hike favourably, given that container handling accounts for 85.5% of Westports’ 2024 revenue. Its pan‑phased approach is likely to benefit from the Westports 2 terminal expansion, though only a quarter of transshipment contracts are renewed annually, resulting in a gradual earnings uplift through second half of 2025. Despite the positive tariff narrative, ongoing geopolitical instability from the Israel‑Iran conflict to reciprocal US tariffs continues to threaten seaborne trade flows. RHB Research cautioned that the full impact of these uncertainties on shipping volumes remains unclear. A mid‑June drayage strike in Port Klang has also disrupted container movements, compounding concerns over possible congestion at terminals. Technically, Westports has broken above RM5.00, with strong trading volume of 4.7 million shares supporting the rebound from RM5.03 LACP. The stock’s intraday range inched between RM5.09 and RM5.40, hinting at renewed investor confidence. title: Nikkei Rises Ahead Of BOJ Decision, Chip Stocks Shine
body: Japan’s Nikkei share average edged up on Tuesday, supported by a tech-led rally and optimism from Wall Street, as investors looked ahead to a key policy decision from the Bank of Japan (BOJ). The Nikkei climbed 0.4% to 38,482.43 by 0053 GMT, while the broader Topix added 0.1%. Among the Topix sectors, growth shares outperformed with a 0.2% gain, while value shares slipped 0.1%. Of the Nikkei’s 225 constituents, 101 rose, 119 declined, and five remained flat. Chip-related counters led the way. Disco soared 6.4%, marking the biggest percentage gain on the index. Advantest jumped 3.8%, while Tokyo Electron gained 3.3%. All three major US stock indexes had closed strongly higher overnight, after signs of easing tensions in the Middle East, with Iran seeking a ceasefire with Israel. Market attention now turns to the BOJ, which is widely expected to hold interest rates steady. However, speculation is mounting that the central bank could reduce its monthly Japanese government bond purchases by as much as half — from 400 billion yen to 200 billion yen — beginning in April next year. The BOJ policy announcement is anticipated between 0230 and 0400 GMT, with Governor Kazuo Ueda’s press conference slated for 0630 GMT. Ueda is expected to reaffirm a hawkish stance on rates despite rising uncertainty stemming from global trade tensions and ongoing geopolitical conflicts. title: Today’s Shares: Gamuda Slips 1.05% At Midday As SST Casts Over Sector
body: Shares of Gamuda Bhd dipped slightly at midday as markets reacted to the impending expansion of Malaysia’s Sales and Service Tax (SST), which is set to start applying a 6% service tax on construction services from 1 July. At 12.35 pm, Gamuda’s stock was down 5 sen or 1.05% at RM4.72, with around 33 million shares traded. The counter had opened at RM4.70, swinging between RM4.70 and RM4.75. Buying interest remains robust with over 4 million shares in the buy queue, while sell volume stands near 1.9 million shares. This pullback reflects expectations that the 6% service tax could affect earnings margins for infrastructure firms. Construction sector players involved in commercial, industrial, or infrastructure projects—including Gamuda—must now register and face the SST levy once their annual revenue surpasses RM1.5 million. The Federation of Malaysian Manufacturers (FMM) emphasised that the new tax aims to bolster fiscal revenue and is part of Budget 2025’s broader measures, yet felt anxious over the readiness of large fixed-price contracts. While residential building projects remain exempt from the service tax, Gamuda’s mixed portfolio of infrastructure ventures places it at the centre of investor concern. The construction sector, especially firms like Gamuda, may need to absorb or renegotiate the tax impact. Notably, the Master Builders Association Malaysia (MBAM) has voiced strain over this levy, citing cash flow disruption and urging clarity on transitional arrangements. Despite these concerns, the broader market remains cautiously optimistic. The broader FMKLCI index moved slightly lower, and investors appear to be cautiously absorbing the implications of the SST levy before the second half of 2025 kicks in. Gamuda, a major infrastructure and construction player, is expected to adjust pricing or contract structures to manage the new levy. Market watchers will be tracking commentary from the company and government clarifications in the coming weeks to gauge the levy’s full impact. title: Ringgit Rises Amid Geopolitical Jitters, Strengthens Across the Board
body: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar and a basket of other major and ASEAN currencies on Monday, buoyed by cautious trading sentiment following heightened geopolitical risks in the Middle East. At 8am, the local currency advanced to 4.2365/2600 against the greenback compared to Friday’s close of 4.2435/2480. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid attributed the currency market’s risk-off mode to the ongoing Israel-Iran military conflict. “Risks of the conflict expanded in scope which undermined US military bases and assets in the Middle East region. It’s going to be a risk-off mode in the currencies market,” he told local media. The ringgit also appreciated against regional currencies, strengthening against the Singapore dollar to 3.3020/3206 from 3.3077/3118, the Thai baht to 13.0310/1101 from 13.0807/1018, the Indonesian rupiah to 259.8/261.4 from 260.2/260.6, and the Philippine peso to 7.54/7.59 from 7.55/7.56. Dr Afzanizam said attention is now on oil prices, with Brent crude hovering around US$75.67 per barrel after briefly touching US$78.32. “Judging from the prevailing oil price condition, it appears the risk-off mode has yet to result in significantly higher crude oil prices,” he noted. Against major currencies, the ringgit also saw gains. It improved against the Japanese yen to 2.9300/9467 from 2.9448/9482, climbed against the British pound to 5.7379/7697 from 5.7482/7543, and firmed up versus the euro at 4.8872/9143 from 4.8906/8958. title: Weekly Wrap: Wall Street Ends Mixed As Fed Cools Hopes For Rate Cuts
body: The Wall Street closed the week on a mixed note, with investors reacting to softer inflation data and a more cautious Federal Reserve (Fed) policy outlook. The S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average posted modest losses, while the Nasdaq Composite extended its winning streak, buoyed by strength in heavyweight tech stocks. title: Oil Prices Surge 7% As Israel-Iran Conflict Sparks Supply Fears
body: Oil prices surged on June 13, posting their sharpest gains since 2022, as escalating hostilities between Israel and Iran rattled global energy markets and stoked fears of major supply disruptions from the Middle East. Brent crude futures settled 7.02% higher at US$74.23 a barrel, after briefly spiking over 13% to US$78.50, their highest intraday level since late January. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude closed up 7.62% at US$72.98, following a jump to US$77.62, its strongest since January 21. The price swings came as Israel launched strikes on Iranian nuclear and military targets on June 13, marking the beginning of what it called a “prolonged operation” to thwart Tehran’s nuclear ambitions. Iran responded later in the day with missile attacks on Tel Aviv, according to media reports, intensifying fears of a wider regional conflict. The turmoil adds fresh uncertainty to oil markets already on edge. Iran, a key OPEC member, exports over two million barrels per day (bpd) and produces roughly 3.3 million bpd. Analysts say any sustained disruption to its output or to shipments through the Strait of Hormuz, which handles nearly 20% of global oil flows, could significantly tighten supply. Despite the flare-up, Iran’s national oil company said refining and storage facilities remain operational. Meanwhile, the US oil rig count declined by three this week to 439, the lowest since October 2021, signalling limited domestic supply response in the short term. The sharp price rally mirrors the market shock seen in early 2022, when Russia’s invasion of Ukraine triggered a spike in global energy costs. With geopolitical tensions mounting and crude benchmarks up over 12% on the week, markets are bracing for more volatility ahead. title: US Stocks Retreat From Record Highs As Safe-Haven Demand Rises
body: US stocks edged lower on Thursday as rising geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and renewed trade uncertainty between Washington and Beijing prompted investors to seek safer assets. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures fell 0.5%, snapping a rally that has largely persisted since early April. The broader MSCI All-Country World Index dipped 0.1%, just under Wednesday’s all-time high. This market pullback comes amid a sharp slide in the US dollar, which has declined around 10% this year. On Thursday, the dollar touched its lowest level since late April, a three-year low, as risk sentiment weakened. The euro rose to US$1.1535, a seven-week high, while the Swiss franc and Japanese yen both strengthened, with the dollar losing about 0.6% against each. Investors responded cautiously after the US administration announced the relocation of personnel from the Middle East due to increased regional threats. Meanwhile, optimism over this week’s apparent breakthrough in US-China trade talks faded, as President Donald Trump hinted at sending out letters to dozens of countries with new trade deal terms. “Markets may have no choice but to respond to Trump’s tariff threat — even if it’s just posturing,” said Charu Chanana, Chief Investment Strategist at Saxobank. On the data front, May’s US consumer inflation remained soft, helped by lower prices in gasoline, housing, and cars. But analysts expect price pressures to intensify once US tariffs filter through the economy. Treasury yields eased, with the 10-year yield dropping below 4.4% and 2-year yields at 3.93%, reflecting shifting rate expectations. A producer inflation report due later today could offer further clarity. Despite market jitters, analysts say the Federal Reserve is likely to hold off on any rate cuts until September, waiting to assess the economic impact of tariffs. Despite these headwinds, analysts acknowledged BAuto’s 10% dividend yield and strong net cash of RM207 million. Still, they cautioned that poor order replenishments and underwhelming new launches may drag earnings further. title: Ringgit Strengthens Further On Weak US Data
body: The ringgit extended its gains against the US dollar at Friday’s open, buoyed by persistent weakness in US economic indicators, according to an analyst. At 8am, the local unit rose to 4.2095/2270 against the greenback, compared to Thursday’s close of 4.2155/2245. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US Dollar Index (DXY) dropped 0.72% to 97.0921—its lowest since March 2022—as latest figures pointed to a cooling labour market and softer inflation pressures. “Such data are seen as critical in shaping the US Federal Reserve’s (Fed) stance ahead of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on June 17 and 18,” he told local media. He noted that the core Producer Price Index (PPI) for May rose 3.0% year-on-year, which was below market expectations of 3.1%. Meanwhile, initial jobless claims climbed to 248,000 last week, above the forecast of 242,000. Mohd Afzanizam said while the Fed is expected to maintain the Federal Funds Rate at 4.50%, markets are focused on the central bank’s upcoming quarterly economic projections. “In March, Fed officials projected the policy rate at 3.9% for 2025, which implies two rate cuts this year. “On that note, we believe emerging market currencies, including the ringgit, are poised to appreciate,” he said. The ringgit, however, traded mostly lower against a basket of major currencies. It gained against the euro to 4.8860/9063 from 4.8765/8869 but weakened against the Japanese yen to 2.9412/9539 from 2.9329/9394 and fell versus the British pound to 5.7363/7601 from 5.7213/7335. Against regional peers, the ringgit showed a mixed performance. It edged higher against the Philippine peso to 7.54/7.58 from 7.55/7.57 and rose slightly versus the Indonesian rupiah to 259.1/260.3 from 259.5/260.2. However, it slipped against the Singapore dollar to 3.2936/3078 from 3.2934/3006 and eased against the Thai baht to 13.0124/0754 from 12.9828/13.0173. title: Wall Street Ends Lower As Geopolitical Tensions Offset Inflation Relief
body: Wall Street closed lower on Wednesday, as escalating tensions in the Middle East unnerved investors despite a cooler-than-expected US inflation report that strengthened expectations for a Federal Reserve rate cut later this year. The S&P 500 slipped 0.34% to 6,018.27, while the Nasdaq fell 0.56% to 19,605.32 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average edged down 0.02% to 42,857.30. Markets initially climbed after data showed US consumer prices rose only 2.4% year-on-year in May, slightly below the 2.5% forecast. However, a report that the US embassy in Iraq was preparing for evacuation due to regional security threats reversed the gains. Tensions rose further after an Iranian official warned of potential strikes on US bases if nuclear talks failed. Despite the geopolitical unease, traders are now pricing in a 70% probability of a Fed rate cut by September, according to CME Group’s FedWatch tool. This sentiment was supported by signs of moderate inflation, which tempered fears that the Trump administration’s tariffs would drive prices sharply higher. Meanwhile, markets also digested news that the US and China had agreed on a framework to reset trade negotiations. President Donald Trump confirmed a deal with Beijing, which includes reciprocal tariffs and commitments on rare earth supplies. However, analysts remain cautious over the implementation of the agreement. Among the S&P 500’s 11 sectors, eight declined, led by consumer discretionary stocks (-1.06%) and materials (-0.94%). On the upside, information technology gained 0.4%, with Tesla rising 0.5% after CEO Elon Musk acknowledged regret over past social media comments targeting Trump. Other notable movers included GitLab, which fell 6% after disappointing quarterly results, and GameStop, down 3.9% following a drop in first-quarter revenue. Overall, declining stocks outpaced advancers by a 1.9-to-one ratio on the S&P 500, which logged 10 new highs and 2 new lows, while the Nasdaq posted 77 new highs and 34 new lows. title: Ringgit Strengthens On Softer US Data, But Slips Against Key Regional, Major Currencies
body: The ringgit continued its upward momentum against the US dollar on Thursday morning, supported by weaker-than-expected US economic data, according to an analyst. At 8am , the local note stood at RM4.2305/2405 versus the greenback, slightly firmer than Wednesday’s close of RM4.2345/2370 . Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US Dollar Index (DXY) dropped 0.47% to 98.631 points , following a softer inflation print from the world’s largest economy. “The short-term US Treasury fell as hope for interest rate cuts has gained momentum, with the two-year yield dropping seven basis points to 3.95%,” he told Bernama . He added, “It appears that expectations for rate cuts would be in the spotlight. The current US Federal Reserve (Fed) chairman’s term ends next May. US President Donald Trump is likely to appoint a Fed chief who aligns with his agenda, that is, to prescribe further monetary easing.” The US Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 2.4% in May, slightly below market expectations of 2.5% , while the core CPI came in at 2.8% , missing the 2.9% consensus forecast. Dr Afzanizam believes the DXY is likely to remain below the 100-point mark for some time, a trend that should favour emerging market currencies like the ringgit. He expects the ringgit to continue trading with an upward bias, likely fluctuating within the RM4.22–RM4.23 range in the near term. Despite its gains against the greenback, the ringgit traded lower against a basket of major currencies at the open. The local currency weakened against the Japanese yen to 2.9344/9415 from 2.9187/9207 , slipped vis-à-vis the British pound to 5.7399/7535 from 5.7166/7200 , and fell against the euro to 4.8693/8808 from 4.8426/8454 . Among its ASEAN peers, the ringgit’s performance was mixed. It inched higher against the Indonesian rupiah at 260.1/260.8 from 260.4/260.6 , and was unchanged versus the Philippine peso at 7.57/7.59 . However, it slid against the Singapore dollar to 3.2953/3033 from 3.2925/2947 , and weakened against the Thai baht to 12.9949/13.0333 from 12.9729/9870 previously. title: US Stocks Rise As Trade Talks With China Offer Tentative Optimism
body: US stock futures climbed on Tuesday as hopes for progress in trade negotiations between the United States and China provided a lift to market sentiment. The second round of talks between top US officials — including Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and Trade Representative Jamieson Greer — and their Chinese counterparts began in London following what US President Donald Trump described as a “positive” first day. “The fact that we’re still near record highs suggests markets are accepting the tone of the talks,” said Tony Sycamore, market analyst at IG. “But the market always likes to see some concrete announcements.” Investors remained cautious but encouraged, with Nasdaq futures up 0.62%, S&P 500 futures rising 0.43% and EUROSTOXX 50 and FTSE futures each gaining about 0.1%. Asian markets extended gains from earlier in the week, as MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan rose 0.5%. However, the US dollar struggled to find firm ground amid ongoing uncertainty over Federal Reserve rate expectations and debt concerns. The dollar edged up 0.45% to 145.25 yen, but fell 0.28% against the euro to $1.1387, while the British pound slipped 0.2% to $1.3523. Market watchers are now eyeing the upcoming US consumer price index (CPI) data on Wednesday, which may shape expectations for the Federal Reserve’s policy path in the coming months. Traders have priced in around 44 basis points worth of rate cuts by year-end, though a stronger CPI print could push back expectations for immediate easing. title: Today’s Shares: IHH Slides 0.4% Despite RM425 Million Q1 Profit Surge
body: Shares of IHH Healthcare Bhd slipped 0.44% to RM6.86 as of 4.27pm on Wednesday, despite a strong year-on-year (YoY) and quarter-on-quarter (QoQ) rebound in earnings for 1QFY25 and an optimistic outlook for the rest of the financial year. The counter opened at RM6.90 and hit a low of RM6.83, with 46.64 million shares traded. It last closed at RM6.89. Kenanga Investment Bank Bhd (Kenanga Research) maintained its “Outperform” rating on IHH, following a 5% YoY increase in core net profit to RM425 million for 1QFY25, which also marked a 34% QoQ jump. The earnings were attributed to better revenue intensity and stronger yield across operations, particularly in Singapore, Malaysia, Türkiye and India. However, quarterly revenue declined 6% QoQ due to hyperinflationary adjustments, although core hospital revenue rose 2%. The group’s EBITDA rose 20% YoY, and no dividend was declared for the quarter. title: Today’s Shares: AirAsia X Shares Ease Despite Potential Gains From Jetstar Asia Exit
body: Shares of AirAsia X Bhd (AAX) slipped 0.57% to RM1.74 as at 3.48pm today, despite a market development that could ease competition in the regional low-cost aviation segment following Jetstar Asia’s announced closure. AAX, listed on the Main Market under the Consumer Products & Services sector, saw its counter trade between a low of RM1.73 and a high of RM1.77 on Tuesday, with over 5.3 million shares exchanging hands. The dip came even as Qantas confirmed earlier today that Jetstar Asia, its Singapore-based budget airline will cease operations on July 31, citing unsustainable costs and intense competition in the region. The move affects 16 intra-Asia routes currently served by Jetstar Asia, including destinations across Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand and China, regions where AirAsia X has a growing presence. Jetstar Asia’s exit could potentially benefit regional low-cost carriers like AirAsia X, which are facing similar margin pressures but now stand to capture displaced demand and routes. Still, the stock showed little immediate reaction, with investors possibly taking a cautious view amid broader aviation sector uncertainties. At the time of writing, AAX had a buy-sell spread of RM1.73 to RM1.74, with last closing price at RM1.75. title: Ringgit Finds Early Strength Amid Renewed US-China Trade Talks
body: The ringgit opened stronger against the US dollar on Wednesday, lifted by cautious optimism as markets watched closely for developments in the ongoing trade negotiations between the United States and China in London. At 8 am, the local unit stood at 4.2290/2380 against the greenback, improving from Tuesday’s close of 4.2360/2420. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid noted that the US dollar index (DXY) fluctuated between 98.962 and 99.358 overnight, reflecting market uncertainty as investors assessed the progress of the US-China talks. “US secretary of commerce Howard Lutnick described the discussion as running well, suggesting the two nations could potentially arrive at a midway (point) in their negotiations,” he told local media. The ringgit also recorded gains against most major and regional currencies. It advanced against the Japanese yen to 2.9200/9264 from 2.9270/9314 and appreciated versus the British pound at 5.7121/7243 from 5.7152/7233. However, it was slightly lower against the euro at 4.8367/8470 compared to 4.8354/8422 previously. Against ASEAN currencies, the ringgit rose across the board. It strengthened to 3.2885/2957 versus the Singapore dollar from 3.2932/2981 and improved against the Thai baht to 12.9664/13.0040 from 12.9712/9955. It was also higher at 7.57/7.59 against the Philippine peso from 7.58/7.60 and edged up to 259.8/260.5 against the Indonesian rupiah from 260.2/260.7. Mohd Afzanizam also highlighted political developments in Washington, where the debate continues over US President Donald Trump’s “Big, Beautiful Bill”. Several Republican senators are reportedly pushing to phase out clean-energy tax credits, arguing that a sudden shift could disrupt investment and employment. He added that the US fiscal outlook remains a point of concern, with deficits and national debt expected to rise. “While market sentiments demonstrated a positive sign, it is still an early day. On that note, we expect the ringgit-dollar exchange to remain range-bound between 4.23 and 4.24 today,” he said. title: Maybank IB Reiterates Buy Call On Frencken Group
body: Maybank Investment Bank Bhd (Maybank IB) has reiterated its BUY rating on Frencken Group Ltd, citing a stronger FY25 earnings outlook and an unchanged target price of S$1.34. The research house continues to list Frencken as its top pick within the Singapore technology sector, supported by the group’s recent decision to invest S$63 million in a new manufacturing facility at Kaki Bukit Avenue 5. Frencken has secured a 33-year lease for the industrial land, with completion of the new plant expected by the first quarter of 2027. The expanded facility will significantly increase its manufacturing footprint, allowing the group to house larger cleanrooms and support rising demand from its semiconductor and life science clients. Maybank IB highlighted that the lack of large cleanroom capabilities in Singapore had previously restricted Frencken’s growth potential with certain wafer fabrication customers. The new facility is expected to address these constraints while boosting efficiency, margins and product range. The plant, with a gross floor area of 28,594 sqm, will consolidate existing operations currently split between Changi North and Seletar Aerospace Link. According to the house, this integration will streamline production workflows, optimise resource allocation and improve operational efficiency. The expansion will be funded through a combination of internal cash flow and external financing. Maybank IB also pointed to broader tailwinds from the ongoing recovery in the global semiconductor industry. With key semiconductor clients also growing their presence in Singapore, Frencken’s timely expansion aligns well with customer needs and market momentum. In addition, the bank noted that the move helps Frencken hedge against geopolitical risks, particularly the potential for escalated trade tensions between the US and China. Despite current global uncertainties, analysts believe Frencken is well-positioned to capture the next wave of industry growth through strategic capacity enhancements. Maybank IB has left its blended FY25/26 price-to-earnings ratio forecast at 13 times, underpinning its unchanged valuation outlook. Frencken’s shares were last traded at S$1.15, implying a 20% upside to the target price. title: ITMAX Eyes Smart City Infrastructure Play
body: Maybank Investment Bank Bhd (Maybank IB) has reiterated its BUY call on ITMAX System Bhd with an unchanged price target of RM4.50, citing strong earnings visibility anchored by its dominant position in the smart city infrastructure space and a promising new AI-enabled growth segment. Maybank IB noted that ITMAX’s CCTV business continues to gain traction, particularly in Johor, where the state has adopted a single-supplier policy for its smart city infrastructure. The company has already secured contracts to install 1,640 CCTV units across four districts in the Iskandar Malaysia region and is now in discussions with authorities in Pengerang, Batu Pahat and Muar. With 12 more districts yet to be awarded, the house described ITMAX’s continued expansion in Johor as a matter of “when” rather than “if.” The research house has currently factored in 2,000 CCTV installations in Johor for FY2025 and FY2026 but highlighted that every additional 1,000 units could raise core earnings by approximately 2.4% to 3.6% over FY2025–FY2027. Momentum outside Johor is also set to accelerate. Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) is targeting 20,000 CCTV units across the capital by end-2028, which implies at least 10,000 more installations in the next three years—a number that analysts confirmed has already been baked into their earnings forecast. ITMAX was also involved in the planning of Kota Kinabalu’s first CCTV network, comprising 1,500 units, and is currently awaiting the tender process. Beyond surveillance, Maybank IB sees potential upside from ITMAX’s latest initiative, the “Digital Twin” project. This AI-enabled platform will develop a virtual 3D model of Kuala Lumpur, complete with buildings, roads and slope analyses, allowing for real-time simulation to support urban planning and decision-making. The project is expected to be completed by December 2025, with monetisation set to begin in FY2026. Analysts estimate potential recurring revenue of RM15 million to RM20 million annually from this digital offering, driven by ITMAX’s data analytics capabilities. With a market capitalisation of RM3.8 billion and shares currently trading at RM3.70, ITMAX remains Maybank IB’s top software pick for its sound fundamentals, strategic government contracts and long-term AI monetisation roadmap. title: IOI Prop’s Singapore Acquisition Fits Into Its Future REIT Ambitions: HLIB
body: Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) has maintained its BUY call on IOI Properties Group (IOIPG), keeping its target price at RM4.05, implying a significant 115.4% capital upside and 119.1% total return. The research house believes the group’s recent acquisition of the remaining 50.1% stake in the South Beach development in Singapore reinforces its long-term strategy and presents a rare opportunity to anchor its future REIT ambitions in a stable and high-value asset. HLIB highlighted that the acquisition, valued at S$834 million (approximately RM2.75 billion), was made possible through IOIPG’s first right of refusal after its joint venture partner, City Developments Ltd, expressed interest to divest. Given IOIPG’s longstanding involvement with the project and operational familiarity, the deal was seen as a natural progression. The bank noted that securing an en-bloc commercial asset of this quality in Singapore is exceptionally rare and significantly reduces development risk. According to HLIB, the full control over South Beach allows IOIPG to optimise operations, unlock synergies and prepare the asset as a cornerstone for a Singapore REIT listing targeted for 2027. Additionally, the group is planning a Malaysia REIT listing by mid-2026, with both exercises expected to unlock significant cash flow—up to RM3.2 billion and RM10.6 billion respectively—if IOIPG retains a 60% stake in each. Management is confident in boosting operational efficiency, especially within the JW Marriott Hotel in South Beach. HLIB noted that by diversifying its guest mix to include more independent travellers and retail clients, the group aims to raise average daily rates to S$600, in line with five-star benchmarks in Singapore, and lift occupancy rates beyond the 76% recorded in 1Q2025. To fund the acquisition, IOIPG has secured financing through bank borrowings and potential sukuk issuance, which HLIB views positively as it helps maintain Shariah compliance—a status the stock recently regained. Management also ruled out any rights issue, easing concerns over equity dilution. Despite the expected rise in net gearing to around 0.93 times, HLIB believes this will gradually decline as cash flow from the upcoming W Residences launch and REIT exercises begin to materialise. The research house also addressed market concerns about IOIPG’s valuation, noting the stock is currently trading at just 0.44 times book value. With high-value assets like IOI City Mall and IOI Central Boulevard still underappreciated by the market, HLIB sees meaningful re-rating potential as monetisation efforts through REITs crystallise the intrinsic value of these properties. HLIB has kept its earnings forecasts unchanged and reiterated that IOIPG remains a compelling proxy for exposure to both Malaysia’s property sector—supported by policy reforms and infrastructure expansion—and Singapore’s resilient real estate market. The group’s diversified portfolio, coupled with clear strategic execution, reinforces confidence in its growth and capital management capabilities. title: Humanica Plots Growth Spurt With M&A And Regional Push
body: Maybank Investment Bank Bhd (Maybank IB) has reiterated its BUY rating on Humanica PCL, maintaining a target price of THB11.90, citing expectations of stronger earnings in the second and third quarters of 2025, alongside potential upside from upcoming mergers and acquisitions. The bank highlighted that despite a weak first quarter, the company remains poised for growth driven by record-high project wins and regional expansion plans. Humanica’s first quarter core profit fell 2% year-on-year and 35% quarter-on-quarter, but secured projects worth THB114 million — a 104% increase year-on-year — which analysts said should translate into stronger financial performance over the coming quarters. These projects include implementations for a large-scale microfinance player in Indonesia with over 70,000 headcount, a major Thai retailer, and a regional company, collectively signalling a significant uplift in revenue momentum. During a recent virtual group meeting, Humanica’s Chief Technology Officer Gordon Enns shared that the company plans to finalise two acquisitions in the coming months. One involves an ERP implementer offering SAP S/4 HANA solutions for large enterprises, which analysts believe could create cross-selling opportunities for Humanica’s core products. The second deal targets a leading HR solution provider in Vietnam, with terms expected to be concluded by the end of June. Maybank IB estimates these acquisitions could add 2% and 7% to the company’s FY25 and FY26 earnings, respectively. Looking ahead, Humanica also aims to expand its domestic sales force in the second half of 2025 to drive further project wins in Thailand for FY26. This strategic move is expected to support continued revenue growth, in line with the company’s 10% topline growth target for the year. However, a potential headwind remains in the form of a weakening Indonesian rupiah. With Indonesia projected to contribute 35% of Humanica’s FY25 core profit, Maybank IB noted that a 10% depreciation of the rupiah against the Thai baht could reduce earnings by 3.5%. As of 10 June, the currency had already weakened by 9% from last year’s average rate. Despite currency pressures, Humanica remains optimistic, citing stronger-than-expected year-to-date project wins. Maybank IB has left its earnings and revenue growth forecasts unchanged at 13% and 10%, respectively, underscoring continued confidence in the company’s fundamentals and growth trajectory. title: Gold Up Nearly RM2,200 In 6 Months, But Global Rally Pauses
body: Gold prices in Malaysia rose slightly on Wednesday, tracking global movements, even as broader sentiment on COMEX Gold turned neutral amid sideways trading. title: Wall Street Ends Slightly Higher As US-China Trade Talks Offer Hope
body: Wall Street closed modestly higher on Monday as renewed optimism over US-China trade talks lifted sentiment, with the S&P 500 inching closer to its record high. Officials from both countries described ongoing negotiations as “fruitful,” with discussions set to resume on Tuesday in London. Traders were encouraged by signs of easing trade tensions, while bond yields slipped as inflation expectations cooled following last week’s selloff. The S&P 500 was little changed by the end of the session, remaining about 2% below its February peak of 6,125. The Nasdaq 100 edged up 0.2%, supported by gains in Tesla Inc., which jumped around 4.5% after President Donald Trump signalled a willingness to reconcile with Elon Musk and continue support for Starlink services. However, Apple Inc. fell more than 1% after its developers conference failed to deliver major artificial intelligence breakthroughs. Despite the subdued moves, major Wall Street firms including Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs, and JPMorgan Chase have grown more bullish on the US stock market, citing resilient economic growth and stronger earnings outlooks. Morgan Stanley’s Michael Wilson reiterated his 12-month target of 6,500 for the S&P 500, while other strategists pointed to the index’s 20% rebound from April lows as a sign of strong underlying momentum. Investors remain watchful ahead of a key inflation report due Wednesday, which will serve as a crucial input for the Federal Reserve’s upcoming policy meeting on June 18. Until then, markets are expected to stay headline-sensitive, with any unexpected developments in trade talks or inflation data likely to sway investor sentiment. body: Shares in Tan Chong Motor Holdings Bhd rose 3.57% to RM0.435 as of 3.15 pm today, extending gains despite persistent concerns over weak sales performance and stiff competition in key markets. This uptick comes even as Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB) maintained a Hold call on the stock with a target price of RM0.42, implying a potential downside of 7.7%. HLIB cautioned that near-term recovery remains limited due to sluggish volumes and margin compression, especially in Malaysia and Indochina. Tan Chong’s core net loss for 1QFY25 narrowed to RM43 million, buoyed slightly by the December 2024 launch of the e-POWER Nissan Kicks and cost-control measures. Still, local sales tumbled 20.6% year-on-year to 1,918 units, with the overall auto industry forecast to soften further this year. Market sentiment appears to be partially buoyed by the group’s deep discount to book value and ownership of strategic land assets, which analysts say offer some downside protection. Tan Chong currently trades at just 0.11 times its 2024 book value per share. The group plans to locally assemble the Wuling Bingo EV by Q4 2025, aiming for a sub-RM100,000 price point, while also expanding GAC and commercial vehicle offerings in Vietnam. However, operations in Laos, Myanmar and Cambodia remain under pressure from inflation and political uncertainty. Despite today’s bounce, analysts remain cautious on the company’s near-term prospects. Related The stock added 1.5 sen from its last close of RM0.42, with more than 633,000 shares traded. title: Ringgit Inches Higher As Markets Watch US-China Trade Talks
body: The ringgit opened marginally stronger against the US dollar on Tuesday as markets remained cautious ahead of further developments in trade negotiations between China and the United States. At 8am, the local note edged up to 4.2275/2370 versus the greenback, compared to Monday’s close of 4.2290/2345. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist, Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid, said the US dollar index (DXY) dipped 0.25% to 98.939 points following encouraging signals from US officials on the status of the negotiations. “The USD/MYR traded within a narrow band of RM4.231 to RM4.2458 yesterday as investors remained cautious, and a similar pattern is likely to persist today,” he said. Afzanizam added that China’s trade data with the US continued to show significant weakness, with exports tumbling 34.5% and imports dropping 18.1% in May—marking the second consecutive month of contraction. He also pointed out that China’s consumer price index has remained negative for four straight months, registering -0.1% year-on-year in April, reflecting persistent weak demand. In early trade, the ringgit was broadly higher against a basket of major currencies. It strengthened against the Japanese yen to 2.9242/9310 from 2.9344/2.9384 on Monday, gained against the British pound to 5.7300/7428 from 5.7392/7466, and appreciated versus the euro to 4.8303/8412 from 4.8316/8379. However, performance was mixed against ASEAN currencies. The ringgit improved against the Singapore dollar to 3.2876/2952 from 3.2908/2953 but declined slightly versus the Thai baht to 12.9463/9846 from 12.9414/9642. It was nearly flat against the Indonesian rupiah at 259.4/260.1 from 259.5/260.0 and remained unchanged against the Philippine peso at 7.57/7.59. title: Sunview Could Benefit From RM17 Billion Solar EPCC Jobs Coming Online
body: MIDF Amanah Investment Bank Bhd (MIDF Research) has maintained its BUY recommendation on Sunview Group Berhad, with an unchanged target price of RM0.54. The bank values Sunview at a price-to-earnings ratio (PER) of 20 times based on its FY26 forecast earnings per share (EPS) of 2.7 sen, noting a discount compared to larger peers in the renewable energy sector. Sunview’s earnings in the coming quarters are expected to be driven primarily by its Corporate Green Power Programme (CGPP) Engineering, Procurement, Construction and Commissioning (EPCC) projects. The group currently holds three CGPP contracts, each with a capacity of 29.99MWac and a combined contract value of RM248 million. Progress on these projects varies with one contract which is free issue, already 70% completed while the other two remain at the initial stages of 10% and 15% completion respectively. The group’s unbilled order book stands at RM374.3 million, providing clear earnings visibility through to FY26. MIDF Research expects further replenishment of the order book from ongoing Large-Scale Solar (LSS) 5 EPCC projects, which are being progressively awarded. Sunview is actively bidding for new contracts with a tender book valued at RM4 billion, comprising RM1.7 billion for LSS projects, RM1.3 billion for Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme (CRESS) jobs, RM734 million for rooftop solar projects, and RM264 million for additional CGPP contracts. MIDF Research remains optimistic about Sunview’s future prospects, especially with the potential influx of sizeable EPCC projects from LSS5, and the upcoming LSS5+ and LSS6 rounds. There is also strong demand for rooftop solar among commercial and industrial segments as well as residential users. Industry estimates indicate that up to RM17 billion worth of solar EPCC jobs are available to industry players, underpinning a healthy growth pipeline. Beyond domestic projects, Sunview is aggressively pursuing opportunities overseas. The group recently established two wholly owned subsidiaries in Uzbekistan, Sunview-Alpha LLC and Sunview Beta LLC, aimed at developing two solar plants with a total capacity of 600MW. The company is currently negotiating with the Uzbekistan Ministry of Energy and expects to sign the power purchase agreement (PPA) within this month, signalling progress on its international expansion. MIDF Research highlights Sunview’s balanced approach as both an EPCC contractor and asset developer, noting its RM1.8 billion worth of tenders for LSS5+, Battery Energy Storage System (BESS), and CRESS projects. This diversified strategy positions Sunview to benefit from multiple segments of Malaysia’s growing renewable energy sector, underpinned by the National Energy Transition Roadmap (NETR) and sustained demand for green power solutions. title: Ringgit Falls Against US Dollar On Economic Concerns
body: The ringgit opened lower against the US dollar on Monday as the American currency strengthened amid renewed uncertainty caused by challenging global economic forecasts for the second half of 2025. At 8:03 am, the local currency was quoted at 4.2375/2560 against the US dollar, compared to 4.2270/2360 on Friday. During early trading, the ringgit was mostly weaker against a basket of major currencies. It edged up against the Japanese yen to 2.9305/9435 from 2.9324/9390 on Friday but declined against the pound to 5.7367/7618 from 5.7212/7334 and slipped versus the euro to 4.8341/8552 from 4.8268/8371. The local currency also saw mixed performance against ASEAN currencies. It strengthened against the Thai baht to 12.9468/13.0121 from 12.9599/9947 on Friday, but weakened against the Singapore dollar to 3.2892/3041 from 3.2862/2934, dropped against the Philippine peso to 7.60/7.64 from 7.58/7.60 and declined versus the Indonesian rupiah to 260.1/261.4 from 259.5/260.2. Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid, Chief Economist at Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd, said the ringgit is expected to trade between RM4.23 and RM4.24 today, following stronger-than-expected US non-farm payroll (NFP) data for May. He said the US NFP increased by 139,000 in May, exceeding the consensus estimate of 126,000, while the unemployment rate remained steady at 4.2% for the third consecutive month. This led to the US Dollar Index (DXY) rising to 99.190 points on Friday. “Latest NFP data shows that the US labour market remains resilient despite facing high tariffs,” he told local media. However, he noted that April’s NFP figures were revised downwards from 177,000 to 147,000, while the US labour force participation rate fell to 62.4% in May from 62.6% in April. “Therefore, although the labour market is still healthy, indicators of slower growth in the data set are becoming more apparent. “Based on weak business and consumer sentiment, economic outlook for the second half of 2025 appears increasingly challenging. In our view, the likelihood of a cut in the US Federal Funds Rate has risen,” he added. Last week, the ringgit strengthened against the US dollar, with USDMYR closing at RM4.2315, marking a weekly gain of 0.6%. title: Bullish On Banking Sector Post Q1 Earnings
body: Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) Research has reiterated its OVERWEIGHT rating on the Malaysian banking sector, citing strategic upside potential following the KLFIN Index’s 7% year-to-date decline. The house maintained BUY calls on Affin (TP: RM3.00), Alliance (TP: RM5.00), AMMB (TP: RM6.20), CIMB (TP: RM8.80), Public Bank (TP: RM5.10), and RHB (TP: RM7.70), while keeping HOLD ratings on BIMB (TP: RM2.40) and Maybank (TP: RM10.70). The preferred picks for a cyclical rebound are CIMB and AMMB, with RHB seen as a high-quality counterbalance offering defensible growth. The 1Q25 earnings season was broadly in line with HLIB’s expectations, with sector earnings rising 4.1% year-on-year (YoY), driven by lower loan impairment provisions. On a quarter-on-quarter (QoQ) basis, however, profits slipped 3.4%, largely due to higher credit charges and weaker associate contributions. BIMB was the only bank to miss estimates, dragged by elevated credit costs, prompting HLIB to revise its target price lower from RM2.60 to RM2.40 while maintaining its HOLD call. Core earnings, adjusted for non-recurring items in 4Q24, saw a 3.4% QoQ decline despite a 3.6% rise in pre-impairment operating profit. Affin’s net interest margin (NIM) notably expanded by 7bps, outperforming peers that mostly posted flat to slightly lower NIMs. Sector-wide loan loss provisions rose 11.6%, while contributions from associates dipped 27.3%. Still, the underlying fundamentals remained steady, supported by healthy loan (+4.3% YoY) and deposit growth (+3.4% YoY). On a YoY basis, earnings growth was bolstered by a 22.9% drop in loan loss provisions and a 31.2% increase in associate contributions. Net interest income grew 3.4%, offsetting a mild 1.3% contraction in non-interest income. Operating expenses rose 2.9%, indicating commendable cost discipline. Alliance and Affin emerged as top performers with 11.1% and 12.6% profit growth respectively, buoyed by strong net interest income and effective cost control. Looking ahead, HLIB expects net interest margins in 2Q25 to remain stable, aided by fresh liquidity from the statutory reserve ratio (SRR) cut and moderating deposit competition. Proactive funding strategies are already in motion, with banks reducing promotional fixed deposit rates by 5–15bps in May, although margin benefits are likely to materialise more fully in the second half of the year. Asset quality is anticipated to hold firm, with the gross impaired loan ratio ticking up just 1bp to 1.38% in the latest quarter. Forecasting a 3.4% compound annual growth rate in sector earnings over FY24–26, HLIB sees valuation support at 1.04x forward price-to-book, below the 10-year mean. Coupled with a 5.4% dividend yield and fortified provision buffers, analysts believe the sector is well-positioned to weather external uncertainties. Risks to the bullish stance include an economic slowdown, persistent deposit pricing pressure, and rising global trade tensions. Markets were closed on June 3 for the snap presidential election, which concluded with a decisive victory for Lee Jae-myung. Investors responded positively to expectations of market-friendly reforms and fiscal stimulus under the new administration. Tech giants led the charge as Samsung Electronics Co Ltd and SK Hynix Inc posted solid gains amid optimism over global chip demand and easing US-China tensions. Meanwhile, steel and energy counters underperformed on worries over new US tariff measures. Foreign investors returned as net buyers, reversing months of outflows driven by geopolitical uncertainty. Analysts attributed the shift to improved policy visibility and attractive valuations, with the KOSPI’s forward price-to-earnings still well below regional peers. With key resistance levels near 2,800–2,820, technical strategists suggest the index could enter a consolidation phase. Eyes will be on upcoming US inflation data and Korea’s fiscal announcements for further direction. Fraser & Neave (F&N) took the biggest hit, sliding 66 sen to RM27.38, followed by Nestlé Malaysia, down 48 sen to RM77.12. title: Wall Street Slips As Tesla Drags, All Eyes On Jobs Report Amid Tariff Tensions
body: US stocks fell on Thursday as a drop in Tesla shares weighed on major indexes, while investors braced for the monthly jobs report that could offer fresh signals on the health of the labour market amid renewed trade war concerns. The Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped 126.69 points, or 0.30%, to 42,301.05, while the S&P 500 lost 12.71 points, or 0.21%, to 5,958.10. The Nasdaq Composite fell 31.13 points, or 0.16%, to 19,429.36. Tensions between Washington and Beijing escalated again as Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump held a phone call reported by state media, amid a fresh row over critical minerals that threatens to undo recent trade truces. Investors are now focusing on Friday’s non-farm payrolls report after recent data showed softer-than-expected private job growth and services sector activity. Initial jobless claims also rose for a second week, fuelling concerns that the US labour market is gradually weakening. “I don’t think it’s a big warning sign right now, but the labour market has been softening,” said Kevin Gordon, senior investment strategist at Charles Schwab. Despite President Trump’s repeated calls to cut interest rates, the Federal Reserve is widely expected to keep rates unchanged at its upcoming meeting later this month, with Chair Jerome Powell maintaining a cautious stance amid ongoing economic uncertainty tied to tariffs. Tesla led decliners, falling 4.5% to a three-week low as its European sales fell for the fifth straight month. Consumer staples were the weakest S&P 500 sector, down nearly 1%, dragged by a 14.9% plunge in Brown-Forman after it forecast lower revenue and profit. Procter & Gamble also dipped 1.3% after announcing it would cut 7,000 jobs, or 6% of its workforce. The market’s recent May rally, driven by optimism over earnings and a brief softening in trade rhetoric, has stalled. The S&P 500 remains nearly 3% below its record high from February. Market breadth was negative, with declining issues outnumbering advancers by a 1.08-to-1 ratio on the NYSE and 1.46-to-1 on the Nasdaq. The S&P 500 recorded 12 new 52-week highs and three new lows, while the Nasdaq posted 37 new highs and 16 new lows. Federal Reserve officials including Adriana Kugler, Jeffrey Schmid, and Patrick Harker are due to speak later in the day, potentially offering further insight into the central bank’s outlook.
