title: Today’s Shares: IOI Corp Up 0.55% To RM3.65 As FFB Output, Cost Control Lift Outlook
body: Shares of IOI Corporation Bhd rose 0.55% to RM3.65 as of 4:25pm today, gaining 2 sen on the back of 4.95 million shares traded, as investor sentiment remained upbeat following improved fresh fruit bunch (FFB) output and a rebound in its manufacturing segment. At the time of writing, the counter was actively traded with 2.2 million shares on the buy queue against 373,000 on the sell side. The stock opened at RM3.61 and touched an intraday high of RM3.65. Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) recently reaffirmed its ‘Buy’ call on IOI, maintaining a target price of RM4.24. This suggests a capital upside of 16.8% from its last traded price of RM3.63, with a total expected return of 19.8% when including dividends. HLIB noted that IOI’s FFB production for FY2025 is likely to surpass its earlier guidance of 1–2% growth, driven by improved weather conditions and sustained output recovery since March. The bank is keeping its full-year FFB growth forecast at 2.5%. Despite ongoing cost pressures, IOI is expected to keep its crude palm oil (CPO) production cost below RM2,100 per metric tonne, aided by stronger FFB volumes in the final quarter. For the first nine months of FY2025, its average CPO cost stood at RM2,104, down 1.5% year-on-year. On the manufacturing front, IOI recorded a turnaround in the third quarter with a RM81.4 million profit before interest and tax, mainly due to stronger margins in its refinery operations. Management expects the segment to maintain current profitability levels, with gradual demand recovery and improved feedstock supply supporting the outlook. IOI’s accelerated replanting strategy and the upcoming construction of a 150,000-tonne zero-waste paper pulp plant via its 45%-owned joint venture Nextgreen IOI Pulp are also expected to bolster long-term growth and diversification. title: Today’s Shares: HLFG Edges Up To RM16.70 As 3Q Profit Jumps 34%
body: Hong Leong Financial Group Bhd (HLFG) saw its share price inch up 0.48% to RM16.70 as at 3.49pm on Thursday, despite a recent downward revision to its earnings forecast by MIDF Research. The stock opened at RM16.62 and traded between RM16.60 and RM16.74, with a trading volume of 57,900 shares. It last closed at RM16.62. MIDF Research maintained its ‘Buy’ rating on HLFG following the group’s stronger-than-expected third quarter FY25 results, but lowered its target price to RM20.63 from RM24.70. The revision reflected higher projected costs moving forward. HLFG posted a core net profit of RM1.12 billion in 3QFY25, up 34% quarter-on-quarter, largely due to overlay writebacks. Its main contributor, Hong Leong Bank, reported solid year-on-year growth of 14% supported by higher net interest and non-interest income. However, other segments showed mixed performance. Hong Leong Assurance’s quarterly pre-tax profit fell 40% while Hong Leong Capital’s earnings slipped 21% due to weaker investment income. Despite the cost headwinds, MIDF expects continued strength in HLFG’s core banking arm, with a projected total return of 27.1% including dividends. title: SMRT Holding Should Pick Pace In FY26
body: Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) has maintained its BUY rating on SMRT Holdings Bhd with an unchanged target price of RM2.07, indicating a potential capital upside of 117.8% from the current price of RM0.95. The house describes recent operational setbacks as transitory, expecting gradual improvement from FY26 onwards, supported by a solid deployment outlook across Tenaga Nasional Berhad (Tenaga), Indonesia’s PLN, and Air Selangor. HLIB highlighted a timing mismatch between Tenaga’s equipment delivery and site provisioning, which has caused approximately 1,600 to 1,900 sites to remain unprovisioned. These sites, when fully provisioned, could contribute an estimated RM1.3 to RM1.6 million in annualised earnings. While equipment sales are recognised upfront upon delivery, recurring managed services revenue depends on site provisioning and activation, which has lagged. Management anticipates clearing this backlog progressively by the end of calendar year 2025. This delay has resulted in a relatively flat quarterly earnings trend for SMRT during the first nine months of FY25. Further complicating near-term growth, HLIB reported delays in project rollouts with PLN in Indonesia following a post-election leadership reshuffle. The reassessment of Phase 2 of the Jakarta rollout, along with deferments in other regional tenders such as Lampung, Nusa Tenggara Timur, Jawa Barat and Kalimantan Timur dan Utara has contributed to subdued overseas performance. Nevertheless, HLIB maintains a positive long-term view on PLN’s digitalisation strategy, citing the country’s higher System Average Interruption Duration Index (SAIDI) and the growing share of renewables in its generation mix, which make smart grid infrastructure rollout critical. On a brighter note, SMRT is in advanced discussions with a new financial services industry player in Indonesia to support ATM connectivity rollout, with a few hundred sites expected to be delivered in the second half of 2025. Unlike the exclusive vendor model seen in prior contracts, this engagement involves an open vendor approach with multiple providers. Despite this, management remains optimistic due to the new customer’s aggressive ATM expansion plans. The bank reaffirmed SMRT’s valuation as attractive, noting a price-to-earnings ratio of 30 times FY26 earnings, which is a discount to the 45 times assigned to ITMAX but higher than KLTEC’s 21 times. HLIB underscores SMRT’s unique position enabling digital transformation across Southeast Asia’s power sector, a critical area of infrastructure modernisation and grid digitalisation. The firm sees substantial earnings potential from growing recurring income streams as more managed sites become operational. With a steadily expanding base of managed sites and strategic exposure to utilities and financial services, SMRT is expected to generate greater earnings stability and consistent growth in recurring revenue, according to HLIB. title: Ringgit Finds Its Feet Amid US Data Drag
body: The ringgit opened stronger against the US dollar on Friday, extending its gains as weaker US economic indicators and ongoing tariff uncertainties dampened demand for the greenback. At 8am, the local note rose to 4.2140/2335 against the US dollar from Thursday’s close of 4.2245/2295. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US Dollar Index (DXY) slipped by 0.05% to 98.741 points following the release of economic data pointing to further slowdown in the US economy. “US Initial Jobless Claims rose to 247,000 last week, marking the second consecutive week of increases, while the Continuous Jobless Claims remained elevated to 1.904 million for the week ending 24 May 2025. “The focus tonight will be on the Nonfarm Payroll (NFP), which is expected to reach 125,000 in May (consensus) from the previous month’s print of 177,000,” he told Bernama . He said the ringgit may continue to climb in the near term, potentially reaching RM4.20, as emerging market currencies appreciate on the back of a weaker US outlook and persistent concerns over tariffs and fiscal strategies. “The prevailing market condition defied the norms because the US dollar has been deemed a safe-haven currency. Traders and investors would normally flock to the US dollar to seek protection against extreme volatility,” he added. Mohd Afzanizam also cautioned that the market remains sensitive to US trade policy developments and political noise, particularly the recent fallout between US President Donald Trump and Elon Musk over fiscal matters, which may rattle investor sentiment. “At the end of the day, it is about prescribing a good policy and implementing it promptly to see the outcome,” he said. The ringgit also gained against most major and regional currencies at the start of the trading day. Against the Japanese yen, the ringgit improved to 2.9343/9481 from 2.9495/9531 on Thursday, and rose against the British pound to 5.7226/7491 from 5.7301/7369. However, it slipped versus the euro to 4.8263/8486 from 4.8235/8292. In ASEAN trade, the ringgit strengthened to 3.2758/2915 against the Singapore dollar from 3.2881/2922, and edged higher against the Indonesian rupiah to 258.7/260.1 from 259.3/259.8. It also surged against the Thai baht to 12.9157/9854 from 12.9925/13.0138 and appreciated against the Philippine peso to 7.57/7.62 from 7.59/7.61. title: Today’s Shares: PetDag Slides 1.14% To RM20.90 Amid Lower Trading Volume
body: Petronas Dagangan Bhd (PetDag)’s share price dipped 1.14% or 24 sen to RM20.90 as of 2.46pm, despite reporting a 28% year-on-year increase in net profit for the first quarter of FY2025. The stock opened at RM21.12 and traded between a high of RM21.36 and a low of RM20.78, with trading volume at 184,900 shares. The company had recently posted a profit after tax of RM293 million for Q1FY25, up from RM228 million a year ago, driven by reduced expenditure across all segments and stronger gross profit margins. Revenue for the quarter, however, edged down slightly to RM9 billion from RM9.3 billion previously. While retail fuel sales saw a decline due to cautious consumer spending during the festive period, the commercial segment helped cushion the impact with higher Jet A1 demand. PetDag also declared a 20 sen interim dividend for the quarter, amounting to RM198.7 million, with payment scheduled for 21 June 2025. title: HLIB Downgrades UMediC After Results Fell Short
body: Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) downgraded UMediC Group Bhd to HOLD from BUY, adjusting its target price to RM0.43 from RM0.69, citing ongoing earnings underperformance and weaker-than-expected revenue in the Distribution division. The house projected a modest capital upside of 7.5% and expect the total return to align accordingly, reflecting cautious sentiment amid persistent challenges. UMediC reported a 3QFY25 core PATMI of RM1.8 million, down 15.1% quarter-on-quarter and 12.2% year-on-year, bringing the 9MFY25 core earnings to RM5.4 million, a 19.6% decline from the previous year. These results fell short of both HLIB’s and consensus full-year forecasts, achieving only 68% and 71% of estimates, respectively. The shortfall was primarily attributed to subdued revenue from the Distribution division, which suffered from a dampened demand for medical devices and consumables. In contrast, the Manufacturing division rebounded strongly with a 78.6% quarter-on-quarter increase in revenue, largely driven by recovering demand for respiratory products. Despite a slight year-on-year revenue growth of 6.9% in the Distribution division, the Manufacturing segment’s revenue fell 10.5%, impacted by a stronger Ringgit against the US dollar, which appreciated by approximately 7.3%, and softer demand for respiratory-related products. The profitability in the Manufacturing division also weakened significantly, with the profit before tax margin declining from 46% to 31%, affected by unfavourable forex movements. Similarly, the Distribution division’s PBT margin shrank to 13% from 19%, likely due to operating leverage pressures. Year-to-date, UMediC’s revenue contracted by 8.6%, with both divisions recording declines—3.2% in Distribution and a steeper 18.5% in Manufacturing. The core PATMI dropped sharply by 19.6%, primarily due to the margin erosion in the Manufacturing segment, where the PBT margin fell to 26% from 38%, again attributed to adverse currency effects. Looking ahead, HLIB remains cautiously optimistic about the Manufacturing division’s respiratory products, buoyed by global healthcare megatrends such as the ageing population. However, ongoing uncertainty persists in the Distribution division dampening overall outlook. In response to these factors and the profit misses over three consecutive quarters, HLIB trimmed its profit forecasts for FY25 to FY27 by 10% to 12%. The downgrade to HOLD is accompanied by a lower valuation multiple, with HLIB reducing its price-to-earnings ratio target to 19 times, two standard deviations below the stock’s three-year average, down from a previous valuation of 26.5 times. This adjustment reflects a more cautious stance following a series of earnings disappointments and a tempered view on future growth prospects. UMediC continues to focus on marketing and distributing branded medical devices and consumables while developing its own medical consumables brand. Despite near-term hurdles, the company’s positioning in healthcare remains relevant, though recovery depends heavily on improving sales dynamics in the Distribution division. title: Gold Climbs 1.32% To RM4,914.12 Amid Global Pullback Signals
body: Gold prices in Malaysia rose 1.32% to RM4,914.12 per ounce at the time of writing, reflecting a RM64.25 increase from the previous level. The yellow metal also posted a 0.21% gain today and has surged 31.07% year-on-year, according to data from goldprice.org. Despite the local uptrend, RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) noted in its technical outlook that COMEX Gold faced stiff resistance at US$3,400 and closed lower at US$3,375.10 overnight, indicating potential for further pullbacks. title: Tech Gains Buoy Wall Street Despite Weak Jobs Data And Tariff Jitters
body: Wall Street crept higher on Wednesday as gains in technology stocks helped offset growing concerns over a slowing US economy and renewed trade tensions, particularly following weak services and employment data. At 10:36am ET, the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 88.09 points, or 0.20%, to 42,605.07, while the S&P 500 added 17.36 points, or 0.29%, to 5,987.73. The Nasdaq Composite climbed 58.41 points, or 0.31%, to 19,459.09. Eight of the 11 major S&P 500 sectors advanced, led by communication services, which rose 1.2%, and information technology, up 0.4%. Investor sentiment remained cautious after the latest ADP National Employment Report showed private employers added the fewest jobs in over two years in May. Meanwhile, the services sector contracted for the first time in nearly a year, with input prices rising — a worrying signal of persistent inflation amid weak growth. “The ADP number adds some short-term volatility, but the real signal will come from Friday’s payrolls data,” said Larry Tentarelli, Chief Technical Strategist at Blue Chip Daily Trend Report. Tensions on the trade front also flared, with President Donald Trump doubling tariffs on imported steel and aluminium to 50%, as a deadline passed for trading partners to submit improved offers ahead of potential new levies in July. Eyes are now on a possible call this week between Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping. Despite current jitters, May marked the best monthly performance since November 2023 for both the S&P 500 and Nasdaq, buoyed by softer trade rhetoric and strong earnings. Barclays has now joined other brokerages in raising its year-end target for the S&P 500, citing easing trade risk and expectations of earnings normalisation in 2026. In corporate movers: Hewlett Packard Enterprise climbed 1.1% after beating second-quarter forecasts on AI server demand. GlobalFoundries gained 2.2% after announcing it would boost capital investments to US$16 billion. Wells Fargo advanced 1.2% as the US Federal Reserve lifted its long-standing US$1.95 trillion asset cap. On the downside, Tesla fell 3.8% following a fifth straight month of declining sales in Europe. CrowdStrike plunged 4.7% after issuing a weaker-than-expected revenue outlook. Dollar Tree tumbled 10.2% after forecasting a sharp 50% drop in Q2 profit, blaming tariff-driven cost volatility. Market breadth was positive, with advancers outpacing decliners by 2.02 to 1 on the NYSE and 1.41 to 1 on the Nasdaq. The S&P 500 saw 19 new 52-week highs, while the Nasdaq logged 63 highs and 23 lows. title: Tech and Utility Stocks Lead Gains As More Counters Close Higher
body: Technology and utility counters led the charge on the stock market on June 5, lifting the broader market as investors rotated into defensives and high-growth names amid improving turnover and positive sentiment. At the close, 641 stocks advanced, surpassing 341 decliners, while 437 counters were unchanged, 937 were untraded and 20 counters were suspended. Total turnover improved to 2.42 billion shares valued at RM2.27 billion, up from 2.4 billion units worth RM2.03 billion the previous day, signalling stronger investor participation. Leading the gainers was Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd, which jumped 42 sen to RM20.36, driven by renewed interest in tech-related counters amid optimism over global semiconductor demand recovery. Tenaga Nasional Bhd also posted a strong performance, rising 26 sen to RM14.20, as utilities attracted buying interest from investors seeking safer bets in a volatile macro environment. YTL Power International Bhd surged 22 sen to RM3.51, making it one of the day’s most actively traded stocks with over 20.7 million shares exchanged, reflecting investor appetite for infrastructure and energy plays. Other notable gainers included Petronas Dagangan Bhd, up 18 sen to RM21.14, and Press Metal Aluminium Holdings Bhd, which rose 15 sen to RM5.05, buoyed by firming commodity prices. On the downside, Nestlé (M) Bhd led the list of losers, falling 76 sen to RM77.60, as profit-taking emerged in consumer staples. United Plantations Bhd slipped 34 sen to RM21.80, tracking softer palm oil prices, while Heineken Malaysia Bhd eased 30 sen to RM27. Country View Bhd and Hong Leong Bank Bhd also posted modest losses, down 19 sen and 12 sen, to close at RM2.20 and RM19.54, respectively. Analysts remain cautiously optimistic, noting that the rebound in tech and defensive stocks could support the index in the near term. With global markets eyeing upcoming US economic data and interest rate signals, the stock market is expected to trade within a narrow range, with rotational plays across sectors likely to persist. title: Ringgit Inches Up Amid Weak US Data, But Mixed Against Other Currencies
body: Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US Dollar Index (DXY) fell by 0.44% to 98.787 points following weaker-than-expected economic indicators. He noted that the US Institute for Supply Management (ISM) Index for the services sector dipped below the critical 50-point line to 49.9 in May, against a market consensus of 52.0 points. “Based on the survey response by the ISM, import tariff was the major source of uncertainties among businesses as it has raised the raw material prices, and some suppliers are holding back inventory given the tariff uncertainties. “This may lead to stronger emerging market currencies, including as the traders and investors would be reassessing the strength of the US economy, and therefore, Friday’s Nonfarm Payroll will be another important barometer to look at,” he told local media. He also pointed out that the upcoming Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on 16-17 June will be a key moment, with the US Federal Reserve expected to release its macroeconomic outlook for the next three years. At 8am, the ringgit strengthened marginally to 4.2410/2495 against the US dollar, compared to Wednesday’s close of 4.2435/2490. Despite the slight uptick against the greenback, the local note weakened against several major currencies. title: Wall Street Gains As Chip Stocks Rally, Investors Await Trump-Xi Talks
body: US markets closed higher on Tuesday, led by gains in chipmakers including Nvidia and Broadcom, as optimism rose over potential trade negotiations between the US and its partners. The Dow Jones Industrial Average added 214.16 points (+0.51%) to 42,519.64, while the S&P 500 rose 34.43 points (+0.58%) to 5,970.37. The Nasdaq Composite gained 156.34 points (+0.81%) to end at 19,398.96. Chip stocks powered tech gains, with the Information Technology sector climbing 1.5%, supported by Nvidia’s 2.9% advance and Broadcom’s 3.2% jump after it began shipping new AI-focused networking chips. Analysts cited optimism around an expected call between President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, potentially addressing chip exports. Investor sentiment was buoyed by hopes that Washington would avoid steep new tariffs that could trigger a recession. “The fact that the US is actively engaged with so many trading partners… has investors feeling more optimistic,” said Northlight Asset Management’s Chief Investment Officer, Chris Zaccarelli. However, signs of a slowing economy emerged. April factory orders dropped 3.7%, while job openings rose but layoffs also increased, according to US Labour Department data. Traders now await Friday’s monthly jobs report for clearer signals. Among individual stocks: Wells Fargo rose 1.2% after the Federal Reserve lifted a US$1.95 trillion asset cap imposed in 2018. Shares climbed another 2% post-market. Dollar General surged 15.8% on strong quarterly sales and an upgraded forecast. Kenvue fell 6%, citing destocking by US and Chinese retailers. Pinterest gained 3.8% after JPMorgan upgraded the stock. Reddit dropped 1.1% following a widespread service outage. Volume on US exchanges reached 15.69 billion shares, below the 20-day average of 17.8 billion. Advancers outpaced decliners on both the NYSE and Nasdaq, with 31 new highs on the S&P 500 and 99 on the Nasdaq. title: Today’s Shares: Kossan Shares Dip 1.2% Amid Ongoing Market Caution
body: Kossan Rubber Industries Bhd (Kossan) saw its share price dip 1.2% to RM1.64 as of the latest close on 4 June 2025, with a trading volume of 1.06 million shares. The stock opened and peaked at RM1.66 during the day before retreating. Despite the recent softness in share performance, Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) maintains a BUY call on Kossan, holding an unchanged target price of RM2.30, signalling a potential upside of 38.5% and a total expected return exceeding 40%. HLIB noted ongoing challenges in Kossan’s sales volume, particularly for its 3.0-3.5g medical examination gloves, due to distributors in the US holding above-normal stock levels. However, restocking activity is anticipated to resume in August as US distributors run down front-loaded inventories, which should help boost sales volumes. Price pressures persist, with the average selling price expected to decline by approximately US$0.5 to US$1.0 per 1,000 pieces, attributed to lower nitrile butadiene rubber costs and intense market competition. Kossan’s strategic shift towards customised and specialised glove solutions continues, with roughly 30% of sales volume coming from these higher-margin products. The company plans to launch three to five new specialised glove products annually, aiming to meet tighter occupational safety standards in developed markets such as the US and Europe. This product focus is expected to strengthen margins and improve competitiveness against volume-driven Chinese manufacturers. Automation is also a priority, with plans to enhance efficiency in packing and quality control within the next year, targeting a labour ratio of 1.5 workers per million pieces monthly. Labour costs currently represent 10-15% of the company’s cost of goods sold. HLIB’s earnings forecasts for fiscal years 2025 to 2027 remain steady, supported by Kossan’s dual strategies of product specialisation and automation, coupled with a strong balance sheet boasting a net cash position of RM1.56 billion—the highest among its peers. These fundamentals underpin HLIB’s positive outlook on Kossan despite near-term market uncertainties. title: Synergies In Deleum’s Regional Expansion
body: MIDF Amanah Investment Bank Bhd (MIDF Research) has maintained its BUY call on Deleum Bhd, with a target price of RM1.92, following the successful completion of the company’s 70% equity acquisition in Indonesia-based PT OSA Industries for US$7 million (approximately RM31.3 million), including a profit guarantee of US$2.7 million for FY2024 and FY2025. The acquisition, completed through Deleum’s wholly owned subsidiary Deleum Services Sdn Bhd, marks a strategic step forward in the group’s regional expansion ambitions. PT OSA, a key player in Indonesia’s valve supply and servicing industry, also serves as the exclusive channel partner for Baker Hughes valves in the country. According to MIDF Research, the transaction is expected to significantly enhance Deleum’s operational footprint in Southeast Asia and deepen its technical capabilities in valve solutions, complementing its existing business under Penaga Dresser Sdn Bhd. The research house said the deal was consistent with Deleum’s long-term strategic direction and anticipated it would lead to operational synergies. These include better valve lifecycle management, streamlined delivery systems, and knowledge transfer between Malaysian and Indonesian teams. Deleum Tightens Southeast Asia Expansion with PT OSAMIDF Research noted that while integration efforts may face challenges related to operational alignment, regulatory differences, and foreign exchange risks, Deleum is likely to manage these issues effectively through its experience and structured integration planning. No changes were made to earnings forecasts, as the acquisition had already been priced into prior estimates. MIDF Research believes the acquisition strengthens Deleum’s ability to serve upstream oil and gas customers in the region and sees it as a meaningful step toward value creation. With the company’s exposure to Southeast Asia’s energy infrastructure sector and robust plans for regional growth, MIDF Research remained optimistic about Deleum’s growth trajectory, citing the latest move as a strategic and timely development. title: Ringgit Strengthens Further Amid US Economic Fragility
body: The ringgit continued its upward trend against the US dollar on Wednesday, buoyed by persistent concerns over the fragility of the US economy and ongoing uncertainty stemming from Washington’s trade policy direction. At 8am, the local currency edged up to 4.2370/2640 against the greenback, from Tuesday’s close of 4.2425/2485. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid noted that recent economic data such as the US ISM Index and Consumer Sentiment Index point to growing caution among businesses and consumers in the US. “The data indicates business and consumers have become more cautious in their spending going forward as the Trump administration pushes forward their agenda on trade policies that are hostile and disruptive to global supply chains,” he told Bernama . At the same time, the ringgit also strengthened against a basket of major and regional currencies. It rose against the Japanese yen to 2.9456/9646 from 2.9695/9739, gained against the euro to 4.8234/8541 from 4.8415/8484, and inched up versus the British pound to 5.7331/7696 from 5.7337/7418. Among ASEAN currencies, the ringgit improved against the Singapore dollar to 3.2868/3082 from 3.2967/3016, climbed vis-à-vis the Thai baht to 12.9786/13.0777 from 13.0334/0603, gained against the Philippine peso to 7.60/7.66 from 7.61/7.63, and edged up against the Indonesian rupiah to 259.7/261.5 from 260.1/260.6. However, not all was bearish for the US dollar. UOB Kay Hian Wealth Advisors Sdn Bhd head of investment research, Mohd Sedek Jantan, highlighted that the US dollar index (DXY) had risen to 99.2 from 98.9. “Improved US labour data is lending support to the greenback. Job openings rose to 7.4 million in April, exceeding forecasts of 7.1 million.” “Wage growth is expected to continue outstripping inflation on average, which should underpin consumer spending and broader economic momentum,” he said. Mohd Sedek added that more clarity on the strength of the US labour market would be seen in Friday’s nonfarm payrolls report. title: Maybank Upbeat On Digiworld Corp’s Double-Digit Growth Outlook
body: Maybank Investment Bank Bhd (Maybank IB) has reiterated its BUY call on Digiworld Corporation (DGW VN), maintaining confidence in the company’s long-term double-digit growth outlook, despite trimming its target price by 4% to VND46,000 due to a lower target price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple of 18.4 times. The research house noted that DGW remains attractively valued at 13 times FY25 estimated P/E, below its three-year forward average of 15 times. DGW’s first quarter results were in line with expectations, with revenue rising 10.7% year-on-year to VND5.52 trillion. This was underpinned by steady momentum across most business segments, notably laptops and tablets, which saw a 22% growth as replacement cycles returned and the company gained market share. Office equipment sales also performed strongly with a 26% increase, supported by a recovering consumption environment and DGW’s continued expansion in the verticals it operates in. The consumer goods segment delivered a 20% growth while home appliances soared 91% year-on-year, buoyed by the inclusion of the Philips brand in late 2024. The mobile phone segment saw more muted growth, largely due to a high base in previous quarters, but remained stable. Margins also improved, with earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) up 58.3% to VND189 billion, leading to a margin of 3.42%, which surpassed Maybank IB’s projection of 2.39%. The improvement was largely attributed to a favourable product mix, with a higher contribution from higher-margin categories such as office equipment and home appliances. Despite an abnormal financial expense of VND77 billion, net profit still climbed 14.6% to VND106 billion, closely aligned with the bank’s forecast. Management remains upbeat for FY25, targeting sales and net profit growth of 15% and 18% respectively, with the year positioned as a “speed-up” period focusing on expanding the distribution portfolio into high-growth areas. Maybank IB projects an even stronger 22% earnings growth to VND543 billion, based on expectations of continued EBIT margin gains. The research house noted that despite some tariff-related concerns, DGW’s strategy to broaden its product mix and extend its distribution reach puts it in a strong position for sustainable growth, reinforcing its view that the stock offers solid upside potential over the next 12 months. title: Long Term View On CapitaLand Positive Despite Private Placement
body: Maybank Investment Bank Bhd (Maybank IB) has maintained its BUY call on CapitaLand Malaysia Trust (CLMT) and raised its dividend discount model-based target price to RM0.76 from RM0.75, despite a proposed private placement that will dilute FY2025 earnings per unit (EPU) and distribution per unit (DPU) by approximately 6%. CLMT announced a private placement of up to 435.4 million new units to raise RM250 million, mainly to repay borrowings used for its logistics and industrial acquisitions. While the placement results in short-term dilution, Maybank IB expects the impact to reverse in FY2026 and FY2027, with forecasted EPU/DPU increasing by around 3% due to cost savings and contributions from new logistics assets. Following this, the research house lifted its FY2025 to FY2027 net profit forecasts by 8%, 18% and 18% respectively. The placement, expected to conclude by 3Q2025, will reduce CLMT’s net gearing to 39.6% from a projected 44.1% post-asset acquisition level. Maybank IB views the exercise positively, citing enhanced balance sheet strength and added headroom for future yield-accretive investments. Proceeds from the placement will partly refinance borrowings for logistics acquisitions worth about RM400 million, including the completed Glenmarie Distribution Centre and upcoming assets in Elmina Business Park, Nusajaya Tech Park, and Senai Airport City. These are slated to complete in 2H2025 and expected to generate RM20 million in gross rental income annually—roughly 4% of CLMT’s estimated FY2026 revenue. The trust’s exposure to industrial and logistics assets will rise from 2.8% to 7.9% of assets under management, contributing an estimated 9% to FY2026 net property income. Maybank IB expects CLMT’s retail segment to remain resilient, driven by steady occupancy rates and mid- to high-single-digit rental reversions, especially in its non-Klang Valley malls. Despite near-term earnings dilution, Maybank IB believes the longer-term outlook is supported by a more diversified portfolio, stronger capital structure, and improved earnings visibility. CLMT currently offers attractive FY2025 and FY2026 net DPU yields of 6.7% and 7.3% respectively. The benchmark Kospi surged 40.94 points, or 1.52%, to reach 2,739.91 within the first 15 minutes of trade. HD Hyundai Heavy Industries, a leading shipbuilder, declined 3.86%. The South Korean won was trading at 1,376.55 against the US dollar as of 9:15 a.m., down 3.45 won from the previous close. title: Wall Street Climbs Despite Tariff Jitters; S&P 500 Ends Higher As Steel Soars, Autos Slide
body: US stocks closed higher on Monday as optimism around trade negotiations outweighed investor jitters over President Donald Trump’s latest tariff hike on steel and aluminium. The S&P 500 rose 24.25 points, or 0.41%, to close at 5,935.94, marking its best monthly performance since November 2023. The Dow Jones Industrial Average edged up 35.41 points, or 0.08%, to 42,305.48, while the Nasdaq Composite climbed 128.85 points, or 0.67%, to 19,242.61. Market sentiment stayed positive even after Trump announced plans to double tariffs on imported steel and aluminium to 50% starting Wednesday, a move that followed accusations that China violated a trade agreement struck in Geneva. In response, China dismissed the claims as “groundless” and pledged firm countermeasures to protect its interests. Despite heightened tensions, investors interpreted the developments as pressure tactics to speed up global trade negotiations. “Markets see the latest round of tariff threats and ramped up rhetoric… as nudges to move negotiations towards the finish line,” said Jamie Cox, managing partner at Harris Financial Group. Steel stocks rallied, with Cleveland-Cliffs surging 23%, while Nucor and Steel Dynamics also posted solid gains. Conversely, automakers took a hit, with Ford down nearly 3.9% and General Motors sliding by a similar margin, on fears of higher input costs. Technology stocks remained a bright spot, led by Nvidia, up 1.7%, and Meta, which rose 3.6%. However, Tesla dropped 1.1% after reporting a decline in monthly sales in Portugal, Denmark, and Sweden. Energy stocks also rose, lifted by OPEC+’s decision to maintain output levels in July, boosting investor confidence in oil market stability. On the economic front, data from the Institute for Supply Management (ISM) showed US manufacturing contracted for the third straight month, while supplier delivery times lengthened due to tariffs, raising concerns over potential supply chain disruptions. Federal Reserve commentary remained cautious, with Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan noting that the central bank is closely monitoring inflation and labour trends before deciding on interest rate adjustments. Traders are now pricing in at least two 25-basis-point rate cuts by year-end, according to LSEG data. Looking ahead, all eyes are on Friday’s nonfarm payrolls report, which could provide key signals on the health of the US labour market amid growing tariff pressures. Market breadth was positive, with advancing issues outpacing decliners by a 1.06-to-1 ratio on the NYSE and 1.11-to-1 on the Nasdaq. Volume on US exchanges totalled 15.67 billion shares, just below the 20-day average of 17.8 billion. The S&P 500 recorded 22 new 52-week highs, while the Nasdaq Composite posted 84 new highs against 80 new lows. title: Today’s Shares: CIMB Slips 1.15% Despite Analysts’ Optimism Post-1QFY25 Results
body: CIMB Group Holdings Bhd’s share price slipped 1.15% to RM6.85 as at 4.19pm on 3 June, down 8 sen from the previous close, despite positive sentiment from analysts following its first-quarter earnings. The stock, trading near the day’s low of RM6.85, recorded a high of RM6.98 earlier in the session, with 109.7 million shares traded. The counter opened at RM6.96 and last closed at RM6.93 on 23 May. The decline came despite RHB Investment Bank, Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB), and CIMB Securities all reiterating their Buy calls on the group. RHB maintained a target price of RM8.40 while HLIB’s stood higher at RM8.80, suggesting capital upsides of 21% and 27% respectively. CIMB’s 1QFY25 net profit rose 2% year-on-year to RM1.97 billion, underpinned by lower loan impairment charges and improved recoveries, especially from Indonesia. Its core capital (CET1) ratio came in at 14.7%, exceeding its 14% internal target, while loan loss coverage remained solid at 102%. title: Sunview’s 40% Share Dip, MIDF Remains Positive
body: MIDF Amanah Investment Bank Bhd (MIDF Research) has maintained a BUY rating on Sunview Group Bhd while revising its target price down to RM0.54 from RM0.62. The house reported that the revision reflects a lower FY26 earnings per share (EPS) estimate of 2.7 sen, applied to a price-to-earnings ratio (PER) of 20 times, which still offers a discount compared to larger peers. Despite a dip in recent quarterly earnings, the outlook remains positive, driven by rising demand for rooftop solar and progress in Engineering, Procurement, Construction and Commissioning (EPCC) projects under the Corporate Green Power Programme (CGPP) and Large Scale Solar (LSS) schemes. Sunview’s core earnings for 4QFY25 fell sharply by 58.9% year-on-year to RM2.0 million, resulting in a cumulative 12-month core profit of RM7.2 million, down 25.3% from the previous year and below MIDF Research’s expectations. The decline was mainly due to EPCC revenue dropping 51.7% to RM222.9 million, and profit before tax decreasing 24.9% to RM31.3 million, attributed to the early stages of CGPP projects compared to the completion of large-scale solar milestones last year. The group’s unbilled order book remains strong at RM374.3 million, providing earnings visibility through FY26. Sunview is actively pursuing additional EPCC contracts, having tendered for up to 330 megawatts (MW) of LSS5 projects. MIDF Research highlighted optimism for future order replenishment from upcoming LSS5+, LSS6 schemes, and growing interest in rooftop solar from commercial, industrial and residential sectors. Industry estimates suggest as much as RM17 billion worth of solar EPCC jobs are available. Sunview is also progressing on its overseas ventures, having established two wholly owned subsidiaries, Sunview-Alpha LLC and Sunview Beta LLC, in Uzbekistan. These subsidiaries aim to develop two solar power plants with a combined capacity of 600MW, with negotiations ongoing ahead of signing power purchase agreements. While earnings forecasts for FY26 remain broadly unchanged at RM13.9 million, minor adjustments were made to revenue and margin assumptions. The revised target price of RM0.54 implies a potential total return of approximately 38.5%, based on the current share price of RM0.39 as of May 30, 2025. Sunview’s prospects are underpinned by strong EPCC order books and expected growth in renewable energy demand linked to Malaysia’s National Energy Transition Roadmap. The company’s share price has experienced a 40% decline over the past year, but the improving pipeline of solar projects and operational execution provide support for a recovery. The focus on rooftop solar and large-scale solar projects positions Sunview favourably amid the country’s accelerating energy transition. title: Ringgit Gains Ground As US Dollar Weakens Amid Tariff Concerns
body: The ringgit rebounded to open higher against the US dollar on Monday, buoyed by a weaker greenback as markets weighed the outlook for US President Donald Trump’s tariff policy. At 8.03am, the local currency strengthened to 4.2165/2490 against the US dollar, improving from last Friday’s close of 4.2530/2605. title: Positive On Alliance Bank Despite Share Price Weakness
body: CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) maintains a BUY call on Alliance Bank Malaysia Bhd (ABMB) with an unchanged target price of RM4.80, following the bank’s announcement that the rights issue price has been fixed at RM3.33 per share. The entitlement basis is set at two rights shares for every 17 existing shares, aligning with CIMB’s earlier expectations. The rights issue is expected to raise RM606.5 million, consistent with the previously indicated amount of RM600 million. The rights issue price represents a discount of approximately 20.1% to the average five-day last traded price of ABMB shares. This adjustment follows a decline in the bank’s share price from RM5.09 in March 2025, when the rights issue was first announced with a price of RM4.20 and an entitlement of three rights shares for every 32 shares. CIMB Securities’ earlier report projected such a revision, estimating the rights price to fall to around RM3.20, with a higher number of rights shares issued to maintain the targeted fundraising amount. The actual number of rights shares to be issued stands at approximately 182.1 million, increasing the total shares outstanding from 1.55 billion to 1.73 billion. CIMB Securities forecasts that the rights issue will strengthen ABMB’s Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital ratio to 14.6% in fiscal year 2026, up from 12.2% in fiscal 2025, supporting the bank’s capital adequacy and capacity for growth. This enhancement is a key factor in maintaining the Buy rating. Looking ahead, the house highlights several key performance indicators for ABMB in FY26. These include a return on equity (ROE) exceeding 10% post-rights issue, loan growth between 8% and 10%, and a net interest margin (NIM) expected to range from 2.40% to 2.45%. The bank also targets a net credit cost of 30 to 35 basis points and a cost-to-income ratio of around 48%, with a dividend payout ratio of 40% to 50%. The bank also notes these figures as catalysts that should underpin the bank’s earnings stability and growth potential. Potential risks flagged by CIMB Securities include higher-than-anticipated credit costs and an increase in the cost of funds, which could impact profitability. However, the bank’s healthy balance sheet and strategic capital raising through the rights issue provide a solid foundation for navigating such challenges. At the time of reporting, ABMB shares were trading at RM4.33 ex-rights, with a market capitalisation of RM6.7 billion. The bank’s major shareholder remains Vertical Theme Sdn Bhd with a 29.1% stake, while the free float stands at 56%. Despite recent share price weakness relative to the broader market, CIMB Securities’ confidence in ABMB’s fundamental prospects remains intact, underpinning its positive outlook. title: Muhibbah’s Steep 67% Discount Makes It Attractive: CIMB
body: CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) has maintained a BUY rating on Muhibbah Engineering Bhd with an unchanged sum-of-the-parts (SOTP) target price of RM1.10, citing the company’s strong position in marine and oil and gas–related infrastructure as well as new growth prospects from its airport-related operations in Cambodia. Muhibbah reported first-quarter 2025 core earnings of RM17.6 million, an 85.5% year-on-year increase and accounting for 26% of both CIMB Securities’ and consensus full-year forecasts. While revenue fell slightly by 2.2% year on year to RM1.25 billion, core profits were boosted by the group’s 21%-stake in Cambodia Airports, which saw a 1.7 times increase in share of associate profits quarter on quarter to RM22.6 million. This was driven by a 22% surge in Cambodian air traffic as tourism in the kingdom continues to rebound strongly. However, core earnings dropped 37% quarter on quarter due to seasonal site activity slowdowns during the festive period. As expected, no dividends were declared for the quarter, though CIMB Securities projects a total dividend per share of 2.3 sen for FY25, implying a yield of 3.8%. A major development for Muhibbah came with Cambodia Airports’ settlement agreement with the Cambodian government concerning the Phnom Penh International Airport (PPIA) concession. Under this deal, Cambodia Airports will receive US$140 million (approximately RM591 million) in compensation for its investments in PPIA, with US$56 million already paid in March 2025. In addition, Cambodia Airports has signed a 15-year management services agreement with Cambodia Airport Investment Co to operate the new Techo International Airport (TIA), scheduled to begin operations on 9 September 2025. TIA will replace PPIA as Phnom Penh’s main gateway. The house noted that the contribution from this management contract has yet to be factored into Muhibbah’s earnings model pending further details on its operational and valuation impact. Despite some near-term uncertainties from the ongoing Petronas-Petroleum Sarawak dispute, Muhibbah’s active construction bid book remains robust at RM2.6 billion, with 62% domestic and 38% foreign contracts. Infrastructure works make up half of the bids, while waste-heat energy and oil and gas projects account for 38% and 12% respectively. Additionally, Muhibbah’s 65%-owned subsidiary Favelle Favco is pursuing RM3 billion worth of crane orders, buoyed by large infrastructure developments in the Middle East, including the New Murabba mixed-use project and preparations for the 2029 Asian Winter Games in NEOM. CIMB Securities highlighted Muhibbah’s valuation appeal, noting that the stock currently trades at a steep 67% discount to its SOTP value. Key catalysts for re-rating include income from the new airport management contract and crane orders from the Middle East. The bank cautioned that a slowdown in oil and gas activity remains a risk but affirmed the Buy rating on the company given its diversified portfolio and strategic growth opportunities. Muhibbah shares closed at RM0.60 as of 30 May 2025, against a 52-week range of RM0.51 to RM1.10, with a market capitalisation of RM438.4 million. title: Life Water Moves Ahead Past Tough Quarter
body: MIDF Amanah Investment Bank Bhd (MIDF Research) maintains a BUY call on Life Water Bhd with an unchanged target price of RM1.00, reflecting confidence in the company’s growth prospects despite a temporary setback in the third quarter of fiscal year 2025 (3QFY25). The house highlights that Life Water’s revenue increased marginally by 0.9% quarter-on-quarter to RM43.1 million, supported by stronger sales of carbonated drinks during festive periods. However, core earnings declined due to temporary production capacity disruptions caused by machinery installations at the Sandakan Sibuga and KK IZ4 plants. Margins also softened slightly following the February minimum wage hike and short-term operational inefficiencies. To address cost pressures, Life Water implemented a price increase averaging 5–7% from May 2025, equivalent to approximately 60 sen per carton. Management expects this revision to more than offset rising costs and anticipates margin recovery to begin in the fourth quarter of FY25, aided by favourable input cost trends such as softer PET resin prices and a stronger ringgit. Life Water is expanding its production capacity, with total annual drinking water output rising 15% to 448 million litres following the January 2025 commencement of its new Keningau plant. Currently operating at 31% utilisation with a single shift, the facility is expected to scale gradually in the coming quarters. Additional capacity upgrades include the installation of a new production line at the Sandakan Sibuga Plant 1, which will add 178 million litres or 40%, bringing total capacity to 626 million litres once completed. Operational efficiency is being enhanced through vertical integration efforts. Life Water is ramping up in-house PET bottle production with two new PET preform moulding machines being installed at its KK IZ8 facility. The first machine has been operational since the first quarter of calendar year 2025, while the second is slated for commissioning in the second half. This move aims to reduce reliance on external suppliers, improve cost control, and secure a stable supply of packaging materials. The company is also strengthening its distribution network to support increased output. By the end of May, Life Water had nearly 90 delivery touchpoints, up from over 75 at its IPO and has acquired additional delivery trucks in preparation for production ramp-up. A new distribution centre in Tawau, Sabah’s East Coast, is under construction and expected to be operational by the first half of 2026. Tawau’s growing population and rising tourism make it a strategic market for Life Water. In a strategic move to diversify its portfolio, Life Water is acquiring a 100% stake in Twinine Sdn Bhd, a Sabah-based sauces and condiments manufacturer, for RM10.5 million. The acquisition price implies a price-to-earnings ratio of approximately 11 times based on Twinine’s FY24 PAT of RM0.95 million. Completion is expected by August 2025, with profit contributions starting in FY26. Twinine’s established brand presence across Sabah’s west coast, Brunei and parts of Sarawak alongside its capacity for nearly doubling production through shift expansion, offers strong operational synergy. The acquisition enables Life Water to leverage existing distribution routes by bundling Twinine’s condiments with its beverage portfolio, enhancing asset productivity and route density. MIDF Research’s positive outlook is underpinned by capacity-driven growth, margin improvements, and portfolio diversification. The forecast remains for Life Water’s earnings to strengthen and margins to expand through FY26, supported by resilient demand, population growth, and sustained tourism recovery in Sabah. The research house’s target price is based on a PER of 12 times FY26 earnings per share of 8.3 sen. title: Hang Seng Index Futures’ Pullback Still Within Uptrend, Traders Advised to Hold Long Positions
body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) is maintaining a long position on the Hang Seng Index Futures (HSIF), despite Monday’s extended correction which saw the index fall 167 points to close at 23,019 points. The index opened higher at 23,180 points and briefly touched an intraday high of 23,219 points before retreating to a low of 22,514 points, signalling continued volatility. However, a rebound in the evening session saw it gain 119 points to last trade at 23,138 points. RHB Research noted that the “long lower shadow” formed on Monday suggests the 50-day simple moving average (SMA) remains a key downside support level. A decisive close below this line could trigger further selling pressure, potentially dragging the index down towards the 22,000-point support level. Nonetheless, as long as the HSIF stays above 22,000 points, the pullback is seen as a healthy correction within a broader uptrend. The house advises traders to maintain long positions initiated at 21,416 points on 14 April, with a stop-loss pegged at 22,000 points to manage downside risk. Immediate support levels are set at 22,000 and 21,000 points, while resistance stands at 24,500 and 26,000 points. title: Cautious On Bank Islam After Weaker Than Expected Q1
body: MIDF Amanah Investment Bank Bhd (MIDF Research), CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) and Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) have all maintained their NEUTRAL calls on Bank Islam Malaysia Bhd (BIMB), following the group’s weaker-than-expected first quarter results for FY25. Target prices were revised downwards to RM2.36 by MIDF Research (from RM2.43), RM2.30 by CIMB Securities (from RM2.35) and RM2.40 by HLIB (from RM2.60), citing heightened credit costs, net interest margin (NIM) compression and emerging capital risks as key headwinds. BIMB’s core net profit for 1QFY25 fell -27% quarter-on-quarter and -2% year-on-year to RM126.3 million. All three research houses noted that the dip was largely attributed to pre-emptive provisions made for the retail segment, with MIDF and CIMB highlighting an overlay allocation of RM14 million to buffer against rising gross impaired loans (GILs). CIMB pointed out that credit cost spiked to 45 basis points in the quarter, up from 25bps in the same period last year, while HLIB flagged the results as below expectations, capturing only 21–22% of full-year forecasts. Analysts also underlined a persistent compression in NIMs, a trend that has continued into April and May, as confirmed by BIMB’s management. MIDF Research estimated a sequential NIM decline of -13bps despite official reporting of a -1bp dip, largely due to tighter deposit competition and regulatory changes affecting housing loan classifications. CIMB Securities observed that while operating income grew by 7% year-on-year, flat net financing income and weaker NIM weighed on performance. While BIMB continues to register solid loan growth—driven by green financing, solar projects and retail loans—this momentum is straining its capital buffers. MIDF Research noted the bank’s Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) ratio has fallen to 13% at the group level and just 12.6% at the bank level, both sitting near or below its internal target. HLIB expressed concern that this low CET1 ratio could hinder future growth prospects despite otherwise undemanding valuations. Asset quality was another shared concern. Both MIDF Research and CIMB Securities observed that house financing-related GILs have been rising over the past three quarters, in contrast with improving trends across the broader industry. CIMB Securities said the group had classified several personal financing accounts as impaired during the quarter, pushing the GIL ratio up to 1.08%. However, management is hopeful of potential writebacks if GILs improve. Forecasts have been adjusted downward across the board. MIDF Research trimmed its FY25 and FY26 core net profit projections by 1%, HLIB by 4–5%, and CIMB by up to 4% to factor in higher credit costs. Dividend yields of 6–7% are expected to provide some support to total returns, although analysts agree that downside risks remain from further NIM compression, weaker non-financing income and capital limitations. Despite these challenges, analysts view BIMB’s current valuations as inexpensive, with MIDF Research noting the stock trades at a forward P/BV of 0.69x—below its five-year average—with an expected total return of 8.3%. However, until greater clarity emerges on asset quality and capital management, a neutral stance remains. title: August Restocking In US Should Boost Kossan’s Sales Volume Back
body: Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) maintains a BUY call on Kossan Rubber Industries Bhd with an unchanged target price of RM2.30, reflecting a capital upside of 38.5% and expected total return of over 40%. The house noted the cautious optimism from management despite soft demand for generic medical examination gloves in the second quarter and July, with restocking expected to resume in August as US distributors run down front-loaded inventories. Kossan reported ongoing challenges in sales volume for its 3.0-3.5g gloves due to distributors maintaining higher-than-usual stock levels, but this is expected to normalise as inventory buffers approach critical levels, given Malaysia-to-US lead times of around two months. Pricing pressures remain, with an anticipated quarter-on-quarter average selling price (ASP) decline of about US$0.5-1.0 per 1,000 pieces, reflecting lower nitrile butadiene rubber (NBR) costs and fierce market competition. A significant strategic focus is Kossan’s shift towards customised and specialised glove solutions, a move driven by rising occupational safety standards and tighter industrial specifications in developed markets like the US and Europe. Kossan currently derives roughly 30% of its sales volume from these specialised products, with the remainder from generic gloves. The company plans to introduce three to five new specialised glove products annually over the next few years, following a strong product rollout in 2023 and 2024. This transition is expected to improve margins and provide a competitive edge against volume-driven Chinese producers. Automation also remains a key priority, with Kossan aiming to increase efficiency in end-of-line processes such as packing and quality control within the next 12 months. This initiative targets a labour ratio of 1.5 workers per million pieces produced monthly, higher than local peers but lower than Intco Medical’s current benchmark, reflecting the additional manual handling required for customised products. Labour costs currently account for 10-15% of the company’s cost of goods sold. Despite uncertainties around supply-demand balance into 2026, HLIB’s earnings forecasts for FY25 to FY27 remain steady, underpinned by Kossan’s dual strategies of product specialisation and automation, alongside a strong balance sheet holding net cash of RM1.56 billion, the highest among peers. These factors support HLIB’s positive outlook and BUY rating on Kossan with a stable target price of RM2.30. title: Ann Joo Could Rebound In 2H On China’s Supply Cut
body: CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) maintains a BUY call on Ann Joo Resources Bhd despite its weaker-than-expected 1Q25 performance, with a lowered target price of RM0.83 from RM1.02. The research house noted that the steel producer posted core losses of RM109 million in the first quarter, missing expectations due to an 18% year-on-year decline in revenue. This was largely driven by lower selling prices and sales volumes, compounded by a two-month blast furnace shutdown. The shutdown, coupled with a longer festive break, led to a 12% quarter-on-quarter drop in top-line revenue. Ann Joo did not declare any dividends for 1Q25, and the forecast now excludes any dividend payments for FY25, reflecting a revised net loss projection of RM178 million. The near-term outlook remains challenging as tariff uncertainties continue to affect domestic and export markets. The US administration’s reciprocal steel tariffs and their impact on global trade sentiment remain a drag on performance. Domestic rebar prices have fallen to RM2,422 per tonne from around RM2,800 in November 2024, although they still hold a 32% premium compared to Chinese rebar prices of RM1,830 per tonne. Despite these pressures, CIMB Securities expects that China’s planned production cuts in the second half of 2025 could ease global steel supply, potentially lifting prices and market sentiment. Demand-side factors also offer a degree of optimism. The gradual rollout of significant infrastructure projects in Malaysia, such as the Penang LRT, Pan Borneo Sabah highway, and various flood mitigation works, may help support steel orders later in the year. Singapore’s government is expected to award between SGD35 billion and SGD39 billion worth of infrastructure contracts, providing additional demand visibility for Ann Joo. CIMB Securities highlighted that these factors could spur an earnings recovery from the second half of 2025 onwards. Despite the earnings downgrade, Ann Joo is trading close to its historical trough with a price-to-book value ratio of about 0.5 times, suggesting much of the downside risk has been priced in. The house maintains a positive view, emphasising that China’s production cuts and infrastructure stimulus in both Malaysia and Singapore serve as key catalysts for a potential rebound. The main risk to this outlook remains a prolonged trade war, which could continue to disrupt market stability. Ann Joo Resources currently holds a market capitalisation of RM550 million, with the Lim family owning a 67.4% stake. The stock has underperformed the market in recent months, down 10.1% over the past three months and nearly 25% over the last year, reflecting broader sector challenges. CIMB Securities’ Buy rating underscores its confidence in a gradual recovery, driven by supply-side discipline and improving demand from infrastructure developments across the region. title: Weekly Wrap: Singapore Stocks Steady Amid Global Uncertainty, Post-Election Confidence
body: The Singapore Straits Times Index (STI) maintained a steady course during the week of May 26 to May 30, 2025, reflecting investor confidence in the nation’s political stability following the recent general election, despite global market uncertainties. The STI hovered around the 3,900-point mark throughout the week, showcasing resilience amid mixed global cues. The index’s stability was underpinned by gains in key sectors, including financials and industrials, offsetting declines in property and trust segments. Financial stocks provided substantial support to the market. Notably, DBS Group Holdings reported a record net profit of S$11.4 billion for its financial year 2024, an 11% increase from the previous year, bolstering investor sentiment. Industrial players like Singapore Technologies Engineering Ltd also contributed positively, with a 3.75% gain observed during the week. Conversely, the property sector faced headwinds. City Developments Ltd experienced a 0.4% decline amid ongoing boardroom disputes, while CapitaLand Investment Ltd saw a 0.38% drop, reflecting cautious investor outlook in the real estate domain. Meanwhile, the outcome of the recent general election, where the People’s Action Party (PAP) retaining its supermajority, securing 87 out of 97 seats with a 65.57% vote share, further reinforced political continuity, instilling confidence among investors regarding Singapore’s economic policies and governance. Analysts highlighted that the election results signalled voters’ trust in the PAP to navigate the nation through global uncertainties. Despite domestic stability, external factors such as concerns over US tariffs and global economic growth prospects influenced market sentiment. Analysts from RHB Bank and OCBC Investment Research anticipate moderate returns for the Singapore market in 2025, citing the significant impact of global economic conditions on the STI, especially given the substantial weightage of banks in the index. Looking ahead, market participants are expected to monitor global economic developments closely. While the Singapore market may not replicate the highs of 2024, its resilience and the government’s strong mandate suggest a stable investment environment. Investors are advised to adopt a cautious approach, focusing on sectors with robust fundamentals amid the evolving global landscape. body: South Korea’s benchmark KOSPI index ended the week of May 26 to May 30 firmly above the 2,600-point level, bolstered by strong gains in the technology sector and improving global trade sentiment. The KOSPI started the week with a sharp rise, surging over 2% on May 26 following the US administration’s move to delay tariffs on the European Union. This policy shift eased investor concerns about escalating global trade conflicts and set a positive tone across Asian markets. By midweek, the index climbed to an eight-month high of 2,720.64, before easing slightly to close at 2,697.67 on May 30 due to profit-taking ahead of the weekend. Despite the pullback, the KOSPI managed to post a robust weekly gain and maintain its position well above the psychological 2,600 threshold. Leading the rally was South Korea’s heavyweight tech sector, with semiconductor stocks showing particular strength. Market leaders like Samsung Electronics Co Ltd and Sk Hynix Inc drew strong investor interest amid rising global demand for memory chips and optimism surrounding AI-driven infrastructure development. Looking ahead, while sentiment remains broadly positive, analysts caution that external risks including upcoming economic data from the US and China, as well as potential interest rate shifts, could influence short-term momentum. Investors will be watching closely in the coming weeks for signals from the Federal Reserve and updates on trade negotiations, which could determine whether the KOSPI can build on its recent strength or enter a consolidation phase. title: Wall Street Ends Flat But Logs Best Month Since Late 2023
body: US stocks closed little changed on May 30 after a turbulent session, as conflicting signals from President Donald Trump on China stirred fresh uncertainty in markets. Despite the day’s volatility, the S&P 500 and Nasdaq notched their biggest monthly gains since November 2023, buoyed by strong earnings, cooling inflation and a late-month rally. The S&P 500 slipped just 0.48 points to finish at 5,911.69, while the Nasdaq Composite lost 62.11 points, or 0.32%, closing at 19,113.77. The Dow Jones Industrial Average edged up 54.34 points, or 0.13%, to 42,270.07. Markets opened lower after Trump accused China of breaching a trade agreement via his Truth Social account, reigniting tariff concerns. But losses narrowed later in the session when Trump struck a more conciliatory tone, saying he hoped to resolve tensions in an upcoming conversation with Chinese President Xi Jinping. Despite the ongoing policy whiplash, May ended on a high note. The S&P 500 gained 6.2% for the month, rebounding from April’s dip, while the Nasdaq surged 9.6%, powered by strong tech earnings and renewed hopes for a Federal Reserve rate cut in September. Meanwhile, data showed US consumer spending rose 2.1% year-over-year in April, supporting views that inflation remains on a manageable path. Traders continued to price in a rate cut later this year. Market breadth was mixed, with declining stocks outpacing gainers on both the NYSE and Nasdaq. Trading volume hit 19.34 billion shares, above the recent 20-day average, as investors navigated a month of headline-driven swings and shifting economic signals. title: Looking Forward To Stronger Quarters From LBS Bina
body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has reiterated its BUY call on LBS Bina Group Bhd with an unchanged target price of RM0.72, implying a 51% upside and an estimated 5% yield. The research house said the property developer’s 1Q25 earnings were in line with expectations despite a year-on-year decline, and projected stronger quarters ahead due to improved sales momentum and upcoming project launches. LBS Bina reported a core profit of RM28.2 million for the quarter, a 6% increase quarter-on-quarter but 8% lower year-on-year, primarily due to the completion of several projects. Revenue dipped 4% year-on-year, although EBIT margins held steady at 18.6%, compared to 15.4% in 4Q24 and 19.4% in 1Q24. The group’s Klang Valley projects remained the main earnings driver, accounting for 86% of quarterly revenue, with key contributions from KITA @ Cybersouth, LBS Alam Perdana, Prestige Residence and the Idaman series. RHB Research noted that LBS recorded RM281 million in property sales in 1Q25, up from RM216 million a year ago, supported by strong demand for the Alam Perdana Industrial Park and the newly launched Cameron Centrum project in Pahang. The latter marked a significant shift in regional contribution, with Pahang making up 16% of total sales compared to just 1% in FY24. Klang Valley projects continued to dominate, contributing 67% of total sales. Meanwhile, unbilled sales stood at RM1.62 billion, providing earnings visibility for the next few years. The group has set a gross development value target of RM2.6 billion in new launches for FY25, mainly spread across Klang Valley and Pahang. Approximately 39% of this will stem from industrial projects in Telok Gong and Alam Perdana, while 38% will come from residential and mixed developments in Cameron Highlands, including Cameron Centrum and Rimbawan. Most of these launches are expected to roll out in the second half of the financial year. RHB Research has kept its earnings forecasts unchanged, citing results that were broadly in line with both its own and consensus expectations. The target price is based on a 65% discount to revised net asset value and includes a 2% premium for ESG considerations. Risks to the outlook include a weaker-than-expected property market, delays in project launches and intensified competition within the sector. title: Axiata’s Strategic Pivot Pays Off, Says RHB Research
body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has maintained a BUY call on Axiata Group Bhd (Axiata), revising its sum-of-parts target price down to RM2.70 from RM3.20, reflecting a potential upside of 30.4% from current levels. The house highlighted that the target price adjustment follows the reclassification of XL Axiata as an associate from a subsidiary as of mid-April, along with the impact of Smartfren’s ongoing losses and integration costs, which have compressed earnings and diluted profitability. Tan emphasised that the share price performance will largely depend on positive transactional outcomes related to the group’s ongoing strategic initiatives. Axiata’s management reaffirmed its priority on de-risking the balance sheet during its 1Q25 results briefing, targeting a net debt to EBITDA ratio of 2.5 times by the end of FY26. The company is focused on monetising non-core assets, with edotco and Linknet identified as primary candidates for divestment. Proceeds from these sales are expected to be used to reduce holding company debt, while the group aims to sustain its quarterly dividend per share of RM0.10 with a view to progressive increases. Regarding edotco, Axiata revealed a limited sales process would be initiated once decisions are finalised and that it is actively pursuing regulatory approvals for the sale of edotco Myanmar ahead of the 30 June deadline. The company also plans to monetise operations in Sri Lanka and Pakistan to rebalance its portfolio towards core Southeast Asian markets, although risks remain due to macroeconomic headwinds in frontier markets. At 1Q25, Axiata’s holding company debt stood at RM9.3 billion, constituting 41% of total debt of RM22.8 billion, marking a 14% year-on-year reduction following an early partial redemption of US$272 million (RM1.1 billion) in bonds during 3Q24. The management has not ruled out further liability management exercises in the near term. The group is poised to receive US$475 million (RM2.1 billion) from the equalisation of its stake in XLS by the Sinarmas Group, which can be deployed to reduce net debt further. Should Axiata divest its 63% stake in edotco at an enterprise value to EBITDA multiple of 8 to 10 times, the company could potentially raise over RM6 billion. This would translate into annual interest cost savings exceeding RM200 million and a projected net debt to EBITDA ratio improvement to 2.4 times, down from 3.0 times in 1Q25. RHB Research has adjusted its FY25 to FY27 core earnings forecasts downwards by 40.8%, 54.3% and 26.8% respectively, to account for the deconsolidation of the Indonesian unit and the reclassification of XLS as an associate, alongside revisions to Linknet and Robi’s estimates. The bank also lowered its target price to RM2.70, reflecting updated valuations of Axiata’s digital telco assets. Risks to the forecasts include weaker-than-expected merger synergies, delays in the asset recycling programme and adverse macroeconomic or geopolitical developments, particularly impacting frontier markets. title: Today’s Shares: SunCon Rises To RM5.88, Up 27% Since January
body: Shares of Sunway Construction Group Bhd (SunCon) noted at 0.86% higher at RM5.88 at 4.05 pm, buoyed by bullish investor sentiment following a major contract award and an upward earnings revision by MIDF Research. The stock gained five sen, trading between RM5.74 and RM5.93, with over 4.9 million shares changing hands. It last closed at RM5.83. The momentum follows a RM1.16 billion contract award from a US-based multinational tech firm for general contractor works on two data centre projects. These works are set to begin immediately and are expected to complete by February 2027. The contract expands SunCon’s order book to RM7.90 billion, of which nearly half (RM3.93 billion) is now tied to data centre developments — solidifying its position as a market leader in Malaysia’s fast-growing digital infrastructure space. Citing strong job wins and sector momentum, MIDF Research maintained a ‘BUY’ call and lifted its target price to RM6.44 from RM5.43, based on FY26 earnings per share of 22.2 sen and a 29x price-to-earnings ratio — one standard deviation above SunCon’s five-year average. The broker also upgraded earnings forecasts for FY25 to FY27 by 14.0%, 10.6% and 11.3%, respectively, reflecting improved visibility and faster billings, particularly from ongoing data centre projects such as the Yondr facility in Johor. Year-to-date, SunCon has secured RM3.50 billion in new contracts, already meeting 58% of its FY25 job replenishment target. Projects include the RM1.5 billion Bukit Chagar RTS TOD and several data centre packages. Despite potential execution risks and material cost pressures, MIDF noted SunCon’s track record in managing technically demanding projects and its diversified project base beyond Sunway-related jobs as key strengths going forward. CIMB Securities trimmed its FY26–FY27 earnings forecasts and revised its target price to RM4.85. title: Ringgit Gains On US Dollar After Court Halts Tariff Block
body: The ringgit opened stronger against the US dollar this morning, buoyed by improved investor confidence in emerging market currencies following a temporary reprieve granted by a US court on Trump-era import tariffs. At 8 am, the local currency surged to 4.2180/2485 against the greenback, up from Thursday’s close of 4.2390/2475. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid explained that the US Dollar Index (DXY) slipped below the 100-point mark to 99.278 after the US Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit stayed a US Court of International Trade ruling that would have blocked most Trump-era tariffs on Wednesday (US time). He noted, “Apart from that, the second estimate for the first quarter of 2025 US gross domestic product (GDP) contracted 0.2 per cent quarter-on-quarter seasonally adjusted annualised rate (SAAR), slightly better than the first estimate of -0.3 per cent but lower than the 2.4 per cent expansion in the previous quarter.” The economist added that recent US economic data indicated weakening conditions, citing Initial Jobless Claims rising to 240,000 last week compared to consensus estimates of 229,000, while Continuous Jobless Claims increased to 1.91 million for the week ending May 17 from 1.89 million the prior week. Traders and investors are now awaiting the Personal Consumption Expenditure (PCE) inflation data. “Consensus is pencilling the headline PCE and Core PCE at a moderate pace of 2.2 per cent and 2.5 per cent in April against 2.3 per cent and 2.6 per cent in the prior month,” he said. “As such, the ringgit is expected to trend higher today, possibly around RM4.21 and RM4.22, owing to a weaker US dollar outlook,” he told Bernama. At the opening, the ringgit appreciated against a basket of major currencies, strengthening to 5.6943/7355 versus the British pound from Thursday’s 5.7091/7205, and gaining against the euro at 4.7992/8339 compared to 4.7803/7899 previously. However, it weakened slightly against the Japanese yen to 2.9349/9563 from yesterday’s close of 2.9188/9249. The local note also traded mostly higher against its ASEAN counterparts. It improved versus the Singapore dollar to 3.2789/3031 from 3.2853/2921 on Thursday, inched up against the Indonesian rupiah to 258.6/260.6 from 259.9/260.5, and advanced against the Philippine peso to 7.56/7.62 from 7.60/7.62. The ringgit, however, slid against the Thai baht to 12.9565/13.0590 from 12.9321/9647 previously. title: Asian Stocks Slip As US Court Reinstates Trump Tariffs
body: Emerging Asian equity markets fell on Friday after a US federal appeals court temporarily reinstated sweeping tariffs imposed by former President Donald Trump. The decision came just a day after a US trade court blocked the duties, ruling Trump had overstepped his authority. The reinstated tariffs have reignited market caution, with investors anticipating that much of Trump’s trade duties could remain in place. “The world is still faced with the tariff reality and markets are taking a more conservative bet that much of Trump’s tariffs would stay,” said Fiona Lim, Senior FX Strategist at Maybank. MSCI’s index of Asian emerging market equities dropped 0.6%. Thailand’s benchmark index fell as much as 1.1% to its lowest in over a month, while Seoul stocks slid nearly 1%. The Philippine market also lost 0.7%. Markets in Indonesia and Taiwan were closed for public holidays. Despite the tariff headlines, the US dollar remained soft on Friday, poised for its fifth consecutive monthly decline amid broader concerns over US fiscal stability. Regional currencies showed a mixed performance but continued their upward trend for May. The Thai baht and South Korean won declined 0.3% and 0.4%, respectively, while the Malaysian ringgit and Philippine peso edged 0.1% higher. The Singapore dollar is on track for its fifth straight monthly gain. The MSCI emerging market currency index rose more than 2% in May, marking its best month since November 2023. The won climbed nearly 4% amid speculation of coordinated currency action following meetings between Seoul and Washington. title: Wall Street Pauses Ahead Of Nvidia Earnings, Fed Minutes
body: Wall Street’s rally hit a breather on Wednesday as investors shifted to wait-and-see mode ahead of Nvidia’s hotly anticipated earnings report and the release of minutes from the US Federal Reserve’s latest policy meeting. At 9:49 a.m. ET, the Dow Jones Industrial Average edged up 50.77 points (+0.12%) to 42,394.42, while the S&P 500 added 3.97 points (+0.07%) to 5,925.57. The Nasdaq Composite was flat, inching down just 0.98 points to 19,198.18. Chipmaker Nvidia rose 0.2% in early trading, with analysts expecting a 66.2% surge in first-quarter revenue. Its results, due after the closing bell, are seen as a major sentiment driver for global AI and tech markets. “There’s kind of a wait-and-see for Nvidia earnings tonight, which have become one of the big macro market movers,” said Baird investment strategist Ross Mayfield. Options traders braced for sector-wide volatility, particularly in the VanEck Semiconductor ETF. Most megacap and growth stocks traded higher, with Alphabet up 1% and Meta Platforms gaining 1.2%. Six of 11 S&P 500 sub-sectors advanced, led by Communication Services and Information Technology. The cautious mood followed Tuesday’s broad-based rally, spurred by easing trade tensions after President Donald Trump backed off threats of a 50% tariff on EU imports. That bounce brought the S&P 500 within 4% of its all-time high. In earnings, Capri Holdings soared nearly 9% after a strong Q4 revenue beat, while Dick’s Sporting Goods rose 2.6% on robust quarterly results. However, Okta tumbled 12% despite maintaining its full-year forecast, citing uncertainty in the economic landscape. Market breadth was slightly negative, with declining stocks outpacing gainers on both the NYSE and Nasdaq. The S&P 500 notched 18 new 52-week highs, while the Nasdaq recorded 38 new highs and 31 new lows. Investors are also watching long-dated US Treasury yields, which nudged higher amid ongoing concerns over fiscal stability. The benchmark 10-year note yield was up 3.9 basis points at 4.47%. Minutes from the Fed’s last meeting, expected at 2 p.m. ET, could shed light on policymakers’ inflation stance, especially following recent tariff-related uncertainties.
