title: Today’s Shares: RHB Bank Slips 2.4% Amid Softer Earnings
body: Shares of RHB Bank Bhd slipped 2.4% to RM6.51 as of 2:49pm today, following the release of its first quarter financial results for FY25, which came in slightly below market expectations. The counter opened at RM6.68 and touched an intraday low of RM6.50, with over 8.1 million shares traded. The decline followed a softer earnings report, although major investment houses CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) and Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) reiterated their BUY recommendations, citing resilient fundamentals, healthy dividend yields and attractive valuations. CIMB Securities maintained its target price at RM7.50, while HLIB reaffirmed a higher TP of RM7.70. RHB’s core earnings for 1QFY25 came in at RM750 million – a 2.7% year-on-year increase but a 5.7% decline from the previous quarter, due largely to lower non-interest income and higher loan loss provisions. Loan growth for the quarter moderated to an annualised 2.4%, prompting RHB to revise its full-year loan growth target to 5–6%, down from the earlier 6–7%. Nonetheless, growth in the residential, non-residential, and auto loan segments remains a positive indicator of the bank’s push into higher-yielding lending. CASA deposits rose 4.4% on an annualised basis, bolstered by successful campaigns such as the MySiswa initiative with the Ministry of Higher Education. This drove a significant 72% quarterly jump in student-related CASA balances to RM750 million, reducing reliance on costlier fixed deposits, which fell by 4% in the same period. Net interest margin (NIM) held steady at 1.84%, with analysts expecting further improvement following changes in statutory reserve requirements. Credit costs remained benign at 17 basis points, and despite a 2.7% QoQ increase in gross impaired loans – largely due to a RM31 million account in Singapore – the impaired loan ratio held firm at 1.5%. RHB’s CET1 ratio stood at a robust 16%, among the highest in the sector, though slight moderation is expected with the upcoming Basel III implementation. Dividend yields remain appealing, with HLIB and CIMB forecasting payouts of 6.7% and 6.5%, respectively. While market sentiment dipped on today’s results, analysts believe catalysts such as better-than-expected NIM, improved asset quality and continued dividend strength could support upside for the stock in the medium term. title: MIDF Lowers HLFG Earnings Forecast On Anticipated Higher Cost
body: MIDF Amanah Investment Bank Bhd (MIDF Research) has maintained its BUY call on Hong Leong Financial Group Bhd (HLFG), though it lowered its target price to RM20.63 from RM24.70, citing a strong set of results for the third quarter of FY25 that came in above both house and street expectations. The house attributed the outperformance primarily to a significant overlay writeback, which lifted group core net profit to RM2.81 billion for the nine-month period, representing 86% and 84% of MIDF Research and consensus full-year estimates, respectively. For 3QFY25, HLFG recorded a core net profit of RM1.12 billion, a quarter-on-quarter jump of 34%, again driven by the release of overlays. This gain more than offset pressures from higher operating expenses and tax charges. The house noted that Hong Leong Bank (HLBK), the group’s main contributor, showed robust 14% year-on-year profit growth for the period, underpinned by stronger net interest income (NII), non-interest income (NOII), and the same overlay effect. HLBK continues to be highlighted as a standout pick for its attractive valuation, rising dividend prospects, and consistent growth trajectory. However, not all subsidiaries delivered equally positive results. Hong Leong Assurance (HLA) reported a 3QFY25 profit before tax (PBT) of RM93 million, down 40% quarter-on-quarter due to weaker insurance service income and lower net investment income, although some of the decline was mitigated by stronger associate contributions. Over the nine-month period, HLA’s PBT slipped 6% year-on-year to RM487 million. Meanwhile, Hong Leong Capital (HLC) posted a PBT of RM15 million for 3QFY25, declining 21% quarter-on-quarter, mainly due to weaker contributions from its investment holding segment. HLC’s cumulative nine-month PBT dropped 23% year-on-year to RM57 million, reflecting lower income from its investment banking and stockbroking divisions. Despite the earnings beat in FY25, MIDF Research has revised HLFG’s FY26F and FY27F earnings downwards by 4% each to account for anticipated higher costs. The revised sum-of-the-parts valuation now applies a higher price-to-book valuation of 1.09 times for HLBK while also increasing the holding company discount from 25% to 35%, which collectively led to the adjusted TP. The house flagged downside risks including weaker contributions from Bank of Chengdu (BOCD), HLA and HLC, but maintained a positive outlook on HLFG’s core banking operations and regional expansion efforts. HLFG’s share price stood at RM16.70 as of 28 May, with MIDF Research projecting a potential total return of 27.1%, inclusive of a 3.6% dividend yield. title: Looking Ahead Into FY26 After Matrix Concepts’ Recent Earning Dip
body: Matrix Concepts Holdings Bhd (Matrix Concepts) has maintained a unanimous BUY rating from leading research houses RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research), MIDF Amanah Investment Bank Bhd (MIDF Research), and Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB), with target prices ranging from RM1.59 to RM1.73, reflecting potential upside of around 15% to 25% from the current share price of RM1.38. Analysts highlighted the company’s strong sales momentum, resilient earnings outlook for FY26, and promising developments in Malaysian Vision Valley (MVV) as key drivers for growth despite recent earnings setbacks. RHB Research reaffirmed its BUY call with a target price of RM1.72, emphasising a 25% upside potential and an attractive yield of about 7% for FY26. The broker noted that Matrix Concepts’ FY25 results fell short of expectations mainly due to slower property sales conversion and increased expenses, including higher staff bonuses and finance costs linked to land acquisition for the MVV City project. Despite this, total property sales for FY25 reached RM1.38 billion, slightly exceeding management’s target. RHB Research expects revenue and expenses to normalise in FY26, with the MVV City industrial land sales contributing positively in the second half of the financial year. MIDF Research also maintained its BUY rating with a target price of RM1.59. It reported that FY25 core net income of RM203 million was within expectations but down 14.7% year on year, affected by slower earnings recognition due to project delays and lower sales conversion. The bank highlighted the strong property sales of RM1.45 billion in FY25, driven largely by township projects in Negeri Sembilan, which accounted for 78% of new sales. MIDF Research expects better earnings in FY26 as these delays normalise and anticipates new sales of RM1.6 billion based on a launch pipeline with a gross development value of RM1.7 billion. Unbilled sales rose to RM1.48 billion, providing one year of earnings visibility. HLIB echoed these views with a BUY call and an unchanged target price of RM1.73. It described Matrix Concepts’ 4QFY25 core profit after tax and minority interests (PATAMI) of RM43 million as slightly below expectations due to ongoing delays in converting sales to revenue and higher administrative costs related to pre-launch activities for MVV township development. Nevertheless, the bank stressed that sales momentum remained robust, with FY25 property sales hitting RM1.38 billion, meeting the company’s full-year target. The group’s FY26 sales target is RM1.6 billion, underpinned by planned launches in MVV, Banting, and Sepang, and an expected recognition of about 40% of RM300 million from industrial land sales in MVV by end-FY26. HLIB views these developments, alongside an expanding geographic presence and contributions from its healthcare division, as catalysts for earnings growth and dividend sustainability, with an attractive FY26 dividend yield of 5.1%. All three research houses acknowledged a temporary earnings dip caused by slower revenue recognition from secured sales and rising administrative expenses, but remain confident in Matrix Concepts’ medium-term prospects, particularly from its industrial land development and ongoing township projects. The company’s net gearing, which increased to 0.16 times in FY25 from net cash previously, is expected to rise moderately as it completes further land acquisitions in MVV. In summary, analysts view Matrix Concepts as well positioned for a stronger FY26, supported by a healthy sales pipeline, strategic landbank monetisation, and operational normalisation, making it a compelling buy for investors seeking both growth and income in the Malaysian property sector. title: Wall Street Rebounds As Trump Eases Tariff Threat On EU
body: US stock index futures surged on Tuesday as markets reopened after the Memorial Day holiday, buoyed by President Donald Trump’s decision to postpone steep tariffs on European imports and dial down trade tensions with the EU. At 4:33 a.m. ET, Dow E-minis rose 526 points (+1.26%), S&P 500 E-minis added 85.75 points (+1.47%) and Nasdaq 100 E-minis gained 346.25 points (+1.65%), signalling a strong Wall Street open. The rally came after Trump rolled back a threat to impose 50% tariffs on EU goods starting June 1, restoring a July 9 deadline to allow for renewed trade talks with the 27-nation bloc. The reversal helped ease investor anxiety following last week’s selloff triggered by fears over US debt and policy uncertainty. Premarket action saw major tech and growth names rebound sharply. Apple rose 1.9%, Alphabet gained 2.3% and Tesla climbed 2.5%, while Nvidia jumped 2.8% ahead of its earnings report due Wednesday. Trump Media & Technology Group soared 10.3% following reports it plans to raise US$3 billion to invest in cryptocurrencies, including bitcoin. Despite the optimism, analysts at Rabobank noted uncertainty remains over whether US-EU talks will yield a resolution, keeping investors cautious. On the economic front, investors await May’s consumer confidence data and Wednesday’s release of US Federal Reserve meeting minutes. Several Fed officials, including Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari, are expected to speak throughout the week. Kashkari has urged holding rates steady until the inflationary impact of tariffs becomes clearer. Additional economic indicators — including May’s Personal Consumption Expenditure (PCE) and a revised Q1 GDP estimate — are also due later in the week. Despite recent volatility, the S&P 500 is trading about 6% below its record high, having recovered from April lows on easing inflation fears and revived risk appetite. However, gold miners such as Newmont fell around 2% as gold prices declined more than 1%. title: Today’s Shares: TNB Climbs 0.71% On Midday Charge
body: Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) shares edged up by 0.71% to RM14.10 as of 2.45pm today, with 21.5 million shares traded. The counter opened at RM14.10, touched a high of RM14.18 and dipped to a low of RM14.08, before settling at its last done price. The trading activity reflects renewed investor interest following positive earnings momentum and continued analyst support. TNB’s performance follows the release of its first-quarter results for FY2025, which drew consistent BUY calls from MIDF Amanah Investment Bank Bhd (MIDF Research), CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities), and Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB). Target prices from the research houses ranged between RM15.13 and RM16.20, indicating potential upside of up to 15%. MIDF Research, which maintained its BUY call with a target price of RM15.13, cited TNB as a major beneficiary of Malaysia’s National Energy Transition Roadmap (NETR). Despite a minor 1.2% drop in electricity demand to 31.5 TWh—blamed on festive holidays and the shorter quarter—TNB’s core earnings jumped 12.4% year-on-year to RM1.03 billion, driven by strong demand fundamentals and regulatory support. Revenue rose 17.6% to RM16.04 billion. A key highlight was the turnaround of TNB’s generation unit (GenCo), which returned to profitability due to stabilising global fuel prices and a higher equivalent availability factor of 82.0%. CIMB Securities echoed the bullish stance with a target price of RM15.80, noting that while revenue declined 1.5% quarter-on-quarter, it was offset by a 4.4% drop in fuel and power purchase costs. Normalised EBITDA rose by 10.9% to RM20.8 billion, while GenCo posted an adjusted profit after tax of RM68 million. The firm also noted that TNB’s capital expenditure stood at RM3.2 billion, largely spent on regulated assets that grew 7% year-on-year. HLIB maintained its BUY recommendation with the highest target price of RM16.20, highlighting an 8% quarter-on-quarter rise in core profit to RM1.1 billion. The bank pointed to strong commercial electricity demand, up 5.1% year-on-year, largely driven by growth from data centres and the services sector. TNB also hit a new peak demand of 20.5 gigawatts in May 2025. HLIB expects further earnings strength in FY25, supported by a RM42.8 billion capital investment under Regulatory Period 4 and a more stable fuel margin environment due to coal price normalisation. While no dividends were declared for the quarter, analysts continue to expect yields in the 3.5% to 3.9% range for the full year. Overall, TNB remains a top pick in the utilities sector, backed by solid fundamentals, strategic alignment with national energy goals and consistent demand growth. title: Today’s Shares: Sime Darby Shares Drop 4.3% Amid Q3 Earnings Miss
body: Sime Darby Berhad’s share price fell 4.28% to RM1.79, extending losses after the group reported disappointing third quarter results for the financial year ending June 2025 (3QFY25). The stock saw heavy trading volume of 25.1 million shares, reflecting investor caution. The conglomerate’s core earnings per share plunged 45% quarter-on-quarter, marking its weakest quarterly performance in 20 quarters. Revenue declined 8% to RM16.3 billion, pressured by weaker contributions from key divisions, including Motors and Industrial. The Motors segment experienced a 35% year-on-year drop in core profit before interest and tax, mainly due to subdued sales in Australasia, Malaysia, and China, although Singapore posted a 12.5% increase supported by rising electric vehicle sales. Meanwhile, the Industrial division suffered margin compression linked to currency fluctuations, including a RM50 million foreign exchange loss due to the Australian dollar’s strength against the US dollar and the Malaysian ringgit’s appreciation against the Australian dollar. Despite these setbacks, Sime Darby’s nine-month revenue rose 8.2% year-on-year, mainly driven by UMW’s doubled contribution following full consolidation. However, core net profit fell 10.8% year-on-year to RM833 million, excluding one-off gains. Headline net profit was bolstered by a RM458 million one-off gain from the Malaysian Vision Valley land sale. Both CIMB Investment Bank and Hong Leong Investment Bank retained their Buy ratings on Sime Darby but lowered their target prices to RM2.15 and RM2.12 respectively, down from RM3.00 and RM2.36, reflecting a cautious outlook. CIMB noted expectations of a gradual recovery in the Industrial parts segment in the latter half of 2025 as inventory costs ease and parts prices stabilise. The Industrial division’s order book grew 13% year-on-year to RM4.8 billion, supported by robust demand from Malaysia and Australasia. Nevertheless, CIMB downgraded its earnings forecasts for 2025 to 2027 by 11–22%, anticipating a 15% drop in core net profit for FY25 before a rebound in FY26. HLIB also revised down earnings by 15% for FY25 but expects Sime Darby to benefit from a strong RM4.8 billion Industrial order book, with significant exposure to Australia’s mining sector and Malaysian infrastructure projects. The bank highlighted resilient Industrial momentum and attractive dividend yields between 6.4% and 7.0% over the next three years. Following the results, Sime Darby’s stock price plunged 13% on 27 May, nearing pre-2018 levels before the UMW de-merger. Analysts cited risks from fuel subsidy cuts and intensifying competition in China but pointed to potential upsides from UMW synergies, stabilising commodity prices, and improved Motors division performance, especially in Singapore and China. Currently, Sime Darby trades below its historical average price-to-earnings ratio, offering an appealing dividend yield of around 5.6% to 6.7%, which may attract investors willing to weather short-term challenges. title: Today’s Shares: Alliance Bank Slips 0.23% To RM4.36
body: Shares of Alliance Bank Malaysia Bhd (ABMB) edged down slightly to RM4.36 in mid-afternoon trade today, despite analysts reaffirming positive outlooks following the bank’s record full-year earnings. At 3:29pm, ABMB was trading at RM4.36, down 0.23% or one sen, with 1.03 million shares exchanged. The counter opened at RM4.39 and ranged between RM4.35 and RM4.40. CIMB Investment Bank and Hong Leong Investment Bank have maintained their BUY recommendations, citing the bank’s strong FY25 results and growth momentum. CIMB kept its target price at RM4.80, while HLIB upgraded the stock from Hold to Buy, albeit trimming its target to RM5.00 from RM5.55. ABMB posted an 8.7% year-on-year rise in net profit to RM750.7 million in FY25—its highest ever—driven by a 14.2% surge in net interest income. The bank’s loan book expanded 12.5% year-on-year in 4QFY25, more than double the industry average, with broad-based gains across mortgages, SMEs and working capital segments. Deposits also rose 14.7%, supported by inflows from East Malaysian entities, lifting CASA ratio to 41%. Net interest margin held firm at 2.43%, and the bank guided for 2.40–2.45% in FY26. Credit quality improved with a gross impaired loans ratio of 1.8% and final dividend of 9.9 sen declared, bringing FY25 total payout to 19.4 sen. Its rights issue is expected to complete by end-July. Management has set new KPIs for FY26 including ROE of over 10% and cost-to-income ratio of 48%. title: Ringgit Slips Amid Firmer Greenback And Tariff Concerns
body: The ringgit opened marginally lower against the US dollar on Wednesday, dragged by a stronger greenback driven by improved US consumer sentiment and ongoing global tariff uncertainty. At 8.05am, the local currency slipped to 4.2350/2500 versus the greenback, down slightly from Tuesday’s close of 4.2345/2430. According to Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid, the US Dollar Index (DXY) climbed 0.59% to 99.521 points overnight, signalling a modest recovery, albeit still below the 100-point threshold. “The uptick tracked the latest US Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index, which climbed to 98 points – largely driven by stronger stock market performance since early April and easing gasoline prices,” he told Bernama . He added that despite the confidence rebound, the US economy still faces downside risks, especially from inflationary pressures linked to tariff policies. At Tuesday’s close, the ringgit had slipped 0.47% to RM4.2388 against the US dollar from RM4.2190, as some traders opted to take profits amid volatility. “Given the firmer dollar and lingering external uncertainties, the ringgit is expected to remain under pressure, trading within a narrower band of RM4.22 to RM4.23 today,” he noted. Against a basket of major currencies, the ringgit strengthened. It appreciated against the Japanese yen to 2.9391/9500 from 2.9425/9486, gained against the euro to 4.8012/8182 from 4.8053/8150, and rose against the British pound to 5.7228/7430 from 5.7352/7467. The local note was mixed against regional peers. It improved against the Singapore dollar at 3.2870/2989 from 3.2894/2963 but weakened versus the Thai baht at 12.9471/13.0025 from 12.9365/9676. It remained flat against both the Philippine peso at 7.62/7.65 and the Indonesian rupiah at 259.9/261.0. title: Japan’s Key Stock Index Snap 4-day Rally
body: Japan’s key stock index snapped a four-day winning streak on Wednesday, as investors sought to lock in profits after an earlier gain briefly took the index above the 38,000 level. The benchmark Nikkei stock index, the 225-issue Nikkei Stock Average, closed at 37,722.40, down 1.71 points from the previous trading day. Early gains were driven by strength in U.S. tech stocks the previous day, sending the Nikkei up more than 400 points at one stage. However, selling pressure increased as investors sought to lock in profits at the higher level. The 38,000 range, where trading has been heavy since the market correction in the summer of 2024, triggered selling from those waiting for a rebound. The broader TOPIX index managed a slight gain for the fourth consecutive day, closing up 0.02 points at 2,769.51. Of the listed stocks on the Tokyo Stock Exchange Prime Market, 763 declined, 792 advanced, and 76 were unchanged. RHB Research noted the rebound above the 20-day simple moving average (SMA) and upward-turning RSI as signs that bearish momentum has stalled, with the broader bullish structure still intact. The index remains above both the 20-day and 50-day SMA lines, reinforcing the uptrend. “As long as HSIF stays above 22,000 points, the recent pullback is seen as healthy consolidation within an ongoing uptrend,” the research house said, maintaining a positive trading bias. RHB Research recommends holding long positions initiated at 21,416 points (based on the April 14 close), with a stop-loss threshold set at 22,000. Immediate resistance is pegged at 24,500 points, with the next at 26,000. Key support levels are at 22,000 and 21,000 points. title: Gold Inches Up To RM14,006.97, But Correction Looms Amid Weak COMEX Momentum
body: Gold prices in Malaysia edged higher to RM14,006.97 per ounce at the time of writing, reflecting a modest gain of RM12.00 or 0.09% for the day, according to data from GoldPrice.org. Despite the slight daily uptick, gold remains down by 2.70% over the past 30 days. However, it has posted a robust 18.75% gain over six months and a 27.12% rise over the past year, underscoring its longer-term resilience. Over a five-year period, gold has surged by 85.49%, and over two decades, it has jumped more than 778%. However, analysts are warning of possible short-term weakness. In its latest technical outlook, RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has maintained a negative trading bias on COMEX Gold, pointing to signs that bullish momentum may have stalled. “COMEX Gold struggled to stay above the 20-day simple moving average (SMA) on Tuesday after pulling back by US$65.40 to close at US$3,300.40,” RHB said. The session opened at US$3,355.60, reaching an intraday high of US$3,356 before slipping to a low of US$3,283. The bearish candlestick formed suggests the precious metal may be headed back into a correction phase, particularly if prices fall below the 20-day SMA. Should that occur, RHB sees the next key support at US$3,150 , with a deeper drop potentially testing US$3,000 . Conversely, US$3,400 remains the immediate resistance level, with US$3,500 serving as the next upside barrier. Until gold convincingly breaks above the US$3,400 mark, the research house advises traders to maintain short positions first initiated at US$3,188.30 on 14 May, while keeping a stop-loss at US$3,400 to manage risk. Although the Malaysian gold price has shown resilience in local currency terms, RHB’s technical indicators suggest caution for those watching the international market trend. title: Asian Markets Waver Despite Wall Street Gains; JGB Auction Undermines Optimism
body: Asian equities were mixed on Wednesday as a rally on Wall Street failed to provide lasting momentum, with a weak Japanese government bond auction shaking investor sentiment across the region. Tokyo stocks ended flat while the yen weakened following the worst take-up for 40-year Japanese government bonds since July, undermining confidence already rattled by last week’s similarly dismal 20-year bond auction. The result reversed Tuesday’s rebound, which had been fuelled by speculation that Japan’s Ministry of Finance might reduce bond issuance volumes. The cost of government borrowing has spiked globally in recent weeks, hitting record highs in Japan. Contributing factors include rising fiscal spending and concerns about tightening monetary policy, particularly as the Bank of Japan (BoJ) continues reducing its purchases of JGBs in response to climbing inflation. Bond prices fell and yields rose as demand sagged. Still, Masahiko Loo, senior fixed income strategist at State Street Global Advisors, noted: “We maintain our long-standing view that the challenges in the JGB market are technical rather than structural.” He added, “Any perceived supply-demand imbalance is more a matter of timing mismatches… We expect these imbalances to be resolved as early as the third quarter of 2025.” Markets across the region showed mixed results. Hong Kong, Sydney, Mumbai, Jakarta and Wellington posted losses. Shanghai was little changed, while Singapore, Seoul, Taipei, Manila and Bangkok moved higher. European markets opened on a firmer note, with London, Frankfurt and Paris posting early gains. On Wall Street, optimism returned as trading resumed after the long weekend. US President Donald Trump’s move to delay 50% tariffs on European Union goods until July helped soothe nerves frayed by his surprise announcement on Friday. Adding to the positive sentiment, Trump posted on Truth Social: “I have just been informed that the E.U. has called to quickly establish meeting dates… This is a positive event, and I hope that they will, FINALLY… open up the European Nations for Trade with the United States of America.” Markets also welcomed stronger-than-expected US consumer confidence data, buoyed by easing trade tensions, particularly with China. Despite the Wall Street lift, overall sentiment in Asia remained cautious as concerns over rising bond yields persisted, especially in the wake of Japan’s disappointing debt auction. New Zealand’s central bank, meanwhile, cut interest rates for the sixth consecutive meeting, but Wellington markets still ended the day in the red. As global investors remain sensitive to bond market developments and political trade moves, the week’s mixed regional performance underscores the fragile balance between monetary tightening fears and brief policy-induced relief. title: US Stock Futures Rebound After Trump Delays Tariffs On Europe
body: US stock futures climbed on Monday as President Donald Trump’s decision to delay proposed tariffs on the European Union helped calm investor jitters and reignited optimism in equity markets. Futures on the Nasdaq 100 surged 1.5%, while contracts on the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 1.2% and 1.1% respectively. The gains came after Trump extended the deadline for imposing 50% tariffs on European goods from June 1 to July 9 following a phone call with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen. The move reversed market losses from Friday, when Trump’s surprise tariff threat had rattled investors. European equities also rebounded, with the Stoxx Europe 600 erasing its previous decline. “The stock market seems to dance to Trump’s tune: first a threat, then a pullback, followed by a rebound,” said Jochen Stanzl, Chief Market Analyst at CMC Markets. He noted that the so-called “Trump Pattern” has become a recurring playbook for risk-tolerant investors anticipating presidential reversals. However, market experts also flagged signs of fatigue among investors, warning that repeated whiplash on trade issues could dampen sentiment. “The rebounds following these selloffs are losing strength,” said Frederic Rozier, Portfolio Manager at Mirabaud France. Elsewhere, anticipation is building around Nvidia Corp’s earnings release on Wednesday, which is seen as a litmus test for AI-driven tech stocks. Meanwhile, the US Federal Reserve’s preferred inflation gauge — the core personal consumption expenditures price index — is due Friday, with a modest rise of 0.1% expected for April. In currency markets, the Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index hovered near its lowest level since July 2023. The euro and British pound each rose 0.2%, while the yen slipped 0.2% to 142.85 per dollar. Bitcoin rallied 2.3% to US$110,150, and ether advanced 1.6% to US$2,564.64. Commodities showed mixed moves. West Texas Intermediate crude inched up 0.1% to US$61.61 a barrel, while spot gold slipped 0.5% to US$3,339.37 an ounce. Cash Treasuries were closed due to holidays in the UK and US, but 10-year Treasury futures pointed to a yield decline of two basis points to 4.51%. Markets are expected to remain sensitive to trade headlines and inflation data in the days ahead, with volatility likely to persist amid global economic uncertainties. title: Today’s Shares: Takaful Steady At RM3.46, Analysts Still Say ‘Buy’
body: Syarikat Takaful Malaysia Keluarga Bhd (STMB) closed unchanged at RM3.46 on Tuesday amid modest trading activity, as analysts maintained their bullish outlook despite a mixed start to the financial year. As of 3.50 pm, STMB’s share price showed no change from its previous close, with 135,500 shares changing hands. The counter opened slightly higher at RM3.48 and traded between RM3.44 and RM3.49 throughout the session. Buy and sell orders were nearly balanced, with buy volume at 107,000 and sell volume at 139,000 shares. The steady performance comes in the wake of STMB’s first-quarter results for FY25, which saw net profit decline by 7.6% year-on-year to RM94.5 million, largely due to RM85.5 million in fair value losses from equity investments. Nonetheless, the result came in line with expectations, contributing 23.5% of full-year earnings estimates. Despite the softer bottom line, the group’s family takaful segment delivered a 43% jump in contributions, underpinned by robust demand for credit-related and medical protection products. Analysts from RHB Investment Bank Bhd, MIDF Amanah Investment Bank Bhd and CIMB Investment Bank Bhd all retained their ‘Buy’ calls on the stock, citing strong fundamentals and solid long-term prospects. RHB kept its target price unchanged at RM4.60, pointing to continued growth from bancatakaful channels and attractive valuations, with STMB trading at 1.2 times price-to-book – well below its five-year mean. MIDF, while revising its target price slightly to RM4.59, highlighted the company’s digital outreach via its Kaotim app and forecast a healthy dividend yield of over 5%. The bank remained positive despite acknowledging risks tied to reinsurance cost pressures and investment volatility. CIMB Securities adjusted its target price downward to RM4.10, citing reduced investment income and a higher effective tax rate of 37% in Q1. However, it noted improved underwriting margins of 12% and expects mid-single-digit earnings growth in FY25 driven by better operational performance. STMB, valued at approximately RM3.02 billion, continues to enjoy support from institutional investors such as Lembaga Tabung Haji and the Employees Provident Fund. With stable earnings from its core takaful segment and increasing digital penetration, the group remains well-positioned amid a challenging macroeconomic environment. Analysts agreed that the company’s strategic shift away from general takaful volatility towards a more balanced portfolio, along with consistent growth in contributions, supports their positive stance. title: Today’s Shares: MBM Resources Slides 1.94% Despite Steady Q1
body: MBM Resources Bhd (MBMR) shares noted at 1.94% lower at RM5.57 on Bursa Malaysia today, down 11 sen from its previous close, despite posting first-quarter results that came in line with analysts’ expectations. As of 2.50 pm, the counter saw a trading volume of 2.12 million shares, with prices ranging between RM5.51 and RM5.66 during the day. The last done price of RM5.57 is still near target price ranges set by analysts, reflecting a generally neutral sentiment toward the stock. Earlier today, MBMR reported a core net profit of RM71.3 million for the first quarter of financial year 2025, meeting roughly 23% of full-year forecasts. Revenue slipped 6.9% year on year to RM574 million, mainly due to lower sales in its motor trading and assembly segment, which includes Perodua and Volvo brands. CIMB Securities, RHB Investment Bank and MIDF Amanah Investment Bank all maintained their Hold or Neutral ratings on MBMR, with target prices of RM5.80, RM5.55 and RM5.75 respectively. Despite earnings declining 27% quarter-on-quarter—largely due to a high base effect from Perodua’s record Q4 deliveries and a shorter working period—Perodua is still expected to drive over 70% of MBMR’s profit before tax for the year. Demand for key models like the Axia, Bezza and Myvi remains resilient, with two new models and an electric vehicle launch in the pipeline. The group is also investing in long-term growth through outlet upgrades and its upcoming 4S centre under the Jaecoo brand. However, analysts remain cautious due to potential headwinds including fuel subsidy rationalisation, currency risks, and continued industry competition. MBMR’s strong net cash position of RM214 million continues to offer a buffer against economic uncertainties. While near-term earnings growth may remain subdued, its high dividend yield and stable automotive partnerships have analysts seeing the stock as fairly valued in the current environment. title: Today’s Shares: Maybank Shares Dip 0.5% Amid Modest Trading

Investor sentiment appears cautious as management highlighted potential pressure on margins due to expected policy rate cuts and continued elevated costs, including ongoing investments in technology. Asset quality remained stable, although impaired loans rose modestly, mainly in Malaysia and Singapore. Despite these headwinds, Maybank continues to offer an attractive dividend yield estimated at nearly 7% for FY25, which helps support the stock’s valuation. The share price currently trades at about 1.24 times its forecast price-to-book value for FY25. The market response on May 27 reflects this mixed outlook, with the stock seeing moderate buying and selling interest around the RM9.86–RM9.87 range as investors weigh steady earnings against challenges ahead. title: Ringgit Strengthens On Weakening US Dollar, Trade Uncertainty
body: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar on Tuesday, lifted by persistent weakness in the greenback amid investor concerns over the United States’ fiscal direction and unpredictable trade policies. At 8.05 am, the ringgit strengthened to 4.2050/2250 against the US dollar compared with Monday’s close of 4.2155/2220. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US Dollar Index (DXY) had extended its decline, falling to 98.934 points, as investors grew wary of the direction of US trade policy under President Donald Trump. “The delay in implementing the 50% tariff on European Union goods until 9 July 2025 signals uncertainty in the Trump administration’s trade stance, undermining confidence in the US dollar. “Furthermore, the expansionary fiscal measures, which are expected to widen the US fiscal deficit and increase national debt levels, have further weighed on sentiment towards US assets,” he told Bernama. Mohd Afzanizam added that this backdrop favours emerging market currencies like the ringgit, which continue to benefit from improving capital inflows and stronger risk appetite. “Market trends suggest the ringgit could maintain its positive momentum in the immediate term, especially if the US maintains its current policy tone,” he noted. By the close, the ringgit also traded higher against a basket of major currencies. It gained vis-à-vis the euro to 4.7903/8131 from 4.7972/8046, rose against the British pound to 5.7058/7329 from 5.7175/7263, and improved against the Japanese yen to 2.9500/9643 from 2.9506/9553. Against its ASEAN peers, the local note advanced across the board. It appreciated against the Singapore dollar to 3.2757/2915 from 3.2826/2879, strengthened against the Thai baht to 12.8992/9745 from 12.9231/9466, gained vis-à-vis the Philippine peso to 7.58/7.63 from 7.60/7.62, and edged up against the Indonesian rupiah to 258.7/260.1 from 259.4/259.9 previously. title: E-Invoicing Boom Lifts AutoCount To Record RM13.7 Million Profit In Q1
body: The adoption of Malaysia’s e-invoicing initiative has fuelled a record-breaking quarter for AutoCount Dotcom Berhad, which posted its highest-ever core profit after tax of RM13.65 million for the first quarter ended March 31, 2025, (Q1 FY2025), a 235.4% jump from RM4.07 million in the same period last year. The company also recorded its highest-ever quarterly revenue of RM25.55 million, up 86.9% year-on-year, largely driven by surging demand for its e-invoicing module in line with the government’s digitalisation mandate. Operating cash flow stood at RM17.32 million, while net profit margin expanded to 53.4%, supported by fixed operating costs that did not rise in tandem with revenue. Managing Director YT Choo said, “Our record performance in Q1 FY2025 highlights our strategic success in capitalising on the growing e-invoicing market.” The outlook remains upbeat as Phase 3 of Malaysia’s e-invoicing rollout—targeting businesses with annual revenues between RM500,000 and RM25 million—takes effect on 1 July 2025, followed by Phase 4 on Jan 1, 2026, which includes smaller businesses earning between RM150,000 and RM500,000 annually. title: Cautious But Steady On MBM Resources
body: MBM Resources Bhd’s (MBMR) first-quarter results for financial year 2025 came in line with expectations, prompting analysts from CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities), RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) and MIDF Amanah Investment Bank Bhd (MIDF Research) to maintain their NEUTRAL or HOLD ratings with only minor adjustments to target prices. CIMB Securities maintained a Hold rating with an unchanged target price of RM5.80, RHB Research retained a Neutral stance and a target price of RM5.55, while MIDF Amanah kept Neutral with a slightly reduced target price of RM5.75. All three research houses noted that MBMR offers an attractive dividend yield of around 7% for 2025 and 2026, making the stock appealing for yield-focused investors despite a softer earnings outlook. The group reported a core net profit of RM71.3 million for 1QFY25, largely matching the street and analysts’ full-year forecasts by contributing approximately 23% of expected annual earnings. Revenue fell 6.9% year on year to RM574 million, mainly due to lower sales volumes in the motor trading and assembly segment, which includes Perodua and Volvo vehicles. CIMB Securities highlighted that the decline was due to supply constraints affecting Perodua, as well as increased competition in the premium segment. This trend is consistent with the wider Malaysian automotive industry, where total industry volume dropped 7.3% year on year during the quarter. On a quarter-on-quarter basis, earnings dropped 27%, which analysts attributed to a high base from the previous quarter when Perodua delivered a record 97,700 units. Both RHB and MIDF noted that the shorter working quarter and planned production upgrades weighed on performance. The auto parts segment also faced headwinds, with revenue down 3.4% year on year but outperforming the industry’s total production volume, which fell more sharply by 16.2%. However, higher operating costs led to a decline in profitability for this segment. The outlook for 2025 remains cautious. Perodua’s total industry volume is expected to decline by about 3.7% year on year as it undertakes production upgrades, though sales volumes are forecast to remain relatively resilient with a slight 2.3% dip. Analysts continue to expect Perodua to be the primary earnings driver, contributing over 70% of MBMR’s profit before tax. Key models such as the Axia, Bezza and Myvi are expected to maintain strong demand, supported by the launch of two new models and Perodua’s planned introduction of its first electric vehicle in the second half of the year. MBMR is also focusing on long-term growth through refurbishment of outlets, expansion into new locations and the addition of new dealerships. The group is set to open its first 4S centre under the Jaecoo brand, providing sales, service, spare parts and body and paint services, which should strengthen its retail footprint. Despite softer earnings expected for 2025, analysts agree that MBMR remains fairly valued. RHB Research pointed out that the stock is trading slightly above its historical mean, while MIDF Research noted it is below the sector’s five-year average. CIMB Securities highlighted the group’s healthy net cash position of RM214 million as a buffer against economic uncertainties, including tariff tensions and potential fuel subsidy rationalisation later in the year. In summary, analysts maintain their cautious but steady outlook on MBM Resources. While earnings growth may slow due to supply constraints and industry challenges, the group’s dividend yield and Perodua’s resilient sales underpin a hold recommendation. Potential upside risks include successful new model launches and acquisition opportunities, while downside risks involve delays in product rollout, adverse currency movements and weakened consumer sentiment linked to subsidy cuts. title: Analysts Raise Concerns Over Maybank’s Mid-Term Prospects
body: MIDF Amanah Investment Bank Bhd (MIDF Research) has maintained a NEUTRAL rating on Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank), with an unchanged target price of RM10.20, citing that while the group delivered a decent set of results for the first quarter of financial year 2025 (1QFY25), its outlook remains mixed amid headwinds. CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) also reiterated a HOLD call, keeping its target price at RM9.40, noting that earnings came in below consensus expectations despite modest improvements quarter-on-quarter. Maybank reported a 1QFY25 core net profit of RM2.59 billion, marking a 4% year-on-year and 2% quarter-on-quarter increase, driven primarily by stronger non-interest income (NOII) and lower provisions. MIDF Research noted the performance was within both its and the street’s forecasts, with earnings making up 25% of full-year estimates. However, CIMB Securities highlighted that while earnings were slightly above its forecast by 1%, they missed consensus by 1.1%, flagging weaker-than-expected loan growth and pressure on net interest margins (NIM). NIM fell 2 basis points to 2.04% in the quarter, with management warning that future rate cuts could compress margins further by around 3 basis points per 25 basis point policy rate reduction. MIDF Research observed that while the bank is attempting to mitigate this through cheaper funding alternatives and portfolio rebalancing, the outlook remains cloudy. Additionally, CIMB Securities stated that Maybank’s loan growth was subdued, rising only 2.2% on an annualised basis compared to its 5–6% full-year target and flagged the potential for this target to be revised down due to tariff uncertainties. Asset quality remained relatively stable, though impaired loans rose 3.5% quarter-on-quarter, particularly in Malaysia and Singapore. Nonetheless, both research houses pointed to expected recoveries, notably from Sapura Energy’s restructuring, which may begin contributing by 3QFY25. MIDF Research also noted that provisioning appears under control, with overlays increased to RM1.8 billion. CIMB Securities estimated credit costs at 23 basis points—better than Maybank’s own 30 basis point full-year target. While management has maintained key performance indicators such as a return on equity (ROE) above 11.3%, it acknowledged ongoing pressure from elevated costs. Post-M25+ investments in technology are likely to keep the cost-to-income ratio above the historical ~45% range. MIDF Research added that Maybank’s Indonesian operations remain in transition, with a strategic pivot away from low-margin state-owned enterprise loans and a focus on reducing expensive funding. Despite headwinds, analysts agreed that Maybank’s dividend yield remains a highlight. MIDF Research estimates yields at 6.9% for FY25, among the most attractive in the sector, although it also cautioned that the current valuation—trading at 1.24 times FY25 forecast price-to-book value—is relatively expensive. In sum, while Maybank continues to deliver steady profits and attractive dividends, analysts are cautious on its medium-term prospects, citing risks from NIM compression, slower loan growth and continued cost pressures. title: Trump’s Tariff Threats Roil Asian Markets, EU Levies Delayed
body: Asian stocks displayed a mixed performance on Monday (May 26) after US President Donald Trump reignited trade tensions by threatening the European Union with substantial tariffs, before subsequently extending the deadline for their implementation. Markets had shown signs of stabilising following last week’s bond-fuelled selloff, but Trump escalated tensions by announcing 50 per cent levies against the EU starting June 1, citing that talks were “going nowhere”. Additionally, he threatened smartphone makers with 25 per cent tariffs unless their handsets were manufactured in the United States. On Friday, Wall Street’s three major indexes, along with most European markets, plunged into negative territory in reaction to these developments. However, Asia experienced a brief reprieve after Trump revealed on Sunday that he would delay the EU tariffs until 9 July following a “very nice call” with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen. He added that officials would “rapidly get together and see if we can work something out”. Following this announcement, Tokyo, Shanghai, and Seoul markets rose, while Hong Kong, Sydney, Singapore, Wellington, Taipei, Manila, and Jakarta saw declines. The US dollar remained under pressure after a drop on Friday. Analysts noted that the White House’s sudden and unpredictable policy moves continue to create uncertainty for investors. Concerns also linger over Trump’s proposed bill to extend tax cuts and reduce spending, which could potentially increase the national deficit by trillions of dollars, exerting upward pressure on Treasury yields and raising alarms about the US economy’s stability. Christ Weston of Pepperstone said, “The consensus view was always that the 50 per cent tariffs wouldn’t hold for long anyhow and would have most likely been reduced towards 20 per cent shortly after 1 June. But this action (Sunday) simply highlights that while tariffs will be helpful in keeping the US deficit in check, they are also a primary negotiation tool, where the initial gambit has been swiftly reduced.” Ray Attrill from National Australia Bank remarked, “In what is an otherwise quiet week on the scheduled global data and events calendar … trade discussion look set to dominate the market landscape this week.” Investors are also preparing for the release of the Federal Reserve’s policy meeting minutes this week, seeking insights on officials’ economic outlook amidst ongoing trade tensions. The Fed’s preferred inflation gauge, US personal consumption expenditures, is expected on Friday. Michael Hewson of MCH Market Insights commented, “The bank showed a shift in tone in its post-meeting statement with uncertainty about the economic outlook increasing further, stating that the risks of higher unemployment and inflation have both risen. This is a problem for the Fed’s dual mandate given that these two items could move in the same direction when any policy response may well hinder one over the other.” He added, “The biggest concern is likely to be the sharp drop in US consumer confidence levels in the last few months, however … this could quickly reverse if the US government begins to realise that its tendency to pick fights at every turn is doing more harm than good domestically.” In corporate news, shares of Samsung in Seoul rose over 1 per cent despite Trump’s tariff threats targeting smartphone manufacturers. Meanwhile, Nippon Steel in Tokyo surged as much as 7.4 per cent following Trump’s endorsement of a new “partnership” between the Japanese company and US Steel. This comes amid the ongoing saga of Nippon Steel’s US$14.9 billion takeover of US Steel, first announced in late 2023. Trump stated that US Steel’s headquarters would remain in Pittsburgh and claimed the partnership would create at least 70,000 jobs and contribute US$14 billion to the US economy. Details of the arrangement have yet to be published by either the White House or the companies involved. Following this news, US Steel’s shares soared 21 per cent in New York on Friday. body: KLCCP Stapled Group rose to the No. 2 spot among Bursa Malaysia’s top gainers on Monday, closing 1.95% higher at RM8.87, supported by strong investor interest despite analysts maintaining neutral calls. As of 4.05 pm, the stock gained 17 sen with a volume of 578,300 shares traded, touching an intraday high of RM8.90. Positive rental reversions in the retail segment and the recent acquisition of the remaining 40% stake in Suria KLCC helped lift earnings, with RHB noting a healthy 32% gearing and declining debt costs due to fixed-rate borrowings. MIDF Research highlighted that stronger retail contributions during the festive period offset weaker results in hotel and management services, which were affected by low Ramadan occupancy and ongoing ballroom upgrades at Mandarin Oriental Kuala Lumpur. Retail and office occupancy remained strong at 99% and 100% respectively, while hotel occupancy dipped to 54%. Analysts expect mid-single digit rental reversions and an uptick in office rates, with hotel earnings likely to rebound post-upgrades. title: HLIB Maintains Hold On FGV
body: Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) Research has maintained a HOLD call on FGV Holdings Bhd with an unchanged target price of RM1.26, following the group’s move to acquire full ownership of eight subsidiaries from Koperasi Permodalan Felda Malaysia Bhd (KPF) for RM229.8 million. The house noted that while the earnings uplift from the acquisitions is likely to be limited—especially after accounting for funding costs—the move enhances FGV’s operational control, improves decision-making agility and aligns better with its long-term strategic goals. HLIB has kept its earnings forecasts unchanged for now, pending further updates from FGV’s upcoming results briefing scheduled for 28 May 2025. The acquisitions involve remaining minority stakes in key units including a 16.67% stake in FGV Kernel Products for RM12.9 million, a 33.33% stake in FGV Refineries for RM17.9 million, and a 49% stake in FGV Transport Services for RM77.9 million, among others. The transaction will be funded via a mix of internal funds and bank borrowings, and is expected to be completed by the third quarter of 2025. HLIB stated that based on FY2024 earnings, the acquisitions are not expected to contribute significantly to bottom-line growth. However, the analyst added that the initiative may support long-term gains by streamlining management efficiency across the group’s downstream and support businesses. On the balance sheet, the impact is anticipated to be modest, with net gearing projected to rise slightly from 0.27 times as at 31 December 2024 to 0.31 times post-acquisition. At the current share price of RM1.28, FGV is trading at a slight premium to HLIB’s target price, with a projected capital downside of 1.3%. The expected total return is marginal at 0.3%, supported by a 1.6% dividend yield. Despite recent share price gains, HLIB believes the stock remains fairly valued, given muted earnings visibility and potential margin pressures in its core plantation segment. title: HeveaBoard Could Face Margin Erosion Due To FX Fluctuations
body: Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) has maintained its HOLD call on HeveaBoard, with analyst Jack Heng Shao Jun adjusting the target price downward to RM0.22 from RM0.24, reflecting a more cautious outlook amid disappointing first-quarter results. The latest earnings revealed a core net loss of RM2.3 million for 1QFY25, significantly missing the forecasted core profit of RM1.6 million due to weaker-than-expected revenue performance. Revenue for the quarter declined 10.0% quarter-on-quarter, affected across all business segments. Particleboard sales fell sharply by 29.5%, attributed mainly to an acute shortage of logs during the rainy season. Ready-to-assemble furniture sales slipped 1.4%, while fungi cultivation dropped 1.9%. Despite a modest 3.1% rise in gross profit, supported by a 10.5% reduction in cost of sales, the core loss widened due to lower other income. Year-on-year, revenue dropped 10.6%, weighed by a 28.4% fall in particleboard and a 3.1% decline in ready-to-assemble furniture sales, partially offset by a 6.6% increase in fungi cultivation. The revenue decline was further compounded by a weaker average USD/MYR exchange rate and intensified competition pushing prices lower. HLIB’s analysis highlighted the company’s vulnerability to foreign exchange fluctuations, with over 90% of revenue denominated in US dollars but nearly 90% of costs incurred in ringgit. The lack of natural hedging exposes HeveaBoard to earnings pressure from a weakening US dollar. Additionally, despite a year-to-date 15% drop in crude oil prices, which might reduce resin input costs, this benefit is likely offset by higher labour costs following the minimum wage hike implemented in February. Looking ahead, management expects selling prices to remain stable, but HLIB cautions that profit margins may continue to be squeezed by intense competition and currency headwinds. The persistent US-China trade tensions add further uncertainty, as any deterioration could revive dumping concerns and disrupt order visibility. In response to the disappointing results, HLIB has revised down its profit forecasts to RM0.1 million for FY25 and RM0.6 million for FY26, while introducing estimates for FY27. The target price adjustment reflects a lower price-to-book multiple of 0.30 times on FY25 book value per share of RM0.72, down from the previous 0.35 times, signalling a more conservative valuation. title: Cloudy Oil Sector Casts Shadow On Hibiscus’ Outlook
body: Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) has maintained its HOLD recommendation on Hibiscus Petroleum Bhd with a revised target price of RM1.53, down from RM1.61 previously. The investment bank highlights a cautious outlook given the current external headwinds affecting the oil and gas sector, despite Hibiscus’s undemanding valuation at 4.3 times its forecast earnings for FY26 and a dividend yield of 4.1%. HLIB expects limited downside risk but remains concerned over softer oil prices and geopolitical uncertainties that could weigh on demand. Hibiscus Petroleum reported core earnings of RM51.3 million for the third quarter of FY25, marking a 36% decline quarter-on-quarter and a 57% fall year-on-year. This brought the nine-month core net profit to RM173.3 million, down 55% compared to the same period last year. The results were broadly in line with HLIB’s forecast but fell short of consensus estimates. The weaker earnings were primarily driven by a 33% drop in EBITDA from the PM3 production sharing contract area (CAA), where there were no crude oil sales during the quarter and lower gas volumes sold. Notably, the quarter’s earnings were impacted by a one-off deferred tax liability of RM167.3 million related to the extension of the exploration production licence by two years. On a quarter-on-quarter basis, Hibiscus experienced operational challenges, including reduced output from key assets due to maintenance and technical issues. The North Sabah field, for instance, faced compressor unavailability from June to October 2024, while the South Furious field underwent an eight-day shutdown due to delayed drilling. The UK operations slipped into losses in 1QFY25 following a 38-day turnaround and technical problems with gas compression and oil contamination. Year-on-year, the decline in core profit is further attributed to lower average Brent crude oil prices, which fell to around US$75 per barrel from US$82 per barrel in 1QFY24. Lower revenue across all production areas coupled with increased operating expenses per barrel due to the operational hiccups also pressured earnings. Despite this, Hibiscus managed to expand its EBITDA margin at PM3 by 300 basis points, helped by a reduction in net operating expenditure per barrel. Looking ahead, Hibiscus has guided its offtake volumes to 2.7 million barrels of oil equivalent (boe) for the fourth quarter of FY25 and 2.2 million boe for the first quarter of FY26, slightly higher than the 2.1 million boe recorded in 3QFY25. However, HLIB notes that the potential uplift in volumes may be offset by expected lower average oil prices in the second quarter of calendar year 2025, a stronger ringgit against the US dollar, and more scheduled maintenance activities. HLIB remains cautious about the outlook given the fluid macroeconomic environment. Demand-side uncertainties following slower global economic growth and an aggressive production increase planned by OPEC+ are expected to keep oil prices under pressure in the near term. The bank also points out that Hibiscus’s recent production sharing contract extension for PM3 until 2047 has yet to be fully incorporated into valuation models pending further clarity, which could be accretive to the company’s net present value if included. title: Analysts Flag Allianz’s Life Insurance Business Decline
body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has maintained its NEUTRAL call on Allianz Malaysia Bhd with an unchanged target price of RM19.60, citing signs of creeping challenges in the life insurance segment despite a resilient first-quarter performance for financial year 2025. The house reported Allianz Malaysia’s net profit rose 12% year-on-year to RM211.7 million, supported by stronger underwriting performance across both its general and life insurance arms. The result accounted for 28% of RHB Research’s and 27% of consensus full-year estimates, aligning with expectations. However, the research house cautioned that earnings growth may face headwinds moving forward due to regulatory pressures and a volatile investment environment. Allianz General Insurance Company (AGIC) continued to perform steadily, posting a 21% year-on-year increase in profit before tax to RM160 million. This was driven by a 14% growth in insurance revenue, primarily from the motor and commercial segments, alongside improved underwriting margins and disciplined expense management. RHB Research noted that AGIC’s underwriting margin improved by 1 percentage point year-on-year to 15%, while investment returns contributed RM41 million during the quarter. On the life insurance front, Allianz Life Insurance Malaysia (ALIM) saw a 4% year-on-year increase in profit before tax to RM127 million, supported by improved insurance revenue and margin gains. However, quarter-on-quarter performance declined by 10% as net investment income fell sharply due to marked-to-market losses, likely on domestic equity holdings, amid heightened market volatility. RHB Research warned that continued medical inflation and regulatory developments could dampen sentiment and growth prospects in the life segment. The research house also flagged a 15% year-on-year decline in ALIM’s new business value, though this was partially offset by a 5% quarter-on-quarter increase. The contractual service margin remained flat sequentially, which RHB Research attributed to downward adjustments reflecting weaker investment performance assumptions. Allianz declared a second interim dividend of 63 sen for FY24, which RHB Research believes is likely to be the final payout for the year. This fell short of its earlier forecast of 86 sen, due to a lower-than-expected full-year payout ratio of 21%, compared to the projected 26%. RHB Research made no changes to its earnings forecasts and retained its ESG score for Allianz Malaysia at 3.3 out of 4, with the target price continuing to include a 6% ESG premium. The group is scheduled to hold its post-results briefing on 3 June. title: Wall Street Tumbles As Trump Revives Trade War Rhetoric
body: US stocks ended the week sharply lower on May 23 as President Donald Trump’s renewed threats of tariffs reignited fears of a global trade war, overshadowing otherwise positive signals in the bond market. Markets slid throughout the trading session after Trump floated the possibility of slapping a 25% tariff on Apple and other smartphone manufacturers whose devices are not made in the US. He also escalated tensions with Europe, warning of a potential 50% tariff on European Union imports, citing stagnation in trade negotiations. The selloff hit all major US indices. The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed down 0.6% at 41,603.07. The S&P 500 lost 0.7% to finish at 5,802.82, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite sank 1% to 18,737.21, dragged lower by tech stocks that are particularly vulnerable to tariff risks. Apple shares tumbled 3% following Trump’s comments, leading declines among mega-cap technology names. The company, which assembles a significant portion of its products overseas, could face a major disruption if such tariffs are enacted. The president’s sudden shift back to a combative trade stance comes after a week dominated by heated debate over his expansive tax cut proposal, which narrowly passed the House of Representatives on May 22. The bill, which could add to the federal deficit, now moves to the Senate for consideration. Earlier in the week, concerns over the fiscal implications of the tax plan had pushed US Treasury yields higher. But on May 23, yields fell back, signalling renewed investor appetite for government debt and providing a modest offset to the gloom in equities. Still, the downturn on May 23 illustrates how fragile market sentiment remains in the face of unpredictable policy signals from Washington. As markets brace for further developments, investors are keeping a close eye on both the trajectory of trade talks and the fate of Trump’s tax bill in the Senate — two critical factors that could shape the next chapter in the market’s 2025 story. body: Gold prices experienced a significant uptick this past week as escalating trade tensions and global economic uncertainties prompted investors to seek refuge in the precious metal. title: Wall Street Ends Flat As Tax Bill Passes, Yields Retreat From Highs
body: US stocks closed largely unchanged on Thursday, recovering from earlier losses as Treasury yields eased following the House of Representatives’ approval of President Donald Trump’s tax and spending bill. The S&P 500 slipped 4.89 points or 0.08% to close at 5,839.72, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average edged down 11.37 points or 0.03% to 41,849.07. The Nasdaq Composite, however, gained 45.56 points or 0.27% to end at 18,923.23, supported by gains in megacap tech names. Earlier concerns about the ballooning US deficit had pushed Treasury yields higher, weighing on equities. But Thursday saw some relief, with the 10-year US Treasury yield falling 5.4 basis points to 4.543% after touching its highest since February. The House’s narrow approval of Trump’s tax and spending legislation—which includes an extension of 2017 tax cuts and spending increases—delivered a win for the administration. However, the bill is projected to swell the US$36.2 trillion federal debt by another US$3.8 trillion over the next decade, according to the Congressional Budget Office. “There’s still an overhang in the market around tariffs and rates,” said George Young, partner and portfolio manager at Villere & Co. “Today, the tax bill moved, but we’re still navigating big-picture risks.” On Wall Street, Nvidia, Amazon, and Tesla posted gains, while Alphabet rose to its highest level in nearly three months. Snowflake surged after raising its fiscal 2026 product revenue outlook. On the downside, Analog Devices declined despite exceeding earnings expectations. Green energy stocks such as First Solar fell sharply, amid worries that Trump’s tax bill will roll back several clean energy subsidies. title: Ringgit Strengthens Amid Softer US Dollar And Mixed US Economic Data
body: The ringgit opened stronger against the US dollar on Friday, buoyed by a weaker US Dollar Index (DXY) and a mixed bag of US economic indicators, according to analysts. At 8 am, the local unit rose to 4.2575/2860 against the greenback, improving from Thursday’s close of 4.2705/2765. It also made gains across the board against both major and regional currencies. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the DXY stayed below the 100-point mark, reflecting tempered market sentiment on the dollar. He noted that although the US initial jobless claims were slightly lower than expected at 227,000 (versus a consensus forecast of 230,000), the number of continuing claims rose to 1.90 million from 1.87 million. “This suggests that the labour market is still resilient,” he told local media. Meanwhile, the US manufacturing sector posted positive momentum, with the Purchasing Managers Index (PMI) climbing to 52.3 points in May from 50.2 in April. “A significant rise in new orders was the main driver,” he added. However, other components such as employment were muted, and businesses were increasing inventories in anticipation of higher tariffs and prices. Mohd Afzanizam also pointed to political developments in the US, highlighting the passage of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act by the House of Representatives. The bill extends the 2017 tax cuts, introduces new deductions for tips, and raises the cap on state and local taxes. “Budget deficits are likely to balloon from the current 6.1% of gross domestic product (GDP). This will impact the government’s debt burden, which already stands at 100% of GDP,” he said. He added that a weaker US dollar in this context bodes well for emerging market currencies, including the ringgit. At the same time, the ringgit recorded broad-based gains. It appreciated to 2.9591/9791 against the Japanese yen (from 2.9768/9812), 5.7131/7514 versus the British pound (from 5.7212/7292), and 4.8029/8350 against the euro (from 4.8218/8286). Regionally, it strengthened to 3.2943/3166 against the Singapore dollar (from 3.3061/3110), and to 12.9498/13.0484 against the Thai baht (from 13.0000/0254). The local note also rose to 260.7/262.6 against the Indonesian rupiah (from 261.5/262.0), and 7.65/7.71 vis-a-vis the Philippine peso (from 7.68/7.69). title: MIDF Remains Optimistic On Cahya Mata Sarawak
body: MIDF Amanah Investment Bank Bhd (MIDF Research) has maintained a BUY recommendation on Cahya Mata Sarawak Bhd (CMSB) and raised its target price to RM1.33 from RM1.11, citing steady performance and long-term growth potential despite near-term challenges. The new valuation pegs FY26 forecast earnings per share of 15.7 sen to a price-to-earnings ratio of 8.5 times, aligned with its two-year average. The research house noted that CMSB’s 1QFY25 results were within expectations, with core profit after tax and minority interest (PATAMI) rising 68.9% year-on-year to RM32.1 million. This came despite a revenue contraction of 11.3% to RM246.1 million and a 53.1% drop in profit before tax (PBT) to RM26.9 million, primarily due to slow activity across divisions, particularly in infrastructure and oiltools. Associate and joint venture contributions also declined sharply by 41.5%. CMSB’s cement division recorded largely flat revenue at RM143.2 million but a strong 37.2% year-on-year increase in PBT to RM36.8 million. This was attributed to better cost efficiency following the depreciation of the US dollar against the ringgit, which is expected to ease input costs moving forward. MIDF Research believes the company is well-positioned to benefit from the rollout of major infrastructure and construction projects in Sarawak, especially as the state’s sole cement producer. The group’s oiltools segment faced headwinds, with revenue plunging 44.5% to RM43.3 million and PBT falling more than threefold to RM4.2 million due to reduced rig activities. In contrast, the road maintenance division posted robust gains, with revenue surging 57.2% to RM42.6 million and PBT climbing 31.6% to RM7 million, driven by higher job orders and work completions. However, property development fell into the red with a loss before tax (LBT) of RM1.26 million, in contrast to the previous year’s gains from a land sale. The phosphate division remains a drag, recording an LBT of RM31 million in 1QFY25, a 61.2% increase in losses year-on-year due to unrealised foreign exchange and investment fair value losses. The division has yet to generate revenue as it awaits commercialisation, targeted for the fourth quarter of FY25. The ongoing arbitration with Sesco Bhd over electricity supply termination continues to delay phosphate sales, but management remains optimistic about a resolution in the coming months. With all four furnaces at the Samalaju plant now operational and producing commercially viable products, CMSB expects to begin exports to Japan, Korea and Russia once the arbitration concludes. MIDF Research maintained its confidence in CMSB’s prospects, underscoring its strategic role in Sarawak’s infrastructure landscape and upcoming earnings catalysts including Clinker Line 2 and phosphate plant commercialisation. title: CelcomDigi Slides 0.26% To RM3.91 Despite 11–13% EPS Growth Outlook
body: CelcomDigi Bhd’s share price dipped marginally by 0.26% to RM3.91 as of 4.11pm today, despite continued bullish calls from analysts citing the group’s resilient earnings and integration progress. Trading volume stood at 21.6 million shares, with the stock slipping one sen from the previous close of RM3.92. It opened slightly higher at RM3.93 and hit an intraday high of RM3.96 before easing to a low of RM3.90. RHB Research and CIMB Securities both reiterated their ‘Buy’ ratings, with CIMB maintaining a target price of RM4.10. The stock is currently trading at about 4.6% below that target, reflecting investor caution amid integration costs and a higher effective tax rate. For the first quarter ended March 2025 (1Q25), CelcomDigi posted core pre-tax profits in line with expectations, although consumer service revenue fell 1.7% quarter-on-quarter to RM2.37 billion. Postpaid growth remained steady, rising 0.3% to RM1.07 billion, while prepaid revenue declined 2.9% due to seasonal ARPU softness. The telco’s mobile revenue rose 3.8%, and its solutions segment surged 13.8%. However, the enterprise segment dragged overall performance with an 8.1% revenue drop due to one-off waivers. Home and fibre revenue edged down to RM55 million but benefited from a 9% jump in subscribers. Earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) declined 9.2%, mainly due to higher 5G wholesale fees of RM55 million and RM21 million in integration expenses, partially offset by RM20 million in synergy savings. The effective tax rate rose to 29.5% due to non-deductible costs and revised provisions. Despite these pressures, network integration progress reached 78%, keeping CelcomDigi on track to complete its modernisation by the second half of 2025. Analysts project FY25–27 core earnings per share (EPS) to grow 11–13% annually, driven by merger synergies. Dividend yields are forecast between 4.1% and 5.0% over the next three years, while its FY25 enterprise value to operating free cash flow ratio of 12.8 times is trading at a 15% discount to its five-year average, enhancing its investment appeal. title: CelcomDigi Remains Attractive Among Peers, Analysts
body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) and CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) have both maintained their BUY calls on CelcomDigi Bhd, with CIMB retaining its discounted cash flow-based target price of RM4.10, citing sustained core profitability despite a high effective tax rate and ongoing integration costs. In its first quarter ended March 2025 (1Q25), CelcomDigi reported a core profit before tax in line with expectations, even though total consumer service revenue slipped 1.7% quarter-on-quarter to RM2.37 billion. Postpaid revenue grew marginally by 0.3% to RM1.07 billion, supported by a steady increase in subscriber numbers and a stable average revenue per user (ARPU). Prepaid revenue, however, declined 2.9% due to seasonally weaker ARPU, although subscriber growth showed signs of recovery, rising 0.9% for the second consecutive quarter. CIMB Securities highlighted that mobile and solutions segments showed underlying strength, with mobile revenue up 3.8% quarter-on-quarter and solutions revenue climbing 13.8%. Home and fibre revenue declined slightly to RM55 million, impacted by bundle rebates, but subscriber base saw a healthy 9% quarter-on-quarter increase. Meanwhile, the enterprise segment saw revenue fall 8.1%, dragged by one-off renewal waivers. Despite these revenue fluctuations, normalised EBIT fell 9.2% from the previous quarter due to softer service revenue and higher costs related to 5G wholesale fees, which rose to RM55 million from approximately RM40 million in 4Q24. Integration expenses amounted to RM21 million in the quarter, balanced by RM20 million in synergy savings. The effective tax rate surged to 29.5% as certain costs were non-deductible and past-year tax provisions were revised upward. Still, CIMB Securities remains confident in CelcomDigi’s forward trajectory. By the end of the first quarter, the telco had completed 78% of its network integration and modernisation efforts, keeping it on schedule for full completion by the second half of the year. The firm reaffirmed its full-year guidance, which includes low single-digit revenue growth and mid-single-digit EBIT growth, with capital expenditure expected to remain between 14–16% of sales. CelcomDigi’s FY25–27 core EPS is projected to grow between 11–13% annually, underpinned by merger-related cost synergies. CIMB Securities noted that the company’s FY25 forecast enterprise value to operating free cash flow ratio of 12.8 times is currently trading at a 15% discount to its five-year average, positioning the stock attractively. Dividend yields are forecast between 4.1% and 5.0% over the next three years. title: Asian Markets Steady As Dollar And Treasuries Rebound
body: Asian equity futures edged higher on Friday as a rebound in US Treasuries and the dollar helped calm fiscal worries that had rattled markets earlier in the week. Contracts for Japanese and Australian shares rose, while Chinese benchmarks held steady. Meanwhile, US equity-index futures advanced during early Asian hours after the Nasdaq 100 posted a 0.2% gain, driven by outperformance in big tech. The S&P 500 ended Thursday slightly lower, marking its third consecutive daily decline. Thursday’s rally in Treasuries saw yields ease across the curve, with the 10-year yield falling seven basis points to 4.53%, and the 30-year yield slipping five basis points. The Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index climbed 0.2%. “Market volatility has resurfaced amid renewed uncertainty surrounding trade policy and the fiscal outlook,” said Mark Haefele of UBS Global Wealth Management. Selling in Treasuries earlier in the week was triggered by concerns over the US’s rising debt burden, which were further fuelled by Moody’s Ratings downgrading the country’s sovereign credit. Investors are worried that President Donald Trump’s signature tax bill — recently passed by the House — could exacerbate the budget deficit. Thierry Wizman of Macquarie warned, “Even if the inability to reduce the deficit in the US doesn’t lead to default, a large deficit still implies greater bond supply, and perhaps eventual inflation as the debt is monetised to avoid default.” The rebound in Treasuries was also supported by improved US economic readings. Business activity and output expectations climbed as trade anxieties eased, despite ongoing price pressures. Initial jobless claims dropped to the lowest in four weeks, while existing home sales unexpectedly declined. “The ‘hard’ economic data still do not indicate a US economy in distress,” said Don Rissmiller of Strategas. He added that tariff-related activity may have been front-loaded, and political negotiations around the budget could pressure rate-sensitive sectors as summer approaches. title: Asia Markets Cautiously Higher Amid US Debt Jitters And Tax Bill Progress
body: Asian shares made modest gains on May 23 as investors weighed signs of US fiscal strain against optimism surrounding the passage of US President Donald Trump’s controversial tax bill through the House of Representatives. Despite concerns over ballooning US debt, Asia-Pacific equities stabilised, buoyed by bargain-hunting in beaten-down US Treasuries and hopes of eventual policy clarity. The MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan edged up 0.1%, remaining down 0.4% for the week, ending a five-week winning streak. Japan’s Nikkei led regional gains, climbing 1% after data showed core inflation rose at its fastest annual pace in over two years, raising hopes that domestic demand could finally be firming. Meanwhile, Chinese blue chips and the Hang Seng in Hong Kong were little changed, reflecting investor caution amid broader global volatility. The tentative optimism in Asia followed a muted Wall Street session. While initial enthusiasm was sparked by strong US Purchasing Managers Index (PMI) data for May, which suggested accelerating business activity, equities lost steam by the close. Nasdaq and S&P 500 futures remained flat in early Asian trading, underscoring uncertainty over the longer-term impact of the US tax overhaul. Meanwhile, the yield on 30-year US Treasuries fell another basis point to 5.037% on May 23, retreating from a 19-month peak of 5.161%. In Japan, yields on 30-year government bonds hovered near record highs at 3.175%, surging 23 basis points this week. The spike is now under close scrutiny from the Bank of Japan, raising speculation of possible intervention. On the other hand, currency markets reflected the global unease. The US dollar remained under pressure, down 1.2% for the week against a basket of major peers. The euro gained 0.2% to US$1.1302, poised for its first weekly advance in over a month. Digital assets continued their bullish streak, with Bitcoin gaining 7% this week to trade at US$111,524, just shy of May 22’s all-time high of US$111,965. Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller added to market uncertainty by signalling a potential rate cut later this year, but emphasised that the trajectory depends on how the administration’s trade and fiscal policies evolve. Oil prices extended losses for a fourth straight session, weighed down by prospects of increased output from OPEC+ nations. US crude fell 0.7% to US$60.76 a barrel, down 2.7% for the week. Brent slipped 0.6% to US$64.03. Gold prices held steady at US$3,292 per oz but were on track for a weekly gain of 2.8%, reflecting continued demand for safe-haven assets amid macroeconomic uncertainty. Moving forward, with US fiscal policy now in sharper focus and bond markets flashing warning signals, investors in Asia are proceeding with caution.
