body: US stock markets are poised for a weaker open on Wednesday, as fragile investor sentiment continues to be tested by persistent fiscal worries, geopolitical tensions, and a lack of progress on trade negotiations. US stock futures pointed to a lower start on Wall Street, dragged down by lingering concerns over the country’s ballooning debt and limited traction in trade talks with key allies and adversaries. The mood has remained cautious following Moody’s recent downgrade of the US credit outlook, which reignited worries over Washington’s US$36 trillion debt burden. Compounding these concerns, US President Donald Trump’s push for new tax cuts—estimated to worsen the deficit by up to US$5 trillion—has rattled investors further, raising questions about the country’s long-term fiscal sustainability. Despite a rise in US Treasury yields, with the 30-year bond touching 5% during Asian hours, the US dollar remained under pressure as investors sought refuge in safer currencies. The Japanese yen and Swiss franc both strengthened to two-week highs, while the euro and British pound also gained ground. The pound, in particular, hit a three-week high at US$1.3443 after UK inflation jumped to 3.5% in April. “People are looking at the idea of moving capital out of the US. It’s not a mass exodus, but investors are revisiting opportunities in other markets,” said Chris Weston, head of research at Pepperstone. That shift was reflected in Asia, where stocks climbed, buoyed by renewed optimism in regional markets. MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan hit a seven-month high, rising 1%. Adding to the unease in the US market, oil prices surged more than 1% after a CNN report indicated that Israel may be preparing a strike on Iranian nuclear facilities—raising concerns over supply disruptions in the Middle East. The geopolitical tension added to the growing list of risks already weighing on market confidence. Meanwhile, the Japanese bond market remained volatile, with yields on long-dated bonds hovering near record highs amid concerns about the country’s fiscal capacity to fund fresh stimulus. Gold also rose as a traditional safe haven, with spot prices climbing 0.39% to US$3,301 per ounce—the highest in more than a week—on the back of a weakening dollar and broader risk aversion. Markets are also closely monitoring the ongoing G7 finance ministers’ meeting in Canada for any policy signals that could help reinvigorate stalled trade discussions or address the dollar’s recent weakness. With US Federal Reserve officials signalling caution on interest rate adjustments and acknowledging the inflationary impact of tariffs, market participants are bracing for continued volatility ahead. title: Ringgit Firms Up As US Dollar Falters On Weak Economic Data
body: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar on Thursday, buoyed by a weakening greenback following softer United States economic data and lingering concerns over the country’s fiscal outlook. At 8am, the local note stood at RM4.2590/2895 against the greenback, strengthening from Wednesday’s close of RM4.2685/2735. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid attributed the ringgit’s gains to a persistently weak US dollar environment, exacerbated by Moody’s downgrade of the US sovereign rating last week. “The US Dollar Index (DXY) continues to slip, currently at 99.605 points, even as US Treasury yields rose — five and 12 basis points to 4.02% and 4.60% respectively,” he said, adding that the yield on the 20-year Treasury bond spiked to 5.10% from 4.81% in the previous auction. Afzanizam also noted remarks from former US Treasury Secretary Steve Mnuchin, who voiced concern over rising budget deficits and called for government spending cuts amid plans by the Trump administration to extend the 2017 tax cuts and reform key areas such as Medicaid and energy subsidies. The ringgit also strengthened against a basket of major and regional currencies at the opening. It rose against the euro to RM4.8267/8613 (from RM4.8379/8436), appreciated against the British pound to RM5.7160/7569 (from RM5.7241/7308), and edged up against the Singapore dollar to RM3.3033/3278 (from RM3.3071/3115). It also gained against the Indonesian rupiah at 259.6/261.7 (from 260.2/260.7) and improved against the Philippine peso at 7.65/7.71 (from 7.67/7.68), though it eased slightly against the Japanese yen to 2.9648/9863 and the Thai baht to 13.0217/1262. title: Bitcoin Surges Past US$110,000 Amid Renewed Optimism And Growing Institutional Demand
body: Bitcoin shattered the US$110,000 barrier for the first time in history on May 22, signalling a fresh wave of enthusiasm among investors and traders for the flagship cryptocurrency. Early Asian trading saw Bitcoin climb as much as 2.2%, reaching a high of US$110,707 before trimming some gains. This milestone reflects growing bullish sentiment driven by several key factors. Central to the surge is the recent advancement of a stablecoin bill in the US Senate, which has sparked hopes for clearer regulatory frameworks around digital assets. Market participants are increasingly confident that greater oversight will create a safer environment for crypto operators, encouraging more widespread adoption. Adding fuel to the rally is the persistent buying from institutional heavyweights, notably Michael Saylor’s Strategy company, which has amassed over US$50 billion in Bitcoin. This trend is echoed by a rising number of digital asset hoarders, including a wave of small-cap companies and crypto-focused public firms financing their purchases through convertible bonds, preferred stocks and other innovative financial instruments. Bitcoin’s latest record-breaking rally coincides with an unusual event: US President Donald Trump is set to meet with the largest holders of his own memecoin at a private dinner at his golf club near Washington. The gathering has attracted scrutiny from ethics experts and critics who warn of potential conflicts of interest stemming from the financial transactions benefitting the president. As Bitcoin rides this wave of institutional backing, regulatory progress and market enthusiasm, investors will be watching closely to see whether the cryptocurrency can maintain its momentum and scale even greater heights in the weeks ahead. title: US Stock Futures Slip Ahead Of Fed Speeches, Market Eyes Nvidia Earnings And Debt Concerns
body: US stock futures edged lower on Tuesday as investors awaited remarks from several Federal Reserve officials to gauge how President Donald Trump’s renewed tariff policies might impact the economy heading into the second half of 2025. At least seven Fed officials, including St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem, are expected to deliver speeches throughout the day, amid growing scrutiny over the US government’s rising debt and the recent credit rating downgrade by Moody’s. As of 6.54 am ET, Dow E-minis were down 2 points, S&P 500 E-minis fell 15.5 points (-0.26%) and Nasdaq 100 E-minis dropped 79.75 points (-0.37%). Investor sentiment remained cautious following Moody’s decision to downgrade the US sovereign credit rating from Aaa to Aa1, citing the government’s US$36 trillion debt burden and rising interest costs. While yields on US Treasuries had surged on Monday, the 10-year Treasury yield retreated slightly on Tuesday, falling 1.4 basis points to 4.46%. Despite recent volatility, analysts at JP Morgan maintained their bullish outlook. “Yesterday’s price action does not alter the bullish hypothesis,” the firm said, adding that any weakness stemming from soft consumer earnings or economic data “should be bought” ahead of Nvidia’s upcoming results. Nvidia (NVDA.O) is set to report earnings on May 28, with investors closely watching for cues that could influence broader market sentiment. Amazon (AMZN.O) and Nvidia both slipped about 0.3% in early premarket trading, while most megacap and growth stocks also traded lower. However, some companies provided a lift. Home Depot (HD.N) rose 3% after beating Wall Street’s first-quarter sales estimates, and Amer Sports (AS.N) surged nearly 10% after raising its 2025 revenue forecast. The broader US stock market has posted solid gains so far this month. The S&P 500 is now over 17% higher than its April lows, when Trump’s aggressive tariff measures sparked global market jitters. A temporary US-China trade truce, along with moderating inflation data, has supported the recent rally, although the index remains 3% below its record highs. Investors are also monitoring a key vote in the House of Representatives this week on Trump’s sweeping tax-cut bill, a move expected to add further pressure to the already mounting federal deficit. title: SunCon Surges 5.5% As Analysts Raise Target Prices
body: Shares of Sunway Construction Group Bhd (SunCon) climbed 5.53% to RM5.15 in late afternoon trade, buoyed by bullish analyst sentiment following a stellar first quarter for FY2025. At 3.04 pm, the stock was up 27 sen from its last close of RM4.88, with 63.5 million shares exchanging hands. SunCon opened at RM5.00, hit a high of RM5.23, and dipped to a low of RM4.99 during the day. The rally comes after RHB Research, MIDF Research, and HLIB reaffirmed their BUY calls on the counter, citing stronger-than-expected earnings and robust growth prospects in the data centre (DC) space. RHB Research lifted its target price to RM6.22, indicating a 27% upside, while MIDF and HLIB raised theirs to RM5.43 and RM5.36 respectively. Analysts highlighted a sharp increase in SunCon’s core net profit, which more than doubled year-on-year to an estimated RM82 million, driven by rapid progress in DC projects. The JHB1X0 data centre in Johor, a flagship contract valued at RM3.9 billion, has hit 57% completion and contributed to strong quarterly billings of nearly RM950 million. Another boost came from the Stage 3 DC project worth RM393 million, slated for completion in early 2026. SunCon’s construction segment saw profit before tax jump 196% year-on-year in 1QFY25, with margins improving to 8.2%, up from 7% previously. This reflects efficient project execution, especially at the Yondr DC site in Sedenak Tech Park. Although its precast segment recorded a 50% drop in revenue due to delivery slowdowns, analysts remain positive on a recovery aligned with upcoming housing project launches, particularly from Singapore’s Housing and Development Board. The company’s order book stands at RM6.6 billion, supporting visibility through FY2028. Year-to-date, SunCon has secured RM2.2 billion in new jobs, while its tender pipeline amounts to RM15.9 billion, mainly in DC and infrastructure sectors. HLIB noted a robust quarter-on-quarter increase in net cash, from RM285 million to RM835 million, due to improved receivables collection. The group also declared an interim dividend of 5 sen per share, with analysts expecting stronger payouts ahead. Looking forward, analysts are optimistic that SunCon will achieve its RM5 billion new job target for FY25, fuelled by ongoing DC demand and public infrastructure tenders, including the Penang LRT and airport expansion. With its solid Q1 showing and deep project pipeline, SunCon is seen as well-positioned to capitalise on Malaysia’s growing data and infrastructure buildout. title: Ringgit Muscles Up, Dollar Wavers On Fiscal Fog
body: The ringgit opened stronger against the US dollar on Wednesday, buoyed by a weakening greenback as investors reacted to a softer United States economic outlook amid renewed tariff concerns. At 8am, the local note stood at 4.2790/2960 versus the greenback, improving from Tuesday’s close of 4.2950/3010. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the market was showing signs of caution due to ongoing tariff-related uncertainties that may put pressure on prices and overall economic growth in the US. “The US Dollar Index (DXY) was seen declining by 0.31% to 100.118 points while the US equity prices fell as it entered an overbought territory. “However, the US Treasury yields rose as the recent sovereign rating downgrade on the US government may stall plans for expansionary fiscal policy,” he told local media. Mohd Afzanizam added that sentiment remains guarded, with the US dollar-ringgit exchange rate expected to trade within the 4.28–4.29 range. “Additionally, Malaysia’s exports figure turns out to be better-than-expected in April at 16.4% versus 7.5% estimates among the consensus. “Therefore, this could explain why Bank Negara Malaysia may have refrained from resorting to an outright cut in the overnight policy rate last week as they would want to gather more information in order to prescribe monetary easing,” he said. At the opening, the ringgit also traded mostly higher against a basket of major and regional currencies. title: KKB’s Rosy Outlook As Proxy For East Malaysia Mega Projects
body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) maintains a BUY call on KKB Engineering Bhd with a revised target price of RM1.83, indicating a potential upside of 25% from the current price of RM1.46. The research house expects the group’s first-quarter FY25 core earnings to be between RM4 million and RM7 million, reflecting year-on-year growth of 15% to 102%, supported by improved job progress. The firm highlights KKB’s strong foothold in Sarawak and Sabah, positioning it well to capitalise on upcoming mega projects such as the new international airport and deep-sea port in Sarawak, as well as the Ulu Padas Hydroelectric project in Sabah. As of the end of 4Q24, KKB’s outstanding orderbook stood at approximately RM226 million, with no new job announcements so far in FY25. The tenderbook was valued at around RM254 million, with contract awards expected within the first half of 2025. RHB Research anticipates the tenderbook may have increased given KKB’s ongoing bids for contracts worth about RM500 million, with a success rate estimated between 30% and 40%, and project progress likely to accelerate in FY26. Further opportunities are identified in Sarawak’s ambitious plans to invest RM6 billion in a rural water supply initiative by 2030, which includes replacing approximately 2,740 kilometres of pipelines. KKB has previously secured over RM100 million in contracts under the Sarawak Water Supply Grid Programme between 2019 and 2020, reinforcing its strong local presence. The group’s involvement in projects such as the Borneo Convention Centre Kuching II, where it handled structural steelworks for the original centre in 2007, also underscores its capacity to undertake large-scale infrastructure works. RHB Research has revised down its earnings forecasts for FY25 to FY27 by 14%, 11%, and 1% respectively, reflecting a more cautious view on job wins in FY25, adjusting the target contract value from RM500 million to RM350 million. However, contract replenishment assumptions for FY26 and FY27 remain unchanged at RM600 million and RM500 million. The target price is based on a 17 times price-to-earnings ratio for FY26 earnings per share, with a 2% ESG premium applied, positioning KKB’s valuation near the five-year mean for the Bursa Malaysia Construction Index during the 2017 upcycle. This valuation is justified by expected benefits from Sarawak’s RM10.8 billion development expenditure planned for 2025, up from RM9 billion in 2024. RHB Research identifies potential rerating catalysts including faster-than-expected contract wins in the oil and gas fabrication sector, where KKB last secured a project in November 2023. Additionally, emerging water supply schemes in Sabah, possibly secured by Gamuda, represent further growth avenues for KKB. These developments position KKB Engineering as a key beneficiary of ongoing infrastructure and utility projects in East Malaysia. title: Inari Amertron Drops 6.4% Amid Earnings Concerns, Analyst Ratings Trimmed
body: Inari Amertron Bhd’s share price declined by 6.44% to RM1.89 as of 3.24 pm today, reflecting investor caution following weaker-than-expected third-quarter results and limited short-term growth prospects. The stock opened at RM2.00 before slipping to a low of RM1.89, with trading volume hitting 26.3 million shares. This marks a notable correction from its last closing price of RM2.02. MIDF Amanah Investment Bank Bhd (MIDF Research) has downgraded Inari to a NEUTRAL rating from Trading Sell, cutting its target price to RM2.13 from RM2.29. Similarly, Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) maintained its HOLD recommendation with a fair value of RM2.10. Both research houses cited concerns over earnings risk, softer semiconductor demand and the lack of immediate catalysts. Inari’s normalised net profit for 3QFY25 fell 11.5% year-on-year to RM57.9 million, while revenue slipped 11.3% to RM308.3 million. This was attributed to volume loading weakness across all business segments. A start-up loss of RM4.95 million from its China-based YSIC unit further dragged performance, though core margins remained at a stable 19%. For the nine-month period, cumulative earnings declined by 19% to RM243.1 million, while revenue dropped 8.8% to RM1.05 billion. MIDF noted that results were below expectations, accounting for just 69.8% of full-year forecasts, prompting it to revise FY25–FY27 earnings downwards by up to 10.2%. HLIB highlighted other headwinds, including RM4 million in unrealised forex losses and seasonally weaker demand. While a US customer’s budget smartphone rollout may offer some relief, the group’s near-term outlook remains tepid. Inari also declared a third interim dividend of 1.3 sen, down from 1.9 sen a year ago, bringing the total payout for the first three quarters to 4.3 sen, versus 6.3 sen in the previous corresponding period. Despite the pressure, both research firms acknowledged Inari’s robust balance sheet, supported by RM2 billion in cash reserves and long-term potential in RF and optoelectronics. However, they caution that tariff-related uncertainties and waning smartphone demand could weigh on the stock in the near term. title: AEON, A Solid Defensive Domestic Retail Play
body: AEON Co (M) Berhad (AEON MK) has received unanimous BUY ratings from major research houses, including RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research), MIDF Amanah Investment Bank Bhd (MIDF Research), CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) and Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB). All the houses maintaining target prices ranging from RM1.75 to RM1.82, implying upside potential of between 16% and 20.5% from its current price of around RM1.51. RHB Research highlights AEON’s strong first quarter (1Q25) performance, attributing the 18.4% year-on-year (YoY) growth in net profit to the early timing of Aidil Fitri, which pulled forward festive spending. The bank maintained their Buy call with a target price of RM1.75, citing robust growth prospects in AEON’s property management segment driven by expansion projects and asset enhancement. They also expect the retail segment to benefit from resilient consumer spending and margin expansion through cost-control measures. Despite anticipating softer quarters ahead due to the frontloading of festive sales, RHB Research views the current valuation as attractive amid global market volatility. MIDF Research concurs with a Buy rating and an unchanged target price of RM1.77. Analysts note AEON’s stellar kickstart to FY25 was powered by strong seasonal momentum from double festive periods—Chinese New Year and Hari Raya—and resilient growth in the property management services (PMS) segment. The PMS division’s operating margin expanded significantly due to higher occupancy rates and effective tenancy renewals, while the retail segment benefited from increased spending in food and apparel. MIDF Research also highlights AEON’s strategic initiatives, including private-label expansion and digital integration, which are expected to enhance customer loyalty and long-term growth. CIMB Securities expects a weaker 2Q and 3Q25, citing the absence of festive seasons and ongoing mall renovation works, which could reduce footfall. Nonetheless, they maintain their Buy call and a target price of RM1.75, forecasting 5.8% core net profit growth for FY25, supported by mall rejuvenation and strong property management performance. CIMB Securities underscores AEON’s relatively defensive earnings base and attractive dividend yields of 4.0–5.0% over FY25–27. HLIB maintains a Buy rating with a target price of RM1.82, noting a solid start to the year with 1Q25 revenue growing 7% YoY to RM1.2 billion and net profit surging 18% YoY to RM68.1 million. The bank attributes the growth to higher spending during double festive periods and improved occupancy in the PMS segment. The retail segment’s performance was further supported by disciplined cost control and a lower effective tax rate. Hong Leong is confident AEON will benefit from government initiatives such as EPF Account 3 withdrawals, civil servants’ pay hikes and the minimum wage increase. Across all research houses, AEON’s performance in 1Q25 is considered within expectations, supported by favourable festive timing and solid operational execution. While analysts acknowledge the likelihood of softer quarters ahead, the company’s ongoing expansion plans, strong occupancy rates and resilient consumer spending underpin positive medium-term prospects. AEON’s valuation remains undemanding relative to its historical average, with consensus seeing it as a defensive domestic retail play amid current macroeconomic uncertainties. title: US Stocks Steady Despite Moody’s Credit Rating Downgrade
body: US stocks ended mostly flat on Monday as investors digested Moody’s downgrade of the federal government’s sovereign credit rating due to its ballooning debt. Moody’s cut the US sovereign rating from “Aaa” to “Aa1” after markets closed on Friday, citing the government’s US$36 trillion in outstanding debt and interest obligations. Despite the downgrade, equities recovered from early losses, with the benchmark S&P 500 notching its sixth straight day of gains. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 137.33 points, or 0.32%, to 42,792.07. The S&P 500 gained 5.22 points, or 0.09%, to 5,963.60, while the Nasdaq Composite edged up 4.36 points, or 0.02%, to 19,215.46. Seven of the 11 S&P 500 sectors ended higher, led by healthcare, consumer staples, industrials, materials, and utilities. Energy and consumer discretionary shares were the biggest laggards. Among individual movers, TXNM Energy jumped 7% after announcing its US$11.5 billion acquisition by Blackstone’s infrastructure unit. Novavax surged 15% following US regulatory approval for its COVID-19 vaccine. Regeneron Pharmaceuticals rose 0.4% after confirming plans to acquire 23andMe for US$256 million via bankruptcy auction. Meanwhile, benchmark 10-year US Treasury yields rose by 1 basis point to 4.449%, amid concerns a newly advanced tax-cut bill could further strain the country’s fiscal position. Trading volume on US exchanges totalled 19.41 billion shares, above the 20-day average of 17.34 billion. title: Ringgit Softens As Traders Eye US Fed Signals
body: The ringgit opened marginally lower against the US dollar on Tuesday, with investors treading cautiously ahead of a possible interest rate cut by the United States Federal Reserve, according to an analyst. At 8 am, the local unit eased to 4.2900/3020 against the greenback compared with Monday’s close of 4.2870/2945. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid noted that New York Fed President John Williams and Atlanta Fed President Raphael Bostic have indicated that US policymakers remain in wait-and-see mode, pending further economic data. “The US Dollar Index (DXY) fell 0.66% to 100.426 points, as sentiment in the equities market improved, although several Fed officials remain reluctant to cut rates in the near term,” he told local media. Despite the softer ringgit against the greenback, the local note was mostly higher against a basket of major and regional currencies at the opening. It strengthened against the British pound to 5.7302/7462 from 5.7420/7521, appreciated versus the euro to 4.8181/8316 from 4.8344/8429, and rose against the Japanese yen to 2.9582/9667 from 2.9596/9650. The ringgit also advanced against the Singapore dollar to 3.3120/3218 from 3.3135/3195 and firmed versus the Thai baht to 12.9388/9864 from 12.9630/9924. However, it slipped slightly against the Indonesian rupiah to 261.0/261.9 from 260.8/261.4, and eased against the Philippine peso to 7.70/7.73 from 7.69/7.71. Dr Afzanizam added that the odds of a Fed rate cut in June remain below 10%, based on Fed Fund Rate futures, with US Treasury yields showing slight declines—two and three basis points lower on the two- and 10-year notes respectively, at 3.98% and 4.45%. “Nonetheless, we expect the ringgit to stay supported as market sentiment improves amid tariff negotiations between the US and various countries globally,” he said. title: Dollar Steadies After Moody’s Downgrade, Trump Tax Vote Looms
body: The US dollar steadied on Tuesday after a week-long slide, holding gains as markets awaited a key vote in Washington on President Donald Trump’s sweeping tax cut proposals. The greenback’s pause followed Monday’s broad sell-off, triggered by Moody’s surprise downgrade of the US sovereign credit rating on concerns over the country’s swelling fiscal deficit. Trump is expected to join congressional discussions on Tuesday to bolster support for the tax bill. Nonpartisan analysts estimate the bill could add between US$3 trillion and US$5 trillion to the US$36.2 trillion national debt. The vote comes at a time when investor sentiment remains fragile, shaped by fiscal risks and geopolitical headwinds. Chris Weston, head of research at Pepperstone, said the Moody’s downgrade was “symbolic” but reinforced existing fears. “It highlights what everyone already knew – that US deficits and interest expenses are only going one way, and that Treasury coupon issuance will increase in 2026,” he noted. Adding to the caution, Atlanta Federal Reserve President Raphael Bostic told CNBC on Monday that the Fed may only be able to deliver one more rate cut this year, potentially capped at 25 basis points, as inflation concerns grow amid higher import tariffs. The greenback inched up 0.1% to 144.99 yen after touching 144.66 on Monday, its lowest since 8 May. The dollar index also ticked up 0.1% after dropping 0.6% in the previous session, still down around 10.6% from its January peak—marking one of the sharpest three-month retreats on record. Meanwhile, the Australian dollar held firm at US$0.6449, retaining most of Monday’s 0.8% jump, ahead of the Reserve Bank of Australia’s widely anticipated 25 basis point rate cut later Tuesday. Sterling edged down 0.1% to US$1.3354, while the euro slipped 0.1% to US$1.1234. Sterling last traded at US$1.3359, marginally lower by 0.03% on the day. Investors are now balancing optimism over possible long-term synergies from US fiscal reform with growing discomfort over rising debt, political uncertainty, and potential shifts in Federal Reserve policy—all of which are weighing heavily on US assets. title: Ringgit Strengthens Against Greenback On US Credit Downgrade
body: The ringgit opened stronger against the US dollar today, lifted by a knee-jerk reaction to Moody’s Ratings downgrade of the US sovereign credit rating. At 8.03 am, the local currency appreciated to 4.2850/3140 against the greenback from 4.2900/2980 at last Friday’s close. Moody’s Ratings lowered the US credit rating by one notch to Aa1 from AAA last Friday, citing concerns over worsening fiscal deficits and mounting government debt. “However, the credit rating agency continued to acknowledge the special status of the US dollar as the global reserve currency,” said Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid. “On that note, the US Dollar Index (DXY) could fall from a knee-jerk reaction,” he told local media, adding that the ringgit and other emerging market currencies were expected to appreciate in response. Despite its gain against the US dollar, the ringgit traded mixed against a basket of major currencies. It strengthened against the euro to 4.7495/8269 from 4.8022/8112, but slipped against the British pound to 5.7020/7406 from 5.7018/7125, and edged down versus the Japanese yen to 2.9509/9711 from 2.9470/9527. Among ASEAN currencies, the ringgit traded mostly higher. It climbed against the Singapore dollar to 3.3010/3236 from 3.3041/3105, firmed up versus the Philippine peso to 7.70/7.75 from 7.71/7.73, and advanced against the Indonesian rupiah at 260.5/262.4 from 260.8/261.5. The ringgit, however, weakened slightly against the Thai baht to 12.9024/13.0026 from 12.9003/9318 previously. title: Gold Prices Dip 1.25% Amid Easing Trade Tensions And Stronger Dollar
body: Gold prices experienced their steepest weekly decline in six months during the trading week of May 12-16, 2025, as easing global trade tensions and a strengthening US dollar dampened investor demand for the safe-haven asset. After a robust 22% surge earlier this year, gold prices retreated by 1.25% to close at US$3,185 per oz. The pullback was influenced by US President Donald Trump’s reversal of planned punitive tariffs and a temporary easing of US-China trade tensions, which reduced investor anxiety. In Malaysia, gold prices mirrored the global trend. On May 8, 2025, the price of 24-carat gold stood at RM14,123.02 per oz, reflecting a slight decrease from the previous day’s rate. Analysts suggest that while the short-term outlook for gold may face headwinds due to reduced economic uncertainty and a stronger dollar, structural factors such as persistent global economic concerns and inflation may support gold prices in the long run. Technical analysis indicates that gold prices could fluctuate within the range of US$3,050 to US$3,250 per oz in the second quarter of 2025. Despite the recent dip, investors continue to monitor gold as a hedge against potential economic volatility. Billionaire investor David Einhorn remains optimistic about gold’s trajectory, citing eroding confidence in US fiscal and monetary policy as a key driver for its continued appeal. As markets navigate the evolving economic landscape, gold’s performance in the coming weeks will be closely watched by investors seeking stability amid uncertainty. title: Wall Street Futures Dip As Tariff Truce Optimism Fades, Eyes On Powell’s Speech
body: US stock index futures fell on Thursday as early-week optimism from the US-China tariff truce lost steam, while a Department of Justice (DoJ) probe into UnitedHealth dampened sentiment. As of 7.02 am ET, Dow E-minis were down 130 points (0.31%), S&P 500 E-minis fell 26 points (0.44%), and Nasdaq 100 E-minis dropped 125 points (0.58%), pointing to a weaker open. The pullback follows a volatile week in which major indices surged on news of a 90-day pause in US-China tariff tensions, briefly pushing the S&P 500 back into positive territory for the year. However, the momentum stalled as investors awaited new market catalysts. UnitedHealth Group shares plunged 5.9% in premarket trading after The Wall Street Journal reported a criminal investigation by the DoJ into alleged Medicare fraud. The company responded that it had not been notified of any federal criminal probe. Investors are now turning their attention to a speech by Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell, due later in the day, amid growing speculation that the central bank may hold interest rates steady due to mixed inflation signals and ongoing global trade uncertainty. Adding to the mix, a fresh wave of US economic data—covering April’s producer prices, retail sales, and jobless claims—is expected at 8.30 am ET. Earlier this week, consumer price data showed only a moderate rebound in inflation, reinforcing hopes for a dovish Fed. On the corporate front, Walmart gained 1.5% after posting better-than-expected Q1 US comparable sales, while Cisco Systems climbed 3.4% following an upbeat earnings forecast and the appointment of a new CFO. Foot Locker surged 82.4% after Dick’s Sporting Goods announced a US$2.4 billion buyout of the footwear retailer, marking one of the biggest retail deals of the year. Meanwhile, tech heavyweights Nvidia and Tesla slipped 1.3% and 2.4%, respectively, as profit-taking set in after earlier gains. Energy stocks were also under pressure, with Chevron and ExxonMobil falling over 1% each as oil prices tumbled more than 3%. title: Ringgit Rises Ahead Of Malaysia’s Q1 GDP Release
body: The ringgit opened stronger against the US dollar on Friday, continuing its positive trajectory as markets await the release of Malaysia’s first-quarter (1Q) 2025 gross domestic product (GDP) data. At 8am, the local currency stood at 4.2705/2920 against the greenback, strengthening from Thursday’s close of 4.2795/2870. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said investors are eyeing the GDP announcement closely, with advance estimates pointing to a 4.4% expansion. “The data will be a key factor in Bank Negara Malaysia’s (BNM) decision on whether to ease monetary policy, as well as the forecast for GDP growth this year,” he said. “As such, we expect ringgit to trade more cautiously today,” he told local media. At the opening, the ringgit traded mostly higher against a basket of major currencies. It appreciated against the British pound to 5.6819/7105 from 5.6862/6961 and rose against the euro to 4.7800/8040 from 4.7939/8023. However, it edged lower versus the Japanese yen to 2.9338/9490 from 2.9326/9379. Against its ASEAN peers, the ringgit was mixed. It climbed against the Singapore dollar to 3.2931/3102 from 3.2950/3010, and gained on the Philippine peso at 7.66/7.70 from 7.67/7.69. It also advanced on the Indonesian rupiah to 258.3/259.7 from 258.8/259.4 but slipped against the Thai baht to 12.8630/9367 from 12.8198/8488. Commenting on the broader currency landscape, Mohd Afzanizam highlighted a weaker US Dollar Index (DXY), which declined by 0.16% to 100.87 points. He also noted that the US Producer Price Index (PPI) moderated to 2.4% year-on-year in April, down from 3.4% in both February and March, signalling a cooling inflation trend. “This suggests that inflation in the US will continue to ease and create more room for the US Federal Reserve (Fed) to cut rates this year,” he said. However, he cautioned that recent remarks from Fed chair Jerome Powell may dampen expectations of imminent rate cuts. “Powell’s speech at the Thomas Laubach Research Conference in Washington hinted that the inflation trend is likely to be more erratic due to the supply shocks, which have become more frequent and potentially more persistent. “This could mean the Fed is not keen to ease its monetary policy stance in the near term, which would affect the ringgit,” he said. title: Dialog Shares Dip 5% Amid Margin Recovery Concerns, EPS Cut for FY25
body: Dialog Group Bhd’s shares fell 5.08% to RM1.68 as of 3.47pm on May 16, amid weaker-than-expected financial results and a downward revision of its FY25 earnings forecast by Kenanga Research. The company reported a core profit of RM291.9 million for the nine-month period ended FY25, falling short of both Kenanga’s and consensus expectations at 60% and 56% of full-year estimates respectively. The main drag was a slower-than-anticipated recovery in the Engineering, Procurement, Construction and Commissioning (EPCC) division margins, though the segment broke even in the latest quarter. Kenanga has revised its FY25 forecast earnings down by 10%, citing a less aggressive EPCC margin recovery (from -20% to -26%). However, FY26 estimates remain unchanged, with the research house expecting no repeat of prior cost overruns. Dialog declared a quarterly dividend of RM0.013, bringing the cumulative payout to RM0.037 per share. The stock saw a high of RM1.72 and low of RM1.65 during the trading day, with 15.26 million shares traded. Despite the sell-off, Kenanga has maintained its ‘Outperform’ rating and SoP-based target price of RM1.94, seeing medium-term upside potential. On a year-on-year basis, Dialog’s 9MFY25 revenue dropped 15% and core profit slipped 16%, largely due to lower contributions from the EPCC and upstream segments. Quarter-on-quarter, revenue also dipped 15%, but core profit surged, thanks to a 39% drop in operating expenses and stronger joint venture contributions. The outlook for tank terminal operations remains resilient, while the Phase 3 Pengerang expansion, including ChemOne’s proposed aromatics project, is still under discussion and not yet factored into earnings projections. title: US Stocks Rise On Tariff Truce And Inflation Ease
body: Wall Street’s main indexes are poised to open higher on Wednesday, buoyed by a strong start to the week. Soft inflation data and a US-China tariff truce have lifted sentiment, while President Donald Trump’s Gulf tour has raised hopes for further trade agreements. US stocks have been optimistic since the weekend when the US and China agreed to pause their tariff dispute, aiming to prevent a global economic slowdown. The US will temporarily reduce extra tariffs on Chinese imports to 30% from 145% for three months, while China will lower duties on US imports to 10% from 125% during the same period. Rick Gardner, chief investment officer at RGA Investments, noted that despite ongoing uncertainties, the easing of trade tensions has positively impacted markets. On Tuesday, the S&P 500 finally returned to positive territory for the year, a milestone not seen since late February, although it remains over 4% below its record peaks. Both the S&P 500 and Nasdaq have regained levels last seen before Trump’s April 2 tariff announcement. A 90-day pause for countries other than China, solid earnings reports, and a limited US-UK trade agreement have contributed to the recovery. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq closed higher on Tuesday after US consumer prices rebounded moderately in April, with headline inflation rising 0.2%, slightly below economists’ expectations. At least three US Federal Reserve officials, including Fed Governor Christopher Waller, are scheduled to speak, with Fed Chair Jerome Powell’s remarks on Thursday being a key focus. As of 08.29 am ET, Dow E-minis were up 80 points, or 0.19%, S&P 500 E-minis were up 16 points, or 0.27%, and Nasdaq 100 E-minis were up 79.25 points, or 0.37%. Most megacap and growth stocks rose, with Nvidia leading the charge with a 3% increase. Several US technology firms announced AI deals in the Middle East, and Trump secured US$600 billion in commitments to US companies from Saudi Arabia during his Gulf trip. However, American Eagle Outfitters dropped 12.7% after withdrawing its annual forecasts due to economic uncertainty. As earnings season concludes, Walmart’s results will be closely watched later in the week. title: Sunway REIT Gains 3.63%, Buoyed By Strong 1Q25 Results
body: Sunway Real Estate Investment Trust (Sunway REIT) rose 3.63% to close at RM2.00, up 7 sen, with 42.5 million shares traded as at 3.27 pm today. The stock opened at RM1.93, hit a high of RM2.03, and touched a low of RM1.93. The strong performance comes on the back of its first quarter FY2025 results, which were slightly above forecast and reflected a 20% year-on-year increase in core net profit, largely driven by a 23% rise in revenue. Maybank Investment Bank maintained a BUY call with a target price of RM2.13, citing lower-than-expected finance costs and robust retail segment growth as key contributors. Retail net property income (NPI) surged 34% YoY, supported by contributions from newly acquired assets — including S.163 Mall, six hypermarkets, and S.Kluang Mall — and record-high retail occupancy of 99%. The refurbished Oasis precinct at Sunway Pyramid Mall achieved full occupancy with doubling rents, further cementing the REIT’s retail strength. While the hospitality segment declined 16% YoY due to Ramadan, a recovery is expected in 2Q25. Office NPI was down 11% YoY, though tenant backfilling is in progress. Maybank IB remains optimistic on Sunway REIT’s outlook, supported by upcoming contributions from acquisitions, active asset enhancement initiatives (AEIs), and recovery in hospitality. The proposed disposal of the Sunway University and College campus and the planned acquisition of AEON Mall Seri Manjung are both expected to stabilise gearing at around 40% post-completion. title: Ringgit Softens Against US Dollar Amid Trade Deal Watch
body: The ringgit opened slightly lower against the US dollar as traders continued to monitor the potential trade deal between the US and China, alongside ongoing geopolitical concerns, said an economist. At 8.02 am, the local note slipped to 4.2880/3090 against the greenback from Wednesday’s close of 4.2840/2910. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid noted that while emerging currencies have begun to stabilise, the US Dollar Index (DXY) was gaining ground. “Market sentiments are fairly positive and stable as the standoff between the US and China looks like receding, paving the way for the trade deal at some point in the future,” he told Bernama. “Thus, we foresee dollar-ringgit lingering around its current level today,” he added. The ringgit was traded mixed against its ASEAN counterparts in early dealings. It strengthened versus the Singapore dollar to 3.2942/3110 from 3.3045/3104 and surged against the Thai baht to 12.8226/8989 from 12.8920/9208 previously. title: Ringgit Strengthens As US-China Trade Tensions Subside
body: The ringgit opened stronger against the US dollar on Wednesday, buoyed by easing trade tensions between the United States and China. The development has brought a wave of relief to financial markets, calming recession fears and reigniting risk appetite among investors. Today, the local currency strengthened to 4.3045/3245 compared to Tuesday’s close of 4.3185/3250. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid noted that the US consumer price index (CPI) for April rose 2.3% year-on-year, slightly below market expectations of 2.4%, while core CPI remained at 2.8%. “This cooling in inflation suggests that concerns over tariff-driven price increases may take a backseat for now,” he said. He also indicated that this could give the US Federal Reserve room to consider rate cuts, particularly with the Federal Open Market Committee scheduled to meet on June 17 – 18 to release its updated economic projections. Despite having depreciated by 2.8% against the US dollar since 5 May, the ringgit showed signs of resilience as investor fears over tariff shocks began to ease. With the US and China allowing concessions to advance trade negotiations, market participants have shifted into a more risk-on posture. On Tuesday, the ringgit briefly weakened to RM4.34 during morning trade but rebounded to RM4.32 by the afternoon. Against other major currencies, the ringgit showed mixed performance at the opening. It was slightly stronger versus the Japanese yen but weaker against the euro and British pound. However, the local currency gained ground against most ASEAN peers, including the Singapore dollar, Indonesian rupiah, Thai baht, and Philippine peso. title: Asian Markets Swing As China-US Trade Euphoria Fades
body: Asian stocks fluctuated Wednesday (May 14), with investors struggling to track a strong day on Wall Street as euphoria over the China-US trade detente petered out. But while the days of breathtaking volatility seen through April appear to be over for now, analysts warned that more work was needed for Washington to reach tariff deals with countries and instill a sense of stability. Data showing US inflation unexpectedly slowed last month provided some cheer, though observers pointed out that the real impact of Donald Trump’s “Liberation Day” tolls will not likely be felt until May’s readings. The US president on Tuesday played up a deal with Beijing.”We have the confines of a very, very strong deal with China. But the most exciting part of the deal … that’s the opening up of China to US business,” he told Fox News. His remarks were made aboard Air Force One as he headed off on his Gulf tour, with Saudi Arabia on Tuesday pledging US$600 billion worth of US investments in a range of sectors from defence to artificial intelligence. The agreements – including a huge chip deal for Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices – would boost US jobs, and the stock market is “gonna go a lot higher”, Trump said, citing an “explosion of investment and jobs”. The tech-rich Nasdaq rallied with the S&P 500, which broke back into positive territory for the year, helped slightly by the inflation data. But Asia struggled to extend the rally. Hong Kong, Seoul, Jakarta and Taipei rose more than one percent but Wellington and Manila were flat, while Tokyo, Shanghai, Sydney and Singapore fell. Oil, which had enjoyed a four-day rally on demand optimism and Trump’s warnings to Iran over a nuclear deal, also edged down. Analysts said that while the China deal was welcome, investors were now bracing for the next developments in the US president’s trade standoff with the world as countries look to strike deals with the White House to avert stiff tariffs.”Remember it’s an armistice not a peace treaty – and the tariffs are still at these levels worse than we had before,” Neil Wilson at Saxo Markets said. “Let’s be honest, the market knows this script by heart: Trump escalates. Markets tumble. Back-channels open. China blinks. A deal gets made. Risk rallies,” added Stephen Innes at SPI Asset Management. “The fog has lifted – for now. Whether this cycle brings more sustainable upside or just sets up the next tantrum remains to be seen,” he said. Still, the dialling down of tensions with China saw JPMorgan Chase predict the US economy would grow this year, reversing its earlier forecast for a contraction caused by the tariffs. Investors are also awaiting the release of earnings from Chinese tech titans Alibaba and Tencent, which could provide an idea about how the market heavyweights are coping with the trade upheaval and uncertainty in the world’s number two economy. title: Westports Shares Climb 2.71% Despite Lowered Volume Forecast
body: Westports Holdings Bhd emerged among Bursa Malaysia’s active gainers today, with its share price rising 2.71% to RM4.55 as of 3.32 pm. title: Wall Street Rallies As US-China Tariff Deal Sparks Optimism
body: US stocks soared on Monday as investors cheered a breakthrough in trade tensions between the world’s two largest economies. The US and China announced an agreement to slash tariffs for 90 days, offering a window to negotiate a broader trade deal. The Dow Jones Industrial Average surged 1,160 points, or 2.8%, to record one of its strongest sessions this year. The S&P 500 jumped 3.2%, while the Nasdaq Composite soared 4.3%, powered by a tech rebound. Among the top movers, Meta and Amazon each surged around 8%, while Tesla climbed nearly 7%. Starbucks added more than 6%, and Best Buy rose over 4%, rebounding from earlier warnings over tariff-driven cost increases. The agreement includes a cut in US tariffs on Chinese goods from 145% to 30%, while China will lower duties on US products from 125% to 10%, easing fears of inflation and a potential recession. The rollback follows President Trump’s “Liberation Day” tariff announcement in April and signals a shift in trade policy. “It’s as if the last six weeks have been a bad dream,” Deutsche Bank said in a note to clients. Still, analysts warned that base-level tariffs remain elevated. Carol Schleif of BMO Private Wealth said a 30% levy still represents a significant increase from early Trump-era rates, but the pause is “exactly what the stock market was hoping to see.” UBS estimates show that the new measures lower average US tariffs from 24% to 14%, marking a notable cooling in trade tensions. title: Asian Stocks Rally As US-China Trade War Eases, US Dollar Holds Gains
body: Asian stocks surged on Tuesday, May 13, joining the global rally, while the US dollar retained most of its gains after a temporary halt in the US-China trade war brought relief to markets. Investors were optimistic following the announcement of a 90-day truce between the two largest economies, easing recession fears. Japan’s Nikkei index jumped 2%, reaching its highest level since February 25, and Taiwan’s tech-heavy index followed suit, rising 2%. Chinese stocks saw modest gains in early trading, while Singapore’s Straits Times Index (STI) climbed over 1.5%. This global rally lifted MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan to a six-month peak. The US S&P 500 rose more than 3%, and the Nasdaq surged 4.3% after the US and China agreed to cut tariffs for at least three months. Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo in Singapore, pointed out that the real win was the shift in tone between the US and China. “Words like ‘mutual respect’ and ‘dignity’ mark a sharp departure from the recent confrontational rhetoric, and that’s what markets are cheering,” she said. Under the agreement, the US will cut tariffs on Chinese imports from 145% to 30%, while China will reduce tariffs on US imports from 125% to 10%. Although the market welcomed the news, concerns persist that tariffs could still hurt the global economy. The US dollar surged against the yen, euro, and Swiss franc after the announcement, although it eased slightly on Tuesday, retaining most of its gains. Some analysts, however, warned about the lingering uncertainty from the remaining tariffs. “A de-escalation was inevitable and I think it’s clear there won’t be much durable that comes out of these talks,” said Christopher Hodge, chief US economist at Natixis. “When all is said and done, tariffs will still be dramatically higher and will weigh on US growth.” Fitch Ratings estimated the effective US tariff rate now stands at 13.1%, down from 22.8% before the agreement, but still at levels not seen since 1941 and significantly higher than the 2.3% rate at the end of 2024. With traders now focusing on the details of the trade agreement and the outlook after 90 days, attention will shift to US inflation data expected later on Tuesday. “Should we be treated to another set of soft CPI figures, it could allow traders to refocus on Fed policy and the potential for cuts, and take some steam out of the dollar’s rebound,” said Matt Simpson, senior market analyst at City Index. The easing of trade tensions has led traders to reduce their bets on Federal Reserve rate cuts. The market is now pricing in 57 basis points of cuts this year, down from over 100 basis points during the height of tariff-induced anxiety in mid-April. US Treasury yields rose to a one-month high on Monday and remained near that level on Tuesday. The two-year yield was at 3.9873%, while the 10-year yield was at 4.4512%. In other markets, bitcoin eased by 0.5% to US$102,146, although it stayed above the critical US$100,000 level it reached last week. Oil prices dropped slightly after hitting a two-week high, and gold prices remained steady after falling 2% on Monday as investors moved away from safe-haven assets. title: Markets Rally On Tariff Slash, HKSE Jumps 3%
body: Stock markets, the dollar and oil prices rallied on Monday (May 12) after Chinese and US officials slashed tit-for-tat tariffs for 90 days, fuelling hopes the two sides will pull back from a standoff that has rattled global markets. Hong Kong’s stock market closed up 3 per cent in reaction, while Paris led the way in Europe, gaining 1.4 per cent in midday deals. The big gainer in the French capital was luxury giant LVMH, the maker of Louis Vuitton handbags, whose shares were up nearly 7 per cent. The dollar rallied against the euro, yen and British pound, while oil prices jumped around three per cent. “The market was not expecting the big change to US and China tariff rates, which is very positive for the outlook for the US and the global economy,” said Kathleen Brooks, research director at traders XTB. “The impact of tariffs on growth will now need to be revised lower, which is boosting the dollar … Safe havens like gold are also seeing demand slip away,” she told AFP. Investors have been on a rollercoaster ride since US President Donald Trump unveiled eye-watering tolls on trading partners on Apr 2, with the heftiest saved for Beijing, raising concerns of a trade war between the economic superpowers. Trump had hiked the measures against China to 145 per cent , which were met with retaliatory rates of 125 per cent.However, after two days of highly anticipated negotiations in Geneva, the two countries hailed progress towards ending a crisis that fuelled fears of a global recession. In a joint statement, the United States said it would reduce tolls to 30 per cent while Chinese tariffs on American goods would be cut to 10 per cent. Investors are awaiting the release this week of data on US inflation and retail sales, which will provide a fresh snapshot of the world’s biggest economy since the tariffs were first unveiled. title: Gold Eyes Further Gains Amid Trade Talks And Market Volatility
body: Gold has experienced notable volatility over the past week, reflecting the market’s sensitivity to shifting global trade dynamics and macroeconomic signals. In early sessions, gold surged nearly 6% — a strong rally fuelled by safe-haven demand as investors remained wary of unresolved global trade tensions, particularly involving the US, the UK and China. However, those gains were partially reversed as optimism around a US-UK trade deal and potential progress in upcoming US-China negotiations spurred risk-on sentiment. The modest relief provided by the US-UK agreement, though not the “comprehensive” deal promised by US President Donald Trump, signalled a slight easing in trade friction. This tempered the demand for gold as a defensive asset. Still, the deal’s limited scope and vague terms — alongside continued uncertainty in broader US-China relations — helped gold maintain a weekly gain of over 2%, settling around US$3,316.46 per ounce. This comes after gold hit a record high above US$3,500 last month, driven largely by geopolitical risk, inflation hedging and central bank purchases. Gold’s recent price action reflects a tug-of-war between diminishing haven demand amid softening trade tensions and lingering concerns over global economic stability. If trade negotiations with China fail to deliver concrete progress or if macroeconomic risks intensify, gold may find renewed momentum toward previous highs. Conversely, sustained improvements in economic data and trade relations could continue to pressure the metal in the near term. title: Trump’s Trade War Truce? Markets Soar On Potential China Tariff Cuts
body: Global stock markets saw gains on Friday, fuelled by rising optimism that the worst of the trade war initiated by US President Donald Trump may be over. This optimism follows a deal reached with the United Kingdom, and hints from Trump that he could ease tariffs on China ahead of high-stakes talks set for the weekend. Investors have seen a significant shift in sentiment since Trump unveiled his “Liberation Day” plan last month, which initially sent markets into turmoil and heightened fears of a global recession. However, several countries have stepped forward to negotiate with Washington, hoping to avert the imposition of high tariffs, some reaching as high as 145 per cent on Chinese imports. On Thursday, Britain became the first country to announce a deal with the US, which saw tariffs on British cars reduced and those on steel and aluminium lifted. In return, the UK agreed to open its markets to US beef and other farm products. Both Trump and British Prime Minister Keir Starmer hailed the deal as historic, with Trump suggesting that it could serve as a template for other countries. “This news gives hope that similar deals could be reached with a variety of countries, reducing the long-term damage potentially caused by tariffs,” said David Chao of Invesco. However, analysts suggested that traders were particularly encouraged by Trump’s comments regarding the ongoing trade talks with China. Trump indicated that tariffs on China, currently at 145 per cent, could be reduced. When asked about the possibility of easing tariffs, Trump replied, “It could be,” signalling that negotiations with China could soon see positive movement. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Trade Representative Jamieson Greer are set to meet Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng in Switzerland over the weekend for the first official talks since Trump introduced the tariffs. Trump also mentioned efforts to push through the tax cuts promised during his campaign, adding, “This country will hit a point that you better go out and buy stock.” Stephen Innes of SPI Asset Management noted that while the UK deal was significant, Trump’s tone on China was seen as the key signal for markets. “The president all but greenlit the idea that the days of punitive standoff might give way to negotiated momentum,” he said. Asian markets extended their rally, following Wall Street’s positive performance, with Tokyo surging by over one per cent on trade talks hopes. However, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick warned that trade agreements with Japan and South Korea may take longer, and there is “a lot of work” to be done on a deal with India. Meanwhile, Hong Kong, Sydney, Wellington, Taipei, Manila, and Jakarta all saw advances, alongside gains in London, Paris, and Frankfurt. Despite Shanghai’s dip, with exports to the US dropping by around 20 per cent in April due to the tariffs, other figures provided a glimmer of hope. Total shipments exceeded expectations, and imports fell less than forecast, suggesting that the Chinese economy is navigating the challenges. The resurgence in market confidence also saw a recovery in Bitcoin, which rose above $100,000 for the first time since February, reaching US$104,159 on Thursday. This brings the cryptocurrency closer to its record high of over $109,000, which was seen earlier this year. The group’s recent acquisition of UMW Holdings Bhd adds further complexity. While Toyota and Perodua posted record sales in 2024, both are projecting lower volumes in 2025 due to a broader market slowdown and competition from Chinese brands. The group’s attractive forecast dividend yield of 6.3% for FY2025–26 also continues to appeal to yield-seeking investors. title: MIDF Stays Positive On PetGas’ Natural Gas Power Plant Venture
body: Petronas Gas Bhd (PetGas) has announced that its wholly owned subsidiary, PG Energia Sdn Bhd (PGE), has entered into a shareholding agreement to develop a 120MW power plant in Labuan. MIDF Amanah Investment Bank Bhd (MIDF Research) has maintained a BUY call on the stock with a target price of RM18.67. The joint venture, Rancha Power, involves PGE holding a 60% stake, while Sabah Electricity Sdn Bhd’s (SESB) unit Sustainable Power Sdn Bhd (SPSB) and Sabah Energy Corporation’s (SEC) unit SEC Power Sdn Bhd (SECP) each hold 20%. The commercial operation date for the plant is expected by January 2028 at the latest. The new power plant will be the largest in Labuan, surpassing the existing Patau-Patau Power Station, which has a capacity of 113MW. This development is in line with the rising power demand in the region, which has been increasing steadily by 5-7% annually due to economic growth and population expansion. The commercial and industrial sectors in Labuan also contribute significantly to this demand, with monthly usage reaching up to 20,000kWh. The increase in power consumption underscores the long-term need for more power generation capacity in Labuan. The project is expected to primarily use natural gas, which is seen as a cleaner energy source due to its low CO2 emissions and lower levels of other greenhouse gases compared to other fossil fuels. This aligns with the Malaysian government’s efforts to transition to cleaner energy sources, as outlined in the National Energy Transition Roadmap (NETR) and the Malaysia Renewable Energy Roadmap (MyRER). MIDF Research is positive about the use of natural gas in the power plant, considering its environmental benefits. While the project is promising, there are inherent risks, particularly regarding safety. Although modern power plants are equipped with advanced safety measures to prevent accidents, there remains the possibility of incidents such as gas leaks or explosions. However, the research house believed that the involvement of PETRONAS and state-owned Sabah GLCs, along with strict safety protocols and ongoing monitoring by the Energy Commission and SIRIM, will mitigate these risks. body: Shares of Lotte Chemical Titan Holding Bhd surged over 10% during midday trade on Bursa Malaysia, buoyed by investor optimism following the company’s announcement of a decade-long ethylene supply agreement. As at 2.32 pm, the counter rose RM0.055 or 10.09% to RM0.600, with 360.77 million shares traded, making it one of the most actively traded stocks on the bourse. The stock hit an intraday high of RM0.630 and a low of RM0.550, after opening at RM0.560. title: US Stock Futures Rebound As Trade Talks With China Set To Resume
body: US stock futures rose early Wednesday following news that senior US officials will travel to Switzerland on Thursday for talks with China’s top economic representative, signalling a potential thaw in trade tensions. The meeting is expected to include Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer, possibly laying the groundwork for broader negotiations. It comes after a “tense but courteous” meeting between President Trump and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney on Tuesday. China’s central bank added to the positive momentum by announcing interest rate cuts and liquidity injections into its financial system—its first major move since Trump escalated tariffs in April. In the US, all eyes are on the Federal Reserve, which is widely expected to hold interest rates steady. Investors will be scrutinising comments from Fed Chair Jerome Powell for any signals on inflation risks from tariffs versus economic slowdown concerns. Futures linked to the Dow Jones Industrial Average, S&P 500, and Nasdaq-100 all posted gains in early trading, after the three indexes fell for a second straight session on Tuesday. Meanwhile, benchmark US Treasury yields edged up from Tuesday’s close of 4.305%. Investors are also watching corporate earnings, with results from Uber and Disney expected to provide insight into the impact of global trade uncertainty. Ford and Mattel have already pulled their annual guidance due to market volatility. Global markets were mixed—Asian stocks mostly rose after China’s economic stimulus measures, while European shares edged lower. India’s markets held steady following a military strike on Pakistan. Gold futures pulled back slightly from Tuesday’s record highs. title: Ringgit Strengthens As Fed Holds Rates; Focus Turns To BNM Decision
body: The ringgit opened stronger against the US dollar on Thursday, buoyed by renewed buying interest after the US Federal Reserve (Fed) kept interest rates unchanged, with analysts expecting potential rate cuts later this year. At 8am, the local note advanced to 4.2205/2510 against the greenback compared to Wednesday’s close of 4.2360/2435. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid noted that the US Dollar Index (DXY) gained 0.38% to 99.614 points after the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) maintained its key rate between 4.25% and 4.50%. “It was a unanimous decision and in line with market expectations. Despite that, the FOMC has become increasingly worried about the prospect of higher inflation and unemployment, a situation best described as stagflation (stagnant growth but high inflation),” he said. He added that this economic backdrop presents a dilemma for the Fed in balancing its dual mandate — price stability and maximum employment. Mohd Afzanizam believes the Fed may resort to rate cuts in the second half of the year once there is clearer insight into the effects of tariff shocks. “On that note, the rate thesis for this year remains intact as the inflation risks are seen as transitory, while the downside risk to growth has become elevated,” he said. He also pointed out that the ringgit had depreciated in the past two days but might stabilise within the current trajectory of RM4.23 to RM4.24. Attention now shifts to Bank Negara Malaysia’s (BNM) overnight policy rate decision, with economists divided on the potential outcome from the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC). “We are of the view that BNM will deliver a 25 basis points cut as a pre-emptive measure to support the economy with ongoing tariff negotiations,” he added. The ringgit also performed well against a basket of major and regional currencies in early trading. It rose against the Japanese yen to 2.9336/9550 from 2.9556/9613, gained against the euro to 4.7704/8049 from 4.8104/8189, and strengthened versus the British pound to 5.6090/6496 from 5.6479/6579. title: Profit-Taking Pressures Weigh On Bursa Despite Positive Market Breadth
body: The stock market closed lower on May 8 as profit-taking activity overshadowed bargain-hunting, bucking the positive momentum seen across most regional markets. At 5pm, even though the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) slipped 0.46 per cent, or 7.16 points, to 1,542.74 from 1,549.90 on May 7, the market breadth remained positive with gainers outperforming decliners 514 to 407, while 479 counters were unchanged, 951 were untraded, and nine were suspended. Meanwhile, in a move broadly in line with market expectations, Bank Negara Malaysia held the Overnight Policy Rate steady at 3%, maintaining its stance since May 2023. title: Hang Seng Index Futures Eye Breakout As Rally Builds
body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) is maintaining its bullish outlook on the Hang Seng Index futures (HSIF) after the index extended its upward momentum, rising 58 points to settle at 22,594 on Wednesday, approaching the critical 23,000-point resistance level. The index opened at 22,540 points, swinging between a high of 23,180 and a low of 22,387 before closing with a bullish candlestick. However, in the evening session, it pulled back by 128 points to last trade at 22,466. Despite the “long upper shadow” indicating a strong resistance at 23,000, the “higher high” close and a Relative Strength Index (RSI) above the 50% mark signal that bullish momentum remains intact. “A decisive breakout above 23,000 can strengthen the bullish setup and open the way towards the next resistance at 24,500,” the research house said in a note today. It added that any near-term pullback could find support at the 20-day simple moving average (SMA) line. RHB Research is advising traders to maintain long positions initiated at the 21,416-point level, corresponding to the 14 April close, while raising the stop-loss threshold to 21,500 points from the previous 21,000. Immediate support is now seen at 21,500 points, followed by 21,000, while resistance levels remain at 23,000 and subsequently 24,500. “We remain positive on the HSIF’s trading prospects, with technical indicators still pointing to a continuation of the rally if the 23,000 mark is decisively breached,” it said. title: Ringgit Strengthens As US Dollar Retreats Ahead Of Fed Decision
body: The ringgit climbed higher against the US dollar in early Wednesday trade, buoyed by a retreat in the US Dollar Index (DXY) and declining US Treasury yields, amid signs of cautious investor sentiment. At 8 am, the local currency stood at 4.2120/2300 against the greenback, firming from Tuesday’s close of 4.2285/2360. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid observed that the market remained fragile under the weight of economic uncertainties. “Traders and investors are observing the US Federal Open Market Committee’s (FOMC) assessment of current economic conditions ahead of its policy decision tonight,” he told local media. He added that the ringgit saw some profit-taking following its strong gains on Tuesday, due to lingering concerns in the broader economic landscape. “Given that, we expect the ringgit to stay within a narrow range as market participants await the FOMC outcome tonight. Consensus expects no change to the US Fed Funds Rate, which currently stands at 4.50 per cent,” Afzanizam said. The ringgit also posted gains against a number of major and regional currencies at the opening bell. It appreciated against the Japanese yen at 2.9434/9564 from 2.9502/9556, strengthened against the euro to 4.7764/7968 from 4.7824/7909, and rose versus the British pound to 5.6234/6475 from 5.6302/6402. In regional trade, the local note advanced against the Singapore dollar to 3.2674/2821 from 3.2749/2812, and improved against the Thai baht at 12.8922/9611 from 12.9399/9700. It also traded firmer against the Philippine peso, up to 7.57/7.61 from 7.60/7.62, and gained on the Indonesian rupiah, moving to 256.0/257.2 from 257.0/257.6. title: MR DIY Steady At RM1.74 As Analysts Signal Big Upside
body: MR DIY Group Bhd’s share price remained unchanged at RM1.74 as of 2.17 pm today, with a trading volume of 72.73 million shares. The stock opened at RM1.74 and hit a high of RM1.77 before settling back to its last done price, as investors weighed in on positive analyst sentiments and the group’s strong quarterly results. The consumer home improvement retailer has received multiple BUY recommendations, with RHB Investment Bank Bhd maintaining a target price of RM1.87, CIMB Investment Bank Bhd at RM2.15, and Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd at RM2.30, suggesting potential upsides of up to 37.7%. For the first quarter of FY2025, MR DIY reported a 10% year-on-year (YoY) increase in revenue to RM1.3 billion and a 21% YoY growth in core profit after tax to RM174 million, attributed to festive season sales and operational efficiencies. Same-store sales growth turned positive for the first time in eight quarters, while the group expanded its retail footprint to 1,471 outlets. An interim dividend of 1.4 sen per share was declared, representing a 76% payout ratio, above its 50–65% target range. Despite a slight delay in store openings, MR DIY targets 190 new stores this year, with analysts remaining bullish on its future earnings, citing product diversification and rising discretionary spending as key drivers. title: Markets Rattled As Trump Tariffs Overshadow Fed Calm
body: Equities retreated while US government bonds rallied, with the S&P 500 falling 0.8%, the Nasdaq 100 dropping 0.9%, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average slipping 0.9%. The movement came ahead of a crucial Federal Reserve decision, as financial markets grappled with heightened trade tensions triggered by President Donald Trump’s tariff rhetoric. Trump reiterated his stance on tariffs, suggesting he would define levels and concessions for countries wanting to sidestep heightened duties. This move appeared to dismiss the notion of future negotiations, exacerbating fears of economic fallout from his trade agenda. “Traders wishing to believe the Fed will come to the rescue of the world tomorrow… should think again,” warned Thierry Wizman of Macquarie. Although Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent expressed optimism about ongoing negotiations with trading partners, market participants remained unconvinced. Traders widely expect the Fed to keep interest rates unchanged, choosing to assess how last month’s trade actions affect the broader economy. Michael Brown of Pepperstone stated, “Fading upside in a complacent equity market amid continued trade uncertainty… I also remain a dip buyer in gold, and a rally seller in the dollar.” In extended trading, Marvell Technology Inc. shares sank after trimming revenue guidance and delaying an investor event due to economic uncertainty. Meanwhile, Rivian Automotive Inc. warned of steeper declines in full-year deliveries, and Super Micro Computer Inc.’s outlook fell short. On a more optimistic note, Advanced Micro Devices Inc. provided a bullish forecast. Palantir Technologies Inc. also fell after underwhelming financials, while Constellation Energy Corp. surged as it eyed long-term nuclear energy deals. Hims & Hers Health Inc. reiterated its 2025 guidance, and Archer-Daniels-Midland Co. forecast earnings at the low end due to biofuel and trade policy uncertainties. Despite the Fed’s current hold stance, Deutsche Bank’s Torsten Slok suggested the central bank may lean toward rate cuts, as economic clouds continue to gather. Yields on 10-year Treasuries declined five basis points to 4.29%, while the Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index dropped 0.3%, highlighting investors’ cautious tilt as risk-off sentiment intensified. Strategists at Goldman Sachs noted that valuations now leave “little room” for rallies to continue, while JPMorgan called US assets “not a good place to hide.” HSBC’s Max Kettner maintained a tactically cautious outlook, citing persistently weak fundamentals. Billionaire hedge fund manager Paul Tudor Jones said on CNBC he expects Trump to roll back China tariffs by 50%, but even so, stock markets could reach new lows. “You have Trump locked in on tariffs; the Fed locked in on not cutting rates. That’s not good for the stock market,” he said. Bank of America Corp. revealed retail investors have bought into US equities for 21 straight weeks — the longest streak since at least 2008. According to strategist Jill Carey Hall, these investors are continuing to invest despite a turbulent start to the year, particularly amid Trump’s trade push. Marriott International Inc. cut its growth outlook, citing a more uncertain economic environment. Meanwhile, DoorDash Inc. doubled down on global expansion, confirming its acquisition of London-based Deliveroo Plc alongside a US$1.2 billion deal for hospitality tech firm SevenRooms Inc. title: Gold Prices Dip In Malaysia Despite Global Bullish Momentum
body: Gold prices in Malaysia edged down slightly today, trading at RM14,377.84 per ounce, a decline of RM78.58 or 0.54%, even as global markets showed strong signs of bullish momentum. Data from GoldPrice.org shows that despite today’s pullback, gold has enjoyed a solid uptrend in recent months. Over the past 30 days, the metal has gained 8%, while prices surged 22.86% over the last six months and 31.7% year-on-year. Over the past five years, gold in Malaysia has nearly doubled in value, up 94.95%. On the international front, COMEX gold saw a sharp surge overnight, jumping US$100.50 to settle at US$3,444.50—breaking through the key resistance level of US$3,400. RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) said this decisive breakout signals the end of a correction phase and the start of a renewed uptrend. “The breakout above US$3,400 confirms that the prior correction has ended, with the precious metal now resuming its upwards trajectory,” RHB Research noted, adding that gold is now trading above both the 20- and 50-day simple moving averages, reinforcing a bullish outlook. Following the breakout, RHB Research closed its earlier short positions at US$3,294.10 and initiated long positions at US$3,422.80. The stop-loss is set at US$3,200, with revised support levels at US$3,350 and US$3,200, and resistance now raised to US$3,500 and US$3,700. title: Gamuda Jumps 1.15% On RM1.01 Billion DC Contract Boost
body: Shares in Gamuda Bhd climbed 1.15% to RM4.40 in midday trading today, buoyed by positive sentiment from analysts following the company’s strategic land sale and recent contract win in the data centre (DC) sector. At 12.01pm, Gamuda’s stock rose 5 sen from the previous close of RM4.35, with 71.06 million shares changing hands. The counter opened flat at RM4.35, touched a high of RM4.44, and recorded a low of RM4.35. The upward momentum reflects investor confidence following analyst reports from MIDF Amanah Investment Bank Bhd and CIMB Investment Bank Bhd, both of which reiterated BUY calls. MIDF set a target price of RM5.42, while CIMB pegged theirs at RM5.26, citing the group’s robust pipeline and growing foothold in the DC construction market. Last week, Gamuda announced the sale of 389 acres of land to Pearl Computing Malaysia for RM455.2 million, along with a RM1.01 billion enabling works contract for a major DC hub in Port Dickson. The project will include earthworks, a 65-million-litre-per-day water treatment plant, and off-river storage facilities. CIMB highlighted that the contract would boost Gamuda’s order book by 2.8% to RM37 billion, placing the company in a favourable position for future DC projects, estimated to be worth RM14 billion to RM20 billion in total value. Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd also maintained its BUY recommendation with a target price of RM5.26, reinforcing the view that the contract will enhance Gamuda’s unbilled order book and earnings visibility. Analysts noted that although the land sale itself is expected to contribute marginal profit, the accompanying enabling works are seen as a critical long-term growth driver, especially given Gamuda’s Digital IBS capabilities and strategic integration of land, power, and water infrastructure solutions. Gamuda’s broader project pipeline—including the Sabah water scheme and Penang LRT—adds to the bullish outlook, solidifying its role in large-scale infrastructure and DC development both domestically and abroad. title: FKLI Sees Sideways Movement Below 1,550; FCPO Drops Below RM3,800 — RHB Research
body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) is maintaining a cautiously optimistic stance on the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI Futures (FKLI), despite the index slipping for a second consecutive session on Tuesday and closing with a bearish candlestick. The FKLI opened at 1,535 points and briefly touched a high of 1,546.50 points before retreating to close lower at 1,530.50. RHB Research noted that this “lower low” finish suggests weakening bullish momentum, with the index poised to test support near the 50-day simple moving average (SMA). However, the 1,480-point level remains the critical support, and as long as this level holds, the research house retains a positive trading bias. Traders are advised to hold on to their long positions initiated at 1,462 points, with a stop-loss pegged at 1,480 points. Resistance levels remain at 1,550 and 1,600 points. Meanwhile, the crude palm oil futures (FCPO) continued its bearish trajectory, breaking below RM3,800 to settle at RM3,792 on Tuesday. The commodity saw intensified selling pressure after opening at RM3,822 and reaching a session high of RM3,844, before slipping to a low of RM3,772.
