title: Wall Street Futures Dip On Trump’s New Tariffs, Fed Meeting In Spotlight
body: US stock index futures slid on Monday as investor concerns flared up following former President Donald Trump’s announcement of new tariffs, while attention shifted to the US Federal Reserve’s upcoming policy decision later this week. At 7:07 a.m. ET, Dow E-minis dropped 246 points (-0.59%), S&P 500 E-minis fell 43.25 points (-0.76%), and Nasdaq 100 E-minis slipped 183.25 points (-0.91%). Trump’s move to impose a 100% tariff on movies produced outside the US raised the spectre of a renewed global trade war. Entertainment giants took a hit in premarket trading, with Netflix falling 4.7%, Amazon.com dropping 1.5%, and Walt Disney and Warner Bros. Discovery both losing around 2.2%. Berkshire Hathaway’s Class B shares fell 2.2% after Warren Buffett announced he would step down as CEO, with Greg Abel named his successor. Buffett will remain as chairman. The drop in futures comes after a nine-day winning streak by the S&P 500, its longest run since 2004, buoyed last week by easing tensions between the US and China. However, last week’s data showed that the US economy contracted in Q1 2025 for the first time since 2022, as companies scrambled to import goods ahead of expected tariffs — a worrying sign for broader economic growth despite strong labour market data. The market now awaits the Federal Reserve’s policy meeting, where the central bank is expected to hold interest rates steady. Analysts are watching closely for guidance on potential rate cuts, particularly in light of rising tariff pressures. Traders are currently pricing in a 25 basis-point rate cut by July, and a total of 116 basis points of easing by year-end, according to LSEG data. Later today, the ISM services sector report will provide fresh clues on the state of non-manufacturing activity in the US economy. Elsewhere in corporate moves: Freshpet dropped 2.9% after trimming its annual sales forecast. Onsemi declined 1.7% ahead of its quarterly earnings. Ford and Palantir are expected to report after market close. Gold stocks stood out as winners, tracking higher bullion prices. Gold Fields jumped 6% and Anglogold Ashanti rose 5.4%, mirroring a 2.3% surge in gold prices. Conversely, energy players such as Chevron and ExxonMobil shed about 1% each as crude oil prices retreated on expectations of increased output from OPEC+ producers. title: Stock Watch: Frontken Slips 0.82% Despite Profit Growth In Q1
body: Frontken Corp Bhd’s share price fell 0.82% or 3 sen at RM3.62 on Tuesday, despite reporting a year-on-year profit increase for the first quarter ended March 31, 2025 (1Q25). The stock opened at RM3.65 and traded between a low of RM3.56 and a high of RM3.65, with 1.79 million shares changing hands. It last at RM3.65 at the time of writing (12.14 pm). According to its recent Bursa Malaysia filing, Frontken posted a marginal 6% year-on-year revenue decline to RM140.5 million in 1Q25 from RM132.6 million, mainly due to reduced activity in the oil and gas segment. The decrease was attributed to fewer operational days during Lunar New Year and Ramadan, as well as the absence of one-off projects that had boosted performance a year ago. Despite softer revenue, Frontken’s profit after tax rose 2% to RM34.1 million from RM33.4 million in 1Q24, lifted by stronger contributions from its semiconductor segment and reduced surtax. However, on a quarter-on-quarter basis, profit dropped 19% owing to lower revenue and a withholding tax payment tied to dividends from its Taiwan unit. The group noted that it is closely monitoring the evolving global semiconductor environment, viewing the uncertainties as a chance to strengthen its position. It remains focused on operational efficiency and cost control amid the ongoing global trade war and shifting tariff policies. Frontken reaffirmed its confidence in adapting to market volatility while reinforcing its regional partnerships across the semiconductor supply chain. title: Ringgit Rallies On Hopes Of Trade Resolution, Stronger Sentiment
body: The ringgit extended its upward momentum against the US dollar on Tuesday, opening at 4.1835/2035, firmer than Monday’s close of 4.1990/2035, buoyed by positive sentiment surrounding the local unit. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the currency’s performance was likely driven by speculation that trade agreements may be reached, as US tariff measures could weigh heavily on US economic growth. “On that note, we shall expect the ringgit to remain strong against the US dollar today,” he told local media. Afzanizam also noted that the US Dollar Index (DXY) continued to hover below the 100-point level, standing at 99.831, despite the US Institute for Supply Management (ISM) services index for April coming in better than expected at 51.6 points (Consensus: 50.2 points). Adding to the ringgit’s strength was market confidence stemming from the Special Parliamentary Session on US tariffs held on May 5. During the session, the government expressed its commitment to implement the necessary measures to cushion the impact of the tariff shocks introduced by US President Donald Trump. The ringgit was stronger across major currencies. It rose against the Japanese yen to 2.9111/9252 from 2.9192/9225, strengthened versus the euro to 4.7320/7546 from 4.7629/7680, and appreciated against the British pound to 5.5595/5860 from 5.5868/5928. The local note also climbed against ASEAN currencies. title: Chinese Stocks Surge Post-Holiday Amid US Trade Talks and Strong Domestic Data Boost
body: Chinese stocks climbed on May 6 as investors returned from a five-day holiday, buoyed by encouraging signals from both trade discussions with the US and fresh signs of resilience in domestic consumer spending. The benchmark CSI 300 Index rose as much as 0.6% in early trading, with technology and telecommunication shares leading the charge. The uptick comes as traders weigh remarks from US officials that hint at renewed momentum in trade negotiations between the world’s two largest economies. According to a report by Bloomberg , US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said there could be “substantial progress in the coming weeks” in talks with China, echoing a more measured tone set by President Donald Trump. While Trump indicated openness to reducing tariffs on Chinese goods eventually, he clarified that no meeting with President Xi Jinping is currently planned. China’s Commerce Ministry added to the cautious optimism on May 2 that China is evaluating the potential for restarting trade talks with Washington, another signal that diplomacy may be quietly resuming. Despite the upbeat tone onshore, a gauge of Chinese equities traded in Hong Kong dropped as much as 0.8% in early trading on May 6, after rallying nearly 2% on May 2. The pullback suggests ongoing caution among offshore investors. Hong Kong markets had also been closed on May 5, mirroring the mainland’s extended break. Adding to the positive sentiment was domestic data showing a healthy pickup in consumer activity during the Labour Day holiday. Sales at key retail and catering enterprises rose 6.3% year-on-year, offering a hopeful sign to policymakers aiming to stimulate domestic consumption as a pillar for long-term economic growth. Together, the signals point to a market cautiously optimistic about China’s economic trajectory, which hinges on international diplomacy and internal demand resilience. title: Analysts Warn On Lotte Chemical’s Troubles From Tariffs
body: Lotte Chemical Titan Holdings (LCT) reported a narrowing of its core net loss by 10.4% quarter-on-quarter (QoQ) and 27.0% year-on-year (YoY) to RM159.9 million in its 1Q25 results, which CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) has deemed in line with expectations. This performance was underpinned by improved product spreads, lower depreciation, and a recovery in its associate, Lotte Chemical USA. However, despite these improvements, analysts remain cautious, with CIMB reducing their target price for LCT from RM0.67 to RM0.39 and downgrading the stock to a REDUCE rating due to persistent losses and an uncertain outlook. According to CIMB Securities, the improved 1Q25 performance stemmed from LCT’s strategic product mix optimisation, which involved shifting a larger portion of feedstock towards ethylene production to capitalise on stronger market demand. This was coupled with the temporary shutdown of Naphtha Cracker #1, which helped reduce operating costs. Despite this, LCT’s operating rate declined to 46%, down from 59% in 4Q24, as a result of the shutdown. Consequently, LCT revised its 2025 operating rate guidance downwards to 45–50%, from a previous estimate of 55–60%. CIMB Securities has maintained their earnings forecasts for FY25–27, they noted that LCT’s performance is likely to remain constrained by weak average selling prices, sustained demand weakness, and the impact of recent US tariff announcements. These tariffs are expected to further dampen global trade sentiment and petrochemical demand, particularly in key export markets. The house also warned that the tariffs could result in higher input and logistics costs, which may erode LCT’s cost competitiveness and margin recovery. CIMB Securities has downgraded LCT’s rating to Reduce from Hold as it expects the company to continue facing losses over the next three years due to the challenging operating environment. The house highlighted that the stock’s key upside risk lies in the possibility of privatisation, while the downside risk could come from even greater operational losses. LCT’s 52-week performance has been notably weak, with the stock losing 60.5% over the past year. Lotte Chemical Titan’s prospects face ongoing uncertainty due to these external challenges. CIMB Securities suggests that the company’s current trajectory, driven by the aforementioned factors, points to limited upside in the near term, making it difficult for LCT to recover from its current struggles. As such, the revised target price and downgraded rating reflect a more cautious outlook for the company’s performance in the coming years. title: Ringgit Edges Higher As Weak US Dollar And China Trade News Boost Sentiment
body: The ringgit opened slightly stronger against the US dollar on Monday, supported by dovish sentiment from the US Federal Reserve (Fed) and fresh trade developments concerning China. At 8 am, the local note was quoted at 4.2520/2615 against the greenback, compared to Friday’s close of 4.2560/2600. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the ringgit could remain positive in the near term, as the US dollar is likely to stay weak due to uncertainty over tariff policies and their potential effects on the American economy. “The local note has performed favourably against the greenback as it appreciated to 4.2568, gaining 1.39% on Friday,” he said. Dr Afzanizam added that attention will also be on the special Parliament session, as markets look for measures to cushion the impact of tariff shocks from the US President Donald Trump administration. “Key areas would be the possible revision to the growth forecast and the short-term measure to be announced by the government,” he added. On the global front, the Trump administration signalled possible cuts to tariffs on China, responding to concerns about weakening global trade. Despite resilience in the US labour market, reflected in rising stock prices and bond yields, the US Dollar Index (DXY) edged down 0.05% to 99.984 points. “While the US nonfarm payrolls beat market estimates in April, the monthly average showed that the pace of job creation has scaled down to 133,000 in the first four months of 2025 versus 176,000 monthly average during the same period last year,” he said. He noted that the upcoming Federal Open Market Committee meeting on 6–7 May will be closely watched as markets seek clarity on the Fed’s next interest rate move. The Fed is still widely expected to cut rates in June, with traders pricing in over 100 basis points of easing by year-end. Back home, the ringgit also strengthened against major currencies and regional peers. It rose against the Japanese yen to 2.9389/9459 from 2.9437/9467, gained on the euro to 4.8133/8240 from 4.8297/8342, and appreciated against the British pound to 5.6424/6550 from 5.6639/6692. Regionally, it improved against the Singapore dollar at 3.2778/2857 from 3.2862/2898, the Thai baht at 12.8502/9011 from 12.8697/8903, and slightly against the Philippine peso to 7.64/7.67 from 7.65/7.67. It also edged higher against the Indonesian rupiah to 258.6/259.3 from 258.8/259.3. title: Gold Prices Dip Slightly In Malaysia, Remain Strong Over Long Term
body: Gold prices in Malaysia saw a slight decline today, falling RM63.73 or 0.46% to RM13,754.78 per ounce. The drop follows minor losses across the board, with the price per ounce now at RM13,754.78, while silver also edged lower by RM0.12 or 0.09% to RM136.29. Despite the daily dip, gold remains on a strong upward trajectory over the longer term. Over the past 30 days, prices have risen RM521.96 or 3.93%, and over the past six months, gold has surged by RM2,068.18 or 17.61%. Year-on-year, the precious metal has gained RM2,806.80, marking a 25.50% increase. Over five years, gold has appreciated by a significant RM6,527.65 or 89.57%, and over two decades, prices have skyrocketed RM12,191.10, an impressive 750.71% jump. On the international front, RHB Investment Bank Bhd said COMEX gold continues to consolidate, closing last Friday at US$3,243.30 – just below the 20-day simple moving average (SMA) of US$3,244.70. The bank noted that while the commodity printed a “higher high” close, a long upper shadow on the candle signalled weak bullish momentum. “The yellow metal may extend the consolidation and test the US$3,200 support. In a bearish setup, support is weak and likely to see a bearish breakout. If the US$3,200 level gives way, a lower support is anticipated at the US$3,000 level,” the bank said in a note. RHB recommends maintaining short positions initiated at US$3,294.10 and has revised its stop-loss level to US$3,400. title: Hong Kong Intervenes In Market To Curb Currency Rise
body: Hong Kong’s de-facto central bank said it sold HK$46.54 billion ($6 billion) into the market on Saturday to prevent the local currency from strengthening beyond its official peg to the U.S. dollar, the first such intervention in more than four years. The Hong Kong dollar is pegged to a tight band between 7.75 and 7.85 per U.S. dollar. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority intervened as the Hong Kong dollar touched the strong side of that currency convertibility range. The last time it sold Hong Kong dollars to defend the peg was in October 2020. “Seeing the HKD getting stronger means capital inflows, which is not problematic for Hong Kong,” said Gary Ng, senior economist at Natixis. The aggregate balance, the key gauge of cash in the banking system, will increase to HK$91.31 billion on May 7, an HKMA spokeswoman said on Saturday. title: Ringgit Opens Slightly Higher Amid US Economic Weakness And Global Tariff Concerns
body: The ringgit opened marginally stronger against the US dollar on Friday, supported by weak US economic data and resilient sentiment in Asian markets, despite ongoing concerns over global tariffs. At 8am, the local currency stood at 4.3115/3310 against the greenback, compared to Wednesday’s close of 4.3130/3185. The local market was closed on Thursday in observance of Labour Day. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the marginal appreciation came as the US Institute for Supply Management (ISM) manufacturing index slipped to 48.7 points in April, down from 49.0 in March, signalling contraction amid tariff-related uncertainties. “Respondents to the ISM survey are increasingly anxious and confused over the tariff rulings, which could significantly drive up operating costs and disrupt supply chains,” he told Bernama. He added that continuing claims for US unemployment benefits rose to 1.92 million for the week ending April 19 — the highest since November 2011 — reflecting growing softness in the US labour market. “The US dollar index (DXY) has been lethargic, and with sentiment uncertain, emerging market currencies may continue to see limited movements. For now, the ringgit is likely to trade within a tight range of RM4.31 to RM4.32 due to potential profit-taking,” he added. title: Meta and Microsoft Earnings Lift Markets Despite Trade Uncertainty
body: US stock markets surged on Thursday, with the Nasdaq leading the gains as investor confidence returned following strong earnings from Microsoft and Meta. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite closed up 1.5%, while the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average extended their winning streaks, rising 0.6% and 0.2% respectively. Microsoft jumped 7.6%—its strongest close since January—after issuing an upbeat growth forecast for its Azure cloud division, briefly reclaiming its position as the world’s most valuable company ahead of Apple. Meta also advanced, climbing 4.2% on the back of better-than-expected advertising revenue. The shift in market focus from trade tensions to corporate earnings provided a welcome boost. Robust quarterly results helped reassure investors, with S&P 500 first-quarter earnings now projected to grow 12.9% year-on-year—up from a previous estimate of 8%, according to LSEG data. However, sentiment was tempered after the closing bell, as Amazon shares dropped nearly 4% on the back of weaker-than-anticipated growth in its cloud business. Apple was due to release its results later in the day. While the strong performances from Microsoft and Meta lifted market morale following recent volatility and economic contraction in the US, caution remains. Broader economic indicators—including rising unemployment claims and persistent trade uncertainty—continue to shape the outlook for Big Tech and the wider economy. title: Asian Stocks Gain After China Teases On US Tariff Talks
body: Asian markets largely rose on Friday (May 2), tracking Wall Street gains, as China said it was considering a United States offer to negotiate steep tariffs. US markets forged higher on Thursday following strong results from tech giants Microsoft and Meta that helped offset lingering economic worries.Apple reported first-quarter profit above expectations but warned that US tariffs could cost the company and were disrupting its supply chain. And Amazon reported a 9 per cent rise in first-quarter revenue, but its outlook fell as a potential impact from the US-China trade war rattled investors. Washington’s punishing levies reached 145 per cent on many Chinese products in April, while Beijing has responded with fresh 125 per cent duties on imports from the US. On Friday, China’s commerce ministry said it was evaluating a US offer for negotiations on tariffs, but wanted Washington to show “sincerity” and be ready to scrap levies that have roiled global markets and supply chains. US President Donald Trump has repeatedly claimed that China has reached out for talks on the tariffs, and this week said he believed there was a “very good chance we’re going to make a deal”. Dozens of countries face a 90-day deadline expiring in July to strike an agreement with Washington and avoid higher, country-specific rates. Stephen Innes of SPI Asset Management said Beijing and Washington were now “waving detente flags” in their spiralling trade war. Beijing’s demand for sincerity was an apparent call to ditch the 145 per cent rate, before holding serious talks, Innes said in a note Friday. “But dig a layer deeper, and the path is still littered with landmines,” he added.In Asia trading on Friday, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index was up more than 1 per cent in the morning, while Japan’s main Nikkei index gained about 0.6 per cent. Japan’s envoy for US tariff talks said in Washington on Thursday that a second round of negotiations between the two countries had been “frank and constructive”. Japan, a key US ally and its biggest investor, is subject to the same 10 per cent baseline tariffs imposed on most nations plus steeper levies on cars, steel and aluminium. The Bank of Japan warned earlier that tariffs were fuelling global economic uncertainty and revised down its growth forecasts while keeping its key interest rate steady. Traders are looking ahead to Friday’s US jobs data for April for indications of the US central bank’s path for interest rates. title: Wall Street Extends Rally As Investors Eye Earnings, Tariff Clarity
body: The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 0.8%, or 300 points, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite both added 0.6%. The S&P 500 and Dow are now riding a six-day winning streak, having gained 8% and 6% respectively over the period. Market sentiment has been lifted in recent sessions by a string of better-than-expected earnings and growing optimism that the Trump administration could soften its stance on trade tariffs. While the White House has signalled continued talks with various countries, the lack of concrete outcomes has left investors cautiously hopeful. Among the day’s earnings movers, Honeywell (HON) and Sherwin-Williams (SHW) climbed about 5% each, while Pfizer (PFE) rose 3% and Coca-Cola (KO) edged up nearly 1%. On the downside, Regeneron Pharmaceuticals (REGN) slumped 7%, Spotify (SPOT) dropped 3.5%, and United Parcel Service (UPS) dipped slightly. The automaker’s decision came just ahead of a presidential executive order that reduced import taxes on vehicles and auto parts, aiming to ease industry pressure. Tech stocks were mixed. Tesla (TSLA) rose 2% after the tariff announcement, while Apple (AAPL), Microsoft (MSFT), Nvidia (NVDA), and Meta Platforms (META) posted modest gains under 1%. On the macro front, economic data was light, but attention is shifting to a busy midweek schedule, with GDP and inflation data due Wednesday and the April jobs report on Friday. Analysts are watching closely for any signs that tariffs are weighing on economic momentum. Meanwhile, the US dollar index rose 0.2% to 99.20, rebounding from a three-year low below 98 last week. Gold futures dipped 0.5% to US$3,330 an ounce, pulling back from last week’s record high, while WTI crude slumped 3.1% to US$60.15 per barrel. title: US Stocks Extend Winning Streak As Corporate Profits Outshine Trade Uncertainty
body: Wall Street closed higher on Tuesday, buoyed by a series of stronger-than-expected corporate earnings that lifted investor sentiment despite lingering concerns over US President Donald Trump’s trade policies. The S&P 500 rose 0.6% to 5,560.83, marking its sixth consecutive day of gains. The Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed 300.03 points, or 0.7%, to close at 40,527.62, while the Nasdaq composite added 0.5% to 17,461.32. Honeywell International led gains among blue-chip stocks, jumping 5.4% after reporting earnings and revenue that beat analyst estimates. The company also raised its full-year profit forecast, although CEO Vimal Kapur cautioned about potential headwinds ahead. “We recognise we face an uncertain global demand environment for the remainder of 2025,” he said. Sherwin-Williams followed closely with a 4.8% rise after its earnings topped expectations. CEO Heidi Petz acknowledged continued softness from some customer segments but said the company’s localised supply chain could help mitigate the effects of tariffs. Other companies reporting better-than-expected results had more muted stock reactions. United Parcel Service (UPS) shares dipped 0.4% despite posting stronger earnings for the first quarter. The shipping giant maintained its 2025 financial forecast unchanged and announced plans to cut 20,000 jobs and shut down 73 buildings, citing macroeconomic uncertainty. General Motors also beat earnings estimates but fell 0.6% as the automaker delayed its investor call to Thursday in light of potential changes to trade policy. Meanwhile, JetBlue Airways rose 2.7% even after pulling its full-year forecast, with CEO Joanna Geraghty citing economic uncertainty. Coca-Cola gained 0.8% after overcoming an early dip, with the beverage company calling the impact of tariffs “manageable” and updating some financial projections. Investors continue to monitor the shifting trade landscape, as Trump’s tariffs and inconsistent rollout threaten to disrupt global supply chains. White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt said the president is expected to sign an executive order to ease some of the 25% tariffs on autos. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Trump’s approach is part of a broader strategy, calling it “strategic uncertainty.” Economic data added to the cautious tone. The Conference Board reported a steep drop in consumer expectations, falling to levels not seen since 2011 and typically indicative of a looming recession. Job openings data also came in weaker than forecasted. In the bond market, yields fell in response to the soft economic readings. The 10-year Treasury yield slipped to 4.17% from 4.23% on Monday, raising hopes that the Federal Reserve may eventually resume interest rate cuts to support growth. title: Hang Seng Index Futures Holds Ground Above Key Support, Positive Bias Maintained
body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has maintained a positive trading bias on the Hang Seng Index Futures (HSIF), advising traders to hold their long positions as the index continues to consolidate above key technical levels. The HSIF closed marginally lower by 37 points at 21,972 points on Tuesday, despite hovering above the 20-day simple moving average (SMA). It traded within a narrow range, recording an intraday high of 22,122 points and a low of 21,800 points, before ending the session with another Doji candlestick — a signal of near-term indecision, according to RHB. During the evening session, the index recovered slightly, adding 27 points to last trade at 21,999 points. The research house noted that the broader bullish technical structure remains intact, with the RSI holding near the 50% mark, indicating that momentum is still constructive. RHB Research said that as long as the index stays above the 21,000-point support, the HSIF could eventually break out of its current consolidation phase and resume its upward climb toward the 23,000-point resistance, with a higher resistance target seen at 24,500 points. The research house reiterated its advice for traders to hold long positions initiated at 21,416 points, or based on the closing level on 14 April. A stop-loss threshold remains at 21,000 points to manage downside risk. Immediate support is at 21,000 points, followed by a lower level at 20,000 points, while resistance remains at 23,000 points and 24,500 points on the upside. title: Wall Street Gains As Investors Brace For Earnings, Economic Data
body: US stocks closed mostly higher on Monday, extending last week’s gains as investors positioned ahead of key corporate earnings and economic data releases. The Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed 0.3%, while the S&P 500 added 0.1%, marking the fifth straight session of gains for both indexes. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite slipped 0.1%, despite rallying in the final hours of trading. The earnings calendar is set to pick up pace, with Apple (AAPL), Amazon (AMZN), Microsoft (MSFT) and Meta Platforms (META) scheduled to report this week. Investors are also awaiting quarterly GDP figures, a key inflation reading and the April jobs report, alongside developments on US trade policy under President Trump. title: Ringgit Strengthens Amid Weaker US Dollar Index
body: The ringgit extended its gains in early trade on Tuesday, supported by buying interest in the local note alongside a decline in the US Dollar Index (DXY). At 8am, the ringgit stood higher at 4.3585/3665 against the US dollar, compared with Monday’s close of 4.3615/3665. The DXY slipped 0.46% to 99.010 points as United States businesses were negatively impacted by US import tariffs, said Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid. “At the current juncture, the USDMYR is quite close to its existing support level of 4.3634 and should the dollar-ringgit breach this level, the next support level will be located at 4.2607,” he told Bernama. Mohd Afzanizam added that the ringgit had performed remarkably well so far, noting the local unit strengthened 0.22% against the greenback to 4.3640 yesterday. Elsewhere, Asian currencies showed mixed performances yesterday. The Thai baht and Indonesian rupiah depreciated against the US dollar by 0.02% and 0.15%, respectively, while the Korean won and Indian rupee advanced by 0.36% and 0.49%, respectively. On the global front, Mohd Afzanizam pointed out that calls for a US interest rate cut have grown louder, with the 2-year US Treasury note yield dropping five basis points to 3.69%. At the opening, the ringgit weakened against a basket of major currencies. It fell against the Japanese yen to 3.0657/0718 from 3.0406/0443 at Monday’s close, slipped vis-à-vis the euro to 4.9722/9813 from 4.9507/9564, and declined against the British pound to 5.8552/8660 from 5.8195/8262. It depreciated against the Singapore dollar to 3.3284/3350 from 3.3198/3238 and slid against the Thai baht to 13.0619/0945 from 12.9517/9743. The local note was almost flat vis-à-vis the Philippine peso at 7.72/7.74 compared to 7.73/7.74 on Monday, and little changed against the Indonesian rupiah at 258.5/259.1 from 258.7/259.1 previously. title: PetGas Share Drops 2.4% After Legal Blow And Sarawak Project Exit
body: Petronas Gas Bhd (PetGas) saw its share price fall 2.44% to RM16.82 on Tuesday, down 42 sen from the previous close, amid a wave of negative sentiment linked to recent legal and operational developments involving parent company Petronas. The utility stock, listed on the Main Market, opened at RM17.24 and hit an intraday low of RM16.78, with 432,400 shares traded as of 4:17 PM. The stock’s decline comes amid mounting investor unease following the surprise exit of ConocoPhillips from a US$3.1 billion gas project in Sarawak, reportedly due to a prolonged rift between Petronas and the Sarawak state government. Compounding concerns, the High Court on Monday dismissed Petronas’ application for a stay in proceedings related to a payment suit filed by state oil and gas company Petroleum Sarawak Bhd (Petros), further intensifying the spotlight on federal-state energy tensions. Last week, PetGas also reported efforts to accelerate supply restoration following an explosion at the Puchong City Gate, reaffirming its commitment to ensuring reliability, though the incident added pressure to an already cautious market outlook. PetGas closed at RM16.88 on Friday, and its year-to-date trajectory shows a consolidation phase, with investors now closely watching for clarity on regulatory and project developments. title: MIDF Optimistic On F&N’s Long Term Prospects
body: MIDF Investment Bank Bhd (MIDF Research) and CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) have both maintained their BUY calls on Fraser & Neave Holdings Bhd (F&N) following its 1HFY25 results, citing resilient domestic demand and stable export growth despite temporary headwinds. MIDF Research kept its target price unchanged at RM32.68, while CIMB Securities reiterated its target price of RM29.70. According to MIDF Research, F&N’s 1HFY25 performance was within expectations, with revenue rising 2.7% year-on-year to RM2.72 billion. This was driven by broad-based domestic sales and strengthening regional exports, despite disruptions from severe flooding in East Malaysia which affected festive season sales. The group’s 2QFY25 revenue stood at RM1.33 billion, a marginal 1.4% year-on-year decline, while core PATANCI for the quarter slipped 11.8% to RM142.8 million, mainly due to start-up costs from its AgriValley dairy farm. CIMB Securities noted that F&N’s 1HFY25 core net profit dipped 9.5% year-on-year to RM301 million, impacted by a higher effective tax rate following the expiry of tax incentives for its IndoChina operations and the imposition of withholding taxes. Despite these challenges, the results were deemed within expectations, meeting 55% of CIMB’s full-year forecast and 53% of Bloomberg’s consensus. Both houses pointed out that margin pressures were primarily linked to the early phase investments in the integrated dairy farm in Gemas. MIDF Research highlighted that while F&B Malaysia’s operating margin softened slightly to 11.0% in 1HFY25, overall group operating margins improved to 16.0% year-on-year, aided by better product mix and favourable input costs. CIMB Securities added that while 2QFY25 EBITDA margins narrowed by 1.7 percentage points quarter-on-quarter to 17.4%, this was still a commendable level given the operational challenges. Looking ahead, MIDF Research expressed optimism over F&N’s earnings defensiveness, underscored by stable demand for essential food and beverage products amid inflationary pressures. CIMB Securities echoed similar sentiments, expecting slight earnings moderation in the second half of FY25 due to continued dairy farm start-up losses and normalising IndoChina sales, but remained positive on F&N’s long-term prospects. F&N’s integrated dairy farm continues to be a significant growth initiative, with the company surpassing a cattle population of 2,700 and expecting first milking by June 2025. CIMB Securities believes the venture will contribute to Malaysia’s goal of achieving 100% self-sufficiency in fresh milk production by 2030 and sees strong long-term potential despite initial start-up losses. F&N declared an interim dividend of 30 sen per share for 1HFY25, consistent with the previous year, reflecting its commitment to shareholder returns despite a challenging operating environment. title: Gold Drops RM212 As COMEX Faces Resistance
body: Gold prices in Malaysia slipped today, falling RM212.26 or 1.46% to RM14,344.56 per ounce, in line with global price fluctuations. Despite the US$49.30 gain overnight, RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has reiterated a short position on COMEX gold, citing the continued influence of the “Shooting Star” pattern formed on 22 April. Traders were advised to maintain short positions from US$3,294.10 with a stop-loss at US$3,500. title: Astro Declines 5.26% On Challenging Outlook
body: Astro Malaysia Holdings Bhd’s share price fell 5.26% to close at RM0.180 on Tuesday, with 574,090 shares traded. The stock opened at RM0.190, reached a high of RM0.195, and touched a low of RM0.180 during the session (11.10 am). The decline followed recent updates on Astro’s tax settlement with the Inland Revenue Board, where the company agreed to claim production costs over six years instead of three. Although Maybank Investment Bank Bhd (Maybank IBG) described the cash flow impact as negative in the short term but neutral in the long term, it maintained a ‘SELL’ call on Astro, citing a still-challenging earnings outlook. Maybank IBG previously adjusted Astro’s weighted average cost of capital (WACC) to 12.4% due to a higher risk premium following the tax case and set a revised target price of RM0.12. The house expects consumer headwinds, including higher electricity tariffs and subsidy rationalisation, to further weigh on Astro’s Pay-TV subscriber growth and earnings prospects. At current levels, Astro’s share price is approaching Maybank IBG’s revised valuation, with downside risks persisting. title: Ringgit Opens Flat Amid Tariff Jitters
body: The ringgit opened little changed against the US dollar on Monday, as the US Dollar Index (DXY) snapped a four-week losing streak following its recent dip below the 100-point level. At 8.04am, the local note stood at 4.3700/3900 against the greenback, compared with last Friday’s close of 4.3705/3770. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd Chief Economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the ringgit is expected to remain rangebound due to lingering uncertainties over the United States’ tariff policies. “At the same time, the International Monetary Fund’s cautionary note on the global outlook this year suggests central banks may ease monetary policies further to cushion the impact,” he told local media. Analysts noted that the cautious tone in the market reflected broader concerns about the future direction of US trade policies. Back home, the ringgit traded mostly higher against a basket of major currencies. It strengthened against the Japanese yen to 3.0408/0550 from 3.0431/0481 at Friday’s close, and gained against the British pound to 5.8104/8369 from 5.8128/8214. However, it weakened slightly against the euro, falling to 4.9608/9835 from 4.9596/9670 previously. Meanwhile, the ringgit traded little changed against regional currencies. It was nearly flat against the Singapore dollar at 3.3224/3381 compared with 3.3228/3280 on Friday, remained stable against the Thai baht at 13.0195/0900 from 13.0195/0450, and barely moved against the Philippine peso at 7.77/7.81 from 7.77/7.78. Against the Indonesian rupiah, the local note stood at 259.6/260.9 from 259.6/260.2. title: Markets React To Trump’s Tariffs, US Earnings And Global Data
body: Stocks mostly rose on Monday as investors assessed developments in the ongoing trade war, with countries attempting to temper the eye-watering tariffs imposed by President Donald Trump. The market’s optimism was bolstered by discussions in China regarding plans to boost consumption in the world’s second-largest economy. Markets opened cautiously after a positive run-up last week, with attention now turning to the upcoming earnings season, crucial data releases, and central bank decisions. “We head into month-end and a risk event-heavy trading week, with a ‘cautiously optimistic’ stance adopted by the collective,” said Chris Weston, from Pepperstone. “Whether the move in risk can continue will be determined by the incoming economic data and US company earnings. The bar to beat expectations remains low, and the wall of worry is there for climbing.” Despite lingering caution, there was a sense of optimism among investors, particularly as the White House appeared sensitive to extreme market reactions. Following the plunge in the bond market triggered by Trump’s “Liberation Day” tariffs on April 2, investors felt a renewed sense of control, knowing that the US administration had a threshold and trigger point in response to market reactions. Asia started the day on a healthy note after a strong end to last week’s trading on Wall Street. Major markets such as Tokyo, Hong Kong, Sydney, Seoul, Taipei, Mumbai, Bangkok, Jakarta, and Wellington saw gains, while London, Paris, and Frankfurt also rose. However, Shanghai, Singapore, and Manila saw slight declines, and Hong Kong remained flat. In commodity markets, the positive mood in equities weighed on gold, which had hit a record high of $3,500 last week as investors flocked to safer assets. Traders are hoping that negotiations between the US and other governments can soften the impact of Trump’s tariffs. Reports last week indicated that China might consider exempting some US goods from retaliatory measures, although Beijing officially stated that there were no active negotiations between the two superpowers. An official in China also denied Trump’s claims of a recent phone conversation with President Xi Jinping. Meanwhile, Japanese media reported that a second round of trade talks would be held in Washington on Thursday, which will be closely watched as a barometer for other countries seeking tariff relief. Additionally, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated that a trade “understanding” between South Korea and the US could be reached by the end of the week. In China, government officials were set to hold a news conference on Monday to discuss employment, economic growth, and development, following a recent meeting of the country’s top decision-making body. Leaders are aiming to enhance consumption’s role in stimulating economic growth, while also striving to promote multilateralism and oppose unilateral actions. title: Hang Seng Index Futures Crosses 20-Day SMA, Bulls Eye Higher Gains
body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has maintained its positive trading bias on the Hang Seng Index Futures (HSIF), advising traders to stay on their long positions as the technical setup continues to favour the bulls. In its latest note, RHB Research highlighted that the HSIF successfully crossed above the 20-day simple moving average (SMA) line, closing higher at 22,009 points on Friday. The index had opened at 21,903 points, touched an intraday low of 21,886 points and a high of 22,287 points, before ending the day with a bullish candlestick formation. In the evening session, it added another 46 points to last trade at 22,055 points. “After firming its position above the 20-day SMA line, the bulls are now eyeing the 50-day SMA line as the next hurdle, with the 23,000-point resistance level in sight,” RHB Research said. It added that a bullish crossover above the 50-day SMA line would further improve market sentiment. Downside support remains firm at 21,000 points, providing a cushion for the bullish outlook. The brokerage advised traders to maintain the long position initiated at 21,416 points on 14 April, with a stop-loss placed at 21,000 points to manage risk. RHB Research pegged the immediate support at 21,000 points, followed by a lower support at 20,000 points. On the upside, resistance is seen at 23,000 points, with a higher resistance level set at 24,500 points. title: Wall Street Extends Gains, But Futures Trade Mixed
body: US stocks extended their rebound on Wednesday, with all major indices posting a second straight day of gains. The S&P 500 closed 1.7% higher at 5,375.86, while the Nasdaq Composite surged 2.5%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed more than 400 points, although it gave up part of an earlier 1,100-point gain by the close. However, futures traded flat to mixed on Wednesday night. S&P 500 futures were up 0.1%, Nasdaq 100 futures rose nearly 0.1%, while Dow futures slipped 45 points, or 0.1%. In extended trading, International Business Machines (IBM) fell over 6% despite beating first-quarter earnings and revenue estimates, as it kept its full-year guidance unchanged. Southwest Airlines also dropped more than 3% after announcing plans to cut its flight schedule in the second half of 2025 and withdrawing earnings guidance for 2025 and 2026. Investor sentiment was lifted during regular trading amid renewed optimism over US-China trade ties. Former president Donald Trump signalled a softer approach to Beijing, while Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said there was an “opportunity for a big deal” on trade. Chinese imports are currently subject to a US tariff of 145%. Trump also said he had “no intention” of firing Federal Reserve Chairman Jerome Powell, whose term runs until May 2026. The comment eased market nerves after recent tension between the two, including Trump labelling Powell a “major loser” earlier this week. Despite the rebound, some strategists remain cautious. Wolfe Research’s Rob Ginsberg and Read Harvey described the rally as a typical “bear market rally” with strong internal breadth and volume. They cautioned that a decisive turn in trend indicators is needed before confirming a lasting reversal. All three major indices are tracking for weekly gains, with the Nasdaq up 2.6%, S&P 500 up 1.8%, and Dow on pace for a 1.2% rise. Investors now turn their focus to key earnings from Alphabet, Intel, and PepsiCo on Thursday, along with fresh US data on durable goods orders and weekly jobless claims. title: Stocks In China Open Lower Despite Tariff Talk Down
body: Chinese stocks opened lower on Thursday, with the benchmark Shanghai Composite Index down 0.04 percent to open at 3,295.15 points. The Shenzhen Component Index opened 0.02 percent lower at 9,933.89 points. AFP reported yesterday that US President Donald Trump played up prospects of a “fair deal” on trade with China, but his top officials offered few details of how Washington might de-escalate its damaging tariff war with Beijing. Trump told reporters his country would have a “fair deal with China”, adding that “everything’s active” when asked if Washington was talking to Beijing. But how soon the tariffs can be lowered “depends on them”, Trump said, referring to Beijing, even as he maintained that he gets along “very well” with Chinese President Xi Jinping and hopes they can reach an agreement. Trade tensions between the world’s two biggest economies have soared as Trump ramped up levies on imports from China this year, imposing an additional 145 per cent tariff on many products over practices Washington has deemed unfair, and other issues.Beijing in turn has countered with new 125 per cent tariffs on US goods. title: Ringgit Weakens Against Greenback Amid Softer Tariff Rhetoric

title: Wall Street Rebounds As Trump Calms Markets On Fed, China Tariffs
body: US stocks rallied strongly overnight, lifted by reassuring remarks from President Donald Trump, who said he has no intention of firing Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell and hinted that steep tariffs on Chinese imports may be reduced. The Dow Jones Industrial Average surged 1,017 points or 2.7%, while the Nasdaq Composite and S&P 500 both climbed 2.7% and 2.5%, respectively. The gains came as investors welcomed signs of potential relief in ongoing US-China trade tensions. “We’re not going to keep tariffs at 145%. It won’t be that high. It will come down substantially,” said Trump, easing concerns about the economic impact of his administration’s trade stance. Adding to the market’s optimism, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said he expects a de-escalation in the trade war with China and foresees a deal being reached, according to sources cited by Bloomberg. Stock futures and the US dollar both strengthened following Trump’s comments, while volatility cooled. The Cboe Volatility Index (VIX) fell below 31, after spiking earlier in the week. Despite the rebound, warning signs remain. The International Monetary Fund (IMF) slashed both US and global growth forecasts, citing prolonged tariff uncertainty. Companies like RTX and Kimberly-Clark flagged the financial toll from global trade tensions, with RTX expecting an US$850 million hit. Gold, which soared past US$3,500 a troy ounce earlier Tuesday, eased back but remains a key safe-haven amid market turmoil. Bitcoin also climbed, breaking above US$91,000. Tesla, meanwhile, reported weaker-than-expected earnings after the bell, though its shares remained largely unchanged in after-hours trading. Treasury yields edged lower, with the benchmark 10-year note slipping to 4.389%, as investors weighed ongoing geopolitical risks despite the day’s gains. title: Ringgit Flat As Market Watches Trump’s Fed Remarks, Gains Against Major Currencies
body: The ringgit opened marginally higher against the US dollar this morning, trading at RM4.3825/4150 at 8am, compared to Tuesday’s close of RM4.3835/3905. The local unit’s direction remains influenced by shifting sentiment over recent remarks by US President Donald Trump regarding Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd Chief Economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid noted that Trump’s statement — indicating he has no intention to dismiss Powell — has eased market jitters temporarily. “The latest statement from Trump, saying he has no intention to fire Jerome Powell, has led to a rebound in benchmark equity indices, while the US Dollar Index (DXY) gradually approached the 98-point mark,” he told Bernama. He also highlighted the latest revisions from the International Monetary Fund (IMF), which have further dampened market mood. The IMF recently cut its US GDP growth forecast for 2025 to 1.8% from 2.7%, increasing the likelihood of a recession. “As such, the ringgit could remain slightly weak in the near term, given the rise in DXY today,” said Mohd Afzanizam. Despite its tentative movement against the greenback, the ringgit traded stronger against several major currencies. It appreciated against the Japanese yen at 3.0711/0941 from Tuesday’s 3.1206/1260 close and rose against the British pound to 5.8173/8605 from 5.8590/8683. The local note also firmed against the euro to 4.9755/0123 from 5.0362/0442. Against ASEAN currencies, the ringgit showed a mixed performance. It was higher against the Singapore dollar at 3.3357/3610 from 3.3523/3579 and remained steady versus the Philippine peso at 7.73/7.79. It strengthened against the Thai baht to 13.0397/1508 from 13.1930/2212, while staying flat against the Indonesian rupiah at 259.9/261.9. title: Wall Street Tumbles As Fed, Trade Concerns Rattle Investors
body: US stocks plunged on Monday as investor jitters over monetary policy and escalating trade tensions spurred a broad sell-off, sending the Dow Jones Industrial Average down nearly 1,000 points in what could be its worst April performance since 1932. The Nasdaq led losses with a 2.6% decline after dropping over 3% earlier in the day, dragged by major tech names including Tesla, Nvidia, and Apple. The ICE US Dollar Index tumbled more than 1%, hitting its lowest level in three years, while the euro, pound, yen, and Swiss franc surged against the greenback. Investor sentiment was shaken by President Donald Trump’s renewed pressure on the Federal Reserve, including a post on social media urging immediate rate cuts and calling Fed Chair Jerome Powell “Mr. Too Late, a major loser.” Market anxiety intensified after National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett stated on Friday that the administration was reviewing the possibility of removing Powell. Adding to the tension was weak trade data from South Korea, revealing a sharp drop in exports to the US, reinforcing concerns over global demand and the ongoing tariff disputes. In the bond market, longer-term Treasury yields rose, with the 10-year yield climbing to 4.404%, while gold soared past US$3,400 a troy ounce to a new all-time high. Bitcoin also gained on the back of safe-haven interest. Asian market performance was mixed, with Japan’s Nikkei falling 1.3% and China’s CSI 300 edging up 0.3%. Markets in Europe and Hong Kong remained closed for the Easter holiday. title: Trump vs Powell Round Two: Gold Shines Amid Market Fears
body: Bullion prices soared to another all-time high on Tuesday, while the dollar wobbled and global equities mostly slipped, after former US President Donald Trump unleashed fresh criticism of Federal Reserve Chairman Jerome Powell—stoking fears over the central bank’s independence. Gold breached US$3,457 as investors scrambled for safety, with anxiety gripping markets after Trump called Powell a “major loser” and “Mr. Too Late” in a Monday tirade on Truth Social. He urged pre-emptive interest rate cuts, claiming inflation was virtually non-existent and highlighting recent rate reductions by the European Central Bank. The remarks came days after Trump blasted Powell over inflation concerns tied to new tariffs, saying his “termination cannot come fast enough” and warning, “If I want him out, he’ll be out of there real fast, believe me.” While the initial outburst sparked limited reaction, Monday’s follow-up triggered a sharp selloff, with Wall Street’s three major indices plunging around 2.5%. “The first volley on Thursday had little market reaction, but Monday’s second barrage has seen an intensification of the ‘sell America trade’,” said National Australia Bank’s Tapas Strickland. “Whether or not President Trump is legally able and willing to move against the US Fed, the jousting underscores the loss of US exceptionalism and the very real policy risk for investors,” he added. Amid the turmoil, the US dollar steadied after Monday’s sharp drop but remained fragile against key peers. Equities seesawed in Asia, with Hong Kong, Sydney, Taipei, Jakarta, Wellington and Manila retreating, while Shanghai, Singapore and Seoul managed modest gains. Analysts warn that any attempt by Trump to fire Powell could provoke an investor exodus and shatter confidence in the US economy. “Were Powell to be fired, the initial reaction would be a huge injection of volatility into financial markets, and the most dramatic rush to the exit from US assets that it is possible to imagine,” said Michael Brown, strategist at Pepperstone. “Lower, much lower, equities; Treasuries sold across the board; and, the dollar falling off a cliff. Any sign of the longstanding, independent nature of the Fed coming under threat would see investors across the globe selling every single US-based asset that they have,” he added, noting it could even threaten the stability of the global financial system. The European Commission’s fresh guidance on the Deforestation Regulation and Powell’s fate are now key flashpoints for markets, with investors eyeing whether Trump will attempt to formally remove the Fed chair—raising legal and constitutional questions while threatening an already fragile investor landscape. title: US Stock Plunge, Ringgit May Edge To 4.36 Levels
body: The ringgit continued its upward momentum against the US dollar at Tuesday’s opening, edging closer to test its immediate support level at RM4.36. At 8 am, the local unit advanced to 4.3550/3840 versus the greenback, strengthening from Monday’s close of 4.3670/3735. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US Dollar Index (DXY) slipped nearly 1% to 98.278 points, as financial markets grew increasingly unsettled by President Trump’s repeated attempts to undermine the US Federal Reserve’s independence. “US equities took a plunge again as the US President continued his assault on the Fed Chair, claiming there is no inflation and that therefore the Fed Funds Rate should be lowered. The 10-year US Treasury yield rose by about nine basis points to 4.41%, while the two-year note yielded lower by three basis points to 3.76%,” he told Bernama . “While there could be views that the Fed is always late in the game, there should not be any attempt to compromise its independent judgement. This is an extraordinary situation which exacerbates the already gloomy outlook due to the tariff measures,” he added. The ringgit also posted gains across a basket of major currencies. It strengthened against the Japanese yen to 3.0913/1121 from 3.1046/1095, improved against the euro to 5.0139/0473 from 5.0408/0483, and appreciated against the British pound to 5.8266/8654 from 5.8513/8601 previously. Among ASEAN currencies, the local note traded mostly higher. It gained against the Singapore dollar to 3.3372/3599, improved against the Philippine peso to 7.69/7.74, and rose versus the Thai baht to 13.1187/2184. However, it remained nearly unchanged against the Indonesian rupiah, closing at 259.1/260.9 from 259.8/260.3. title: Oil Slumps Nearly 3% On US-Iran Talks And Demand Fears
body: Crude oil prices fell sharply on Monday, retreating nearly 3% as markets reacted to renewed hopes over a US-Iran nuclear agreement and lingering concerns about global demand. Brent crude settled 2.2% lower at US$66.59 a barrel, while West Texas Intermediate (WTI) dropped 1.92% to US$63.44. The sell-off came amid reports that Washington and Tehran had reached a draft framework for a potential nuclear deal. If finalised, such an agreement could lead to the lifting of sanctions and pave the way for the return of Iranian crude to international markets—reshaping global supply expectations. Analysts said the market is also grappling with a complex backdrop of escalating tariff tensions and economic slowdown fears, particularly as President Donald Trump renewed his criticism of the Federal Reserve, raising fresh concerns about monetary policy stability. The combined uncertainty has triggered a broader risk-off sentiment across financial markets, affecting not only commodities like oil, but also equities. Traders are now closely monitoring key US economic indicators, including the preliminary April manufacturing and services PMI data, for further clues on the strength of oil demand in the near term. body: RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has maintained its long position on the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI Futures (FKLI), despite the index slipping 7 points to close at 1,490 yesterday, signalling a consolidation phase below the key resistance of 1,500. title: CIMB Share Price Dips 2% In Early Trade
body: CIMB share price was down another 2% in early trade, coming in at RM6.73 against yesterday’s closing price of RM6.86. On a year-to-date basis, the share price has come down close to 18% from a high of RM8.39. RHB Investment Bank yesterday downgraded the banking sector to NEUTRAL from Overweight, citing increasing macroeconomic uncertainties. The decision follows the growing concerns around the potential escalation of US reciprocal tariffs, which are now adding more volatility to the market. According to RHB Research, while the pause in tariff hikes offers a brief opportunity for investors to reposition, the outlook for the global economy remains cautious, which typically affects the performance of the banking sector when economic growth slows down or rate cuts are anticipated. The house also revised Malaysia’s GDP growth forecast downwards to 4.5% from 5%, with the risks now leaning towards a lower growth range of 3.5-4% should trade tensions worsen. The firm highlighted that Malaysia’s trade and manufacturing sectors are likely to face increasing challenges due to these ongoing issues, although the Overnight Policy Rate (OPR) is expected to remain at 3% for the time being. This prompted RHB Research to advise a more cautious approach, favouring large-cap banks such as Malayan Banking (MAY), Hong Leong Bank (HLBK), and CIMB, which are less sensitive to rate cuts and better positioned to weather the current turbulence. title: Asian Markets Struggle Amid US Economic Concerns And Dollar Weakness
body: Asian stock markets faced a challenging session on Tuesday, struggling to maintain their ground after US markets were rattled by concerns over President Donald Trump’s attacks on the Federal Reserve and a continued sell-off in US assets. Wall Street saw a steep decline of around 2.5 per cent on Monday, with the dollar falling to three-year lows. The uncertainty surrounding the independence of the Federal Reserve weighed heavily on Treasuries. Despite the turmoil in the US, the losses in Asia were relatively limited, sparking discussions about the potential reallocation of funds to the region’s equities. However, the ongoing concerns about the economic impact of tariffs remained a significant drag on the markets. “The ‘sell America’ trade was in full flight,” said Tapas Strickland, head of market economics at NAB. He added that the President’s vocal criticisms of Fed Chair Jerome Powell, particularly his call for rate cuts, underscored a loss of US exceptionalism and raised policy risks for investors. Strickland pointed out that the political tension was adding to the uncertainty surrounding the US economy. While the selling pressure eased slightly in Asia, it provided some relief for US stock futures, with S&P 500 futures rising 0.4 per cent and Nasdaq futures up 0.5 per cent. Despite this, the market remained on edge as the earnings season continued, with major companies such as Tesla, Alphabet, Boeing, Northrop Grumman, Lockheed Martin, and 3M set to report their results this week. Tesla had already seen a nearly 6 per cent drop on Monday amid reports of production delays. In Asia, Japan’s Nikkei index dipped by 0.3 per cent, while the MSCI Asia-Pacific index excluding Japan fell by 0.2 per cent. However, Chinese blue-chip stocks held steady. European markets fared worse, with futures for the EUROSTOXX 50, FTSE, and DAX all down around 0.7 per cent amid volatile trading. The US bond market also reflected growing concerns. Yields on US 10-year notes stood at 4.40 per cent, having climbed due to fears that President Trump could attempt to replace Powell with someone more inclined to cut rates. This, combined with rising inflation driven by Trump’s tariffs, further exacerbated the uncertainty. The White House’s trade talks, which are ongoing or about to begin, added to the unease, as analysts at JPMorgan noted that the average trade deal takes 18 months to negotiate and 45 months to implement. The loss of confidence in US assets led to a sharp decline in the dollar, which hit its lowest point since March 2022 against a basket of currencies. The dollar also hit a decade-low against the Swiss franc at 0.8038, while the euro briefly rose above US$1.1500, settling at US$1.1486. In contrast, the dollar’s weakness and a surge in demand for safe-haven assets helped gold reach a new record, surpassing US$3,343 an ounce. On the other hand, oil prices saw a slight recovery, with Brent rising 58 cents to US$66.82 a barrel, and US crude adding 51 cents to US$63.59 per barrel, as concerns about a global economic slowdown met the prospect of increased supply from OPEC. The markets now face a crucial week ahead, with earnings reports and trade developments likely to provide more clarity on the economic outlook. title: Tariff Nerves Push Gold To All-Time High At US$3,384
body: Gold prices surged to a fresh record above US$3,384 on Monday as safe haven demand spiked amid growing concerns over President Donald Trump’s tariff strategy and his increasingly public dispute with the US Federal Reserve. The dollar weakened further, falling against most of its peers including the yen and euro, while equity markets were mixed. Tokyo and Taipei ended in the red, pressured by currency strength, whereas Shanghai, Seoul, Singapore, Manila and Jakarta posted gains. The dollar’s decline came in the wake of Trump’s latest remarks on Fed chair Jerome Powell, stoking fears over the central bank’s independence. “If I want him out, he’ll be out of there real fast, believe me,” the president warned, after Powell had said that the White House’s tariffs were “highly likely to generate at least a temporary rise in inflation.” French Finance Minister Eric Lombard said Trump had already “hurt the credibility of the dollar with his aggressive moves on tariffs.” He added that if Powell were forced out, “this credibility will be harmed even more, with developments in the bond market.” Chicago Federal Reserve President Austan Goolsbee echoed these concerns, stating, “There’s virtual unanimity among economists that monetary independence from political interference… is really important.” Meanwhile, the White House is reportedly in talks with China. “Yeah, we’re talking to China,” Trump said last week. “I think we’re going to make a very good deal with China.” However, Beijing pushed back hard on Monday, warning other countries not to sign deals that compromise Chinese interests. “Appeasement will not bring peace, and compromise will not be respected,” a commerce ministry spokesperson said. “To seek one’s own temporary selfish interests at the expense of others’ interests is to seek the skin of a tiger,” the ministry added. That approach, it warned, “will ultimately fail on both ends and harm others.” While several nations, including Japan, are exploring ways to reduce the impact of US tariffs, China has been singled out for harsher measures — facing levies of up to 145% on some exports, while responding with duties of 125% on US goods. Oil prices also fell Monday, with fears over global economic growth and weak energy demand clouding the outlook. Trading volumes were lighter than usual due to Easter Monday holidays in several markets. Investors are closely watching this week’s upcoming global manufacturing data for signs of the early effects of Trump’s protectionist measures. Stephen Innes of SPI Asset Management said, “One thing that’s absolutely clear — and no longer debatable — is that the reputational hit to the US brand is real, and it’s not fading quietly into the next news cycle.” “It’s sticking. Investors, allies, and even central banks are starting to bake in the idea that American policymaking, both fiscal and monetary, is now a geopolitical variable — not a given,” he added. title: Wall Street Slips As Trump Targets Fed Chair, UnitedHealth Weighs On Dow
body: US stocks ended mixed on Thursday, as sharp losses in UnitedHealth shares dragged the Dow Jones Industrial Average lower, while tensions between the White House and the Federal Reserve unsettled investor sentiment. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1.3%, pressured by a more than 20% plunge in UnitedHealth following disappointing results. As a price-weighted index, the Dow was particularly sensitive to the drop in UnitedHealth’s share price. In contrast, the S&P 500 managed a marginal gain of 0.1%, while the Nasdaq Composite closed nearly flat. Despite losses among most of the Magnificent Seven tech stocks, the index held steady. Thursday’s market moves marked a rare occurrence — the first recorded instance since 1928 where the Dow fell more than 1% while the S&P 500 posted gains, according to Dow Jones Market Data. President Donald Trump reignited pressure on Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell, stating that Powell’s “termination cannot come fast enough.” Trump accused Powell of acting too slowly on interest rate cuts, contrasting the Fed’s approach with the European Central Bank, which slashed rates by 25 basis points in its seventh cut over eight meetings. Adding to the uncertainty, The Wall Street Journal reported that Trump had spoken in recent months with former Fed governor Kevin Warsh about potentially replacing Powell before the end of his term. Investors are concerned about the Fed’s independence amid these escalating tensions. Powell on Wednesday warned of a “strong likelihood” of economic impact from higher tariffs, but suggested the Fed may prioritise inflation control over employment growth. Meanwhile, geopolitical risks continued to weigh on sentiment. Nvidia dropped nearly 3%, extending losses from Wednesday after the US announced new export restrictions to China. President Trump later said he was in contact with China’s top leadership on a potential tariff deal. On the corporate front, earnings from American Express, Blackstone, and TSMC rolled in. TSMC, the world’s largest contract chip maker, posted a stronger-than-expected Q1 profit, offering a rare bright spot amid the volatility. title: Ringgit Edges Higher As US-China Tensions Keep Dollar Soft
body: The ringgit opened firmer against the US dollar on Friday, lifted by continued softness in the US Dollar Index (DXY), which stayed below the 100-point mark amid ongoing US-China trade tensions. At 8am, the local note improved to RM4.3995/4150 against the greenback from Thursday’s close of RM4.4050/4095. “Given the current weakness in the greenback, the US dollar-ringgit pair is expected to remain around the RM4.40 level,” said Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid, speaking to Bernama. He noted the ringgit appreciated 0.08% to RM4.4073 against the US dollar on Thursday, aligning with the softer DXY. US labour market data also lent weight to the outlook, with initial jobless claims falling to 215,000 last week, signalling relative resilience despite the broader economic uncertainty. Elsewhere, the ringgit traded mixed against a basket of major currencies. It was weaker against the Japanese yen at 3.0893/1019 from 3.0849/0883, and slipped against the British pound to 5.8368/8574 from 5.8331/8391. However, it gained slightly on the euro, trading at 5.0027/0203 compared to 5.0102/0154 previously. Against regional currencies, the local unit performed more favourably. It rose against the Singapore dollar to 3.3548/3705 from 3.3562/3601, and firmed versus the Thai baht at 13.1651/2491 from 13.2211/2417. The ringgit also held steady against the Indonesian rupiah at 261.3/262.4, and appreciated slightly against the Philippine peso at 7.76/7.80 compared with 7.77/7.79 previously. title: How’s The Market After The Relief Rally?
body: In line with higher regional markets, KLCI gained 6.4 pts to 1,483.3, heading towards the envisaged 1,475-1,500 gap as investors weighed lingering US-China tariff tensions against optimism surrounding President Xi Jinping’s three-day state visit to Malaysia. Market breadth improved to 1.36 (from 0.56), though trading volume slipped 16.7% to 2.45bn shares worth RM1.61bn, reflecting cautious sentiment. On fund flows, local institutions extended their net buying streak to 39th consecutive day (+RM38m, Apr: +RM2.65bn, YTD: +RM10.37bn) while local retailers (-RM22m Apr: +RM119m, YTD: +RM2.36bn) alongside foreign institutions (-RM16m, Apr:-RM2.77bn, YTD:-RM12.73bn) emerged as major net sellers. Following a 7% relief rally from the 21-month low of 1,386.6 to 1,483.3, profit-taking may emerge to limit further upside, especially near the key 1,475-1,500 resistance gap (7 Apr). A decisive breakout above 1,500 after consolidation could unlock further gains toward stronger resistance levels at 1,518 (200W MA), 1,535 (50% FR), and 1,556 (upper BB). Conversely, a break below 1,468 (long-term uptrend line from the Covid-19 low) may trigger a downward move toward 1,457 (23.6% FR), 1,425 (13% FR), and potentially 1,400 Mirroring Wall Street’s renewed selloff, the near-term outlook for the KLCI may remain volatile as investors navigate escalating US-China tensions, rising recession risks, Fed policy uncertainty, treasury market swings, ongoing earnings season, and tariff-related noises. Hong Leong Investment Bank said said, downside risks appear limited, with strong technical support at the 1,400–1,430–1,450 zones likely to attract bargain hunting. This is underpinned by KLCI’s undemanding valuation of 12.5x CY26 P/E (near -1.5SD below its 5-year average) and a historic low in foreign shareholding at 19.3% as of March. title: Holy Day, No Play: Markets Shut For Good Friday
body: Stock markets across the globe are observing Good Friday today, a key Christian holiday marking the crucifixion of Jesus Christ. As a result, multiple major exchanges and funds have temporarily halted trading, giving market participants a momentary pause during a bustling spring season. Both the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) and the Nasdaq Stock Market are closed today in observance of Good Friday. While not a federal holiday, the closure follows tradition. The US bond market also ceased trading early on Thursday at 2 pm ET and remains closed today. Normal trading activities will resume on Monday, 21 April 2025. In India, the National Stock Exchange (NSE) and Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) are shut for the day, affecting all segments including equities, equity derivatives, currency derivatives, and securities lending and borrowing (SLB). The Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX) is closed for the morning session and will reopen in the evening from 5.00 pm to 11.30 pm. Full trading across Indian markets will resume on Monday. Good Friday is among 14 market holidays scheduled for 2025 in India. Trading is paused for a broad list of ETFs and financial instruments that are tied to the above markets or follow global exchange schedules, including: Asia-Pacific ETFs : EAXJ, EEM, EEMA, FAXJ, FEM, FEMA, FNAU, FNAXJ, FNEA, FNEM, FNEMK, FNID, FNJP, FNMY, FNNZ, FNPH, FNSA, FNTH, FNTW, FNVN Multi-Region Funds : MCNAX, MCNEU, MCNJP, MCNUS, MCNWO, NSG, NSP India and Southeast Asia Specific ETFs : FNAU, FNID, FNJP, FNMY, FNNZ, FNPH, FNSA, FNTH, FNTW, FNVN Additional Affected Funds : AMAF, AMF, AMMF, BTR, FRT, FRTO, MKP, MKPO, OIL, RT, SMP, SMPO, TF, TFO, WMP, WMPO While some markets in Europe and Asia may remain open with limited hours, trading volume is expected to be muted globally. Investors are encouraged to review exchange-specific calendars to confirm resumption schedules and plan trades accordingly. This coordinated closure underscores the respect for religious and cultural traditions that continue to shape operations across international financial markets. title: All Eyes On Ancom’s Brazil Development
body: Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) has maintained its BUY call on Ancom Nylex, with an unchanged target price of RM1.13, citing expected earnings recovery and growth prospects from the upcoming commercialisation of a new agrichemical product. The research house noted that the company’s 9MFY25 core earnings of RM43.3 million, which declined 29% year-on-year, were within its expectations but fell slightly short of consensus forecasts. HLIB highlighted that the core net profit jumped 71% quarter-on-quarter to RM18.7 million in 3QFY25, driven by a recovery in the agrichemical (Agrichem) segment. The prior quarter had been impacted by a spike in international freight costs and unfavourable foreign exchange movements due to heightened geopolitical tensions. The easing of freight costs in 4QFY25 is expected to further support Ancom Nylex’s earnings recovery. Despite ongoing geopolitical uncertainties, demand for the group’s agrichem products remains stable, according to the research house. This resilience is attributed to low demand elasticity and limited substitutes for the active ingredients (AIs) produced by the company. HLIB added that the US market represents approximately 10% of Ancom Nylex’s agrichem revenue, implying limited exposure to potential downside risks from that region. Looking ahead, HLIB anticipates FY26 earnings to be underpinned by the commercialisation of a new product, Chemical T, in the second quarter of calendar year 2025. The compound is expected to reach a production capacity of 1,000 metric tonnes annually. Additionally, the group’s registration for MSMA labelling on soybean crops in Brazil remains on track for approval by mid-2025. If successful, this would allow Ancom Nylex to enter Brazil’s vast soybean herbicide market, which is estimated to be five times larger than its current sugarcane market. Valuation-wise, HLIB’s RM1.13 target price is based on a 15 times price-to-earnings multiple on forecasted FY26 earnings, a slight discount to the global peer average of 17.5 times. The research house continues to favour Ancom Nylex for its position as the sole large-scale AI producer for herbicides in Southeast Asia, a niche that comes with high entry barriers, and for its pipeline of new AI products set to drive future earnings. title: Tokyo Stocks Rally On Hopes For US Trade Deal Despite Fed Warning
body: Optimism over Japan–US trade talks lifted Tokyo’s benchmark Nikkei 225 by 1.4%, closing at 34,377.60, with gains echoed across several Asian markets despite warnings from US Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell about potential economic headwinds stemming from new US tariffs. Investors took comfort in progress between Tokyo and Washington, particularly given Japan’s position as the largest foreign investor in the United States. “Big Progress!” US President Donald Trump posted on social media, while Japan’s envoy Ryosei Akazawa noted, “I understand that the US wants to make a deal within the 90 days. For our part, we want to do it as soon as possible.” Japanese Prime Minister Shigeru Ishiba added, “The talks won’t be easy,” but confirmed that Trump had “expressed his desire to give the negotiations… the highest priority.” Besides Tokyo, gains were recorded in Hong Kong (+1.2% to 21,317.46), Singapore, Mumbai, Shanghai (+0.1% to 3,280.34), Sydney, Seoul, Wellington and Jakarta. However, Taipei and Bangkok posted slight declines. Despite market gains, concerns persisted following Powell’s remarks in Chicago. “Tariffs are highly likely to generate at least a temporary rise in inflation,” he said, adding that “you’ll probably see continued volatility.” He cautioned that the Federal Reserve might be forced into a “challenging scenario” where it must choose between tackling inflation or preserving employment. Chris Weston of Pepperstone noted, “Powell has again frustrated some, who perhaps optimistically felt he might change the messaging… a factor that is priced at 80 percent by interest rate swaps traders.” The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 1.7% to close at 39,669.39, while gold continued its rally, breaching US$3,357 amid fears of prolonged trade tensions. Oil prices extended gains after the US sanctioned a second Chinese “teapot” refinery for buying Iranian crude. The State Department said the measures against Shandong Shengxing Chemical were part of efforts to “drive Iran’s illicit oil exports” to zero. The World Trade Organization’s Director-General, Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, expressed alarm over the escalating trade war. “I am very concerned,” she said, warning that China–US trade volumes could collapse by as much as 81%. London’s FTSE 100 slipped 0.5% to 8,230.71 at the open. The euro fell to $1.1333, the pound edged down to $1.3231, while the dollar strengthened to 142.69 yen. title: Ringgit Opens Higher, Boosted By Softer US Dollar Index
body: The ringgit started Thursday on a firmer note against the US dollar, appreciating to RM4.3960/4080 at 8am from RM4.4085/4135 at Wednesday’s close. Despite the gain, trading remained range-bound as market participants kept a close eye on ongoing uncertainties tied to US tariff policies. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US Dollar Index (DXY) fell by 0.83% to 99.380 points, following comments from Federal Reserve chairman Jerome Powell, who acknowledged the significant uncertainty around US trade measures. Afzanizam noted that Powell had also warned these policy flip-flops could undermine the Fed’s dual mandate of maintaining price stability and full employment. He added, “Yesterday, the ringgit strengthened by 0.34% against the US dollar to RM4.4110. Given the softer DXY, the US dollar-ringgit pair could trade within the RM4.4000 to RM4.4100 range today.” US equity futures were also hit as investors expressed disappointment over the Fed’s more cautious, wait-and-see stance—falling short of market hopes for a firm move on rate cuts. The ringgit traded mostly lower against major currencies. It eased against the euro to 5.0088/0225 from 5.0072/0129 and fell versus the Japanese yen to 3.0947/1036 from 3.0861/0898. However, it appreciated against the British pound, rising to 5.8159/8318 from 5.8488/8554. Against ASEAN currencies, the ringgit was mostly firmer. It inched higher against the Indonesian rupiah at 261.0/261.9 from 261.8/262.2, rose against the Philippine peso to 7.74/7.77 from 7.76/7.78, and improved vis-à-vis the Singapore dollar to 3.3527/3623 from 3.3537/3578. However, it edged lower against the Thai baht, slipping to 13.2810/3297 from 13.2547/2773.
