title: Nasdaq Sinks 3% As US Tightens Nvidia Export Curbs, Fed Flags Trade War Risks
body: US markets plunged overnight as tech stocks led a broad-based sell-off, triggered by fresh trade curbs on semiconductor exports to China and a stark warning from Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell over the economic fallout from ongoing tariff tensions. The Nasdaq Composite tumbled 3.1%, weighed down by a 6.9% drop in Nvidia after the chipmaker said it would incur a US$5.5 billion charge due to new US restrictions on exports of its H20 AI processors. The curbs, which also affect rival AMD, target chips previously designed to comply with existing US export rules. The Dow Jones Industrial Average shed 700 points, or 1.7%, while the S&P 500 slid 2.2%. Wall Street’s fear gauge, the Cboe Volatility Index, surged 8% as investor anxiety escalated. Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell added to market jitters, warning that the central bank may face “difficult trade-offs” in shielding the US economy from damage caused by President Trump’s intensifying trade war. Investors were left disappointed by the lack of clarity on interest rate cuts. Tech sector woes deepened after ASML, a key supplier of semiconductor equipment, reported weaker-than-expected orders and flagged potential disruption from tariffs. Its shares fell 5.2%. Trade-related uncertainty also rocked traditional sectors. Shares in J.B. Hunt Transport Services slumped 7.7% after the logistics giant posted an 8% drop in quarterly earnings, citing a slowdown in retail shipments. Adding to the drama, US retail sales data showed a 1.4% surge in March, as consumers rushed to purchase cars ahead of expected tariff hikes. Meanwhile, California state leaders announced plans to sue the Trump administration over trade measures, and President Trump said he would personally join upcoming talks with a Japanese delegation. In China, a new trade negotiator was appointed as data showed the country maintained its quarterly growth pace, bolstered by a surge in pre-tariff export activity. Asian and European markets also closed in the red. Investors now brace for further volatility as the global trade landscape grows more uncertain. title: US Stocks Lower As Nvidia Weighs On Nasdaq
body: Wall Street stocks fell early Wednesday (Apr 16) despite strong US retail sales data, with the Nasdaq decisively lower after Nvidia disclosed a large financial hit from American export restrictions to China. About 15 minutes into trading, the Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 0.3 per cent at 40,236.71. The broad-based S&P 500 shed 0.9 per cent to 5,346.96, while the tech-rich Nasdaq Composite Index tumbled 1.7 per cent to 16,546.37. US markets have stabilised this week after upheaval in the Treasury market last week. Investors are hoping that President Trump’s decision to pull back from some tariffs will open the door to trade deals. Among individual companies, United Airlines surged 5.2 per cent after reporting better than expected profits despite what it called a “challenging macroeconomic environment”. title: US Stock Futures Decline As Nvidia’s China Chip Export Curbs Rattle Markets
body: US stock futures retreated sharply on Tuesday evening after Nvidia Corp revealed new export restrictions to China that could cost the chipmaker US$5.5 billion, adding fresh uncertainty to markets already on edge over President Donald Trump’s evolving trade policy. Futures tied to the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 0.5%, while S&P 500 futures fell 0.8%. Contracts linked to the Nasdaq Composite slumped 1.2%, reflecting pressure on technology shares following Nvidia’s announcement. The slide came after a new filing from Nvidia disclosed that the US government now requires licences for the export of its H20 artificial intelligence chip to China. The company warned the move would result in multibillion-dollar charges, triggering a sharp sell-off in its shares during after-hours trading. Earlier in the day, Wall Street’s major indexes had already shown signs of fatigue, paring gains as traders remained wary of the direction of Trump’s trade policy. The White House has paused certain tariffs on consumer electronics but is now reportedly weighing new levies on pharmaceuticals, semiconductors, and critical minerals. Meanwhile, exemptions on auto duties are still under review, and negotiations with several trading partners remain ongoing following a temporary 90-day halt on most “reciprocal” tariffs introduced last week. With investor sentiment wavering and major tech firms in the spotlight, markets are expected to remain volatile as geopolitical and regulatory risks continue to cast a shadow over global trade and corporate earnings. title: US Stock Futures Dip After S&P 500 Rally; Earnings Season in Focus
body: US stock futures slipped Monday night following back-to-back gains on Wall Street, as investors turned cautious ahead of a key week for first-quarter earnings. Dow Jones Industrial Average futures dropped 81 points, or 0.2%, while S&P 500 futures and Nasdaq 100 futures fell 0.2% and 0.3%, respectively. The decline came after a strong performance during Monday’s regular session, driven by tech stocks and optimism around tariff relief. The Dow closed 312.08 points higher (+0.78%), the S&P 500 climbed 0.79%, and the Nasdaq Composite rose 0.64%. Markets rallied after US Customs and Border Protection announced tariff exemptions on consumer electronics such as smartphones and semiconductors. However, uncertainty lingered as President Donald Trump and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick hinted the exemptions may only be temporary. Investors are now shifting focus to a wave of earnings reports, with Bank of America, Citigroup, Johnson & Johnson, and PNC Financial all set to report before Tuesday’s opening bell. Still, analysts warn that this earnings season may offer limited clarity on how companies are navigating Trump’s evolving tariff policy. “We’re just going to hear a lot of uncertainty,” said Brenda Vingiello, Chief Investment Officer of Sand Hill Global Advisors, on CNBC. “I don’t think we’re going to have a lot of answers after this earnings season other than that Q1 was probably pretty good.” Tuesday will also see the release of March’s import and export price indexes, along with the Empire State Manufacturing Survey from the New York Fed. Despite near-term volatility, Oppenheimer Chief Investment Strategist John Stoltzfus maintained a bullish outlook. “We remain positive on stocks,” he wrote, adding that pullbacks this year have mostly resembled “trims” and “haircuts” rather than a shift in trend. He believes the bull market remains intact, supported by strong fundamentals and ongoing tech innovation. Stoltzfus named information technology, communications services, consumer discretionary, financials, and industrials as his top sector picks for the current cycle. title: The Yuan Strengthens Amid Strong Trade Report
body: The central parity rate of the Chinese currency renminbi, or the yuan, strengthened 14 pips to 7.2096 against the U.S. dollar Tuesday, according to the China Foreign Exchange Trade System. In China’s spot foreign exchange market, the yuan is allowed to rise or fall by 2 percent from the central parity rate each trading day. The central parity rate of the yuan against the U.S. dollar is based on a weighted average of prices offered by market makers before the opening of the interbank market each business day. Incidentally, China reported its trade data with total goods imports and exports expanding 1.3 percent year on year in the first quarter of this year. According to the General Administration of Customs (GAC), China’s exports during the period rose 6.9 percent to 6.13 trillion yuan (about 850.1 billion U.S. dollars) while imports fell 6 percent to 4.17 trillion yuan. Despite the weak momentum of global economic growth, intensified trade protectionism and geopolitical tensions, China’s foreign trade has maintained stable growth with progress in high-quality development this year, Wang Lingjun, deputy head of the GAC, told a press conference. title: Tencent Holdings Stocks Grossly Oversold, Poised For Climb: HLIB
body: Tencent reported strong financial results for FY2024, with total revenue reaching RMB660.3 billion, an 8% year-over-year increase, and net profits surging by 66% year-over-year to RMB196.5 billion. The company’s robust performance was primarily driven by: Strong Gaming Growth: Tencent’s gaming division saw significant growth, fueled by the continued success of evergreen titles like Honor of Kings (HoK), Peacekeeper Elite, and VALORANT, as well as new game releases such as DNF Mobile and Delta Force. Domestic game revenue increased by 23% year-over-year, benefiting from the easing of regulations in China’s gaming sector. Surge in Marketing Services: Revenue from marketing services increased by 17% year-over-year, driven by higher user engagement across platforms including Video Accounts, WeChat Moments, and Tencent’s mobile ad network. The integration of DeepSeek across core products like WeChat and Yuanbao was a key factor in this growth. Steady Expansion in Fintech & Business Services: Tencent’s Fintech and Business services segment grew by 4% year-over-year, generating RMB212.0 billion in revenue. This expansion was supported by the company’s HunYuan (HY) Foundation Model, which facilitated the deployment of AI in internal applications like ad targeting, positioning Tencent for future growth in consumer AI interactions through Yuanbao, Weixin, and other services. Bloomberg projects a commendable 10.3% EPS CAGR for Tencent from FY24 to FY26, highlighting the company’s ability to adapt, innovate, and achieve growth in a dynamic market. This growth is expected to be driven by: AI Advancements & Integration: Tencent is heavily investing in AI, utilizing its HY Foundation model, which includes large language models (LLM), multi-modal models, and open-sourced HY models. These AI innovations are accelerating the integration of AI into enterprise-facing services (IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS) and enhancing existing business segments like ad targeting, content creation, and entertainment production. AI-Enhanced Gaming & User Engagement: Tencent is leveraging AI to improve user experience in gaming through game matching and coaching systems. These enhancements are projected to increase user retention in major titles like Honor of Kings and Valorant, boosting revenue from the Value-Added Services (VAS) segment. B2B AI Solutions: Tencent has integrated AI into its SaaS solutions, such as Tencent Meeting and Tencent Docs, to scale its B2B operations. The addition of automated summaries and real-time transcriptions has reportedly driven a 100% year-over-year increase in monthly active users, reaching 15 million, indicating strong demand for these tools. Strategic Partnerships & International Expansion: Tencent is pursuing global expansion through strategic partnerships. This includes a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with Mega Berjaya Teknologi, a leading cloud service provider in Indonesia, to support digital transformation in the region and expand Tencent’s network among Indonesian businesses. Tencent Cloud also launched its first Middle East Cloud Region in Saudi Arabia in February 2025, with plans to launch new availability zones later in the year, facilitating broader SaaS and PaaS offerings in the region. Hong Leong Investment Berhad believes Tencent is currently trading at an undemanding FY26E P/E of 17.8x, well below the industry average of 27x. After sliding 23.4% from YTD high at HKD547 (7 Mar) to HKD419 (9 Apr) amid Trump’s tariff angst and global recessionary fears, the stock has gradually recovered to end at HKH454. A successful refill of the HKD462-491 gap could lift the stock to revisit HKD504 (23.6% FR) and HKD523 (13% FR) zones. Major supports are lying at HKD434 (61.8% FR) and HKD417 (200D MA). A breakdown below 200D MA will lead to further rout towards HKD400. title: Ringgit Strengthens Against US Dollar As Tariff Policy Uncertainty Weighs On Greenback
body: The ringgit extended its gains against the US dollar on Tuesday, supported by weakening sentiment for the greenback amid ongoing ambiguity over US tariff policies. At 8am, the local currency stood stronger at RM4.4085/4215 versus the greenback, compared to Monday’s close of RM4.4100/4160. According to Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid, the inconsistent messaging around the US administration’s import tariffs — including potential new levies on semiconductors and pharmaceuticals — has made it difficult for markets to gauge macroeconomic direction. “The US Dollar Index (DXY) has slipped to 99.640 points, indicating a shift in sentiment as investors seek safer assets,” he said. He also noted that gold prices remain elevated, with spot gold trading at US$3,227.40 per ounce, a 23% surge from the beginning of the year, signalling investor caution. Afzanizam expects the ringgit to remain in the RM4.40–RM4.41 range for the day, driven by the softer dollar. The ringgit also advanced against several major currencies. It rose to 3.0773/0868 against the Japanese yen, 4.9975/5.0122 against the euro, and 5.8073/8244 versus the British pound. Among ASEAN currencies, the ringgit appreciated against the Thai baht (13.1182/1745) and the Singapore dollar (3.3494/3595), but was largely unchanged against the Indonesian rupiah (262.5/263.5) and Philippine peso (7.72/7.75). title: Ringgit Extends Gains As US Dollar Slips On Trade Concerns
body: The ringgit opened stronger against the US dollar on Monday, extending its recent gains as the greenback weakened to a fresh three-year low amid ongoing US-China trade tensions. At 8am, the ringgit stood at 4.4185/4270 against the US dollar, up 1.06% from last Friday’s close of 4.4200/4265. The US Dollar Index (DXY) slipped below the 100-point mark, a move described as puzzling by Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid, considering the prevailing global risk aversion surrounding trade and tariff uncertainties. He said market sentiment remained fragile despite US President Donald Trump’s announcement over the weekend that tariffs on smartphones and computers would be temporarily lifted. “US data, particularly the University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index, dropped to 50.8 points in April, suggesting consumers may stay cautious with their spending. “On that note, we sense that the dollar-ringgit is likely to stay within a narrow range, though with a slight positive bias, as the DXY has declined quite significantly,” he told Bernama. Against major currencies, the ringgit also posted broad gains. It rose against the Japanese yen to 3.0761/0822 from 3.0952/1000, advanced against the euro to 5.0123/0220 from 5.0207/0281, and appreciated slightly against the British pound to 5.7820/7932 from 5.7849/7934. Among ASEAN currencies, the ringgit was mixed. It edged up against the Singapore dollar at 3.3491/3566 from 3.3495/3549 but slipped against the Thai baht to 13.1778/2141 from 13.1599/1902. It was largely unchanged against the Indonesian rupiah at 263.0/263.7 versus 263.1/263.6 previously, and flat against the Philippine peso at 7.75/7.77. title: Nikkei Rises As iPhone-Related Stocks Jump
body: Japan’s Nikkei share average ended higher on April 14, as iPhone-related shares jumped after the US excluded smartphones and other electronics from steep tariffs. The Nikkei gained 1.18% to close at 33,982.36, after gaining as much as 2.22% earlier in the session. The broader Topix rose 0.88% to end at 2,488.51. US President Donald Trump’s administration granted exclusions from steep tariffs on smartphones, computers and some other electronics imported largely from China, providing a big break to tech firms like Apple Inc that rely on imported products. However, both Trump and US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick said over the weekend these goods will come under separate tariffs, along with semiconductors, that may be imposed in a month or so. Shares of iPhone suppliers rose on April, with Murata Manufacturing gaining 1.65%. TDK jumped 4.27% and Taiyo Yuden surged 6%. Chip-testing equipment maker Advantest jumped 4.92% to provide the biggest boost to the Nikkei. Of more than 1,600 stocks trading on the Tokyo Stock Exchange’s prime market, 80% rose, 16% fell, while 2% traded flat. title: Gold Hits Fresh Record On Weaker Dollar, Trade War Uncertainty
body: Gold surged to a new all-time high of US$3,245.75 on Monday as investors flocked to the safe-haven asset amid fresh uncertainties over US trade policy and a weakening dollar. Despite initial optimism following the White House’s announcement that smartphones, semiconductors, and other electronics would be temporarily exempted from new tariffs, market jitters resurfaced after US President Donald Trump said the exemptions had been “misconstrued”. The dollar extended its losses against major currencies, with the euro rising to a three-year high of US$1.1396 and the Swiss franc climbing to its strongest level in a decade, further boosting gold prices. Adding to the momentum were concerns over the stability of US treasuries, with fears that countries like China may divest from their holdings, undermining the greenback’s traditional safe-haven appeal. Boston Federal Reserve president Susan Collins said the central bank would “absolutely be prepared” to act if market conditions worsened, citing expectations for inflation to rise “well above” 3% this year. Amid the uncertainty, Asian stock markets rallied, tracking gains on Wall Street, though the broader risk sentiment failed to dent demand for gold. body: Bursa Malaysia closed sharply higher on Monday, lifted by improved investor sentiment across Asia following the United States’ temporary exemption of reciprocal tariffs on popular electronic products. The FBM KLCI ended the day 26.10 points or 1.79% higher at 1,480.86, regaining the 1,480-point level, with Press Metal Aluminium Holdings Bhd (PMETAL) and Mr DIY Group (M) Bhd among the top gainers. Market breadth was positive with 798 gainers, 248 decliners, and 359 counters unchanged, while 969 stocks saw no trades. Total turnover stood at 2.99 billion shares valued at RM2.06 billion. The FTSE Bursa Malaysia All-Share Index also advanced, finishing at 10,999.76, up 189.68 points. Meanwhile, the ringgit stood at 4.4170 against the US dollar as at 5pm. title: Innovative Digital Tools from JOI® & Intel® Make Digital Learning Adoption Faster And Easier
body: In recent years, the education sector has seen a noticeable increase in educational standards, advancement and innovations. As the pace of change increases, the education sector must provide a holistic and quality education to support the adoption of digital learning in the digital age. As such, schools and other educational institutions have begun to adopt modern teaching methods through interactive intelligent boards, projectors, smart notebooks and more to ensure no one is left behind in this technological advancement era. On that note, SNS Network (M) Sdn Bhd, as a prominent ICT solution provider, introduced JOI® Smart Classroom and JOI® Virtual Lab Solutions, a flexible digital learning solution that is capable of enhancing collaborative learning and streamlining classroom management to ensure interactive and engaging lessons while at the same time ensuring digital learning can be easily adapted by all education institutions. With its state-of-the-art technology and Intel® based architecture solutions, both JOI® Smart Classroom and JOI® Virtual Lab Solutions offer an educational ecosystem that is suitable for both teachers and students, providing a flexible learning approach for different environments and settings, and their effectiveness lies in the use of sophis1cated technological equipment, as well as the layout and the implementation of a more flexible learning environment. The JOI® Smartboard allows multiple users to write on the board at the time as it can support a maximum of 40-touch point JOI® Smartboard At the heart of JOI® Smart Classroom is the JOI® Smartboard, a touchscreen-based interactive whiteboard software which supports a maximum of 40-point touch, with the writing precision reaching +-1mm and writing height as low as 2mm. Equipped with the latest Intel® Core™ processing chipset, the JOI® Smartboard enables better interaction between teachers and students as it allows multiple users to write on the board at the time. The JOI® Smartboard comes with a camera and microphone with a pickup range of up to 8m, and supports multi-operating systems (OS) and multi-modules as it has a built-in Android system. It even supports teamwork with four-split screen casting, allowing multiple users to interact simultaneously. Overall, this device will make online learning much more interesting as information can be conveyed easily and interactively through demonstration methods. The JOI® Smart Sense makes classroom management easier for teachers as this digital tool can streamline attendance tracking easily JOI® Smart Sense Complementing the JOI® Smartboard is the JOI® Smart Sense, an artificial intelligence-powered system that automates attendance and health checks. Armed with the latest Intel® Core™ processors which provide the computing power needed for seamless and interactive engagement, the JOI® Smart Sense makes classroom management easier for teachers as this digital tool can streamline attendance tracking easily thanks to its automated identification and verification features that seamlessly match records with the database. For the touch-free temperature checks, the processing begins with the detection of temperature by its built-in temperature scanner when there is a human close by and via the detection of temperature, relevant information will be processed and displayed. This entire process happens within a very short turnaround time thanks to its latest Intel® Core™ Processors. With touch-free temperature monitoring and facial recognition, educators can focus on teaching, knowing that safety and efficiency are seamlessly handled. The JOI® Virtual Lab Solution is a connected education kit that is boosted by a powerful mini-PC from Intel® which allows up to four guests to access the system simultaneously, ensuring collaborative and immersive learning JOI® Virtual Lab Solutions The JOI® Virtual Lab Solution is an end-to-end platform designed to revolutionise the learning experience. It is a connected education kit that is boosted by a powerful mini-PC from Intel® which allows up to four guests to access the system simultaneously, ensuring collaborative and immersive learning. With support for multiple OS including Windows, Linux and Ubuntu, this solution is versatile and easy to use, catering to diverse educational needs and significant benefits to the learning environment. This solution not only levels the playing field for students in underserved areas but also promotes sustainability and cost savings. JOI® Virtual Lab Solutions is designed for classrooms of various sizes and needs, offering easy scalability without the need for additional hardware investments. This Intel®-powered solution facilitates smooth device integration, making it ideal for both hybrid classrooms and collaborative learning environments, ultimately improving the educational experience for students and teachers alike. Enhanced Learning Experience Together with JOI® devices like the JOI® Book 133 Pro, JOI Classmate® 10 and JOI® Book 5115 that come with sleek or durable designs, portability and robust processing power with Intel® chipset, the JOI® Smart Classroom and JOI® Virtual Lab Solutions allow students and educators to seamlessly integrate multimedia tools and software for an enriched classroom experience, and the education sector to hasten its digital learning adaption. All these modern devices, powered by Intel® processors, are specifically designed to optimise teaching and learning experiences by offering efficient task processing and minimising downtime. Seamless Device Collaboration To ensure seamless device collaboration, the JOI® Smart Classroom app is there to make sure the JOI® Smartboard connects seamlessly with JOI® devices, making the class more interactive and engaging. Along with the JOI® Virtual Lab solution, which enables multi-OS usage simultaneously, it offers educators and students various options. This flexibility enhances learning experiences, creating a more dynamic and customisable classroom environment. Whether it’s hybrid setups involving video conferencing or in-person collaborative projects, JOI® with Intel® solutions provide the tools to succeed. Scalable, Customisable, Secure As institutions grow, so do their educational needs. The JOI® Smart Classroom and JOI® Virtual Lab solution powered by Intel® enable a scalable, customisable and secure classroom environment by offering flexible configurations and compatibility with multiple operating systems. Educators can tailor learning experiences to meet specific needs, while students benefit from diverse educational tools. In the era of heighten digital era, security is a key feature, with solutions safeguarding sensitive data and providing secure access to resources. Together, these features foster an adaptable, efficient and secure learning space, enhancing both teaching and student engagement.
